note: AI-written plain-language summaries (Claude) for roll calls whose official source has none. Each was written from the official page in basisUrl and is shown labeled as AI-generated. Applied only when the bill title matches.

ak:HB 1.title: SPECIE AS LEGAL TENDER
ak:HB 1.summary: Includes gold and silver specie (coin and stamped bullion) from qualifying governments in Alaska's legal tender without requiring anyone to accept it, and bars borough and city sales or use taxes on its metal value.

ak:HB 10.title: ADD FACULTY MEMBER UNIV BOARD OF REGENTS
ak:HB 10.summary: Adds a tenured faculty regent, raising the University of Alaska Board of Regents from 11 to 12 members until February 1, 2033, when it returns to 11.

ak:HB 101.title: CRIMES AGAINST MINORS; AGE CONSENT TO 18
ak:HB 101.summary: Raises from 16 to 18 the victim age in civil claims for sexual abuse and in crimes including murder, assault, stalking, child endangerment and enticement; adds 16- and 17-year-old victims to sexual abuse of a minor offenses; raises the child-witness age.

ak:HB 110.title: HEALTH CARE/LICENSURE COMPACTS/SOCIAL WRK
ak:HB 110.summary: Enacts the Multistate Nurse Licensure Compact and sets fees, with multistate license fees for registered and practical nurses at double the single-state fee (amendment 2 to a bill on a social work licensure compact).

ak:HB 116.title: COMMERCIAL FISHING INSURANCE CO-OP
ak:HB 116.summary: Exempts agreements among commercial fishermen to pool contributions for paying liability claims or vessel and gear losses from Alaska's insurance code.

ak:HB 117.title: ELEC MONITOR TRAWL FISHERY/SET NET PERMIT
ak:HB 117.summary: Sets conditions for electronic monitoring of fishing vessels using trawl gear in a finfish fishery and creates a new administrative area on the east side of Cook Inlet for regulating commercial set net permits.

ak:HB 121.title: ACCOUNTING; PRIVATE PRO. CONSERVATORS
ak:HB 121.summary: Removes the 150-semester-hour education requirement for CPA licensure; drops conditions on other states' licensing standards for out-of-state accountants' practice privilege; extends it to out-of-state firms over half CPA-owned; lets licensed CPAs qualify as private professional conservators.

ak:HB 123.title: TAXATION: VEHICLE RENTALS, SUBPOENAS
ak:HB 123.summary: Lowers the passenger vehicle rental tax from 10 to 9 percent (7 percent through a rental platform until July 2028), requires platforms with over 200 transactions to collect it, and limits tax-record subpoena enforcement to Alaska superior court.

ak:HB 125.title: BOARD OF FISHERIES MEMBERSHIP
ak:HB 125.summary: Requires the governor to appoint the seven Board of Fisheries members as two commercial fishing, two sport fishing, two subsistence fishing and one scientific member; current members serve out their terms.

ak:HB 126.title: REINSTATEMENT NATIVE CORPS/ANCSA REPORTS
ak:HB 126.summary: Adds to a Native village corporation reinstatement bill a provision letting dissolved religious nonprofit and religious corporations be reinstated at any time if no cause for dissolution is shown, or the default is corrected and double the delinquent amount paid.

ak:HB 13.title: MUNICIPAL PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTIONS; REFUND
ak:HB 13.summary: Lets municipalities exempt from property tax, without the $10,000 cap, homes of volunteer firefighters, medical and hazardous-materials responders; also converted long-term rentals, mobile home parks, low-income rentals, residents' homes and first-time buyers' homes; changes refund interest.

ak:HB 130.title: STATE EMPLOYEES: FLEXIBLE TIME CREDIT
ak:HB 130.summary: Requires the state to grant paid time off, as flexible time credit, to executive-branch classified employees not eligible for overtime for hours worked beyond their standard workweek.

ak:HB 133.title: PAYMENT OF CONTRACTS
ak:HB 133.summary: Requires state agencies, from July 2027, to pay contractors, and nonprofits, municipalities and Alaska Native organizations on grants, within 45 days of a compliant payment request (30 days from July 2028), with interest if late.

ak:HB 14.title: MED ASSIST;INSURANCE;DISABILITY/WORK COMP
ak:HB 14.summary: Requires insurers to pay for telehealth at least the in-person rate, repeals the catastrophic illness and chronic and acute medical assistance programs, and changes workers' compensation and disability benefits for certain firefighters.

ak:HB 16.title: CAMPAIGN FINANCE;CONTRIBUTION LIMITS;APOC
ak:HB 16.summary: Requires non-individual election spenders to have an in-state address or agent, raises contribution limits (individuals to candidates: $2,000 per election cycle, from $500 a year), adjusts them for inflation once a decade from 2031, and repeals two provisions limiting the foreign-influenced corporation spending ban.

ak:HB 17.title: DISABLED VETERANS: RETIREMENT BENEFITS
ak:HB 17.summary: Lets terminated public employees who are veterans rated permanently and totally disabled for a service-connected condition get a normal retirement benefit at any age with five years of service; repeals the bar on counting military service credit toward normal retirement and two related provisions.

ak:HB 173.title: LIC.: OCCUP/PHYS THERAPY;SPEECH;AUDIOLOGY
ak:HB 173.summary: Changes licensing for occupational and physical therapists and assistants, audiologists and speech-language pathologists, adds occupational therapist licensure compact privileges, creates a board executive administrator, and requires fingerprint-based national background checks.

ak:HB 174.title: REAA FUND: MT. EDGECUMBE, TEACHER HOUSING
ak:HB 174.summary: Allows the school fund for rural and small-district schools to pay for Mt. Edgecumbe High School construction and major maintenance and for teacher housing maintenance, and removes the $70 million cap on the fund balance.

ak:HB 176.title: UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FEES
ak:HB 176.summary: As passed by the House, requires the University of Alaska to give enrolled students 30 days' email notice before imposing a new fee or fee increase, and to provide itemized billing statements.

ak:HB 184.title: AIDEA: WORKFORCE HOUSING DEV.; MUNI TAX
ak:HB 184.summary: Adds financing of new workforce housing facilities with three or more units to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority's purposes, and repeals sec. 2, ch. 64, SLA 2018, concerning a mandatory municipal property tax exemption for certain authority assets.

ak:HB 193.title: UNEMPLOYMENT BEN; PAID LEAVE: PARENT/SICK
ak:HB 193.summary: Removes the condition that an employee work for an employer with 25 or more employees when a paid parental leave claim is made (amendment 1 to a bill creating paid parental leave and sick leave rules).

ak:HB 194.title: OIL/GAS CORP. INCOME TAX; ROYALTY SALE
ak:HB 194.summary: Creates an income tax on partnerships, LLCs, S corporations and sole proprietorships producing or transporting oil or gas in Alaska, at 5 to 9.4 percent on income above $1 million, and approves the sale of state royalty oil to Marathon Petroleum.

ak:HB 195.title: PHARMACISTS; PHYSICIAN ASSOCIATES
ak:HB 195.summary: Changes the term 'physician assistant' to 'physician associate', requires dentists, physicians, advanced practice nurses and optometrists to offer an opioid overdose drug prescription with certain opioid prescriptions, and changes pharmacists' collaborative practice, drug administration and licensing reciprocity rules.

ak:HB 20.title: PROHIBIT FEES FOR PAPER DOCUMENTS
ak:HB 20.summary: Bars insurers and other businesses from charging an additional fee or different rate for providing paper statements, invoices, notices or other documents, though duplicate copies may be charged.

ak:HB 202.title: NAME STATE VEGETABLE GIANT CABBAGE
ak:HB 202.summary: Designates the O-S Cross cabbage, known as giant green cabbage, as Alaska's official state vegetable.

ak:HB 211.title: INSURANCE: PREPAID LEGAL PLANS
ak:HB 211.summary: Exempts prepaid legal plans, where members prepay for legal services from contracted attorneys paid fixed fees, from state insurance law, and sets disclosure, advertising and disenrollment rules for the plans.

ak:HB 214.title: INSURANCE; TRANSPORT/DELIVERY NETWORK CO.
ak:HB 214.summary: Extends rideshare insurance rules to delivery couriers, requires companies to carry group occupational accident insurance of $1 million per accident for drivers and couriers, lets auto insurers exclude coverage while they work, and excludes couriers from workers' compensation.

ak:HB 216.title: TRANSFER OF RAILROAD LAND TO WHITTIER
ak:HB 216.summary: Authorizes the Alaska Railroad Corporation to convey its interest in the surface estate of about 84.8 acres of rail land in five areas of Whittier to the City of Whittier for fair market value.

ak:HB 221.title: ARTS AND CULTURE DAY
ak:HB 221.summary: Establishes the first Friday of every October as Alaska Arts and Culture Day.

ak:HB 23.title: STATE COMMISSION FOR CIVIL RIGHTS
ak:HB 23.summary: Renames the State Commission for Human Rights the Alaska State Commission for Civil Rights; lets the governor remove commissioners for cause; covers charitable, educational and religious nonprofits as employers; adds a defense for religious employers hiring for religious roles; changes report and conciliation rules.

ak:HB 239.title: CRIME/CNTRL SUBST/ADDRESS CONFIDENTIALITY
ak:HB 239.summary: Changes criminal law on offenses including sexual abuse of a minor, assault, stalking, homicide, and generated child sexual abuse material, adds sentencing and parole changes, and creates an address confidentiality program.

ak:HB 243.title: BARBERS & HAIRDRESSERS BD LICENSING
ak:HB 243.summary: Changes the Board of Barbers and Hairdressers' role from approving issuance of licenses and permits, including school licenses, to authorizing the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development to issue them.

ak:HB 244.title: CNA TRAINING
ak:HB 244.summary: Requires certified nurse aide training programs to teach client communication, observation, care planning and dementia-care skills, among other topics, starting January 1, 2027.

ak:HB 246.title: SPECIAL EDUCATION SERVICE AGENCY FUNDING
ak:HB 246.summary: Raises the minimum annual state allocation to the special education service agency from $23.13 to $26.89 per student in average daily membership, retroactive to July 1, 2026.

ak:HB 249.title: TRANSFER VEHICLE TITLE TO INSURER
ak:HB 249.summary: Lets a vehicle owner who transfers title to an insurance company after a damages payment sign supporting documents, such as a power of attorney and odometer disclosure, electronically without notarization.

ak:HB 25.title: DISPOSABLE FOOD SERVICE WARE
ak:HB 25.summary: Bars restaurants from serving prepared food in polystyrene foam disposable food service ware and bars the state from using or buying it, with exceptions.

ak:HB 26.title: STATEWIDE PUBLIC & COMMUNITY TRANSIT PLAN
ak:HB 26.summary: Requires a statewide public and community transit plan from the Department of Transportation and Public Facilities and defines 'tribal entity' for the department.

ak:HB 261.title: EDUCATION FUNDING
ak:HB 261.summary: Changes the school funding formula to count the greater of a school's prior three-year average, prior-year or current enrollment, and repeals the offset for enrollment drops of five percent or more.

ak:HB 262.title: NUMBER OF SUPERIOR COURT JUDGES
ak:HB 262.summary: Raises the number of superior court judges in the third judicial district from 28 to 29, and the statewide total from 45 to 46, effective July 1, 2026.

ak:HB 263.title: APPROP: OPERATING BUDGET;FUNDS;SUPP
ak:HB 263.summary: Makes appropriations for state government operating and loan program expenses for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026, capitalizes funds, amends existing appropriations, and makes supplemental appropriations.

ak:HB 265.title: APPROP: MENTAL HEALTH BUDGET
ak:HB 265.summary: Makes appropriations for operating and capital expenses of the state's integrated comprehensive mental health program for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026.

ak:HB 27.title: MEDICAL MAJOR EMERGENCIES; CPR CURRICULUM
ak:HB 27.summary: Requires the Department of Education and Early Development to adopt hands-only CPR curricula for public school students, and lets the health commissioner set designations for levels of care for major emergencies such as heart attack and stroke.

ak:HB 278.title: ECONOMIC DEV:AK-IRELAND TRADE COMM.
ak:HB 278.summary: Creates the Alaska-Ireland Trade Commission in the state commerce department, with nine members (five appointed by the governor, two by the House speaker, two by the Senate president), to promote trade, investment and exchanges between Alaska and Ireland.

ak:HB 28.title: EDU: SCHOOLS/TEACHERS/SCHOOL BD/LOAN PRGM
ak:HB 28.summary: Changes education law, including school district energy cost reimbursement, substitute teaching, school board member qualifications, school consolidation, and local contributions to school funding, and creates a teacher student loan repayment pilot program.

ak:HB 280.title: APPORTION TAXABLE INCOME
ak:HB 280.summary: Changes the Multistate Tax Compact and how income is apportioned to Alaska, including income of broadcasters, financial institutions and telecommunications providers, for tax years starting January 1, 2027.

ak:HB 289.title: APPROP: SUPPLEMENTAL
ak:HB 289.summary: Makes supplemental, capital and other appropriations, amends existing appropriations, and capitalizes funds.

ak:HB 298.title: LEGISLATIVE ETHICS CMTE & PROCEEDINGS
ak:HB 298.summary: Changes how the Select Committee on Legislative Ethics handles complaints, including seven-day acknowledgment and 10-day screening deadlines; lets it subpoena documents when its chair authorizes; and excludes its public members and employees from ombudsman jurisdiction.

ak:HB 302.title: TRAVEL INSURANCE; UNEMPLOYMENT BENEFITS
ak:HB 302.summary: Sets rules for selling travel insurance, including rebates, advertising and powers of the insurance director, and changes weekly unemployment benefit amounts.

ak:HB 31.title: VESSELS: REGISTRATION/DERELICT FUND
ak:HB 31.summary: Exempts commercial vessels with Coast Guard documentation and a state commercial fishing license from state boat registration, and repeals the derelict vessel prevention fund, sending its balance and unclaimed vessel-sale proceeds to the general fund.

ak:HB 314.title: ARCH, ENG, SURVEYORS; REG INT DESIGN
ak:HB 314.summary: Sets registration and practice requirements for interior designers, extends the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors, and changes the scope of certification for those professions.

ak:HB 33.title: CONFLICT OF INTEREST: BDS FISHERIES/GAME
ak:HB 33.summary: Lets Board of Fisheries and Board of Game members who disclose a personal or financial interest tied to their or an immediate family member's involvement in a fish- or game-related business or organization keep deliberating and participating, but bars voting if a violation would result.

ak:HB 337.title: EXTEND WEST COAST STORM DISASTER
ak:HB 337.summary: Approves earlier declarations and extends the governor's October 9, 2025 disaster emergency declaration for the 2025 West Coast Storm until March 8, 2026.

ak:HB 35.title: PRISONERS: ELECTRONIC DEVICES, ID CARDS
ak:HB 35.summary: Lets state correctional facilities approve prisoner computer or tablet use for reentry, education, vocational training, legal research, visitation and health care, bars replacing in-person visitation with them, bars fees for e-mail or electronic visitation, and changes ID card rules.

ak:HB 36.title: FOSTER CHILDREN: PSYCH. TREATMENT/HOMES
ak:HB 36.summary: Defines and licenses treatment foster homes; lets the state place foster children in hospitals for short-term psychiatric care, with notice within 24 hours and court review within seven days; adds out-of-state psychiatric placements to an annual report.

ak:HB 363.title: ALCOHOL: PATRIOTIC ORGS; CLUB LICENSES
ak:HB 363.summary: Lets patriotic organizations such as the American Legion and VFW sell or dispense all alcoholic beverages, not just beer and wine, at their event permits, and lets members of any licensed patriotic organization buy under club licenses without a reciprocity agreement.

ak:HB 388.title: BULK FUEL LOAN CAP
ak:HB 388.summary: Raises the maximum bulk fuel loan to one borrower from $750,000 to $1,500,000, and lets the legislature appropriate money to the bulk fuel revolving loan fund in fiscal years 2026 and 2027 to cover such loans.

ak:HB 39.title: EDUCATION FOR DEAF & HARD OF HEARING
ak:HB 39.summary: Requires school districts, to the maximum extent possible, to give parents of deaf or hard-of-hearing children neutral information on hearing technology and communication methods and to provide services in the parent's chosen method; has the state support programs for deaf students.

ak:HB 47.title: CHLD SEX ABUSE MAT; GEN IMAGES; SOC MEDIA
ak:HB 47.summary: Adds the Alaska Social Media Regulation Act: platforms verify ages, get parental consent for minors' accounts, may not show minors ads or algorithm-personalized content, and block minors from 10:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. unless a parent changes it (amendment 5).

ak:HB 48.title: CIVIL LEGAL SERVICES FUND
ak:HB 48.summary: Raises the share of court filing fees that may be appropriated to the civil legal services fund from 10 percent to 25 percent.

ak:HB 50.title: SNOW CLASSICS
ak:HB 50.summary: As introduced, broadens the legal definition of a "snow classic" game of chance to a prize for the closest guess of snow accumulation at any specific location and time, rather than only the Mount Alyeska contest.

ak:HB 52.title: MINORS & PSYCHIATRIC HOSPITALS
ak:HB 52.summary: Gives minors in psychiatric hospitals a right, with exceptions, to at least two cumulative hours weekly of confidential phone or video contact with a parent, guardian or approved adult, and requires reporting of seclusion and restraint, annual reports and twice-yearly unannounced inspections.

ak:HB 53.title: APPROP: OPERATING BUDGET; CAP; SUPP
ak:HB 53.summary: Appropriates money for state government operating and loan program expenses for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2025, capitalizes funds, amends existing appropriations, and makes supplemental appropriations.

ak:HB 55.title: APPROP: MENTAL HEALTH BUDGET
ak:HB 55.summary: Appropriates money for the operating and capital expenses of the state's integrated comprehensive mental health program for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2025.

ak:HB 56.title: APPROP: SUPP; FUND CAP; CAP; AMENDING
ak:HB 56.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2025, and capital appropriations, amends and repeals some existing appropriations, and capitalizes funds.

ak:HB 57.title: SCHOOLS: COMM. DEVICES/CLASS SIZE/FUNDING
ak:HB 57.summary: Raises the base student allocation to $6,660, requires districts to set target class sizes of at most 23 (pre-K to grade 6) and 30 (grades 7 to 12), sets reading incentive grants of at least $450 per student, and creates an education funding task force.

ak:HB 58.title: OPA: PUBLIC ADVOCATE APPOINTMENT
ak:HB 58.summary: Has the governor appoint the public advocate from judicial council nominees, subject to legislative confirmation, for a four-year term, removable for good cause, and gives the advocate the office's fee-setting and procurement determinations.

ak:HB 62.title: SEXUAL ASSAULT EXAMINATION KITS/TRACKING
ak:HB 62.summary: Requires health care providers to notify police within 14 days of using a sexual assault exam kit; shortens police lab-submission from 30 to 20 days and lab testing from six months to 120 days; creates a kit tracking system.

ak:HB 65.title: RAILROAD CORP. FINANCING
ak:HB 65.summary: Raises the maximum revenue bonds the Alaska Railroad Corporation may issue to replace its Seward passenger dock and terminal from $60 million to $135 million.

ak:HB 69.title: EDUCATION: FUNDING
ak:HB 69.summary: Raises the base student allocation used in the state school funding formula from $5,960 to $6,960, effective July 1, 2025.

ak:HB 70.title: EMERGENCY MED SVCS; OPERATIONAL CANINES
ak:HB 70.summary: Lets emergency medical technicians and paramedics give emergency care to injured operational canines, sets related liability rules, and lets veterinarians share a canine's medical records with the responders who treated it.

ak:HB 73.title: COMPLEX CARE RESIDENTIAL HOMES
ak:HB 73.summary: Creates a licensing category, under the Department of Health's care-facility law, for complex care residential homes that give 24-hour multidisciplinary care to people with mental, behavioral, medical or disability-related needs; takes effect July 1, 2027.

ak:HB 75.title: PERM FUND; EMPLOYMENT; ELIGIBILITY
ak:HB 75.summary: Requires national criminal history checks for certain Revenue Department dividend staff, extends the military-service absence allowed for dividend eligibility to all uniformed services, and allows electronic notice of debt collection against a dividend.

ak:HB 78.title: RETIREMENT SYSTEMS; DEFINED BENEFIT OPT.
ak:HB 78.summary: Lets certain teachers and public employees choose between the defined benefit and defined contribution retirement plans, and changes contributions, benefits and retiree health eligibility for members who joined after June 30, 2006.

ak:HB 79.title: VIC FISCHER MARINE PARK; RESEARCH PROGRAM
ak:HB 79.summary: Renames the University of Alaska's Institute of Social and Economic Research as the Vic Fischer Institute of Social and Economic Research and names the Vic Fischer Shoup Bay State Marine Park.

ak:HB 93.title: RESIDENCY REQ: HUNTING, TRAPPING, FISHING
ak:HB 93.summary: Changes residency requirements for hunting, trapping and sport fishing, including that permanent ID card holders keep meeting residency rules to use the card.

ak:HB 96.title: HOME CARE EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS ADV BOARD
ak:HB 96.summary: Creates a Home Care Employment Standards Advisory Board in the Department of Health and requires agencies providing personal care services to spend at least 70 percent of department funding on employee pay and benefits from July 2027 (80 percent from 2030), with hardship exemptions.

ak:HCR 11.title: EXTEND WEST COAST STORM DISASTER
ak:HCR 11.summary: Extends the governor's October 9, 2025 disaster emergency declaration for the 2025 West Coast Storm until April 7, 2026.

ak:HCR 12.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 64
ak:HCR 12.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider Senate Bill 64, an elections bill covering voting, registration, campaign contributions and election crimes.

ak:HCR 13.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 146
ak:HCR 13.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 146, on the regional educational attendance area and small municipal school district fund, Mt. Edgecumbe High School and teacher housing, can be considered.

ak:HCR 14.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 9
ak:HCR 14.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 9, on the surrender of infants, can be considered.

ak:HCR 16.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 230
ak:HCR 16.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 230, on the boundaries of the Jonesville Public Use Area, can be considered.

ak:HCR 17.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 86
ak:HCR 17.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 86, on licensing money transmission businesses and virtual currency, can be considered.

ak:HCR 18.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 21
ak:HCR 18.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 21, which establishes the Alaska Work and Save Program in the Department of Revenue, can be considered.

ak:HCR 19.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 143
ak:HCR 19.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 143, on school board member terms and the size of second class city councils, can be considered.

ak:HCR 21.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 237
ak:HCR 21.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 237, on Department of Administration data sharing for driver's license data verification, can be considered.

ak:HCR 23.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 29
ak:HCR 23.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 29, on an executive administrator for the Big Game Commercial Services Board, can be considered.

ak:HCR 24.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 200
ak:HCR 24.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider Senate Bill 200, on municipal assessment of farm or agricultural land.

ak:HCR 26.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 208
ak:HCR 26.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 208, on selling and leasing state land for agricultural uses, can be considered.

ak:HCR 29.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 239
ak:HCR 29.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 239, on registering and titling legally imported motor vehicles, can be considered.

ak:HCR 30.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 211
ak:HCR 30.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that Senate Bill 211, which extends the termination dates of six professional boards and commissions, can be considered.

ak:HCR 32.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 24
ak:HCR 32.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider Senate Bill 24, on tobacco, nicotine and e-cigarette age limits and taxes.

ak:HCR 4.title: MYOSITIS AWARENESS MONTH
ak:HCR 4.summary: Proclaims May 2026 as Myositis Awareness Month in Alaska, citing the rare autoimmune muscle diseases collectively called myositis.

ak:HCR 6.title: US MARINE CORPS 250TH BIRTHDAY
ak:HCR 6.summary: Commemorates the 250th birthday of the United States Marine Corps and pays tribute to current and past Marines.

ak:HCR 7.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR SB 57
ak:HCR 7.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider Senate Bill 57, a bill making capital and other appropriations, reappropriations and fund capitalizations.

ak:HCR 9.title: DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE ANNIVERSARY
ak:HCR 9.summary: Honors the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence and of the founding of the United States, and encourages commemorative events and stronger civics education.

ak:HCR301.title: CARRY-OVER OF BILLS TO SPEC SESSION
ak:HCR301.summary: Suspends the Uniform Rules so that House Bill 381, on taxing natural gas pipeline property, can carry over from the Second Regular and Second Special Sessions into the Third Special Session.

ak:HCR302.title: AUTHORIZING A RECESS LONGER THAN 3 DAYS
ak:HCR302.summary: Allows the Senate and the House each to recess for more than three days during the Third Special Session of the 34th Legislature.

ak:HJR 11.title: RECOGNIZING ALASKA/CANADA RELATIONSHIP
ak:HJR 11.summary: Recognizes the Alaska-Canada relationship, opposes restrictive trade measures or tolls that would harm it, and honors the alliance between Alaska and Canada.

ak:HJR 14.title: PORT MACKENZIE & NORTHERN RAIL EXTENSIONS
ak:HJR 14.summary: Supports completing the Port MacKenzie and Northern Rail Extensions, expanding defensive capabilities at Fort Greely, and Arctic infrastructure development, and encourages the Alaska Railroad to take a community-minded approach to rail expansion.

ak:HJR 15.title: WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS
ak:HJR 15.summary: Urges the Governor, state agencies, municipalities and Alaska's congressional delegation to prepare for the wildfire season.

ak:HJR 18.title: URGING SUPPORT FOR NATURAL GAS PROJECT
ak:HJR 18.summary: Expresses support for the Alaska Liquefied Natural Gas Project and asks the Interior Secretary, Energy Department, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Alaska's congressional delegation and federal agencies to expedite approvals.

ak:HJR 20.title: HIRING OF APPRENTICES/VETERANS
ak:HJR 20.summary: Encourages Congress to require Defense Department construction offerors to set a goal that at least 10 percent of workers are apprentices or postsecondary program participants, and to require contractors using apprentices to ensure at least 10 percent are veterans.

ak:HJR 25.title: INTERNATIONAL TEACHER VISAS
ak:HJR 25.summary: Supports and encourages continued recruitment and retention of international educators on J-1 and H-1B visas in Alaska, and urges policymakers to adjust or extend visa status when permissible and increase job mobility for them.

ak:HJR 28.title: SUPPORT KIDS ONLINE SAFETY ACT
ak:HJR 28.summary: Calls on the U.S. Congress and the President to pass and sign S. 1748, the Kids Online Safety Act, a federal bill on online platform safeguards for users under 17.

ak:HJR 29.title: BAN ON RUSSIAN SEAFOOD
ak:HJR 29.summary: Supports further extension and enforcement of Executive Orders 14024, 14068 and 14114 on Russian seafood imports, and urges the President, federal agencies and Congress to consider additional measures prohibiting those imports.

ak:HJR 32.title: RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM
ak:HJR 32.summary: Expresses commitment to the federal rural health transformation program, noting Alaska's $272 million first-year award; urges the governor to seek federal clarification and report to the legislature, and the congressional delegation to defend the state's funding.

ak:HJR 38.title: PUBLIC SAFETY TELECOMMUNICATORS
ak:HJR 38.summary: Urges the U.S. House to pass the Enhancing First Response Act (S.725), which reclassifies public safety telecommunicators as a protective service occupation, and commends the Senate for passing it.

ak:HJR 39.title: WAIVE VISA FEES FOR TEACHERS
ak:HJR 39.summary: Urges the federal government to waive the $100,000 H-1B visa fee for educators hired in Alaska.

ak:HJR 4.title: RES. TO MAINTAIN DENALI AS OFFICIAL NAME
ak:HJR 4.summary: Urges the President, the Interior Secretary, the U.S. Board on Geographic Names and Alaska's congressional delegation to keep Denali as the official name of North America's tallest mountain.

ak:HJR 44.title: SUPPORT NATIVE CORP BUSINESS DEVELOP PRGM
ak:HJR 44.summary: Urges federal officials to support the ability of Alaska Native corporations and tribally owned entities to take part in the U.S. Small Business Administration's 8(a) Business Development Program.

ak:HJR 45.title: SUPPORT SPECIAL EDUCATION FUNDING
ak:HJR 45.summary: Urges Congress to fund the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act at no less than 40 percent of average per-pupil special education cost, including by passing H.R. 2598.

ak:HJR 46.title: TYPHOON HALONG; SUPPORT COMM. RELOCATION
ak:HJR 46.summary: Recognizes the decision of Kipnuk and Kwigillingok to relocate after Typhoon Halong, and urges the governor to develop a relocation framework and the congressional delegation to restore and expand federal funding for community relocation.

ak:HJR 5.title: SECURE RURAL SCHOOLS PROGRAM
ak:HJR 5.summary: Urges Congress and the President to reinstate the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 and make its funding mechanism for rural counties near national forests permanent.

ak:HJR 6.title: SUPPORT UNIVERSAL SERVICE FUND
ak:HJR 6.summary: Urges Alaska's congressional delegation and other members of Congress to safeguard funding and authority of the Universal Service Fund, including through legislation if needed to address legal concerns raised by court rulings.

ak:HJR 9.title: EXTEND AFFORDABLE CARE ACT TAX CREDITS
ak:HJR 9.summary: Urges Congress to extend the enhanced Affordable Care Act health insurance premium tax credits that are set to expire at the end of 2025.

ak:HR 1.title: HOUSE SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON FISHERIES
ak:HR 1.summary: Establishes a House Special Committee on Fisheries to study fishery issues, with members chosen by the Speaker, lasting until the 35th Legislature convenes.

ak:HR 2.title: HOUSE SPECIAL CMTE: TRIBAL AFFAIRS
ak:HR 2.summary: Establishes a House Special Committee on Tribal Affairs, with members chosen by the Speaker.

ak:HR 3.title: HOUSE SPECIAL COMMITTEE ON ENERGY
ak:HR 3.summary: Establishes a House Special Committee on Energy to study energy use and development, with members chosen by the Speaker, lasting until the 35th Legislature convenes.

ak:SB 104.title: VEHICLES/BOATS: TRANSFER ON DEATH TITLE
ak:SB 104.summary: Lets owners of boats and vehicles get a transfer-on-death certificate of title naming up to two beneficiaries, and adds common interest community unit ownership interests to property that can pass by transfer-on-death deed.

ak:SB 111.title: DIGITAL PRODUCT REPAIR
ak:SB 111.summary: Amendment limits a digital-product right-to-repair bill to repairs outside the manufacturer's warranty, lists items manufacturers need not supply, such as source code, and makes the attorney general the sole enforcer, with no private lawsuits.

ak:SB 113.title: APPORTION TAXABLE INCOME;DIGITAL BUSINESS
ak:SB 113.summary: Changes how multistate corporate income is apportioned to Alaska and requires businesses with at least 50 percent of Alaska sales from electronic transmissions, computer-related services or internet sales to apportion income by the sales factor alone, from 2026.

ak:SB 130.title: FISHERIES PROD DEVELOPMENT TAX CREDIT
ak:SB 130.summary: Extends the fisheries product development tax credit to property placed in service through 2036 instead of 2026, expands eligible fish from five listed species to any fish or shellfish, and reports credit totals by species rather than type.

ak:SB 132.title: OMNIBUS INSURANCE BILL
ak:SB 132.summary: Changes many insurance laws, including a one-year-after-discovery prosecution window for life insurance offenses, licensing instead of registration of pharmacy benefits managers and third-party administrators, colorectal cancer screening coverage, and surplus lines broker rules.

ak:SB 133.title: INSURANCE; PRIOR AUTHORIZATIONS
ak:SB 133.summary: Requires insurers to decide standard prior authorization requests within 72 hours and expedited ones within 24 hours, treats late responses as approvals, sets a prior authorization data interface, and limits step therapy, for plans from 2027.

ak:SB 134.title: PHARMACY BENEFITS MANAGER;3RD PARTY ADMIN
ak:SB 134.summary: Requires third-party administrators to be licensed rather than registered, and lets the insurance director examine them and pharmacy benefits managers whenever the director finds an examination necessary.

ak:SB 137.title: EXTND BDS:MIDWIVE/NURSING/VET EXAM/PAROLE
ak:SB 137.summary: Extends the termination dates of the Boards of Certified Direct-Entry Midwives, Nursing and Veterinary Examiners to June 30, 2031, and the Board of Parole to June 30, 2029.

ak:SB 140.title: FIRE STATION GRANT PROGRAM
ak:SB 140.summary: Creates a fire station grant program and fund, with matching grants covering up to 50% of project costs for building or renovating fire stations, subject to appropriation.

ak:SB 143.title: SCHOOL BD TERMS, TRAINING; CITY COUNCILS
ak:SB 143.summary: Adds a requirement that borough school boards adopt and maintain a balanced budget and lets the education commissioner review school district audits and implement corrective measures (amendment 2 to a bill on school board training and terms).

ak:SB 146.title: REAA & SMALL MUNI FUND: MT. EDGECUMBE
ak:SB 146.summary: Allows the school fund for rural and small-district schools to pay for Mt. Edgecumbe High School construction and major maintenance and for teacher housing maintenance, and removes the $70 million cap on the fund balance.

ak:SB 15.title: ALCOHOL: SALE, WARNING SIGNS
ak:SB 15.summary: Lets 18- to 20-year-olds employed at listed licensed businesses, such as restaurants and hotels, sell and serve alcohol, except adult entertainment businesses; lets patriotic clubs sell to reciprocal clubs' members; extends theater alcohol service to two hours before events; adds cancer wording to warning signs.

ak:SB 152.title: HAROLD ESMAILKA AIRPORT AT RUBY
ak:SB 152.summary: Names the state-owned public use airport at Ruby the Harold Esmailka Airport.

ak:SB 156.title: AK COMMERCIAL FISHING & AG BANK; LOANS
ak:SB 156.summary: Directs the Commerce Department, subject to appropriation, to buy nonvoting preferred shares of the Alaska Commercial Fishing and Agriculture Bank so it can make commercial fishing loans; the bank must repurchase the shares after 20 years.

ak:SB 158.title: COOK INLET: NEW ADMIN AREA
ak:SB 158.summary: Creates a separate administrative area for commercial set net permits on the east side of Cook Inlet, and reassigns permits on January 1, 2027, to holders who show past fishing there.

ak:SB 163.title: REPEAL CERTAIN INACTIVE FUNDS/ACCOUNTS
ak:SB 163.summary: Repeals three inactive state funds and accounts: the public access fund, the Alaska temporary assistance program emergency account, and the 2001 Special Olympics World Winter Games reserve fund, effective July 1, 2026.

ak:SB 164.title: ELIMINATE TAX DISCOUNTS
ak:SB 164.summary: Eliminates the deductions businesses may keep when remitting motor fuel and tobacco taxes and tire fees (for motor fuel, 1 percent up to $100 a month) and ends discounts on cigarette stamps.

ak:SB 167.title: PFD ELIGIBILITY; PFD FOR OVERTURN CONVIC.
ak:SB 167.summary: Lets a person who lost permanent fund dividends because of a conviction receive them for the ineligible years if the conviction is vacated or reversed and the charges are dismissed or the person is acquitted on retrial; application is due within two years.

ak:SB 170.title: GAMING; ELECTRONIC PULL-TABS
ak:SB 170.summary: Changes gaming rules: allows gaming on state ferries with a $10,000 annual permit, revises bingo and pull-tab rules, regulates electronic pull-tab systems, and ends the requirement to notify local governments of applications.

ak:SB 174.title: INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT
ak:SB 174.summary: Lets people release vaccinated, ear-tipped, spayed or neutered community cats where found, creates a spay and neuter assistance fund and program reimbursing providers for low-income households' pets, and creates the Alaska Invasive Species Council (House Finance substitute).

ak:SB 178.title: EXPAND EARLY INTERVENTION SERVICES
ak:SB 178.summary: Adds early intervention services for eligible children under three to Medicaid optional services, if federal approval is obtained, and limits state early intervention eligibility to children with a developmental delay or disability, removing at-risk children.

ak:SB 181.title: EMPLOYMENT INFORMATION DISCLOSURE
ak:SB 181.summary: Adds program evaluation, educational outreach and public policy research as permitted purposes for the Department of Labor and Workforce Development to share information it obtains with other state agencies, including the University of Alaska, under written agreements limiting further disclosure.

ak:SB 183.title: POWERS: LB&A COMMITTEE; LEGISLATIVE AUDIT
ak:SB 183.summary: Expands the offense of hindering the Legislative Budget and Audit Committee to cover failing to cooperate in assembling or generating requested information in the requested format, and adds matching cooperation duties for state officials and agencies.

ak:SB 185.title: INSURANCE; REBATES; ADVERTISING
ak:SB 185.summary: Allows insurers and producers to offer value-added services and limited gifts to customers, with services capped at the greater of $250 per policy term or 5% of premium, and bars advertising coverage as "free" or "no cost."

ak:SB 187.title: SCHOOL NUTRITION/MEAL: PROHIBIT FOOD DYES
ak:SB 187.summary: Bars public schools from serving breakfast or lunch foods or drinks containing red dye 3, red dye 40, yellow dyes 5 and 6, blue dyes 1 and 2, or green dye 3, starting January 1, 2028.

ak:SB 192.title: EVACUATION DESIGNATION LEVELS
ak:SB 192.summary: Requires evacuation plans, maps and public messaging to use three designations: 'Level 1 Ready' (green), 'Level 2 Set' (yellow) and 'Level 3 Go' (red).

ak:SB 20.title: CPR CURRICULUM
ak:SB 20.summary: Requires the Department of Education to adopt hands-only CPR curricula, including defibrillator use, and requires public schools to offer the instruction at the grade levels the department sets.

ak:SB 200.title: MUNI: SVC AREAS; FARM & AGRICULTURAL LAND
ak:SB 200.summary: Changes voter-approval rules for abolishing, replacing or altering certain municipal service areas, and changes the farm use definition for property assessment, including dropping the human or animal consumption limit and excluding marijuana production.

ak:SB 208.title: AGRICULTURAL LAND; HEMP; STATE VEGETABLE
ak:SB 208.summary: Defines 'agricultural purposes' under the Alaska Land Act to include commercial crop and livestock production, dairying, greenhouses, land improvements and agricultural tourism (amendment 4 to a bill on hemp, state land sales for agriculture, and a state vegetable).

ak:SB 21.title: AK WORK & SAVE PRGRM; PFD INVESTMENT ACCT
ak:SB 21.summary: Creates the Alaska Work and Save Program in the Department of Revenue, with automatic opt-out enrollment for employees of employers (over five staff for three years) offering no retirement plan, and lets dividend applicants direct their permanent fund dividend into an investment account.

ak:SB 211.title: EXTEND OCCUPATIONAL LICENSING BOARDS
ak:SB 211.summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors to June 30, 2033 (amendment 1 added this to the bill).

ak:SB 214.title: APPROP: CAPITAL/FUNDS/SUPP/REAPPROP/AMEND
ak:SB 214.summary: Makes capital project appropriations, supplemental appropriations and reappropriations, capitalizes funds, and amends existing appropriations.

ak:SB 23.title: CIVICS EDUCATION
ak:SB 23.summary: Requires the state board of education to list open educational resources on civics and comparative government, and requires students entering ninth grade from July 2027 to pass a civics course or assessment to receive a diploma, with exceptions.

ak:SB 230.title: REFUGES/HABITAT AREAS/PUBLIC USE AREA
ak:SB 230.summary: Changes boundaries and legal land descriptions of state game refuges and critical habitat areas, including the Izembek Refuge and Palmer Hay Flats, and changes the boundaries of the Jonesville Public Use Area.

ak:SB 237.title: ELECTRONIC DRIVER'S LICENSES/DATA SHARING
ak:SB 237.summary: Lets holders of physical IDs and driver's licenses apply for electronic versions, provides that showing an electronic ID on a phone is not consent to search the phone, and lets the commissioner of administration make data-exchange agreements such as with the National Driver Register.

ak:SB 24.title: TOBACCO/NICOTINE/E-CIG AGE; E-CIG TAX
ak:SB 24.summary: Changes the bill's tax on closed electronic smoking and vapor products from 25 percent of retail price to 75 percent of wholesale price, levied on importing, making or shipping them (amendment 3 to a bill raising the tobacco age to 21).

ak:SB 249.title: VIRTUAL CURRENCY KIOSKS
ak:SB 249.summary: Requires virtual currency kiosk operators to hold a money transmission license and state approval of kiosk locations, file quarterly and annual reports, and show customers fraud and risk warnings and fee disclosures.

ak:SB 250.title: DATA CENTERS, UTILITIES
ak:SB 250.summary: Requires utilities serving larger data centers to sign commission-approved contracts assigning infrastructure and variable costs directly to the data center, keeps those costs out of other customers' rates, and requires municipal community benefit agreements.

ak:SB 252.title: UCC: SECURED TRANS.; ELECTRONIC RECORDS
ak:SB 252.summary: Updates Alaska's Uniform Commercial Code provisions on secured transactions, sales, negotiable instruments and related topics, and adds rules for controllable electronic records, controllable accounts and controllable payment intangibles.

ak:SB 258.title: CONTRACT: LICENSING SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS
ak:SB 258.summary: Bars software license contracts of the state and its political subdivisions from limiting where the software is installed or run on desktop or server hardware, with exceptions for federal accreditation, security certification and technical architecture needs.

ak:SB 26.title: ELIMINATE DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME
ak:SB 26.summary: As introduced, petitions the U.S. Department of Transportation to place all of Alaska in the Pacific time zone and exempts the state from daylight saving time, effective only if that change is made by 2035.

ak:SB 282.title: MILITARY: JT ARMED SVCS COMMITTEE
ak:SB 282.summary: Requires at least two minority members from each chamber on the Joint Armed Services Committee, up from one, and replaces annual department reports to the committee with a biennial report to the legislature.

ak:SB 29.title: BIG GAME COMM. SVS BD/BD DENTAL EXAMINERS
ak:SB 29.summary: Creates an executive administrator position for the Board of Dental Examiners and provides for an executive administrator for the Big Game Commercial Services Board.

ak:SB 35.title: TRANSPORTATION/DELIVERY NETWORK COMPANIES
ak:SB 35.summary: Extends rideshare insurance rules to delivery couriers, requires companies to carry group occupational accident insurance of $1 million per accident for drivers and couriers, lets auto insurers exclude coverage while they work, and excludes couriers from workers' compensation.

ak:SB 39.title: LOANS UNDER $25,000; PAYDAY LOANS
ak:SB 39.summary: Changes the law on loans of $25,000 or less, including payday and deferred deposit loans, pawnbroker licensing exemptions, interest computation, and participation in the national licensing registry.

ak:SB 40.title: HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH
ak:SB 40.summary: Establishes September 15 to October 15 each year as Hispanic Heritage Month.

ak:SB 41.title: PUBLIC SCHOOLS: MENTAL HEALTH EDUCATION
ak:SB 41.summary: Requires the state board of education to set mental health instruction guidelines, requires school board policies to give parents two weeks' notice before a mental health class or program, and adds mental health to health education topics districts are encouraged to teach.

ak:SB 43.title: WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH
ak:SB 43.summary: Establishes March each year as Women's History Month, which schools, groups and others may observe with activities honoring women's contributions.

ak:SB 47.title: CHUGACH STATE PARK EASEMENTS
ak:SB 47.summary: Lets the state grant a municipality an easement or right-of-way in Chugach State Park to repair, maintain and build roads, at the municipality's cost, after a hearing and a finding that it improves public access.

ak:SB 50.title: MUNICIPAL COMPREHENSIVE PLANS: HOUSING
ak:SB 50.summary: Adds a housing development plan to the items that a first or second class borough comprehensive plan may include.

ak:SB 54.title: ARCH, ENG, SURVEYORS; REG INT DESIGN
ak:SB 54.summary: Sets registration and practice requirements for interior designers, extends the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors, and changes the scope of certification for those professions.

ak:SB 57.title: APPROP: CAPITAL/FUNDS/SUPP/AMEND/REAPPROP
ak:SB 57.summary: Makes capital appropriations, supplemental appropriations and reappropriations, amends and repeals some existing appropriations, and capitalizes state funds.

ak:SB 6.title: ASIAN AMERICAN/PACIFIC ISLANDER PROGRAM
ak:SB 6.summary: Requires each Alaska school district to provide students in kindergarten through grade 12 instruction on the history and contributions of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders.

ak:SB 60.title: ESTABLISH ME/CHRONIC FATIGUE SYNDROME DAY
ak:SB 60.summary: Establishes May 12 of each year as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Day of Recognition in Alaska, which civic groups and the public may observe.

ak:SB 63.title: LOCAL BOUNDARY COMMISSION
ak:SB 63.summary: Increases the Local Boundary Commission from five to six members, lengthens terms from five to six years, and has the commission select its chair rather than the at-large member serving as chair.

ak:SB 64.title: ELECTIONS
ak:SB 64.summary: Adds federally recognized tribal ID cards to the IDs that first-time voters who registered by mail or fax may submit with absentee ballots, and removes hunting or fishing licenses and utility bills, bank statements, paychecks and government documents (amendment 1).

ak:SB 79.title: PAYMENT OF WAGES; PAYROLL CARD ACCOUNT
ak:SB 79.summary: Lets employers pay wages to a payroll card account if the employee agrees or has not chosen another deposit method, and bars card fees for applying, the initial card and one yearly replacement, wage transfers, and point-of-sale purchases.

ak:SB 80.title: EXTEND BOARDS
ak:SB 80.summary: Amendment adds the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors to a bill extending four agencies' termination dates, extending its sunset to June 30, 2033.

ak:SB 83.title: TELEHEALTH: COVERAGE, REIMBURSEMENT RATES
ak:SB 83.summary: Amendment to an amendment on telehealth reimbursement: applies a rule that insurers apply reimbursement rates uniformly to providers only when no contract between insurer and provider sets allowable charges.

ak:SB 86.title: MONEY TRANSMISSION; VIRTUAL CURRENCY
ak:SB 86.summary: Replaces Alaska's money transmission licensing rules, requiring licenses through a nationwide multistate system and covering virtual currency, authorized delegates, record keeping, enforcement, payroll processing, currency exchange licenses and abandoned virtual currency.

ak:SB 87.title: REJECT COMP COMMISSION RECOMMENDATIONS
ak:SB 87.summary: Rejects the recommendations in the 2025 final report of the State Officers Compensation Commission, and takes effect immediately.

ak:SB 89.title: PHYSICIAN ASSISTANT SCOPE OF PRACTICE
ak:SB 89.summary: Sets physician assistant scope of practice under written collaborative agreements with physicians, with none required at certain facilities or with board authorization, and sets licensing qualifications and temporary permit rules for physician assistants.

ak:SB 9.title: SURRENDER OF INFANTS; INF. SAFETY DEVICE
ak:SB 9.summary: Lets a parent surrender an infant through an infant safety device at an authorized facility, sets device requirements such as video monitoring and an automated lock, and limits civil history license denials based only on infant surrender.

ak:SB 96.title: CHILD CARE: TAX CREDITS
ak:SB 96.summary: Expands Alaska education tax credits to cover employer costs for child care: running a facility for employees' children, gifts to nonprofit child care facilities, and payments offsetting employees' child care costs. Credit limits are inflation-adjusted every five years from 2030.

ak:SB 97.title: BIG GAME GUIDE PERMIT PROGRAM
ak:SB 97.summary: As introduced, creates a big game guide concession area permit program in which the Board of Game approves concession areas, within a single game management unit, administered by the Department of Natural Resources.

ak:SCR 10.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 36
ak:SCR 10.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 36, on placing foster children in psychiatric hospitals and care of children in state custody in facilities outside the state, can be considered.

ak:SCR 12.title: EXTEND WEST COAST STORM DISASTER
ak:SCR 12.summary: Extends the governor's October 9, 2025 disaster declaration for the 2025 West Coast Storm until March 8, 2026 and approves a $5.5 million increase in the financing plan.

ak:SCR 13.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 126
ak:SCR 13.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 126, on reinstating Native village corporations and religious nonprofit corporations, can be considered.

ak:SCR 14.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 13
ak:SCR 14.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 13, on optional municipal property tax exemptions for certain rental units, mobile home parks, low-income rentals, permanent residences and first-time homebuyers, can be considered.

ak:SCR 15.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 194
ak:SCR 15.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 194, approving and ratifying the state's sale of royalty oil to Marathon Petroleum Supply and Trading Company LLC.

ak:SCR 16.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HCR 4
ak:SCR 16.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Concurrent Resolution 4, which proclaims a Myositis Awareness Month, can be considered.

ak:SCR 17.title: REGIONAL EDUCATIONAL ATTENDANCE AREAS
ak:SCR 17.summary: Recognizes the 50th anniversary of Alaska's regional educational attendance areas, which operate public schools in rural parts of the state, and celebrates their contributions to education and community life.

ak:SCR 18.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HJR 18
ak:SCR 18.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Joint Resolution 18, supporting the Alaska Liquefied Natural Gas Project.

ak:SCR 19.title: EXTEND WEST COAST STORM DISASTER
ak:SCR 19.summary: Extends the governor's October 9, 2025 disaster declaration for the 2025 West Coast Storm and approves an amended financing plan of $62.83 million (amendment 1 added the financing plan).

ak:SCR 21.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 28
ak:SCR 21.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 28, which creates a student loan repayment pilot program, can be considered.

ak:SCR 22.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 239
ak:SCR 22.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 239, on criminally negligent homicide and an operator's duty after an accident, can be considered.

ak:SCR 23.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 263
ak:SCR 23.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so House Bill 263, the state operating budget and supplemental appropriations bill, can be considered with its expanded title.

ak:SCR 24.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 184
ak:SCR 24.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 184, on workforce housing financing by the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority.

ak:SCR 25.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 110
ak:SCR 25.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 110, relating to a social work licensure compact and the practice of social work.

ak:SCR 27.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 173
ak:SCR 27.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 173, on occupational therapist and assistant licensure and an occupational therapist licensure compact, can be considered.

ak:SCR 28.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 302
ak:SCR 28.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 302, on travel insurance.

ak:SCR 29.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 117
ak:SCR 29.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 117, on commercial set gillnet fishing, can be considered.

ak:SCR 3.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 69
ak:SCR 3.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 69, a broad education bill covering open enrollment, charter schools, school accountability reports, the base student allocation and phone use in schools.

ak:SCR 30.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 79
ak:SCR 30.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 79, which names the Vic Fischer Shoup Bay State Marine Park, can be considered.

ak:SCR 32.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 23
ak:SCR 32.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 23, which renames the State Commission for Human Rights the Alaska State Commission for Civil Rights, can be considered.

ak:SCR 33.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 27
ak:SCR 33.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 27, on medical care for major emergencies, can be considered.

ak:SCR 36.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 14
ak:SCR 36.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 14, which repeals the catastrophic illness and chronic and acute medical assistance programs.

ak:SCR 4.title: MENTAL HEALTH MONTH; TARDIVE DYSK WEEK
ak:SCR 4.summary: Designates May 2025 as Mental Health Awareness Month and May 4-10, 2025, as Tardive Dyskinesia Awareness Week in Alaska.

ak:SCR 5.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 57
ak:SCR 5.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 57, relating to wireless telecommunications devices in public schools.

ak:SCR 6.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 121
ak:SCR 6.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so that House Bill 121, on the practice of accounting, can be considered.

ak:SCR 7.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 75
ak:SCR 7.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 75, covering Revenue Department background checks, permanent fund dividend absences and confidentiality, and electronic debt-collection notices.

ak:SCR 8.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 35
ak:SCR 8.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 35, on prisoners' use of electronic devices.

ak:SCR 9.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 70
ak:SCR 9.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changes to a bill's title so the Legislature can consider House Bill 70, which covers emergency medical services for operational canines, EMT and paramedic duties and liability, and veterinary practice.

ak:SCR101.title: AUTHORIZING A RECESS LONGER THAN 3 DAYS
ak:SCR101.summary: Allows the Senate and House each to recess for more than three days during the First Special Session of the 34th Legislature.

ak:SCR201.title: AUTHORIZING A RECESS LONGER THAN 3 DAYS
ak:SCR201.summary: Allows the Senate and House each to recess for more than three days during the Second Special Session of the 34th Legislature.

ak:SCR202.title: CARRY-OVER OF BILLS TO SPEC SESSION
ak:SCR202.summary: Suspends legislative rules so House Bill 381 and Senate Bill 280, on taxing natural gas pipeline property, can carry over from the regular session to the Second Special Session.

ak:SCR203.title: SUSPEND UNIFORM RULES FOR HB 381
ak:SCR203.summary: Suspends legislative rules on changing a bill's title so House Bill 381, on taxes and agreements for a natural gas pipeline project, can be considered with its expanded title.

ak:SJR 10.title: HMONG VETERANS; CONGRESSIONAL GOLD MEDAL
ak:SJR 10.summary: Encourages Congress to award the Congressional Gold Medal to Hmong veterans of the Vietnam War.

ak:SJR 12.title: NOAA BUOY OUTAGES
ak:SJR 12.summary: Urges Congress to require NOAA, through appropriations language, to restore and keep reliable the National Data Buoy Center weather and ocean stations in Alaska that have suffered outages.

ak:SJR 15.title: OPPOSE MEDICAID CUTS
ak:SJR 15.summary: Calls on Alaska's congressional delegation to oppose cuts to federal spending on Medicaid.

ak:SJR 16.title: FEDERAL ENSURING LASTING SMILES ACT
ak:SJR 16.summary: Urges Alaska's congressional delegation to support the Ensuring Lasting Smiles Act, which would require private health plans to cover medically necessary treatment for congenital anomalies such as cleft lip and palate.

ak:SJR 17.title: HONORING THE ENERGY COUNCIL
ak:SJR 17.summary: Recognizes and honors the 50th anniversary of The Energy Council, a forum for legislators from energy-producing states and Canadian provinces to discuss energy policy.

ak:SJR 19.title: ANWR & NAT'L PETRO RESERVE: STATE SHARE
ak:SJR 19.summary: Urges Congress to give Alaska 90 percent of bonuses, royalties and rentals from federal leases on the coastal plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and of the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska.

ak:SJR 2.title: CONST. AM: VOTES NEEDED FOR VETO OVERRIDE
ak:SJR 2.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment lowering the vote needed to override a veto of revenue and appropriation bills from three-fourths to two-thirds of the Legislature, the same as other bills.

ak:SJR 20.title: CLEAN UP MARINE DEBRIS
ak:SJR 20.summary: Supports federal, state and local efforts to clean up marine debris on Alaska's shorelines, and urges NOAA, the EPA and other federal agencies to provide more funding and to remove barriers for tribes and rural communities seeking it.

ak:SJR 25.title: SUPPORTING US-MEXICO-CANADA AGREEMENT
ak:SJR 25.summary: Expresses support for extending and modernizing the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, for a program simplifying border crossings for trusted commuters, and for free trade with Canada and Mexico.

ak:SJR 28.title: SUPPORTING J-1 & H-1B VISA PROGRAMS
ak:SJR 28.summary: Expresses support for workers in Alaska under the J-1, H-1B and H-2B visa programs, encourages employers to use them after domestic recruitment, and urges Alaska's congressional delegation and federal policymakers to preserve and strengthen them.

ak:SJR 29.title: CONST. AM: EDUCATION FUND
ak:SJR 29.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the next general election ballot, letting the Legislature create an education fund of transferred land, appropriated money and earnings, usable only for public education and exempt from Article IX, section 7.

ak:SJR 30.title: SUPPORT MILITARY&INCREASE INFRASTRUCTURE
ak:SJR 30.summary: Expresses gratitude to the U.S. military and supports expanding Alaska military bases, dual-use facilities and public-military partnerships, including enhanced-use leases, to provide housing, infrastructure and resources for service members and families.

ak:SJR 8.title: INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS WITH TAIWAN
ak:SJR 8.summary: Supports reopening an Alaska Trade Office in Taiwan, expanding educational exchanges, and a U.S.-Taiwan trade agreement, and reaffirms the state's relationship with Taiwan.

ak:SR 1.title: SENATE SPECIAL COMMITTEE ARCTIC AFFAIRS
ak:SR 1.summary: Establishes a Senate Special Committee on Arctic Affairs of five senators, appointed by the Senate President, to study Arctic issues.

ak:SR 2.title: SENATE SPECIAL WORLD TRADE COMMITTEE
ak:SR 2.summary: Establishes a Senate Special Committee on World Trade to study world trade issues, with members chosen by the Senate President, ending when the 35th Legislature convenes.

ak:SR 3.title: SAMOAN SERVICE & VOTING RIGHTS
ak:SR 3.summary: Urges Congress to let American Samoans serve as commissioned officers in the U.S. uniformed services and to give them the right to vote in federal elections.

ar:HB1001.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF THE NINETY-FIFTH GENERAL ASSEMBLY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1001.summary: Appropriates $2,275,160 for House of Representatives expenses for fiscal year 2025-26, covering employee salaries, matching and operations, and allows transfers between House appropriations.

ar:HB1002.title: THE GENERAL APPROPRIATION ACT FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1002.summary: Appropriates $830,000 for judges' travel and expenses, $368,000 for House members' and $200,000 for Senate members' interim expense reimbursements, for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1004.title: TO REQUIRE MEDICAID COVERAGE FOR POSTPARTUM MOTHERS FOR ONE YEAR AFTER GIVING BIRTH.
ar:HB1004.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to extend Medicaid postpartum coverage to one year after birth and to seek the federal approval needed, including use of Children's Health Insurance Program funding.

ar:HB1005.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1005.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Education for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1006.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND LICENSING - BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1006.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Labor and Licensing - Boards and Commissions for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1007.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - DIVISION OF ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION - PUBLIC SCHOOL FUND APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1007.summary: Appropriates money from the Public School Fund for the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education for 2026-27, including about $3.66 billion in the main section, the school computer network, Office of Education Renewal Zones, and sexual risk avoidance education.

ar:HB1014.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES - DIVISION OF PROVIDER SERVICES AND QUALITY ASSURANCE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1014.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Human Services - Division of Provider Services and Quality Assurance for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1017.title: TO AMEND THE LAW REGARDING PAID MATERNITY LEAVE FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL EMPLOYEES; AND TO REQUIRE THE DIVISION OF ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION TO PAY FOR INCURRED COSTS FOR APPROVED PAID MATERNITY LEAVE.
ar:HB1017.summary: Requires the education division to pay 100% of incurred costs of approved paid maternity leave for public school employees, replacing the current 50-50 split between the state and the school district.

ar:HB1020.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1020.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Arkansas Department of Transportation for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1021.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY - MID-SOUTH APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1021.summary: Appropriates $6,517,317 for state operations and $25,000,000 from cash funds for Arkansas State University–Mid-South for fiscal year 2026-27, plus funds for ADTEC and University Center Partners.

ar:HB1022.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS DEVELOPMENT FINANCE AUTHORITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1022.summary: Appropriates $15 million for a federal National Housing Trust Fund grant program and about $2.3 million for the Emergency Solutions Grant through the Arkansas Development Finance Authority for 2026-27.

ar:HB1023.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES - SECRETARY'S OFFICE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1023.summary: Appropriates money for the Department of Human Services Secretary's Office for 2026-27, covering salaries, operations, building construction, consolidated cost and grants.

ar:HB1026.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY - MOUNTAIN HOME APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1026.summary: Appropriates $4,742,527 for state operations and $26,525,000 from cash funds for Arkansas State University–Mountain Home for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1027.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH - HEALTH SERVICES PERMIT AGENCY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1027.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Health - Health Services Permit Agency for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1028.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - STATE BANK DEPARTMENT AND STATE SECURITIES DEPARTMENT APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1028.summary: Appropriates, for fiscal year 2026-27, $14,768,700 for State Bank Department operations, $4,486,527 for State Securities Department operations, and $316,000 from the Investor Education Fund.

ar:HB1029.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - CITY-COUNTY TOURIST MEETING AND ENTERTAINMENT FACILITIES ASSISTANCE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1029.summary: Appropriates $887,908 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, for the Treasurer of State to make payments to publicly owned tourist and entertainment facilities under the City-County Tourist Meeting and Entertainment Facilities Assistance Law.

ar:HB1030.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1030.summary: Appropriates $42 million from the College Savings Bond Fund and $43 million from the Water, Waste Disposal and Pollution Abatement Facilities Bond Fund for bond refunds and debt service in fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1031.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF ATTORNEY GENERAL APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1031.summary: Appropriates $26,392,710 for Attorney General operations in fiscal year 2026-27, plus separate amounts for the Medicaid Fraud Division, Internet Crimes Against Children, the disability investigation program, and settlement funds.

ar:HB1032.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS - PULASKI TECHNICAL COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1032.summary: Appropriates $18,255,338 for state operations and $81,135,000 from cash funds for the University of Arkansas–Pulaski Technical College for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1033.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - REFUND OF LOCAL TAXES APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1033.summary: Appropriates $1.13 billion for refunds of cities' shares and $990 million for counties' shares of local sales and use taxes from the Local Sales and Use Tax Trust Fund for fiscal 2026-27.

ar:HB1035.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH - TOBACCO PREVENTION AND CESSATION PROGRAMS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1035.summary: Appropriates money for salaries, extra help and program expenses of the Department of Health's tobacco prevention and cessation programs for the 2026-27 fiscal year.

ar:HB1036.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1036.summary: Appropriates money for the Department of Health for 2026-27, including operations, the trauma system, emergency medical services, $60 million for WIC food instruments, interpreters for deaf people, and credentialing for full independent practice.

ar:HB1038.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - CHILD SUPPORT ENFORCEMENT APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1038.summary: Appropriates $77,949,301 for Child Support Enforcement operations at the Department of Finance and Administration for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1039.title: AN ACT FOR THE NATIONAL PARK COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1039.summary: Appropriates $12,380,951 for state operations and $21,500,000 from cash funds for National Park College for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1040.title: AN ACT FOR THE STATE DEPARTMENT FOR SOCIAL SECURITY ADMINISTRATION DISABILITY DETERMINATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1040.summary: Appropriates $77,845,835 for operations of the Disability Determination for Social Security Administration program for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1041.title: AN ACT FOR THE SECRETARY OF STATE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1041.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Secretary of State for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1042.title: AN ACT FOR ARKANSAS LEGISLATIVE AUDIT OF THE LEGISLATIVE JOINT AUDITING COMMITTEE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1042.summary: Appropriates $49,980,832 for Arkansas Legislative Audit operations for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1043.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS GOVERNOR'S MANSION COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1043.summary: Appropriates $1,500,250 for Governor's Mansion Commission operations, plus a separate amount for the Grand Hall, mansion and grounds, for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1044.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS COURT OF APPEALS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1044.summary: Appropriates $6,585,195 for Arkansas Court of Appeals operations for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1045.title: TO PLACE CERTAIN REQUIREMENTS ON AN INDIVIDUAL PLANNING A CROP RESIDUE BURN; AND TO ADDRESS LIABILITY OF AN INDIVIDUAL WHO HAS FOLLOWED CROP RESIDUE BURN REQUIREMENTS.
ar:HB1045.summary: Requires crop residue burns to be reported to the Department of Agriculture and follow state smoke management guidelines, and shields those who comply from civil liability unless the claimant proves negligence.

ar:HB1046.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - ARKANSAS WATERWAYS COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1046.summary: Appropriates $335,324 for Arkansas Waterways Commission operations, $5,000,000 for waterway development grants, and $2,000,000 for river navigation system expenses for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1047.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS NORTHEASTERN COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1047.summary: Appropriates $11,218,832 for state operations and $27,554,350 from cash funds for Arkansas Northeastern College for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1048.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE INCIDENTAL SALE OF GOAT MILK, SHEEP MILK, AND WHOLE MILK THAT HAS NOT BEEN PASTEURIZED; AND TO CLARIFY THAT THE INCIDENTAL SALE OF RAW MILK IS NOT LIMITED TO A SALE ON THE FARM.
ar:HB1048.summary: Adds farmers' markets and delivery from the farm to where incidental direct-to-consumer sales of raw goat milk, raw sheep milk and unpasteurized whole milk are not prohibited by the subchapter; advertising of such sales remains allowed.

ar:HB1049.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - ANIMAL RESCUE SHELTERS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1049.summary: Appropriates $25,000 for cities and $25,000 for counties for fiscal 2026-2027 from the Animal Rescue and Shelter Trust Fund, for operating and building government-owned animal rescue shelters.

ar:HB1050.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - AMENDMENT 74 PROPERTY TAX APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1050.summary: Appropriates $1.8 billion from the Uniform Tax Rate Trust Fund to the Treasurer of State for redistributing property tax funds to counties, as the state constitution's Amendment 74 requires, for fiscal 2026-27.

ar:HB1051.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE & ADMINISTRATION - REGULATORY DIVISION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1051.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Finance and Administration - Regulatory Division for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1052.title: AN ACT TO MAKE AN APPROPRIATION FOR STATE TURNBACK FOR COUNTIES AND MUNICIPALITIES BY THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30, 2027; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
ar:HB1052.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2026-27 state turnback money for the Treasurer of State to distribute to cities and counties, including $29.4 million in general revenue for cities, $21.4 million for counties, and $450 million in property tax relief for counties.

ar:HB1053.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT LITTLE ROCK APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1053.summary: Appropriates money for salaries, operations, cash funds and a nanotechnology center at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock for the 2026-27 fiscal year.

ar:HB1055.title: TO ESTABLISH COVERAGE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT TO SLOW THE PROGRESSION OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE OR OTHER DEMENTIA-RELATED DISEASE UNDER THE STATE AND PUBLIC SCHOOL LIFE AND HEALTH INSURANCE PROGRAM.
ar:HB1055.summary: Requires state and public school employee health plans issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2026 to cover FDA-approved diagnosis and treatment of Alzheimer's disease and other dementia, as determined by a physician.

ar:HB1056.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - MARTIN LUTHER KING, JR. COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1056.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Education - Martin Luther King, Jr. Commission for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1057.title: AN ACT FOR THE NORTH ARKANSAS COLLEGE OF THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1057.summary: Appropriates $9,700,232 for state operations and $37,490,000 from cash funds for North Arkansas College for fiscal year 2026-27, and adopts special-language code amendments.

ar:HB1058.title: AN ACT FOR THE UAMS - REYNOLDS CENTER ON AGING, BOOZMAN COLLEGE OF PUBLIC HEALTH, ARK. BIOSCIENCES INSTITUTE, & THE AREA HEALTH ED. CENTER IN HELENA APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1058.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2026-27 funds to UAMS units: $2,320,796 Reynolds Center on Aging, $3,195,946 Boozman College of Public Health, $6,180,957 Arkansas Biosciences Institute, and $2,235,565 Area Health Education Center in Helena.

ar:HB1059.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - DIVISION OF PUBLIC SCHOOL ACADEMIC FACILITIES AND TRANSPORTATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1059.summary: Appropriates $3,065,682 for operations and $215,340,489 for programs of the Division of Public School Academic Facilities and Transportation for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1060.title: TO REVISE THE INSTRUCTION PROVIDED ON THE FAILURE OF COMMUNIST AND AUTOCRATIC SYSTEMS AND TO REINFORCE IN REQUIRED INSTRUCTION THE RESILIENCY OF THE CONSTITUTIONAL REPUBLIC SYSTEM ADOPTED BY THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
ar:HB1060.summary: Requires the Department of Education to update grades 7-12 social studies standards before 2026-27 to compare the U.S. constitutional republic with communist, autocratic and other democratic systems, including records of mass murder, oppression and economic collapse under communism and autocracy.

ar:HB1061.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND LICENSING - DIVISION OF LABOR APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1061.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Labor and Licensing - Division of Labor for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1062.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES - MEDICAID TOBACCO SETTLEMENT PROGRAM APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1062.summary: Appropriates money for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, for the Department of Human Services' Medicaid Tobacco Settlement Program, covering medical services and aging, adult and behavioral health services, and sets related staff positions.
