ar:HB1063.title: TO AMEND THE ACHIEVING A BETTER LIFE EXPERIENCE PROGRAM ACT; AND TO AMEND THE DEFINITIONS OF "DISABILITY CERTIFICATION" AND "ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUAL" TO CHANGE DISABILITY ONSET AGE FROM TWENTY-SIX TO FORTY-SIX.
ar:HB1063.summary: Raises from 26 to 46 the age before which a disability must have begun to qualify for an ABLE account, effective January 1, 2026.

ar:HB1064.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - DISBURSING OFFICER APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1064.summary: Appropriates money through the Disbursing Officer for 2026-27 for miscellaneous grants and transfers, including $80 million for pension and relief funds, up to $2 billion in federal grants, $16.25 million for disaster assistance, and unemployment claims.

ar:HB1066.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT - DIVISION OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1066.summary: Appropriates money for the Division of Environmental Quality for 2026-27, covering state and federal operations and programs for wastewater licensing, land reclamation, hazardous waste permits, abandoned mines and surface coal mining.

ar:HB1067.title: CONCERNING FIREARM HOLD AGREEMENTS; AND TO PROVIDE CIVIL IMMUNITY TO A FEDERAL FIREARMS LICENSEE WHO AGREES TO HOLD A FIREARM FOR AN INDIVIDUAL.
ar:HB1067.summary: Gives a federal firearms licensee civil immunity for injury or death arising from a firearm hold agreement, including returning the firearm to its owner, unless the act was otherwise unlawful conduct.

ar:HB1068.title: TO INCLUDE EMPLOYEES OF A METROPOLITAN PORT AUTHORITY IN THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE ARKANSAS EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1068.summary: Adds employees of metropolitan port authorities to those eligible for membership in the Arkansas Public Employees' Retirement System, and adds those authorities to the list of participating public employers.

ar:HB1069.title: AN ACT FOR THE OZARKA COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1069.summary: Appropriates $4,644,419 for state operations and $15,501,000 from cash funds for Ozarka College for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1070.title: TO CREATE THE BALLOT DRAW STANDARDIZATION ACT OF 2025.
ar:HB1070.summary: Creates the Ballot Draw Standardization Act of 2025, setting rules for drawing lots on candidate ballot order: candidates or designees draw, with limits on one person drawing for several candidates, and candidate lists show filing order with filing date and time.

ar:HB1071.title: TO AMEND THE FRANK BROYLES PUBLICITY RIGHTS PROTECTION ACT OF 2016; AND TO PROVIDE PROTECTIONS FOR AN INDIVIDUAL WHOSE PHOTOGRAPH, VOICE, OR LIKENESS IS REPRODUCED THROUGH MEANS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND USED COMMERCIALLY.
ar:HB1071.summary: Extends Arkansas's publicity rights law to cover a person's image, video, likeness and voice when reproduced through artificial intelligence and used commercially.

ar:HB1072.title: TO CLARIFY THE REQUIREMENTS FOR ESTABLISHING ELIGIBILITY FOR THE PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION FOR DISABLED VETERANS, SURVIVING SPOUSES, AND MINOR DEPENDENT CHILDREN.
ar:HB1072.summary: Requires the Department of Veterans Affairs letter for the disabled veteran property tax exemption to be submitted only once, not annually, and requires taxpayers who no longer qualify as disabled veterans to notify the county collector.

ar:HB1073.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1073.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2026-27 funds for the Public Service Commission: $11,730,062 for the Utilities Division, $1,424,387 for the Tax Division, and $1,064,899 for the Pipeline Safety Program.

ar:HB1074.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT - OIL AND GAS COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1074.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Energy and Environment - Oil and Gas Commission for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:HB1075.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AND THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE - ARKANSAS BIOSCIENCES INSTITUTES APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1075.summary: Appropriates money from the Tobacco Settlement Program Fund for personal services and operating expenses of the Arkansas Biosciences Institutes at the University of Arkansas and its Division of Agriculture for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027.

ar:HB1076.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS - FORT SMITH APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1076.summary: Appropriates $27,946,966 for state operations and $133,280,000 from cash funds for the University of Arkansas–Fort Smith for fiscal year 2026-27.

ar:HB1079.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR GENETIC TESTING FOR AN INHERITED GENE MUTATION FOR CERTAIN INDIVIDUALS; AND TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR EVIDENCE-BASED CANCER IMAGING FOR CERTAIN INDIVIDUALS.
ar:HB1079.summary: Requires health plans, from 2026, to cover genetic testing for inherited cancer-risk mutations (personal or family history of cancer) and evidence-based cancer imaging (increased risk), with no deductible, copay or coinsurance except under state and school employee plans or self-funded governmental plans.

ar:HB1080.title: TO REPEAL THE REQUIREMENT FOR A FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT FOR BILLS RELATED TO HEALTH BENEFIT PLANS; AND TO REPEAL THE BILL FILING DEADLINE FOR BILLS AFFECTING HEALTH BENEFIT PLANS OF ENTITIES OF THE STATE.
ar:HB1080.summary: Repeals the fiscal impact statement requirement for bills raising health benefit plan costs for state entities, and the 15-day introduction deadline for such bills and for bills affecting the state and public school insurance program.

ar:HB1081.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT - OIL AND GAS COMMISSION REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1081.summary: Reappropriates unspent balances of up to $275,274 in federal funds and $296,552 in cash funds for roof repair of the Oil and Gas Commission's education center and warehouse, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:HB1086.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS - PULASKI TECHNICAL COLLEGE SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1086.summary: Appropriates an additional $25 million in cash funds for capital improvements at the University of Arkansas - Pulaski Technical College for fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1087.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - RACING COMMISSION SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1087.summary: Appropriates an extra $7,000 for fiscal 2025-2026 for operating expenses of the Racing Commission's Casino Gaming Section, on top of the earlier appropriation.

ar:HB1088.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - DISBURSING OFFICER SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1088.summary: Adds $8 million for firemen's and police officers' pension and relief funds and $5 million for payments to fire departments for fiscal 2025-26, on top of earlier appropriations.

ar:HB1089.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - DISBURSING OFFICER SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1089.summary: Appropriates $1.5 million more for fiscal 2025-2026 for Pregnancy Help Organization grants, on top of the earlier appropriation, and transfers $3.5 million from the General Revenue Allotment Reserve Fund to fund those grants.

ar:HB1090.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - ARKANSAS DEVELOPMENT FINANCE AUTHORITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1090.summary: Appropriates about $27.9 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the Arkansas Development Finance Authority and sets its maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1091.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1091.summary: Appropriates about $357.7 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the Department of Health across several accounts, and sets maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1092.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS - DIVISION OF COMMUNITY CORRECTION REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1092.summary: Reappropriates up to $671,398 in unspent Community Correction Revolving Fund money for repairs, construction and improvements to Division of Community Correction property, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:HB1093.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH - HEALTH SERVICES PERMIT AGENCY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1093.summary: Sets four staff positions and appropriates $480,500 for the Department of Health's Health Services Permit Agency for fiscal year 2025-2026, with unspent fee and fine revenue carried forward.

ar:HB1094.title: AN ACT TO MAKE AN APPROPRIATION FOR STATE TURNBACK FOR COUNTIES AND MUNICIPALITIES BY THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1094.summary: Appropriates an extra $90 million for fiscal 2025-2026 from the Property Tax Relief Trust Fund for the Treasurer of State to distribute to counties, on top of the earlier appropriation.

ar:HB1095.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - STATE BANK DEPARTMENT AND STATE SECURITIES DEPARTMENT APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1095.summary: Appropriates about $19.6 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the State Bank Department and State Securities Department, and sets their maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1097.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF PARKS, HERITAGE, AND TOURISM - DIVISION OF HERITAGE REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1097.summary: Carries unspent balances of earlier appropriations for the Division of Heritage into the next fiscal year, effective July 1, 2026, including up to $750,000 for special maintenance and up to $10 million for acquiring or preserving state lands and historic sites.

ar:HB1098.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF PARKS, HERITAGE, AND TOURISM - STATE PARKS AND TOURISM DIVISIONS REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1098.summary: Reappropriates up to $20 million, the unspent balance of a 2025 appropriation, from the Natural and Cultural Resources Grant and Trust Fund for state-owned lands, historic sites and buildings, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:HB1099.title: AN ACT FOR THE STATE BOARD OF ELECTION COMMISSIONERS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1099.summary: Appropriates $9.04 million for the State Board of Election Commissioners for fiscal 2025-2026: about $1.1 million for operations, $6.34 million for election expenses and $1.6 million for the nonpartisan general election, and sets 9 positions.

ar:HB1100.title: TO AMEND THE REVENUE STABILIZATION LAW; TO CREATE FUNDS; TO MAKE TRANSFERS TO AND FROM FUNDS AND FUND ACCOUNTS; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1100.summary: Sets 2026-27 revenue allocations to state funds, including $6.64 billion in the first allocation tier, and transfers $100 million to a Medicaid set-aside, $70 million to a Children's Educational Freedom Account set-aside, and other amounts to reserve set-asides.

ar:HB1101.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS GOVERNOR'S MANSION COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1101.summary: Appropriates $1,500,250 from the State Central Services Fund for Governor's Mansion Commission operations in fiscal year 2025-2026, and authorizes 10 regular employees and up to four extra-help employees.

ar:HB1102.title: AN ACT TO MAKE AN APPROPRIATION FOR STATE TURNBACK FOR COUNTIES AND MUNICIPALITIES BY THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30, 2026; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
ar:HB1102.summary: Appropriates funds to the Treasurer of State for distribution to cities and counties in fiscal 2025-26, including $215 million in special revenues to cities and $300 million in property tax relief to counties.

ar:HB1103.title: TO INCREASE THE HOMESTEAD PROPERTY TAX CREDIT.
ar:HB1103.summary: Raises the homestead property tax credit from $600 to $675, for assessment years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

ar:HB1104.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND LICENSING - DIVISION OF LABOR APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1104.summary: Sets maximum staffing, extra help and operating appropriations for the Department of Labor and Licensing, including its Division of Labor, for fiscal year 2025-2026.

ar:HB1105.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES - SECRETARY'S OFFICE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1105.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2025-26 funds for the Department of Human Services Secretary's Office, including $355,720 for the Secretary, $69,760,347 for operations and $821,500 for consolidated costs, plus building construction and grant funds.

ar:HB1108.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - REFUND OF LOCAL TAXES APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1108.summary: Appropriates $1,100,000,000 for refunding cities' share and $990,000,000 for counties' share of local sales and use taxes through the Treasurer of State for fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1109.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - AMENDMENT 74 PROPERTY TAX APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1109.summary: Appropriates $1,750,000,000 from the Uniform Tax Rate Trust Fund for the Treasurer of State to distribute property tax funds to counties under Amendment 74 in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1110.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - ANIMAL RESCUE SHELTERS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1110.summary: Appropriates $25,000 for cities and $25,000 for counties from the Animal Rescue and Shelter Trust Fund for government-owned animal rescue shelters in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1111.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT AND EMERGENCY MEDICAL APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1111.summary: Appropriates $300,000 each from the Citizens First Responder Safety Enhancement Fund for the Arkansas Ambulance Association and the Arkansas Association of Chiefs of Police in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1112.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - CITY-COUNTY TOURIST MEETING AND ENTERTAINMENT FACILITIES ASSISTANCE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1112.summary: Appropriates $887,908 from the City-County Tourist Facilities Aid Fund to the Treasurer of State for fiscal year 2025-2026, for debt service and operating expenses of eligible publicly owned tourist meeting and entertainment facilities.

ar:HB1113.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER OF STATE - GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1113.summary: Appropriates $42,000,000 for college savings and higher education bond payments and $43,000,000 for water, waste disposal, and pollution abatement bond payments in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1114.title: AN ACT FOR THE COMMISSIONER OF STATE LANDS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1114.summary: Appropriates about $37.2 million for the Commissioner of State Lands for fiscal 2025-2026, including $4.4 million for operations, $32.3 million for delinquent-tax land programs, and amounts for capital outlay and submerged lands projects.

ar:HB1117.title: CONCERNING THE ADMINISTRATION OF INSTRUCTION ON FIREARM SAFETY IN PUBLIC SCHOOL DISTRICTS AND OPEN-ENROLLMENT PUBLIC CHARTER SCHOOLS.
ar:HB1117.summary: Requires public school districts and open-enrollment charter schools to give annual firearm safety instruction from 2025-2026, from a grade set by the education division and Game and Fish Commission through grade 12, using approved curricula with no brand or organizational affiliation.

ar:HB1118.title: TO AMEND THE LAWS CONCERNING THE MANAGEMENT OF PREMIUM TAXES UNDER THE ARKANSAS FIRE AND POLICE PENSION REVIEW BOARD; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1118.summary: Moves administration of the Policemen's Pension Supplement Program, Future Supplement Fund and related premium-tax duties from the Fire and Police Pension Review Board to the Department of Finance and Administration, and repeals the board's funding certification for underfunded plans.

ar:HB1119.title: TO AMEND THE PROVISIONS REGARDING DELINQUENT PAYMENTS BY A POLITICAL SUBDIVISION UNDER THE ARKANSAS LOCAL POLICE AND FIRE RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1119.summary: Shortens to five calendar days, from ten, the time before a local government's late payment or report to the Local Police and Fire Retirement System becomes a delinquency that can lead to withholding of state money.

ar:HB1120.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT SYSTEM APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1120.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2025-26 funds for the Public Employees Retirement System ($142.7 million operations, $725 million cash), State Police Retirement, and Judicial Retirement, and caps regular employees at 78.

ar:HB1121.title: TO REPEAL THE LAW CONCERNING THE TRANSFER OF TAX-FORFEITED LANDS TO STATE INSTITUTIONS.
ar:HB1121.summary: Repeals the law letting the Commissioner of State Lands give tax-forfeited land to state agencies, institutions, counties, cities and school districts for a $1 fee.

ar:HB1123.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - MARTIN LUTHER KING, JR. COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1123.summary: Caps the Martin Luther King, Jr. Commission at 4 regular employees and appropriates $383,978 for operations and $91,123 in cash funds for fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1124.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1124.summary: Appropriates about $248 million for fiscal 2025-26 for Department of Finance and Administration programs, and sets maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1125.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE & ADMINISTRATION - REGULATORY DIVISION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1125.summary: Appropriates funds for fiscal 2025-2026 for the Department of Finance and Administration's Regulatory Division and Racing Commission, including $4,378,056 for Regulatory Division operations from the Miscellaneous Agencies Fund, and authorizes 71 Regulatory Division positions.

ar:HB1127.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - ARKANSAS STATE LIBRARY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1127.summary: Appropriates about $6.9 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the Arkansas State Library, including aid to public libraries, and sets its maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1128.title: AN ACT FOR ARKANSAS LEGISLATIVE AUDIT OF THE LEGISLATIVE JOINT AUDITING COMMITTEE SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:HB1128.summary: Authorizes ten extra-help employees and appropriates $47,220 for Arkansas Legislative Audit for fiscal 2024-25.

ar:HB1129.title: TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF "HOMESTEAD" FOR THE PURPOSE OF THE PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION FOR DISABLED VETERANS, SURVIVING SPOUSES, AND MINOR DEPENDENT CHILDREN.
ar:HB1129.summary: Raises from 40 to 160 the acres of contiguous land that count as a homestead for the disabled veteran property tax exemption, for assessment years beginning January 1, 2025.

ar:HB1131.title: TO AUTHORIZE AN ADVANCED PRACTICE REGISTERED NURSE TO DELEGATE CERTAIN TASKS TO MEDICAL ASSISTANTS AND OTHER UNLICENSED STAFF.
ar:HB1131.summary: Lets an advanced practice registered nurse delegate tasks such as giving medications and immunizations and drawing blood to trained unlicensed staff, who stay under the nurse's supervision, with Board of Nursing rules on training and limits.

ar:HB1133.title: TO AUTHORIZE NORTHWEST TECHNICAL INSTITUTE TO APPOINT A PRESIDENT WITH AN INDUSTRY BACKGROUND; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1133.summary: Allows Northwest Technical Institute to appoint a president with an industry background instead of an education background.

ar:HB1135.title: TO ALLOW THE ISSUANCE OF A DIGITIZED IDENTIFICATION CARD; TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE FEE FOR ISSUANCE OF A DIGITIZED DRIVER'S LICENSE OR DIGITIZED IDENTIFICATION CARD; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1135.summary: Allows digitized state identification cards, in addition to digitized driver's licenses, and lets the Office of Driver Services charge a fee of up to $10 per digitized license or ID card issued.

ar:HB1137.title: AN ACT TO SEPARATE THE OFFICES OF SHERIFF AND TAX COLLECTOR IN SEARCY COUNTY.
ar:HB1137.summary: Separates the offices of sheriff and tax collector in Searcy County, with both elected in 2026 and taking office January 1, 2027.

ar:HB1138.title: TO AUTHORIZE CERTAIN MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS TO CERTIFY TO THE OFFICE OF MOTOR VEHICLE ELIGIBILITY FOR A SPECIAL LICENSE PLATE, CERTIFICATE, OR PARKING DECAL FOR A PERSON WITH A DISABILITY.
ar:HB1138.summary: Adds advanced practice registered nurses, physician assistants, and physical therapists to the physicians who can certify a person's disability to the Office of Motor Vehicle for disability parking plates, placards, and decals.

ar:HB1142.title: TO CREATE THE REPRODUCTIVE EMPOWERMENT AND SUPPORT THROUGH OPTIMAL RESTORATION (RESTORE) ACT.
ar:HB1142.summary: Creates the RESTORE Act: bars recipients of state or local funds from penalizing providers who decline to take part in assisted reproductive technology; requires Title X-funded facilities to include fertility awareness-based methods; adds restorative reproductive medicine to required insurance coverage.

ar:HB1145.title: TO INCREASE THE PURCHASE AMOUNT AUTHORIZED FOR ADDITIONAL AFTER-MARKET EQUIPMENT FOR A NEW MOTOR VEHICLE PURCHASED BY A COUNTY OR MUNICIPALITY.
ar:HB1145.summary: Raises from $1,200 to $2,000 (counties) and from $600 to $2,000 (cities) how much after-market equipment or options may be added above the fleet price when buying a new motor vehicle without soliciting bids.

ar:HB1146.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF ATTORNEY GENERAL APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1146.summary: Appropriates funds to the Office of Attorney General for the 2025-2026 fiscal year, including about $26.4 million for operations, and sets maximum employee numbers and salary rates.

ar:HB1148.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS PRIVACY ACT; AND TO ADDRESS CERTAIN IMAGES CAPTURED BY UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS.
ar:HB1148.summary: Creates the Arkansas Privacy Act: makes it a Class C misdemeanor to use a drone to capture an image of a person or private property for surveillance (exceptions include law enforcement), penalizes possessing or sharing such images, and allows civil damages.

ar:HB1150.title: TO PROHIBIT A PHARMACY BENEFITS MANAGER FROM OBTAINING CERTAIN PHARMACY PERMITS.
ar:HB1150.summary: Bars pharmacy benefits managers and their affiliates from holding retail pharmacy permits, including mail-order, and requires the Board of Pharmacy to revoke or not renew violators' permits, with limited-use permits for rare drugs.

ar:HB1151.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - DIVISION OF CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1151.summary: Appropriates funds for the Division of Career and Technical Education for fiscal 2025-2026, including $2.99 million for operations, $18.9 million in federal funds, $23.2 million for vocational center aid and $4.74 million for start-up grants.

ar:HB1152.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - DIVISION OF PUBLIC SCHOOL ACADEMIC FACILITIES AND TRANSPORTATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1152.summary: Appropriates about $218 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the Division of Public School Academic Facilities and Transportation, and sets its maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1153.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE - PROMOTION BOARDS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1153.summary: Sets appropriations from agricultural promotion board funds, such as the Beef Council ($1,067,076) and Catfish Promotion Board ($120,000), for the Department of Agriculture for fiscal year 2025-2026.

ar:HB1155.title: TO CREATE A REBUTTABLE PRESUMPTION OF QUALIFICATION FOR DISABILITY RETIREMENT BENEFITS UNDER THE ARKANSAS TEACHER RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1155.summary: Adds a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs 100% permanent and total disability rating as a second way, besides a Social Security favorable determination letter, to create a rebuttable presumption that a Teacher Retirement System member qualifies for disability retirement.

ar:HB1156.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ELIGIBILITY OF A SURVIVING SPOUSE FOR SURVIVOR ANNUITY BENEFITS UNDER THE ARKANSAS TEACHER RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1156.summary: Shortens from two years to one year the minimum marriage length before a surviving spouse of an active Teacher Retirement System member receives the survivor annuity.

ar:HB1157.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING SURVIVOR ANNUITY BENEFITS FOR DEPENDENT CHILDREN UNDER THE ARKANSAS TEACHER RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1157.summary: Makes a deceased active teacher's child a dependent child eligible for the Teacher Retirement System annuity until age 22, replacing the age-18 limit and full-time student conditions, and extends dependent child annuities to children of disability retirees.

ar:HB1158.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ELECTION OF A DISTRIBUTION OPTION UNDER THE TEACHER DEFERRED RETIREMENT OPTION PLAN; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1158.summary: Lets a Teacher Deferred Retirement Option member cancel and change a distribution election once, before the end of the second full month after retirement, if no lump-sum rollover was chosen and any overpaid amounts are repaid.

ar:HB1160.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING PERMISSIVE SERVICE CREDIT FOR GAP YEAR SERVICE UNDER THE ARKANSAS TEACHER RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1160.summary: Replaces teacher "gap years" with quarter-year "gap periods" for Teacher Retirement System permissive service credit, letting eligible members buy one-quarter year of credit per gap period instead of one year per gap year.

ar:HB1161.title: TO CLARIFY THE LAW CONCERNING AN ELECTION TO CHANGE ANNUITY OPTIONS WITHIN ONE YEAR OF RETIREMENT UNDER THE ARKANSAS TEACHER RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1161.summary: Removes 1994 and 1995 date references from the one-time option for Teacher Retirement System retirees to change annuity options within one year of retirement, and makes the change effective the month after requirements are met instead of retroactively.

ar:HB1163.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND LICENSING - BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1163.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2025-26 operating funds for licensing boards in the Department of Labor and Licensing, including accountancy, appraisers, athletic commission, architects, auctioneers, bail bonds, barbers, contractors, real estate and towing boards.

ar:HB1164.title: TO ALLOW A PHYSICIAN OR HEALTHCARE PROVIDER TO OFFER COGNITIVE ASSESSMENTS FOR CERTAIN PATIENTS; AND TO MANDATE THAT INSURANCE POLICIES COVER ASSESSMENTS FOR COGNITIVE FUNCTION FOR CERTAIN PATIENTS.
ar:HB1164.summary: Allows physicians and health care providers to offer an annual cognitive assessment to patients 60 or older, or 45 or older at higher risk of dementia, and requires patient refusals to be documented. Also mandates insurance coverage of the assessments.

ar:HB1166.title: TO CLARIFY THE TYPES OF EPINEPHRINE FOR USE IN ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN THIS STATE.
ar:HB1166.summary: Defines "epinephrine" for school use as FDA-approved auto-injectors and nasal spray, replacing "auto-injectable epinephrine" in the rules on students carrying it and school staff administering it, so nasal spray is covered.

ar:HB1167.title: TO MODIFY THE SIGNATURE AUTHORITY FOR ADVANCED PRACTICE REGISTERED NURSES AND PHYSICIAN ASSISTANTS; AND TO CLARIFY THAT DURABLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT INCLUDES DIABETIC SHOES AND SHOE INSERTS.
ar:HB1167.summary: Adds authorizations for durable medical equipment, including orthotics, prosthetics and diabetic shoes or inserts, to the forms that advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants may sign in place of a physician.

ar:HB1169.title: TO CLARIFY THE ADMISSION CRITERIA FOR AN INVOLUNTARY COMMITMENT TO INCLUDE A PERSON WHO IS IN A MENTAL CONDITION AS A RESULT OF A MEDICAL CONDITION.
ar:HB1169.summary: Expands involuntary admission criteria to include a person whose medical condition, such as dementia, encephalitis or delirium, causes a behavioral health impairment that makes the person a clear and present danger.

ar:HB1171.title: TO MODIFY THE MEDICAID PROVIDER-LED ORGANIZED CARE ACT; AND TO AUTHORIZE AN ABBREVIATED INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT FOR CERTAIN BENEFICIARIES ENROLLED IN A RISK-BASED PROVIDER ORGANIZATION.
ar:HB1171.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to use an abbreviated independent assessment, such as a desk review, for people already approved for home- and community-based services who have chronic, long-term conditions and are in a risk-based provider organization.

ar:HB1173.title: TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF "BEER" TO CHANGE THE ALLOWABLE ALCOHOLIC CONTENT AND TO INCLUDE MALT BEVERAGES.
ar:HB1173.summary: Raises the maximum alcohol content of beer from 5 percent to 14 percent by weight and defines "malt beverage" as grain-brewed liquor of 5 to 21 percent alcohol by weight.

ar:HB1174.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS - DIVISION OF CORRECTION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1174.summary: Appropriates money for Division of Correction operations in fiscal year 2025-2026, including $365 million for inmate care and custody, plus county jail reimbursement, work release, prison industry and farm programs.

ar:HB1175.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF PARKS, HERITAGE, AND TOURISM - DIVISION OF HERITAGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1175.summary: Appropriates funds and sets staff positions and salary grades for the Department of Parks, Heritage, and Tourism, including shared services and the Division of Heritage, for 2025-2026, covering state operations, Amendment 75 conservation tax operations, historic preservation, and arts council programs.

ar:HB1176.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY - DIVISION OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1176.summary: Appropriates about $471 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the Division of Emergency Management, including disaster relief grants, and sets maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:HB1178.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE CONTRACTING OF A MUNICIPAL ATTORNEY; TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING SUMS COLLECTED BY DISTRICT COURTS; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING COST SHARING FOR DISTRICT COURT EXPENSES.
ar:HB1178.summary: Lets second-class cities and incorporated towns without a city attorney office contract with an attorney, and revises how district court fines, fees and costs are recorded and distributed among cities, towns and counties.

ar:HB1180.title: TO CREATE THE BABY OLIVIA ACT.
ar:HB1180.summary: As passed by the House, requires public school districts and charter schools to add a discussion of human growth and development inside the womb to an existing health and safety course beginning in fifth grade.

ar:HB1181.title: TO AMEND THE FULL PRACTICE AUTHORITY OF A CERTIFIED NURSE MIDWIFE TO ALLOW ADMITTING PRIVILEGES.
ar:HB1181.summary: Adds to certified nurse midwives' full practice authority the ability to admit and discharge patients at licensed hospitals where granted privileges, and to sign birth and death certificates.

ar:HB1182.title: TO REPLACE THE DEFINED TERM "MEDICATION ASSISTIVE PERSON" WITH THE DEFINED TERM "CERTIFIED MEDICATION ASSISTANT" THROUGHOUT § 17-87-701 ET SEQ.
ar:HB1182.summary: Renames medication assistive persons "certified medication assistants," removes the one-year nurse-aide registration and experience requirements, raises minimum training from 100 to 115 hours, and permits them to give subcutaneous insulin injections.

ar:HB1183.title: TO CREATE THE REGISTERED DIALYSIS PATIENT CARE TECHNICIAN ACT.
ar:HB1183.summary: Creates a state registry of dialysis patient care technicians run by the Board of Nursing. Registrants need a diploma or GED, training, national certification within 18 months of hire and a fee, and may give hemodialysis care under a registered nurse's delegation.

ar:HB1184.title: TO AMEND THE FAIR MORTGAGE LENDING ACT; AND TO PROTECT A CONSUMER'S PRIVACY IN CERTAIN MORTGAGE APPLICATIONS.
ar:HB1184.summary: Bars loan officers from using "mortgage trigger leads" (contacts based on credit reports pulled after a credit application) in misleading ways, including omitting required disclosures, contacting consumers who opted out of prescreened offers, or calling numbers on the national Do-Not-Call registry.

ar:HB1185.title: TO ADOPT THE DIETITIAN LICENSURE COMPACT IN ARKANSAS.
ar:HB1185.summary: Enters Arkansas into the Dietitian Licensure Compact, which lets licensed dietitians from member states obtain a compact privilege to practice in Arkansas, and Arkansas dietitians to practice in other member states.

ar:HB1186.title: TO CREATE THE PAIN RELIEF PARITY ACT; AND TO REQUIRE PAIN RELIEF PARITY IN THE ARKANSAS MEDICAID PROGRAM.
ar:HB1186.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services not to disadvantage FDA-approved non-opioid pain drugs with no therapeutic equivalent on the Medicaid preferred drug list relative to opioids, such as by marking them non-preferred or imposing stricter prior authorization or step therapy.

ar:HB1187.title: TO AUTHORIZE A LICENSURE BY ENDORSEMENT FOR MARRIAGE AND FAMILY THERAPISTS.
ar:HB1187.summary: Requires the Board of Examiners in Counseling to license marriage and family therapists already licensed in good standing in another state, if they have no disqualifying criminal offense and no pending complaint or investigation.

ar:HB1189.title: AN ACT TO AMEND NOVICE TEACHER MENTORING REQUIREMENTS UNDER THE TEACHER EXCELLENCE AND SUPPORT SYSTEM; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
ar:HB1189.summary: Exempts a novice teacher who has completed a Division of Elementary and Secondary Education-approved year-long residency from the required novice teacher mentoring under the Teacher Excellence and Support System.

ar:HB1191.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1191.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2025-2026 operations of the Department of Public Safety, including State Police, crime lab, law enforcement training, crime information center, and crime victims reparations, and sets maximum employee counts and salary grades.

ar:HB1193.title: TO REQUIRE AN INSURER TO INCLUDE A LIENHOLDER ON PAYMENTS MADE UNDER AN INSURANCE POLICY.
ar:HB1193.summary: As passed by the House, requires a motor vehicle liability insurer to name a perfected auto loan lienholder that has a physical location in Arkansas as a payee on payments for damage to a motor vehicle.

ar:HB1194.title: TO AMEND ARKANSAS LAW CONCERNING THE PLACEMENT OF A MONUMENT ON THE STATE CAPITOL GROUNDS IN RECOGNITION AND APPRECIATION OF THE INTEGRATION OF HOXIE PUBLIC SCHOOLS.
ar:HB1194.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to permit and arrange a monument on the Capitol grounds commemorating the 1955 integration of Hoxie public schools, funded by gifts to a new trust fund, with design and site approved after consulting the Capitol Arts and Grounds Commission.

ar:HB1196.title: TO SEPARATE THE OFFICES OF SHERIFF AND TAX COLLECTOR IN MONTGOMERY COUNTY.
ar:HB1196.summary: Separates the offices of sheriff and tax collector in Montgomery County, with both elected in 2026 and taking office January 1, 2027.

ar:HB1199.title: TO REPEAL THE STATUTE CONCERNING THE PROHIBITION AGAINST A SCHOOL DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS GRANTING A LEGAL TRANSFER UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS.
ar:HB1199.summary: Repeals the law barring school boards from granting student transfers that would violate a desegregation court order, along with the affidavit requirement and state-aid withholding that enforced it.

ar:HB1200.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT - DIVISION OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1200.summary: Appropriates money for Division of Environmental Quality operations in fiscal year 2025-2026, including state and federal operations and programs for waste water, land reclamation, hazardous waste, storage tanks, and energy.

ar:HB1201.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1201.summary: Appropriates $2.72 billion for Department of Transportation operations in fiscal 2025-26, plus appropriations including state aid roads and streets, public transit, weather warning, and intermodal facility grants.

ar:HB1202.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - DISBURSING OFFICER APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1202.summary: Appropriates fiscal 2025-26 funds for the Finance and Administration Disbursing Officer, including $103,550,000 in supplemental appropriations to agencies and constitutional officers, $2.1 billion for miscellaneous federal programs, and disaster, unemployment and other programs.

ar:HB1204.title: TO ESTABLISH RECOVERY OF DAMAGES FOR NECESSARY MEDICAL CARE, TREATMENT, OR SERVICES RENDERED.
ar:HB1204.summary: Limits recovery of past medical costs in civil damages to amounts actually paid by or for the plaintiff, or amounts still unpaid for which the plaintiff or a third party is legally responsible.

ar:HB1205.title: TO AMEND THE INDEPENDENT INSPECTIONS OF A MODULAR BUILDING FOR CODE COMPLIANCE; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1205.summary: Allows modular building manufacturers to use third-party inspection agencies listed with any ISO/IEC 17011-compliant accreditation body, not only the International Accreditation Service, for code-compliance inspections.

ar:HB1206.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - DIVISION OF ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION - PUBLIC SCHOOL FUND APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1206.summary: Appropriates about $3.48 billion from the Public School Fund for fiscal year 2025-2026 for public school funding, plus funds for the Arkansas Public School Computer Network and the Office of Education Renewal Zones.

ar:HB1207.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS AND CLARIFY LANGUAGE FOR THE PROPER ADMINISTRATION OF BENEFITS UNDER THE STATE POLICE RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1207.summary: Raises from 22 to 23 the college age limit for survivor benefits of children of state police officers killed on duty without system membership, repeals a Tier Two consumer-price-index benefit cap, and lets courts order retirant benefits paid into court for willful child nonsupport.

ar:HB1208.title: TO ALLOW THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM TO COLLECT AMOUNTS OF OVERPAYMENTS FOR DEBTS OWED TO A STATE SUPPORTED RETIREMENT SYSTEM ADMINISTERED BY THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1208.summary: Adds the Judicial Retirement System and State Police Retirement System to agencies that may collect debts through state tax refund setoffs, and covers overpayments from retirement systems the Public Employees' Retirement System administers.

ar:HB1209.title: FOR THE PROPER ADMINISTRATION OF BENEFITS BY THE ARKANSAS JUDICIAL RETIREMENT SYSTEM REGARDING THE SUBJECTION OF ANNUITY RIGHTS TO PROCESS OF LAW AND CORRECTION OF ERRORS.
ar:HB1209.summary: Adds Judicial Retirement System rules shielding annuity rights from garnishment and similar process, with exceptions for employer setoff of embezzlement or fraud claims and court-ordered payment into court for willful nonsupport of minor children, and sets error-correction procedures with five-year overpayment limits.

ar:HB1210.title: TO AMEND THE LAWS CONCERNING TRANSFER OF FUNDS FOR THE COSTS OF ADMINISTERING THE ARKANSAS JUDICIAL RETIREMENT SYSTEM AND THE STATE POLICE RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1210.summary: Starting July 1, 2027, requires the Judges and State Police retirement funds to reimburse the Public Employees' Retirement System for administering them, using a 50/50 weighting of each system's share of assets and membership.

ar:HB1211.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS AND CLARIFY LANGUAGE FOR THE PROPER ADMINISTRATION OF BENEFITS UNDER THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1211.summary: Revises the Public Employees' Retirement System's list of recurring payments counted as compensation and consolidates its rules on forfeiting benefits until employment-termination requirements are met into one section.

ar:HB1213.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS ATHLETIC TRAINERS ACT; TO CLARIFY THE DEFINITION OF "ATHLETE"; AND TO DEFINE "HEALTHCARE PROVIDER" REGARDING STUDENT ATHLETE CONCUSSION EDUCATION.
ar:HB1213.summary: As passed by the House, defines "athlete" under the Athletic Trainers Act by activities of recreation, sport, exercise or tactical duty, and defines "healthcare provider" for student concussion education as physicians, neuropsychologists, advanced practice nurses, athletic trainers, physician assistants or physical therapists.

ar:HB1214.title: TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF PRIMARY INSTRUCTOR WITHIN THE LONG-TERM CARE AIDE TRAINING ACT.
ar:HB1214.summary: Changes the primary instructor definition in the Long-Term Care Aide Training Act: extends the window for required long-term care nursing experience from five to ten years, requires an annual eight-hour class authorized by the Department of Human Services, and defines general nursing experience.

ar:HB1215.title: TO AUTHORIZE A COACH OR ATHLETICS PERSONNEL MEMBER OF THE OPPOSITE SEX TO ADDRESS, SUPERVISE, OR TREAT STUDENT ATHLETES IN A MULTIPLE OCCUPANCY RESTROOM OR CHANGING AREA UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS.
ar:HB1215.summary: Adds an exception to public school sex-designated restroom rules: coaches and athletics personnel may enter an opposite-sex restroom or changing area to supervise or treat student athletes around athletic events, if no one is undressed and another adult is present.

ar:HB1217.title: TO ESTABLISH THE INTERSTATE MASSAGE COMPACT IN ARKANSAS.
ar:HB1217.summary: Enters Arkansas into the Interstate Massage Compact, creating a multistate license pathway that lets licensed massage therapists practice in other member states, with an interstate commission to administer it.

ar:HB1218.title: TO CREATE LICENSURE FOR THERAPEUTIC RECREATION SPECIALISTS; AND TO CREATE THE THERAPEUTIC RECREATION PRACTICE ACT.
ar:HB1218.summary: Creates the Therapeutic Recreation Practice Act, licensing therapeutic recreation specialists through the Department of Health with a five-member advisory committee, and sets licensure qualifications, temporary licenses, renewals and title protection.

ar:HB1220.title: TO AMEND THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE ARKANSAS NATURAL AND CULTURAL RESOURCES COUNCIL.
ar:HB1220.summary: Allows the Commissioner of State Lands to be represented on the Arkansas Natural and Cultural Resources Council by a designee.

ar:HB1221.title: TO AMEND ARKANSAS LAW CONCERNING INITIATIVES, REFERENDA, AND CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1221.summary: Voids initiative and referendum petition signatures obtained after the next general election following ballot title certification, and makes that certification expire on that election date.

ar:HB1222.title: TO REQUIRE THE ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW BALLOT TITLES FOR CONFLICTS WITH THE UNITED STATES CONSTITUTION AND FEDERAL STATUTES; AND TO PROHIBIT THE SUBMISSION OF CONFLICTING INITIATIVE PETITIONS AND REFERENDUM PETITIONS.
ar:HB1222.summary: Lets the Attorney General reject proposed initiated acts and amendments whose text conflicts with the U.S. Constitution or a federal statute, and bars sponsors from submitting multiple conflicting petitions, except after a rejection or after the general election following a certification.

ar:HB1223.title: TO ALLOW A CANDIDATE FOR THE OFFICE OF JUSTICE OF THE SUPREME COURT OR JUDGE OF THE COURT OF APPEALS WHO IS SERVING IN THAT POSITION AS AN APPOINTEE TO USE THE TITLE OF THAT POSITION AS A PREFIX ON THE BALLOT.
ar:HB1223.summary: Adds Supreme Court justices and Court of Appeals judges who are serving as appointees, and running for that office, to those allowed to use their title as a ballot prefix after serving at least twelve months.

ar:HB1225.title: AN ACT FOR THE BLACK RIVER TECHNICAL COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1225.summary: Caps regular employees at 222 and appropriates up to $9,903,675 for state operations and $42,924,800 in cash funds for Black River Technical College in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1226.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY - MOUNTAIN HOME APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1226.summary: Caps regular employees at 198 and appropriates up to $4,615,410 for state operations and $16,525,000 in cash funds for Arkansas State University - Mountain Home in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1227.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS - PULASKI TECHNICAL COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1227.summary: Caps regular employees at 780 and appropriates up to $17,816,509 for state operations and $56,135,000 in cash funds for University of Arkansas - Pulaski Technical College in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1228.title: AN ACT FOR THE NORTHWEST ARKANSAS COMMUNITY COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1228.summary: Appropriates up to $13,732,517 for state operations and $78,479,696 in cash funds for Northwest Arkansas Community College in fiscal 2025-26. Also appropriates $274,075 for its child protection training center.

ar:HB1229.title: AN ACT FOR THE OZARKA COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1229.summary: Caps regular employees at 220 and appropriates up to $4,677,917 for state operations and $15,501,000 in cash funds for Ozarka College in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1230.title: AN ACT FOR THE NORTH ARKANSAS COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1230.summary: Caps regular employees at 381 and appropriates up to $9,260,452 for state operations and $37,490,000 in cash funds for North Arkansas College in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1231.title: AN ACT FOR THE PHILLIPS COMMUNITY COLLEGE OF THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1231.summary: Caps regular employees at 296 and appropriates up to $10,987,804 for state operations and $25,275,000 in cash funds for Phillips Community College of the University of Arkansas in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1233.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS NORTHEASTERN COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1233.summary: Caps regular employees at 255 and appropriates up to $11,272,736 for state operations and $26,428,000 in cash funds for Arkansas Northeastern College in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1234.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS COMMUNITY COLLEGE AT HOPE-TEXARKANA APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1234.summary: Caps regular employees at 214 and appropriates up to $6,839,312 for state operations and $18,490,197 in cash funds for University of Arkansas Community College at Hope-Texarkana in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1235.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS EAST ARKANSAS COMMUNITY COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1235.summary: Appropriates funds for the University of Arkansas East Arkansas Community College for fiscal 2025-2026: $11.2 million for state operations and $28.2 million from cash funds.

ar:HB1236.title: TO ALLOW A PUBLIC SCHOOL EMPLOYEE TO BE RELEASED FROM HIS OR HER CONTRACT BY A CERTAIN DATE UPON HIS OR HER WRITTEN REQUEST; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1236.summary: Allows a public school or open-enrollment charter school employee to rescind a signed contract for the next school year by written notice before the end of the business day on May 15, or the prior Friday if May 15 is a weekend.

ar:HB1237.title: TO PROHIBIT MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS FROM SOLICITING INJURED INDIVIDUALS; AND TO SET PENALTIES FOR A VIOLATION OF THE PROHIBITION OF SOLICITATION OF INJURED INDIVIDUALS.
ar:HB1237.summary: Bars medical professionals from soliciting people injured in an accident or disaster for treatment unless they have a prior relationship or 30 days have passed; makes violation a Class D felony and voids related payment agreements.

ar:HB1238.title: TO AUTHORIZE A MORTGAGOR TO RECOVER FEES IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER THE STATUTORY FORECLOSURE LAW.
ar:HB1238.summary: As passed by the House, allows a mortgagor to recover attorney's fees if successful in setting aside a statutory foreclosure sale because of a defect in the process, unless the mortgagor halts the foreclosure only by paying the debt owed.

ar:HB1241.title: TO ENSURE THAT THE ARKANSAS MEDICAID PROGRAM REIMBURSES FOR DENTAL AND ANESTHESIA COSTS FOR HIGH COMPLEXITY ORAL HEALTH CARE.
ar:HB1241.summary: Requires Arkansas Medicaid to reimburse accredited dental schools and academic medical centers up to $3,750 per episode and $5,000 per year for dental and anesthesia costs of adults with high complexity oral health care needing sedation.

ar:HB1242.title: TO AMEND THE MECHANISM BY WHICH SCHOOL NURSES ARE COMPENSATED.
ar:HB1242.summary: Requires districts, starting in 2027-28, to pay school nurses at least the classroom-teacher minimum base salary on a 190-day schedule (90% or 80% for nurses without a bachelor's degree), and excludes nurses from the classified-employee definition.

ar:HB1243.title: TO INCREASE TRANSPARENCY REGARDING CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTIONS AND EXPENDITURES; TO AMEND CAMPAIGN FINANCE REPORTING AND PROTECT ELECTION INTEGRITY; AND TO AMEND PORTIONS OF INITIATED ACT 1 OF 1996.
ar:HB1243.summary: Changes campaign finance reporting for school district, township, municipal and county candidates: adds monthly reports in election years, sets the non-election-year annual report due December 31, and lets candidates with $500 to $5,000 in activity file only pre-election and final reports.

ar:HB1245.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS BEHAVIOR ANALYST REGISTRATION ACT.
ar:HB1245.summary: Creates the Arkansas Behavior Analyst Registration Act: only people registered with the Arkansas Psychology Board, with a fee up to $200 and Behavior Analyst Certification Board certification, may use the title registered behavior analyst; violations carry fines.

ar:HB1247.title: AN ACT FOR THE COSSATOT COMMUNITY COLLEGE OF THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1247.summary: Caps regular employees at 204 and appropriates up to $5,355,703 for state operations and $13,941,250 in cash funds for Cossatot Community College of the University of Arkansas in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1248.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY - MID-SOUTH APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1248.summary: Caps regular employees at 300 and appropriates up to $6,561,348 for state operations and $25,000,000 in cash funds for Arkansas State University - Mid-South in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1249.title: AN ACT FOR THE NATIONAL PARK COLLEGE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1249.summary: Caps regular employees at 380 and appropriates up to $12,046,523 for state operations and $21,420,000 in cash funds for National Park College in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1251.title: TO ESTABLISH THE ARKANSAS ANESTHESIOLOGIST ASSISTANT ACT; AND TO PROVIDE FOR LICENSURE OF ANESTHESIOLOGIST ASSISTANTS.
ar:HB1251.summary: Creates the Arkansas Anesthesiologist Assistant Act, with the State Medical Board licensing graduates of accredited programs who pass a national exam, to work under on-site supervision of an anesthesiologist under a protocol filed with the board.

ar:HB1252.title: TO ESTABLISH THE CERTIFIED COMMUNITY-BASED DOULA CERTIFICATION ACT; AND TO CERTIFY BIRTH AND POSTPARTUM DOULAS IN THIS STATE TO IMPROVE MATERNAL AND INFANT OUTCOMES.
ar:HB1252.summary: Creates a Department of Health certification for community-based doulas 18 or older holding an existing doula certification, with a $50 fee, valid two years, renewal needing ten training hours. Requires a public registry and Medicaid and health plan payment for certified doulas.

ar:HB1253.title: TO ADOPT THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES PERSONNEL LICENSURE INTERSTATE COMPACT IN ARKANSAS.
ar:HB1253.summary: Enters Arkansas into the Emergency Medical Services Personnel Licensure Interstate Compact (REPLICA), which gives EMTs, advanced EMTs and paramedics licensed in member states legal recognition to practice in Arkansas, and Arkansas-licensed EMS personnel to practice in other member states.

ar:HB1254.title: TO AUTHORIZE A LICENSED PSYCHOLOGICAL PRACTITIONER TO PRACTICE INDEPENDENTLY IN THIS STATE; AND TO REMOVE THE INDEPENDENT PRACTICE PRIVILEGES FROM PSYCHOLOGICAL EXAMINERS.
ar:HB1254.summary: Creates the licensed psychological practitioner, who may practice independently except in neuropsychological, forensic and projective personality assessment, sets its qualifications, removes independent practice from psychological examiners, and ends new examiner licenses after 2026.

ar:HB1255.title: TO AMEND THE COVERAGE OF A CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITOR IN THE ARKANSAS MEDICAID PROGRAM.
ar:HB1255.summary: Adds durable medical equipment providers as a way for Medicaid beneficiaries to get continuous glucose monitors, alongside pharmacies, and requires consistent approval rules and reimbursement to equipment providers of at least the Medicare rate.

ar:HB1256.title: TO REQUIRE THE ARKANSAS BOARD OF EXAMINERS IN COUNSELING TO ISSUE A PROVISIONAL LICENSE FOR A LICENSED ASSOCIATE COUNSELOR AND A LICENSED ASSOCIATE MARRIAGE AND FAMILY THERAPIST.
ar:HB1256.summary: Requires the Board of Examiners in Counseling to issue a one-year, non-renewable provisional license, with up to three exam attempts, to qualified applicants for licensed associate counselor and associate marriage and family therapist.

ar:HB1257.title: TO REMOVE THE LIMITATION OF THE PRACTICE OF NEUROPSYCHOLOGY FROM TECHNICIANS EMPLOYED BY PSYCHOLOGISTS; AND TO ALLOW PSYCHOLOGY TECHNICIANS TO BE EMPLOYED BY PSYCHOLOGISTS.
ar:HB1257.summary: Lets psychologists or healthcare facilities employ technicians for psychological, not only neuropsychological, testing under supervision; requires 80 hours of training, caps supervisors at four full-time technicians, and requires Medicaid and health plans to reimburse psychologists for technician-administered testing.

ar:HB1258.title: TO CREATE THE COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER ACT; AND TO ESTABLISH A STATEWIDE CERTIFICATION FOR COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS.
ar:HB1258.summary: Creates the Community Health Worker Act, under which the Department of Health certifies community health workers who are 18 or older and meet training or experience requirements, for a $50 application fee.

ar:HB1259.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AND THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE - ARKANSAS BIOSCIENCES INSTITUTES APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1259.summary: Appropriates $2,375,563 for the Arkansas Biosciences Institute and $2,415,432 for the Division of Agriculture's biosciences work from tobacco settlement funds in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1260.title: AN ACT FOR THE SOUTHERN ARKANSAS UNIVERSITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1260.summary: Caps regular employees at 529 and appropriates up to $20,691,358 for state operations and $55,732,048 in cash funds for Southern Arkansas University in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1261.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS TECH UNIVERSITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1261.summary: Appropriates up to $41,655,669 for state operations and $178,799,358 in cash funds for Arkansas Tech University in fiscal 2025-26. Also appropriates $2,004,769 for Arkansas Tech Institute.

ar:HB1262.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY - ARKANSAS BIOSCIENCES INSTITUTE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1262.summary: Caps Arkansas Biosciences Institute (Arkansas State University) staff at 43 and appropriates $5,643,838 from tobacco settlement funds for fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1263.title: TO CREATE THE OFFENSE OF UNLAWFUL REMOVAL OR FAILURE TO CHARGE AN ELECTRONIC MONITORING DEVICE.
ar:HB1263.summary: Makes it a crime for a person ordered to wear an electronic monitoring device as a condition of probation, parole or pretrial release to knowingly remove it or fail to charge it so that it cannot track them, with a defense for emergencies.

ar:HB1264.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS - FORT SMITH APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1264.summary: Appropriates up to $27,293,081 for state operations and $118,280,000 in cash funds for the University of Arkansas - Fort Smith in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1266.title: AN ACT FOR THE HENDERSON STATE UNIVERSITY APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1266.summary: Caps regular employees at 555 and appropriates up to $22,910,355 for state operations and $79,300,000 in cash funds for Henderson State University in fiscal 2025-26.

ar:HB1267.title: AN ACT FOR THE UAMS - REYNOLDS CENTER ON AGING, BOOZMAN COLLEGE OF PUBLIC HEALTH, ARK. BIOSCIENCES INSTITUTE, & THE AREA HEALTH ED. CENTER IN HELENA APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:HB1267.summary: Appropriates tobacco settlement funds for UAMS programs in fiscal 2025-26: Reynolds Center on Aging, Boozman College of Public Health, Arkansas Biosciences Institute, and the Helena area health education center.

ar:HB1268.title: TO ALLOW A PUBLIC TRANSIT AUTHORITY TO BECOME A PARTICIPATING PUBLIC EMPLOYER AND FOR ITS EMPLOYEES TO BECOME MEMBERS OF THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1268.summary: Allows a public transit authority to become a participating public employer in the Arkansas Public Employees' Retirement System, so its employees can become members.

ar:HB1272.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING PROPERTY VACATED BY A MUNICIPALITY; AND TO REQUIRE VESTED ABANDONED PROPERTY BE CONVEYED WITH THE ABUTTING REAL ESTATE.
ar:HB1272.summary: Provides that a conveyance of land abutting a street or alley a city abandoned includes the abandoned portion unless the owner expressly reserves it, amends plats to add it, and applies retroactively to abandonments after February 6, 1945.

ar:HB1273.title: TO PROVIDE THAT A LIEN CREATED BY THE ENTRY OF CERTIFICATE OF INDEBTEDNESS ISSUED BY THE SECRETARY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION IS NOT SUPERIOR TO A PURCHASE MONEY MORTGAGE.
ar:HB1273.summary: Provides that the state lien created by a Department of Finance and Administration certificate of indebtedness is not superior to a purchase money mortgage.

ar:HB1274.title: TO ALLOW A TITLE INSURANCE AGENT, TITLE INSURER, OR TITLE COMPANY TO PAY REAL PROPERTY TAXES IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE ISSUANCE OF A TITLE.
ar:HB1274.summary: Requires county collectors to answer a title or closing agent's request for real estate and delinquent personal property tax owed within three business days; if they fail, they must accept the real estate tax payment without requiring the personal property taxes.

ar:HB1275.title: TO PROHIBIT PRIOR AUTHORIZATIONS FOR HEALTHCARE SERVICES PROVIDED FOR TREATMENT OF A MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS.
ar:HB1275.summary: Bars health benefit plans from requiring prior authorization or precertification for healthcare services given to a person in a mental health crisis, including at crisis stabilization units and emergency departments.

ar:HB1276.title: CONCERNING SPOUSAL RETIREMENT BENEFITS FOR SPOUSES OF CERTAIN MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEES.
ar:HB1276.summary: Lets certain cities, at their option, pay a surviving spouse married ten or more years half the retirement benefit of a deceased city attorney, deputy city clerk, mayor or treasurer who was retired or eligible to retire; payment ends on remarriage.

ar:HB1277.title: TO AMEND PAYMENTS FOR CORRECTIVE ACTION REGARDING PETROLEUM STORAGE TANKS.
ar:HB1277.summary: Replaces the fixed $7,500 deductible tank owners or operators must spend before Petroleum Storage Tank Trust Fund corrective-action payments with one set by rule, up to $30,000, with higher deductibles for rule violations, and removes the payment-denial provision for unreported releases.

ar:HB1278.title: TO REQUIRE SURVEYORS TO TAKE CERTAIN ACTIONS BEFORE ENTERING ONTO A COMMERCIAL POULTRY FARM.
ar:HB1278.summary: Requires surveyors to notify the owner and follow the farm's visitor and biosecurity protocols before entering a commercial poultry farm, defined as having poultry houses over 5,000 square feet.

ar:HB1279.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS EGG MARKETING ACT OF 1969; AND TO AUTHORIZE REPACKAGING OF EGGS BY A RETAILER IF CERTAIN CRITERIA IS MET.
ar:HB1279.summary: Allows retailers to replace missing or broken eggs in a carton with eggs from the same packer, brand, grade, size and expiration or lot code that are visibly clean.

ar:HB1282.title: CONCERNING THE UNAUTHORIZED PRACTICE OF LAW.
ar:HB1282.summary: Changes the unauthorized practice of law offense in personal injury and property damage matters so it applies to acting for any economic benefit, rather than only a direct economic benefit.

ar:HB1283.title: TO REQUIRE THE DIVISION OF ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION TO INCLUDE DIGITAL MEDIA STANDARDS IN KINDERGARTEN THROUGH GRADE TWELVE LIBRARY MEDIA STANDARDS.
ar:HB1283.summary: Requires the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education, by the 2026-27 school year, to add digital media standards to the K-12 library media standards, covering digital citizenship, digital wellness, internet safety, social media literacy and proper use of artificial intelligence.

ar:HB1285.title: TO ESTABLISH AN EXEMPTION PROGRAM FOR AMBULANCE SERVICE'S OPERATORS FOR CERTAIN HEALTHCARE SERVICES.
ar:HB1285.summary: Directs the Emergency Medical Services Advisory Council to set 911 emergency protocols exempt from the requirement that ambulance crews consult by telemedicine before treating in place or transporting a patient to an alternative destination.

ar:HB1286.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS TRIAGE, TREAT, AND TRANSPORT TO ALTERNATIVE DESTINATION ACT.
ar:HB1286.summary: Removes the January 1, 2024 start date from the requirement that health insurers cover ambulance treatment in place and triage or transport to alternative destinations coordinated through telemedicine, and rewords coverage when an enrollee declines transport against medical advice.

ar:HB1287.title: TO AMEND THE HEALTHCARE CONTRACTING SIMPLIFICATION ACT; TO DEFINE "DOWNCODE" UNDER THE HEALTHCARE CONTRACTING SIMPLIFICATION ACT; AND TO REQUIRE NOTIFICATION BY CONTRACTING ENTITIES OF DOWNCODING.
ar:HB1287.summary: Defines "downcode" as changing a healthcare claim to a lower-cost service than billed, and requires a contracting entity to notify the provider within 30 days of processing a claim it downcodes.

ar:HB1288.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS HEALTH CARE CONSUMER ACT; AND TO REQUIRE A HEALTHCARE INSURER TO MAKE CERTAIN RETROACTIVE PAYMENTS TO A PROVIDER UPON CREDENTIALING OF A PROVIDER.
ar:HB1288.summary: Defines the date from which a health insurer treats an approved applicant physician as participating for payment as the date it receives the physician's credentialing information from the State Medical Board's verification service; exempts Arkansas Medicaid.

ar:HB1290.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR MENTAL HEALTH WELLNESS EXAMINATIONS; AND TO ESTABLISH THE ARKANSAS SUPPORT OF MENTAL HEALTH WELLNESS EXAMINATIONS ACT.
ar:HB1290.summary: Requires health plans, starting January 1, 2026, to cover one annual standalone mental health wellness exam by a licensed mental health professional, generally with no deductible, copayment or coinsurance.

ar:HB1291.title: TO EXCLUDE CERTAIN MINOR LEAGUE BASEBALL PLAYERS FROM THE DEFINITION OF "EMPLOYEE" UNDER THE MINIMUM WAGE ACT OF THE STATE OF ARKANSAS IMPACTING THE LAW RESULTING FROM INITIATED ACT 5 OF 2018.
ar:HB1291.summary: Excludes minor league baseball players paid under a collective bargaining agreement from the definition of "employee" in the state Minimum Wage Act.

ar:HB1292.title: TO AMEND THE RESIDENCY REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ADOPTION OF A MINOR.
ar:HB1292.summary: Changes adoption residency rules: for children in Department of Human Services custody, adds exemptions for infants under six months and a director waiver for youth 16 or older in life-skills or vocational programs. For others, six months run from licensed-agency placement or petition filing.

ar:HB1293.title: TO INCREASE THE PAYMENT OF A CLAIM TO DESIGNATED BENEFICIARIES OR SURVIVORS OF CERTAIN PUBLIC EMPLOYEES KILLED IN THE LINE OF DUTY.
ar:HB1293.summary: Raises the state's additional death payment for public employees killed in the line of duty, including firefighters who die of certain cancers, from $150,000 to $250,000, and adds state highway employees to those covered.

ar:HB1296.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR HEALTHCARE SERVICES PROVIDED IN MOBILE UNITS.
ar:HB1296.summary: Requires health insurers to cover services delivered in mobile health units that they cover elsewhere, with cost sharing no less favorable than at other places of service.

ar:HB1298.title: TO MODIFY PAYMENT OF BENEFITS FOR CERTAIN HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS UNDER A HEALTH BENEFIT PLAN.
ar:HB1298.summary: Requires health insurers, including Medicaid, to pay out-of-network claims for hospital, nursing, medical or surgical services directly to the provider who gave the service, and extends payment-of-benefits rules to health benefit plans.

ar:HB1300.title: TO AMEND THE PRIOR AUTHORIZATION TRANSPARENCY ACT.
ar:HB1300.summary: Broadens the definition of prior authorization, requires utilization review entities' online lists of services needing it to be machine-readable with billing codes, adds fines for violations, and creates a trust fund from the fines.

ar:HB1301.title: TO AMEND THE PRIOR AUTHORIZATION TRANSPARENCY ACT.
ar:HB1301.summary: Revises the "gold card" prior-authorization rules: insurers must extend exemptions to providers sharing a tax ID if either party elects, give 30 days' notice (up from 25) before rescinding one, and allow at least 60 days (up from 30) for records.

ar:HB1303.title: TO CREATE THE SUSTAINABLE AVIATION FUEL INCENTIVE ACT; AND TO CREATE AN INCOME TAX CREDIT RELATED TO SUSTAINABLE AVIATION FUEL.
ar:HB1303.summary: Creates an income tax credit of 30% of equipment costs for a wood-based sustainable aviation fuel manufacturer that invests over $2 billion in a facility employing 75 or more people and starts construction by December 31, 2027.

ar:HB1307.title: TO ENSURE RESPONSIBLE FUND MANAGEMENT; AND TO AMEND THE UNIFORM PRUDENT MANAGEMENT OF INSTITUTIONAL FUNDS ACT (2006).
ar:HB1307.summary: Bars government institutions, including public colleges, from considering or directing service providers toward certain goals when managing charitable funds: emissions cuts, board or hiring targets by protected characteristic, abortion or gender-reassignment access, and firearm limits. Exempts pre-2024 donor intent.

ar:HB1309.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING COVERAGE OF EXAMINATIONS FOR BREAST CANCER; AND TO CLARIFY THE COST-SHARING REQUIREMENTS FOR EXAMINATIONS FOR BREAST CANCER.
ar:HB1309.summary: Bars health benefit plans from imposing any cost-sharing, not only copayments or deductibles, on screening mammograms and breast ultrasounds, even for services on different dates or several on one date. Removes the January 1, 1990 date from the rule on unaccredited facilities.

ar:HB1310.title: TO AMEND THE NEWBORN UMBILICAL CORD BLOOD INITIATIVE ACT; TO ABOLISH THE ARKANSAS COMMISSION FOR THE NEWBORN UMBILICAL CORD BLOOD INITIATIVE; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1310.summary: Abolishes the Commission for the Newborn Umbilical Cord Blood Initiative, transfers its duties and funds to UAMS, and makes UAMS responsible for maintaining the Newborn Umbilical Cord Blood Bank.

ar:HB1311.title: TO DIRECT THE LEGISLATIVE AUDITOR TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM FOR APPROPRIATED FUNDS OF CITIES OF THE SECOND CLASS AND INCORPORATED TOWNS.
ar:HB1311.summary: Directs the Legislative Auditor to develop a uniform chart of accounts for cities of the second class and incorporated towns, and to complete a process for phasing in its use within 36 months of the act taking effect.

ar:HB1312.title: TO AMEND PUBLIC SCHOOL FUNDING AMOUNTS UNDER THE PUBLIC SCHOOL FUNDING ACT OF 2003.
ar:HB1312.summary: Sets per-student foundation funding at $8,162 for 2025-26 and $8,037 from 2026-27, with the $333 employer insurance contribution paid directly to the Employee Benefits Division; also changes alternative-learning, English-learner, enhanced-achievement and teacher-salary-equalization amounts.

ar:HB1313.title: TO EXPAND HEALTH BENEFIT COVERAGE FOR CERTAIN FIREFIGHTER RETIREES OF MUNICIPALITIES AND COUNTIES.
ar:HB1313.summary: Extends to retired firefighters the right, now given to retired police officers, to join their municipal or county health plan until Medicare eligibility, with a 60-day guaranteed enrollment window after retirement.

ar:HB1314.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING CERTAIN AUDITS OF HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS; AND TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS MEDICAL AUDIT BILL OF RIGHTS ACT.
ar:HB1314.summary: Creates the Arkansas Medical Audit Bill of Rights Act, setting rules for insurer and payor audits of healthcare providers: one week's notice, same-specialty review of clinical judgments, claim limits, no more than two audits a year, no extrapolation, and 60 days to respond.

ar:HB1315.title: TO AUTHORIZE A BLOOD TYPE DESIGNATION TO BE PLACED ON A DRIVER'S LICENSE OR IDENTIFICATION CARD.
ar:HB1315.summary: Lets a person, or a parent or guardian, request a blood type designation on a driver's license or ID card by submitting a signed form and the usual fee. The applicant is responsible for the accuracy of the information.

ar:HB1316.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR LUNG CANCER SCREENINGS.
ar:HB1316.summary: Requires health plans, starting January 1, 2026, to cover lung cancer screenings and follow-up care per American Cancer Society guidelines, not subject to the annual deductible, copayment or coinsurance limits set for other benefits.

ar:HB1317.title: TO AMEND LAWS CONCERNING FRAUD AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT TO INCLUDE FRAUD AGAINST A STATE SUPPORTED RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1317.summary: Makes false statements or falsified records meant to defraud state-supported retirement systems, including the judicial system, a Class D felony (previously a misdemeanor for two systems), and lets a system’s executive director refer cases to the Attorney General or Sixth Judicial District prosecutor.

ar:HB1318.title: TO AMEND THE EXCURSION TRAIN PERMIT TO INCLUDE EXCURSION BOATS.
ar:HB1318.summary: Lets operators of excursion boats, as well as excursion trains, apply to the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division for a permit to sell and serve alcoholic beverages on scheduled, fixed-route trips.

ar:HB1321.title: TO REGULATE STEP THERAPY AND FAIL FIRST PROTOCOLS CONCERNING CERTAIN PRESCRIBED VENTILATORS.
ar:HB1321.summary: Bars health insurers from requiring step therapy or fail-first protocols for a prescribed noninvasive ventilator in certain cases, and requires Medicaid managed care plans to pay at least 100% of the Medicaid fee schedule for ventilators.

ar:HB1322.title: TO AMEND THE LAWS UNDER THE ARKANSAS LOCAL POLICE AND FIRE RETIREMENT SYSTEM CONCERNING LINE-OF-DUTY DEATH FROM OCCUPATIONAL CANCER; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1322.summary: Includes specified cancers diagnosed while on duty among the diseases that qualify an active Local Police and Fire Retirement System member's death for line-of-duty survivor benefits; the finding can be rebutted by a preponderance of the evidence.

ar:HB1324.title: TO AMEND THE TIME OF PERMISSIBLE SALES OF FIREWORKS IN THIS STATE.
ar:HB1324.summary: Moves the start of the summer retail fireworks sales period from June 20 to June 13; sales still run through July 10 and from December 10 through January 5.

ar:HB1325.title: TO ALLOW A MEMBER OF THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM TO RECEIVE SERVICE CREDIT FROM SERVICE UNDER AN ALTERNATE RETIREMENT PLAN TO MEET ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS.
ar:HB1325.summary: Lets a public employees' retirement system member count years in a prior alternate retirement plan toward benefit eligibility, if never vested or paid out from that plan and the system verifies documentation.

ar:HB1326.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING SPECIAL ALLOWANCES TO ENCOURAGE EARLY RETIREMENT AND MANAGE EARLY RETIREMENT WINDOW INCENTIVES FOR EMPLOYEES OF INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1326.summary: Extends early-retirement special allowances at public colleges and universities to staff as well as faculty, ends the tenured/nontenured distinction and the 5% payroll cap, and replaces the age-55 or Civil Service test with eligibility under any state-sponsored retirement program.

ar:HB1327.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ELIGIBILITY OF CERTAIN RETIRED EMPLOYEES UNDER THE STATE AND PUBLIC SCHOOL LIFE AND HEALTH INSURANCE PROGRAM.
ar:HB1327.summary: Changes retiree eligibility for the State and Public School Life and Health Insurance Program: requires vested rather than participating membership in a listed retirement system, replaces "drawing benefits" with retired "as determined by" that system, and makes five-year coverage rules yield to federal law.

ar:HB1332.title: TO REQUIRE THE ARKANSAS MEDICAID PROGRAM TO EVALUATE CLAIMS FOR DIAGNOSES FREQUENCY OF OBESITY-RELATED CONDITIONS AND PRESENT THE COSTS.
ar:HB1332.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to report Medicaid claims data and costs for obesity-related conditions to legislative committees, and requires health plans to let policyholders buy optional coverage for FDA-approved anti-obesity medications.

ar:HB1333.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR BREASTFEEDING AND LACTATION CONSULTANT SERVICES.
ar:HB1333.summary: Requires health plans, from January 1, 2026, including Medicaid, ARKids First and the Health and Opportunity for Me program, to cover outpatient breastfeeding and lactation consultant services with no deductible, copay or coinsurance, and requires Medicaid to reimburse qualifying lactation consultants.

ar:HB1336.title: TO AMEND THE SURVIVORS' BENEFIT OPTIONS UNDER THE STATE POLICE RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO AMEND THE PROVISIONS CONCERNING THE TIER TWO DEFERRED RETIREMENT OPTION PLAN UNDER THE STATE POLICE RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1336.summary: Raises the State Police Tier Two DROP contribution from 72% to 100% of the monthly retirement benefit, and raises the fee for a copy of a basic accident report from $10 to $25 (still $10 for people involved).

ar:HB1341.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING BENEFITS UNDER THE ARKANSAS LOCAL POLICE AND FIRE RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF "PAY" UNDER THE ARKANSAS LOCAL POLICE AND FIRE RETIREMENT SYSTEM.
ar:HB1341.summary: Lets active Local Police and Fire Retirement System members receiving temporary workers' compensation remit it to their employer so full pay is reported, capped at pay they would have earned, and updates the Internal Revenue Code limit date to January 1, 2025.

ar:HB1344.title: CONCERNING ADMINISTRATION OF THE ARKANSAS TEACHER RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO CORRECT THE NAME OF THE ARKANSAS SCHOOL FOR THE BLIND AND THE ARKANSAS SCHOOL FOR THE DEAF UNDER TITLE 24 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE.
ar:HB1344.summary: Updates Teacher Retirement System provisions to call the Schools for the Blind and Deaf "former" and add the Arkansas School for the Deaf and Blind; takes effect only if HB1810, merging the schools, is enacted.

ar:HB1348.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING SURVIVOR BENEFITS FOR THE DEPENDENT CHILD OF A MEMBER OF THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT SYSTEM OR A MEMBER OF THE STATE POLICE RETIREMENT SYSTEM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1348.summary: As introduced, raises to 23, from 18 (or 23 only for full-time students), the age limit for a deceased member's or retiree's child to receive a survivor annuity from the public employees' or State Police retirement systems.

ar:HB1352.title: TO AMEND VARIOUS LAWS CONCERNING ACTIONS RELATED TO CERTAIN FOREIGN ENTITIES.
ar:HB1352.summary: Withholds state funding from public colleges that host a Confucius Institute, bars them from investing in Chinese companies, and prohibits cities from forming or keeping sister-city ties with parties from countries under U.S. arms-trade restrictions.

ar:HB1353.title: TO REGULATE A VISION BENEFIT MANAGER; TO AMEND THE VISION CARE PLAN ACT OF 2015; TO AMEND THE HEALTHCARE CONTRACTING SIMPLIFICATION ACT.
ar:HB1353.summary: As introduced, bars insurers and vision benefit managers from paying vision providers less than the Medicare rate for covered services, steering enrollees to particular providers or affiliated retailers, and using extrapolation in provider audits.

ar:HB1355.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 5 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING CRIMINAL OFFENSES.
ar:HB1355.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 5 of the Arkansas Code (criminal offenses), clarifying references in provisions on fines, seized property, death by delivery and gang-used premises. The bill states it makes only technical, not substantive, changes.

ar:HB1356.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 12 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING LAW ENFORCEMENT, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND MILITARY AFFAIRS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
ar:HB1356.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 12 of the Arkansas Code (law enforcement and emergency management), adding clarifying language and fixing references in provisions such as sex offender records and the Child Maltreatment Act. The bill states the changes are technical, not substantive.

ar:HB1357.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 16 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING PRACTICE, PROCEDURE, AND COURTS.
ar:HB1357.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 16 of the Arkansas Code (practice, procedure and courts), including parole and post-release supervision provisions and repeal of an obsolete definition. The bill states it makes only technical, not substantive, changes.

ar:HB1358.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 18 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING PROPERTY.
ar:HB1358.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 18 of the Arkansas Code (property), updating provisions on land ownership by foreign-party-controlled businesses and related definitions. The bill states it makes only technical, not substantive, changes.

ar:HB1359.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 19 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING PUBLIC FINANCE.
ar:HB1359.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 19 of the Arkansas Code (public finance), repealing obsolete language on cash fund exemptions and the State Insurance Department Trust Fund. The bill states it makes only technical, not substantive, changes.

ar:HB1360.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 20 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING PUBLIC HEALTH AND WELFARE.
ar:HB1360.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 20 of the Arkansas Code (public health and welfare), including school building egress and hemp-derived product permit provisions. The bill states it makes only technical, not substantive, changes.

ar:HB1361.title: TO MAKE TECHNICAL CORRECTIONS TO TITLE 23 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING PUBLIC UTILITIES AND REGULATED INDUSTRIES.
ar:HB1361.summary: Makes technical corrections to Title 23 of the Arkansas Code (public utilities and regulated industries), including money services, insurance and health insurance marketplace provisions, and repeals an expired subchapter. The bill states the changes are technical, not substantive.
