ar:HB1666.summary: Makes the Arkansas cyber response program secondary to any insurance a county, city or school district has, repeals its coverage of damages from civil-rights violations and officials' tortious conduct, and eliminates the cyber response panel.

ar:HB1671.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE GROSS RECEIPTS TAX; AND TO CREATE A GENERAL SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION FOR SALES TO QUALIFIED NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS.
ar:HB1671.summary: Exempts from state sales and use tax purchases by qualifying 501(c)(3) nonprofits with annual budgets under $200,000 that provide charitable community services, excluding items such as vehicles, boats, computers, appliances, phones, televisions and alcohol; nonprofits must apply to the revenue department.

ar:HB1672.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE TO CREATE A MORE EFFICIENT SYSTEM FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS OF INNOVATION IN ARKANSAS.
ar:HB1672.summary: Repeals the district of innovation program, treats former schools of innovation as conversion charter schools that keep their waivers through the current approval cycle, and sets waiver end dates for existing conversion charter schools by their 2022-23 letter grades.

ar:HB1673.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING BARBERS.
ar:HB1673.summary: Revises barber licensing law, including removing the notarization and Social Security card application requirements, changing reciprocity terms for barbers licensed elsewhere, and adjusting barber school and college rules.

ar:HB1677.title: TO AUTHORIZE ALCOHOL AND DRUG ABUSE TREATMENT PROGRAMS TO MAINTAIN EMERGENCY MEDICATION KITS.
ar:HB1677.summary: Allows alcohol and drug abuse treatment programs with medical staff to keep an emergency medication kit supplied by one designated licensed pharmacy, stored locked and given only by licensed medical personnel on a physician or APRN order.

ar:HB1679.title: TO AMEND THE REVISED ARKANSAS ANATOMICAL GIFT ACT; TO ALLOW CERTAIN CLASSES OF PERSONS TO REVOKE OR AMEND AN ANATOMICAL GIFT UPON THE DEATH OF THE DONOR; AND TO REQUIRE CERTAIN REPORTING OF PROCUREMENT ORGANIZATIONS.
ar:HB1679.summary: Allows an agent under a health care power of attorney, or family members in a set order of priority, to modify or revoke an incapacitated or deceased donor's anatomical gift, and requires private procurement organizations to report to the Legislative Council.

ar:HB1680.title: TO PREVENT A FOREIGN-PARTY-CONTROLLED BUSINESS FROM LEASING LAND; AND TO PROHIBIT A PROHIBITED FOREIGN PARTY FROM HOLDING AN INTEREST IN REAL PROPERTY OR AGRICULTURAL LAND IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1680.summary: Bars foreign-party-controlled businesses from leasing land in Arkansas, bars prohibited foreign parties from holding agricultural land within ten miles of critical infrastructure, and shortens the divestment deadline from two years to one.

ar:HB1681.title: TO ESTABLISH THE WATER AND SEWER TREATMENT FACILITIES GRANT PROGRAM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1681.summary: Creates a matching grant program for shovel-ready water and sewer treatment projects, with 80% of funds for larger systems and 20% for those serving 1,200 or fewer people, expiring after five years.

ar:HB1682.title: TO CREATE THE GOOD NEIGHBOR ACT; AND TO CLARIFY FOOD DONATION LIABILITY AND IMMUNITY.
ar:HB1682.summary: Replaces the food-donor liability law with the "Arkansas Good Neighbor Act": donors, gleaners and recipient churches or nonprofits acting in good faith and disclosing the food's condition are not liable, except for gross negligence, recklessness or intentional misconduct.

ar:HB1683.title: TO PROHIBIT THE PROCUREMENT BY A GOVERNMENTAL ENTITY OF AN ELECTRIC VEHICLE OR A COMPONENT OF AN ELECTRIC VEHICLE THAT WAS MANUFACTURED IN WHOLE OR IN PART USING FORCED LABOR.
ar:HB1683.summary: Bars governmental entities from contracting to buy electric vehicles or components unless the manufacturer certifies under oath that no forced labor was used in production, with civil penalties for knowingly false certifications.

ar:HB1685.title: TO CREATE THE GROCERY TAX RELIEF ACT; TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE SALES AND USE TAXES LEVIED ON FOOD AND FOOD INGREDIENTS, AS AFFIRMED BY REFERRED ACT 19 OF 1958; AND TO EXEMPT GROCERIES FROM STATE SALES AND USE TAXES.
ar:HB1685.summary: Creates the Grocery Tax Relief Act, exempting food and food ingredients from state sales and use taxes while leaving city and county taxes on them in place.

ar:HB1686.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING LICENSES TO CARRY CONCEALED HANDGUNS.
ar:HB1686.summary: Changes concealed handgun license law: an arresting officer notifies the State Police director instead of confiscating the license, lost and duplicate license provisions are removed, and licensees carry and display the electronic license rather than a paper one.

ar:HB1688.title: TO AMEND ARKANSAS LAW CONCERNING THE USE OF A DEALER'S EXTRA LICENSE PLATE.
ar:HB1688.summary: Adds community events such as parades and car shows, and manufacturer dealership-agreement compliance, to permitted uses of dealer extra license plates; lets owners and officers use them; exempts use of plated vehicles held for sale from gross receipts and compensating use taxes.

ar:HB1689.title: TO REQUIRE A PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOL TO GRANT ACCESS TO ITS FACILITIES TO MILITARY RECRUITERS; AND TO REQUIRE CERTAIN STATE-SUPPORTED POSTSECONDARY INSTITUTIONS TO GRANT ACCESS TO ITS FACILITIES TO MILITARY RECRUITERS.
ar:HB1689.summary: Requires public high schools to give military recruiters access to students in grades 10-12 on the same basis as employers and colleges, with no extra privacy, administrative or parental consent barriers.

ar:HB1690.title: TO TRANSFER THE NUCLEAR PLANNING AND RESPONSE PROGRAM FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO THE DIVISION OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1690.summary: Transfers the Nuclear Planning and Response Program from the Department of Health to the Division of Emergency Management in the Department of Public Safety on July 1, 2025, with its authority, staff, property, funds and existing rules.

ar:HB1691.title: TO PROVIDE FOR CERTAIN PROPERTY TO BE EXEMPT FROM TAXATION; AND TO PROVIDE THAT CERTAIN MOTOR VEHICLES USED EXCLUSIVELY FOR PUBLIC CHARITY ARE EXEMPT FROM PERSONAL PROPERTY TAX.
ar:HB1691.summary: Exempts from personal property tax motor vehicles used exclusively for public charity that are leased at least 12 months by a public charity institution, for assessment years beginning January 1, 2026.

ar:HB1692.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING POLYGRAPH EXAMINERS AND VOICE STRESS ANALYSIS EXAMINERS; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING PRIVATE INVESTIGATORS AND PRIVATE SECURITY AGENCIES.
ar:HB1692.summary: Removes crimes of moral turpitude from the offenses that can bar or end polygraph, voice stress, private investigator and security licenses, repeals police notice on security officer commission applications, and allows electronic commission ID cards.

ar:HB1693.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING DAMAGED OR DEFECTIVE BALLOTS; AND TO ALLOW THE STATE BOARD OF ELECTION COMMISSIONERS TO PROMULGATE RULES REGARDING THE DUPLICATION OF DAMAGED OR DEFECTIVE BALLOTS.
ar:HB1693.summary: Removes the central-counting-facility and manual-count provisions for duplicating damaged ballots, directs the State Board of Election Commissioners to write rules on duplication, and adds the number of ballots awaiting duplication to preliminary election-night results.

ar:HB1694.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING ALTERNATIVES TO ELECTRONIC FILING FOR CAMPAIGN FINANCE REPORTS.
ar:HB1694.summary: As introduced, repeals the option for candidates to file campaign contribution and expenditure reports on paper, including the notarized-affidavit requirement, so reports must be filed electronically.

ar:HB1695.title: TO CLARIFY THE FORECLOSURE PROCESS FOR PROPERTY SUBJECT TO A MUNICIPAL LIEN; TO ALLOW A MUNICIPALITY TO PETITION TO SET ASIDE THE SALE OF PROPERTY TO CERTAIN PERSONS; AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE PRIORITY OF UNRECORDED MUNICIPAL LIENS.
ar:HB1695.summary: Raises the caps on cleanup costs a city's lien can take priority for (for example $2,000 for mowing and $30,000 for environmental cleanup), requires liens to be filed with the county recorder, and lets cities petition courts to sell neglected properties at a public sale.

ar:HB1696.title: TO ESTABLISH THE STRENGTHENING ARKANSAS EDUCATION ACT; AND TO PROVIDE A CORE CURRICULUM AT STATE-SUPPORTED INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION.
ar:HB1696.summary: Creates a 15-credit-hour core of introductory survey courses (communication, critical thinking, American history and government) for state-supported colleges starting fall 2027, and repeals the existing baccalaureate American history or civil government course requirement.

ar:HB1697.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF TITLE 6 AND TITLE 19 OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING PROVISIONAL POSITIONS AND MOTOR VEHICLE RESTRICTIONS FOR STATE-SUPPORTED INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1697.summary: Raises the cap on new or additional positions at ASU-Jonesboro, Northwest Arkansas Community College, UA Fayetteville and UA Pine Bluff, and raises motor vehicle limits at five higher-education institutions, effective July 1, 2025.

ar:HB1700.title: TO AMEND THE PRIOR AUTHORIZATION TRANSPARENCY ACT; AND TO CLARIFY THE PROCESS OF AN ADVERSE DETERMINATION NOTICE UNDER THE PRIOR AUTHORIZATION TRANSPARENCY ACT.
ar:HB1700.summary: Changes adverse-determination notices to give providers a physician's phone number rather than name, requires the physician to disclose name and license on contact, adds a subscriber notice, and deems prior authorization approved if a provider sends the Insurance Department a violation recording.

ar:HB1701.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING SEWER COLLECTION AND SEWER TREATMENT PROVIDERS AND RELATED SERVICES.
ar:HB1701.summary: Requires sewer and wastewater providers to obtain rate studies every five years, starting 2028 to 2030 by customer count, and set rates covering operating and capital costs; defines fiscal distress, with improvement plans and board training.

ar:HB1703.title: TO PROVIDE A DRUG REIMBURSEMENT PROCESS FOR CERTAIN HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS.
ar:HB1703.summary: Requires insurers and contracting entities to offer healthcare providers an appeal to challenge drug reimbursement below their acquisition cost, and, if upheld, to raise payment to at least 110% of acquisition cost within 30 business days and reprocess claims.

ar:HB1704.title: TO AMEND THE LAW REGARDING CHILD CUSTODY IN MATTERS WHERE A PARENT IS A FIRST RESPONDER.
ar:HB1704.summary: Applies to parents who are first responders (firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, law enforcement) the custody rules for mobilized military parents: courts may not permanently change custody or visitation based solely on work schedule, and decide any temporary modification.

ar:HB1705.title: TO REQUIRE INFORMATION CONCERNING HOW THE RELIGIOUS AND MORAL BELIEFS OF THE FOUNDING FATHERS INFLUENCED THE FOUNDING OF THE UNITED STATES TO BE EMBEDDED INTO EXISTING SOCIAL STUDIES STANDARDS.
ar:HB1705.summary: Requires the State Board of Education, starting 2026-27, to add to grade 6-12 social studies instruction on the founding fathers' religious and moral beliefs and how they influenced the founding documents, including the Declaration of Independence preamble.

ar:HB1706.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING ELECTIONS; AND TO PROHIBIT RANKED CHOICE VOTING.
ar:HB1706.summary: Bans ranked choice voting in any local, state or federal election or nomination in Arkansas, voids conflicting local ordinances, and exempts military and overseas absentee voters.

ar:HB1707.title: TO REQUIRE CERTAIN CANDIDATES TO FILE REPORTS WITH THE SECRETARY OF STATE; TO AMEND PORTIONS OF INITIATED ACT 1 OF 1996; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1707.summary: Requires candidates for school district, township, municipal and county offices to file campaign finance reports electronically with the Secretary of State instead of the county clerk. The Secretary keeps them eight years, then sends them to State Archives, and offers an online search.

ar:HB1712.title: TO ESTABLISH THE SOCIAL WORK LICENSURE COMPACT IN THIS STATE.
ar:HB1712.summary: Enacts the Social Work Licensure Compact in Arkansas, letting licensed social workers in member states practice in Arkansas under a multistate privilege without a separate license, while keeping state licensing authority.

ar:HB1713.title: TO REQUIRE BALLOT TITLES FOR INITIATED MEASURES TO BE AT OR UNDER A CERTAIN READING LEVEL; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1713.summary: Bars the Attorney General from certifying a proposed ballot title for an initiative or referendum petition if it reads above an eighth-grade level on the Flesch-Kincaid formula. Does not apply to titles the Attorney General already certified before the act takes effect.

ar:HB1714.title: TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF PAID CANVASSER.
ar:HB1714.summary: As introduced, expands the definition of paid canvasser for local option, initiative and referendum petitions to include anyone who receives an item of value (listed examples include food, lodging, travel, bonuses and gift cards) before or after a signature is solicited.

ar:HB1716.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ASSESSMENT AND COLLECTION OF TAXES BY THE SECRETARY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION; AND TO PROHIBIT THE ASSESSMENT OF SALES AND USE TAX IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1716.summary: Bars the state from assessing sales or use tax on the same item for a taxpayer who already won a ruling that the purchase was exempt and uses it the same way, unless a later law, rule or Supreme Court decision materially changes the exemption.

ar:HB1717.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS CHILDREN AND TEENS' ONLINE PRIVACY PROTECTION ACT.
ar:HB1717.summary: Requires operators of websites and apps directed at, or knowingly collecting data from, children 12 and under or teens 13 to 16 to give notice, obtain teen consent, and limit targeted advertising and data collection; the Attorney General enforces, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:HB1719.title: TO AMEND THE DAYS INCLUDED IN THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MATERNITY LEAVE DAYS APPROVED BY A SCHOOL THAT OFFERS MATERNITY LEAVE.
ar:HB1719.summary: Excludes school holidays and other non-class days from the days counted against a school's approved maternity leave, and treats leave days falling on unpaid contract days as paid maternity leave.

ar:HB1721.title: TO AMEND SECTIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE TO PROHIBIT GREYHOUND RACING AND SIMULCASTING OF GREYHOUND RACING.
ar:HB1721.summary: Starting January 1, 2028, bars horse racing franchise holders, greyhound racing franchise holders and casino licensees from conducting greyhound racing or accepting live or simulcast wagers on it, and removes greyhound racing from pari-mutuel wagering law.

ar:HB1724.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS OF DIRECTORS AND SCHOOL BOARD ELECTIONS; AND TO AMEND THE DATE ON WHICH AN ELECTION OF A SCHOOL DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS IS HELD.
ar:HB1724.summary: Sets school board terms at four or six years instead of three to five, staggers them so equal numbers are elected each cycle, moves school board elections to the preferential primary date, revises vacancy filling, and ends district election-date policies.

ar:HB1725.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF SHERIFF; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING COMPENSATION FOR THE OFFICE OF SHERIFF.
ar:HB1725.summary: Requires a newly elected or appointed sheriff to document with the county clerk within 10 days whether he or she has law enforcement training or eligibility. Without it, the quorum court must set the sheriff's salary at the statutory minimum.

ar:HB1726.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS KIDS ONLINE SAFETY ACT.
ar:HB1726.summary: Creates the Arkansas Kids Online Safety Act, requiring online platforms aimed at users 16 or younger to take reasonable measures against listed harms to minors and give minors and parents tools to limit contact, restrict personal data, limit autoplay and rewards, and control recommendations.

ar:HB1728.title: TO REQUIRE REPORTING ON THE NUMBER OF STUDENTS RECEIVING ACCOMMODATIONS FOR A DISABILITY AT INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION.
ar:HB1728.summary: Requires colleges that receive federal student aid to report annually to the Division of Higher Education the number of students registered to receive disability accommodations, with related data on undergraduates.

ar:HB1729.title: TO AMEND THE HOMESTEAD EXEMPTION ACT; AND TO PROVIDE THAT A HOMESTEAD OWNED BY A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY IS ELIGIBLE FOR THE HOMESTEAD EXEMPTION IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1729.summary: Lets a member of a limited liability company claim the homestead exemption for a home the LLC owns if its members are a married couple, or its sole member is a married person or head of a family.

ar:HB1730.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ISSUANCE AND TRANSFER OF WHOLESALE PERMITS.
ar:HB1730.summary: Allows new alcohol wholesaler permits to be issued on or after July 1, 2026, and new minimum wholesaler permits on or after the act's effective date, replacing the ban on new permits issued after September 1, 2013.

ar:HB1732.title: TO INCREASE THE AMOUNT OF THE INCOME TAX DEDUCTION ALLOWED FOR A TEACHER'S CLASSROOM INVESTMENT.
ar:HB1732.summary: Doubles the maximum income tax deduction for a teacher's classroom investment from $500 to $1,000 per taxpayer, or from $1,000 to $2,000 for joint filers who are both teachers, starting tax year 2025.

ar:HB1733.title: TO AMEND VARIOUS PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING THE ARKANSAS BETTER CHANCE PROGRAM ACT.
ar:HB1733.summary: Requires the Division of Elementary and Secondary Education to set the same eligibility criteria for the Arkansas Better Chance and Better Chance for School Success programs, lets any child from birth to age 5 meeting one qualification join either, and repeals the income-based criteria statute.

ar:HB1734.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING DEATH CERTIFICATES; AND TO CLARIFY THE MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS WHO MAY SIGN A MEDICAL CERTIFICATE OF DEATH AND PRONOUNCE DEATH OF A PATIENT.
ar:HB1734.summary: As passed by the House, lets an advanced practice registered nurse complete and sign a medical certificate of death and pronounce death of a patient in a hospital, if the hospital's medical director gives the nurse that authority.

ar:HB1735.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS UNDERGROUND FACILITIES DAMAGE PREVENTION ACT; AND TO REVISE MEMBERSHIP IN THE ONE CALL CENTER UNDER THE ARKANSAS UNDERGROUND FACILITIES DAMAGE PREVENTION ACT.
ar:HB1735.summary: Sets a $1,000 fine for an underground-facility operator that fails to join the One Call Center within 30 days of a written warning, plus up to $500 for each further 30 days, unless the Public Service Commission grants an exemption or waiver.

ar:HB1736.title: TO AMEND ARTICLE 9 OF THE UNIFORM COMMERCIAL CODE.
ar:HB1736.summary: Exempts security interests in ownership interests in general partnerships, limited partnerships and limited liability companies from the Uniform Commercial Code rules that make contract terms restricting assignment or transfer ineffective.

ar:HB1737.title: TO AMEND THE TRANSMITTING UTILITY ACT; AND TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF "TRANSMITTING UTILITY" TO INCLUDE FIBER OPTIC AND BROADBAND LINES.
ar:HB1737.summary: Expands the definition of "transmitting utility" in the Transmitting Utility Act to include entities providing fiber optic communication, broadband internet or similar high-speed data transmission services.

ar:HB1739.title: TO ADOPT THE UNIFORM ELECTRONIC LEGAL MATERIALS ACT.
ar:HB1739.summary: Adopts the Uniform Electronic Legal Materials Act, requiring official publishers of the Constitution, Arkansas Code, and agency rules published only electronically to designate them official, authenticate them, and preserve them.

ar:HB1740.title: TO EXEMPT CERTAIN AGRICULTURAL INFORMATION FROM THE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT OF 1967.
ar:HB1740.summary: Exempts certificates of veterinary inspection and personal information tied to animal electronic ID tags held by the Department of Agriculture from the Freedom of Information Act.

ar:HB1741.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS AGRICULTURAL LIMING MATERIALS ACT.
ar:HB1741.summary: Transfers sampling, stop-sale, deficiency-penalty, registration and quarterly-tonnage-report duties under the Agricultural Liming Materials Act from the State Plant Board to the Department of Agriculture, which invoices the per-ton payments instead of receiving them with reports.

ar:HB1742.title: TO AMEND THE LAW RELATED TO SEED CERTIFICATION.
ar:HB1742.summary: Changes seed certification law to have the Department of Agriculture, rather than the State Plant Board, certify seed and issue and revoke certificates, with the Plant Board keeping rulemaking and appeals.

ar:HB1743.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS FEED LAW OF 1997.
ar:HB1743.summary: Changes the Arkansas Feed Law of 1997 to have the Department of Agriculture, rather than the State Plant Board, administer commercial feed registration, licensing and sampling.

ar:HB1744.title: TO AMEND THE LAW RELATED TO FERTILIZER.
ar:HB1744.summary: Changes fertilizer law to have fertilizer and fertilizer material registration filed with the Department of Agriculture instead of the State Plant Board.

ar:HB1745.title: TO REQUIRE CERTAIN COMMERCIAL DRIVER LICENSE HOLDERS TO POSSESS A UNITED STATES WORK AUTHORIZATION; TO REQUIRE THE OPERATOR OF A COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE TO HAVE ENGLISH PROFICIENCY; AND TO CREATE RELATED OFFENSES.
ar:HB1745.summary: Makes it a Class D felony to present a false foreign commercial license or to drive a commercial vehicle on a foreign commercial license without a work permit in possession (a misdemeanor if one was issued), and revises which commercial licenses Arkansas recognizes.

ar:HB1746.title: TO AMEND THE UNIFORM COMMERCIAL CODE.
ar:HB1746.summary: Amends Arkansas's Uniform Commercial Code to add rules for controllable electronic records and electronic money, and to replace "writing" with "record" in some provisions, effective September 1, 2026.

ar:HB1749.title: TO ADOPT THE UNIFORM TRUST DECANTING ACT.
ar:HB1749.summary: Adopts the Uniform Trust Decanting Act, which sets rules for a trustee with discretion over principal to distribute it into a new or modified trust.

ar:HB1751.title: TO REQUIRE AN APPLICANT FOR TEMPORARY ASSISTANCE FOR NEEDY FAMILIES PROGRAM BENEFITS TO ENGAGE IN JOB SEARCH ACTIVITIES WHILE THE APPLICATION IS BEING PROCESSED.
ar:HB1751.summary: Requires job-ready applicants for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families and the Arkansas Work Pays Program to engage in job search activities while their applications are being processed.

ar:HB1752.title: TO EXEMPT CERTAIN SAVINGS PLANS FROM THE EXECUTION OF A JUDGMENT.
ar:HB1752.summary: Exempts additional savings plans, such as health savings accounts, inherited IRAs, and 529 and Coverdell education accounts, from attachment, execution and seizure to satisfy a person's debts.

ar:HB1756.title: TO ALLOW A PARENT, LEGAL GUARDIAN, OR PERSON STANDING IN LOCO PARENTIS TO A STUDENT TO DOCUMENT AND MAINTAIN THE COMMUNITY SERVICE HOURS THE STUDENT OBTAINS.
ar:HB1756.summary: Lets a parent or guardian document and attest to a student's required 75 hours of community service, replacing the requirement that the service agency certify the hours; the Department of Education may audit the documentation.

ar:HB1757.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING RAILROADS; AND TO CREATE THE OFFENSE OF TAMPERING WITH RAIL INFRASTRUCTURE.
ar:HB1757.summary: Creates the Class D felony of tampering with rail infrastructure, covering recklessly obstructing or interfering with tracks, signals, trains and related equipment without lawful authority, plus related assaults, threats and false reports.

ar:HB1759.title: TO INCREASE THE AMOUNT OF TIME A TAXPAYER HAS TO ASSESS TANGIBLE PERSONAL PROPERTY ACQUIRED DURING A CERTAIN TIME PERIOD.
ar:HB1759.summary: Changes the assessment window for tangible personal property acquired between January 1 and May 31 from 30 to 60 days after acquisition, and moves the start of the separate late-spring acquisition period from May 2 to April 1.

ar:HB1760.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE JURISDICTION TO CONSIDER CERTAIN PETITIONS FOR THE ADJUSTMENT OF A PROPERTY ASSESSMENT.
ar:HB1760.summary: Bars county equalization boards from hearing petitions on homestead tax relief eligibility for disabled or age-65-and-older owners, and requires those petitions to be filed with the county court.

ar:HB1762.title: TO REQUIRE REVOCATION OF A PERMIT FOR THE DISPOSAL OF INDUSTRIAL WASTE IN AN AGRICULTURAL OR PASTORAL APPLICATION FOR A CERTAIN NUMBER OF VIOLATIONS.
ar:HB1762.summary: Requires the Division of Environmental Quality to assess the maximum penalty for each violation by an industrial wastewater residuals land-application permit holder that causes over-application or precipitation-related surface application, and directs the Pollution Control and Ecology Commission to begin rulemaking on no-discharge land application permits.

ar:HB1763.title: TO AMEND THE HUMAN TRAFFICKING ACT OF 2013; AND TO CREATE THE OFFENSE OF UNLAWFUL USE OF A COMMUNICATION DEVICE DURING THE COMMISSION OF A HUMAN TRAFFICKING OFFENSE.
ar:HB1763.summary: Makes it a Class C felony to knowingly use a communication device to commit or facilitate a human trafficking felony, with each use counted as a separate offense.

ar:HB1764.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING A VIOLATION OF AN ORDER OF PROTECTION.
ar:HB1764.summary: Counts a prior violation of another state's or foreign jurisdiction's equivalent domestic abuse protection order, as well as an Arkansas conviction, toward the Class D felony penalty for violating an order of protection within five years.

ar:HB1766.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS RESPOND, INNOVATE, SUCCEED, AND EMPOWER (RISE) ACT.
ar:HB1766.summary: Creates the RISE Act, requiring colleges and universities to adopt a policy to consider documents such as IEPs, Section 504 plans or military-service disability records when deciding whether a student has a disability.

ar:HB1767.title: TO ABOLISH THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES ADVISORY COUNCIL; AND TO CREATE THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE.
ar:HB1767.summary: Abolishes the Emergency Medical Services Advisory Council and creates an 11-member Emergency Medical Services Advisory Committee in the Department of Health, appointed by the State Board of Health, to take over its duties; existing rules stay in effect.

ar:HB1768.title: TO REQUIRE A SOLID WASTE LANDFILL CONTRACT RELATING TO A HOST FEE TO BE VOTED ON AT A REGULARLY SCHEDULED MEETING OF A HOST COMMUNITY IN WHICH THE LANDFILL IS LOCATED.
ar:HB1768.summary: Requires landfill host fee contracts to be voted on at a regularly scheduled meeting of the host city and county, limits each term to four years, and bars host fees that last in perpetuity.

ar:HB1770.title: TO ESTABLISH THE PREGNANCY PARKING ACT; TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING PARKING FOR A PERSON WITH A DISABILITY; AND TO AUTHORIZE THE ISSUANCE OF A TEMPORARY SPECIAL CERTIFICATE TO PREGNANT WOMEN.
ar:HB1770.summary: Creates the Pregnancy Parking Act, letting a physician-confirmed pregnant woman get a temporary disability parking certificate that expires one year after she gives birth.

ar:HB1771.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING DISCLOSURES TO POLICYHOLDERS; AND TO REQUIRE MONTHLY REPORTING BY INSURERS.
ar:HB1771.summary: Changes insurer reports to group health policyholders: applies to those with more than 50 insured employees (up from 25), adds monthly pharmacy claims and a high-cost claimant report for members over $10,000, provided within 30 days, at most quarterly.

ar:HB1772.title: CONCERNING VEGETABLE GARDEN PROTECTION.
ar:HB1772.summary: Bars counties and cities from prohibiting vegetable gardens on residential property, while allowing local rules on specifics such as water use during drought, and lets people garden on their own or, with permission, others' private property.

ar:HB1774.title: TO AMEND THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE ARKANSAS FAIR HOUSING COMMISSION.
ar:HB1774.summary: Reduces the Arkansas Fair Housing Commission from thirteen to seven members: five with real estate, homebuilding, mortgage lending, banking or related experience appointed by the Governor, and one each appointed by the Senate President Pro Tempore and the House Speaker.

ar:HB1777.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE OFFENSE OF SEXUALLY GROOMING A CHILD; AND TO INCLUDE BRIBING OR ATTEMPTING TO BRIBE A CHILD IN THE OFFENSE OF SEXUALLY GROOMING A CHILD.
ar:HB1777.summary: Redefines sexually grooming a child 13 or younger as, with purpose to entice the child into sexual activity, giving the child sexually explicit material or bribing the child, and adds a definition of "bribe".

ar:HB1778.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE CRIMINAL OFFENSE OF STALKING TO INCLUDE PLACING A PERSON IN FEAR OF SEXUAL ACTS; AND TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF COURSE OF CONDUCT WITH RESPECT TO STALKING.
ar:HB1778.summary: Adds threats placing a person, or a family or household member, in imminent fear of unwanted sexual contact to second-degree stalking, and specifies that a course of conduct includes mail and electronic messages.

ar:HB1779.title: TO AMEND THE LAW RELATED TO THEFT OF PROPERTY; AND ENHANCE THE OFFENSE CLASSIFICATION FOR THE THEFT OF A POSTAL PACKAGE DELIVERED TO A PERSON'S RESIDENCE AND LEFT WITHIN THE CURTILAGE OF THE RESIDENCE.
ar:HB1779.summary: Classifies theft of a postal package taken from the grounds of a residence or from a delivery vehicle along its route as a Class C felony.

ar:HB1780.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE RETENTION OF PROPERTY RELATED TO A FELONY INVESTIGATION.
ar:HB1780.summary: Lets a county sheriff's office release items held in a felony investigation before the statute of limitations lapses, if a court orders it or the prosecutor says there will be no prosecution.

ar:HB1782.title: TO PROHIBIT OVER-THE-COUNTER DIET PILLS FROM BEING SOLD, TRANSFERRED, OR OTHERWISE FURNISHED TO A PERSON WHO IS UNDER EIGHTEEN YEARS OF AGE.
ar:HB1782.summary: Bars retailers from selling or giving over-the-counter diet pills to anyone under 18, requires them to request valid identification from purchasers who appear to be under 18, and sets a fine of up to $2,000.

ar:HB1783.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE REDUCTION OF A CITY OF THE FIRST CLASS TO A CITY OF THE SECOND CLASS.
ar:HB1783.summary: Raises the population threshold for a first-class city to reduce itself to a second-class city from under 5,000 to under 7,500 under the latest census, and requires an ordinance rather than a resolution.

ar:HB1784.title: TO MODIFY THE INFORMAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION PROCESS FOR LONG-TERM CARE FACILITIES.
ar:HB1784.summary: Changes long-term care facility informal dispute resolution hearings: allows attorneys and recording, requires written determinations within seven days of the hearing, and repeals the required post-hearing reports and quarterly reports.

ar:HB1785.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE MEMBERS OF A COUNTY DEPOSITORY BOARD.
ar:HB1785.summary: Requires a county quorum court, where the treasurer and collector offices are combined, to select by ordinance another elected county constitutional officer as the third member of the county depository board.

ar:HB1786.title: TO PROVIDE ELIGIBILITY FOR A TUITION BENEFIT TO SOLDIERS AND AIRMEN OF THE ARKANSAS NATIONAL GUARD ATTENDING CERTAIN PRIVATE TWO-YEAR AND FOUR-YEAR COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES.
ar:HB1786.summary: Lets Arkansas National Guard soldiers and airmen attending private, nonprofit Arkansas colleges receive a tuition benefit up to what they would get at a state-supported college or university.

ar:HB1788.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS HEALTH CARE CONSUMER ACT; AND TO REDUCE THE TIME ALLOWED FOR PROCESSING AN APPLICATION OF A PROVIDER.
ar:HB1788.summary: Shortens the time a health insurer has to decide a non-physician provider's participation application or renewal request from 180 to 90 calendar days; the 60-day period for physicians is unchanged.

ar:HB1789.title: TO RESTRICT A LOCAL GOVERNMENT FROM PROVIDING FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE OF ISSUING AN IDENTIFICATION CARD TO AN INDIVIDUAL IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1789.summary: Bars cities, counties and towns from issuing local identification cards to people who cannot show lawful presence in the U.S., or from funding anyone else to issue them.

ar:HB1790.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE REGULATION OF SHORT-TERM RENTALS BY A LOCAL GOVERNMENT.
ar:HB1790.summary: Bars cities, towns and counties from banning short-term rentals or capping their number jurisdiction-wide, while letting them require permits with fees and owner contact information, and suspend permits after repeated violations or a felony at the rental.

ar:HB1794.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS FOR REAL ESTATE LICENSEES; AND TO CREATE CONTINUING EDUCATION EXEMPTIONS FOR CERTAIN REAL ESTATE BROKER LICENSEES.
ar:HB1794.summary: Lets the Real Estate Commission's executive director waive continuing education for health reasons or licensee achievements, and allows exemption on application for licensees aged 72 or older with 25 years of continuous licensure and a clean five-year disciplinary and education record.

ar:HB1796.title: TO REQUIRE THE DISPLAY OF GENDER INFORMATION ON AN ARKANSAS DRIVER’S LICENSE OR IDENTIFICATION CARD.
ar:HB1796.summary: Requires Arkansas driver's licenses and ID cards to state gender as "M" or "F", matching the applicant's identity document or, if it shows "X" or none, a form the applicant completes; bars "X" or blank entries; allows changes only with an amended birth certificate.

ar:HB1797.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ARKANSAS DEVELOPMENT FINANCE AUTHORITY; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1797.summary: Moves the Arkansas Development Finance Authority out of the Department of Commerce to operate as an independent state instrumentality, exempts its rules from the state Administrative Procedure Act, and makes it subject to legislative audit.

ar:HB1798.title: TO ESTABLISH A GREEN ENVELOPE PROGRAM.
ar:HB1798.summary: Requires the Department of Finance and Administration to make available by January 1, 2026 a green envelope for a driver's documents, with guidelines for law enforcement on the outside, which people diagnosed with mental illness may request at a local department office.

ar:HB1799.title: TO AMEND THE PERMISSIBLE METHODS OF REPORTING UNDER THE CHILD MALTREATMENT ACT.
ar:HB1799.summary: Removes facsimile transmission from the permitted methods for mandated reporters to report child maltreatment, leaving telephone calls and online reporting.

ar:HB1800.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING DISCLOSURE FOR CAMPAIGN FINANCE; TO REQUIRE DISCLOSURE BY A REPRESENTATIVE OF A HOSTILE FOREIGN PRINCIPAL; AND TO AMEND PORTIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE THAT RESULTED FROM INITIATED ACT 1 OF 1990.
ar:HB1800.summary: Requires representatives of hostile foreign principals (China, Russia, North Korea, Iran) and political organizations that received money from them within five years to register with the Secretary of State and update filings.

ar:HB1801.title: TO AUTHORIZE AN OUTSOURCING FACILITY OF LEGEND DRUGS AND CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES THAT COMPOUNDS A PRODUCT TO SELL THE COMPOUNDED PRODUCT TO CERTAIN ENTITIES.
ar:HB1801.summary: Allows an FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facility with an Arkansas pharmacy board permit to sell compounded drugs only to Arkansas-licensed retail pharmacies, healthcare facilities and providers; bars sales to wholesalers and others; requires federal good manufacturing practices.

ar:HB1802.title: TO CREATE THE TALENT RECRUITMENT GRANT PROGRAM; AND TO PROVIDE INCENTIVES FOR INDIVIDUALS TO RELOCATE TO THE STATE.
ar:HB1802.summary: Creates a grant program, run by the Association of Arkansas Development Organizations, giving cities and nonprofits up to $500,000 a year to offer incentives to out-of-state remote workers earning at least $55,000, or new hires, who relocate to Arkansas. Grantees must cover 20% of costs.

ar:HB1803.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE PLACEMENT OF A MONUMENT ON THE STATE CAPITOL GROUNDS IN RECOGNITION AND HONOR OF MAURICE LEE “FOOTSIE” BRITT.
ar:HB1803.summary: Establishes the Maurice Lee "Footsie" Britt Memorial Bust Fund and requires the Secretary of State to arrange placement of a memorial bust of him in the State Capitol.

ar:HB1805.title: TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF "BULLYING"; AND TO CREATE A PROCESS WHEREBY A PUBLIC SCHOOL MAY CONDUCT MULTIPLE, SIMULTANEOUS INVESTIGATIONS INTO THE SAME ALLEGATION OF BULLYING UNDER CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1805.summary: Changes the school definition of bullying to require a power imbalance and repeated or likely repeated acts, and lets schools investigate one incident under a single process when it also may violate another law.

ar:HB1806.title: TO PROVIDE CURRICULUM TRANSPARENCY FOR PARENTS OF KINDERGARTEN THROUGH GRADE TWELVE STUDENTS; AND TO ALLOW A PARENT TO REVIEW AND OPT OUT OF SELECTED LIBRARY MEDIA MATERIALS FOR HIS OR HER CHILD.
ar:HB1806.summary: Directs the state education division to build an online portal, by January 15, 2026 if funded, where parents can search school textbooks and library materials and opt their child out of selected library media materials.

ar:HB1807.title: TO AMEND THE SALES TAX EXEMPTION FOR AIRCRAFT HELD FOR RESALE AND USED FOR RENTAL OR CHARTER; AND TO CLARIFY THE PERSONS ELIGIBLE FOR THE SALES TAX EXEMPTION FOR AIRCRAFT HELD FOR RESALE AND USED FOR RENTAL OR CHARTER.
ar:HB1807.summary: Defines the business of selling aircraft for the sales tax exemption on aircraft held for resale and rented or chartered, and requires a person acquiring an aircraft to rent or lease to show annual rental revenue of at least 7.5% of its net price.

ar:HB1808.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING MUNICIPAL FIRE DEPARTMENTS; AND TO CREATE THE BILL OF RIGHTS FOR FIREFIGHTERS.
ar:HB1808.summary: Lets cities adopt by ordinance a recommended firefighters' bill of rights with minimum interrogation and discipline standards such as recorded questioning, written charges, a predisciplinary hearing, and no retaliation for exercising these rights.

ar:HB1809.title: TO ALLOW FOR PROPERTY OWNED BY A TRUST OR A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY TO QUALIFY AS A HOMESTEAD FOR PURPOSES OF THE PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION FOR DISABLED VETERANS IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1809.summary: Counts a disabled veteran's home held in a revocable or irrevocable trust, or a limited liability company owned by the veteran and spouse, as a homestead for the disabled-veteran property tax exemption.

ar:HB1810.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING THE ARKANSAS SCHOOL FOR THE BLIND AND THE ARKANSAS SCHOOL FOR THE DEAF; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1810.summary: Transfers the Arkansas School for the Blind and the Arkansas School for the Deaf, with their functions, staff, property and funds, to the Arkansas School for the Deaf and Blind, and updates state law references. Declares an emergency.

ar:HB1812.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT; TO CREATE AN EXCEPTION TO ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENTS FOR A STUDENT WHO TAKES A GED TEST; AND TO AMEND THE SCORE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE GED TEST.
ar:HB1812.summary: Stops counting students who pass a GED test as dropouts in district graduation-rate calculations, adds GED recipients to those exempt from school attendance, and changes requirements for students seeking adult education enrollment or the GED test.

ar:HB1814.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING MUNICIPAL AUTHORITY OVER UTILITIES; AND TO REVISE THE DEFINITION OF "PUBLIC UTILITY" UNDER TITLE 14, CHAPTER 200.
ar:HB1814.summary: Revises the definition of "public utility" in municipal utility law by changing the citation for excluded water or light commissions from § 14-201-101 et seq. to §§ 14-201-101 through 14-201-129.

ar:HB1815.title: TO AMEND THE STATE'S JURISDICTION OVER FEDERAL LANDS; AND TO RETAIN JUVENILE JUSTICE JURISDICTION BY THE STATE.
ar:HB1815.summary: Gives circuit court juvenile divisions exclusive jurisdiction over delinquency cases for state-law crimes on military installations with concurrent jurisdiction; sends federal-land jurisdiction transfer notices to the Legislative Council when the legislature is not in session; allows reciprocal agreements with federal agencies.

ar:HB1817.title: TO ESTABLISH ELIJAH'S LAW IN ARKANSAS; AND TO REQUIRE THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO ESTABLISH A STATEWIDE ANAPHYLAXIS POLICY FOR CHILDCARE FACILITIES.
ar:HB1817.summary: Creates "Elijah's Law," requiring the Department of Education, consulting the Department of Health, to set a childcare anaphylaxis policy with weight-based epinephrine dosing, emergency protocols, training and medication access, inspection requirements, and parent notification.

ar:HB1820.title: TO REGULATE AUTOMATIC RENEWAL AND CONTINUOUS SERVICE OFFERS.
ar:HB1820.summary: Regulates automatic renewal and continuous service offers: businesses must clearly disclose terms, such as recurring charges and cancellation policy, obtain the consumer's express consent before charging, and send an acknowledgment of the terms and how to cancel.

ar:HB1821.title: TO CREATE A MORE SUSTAINABLE SYSTEM OF PROPERTY INSURANCE FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS, INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION, AND STATE-OWNED PROPERTY; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1821.summary: Creates a State Captive Insurance Program, run through the Department of Transformation and Shared Services, to insure property of public schools, state-supported colleges and state agencies, requires participation by entities accepting state facility funding, and bars public insurance adjusters.

ar:HB1824.title: TO CREATE THE DOG AND CAT RESCUE ACT: DAISY'S LAW.
ar:HB1824.summary: Allows a law enforcement officer, after an animal cruelty complaint, to temporarily secure a dog or cat and place it in appropriate custody if its condition would likely deteriorate, using the condition of the owner's other dogs or cats as evidence.

ar:HB1826.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR DELIVERY OF A NEWBORN IN A LICENSED BIRTHING CENTER.
ar:HB1826.summary: Requires health plans, including Medicaid, to cover birthing services at licensed birthing centers on the same terms as hospital birthing services from January 1, 2026, with no higher deductible, copay or out-of-pocket limits.

ar:HB1827.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS HUNTING HERITAGE PROTECTION ACT.
ar:HB1827.summary: Resets the no-net-loss baseline for hunting acreage on Game and Fish Commission-managed lands from August 12, 2005 to January 1, 2025, requires replacement acreage near closed hunting land, and replaces public safety and homeland security with fish or wildlife management as closure grounds.

ar:HB1828.title: TO CREATE A SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION FOR INSPIRATION POINT CENTER FOR THE ARTS, INC.
ar:HB1828.summary: Exempts purchases of goods, digital products and services by Inspiration Point Center for the Arts, Inc. from state sales tax, effective the first day of the calendar quarter after the act takes effect.

ar:HB1829.title: TO AMEND THE DOMESTIC ABUSE ACT OF 1991; TO PROVIDE FOR REMOTE TESTIMONY IN CERTAIN INSTANCES IN A HEARING UNDER THE DOMESTIC ABUSE ACT OF 1991; AND TO PROVIDE OVERSIGHT FOR A DOMESTIC VIOLENCE INTERVENTION PROGRAM.
ar:HB1829.summary: Expands the domestic abuse definition to include "course of control" and "disturbing the peace" patterns; allows testimony outside another party's presence; requires each sheriff's office to designate an officer to attempt service within two hours; schedules expedited contempt hearings; regulates intervention programs.

ar:HB1831.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE USE OF SETTLEMENT FUNDS BY THE ATTORNEY GENERAL.
ar:HB1831.summary: Extends the law governing the Attorney General's use of settlement funds to civil penalties the Attorney General collects when no other law specifies their use.

ar:HB1832.title: TO AMEND THE RULES OF THE SUPREME COURT AND COURT OF APPEALS OF THE STATE OF ARKANSAS; AND TO AMEND A RULE OF THE SUPREME COURT AND COURT OF APPEALS UNDER THE AUTHORITY GRANTED BY THE ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION.
ar:HB1832.summary: Gives the Court of Appeals exclusive original jurisdiction over lawsuits seeking to have a state law or rule declared unconstitutional in all its applications, with appeals going to the Supreme Court.

ar:HB1833.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE ADMISSIONS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS COLLEGE OF MEDICINE.
ar:HB1833.summary: Sets College of Medicine freshman seats at 25 per congressional district plus 25 for Arkansas residents, replacing percentage allocations; seats a district cannot fill go first to qualified Arkansas residents.

ar:HB1834.title: TO AMEND ARKANSAS LAW CONCERNING THE LICENSING AND REGULATION OF MOTOR VEHICLES.
ar:HB1834.summary: Adds misuse of a dealer's extra license plate to prohibited dealer practices, and replaces the $0 to $129 dealer service and handling fee range with a limit of reasonable document-handling and administrative costs.

ar:HB1835.title: CONCERNING SPECIALTY COURT PROGRAMS; AND TO UPDATE AND CLARIFY THE LAW CONCERNING DRUG COURT, MENTAL HEALTH COURT, VETERANS COURT, AND DWI/BWI SPECIALTY COURT PROGRAMS.
ar:HB1835.summary: Creates a specialty court subchapter letting judges dismiss cases and seal records after program completion on a prosecutor's recommendation, and letting participants finish programs in another county; repeals the pre-adjudication probation sealing section and revises program definitions and attorney contracting.

ar:HB1837.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING DISCLOSURE FOR MATTERS REFERRED TO VOTERS; AND TO BAN FOREIGN FUNDING FOR BALLOT MEASURES; TO AMEND PORTIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE THAT RESULTED FROM INITIATED ACT 1 OF 1996.
ar:HB1837.summary: Bars ballot-measure committees from knowingly accepting money from foreign nationals and other prohibited sources, requires donor and committee affirmations, lets the Attorney General sue for up to twice the prohibited amount, and limits government disclosure of nonprofit donors.

ar:HB1839.title: TO AMEND THE PROCEDURES FOR THE DECLARATION OF LEGAL DEATH OF A MISSING PERSON.
ar:HB1839.summary: Replaces the declaration-of-heirs statute with a probate court petition to declare a missing person legally dead, requiring a search affidavit, notice to close relatives and parties with a financial interest of at least $5,000, and a hearing at least 90 days after filing.

ar:HB1840.title: TO AMEND THE MEDICAID PROVIDER-LED ORGANIZED CARE ACT TO ENSURE THAT SEDATION DENTISTRY IS COVERED BY RISK-BASED PROVIDER ORGANIZATIONS.
ar:HB1840.summary: Adds sedation dentistry to the Medicaid Provider-Led Organized Care Act, so risk-based provider organizations process claims for it even though other capitated dental benefits stay excluded.

ar:HB1841.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS REVENUE INVESTMENT IN VITAL EMS SYSTEMS (ARRIVES) ACT; AND TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS REVENUE INVESTMENT IN VITAL EMS SYSTEMS (ARRIVES) FUND FOR EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES AGENCIES.
ar:HB1841.summary: Creates the ARRIVES Fund and Act, under which the Department of Health distributes fund money to eligible ground ambulance agencies by county population tier. Agencies must be licensed three years and offer advanced life support, or basic life support if upgrading within a year.

ar:HB1843.title: CONCERNING RECORDS AND PHOTOGRAPHS KEPT BY THE STATE CRIME LABORATORY.
ar:HB1843.summary: Adds the Arkansas Drug Director to the list of people to whom the State Crime Laboratory may release confidential records and photographs.

ar:HB1844.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE OFFENSE OF FLEEING BY MEANS OF A VEHICLE OR CONVEYANCE; AND TO INCREASE THE PENALTY FOR A PERSON WHO JUMPS FROM A MOVING VEHICLE OR CONVEYANCE WHILE FLEEING.
ar:HB1844.summary: Sets the penalty for fleeing in a vehicle at Class C, B or A felony, depending on the existing fleeing category, when the person exits the vehicle while it is still moving and keeps fleeing on foot.

ar:HB1845.title: TO ALLOW THE ELECTRONIC ADMINISTRATION OF DOCUMENTS RELATED TO THE OWNERSHIP OF MOTOR VEHICLES; TO AUTHORIZE ELECTRONIC LIEN, TITLING, AND REGISTRATION SYSTEMS; AND TO AUTHORIZE THE CREATION OF A SECURE DIGITAL TITLE SYSTEM.
ar:HB1845.summary: Allows electronic odometer disclosures and other electronic motor vehicle ownership documents, authorizes electronic lien, titling and registration systems, and allows creation of a secure digital title system.

ar:HB1846.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS 2036 COMMISSION.
ar:HB1846.summary: Creates the eight-member Arkansas 2036 Commission, serving through 2036, to plan observance of the state's 200th birthday, explore a commemorative landmark, and assist heritage programs.

ar:HB1847.title: TO AUTHORIZE THE ARKANSAS RACING COMMISSION TO MAINTAIN A STATEWIDE SELF-EXCLUSION LIST.
ar:HB1847.summary: Lets the Arkansas Racing Commission keep a statewide casino self-exclusion list through a multi-state program or agreements with other states, replacing separate casino lists, and makes listed individuals' winnings subject to forfeiture after notice and a hearing.

ar:HB1850.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING GROUND AMBULANCE SERVICES; TO CLARIFY THE MINIMUM ALLOWABLE REIMBURSEMENT FOR GROUND AMBULANCE SERVICES; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1850.summary: Sets the minimum insurer payment for ground ambulance services, absent local rates, at the lesser of 325% of the Medicare rural ambulance rate for Arkansas or the provider's billed charges, from July 1, 2025.

ar:HB1851.title: TO AMEND THE SALES TAX EXEMPTION FOR FOOD, FOOD INGREDIENTS, AND PREPARED FOOD SOLD IN A PUBLIC, COMMON, HIGH SCHOOL, OR COLLEGE CAFETERIA OR DINING FACILITY.
ar:HB1851.summary: Treats school, high school, and college cafeterias and dining facilities as exempt from sales tax on food even when a for-profit third party provides their services or management, if they are primarily for teachers and pupils and not run for profit.

ar:HB1852.title: TO ESTABLISH A RIGHT TO REPAIR FOR CERTAIN AGRICULTURAL EQUIPMENT.
ar:HB1852.summary: Creates a right to repair for agricultural equipment, requiring manufacturers to make tools, software, documentation, codes and data available on fair and reasonable terms to farmers and independent repair facilities.

ar:HB1853.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING AGENCY RELATIONSHIP AND DUTIES RELATED TO REAL ESTATE LICENSES; AND TO CLARIFY THE OBLIGATIONS OF DUAL AGENCY.
ar:HB1853.summary: Lets real estate licensees' clients who consent to dual agency waive the licensee's duty of absolute fidelity by contract, and allows contracts to limit disclosure of confidential information by a dual agent.

ar:HB1854.title: TO EXEMPT A HOME CAREGIVER FROM HOME CAREGIVER TRAINING IF HE OR SHE PREVIOUSLY COMPLETED TRAINING.
ar:HB1854.summary: Exempts a home caregiver from home caregiver training if he or she previously completed the training and provides documentation.

ar:HB1855.title: TO AMEND THE LAWS CONCERNING THE POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND THE ARKANSAS FORESTRY COMMISSION; AND TO AMEND THE LAWS RELATING TO FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT BOUNDARIES.
ar:HB1855.summary: Changes fire protection district law so the Department of Agriculture, rather than the Forestry Commission, may recommend boundary adjustments to the county court for overlapping, abutting or contiguous districts.

ar:HB1859.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING MASTECTOMIES.
ar:HB1859.summary: Requires mastectomy benefits in health plans to cover tissue-support mesh and nerve grafts, with supplies reimbursed at no less than acquisition cost, and updates the federal-law reference to January 1, 2025; excludes the state and public school employee plan.

ar:HB1863.title: TO AMEND THE TRANSPORTATION BENEFIT MANAGER ACT; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1863.summary: Repeals the requirement that insurers and transportation benefit managers pay ambulance providers 250% of the Medicare rural rate, and requires the Arkansas Ambulance Association to collect local government ambulance rates and report them annually to the Insurance Commissioner.

ar:HB1865.title: TO CREATE AN ENHANCED PENALTY FOR CERTAIN OFFENSES AGAINST A CHILD.
ar:HB1865.summary: Creates an enhanced penalty for adults in a position of trust or authority over a child who commit listed felonies against the child, with minimum prison terms of 1 to 30 years by felony class and no parole or early release during the minimum.

ar:HB1866.title: TO CREATE ELI'S LAW; AND TO REQUIRE EACH PUBLIC SCHOOL TO INSTALL AN AUDIO RECORDING DEVICE IN EACH LOCKER ROOM AND DRESSING ROOM ON THE PUBLIC SCHOOL CAMPUS.
ar:HB1866.summary: Requires each public school district and charter school, starting in 2027-28, to install audio recording devices in locker rooms and changing rooms with posted notices, and keep recordings at least 90 days but no more than 12 months absent an allegation.

ar:HB1869.title: TO CREATE THE MATERNAL OUTCOMES MANAGEMENT SYSTEM WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH; AND TO ORGANIZE MATERNAL HEALTH RESOURCES.
ar:HB1869.summary: Directs the Department of Health, subject to funding, to create a Maternal Outcomes Management System that organizes maternal health resources, educates patients and clinicians, gives grants to designated birthing hospitals, and collects hospital maternal health data.

ar:HB1870.title: CONCERNING VOTER REGISTRATION LISTS; AND TO ALLOW THE SECRETARY OF STATE TO PROVIDE A VOTER REGISTRATION LIST TO FEDERAL COURTS.
ar:HB1870.summary: Lets the Secretary of State give voter registration lists to federal courts for jury selection if the court reports jurors disqualified as noncitizens, felons, deceased or nonresidents.

ar:HB1872.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE FEES THAT MAY BE COLLECTED BY A COUNTY SHERIFF; AND TO ALLOW A COUNTY SHERIFF TO COLLECT FEES FOR ATTEMPTED SERVICE IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES.
ar:HB1872.summary: Revises county sheriff fees, allowing the sheriff to charge fees such as $30 for attempted service of summonses and court notices, and including the $50 arrest warrant service fee in the court's judgment of conviction.

ar:HB1873.title: CONCERNING NOTIFICATION TO PERSONS ELECTED TO SERVE AS A MEMBER OF THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE YEARS OF SERVICE REMAINING BEFORE REACHING THE LIMITATION ON SERVICE UNDER THE ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION.
ar:HB1873.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to notify a newly certified General Assembly winner, within 30 days, how many years the member may serve before reaching the constitutional service limit.

ar:HB1874.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE USE OF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FUNDING THAT EXCEEDS THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT AWARDED TO PUBLIC SCHOOLS FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS UNDER THE PUBLIC SCHOOL FUNDING ACT OF 2003.
ar:HB1874.summary: Requires professional development funding above the $41-per-student base amount to be used by the state education division for professional learning communities that support implementing the LEARNS Act.

ar:HB1875.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE USE OF AN IGNITION INTERLOCK DEVICE; AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE EXTENSION OF THE MANDATORY PERIOD FOR THE USE OF AN IGNITION INTERLOCK DEVICE.
ar:HB1875.summary: Sets the ignition interlock lockout level at 0.025% blood alcohol, adds device requirements such as random retests and photos, and allows extending the mandatory use period for failed or skipped tests in the final 60 days.

ar:HB1876.title: REGARDING THE OWNERSHIP OF MODEL TRAINING AND CONTENT GENERATED BY A GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOL.
ar:HB1876.summary: Provides that a person who gives input to a generative AI tool owns the generated content, and one who provides training data owns the trained model, if lawful; work done at an employer's direction belongs to the employer.

ar:HB1877.title: CONCERNING CRIMINAL OFFENSES RELATED TO POSSESSION OF SEXUALLY EXPLICIT MATERIAL THAT DEPICTS A CHILD; AND TO INCLUDE A COMPUTER GENERATED IMAGE THAT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE IMAGE OF A CHILD.
ar:HB1877.summary: Adds computer-generated images indistinguishable from an actual child to the offenses of selling, distributing, possessing or viewing sexually explicit child material. Exempts law enforcement investigations and, for interactive computer services, content from others and good-faith AI safety testing.

ar:HB1878.title: TO ENSURE EARLY VOTING ACCESS FOR ARKANSANS RESIDING IN POPULATION CENTERS; AND TO REQUIRE A COUNTY BOARD OF ELECTION COMMISSIONERS TO CONDUCT EARLY VOTING IN A CITY IN CERTAIN INSTANCES.
ar:HB1878.summary: As introduced, requires a county board of election commissioners to hold early voting for primary and general elections at a polling site in each city of more than 15,000 people where the county clerk is not conducting early voting.

ar:HB1879.title: TO REQUIRE ALL CITY COUNCILS AND COUNTY QUORUM COURTS TO POST VIDEO RECORDINGS OF PUBLIC MEETINGS; AND TO REQUIRE ALL PUBLIC MEETINGS OF CITY COUNCILS OR COUNTY QUORUM COURTS TO BE RECORDED IN VIDEO FORMAT.
ar:HB1879.summary: Requires city councils and county quorum courts to video-record officially scheduled, special and called open meetings and post the video on their website, or a social media account if none, within 24 hours; compliance is due within one year.

ar:HB1886.title: TO DESIGNATE THE LABRADOR RETRIEVER AS THE OFFICIAL CANINE OF THE STATE OF ARKANSAS.
ar:HB1886.summary: Designates the Labrador retriever as the official state canine of Arkansas.

ar:HB1887.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING STATEWIDE CHILD ABDUCTION RESPONSE TEAMS.
ar:HB1887.summary: Removes the requirement that agencies on statewide child abduction response teams execute a memorandum of understanding, and removes the Criminal Justice Institute's duty to coordinate team certification and recertification.

ar:HB1889.title: TO AMEND THE LIMITATIONS ON ACCESS TO A DISPENSARY OR CULTIVATION FACILITY; AND TO AUTHORIZE A DISPENSARY TO DELIVER ORDERS VIA A DELIVERY VEHICLE OR VIA A DRIVE-THROUGH WINDOW.
ar:HB1889.summary: Allows dispensaries to deliver medical marijuana to qualified patients or caregivers by vehicle to a residential address or at a drive-through window, same day as the order is processed, with ID checks and separate packaging; extends visitor-access rules to dispensaries.

ar:HB1891.title: TO ALLOW A PERSON FILING AS A CANDIDATE FOR THE OFFICE OF JUSTICE OF THE SUPREME COURT OR JUDGE OF THE COURT OF APPEALS WHO IS AN APPOINTEE IN THAT POSITION TO USE THE TITLE OF THAT POSITION AS A PREFIX WHEN FILING AS A CANDIDATE.
ar:HB1891.summary: Adds Supreme Court justices and Court of Appeals judges to the appointed judges who may use their judicial title as a ballot prefix after serving at least 12 months in the position.

ar:HB1893.title: TO AUTHORIZE A PRIVATE PROPERTY OWNER OR BUSINESS OWNER TO BAN AN EMOTIONAL SUPPORT ANIMAL FROM THE PRIVATE PROPERTY OR THE BUSINESS PREMISES; AND TO REGULATE LIABILITY ON PRIVATE PROPERTY RELATED TO EMOTIONAL SUPPORT ANIMALS.
ar:HB1893.summary: Lets private property and business owners ban emotional support animals, unless federal law requires otherwise, and limits owner liability for injuries to customers or visitors caused by such an animal to cases of gross negligence.

ar:HB1894.title: TO ESTABLISH A METHOD OF VALUATION FOR REAL PROPERTY USED FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING; AND TO ESTABLISH A METHOD OF VALUATION FOR CERTAIN REAL PROPERTY UNDER ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION, ARTICLE 16, § 5.
ar:HB1894.summary: Directs the Assessment Coordination Division to adopt rules, by January 1, 2026, for assessing real property with rent or operating restrictions tied to federal low-income housing tax credits, HOME program funds or USDA incentives.

ar:HB1895.title: TO ALLOW A CORPORATION OR VOLUNTARY ASSOCIATION TO EMPLOY IN-HOUSE ATTORNEYS TO REPRESENT AFFILIATES OF THE CORPORATION OR VOLUNTARY ASSOCIATION.
ar:HB1895.summary: Allows a for-profit corporation or voluntary association to employ in-house attorneys for its affiliates' affairs and litigation, defining affiliates as related entities such as parents, subsidiaries, and siblings, without violating the ban on corporate practice of law.

ar:HB1896.title: TO CREATE THE JUNK FEE ELIMINATING ACT OF 2025; TO ABOLISH THE INFORMATION NETWORK OF ARKANSAS; AND TO TRANSFER ANY REMAINING DUTIES OF THE INFORMATION NETWORK OF ARKANSAS TO THE DIVISION OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS.
ar:HB1896.summary: Abolishes the Information Network of Arkansas and transfers its duties, contracts, personnel, property and unspent funds to the Division of Information Systems.

ar:HB1898.title: TO CREATE THE REGULATORY DIVISION AND THE REGULATORY ENFORCEMENT DIVISION IN THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION; AND TO ALLOW PERSONNEL OF THE REGULATORY ENFORCEMENT DIVISION TO BE DESIGNATED AS AGENTS.
ar:HB1898.summary: Creates a Regulatory Division in the Department of Finance and Administration overseeing alcohol, tobacco and racing regulators, and a Regulatory Enforcement Division, designated a law enforcement agency, whose agents investigate tobacco, alcohol, medical marijuana and gambling violations.

ar:HB1901.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING PASSPORT FEES COLLECTED BY COUNTY PASSPORT ACCEPTANCE FACILITIES.
ar:HB1901.summary: Requires county passport acceptance facilities to collect application and photo, mail and expedite fees, deposit the retained fees in a passport acceptance facility fund, and spend them as appropriated by the quorum court on the office.

ar:HB1903.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE TO PROVIDE SCHOOL DISTRICTS WITH FLEXIBILITY REGARDING ALTERNATIVE LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS.
ar:HB1903.summary: Changes the requirement that school districts provide alternative learning environments into an option, and makes the discipline policy's placement provision apply only to districts that provide one.

ar:HB1913.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING DRIVER'S LICENSES; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE QUALIFICATIONS FOR AN INTERMEDIATE DRIVER'S LICENSE.
ar:HB1913.summary: Lets people 16 and older, including adults, get an intermediate driver's license; it expires and can renew as a regular license once the holder has had 12 months free of serious accidents or violations and, if licensed before 18, has turned 18.

ar:HB1915.title: TO DIRECT THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES TO REQUEST A BROAD-BASED CATEGORICAL ELIGIBILITY WAIVER FOR THE SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM; AND TO AMEND THE ASSET LIMITS UNDER THE PROGRAM.
ar:HB1915.summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to request a federal broad-based categorical eligibility waiver for SNAP, sets the asset limit at $6,000 adjusted for inflation every two years, and repeals the temporary asset-limit increase for households.

ar:HB1916.title: TO AMEND THE PROTECTING MINORS FROM MEDICAL MALPRACTICE ACT OF 2023; AND TO INCLUDE GENDER-AFFIRMING INTERVENTIONS AS A RIGHT OF ACTION FOR MEDICAL MALPRACTICE.
ar:HB1916.summary: Defines "gender-affirming intervention" (including puberty blockers and cross-sex hormone therapy) and adds it to the minor medical malpractice law, making healthcare and mental health professionals who perform it on a minor liable for injury and subject to its consent and defense rules.

ar:HB1917.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS STUDENT-ATHLETE PUBLICITY RIGHTS ACT; AND TO AMEND THE LAW RELATED TO ATHLETIC PROGRAM FUNDING.
ar:HB1917.summary: Lets colleges and their foundations pay student-athletes for, and license, their name, image and likeness; lets schools rescind benefits over conflicting contracts; exempts school-paid income from state income tax; makes athletes' agreement details exempt from public-records disclosure.

ar:HB1918.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING SPECIE OR LEGAL TENDER; TO AUTHORIZE THE USE OF A BULLION DEPOSITORY; AND TO ALLOW FOR A PRECIOUS METALS-BACKED ELECTRONIC SYSTEM.
ar:HB1918.summary: Defines bullion depositories, precious metals-backed electronic payment systems and "transactional gold and silver" (redeemable electronic representations of physical gold or silver) in the specie law, and directs the Chief Fiscal Officer to adopt rules approving payment-system vendors.

ar:HB1919.title: TO CREATE THE PUBLIC SCHOOL ACCESS AND TRANSPARENCY ACT; AND TO REQUIRE PUBLIC ACCESS TO LEARNING MATERIALS.
ar:HB1919.summary: Adds school learning materials to public records under the Freedom of Information Act and bars schools from denying access on copyright grounds; recipients may not publish or distribute copyrighted materials beyond inspection and limited copies.

ar:HB1921.title: TO AMEND THE CHILD WELFARE AGENCY LICENSING ACT; TO AMEND THE TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION PROCESS FOR FOSTER PARENTS; AND TO STREAMLINE THE PROCESS OF TRAINING AND CERTIFYING RELATIVES AS FOSTER PARENTS.
ar:HB1921.summary: Bars the Division of Children and Family Services from requiring more than 15 hours of initial and 6 hours of annual foster home training, and directs it to streamline training rules for provisional foster homes.

ar:HB1922.title: TO AMEND THE CONSOLIDATED INCENTIVE ACT OF 2003; TO CREATE AN INCOME TAX CREDIT FOR RELOCATING CORPORATE HEADQUARTERS TO THIS STATE; AND TO ENCOURAGE CORPORATIONS TO RELOCATE TO ARKANSAS.
ar:HB1922.summary: Lets the director award a corporate headquarters relocating to Arkansas an income tax credit of up to 50% of new-employee payroll, requiring 150 to 300 new jobs by county tier, and repeals the technology-based enterprise investment credit.

ar:HB1923.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS TOURISM DEVELOPMENT ACT; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING NATURAL STATE INITIATIVE OPPORTUNITY ZONES.
ar:HB1923.summary: Lowers the minimum investment for tourism attraction projects in Natural State Initiative Opportunity Zones to $50,000 in high-unemployment counties and $150,000 elsewhere, and widens zone boundaries from one-eighth mile to one mile outside parks and sites.

ar:HB1925.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING ABSENTEE BALLOTS; TO AMEND THE ABSENTEE BALLOT VOTER STATEMENT; AND TO REQUIRE A WITNESS FOR THE SIGNATURE OF AN ABSENTEE VOTER STATEMENT.
ar:HB1925.summary: Requires an adult witness to an absentee voter's signing of the sworn statement, except for voters unable to reach the polls due to illness, disability or religious observance, long-term care residents, and military voters or dependents living outside the county; revises voter statement wording.

ar:HB1926.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE SUSPENSION, REVOCATION, OR NONRENEWAL OF A PERSON'S DRIVER'S LICENSE FOR FAILURE TO PAY A COURT-ORDERED FINE; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING A DEFENDANT'S INABILITY TO PAY A COURT-ORDERED FINE.
ar:HB1926.summary: Requires defendants who claim they cannot pay a court fine to give the court details of monthly income and expenses, and requires courts to consider this before requesting a driver's license suspension, revocation, or nonrenewal for nonpayment.

ar:HB1927.title: TO AMEND A PROVISION OF ACTS 2025, NO. 408, CONCERNING THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF ACTS 2025, NO. 408; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1927.summary: Corrects the effective date in the emergency clause of Acts 2025, No. 408 from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2025, and declares an emergency.

ar:HB1928.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS SOIL NUTRIENT APPLICATION AND POULTRY LITTER UTILIZATION ACT.
ar:HB1928.summary: Bars civil or criminal liability for applying nutrients consistently with an approved nutrient or poultry litter management plan, and bars lawsuits or criminal charges based on administrative violations, except commission administrative fines.

ar:HB1929.title: TO CREATE THE RECOGNIZING JUDEA AND SAMARIA ACT; AND TO PROHIBIT STATE AGENCIES FROM USING THE TERM "WEST BANK" IN OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT MATERIALS.
ar:HB1929.summary: Bars state agencies from using the term "West Bank" in official materials, with the stated intent of using "Judea and Samaria" instead; an agency's executive head may waive the bar and must explain the waiver to the legislature.

ar:HB1930.title: TO MANDATE MINIMUM REIMBURSEMENT LEVELS FOR HEALTHCARE SERVICES.
ar:HB1930.summary: Requires health benefit plans to pay providers a minimum reimbursement level set by the Insurance Commissioner from neighboring states' commercial-to-Medicare price ratios, phased in from 45% in 2026 to 100% in 2030; insurers must document compliance.

ar:HB1931.title: TO CREATE THE RECIDIVISM REDUCTION SYSTEM WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1931.summary: Creates a Recidivism Reduction System within the Department of Corrections, requiring a risk and needs assessment at intake, individualized case plans, periodic reassessment, evidence-based programming, and incentives for inmates to participate.

ar:HB1933.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING A SCHOOL DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS; AND TO CREATE A RECALL ELECTION AND PETITION FOR REMOVAL FOR A MEMBER OF A SCHOOL DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS.
ar:HB1933.summary: Makes school district board members subject to recall by majority vote of voters, on a petition signed by at least 35% of eligible electors, with signatures verified by the county clerk and the election held at the next school board election.

ar:HB1934.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS FORWARD ENGAGEMENT COMMITTEE ACT; AND TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS FORWARD ENGAGEMENT COMMITTEE WORKING GROUP.
ar:HB1934.summary: Creates a working group, the Arkansas Forward Engagement Committee, to review state spending for waste and inefficiency and to review unnecessary or burdensome regulations.

ar:HB1935.title: TO CREATE A MODERNIZATION AND AUTOMATION TAX CREDIT TO ENCOURAGE INVESTMENT BY EXISTING BUSINESSES WITHIN THE STATE.
ar:HB1935.summary: Replaces the retention sales-and-use-tax credit with a modernization and automation credit of up to 5% of project costs for Arkansas businesses incurring at least $25 million and receiving a positive cost-benefit analysis; caps credits used at $2 million per applicant yearly.

ar:HB1937.title: TO AMEND THE METHOD OF VALUATION FOR MINERAL RIGHTS UNDER ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION, ARTICLE 16, § 5; AND TO CLARIFY THE METHOD OF VALUATION FOR OIL AND GAS WELL PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT.
ar:HB1937.summary: Extends the oil well property tax valuation rules to gas wells, applying the uniform expense allowance and income approach per 1,000 cubic feet of gas as well as per barrel of oil, for assessment years starting January 1, 2025.

ar:HB1938.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING THE CREATION OF DISTRICT STRATEGIC PLANS AND THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE DIVISION OF ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION.
ar:HB1938.summary: Requires districts and open-enrollment charters to submit annual district strategic plans to the state education division, which must create a unified application system for state and federal plans; ends district support plans and moves parental involvement plans into school improvement plans.

ar:HB1939.title: TO AMEND ELIGIBILITY FOR TEACHER INCENTIVE AND MERIT PAY; TO AMEND REQUIREMENTS FOR SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS; AND TO AMEND SCHOOL DISTRICT REQUIREMENTS UNDER THE MERIT TEACHER INCENTIVE FUND PROGRAM.
ar:HB1939.summary: Bars a person from receiving National Board certification bonus funds unless requirements were met by July 1, 2025, allows digital summative evaluations, and requires schools to give an annual rating in years without a summative evaluation, tied to Merit Teacher Incentive Fund eligibility.

ar:HB1941.title: CONCERNING DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS; AND TO PROTECT ARKANSAS STUDENTS BY ENSURING THE EFFICIENT DISPOSITION OF ETHICS COMPLAINTS AGAINST TEACHERS.
ar:HB1941.summary: Limits Professional Licensure Standards Board members to three terms; lets the board order educator ethics sanctions, from warnings to license revocation, appealable to the State Board of Education; repeals the School Worker Defense Program Advisory Board and Academic Facilities Review Board.

ar:HB1942.title: TO REQUIRE CERTAIN REIMBURSEMENT RATES FOR HOME- AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES WITHIN RISK-BASED PROVIDER ORGANIZATIONS.
ar:HB1942.summary: Requires a rate study by October 1, 2025 for home- and community-based services in Medicaid risk-based provider organizations, sets the resulting rates as minimum payments, and lets increases over 10% be phased in over two years.

ar:HB1943.title: TO AMEND THE MEDICAID PROVIDER-LED ORGANIZED CARE ACT; TO IMPROVE THE ENROLLMENT AND SELECTION PROCESS IN RISK-BASED PROVIDER ORGANIZATIONS; AND TO EMPOWER BENEFICIARIES WITH INFORMATION.
ar:HB1943.summary: Requires Medicaid risk-based provider organizations to keep an online quality rating system (service wait times, caseloads, member satisfaction) and real-time provider directories, and requires the Department of Human Services to run a beneficiary support office, from January 1, 2026.

ar:HB1944.title: TO AUTHORIZE THE ISSUANCE AND RENEWAL OF A SPECIAL LICENSE PLATE TO PROMOTE AND SUPPORT THE ARKANSAS EMS FOUNDATION; AND TO REPEAL THE GRAND LODGE OF ARKANSAS SPECIAL LICENSE PLATE.
ar:HB1944.summary: Authorizes an Arkansas EMS Foundation special license plate, costing a $25 contribution to the foundation plus a $10 handling fee on top of registration, and repeals the Grand Lodge of Arkansas special plate.

ar:HB1945.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS OPPORTUNITY PUBLIC SCHOOL CHOICE ACT; TO AMEND THE PUBLIC SCHOOL CHOICE ACT OF 2015; AND TO ALLOW A STUDENT TO TRANSFER TO ANOTHER PUBLIC SCHOOL WITHIN HIS OR HER RESIDENT DISTRICT.
ar:HB1945.summary: Lets students transfer to another public school within their resident district under the school choice laws, requires districts to adopt and post a transfer policy, and lets a district claim lack of capacity once 95% of grade-level seats are filled.

ar:HB1946.title: TO REQUIRE HUMAN GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS.
ar:HB1946.summary: Requires public schools with grades 6 through 12 to include, from 2025-26, human growth and development instruction with an ultrasound video of early fetal development and an animation of fertilization through birth in classes on human biology, contraception or sexually transmitted diseases.

ar:HB1949.title: TO ADD MEDICAL, EMERGENCY MEDICAL, AND AMBULANCE SERVICES TO THE LIST OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES FOR PURPOSES OF PROCUREMENT.
ar:HB1949.summary: Adds medical, emergency medical and ambulance services to the professional consultant services that political subdivisions must procure without competitive bidding.

ar:HB1951.title: TO SET FORTH AUTHORIZED DOMAIN EXTENSIONS FOR HIGHER EDUCATION AND GOVERNMENT WEBSITES.
ar:HB1951.summary: Requires public accredited colleges to use .edu, and municipalities and state agencies to use .gov (or .mil, for agencies), for websites and email addresses, with exceptions for internal, temporary, and partnership sites, and waivers.

ar:HB1952.title: TO ASSIST THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE STATE ATHLETIC COMMISSION; TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO THE STATE ATHLETIC COMMISSION TO CONTINUE ITS MISSION TO PROMOTE A ROBUST, HEALTHY, AND SAFE COMBATIVE SPORTS INDUSTRY.
ar:HB1952.summary: Places professional wrestling events with 1,500 or more attendees under State Athletic Commission authority, allows referee and judge training from other commission-approved organizations, and requires promoters to reimburse the commission's event costs, including inspectors up to $125 a day.

ar:HB1954.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS BEHAVIOR ANALYST REGISTRATION ACT; AND TO INCLUDE QUALIFIED BEHAVIOR ANALYSTS UNDER THE ARKANSAS BEHAVIOR ANALYST REGISTRATION ACT.
ar:HB1954.summary: Creates registration of behavior analysts by the Arkansas Psychology Board and bars unregistered people from calling themselves registered behavior analysts, with fines for violations.

ar:HB1955.title: TO REPEAL THE SHIELDED OUTDOOR LIGHTING ACT.
ar:HB1955.summary: Repeals the Shielded Outdoor Lighting Act, including its rule that public funds not install unshielded outdoor lights, its mercury-bulb landfill rule, and its utility shielded-lighting option.

ar:HB1956.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS NIGHTTIME ENVIRONMENT PROTECTION ACT.
ar:HB1956.summary: Bars state agencies, counties, cities and investor-owned utilities from installing new or replacement street or parking lighting unless fixtures are full cutoff, within recommended brightness, and at most 3,000 K in residential areas or 4,000 K elsewhere, with exemptions.

ar:HB1957.title: TO AMEND THE UNSOLICITED COMMERCIAL AND SEXUALLY EXPLICIT ELECTRONIC MAIL PREVENTION ACT TO INCLUDE UNSOLICITED COMMERCIAL AND SEXUALLY EXPLICIT TEXT MESSAGES.
ar:HB1957.summary: Extends Arkansas's unsolicited commercial and sexually explicit email law to text messages, requiring sender identification and opt-out, and allows phone service providers to block violating messages.

ar:HB1958.title: TO REQUIRE PUBLIC ENTITIES TO CREATE A POLICY CONCERNING THE AUTHORIZED USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
ar:HB1958.summary: Requires public entities to adopt a policy defining authorized use of artificial intelligence and automated decision tools and requiring an authorized human employee to make final decisions, and to train employees on it, in addition to existing technology and cybersecurity policies.

ar:HB1959.title: TO ABOLISH THE USE OF A WRIT OF SCIRE FACIAS AS THE MEANS OF REVIVING AN OUTSTANDING JUDGMENT; TO ALLOW A JUDGMENT TO BE REVIVED BY NOTICE; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE FEES TO BE CHARGED BY CLERKS OF THE CIRCUIT COURTS.
ar:HB1959.summary: Replaces the writ of scire facias with a filed notice to revive an outstanding judgment, served on the debtor by first class mail, continuing the judgment lien for another ten years.

ar:HB1960.title: TO PROVIDE THAT THE LESSEE OF A LEASED MOTOR VEHICLE IS THE OWNER FOR PURPOSES OF THE ASSESSMENT AND PAYMENT OF PROPERTY TAXES; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING LOCAL SALES AND USE TAXES ON CERTAIN TANGIBLE PERSONAL PROPERTY.
ar:HB1960.summary: Treats the lessee of a motor vehicle leased over 30 days as its owner for personal property tax assessment, and applies the $2,500 local sales tax cap to total periodic lease payments.

ar:HB1961.title: TO ALLOW MEDICAL PROVIDERS TEMPORARY EXEMPTIONS FROM FEDERAL INFORMATION-BLOCKING REGULATIONS TO SAFEGUARD PATIENTS DURING INFORMATION DISCLOSURE; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1961.summary: Lets a medical provider temporarily withhold medical records from a patient for up to 30 days to review them and schedule a discussion, if it reasonably believes immediate release could adversely affect the patient's health or safety.

ar:HB1963.title: TO CLARIFY THAT AN ADVANCED PRACTICE REGISTERED NURSE WHO PRESCRIBES A STIMULANT MAY SUBSTITUTE A THERAPEUTICALLY EQUIVALENT MEDICATION.
ar:HB1963.summary: Lets an advanced practice registered nurse substitute a therapeutically equivalent medication when continuing a physician-initiated stimulant prescription, and requires notifying the original prescribing physician of the substitution.

ar:HB1964.title: TO MOVE THE CHILD WELFARE OMBUDSMAN DIVISION AND THE JUVENILE OMBUDSMAN DIVISION TO THE DEPARTMENT OF INSPECTOR GENERAL; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:HB1964.summary: Moves the Child Welfare Ombudsman and Juvenile Ombudsman from their current agencies to a new Division of Ombudsmen within the Department of Inspector General, reporting to its secretary.

ar:HB1965.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS HEALTHY FOOD RETAIL ACT OF 2025; AND TO PROVIDE FINANCIAL INCENTIVES FOR HEALTHY FOOD RETAILERS IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES.
