ar:SB586.summary: Requires a constitutional amendment proposed under Article 5, Section 1 of the Arkansas Constitution to receive at least two-thirds of the votes cast to take effect, instead of a majority.

ar:SB59.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - EDUCATIONAL TELEVISION DIVISION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB59.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Education - Educational Television Division for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:SB590.title: TO CREATE THE RECIDIVISM REDUCTION SYSTEM WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB590.summary: Creates a Recidivism Reduction System in the Department of Corrections requiring a risk and needs assessment at intake, individual case plans, periodic reassessment, evidence-based programming, and incentives for inmate participation.

ar:SB591.title: TO PROHIBIT RACE-SELECTION ABORTION IN THIS STATE; AND TO CREATE THE RACE DISCRIMINATION BY ABORTION PROHIBITION ACT.
ar:SB591.summary: Bans abortions sought solely because of the unborn child's race, requires providers to ask whether the woman knows the race and request her pregnancy records, and sets criminal, civil and license penalties. Takes effect only if the state's abortion bans are enjoined or amended.

ar:SB596.title: TO AMEND THE LAW REGARDING ENERGY; TO ESTABLISH A STATE ENERGY POLICY; TO REGULATE RETIREMENT OF DISPATCHABLE ELECTRIC GENERATION FACILITIES; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB596.summary: Sets a state energy policy for an adequate, reliable, dispatchable electric system and requires utilities to get Public Service Commission approval to retire dispatchable plants of 100 MW or larger, with a presumption against retirement and a ruling within 180 days.

ar:SB597.title: TO CREATE THE CRIMINAL OFFENSE OF THREAT OF HARM UPON A FINANCIAL INSTITUTION EMPLOYEE.
ar:SB597.summary: Creates a Class B misdemeanor offense of purposely engaging in conduct that threatens or endangers a bank, credit union, savings and loan or mortgage lender employee while at work.

ar:SB598.title: TO AMEND VARIOUS LAWS RELATED TO THE DIVISION OF WORKFORCE SERVICES; AND TO AMEND THE DEFINITION OF "EMPLOYEE" UNDER THE WORKERS' COMPENSATION LAW RESULTING FROM INITIATED ACT 4 OF 1948.
ar:SB598.summary: Revises workforce services laws, replacing the "twenty-factor test" for employment status with factors enumerated by the IRS, shortening the short-term layoff period from 10 to 3 weeks, and updating unemployment and workforce program provisions.

ar:SB599.title: TO ELIMINATE INTERLOCUTORY DECREES OF ADOPTION; AND TO AMEND THE REVISED UNIFORM ADOPTION ACT.
ar:SB599.summary: Eliminates interlocutory decrees of adoption so a court issues only a final decree, and updates related laws; applies only to decrees entered after the act takes effect, and earlier interlocutory decrees stay valid.

ar:SB60.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS PUBLIC DEFENDER COMMISSION REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:SB60.summary: Reappropriates up to $167,641 in unspent funds for the Public Defender Commission's expenses on resentencing juveniles sentenced to mandatory life without parole, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:SB600.title: TO REGULATE CONTRACTS; TO MANDATE CONTRACTUAL PROVISIONS FOR CERTAIN CONTRACTS; AND TO CLARIFY PROPER JURISDICTION FOR CERTAIN CONTACTS.
ar:SB600.summary: Provides that Arkansas law and Arkansas courts govern contracts of $100,000 or less made in Arkansas by an Arkansas resident to buy or finance real property, or personal property used as a dwelling, despite any contrary contract term.

ar:SB601.title: TO CREATE A PATHWAY FOR A GRADUATE OF A FOREIGN MEDICAL SCHOOL TO BE LICENSED IN THIS STATE IF HE OR SHE IS OFFERED FULL-TIME EMPLOYMENT AS A PHYSICIAN FROM A HEALTHCARE PROVIDER.
ar:SB601.summary: Creates a one-year renewable provisional medical license for foreign-trained physicians with a full-time job offer from a provider serving an underserved population, an active foreign license, recent practice and ECFMG certification. Requires three years with that employer and a sponsoring physician.

ar:SB602.title: TO PROHIBIT INSURANCE COMPANIES AND APPRAISERS FROM REQUIRING AN INSURED TO USE CERTAIN FACILITIES TO REPAIR OR REPLACE DAMAGED MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY GLASS; AND TO PROVIDE PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS.
ar:SB602.summary: Bars insurers and appraisers from requiring an insured to use a specific facility or glass shop for motor vehicle safety glass repair, or from saying that using another shop may cause delays.

ar:SB604.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE REGARDING THE COURSE CHOICE PROGRAM.
ar:SB604.summary: Changes the Course Choice Program: adds provider types, bars D- or F-rated public schools from offering courses, limits eligible students to grades 6-12, sets the course payment cap at 8 percent of per-pupil funding, and moves the rulemaking deadline to 2026-27.

ar:SB605.title: TO CREATE THE DELTA TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL EXCISE TAX ACT; AND TO TAX DELTA TETRAHYDROCANNABINOL PRODUCTS.
ar:SB605.summary: Imposes a 50% excise tax on gross receipts from sales of delta tetrahydrocannabinol products, including hemp-derived THC products, collected and administered like sales tax.

ar:SB608.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING RUNOFF ELECTIONS FOR COUNTY AND MUNICIPAL OFFICERS.
ar:SB608.summary: Repeals the exception that lets a municipal candidate with 40% of the vote and 20% more than the runner-up avoid a runoff, so municipal races without a majority go to a runoff, as county races do.

ar:SB61.title: TO AUTHORIZE VETERINARY TELEMEDICINE IN THIS STATE; AND TO SET CERTAIN STANDARDS FOR VETERINARY TELEMEDICINE.
ar:SB61.summary: Authorizes veterinary telemedicine by licensed veterinarians for animals in Arkansas. In emergency or urgent cases a veterinarian may skip a prior client relationship if one is established within 7 days for small animals or 21 days for large animals.

ar:SB610.title: TO AMEND THE GENERATING ARKANSAS JOBS ACT OF 2025; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB610.summary: Extends from 60 to 90 days the Public Service Commission's deadline to review annual update filings under the Generating Arkansas Jobs Act of 2025, revises the approval standard for cooperative rider rate schedules, and takes effect immediately.

ar:SB611.title: TO AMEND THE SOCIAL MEDIA SAFETY ACT.
ar:SB611.summary: Amends the Social Media Safety Act: lowers the minor age from 18 to 16, requires platforms to avoid addictive practices and block age-verification circumvention, raises the penalty from $2,500 to $10,000 per violation, lets parents sue, and creates a Crimes Against Children Fund.

ar:SB613.title: TO CREATE AN ELECTION PROCEDURE TO DETERMINE FLUORIDATION OF A PUBLIC WATER SYSTEM.
ar:SB613.summary: Creates a fluoridation election for public water systems serving 5,000 or more people, called by petition of registered voters equal to 38% of those served; if a majority votes to prohibit it, the system stops fluoridating within 30 days.

ar:SB614.title: TO AMEND THE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT OF 1967; AND TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING OPEN PUBLIC MEETINGS.
ar:SB614.summary: Limits courts to invalidating a government body's bond-issuing action over open-meetings violations to 30 days after the action; later findings require the body to cure the violation or members to pay $1,000 penalties each.

ar:SB615.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING ENERGY; AND TO REGULATE NONEXPORT FACILITIES.
ar:SB615.summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to adopt rules by March 1, 2026 for nonexport facilities, which generate power on site without intentionally feeding it to the utility, including safety standards and expedited interconnection review.

ar:SB618.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS STUDENT DUE PROCESS AND PROTECTION ACT.
ar:SB618.summary: Requires colleges to advise students under investigation or discipline that they may have an attorney, and shortens the deadline to appeal a decision from 25 days to 7 days.

ar:SB619.title: CONCERNING THE FORMATION OF AN ISOLATED SCHOOL DISTRICT.
ar:SB619.summary: Lets an isolated school detach from a district it was consolidated into and become its own district, after a petition signed by 350 voters or 51 percent of voters in its area and a local election; sets a five-member board.

ar:SB620.title: TO PROVIDE A SAFETY VALVE AND APPEAL RIGHT FOR A MINOR DEFENDANT WHO IS ALSO A VICTIM OF HUMAN TRAFFICKING; AND TO AMEND THE HUMAN TRAFFICKING ACT OF 2013.
ar:SB620.summary: Allows people 17 or younger to raise trafficking victimhood as an affirmative defense to nonviolent offenses, and requires courts to consider trafficking, abuse and trauma when transferring juvenile cases or sentencing people for offenses committed as minors.

ar:SB621.title: TO CLARIFY ENFORCEMENT PROVISIONS AGAINST A HEALTHCARE INSURER; TO RETROACTIVELY APPLY TO A HEALTHCARE CONTRACT FOR THE BENEFIT OF A TEMPORARY HOSPITAL FACILITY; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB621.summary: Requires health insurers to offer temporary hospital facilities a contract within 30 days at standard terms and reimburse them at licensed-hospital rates, applying retroactively to Executive Order 20-06, with Insurance Commissioner enforcement.

ar:SB624.title: TO AMEND THE ARKANSAS OPPORTUNITY PUBLIC SCHOOL CHOICE ACT; TO AMEND THE PUBLIC SCHOOL CHOICE ACT OF 2015; AND TO ALLOW A STUDENT TO TRANSFER TO ANOTHER PUBLIC SCHOOL WITHIN HIS OR HER RESIDENT DISTRICT.
ar:SB624.summary: Extends the Opportunity and Public School Choice Acts to transfers between public schools within a student's resident district, adds a parent's belief that a transfer serves the student's best interest as a ground, and lets districts claim lack of capacity at 95% of seats filled.

ar:SB625.title: TO AMEND PROVISIONS OF THE ARKANSAS CODE CONCERNING THE ARKANSAS CHILDREN'S EDUCATIONAL FREEDOM ACCOUNT PROGRAM; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB625.summary: Changes the Educational Freedom Account program to define allowed education expenses, including capping transportation and extracurricular costs at 25% of a student's account funds each, and sets application and account-fund rules. Declares an emergency.

ar:SB627.title: TO ASSIST THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE CODE ENFORCEMENT SECTION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND LICENSING AND THE STATE'S ELECTRICIAN, HVACR, ELEVATOR, AND BOILER SAFETY LAWS.
ar:SB627.summary: Revises electrician, HVACR, elevator and boiler safety laws, including repealing the air conditioning electrician and electrical contractor licenses, extending from 10 to 75 feet the HVACR wiring work allowed without an electrician license, and raising maximum civil penalties to $1,000 per day.

ar:SB629.title: TO ALLOW AN OFFICER OF A CLOSELY HELD CORPORATION TO REPRESENT THE CORPORATION IN COURT FOR THE PURPOSE OF EVICTION PROCEEDINGS AND UNLAWFUL DETAINER PROCEEDINGS.
ar:SB629.summary: Allows an officer of a closely held corporation with fewer than 20 shareholders to represent it in eviction and unlawful detainer court proceedings without being an attorney.

ar:SB63.title: TO AMEND ARKANSAS LAW CONCERNING REPORTS BY THE SECRETARIES OF CABINET-LEVEL DEPARTMENTS ON THE STATE OF THEIR DEPARTMENTS.
ar:SB63.summary: Repeals the requirement that the secretaries of several cabinet-level departments give the Legislative Council an oral report on their department's state by November 1 of each odd-numbered year.

ar:SB632.title: TO AMEND THE FOOD, DRUG, AND COSMETIC ACT; AND TO REQUIRE WARNING LABELS FOR HAIR RELAXERS THAT CONTAIN CERTAIN CHEMICALS.
ar:SB632.summary: Requires hair relaxers sold in Arkansas that contain a carcinogen or reproductive toxicant to carry a warning label in at least 12-point type stating the chemical is known to cause cancer, birth defects or other reproductive harm.

ar:SB634.title: TO CREATE THE DIVISION OF INTERSCHOLASTIC ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE DIVISION OF ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION.
ar:SB634.summary: Creates a Division of Interscholastic Activities within the state education department, led by an assistant commissioner, to oversee grade 6-12 sports and other competitive activities at public and charter schools, and at private schools that opt in.

ar:SB635.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES; AND TO AUTHORIZE BOTTLE LOCKERS IN CERTAIN RESTAURANTS.
ar:SB635.summary: Allows restaurants in wet territory with an on-premises alcohol permit to offer guests bottle lockers for storing purchased alcoholic beverages for later consumption, for a storage fee.

ar:SB636.title: AN ACT TO TRANSFER FUNDS; DEFINE THE MONIES TO BE AVAILABLE IN THE RESTRICTED RESERVE FUND; AND ALLOW ADDITIONAL FUNDS TO BE MADE AVAILABLE FOR STATE DEPARTMENTS, AGENCIES AND INSTITUTIONS; AND TO DECLARE AND EMERGENCY.
ar:SB636.summary: Moves unobligated balances from several set-asides and funds into the Restricted Reserve Fund, then sets aside about $437 million there for listed purposes such as Medicaid, education freedom accounts and school facilities. Declares an emergency.

ar:SB637.title: TO AMEND THE REVENUE STABILIZATION LAW; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB637.summary: Amends the Revenue Stabilization Law to set how general revenues are divided monthly among state funds and agencies for fiscal 2025-2026 and later, with the first allocation tier capped at about $6.49 billion. Declares an emergency.

ar:SB638.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE COLLECTION OF SALES AND USE TAX ON THE SALE OF A NEW OR USED MOTORBOAT; AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE DIRECT PAYMENT OF SALES AND USE TAX ON A MOTORBOAT SOLD BY A MOTORBOAT DEALER.
ar:SB638.summary: Requires motorboat buyers to pay sales and use tax directly to the Department of Finance and Administration when registering a new or used boat bought from a dealer, rather than through the dealer, with a 10% penalty for late payment.

ar:SB639.title: TO CREATE THE ARKANSAS WIND ENERGY DEVELOPMENT ACT.
ar:SB639.summary: Creates the Arkansas Wind Energy Development Act: requires Public Service Commission permits ($2,500 filing fee), turbine setbacks from nonparticipating neighbors' property lines (greater of 3.5 times turbine height or 2,500 feet), one mile from schools, towns and other listed places, and an environmental impact assessment.

ar:SB64.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - EDUCATIONAL TELEVISION DIVISION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB64.summary: Appropriates about $18.1 million for fiscal 2025-26 for the Department of Education's Educational Television Division (Arkansas PBS) and sets its maximum staffing and salary levels.

ar:SB640.title: TO RECONSTITUTE THE STATE LIBRARY BOARD.
ar:SB640.summary: Ends the terms of all current State Library Board members and has the Governor appoint seven new members with staggered terms of one, three, five, and seven years drawn by lot.

ar:SB65.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF SHARED ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES - OFFICE OF STATE TECHNOLOGY REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:SB65.summary: Reappropriates up to $1,357,050 in unspent funds to replace the uninterruptible power supply at the state Data Center West facility in Little Rock, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:SB67.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS FOR MEDICAL SCIENCES SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:SB67.summary: Appropriates an extra $5 million for fiscal 2025-2026 to the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences for its High-Risk Pregnancy Program and IDHI Stroke Program, and transfers $5 million from the General Revenue Allotment Reserve Fund to pay for it.

ar:SB68.title: TO ALLOW VETERINARY TECHNICIANS, VETERINARY TECHNOLOGISTS, AND VETERINARY TECHNICIAN SPECIALISTS TO GO TO A LOCATION OTHER THAN THE LOCATION OF THE SUPERVISING VETERINARIAN TO PROVIDE SERVICES BASED ON AN EMERGENCY CALL.
ar:SB68.summary: Lets a veterinarian who indirectly supervises a veterinary technician, technologist or technician specialist authorize them to go to a different location to provide services for an emergency call.

ar:SB69.title: AN ACT FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS - DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:SB69.summary: Appropriates an additional $30 million in cash funds for capital improvements at the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture for fiscal 2025-26.

ar:SB7.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - STATE INSURANCE DEPARTMENT APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB7.summary: Appropriates money for the State Insurance Department for the 2026-27 fiscal year, covering operations, fraud investigation, prepaid funeral programs, continuing education and state and public school employee claims.

ar:SB70.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:SB70.summary: Reappropriates unspent balances of up to $114 million and $30,031,020 for replacing the Department of Health's main facility, effective July 1, 2026.

ar:SB72.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - ARKANSAS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION REAPPROPRIATION.
ar:SB72.summary: Carries unspent balances of earlier capital-improvement appropriations for the Arkansas Economic Development Commission into the next fiscal year, effective July 1, 2026, including up to $129,082 for minority-owned business development.

ar:SB73.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE - ARKANSAS ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION.
ar:SB73.summary: Appropriates an extra $10 million for fiscal 2025-2026 to the Rural Services Division's Community Assistance Grant Program of the Arkansas Economic Development Commission, and transfers $10 million from the General Revenue Allotment Reserve Fund to fund it.

ar:SB74.title: AN ACT TO MAKE AN APPROPRIATION FOR THE PAYMENT OF APPROVED CLAIMS.
ar:SB74.summary: Appropriates money from several state funds to pay claims against the State of Arkansas to named payees, through the Revenue Services Division, the State Insurance Department and other agencies.

ar:SB75.title: TO AMEND THE REVENUE STABILIZATION LAW; TO CREATE FUNDS; TO MAKE TRANSFERS TO AND FROM FUNDS AND FUND ACCOUNTS; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB75.summary: Sets 2026-27 revenue allocations to state funds, including $6.64 billion in the first allocation tier, and transfers $100 million to a Medicaid set-aside, $70 million to a Children's Educational Freedom Account set-aside, and other amounts to reserve set-asides.

ar:SB76.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE AND ADMINISTRATION - DISBURSING OFFICER APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB76.summary: Appropriates $2 million from a cash fund to the Department of Finance and Administration for capital-improvement matching grants to county extension offices, through the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027.

ar:SB77.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - EDUCATIONAL TELEVISION DIVISION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB77.summary: Appropriates $550,000 for fiscal 2026-27 to pay the Educational Television Division's Public Broadcasting Service membership dues, matched one-to-one with private donations that must be certified before funds are paid.

ar:SB78.title: TO REQUIRE THAT THE DRIVER’S INSTRUCTION MANUAL AND THE DRIVER’S LICENSE EXAMINATION INCLUDE INFORMATION ABOUT THE SAFE OPERATION OF A MOTOR VEHICLE IN A HIGHWAY WORK ZONE.
ar:SB78.summary: Requires the written driver's license test to include questions on safe driving in highway work zones, and adds statistics, testimonials from construction workers and families, slowing-down guidance and a question-and-answer section to the driver's manual's work zone content.

ar:SB8.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB8.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Commerce for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:SB80.title: AN ACT FOR THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR - LEGISLATIVE LIAISONS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2024-2025 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB80.summary: Appropriates $226,250 to the Governor's office for fiscal 2024-25 and authorizes one lead legislative liaison at up to $250 per diem and nine liaisons at up to $200 per diem on days the General Assembly is in regular session.

ar:SB81.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF PARKS, HERITAGE, AND TOURISM - STATE PARKS AND TOURISM DIVISIONS APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB81.summary: Sets staffing limits and appropriates funds for fiscal year 2025-26 operations of the state parks and tourism divisions of the Department of Parks, Heritage, and Tourism.

ar:SB83.title: TO MANDATE COVERAGE FOR BREAST RECONSTRUCTION SURGERIES; TO REQUIRE PRIOR AUTHORIZATION FOR BREAST RECONSTRUCTION SURGERIES; AND TO ESTABLISH A MINIMUM REIMBURSEMENT RATE FOR BREAST RECONSTRUCTION SURGERIES.
ar:SB83.summary: Requires health plans, from January 1, 2026, to cover breast reconstruction surgery at in-network cost sharing, requires insurers to require prior authorization, and sets out-of-network reimbursement when an insurer has no participating provider.

ar:SB88.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION - DIVISION OF HIGHER EDUCATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB88.summary: Appropriates money for the Division of Higher Education for fiscal year 2025-2026, including $4.5 million for general operations, $71.6 million for student assistance grants and scholarships, and funds for career education, AmeriCorps, and Northwest Technical Institute.

ar:SB89.title: TO AMEND THE INFORMATION THAT A SCHOOL DISTRICT SHALL PROVIDE ELECTRONICALLY WITH RESPECT TO ITS SCHOOL DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS.
ar:SB89.summary: Requires school districts to post board meeting minutes, including emergency meetings, within 24 hours of approval; agendas 24 hours before regular meetings and two hours before special or emergency ones; and board members' names, emails, positions and terms.

ar:SB9.title: AN ACT FOR THE ARKANSAS MINORITY HEALTH INITIATIVE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH - ARKANSAS MINORITY HEALTH COMMISSION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2026-2027 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB9.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal 2026-2027 for the Arkansas Minority Health Initiative of the Department of Health, including salaries, operations and screening and treatment programs, and sets its maximum of six staff positions.

ar:SB90.title: TO REQUIRE MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC TO BE AFFORDED THE OPPORTUNITY TO PRESENT PUBLIC COMMENT AT EACH MEETING OF A SCHOOL DISTRICT BOARD OF DIRECTORS.
ar:SB90.summary: Requires school district boards to let district residents, parents or guardians of students, and district employees give public comment on matters within the board's authority before it considers business or goes into executive session.

ar:SB91.title: TO PROVIDE THAT LOCAL GOVERNMENTAL UNITS SHALL HAVE NO AUTHORITY TO REGULATE OR CONTROL THE AMOUNT CHARGED FOR A RENTAL APPLICATION FEE OR RENTAL DEPOSIT FOR PRIVATE RESIDENTIAL OR COMMERCIAL PROPERTY.
ar:SB91.summary: Extends the existing ban on local rent-control ordinances to also cover rental application fees and rental deposits for private residential or commercial property.

ar:SB92.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSFORMATION AND SHARED SERVICES APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB92.summary: Sets the 2025-26 fiscal-year staffing limits, pay grades, and appropriations for the Department of Transformation and Shared Services.

ar:SB93.title: AN ACT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION APPROPRIATION FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR.
ar:SB93.summary: Appropriates money for personal services and operating expenses of the Department of Education for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, and sets its maximum staff positions and salary rates.

ar:SB94.title: TO AMEND THE REQUIREMENT FOR NEW ALL-TERRAIN VEHICLE DEALERS AND NEW LOW SPEED VEHICLE DEALERS TO MAINTAIN SERVICE AND PARTS STORAGE AREAS.
ar:SB94.summary: Exempts new all-terrain and low-speed vehicle dealers from having an on-site service area or doing repairs at their location, if they provide service or name a provider within 40 miles and report it annually.

ar:SB97.title: TO AUTHORIZE THE ISSUANCE OF ADDITIONAL RETAIL LIQUOR PERMITS TO CERTAIN EXISTING HOLDERS OF RETAIL LIQUOR PERMITS.
ar:SB97.summary: Lets a holder of one retail liquor permit obtain up to two more, no more than one per county, with additional permits allowed only in counties of 200,000 or more people.

ar:SB98.title: TO AMEND THE LAW REGARDING ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES; TO AUTHORIZE THE THIRD-PARTY DELIVERY OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES FROM CERTAIN RETAILERS; AND TO CREATE A THIRD-PARTY DELIVERY PERMIT.
ar:SB98.summary: Creates a third-party delivery permit ($500 annual fee) letting delivery services bring alcohol from retailers to adults 21 or older in areas where sales are legal, using drivers who are 21 or older, licensed and felony-free, who check ID.

ar:SB99.title: TO AUTHORIZE A PHYSICIAN ASSISTANT TO DELEGATE CERTAIN TASKS.
ar:SB99.summary: Lets a physician assistant, as well as a physician, delegate medical tasks, including administering some drugs, to qualified unlicensed employees, under State Medical Board rules.

ar:SJR11.title: A CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT TO AMEND ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION, ARTICLE 2, § 5, TO PROTECT THE RIGHT TO KEEP AND BEAR ARMS.
ar:SJR11.summary: Proposes amending the Constitution's right to keep and bear arms to add lawful hunting, recreation and any other lawful purpose, cover ammunition, firearm accessories and components, and call the right natural, fundamental and individual. Takes effect January 1, 2027 if voters approve.

ar:SJR15.title: A CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT CONCERNING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN THE STATE OF ARKANSAS; AND AUTHORIZING THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY TO PROVIDE FOR THE CREATION OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DISTRICTS TO PROMOTE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT.
ar:SJR15.summary: Proposes amending the Arkansas Constitution to let the legislature create economic development programs and districts and make public loans and grants for them, let districts issue bonds outside certain debt limits, and exempt district property from taxes other than the district's.

az:HB 2010.title: digital goods; seller's requirements; enforcement
az:HB 2010.summary: Requires digital goods sellers advertising "buy" or "purchase" to disclose it is a license with restrictions and revocation terms; if access is later permanently lost, requires a prorated refund of 20 percent per year for up to five years on goods costing $20 or more.

az:HB 2013.title: exceptional events; air quality; wildfires
az:HB 2013.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to submit an exceptional event demonstration to the U.S. EPA when a wildfire over 25,000 acres on federally managed land affects Arizona through smoke or land damage.

az:HB 2015.title: budget procedures; late filing penalty
az:HB 2015.summary: Sets penalties for organizations that fail to submit accurate financial statements to the Department of Administration for federal single audits, capped each fiscal year at $8 million or 1 percent of their General Fund appropriation, whichever is less.

az:HB 2016.title: tax returns; late filing; penalties
az:HB 2016.summary: Bars the Department of Revenue from assessing the late-filing penalty on income tax returns showing zero liability, for taxable periods beginning January 1, 2026.

az:HB 2028.title: DWR; application; administrative completeness
az:HB 2028.summary: Allows a court to order an indigent defendant experiencing homelessness to perform community restitution instead of paying the $20 assessment deposited in the Judicial Collection Enhancement Fund.

az:HB 2041.title: child neglect; financial resources; exception
az:HB 2041.summary: Bars treating a parent, guardian or custodian as having abused or neglected a child solely because a lack of financial resources leaves them unable to provide supervision, food, clothing, shelter or medical care.

az:HB 2047.title: writ of restitution; criminal trespass
az:HB 2047.summary: Makes it first-degree rather than third-degree criminal trespass for a person served with a writ of restitution after an eviction to remain in or return to the property.

az:HB 2086.title: vaccination mandates; masks; prohibition
az:HB 2086.summary: Extends the ban on government mask requirements beyond government premises to all residents, and the ban on government vaccine requirements from COVID-19 to any disease or virus, overriding other vaccination laws; removes exemptions for health care districts and institutions.

az:HB 2100.title: small land subdivision; requirements
az:HB 2100.summary: Lets county boards of supervisors authorize small subdivisions of six to ten parcels of two or more acres not subject to assured water supply rules, and lets the Real Estate Commissioner issue public reports allowing their sale.

az:HB 2105.title: agricultural property; inspections; notice
az:HB 2105.summary: Requires the Department of Revenue, for property inspections, and county assessors, for agricultural property, to give owners advance notice of the inspection date and a copy of the report; bars consecutive-year on-site assessor inspections of agricultural property unless listed changes occur.

az:HB 2113.title: public service corporation; rates; intervenor
az:HB 2113.summary: Requires the Residential Utility Consumer Office director to intervene in a utility rate case when the proposed increase to residential customers is 100 percent or more.

az:HB 2114.title: motorcycle registration requirements; safety fund
az:HB 2114.summary: Requires at least one registered owner to hold a motorcycle license to renew a motorcycle registration, with a 30-day temporary registration for those enrolled in an approved training program; trusts need a licensed trustee; business-owned motorcycles are exempt.

az:HB 2118.title: mobile food vendors; licensure
az:HB 2118.summary: Bars cities and towns from requiring mobile food vendors to obtain a local regulatory permit or license, and removes the allowance for local licenses requiring background checks or identification.

az:HB 2133.title: sexual material; consent; synthetic depiction
az:HB 2133.summary: Exempts clearly manipulated parody, comedy, artistic or critical works from the offense of disclosing nude or sexual images; requires commercial websites publishing sexual material to have uploaders verify depicted people's consent and adult age; violators face $10,000 per day.

az:HB 2134.title: critical infrastructure; foreign adversaries; prohibition
az:HB 2134.summary: Bars use of software and communications equipment from Chinese companies in Arizona critical infrastructure, overrides contracts allowing foreign access or control, and sets certification, reporting and publication requirements.

az:HB 2140.title: bullion depository; state monies; treasurer
az:HB 2140.summary: Allows the State Treasurer to invest up to 10 percent of state trust and treasury monies in physical gold or silver bullion held in a U.S. commercial depository meeting security, insurance and audit standards.

az:HB 2170.title: state contracts; foreign adversary; prohibition
az:HB 2170.summary: Bars companies domiciled in China and controlled by its government, military or ruling party from state contracts for electronic or information technology, requires bidders to certify they are not domiciled in China, and sets a $100,000 civil penalty for false certification.

az:HB 2174.title: insurance; modeling organizations; predictive models
az:HB 2174.summary: Renames advisory organizations as model and data organizations, applies the same rules to them, and removes the insurance director's authority to examine them.

az:HB 2244.title: evictions; satisfaction of judgments
az:HB 2244.summary: Sets that if a landlord does not respond within 15 days to a tenant's motion to compel satisfaction of an eviction judgment, the filing fee is waived, no hearing is held, and the judgment is deemed satisfied on proof of payment.

az:HB 2248.title: medical interventions; prohibition
az:HB 2248.summary: Bars governments, businesses, schools and ticket issuers from denying employment, entry or service based on whether a person has received or used a medical intervention, with exceptions.

az:HB 2249.title: parents' bill of rights; remedies
az:HB 2249.summary: Bars school districts and employees from facilitating a minor's social transitioning, such as using a different name or pronouns, without both parents' written consent; adds parental access to the full educational record; sets minimum liability of $500,000 per instance for governmental entities, $20,000 for officials.

az:HB 2257.title: HOV lane; blood transport vehicles
az:HB 2257.summary: Changes the split of watercraft registration fees to 55 percent (was 65) for the Watercraft Licensing Fund, and sets fixed county percentages for the Law Enforcement and Boating Safety Fund in place of a Game and Fish Commission formula.

az:HB 2265.title: courts; fees; assessments
az:HB 2265.summary: Bars courts from assessing certain costs of appointed counsel, limits new court fees absent express statutory authorization, and adds fee prohibitions in criminal cases.

az:HB 2279.title: commercial river outfitters; limited liability
az:HB 2279.summary: Gives commercial river outfitters in Grand Canyon National Park immunity from claims arising out of a river trip's inherent risks, and from ordinary negligence claims waived in a liability release; does not cover gross negligence or willful acts.

az:HB 2305.title: private towing carriers; regulation; rates
az:HB 2305.summary: Makes private-property towing rates a statewide concern not open to further local regulation; cities, towns and counties without rates on January 1, 2026 default to the Department of Public Safety tow agreement rate, and existing local rates must be updated by July 1, 2027.

az:HB 2311.title: artificial intelligence service; disclosures; requirements
az:HB 2311.summary: Requires operators of conversational AI services to disclose users are interacting with AI, limits sexual and self-harm content, sets rules for minor account holders and age-verification data; the attorney general can seek $1,000 per violation, up to $500,000 per operator, from September 30, 2027.

az:HB 2321.title: DCS; credit freeze; consumer reporting
az:HB 2321.summary: Requires the Department of Child Safety to place a security freeze on a dependent child's credit record within 30 days of placement, keep it until age 16 when the child may keep or remove it, and notify parents or guardians.

az:HB 2322.title: DCS; investigations; interviews; recording
az:HB 2322.summary: Requires the Department of Child Safety, if federal grant funding is enacted, to audio or video record interviews with children in investigations and to apply for federal grants to support it.

az:HB 2327.title: identifying information; records; confidentiality
az:HB 2327.summary: Lets eligible people ask county recorders, assessors and treasurers to block public access to information that could identify them.

az:HB 2379.title: school district governing boards; training
az:HB 2379.summary: Requires each school district governing board member to complete school finance training within 45 days after their term begins, and sets requirements for the training program.

az:HB 2380.title: school districts; board meetings; expenditures
az:HB 2380.summary: Requires school district boards to hold meetings at a public facility in the district and give public access to meeting materials and recordings, lets members pull items from consent agendas, and sets rules for approving out-of-state travel.

az:HB 2397.title: homeowners' associations; property covenants; disclosures
az:HB 2397.summary: Changes resale disclosure rules for condominiums and planned communities: associations must give buyers added documents, including recent board meeting minutes, a financial statement and insurance information, may deliver them electronically, and must update the report on an owner's request.

az:HB 2404.title: authorized transporters
az:HB 2404.summary: As amended, starting January 1, 2030, requires authorized transporters to apprehend and transport people for mental health services and bars peace officers from transporting them from hospitals or locked behavioral health units, with exceptions.

az:HB 2406.title: department of veterans' services; study
az:HB 2406.summary: Makes images, recordings and 911 calls involving deceased minors and child abuse victims confidential except to parents, investigators, courts and others listed; sets a $100,000 civil penalty per violation for profiting from death scene images and a class 1 misdemeanor for knowing unauthorized release.

az:HB 2408.title: nursing board; regulatory actions; expungement
az:HB 2408.summary: Changes Arizona Board of Nursing complaint handling: complainants generally must identify themselves, complaints are prioritized by patient harm, nurses get notice and file access, the board has 180 days to act, and the board may expunge some discipline once.

az:HB 2417.title: excessive speed; speed inhibiting device
az:HB 2417.summary: Lets courts, on a person's request, order speed inhibiting devices on vehicles instead of license suspension or revocation for certain traffic offenses, with set durations, compliance requirements and penalties.

az:HB 2460.title: business property; theft; penalties; prohibition
az:HB 2460.summary: Bars counties and municipalities from adopting ordinances that penalize a business for theft of its movable property.

az:HB 2477.title: Arizona's education savings plan; revisions
az:HB 2477.summary: Conforms Arizona's 529 education savings plan to federal law: raises the K-12 qualified withdrawal cap to $20,000, allows unlimited transfers to ABLE accounts, and sets Roth IRA transfer rules, including a $35,000 aggregate cap.

az:HB 2481.title: school districts; records; noncompliance; penalties
az:HB 2481.summary: Requires school districts that fail to fix financial records deficiencies within 90 days to complete training and interventions; after 18 months, makes the superintendent ineligible for performance pay and bars bond and district additional assistance override elections until fixed.

az:HB 2482.title: building renewal grants; procurement practices
az:HB 2482.summary: Caps individual job orders at $1 million for non-emergency construction projects funded by Building Renewal Grant monies, and requires the School Facilities Division to verify that projects are not split to avoid the cap.

az:HB 2502.title: ASRS; retirement; elected officials
az:HB 2502.summary: Lets an elected official who has reached normal retirement date retire from the state retirement system without resigning from office, and requires the employer to pay the alternate contribution rate.

az:HB 2592.title: artificial intelligence; state agencies; rules
az:HB 2592.summary: Requires state budget units to identify uses of artificial intelligence that reduce administrative burdens, eliminate regulations that unnecessarily restrict AI innovation and streamline AI procurement, and requires the Department of Administration to report annually by December 1.

az:HB 2611.title: group homes; safety; training; rights
az:HB 2611.summary: Adds foster children's rights to join enrichment activities and be free of bullying or discrimination, and bars retaliation for reporting violations; for group foster homes, requires drug-test reporting, removal of employees after positive results, and rules on background checks, training, security and unannounced inspections.

az:HB 2660.title: health boards; licensure decisions; investigation
az:HB 2660.summary: Requires a health professional facing criminal charges to stop practicing after an adverse board licensing decision. Otherwise they may keep practicing until the board sends case details and an affidavit to the Office of Administrative Hearings within 30 days, or the appeal ends.

az:HB 2661.title: parents' rights; guardianship; notice; attestation
az:HB 2661.summary: Adds to the rights of parents or guardians under a Department of Child Safety abuse or neglect investigation the right to be told they may delegate temporary guardianship of the child.

az:HB 2662.title: parenting time; expert testimony; qualifications
az:HB 2662.summary: Allows a court in a parenting-time case involving alleged domestic violence or abuse to hear expert testimony only from witnesses with clinical experience working with victims, and limits the psychological methods experts may use to empirically established ones.

az:HB 2702.title: continuation; ACJC
az:HB 2702.summary: Extends the termination date of the Arizona Criminal Justice Commission from July 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025, applying retroactively from July 1, 2025.

az:HB 2729.title: nursing board; continuation
az:HB 2729.summary: Continues the Arizona State Board of Nursing, the Board of Occupational Therapy Examiners, the Regulatory Board of Physician Assistants and the Department of Economic Security until July 1, 2030, and the Board of Pharmacy until July 1, 2032.

az:HB 2733.title: pharmacy board; renewals; ownership change
az:HB 2733.summary: Lets pharmacists and technicians finish continuing education after filing a renewal if done before the license expires, expands permitted prescription delivery locations, and lets pharmacies keep operating under their existing permit during a change of ownership if conditions are met.

az:HB 2745.title: legislative subpoena; perjury; refusal; contempt
az:HB 2745.summary: Lets the Senate President, Speaker or a committee chairperson issue an order holding a witness in contempt for ignoring a legislative subpoena, after notice and an opportunity for a hearing, and allows a county sheriff to arrest the witness.

az:HB 2755.title: state land use; highest; best
az:HB 2755.summary: Lets holders of underperforming commercial state land leases, or leases expired under a year, apply to buy the land; requires the commissioner to appraise and sell it at public auction within 18 months of the application, and give lessees ample notice before ending such leases.

az:HB 2762.title: food products; labeling; cultivated cells
az:HB 2762.summary: Requires labels reading cell-cultivated or cell-cultured on food products derived from cultivated cells, placed by the manufacturer, packager or retailer.

az:HB 2763.title: shooting range; closure; conditions
az:HB 2763.summary: Adds a condition to closing a shooting range: the Legislature must adopt a joint resolution approving the Game and Fish Commission's closure.

az:HB 2771.title: community supervision; rehabilitation; costs
az:HB 2771.summary: Lets the Department of Corrections require, as a condition of community supervision, that a prisoner pay reasonable costs of participating in a rehabilitation program.

az:HB 2780.title: judicial foreclosure; excess proceeds sale
az:HB 2780.summary: Changes tax-lien foreclosure rules: lets certificate-of-purchase holders, as well as owners, ask the court whether an excess-proceeds sale is reasonable, sets the minimum bid at the judgment's opening bid, and limits suits over late sale-proceeds distributions to parties entitled to proceeds.

az:HB 2782.title: corporation commission; utilities; amortization; tariffs
az:HB 2782.summary: Requires the Corporation Commission and utilities to make disclosures when a regulatory asset is included in rate base or reflected in rates based on a test year or historical balance.

az:HB 2786.title: TPT; exemption; textbook rental
az:HB 2786.summary: Exempts from the transaction privilege tax the rental of textbooks by bookstores, matching the existing sales-tax exemption for textbooks required by state universities and community colleges.

az:HB 2800.title: ignition interlock devices; violation; classification
az:HB 2800.summary: Raises from a class 1 misdemeanor to a class 6 felony the penalty for knowingly lending a vehicle without an ignition interlock device to a DUI-restricted driver who then causes a collision with serious injury or death.

az:HB 2830.title: fetal and prenatal development; instruction
az:HB 2830.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt age-appropriate science standards that include instruction on fetal and prenatal human development.

az:HB 2873.title: competitive sealed bidding; questions; answers
az:HB 2873.summary: As amended, lets a person or organization withdraw a municipal referendum petition by written notice before the measure qualifies for the ballot, applies to notices filed by December 31, 2025, and takes effect immediately.

az:HB 2874.title: campaign committees; termination statements; contributions
az:HB 2874.summary: Changes how late-filing penalties are assessed for campaign committees that file termination statements, letting treasurers certify the committee received no contributions. Applies retroactive to July 6, 2016, as an emergency measure.

az:HB 2941.title: motorcycles; reckless driving
az:HB 2941.summary: Classifies riding a motorcycle between lanes of traffic, or passing in the same lane, as reckless driving, a class 2 misdemeanor, except where authorized.

az:HB 2950.title: tourism improvement areas; municipalities; counties
az:HB 2950.summary: Allows cities and counties to create tourism improvement areas funded by assessments on lodging businesses, managed by a destination marketing organization, and sets procedures for formation petitions, hearings, assessments and dissolution.

az:HB 2957.title: driver license; enhanced; mobile; prohibition
az:HB 2957.summary: Bars the state, cities, towns and counties from requiring digital or mobile driver licenses and requires physical licenses to be accepted; requires the transportation department to keep issuing non-REAL ID licenses, with limits on retaining documents and sharing data.

az:HB 2960.title: veterans' court fund; grant program
az:HB 2960.summary: Creates the Veterans' Specialty Court Grant Program, run by the Administrative Office of the Courts, to fund new and existing veterans' courts in counties and municipalities, with annual grantee reports.

az:HB 2970.title: fraudulent schemes; artifices; jurisdiction
az:HB 2970.summary: Provides that in fraudulent scheme prosecutions the state need not prove all unlawful acts happened in Arizona or one jurisdiction, and that this is no defense.

az:HB 2979.title: credit unions; certificates; powers; committee
az:HB 2979.summary: Changes credit union law: the state deputy director must acknowledge or seek more information on bylaw, name-change and office-location requests within ten business days, then decide within 30 business days (60 for offices); share par value becomes optional.

az:HB 2986.title: department of environmental quality; programs
az:HB 2986.summary: Replaces the state Recycling Fund with a Solid Waste Fee Fund with broader uses, exempts lead-acid battery recyclers from federal or state authorization and solid waste fee registration, and extends certain air-plan revision enactment dates from July 2027 to July 2029.

az:HB 2995.title: domestic relations; domestic violence
az:HB 2995.summary: Extends the domestic violence presumption to parenting time as well as legal decision-making, requires written court findings, revises rebuttal factors, requires clear and convincing evidence to overcome it for decision-making or unsupervised time, and defines coercive control.

az:HB 4010.title: genetic counselors; board; licensure
az:HB 4010.summary: Creates the Board of Genetic Counselors to license and regulate genetic counselors, and requires practitioners to be licensed in Arizona on completion of Board rulemaking and no later than October 1, 2026.

az:HB 4018.title: technical correction; public records
az:HB 4018.summary: Lets a county sheriff use volunteer posse and reserve organizations and gives the sheriff exclusive authority to regulate their organization and equipment under written policy.

az:HB 4042.title: termination; parent-child relationship; service
az:HB 4042.summary: Requires a potential father who files a paternity action after notice of adoption proceedings to serve the mother within 30 days or automatically waive notice of termination proceedings; failure may also support terminating the parent-child relationship.

az:HB 4043.title: training; AEDs; CPR; school personnel
az:HB 4043.summary: Requires each school district and charter school campus to have, from August 1, 2027, at least one employee trained in CPR and first aid, and in AED use if the campus has one.

az:HB 4049.title: attorney general; legal counsel; exemption
az:HB 4049.summary: Lets the Department of Child Safety employ its own legal counsel, and requires the Attorney General to represent the state's interest, not the department, in child-welfare cases alleging department misconduct.

az:HB 4056.title: technical correction; double punishment
az:HB 4056.summary: Bars charging a legislator any fee for a public records request made in an official capacity, and requires the records be provided in any format the legislator requests.

az:HB 4117.title: disturbing religious services; worship
az:HB 4117.summary: Makes it a class 1 misdemeanor to intentionally block entry to a place of worship or cause a protracted disruption of a religious service; a class 6 felony for repeat offenses, force or threats, or group blocking of entry. Peaceful protest is exempt.

az:SB 1011.title: medical examiners; sudden infant death
az:SB 1011.summary: Requires medical examiners or forensic pathologists, in sudden and unexplained infant deaths, to review the infant's immunization history and any countermeasures given in the 90 days before death, and report the death to a national case registry.

az:SB 1012.title: concealed weapons; notice; repeal
az:SB 1012.summary: Lets permit holders who do not drink carry concealed handguns in restaurants with only a restaurant liquor license; allows license suspension over concealed handguns only for gross negligence; limits licensee liability for handgun-caused harm unless a court or jury finds specified conduct.

az:SB 1013.title: public employees; merit; hiring practices
az:SB 1013.summary: Bars the state and political subdivisions from adopting hiring policies based on anything other than merit, or from manipulating employee composition by race, ethnicity, sex or national origin; allows lawsuits with attorney fees; keeps veterans' preference.

az:SB 1015.title: gender transition procedures; provider liability
az:SB 1015.summary: Makes health professionals who provide gender transition procedures to minors strictly liable for related injury and detransition costs within 25 years, and allows injured persons to sue for damages, including punitive damages, and attorney fees.

az:SB 1018.title: foreign law; sharia law; prohibition
az:SB 1018.summary: Adds Sharia law, and foreign, religious or cultural customs or practices that allow or excuse listed conduct such as honor killings or forced marriage, to the definition of foreign law in Arizona's limit on applying foreign law in courts.

az:SB 1037.title: voting; equipment; internet; custody; violation
az:SB 1037.summary: Bars internet connectivity in voting and tabulating equipment, requires tamper-sealed ports and chain-of-custody logs at polling places and no ports on counting-center equipment, requires nonstop online video of counting-center activity, and makes negligent violations class 1 misdemeanors.

az:SB 1038.title: cast vote record; public record
az:SB 1038.summary: Requires county boards of supervisors or election officers to send the cast vote record to the Secretary of State within 48 hours after the county canvass, unaltered except for precincts with fewer than 25 registered voters, and makes it a public record.

az:SB 1040.title: voter registration rolls; internet access
az:SB 1040.summary: Requires county recorders to give the public free, read-only, downloadable internet access to voter registration rolls; extends the political-and-election use limit to the rolls; removes the fee schedule and the existing limits on posting voter data online and on access to certain personal details.

az:SB 1053.title: concealed weapons permits; fees
az:SB 1053.summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety to charge separate concealed weapons permit fees for residents and non-residents, with the resident fee set at 10% of the non-resident fee.

az:SB 1057.title: watermark; paper ballots
az:SB 1057.summary: Repeals and re-enacts the existing ballot-paper section without changing its text: vendors must hold ISO 27001, 17025 or 9001:2015 certification, and ballots must use at least three listed anti-fraud features such as watermarked paper, holographic foil or security inks.

az:SB 1060.title: voter registration; temporary absence
az:SB 1060.summary: Repeals the provisions letting a U.S. citizen who has never lived in the U.S., and whose U.S.-citizen parent is registered to vote in Arizona, register and vote by federal write-in early ballot, and removes the matching residence rule.

az:SB 1061.title: fentanyl; sale amount; nine grams
az:SB 1061.summary: Lowers from 200 grams to 9 grams the amount of fentanyl in a sale to another person that triggers specified criminal sentencing ranges.

az:SB 1068.title: disruption; educational institution; concealed weapon
az:SB 1068.summary: Bars the governing board of any university, college or community college from enforcing a policy that prohibits concealed weapon permit holders from possessing a concealed weapon, or prohibits the lawful transport or storage of a firearm.

az:SB 1069.title: prohibited weapons; muffling device; repeal
az:SB 1069.summary: Removes devices designed to muffle the sound of a firearm (silencers) from the state's definition of prohibited weapons.

az:SB 1075.title: foreign entities; land; legislative approval
az:SB 1075.summary: Bars sale, lease or sublease of Arizona land to a foreign entity hostile to the United States without Foreign Entity Review Commission approval, requires grantee identification be filed with the Department of Real Estate, and allows the Attorney General to seek civil penalties.

az:SB 1095.title: gender transition; minors; prohibitions
az:SB 1095.summary: Extends Arizona's ban on gender reassignment surgery for minors to all gender transition procedures, including puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones, and to other health professionals; also bars referrals for them; effective April 1, 2027.

az:SB 1113.title: service of process; evaluation agencies
az:SB 1113.summary: Lets a court authorize employees of a licensed screening or evaluation agency to serve evaluation or treatment petition documents on a patient already admitted to the facility; the agency may be reimbursed for this only under a county contract.

az:SB 1121.title: radiation protection systems; medical procedures
az:SB 1121.summary: Bars hospitals from requiring health professionals to wear lead aprons during cardiac catheterization procedures using real-time x-ray when the room has a radiation protection system.

az:SB 1124.title: health boards; evaluations; notice
az:SB 1124.summary: Requires health profession regulatory boards to vote on, and give the professional at least 14 days' notice with a summary of the complaint before, ordering a psychological or psychiatric evaluation. The professional may submit a written response and testify.

az:SB 1127.title: duty to report; abuse; neglect
az:SB 1127.summary: Requires mandatory reporters with direct knowledge of child abuse or neglect to report to the Department of Child Safety rather than delegate, except in health care institutions; bars school resource and safety officers from supervising law enforcement investigations of school employee conduct involving minors.

az:SB 1133.title: candidate financial disclosures; public officers
az:SB 1133.summary: Treats a candidate who has filed the annual public-officer financial disclosure as meeting the candidate disclosure requirement, so no second filing is needed, for statewide and legislative candidates now and for all other offices from January 1, 2027.

az:SB 1135.title: death benefits; burial costs
az:SB 1135.summary: Raises the burial expense amount paid as a workers' compensation death benefit from $5,000 to $10,000.

az:SB 1136.title: workers' compensation; death benefits; remarriage
az:SB 1136.summary: Lets the surviving spouse of a first responder keep receiving workers' compensation death benefits for life, including spouses who lost benefits through remarriage on or after January 1, 2000, going forward only.

az:SB 1145.title: behavior analysts; committee; regulatory authority
az:SB 1145.summary: Delegates, starting January 1, 2027, the Board of Psychologist Examiners' authority to license and regulate behavior analysts to the Committee on Behavior Analysts and reduces the Board's membership from 10 to 8.

az:SB 1160.title: drones; entertainment districts; prohibition
az:SB 1160.summary: Makes it a class 1 misdemeanor to intentionally operate a civil drone within 5,280 feet of, or 5,280 feet above, a ticketed entertainment event, with exceptions such as written consent, venue and utility employees, and owners over their own property.

az:SB 1162.title: health care institutions; licensing; complaints
az:SB 1162.summary: As amended, requires the health department and AHCCCS to review overlapping monitoring and compliance functions for health care institution licensing, and sets qualifications, training and scope of practice for behavioral health technicians.

az:SB 1164.title: ALTCS; providers; change of ownership
az:SB 1164.summary: Sets change-of-ownership procedures so licensed skilled nursing and assisted living facilities can keep processing claims for services to Arizona Long-Term Care System members.

az:SB 1165.title: insurance; cost sharing; breast exams
az:SB 1165.summary: Bars health insurers from imposing cost sharing for breast cancer screening and additional screening needed to complete it, for policies issued on or after January 1, 2027.

az:SB 1167.title: cities; towns; counties; posting; website
az:SB 1167.summary: Lets cities, towns and counties meet legal notice advertising requirements by posting on their own website and the website of a qualified newspaper.

az:SB 1174.title: DCS; intake hotline; case history
az:SB 1174.summary: Requires, from January 1, 2027, the Department of Child Safety intake hotline to produce one report covering the full hotline and investigation history of a child and the child's siblings.

az:SB 1180.title: DOR; income tax forms; conformity
az:SB 1180.summary: Extends the deadline for penalty-free amended returns after federal tax nonconformity to the extended due date of the second following year, sets publication dates for supplemental forms, and has the Department of Revenue assume conformity when preparing forms.

az:SB 1184.title: HOAs; uniformed services division flags
az:SB 1184.summary: Adds outdoor displays of Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force and Coast Guard flags to the flags condominium and planned community associations cannot prohibit.

az:SB 1188.title: approved medications; scheduling; prescription authority
az:SB 1188.summary: Makes FDA-approved drugs scheduled or rescheduled by the DEA take the same classification under Arizona law, and be prescribable unless Schedule I.

az:SB 1189.title: campaign spending; personal security
az:SB 1189.summary: Lets a candidate committee spend campaign money on the personal security of the candidate and family members.

az:SB 1193.title: personal identifying information; disclosure; prohibition
az:SB 1193.summary: Bars the Department of Health Services from selling or disclosing personal identifying information of people it licenses or certifies, including emergency medical care technicians, without their consent, with exceptions.

az:SB 1198.title: Arizona beef council; continuation
az:SB 1198.summary: Continues the Arizona Beef Council and the State Veterinary Medical Examining Board until July 1, 2034.

az:SB 1205.title: motor vehicle booting; fees; regulation
az:SB 1205.summary: Sets state rules for vehicle booting by cities, towns and booting services, including signage requirements for private property owners, fee requirements and penalties for violations.

az:SB 1206.title: storm related insurance claims
az:SB 1206.summary: Bars adjusters from working on repairs for claims they adjust and from soliciting clients during an active loss event or emergency response; bars contractors from soliciting then, or paying or promising to pay a policyholder's deductible on catastrophic storm claims.

az:SB 1210.title: private postsecondary education; nondomiciled institutions
az:SB 1210.summary: Creates a separate registration process for private postsecondary schools based outside Arizona, setting the information they must submit to the state board.

az:SB 1212.title: health insurance; reimbursement rates; vaccines
az:SB 1212.summary: Bars health insurers, beginning January 1, 2027, from paying a health professional a different reimbursement rate because a covered patient refuses one or more vaccines.

az:SB 1214.title: stem cells; birth tissue; therapy
az:SB 1214.summary: As amended, allows providers to perform stem cell and regenerative therapies not approved by the FDA if they meet training, sourcing and written informed consent requirements.

az:SB 1215.title: firefighters; occupational disease; cancers
az:SB 1215.summary: Clarifies, retroactive to July 1, 2021, which conditions are presumed work-related for workers' compensation coverage of peace officers, firefighters and fire investigators.

az:SB 1221.title: tax laws; interpretation; application; hearing
az:SB 1221.summary: Requires the Department of Revenue to notify the Legislature before adopting a tax-law interpretation that adversely affects taxpayers, and to testify if the Legislature holds a hearing.

az:SB 1233.title: administrative deficiencies; cure period
az:SB 1233.summary: Bars the Department of Health Services, AHCCCS and Department of Economic Security from disciplining or taking enforcement action against a licensed or contracted facility with only administrative deficiencies unless the facility first gets 72 hours to cure them.

az:SB 1235.title: EMS reciprocity; compact.
az:SB 1235.summary: Adopts the Emergency Medical Services Personnel Licensure Interstate Compact, letting EMS personnel in participating states obtain licensure in other compact states.

az:SB 1242.title: mental health; hearings; audiovisual technology
az:SB 1242.summary: Changes procedures for court-ordered mental health evaluation and treatment, including virtual hearings and testimony, and sets care-coordination requirements between treatment agencies and secure behavioral health residential facilities.

az:SB 1243.title: court-ordered treatment; guardians; notice; release
az:SB 1243.summary: Adds guardians to those a mental health agency's medical director must notify before a court-ordered patient's release, and lets guardians apply to continue court-ordered treatment.

az:SB 1246.title: homeowners' associations; foreclosure process
az:SB 1246.summary: Raises the delinquency threshold for foreclosing a condominium association's assessment lien from one year or $1,200 to eighteen months or $10,000, and for special assessments of $10,000 or more in condominiums and homeowners' associations applies only the eighteen-month threshold.

az:SB 1253.title: safe haven providers; hospital deliveries
az:SB 1253.summary: Lets a parent or agent surrender a newborn at the hospital of birth without first being discharged and later returning to complete the surrender.

az:SB 1259.title: campaigns; protected residential addresses
az:SB 1259.summary: Lets a person whose residential address is protected by a court-sealed voter record give an alternate mailing address and attest they reside in the district they propose to represent, on committee organization statements and annual public officer financial disclosures.

az:SB 1270.title: correctional officers; supplemental contributions
az:SB 1270.summary: Lets Correction Officer Retirement Plan employers make supplemental contribution payments of up to $5,000 per person per year to Tier 3 members hired on or after July 1, 2018.

az:SB 1274.title: special plate; police foundation
az:SB 1274.summary: Creates a timeshare salesperson license, effective July 1, 2027, and sets licensure requirements and qualifications.

az:SB 1275.title: mandatory prison sentences; judicial discretion
az:SB 1275.summary: As amended, lets a county attorney set up a Veterans Diversion Program to prosecute and treat defendants whose mental health condition is related to military service.

az:SB 1280.title: public monies; Mexican wolf; prohibition
az:SB 1280.summary: Bars the Game and Fish Commission from transporting Mexican gray wolf puppies into Arizona or using public money or resources to do so.

az:SB 1281.title: federal government; land acquisition; consent
az:SB 1281.summary: Requires escrow agents to notify the Senate president and House speaker when private land goes into escrow for sale to the federal government, and extends the State Land Department's catalog and boundary review from national monuments to other listed federal designations.

az:SB 1286.title: veterinarian visits; electronic means; prescriptions
az:SB 1286.summary: Extends from 14 to 30 days the period a veterinarian may prescribe and renew non-antimicrobial, non-flea-and-tick drugs after an electronic examination; allows one electronic antimicrobial prescription of up to 14 days, and flea and tick prescriptions of up to three months.

az:SB 1290.title: agricultural property; inspections; notice.
az:SB 1290.summary: As amended, bars a planned community board from taking action on an item under consideration during the closed portion of a meeting.

az:SB 1292.title: PSPRS; investments
az:SB 1292.summary: Limits the public safety retirement system's five-percent cap on voting stock ownership to publicly traded corporations.

az:SB 1315.title: public schools; interoperable communications; requirements
az:SB 1315.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools that receive state or local law enforcement money for interoperable communications to maintain capabilities to alert and talk with law enforcement in school emergencies and file annual affidavits; agencies with available money must offer it.

az:SB 1318.title: mammography results; notice; repeal
az:SB 1318.summary: Repeals the requirement that health care facilities give patients identified as having heterogeneously dense or extremely dense breasts a specified notice.

az:SB 1326.title: victims' rights; attorney fees; costs
az:SB 1326.summary: Allows a court to order a party who intentionally, knowingly or with gross negligence violates a crime victim's rights to pay the victim's reasonable attorney fees and costs of enforcing those rights.

az:SB 1327.title: ABOR; foreign countries; restrictions; penalties
az:SB 1327.summary: Requires the Board of Regents to have each public university adopt a research security policy to guard research against foreign influence, and sets required policy elements and reporting to the Board.

az:SB 1332.title: light rail expansion; participation; prohibition
az:SB 1332.summary: Requires the Auditor General, with an independent transportation research entity, to review light rail expansion in Maricopa County by December 31, 2027, comparing it with other transit options, and report to the governor and legislative leaders; the act is repealed after June 30, 2028.

az:SB 1335.title: water banking; annual report; posting
az:SB 1335.summary: Lets a holder of groundwater savings credits keep irrigating the land under its former irrigation grandfathered right for up to two years after the credits are issued, under a temporary permit from the Department of Water Resources.

az:SB 1336.title: state land department; continuation; oversight
az:SB 1336.summary: Continues the State Land Department until July 1, 2030, creates a joint legislative ad hoc committee on state land oversight, changes mineral exploration permit rules, and lets the land commissioner renew some production leases without public auction.

az:SB 1338.title: state; local public benefits; eligibility
az:SB 1338.summary: Removes the exclusion for state public retirement system benefits from the definition of state or local public benefit, and lists persons who are ineligible to receive any state or local public benefit.

az:SB 1345.title: health facilities; anonymous complaints; prohibition
az:SB 1345.summary: Requires the Department of Health Services to approve or deny initial health care institution license applications within 90 days and submit third-party accreditation survey results for certification within 30 days; lets its Director set initial licensing inspection fees by rule.

az:SB 1366.title: commercial buildings; telecommunications services
az:SB 1366.summary: Creates the Public Property Towing and Impound Practices Study Committee.

az:SB 1399.title: prepaid capitated contractors; cost reports
az:SB 1399.summary: Requires the state Medicaid agency (AHCCCS) to report to the Legislature and Governor each December 1 the share of money its prepaid managed-care contractors spend on provider payments and on categories of administrative costs.

az:SB 1416.title: missing; kidnapped children; reporting requirements
az:SB 1416.summary: Changes reporting rules for missing or runaway children: police must publicize information within 24 hours, may not label a child a runaway in public notices unless needed for safety or an investigation, and train staff every two years.

az:SB 1418.title: corporation commission; small modular reactors
az:SB 1418.summary: Lets a utility build a small modular reactor co-located with an extra high load factor customer after 30 days' notice to the Corporation Commission, without an application or environmental compatibility certificate.

az:SB 1419.title: solar energy; inspection; contractors
az:SB 1419.summary: As amended in committee of the whole, requires solar contractors to verify roof structure before installing, meet wind, load, structural and seismic codes, and fix deficiencies a third-party inspector finds, and requires bold-type and initialed disclosures in solar financing, sale or lease agreements.

az:SB 1421.title: undocumented aliens; financial services
az:SB 1421.summary: Bars financial institutions and check cashers from accepting IDs issued exclusively to undocumented immigrants, makes loans on applications allowing an ITIN as identification unlawful, and requires proof of lawful presence for foreign remittance transfers, with monthly confirmations to the state regulator.

az:SB 1422.title: credit enhancement eligibility board; continuation
az:SB 1422.summary: Continues the Credit Enhancement Eligibility Board, which oversees the program guaranteeing financing for achievement district public schools, for 10 years, until July 1, 2036.

az:SB 1423.title: WICHE; continuation
az:SB 1423.summary: Continues the Western Interstate Commission for Higher Education in Arizona for 10 years.

az:SB 1428.title: board of supervisors; membership
az:SB 1428.summary: Enlarges county boards of supervisors to seven members in counties of 1 to 3 million people and nine in counties above 3 million, starting January 1, 2033.

az:SB 1429.title: board of directors; commerce authority.
az:SB 1429.summary: Applies a strict compliance standard of review to city, town and county initiatives and referenda, and adds requirements for petition circulators.

az:SB 1445.title: water quality; testing; on-site
az:SB 1445.summary: Lets cities and towns of 1,000 to 9,999 people test bacteriological samples on-site, and bars the Department of Environmental Quality from requiring more than 1,000 gallons of storage at community water systems with 25 or fewer connections in counties of 400,000 or fewer.

az:SB 1446.title: social workers; documentation; dialysis centers
az:SB 1446.summary: Bars the state health department from requiring dialysis-center social workers to document a patient's progress more often than quarterly, unless federal Medicare and Medicaid rules require it.

az:SB 1448.title: aggravated assault; utility workers
az:SB 1448.summary: Classifies assault as aggravated assault when the offender knows or has reason to know the victim is an on-duty employee of a utility or a licensed telecommunications or video service provider.

az:SB 1452.title: cargo theft task force
az:SB 1452.summary: Directs the Attorney General to create a Cargo Theft Task Force, subject to legislative appropriation, to investigate cargo theft and related offenses, with set membership and annual reporting.

az:SB 1456.title: ADOT; primitive roads; designation
az:SB 1456.summary: Exempts employers and associations with at least 500 employees or members from the bond that authorized third-party driver license providers must post.

az:SB 1457.title: air mobility fund; border security
az:SB 1457.summary: Allows the advanced air mobility fund to be used to buy advanced air mobility vehicles for border security, giving priority to counties along the international border.

az:SB 1475.title: interscholastic activities; criminal offenses; ineligibility
az:SB 1475.summary: Requires school district boards to bar students from school-sponsored interscholastic activities if convicted of, or admitting to, listed offenses such as aggravated assault, sex offenses, stalking and domestic violence, and to require students to certify whether they committed one.

az:SB 1476.title: child neglect; prenatal substance exposure
az:SB 1476.summary: Makes it a class 6 felony for a person with custody to neglect a child through conduct that harms the child, when it involves a newborn's prenatal drug exposure or fetal alcohol findings; a mother who completed treatment during pregnancy has an affirmative defense.

az:SB 1477.title: assisted living facilities; referral agents
az:SB 1477.summary: Requires assisted living referral agencies to document that referral agents are not on the adult protective services registry, or use an accredited provider for criminal history checks, and to carry $1 million per occurrence and $3 million aggregate general and professional liability insurance.

az:SB 1493.title: disciplinary action; appeal; superior court
az:SB 1493.summary: As amended, requires an employer that does not reinstate a law enforcement officer whose termination is found without just cause in both an initial appeal and a later superior court action to pay the officer's costs and reasonable attorney and expert fees.

az:SB 1494.title: technical correction; open pit mining
az:SB 1494.summary: Bars health care providers, institutions and drug manufacturers from paying enrollees' health insurance premiums unless federal law allows, bars clinicians from advising patients to switch plans unless licensed insurance producers, and sets civil penalties of at least $1,000 per violation.

az:SB 1497.title: classical learning; tests; examinations
az:SB 1497.summary: Requires school districts with a self-insurance program and at least 300 employees to obtain coverage quotes at least once every four years.

az:SB 1511.title: commercial vehicles; operator; lawful presence
az:SB 1511.summary: Bars holders of nondomiciled commercial driver licenses from operating in Arizona without evidence of lawful immigration status or lawful presence, with penalties including out-of-service orders and impoundment of the vehicle and cargo.

az:SB 1520.title: agencies; immigration; data sharing
az:SB 1520.summary: Requires this state and its agencies to share any data the federal government requests about unauthorized immigrants or visa overstayers; the requirement is repealed after December 31, 2028.

az:SB 1549.title: ultralight vehicles; definition
az:SB 1549.summary: Adds ultralight vehicles, meaning single-occupant aircraft without airworthiness certificates under set weight and fuel limits, to the definition of advanced air mobility.

az:SB 1560.title: cap; water supply development fund
az:SB 1560.summary: Raises the cap on a single loan from the Water Supply Development Revolving Fund from $3 million to $20 million.

az:SB 1561.title: assisted living; notice; study committee
az:SB 1561.summary: Requires assisted living discharge or eviction notices to include a statement of the resident's rights, and re-establishes the 25-member Vulnerable Adult System Study Committee with set membership, duties and reporting requirements.

az:SB 1563.title: barbering and cosmetology board; continuation
az:SB 1563.summary: Continues the Board of Barbering and Cosmetology until July 1, 2034 and lowers the maximum fees for many licenses and renewals.

az:SB 1564.title: electronic monitoring; long-term care
az:SB 1564.summary: Requires assisted living facilities and nursing care institutions to tell the Department of Health Services by December 1, 2026 whether they allow or use electronic monitoring devices, and requires the department to post that information publicly.

az:SB 1572.title: public schools; civics instruction requirement
az:SB 1572.summary: Requires each public school to observe Celebrate Freedom Week, with instruction on the Declaration of Independence and Constitution in social studies courses and a student recitation of a Declaration passage in grades 3-12. Sets exemptions and State Board of Education duties.

az:SB 1573.title: judicial determinations; religious sectarian laws
az:SB 1573.summary: Bars courts, including federal courts sitting in diversity, from relying on religious sectarian law as controlling or persuasive authority. Exempts law based on Anglo-American legal tradition and recognition of a traditional marriage between a man and a woman.

az:SB 1620.title: Arizona space commission; board; membership
az:SB 1620.summary: Requires municipalities to set a reimbursement process for telecommunications utility facility relocation costs and to give the utility public notice of voter-approved bond projects at least 30 days before requesting relocation.

az:SB 1624.title: photo radar enforcement; civil penalty
az:SB 1624.summary: Caps the penalty for photo-enforcement traffic violations at $75 with exceptions, sends $15 to the Peace Officer Training Equipment Fund, and bars using such violations to set insurance or affect driving privileges.

az:SB 1627.title: schools; prohibition; unmanned aircraft
az:SB 1627.summary: Makes it a class 3 misdemeanor for a hobby or recreational drone operator to photograph or loiter 200 feet or less above posted, non-residential K-12 school property after being told to leave; people with legal authority over the property or the owner's consent are exempt.

az:SB 1630.title: home; community-based services; mental illness
az:SB 1630.summary: Creates a three-year pilot, pending federal approval, for enhanced residential treatment services for adults with serious mental illness, run by AHCCCS with enrollment capped at 60 members unless data supports raising it; also adds licensing for enhanced residential treatment facilities.

az:SB 1631.title: DCS; sexual abuse allegations; interviews
az:SB 1631.summary: Requires the Department of Child Safety to have a trained forensic interviewer interview a child within 72 hours of a sexual abuse allegation, unless it documents good cause such as hospitalization, the child being out of state, or an unresponsive parent.

az:SB 1662.title: probation supervision; least restrictive conditions
