az:SB 1662.summary: Directs courts that grant probation to impose only conditions that are reasonably necessary, individually tailored and serve specific purposes.

az:SB 1669.title: sexual offenses; victim; evidence
az:SB 1669.summary: Replaces "trauma" with "physical injury" in the exception allowing evidence of a sexual offense victim's specific sexual activity that shows the source of semen, pregnancy, disease or injury.

az:SB 1671.title: gaming; racing; boxing; conflict-of-interest continuation
az:SB 1671.summary: Continues the racing and boxing commissions and the Department of Gaming until July 1, 2032, requires conflict-of-interest disclosure forms from their directors and employees, and adds complaint tracking and an annual complaint report for the gaming department.

az:SB 1711.title: age-appropriate resources; inappropriate contact; schools
az:SB 1711.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to compile recommended resources for age-appropriate education on recognizing and preventing inappropriate contact, and requires public schools to make them available to students and parents.

az:SB 1713.title: AHCCCS; procurement; contracting
az:SB 1713.summary: Lets pharmacists, under a Board of Pharmacy protocol, order CLIA-waived tests and start treatment for flu, strep throat and COVID-19 (minors need parental consent; no opioids), and start HIV prevention medications.

az:SB 1723.title: domestic violence; release conditions
az:SB 1723.summary: Requires judges to impose electronic monitoring, where available, and a no-contact order on people released after a domestic violence charge causing physical harm; bars unsupervised parenting time on a finding of significant domestic violence; lets courts require order-of-protection defendants to give identifying information.

az:SB 1741.title: public schools; released time courses
az:SB 1741.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to let students attend released time courses of religious instruction during the school day, with parental consent and academic credit, and lets adversely affected persons sue for violations.

az:SB 1808.title: homeowners' associations; allied countries' flags
az:SB 1808.summary: Adds a flag from a nation allied with the United States as a major non-NATO ally and established on May 14, 1948 to the flags that condominium and planned community associations may not prohibit owners from displaying.

az:SB 1814.title: substance use disorder treatment; committee
az:SB 1814.summary: Creates the Substance Use Disorder Treatment Standards and Oversight Study Committee to review treatment programs, access gaps, standards and funding needs, and sets its membership and reporting duties.

az:SB 1821.title: DCS; training; child placement; management
az:SB 1821.summary: Lets the Auditor General's team review DCS's case management system, lets DCS make unannounced inspections of group and kinship foster homes, and requires new child safety workers to train at least one year under an experienced worker.

ca:AB 1156.title: Williamson Act contracts: cancellation fees: photovoltaic solar facilities.
ca:AB 1156.summary: Removes city and county power to waive or defer Williamson Act cancellation fees and lets the Natural Resources Secretary do so on landowner application, including for solar facilities meeting set conditions. Until 2037, requires approving qualifying extensions and waiving fees once the project is built.

ca:AB 1267.title: Marriage: prohibition on minors.
ca:AB 1267.summary: Repeals the authorization for people under 18 to get a marriage license or register a domestic partnership, prohibiting both.

ca:AB 1278.title: Mortgages: hazard insurance proceeds: interest.
ca:AB 1278.summary: Allows interest on mortgage loss-draft accounts holding hazard insurance proceeds to be paid directly to the borrower, rather than only credited to the account, annually or at account termination, and treats such checks uncashed after 90 days as canceled.

ca:AB 1301.title: Electricity.
ca:AB 1301.summary: Abolishes the Electricity Oversight Board and Power Exchange, drops the attorney requirement for the Energy Commission's public advisor, extends the Energy Conservation Assistance Act's repeal date to 2038, and moves several existing reporting deadlines.

ca:AB 1486.title: Climate resiliency: research farms: grant program.
ca:AB 1486.summary: Lets the Education Department advance payments to the Department of Food and Agriculture for Proposition 4 research farm grants in 2026-27 and 2027-28, exempts those contracts from General Services approval, and counts building or upgrading research farms.

ca:AB 1537.title: Peace officers: secondary employment.
ca:AB 1537.summary: Bars certain peace officers from secondary employment involving immigration enforcement, makes violations grounds for decertification, and requires officers to report related job offers to their agency, which must keep records.

ca:AB 1581.title: Pupils: data reporting: American Indian and Alaska Native pupils.
ca:AB 1581.summary: Requires the Department of Education, by July 1, 2028 and each July 1 after, to post statewide aggregate data for American Indian and Alaska Native pupils: number of pupils, achievement, suspension and expulsion, chronic absenteeism and graduation rates.

ca:AB 1645.title: Corrections: Humanizing and Uniting Generations Safely Act of 2026.
ca:AB 1645.summary: Enacts the Humanizing and Uniting Generations Safely Act: prison visiting regulations must consider the importance of physical contact, and the department may not unreasonably restrict nonsexual contact or discipline for physical contact without first giving a warning.

ca:AB 1656.title: Human trafficking case continuances.
ca:AB 1656.summary: In human trafficking cases, requires courts to give great weight to a prosecutor's conflicting trial or hearing when deciding on a continuance, allowing one continuance of up to 10 additional court days for that reason.

ca:AB 1679.title: Local pop-up small business program.
ca:AB 1679.summary: Requires cities and counties to allow temporary pop-up small businesses to operate up to 120 days in eligible commercial spaces without full permanent-occupancy compliance, while meeting temporary health and safety standards.

ca:AB 1688.title: Child abuse or neglect: reporting.
ca:AB 1688.summary: Requires county welfare agencies to send notice of substantiated abuse or neglect in out-of-home placements, or removals from them, to the parents' or guardians' attorney in dependency court, and tribal representative for Indian children.

ca:AB 1740.title: Coastal resources: local coastal program: coastal development permits: City of Santa Monica.
ca:AB 1740.summary: Requires Santa Monica to submit a complete local coastal program by January 1, 2029, sets Coastal Commission deadlines (45 days to list issues, six months to act), and changes coastal permit and amendment rules for converting road right-of-way to bicycle, transit or pedestrian use.

ca:AB 1766.title: Health curriculum framework: human trafficking and online safety.
ca:AB 1766.summary: Requires the Instructional Quality Commission to consider adding human trafficking and online safety content, including deepfakes and digital citizenship, to the health curriculum framework when next revised on or after January 1, 2027, and the Department of Education to post related information.

ca:AB 1776.title: Cartwright Act: violations.
ca:AB 1776.summary: Prohibits monopolizing or monopsonizing any part of trade or commerce, requires plaintiffs to prove substantial market power, exempts small businesses, and limits enforcement actions to the Attorney General or district attorneys.

ca:AB 1784.title: Postsecondary education: nondiscrimination: pregnancy or pregnancy-related issues.
ca:AB 1784.summary: Adds ancestry, national origin, medical condition, marital status, familial status, citizenship and primary language to postsecondary nondiscrimination policy and, from September 1, 2027, bars discrimination based on pregnancy, marital status or family status.

ca:AB 1793.title: Cash payments: calculation.
ca:AB 1793.summary: Enacts the California Common Cents Act, requiring merchants to round cash transaction totals to the nearest five cents, with rounding disregarded for tax calculations.

ca:AB 1860.title: School facilities: design-build: alternative design-build: county superintendents of schools.
ca:AB 1860.summary: Authorizes county superintendents of schools to use design-build and alternative design-build contracts on the same terms as school districts, with exclusive authority to award them for county offices of education.

ca:AB 1876.title: Health care coverage: nondiscrimination.
ca:AB 1876.summary: Bars health plans and insurers from excluding, denying benefits to, or discriminating against enrollees based on race, color, national origin, age, disability, or sex, with sex defined to include sex characteristics, pregnancy and gender identity.

ca:AB 1877.title: Domestic violence: protective orders.
ca:AB 1877.summary: Makes violating certain criminal protective or stay-away orders a misdemeanor or felony when the underlying case involved a felony, makes repeat convictions felonies, and requires courts to weigh alleged injury when setting bail.

ca:AB 1881.title: California Indian Freedom Act of 2026.
ca:AB 1881.summary: Enacts the California Indian Freedom Act of 2026, barring governmental agencies from substantially burdening California tribes' religious practices or sacred site access on state lands without a compelling interest, starting January 1, 2028.

ca:AB 1883.title: Workplace surveillance tools.
ca:AB 1883.summary: Bars employers, including governmental entities, from using AI workplace surveillance tools that collect neural data or recognize emotional states, with exceptions; the Labor Commissioner or public prosecutors enforce, with civil penalties up to $500 per violation.

ca:AB 1886.title: Wards: probation.
ca:AB 1886.summary: Applies the 12-month probation limit to wards placed in out-of-home placements, lets courts extend probation but bars new conditions during the extension, and exempts wards committed to secure youth treatment facilities.

ca:AB 1896.title: Public employment: disqualifications.
ca:AB 1896.summary: From 2028, bars, with exceptions, former officers or contractors who personally engaged in immigration enforcement from peace officer and other public employment, requires applicant declarations under penalty of perjury, and lets agencies consider verified news and social media in background checks.

ca:AB 1904.title: Teachers: credentialed educator apprenticeship programs.
ca:AB 1904.summary: Requires the Commission on Teacher Credentialing and the Division of Apprenticeship Standards to partner in approving and monitoring credentialed educator apprenticeship programs, and lets the commission issue apprenticeship permits to educator candidates without a credential who are employed by local educational agencies.

ca:AB 1908.title: Settlement agreements: victims' compensation funding.
ca:AB 1908.summary: Allows courts to enforce, after dismissal, settlements of tort claims against local public entities that are eligible for payment from a victims' compensation fund or similar program; takes effect immediately.

ca:AB 1918.title: Human trafficking: body art practitioners.
ca:AB 1918.summary: Requires body art facilities, by July 1, 2027, to post a human trafficking notice and train employees and registered practitioners, and allows training from nonprofit or Department of Justice materials.

ca:AB 1927.title: Bail Consumer Protection Act.
ca:AB 1927.summary: Makes it a crime to impersonate a licensed bail agent while soliciting bail, or to hire someone to solicit bail when the hirer knew or should have known they are impersonating a licensed bail agent.

ca:AB 1940.title: Unlawful practices: discrimination: menopause.
ca:AB 1940.summary: Adds perimenopause, menopause, postmenopause and related medical conditions to the definition of sex in the Fair Employment and Housing Act and the Unruh Civil Rights Act.

ca:AB 1941.title: Organized metal theft.
ca:AB 1941.summary: Creates the crime of organized metal theft, covering acting with others to steal, receive or possess stolen metal for sale, or recruiting, directing or financing metal theft; punishable as a misdemeanor or felony.

ca:AB 1944.title: Zero-emission transit buses: axle weight.
ca:AB 1944.summary: Until January 1, 2032, sets higher axle weight limits, up to 25,000 pounds, for zero-emission transit buses procured through solicitations issued between 2027 and 2031.

ca:AB 1997.title: Land use: housing development approvals: timelines and processes.
ca:AB 1997.summary: Requires a local agency to approve or disapprove a housing development project within 30 days after certification of its environmental impact report, under specified conditions.

ca:AB 2007.title: Youth programs: identifying information of youth.
ca:AB 2007.summary: Bars nonschool youth programs from using a youth's picture, video, audio, likeness or statements publicly without a parent's written consent, bars making enrollment depend on consent, and lets parents revoke consent and sue.

ca:AB 2011.title: Nonquantitative treatment limitations.
ca:AB 2011.summary: Requires health plans and insurers to follow federal mental health parity rules and guidance as they existed on January 1, 2025, and has the managed care and insurance departments review conflicts with federal rules and jointly issue compliance guidance.

ca:AB 2038.title: Residential property insurance: cancellations and nonrenewals.
ca:AB 2038.summary: Raises from two to three annual periods (36 months) the renewal period insurers must offer after a disaster-caused total loss of a primary structure, and from one to two years the ban on cancelling or non-renewing policies in or next to a fire perimeter.

ca:AB 2065.title: Rates: prohibited cost recovery.
ca:AB 2065.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to find prohibited cost recovery when a utility records ratepayer-excluded costs, to disallow those costs and fine the utility one to three times the amount, and requires annual utility reports on instances.

ca:AB 2076.title: The Parent's Accountability and Child Protection Act: online marketplaces: nitrous oxide.
ca:AB 2076.summary: Adds nitrous oxide to products online sellers must verify age for, bars paying for such products with gift cards, and lets courts raise penalties to up to $250,000 per violation for businesses with over $25 million in annual revenue.

ca:AB 2084.title: Corporation Tax Law: tax-exempt organizations: revocation of tax-exempt status.
ca:AB 2084.summary: Lets the Franchise Tax Board, at its discretion, keep a nonprofit's state tax exemption after its federal exemption is suspended or revoked, if the cause was not fraud, fund misuse, failure to file, or other reporting or governance breaches.

ca:AB 2116.title: Commercial financing.
ca:AB 2116.summary: Beginning January 1, 2028, regulates commercial financing such as factoring and business loans under the Financing Law, requires providers and brokers to be licensed from July 1, 2028, and bans confessions of judgment before default.

ca:AB 2128.title: Housing authorities: term limits and work requirements.
ca:AB 2128.summary: Bars housing authorities and similar providers from imposing term limits or work requirements as a condition of housing eligibility or rent subsidy, unless federal law requires them, while allowing voluntary job training programs.

ca:AB 2179.title: Workplace violence: restraining orders.
ca:AB 2179.summary: Beginning January 1, 2028, lets parties and witnesses appear remotely, free of charge, at workplace violence restraining order hearings, and requires courts to set remote-appearance rules and accept electronic filings.

ca:AB 2222.title: Personal Income Tax Law and Corporation Tax Law: credits: local news outlets: business expense deduction: excessive employee remuneration.
ca:AB 2222.summary: Creates a tax credit for 2027 through 2031: $20,000 per full-time qualifying journalist (up to five), $15,000 for each beyond five, $7,500 per part-time journalist, and an extra $15,000 per new full-time journalism position.

ca:AB 2231.title: California Environmental Quality Act: hospital projects.
ca:AB 2231.summary: Creates streamlined environmental and judicial review procedures, with labor requirements, for a hospital campus construction project in the City of Santa Clara that the city council certifies as meeting specified conditions.

ca:AB 2263.title: Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority: employee housing: transit-oriented joint development projects.
ca:AB 2263.summary: Authorizes the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority to acquire property for employee housing projects serving its employees and the public, and to build affordable rental and for-sale housing for employees, with an annual report to the Legislature.

ca:AB 2313.title: Gas corporations: gas distribution service line replacements: alternatives.
ca:AB 2313.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to have each gas utility, by January 1, 2028, offer certain residential customers whose gas service line is to be replaced a monetary incentive to end gas service instead; emergency replacements are exempt.

ca:AB 2329.title: Surplus residential property: condition-adjusted price of the fair market value: Cities of Pasadena and South Pasadena.
ca:AB 2329.summary: Changes sales of surplus State Route 710 homes in Los Angeles County: offers to former owners, occupants and tenants use a condition-adjusted fair market value as of October 13, 2019, buyers may get purchase assistance, and the selling agency need not make repairs.

ca:AB 2346.title: Vehicles: electric bicycles and speed limits.
ca:AB 2346.summary: From January 1, 2029, requires electric bicycles to have front and rear lamps, class 2 models to have speedometers, and sellers to disclose class and top speed; lets local authorities set 10, 15 or 20 mph path limits.

ca:AB 2397.title: Local government: community facilities districts: financing.
ca:AB 2397.summary: Bars a local legislative body from abandoning, or refusing to levy taxes or incur bonds for, a landowner-petitioned community facilities district financing facilities for housing that includes very low-, low- or moderate-income households, without making specified findings.

ca:AB 2405.title: Mental health.
ca:AB 2405.summary: Requires peace officers taking a person to a designated mental health facility for assessment to take them to the closest appropriate facility, and lets the person state a facility preference.

ca:AB 2413.title: Large-format public advertisements: public expense.
ca:AB 2413.summary: Bars publicly funded billboards, bus wraps, bus stop ads and similar large ads of 24 by 36 inches or more that include a photograph of an elected officer affiliated with the agency.

ca:AB 2437.title: Impounded vehicles.
ca:AB 2437.summary: Adds debit cards to the payment methods vehicle storage facilities must accept for towing and storage fees, and treats requiring ownership documents beyond those specified as refusing to release a vehicle to its legal owner.

ca:AB 2493.title: Electrical corporations: interconnection: Public Utilities Commission: transmission development monitor.
ca:AB 2493.summary: Requires large electrical utilities and transmission owners to submit project schedules for transmission projects needing Public Utilities Commission approval, and requires the commission to create a transmission development monitor by October 1, 2027 to review progress.

ca:AB 2499.title: Health care coverage: claims payments.
ca:AB 2499.summary: As passed by the Assembly, requires the state occupational safety division to propose a heat standard for prison workers by July 1, 2027, and the corrections department to set interim relief measures for excessive weather by April 1, 2027 and run a temperature-monitoring pilot.

ca:AB 2524.title: Pupils: work permits: issuance.
ca:AB 2524.summary: Lets county probation departments and county child welfare agencies issue work permits to certain minors under juvenile court jurisdiction.

ca:AB 2532.title: Cannabis: labels, packaging, and advertising.
ca:AB 2532.summary: Requires edible cannabis and cannabis beverage labels to list the Poison Help line number, and from July 1, 2027 requires serving-size lines on transparent multi-serving beverage containers.

ca:AB 2542.title: Human remains: disposition.
ca:AB 2542.summary: Passes control of a decedent's remains to the next of kin if a funeral director or cemetery authority knows the right-holder was under a domestic violence order against the decedent, or a court determination shows that would be contrary to the decedent's best interests.

ca:AB 2563.title: Sex discrimination: scope.
ca:AB 2563.summary: Requires that state laws banning sex or gender discrimination be interpreted to prohibit sex discrimination, defined to include discrimination based on actual or perceived characteristics, including degree of conformity to sex or gender stereotypes.

ca:AB 2595.title: San Mateo Electric Bicycle Safety Pilot Program.
ca:AB 2595.summary: Until January 1, 2031, lets San Mateo County and its local authorities ban children under 12 from riding class 1 or 2 electric bicycles, with a warning for 60 days and then a $25 fine.

ca:AB 2601.title: Planning and zoning: housing development: streamlined approval and subdivisions.
ca:AB 2601.summary: Makes a housing development of up to two units in a single-family zone eligible for processing alongside an urban lot split parcel map, and lets local agencies condition permits on first recording that map.

ca:AB 2647.title: Energy: nuclear powerplants: assessment.
ca:AB 2647.summary: Requires the Energy Commission to complete by January 1, 2028 an assessment of advanced nuclear technology for critical infrastructure and whether new in-state nuclear plants could meet electricity needs.

ca:AB 2656.title: Public employees: notice: artificial intelligence performing service within scope of work.
ca:AB 2656.summary: Requires certain public employers to give a recognized employee organization 45 days' written notice before developing, buying, or requiring generative AI to perform work within that union's job classifications.

ca:AB 2663.title: Alcoholic beverages: retail on-sale license: off-sale privileges.
ca:AB 2663.summary: Extends to December 31, 2029 the authority of restaurants with off-sale privileges, and breweries, wineries and distillers operating restaurants, to sell distilled spirits and non-beer alcoholic drinks for off-premises consumption; takes effect immediately.

ca:AB 2700.title: Public Utilities Commission: electrical corporations: wildfire victim restitution shortfalls: report: restitution mechanisms.
ca:AB 2700.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission, by January 1, 2028, to report on unpaid restitution to victims of utility-caused wildfires before July 12, 2019, and recommend mechanisms for electrical corporations to pay those shortfalls.

ca:AB 2706.title: Acidified foods and low-acid foods.
ca:AB 2706.summary: Repeals the state's cannery licensing system, requires makers of acidified and low-acid foods to register and use a scheduled process from a processing authority, deems foods made without one misbranded, and adds a $350 annual fee.

ca:AB 2724.title: Insurance: distressed areas.
ca:AB 2724.summary: Requires the Department of Insurance, by July 1, 2027 and yearly, to update distressed areas based on wildland-urban interface changes and hold a public meeting on FAIR Plan factors, and to publish a list of wildland-urban interface ZIP Codes by January 1, 2028.

ca:AB 2739.title: Water: affordability and system stabilization.
ca:AB 2739.summary: Creates a Water Affordability and System Stabilization Trust under the State Treasurer, funded by General Fund transfers; its income goes to water rate assistance and community water affordability funds, 45% each for 25 years, then 50% each.

ca:AB 40.title: California Environmental Quality Act: environmental impact reports: coal handling, storage, and export.
ca:AB 40.summary: Requires an environmental impact report before approving a large-volume bulk coal facility (over 5 million short tons yearly), and bars relying on an existing report when capacity or coal type changes.

ca:AB 635.title: Mobilehome Residency Law Protection Program: Attorney General.
ca:AB 635.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to refer alleged Mobilehome Residency Law and park closure violations to a nonprofit legal services provider within five days, and lets it refer local ordinance violations to enforcement agencies.

ca:AB 647.title: Abandoned recreational vehicles.
ca:AB 647.summary: Extends to January 1, 2032 the authority of Alameda and Los Angeles counties to dispose of abandoned recreational vehicles valued at $4,000 or less, and extends it to any public agency in those counties and to state agencies.

ca:AB 672.title: Real property tax: welfare exemption: community land trusts.
ca:AB 672.summary: Extends to January 1, 2032 the property tax welfare exemption for community land trust property being developed or rehabilitated as housing, and adjusts related lien-date rules.

ca:AB 685.title: Small Business Development Technical Assistance.
ca:AB 685.summary: Revises eligibility for state small business technical assistance center grants, lets centers apply as a network under one fiscal agent, and requires uniform performance metrics, monitoring, and reports to the Legislature.

ca:AB 801.title: Nondiscrimination.
ca:AB 801.summary: Enacts the California Fair Lending Examination Act, requiring the financial regulator to examine certain banks and credit unions at least every four years for compliance with mortgage-lending nondiscrimination laws, and to add that check to mortgage lender examinations.

ca:AB 864.title: Hazardous waste: solar photovoltaic modules.
ca:AB 864.summary: Requires the Department of Toxic Substances Control to hold public workshops by July 1, 2028, and evaluate by July 1, 2029, whether a federal exclusion for hazardous material transferred for reclamation could apply to end-of-life solar panels; permits adopting it by regulation.

ca:AB 982.title: Mining: The Surface Mining and Reclamation Act of 1975: mining operations status: idle reserve mine status.
ca:AB 982.summary: Until January 1, 2033, lets idle aggregate surface mines apply for "Idle Reserve Mine Status," which lets the local lead agency extend an interim management plan by up to 10 years after state review.

ca:SB 1009.title: Juveniles: detention.
ca:SB 1009.summary: Bars juvenile court from detaining a minor in juvenile hall, or committing a ward to physical confinement, unless it finds a less restrictive alternative unsuitable, and requires considering efforts to avoid removal from the home and whether services could allow return.

ca:SB 1012.title: Employment of inmates.
ca:SB 1012.summary: Requires a state committee to help graduates of the California Conservation Camp program enter construction craft laborer apprenticeships, counts program participation as qualifying experience from July 1, 2027, and requires a completion certificate.

ca:SB 1030.title: CalWORKs: unrelated adult male.
ca:SB 1030.summary: Beginning July 1, 2027 or later, repeals the CalWORKs requirement that an unrelated adult male living with a family applying for aid make a financial contribution to the family.

ca:SB 1047.title: Neurodegenerative disease registry program.
ca:SB 1047.summary: Requires the state health department to collect data on frontotemporal degeneration, adds other dementias to the neurodegenerative disease registry, and extends the registry program to January 1, 2032.

ca:SB 1049.title: Health care claims reimbursement.
ca:SB 1049.summary: Gives claimants at least 90 days to submit a corrected claim after a health plan or insurer denies a claim or sends an overpayment notice over a fixable defect, and bars denying it as late.

ca:SB 1051.title: Foster care: childcare.
ca:SB 1051.summary: Authorizes childcare navigators to refer foster children to the county welfare department for the Emergency Child Care Bridge Program for Foster Children, and requires participating counties to determine eligibility of referred children.

ca:SB 1056.title: Criminal procedure.
ca:SB 1056.summary: Requires courts in specified criminal cases involving sexually explicit material of an adult victim to issue a protective order limiting copying and disclosure of the material, while preserving the defendant's ability to prepare a defense.

ca:SB 1073.title: Income taxes: voluntary contributions: Black Cultural District Voluntary Tax Contribution Fund.
ca:SB 1073.summary: Lets taxpayers designate part of their return for a new Black Cultural District Voluntary Tax Contribution Fund, which pays for construction and maintenance of the Black Cultural District in south Los Angeles, for tax years 2026 through 2032.

ca:SB 1085.title: Water supply planning: housing developments.
ca:SB 1085.summary: Requires cities and counties to ask water suppliers, within 15 days of a qualifying housing application, whether the project's water demand is in their urban water plan, and sets a 45-day deadline for water supply assessments for certain housing projects.

ca:SB 1090.title: Planning and zoning: housing development projects: urban lot splits: subdivisions: 2025 Eaton Wildfire: Altadena.
ca:SB 1090.summary: Until January 1, 2030, exempts housing applications and lot-split maps in Altadena ZIP codes 91001 and 91003, filed on or after October 1, 2026, from state ministerial approval requirements, with exceptions.

ca:SB 1098.title: Public Utilities Commission: memorandum and balancing accounts.
ca:SB 1098.summary: Makes the general rate case the primary way to set electric and gas utility revenue requirements, allows memorandum and balancing accounts only for costs that cannot reasonably be anticipated, and requires reviewing existing accounts in the next rate case, closing those not needed.

ca:SB 1099.title: State and local public benefits.
ca:SB 1099.summary: Clarifies that cities', counties' and hospital districts' existing authority to aid people who would otherwise qualify but for a federal welfare law's limits counts as authorization to provide a state or local public benefit under that law.

ca:SB 1107.title: School facilities: design-build: shade structures.
ca:SB 1107.summary: Until December 31, 2031, lets school districts bundle design-build contracts for shade structures at multiple sites in one solicitation when total value is above $1 million up to $10 million, awarding each project as a separate contract.

ca:SB 1111.title: Digital replicas.
ca:SB 1111.summary: Clarifies that a person's voice or likeness includes computer-generated digital replicas for right-of-publicity claims and false impersonation law, and removes a rebuttable presumption for employee likenesses in advertisements.

ca:SB 1130.title: Invasion of privacy: wearable recording devices.
ca:SB 1130.summary: Bars using a wearable recording device to capture sound or video of others in areas of a business where they expect privacy, without their explicit consent, and bars disabling its recording indicator, with exemptions for hearing and communication aids.

ca:SB 1148.title: Security guards: training.
ca:SB 1148.summary: Allows security guards and proprietary private security officers who completed an arrest-powers and use-of-force course to complete their required security-skills training before registration is issued.

ca:SB 1159.title: Artificial intelligence: transparency and governance.
ca:SB 1159.summary: Provides that AI systems, autonomous agents and robots are not a "person" or member of the public under state public records, open meeting, rulemaking, Coastal Act and CEQA laws, and bars knowingly using AI to falsely show a person engaged with an agency.

ca:SB 1167.title: Vehicles: electric bicycles.
ca:SB 1167.summary: Revises which vehicles may not be advertised or sold as electric bicycles, including motor-driven cycles and mopeds, and updates the Vehicle Code definitions of motor-driven cycle and moped.

ca:SB 1172.title: Bradley-Burns Uniform Local Sales and Use Tax Law: tax sharing agreements.
ca:SB 1172.summary: Caps consultant compensation on sales tax sharing agreements at the lower of 5 percent of shared revenue or $250,000, for agreements entered on or after January 1, 2027.

ca:SB 1190.title: Child welfare: transport escort services.
ca:SB 1190.summary: Expands transport escort service rules to any minor transport, exempts rideshare, community care facilities and private childcare, requires trustline registry information for out-of-state trips, limits behavioral restraints, and lets the Attorney General sue to enforce.

ca:SB 1203.title: Security services.
ca:SB 1203.summary: From 2029, requires 42 hours of classroom training for proprietary private security officers, including 2 hours on workers' rights, plus 12 paid hours of annual skills training with 4 on de-escalation, and raises certain recordkeeping fines from $500 to $1,000.

ca:SB 1209.title: Insurance: examination of insurers.
ca:SB 1209.summary: Requires insurers examined by the Insurance Commissioner to correct violations identified in the report, subjects non-correcting insurers to penalties, and lets the commissioner issue show-cause orders to compel compliance.

ca:SB 1223.title: Fairs: contracting.
ca:SB 1223.summary: Bars fairs from issuing bid invitations or requests for proposals for services in a way that limits bidding to one bidder, except as specified, and voids contracts awarded in violation.

ca:SB 1237.title: Civil Rights Department.
ca:SB 1237.summary: Raises the penalty for repeat failures to file employer pay data reports to up to $1,000 per employee, and requires the Civil Rights Department to publish the number of reports submitted each year.

ca:SB 1246.title: Autonomous vehicles.
ca:SB 1246.summary: Requires autonomous vehicle makers to maintain capacity for peak concurrent remote assistance sessions, keep remote drivers in the U.S. with California-valid licenses, and immediately dispatch local incident technicians after crashes or emergency-official requests.

ca:SB 1255.title: Postsecondary education: Designation of California Hispanic-Serving Institutions.
ca:SB 1255.summary: Establishes, upon appropriation, a California Hispanic-Serving Institutions designation and governing board, with the California State University Chancellor's office managing applications for campuses serving Latino students.

ca:SB 1359.title: Natural Gas Ratepayer Protection Act.
ca:SB 1359.summary: Requires gas utilities to report annually on gas pipeline replacement spending, and requires the Public Utilities Commission to consider a depreciation framework that reflects expected declines in gas demand.

ca:SB 1369.title: Recall petitions.
ca:SB 1369.summary: Requires paid petition signature gatherers to orally tell each person they are paid, and sets a 120-day deadline to submit recall petitions for superior court judges in jurisdictions with 50,000 or more registered voters.

ca:SB 1379.title: County of Riverside: separation of county offices: in-custody reports.
ca:SB 1379.summary: Requires Riverside County to separate the sheriff and coroner offices by July 1, 2027, create a medical examiner office to handle death investigations, and publish information on in-custody persons online.

ca:SB 1406.title: Sales and Use Tax Law: vehicles: shell companies.
ca:SB 1406.summary: Treats a partnership as a California resident for the vehicle, vessel and aircraft use-tax presumption if 50% of its interests are held by residents, treats shell companies with a resident owner as residents, and makes shell company officers and owners personally liable for unpaid tax.

ca:SB 1417.title: Mutual water companies: assessments and water charges: notice.
ca:SB 1417.summary: Bars mutual water companies from billing shareholders' tenants for water costs, with exceptions, and requires those operating public water systems to give notice and hold a public meeting before an assessment or a water charge increase above 20%.

ca:SB 226.title: Infrastructure revitalization financing districts.
ca:SB 226.summary: Specifies that the commercial or industrial structures for private use that infrastructure revitalization financing districts may finance include entertainment or sports facilities.

ca:SB 331.title: Health care coverage: hearing aids.
ca:SB 331.summary: Requires large-group health plans issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2028 to cover medically necessary hearing aids and related services for enrollees under 21, and lets plans cap coverage at $3,000 per device.

ca:SB 342.title: Contractors: unlicensed work.
ca:SB 342.summary: Lets a contractor sue for pay on specified projects, including public works and commercial or institutional construction, if licensed when the contract was signed and during the work billed, and limits repayment claims against unlicensed contractors on those projects to the unlicensed period.

ca:SB 401.title: Political Reform Act of 1974: filing deadlines: emergency situations.
ca:SB 401.summary: Lets the Fair Political Practices Commission extend filing deadlines by up to 60 days for people in emergency-affected areas, except during the 90 days before an election.

ca:SB 503.title: Health care services: artificial intelligence.
ca:SB 503.summary: Requires developers and deployers of AI clinical decision support systems to identify risks of biased impacts, and developers to provide statements of intended uses, known risks, and documentation to deployers.

ca:SB 549.title: Heritage schools: enrollment and notice.
ca:SB 549.summary: Expands the definition of "heritage school" to include schools serving children younger than 4 years 9 months in kindergarten through grade 12, and requires enrollment notice that the Department of Education does not regulate or monitor them.

ca:SB 577.title: Public entities.
ca:SB 577.summary: Shortens from 5 to 3 years the discovery-based filing window for childhood sexual assault claims from before 2024, and requires plaintiffs 40 or older suing public entities over them to prove by clear and convincing evidence that the entity knew of misconduct.

ca:SB 677.title: Housing financing: joint powers agreements: bond approvals: subdivisions: tentative and final maps: appeals.
ca:SB 677.summary: States that a joint powers authority's jurisdiction covers the combined area of its members, and lets the State Treasurer join such authorities without Department of General Services approval to give federal tax approvals for certain rental housing bonds.

ca:SB 685.title: Special education: nonpublic schools and agencies.
ca:SB 685.summary: Removes the requirement that nonpublic special education schools be nonsectarian, while barring public funds from paying for religious instruction and barring religious instruction for pupils placed by local education agencies.

ca:SB 692.title: Vehicles: homelessness.
ca:SB 692.summary: Authorizes city and county agencies to dismantle an abandoned vehicle that cannot be moved and was declared a nuisance or hazard, after posting notice at least 15 days beforehand and notifying owners, who may request a hearing.

ca:SB 715.title: Elections.
ca:SB 715.summary: Moves the Secretary of State's deadline to notify partisan and voter-nominated candidates of their opponents from 73 to 78 days before an election, moves other election deadlines earlier, and requires candidates to certify ballot designation worksheets under penalty of perjury.

ca:SB 804.title: Hydrogen Pipeline Safety Act.
ca:SB 804.summary: Creates the Hydrogen Pipeline Safety Act, making the State Fire Marshal regulate hydrogen pipeline operation and safety, with operator fees and civil penalties like those under the existing hazardous liquid pipeline safety law.

ca:SB 811.title: Hazardous materials: metal shredding facilities.
ca:SB 811.summary: Creates a permit system run by the Department of Toxic Substances Control for metal shredding facilities, with application requirements, public meetings, and operating and transport rules, separate from hazardous waste law.

ca:SB 832.title: Upper Los Angeles River and Tributaries Working Group: membership: revitalization plan.
ca:SB 832.summary: Raises the maximum appointees to the Upper Los Angeles River and Tributaries Working Group from 23 to 25, requires one to represent the council district with the most river miles, and requires yearly meetings to evaluate the plan and propose amendments.

ca:SB 868.title: Electricity: portable solar generation devices.
ca:SB 868.summary: Until January 1, 2030, exempts portable solar generation devices from interconnection requirements and bars utilities from charging customers fees for using them.

ca:SB 903.title: Mental health professionals: artificial intelligence.
ca:SB 903.summary: Limits use of artificial intelligence in psychotherapy to administrative or supplementary support, and requires patients be informed and consent before AI records, transcribes, or screens them for psychotherapy.

ca:SB 905.title: Electricity.
ca:SB 905.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to consider reduced returns on equity for certain utility capital costs, open a rulemaking on alternative financing with a report by December 31, 2028, and require large electric utilities to publish grid utilization data.

ca:SB 913.title: Resource adequacy: aggregated distributed energy resources.
ca:SB 913.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission, by June 30, 2028, to improve pathways for aggregated distributed energy resources to count as resource adequacy capacity, without duplicate compensation for net metering customers.

ca:SB 930.title: Student Test Taker Privacy Protection Act: end-to-end encryption.
ca:SB 930.summary: Beginning July 1, 2027, requires businesses providing exam proctoring to school districts, county offices of education and charter schools for classroom exams to use end-to-end encryption, meaning data is unreadable by anyone but the intended recipient, including the proctoring business.

ca:SB 938.title: Peace officers: training requirements.
ca:SB 938.summary: Provides that service as a federal immigration inspection, border enforcement, or removal officer, and its training, does not alone qualify for a Regular Basic Course Waiver for peace officer training.

ca:SB 941.title: Private detention facilities: canteens.
ca:SB 941.summary: Caps the price of commissary items at private for-profit detention facilities at a 35 percent markup above the vendor price.

ca:SB 944.title: Medi-Cal: acupuncture.
ca:SB 944.summary: Makes acupuncture a covered Medi-Cal benefit subject to utilization controls and federal funding, instead of covered only when federal matching funds are provided, and covers it subject to appropriation if federal funds are unavailable.

ca:SB 945.title: School curriculum: physical education framework: cardiopulmonary resuscitation: automated external defibrillators.
ca:SB 945.summary: Requires the Instructional Quality Commission, when the physical education framework is next revised after January 1, 2027, to consider including content on the importance, performance and use of compression-only CPR and automated external defibrillators.

ca:SB 947.title: Employment: automated decision systems.
ca:SB 947.summary: Beginning July 1, 2027, bars employers from relying solely on an automated decision system for discipline or termination, requires human corroboration, written notice and employee access to their data used, and bars retaliation; the Labor Commissioner enforces.

ca:SB 951.title: Employment: technological displacement: notice.
ca:SB 951.summary: Requires employers giving mass layoff notice due to AI or automation to describe the affected job functions, directs the state to publish summaries of such notices, and requires a report to the Legislature on AI's hiring effects by 2028.

ca:SB 996.title: Manufactured housing: conformity.
ca:SB 996.summary: Changes the state definition of manufactured home to a structure built on or after June 15, 1976, with or without a foundation, matching the federal definition.

co:HJR25-1001.title: State of the State
co:HJR25-1001.summary: Calls a joint session of the House and Senate on January 9, 2025 to hear a message from the Governor, and appoints a committee to escort him.

co:HJR25-1002.title: State of the Judiciary
co:HJR25-1002.summary: Calls a joint session of the House and Senate on January 10, 2025 to hear a message from the Chief Justice of the Colorado Supreme Court, and appoints an escort committee.

co:HJR25-1003.title: Joint Session Address by Tribal Councils
co:HJR25-1003.summary: Amends a resolution calling a joint session to hear Ute tribal councils, changing wording: the Southern Ute Indian Tribe "of Ignacio" becomes "near Ignacio," "Capote" becomes "Kaputa," "Ute Nations" becomes "Nuuchiu," and two tribal council names are shortened.

co:HJR25-1004.title: Water Project Eligibility Lists
co:HJR25-1004.summary: Approves additions, modifications and deletions to the drinking water and water pollution control project eligibility lists for the revolving funds administered by the Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority.

co:HJR25-1005.title: Commemoration of Martin Luther King Jr. Day
co:HJR25-1005.summary: Encourages observances across Colorado to commemorate Martin Luther King Jr. Day and commends the state board of education for adding his legacy to the social studies standards.

co:HJR25-1007.title: Troy Jackson Memorial Highway
co:HJR25-1007.summary: Designates a stretch of Interstate 25 (southbound from mile marker 199.4 and northbound at mile marker 194.8) as the Firefighters Memorial Highway in memory of Chief Troy Jackson.

co:HJR25-1008.title: Honoring Co-Responders & Behavioral Professionals
co:HJR25-1008.summary: Designates September 14 to 20, 2025 as Co-Responder Units and Behavioral Health Crisis Professionals Week in Colorado.

co:HJR25-1009.title: Black History Month February of 2025
co:HJR25-1009.summary: Recognizes February 2025 as Black History Month in Colorado.

co:HJR25-1024.title: Sand Creek Massacre Memorial
co:HJR25-1024.summary: Approves a plan to install a Sand Creek Massacre memorial on the west grounds of the state capitol and to lend the "Union Soldier" statue long-term to the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs for display.

co:HJR25-1026.title: Designate Representative Hugh McKean Memorial Highway
co:HJR25-1026.summary: Designates Colorado Highway 402 from U.S. 287 to Interstate 25 as the Rep. Hugh McKean Memorial Highway, and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:HJR25-1027.title: Designate Commissioner Lew Gaiter III Memorial Highway
co:HJR25-1027.summary: Designates part of Colorado Highway 1 in Larimer County, from East County Road 60 to Interstate 25, as the Commissioner Lew Gaiter III Memorial Highway, and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:HJR25-1028.title: Designate April 25 Colorado Sportsmen's Day 2025
co:HJR25-1028.summary: Urges legislators and institutions to join and work with the Colorado Legislative Sportsmen's Caucus and declares April 25, 2025 as Sportsmen's Day in Colorado.

co:HJR25-1030.title: Products with Forced Labor Components
co:HJR25-1030.summary: Declares that Colorado will use its purchasing power to support businesses whose products are ethically sourced or made without forced labor, and encourages state and local economic development offices to pursue attracting such businesses to Colorado.

co:HJR26-1001.title: General Assembly Positions & Salary Ranges
co:HJR26-1001.summary: Creates the officer and employee positions, with salary ranges, for the 2026 legislative session of the General Assembly.

co:HJR26-1017.title: Ute Water Rights
co:HJR26-1017.summary: Urges the United States to meet its trust obligations to the Southern Ute and Ute Mountain Ute tribes on reserved water rights, including rehabilitating the Pine River irrigation project and funding Ute Mountain Ute water infrastructure.

co:HJR26-1018.title: Plains-to-Pines Scenic Corridor
co:HJR26-1018.summary: Designates State Highway 86 through Elbert County as the "Plains-to-Pines Scenic Corridor", and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs and landscaping.

co:HJR26-1020.title: International Women's Day
co:HJR26-1020.summary: Honors women's achievements, recognizes March 8 as International Women's Day in Colorado, and commits the General Assembly to supporting policies that remove barriers to opportunity for women.

co:HJR26-1022.title: Boulder County Road of Remembrance
co:HJR26-1022.summary: Designates Arapahoe Road in Boulder County, from U.S. 36 to U.S. 287, as the "Road of Remembrance", and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:HJR26-1023.title: Latino/a Advocacy Day
co:HJR26-1023.summary: Recognizes the achievements of Latinas and Latinos in Colorado, honors Latino/a Advocacy Day participants, and states the General Assembly's commitment to creating a Colorado that will one day work for all, regardless of immigration status.

co:HJR26-1024.title: Designate Educators & Teachers Memorial Highway
co:HJR26-1024.summary: Designates State Highway 92 from mile marker 3 to mile marker 7, through Read, as the Educators and Teachers Memorial Highway, and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:HJR26-1026.title: Governor Roy Romer Memorial Highway
co:HJR26-1026.summary: Honors former Governor Roy Romer and lets the transportation department accept donations to sign Interstate 25 in Denver County, mile markers 204.51 to 213.13, as the Governor Roy Romer Memorial Highway.

co:HJR26-1028.title: Full and Fair Funding of Public Schools
co:HJR26-1028.summary: Reaffirms the importance of fair and full funding of public education and states the House's intent to review the school-finance adequacy studies, pick a methodology, and develop a multi-year plan, with revenue triggers, to phase in recommendations.

co:HJR26-1030.title: Mono & Matt Road Designation
co:HJR26-1030.summary: Designates Colorado Highway 14 in Weld County between mile markers 165 and 167 as "Mono & Matt Road", and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:HJR26-1031.title: 2027 Session Convening Date & Deadlines
co:HJR26-1031.summary: Sets Monday, January 11, 2027 as the convening date of the 2027 legislative session and adds Joint Rule 22B, an alternative schedule of bill-filing, introduction and other legislative deadlines for that session.

co:HJR26-1032.title: Notify Governor of Adjournment
co:HJR26-1032.summary: Appoints a five-member joint committee to notify the Governor that the 2026 legislative session is about to adjourn sine die.

co:SJR25-001.title: Temporary Joint Rules
co:SJR25-001.summary: Adopts the Seventy-fourth General Assembly's joint rules as the temporary joint rules of the Seventy-fifth General Assembly.

co:SJR25-003.title: Colorado Commission on Uniform State Laws Appointments
co:SJR25-003.summary: Appoints Senator Marc Snyder, Representative Cecelia Espenoza, Bob Gardner, Claire Levy, Anne McGihon and Joseph Whitfield to the Colorado Commission on Uniform State Laws for two-year terms.

co:SJR25-004.title: Reproductive Rights and Justice Day
co:SJR25-004.summary: Affirms that Colorado will continue to protect reproductive rights and access to essential medical care, and designates January 22 each year as Reproductive Rights and Justice Day.

co:SJR25-005.title: Missing Persons Day
co:SJR25-005.summary: Designates February 4 of each year as Missing Persons Day in Colorado.

co:SJR25-006.title: Condemnation of January 6 Insurrection Pardons
co:SJR25-006.summary: Condemns the pardons of people involved in the January 6, 2021 events at the U.S. Capitol and condemns the firing of FBI agents assigned to those cases.

co:SJR25-009.title: Protection of Colorado's Public Lands
co:SJR25-009.summary: Declares support for keeping national public lands under federal stewardship, opposes efforts to sell, transfer or dispose of them, and urges Colorado's governor, attorney general and congressional delegation to oppose such efforts.

co:SJR25-011.title: Latino/a Advocacy Day 2025
co:SJR25-011.summary: Recognizes the achievements of Latinas and Latinos in Colorado, honors Latino/a Advocacy Day participants, and states the General Assembly's commitment to creating a Colorado that will one day work for all, regardless of immigration status.

co:SJR25-015.title: Officer Evan A. Dunn Memorial Highway
co:SJR25-015.summary: Designates Colorado Highway 58 from mile marker 0 to Golden's eastern city limits as the Officer Evan A. Dunn Memorial Highway, and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:SJR25-017.title: Honoring Daniel T. Griffin
co:SJR25-017.summary: Designates the North Academy Bridge over Interstate 25 in Colorado Springs as the Naval Aviation Pilot and Aviation Machinist Mate Petty Officer First Class Daniel T. Griffin Bridge, honoring a Navy pilot killed in the Pearl Harbor attack.

co:SJR25-019.title: Colorado Home Education Day
co:SJR25-019.summary: Recognizes April 10, 2025 as Home Education Day in Colorado.

co:SJR25-021.title: Full & Fair Funding of Public Schools
co:SJR25-021.summary: Reaffirms the importance of fair and full funding of public education and states the Senate's intent to review the school-finance adequacy studies, pick a methodology, and develop a multi-year plan, with revenue triggers, to phase in recommendations.

co:SJR25-023.title: Notify Governor of Adjournment
co:SJR25-023.summary: Appoints a joint committee of two senators and three representatives to notify the Governor that the 2025 legislative session is about to adjourn sine die.

co:SJR25-024.title: Adjourn Sine Die
co:SJR25-024.summary: Provides that the General Assembly's first regular session, when it adjourns on May 7, 2025, stands adjourned sine die.

co:SJR26-001.title: Water Projects Eligibility Lists
co:SJR26-001.summary: Adopts additions, modifications and deletions to the Drinking Water and Water Pollution Control project eligibility lists for the revolving funds run by the Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority.

co:SJR26-002.title: State of the State
co:SJR26-002.summary: Schedules a joint session of the House and Senate at 11:00 a.m. on January 15, 2026 to hear a message from the Governor, and provides for a committee of three senators and three representatives to escort the Governor.

co:SJR26-003.title: Joint Session Address by Tribal Councils
co:SJR26-003.summary: Calls a joint session of the Senate and House on January 16, 2026, to hear a message from the Ute Mountain Ute and Southern Ute tribal councils, and appoints a committee to escort the tribal representatives.

co:SJR26-006.title: Coloradans Navigating Complex United States Immigration System
co:SJR26-006.summary: Reaffirms immigrant Coloradans' civil rights; calls on federal immigration authorities to end masked or unidentified personnel and avoid enforcement near courthouses, schools and clinics except in narrow cases; and urges federal immigration reform, including citizenship pathways.

co:SJR26-007.title: Black History Month February of 2026
co:SJR26-007.summary: Recognizes February 2026 as the 100th Black History Month and honors the contributions of Americans of African descent to Colorado and the United States.

co:SJR26-011.title: Designate Sergeant John "Jack" Thurman Memorial Highway
co:SJR26-011.summary: Designates U.S. Highway 34 between Wilson Avenue and North County Road 23H as the Sgt. John "Jack" Thurman Memorial Highway, and lets the transportation department accept donations for signs.

co:SJR26-015.title: Protecting Colorado's National Public Lands
co:SJR26-015.summary: Declares support for keeping national public lands under federal management, opposes efforts to reduce public input in their management, and asks Colorado's congressional delegation, governor and attorney general to defend those public processes.

co:SJR26-016.title: Improve Retirement Readiness & Financial Well-Being
co:SJR26-016.summary: Encourages workers to seek financial education about retirement and says the General Assembly should consider adding lifetime income options to the PERA defined contribution and voluntary savings plans.

co:SJR26-017.title: Reappoint Kerri L. Hunter as State Auditor
co:SJR26-017.summary: Reappoints Kerri L. Hunter as state auditor for a term from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2031.

co:SJR26-018.title: Recognizing Celebration of Nowruz
co:SJR26-018.summary: Recognizes the celebration of Nowruz, expresses support for civil rights and democratic freedoms for the Iranian people, and mourns civilians killed in violence and war.

co:SJR26-020.title: Recognize Home Education Day
co:SJR26-020.summary: Recognizes April 9, 2026 as Home Education Day in Colorado and honors home educators and home-educated children.

co:SJR26-022.title: Plastic Pollution Awareness
co:SJR26-022.summary: Designates July 12 through 18, 2026 as Plastic Pollution Awareness Week in Colorado, citing the need to raise awareness of plastic pollution and its sources.

co:SJR26-023.title: Recognize Young Americans Bank
co:SJR26-023.summary: Recognizes the contributions of Young Americans Bank and the Young Americans Center for Financial Education to financial literacy education for Colorado students.

co:SJR26-024.title: Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month
co:SJR26-024.summary: Designates May 2026 as Motorcycle Safety Awareness Month in Colorado.

co:SJR26-026.title: Adjourn Sine Die
co:SJR26-026.summary: Provides that the General Assembly's second regular session, when it adjourns on May 13, 2026, stands adjourned sine die.

ct:HB 5001.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ABSENTEE VOTING FOR ALL AND VARIOUS OTHER REFORMS RELATED TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF ELECTIONS.
ct:HB 5001.summary: As amended, allows no-excuse absentee voting, consolidates absentee ballot envelopes, sets a process to cure unsigned ballots, requires risk-limiting audits, and bars law enforcement, and anyone wearing a mask, from within 250 feet of election sites, with exceptions.

ct:HB 5003.title: AN ACT CONCERNING WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND WORKING CONDITIONS IN THE STATE.
ct:HB 5003.summary: Strikes, by amendment, the section letting food service establishments sell lobsters longer or shorter than Lobster Management Area 6 legal sizes if not taken from Area 6 waters or landed in Connecticut, legal where taken, and documented in writing.

ct:HB 5004.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CHILD WELFARE ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY.
ct:HB 5004.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Families to make emergency placements with relatives or close family friends when conditions are met, allows appeal of foster license denials, creates caregiver grants (maximum $625) and after-school grants, and requires a public online dashboard.

ct:HB 5039.title: AN ACT REQUIRING TRANSPARENCY AND ADDITIONAL OVERSIGHT OF THE DISTRIBUTION OF CERTAIN LEGISLATIVELY DIRECTED FUNDS AND APPROPRIATIONS FOR OTHER EXPENSES.
ct:HB 5039.summary: Limits state agencies from funding entities at the General Assembly's direction unless legislation or budget sheets name the recipient, requires uniform Office of Policy and Management procedures and recipient and agency reports, and restricts certain uses of agencies' Other Expenses appropriations.

ct:HB 5043.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONVERTIBLE PISTOLS, UNFINISHED FRAMES OR UNFINISHED LOWER RECEIVERS, VOLUNTARY RELINQUISHMENT OF FIREARMS AND AMMUNITION AND REFUNDABILITY OF PERMITS FOR SALE AT RETAIL OF FIREARMS AND FOR CARRYING OF PISTOLS AND REVOLVERS.
ct:HB 5043.summary: Makes it a class D felony to knowingly sell or import convertible pistols made on or after October 1, 2026, bars unpermitted sales of unfinished frames and receivers, allows voluntary surrender of firearms to police, and requires $70 pistol permit refunds when deadlines are missed.

ct:HB 5126.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR MINOR AND TECHNICAL REVISIONS TO STATUTES CONCERNING CONSUMER PROTECTION.
ct:HB 5126.summary: Makes technical changes to statutes on the home condition disclosure form, homemaker-companion agencies, and the Connecticut Data Privacy Act.

ct:HB 5127.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CREDIT CARDS AND HEALTH AND VETERINARY CARE SERVICES.
ct:HB 5127.summary: As amended, starting January 1, 2027, bars health care and veterinary providers from promoting third-party financing in certain ways, completing applications, or charging a financing account before the service date; requires a written disclosure before discussing financing terms.

ct:HB 5140.title: AN ACT ALLOWING DENTAL HYGIENISTS TO PROVIDE DENTAL HYGIENE SERVICES IN PATIENTS' PRIVATE RESIDENCES.
ct:HB 5140.summary: Allows dental hygienists with at least two years of practice to provide dental hygiene services in a patient's private residence, subject to the requirements for public health facility practice and state regulations.

ct:HB 5141.title: AN ACT REQUIRING FEAR OF RETALIATION TRAINING FOR PERSONS PROVIDING ASSISTED LIVING SERVICES IN MANAGED RESIDENTIAL COMMUNITIES.
ct:HB 5141.summary: Requires assisted living services agencies in managed residential communities to give all employees annual training on residents' fear of retaliation, covering complaint rights, examples of retaliation, and ways to prevent it.

ct:HB 5142.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE USE OF TECHNOLOGY FOR VIRTUAL MONITORING IN RESIDENTIAL CARE HOMES.
ct:HB 5142.summary: Allows residential care home residents to use their own audio or video devices to remotely monitor their rooms, with notice and consent requirements for roommates, and limits nursing homes' liability immunity while extending similar immunity to residential care homes.

ct:HB 5143.title: AN ACT REQUIRING TRAINING FOR HOMEMAKER-COMPANION AGENCY EMPLOYEES.
ct:HB 5143.summary: Requires homemaker-companion agencies to provide at least eight hours of paid training yearly starting January 1, 2027, and registries to ensure referred workers complete approved training.

ct:HB 5145.title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PUBLIC UTILITIES REGULATORY COMMISSION TO REPORT ON THE REVIEW PROCESS FOR CERTAIN WATER COMPANIES THAT REQUEST TO CEASE OPERATIONS.
ct:HB 5145.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority to report by January 15, 2027 on water company requests to cease operations or discontinue service over the past two years, including docket timelines and materials used.

ct:HB 5146.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A STUDY OF THE REMEDIATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF BROWNFIELDS IN THIS STATE.
ct:HB 5146.summary: Directs the state brownfields working group to study brownfield remediation and development issues, including those caused by the release-based cleanup program, and report to legislative committees by January 1, 2027.

ct:HB 5155.title: AN ACT CONCERNING PESTICIDE REPORTING MODERNIZATION.
ct:HB 5155.summary: Establishes a legislative working group, including state agency, farm, industry and environmental representatives, to examine creating a searchable database of pesticide sales and use, reviewing costs and the databases of at least two other states.

ct:HB 5163.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A TASK FORCE TO STUDY METHODS AND PROGRAMS FOR IMPROVING AFFORDABILITY FOR CHILDREN, FAMILIES AND YOUNG PROFESSIONALS.
ct:HB 5163.summary: Establishes a task force to study programs and barriers affecting affordability for children, families and young professionals, including cash assistance, child care costs, housing, transportation and health care access, and to recommend policies and identify funding sources.

ct:HB 5165.title: AN ACT REQUIRING AN EVALUATION OF THE APPOINTMENT OF A RECEIVER TO MANAGE HOSPITALS IN FINANCIAL DISTRESS OR OPERATIONAL CRISIS.
ct:HB 5165.summary: As amended, requires the Commissioner of Public Health to evaluate whether the Attorney General should be authorized to petition Superior Court to appoint a receiver for hospitals meeting defined financial distress or operational crisis criteria, and to report by October 1, 2027.

ct:HB 5208.title: AN ACT CONCERNING DATA SECURITY, PAYROLL PROCESSING, CONSUMER FRAUD PROTECTION, MORTGAGE LOANS AND EMPLOYEE CREDIT RATES.
ct:HB 5208.summary: As amended, requires Department of Banking-regulated entities to adopt written data security programs; requires licensees, banks and credit unions to report data security incidents to the department within three business days; orders a payroll-check study and a fraud working group; narrows flood-insurance notice duties.

ct:HB 5211.title: AN ACT CONCERNING COMMERCIAL FINANCING.
ct:HB 5211.summary: Starting July 1, 2027, applies disclosure and registration rules to all sales-based financing, removing the $250,000 exemption, and requires an estimated APR disclosure; from October 1, 2026, voids confidentiality clauses in new financing contracts.

ct:HB 5215.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TECHNICAL REVISIONS TO THE EDUCATION AND EARLY CHILDHOOD STATUTES.
ct:HB 5215.summary: Makes technical changes to education and early childhood statutes, effective upon passage.

ct:HB 5222.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONSUMER PROTECTION, CANNABIS, DATA PRIVACY, FIRE INSPECTIONS, CRIMINAL MISCHIEF AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
ct:HB 5222.summary: Makes various changes, including data broker, facial recognition and surveillance pricing rules, a cannabis flower THC limit, ticket sales rules, mold remediation, a residential fire inspection pilot, and criminal penalties for damaging critical infrastructure.

ct:HB 5224.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF CONSUMER PROTECTION'S RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING VARIOUS GUARANTY FUNDS.
ct:HB 5224.summary: Amends Special Act 14-12 to redescribe the Point Stratford Infrastructure Improvement District in Stratford as three assessor parcels, and includes off-site locations that government agencies require for project improvements.

ct:HB 5229.title: AN ACT CONCERNING GAMING.
ct:HB 5229.summary: Makes gaming changes, including requiring a toll-free help line for online wagering licensees, limiting gaming ads aimed at minors or on college campuses, and requiring a study of prediction markets.

ct:HB 5239.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF DEVELOPMENTAL SERVICES' RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING THE INDEPENDENT MORTALITY REVIEW BOARD AND FATALITY REVIEW BOARD.
ct:HB 5239.summary: Establishes the Department of Developmental Services' Independent Mortality Review Board in statute, removing the reference to Executive Order 57, and lets the chairperson add members as long as most are not department employees.

ct:HB 5240.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF DEVELOPMENTAL SERVICES' RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO DEVELOPMENTAL SERVICES STATUTES.
ct:HB 5240.summary: Allows the Department of Developmental Services to pay housing subsidies directly to landlords and changes its community residential facility loan program, including raising the maximum capital repair loan and requiring borrowers to be licensed or certified providers.

ct:HB 5243.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A WORKING GROUP TO DEVELOP AN ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND TOURISM PLAN FOR THE GREATER MYSTIC AREA.
ct:HB 5243.summary: Creates a working group to develop an economic development and tourism plan for Groton and Stonington, examining funding sources for Stonington Harbor breakwater restoration, traffic and parking options, and easements and infrastructure for coastal resiliency.

ct:HB 5244.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT'S RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING THE AGENCY FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE CAP AND EMPLOYMENT PROMISSORY NOTES.
ct:HB 5244.summary: Raises from $10 million to $25 million the two-year cap on financial assistance for a business project without legislative approval, and lets employers with over 25 employees require employees to sign promissory notes repaying employer-paid H-1B visa fees.

ct:HB 5246.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TECHNICAL REVISIONS TO STATUTES CONCERNING ENERGY AND TECHNOLOGY.
ct:HB 5246.summary: Makes technical changes to energy-related statutes.

ct:HB 5247.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A TEST BED TECHNOLOGIES PROGRAM.
ct:HB 5247.summary: Lets state agencies pilot-test technologies or processes from small contractors or minority business enterprises that may cut operating costs, paid for by the applicant, with Administrative Services evaluating projects and later purchases possible under a competitive-bidding waiver.

ct:HB 5256.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PROCESS FOR INITIATING LOCAL LEGISLATION IN THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY.
ct:HB 5256.summary: Eliminates the requirement that a town or district seeking a change to its special act powers file its request with the secretary of the state 10 days before the legislative session.

ct:HB 5259.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE EDUCATION OF HOMELESS CHILDREN AND YOUTH.
ct:HB 5259.summary: Ties the existing requirement that boards of education serve homeless children and youth under the federal McKinney-Vento Act to the law as it stood on December 23, 2022.

ct:HB 5265.title: AN ACT CONCERNING COURT-ORDERED ACCOUNTINGS OF COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITY FINANCIAL RECORDS AND REVISING THE DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITIES.
ct:HB 5265.summary: Lets unit owners holding at least 20% of an association's votes petition the court for an independent audit, with a CPA's opinion of apparent fraud and no similar audit in the prior 12 months; adds a common interest statement to residential condition reports.

ct:HB 5281.title: AN ACT CONCERNING PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT.
ct:HB 5281.summary: As amended, raises from 10,000 to 20,000 the population ceiling for distressed or environmental justice towns where voters may petition for a referendum reversing a state permit approval or denial for a new waste incinerator or similar facility.

ct:HB 5287.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TECHNICAL REVISIONS TO STATUTES RELATING TO PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT.
ct:HB 5287.summary: Makes technical changes to statutes on municipal debt financing and planning, effective October 1, 2026.

ct:HB 5288.title: AN ACT CONCERNING UTILITY CONNECTIONS FOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS.
ct:HB 5288.summary: Applies the as-of-right accessory dwelling unit zoning rules to towns exercising zoning power under special acts, and bars investor-owned water companies from requiring separate utility connections or imposing connection fees or capacity charges for such units.

ct:HB 5291.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF EMERGENCY SERVICES AND PUBLIC PROTECTION'S RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING VARIOUS STATUTES RELATING TO PUBLIC SAFETY.
ct:HB 5291.summary: Makes assorted public safety changes, including requiring fire departments to notify the state of a new fire chief within 10 business days, limiting the test-result delivery deadline to breath tests, and changing DNA testing, police training council and fireworks certificate rules.

ct:HB 5295.title: AN ACT NAMING THE CONNECTICUT NATIONAL GUARD READINESS CENTER IN THE TOWN OF PUTNAM.
ct:HB 5295.summary: Names the state military readiness center in Putnam the John N. Dempsey Putnam National Guard Readiness Center.

ct:HB 5311.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE NONISSUANCE OF A STANDING CRIMINAL PROTECTIVE ORDER IN THE CASE OF A FAMILY VIOLENCE CRIME.
ct:HB 5311.summary: Requires a court that does not issue a standing criminal protective order after a family violence crime conviction, or a not-guilty finding by reason of mental disease or defect, to state its reasons on the record.

ct:HB 5312.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CIVIL ACTION FOR THE OFFICE OF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL AND A PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION FOR VICTIMS OF UNLAWFUL DISSEMINATION OF A SYNTHETICALLY CREATED INTIMATE IMAGE.
ct:HB 5312.summary: Lets people harmed by the knowing, intentional dissemination of a synthetically created intimate image sue for an injunction and damages, and requires covered platforms to set up a removal-request process and act on requests within 48 hours.

ct:HB 5313.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A PLAN FOR THE USE OF UNIFORM STATE-WIDE CASE IDENTIFICATION CODES IN DOMESTIC VIOLENCE CASES.
ct:HB 5313.summary: Requires the Chief Court Administrator to develop a plan by July 1, 2027 for uniform statewide case identification codes for criminal domestic violence cases in judicial, prosecution and public safety data systems.

ct:HB 5323.title: AN ACT CONCERNING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO THE EDUCATION STATUTES.
ct:HB 5323.summary: Makes several education changes, including letting retired parole officers provide armed school security, barring schools from setting grade 9-12 athletic academic eligibility above Connecticut Interscholastic Athletic Conference standards, creating a therapeutic arts grant program, and starting a school administrator mentorship pilot.

ct:HB 5331.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE AIR PERMITS OF CERTAIN CREMATORIES.
ct:HB 5331.summary: Requires the environmental protection commissioner to convene a working group by June 15, 2026 to evaluate mercury vapor and fine particulate emission factors from crematories and recommend their use in permit reviews, reporting by January 15, 2027.

ct:HB 5332.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CERTAIN BOATING REGULATIONS.
ct:HB 5332.summary: Changes boating rules: requires operators to bar passengers from sitting on the gunwale with legs outside or standing on it above slow-no-wake speed, requires owner contact information on boats not registered in a state or federally, and raises abandoned-boat fines to $750-$1,000.

ct:HB 5333.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REGULATION OF STRIPED BASS FISHING IN THE STATE, A WORKING GROUP CONCERNING THE WILDLIFE CONSERVATION PROGRAM AND PROCEDURES CONCERNING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF FISH PASSAGES.
ct:HB 5333.summary: Limits striped bass fishing to catch and release from December 1 to March 31, sets fines of $150 to $500 for violations, creates a wildlife conservation program working group, and lets people petition for fish passages at certain hydroelectric dams.

ct:HB 5334.title: AN ACT CONCERNING RIPARIAN AREAS.
ct:HB 5334.summary: Requires the energy and environmental protection commissioner to use available FY 27 state funds to hire an employee to train inland wetlands commissions, including on preserving riparian areas.

ct:HB 5336.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ADVANCED NUCLEAR ENERGY.
ct:HB 5336.summary: Requires the Council for Advancing Nuclear Energy Development to study skilled-labor needs in advanced nuclear energy, consulting building-trades and apprenticeship groups, with a progress report due February 15, 2027 and a final report February 1, 2028.

ct:HB 5343.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REPORTING OF ADVERTISING PURCHASED BY THE STATE.
ct:HB 5343.summary: Requires executive branch state agencies to give the Administrative Services commissioner annual summaries of advertising purchased, requires the commissioner to report to the legislature by January 1, 2027, and requires UConn and the state colleges and universities to report separately.

ct:HB 5349.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A POLICE OFFICER TRAINING PROGRAM AND THE ROUNDING OF CERTAIN CASH PURCHASES.
ct:HB 5349.summary: Requires the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection to set up, by 2028, a one-day police officer training program with a West Haven college, and lets merchants round in-person cash purchase totals to the nearest five cents from January 1, 2027.

ct:HB 5350.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CANNABIS, HEMP AND INFUSED BEVERAGE REGULATION.
ct:HB 5350.summary: Renames "marijuana" as "cannabis" in state law, lets qualifying out-of-state medical patients buy medical cannabis, bars retailers from keeping age-verification data over 24 hours without written consent, limits retailer credit from producers to 30 days, and creates a cannabis regulatory working group.

ct:HB 5352.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE AUTHORITY OF THE STATE ELECTIONS ENFORCEMENT COMMISSION AND MANDATORY DISMISSAL OF COMPLAINTS.
ct:HB 5352.summary: Exempts complaints received on or after October 1, 2026 about potential violations of prohibited acts under state election law from the rule requiring the State Elections Enforcement Commission to dismiss complaints not decided within one year.

ct:HB 5354.title: AN ACT CONCERNING MEDICAID PROVIDER AUDITS.
ct:HB 5354.summary: Bars the Department of Social Services from finding Medicaid provider overpayments or underpayments by extrapolation unless the provider has sustained or high payment errors, the commissioner finds in good faith that it is committing fraud, or documented education failed to correct errors.

ct:HB 5373.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE INSURANCE DEPARTMENT'S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REVISIONS TO THE INSURANCE STATUTES.
ct:HB 5373.summary: Makes insurance law changes: allows electronic service of notices by the insurance commissioner, ends the terrorism insurance mandate for condo associations, sets annual formulary-change notices, and revises external review deadlines and third-party administrator contract rules.

ct:HB 5374.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HEALTH COVERAGE MANDATES FOR CERTAIN HEALTH CONDITIONS.
ct:HB 5374.summary: Starting January 1, 2027, requires state-regulated health plans to cover PANDAS/PANS treatment, athletic prosthetic devices, scalp cooling systems during chemotherapy, and infertility diagnosis and treatment under a broader definition of infertility.

ct:HB 5375.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE INSURANCE AND REAL ESTATE COMMITTEE WORKING GROUPS.
ct:HB 5375.summary: Requires health carriers and pharmacy benefit managers to reimburse pharmacists for covered clinical services and include them in provider networks, and directs the insurance commissioner to study pooled liability insurance for state-contracted nonprofits by November 1, 2026.

ct:HB 5377.title: AN ACT CONCERNING RETURN OF HEALTH CARE PROVIDER PAYMENTS.
ct:HB 5377.summary: Shortens from 18 to 12 months the period in which a health organization may deny or claw back a provider payment after a clean claim, sets a 30-business-day appeal decision deadline, and extends these rules to health insurance carriers starting January 1, 2027.

ct:HB 5381.title: AN ACT CONCERNING UNLAWFUL FUNERAL SERVICE PRACTICES.
ct:HB 5381.summary: Creates a funeral service guaranty account for the Department of Consumer Protection to pay restitution to victims of fraud in funeral contracts, adds required disclosures to those contracts, and creates a working group on prepaid funeral contracts.

ct:HB 5385.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A TASK FORCE TO STUDY UNDUE DELAY IN WORKERS' COMPENSATION CLAIMS BY POLICE OFFICERS AND FIREFIGHTERS.
ct:HB 5385.summary: Creates a task force to study causes of undue delay in workers' compensation claims by police officers and firefighters, including administrative processing, medical provider availability and insurer authorization requirements.

ct:HB 5391.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE ENFORCEMENT OF ZONING REGULATIONS.
ct:HB 5391.summary: Lets municipalities that zone under a special act enforce zoning regulations the same way as other towns, including court injunctions, criminal penalties and civil penalties of up to $2,500.
