ct:HB 5401.title: AN ACT CONCERNING REVISIONS TO THE STATE BUILDING CODE, STATE FIRE PREVENTION CODE AND FIRE SAFETY CODE.
ct:HB 5401.summary: Extends from 18 months to two years the deadline to update the state building, fire prevention and fire safety codes after model code revisions, provides that no updates are required between the 2024 and 2030 model codes, and requires a report by January 1, 2029.

ct:HB 5406.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ASSORTED MEASURES RECOGNIZING AND HONORING THE HEROISM OF VETERANS AND MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND MAKING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO STATUTES RELATED TO VETERANS' AND MILITARY AFFAIRS.
ct:HB 5406.summary: As amended, creates a veterans dental care program (up to $3,000 per veteran yearly, $1 million per fiscal year), extends some DMV grace periods for armed forces members from 60 to 90 days, waives original license and ID fees for verified veterans, and adds tax deductions.

ct:HB 5421.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN ACCOUNT TO PROVIDE PATIENT LIFTS TO CERTAIN HEALTH CARE OFFICES AND FACILITIES.
ct:HB 5421.summary: Creates a health care facility patient lift account administered by the State Treasurer, from which the Department of Public Health makes grants to physician practices, imaging centers and health care facilities to buy patient lifts.

ct:HB 5426.title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE AVAILABILITY OF AN ADVISOR DURING DISCIPLINARY PROCEEDINGS AT INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION.
ct:HB 5426.summary: Requires public higher education institutions to adopt a policy by August 1, 2026 letting students name an advisor for disciplinary proceedings that could lead to suspension, probation, expulsion or an athletics ban; the advisor gets communications and attends meetings but may not participate unless permitted.

ct:HB 5431.title: AN ACT CONCERNING COOPERATIVE CORPORATIONS.
ct:HB 5431.summary: Lets cooperative associations organize as cooperative corporations and sets rules for their organization and governance, including one-year board terms or staggered terms of up to five years.

ct:HB 5442.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION FOR AND TAX AGREEMENTS RELATED TO CERTAIN CLASS I RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES.
ct:HB 5442.summary: Extends the solar capacity tax on systems over one megawatt to those permitted on or after July 1, 2025 (19 tax years, not 20, if permitted before July 1, 2026), and limits a solar property tax exemption to systems permitted since July 1, 2025.

ct:HB 5447.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE TRANSFORMING CHILDREN'S BEHAVIORAL HEALTH POLICY AND PLANNING COMMITTEE.
ct:HB 5447.summary: Creates working groups on eating disorder treatment and a statewide food education roadmap, orders a study of an inpatient psychiatric facility for young people with developmental disabilities, and requires school-based health centers to screen grades 6-12 for disordered eating.

ct:HB 5450.title: AN ACT DISSOLVING THE BROOKLYN FIRE DISTRICT.
ct:HB 5450.summary: Dissolves the Brooklyn Fire District, transfers its funds and property to the town of Brooklyn, and repeals the 1899 special act that created it, effective October 1, 2026.

ct:HB 5460.title: AN ACT CONCERNING STATE-WIDE FIRE PROTECTION.
ct:HB 5460.summary: Requires fire protection entities to register with their municipality, and municipalities to adopt local fire protection plans, by July 1, 2027; directs the fire commission to set plan-rating standards; creates a Connecticut Fire program and a Comptroller study of centralizing firefighter benefits.

ct:HB 5464.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING RECOMMENDATIONS FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND CONCERNING VEGETATION MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES, TRANSPORTATION NETWORK COMPANIES AND RIDER SAFETY, TRAFFIC SIGNAL MODERNIZATION GRANT PROGRAM, ENCAMPMENTS, MARINE PILOT LICENSE FEES, MOTOR VEHICLE MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT, DISTRACTED DRIVING, A TASK FORCE TO STUDY ACCESS TO PARKING FOR HOME HEALTH AGENCIES AND A WORKING GROUP TO STUDY USE OF ALTERNATIVE FUELS AND TECHNOLOGIES IN SCHOOL BUS FLEETS.
ct:HB 5464.summary: Makes many transportation changes, including allowing state purchase of diesel transit buses, revising electric vehicle charging and zero-emission school bus requirements, updating the distracted driving law, and adding rider-safety rules for ride-hail companies.

ct:HB 5467.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DESIGNATION OF A DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT EMPLOYEE FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING CONCIERGE SERVICES TO SMALL BUSINESSES.
ct:HB 5467.summary: Requires the Department of Economic and Community Development commissioner to designate an existing department employee to provide concierge services to small businesses, including information and help with the department's programs. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

ct:HB 5468.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PROVISION OF PARENT-MANAGED LEARNING.
ct:HB 5468.summary: Starting with the 2028-29 school year, requires parents to file an annual form stating whether their child will attend public school, nonpublic school or parent-managed learning (homeschooling), and requires in-person withdrawal with a child-abuse records check for adults in the home.

ct:HB 5472.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE SAFETY OF ENERGY GENERATION SOURCES AND ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS.
ct:HB 5472.summary: Allows the energy and environmental protection commissioner, within appropriations, to set up a review of environmental impacts of energy storage systems over one megawatt within 1,000 feet of aquifers or similar groundwater resources, and to require a safety study.

ct:HB 5476.title: AN ACT CONCERNING OVERSIGHT OF EFFORTS TO PREVENT HUMAN TRAFFICKING AND THE USE OF CONFIDENTIAL CRISIS HOTLINES AT CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTIONS.
ct:HB 5476.summary: Directs the Office of Policy and Management's Criminal Justice Policy and Planning Division to develop a plan coordinating state anti-human-trafficking efforts by January 1, 2027, and changes Trafficking in Persons Council membership and related training.

ct:HB 5481.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A PILOT PROGRAM TO TREAT CERTAIN MEDICAID PATIENTS AT A SHORT-TERM HOSPITAL SPECIAL HOSPICE.
ct:HB 5481.summary: Requires the Social Services commissioner to develop a pilot program using a short-term hospital special hospice to treat Medicaid patients with advanced illness who cannot be safely managed at home, with a report by January 15, 2027.

ct:HB 5485.title: AN ACT CONCERNING SUPPORTED DECISION-MAKING STUDY.
ct:HB 5485.summary: Creates a working group to study supported decision-making agreements, in which adults choose supporters to help them make decisions, and to report recommendations by December 31, 2026.

ct:HB 5491.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CENTRALIZATION OF WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT INFORMATION.
ct:HB 5491.summary: Requires the labor commissioner to create a centralized webpage by January 1, 2027 with workforce development resources and links to outside sources, and to update it semi-annually.

ct:HB 5493.title: AN ACT REQUIRING A STUDY TO ESTABLISH A PROGRAM TO PROVIDE STIPENDS FOR THE CONNECTICUT CIVIL AIR PATROL.
ct:HB 5493.summary: Requires the Comptroller to study the cost and feasibility of stipends for Civil Air Patrol members who miss work for emergency response or required training, and report by January 1, 2027.

ct:HB 5497.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A TASK FORCE TO STUDY THE EFFECTS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE TRADES INDUSTRY.
ct:HB 5497.summary: Creates a task force to study how artificial intelligence affects the trades industry, including job displacement and the artificial intelligence content of Technical Education and Career System coursework.

ct:HB 5509.title: AN ACT CONCERNING JUSTICES OF THE PEACE.
ct:HB 5509.summary: Requires a 48-hour wait before a marriage license is issued, defines official misconduct for justices of the peace, has the secretary of the state investigate it and issue warnings or suspend or revoke appointments, and requires a duties manual and a working group.

ct:HB 5514.title: AN ACT CONCERNING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH STATUTES.
ct:HB 5514.summary: Makes public health changes, including a working group on assisted living communities, written patient notice of medical records retention periods, and letting nonprofits give free eyeglasses to a person's authorized representative.

ct:HB 5515.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF MENTAL HEALTH AND ADDICTION SERVICES' RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING ACCESS TO OPIOID OVERDOSE REVERSAL MEDICATION AND VARIOUS REVISIONS TO MENTAL HEALTH AND ADDICTION STATUTES.
ct:HB 5515.summary: Lets any person give another an over-the-counter opioid overdose reversal medication with civil and criminal immunity, expands its use in schools, and changes mental health advisory board rules and coordination on counseling after mass shootings.

ct:HB 5518.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH'S RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING SUBSURFACE SEWAGE ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS, WATER OPERATOR APPRENTICES AND VARIOUS REVISIONS TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH AND DRINKING WATER STATUTES.
ct:HB 5518.summary: Changes Department of Public Health oversight of bottled water, including a required schedule of PFAS and other contaminants, and of environmental laboratories, asbestos professionals, crematories, subsurface sewage enforcement officers, and apprentice water system operators.

ct:HB 5521.title: AN ACT CONCERNING STERILE CULTIVARS, APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF CERTAIN MATERIALS AS FILL AND THE REVISION OF CERTAIN HOUSING-RELATED STATUTES.
ct:HB 5521.summary: Requires the Agricultural Experiment Station to report by January 15, 2027 on sterile cultivars and Japanese barberry, revises the DEEP fill-material pilot program, and changes housing statutes, including affordable housing appeal moratoriums and parking requirements.

ct:HB 5525.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A RAPID RESPONSE PROGRAM FOR CERTAIN AQUATIC INVASIVE SPECIES.
ct:HB 5525.summary: Sets rapid response steps and timelines for eradicating or containing hydrilla and other aquatic invasive plants, and requires the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station's invasive species office to develop a hydrilla response plan and a statewide management plan.

ct:HB 5532.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE OFFICE OF STATE ETHICS FOR REVISIONS TO THE STATE CODES OF ETHICS, REDEFINING "GIFT" FOR PURPOSES OF SAID CODES AND INCREASING VARIOUS MONETARY THRESHOLDS IN SAID CODES.
ct:HB 5532.summary: Raises financial thresholds in the state Code of Ethics, including the gift limit, cuts the Citizen's Ethics Advisory Board quorum from six to five, and exempts one in-state college sporting event per year from the gift definition.

ct:HB 5534.title: AN ACT DESIGNATING THE STATE AS THE BIRTHPLACE OF THE BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB MOVEMENT, THE STATE AMPHIBIAN AND THE STATE ROCK.
ct:HB 5534.summary: Designates Connecticut as the birthplace of the Boys and Girls Club movement, the spring peeper as the state amphibian, and Housatonic marble as the state rock.

ct:HB 5557.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A PLAN TO REVISE THE DEFINITION OF INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF WORKING GROUPS ON AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE EDUCATION AND NONEMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION REIMBURSEMENT.
ct:HB 5557.summary: Requires the Developmental Services commissioner to plan a standard definition of intellectual disability and report by July 1, 2027, and creates an American Sign Language education working group advising the Department of Education.

ct:HB 5558.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF DEVELOPMENTAL SERVICES' ABUSE AND NEGLECT INVESTIGATIONS.
ct:HB 5558.summary: Requires the Department of Developmental Services to give abuse and neglect investigation reports to the alleged victim's parent or legal representative on request, expands its annual abuse report, and requires a guide on reporting processes for certain people with intellectual disabilities.

ct:HB 5561.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A FIVE-YEAR MEDICAID RATE REVIEW, DENTAL REPRESENTATION ON A MEDICAL ASSISTANCE OVERSIGHT COUNCIL, BIOMARKER TESTING AND OPIOID PRESCRIPTION COVERAGE REQUIREMENTS AND A STUDY CONCERNING PAYMENT OF SPOUSES FOR STATE-SUBSIDIZED HOME CARE.
ct:HB 5561.summary: Requires the Social Services commissioner to set up a five-year Medicaid rate review benchmarked to Medicare where possible, with public comment and consolidated fee schedules, a full review by 2032, and annual reports from 2028.

ct:HB 5562.title: AN ACT CONCERNING VARIOUS REVISIONS TO HUMAN SERVICES STATUTES.
ct:HB 5562.summary: Makes assorted human services changes, including DSS contact postings at managed residential communities, wider access to the Developmental Services registry of employees terminated for substantiated abuse or neglect, changes to long-term care committees, and a one-time rather than annual SNAP staggering report.

ct:HB 5563.title: AN ACT CONCERNING VARIOUS CRIMINAL LAW AND CRIMINAL JUSTICE PROPOSALS, CERTIFICATES OF APPROVAL FOR AIRPORTS, HELIPORTS, VERTIPORTS, RESTRICTED LANDING AREAS AND OTHER AIR NAVIGATION FACILITIES, POLICE COLLABORATION WITH SOCIAL WORKERS, SURVEILLANCE PRICING, EDUCATION COST SHARING AND WITHHOLDING OF TAXES FROM LUMP SUM PAYMENTS.
ct:HB 5563.summary: Extends the organized retail theft period from 180 to 365 days, adds larceny crimes of fostering sale of stolen property and gift card crime, raises shoplifting punitive damages from $300 to $1,000, bars retail sellers from surveillance pricing, and registers low-use air facilities.

ct:HB 5565.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A STUDY OF THE CIVIL AND CRIMINAL LAWS OF THIS STATE.
ct:HB 5565.summary: Lengthens the organized retail theft period from 180 to 365 days and raises the punitive damages cap in shoplifting civil suits from $300 to $1,000, among many other changes to criminal and civil laws.

ct:HB 5567.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HEALTH CARE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION FACILITIES.
ct:HB 5567.summary: Requires the Department of Correction to provide incarcerated people health care free of charge and in a timely way and to implement electronic health records, and requires the correction ombuds to hire a mental health clinician.

ct:HB 5572.title: AN ACT CONVEYING A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF WOODBURY.
ct:HB 5572.summary: Directs the Transportation commissioner to convey about one acre of state highway right-of-way, the town's South Green with veterans monuments, to Woodbury for administrative costs. The town must use it as a commemorative memorial green or it reverts to the state.

ct:HB 5573.title: AN ACT CONVEYING A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE CITY OF TORRINGTON.
ct:HB 5573.summary: Requires the Transportation commissioner to convey a 0.22-acre North Elm Street parcel in Torrington to the city for administrative costs, to be used for open space or relocating a trail, or it reverts to the state.

ct:HB 5574.title: AN ACT AMENDING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF HAMDEN.
ct:HB 5574.summary: Amends a prior act conveying the former High Meadows property, about 50.29 acres in Hamden, to the town for $1.5 million, extending the conveyance deadline from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

ct:HB 5575.title: AN ACT CONVEYING A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE CITY OF SHELTON.
ct:HB 5575.summary: Requires the Administrative Services commissioner to convey a 6.49-acre River Road parcel in Shelton to the city for $350,000 plus administrative costs, with the state keeping an easement for landfill monitoring wells.

ct:HB 5577.title: AN ACT AMENDING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF LAND TO THE TOWN OF SOMERS.
ct:HB 5577.summary: Amends a prior act conveying a state parcel in Somers to the town for public safety use, setting the price at the state's administrative costs instead of appraised value and correcting the boundary description.

ct:HB 5578.title: AN ACT AMENDING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE CHESPROCOTT HEALTH DISTRICT.
ct:HB 5578.summary: Amends a prior act conveying a Cheshire Correctional Institute parcel to the Chesprocott Health District, allowing temporary housing by a nonprofit that meets local zoning, with any sale to the nonprofit at fair market value.

ct:HB 5579.title: AN ACT AMENDING A CONVEYANCE OF PARCELS OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF CHESHIRE.
ct:HB 5579.summary: Amends a prior act conveying three state parcels in Cheshire to the town, allowing their sale for economic development, a medical facility, housing or open space before July 1, 2031, at fair market value.

ct:HB 5580.title: AN ACT AMENDING A PRIOR CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF STRATFORD TO PERMIT THE PARCEL TO BE SOLD, TRANSFERRED OR LEASED.
ct:HB 5580.summary: Amends a prior act on a Stratford parcel released from a school-purposes-only deed restriction, limiting its use to parking and requiring any sale or lease at fair market value, with proceeds to the Special Transportation Fund.

ct:HB 5581.title: AN ACT AMENDING A PRIOR CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF ROCKY HILL.
ct:HB 5581.summary: Amends a prior land conveyance so the Transportation commissioner conveys about 5.3 acres at 1090 Maple Street to Rocky Hill for administrative costs only, not appraised market value. The town must use it for open space or passive recreation, or it reverts.

ct:HB 5583.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONVEYANCE OF PARCELS OF STATE LAND IN THE TOWN OF DERBY.
ct:HB 5583.summary: Requires the Transportation commissioner to convey about 1.5 acres of state land in Derby to the Connecticut Municipal Development Authority at fair market value plus administrative costs.

ct:SB 1.title: AN ACT MAKING ADJUSTMENTS TO THE STATE BUDGET FOR THE BIENNIUM ENDING JUNE 30, 2027, MAKING DEFICIENCY APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30, 2026, AUTHORIZING AND ADJUSTING BONDS OF THE STATE AND CONCERNING PROVISIONS RELATING TO REVENUE, SCHOOL CONSTRUCTION AND OTHER ITEMS TO IMPLEMENT THE STATE BUDGET.
ct:SB 1.summary: Creates, by amendment, a municipal property tax relief fund and transfers sales and use tax revenue above the fiscal 2026 level into it, starting in fiscal 2028, for distribution to municipalities.

ct:SB 116.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PREVENTION OF HUMAN TRAFFICKING.
ct:SB 116.summary: Requires hotel, motel and inn operators to register with the Department of Consumer Protection from January 1, 2027, with a fee of $50 per lodging under 15 rooms or $200 for 15 or more rooms, and lets the department audit their records.

ct:SB 123.title: AN ACT CONCERNING PUBLIC HEARINGS FOR CERTAIN RATE INCREASES AT ASSISTED LIVING FACILITIES, MUNICIPAL AGENTS FOR AGING, EMERGENCY POWER GENERATOR REQUIREMENTS FOR CERTAIN MULTIFAMILY HOUSING PROJECTS, PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT FOR HOME HEALTH AIDE EMPLOYEES, THE NURSING HOME BED MORATORIUM AND NURSING HOME RESIDENT DATA.
ct:SB 123.summary: Requires assisted living agencies to hold an informational hearing before fee increases over 10% and give residents their three-year fee history on request, and makes other changes to laws on older adults and home health aides.

ct:SB 125.title: AN ACT REQUIRING NURSING HOMES TO ANNUALLY REPORT CERTAIN OWNERSHIP INFORMATION REGARDING INVESTMENT ENTITIES, ACQUIRE, IF FEASIBLE, A SURETY BOND OR A SIMILAR FORM OF SECURITY IN AN AMOUNT EQUAL TO NINETY DAYS OF OPERATING COSTS, MAINTAIN FULL GOVERNANCE CONTROL AND AUTHORITY OVER NURSING HOME ASSETS AND ACTIVITIES AND ANNUALLY ATTEST THAT NO INVESTMENT ENTITY HAS CONTROL OVER NURSING HOME RESIDENT HEALTH, SAFETY OR CARE.
ct:SB 125.summary: Requires Medicaid nursing homes to report investment entities with 5% or more ownership and, from February 2028, attest none controls resident care and keep licensee governance control. Homes with such owners need a 90-day operating-cost surety bond if the state identifies a feasible one.

ct:SB 132.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CONNECTICUT-GERMANY AND CONNECTICUT-INDIA TRADE COMMISSIONS.
ct:SB 132.summary: Establishes Connecticut-Germany and Connecticut-India trade commissions within the Legislative Department, each with appointed members, to promote trade, investment and exchanges between Connecticut and each country.

ct:SB 134.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN AIRPORT DEVELOPMENT ZONE IN THE TOWN OF PLAINVILLE.
ct:SB 134.summary: Establishes an airport development zone in Plainville made up of nine census blocks, making taxpayers there eligible for partial property tax exemptions on qualifying manufacturing facilities and machinery.

ct:SB 137.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE OFFICE OF EARLY CHILDHOOD.
ct:SB 137.summary: Adds a pediatrician to the Early Childhood Cabinet, raises Smart Start grant limits, requires youth camps to give contact information and receive emergency notifications, and expands background-check and child abuse registry notification rules for child care providers.

ct:SB 138.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION.
ct:SB 138.summary: Moves charter school approvals onto the biennial state budget cycle, sets how magnet school transportation grants to regional service centers are paid, changes regional school study report contents, and repeals several annual State Department of Education reports.

ct:SB 147.title: AN ACT CONCERNING A STUDY ON THE NEED FOR EXTENDED PRODUCER RESPONSIBILITY FOR ELECTRONIC NICOTINE DELIVERY SYSTEMS AND VAPOR PRODUCTS AND INCLUDING AEROSOL PAINTS UNDER THE PAINT STEWARDSHIP PROGRAM.
ct:SB 147.summary: Expands Connecticut's paint recycling program to include aerosol coating products and bans selling paint products from producers that do not join the program. Allows the environment department to charge the program operator an annual fee of up to $50,000.

ct:SB 148.title: AN ACT CONCERNING REVISIONS TO AQUACULTURE-RELATED STATUTES AND PROVIDING FOR CERTAIN FARMING-RELATED PROGRAMS.
ct:SB 148.summary: Creates a Dairy Modernization Grant Program and a Dairy Farming Sustainability Working Group in the Department of Agriculture, orders a study of natural gas rates for commercial and agricultural customers, and revises the farmers' market nutrition programs.

ct:SB 155.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CHILDREN AND FAMILIES AND THE DATA LINK CONNECTICUT SYSTEM.
ct:SB 155.summary: Merges Department of Children and Families reporting requirements from nine statutes into one annual report starting October 15, 2027, and renames the state P20 WIN education and workforce data system DataLinkCT.

ct:SB 156.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A TASK FORCE TO STUDY THE VOLUNTARY SURRENDER OF INFANTS.
ct:SB 156.summary: Creates a task force to study the state's infant voluntary surrender law and related agency and hospital procedures, including whether they create or perpetuate disparities among parents who surrender infants.

ct:SB 157.title: AN ACT CONCERNING MUNICIPAL CAMP SAFETY.
ct:SB 157.summary: Specifies that mandated reporter duties for youth camp staff apply to municipal camps, and requires the Office of Early Childhood to report by January 1, 2027 on each municipal youth camp's facilities, staffing, training and policies.

ct:SB 191.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE PSYCHEDELIC-ASSISTED THERAPY PILOT PROGRAM.
ct:SB 191.summary: Opens the state psychedelic-assisted therapy pilot to Connecticut residents 18 or older meeting clinical criteria, rather than only veterans, retired first responders and health care workers, and removes the requirement to end it if the DEA approves MDMA and psilocybin.

ct:SB 196.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HOSPITAL SALE-LEASEBACK TRANSACTIONS AND ATTESTATIONS CONCERNING LACK OF A CONTROLLING INTEREST OF A HOSPITAL OR OF INTERFERENCE WITH THE PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT AND CLINICAL DECISIONS OF CERTAIN HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS OF A HOSPITAL BY A PRIVATE EQUITY ENTITY.
ct:SB 196.summary: Bans hospital sale-leasebacks of main campus property starting July 1, 2027, and requires hospitals to attest annually to the Department of Public Health that no private equity entity controls them, with fines up to $2,000 for failing to attest.

ct:SB 218.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE COMMUNITY BANK AND CREDIT UNION INVESTMENT PROGRAM, MORTGAGE PAYMENTS, PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS OF RENTAL SECURITY DEPOSIT REQUIREMENTS, CERTAIN APPROVALS BY THE BANKING COMMISSIONER, CONNECTICUT BRANCH APPLICATIONS AND SECURED CREDIT CARDS.
ct:SB 218.summary: Changes banking laws: sets the minimum rate the treasurer may accept under the Community Bank and Credit Union Initiative, requires lenders to accept extra principal payments on certain home loans, expressly allows civil penalties up to $100,000 for security deposit violations, and eases branch applications.

ct:SB 220.title: AN ACT CONCERNING STUDENT LITERACY, ASPIRING EDUCATORS, AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE AS PART OF THE WORLD LANGUAGES CURRICULUM AND THE PARAEDUCATOR HEALTH BENEFIT PLAN SUBSIDY PROGRAM.
ct:SB 220.summary: Requires state reading-intervention guidance, opens the educator scholarship to "aspiring educators" from underrepresented groups with no alliance-district high school requirement, creates an American Sign Language education working group, and makes paraeducator health care subsidies permanent, adding charter schools.

ct:SB 246.title: AN ACT REQUIRING A STUDY OF NATURAL GAS RATES FOR COMMERCIAL AND AGRICULTURAL CUSTOMERS.
ct:SB 246.summary: Requires the energy and environmental protection commissioner to study natural gas rates, including demand charges, for commercial and agricultural customers with intermittent peak demand, and report recommendations by January 15, 2027.

ct:SB 247.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE AUDITORS OF PUBLIC ACCOUNTS.
ct:SB 247.summary: Extends the bar on state agency settlements to agreements that keep an employee from working while still paid, with exceptions; requires foundation agreements to state whether the foundation reimburses state employee costs; sets a six-month deadline for quasi-public annual reports.

ct:SB 259.title: AN ACT CONCERNING FEMALE GENITAL MUTILATION.
ct:SB 259.summary: Makes performing female genital mutilation on a minor a class D felony (up to five years in prison and a $5,000 fine), allows special testimony procedures for child victims 12 or younger, and lets victims sue.

ct:SB 268.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMPTROLLER TO WITHHOLD PAYMENT FOR VIOLATIONS OF THE PREVAILING WAGE STATUTES.
ct:SB 268.summary: Requires the comptroller, after a labor commissioner's prevailing-wage stop-work notice, to warn the contractor, and lets the comptroller withhold payment if it stays noncompliant 10 business days later, until the order is released, penalties are paid, or a settlement is final.

ct:SB 277.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES' RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING THE CODE OFFICIAL CAREER PATHWAY, THE FIRE SAFETY CODE, BURN INJURY REPORTS AND STATE BUILDING CODE PROVISIONS RELATING TO ACCESSIBILITY.
ct:SB 277.summary: Requires the state fire marshal to convene a working group on the code official career pathway, lets her issue official Fire Safety Code interpretations on request, and changes burn-injury reporting and State Building Code variation rules.

ct:SB 282.title: AN ACT APPROPRIATING FUNDS TO THE NEGLECTED CEMETERY ACCOUNT AND CONCERNING CARE AND MAINTENANCE OF WARTIME VETERANS' GRAVES.
ct:SB 282.summary: Transfers $100,000 for FY 27 to the neglected cemetery account for municipal grants to maintain wartime veterans' graves, and requires the Veterans Affairs Department to take online reports of uncared-for graves and notify the town within seven days.

ct:SB 291.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES OF THE STATE MARSHAL COMMISSION, THE STATE MARSHALS ADVISORY BOARD AND STATE MARSHALS.
ct:SB 291.summary: Expands the State Marshal Commission's responsibilities, sets procedures for filling state marshal vacancies including an interview committee and training requirements, and requires annual reports to the Judiciary Committee starting January 1, 2027.

ct:SB 292.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEFINITION OF "CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE MATERIAL".
ct:SB 292.summary: Expands the definition of child sexual abuse material to include sexually explicit depictions virtually indistinguishable from a person under 16, excluding drawings, cartoons, sculptures and paintings, subjecting possession, importation and transmission to existing charges.

ct:SB 294.title: AN ACT CONCERNING TRADE NAMES, FRAUDULENT FILINGS, IMPERMISSIBLE BUSINESS SOLICITATIONS, DISSOLUTION OF CORPORATIONS, THE ISSUANCE OF AN APOSTILLE AND FEES CHARGED BY A NOTARY.
ct:SB 294.summary: Expands the trade name law, including recording by town clerks and banned words, sets rules for businesses that charge fees to file or retrieve Secretary of the State documents, and adjusts how the Secretary handles business data she cannot verify.

ct:SB 296.title: AN ACT CONCERNING RECOMMENDATIONS FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF CONSUMER PROTECTION WITH RESPECT TO THE CONNECTICUT UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES ACT AND SPORTS WAGERING.
ct:SB 296.summary: Raises from $10,000 to $25,000 per consumer the limit for cases where the Department of Consumer Protection can require restitution for unfair trade practices, adds sports-wager tampering to the crime of cheating, and lets the attorney general seek orders against unlicensed sports wagering.

ct:SB 298.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REALLOCATION OF CERTAIN STATE FUNDS AND VARIOUS PROVISIONS RELATING TO EDUCATION, PUBLIC SAFETY, GENERAL GOVERNMENT, ELECTIONS, INTERMEDIATE CARE FACILITIES AND WAREHOUSE DISTRIBUTION CENTERS.
ct:SB 298.summary: Reallocates state funds; creates a state Seal of Civics Education for diplomas; limits UConn Health neuromodulation center treatment to disabled veterans; bars active-assailant simulations in school crisis drills; creates a 15-member working group on antisemitism in schools.

ct:SB 305.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A WORKING GROUP TO STUDY STATE-WIDE MARKETING AND TOURISM IN THE STATE.
ct:SB 305.summary: Establishes a working group, including legislators and state officials, to study statewide marketing and tourism, and requires a report on its findings and recommendations to the Commerce Committee by January 1, 2027.

ct:SB 306.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND COMPREHENSIVE ENERGY STRATEGY.
ct:SB 306.summary: Requires the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection commissioner to consult other state officials, including economic development, housing, transportation and the consumer counsel, when preparing the comprehensive energy strategy, and to send it to the Commerce Committee.

ct:SB 307.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT'S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REVISIONS TO THE COMMERCE STATUTES AND PROHIBITING SCHOLARSHIP DISPLACEMENT FOR CERTAIN STUDENTS AT PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION.
ct:SB 307.summary: Renames the Small Business Express Program the Small Business Boost Program, replaces the minority business loan fund with a Connecticut Opportunity Fund, raises the two-year business aid cap from $10 million to $25 million, and generally bars public colleges from reducing aid over private scholarships.

ct:SB 310.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PILOT PROGRAM TO TRAIN CERTIFIED WASTEWATER TREATMENT FACILITY OPERATORS.
ct:SB 310.summary: Requires the Technical Education and Career System to start a pilot program in the 2026 school year offering courses that train students to become certified wastewater treatment operators, with a report due January 1, 2027.

ct:SB 317.title: AN ACT CONCERNING RESOURCE RECOVERY FACILITIES IN THE STATE.
ct:SB 317.summary: Requires the energy and environmental protection commissioner to convene a working group on suspending, for up to five fiscal years, a state fee for one or more resource recovery facilities, and to report by January 1, 2027.

ct:SB 318.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ANIMAL WELFARE.
ct:SB 318.summary: Lets the state veterinarian issue disease-prevention orders for any animal or poultry disease, not only contagious ones, and requires a study of pet placement for domestic violence victims and a working group on the animal population control program.

ct:SB 319.title: AN ACT CONCERNING BATTERY-POWERED LAWN EQUIPMENT FUNDING FOR MUNICIPALITIES, REGIONAL SCHOOLS AND COMMERCIAL LANDSCAPERS.
ct:SB 319.summary: Requires the Connecticut Green Bank to create loan products by January 31, 2028 to help commercial landscapers buy or lease battery-powered lawn equipment, and requires DEEP to reactivate a fund for municipalities and regional schools starting October 1, 2027.

ct:SB 321.title: AN ACT CONCERNING REQUIREMENTS FOR CERTAIN EXCAVATION PROJECTS.
ct:SB 321.summary: Replaces the approval process for underground telecommunications and broadband facilities in public rights-of-way with notices to the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority 30 days ahead for facilities over 500 feet (five days for others) and to the Department of Transportation for state highways.

ct:SB 323.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE OFFICE OF STATE ETHICS FOR REVISIONS TO THE STATE CODES OF ETHICS.
ct:SB 323.summary: Expands the state ethics code's conflict-of-interest definition to cover actions affecting an official's or spouse's non-state employer, and lowers the Citizen's Ethics Advisory Board quorum from six to five.

ct:SB 335.title: AN ACT CONCERNING UTILITY CHARGES FOR RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS.
ct:SB 335.summary: Prohibits residential rental agreements from requiring tenants to pay for utilities unless a separate meter measures utilities delivered exclusively to their dwelling unit, for agreements entered or renewed on or after October 1, 2026.

ct:SB 340.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONTINUING REAL ESTATE EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS, PUBLIC MARKETING OF CERTAIN REAL ESTATE LISTINGS AND REVISING THE TITLE OF A REAL ESTATE SALESPERSON TO A REAL ESTATE AGENT.
ct:SB 340.summary: Sets a two-hour minimum for approved real estate continuing education courses, renames real estate salespersons as real estate agents from January 1, 2027, and sets public marketing rules for brokers and agents representing sellers or landlords of residential property.

ct:SB 342.title: AN ACT CONCERNING HEALTH COVERAGE.
ct:SB 342.summary: As amended, requires health carriers that use software or AI to automatically downcode or deny provider claims to send the provider electronic notice within ten days, with a clinical rationale; lets providers appeal within 60 days; requires annual reports to the Insurance Commissioner.

ct:SB 346.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE MODIFICATIONS TO THE GOVERNOR'S WORKFORCE COUNCIL.
ct:SB 346.summary: Raises the governor's business-representative appointments to the Governor's Workforce Council from 24 to 30, adds labor and vocational rehabilitation members, and caps the council at 62 members.

ct:SB 349.title: AN ACT CONCERNING MODIFICATIONS TO THE FIREFIGHTERS CANCER RELIEF FUND.
ct:SB 349.summary: Combines the treasurer's two annual reports on firefighter cancer benefit programs into one report, first due October 1, 2026, and changes the required contents to program expenditures and account income sources.

ct:SB 362.title: AN ACT CONCERNING REVISIONS TO STATUTES RELATING TO MUNICIPAL PROPERTY TAX ASSESSMENT.
ct:SB 362.summary: Changes municipal property tax assessment laws, including capping the taxable value of older motor vehicles, requiring all towns to use the uniform personal property valuation method, and delaying filing deadlines that fall on weekends or holidays.

ct:SB 367.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A WORKING GROUP TO STUDY ROADSIDE SAFETY CONCERNS ASSOCIATED WITH WRECKERS AND TOWING AND RECOVERY PROFESSIONALS.
ct:SB 367.summary: Creates a working group to study roadside safety concerns for tow and recovery workers, including what light colors and types wreckers may use, and report by January 1, 2027.

ct:SB 369.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING VARIOUS REQUIREMENTS REGARDING ELEVATORS.
ct:SB 369.summary: Requires owners of residential buildings with elevators to maintain them, give tenants advance notice of maintenance and of outages, and give local building officials repair plans; sets fines of up to $250 for a first violation and $500 for later ones.

ct:SB 370.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE HOURLY COMPENSATION FOR ADJUNCT FIRE INSTRUCTORS.
ct:SB 370.summary: Requires the Administrative Services commissioner to raise Connecticut Fire Academy adjunct fire instructors' hourly pay each year, starting July 1, 2026, by the same percentage as the general wage increase in the latest state employee bargaining agreement.

ct:SB 375.title: AN ACT CONCERNING SCHOOL MAPPING DATA SERVICES.
ct:SB 375.summary: Allows the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection to run a grant program starting in FY 27, within appropriations, to help municipalities and police departments pay for school mapping data that meets set requirements.

ct:SB 383.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE OFFICE OF WORKFORCE STRATEGY RELATED TO HIGHER EDUCATION.
ct:SB 383.summary: Ends the required human services career pipeline program but keeps a plan requirement, extends the commercial driver's license training program deadline to January 1, 2027, and ends the required HVAC pipeline pilot program.

ct:SB 391.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE AVAILABILITY OF BREAST CANCER SCREENING, DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT SERVICES FOR WOMEN COMMITTED TO THE CUSTODY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION.
ct:SB 391.summary: Allows the Department of Correction to arrange breast cancer screening, diagnosis and treatment for women in custody at licensed facilities closer than UConn Health Center, including mammograms when it cannot provide them on site.

ct:SB 393.title: AN ACT CONCERNING SPECIAL ELECTIONS TO FILL VACANCIES DUE TO THE DEATH OF CERTAIN ELECTED OFFICIALS.
ct:SB 393.summary: Changes the time for the governor to issue a special election writ after a U.S. senator, U.S. representative or General Assembly member dies, from within 10 days to 7 to 17 days after the death, and requires a seven-day wait after a probate judge's death.

ct:SB 397.title: AN ACT CONCERNING DEMOCRACY AND GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTABILITY AND THE USE AND RETENTION OF DATA DERIVED FROM AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER SYSTEMS.
ct:SB 397.summary: Creates a state-law lawsuit against individuals, including federal officers, who deprive people of U.S. constitutional rights under color of law. Bars peace officers, with exceptions, from wearing facial coverings when interacting with the public, requires badge identification, and limits license plate reader use.

ct:SB 4.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONSUMER PRIVACY AND PROTECTION.
ct:SB 4.summary: Makes changes to consumer privacy laws: requires data brokers to register and honor consumer deletion requests, limits pricing based on consumers' personal data, regulates direct-to-consumer genetic testing, and sets rules on advertisement volume when streaming.

ct:SB 400.title: AN ACT CONCERNING PROBATE COURT OPERATIONS.
ct:SB 400.summary: Changes probate court operations: lets regional children's probate courts hear name changes, lets nonresidents under a federal firearms disability from a Connecticut probate decision petition that court to restore firearm rights, and extends confidentiality to minor guardianship records.

ct:SB 407.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSIONER OF MOTOR VEHICLES TO ISSUE PERMITS ALLOWING ORGAN TRANSPORT VEHICLES TO USE CERTAIN LIGHTS.
ct:SB 407.summary: Allows the motor vehicles commissioner to permit organ transport vehicles, operated by procurement organization employees carrying organ parts, to use blue, red, yellow or white lights, including flashing lights.

ct:SB 413.title: AN ACT REVISING VARIOUS MOTOR VEHICLE STATUTES, IMPLEMENTING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND CONCERNING YOUTH INSTRUCTION PERMITS, AUTOMOBILE DEALERS AND MANUFACTURERS AND THE TOWING AND STORAGE OF MOTOR VEHICLES.
ct:SB 413.summary: Changes motor vehicle laws, including redesigned accessible parking placards, an e-scooter weight limit, dealer conveyance fee and franchise rules, e-bike definitions, towing rates and an electronic towed-vehicle portal, and privacy for vessel records.

ct:SB 417.title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO ESTABLISH AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SMALL BUSINESS PROGRAM.
ct:SB 417.summary: Directs the Department of Economic and Community Development to develop a plan for a program giving small businesses financial help to adopt artificial intelligence, with employee training required, and to report by January 1, 2027.

ct:SB 423.title: AN ACT CONCERNING OVERSIGHT OVER HIGHER EDUCATION.
ct:SB 423.summary: Changes reporting on the community college consolidation, moving the annual report due date to August 1 and sending it to the Government Oversight Committee, and requires a December 31, 2026 report comparing state college system staffing levels in 2011, 2019 and 2026.

ct:SB 427.title: AN ACT CONCERNING DUAL ENROLLMENT PROGRAMS.
ct:SB 427.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to appoint a dual and concurrent enrollment course coordinator by January 1, 2027, and lets higher education institutions apply for reimbursement of fee waivers for high-need students.

ct:SB 430.title: AN ACT ADOPTING THE INTEGRATED SETTING STANDARD OF THE AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT FOR PUBLIC ENTITIES.
ct:SB 430.summary: Requires state and local public entities to administer services in the most integrated setting appropriate for people with disabilities, and lets aggrieved people file complaints with the Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities.

ct:SB 431.title: AN ACT CONCERNING PALLIATIVE AND HOSPICE CARE IN LITCHFIELD COUNTY.
ct:SB 431.summary: Requires the Social Services commissioner to study the need for palliative and hospice care in Litchfield County and report by January 1, 2027, and allows a pilot program if a need is found.

ct:SB 439.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ELECTRONIC SURVEILLANCE DEVICES AND SYSTEMS AND SELF-SERVICE KIOSKS IN EMPLOYEE LOUNGES.
ct:SB 439.summary: Allows third-party vendors running self-service kiosks to use video-only surveillance of the kiosk checkout and display areas in employee lounges, bars employers from viewing it except to report alleged theft, and applies fines to vendor violations.

ct:SB 444.title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING CERTAIN MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEES TO SERVE ON MUNICIPAL BOARDS OF FINANCE.
ct:SB 444.summary: Lets municipal employees serve on their town's board of finance if any stipend they receive is under $10,000 in a rolling 12-month period.

ct:SB 449.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE INTERGOVERNMENTAL POLICY AND PLANNING DIVISION WITHIN THE OFFICE OF POLICY AND MANAGEMENT.
ct:SB 449.summary: Requires OPM to identify state property qualifying as PA 490 land so towns classify and value it that way, ends a child care zoning certification, repeals the Intertown equipment incentive program, and delays school repair grant notices to April 1.

ct:SB 452.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE RELEASE OF LIGHTER-THAN-AIR BALLOONS.
ct:SB 452.summary: Bans knowingly releasing helium or other lighter-than-air balloons into the atmosphere, replacing the nine-balloon allowance, and from 2027 requires retailers to attach weights to balloons they sell, with a $20 civil penalty per violation.

ct:SB 457.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE STATE'S BOTTLE BILL.
ct:SB 457.summary: Sets misdemeanor or felony penalties, by volume from 5,000 containers, for willfully collecting refunds on containers not bought in Connecticut, and ends reduced redemption-center handling fees by July 1, 2027 or once scanning technology is used.

ct:SB 458.title: AN ACT DESIGNATING VARIOUS DAYS AND MONTHS.
ct:SB 458.summary: Requires the governor to proclaim days and months including Hartford Whalers Day (January 11), Good Neighbor Day (September 28), Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month (September) and Military Suicide Remembrance and Awareness Day (September 30).

ct:SB 470.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE LEGISLATIVE COMMISSIONERS' RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TECHNICAL AND MINOR REVISIONS TO THE GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION STATUTES.
ct:SB 470.summary: Allows certain contracts of state higher-education units made or amended after passage, rather than after July 1, 2026, to include either the state nondiscrimination contract text or a nondiscrimination affirmation, and makes technical changes to government administration statutes.

ct:SB 472.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE ELECTRONIC SURVEILLANCE OF EMPLOYEES.
ct:SB 472.summary: Requires employers that electronically monitor employees to name the specific monitored locations in their notice and post it there, with exceptions for security reasons and airports, and to give new hires a plain-language statement on monitoring permitted without notice.

ct:SB 473.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE REVISOR'S TECHNICAL REVISIONS TO THE GENERAL STATUTES.
ct:SB 473.summary: Corrects statutory references and makes other technical changes throughout the general statutes.

ct:SB 477.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE FAILURE TO FILE FOR CERTAIN GRAND LIST EXEMPTIONS, A MUNICIPAL OPTION TO ABATE DELINQUENT PROPERTY TAXES ON CERTAIN PARCELS OF LAND, ALLOCATIONS OF CERTAIN STATE FUNDS AND ITEMS IMPLEMENTING THE STATE BUDGET FOR THE BIENNIUM ENDING JUNE 30, 2027.
ct:SB 477.summary: Lets taxpayers in certain towns claim property tax exemptions despite missed filing deadlines, lets towns abate delinquent taxes on qualifying land on the 2013 and 2014 grand lists, raises judges' pay about 4.4% in FY 27, and revises many other budget-bill provisions.

ct:SB 478.title: AN ACT CONCERNING CONSUMER SAFEGUARDS FOR LONG-TERM CARE POLICIES.
ct:SB 478.summary: Requires long-term care insurers and the Insurance Department to report annually on policy losses, and lets the insurance commissioner investigate and discipline insurers that violate long-term care insurance laws.

ct:SB 483.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CRIME OF DIGITAL DEFRAUDING.
ct:SB 483.summary: Makes it larceny to make and share a digitally forged image, video or audio recording of a person, without their consent, with intent to financially injure someone. Allows a defense if the defendant took reasonable steps to disclose the forgery. Effective October 1, 2026.

ct:SB 484.title: AN ACT CONCERNING DISTRACTED DRIVING AND THE SAFE OPERATION OF A MOTOR VEHICLE IN A HIGHWAY WORK ZONE.
ct:SB 484.summary: Makes driving in a highway work zone while doing anything the distracted driving law prohibits a per se reckless driving violation, a criminal offense, and bars prosecuting the same act as both reckless and distracted driving.

ct:SB 488.title: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE TREASURER'S RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REVISIONS TO THE UNCLAIMED PROPERTY PROGRAM AND SECOND INJURY FUND.
ct:SB 488.summary: Changes unclaimed property laws, including ways to show interest in property, early transfers to the treasurer and ending required automatic returns of property under $50, and limits the Second Injury Fund's liability for reimbursing employers and insurers.

ct:SB 5.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ONLINE SAFETY.
ct:SB 5.summary: Bars AI subscription providers from signing or renewing without written disclosure of key terms, restricts AI companions for minors, requires notices and self-harm detection, adds whistleblower rules for frontier AI developers, regulates automated employment decisions, and creates a Connecticut AI Academy.

ct:SB 508.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE SUSPENSION OF AN OPERATOR'S LICENSE FOR REPEATEDLY FAILING TO STOP FOR A SCHOOL BUS.
ct:SB 508.summary: Requires the motor vehicles commissioner to suspend a driver's license for six months, without a hearing, after a third or subsequent violation of the law on stopping for a school bus.

ct:SB 509.title: AN ACT CONCERNING ADDRESS VERIFICATION REFORMS FOR REGISTRANTS.
ct:SB 509.summary: As amended, creates an affirmative defense to sex offender registration violations if circumstances beyond the person's control, which they did not cause, prevented compliance and they comply within 20 business days; requires registrants to submit proof of residency to the emergency services and public protection department 75 to 90 days after registering.

ct:SB 518.title: AN ACT AMENDING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND IN THE CITY OF MIDDLETOWN.
ct:SB 518.summary: Changes the reversion condition on a ten-acre Middletown parcel conveyed to Shiloh Baptist Community Development Corporation: the land reverts to the state unless construction starts or a financing loan is signed by June 30, 2029, rather than unless it is used by then.

ct:SB 519.title: AN ACT AMENDING A PRIOR CONVEYANCE OF STATE LAND TO THE BRIDGEPORT PORT AUTHORITY.
ct:SB 519.summary: Amends a prior act conveying about 1.008 acres of state land in Bridgeport to the Bridgeport Port Authority, setting the price of any sale or lease at $119,000 instead of appraised value.

ct:SB 520.title: AN ACT REPEALING A CONVEYANCE OF A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE TOWN OF CANTON.
ct:SB 520.summary: Repeals Special Act 24-20, a prior act conveying a parcel of state land to the town of Canton.

ct:SB 521.title: AN ACT CONVEYING A PARCEL OF STATE LAND TO THE NORTHWEST RESOURCE RECOVERY AUTHORITY.
ct:SB 521.summary: Directs the Administrative Services commissioner to convey a roughly four-acre Torrington parcel with the Torrington Transfer Station to the Northwest Resource Recovery Authority for administrative costs. The authority must use it as a public transfer station or it reverts to the state.

ct:SB 87.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NONPROFIT PROVIDER ADVISORY BOARD AND PROHIBITING AUTO INSURANCE PENALTIES ON VOLUNTEER DRIVERS PROVIDING TRANSPORTATION TO NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS.
ct:SB 87.summary: Creates a 23-member Nonprofit Provider Advisory Board within the Office of Policy and Management and bars auto insurers from refusing to renew or raising rates solely because a driver is an unpaid volunteer driver for nonprofits.

ct:SB 89.title: AN ACT UPDATING PRISON RAPE ELIMINATION STANDARDS.
ct:SB 89.summary: Requires state agencies and local governments that hold offenders to comply with the federal Prison Rape Elimination Act as of January 1, 2024, adds duty-to-intervene and sexual assault crisis-service standards, and requires sexual assault reports be copied to the Correction Ombuds.

ct:SB 9.title: AN ACT SUPPORTING COMMUTERS AND MICROTRANSIT SERVICES AND CONCERNING PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION.
ct:SB 9.summary: Allows employers tax credits for commuting benefits, extends the DOT microtransit pilot from two to three years, sets aside $4 million for Shore Line East and $3 million for added service, and creates free bus passes for students and veterans.

ct:SB 90.title: AN ACT REVISING AND CONSOLIDATING THE HATE CRIMES STATUTES.
ct:SB 90.summary: Combines Connecticut's bias-crime laws into one protected-category framework, labels bias-motivated offenses as hate crimes, extends persistent-offender status to them, and allows hate-crimes diversion programs for offenders.

dc:B 26-0016.title: Strategic Parking Enforcement Enhancement Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0016.summary: As amended by substitute, creates a Department of Public Works reimbursable detail program assigning overtime parking enforcement officers to businesses, nonprofits, universities, business improvement districts and others under written agreements, and lets campus police who opt in and certify training issue parking citations in set areas around their campuses.

dc:B 26-0047.title: Funeral Directors Licensing Reform Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0047.summary: Changes funeral director licensing requirements, creates a separate embalmer's license, revises apprenticeship and supervision rules, and updates the Board of Funeral Directors' composition. Existing licensed funeral directors automatically receive an embalmer's license.

dc:B 26-0049.title: Seasonal Pricing and Price Gouging Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0049.summary: Makes a declared public emergency trigger the price-gouging ban, bars buying designated goods above Mayor- or federally set quantities in emergencies, and from 2027 limits emergency rental-vehicle and 95%-occupied hotel prices to 10% above same-week prices in an earlier year.

dc:B 26-0174.title: Enhancing Consumer Protection Procedures Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0174.summary: Expands D.C. consumer protection enforcement, including fines and fees for not complying with investigative subpoenas, asset freezes, treating failure to post prices as an unfair trade practice, bans on retaliation for complaints, and added authority for the Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection.

dc:B 26-0181.title: Short-Term Disability Insurance Benefit Protection Clarification Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0181.summary: Clarifies that the existing ban on insurers reducing short-term disability benefits because of District paid leave benefits applies regardless of where the policy was issued, and makes the ban enforceable under District insurance law.

dc:B 26-0243.title: Automatic Enrollment for Utility Affordability Programs Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0243.summary: As drafted in the committee print, requires the Department of Energy and Environment to implement, within one year of the act's applicability date, a process to automatically identify households eligible for utility affordability programs; utilities then confirm eligibility and enroll them.

dc:B 26-0244.title: Micromobility Fire Safety Standards Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0244.summary: Amends the micromobility fire safety bill to name Global Accreditation Cooperation as the accrediting body, correct a battery standard citation, let any certification body test products, and give shared-fleet operators six months for alternate e-bike testing.

dc:B 26-0245.title: Personal Delivery Device Weight Limit Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0245.summary: Raises the weight limit for personal delivery devices to 275 pounds, excluding cargo, or a higher limit set by the Department of Transportation through rulemaking, and repeals the earlier temporary weight-limit act.

dc:B 26-0285.title: Climatizing Our Overheated Living Spaces Regulation Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0285.summary: Moves the applicability date of the D.C. rental heating and cooling bill from May 1 to April 1, 2027. The bill sets heat and air conditioning season dates and indoor temperature ranges for rental housing.

dc:B 26-0422.title: Glazier Licensing Standards and Certification Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0422.summary: Establishes licensing and certification requirements for glaziers and glazing contractors in D.C. and adds two glazier and glazing contractor members to the Board of Industrial Trades.

dc:B 26-0427.title: Cybersecurity and Accountability Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0427.summary: Changes the insurance cybersecurity bill's confidentiality section: submitted documents are not subject to subpoena or discovery requests to the insurance commissioner, but no privilege bars private civil-damages plaintiffs from seeking them directly from a licensee.

dc:B 26-0436.title: Fair Initiatives Lend Transparency to Every Resident Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0436.summary: Requires the Board of Elections to reject initiatives covering more than one subject, extends the advisory-opinion deadline from 15 to 30 days, and adds fiscal impact statements, public comment, a public meeting, and fiscal impact summaries on petitions and ballots.

dc:B 26-0444.title: Food Policy Council Procurement Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0444.summary: Changes the Food Policy Council's report from annual to every three years starting September 30, 2027, and has the Food Policy Director's office oversee and advise on food purchasing by District agencies and contractors that regularly buy food.

dc:B 26-0494.title: Accountancy Practice Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0494.summary: Authorizes 4-year basic business licenses and fee refunds, exempts motor clubs doing private towing from identifying a storage lot, lets the Mayor add CPA licensure requirements by rule, and changes degree, experience and out-of-state practice-privilege rules for accountants.

dc:B 26-0526.title: Leading Education Access for Reentry and Necessary Success (LEARNS) Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0526.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to provide special education to eligible detained people from age 18, expands eligibility for special education evaluations, and requires an online portal to track grievances and service requests.

dc:B 26-0547.title: Green Death Care Option Amendment Act of 2025 (now known as "Posthumous Care Modernization Amendment Act of 2026")
dc:B 26-0547.summary: Allows funeral establishments to reduce human remains by alkaline hydrolysis (water, alkaline chemicals and heat), defines cremation as incineration, and, like cremation ashes, excludes its product from the vital records definition of human remains.

dc:B 26-0548.title: Washington Commanders Motor Vehicle Identification Tags Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0548.summary: Authorizes the Mayor to design and issue Washington Commanders motor vehicle tags. Residents pay a $25 application fee and $20 annual display fee, or amounts set by rule, deposited in the State Athletic Activities, Programs, and Office Fund.

dc:B 26-0554.title: Commercial Driver’s License Amendment Act of 2025
dc:B 26-0554.summary: Updates D.C. commercial driver's license law to current federal code citations and revises disqualification standards, including disqualifying drivers convicted of fraud tied to commercial licenses or permits or who fail required retests after suspected fraud.

dc:B 26-0564.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0564.summary: Exempts the property at 219 Riggs Road NE from District real property tax while it is owned by Food & Friends, Inc. and used for charitable food distribution or related services, applying as of October 1, 2025.

dc:B 26-0619.title: Eric’s ID Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0619.summary: Requires the DMV to offer license, permit and ID card applicants an optional nonapparent-disability indicator, designated as a butterfly symbol; bars requiring proof; and requires police to train sworn officers on interactions with people who carry the indicator.

dc:B 26-0641.title: Archdiocese of Washington Parish Real Property, Deed Recordation, and Transfer Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0641.summary: Confirms listed parcels owned by the Archbishop of Washington or named parishes are exempt from deed recordation and transfer taxes, and, for most, real property tax while used for religious, charitable or educational services; treats no-cost transfers to parishes as supplemental deeds.

dc:B 26-0663.title: Fiscal Year 2026 Revised Local Budget Temporary Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0663.summary: Temporarily adjusts the FY2026 local budget, decreasing it by $101,257,922 overall, with changes to agency allocations that reflect revenue and cost changes.

dc:B 26-0700.title: Reservoir District Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0700.summary: Defines the one-third affordable set-aside of rental units for the Reservoir District tax exemption in Square 3128 under the federal tax-credit definition (26 U.S.C. 42(g)(2)(A)), with units open to households within HUD's 80 percent Multifamily Tax Subsidy income limit.

dc:B 26-0711.title: Entertainment Establishment Employee Safety Extension Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0711.summary: Allows, on a temporary basis, retail establishments with on-premises Class C or D retailer licenses, and restaurants open 24 hours or at 3 a.m. at least two days a week, to refuse cash if a conspicuous notice is posted on the door or menu.

dc:B 26-0713.title: Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Technical Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0713.summary: Temporarily expands the Police Complaints Board to nine members, lets the Office of Police Complaints' executive director open complaints over unalleged abuse or misuse of police powers, including failure to intervene in or report excessive force, and limits certain provisions to victims under 18.

dc:B 26-0716.title: Public Service Commission Term Holdover Extension Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0716.summary: On a temporary basis, extends to 270 days after term expiration the period a Public Service Commission commissioner may keep serving in a holdover capacity.

dc:B 26-0722.title: Language Access Rulemaking Authority Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0722.summary: Temporarily requires the Mayor to issue rules implementing the Language Access Act of 2004, applying as of June 19, 2004.

dc:B 26-0729.title: Private Vehicle-for-Hire Operator Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0729.summary: Temporarily redefines a private vehicle-for-hire operator as an individual who uses a company's digital dispatch to drive a motor vehicle providing passenger transportation. Applies retroactively to March 1, 2024.

dc:B 26-0733.title: Prearrest Diversion Task Force Recommendations Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0733.summary: Temporarily resets deadlines for the Prearrest Diversion Task Force to issue recommendations on diverting certain misdemeanor offenses and categories of people from arrest, to June 2025 for initial recommendations and July 31, 2026 for the next set.

dc:B 26-0735.title: Special Education for Young Adults in the Custody of the Department of Corrections Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0735.summary: Temporarily designates the Department of Corrections to provide a free appropriate public education under federal and D.C. special education law, during school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027, to detained individuals with disabilities in its custody from age 18.

dc:B 26-0752.title: Health and Human Service Programs and Benefits Eligibility and Delivery Data-Sharing Clarifications Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0752.summary: Temporarily clarifies that the Department of Human Services may share records within the department and with other District agencies to determine eligibility for federal and District health and human service programs, subject to existing data-sharing law.

dc:B 26-0760.title: Medical Cannabis Licensing and Unlicensed Establishment Enforcement Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0760.summary: Temporarily extends medical cannabis conditional licenses by one year, treats establishments selling Schedule I substances as unlicensed, authorizes enforcement against all unlicensed establishments from April 1, 2025, and lets summary closures continue while the danger persists or is likely to recur.

dc:B 26-0764.title: The Omnibus Barry Farm Redevelopment Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0764.summary: Temporarily lets the Surveyor record Barry Farm street and alley closing and dedication plats in phases, with deadlines running from December 2028 for Phase 1A to December 2034 for Phases 2A and 2B.

dc:B 26-0766.title: Restoration of Covenanted Roads and Alleys by the District Government Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0766.summary: Temporarily lets the Mayor repair private rights-of-way used for District trash removal, with owner consent, a liability release and indemnification, when the owner has no duty to maintain them and they are not in good repair.

dc:B 26-0768.title: Net Zero Continuity Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0768.summary: Temporarily exempts District-owned or funded temporary buildings and additions under 10,000 square feet from net-zero-energy standards, and delays certain energy requirements for public safety facilities, aquatics centers with natatoriums and new residential projects until the Mayor's final regulations take effect.

dc:B 26-0779.title: Ballpark Bonds Loan Repayment Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0779.summary: Temporarily directs FY2027 sports facilities fee revenue, up to $49,505,000, to pay debt service on ballpark early-redemption borrowing and RFK infrastructure bonds, with the remainder going to the General Fund.

dc:B 26-0780.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0780.summary: On an emergency basis, exempts from real property tax the 219 Riggs Road NE property owned by Food & Friends, Inc., as long as it is used for charitable food distribution or related services. Applies to 100% of the land as of October 1, 2025.

dc:B 26-0781.title: Food & Friends Property Tax Exemption Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0781.summary: On a temporary basis, exempts from real property tax the 219 Riggs Road NE property owned by Food & Friends, Inc., as long as it is used for charitable food distribution or related services, applying to 100% of the land.

dc:B 26-0782.title: Broadband Price Transparency Regulation Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0782.summary: On an emergency basis, deems broadband internet sellers that follow the federal broadband consumer label rules in effect January 1, 2026 compliant with D.C.'s requirement that advertised prices include all mandatory fees.

dc:B 26-0783.title: Broadband Price Transparency Regulation Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0783.summary: On a temporary basis, deems broadband internet sellers that follow the federal broadband consumer label rules in effect January 1, 2026 compliant with D.C.'s requirement that advertised prices include all mandatory fees.

dc:B 26-0784.title: Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Technical Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0784.summary: On an emergency basis, expands the Police Complaints Board from five to nine members, lets the Office of Police Complaints' executive director open complaints over unalleged abuse or misuse of police powers, and limits certain provisions to victims under 18.

dc:B 26-0785.title: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Rental Vehicle Sales Tax Clarification Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0785.summary: On an emergency basis, restates the rental vehicle sales tax rates, 9.25% through September 30, 2026 and 11% afterward, and reverts the FY2027 budget act's peer-to-peer car sharing wording to prior language.

dc:B 26-0786.title: Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Rental Vehicle Sales Tax Clarification Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0786.summary: Temporarily restates the rental vehicle sales tax rates, 9.25% through September 30, 2026 and 11% afterward, in the FY2027 budget support laws and reverts their peer-to-peer car sharing wording to prior language.

dc:B 26-0787.title: Community Schools Grant Program Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0787.summary: Amends, on an emergency basis, the Community Schools Incentive Act so Community Schools Task Force appointees must be "individuals" rather than "District residents." The act lasts up to 90 days.

dc:B 26-0788.title: Community Schools Grant Program Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0788.summary: Temporarily removes the requirement that Community Schools Task Force appointees be District residents, allowing any individuals to be appointed.

dc:B 26-0789.title: Duke District BID Grantmaking Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0789.summary: Requires the Department of Small and Local Business Development to award a $1 million grant from the Performance Parking Zone Fund to the Duke Business Improvement District Corporation in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, as emergency legislation.

dc:B 26-0790.title: Duke District BID Grantmaking Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0790.summary: Requires, on a temporary basis, the Department of Small and Local Business Development to award a $1 million grant in the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 to the Duke District Business Improvement District for the Greater Shaw/U Street area.

dc:B 26-0791.title: Extension of Substance Use and Targeted Outreach Grants Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0791.summary: Requires, on an emergency basis, the Department of Behavioral Health to give Fiscal Year 2027 grants to the Fiscal Year 2026 Targeted Outreach pilot grantees to continue services, and authorizes Opioid Abatement Fund spending on them. The act lasts up to 90 days.

dc:B 26-0792.title: Extension of Substance Use and Targeted Outreach Grants Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0792.summary: Requires, on a temporary basis, the Department of Behavioral Health to give Fiscal Year 2027 grants to the Fiscal Year 2026 Targeted Outreach pilot grantees to continue services, and allows it to spend Opioid Abatement Fund money on the program.

dc:B 26-0793.title: Modification Nos. M0008, M0009 and M0010 to Contract No. CW110323 with Tag-B Parking, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0793.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with Tag-B Parking, LLC for private student transportation and attendant services, exercises the rest of option year three, and authorizes payment up to $18,710,208.

dc:B 26-0794.title: Modification Nos. M0010, M0011, and M0012 to Contract No. CW110212 with USA Guided Tours DC, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0794.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with USA Guided Tours DC, LLC for transportation of students with disabilities, exercises the third option year, and authorizes payment up to $7,722,000.

dc:B 26-0795.title: Modification Nos. M0007 and M0008 to Contract No. CW110321 with Miles Away Charter, LLC Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0795.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with Miles Away Charter, LLC for transportation of students with disabilities, exercises the third option year, and authorizes payment up to $1,465,200.

dc:B 26-0796.title: Modification Nos. M04, M05 and M06 to Contract No. CW106884 with See Forever Foundation Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0796.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with See Forever Foundation for an education program for youth in the custody of the Department of Youth Rehabilitation Services, and authorizes payment up to $3,968,957.85.

dc:B 26-0797.title: Modification Nos. M0009, M00010 and M0011 to Contract No. CW110208 with Ramjay Inc., Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0797.summary: On an emergency basis, approves modifications to a contract with Ramjay Inc. for transportation of students with disabilities, exercises the third option year, and authorizes payment up to $4,802,490.

dc:B 26-0800.title: Modification No. M003 to Contract No. DCRL-2026-C-0024 with Crawford Consulting and Mental Health Service, Inc. Approval and Payment Authorization Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0800.summary: On an emergency basis, approves Modification No. M003 to a contract with Crawford Consulting and Mental Health Service, Inc. for community-based residential and social services, and authorizes payment up to $1,774,850.84.

dc:B 26-0824.title: Health and Human Service Programs and Benefits Eligibility and Delivery Data-Sharing Clarifications Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0824.summary: On an emergency basis, makes Department of Human Services record-sharing under the Homeless Services Reform Act subject to the Data-Sharing and Information Coordination Act's uses and disclosures, and widens that act's definition of agency to include subdivisions of agencies.

dc:B 26-0825.title: Alternative Breakfast Service Model Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0825.summary: On an emergency basis, changes school breakfast rules so Title I elementary schools with low participation may serve all students grab-and-go breakfast, breakfast in the classroom, or both.

dc:B 26-0826.title: Alternative Breakfast Service Model Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0826.summary: On a temporary basis, changes school breakfast rules so Title I elementary schools with low participation may serve all students grab-and-go breakfast, breakfast in the classroom, or both.

dc:B 26-0827.title: Porchfest Permitting Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0827.summary: On an emergency basis, lets District residents apply for a block party permit to close their street for a Porchfest (a free music festival on porches or yards), and adds Porchfests to the District's policy of approving block parties.

dc:B 26-0828.title: Porchfest Permitting Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0828.summary: On a temporary basis, lets District residents apply for a block party permit to close their street for a Porchfest, a free neighborhood music festival held on residents' porches or yards.

dc:B 26-0836.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Gold Line Bus Rapid Transit Phase 1 Fiscal Year 2027 and 2028 Reimbursable Agreement Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0836.summary: On an emergency basis, approves an agreement giving the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority $5 million in District capital funds for planning, environmental review and preliminary design of Phase 1 of a Gold Line bus rapid transit route on H Street and Benning Road.

dc:B 26-0840.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Stadium-Armory Station Improvements Fiscal Year 2026 to Fiscal Year 2030 Reimbursable Agreement Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0840.summary: On an emergency basis, approves an agreement giving the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority $300 million in District capital funds to design and build improvements at the Stadium-Armory Metrorail Station.

dc:B 26-0847.title: Net Zero Continuity Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0847.summary: On an emergency basis, exempts certain District-owned and -funded projects, such as temporary buildings, additions under 10,000 square feet, and police and fire facilities, from net-zero-energy standards, and revises that standard's definition and the projects it covers.

dc:B 26-0848.title: Private Vehicle-for-Hire Operator Clarification Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0848.summary: On an emergency basis, defines a private vehicle-for-hire operator as an individual who uses a private vehicle-for-hire company's digital dispatch to drive passengers in a motor vehicle, applying as of March 1, 2024.

dc:B 26-0849.title: Language Access Rulemaking Authority Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0849.summary: On an emergency basis, requires the Mayor to issue rules to carry out the Language Access Act of 2004, applying as of June 19, 2004.

dc:B 26-0851.title: Homeless Services Contract Adjustment Temporary Amendment Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0851.summary: On a temporary basis, requires the Office of Contracting and Procurement to decide, within 45 calendar days of a complete request, whether a homeless services contractor is owed a contract adjustment after a federal wage determination changes.

dc:B 26-0852.title: University of the District of Columbia Multiyear Contract No. PO-GF-2026-C-0019 with Ellucian Company LLC Contract Emergency Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0852.summary: On an emergency basis, approves a multiyear contract between the University of the District of Columbia and Ellucian Company LLC to move the university's enterprise software systems to a cloud-based service.

dc:CER 26-0207.title: Dr. Tiffany L. Lancaster Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0207.summary: Honors Dr. Tiffany L. Lancaster for her contributions to the District and her public service, culture and advancement of others.

dc:CER 26-0208.title: Philip Lepanto Ceremonial Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0208.summary: Remembers and honors the life of Philip A. Lepanto, including his service as an Advisory Neighborhood Commissioner.

dc:CER 26-0209.title: 17th Street High Heel Race Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0209.summary: Celebrates the annual 17th Street High Heel Race, a District LGBTQ+ tradition that began in 1986.

dc:CER 26-0210.title: Robert A. Kennedy, Jr. Memorial Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0210.summary: Honors the life of Robert A. Kennedy Jr. and his advocacy for people with disabilities in the District.

dc:CER 26-0212.title: Battle’s Transportation, Inc. Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0212.summary: Honors Battle's Transportation, Inc., a District passenger transportation company founded in 1976, for fifty years of service.

dc:CER 26-0213.title: Robert Vinson Brannum Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0213.summary: Honors Robert Vinson Brannum, a native Washingtonian and Air Force veteran, for his civic, veterans and community service in Ward 5.

dc:CER 26-0214.title: Capital Queens Women’s Sports Week Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0214.summary: Recognizes the inaugural Capital Queens Women's Sports Week, held September 20 to 26 and established jointly by the Washington Spirit and Washington Mystics.

dc:CER 26-0215.title: Lindsey Parker Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0215.summary: Honors Lindsey Parker for her work in District government, including as Director of the Office of the Chief Technology Officer and in the Mayor's office.

dc:CER 26-0216.title: Kevin Donahue Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0216.summary: Honors Kevin Donahue for his service to District residents as City Administrator.

dc:CER 26-0217.title: Hattie Holmes Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0217.summary: Honors the Hattie Holmes Senior Wellness Center for its commitment to and impact on the community.

dc:CER 26-0218.title: Congress Heights Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0218.summary: Honors the Congress Heights Senior Wellness Center in Ward 8 for its programming for District adults aged 60 and older.

dc:CER 26-0219.title: Iona Senior Services Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0219.summary: Honors Iona Senior Services for its work and service to communities across the District.

dc:CER 26-0220.title: Bernice Fonteneau Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0220.summary: Honors the Bernice Fonteneau Senior Wellness Center in Ward 1 as a community resource since 2011 serving adults aged 60 and older.

dc:CER 26-0221.title: Hayes Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0221.summary: Honors the Hayes Senior Wellness Center in Ward 6 for its role as a community resource for adults aged 60 and older.

dc:CER 26-0222.title: Washington Home Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0222.summary: Honors Iona's Washington Home Center in Ward 8 for its support of older adults, caregivers and families.

dc:CER 26-0223.title: Model Cities Senior Wellness Center Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0223.summary: Honors the Model Cities Senior Wellness Center in Ward 5 for its role as a community resource for seniors.

dc:CER 26-0224.title: Vida Senior Services Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0224.summary: Honors Vida Senior Services for more than five decades of services to older adults, including free meals, health screenings and mental health support.

dc:CER 26-0225.title: DC Table Tennis Day Recognition Resolution of 2026
dc:CER 26-0225.summary: Recognizes October 10, 2026, and the second Saturday of each October after it, as DC Table Tennis Day in the District.

dc:PR 26-0671.title: Board of Library Trustees Denise Rolark Barnes Confirmation Resolution of 2026
dc:PR 26-0671.summary: Confirms Denise Rolark Barnes to the Board of Library Trustees for a term ending January 5, 2031.

dc:PR 26-0672.title: Board of Library Trustees Mary Early Confirmation Resolution of 2026
