ia:HF 2598.summary: Requires applicants for an initial commercial driver's license to certify they completed a human trafficking prevention course of at least 30 minutes, starting March 1, 2027 or when the transportation department's new records system phase takes effect, if earlier.

ia:HF 2602.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of massage establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2602.summary: Requires massage therapy establishments, other than sole practitioners and certain exempt locations, to hold a Board of Massage Therapy license starting January 1, 2027, with possible inspections and fingerprint background checks.

ia:HF 2610.title: A bill for an act relating to education programs and systems, including career and technical education expenditures and definitions, statewide lower division general education framework and common course numbering systems, and the implementation of a statewide corequisite model in Iowa community colleges.
ia:HF 2610.summary: Lets the education department allow career academy grant recipients to deposit grant money into a protected investment or endowment account, with only earnings spent, and provides that a regional center may include a physical facility, a career academy program, or both.

ia:HF 2615.title: Relating to thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons
ia:HF 2615.summary: Requires thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons to be separate, non-overlapping meets, with no races for both breeds on the same day, unless the breed owners' associations and the Polk County track licensee agree in writing to a mixed meet.

ia:HF 2617.title: A bill for an act relating to abandoned vehicles.
ia:HF 2617.summary: As passed by the House, rewrites Iowa's abandoned-vehicle law: sets who may tow and impound, requires notice to owners within ten days giving 20 days to reclaim the vehicle or retrieve belongings, and sets rules for selling unclaimed vehicles and distributing proceeds.

ia:HF 2633.title: A bill for an act relating to living organ donors and life insurance, disability insurance, and long-term care insurance.
ia:HF 2633.summary: Bars life, disability and long-term care insurers from declining or limiting coverage, or varying terms and price, based solely on a person being a living organ donor.

ia:HF 2634.title: A bill for an act relating to preneed sellers, sales agents and sales agent applicants, and government cemeteries.
ia:HF 2634.summary: Changes preneed funeral and cemetery rules: repeals the sales agent annual report requirement and creates a "government cemetery" category, for cemeteries run by a city, county or township, excluded from perpetual-care cemetery requirements.

ia:HF 2635.title: A bill for an act relating to health carriers standards of conduct; utilization review organizations, artificial intelligence, audits, and prior authorizations; certificate of need processes; and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2635.summary: As passed by the House, sets audit deadlines for health insurers' utilization review, bars carrier penalties for out-of-network referrals, requires qualified reviewers for prior authorization denials, exempts some cancer screenings from prior authorization, and raises certificate-of-need dollar thresholds.

ia:HF 2655.title: A bill for an act relating to the operating privileges of drivers of authorized emergency vehicles and police officers riding police bicycles.
ia:HF 2655.summary: Extends to all authorized emergency vehicle drivers, except designated towing vehicles, the allowances to proceed past red signals and stop signs after slowing and to exceed speed limits without recklessly endangering life or property.

ia:HF 2667.title: Relating to project design standards and specifications, including by providing for a statewide urban design and specifications board and requiring certain reports to city councils regarding noncompliant projects
ia:HF 2667.summary: Creates a statewide urban design and specifications board, coordinated by the Department of Transportation and Iowa State University, to publish design and specifications manuals. Requires a report on added costs before a city council approves a street project that departs from state standards.

ia:HF 2670.title: Relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to summative testing in schools and the educational program provided to students enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2670.summary: Adds grade 8 and 11 social studies assessments (from 2027-28), drops "common core" from assessment alignment, ends state equity coordinator standards, removes "multicultural, gender-fair" and global-perspectives language from accreditation rules, and lets agriculture coursework count toward math units.

ia:HF 2676.title: Relating to health-related matters, including health- related professions, nutrition, medication, and education, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2676.summary: Requires nutrition continuing education for certain physicians and, from 2028, 40 hours of nutrition coursework in medical school; allows over-the-counter ivermectin; bans listed dyes and additives in school meals; limits K-5 digital instruction to 60 minutes daily; changes school physical activity and SNAP rules.

ia:HF 2678.title: A bill for an act providing for certain persons acting under the jurisdiction of the secretary of state, including by providing for information from required filings, and the administrative dissolution of certain entities, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2678.summary: Lets the Secretary of State remove unauthorized personal information from business filings, send interrogatories to entities suspected of fraudulent or unlawful use, and dissolve those that concede violations or fail to respond; also adds out-of-state owners to agricultural landholding reports.

ia:HF 2694.title: A bill for an act relating to the regulation of certain places and activities by the governor.
ia:HF 2694.summary: As passed by the House, bars the governor from closing or regulating places or practices of worship; bars disaster-emergency measures that change election rules without legislative approval, regulate conduct in private residences or require vaccination; and bars requiring private businesses to close in public health disasters.

ia:HF 2695.title: A bill for an act relating to the application of foreign law and limiting changes in venue of civil actions, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2695.summary: Bars courts and tribunals from transferring a civil case if that would apply foreign law violating a constitutional right, and voids rulings and contract provisions based on foreign law that deny a party a right guaranteed by the U.S. or Iowa constitutions.

ia:HF 2706.title: A bill for an act relating to judicial officers, including magistrate appointments in judicial election districts, senior magistrates, and judicial officer compensation, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2706.summary: Changes judicial officer rules, including appointing magistrates by judicial election district instead of by county, and addressing senior magistrates and judicial officer compensation.

ia:HF 2707.title: Relating to alignment of delivery of health and human services programs and services, aging and disability services, and volunteer services, and including applicability and effective date provisions
ia:HF 2707.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to divide the state into health and human services districts, initially matching the behavioral health districts. Bars redesignating aging planning areas before 2027 pending a cost review and report, and creates a department volunteerism subunit.

ia:HF 2711.title: Relating to state policies and programs with race or gender requirements
ia:HF 2711.summary: Repeals state affirmative action requirements, repeals or renames several race- and gender-specific education programs, drops race and ethnicity references from certificate-of-need review, and removes bias-prevention topics from required law enforcement training.

ia:HF 2724.title: Requiring the board of educational examiners to establish additional endorsements and authorizations
ia:HF 2724.summary: Directs the Board of Educational Examiners to create additional teaching endorsements in fine arts, mathematics and science for bachelor's degree holders (authority repealed July 1, 2030), a K-12 instructional strategist II endorsement without a graduate degree, and an activities administration authorization.

ia:HF 2749.title: A bill for an act relating to real estate transfer tax, including declarations of value.
ia:HF 2749.summary: Exempts deeds that transfer trust assets to beneficiaries without payment from the requirement to file a declaration of value with the county recorder.

ia:HF 2754.title: Relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to charter school approval, contracts, funding, and operations, services provided to charter schools by area education agencies, charter school student participation in ex tracurricular activities provided by public schools, the Iowa public employees’ retirement system, education savings accounts, independent accreditation, teacher training and licensure, the statewide voluntary preschool program, the district- to-community c ol...
ia:HF 2754.summary: Changes charter school approval, funding and operations, covers charter school employees under IPERS, creates a charter school facilities loan program, adds a semester application window for education savings accounts, lets charter and nonpublic students join public school activities, and changes preschool and accreditation rules.

ia:HF 2756.title: A bill for an act relating to licensing of service companies, motor vehicle service contracts, and residential service contracts, and providing civil penalties and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2756.summary: Revises Iowa's motor vehicle and residential service contract law effective January 1, 2027: lowers the license renewal fee from $500 to $200, requires licensees to report ownership, officer and out-of-state enforcement changes within 30 days, and requires keeping a license while contracts remain in force.

ia:HF 2757.title: A bill for an act relating to nuclear electric generation facilities by creating sales and use tax exemptions and refunds, making appropriations to the state board of regents for establishing and maintaining a nuclear energy workforce, making penalties applicable, and including applicability and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2757.summary: Exempts property and services used to build, expand, repair, or restart nuclear power plants from sales and use tax until commercial operation, if the facility pays $2,200 per megawatt of capacity annually, up to four years, into a Board of Regents nuclear workforce fund.

ia:HF 2761.title: A bill for an act relating to driver’s licenses and nonoperator’s identification cards marked to reflect gold star status.
ia:HF 2761.summary: As introduced, lets surviving spouses, parents, children and siblings of service members who died on active duty during a time of military conflict, or as a result of that service, request that their driver's license or ID card be marked "GOLD STAR FAMILY."

ia:HF 2765.title: A bill for an act providing for the regulation of mining, making penalties applicable, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2765.summary: Requires the state soil conservation division to adopt rules, including emergency rules, for land subsidence above underground mines on public land or public rights-of-way, covering reporting, repair-plan engineer qualifications, and repair timeliness. Takes effect on enactment.

ia:HF 2766.title: A bill for an act relating to captive insurance companies and life captive reinsurance companies, and including civil penalties.
ia:HF 2766.summary: Makes gross premiums tax returns of insurance and captive insurance companies confidential, with a serious misdemeanor for state employees who publish them, and changes rules for captive insurance and life captive reinsurance companies.

ia:HF 2768.title: Relating to and making appropriations for state government administration and regulation, including the department of administrative services, auditor of state, ethics and campaign disclosure board, offices of governor and lieutenant governor, department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, department of insurance and financial services, department of management, Iowa public employees’ retirement system, public information board, department of revenue, secretary of state, treasurer of stat...
ia:HF 2768.summary: Appropriates FY 2026-27 general fund money to administrative, financial, and regulatory agencies, including administrative services, the auditor, revenue, the secretary of state, and the utilities commission, and redirects certain fireworks, amusement device, and boxing fees to the licensing and regulation fund.

ia:HF 2769.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the judicial branch.
ia:HF 2769.summary: Replaces the bill with judicial branch appropriations for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026, including about $202.7 million for judicial salaries and court operations, $3.6 million for jury and witness fees, and $3.29 million for court-ordered juvenile services.

ia:HF 2770.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the justice system, providing fees, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2770.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of justice, corrections, public safety and public defense and other justice agencies, raises state-paid appointed counsel pay by $4 per hour from July 1, 2026, and creates an attorney loan repayment program.

ia:HF 2771.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations involving state government entities associated with agriculture, natural resources, and environmental protection, and including contingent effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2771.summary: Appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of agriculture and natural resources, the Iowa Finance Authority, and Iowa State University and the University of Iowa, and makes Iowa Code changes.

ia:HF 2772.title: Relating to and making appropriations for the economic development of the state, including to the economic development authority, Iowa finance authority, department of workforce development, and state board of regents and certain regents institutions, and codifying the housing renewal program
ia:HF 2772.summary: Appropriates FY 2026-27 money to the Economic Development Authority, Finance Authority, Workforce Development, and regents universities, and codifies the housing renewal program, with repayments retained by the nonprofit Iowa affiliate for new awards.

ia:HF 2778.title: A bill for an act modifying the individual income tax credit for emergency medical services personnel to include volunteer ambulance drivers, and including retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2778.summary: As introduced, extends the $250 individual income tax credit for emergency medical services personnel to volunteer ambulance drivers, applying to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

ia:HF 2779.title: A bill for an act relating to authorizations to conduct advance deposit wagering.
ia:HF 2779.summary: Requires the racing and gaming commission to authorize entities meeting simulcasting licensure rules, instead of the Polk County racetrack licensee, to run advance deposit wagering, and bars phone or electronic wagers within five miles of a racetrack without the track's agreement.

ia:HF 2780.title: A bill for an act relating to alcoholic beverage control by providing for certificates of compliance and the issuance of class “A” wine permits to nonnative wine manufacturers, permitting cities to create social districts for the consumption of alcoholic beverages, and providing fees.
ia:HF 2780.summary: Changes alcohol permit rules by removing the distiller's certificate requirement for some brand resellers, allowing class A wine permits for nonnative wine makers, and letting cities create social districts for drinking alcohol in certain public places.

ia:HF 2781.title: Relating to allocations of moneys from the juvenile detention home fund
ia:HF 2781.summary: Distributes $150,000 from the juvenile detention home fund to each eligible county or multicounty detention home, then splits the remaining money by each home's share of prior-year costs, replacing the current cost-share-only distribution.

ia:HF 2782.title: Relating to and making appropriations to the department of veterans affairs and the department of health and human services, including aging and disability services, behavioral health, public health, and community access and eligibility; the medical assistance program, state supplementary assistance, Hawki, and other health- related programs; family well-being and protection; state-operated specialty care; administration and compliance; transfers, cash flow, and nonreversions; report on nonre...
ia:HF 2782.summary: Appropriates FY 2026-27 money to the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Department of Health and Human Services, covering Medicaid, Hawki, behavioral and public health, child care assistance, and child protective services, and requires quarterly reports on nonreverted funds.

ia:HF 2783.title: Relating to and making appropriations to the education system, including the funding and operation of the department for the blind, department of education, state board of regents, and department of workforce development, and modifying provisions related to the Iowa special education council, the school budget review committee, and the calculation of basic enrollment, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2783.summary: Appropriates FY 2026-27 money to the Department for the Blind, Department of Education, and regents universities. Caps the at-risk children appropriation at $10,524,389, sets the work-study appropriation to zero, and repeals the for-profit college tuition grant program.

ia:HF 2785.title: A bill for an act extending the biodiesel blended fuel tax credit.
ia:HF 2785.summary: Extends the repeal date of the biodiesel blended fuel promotion tax credit for retail dealers, for individual and corporate income taxes, from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2033.

ia:HF 2786.title: A bill for an act modifying the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel production.
ia:HF 2786.summary: Raises the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel producers from 4 to 5 cents per gallon produced in Iowa and moves the refund's repeal date from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2031.

ia:HF 2787.title: Prohibiting warrant resolution clinics, including enforcement mechanisms, providing penalties, and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 2787.summary: Prohibits warrant resolution clinics, events letting people with outstanding warrants resolve them without immediate arrest. Makes knowing violations simple misdemeanors, adds removal from office for officials and civil penalties up to $10,000 for private organizers, and overrides local policies.

ia:HF 2788.title: A bill for an act relating to abortions including definitions, informed consent, dispensing of abortion-inducing drugs, and other abortion-related provisions.
ia:HF 2788.summary: Requires a pre-abortion in-person physician exam including screening for coercion or abuse. Sets informed-consent steps for drug-induced abortions, requires abortion-inducing drugs be dispensed to the patient in a health care setting, and lets the woman or her representative sue those who dispense otherwise.

ia:HF 2791.title: A bill for an act permitting an exchange of the cash reserve levy for another local levy within the school budget for certain school districts to correct for an extreme circumstance and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2791.summary: As introduced, lets school districts whose taxable value fell by $100 million or more from a single-property correction exceed the cash reserve levy limit for 2026-27, if they cut other levies by at least as much. Takes effect on enactment.

ia:HF 2793.title: A bill for an act relating to a railway tracks overpass and underpass fund, and making appropriations.
ia:HF 2793.summary: As introduced, creates a railway tracks overpass and underpass fund under the Department of Transportation to give grants to cities and counties for building highway overpasses and underpasses across railway tracks.

ia:HF 2794.title: A bill for an act establishing a sexual assault forensic examination center grant program and trust fund.
ia:HF 2794.summary: Creates a grant program in the Department of Justice under which, if funded, the attorney general contracts with a nonprofit not affiliated with a hospital to run sexual assault forensic examination centers, with annual reports to the attorney general and legislature.

ia:HF 2797.title: A bill for an act relating to the peace officer, public safety, and emergency personnel bill of rights, and providing fees.
ia:HF 2797.summary: Requires courts to award attorney fees, expenses and costs to a peace officer who wins a challenge to placement on a prosecutor's Brady-Giglio list, paid by the state or local government responsible for the prosecuting agency; applies to placements since July 1, 2021.

ia:HF 2799.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the economic development authority, the utilities commission, and the department of education, including creation of the headquarters expansion and development for growth and employment program, and the business incentives for growth program training fund; repeal of the new jobs tax credit program; the major economic growth attraction program; load forecasting and analysis of electric transmission system expansion plans; creation of the electric transmission system expansion planning and analysis and load forecasting fund; the industrial new jobs training program; and establishing the new jobs training program interim study committee; and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2799.summary: Creates the EDGE headquarters tax incentive program and a training fund, repeals the New Jobs Tax Credit, has the economic development authority commission an Iowa State University electricity load forecast every two years, and changes industrial new jobs training.

ia:HF 2800.title: A bill for an act relating to state and local government and finances, including by making, modifying, limiting, or reducing appropriations, distributions, or transfers, authorizing expenditure of unappropriated moneys in special funds, making corrections, and providing for properly related matters including the national electrical code, local civil rights laws, political party state central committees, noxious weeds, nonresident deer hunting licenses, proprietary treatment systems, poultry associations, tax credits, alternative nicotine and vapor products, public assistance programs, judicial branch and county attorney salaries, civil litigation abuse, human trafficking, federal grants and loans notifications, quarterly payments to area education agencies, civic proficiency in higher education, charter schools under the Iowa public employees’ retirement system, school district incentives, extracurricular interscholastic eligibility, and levy increases, and including effective date, applicability, and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2800.summary: Makes appropriation changes and many related government provisions, including the National Electrical Code, local civil rights laws, a health care access tax credit, judicial and county attorney salaries, a civil litigation abuse cause of action, and school district levy increases.

ia:HF 2801.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2801.summary: Lets the economic development authority award either a tax credit of up to 5 percent of qualifying investment to up to two businesses, or up to 10 percent, paid over 10 years, to one business in a rural county.

ia:HF 523.title: A bill for an act relating to the ability of peace officers to file a petition for emergency protective orders on behalf of persons seeking relief from domestic abuse.
ia:HF 523.summary: As introduced, lets a peace officer file a petition for a 72-hour emergency protective order for a person who says they are in present danger of domestic abuse and asks the officer to file it.

ia:HF 571.title: Relating to protections for medical practitioners, health care institutions, and health care payors including those related to the exercise of conscience, whistleblower activities, and free speech, and providing penalties
ia:HF 571.summary: Allows medical practitioners and health care institutions to refuse to take part in or pay for health care services that violate their conscience, bars discrimination and liability for doing so, and bars discrimination for whistleblowing and licensing sanctions for protected speech.

ia:HF 640.title: A bill for an act concerning self-storage facilities, including acceptances and defaults of rental agreements.
ia:HF 640.summary: Changes self-storage rules: a renter who keeps a unit without signing a written agreement within 30 days is treated as accepting it, operators give 15 days' notice to remove property after non-rent defaults, and residential use is an immediate default.

ia:HF 648.title: A bill for an act relating to a licensed sedation provider host permit for a dentist.
ia:HF 648.summary: Creates a sedation provider host permit letting a dentist who completes a board-approved course and meets equipment and life-support training requirements employ a sedation provider to give moderate sedation to patients 13 and older and monitor them.

ia:HF 703.title: A bill for an act concerning information regarding certain state and federal student loan programs.
ia:HF 703.summary: Requires the Iowa College Aid Bureau to compare estimated rates on federal Direct PLUS loans with state college family and partnership loans, publish a statement if the state loans may be lower, and notify Iowa colleges, which must include it in aid offers.

ia:HF 766.title: Relating to motor vehicle window tint, and making penalties applicable
ia:HF 766.summary: Bars driving with a front windshield under 70 percent light transmittance or front side windows under 50 percent, replacing the current excessively-dark-or-reflective standard, and exempts law enforcement vehicles.

ia:HF 777.title: A bill for an act relating to applications for a motor vehicle salvage certificate of title by an insurer without surrendering the certificate of title or manufacturer’s or importer’s statement of origin, making penalties applicable, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 777.summary: Lets supporting documents for an insurer's salvage-title application, such as a power of attorney, be signed under penalty of perjury, including electronically, instead of notarized; relieves the department and county treasurers of liability for relying on them after reasonable verification. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

ia:HF 864.title: A bill for an act requiring persons who operate certain internet sites, applications, or a segment of an internet site or application that contains material pornographic for minors to perform reasonable age verification.
ia:HF 864.summary: Requires operators of sites or apps with a substantial portion of content pornographic for minors to use reasonable age verification, limits retention of users' identifying data, exempts news organizations and internet access providers, and lets the attorney general enforce.

ia:HF 907.title: A bill for an act requiring the department of transportation to provide for the registration of noncommercial fleet vehicles and issue special noncommercial fleet vehicle registration plates.
ia:HF 907.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation, by December 1, 2028, to create a registration program and special reassignable plates, exempt from annual validation stickers, for noncommercial fleet vehicles: groups of two or more commonly owned or controlled vehicles used for business.

ia:HF 917.title: A bill for an act relating to civil liability actions against motocross facilities.
ia:HF 917.summary: Shields motocross facility operators from liability for injuries or deaths from the inherent risks of motocross, except for intentional injury, negligence, unsafe equipment, or failure to use reasonable care, and requires posted warning signs.

ia:HF 960.title: A bill for an act relating to the sales tax exemption for the purchase of central office equipment or transmission equipment used by certain entities primarily in the furnishing of telecommunications services on a commercial basis.
ia:HF 960.summary: Expands the sales tax exemption for telecommunications central office and transmission equipment by dropping "primarily" and adding internet access services, for carriers, cable operators, utilities, cooperatives, and mobile radio providers.

ia:HF 990.title: A bill for an act relating to the issuance of medical cannabidiol registration cards and licensure of medical cannabidiol dispensaries.
ia:HF 990.summary: Removes the Iowa residency requirement for a medical cannabidiol registration card and lets the Department of Health and Human Services license up to 10 medical cannabidiol dispensaries instead of 5.

ia:HF 992.title: A bill for an act relating to the fee for duplicates or other evidence of interstate fuel use tax permits or licenses.
ia:HF 992.summary: As introduced, raises the fee for a duplicate or other evidence of an interstate fuel permit or license from 50 cents to $1.

ia:SF 176.title: A bill for an act relating to participation in cocurricular and extracurricular activities offered by school districts by pupils who open enroll for purposes of receiving educational instruction and course content primarily over the internet.
ia:SF 176.summary: As introduced, lets students who open enroll in online instruction take part in their home district's extracurricular activities only if the online school's own attendance center does not sponsor those activities.

ia:SF 2039.title: Providing for intervention by members of the general assembly in proceedings for judicial review of agency action under the Iowa administrative procedure Act
ia:SF 2039.summary: Allows the Senate majority and minority leaders, the House speaker, and the House minority leader each to intervene in court review of state agency action, and lets other legislators join their motions.

ia:SF 2086.title: A bill for an act authorizing schools to offer an elective junior fire fighter program to students enrolled in grades eleven and twelve.
ia:SF 2086.summary: Lets schools offer an elective junior fire fighter program to grade 11 and 12 students under an agreement with a local fire department; participants may take Firefighter I certification tests, but certification is issued only at age 18.

ia:SF 2088.title: A bill for an act relating to transportation, including the administration and regulation of matters associated with the operation, registration, and titling of motor vehicles and the Mississippi river parkway commission, making penalties applicable, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2088.summary: Raises the property damage level that requires a driver crash report from $1,500 to $5,000, requires reports from uninsured drivers, allows online renewal of nonoperator IDs and replacement of licenses, and has the state transportation department run one vehicle records system counties must use.

ia:SF 2114.title: A bill for an act relating to intimidation with a dangerous weapon, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 2114.summary: Extends intimidation with a dangerous weapon (class C with intent to injure or provoke fear or anger, class D without) to shooting or discharging at another person, and removes the assembly-of-people and reasonable-fear-of-serious-injury elements.

ia:SF 2139.title: A bill for an act enacting the athletic trainer compact.
ia:SF 2139.summary: Enacts the athletic trainer licensure compact, letting a trainer licensed in one participating state practice in another through a compact privilege without a separate license; the compact takes effect when seven states adopt it.

ia:SF 2168.title: Relating to programs and procedures of the department of workforce development and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2168.summary: Requires a reemployment case management program for unemployment claimants, replaces mailed notices with email or online portal notices, repeals the summer youth intern pilot program, and adds four members to the state workforce board.

ia:SF 2187.title: A bill for an act relating to the verification of citizenship and immigration status of persons who apply for or renew a driver’s license or nonoperator’s identification card, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2187.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to use the federal SAVE system to verify citizenship or immigration status of driver's license and ID card applicants and renewers who do not prove citizenship, and bars issuing or renewing if lawful presence cannot be verified.

ia:SF 2189.title: A bill for an act relating to information required for nonresidents who apply for vehicle registration and issuance of a certificate of title.
ia:SF 2189.summary: Lets a nonresident who owns Iowa real property and uses the vehicle mainly there register or title it by showing reasonable proof of owning the property, and list an out-of-state license number instead of the vehicle's primary user's Iowa details.

ia:SF 2201.title: Relating to school funding by establishing the state percent of growth and the categorical state percent of growth for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, modifying provisions relating to property tax replacement payments, transportation equity aid fun ding, funding for school district budget adjustments, and school district enrollment, establishing an education support personnel salary supplement, making appropriations, and including effective date and applicability provisions
ia:SF 2201.summary: Sets the school funding growth percent at 2 percent for the budget year starting July 1, 2026, caps transportation equity aid at $1 million per district, appropriates $7 million for education support personnel pay, and adds a January adjusted-enrollment count.

ia:SF 2207.title: Relating to the submission of proposed legislation by state departments and agencies
ia:SF 2207.summary: Moves the deadline for state departments and agencies to submit proposed bills to the Legislative Services Agency from 45 to 60 days before a legislative session convenes.

ia:SF 2218.title: A bill for an act relating to state regulatory compliance and eligibility requirements, including by modifying provisions related to the verification of the identity and employment eligibility of individuals by the board of educational examiners, school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools; the provision of a false social security number to an employer, prospective employer, or a potential employee; qualifications for employment, professional licensure, voter registration, and bail; making penalties applicable; and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2218.summary: Requires work authorization proof for teacher licenses, E-Verify by public employers, and SAVE checks for professional licenses and voter rolls; bars unauthorized aliens from registering to vote; fines employers knowingly employing workers using another's Social Security number; sets pretrial detention presumptions.

ia:SF 2219.title: A bill for an act requiring boards of directors of school districts, governing boards of charter schools, and authorities in charge of accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies related to exempting student absences for school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, and projects.
ia:SF 2219.summary: Requires school districts, charter schools, and accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies granting exempt absences, with make-up of missed classwork, for students involved in school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, or projects.

ia:SF 2220.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa statewide assessment of student progress and programs for gifted and talented children, and by requiring school districts to develop an advanced mathematics pathway and implement procedures for subject acceleration and whole-grade acceleration, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2220.summary: Moves the statewide science assessment from grade 10 to grade 11, requires school districts to set uniform procedures for identifying and serving gifted and talented students, and requires advanced math pathways and procedures for subject and whole-grade acceleration.

ia:SF 2263.title: Relating to the carrying, transportation, and possession of weapons, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2263.summary: Allows dangerous weapons, out of sight in locked vehicles, in government parking lots; bars human services rules against firearms in foster-child vehicles; renames weapons free zones "enhanced weapons penalty zones"; and bars state and local enforcement of red flag gun seizures.

ia:SF 2280.title: A bill for an act relating to the safety of persons in certain professions involved with the judicial system, including authorizing a member of the general assembly, judicial officer, attorney general, deputy attorney general, or assistant attorney general to be issued a professional permit to carry weapons, establishing the criminal offenses of threatening and the malicious sharing of personal information of a general assembly member or a judicial officer or a general assembly member’s or a judicial officer’s immediate family, and considering true threats to public officials as harassment, and providing penalties.
ia:SF 2280.summary: Allows legislators, judicial officers, and attorneys in the attorney general's office to get professional permits to carry weapons, makes threatening them or immediate family with specified intent a class C felony, and makes malicious sharing of their personal information a serious misdemeanor.

ia:SF 2284.title: A bill for an act relating to the use of automated systems that detect traffic violations or registration plate information, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 2284.summary: Sets rules for automatic license plate readers, including a local ordinance requirement, Department of Public Safety approved models, a facial recognition ban, search logs, deletion of images after 30 days, and limits on sharing images, with simple misdemeanor penalties.

ia:SF 2289.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2289.summary: Lets the gaming commission issue cease-and-desist orders to unlicensed gambling operators, adds sports wagering to lifetime gambling bans, raises the commission members' expense cap from $30,000 to $45,000, conditions state withholding on certain winnings on federal reporting, and lets pediatric palliative facilities serve zero residents.

ia:SF 2296.title: A bill for an act relating to digital financial kiosks, modifying civil penalties, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2296.summary: Changes Iowa's digital-asset kiosk law: requires kiosk operators to hold a money transmission license, redefines digital financial asset, measures charges against prevailing market value, and treats violations as unlawful practices enforced under the attorney general's consumer fraud authority.

ia:SF 2299.title: Relating to the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program
ia:SF 2299.summary: Requires a student or their parent or guardian, if the school asks, to repay the school the amount it paid a community college for a concurrent enrollment course the student fails.

ia:SF 2304.title: A bill for an act relating to certain public utilities, including the development of ratemaking principles permitted for recovery costs of certain investments in infrastructure by water and wastewater utilities and cost considerations for acquisitions of water, sanitary sewer, or storm water utilities.
ia:SF 2304.summary: Lets investor-owned water and wastewater utilities recover costs of certain required infrastructure projects through a monthly customer charge after the Utilities Commission approves a multiyear plan, capping charge revenue at 10 percent of authorized revenue requirement.

ia:SF 2318.title: A bill for an act relating to nonresident deer hunting licenses.
ia:SF 2318.summary: Requires nonresident deer hunters who buy an antlered or any-sex license to also buy an antlerless-only license unless the state commission designates the hunting zone as exempt; current law requires the second license in every zone.

ia:SF 2320.title: A bill for an act modifying provisions related to the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program.
ia:SF 2320.summary: Requires students to take the in-person version of a community college course offered both in person and online through concurrent enrollment, unless the school superintendent or designee authorizes the online version.

ia:SF 2365.title: A bill for an act relating to public improvement contracts, including notice requirements.
ia:SF 2365.summary: Requires a public body to send the principal contractor, surety and claimants written notice of the date it finally accepted a public improvement within 14 days, and shields the body from liability for failing to send it.

ia:SF 2378.title: Relating to the ability of property owners to protest proposed changes in zoning districts
ia:SF 2378.summary: Repeals the right of property owners to file a written protest against a proposed zoning district change, which currently requires a three-fourths council vote to override when filed by owners of 20 percent of nearby land.

ia:SF 2379.title: A bill for an act relating to victim protections including victim counselors, protective orders, sex offender registration, rights of sexual abuse victims, mental competency and civil commitment, restitution, and victim rights, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2379.summary: Changes crime victim laws, including confidentiality of victim counselor communications, protective orders, sex offender registration, sexual abuse evidence, victim rights, restoration of mental competency, and restitution.

ia:SF 2399.title: A bill for an act relating to bail and bond amounts and conditions.
ia:SF 2399.summary: Bars magistrates from setting bail below the uniform bond schedule without written justification, limits release on own recognizance to nonviolent, nondrug simple or serious misdemeanors, and directs the Judicial Council to update the bond schedule by July 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2417.title: A bill for an act establishing requirements and guidelines for conversational AI services, and providing civil penalties, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2417.summary: Requires operators of public conversational AI services to disclose AI status to minors, avoid unpredictable engagement rewards for minors, limit sexual content, and adopt suicide and self-harm referral protocols; attorney general enforces, with $1,000-per-violation penalties up to $500,000 per operator, from July 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2422.title: Relating to the supplemental nutrition assistance program, the medical assistance program, the Iowa health and wellness plan, and other programs under the purview of the department of health and human services and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2422.summary: Adds the federal SAVE system to the sources used to verify public assistance eligibility, limits retroactive Medicaid eligibility to two months for pregnant women, children, and nursing facility residents, and requires legislative approval for Medicaid waivers that raise costs or expand coverage.

ia:SF 2426.title: A bill for an act relating to sufficient English language proficiency requirements for commercial drivers, providing penalties, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2426.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to test English proficiency of commercial driver's license and learner's permit applicants and renewals and deny those who fail, makes driving a commercial vehicle without proficiency a serious misdemeanor, and bars carriers from employing such drivers ($10,000 fine).

ia:SF 2428.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the duties of the department of education; the discipline of students enrolled in school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools who cause violent or nonviolent disruptions; the responsibilities and powers of the department of education, school district teachers, and other educational staff related to students who have individualized education programs or plans under section 504 of the federal Rehabilitation Act; school district professional development plans; and authorizing teachers to request a meeting of a student’s individualized education program team.
ia:SF 2428.summary: Authorizes teachers to remove students for nonviolent classroom disruptions and requires removal for violent ones, creates oversight committees on readmission, sets individualized education program team duties and training, and creates an attendance center pilot program.

ia:SF 2429.title: A bill for an act relating to fluid milk products annual permits, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2429.summary: Raises the maximum gross weight for annual permits for vehicles hauling fluid milk products to or from milk plants on primary roads from 96,000 to 136,000 pounds, effective January 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2430.title: A bill for an act relating to the display of flags at half-staff on public buildings.
ia:SF 2430.summary: Requires custodians of public buildings to follow governor's proclamations on flying the U.S. and Iowa flags at half-staff, and lets the attorney general take legal action over violations.

ia:SF 2453.title: Providing for investment by regents institutions in certified innovation funds and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2453.summary: Requires foundations affiliated with the University of Iowa, Iowa State, and Northern Iowa to invest at least 1 percent of endowment assets in state-certified innovation funds by July 1, 2027, with one-year waivers from the foundation board and annual reporting.

ia:SF 2465.title: A bill for an act relating to agriculture, including by providing for the powers and duties of the department of agriculture and land stewardship, including the promotion and regulation of commodities and products, the regulation of the transportation of agricultural items, the use of agricultural land, sales and use taxes, and veterinary practice and income taxes, making penalties applicable, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2465.summary: Makes many agriculture changes, including Choose Iowa program membership and school purchasing provisions, grain dealer and weights and measures rules, agricultural tourism and land use provisions, a honeybee sales tax exemption, and rural veterinarian loan repayment changes.

ia:SF 2467.title: A bill for an act concerning reimbursement of the attorney general for services relating to the second injury fund for workers’ compensation.
ia:SF 2467.summary: Raises the annual cap on reimbursement to the attorney general from the workers' compensation Second Injury Fund for legal services from $450,000 to $900,000.

ia:SF 2468.title: A bill for an act providing for the conversion of partnerships into other forms of domestic or foreign organizations, and providing for fees.
ia:SF 2468.summary: Lets Iowa general partnerships convert into other business forms, such as limited partnerships, LLCs, corporations, nonprofits or business trusts, or into out-of-state organizations, with partner approval, a filed plan and articles of conversion, and a $50 filing fee.

ia:SF 2471.title: A bill for an act relating to fees for lifetime fur harvester licenses.
ia:SF 2471.summary: Sets the fee for a lifetime fur harvester license for Iowa residents disabled in military service at $5 plus any processing fee, instead of a fee set by Department of Natural Resources rules.

ia:SF 2472.title: A bill for an act relating to state and local government taxes, fees, financial authority, and budgets, by modifying property assessment provisions, divisions of revenue, and funding from the secure an advanced vision for education fund, establishing a program for first-time homebuyers, modifying and making appropriations, and including effective date, applicability, and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2472.summary: Limits county and city general property tax levy rates for fiscal years 2027-28 through 2029-30 to yield about 102 percent of the prior year's dollars excluding new valuation, creates the FirstHome Iowa program, and changes urban renewal rules.

ia:SF 2474.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa dyslexia board and requiring the department of education to prepare a report related to cardiac emergency response plans and automated external defibrillators.
ia:SF 2474.summary: Requires the Department of Education to report to the legislature by January 15, 2027 how many schools have cardiac emergency response plans and where each school's defibrillators are located, and extends the Iowa dyslexia board's repeal date from 2027 to 2032.

ia:SF 2478.title: A bill for an act relating to transportation and other infrastructure-related appropriations to the department of transportation, including allocation and use of moneys from the road use tax fund and the primary road fund.
ia:SF 2478.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 from the road use tax fund and primary road fund to the Department of Transportation for operations, motor vehicle services, and facility maintenance.

ia:SF 2484.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations from the rebuild Iowa infrastructure fund, technology reinvestment fund, and renewable fuel infrastructure fund, providing for related matters including financial assistance eligibility for regional sports authority districts, department of health and human services information technology systems, the railway tracks overpass and underpass fund, and eligibility for entities to receive financial assistance from both the Iowa major events and tourism fund and the sports tourism infrastructure program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2484.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 from the Rebuild Iowa Infrastructure Fund and Technology Reinvestment Fund for state infrastructure and technology projects, changes some earlier appropriations, and raises the Capitol maintenance fund deposit from $500,000 to $750,000.

ia:SF 2488.title: Relating to early childhood and family services, including the creation of an early childhood and family services system, making appropriations, convening an early childhood Iowa interim study committee, and including applicability, retroactive applicability, and effective date provisions
ia:SF 2488.summary: Creates an early childhood and family services system under the Department of Health and Human Services with district advisory councils, repeals the child welfare decategorization initiative, lets area boards transfer home visiting to the system, and convenes an interim study committee.

ia:SF 2490.title: A bill for an act relating to oil and gas production, including filing requirements, the authority of the department of natural resources, confidential information, pooling orders, negotiation of surface damage, imposition and distribution of a tax, and jurisdiction, and providing civil penalties.
ia:SF 2490.summary: Changes oil and gas production law: yearly filings with the Department of Natural Resources, variances from its rules, five-year confidentiality, pooling orders, surface-owner permission and damage agreements, a severance tax on production, and a bar on most local limits on oil and gas operations.

ia:SF 2492.title: A bill for an act creating a state corporate income tax deduction for net controlled foreign corporation tested income, and including retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2492.summary: Removes the reference to global intangible low-taxed income from Iowa's corporate deduction for income under federal section 951A, so it covers net controlled foreign corporation tested income, which replaced it. Applies to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

ia:SF 2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the excise tax on certain ethanol blended gasoline purchased exclusively for use in an implement of husbandry used in agricultural production.
ia:SF 2493.summary: Exempts ethanol-blended gasoline with more than 85 percent ethanol from the motor fuel excise tax when bought at a terminal or refinery rack for farm implements, with buyers documenting purchases using a Department of Revenue exemption certificate.

ia:SF 2496.title: A bill for an act relating to Iowa’s urban renewal law by modifying the division of revenue for certain emergency medical services property tax levies, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2496.summary: Excludes property taxes for emergency medical services levies from the tax increment financing revenue division in urban renewal areas, for taxes due in fiscal years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

ia:SF 2497.title: A bill for an act providing for an assignment of assets for the benefit of creditors, exempting the related tax on the transfer of real estate, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2497.summary: Replaces Iowa's current assignment-for-creditors law with the Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act, setting rules for a debtor's transfer of all assets to an assignee who pays creditors, with creditor notice. Exempts the transfer from real estate transfer tax. Effective January 1, 2027.

ia:SF 273.title: A bill for an act relating to mandatory reporting to the board of educational examiners of licensed school employees who engage in grooming behavior toward students.
ia:SF 273.summary: As introduced, redefines "grooming behavior" that schools must report to the board of educational examiners as a pattern of behavior to entice or entrap a student in order to take advantage of the student, including through a sex act.

ia:SF 274.title: A bill for an act relating to forms of payment for entry into an extracurricular interscholastic athletic contest or competition.
ia:SF 274.summary: Requires public schools, and organizations registering with the Department of Education, to accept legal tender as payment for entry to interscholastic athletic events they sponsor, with some exceptions.

ia:SF 304.title: Providing an exception to a minor’s legal capacity to consent to the provision of medical care or services for a sexually transmitted disease or infection
ia:SF 304.summary: Removes a minor's legal capacity to consent to vaccinations for sexually transmitted diseases or infections, while leaving minors able to consent to other prevention, diagnosis and treatment of them.

ia:SF 378.title: Relating to the default speed limit for all vehicular traffic, and making penalties applicable
ia:SF 378.summary: Raises the default speed limit from 55 to 60 mph and extends to zones up to 60 mph the rule that a driver's first two speeding violations of 10 mph or less in 12 months are not counted against them.

ia:SF 469.title: Creating an emeritus license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery
ia:SF 469.summary: Creates an emeritus medical license for physicians 60 or older who mainly supervise and train resident physicians: valid three years, renewable once, exempt from continuing education, at half the usual fees, and not issued before January 1, 2026.

ia:SF 472.title: A bill for an act relating to retention and recertification elections for public employee collective bargaining units and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 472.summary: Exempts from the bill's retention and recertification elections any public employee bargaining unit in which at least 30 percent of members are public safety employees.

ia:SF 473.title: Relating to certain sincerely held religious or moral beliefs of child foster care providers and prospective adoptive parents
ia:SF 473.summary: Bars the state from requiring foster-parent or adoption applicants to accept sexual-orientation or gender-identity policies that conflict with their religious or moral beliefs, or rejecting them over those beliefs; religious agencies under state contract need not provide services contrary to their beliefs.

ia:SF 492.title: A bill for an act relating to the acquisition of certain vehicles by a vehicle recycler, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 492.summary: Bars licensed vehicle recyclers from buying a titleless vehicle at least 12 model years old for under $1,000 unless they check state records for lienholders, except when buying from a scrap metal dealer.

ia:SF 512.title: Relating to statutes of limitations in civil actions
ia:SF 512.summary: As introduced, provides that the time limits for filing civil lawsuits under Iowa Code section 614.1 may be changed only by an Act of the General Assembly.

ia:SF 542.title: A bill for an act relating to the suspension of child support and medical support in certain circumstances.
ia:SF 542.summary: Lets a court suspend a child or medical support order, without advance notice, on application of the paying person when juvenile court places the child with them; parties may object within 21 days, and the obligation generally ends 60 days after the juvenile case ends.

ia:SF 563.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of crematory operators and funeral establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 563.summary: Requires the Board of Mortuary Science to adopt rules licensing crematory operators, including a specialized cremation course, to license funeral directors who apply, and lets either operate a cremation establishment.

ia:SF 629.title: A bill for an act providing for an expedited filing service for filers of business documents administered by the secretary of state, and providing fees.
ia:SF 629.summary: Adds two faster expedited-filing options for business documents at the Secretary of State: a one-hour service for a $200 surcharge and same-day service for $125, alongside the existing two-day ($50) and five-day ($15) options.

ia:SF 639.title: A bill for an act creating a specialty business court, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 639.summary: Adds that an action may be transferred to the new specialty business court if all parties consent in writing to the assignment or transfer.

ia:SF 654.title: A bill for an act relating to wildlife, including the treatment of beaver dams, identification for traps, snares, and tree stands, maximum fur dealer license fees, and deer depredation, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 654.summary: Requires metal ID plates on deer tree stands on public land ($30 fine), lets owners' agents and drainage districts breach beaver dams, lets trap and snare tags show a department-issued ID number, and caps fur dealer license fees at $50 a year.

ia:SF 93.title: A bill for an act relating to qualifications to serve as a commissioner or an executive director for a county commission of veteran affairs. Effective date: 07/01/2026.
ia:SF 93.summary: Allows Iowa residents who are current or former Iowa National Guard or Iowa-based reserve members, with satisfactory service or an honorable discharge, not only veterans, to serve on county veterans affairs commissions; executive directors must still be veterans.

ia:SJR 11.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the State of Iowa relating to requirements for certain state tax law changes
ia:SJR 11.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment requiring a two-thirds vote of each legislative chamber to raise income tax rates or create a new state income-based tax; it goes to voters in November 2026.

id:H 491.title: EMERGENCY FIRST AID – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding immunity of persons giving first aid from damage claims.
id:H 491.summary: Extends civil damage immunity for good-faith, uncompensated help at an accident or emergency scene to mental health or suicidal crises, adding emergency psychological attention, including responding to suicidal thoughts. Gross negligence remains excluded.

id:H 508.title: TRANSPORTATION – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding bicycle and pedestrian projects.
id:H 508.summary: As introduced, revises a definition in Idaho transportation code, allows federal funds and grants to be used to improve bicycle and pedestrian facilities, and amends a provision on violations.

id:H 516.title: EDUCATION – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding the prohibition of taxpayer funding of teachers unions.
id:H 516.summary: Bars school districts from deducting teachers union dues, distributing union communications, or paying leave for union activities, with exceptions; paid representational time requires the union to reimburse the district. Sets civil penalties of up to $250, $1,500 or $2,500 by violation type.

id:H 522.title: UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding unmanned aircraft systems near Department of Correction facilities.
id:H 522.summary: As amended in the Senate, makes it a misdemeanor, with a fine up to $1,000 or six months in jail, to fly a drone within 400 feet above a state prison's perimeter, and lets officials take reasonable measures against drones used harmfully there.

id:H 542.title: SOCIAL MEDIA – Adds to existing law to establish the Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act.
id:H 542.summary: As amended in the Senate, requires social media platforms with $1 billion or more in advertising revenue to get verifiable parental consent for accounts of users 16 and under and bars addictive interface features and profile-based ads in those users' feeds.

id:H 561.title: STATE GOVERNMENT AND STATE AFFAIRS – Amends existing law to revise and remove provisions regarding flags flown by a governmental entity, to provide a penalty, and to establish provisions regarding enforcement by the Attorney General.
id:H 561.summary: As amended in the Senate, revises the list of flags governments may display and sets a $2,000-per-flag, per-day civil penalty for violations; the Attorney General sues after giving 10 days' written notice to cure.

id:H 570.title: RECKLESS DRIVING – Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding reckless driving.
id:H 570.summary: Adds driving more than 20 mph over the posted limit in an active school zone with children present and visible, or an active construction zone with workers present and visible, to the reckless driving offense, a misdemeanor.

id:H 575.title: STATE CONTROLLER – Amends existing law to provide that the State Controller shall publish a list of asset forfeitures and to provide that law enforcement shall report asset forfeiture information to the State Controller.
id:H 575.summary: Requires the state controller to store and publish a current list of asset forfeitures, and requires state, county and local law enforcement agencies to share forfeiture information with the controller.

id:H 585.title: ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, AND HVAC INSPECTIONS – Adds to existing law to provide for timely electrical, plumbing, and HVAC inspections and the option for third-party inspections in certain situations.
id:H 585.summary: Lets permit holders hire a third-party inspector, with a fee refund, when an electrical, plumbing or HVAC inspection is not done within 48 business hours, and requires a 10 percent refund when no reason for a failed inspection is given within three business days.

id:H 602.title: FOREIGN LAWS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions prohibiting the use of foreign laws in Idaho courts.
id:H 602.summary: As introduced, bars the use of foreign laws and foreign legal doctrines in Idaho courts.

id:H 629.title: TRANSPORTATION – Amends existing law to provide for a printed copy of a registration card for vehicles.
id:H 629.summary: As amended in the Senate, requires a person issued a vehicle registration card electronically to print it, and lets the printed copy satisfy the requirement to carry the card in the vehicle.

id:H 631.title: AGRICULTURAL CERTIFICATES OF FREE SALE – Amends existing law to integrate IDAPA 02.01.05 into Idaho Code.
id:H 631.summary: Writes Certificates of Free Sale into Idaho Code, letting exporters apply to the agriculture department for a fee it sets of up to $100, and voids administrative rule IDAPA 02.01.05 on July 1, 2026.

id:H 637.title: GOLD AND SILVER – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding gold and silver coin and specie.
id:H 637.summary: Expands Idaho's gold and silver coin and specie legal-tender provision, enacted in 2025, from coin minted domestically to foreign or domestic coin, and moves the section to a new code number.

id:H 648.title: INSURANCE – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding coverage of anticancer medications under health benefit plans.
id:H 648.summary: Requires health benefit plans issued or renewed from January 2027 that cover anticancer drugs to apply the same copayment, coinsurance and deductible to oral anticancer drugs as to injected or intravenous ones.

id:H 650.title: STATE GOVERNMENT AND STATE AFFAIRS – Adds to existing law to provide for state sovereignty, jurisdictional presumption, and a limitation on federal power.
id:H 650.summary: As introduced, declares a strong presumption that Idaho has jurisdiction over matters within the state unless the U.S. Constitution clearly and specifically grants authority to the federal government.

id:H 665.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amending existing law to revise provisions regarding Appaloosa license plates.
id:H 665.summary: Changes the recipient of Appaloosa license plate fees to the Appaloosa Museum and Heritage Center Foundation, broadens the fee purpose to horse education and programming, and raises the plate's vehicle weight limit from 16,000 to 26,000 pounds.

id:H 667.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amends existing law to eliminate the nondomiciled CDL program in Idaho.
id:H 667.summary: As introduced, bars Idaho from honoring learner's permits from other states or countries for commercial driver's licenses, which will be issued only to those who complete the entire process in Idaho.

id:H 674.title: TELECOMMUNICATION SERVICE – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding the discontinuation of telecommunication service.
id:H 674.summary: As introduced, lets a telephone company discontinue local service if the Federal Communications Commission permits it, and requires the Public Utilities Commission to adopt the FCC's discontinuance findings.

id:H 678.title: TRAPPING – Adds to existing law to provide for the checking of wolf traps.
id:H 678.summary: Requires anyone setting a trap or snare for gray wolves to inspect it every 72 hours and promptly remove any catch; inspection may be in person or by a remote camera with an unobstructed view.

id:H 681.title: CRIMINAL PROCEDURE – Amends existing law to provide that there shall be no statute of limitations for certain felonies.
id:H 681.summary: Removes the statute of limitations for prosecuting aggravated lewd conduct with a child and producing sexually exploitative material, adding them to crimes such as murder and certain rapes that can be prosecuted at any time.

id:H 683.title: SEX OFFENDERS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding where a sex offender resides.
id:H 683.summary: Redefines a registered sex offender's residence as where the offender habitually lives, including homeless locations and places visited over five hours more than five times in 30 days, and revises the facility exception to the 500-foot school and daycare residence ban.

id:H 684.title: COUNTY SHERIFFS – Adds to existing law to authorize a sheriff’s office to seek reimbursement for costs of recapture.
id:H 684.summary: Allows a county sheriff's office that travels out of state to retrieve an absconded prisoner, probationer or parolee to seek invoiced reimbursement; requires the Department of Correction to budget for it and ensure payment within 30 days.

id:H 689.title: ADMINISTRATIVE SUBPOENAS – Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding an administrative subpoena.
id:H 689.summary: Adds the crime of visual representations of the sexual abuse of children, which includes AI-generated images, to the offenses for which prosecutors or the attorney general may subpoena electronic service providers for subscriber identifying records.

id:H 690.title: ATTORNEY GENERAL – Amends and repeals existing law to remove provisions regarding sobriety and drug monitoring programs.
id:H 690.summary: Repeals the statutes creating sobriety and drug monitoring programs in the attorney general's office, and removes the reference to them in the attorney general's list of duties.

id:H 696.title: PRISONERS – Amends existing law to revise the definition of “sexual contact.”
id:H 696.summary: Broadens the definition of sexual contact in Idaho's law on sexual contact with prisoners and supervised offenders to include contact between the mouth and any body part, and any willful touching over or under clothing intended to arouse or gratify.

id:H 706.title: IDAHO BUILDING CODES – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding single stairway building exceptions.
id:H 706.summary: Lets local governments allow apartment buildings up to six stories to be served by a single interior exit stair if they meet fire-safety standards, such as sprinklers throughout, a two-hour fire-rated stairway and elevator shaft, and no more than four units per floor.

id:H 711.title: EDUCATION – Amends and adds to existing law to provide for alternative authorization for administrators and to authorize the use of funds for related mentoring.
id:H 711.summary: Creates a three-year interim certificate for school principals and superintendents without an administrator certificate, requiring a bachelor's degree, five years of relevant experience, coursework and mentoring by a certified administrator, and lets districts use mentoring funds for it.

id:H 721.title: IDAHO BUILDING CODE ACT – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding public school building plan reviews.
id:H 721.summary: Requires permitting authorities to complete initial plan review for public works within 30 calendar days and removes the requirement that school districts get plan approval before advertising for bids on school construction.

id:H 722.title: TAXATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding certain rate-regulated electric companies and gas companies.
id:H 722.summary: Changes filing, billing and payment dates for the kilowatt-hour and therm taxes on rate-regulated electric and gas companies created by 2025's HB 329, and establishes a rate-regulated tax fund for the proceeds.

id:H 728.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding educational staff, teachers, and certificates.
id:H 728.summary: Revises school staff definitions, adding classified staff and instructional support staff; extends the State Board of Education's lifetime-certificate rulemaking authority to pupil service and other certificated staff; corrects education code references.

id:H 730.title: SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program integrity measures and verification.
id:H 730.summary: Requires Health and Welfare to match SNAP households against lottery winnings of $3,000 or more and other databases, verify applicants' citizenship or immigration status, and disenroll those not lawfully present; bars income and asset limits above federal standards.

id:H 750.title: TRANSACTIONS – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding programmable money.
id:H 750.summary: As amended, excludes "programmable money" from the Uniform Commercial Code definition of money, bars issuers from denying transactions based on listed lawful characteristics, activities or social credit scores, and sets civil remedies and misdemeanor penalties.

id:H 752.title: INDECENCY AND OBSCENITY – Adds to existing law to prohibit a person from entering a restroom or changing room of the opposite sex, to provide a penalty, and to provide exceptions.
id:H 752.summary: As introduced, makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly enter a restroom, changing room, locker room or shower room in a government building or public accommodation designated for the opposite biological sex; a repeat conviction within five years is a felony, with exceptions.

id:H 758.title: DAYCARE LICENSING – Amends existing law to provide for supervision requirements while a child is sleeping and to establish an exception regarding children to be counted in attendance at a daycare.
id:H 758.summary: As amended in the Senate, lets daycare providers meet the supervision rule for sleeping children by using live video and audio while staying nearby, and stops counting a home provider's own children aged five or older toward child-to-staff ratios.

id:H 761.title: WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL – Amends and repeals existing law to provide for the consolidation of the Idaho STEM Action Center into the Workforce Development Council.
id:H 761.summary: Repeals the STEM Action Center statute, advisory board and STEM school designation, has the Workforce Development Council coordinate STEM education through June 30, 2036, and moves STEM education fund money to the council's training fund.

id:H 765.title: TAXING DISTRICTS – Amends existing law to allow fire protection districts to enter into certain agreements to transfer territory and to allow certain taxing districts to be exempt from certain budget limitations.
id:H 765.summary: Lets a fire protection district annex territory from another with both boards' consent, adjusts new construction roll values for fire and library district de-annexations, and exempts those districts' annexations from the 8% annual property tax budget increase limit.

id:H 766.title: DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEES – Amends existing law to revise a definition regarding which governmental entities are authorized to adopt development impact fees.
id:H 766.summary: As introduced, adds fire and ambulance service districts to the entities that may adopt development impact fee ordinances, alongside cities, counties and single county-wide highway districts.

id:H 772.title: INDUSTRIAL HEMP – Amends existing law to provide for negligent violations.
id:H 772.summary: Provides that industrial hemp producers do not commit a negligent violation if the hemp is grown only for grain or fiber, the producer made reasonable efforts to follow THC and state-plan rules, and total THC is 1 percent or less by dry weight.

id:H 773.title: DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE – Amends and repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions.
id:H 773.summary: Repeals 19 sections of Idaho law, 17 on the Idaho Corporate Credit Union and two on cemeteries, and removes a credit union liquidity-reserve provision that refers to it, under the Idaho Code Cleanup Act.

id:H 776.title: CHILD PROTECTION – Adds to existing law to provide for safety checks for children under one year of age.
id:H 776.summary: Requires Health and Welfare to verify within 12 hours a reported risk factor, such as prior termination of parental rights, for a caregiver of a child under age 1, then give verified cases a priority response and a written safety assessment.

id:H 788.title: MEDICAID – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding Medicaid prior authorization exemptions for certain preceptorships.
id:H 788.summary: As amended in the Senate, gives physicians, physician assistants and advanced practice nurses in family medicine, psychiatry or obstetrics who provide 360 preceptorship hours a year, 60 percent in rural or underserved areas, a 12-month Medicaid prior authorization exemption, capped at 100 per specialty yearly.

id:H 789.title: THE COEUR D’ALENE TRIBE WATER RIGHTS – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding the 2026 Coeur d’Alene Tribe water rights settlement agreement and to provide for the Coeur d’Alene tribal water supply bank.
id:H 789.summary: Ratifies the 2026 Coeur d'Alene Tribe water rights settlement agreement, directs state agencies to carry it out, and requires the Water Resource Board to appoint a local rental committee for a water supply bank renting the tribe's reserved water rights off-reservation.

id:H 792.title: TAXATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding certain sales tax exemptions for occasional sales and small sellers.
id:H 792.summary: Allows a homeowner with more than two home yard sales in a calendar year to qualify as a small seller, exempt from sales tax, if total sales are under $5,000.

id:H 797.title: FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICTS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the residence qualifications for fire protection district commissioners.
id:H 797.summary: Requires fire protection district commissioners to live in the subdistrict they represent for at least 90 consecutive days before appointment or election, in addition to living in the district for a year.

id:H 798.title: STATE TREASURER – Repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions relating to securities lending agreements.
id:H 798.summary: Repeals Section 67-1210B of Idaho Code on state securities lending agreements, which the bill's intent section calls obsolete, outdated or unnecessary; the statement of purpose says securities lending ended in December 2015.

id:H 799.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES – Repeals existing law to remove obsolete provisions regarding the prohibition and sale of liquors and wines.
id:H 799.summary: Repeals three alcohol statutes: a provision on convictions before the 1939 Liquor Act, a requirement that sellers furnish price lists, and a requirement to file attorney contact information with the State Liquor Division.

id:H 800.title: MANUFACTURED HOMES – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding siting of manufactured homes in residential areas.
id:H 800.summary: Lowers the minimum size cities and counties may require for manufactured homes outside mobile home parks from 1,000 to 400 square feet (single-section) or 800 (multisectional), and limits multi-unit manufactured homes to areas where multifamily housing is allowed.

id:H 803.title: EXECUTION – Amends existing law to provide that procedures used in an execution shall not be subject to certain provisions of law.
