in:SB 199.summary: Makes various education changes, including reports due December 1, 2026 on civic literacy and paid leave, added requirements for schools with low reading-test pass rates, and a review of accrediting agencies by the higher education commission.

in:SB 2.title: Bail procedures.
in:SB 2.summary: Makes non-murder offenses non-bailable when the state proves the evidence is strong and, by clear and convincing evidence, that the arrestee is dangerous and no release conditions would protect the public, and sets bail hearing procedures.

in:SB 200.title: Public school matters.
in:SB 200.summary: Voids certain indemnity, choice-of-law and automatic-renewal clauses in school vendor contracts made or renewed after June 30, 2026, lets youth organizations file grievances if schools deny them access to students, and requires schools that allow colleges to present to students to allow military personnel too.

in:SB 204.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 204.summary: Lets teachers licensed at charter schools seek an initial practitioner license, bars uniform academic-needs salary increases across a bargaining unit, repeals the student athlete cardiac arrest provisions, and bars requiring immunization for health-program clinical training when a parent or student objects on religious grounds.

in:SB 222.title: Family and social services administration matters.
in:SB 222.summary: Counts 9-8-8 crisis response centers and mobile crisis teams as first responders, requires certified peers to be trained by the state or an accredited body, and limits Medicaid presumptive eligibility determinations to qualified providers.

in:SB 225.title: Health matters.
in:SB 225.summary: Bars hospitals and debt collectors from collecting medical debt when the hospital is out of compliance with specified statutes, requires 60 days' notice to the health department before a hospital closes or ends a service line, and changes surgical center rules.

in:SB 226.title: Indiana department of administration.
in:SB 226.summary: Lets the Indiana department of administration use category management for state purchasing, requires an independent verification and validation program for state contracts, and requires agencies to submit annual procurement plans.

in:SB 227.title: Counter action against unmanned aircraft systems (UAS).
in:SB 227.summary: Makes the state police the statewide coordinator of counter-drone activities, taking effect only if federal law authorizes state or local police to detect or neutralize drones and the governor publishes notice; lets it designate local participating agencies and Indianapolis as a pilot site.

in:SB 228.title: Midwest continental divide commission.
in:SB 228.summary: Changes the Midwest continental divide commission's law so its land use and zoning plan is a plan rather than an overlay district, and addresses zoning changes or variances within half a mile of an approved trail project.

in:SB 23.title: Alcoholic beverage permits for county fairs.
in:SB 23.summary: Lets the alcohol and tobacco commission issue permits to sell alcohol on county fairgrounds run by a local board, and adds local-board events to activities allowed under existing winery, brewer, distiller and retailer permits.

in:SB 230.title: Department of agriculture.
in:SB 230.summary: Changes the role of supervisors on soil and conservation boards, drops the requirement that landfill inspectors send reports to the soil conservation division, withholds funding from districts missing the March 31 financial statement deadline, and repeals the Indiana land resource council.

in:SB 232.title: Real property appraisals.
in:SB 232.summary: Allows the city of Gary to hire an appraiser to appraise city-owned property it plans to sell, and bars city employees and officials from buying property the appraiser appraised.

in:SB 233.title: Powers and duties of the election commission.
in:SB 233.summary: Creates a separate Election Commission process to disband inactive state-level campaign committees, and requires rather than allows the commission to assess civil penalties of up to $1,000 or $500 for certain violations, plus a $500 penalty for electronic filing violations.

in:SB 239.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 239.summary: Allows converting existing public schools to charter schools under added conditions, lets innovation network charter schools contract with several school corporations, revises closed school building transfers, and requires notice to parents of students at risk of missing grade-level math proficiency.

in:SB 241.title: Utility service enhancement improvement costs.
in:SB 241.summary: Raises from 2,000 to 3,000 the customer count below which a water-service conservancy district may leave state utility commission jurisdiction, limits tap and capacity fees for nonprofit workforce housing, and lets water utilities adjust rates for chemical and power cost changes over 3%.

in:SB 243.title: Various tax matters.
in:SB 243.summary: Updates Indiana income tax law to match federal changes in the 2025 federal budget act, allows electronic delivery of tax department documents, extends the deadline for federal audit adjustments from 180 days to one year, and changes cigarette, petroleum severance and alcohol tax rules.

in:SB 246.title: Redaction of court records.
in:SB 246.summary: Requires redaction of names and other identifying information of child victims and child witnesses in criminal cases, using anonymous labels like "Child Witness No. 1" rather than initials or family relationships.

in:SB 249.title: State chemist.
in:SB 249.summary: Writes state animal food rules into law, covering commercial feed and pet food labels, ingredients, additives, manufacturing practices, inspection fees and feed licenses.

in:SB 25.title: School board candidates.
in:SB 25.summary: Sets the order in which school board candidates appear on the ballot within designated groups, listing candidates alphabetically by surname.

in:SB 254.title: Ivy Tech Community College.
in:SB 254.summary: Consolidates Ivy Tech's duties and board responsibilities, adds logistics, information technology and life sciences as trustee expertise, sets campus board roles, and requires the Indiana Economic Development Corporation to create an education-to-employment research program and data framework by December 1, 2026.

in:SB 259.title: Partnership composite returns.
in:SB 259.summary: Removes penalties for pass-through entities that leave nonresident partners, shareholders or beneficiaries with no positive distributive share income off a composite return.

in:SB 261.title: Criminal vandalism.
in:SB 261.summary: Renames criminal mischief as criminal vandalism, folds institutional, cemetery, railroad and critical infrastructure mischief into it with the same penalties and defenses, and moves cave damage and refuse provisions.

in:SB 262.title: INSPECT program.
in:SB 262.summary: Sets when pharmacies and other dispensers need not report to the INSPECT prescription monitoring program, requires opioid treatment programs to follow federal consent rules before reporting, and lets the pharmacy board share program data with health and social services officials.

in:SB 27.title: Stadium authority.
in:SB 27.summary: Creates the northwest Indiana stadium authority and board with power to finance and build a stadium using bonds, and changes Lake and Porter County food, beverage and innkeeper taxes and lets Hammond impose an admissions tax.

in:SB 270.title: Township mergers.
in:SB 270.summary: Requires the state to score township governments by performance by the end of 2026, and generally requires townships scoring four or more points to merge with another township or reorganize with a municipality, with mergers effective by January 1, 2029.

in:SB 271.title: Telecommunications wire and valuable metal dealers.
in:SB 271.summary: Adds telecommunications network wire to the definition of valuable metal for metal dealer laws, bars selling or buying it unless conditions are met, and lets people who suffer losses from violations sue for damages.

in:SB 275.title: FSSA fiscal matters.
in:SB 275.summary: Requires waiver service providers to give recipients documentation to review for errors, sets a time frame for the disability services bureau to decide requests for more service units, and creates some Medicaid reimbursement exemptions under value-based arrangements.

in:SB 277.title: Indiana department of environmental management.
in:SB 277.summary: Changes the structure and powers of the environmental management department and rules board, bars decisions based solely on unpromulgated federal risk values, and revises permitting, hearing, reporting, water pollution and waste statutes.

in:SB 285.title: Housing matters.
in:SB 285.summary: Bars camping or long-term sheltering on public land unless authorized, directs officers to assess whether emergency detention is warranted, defines gravely disabled for involuntary commitment, and sets criteria for homeless-services funding applicants.

in:SB 291.title: Court security.
in:SB 291.summary: Lets judges and household family members ask public agencies to stop publishing or remove their personal information, with a civil action against agencies that fail to; lets the supreme court and court of appeals each appoint a court marshal with limited police powers.

in:SB 293.title: Pharmacist licensure.
in:SB 293.summary: Requires passing the North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination to be licensed as a pharmacist, removes an exam requirement for certain pharmacists seeking license reciprocity, and voids conflicting rules.

in:SB 3.title: Constitutional amendment ballot language.
in:SB 3.summary: Sets the ballot language for the proposed constitutional amendment concerning bail.

in:SB 4.title: Various fiscal matters.
in:SB 4.summary: Requires a fiscal impact analysis of all gubernatorial executive orders within seven days, lowers the proposed-rule cost threshold for budget committee review to $500,000, and changes community mental health center funding and reporting rules.

in:SB 56.title: Veterinary licensing.
in:SB 56.summary: Lets the board of veterinary medicine license veterinarians and registered veterinary technicians without an examination if they meet health care professional reciprocity requirements.

in:SB 6.title: Extension of water or wastewater mains.
in:SB 6.summary: Requires municipal utilities to mail written notice to affected landowners and the county plan commission, and post information online, before condemning land for water or wastewater main extensions outside city limits or the utility's service territory.

in:SB 71.title: Various probate matters.
in:SB 71.summary: Creates a guardianship code revision task force and changes rules on paying property or debts owed to minors, up to $25,000 without a court order, court approval of minors' claim settlements, and transfers under the Uniform Transfers to Minors Act.

in:SB 76.title: Immigration matters.
in:SB 76.summary: Lets the attorney general defend officers, governments or colleges sued over certain immigration matters; requires governments holding a person under an immigration detainer request to comply and notify the judge; and bars employers from knowingly hiring unauthorized aliens, enforced by the attorney general.

in:SB 80.title: Code publication.
in:SB 80.summary: Resolves amend-repeal conflicts from the 2025 session, relocates definitions chapters in alphabetical order, and updates cross-references, with no substantive change to law.

in:SB 88.title: Education matters.
in:SB 88.summary: Changes good citizenship instruction requirements, requires state colleges to accept the Classic Learning Test like the ACT or SAT for admission, and has the education department list schools offering exams to students enrolled elsewhere.

in:SB 89.title: Three-way permits.
in:SB 89.summary: Lets the alcohol and tobacco commission issue new three-way alcohol permits: three each to Schererville and Lafayette, two each to West Lafayette, Delphi and Bloomington, and eight to restaurants in a Michigan City transit district.

in:SB 9.title: Victim impact statements.
in:SB 9.summary: Requires a defendant to be present in the courtroom when a victim speaks about the crime and sentence, unless safety risk or disruption, and lets a court hold a later hearing for the victim if the defendant skipped sentencing.

in:SB 91.title: Syringe exchange program.
in:SB 91.summary: Bars syringe exchange programs from operating fixed sites within 1,000 feet of specified facilities, bars providing chemical reagents or precursors, sets participation requirements, and lets the health department deny, suspend or revoke registrations for violations.

in:SB 92.title: Community corrections trust funds.
in:SB 92.summary: Lets counties running community corrections programs set up a county community corrections trust fund, with set funding sources, permitted uses, and reporting and audit requirements.

in:SJR 1.title: Constitutional amendment concerning bail.
in:SJR 1.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment making offenses other than murder or treason not bailable if the proof is evident or the presumption strong and the state shows by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect others or the community.

ks:HB 2004.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2004 by Committee on Government Efficiency - .Requiring the secretary for children and families and the office of inspector general to exchange information and documents related to cash assistance, childcare assistance and food assistance fraud investigations and requiring the secretary for children and families and the secretary of health and environment to execute a memorandum of understanding or other written data-sharing instrument upon written request of the United States department of agriculture or the United States department of health and human services and comply with data requests from such federal agencies.
ks:HB 2004.summary: Requires the children and families agency and the inspector general to share records on cash, child care and food assistance recipients within 30 days of a request. Requires state agencies to give federal agriculture and health departments requested program data within 60 days.

ks:HB 2018.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2018 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Creating the crime of interference with the conduct of a religious assembly, providing criminal penalties therefor and providing for a civil cause of action for damages.
ks:HB 2018.summary: Creates crimes of interfering, by force, threat or physical obstruction, with people exercising religious freedom at a place of worship, an aggravated version with a weapon, and reckless damage to worship property. Allows civil damages suits and Attorney General enforcement.

ks:HB 2022.title: Requiring special elections be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March or on the same day as a primary or general election.
ks:HB 2022.summary: Requires special elections to be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March or on the same day as a general or primary election, and makes conforming changes to other election laws.

ks:HB 2028.title: Reviving a law providing for discounted hunting and fishing licenses for persons who are 65 years of age or older; changing the amount charged for lifetime hunting and fishing licenses for children five and younger to $300 and for those children ages six to 15 to $400, prohibiting non-residents from hunting migratory waterfowl on public lands during the hunting season except on Sundays, Mondays, and Tuesdays; raising certain hunting fees; and requiring the department of wildlife and parks to report to the house and senate committees on agriculture and natural resources on the impact of limiting out of state waterfowl hunters.
ks:HB 2028.summary: Revives the discounted lifetime hunting and fishing pass for Kansans 65 and older, sets lifetime kids' licenses at $300 (age 5 and under) and $400 (6 to 15), and limits nonresident waterfowl hunting on state and listed federal lands to Sunday through Tuesday.

ks:HB 2029.title: Reconciling multiple amendments to certain statutes.
ks:HB 2029.summary: As amended, designates part of K-5 in Wyandotte County, from North 18th to North 38th Street, as the Rep Marvin S Robinson Memorial Highway and removes the shared I-635 portion from the Harry Darby Memorial Highway designation.

ks:HB 2030.title: Excluding dealers and manufacturers of trailers from certain provisions of the vehicle dealers and manufacturers licensing act.
ks:HB 2030.summary: Exempts dealers and manufacturers of most trailers, other than semitrailers and travel trailers, from vehicle dealer licensing act provisions on franchise termination, warranty defects, dealership ownership changes and location, and dealer-manufacturer disputes.

ks:HB 2031.title: Providing that driving school instructors and motorcycle instructors may possess a driver's license or motorcycle driver's license from any state.
ks:HB 2031.summary: Lets driving school and motorcycle instructors hold a valid driver's license from any state rather than only Kansas, and requires motorcycle instructors to hold a class M or equivalent out-of-state motorcycle license.

ks:HB 2033.title: Including programs and services provided by nonprofit organizations accredited by the international multisensory structured language education council as approved at-risk educational programs.
ks:HB 2033.summary: Adds nonprofits accredited by the International Multisensory Structured Language Education Council to the approved at-risk education programs that can receive money from school districts' at-risk education funds.

ks:HB 2036.title: Providing a Kansas income tax subtraction modification for certain amounts received as compensation for members of the armed forces.
ks:HB 2036.summary: Creates a Kansas income tax subtraction, starting in tax year 2027, for active-duty armed forces compensation up to the pay of a senior enlisted member as set by the Defense Department.

ks:HB 2037.title: Increasing the membership of the council on travel and tourism, updating the house legislative committee assignment required for council members appointed from the house, and removing provisions requiring allocation of funds from the matching grant program for the promotion of tourism for private, public and nonprofit entities and limiting the percentage of such funds granted to a single entity.
ks:HB 2037.summary: Expands the Council on Travel and Tourism from 17 to 20 members with three new governor appointees, and removes the 75 percent public or nonprofit allocation and 20 percent entity limit for tourism matching grants.

ks:HB 2040.title: Extending the time in which the state corporation commission shall make a final order on a transmission line siting application.
ks:HB 2040.summary: Extends the deadline for the Kansas Corporation Commission to issue a final order on an electric transmission line siting application from 120 to 180 days.

ks:HB 2042.title: Authorizing the adoption of certain rules and regulations related to hazardous waste monitoring and permit application fees by the Kansas department of health and environment.
ks:HB 2042.summary: Authorizes the state health department to adopt proposed permanent rules KAR 28-31-10 and 28-31-10b, covering hazardous waste monitoring and permit application fees.

ks:HB 2043.title: Providing a protest petition to contest certain increases in property tax revenues and continuing reimbursements from the taxpayer notification costs fund for an additional five years.
ks:HB 2043.summary: Lets voters contest non-school local budgets raising property taxes above the prior year plus inflation (up to 3 percent) by protest petition signed by 10 percent of the district's Secretary of State vote total; extends state reimbursement of rate notice costs.

ks:HB 2044.title: Providing a income tax subtraction modification for amounts received as compensation for serving in the armed forces and providing that a person shall not lose eligibility for a homestead property tax refund claim or the selective assistance for effective senior relief (SAFESR) income tax credit if the appraised valuation of the homestead subsequently exceeds $350,000 after qualifying in a previous tax year.
ks:HB 2044.summary: Creates a Kansas income tax subtraction for active-duty military pay up to a senior enlisted member's level from tax year 2027, and keeps Homestead and SAFESR eligibility for prior refund recipients whose home value later exceeds $350,000.

ks:HB 2045.title: Reducing certain license fees and training requirements for child care staff, creating a process for day care facility licensees to apply for temporary waiver of certain statutory requirements, authorizing the secretary of health and environment to develop and operate pilot programs to increase child care availability or capacity, transferring certain child care programs to the Kansas office of early childhood and creating day care licensing duties of the director of early childhood.
ks:HB 2045.summary: Creates the Kansas Office of Early Childhood under a governor-appointed director, moves child care licensing statutes from the health department to it, and changes definitions, staffing and training requirements for child care centers and homes.

ks:HB 2046.title: Authorizing insurers to file certain travel insurance policies under the accident and health line of insurance.
ks:HB 2046.summary: Allows travel insurance covering sickness, accident, disability or death while traveling, alone or with emergency evacuation or repatriation coverage, to be filed as either accident and health or inland marine insurance.

ks:HB 2047.title: Providing for the establishment of an online insurance verification system for the verification of evidence of motor vehicle liability insurance.
ks:HB 2047.summary: Creates the Real Time Motor Vehicle Insurance Verification Act, requiring the Insurance Commissioner to set up a web-based system for verifying motor vehicle liability insurance, with insurers required to cooperate; it is the only system allowed for that purpose.

ks:HB 2048.title: Eliminating the requirement that the commissioner submit certain reports to the governor and removing certain specific entities from the definition of person for the purpose of enforcing insurance law.
ks:HB 2048.summary: Removes the requirement that the insurance commissioner send an annual report to the governor and narrows the definition of person used in enforcing insurance law by dropping references to specific entities.

ks:HB 2049.title: Updating public adjuster and insurance agent statutes pertaining to suspension, revocation, denial of licensure and licensure renewal.
ks:HB 2049.summary: Allows the Insurance Commissioner to check the status of other licenses when reviewing insurance agent and public adjuster applications, and to suspend, revoke or refuse a public adjuster's license for failing to answer a Commissioner inquiry.

ks:HB 2050.title: Authorizing the commissioner of insurance to set the amount of certain fees and cause the publication of such fees in the Kansas register, authorizing the commissioner to reduce the number of board members on certain insurance-related boards, renaming the Kansas insurance department as the Kansas department of insurance, renaming the office of the securities commissioner as the department of insurance, securities division, renaming the securities commissioner as the department of insurance, assistant commissioner, securities division and eliminating the requirement of senate confirmation for appointees to such position, requiring the commissioner of insurance to maintain a list of eligible nonadmitted insurers and authorizing such nonadmitted insurers to transact business in Kansas with vehicle dealers and to provide excess coverage insurance on Kansas risks.
ks:HB 2050.summary: Lets the Insurance Commissioner set insurance fees and fines, capped at current statutory amounts, publish them each December 1, and shrink certain appointed boards; renames the Insurance Department and puts the securities office under it as a division.

ks:HB 2052.title: Updating cross references in the personal and family protection act regarding the eligibility requirements to obtain a license to carry a concealed handgun, requiring the surrender of a suspended or revoked license, providing for a transition from a provisional license to a standard license and prohibiting the collection of personal information of an off-duty law enforcement officer entering buildings while armed or requiring such officer to wear any item identifying such person as a law enforcement officer or being armed.
ks:HB 2052.summary: Lets provisional concealed carry license holders request a standard license at 21, requires surrender of suspended or revoked licenses, and bars collecting personal information from armed off-duty law enforcement officers entering buildings or requiring them to wear identification.

ks:HB 2054.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2054 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Increasing the limits on certain campaign contributions under the campaign finance act.
ks:HB 2054.summary: Raises campaign contribution limits (statewide offices $2,000 to $4,000, House $500 to $1,000, Senate $1,000 to $2,000 per election) and removes limits on party committee contributions to candidates in general elections.

ks:HB 2060.title: Senate Substitute for Substitute for HB 2060 by Committee on Local Government, Transparency and Ethics - Providing for the treatment of the reimbursement for expenses incurred for travel and activities in attending conferences or events by certain specified nonprofit organizations and discounted or free access to entertainment, sporting events or other activities.
ks:HB 2060.summary: Lets legislators accept travel reimbursement from any nonprofit, nonpartisan organization that does not lobby in Kansas, and changes rules on executive branch employees receiving tickets or access to entertainment and sporting events.

ks:HB 2061.title: Including aboveground and belowground lines, cables and wires in the definition of a critical infrastructure facility used for telecommunications or video services for the crimes of trespassing on a critical infrastructure facility and criminal damage to a critical infrastructure facility.
ks:HB 2061.summary: Expands the definition of critical infrastructure facility for trespass and criminal damage crimes to include any aboveground or belowground telecommunications, broadband or video line, cable or wire, plus towers, antennas and related buildings.

ks:HB 2065.title: Providing for the appointment of delegates to a convention under article V of the constitution of the United States and prescribing the duties and responsibilities of such delegates.
ks:HB 2065.summary: Sets a process to appoint Kansas delegates and alternates to any Article V constitutional convention, specifies their duties and instructions, and creates a recall procedure and a way to investigate and prosecute delegate oath violations.

ks:HB 2068.title: Establishing the remote practice of pharmacy, requiring certain conditions for such practice and limiting activities performed under such practice, permitting a pharmacist to initiate therapy for certain conditions consistent with the pharmacist's education, training and experience, adding pharmacists who initiate such therapy to the healthcare stabilization fund and allowing a pharmacist to dispense a one-time emergency refill of a noncontrolled prescription drug for up to a 90-day supply when no refills remain, adopting compounding standards established by the United States pharmacopeia and allowing for exemptions from such standards and removing the authority of the state board of pharmacy to authorize individuals to access the prescription monitoring program database by rules and regulations.
ks:HB 2068.summary: Lets pharmacists start therapy for certain conditions, such as minor self-limiting ones, and give one-time 90-day emergency refills; adopts U.S. Pharmacopeia compounding standards, removes the pharmacy board's rule-based authority over prescription-monitoring access, and sets conditions for remote pharmacy practice.

ks:HB 2069.title: Enacting the school psychologist compact, the dietitian compact, the cosmetology compact and the physicians assistant compact to provide interstate practice privileges.
ks:HB 2069.summary: Enacts four interstate licensure compacts: for school psychologists, dietitians, cosmetologists and physician assistants.

ks:HB 2070.title: Enacting the dietitian licensure compact to provide interstate practice privileges for dietitians.
ks:HB 2070.summary: Enacts the Dietitian Compact, which creates interstate practice privileges for dietitians; it becomes active once seven states enact it.

ks:HB 2083.title: Providing a property tax exemption for new energy storage systems and excluding new energy storage systems from the commercial and industrial machinery and equipment exemption.
ks:HB 2083.summary: Exempts energy storage systems that begin construction on or after January 1, 2025 from property tax for 10 tax years, and excludes them from the commercial and industrial machinery and equipment exemption.

ks:HB 2085.title: Extending the expiration of permits issued under the water pollution control permit system from five to 10 years.
ks:HB 2085.summary: Allows the Secretary of Health and Environment to issue water pollution control permits for ten years instead of the current five.

ks:HB 2086.title: Adjusting the KPERS 3 dividend interest credit by lowering the dividend interest credit threshold to 5% and increasing the dividend share to 80%.
ks:HB 2086.summary: Raises the Tier 3 KPERS discretionary dividend credit from 75 to 80 percent of the five-year average net compound return, and lowers the return threshold needed to qualify from 6 to 5 percent.

ks:HB 2087.title: Authorizing certain nonadmitted insurers to transact certain business in Kansas and requiring the commissioner of insurance to maintain a list of eligible nonadmitted insurers.
ks:HB 2087.summary: As amended, replaces "insurer not authorized to do business" with "eligible nonadmitted insurer," has the insurance commissioner keep a list of them, and lets other nonadmitted insurers meeting federal surplus lines standards do business in Kansas.

ks:HB 2088.title: Requiring local governments to meet specified deadlines for issuing building permits and requiring the department of health and environment to issue a response to an applicant's submitted notice of intent to discharge stormwater runoff from construction activities within 45 days of submission.
ks:HB 2088.summary: Requires local governments to approve or deny single-family building permits within 60 days of a complete application or the permit is deemed approved, and requires the health department to act on construction stormwater notices within 45 days.

ks:HB 2092.title: Setting the time for professional employer organization registration expiration, renewal and the filing of audits with the secretary of state, limiting the method of providing surety for professional employer organizations with insufficient working capital to bonds and eliminating a market value measure of the sufficiency of such bonds.
ks:HB 2092.summary: Sets professional employer organization registrations to expire October 15 after issuance, requires an annual audit with renewal, and limits security for organizations with insufficient working capital to a bond of at least the required amount plus $100,000.

ks:HB 2096.title: Providing for transferability of Kansas housing investor tax credits from the year that the credit was originally issued.
ks:HB 2096.summary: Lets buyers of Kansas housing investor tax credits begin claiming them in the year of the qualifying investment rather than the year of transfer, retroactive to tax year 2022.

ks:HB 2099.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2099 by Committee on Local Government, Transparency and Ethics - Authorizing the secretary of corrections on behalf of the state of Kansas to convey certain real property located in Leavenworth county, Kansas, to Leavenworth county.
ks:HB 2099.summary: Authorizes the corrections secretary to convey a 57-acre parcel to Leavenworth County by quitclaim deed, with the county paying all costs and the Attorney General approving the deed. The conveyance is exempt from appraisal requirements.

ks:HB 2101.title: Prohibiting municipalities from adopting and implementing a guaranteed income program.
ks:HB 2101.summary: Bars cities and counties from adopting or enforcing guaranteed income programs, meaning regular cash payments funded by tax revenue, unless the Legislature approves them. Voids such ordinances or resolutions adopted before July 1, 2025.

ks:HB 2102.title: Substitute for HB 2102 by Committee on Education - Providing for the advance enrollment of a military student whose parent or person acting as parent will be stationed in this state and correcting federal statutory citations in the interstate compact on educational opportunity for military children.
ks:HB 2102.summary: Requires school districts to allow advance enrollment of military students whose parent will be stationed at a Kansas installation this or next school year, with no proof of address required, and extends this to existing pre-K programs.

ks:HB 2106.title: Banning contributions from foreign nationals for the support or defeat of a proposed amendment to the Kansas constitution.
ks:HB 2106.summary: As amended by the House committee, bans accepting contributions or expenditures from foreign nationals for activity promoting or opposing a Kansas constitutional amendment, adds certification requirements for reports, and lets the Attorney General prosecute violations.

ks:HB 2107.title: Providing for claims to recover economic damages from fire events caused by electric public utilities, establishing a statute of limitations for such claims and requiring the state corporation commission to convene a workshop on utility wildfire risk and mitigation.
ks:HB 2107.summary: Sets a two-year statute of limitations for wildfire claims against electric utilities, allows economic and non-economic damages, caps punitive damages at $5 million, and requires the Corporation Commission to hold a wildfire risk workshop.

ks:HB 2110.title: Eliminating the requirement that the state 911 board shall contract with a local collection point administrator for services, rescheduling the date on which the state 911 operations fund, state 911 grant fund and state 911 fund shall be established, requiring certain transfers to be made to the state 911 operations fund and rescheduling the date for transferring all 911 fee moneys currently held outside the state treasury to the state treasury.
ks:HB 2110.summary: Removes the requirement that the State 911 Board contract with a local collection point administrator, reschedules when the 911 funds are established, requires transfers to the State 911 Operations Fund, and removes the 911 fee transfer cap on the Grant Fund.

ks:HB 2111.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2111 by Committee on Agriculture and Natural Resources - Exempting certain registered agritourism operations from local code and regulation enforcement.
ks:HB 2111.summary: Bars cities and counties from enforcing building codes, ordinances, or permit and license requirements against non-public registered agritourism locations: working farms of 160 acres or less with an agricultural education facility, open to the public by invitation only.

ks:HB 2113.title: Establishing the state conservation fund and transferring $2,500,000 to such fund and providing for the enhanced transfer of moneys from the state general fund to the state water plan fund and from the state water plan fund to the water technical assistance fund and the water project grant fund.
ks:HB 2113.summary: Creates a State Conservation Fund with a $2.5 million General Fund transfer each July 1, raises the transfer to the State Water Plan Fund from $35 million to $55 million, and sets transfers from it to the water technical assistance and water projects grant funds.

ks:HB 2114.title: Substitute for HB 2114 by Committee on Agriculture and Natural Resources - Clarifying which structures shall be considered water obstructions and not a dam, increasing application fees for a permit to construct, modify or add to a dam, requiring post-construction permit fees and requiring any licensed professional engineer who conducts inspections required by the act to be approved by the chief engineer or a certified intern engineer who is under the supervision of a licensed professional engineer.
ks:HB 2114.summary: Changes dam law: treats some structures as water obstructions rather than dams, raises dam permit application fees from $200 to $250-$1,000 by hazard class, adds post-construction permit fees, and requires inundation maps.

ks:HB 2116.title: Requiring that certain contractual provisions be incorporated in all contracts for certain cities and counties, including the provisions of form DA-146a, with certain exceptions.
ks:HB 2116.summary: Requires second- and third-class cities and counties under 35,000 people to include the state's standard contract provisions (Form DA-146a) in contracts after July 1, 2026, unless the governing body votes to omit some; indemnity and governing-law terms cannot be omitted.

ks:HB 2117.title: Modifying certain business filing and fee requirements for business trusts, foreign corporations and limited partnerships; authorizing professional corporations or limited liability companies formed or organized to render a professional service to participate in transactions under the business entity transactions act; and making certain information provided by registered agents a public record.
ks:HB 2117.summary: Changes business filing rules: lets business trusts withdraw by filing a dissolution certificate with a fee up to $150, allows certain professional service entities to use the Business Entity Transactions Act, and makes former registered agent information public record.

ks:HB 2118.title: Requiring any person who solicits a fee for filing or retrieving certain documents from the federal government, the state, a state agency or a local government to give certain notices to consumers and providing that violation of such requirements is a deceptive act or practice subject to penalties under the Kansas consumer protection act.
ks:HB 2118.summary: Requires solicitations offering to file or retrieve government documents for a fee to state that the offer is not from a government agency and no payment is required. Violations are penalized under the Kansas Consumer Protection Act.

ks:HB 2119.title: Discontinuing the Kansas affordable housing tax credit for qualified developments receiving a 4% federal tax credit.
ks:HB 2119.summary: As amended by the House committee, ends the Kansas Affordable Housing Tax Credit Act after the 2025 allocation plan, and bars accepting applications for 4 percent credits after Aug. 15, 2025 and 9 percent credits after May 23, 2025, with approval deadlines of Nov. 14 and Aug. 8.

ks:HB 2120.title: Authorizing the state board of regents to sell and convey certain real property in Riley county, Kansas, and Douglas county, Nebraska, on behalf of Kansas state university and Kansas state university veterinary medical center.
ks:HB 2120.summary: Authorizes the State Board of Regents to sell certain real property parcels in Manhattan, Kansas, and Omaha, Nebraska, on behalf of Kansas State University and its Veterinary Medical Center, after the Attorney General approves the deeds.

ks:HB 2121.title: Increasing the annual license fees of electric and hybrid passenger vehicles and trucks and electric motorcycles and distributing the fees to the state highway fund and the special city and county highway fund.
ks:HB 2121.summary: As amended by the House committee, raises annual registration fees from $50 to $85 for hybrids, $50 to $100 for plug-in hybrids and $100 to $165 for electric vehicles, adds fees for electric motorcycles and trucks up to 12,000 pounds, and directs the money to highway funds, effective January 1, 2026.

ks:HB 2122.title: Increasing the annual license fees of electric and hybrid passenger vehicles, trucks and electric motorcycles and distributing the fees to the state highway fund and the special city and county highway fund, modifying the threshold limit for allowing quarterly payments of certain truck and truck tractor annual vehicle registration fees and eliminating the two-quarter grace period for truck or truck tractor owners that have delinquent quarterly payments before certain penalties apply.
ks:HB 2122.summary: Raises annual registration fees for electric and hybrid vehicles (all-electric cars from $100 to $165), adds fees for electric motorcycles and light electric trucks, sends the money to highway funds, and raises the truck installment-payment threshold to $300.

ks:HB 2124.title: Providing cities the authority to allow the driving of golf carts upon sidewalks and permitting local authorities with jurisdiction over city residence districts to reduce the maximum speed limit from 30 miles per hour to 25 miles per hour without an engineering and traffic investigation.
ks:HB 2124.summary: Lets local authorities lower residence district speed limits from 30 to 25 mph without an engineering and traffic investigation, and lets cities allow golf carts on sidewalks beside streets where golf carts are banned.

ks:HB 2125.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2125 by Committee on Assessment and Taxation - Modifying the deadline for mailing property tax statements to taxpayers and the deadline for governing bodies to certify the amount of property tax to be levied to the county clerk, providing for the county clerk's use of the previous year's budget when a taxing subdivision fails to timely file its budget, modifying the content requirements of the revenue neutral rate hearing notice for property tax purposes, extending reimbursement from the taxpayer notification costs fund for printing and postage costs for county clerks for calendar years 2025 and 2026, prohibiting a filing fee when a previous appeal remains pending before the board of tax appeals and authorizing the continuation of the 20-mill statewide property tax levy for schools.
ks:HB 2125.summary: As passed by the House, authorizes Pawnee County commissioners to put to voters a countywide sales tax of up to 1 percent to finance health care services listed in the ballot question and county public safety operations.

ks:HB 2128.title: Authorizing the commissioner of insurance to select and announce the version of certain instructions, calculations and documents in effect for the upcoming calendar year and cause such announcement to be published in the Kansas register, allowing certain life insurers to follow health financial reports and adopting certain provisions from the national association of insurance commissioners holding company system regulatory act relating to group capital calculations and liquidity stress testing.
ks:HB 2128.summary: Requires the Insurance Commissioner to announce by December 1 each year which NAIC capital instructions apply, and requires ultimate controlling persons of registered insurers to file group capital calculations (with exemptions) and, if in scope, liquidity stress test results.

ks:HB 2131.title: Requiring prosecutors to disclose their intent to introduce testimony from a jailhouse witness and to forward related information to the Kansas bureau of investigation.
ks:HB 2131.summary: Requires prosecutors to disclose intent to use jailhouse witness testimony, along with the witness's criminal history, cooperation agreements and benefits, the statements at issue, and any recantations.

ks:HB 2132.title: Substitute for Substitute for HB 2132 by Committee on Child Welfare and Foster Care - Determining when a law enforcement officer may or shall take a child into custody.
ks:HB 2132.summary: Makes it discretionary rather than mandatory for a law enforcement officer to take a child under 18 into custody when the officer believes the child will be harmed if not removed or is in a behavioral health crisis likely to cause harm.

ks:HB 2145.title: Substitute for HB 2145 by Committee on Local Government - Establishing the Butler county fair board to consist of 15 members, providing for the appointment of members to such board and allowing up to five members of such board to be appointed from the county at large.
ks:HB 2145.summary: Sets the Butler County Fair Board at 15 members appointed by county commissioners, at most five at large and otherwise one per commission district where possible, and moves Cloud County fair board membership rules into the fair association statute.

ks:HB 2152.title: Substitute for HB 2152 by Committee on Financial Institutions and Pensions - Mandating financial institutions to secure governmental unit deposits in excess of the amount insured or guaranteed by the FDIC by utilizing a public moneys pooled method of securities, prohibiting investment advisers that execute bids for the investment of public moneys from managing moneys directly from such bid, allowing governmental unit deposits to be invested at a rate agreed upon by the governmental unit and the financial institution, requiring certification from a governmental unit that deposits in the municipal investment pool fund were first offered to a financial institution in the preceding year and allowing financial institutions to file complaints upon the failure to comply.
ks:HB 2152.summary: Requires financial institutions to secure government deposits above FDIC insurance through a public moneys pooled method, bars investment advisers from directly managing bid-based public money investments, and sets default procedures and a complaint process.

ks:HB 2155.title: Specifying that sheriffs have liability for official acts related to charge and custody of jails.
ks:HB 2155.summary: Specifies that sheriffs and their sureties are liable for official acts related to the charge and custody of county jails.

ks:HB 2158.title: Permitting beekeepers who meet certain requirements to sell packaged honey and honeycombs without holding a food establishment or food processing plant license under the Kansas food, drug and cosmetic act.
ks:HB 2158.summary: Exempts beekeepers who meet listed requirements from needing a state food establishment or food processor license to sell packaged honey or honeycomb at retail.

ks:HB 2160.title: Enacting the municipal employee whistleblower act to provide statutory protections for municipal employees who report or disclose unlawful or dangerous conduct.
ks:HB 2160.summary: Creates the Kansas Municipal Employee Whistleblower Act, barring supervisors in counties, cities and school districts from disciplining employees for discussing public concerns with governing body members or auditors, reporting violations of law, or disclosing misappropriated municipal money.

ks:HB 2166.title: Continuing in existence certain exceptions to the disclosure of public records under the open records act.
ks:HB 2166.summary: Continues two exceptions to the Kansas Open Records Act: COVID-19 records held by local health officers and records of Board of Healing Arts investigations into acupuncturist impairment.

ks:HB 2168.title: Extending the amount of time required for reports to be filed with the state historical society for certain United States public land surveys from 30 to 90 days.
ks:HB 2168.summary: Extends from 30 to 90 days the time for land surveyors to file public land survey reference and restoration reports with the State Historical Society, and lets a county commission designate a filing office where no county surveyor exists.

ks:HB 2169.title: Providing for an exemption from remediation costs or other liability from prior commercial pesticide application by the United States army for owners of certain nonresidential property located in Johnson county.
ks:HB 2169.summary: Bars state agencies and subdivisions from ordering cleanup or seeking costs from owners of non-residential former U.S. Army land in Johnson County for pesticides the Army applied before 2005.

ks:HB 2170.title: Designating the first full week of February as Kansas burn awareness week.
ks:HB 2170.summary: Designates the first full week of February as Kansas Burn Awareness Week, to commemorate burn victims, raise awareness of accidental burn injuries and educate the public about prevention.

ks:HB 2172.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2172 by Committee on Agriculture and Natural Resources - Establishing the water program task force to evaluate the state's water program and funding for such program and requiring the task force to establish a water planning work group and submit a report the legislature and the governor.
ks:HB 2172.summary: Creates a 16-member Water Program Task Force and a 5-member Water Planning Work Group to study water policy and funding and make recommendations to the Legislature.

ks:HB 2177.title: Increasing the criminal penalties for certain violations of fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer when the person has prior convictions of the offense.
ks:HB 2177.summary: Raises the felony penalty for fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer when the driver has prior felony fleeing convictions, escalating the sentence level for repeat offenders.

ks:HB 2182.title: Prohibiting a sheriff from charging a fee for service of process for proceedings under the protection from abuse act and the protection from stalking, sexual assault or human trafficking act.
ks:HB 2182.summary: Bars sheriffs from charging a fee for serving process in protection from abuse and protection from stalking, sexual assault and human trafficking proceedings, including similar proceedings from other jurisdictions.

ks:HB 2183.title: Modifying elements in the crimes of sexual exploitation of a child, unlawful transmission of a visual depiction of a child and breach of privacy to prohibit certain acts related to visual depictions in which the person depicted is indistinguishable from a real child, morphed from a real child's image or generated without any actual child involvement, provide an exception for cable services in the crime of breach of privacy and prohibit dissemination of certain items that appear to depict or purport to depict an identifiable person.
ks:HB 2183.summary: Bars state courts and administrative hearing officers from deferring to a state agency's reading of statutes and rules, requiring them to interpret these de novo and resolve remaining doubt consistently with individual constitutional rights.

ks:HB 2185.title: Updating the Kansas national guard educational assistance act to include dependents of national guard members and the Kansas national guard educational master's for enhanced readiness and global excellence (EMERGE) program to include other advanced degrees.
ks:HB 2185.summary: Extends Kansas National Guard educational assistance to dependents of Guard members, who can be sponsored by an eligible member, and expands the EMERGE master's program to cover other advanced degrees.

ks:HB 2188.title: Enacting the defend the guard act to prescribe when the Kansas national guard may be released from the state for active duty combat.
ks:HB 2188.summary: As introduced, bars the Kansas National Guard from being sent out of state into active duty combat unless Congress has declared war or formally called forth the Guard to execute federal laws, repel invasion or suppress insurrection. The governor may still consent to Title 32 civil-support deployments.

ks:HB 2192.title: Limiting or prohibiting work release for people convicted of a second or third offense of domestic battery, requiring an offender convicted of a first offense to undergo a domestic violence offender assessment, excluding certain offenders convicted of a nonperson felony from participation in certified drug abuse treatment programs and authorizing community correctional services officers to complete criminal risk-need assessments for divertees who are committed to such programs.
ks:HB 2192.summary: Requires a domestic violence offender assessment as a release condition for first-time domestic battery offenders, raises minimum imprisonment before work release for a second offense from 5 to 20 days, and removes work release for a third or later offense.

ks:HB 2195.title: Establishing the Kansas technical college operating grant fund administered by the state board of regents.
ks:HB 2195.summary: Creates the Kansas Technical College Operating Grant Fund, administered by the State Board of Regents, with money spent on instruction and operations to meet targets set by the Postsecondary Technical Education Authority.

ks:HB 2201.title: Providing for the FFA, route 66 association of Kansas and blackout distinctive license plates, creating the license plate replacement fund and modifying requirements for the issuance and production of license plates and the documentation requirements for military license plate applications.
ks:HB 2201.summary: Authorizes FFA, Route 66 Association and blackout-style distinctive license plates from January 1, 2026, creates a plate replacement fund from the blackout plate's $50 fee, and changes rules for veteran specialized and personalized plates.

ks:HB 2204.title: Declaring that the world health organization, the united nations and the world economic forum have no power within the state of Kansas or any political subdivisions thereof to enforce any rule, regulation, fee, tax, policy or mandate.
ks:HB 2204.summary: Declares the World Health Organization, United Nations and World Economic Forum have no jurisdiction in Kansas and bars the state, its agencies and local governments from enforcing any of their rules, fees, taxes, policies or mandates.

ks:HB 2206.title: Renaming the Kansas governmental ethics commission to the Kansas public disclosure commission, defining terms in the campaign finance act, requiring the filing of statements of independent expenditures, prohibiting agreements requiring contributions in the name of another and requiring the termination of unused campaign finance accounts.
ks:HB 2206.summary: Renames the Kansas Governmental Ethics Commission the Kansas Public Disclosure Commission, requires closing campaign accounts of officeholders who decline to run or lose re-election, and amends other campaign finance rules.

ks:HB 2212.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2212 by Committee on Judiciary - Authorizing the governor to make a declaration of need for enhanced public safety and security for an extraordinary event and providing certain powers to the governor during a period of such declaration.
ks:HB 2212.summary: Lets the governor proclaim a need for enhanced public safety and security for an extraordinary event, such as the World Cup, Olympics, Super Bowl or a national political convention, and grants certain powers during that period.

ks:HB 2214.title: Enacting the safeguarding American veteran empowerment (SAVE) act to limit compensation for assisting in veterans benefits matters.
ks:HB 2214.summary: Enacts the SAVE Act, barring compensation for referring a veteran to others, and for services on claims filed within one year of active-duty release unless the veteran signs a waiver; requires written fee agreements before services.

ks:HB 2215.title: Modifying the definition of public-private partnership to increase the allowable cost-share limit for expenditures by the department of corrections on certain correctional institution construction projects.
ks:HB 2215.summary: Raises the maximum Department of Corrections contribution to a public-private partnership for a correctional building from 25 percent to 50 percent of total cost.

ks:HB 2217.title: Expanding the scope of the inspector general to audit and investigate all state cash, food or health assistance programs and granting the inspector general the power to subpoena, administer oaths and execute search warrants thereto.
ks:HB 2217.summary: Expands the Attorney General's Inspector General to audit and investigate all state cash, food and health assistance programs, and grants power to subpoena, administer oaths and execute search warrants.

ks:HB 2219.title: Enacting the physician assistant licensure compact to provide interstate practice privileges for physician assistants.
ks:HB 2219.summary: Enacts the Physician Assistant Licensure Compact, which gives physician assistants licensed in member states privileges to practice across state lines.

ks:HB 2220.title: Permitting local authorities with jurisdiction over city residence districts to reduce the maximum speed limit from 30 miles per hour to 25 miles per hour without an engineering and traffic investigation.
ks:HB 2220.summary: Lets local authorities lower the speed limit in residence districts from 30 to 25 miles per hour without first conducting an engineering and traffic investigation.

ks:HB 2221.title: Abolishing the department of corrections alcohol and drug abuse treatment fund, creating the Kansas department for aging and disability services alcohol and drug abuse treatment fund and transferring the moneys and liabilities from such abolished fund to the Kansas department for aging and disability services alcohol and drug abuse treatment fund.
ks:HB 2221.summary: Creates an Alcohol and Drug Abuse Treatment Fund in the Department for Aging and Disability Services, transfers money and liabilities to it from the Department of Corrections fund on July 1, 2025, and abolishes that corrections fund.

ks:HB 2222.title: Requiring ignition interlock device manufacturers to pay fees to the state for the administration of the ignition interlock program.
ks:HB 2222.summary: Requires ignition interlock device manufacturers to pay the Highway Patrol a one-time $10 fee per device installed in Kansas and $5 per month per device in use, with no monthly fee for reduced-cost program users.

ks:HB 2223.title: Modifying certain provisions of the optometry law relating to scope of practice, definitions and credentialing requirements.
ks:HB 2223.summary: Expands what optometrists may do, allowing use of medical devices and prescribing drugs by all routes except injections within the eye, and allowing specified procedures such as removing non-perforating foreign bodies from the cornea.

ks:HB 2228.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2228 by Committee on Judiciary - Requiring that a political subdivision hold an open meeting to discuss a contingency fee contract for legal services before approving such contract and requiring the attorney general to approve such contracts.
ks:HB 2228.summary: Requires political subdivisions to hold an open meeting and make written findings before approving a contingent-fee legal services contract, and requires Attorney General approval before it takes effect; the provisions expire July 1, 2029.

ks:HB 2231.title: Providing an additional personal exemption for head of household tax filers and increasing the personal exemption for certain disabled veterans for purposes of income tax, modifying the definition of household income related to increased property tax homestead refund claims, providing for the apportionment of business income by the single sales factor and the apportionment of financial institution income by the receipts factor, providing for the apportionment pursuant to the three-factor test of a manufacturer who sells alcoholic liquor, requiring the use of single sales factor pursuant to the multistate tax compact, establishing deductions from income when using the single sales factor and receipts factor, providing for the decrease in corporate income tax rates, determining when sales other than tangible personal property are made in the state, excluding sales of a unitary business group of electric and natural gas public utilities, providing property tax exemptions for certain personal property including watercraft, marine equipment, off-road vehicles, motorized bicycles and certain trailers.
ks:HB 2231.summary: Allows head-of-household filers a $2,320 extra personal exemption (matching disabled veterans), redefines income for the homestead tax-freeze refund, apportions multistate corporate income by Kansas sales from 2027, and exempts certain personal property from tax.

ks:HB 2237.title: Authorizing hiring, recruitment and retention bonuses in state agencies' employee award and recognition program, increasing the limitation on such award or bonus to $10,000, eliminating the secretary of administration's authority to adopt rules and regulations and requiring such secretary to submit an annual report to certain legislative committees concerning such awards and bonuses.
ks:HB 2237.summary: Raises the cap on total awards and bonuses a state employee may receive in a fiscal year from $3,500 to $10,000. Awards over $3,500 for most executive branch employees need the governor's approval. Requires agencies to report awards annually.

ks:HB 2238.title: Directing legislative administrative services to prepare all committee minutes.
ks:HB 2238.summary: As amended, moves the job of preparing interim legislative committee meeting minutes from the Legislative Research Department to Legislative Administrative Services.

ks:HB 2240.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2240 by Committee on Government Efficiency - Requiring legislative approval prior to any state agency seeking or implementing a public assistance program waiver or other authorization from the federal government that expands eligibility for any public assistance program, increases cost to the state or makes certain changes in services for persons with intellectual or developmental disabilities and authorizing the legislative coordinating council to act on agency requests when the legislature is not in session.
ks:HB 2240.summary: Bars state agencies from July 1, 2025 from seeking federal public assistance waivers that expand eligibility or raise state costs, or changing intellectual and developmental disability services, without approval from the Legislature or Legislative Coordinating Council.

ks:HB 2242.title: Authorizing the governor to accept requests of concurrent jurisdiction from the federal government in certain circumstances.
ks:HB 2242.summary: Authorizes the Governor to accept a federal request for concurrent jurisdiction over U.S. military land in Kansas, effective after a written federal offer, written acceptance and recording with the Secretary of State.

ks:HB 2243.title: Requiring the secretary for children and families to enter into a memorandum of understanding with military organizations and create a referral process for children in need of care cases involving children of military personnel to provide families with services that a military family advocacy program offers.
ks:HB 2243.summary: Requires the Secretary for Children and Families to sign a memorandum of understanding with Kansas military installations and the National Guard setting a process to refer child-in-need-of-care cases involving a military parent or guardian to military family advocacy programs.

ks:HB 2245.title: Transferring officers, employees, powers, duties and functions relating to the state health care benefits program from the division of the state employee health benefits plan of the department of administration to the insurance department, establishing the commissioner of insurance as the chairperson of the Kansas state employees health care commission, providing that all management functions of such commission be administered by the commissioner of insurance and eliminating a pilot program regarding employer contributions for certain children.
ks:HB 2245.summary: Moves the state employee health plan and the state workers compensation self-insurance fund from the Department of Administration to the Department of Insurance effective July 1, 2027, and makes the insurance commissioner chair of the State Employees Health Care Commission.

ks:HB 2246.title: Enacting the consumer protection related to hospital price transparency act.
ks:HB 2246.summary: Creates the Consumer Protection Related to Hospital Price Transparency Act, requiring licensed hospitals to make pricing information available to the public and giving the Attorney General enforcement authority.

ks:HB 2249.title: Requiring the secretary for aging and disability services to grant physical environment waivers for certain rural emergency hospitals to provide skilled nursing facility care and establishing the south central regional mental health hospital.
ks:HB 2249.summary: Lets the aging and disability services secretary grant waivers so rural emergency hospitals can convert up to 10 swing beds to skilled nursing beds, creates the South Central Regional Mental Health Hospital, and updates state hospital catchment areas.

ks:HB 2250.title: Substitute for HB 2250 by Committee on Health and Human Services - Permitting the use of expedited partner therapy to treat sexually transmitted infections, authorizing a licensed private psychiatric hospital to maintain a stock supply of emergency medication kits for pharmaceutical emergencies, allowing expired emergency opioid antagonists to be used to treat an opioid overdose, permitting first responders to distribute and administer expired emergency opioid antagonists, permitting a pharmacist to distribute epinephrine delivery systems to a school for use in emergency medication kits and amending definitions related to medication in schools to allow for use of epinephrine delivery systems.
ks:HB 2250.summary: Adds giving an emergency opioid antagonist to the acts that cannot be prosecuted in overdose cases, lets private psychiatric hospitals keep emergency medication kits, lets pharmacists give schools epinephrine for kits, and allows expedited partner therapy for sexually transmitted diseases.

ks:HB 2254.title: Requiring milk processors to hold payments in trust for milk producers until full payment is received, with funds in escrow considered held in trust.
ks:HB 2254.summary: Requires milk processors to hold payments from milk sales in trust for the milk producer until the producer has been paid in full.

ks:HB 2255.title: Amending definitions concerning weights and measurers increasing minimum invoice fees, requiring licenses and education for service company operators and mandating annual device inspections, except for devices with a nominal capacity of 250 pounds or greater used in grain elevators; increasing the CREP acreage cap to 60,000 acres, clarifying eligibility and criteria, allowing exceptions for specific conditions and modifying reporting requirements to cover the last five years.
ks:HB 2255.summary: Raises the state Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program acreage cap from 40,000 to 60,000 with a 20 percent county limit, raises the weights-and-measures minimum invoice fee from $50 to $70 and calibration fees, and consolidates the weights-and-measures statutes.

ks:HB 2261.title: Providing that Kansas highway patrols officers majors are to be within the unclassified service under the Kansas civil service act and a superintendent, assistant superintendent or major shall be returned to a rank with permanent status not lower than the rank held when the officer was appointed to such respective position.
ks:HB 2261.summary: Adds Kansas Highway Patrol majors to the unclassified civil service and gives permanent status to officers returning to a classified position after serving in an unclassified one.

ks:HB 2271.title: Removing the expiration of provisions relating to moving cybersecurity services under the chief information technology officer of each branch of government.
ks:HB 2271.summary: Removes the July 1, 2026 sunset on state information technology and cybersecurity organization provisions, making them permanent, and adds the Joint Committee on Information Technology as a recipient of two reports.

ks:HB 2273.title: Adding a citation to the federal register to the definition of veteran and disabled veteran.
ks:HB 2273.summary: Changes the definitions of "veteran" and "disabled veteran" in several Kansas statutes to include the groups listed in 38 CFR 3.7, and adds a veteran definition to the 1st Infantry Division license plate statute.

ks:HB 2274.title: Designating Kansas as a purple heart state and permitting homeless veterans to use alternative forms of proof of identity and residency when applying for nondriver identification cards.
ks:HB 2274.summary: Includes military spouses in the definition of a complete application for occupational license fee waivers, even when the spouse's service member is not considered active duty.

ks:HB 2275.title: Providing countywide retailers' sales tax authority for Finney, Pawnee, Seward and Jackson counties, providing that countywide retailers' sales tax apportionment based on tangible property tax levies remain unchanged until December 31, 2026, and excluding exempt sales of certain custom meat processing services from sales tax exemption certificate requirements.
ks:HB 2275.summary: Lets Finney, Jackson, Pawnee and Seward counties ask voters to approve countywide sales taxes, keeps levy-based countywide sales tax apportionment unchanged through December 31, 2026, and lets the custom meat processing sales tax exemption be claimed without exemption certificates.

ks:HB 2289.title: Limiting and discontinuing the Kansas affordable housing tax credit and expanding transferability of Kansas housing investor tax credits.
ks:HB 2289.summary: Ends the Kansas Affordable Housing Tax Credit match in stages, limits the 9 percent match to $8.8 million a year from 2026, and lets transferees claim Kansas Housing Investor Tax Credits retroactive to tax year 2022.

ks:HB 2291.title: Creating the regulatory relief division within the office of the attorney general and establishing the general regulatory sandbox program to waive or suspend rules and regulations for program participants.
ks:HB 2291.summary: Creates a regulatory sandbox program in a new Regulatory Relief Division of the Attorney General's office, letting applicants petition for relief from state licensing laws for innovative business offerings, excluding liquor and cereal malt beverage applications.

ks:HB 2294.title: Reducing certain license fees and training requirements for staff of child care centers, creating a process for day care facility licensees to apply for temporary waiver of certain statutory requirements , authorizing the secretary to develop and operate pilot programs to increase child care facility availability or capacity, transferring certain child care programs to the Kansas office of early childhood and separating licensing duties between the secretary for health and environment and the executive director of early childhood.
ks:HB 2294.summary: Creates the Kansas Office of Early Childhood under a governor-appointed director, moves child care licensing statutes from the health department to it, and changes definitions, staffing and training requirements for child care centers and homes.

ks:HB 2299.title: Senate Substitute for Substitute for HB2299 by Committee on Education - Providing that certain statutory references to accredited nonpublic schools mean nonpublic schools accredited by the state board of education, requiring that schools accredited by a national or regional accrediting agency shall have the same rights as schools accredited by the state board, requiring school districts and accredited nonpublic schools to prohibit the use of personal electronic communication devices during the school day and prohibiting employees of a school district from using social media to communicate with students for official school purposes.
ks:HB 2299.summary: Requires school districts and accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies banning student use of personal electronic devices during the school day, with devices off and stored out of reach, and barring employees from private social media contact with students; adds nonpublic school accreditation provisions.

ks:HB 2304.title: Requiring local governments to report certain local economic development incentive program information to the secretary of commerce, defining such programs, requiring the secretary of commerce to post such information on the economic development incentive program database maintained by the secretary and requiring certain search result presentation and report formats.
ks:HB 2304.summary: Requires local governments to report information on local economic development incentive programs to the Secretary of Commerce for the state transparency database.

ks:HB 2307.title: Transferring the power to authorize and oversee certain activities regarding prenatal and postnatal diagnosed conditions awareness programs from the department of health and environment to the Kansas council on developmental disabilities.
ks:HB 2307.summary: Moves authority over the prenatally and postnatally diagnosed conditions awareness programs from the Department of Health and Environment to the Kansas Council on Developmental Disabilities, creates a program fund, and transfers $25,000 into it once.

ks:HB 2311.title: Prohibiting the secretary from adopting and enforcing policies for placement, custody and appointment of a custodian that may conflict with sincerely held religious or moral beliefs regarding sexual orientation or gender identity and creating a right of action for violations.
ks:HB 2311.summary: Bars the Secretary for Children and Families from adopting policies that require out-of-home, adoptive or custodian applicants to affirm governmental policy on sexual orientation or gender identity conflicting with their religious or moral beliefs, or that disqualify them for those beliefs; allows suits against DCF.

ks:HB 2312.title: Excluding certain offenders convicted of a nonperson felony from participation in certified drug abuse treatment programs and authorizing community correctional services officers to complete criminal risk-need assessments for divertees who are committed to such programs.
ks:HB 2312.summary: Excludes offenders convicted of non-drug felonies carrying presumptive imprisonment from SB 123 drug treatment programs and lets community corrections officers perform risk-need assessments for defendants considered for diversion into certified drug abuse treatment programs.

ks:HB 2313.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2313 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Prohibiting the use of the artificial intelligence platform DeepSeek and other artificial intelligence platforms controlled by a country of concern on state-owned devices and on any state network and the use of genetic sequencers or operational software used for genetic analysis that is produced in a foreign adversary.
ks:HB 2313.summary: Bars state agencies from letting employees access designated foreign-adversary AI platforms such as DeepSeek on state devices and networks, and bars medical and research facilities from using genetic sequencers and software made by foreign adversaries.

ks:HB 2318.title: Providing that future personal and corporate income tax rate decreases be contingent on exceeding tax receipt revenues.
ks:HB 2318.summary: Makes future state income and privilege tax rate cuts depend on General Fund receipts exceeding the inflation-adjusted FY 2024 amount and on the Budget Stabilization Fund balance.

ks:HB 2320.title: Authorizing children in the custody of the secretary of the department for children and families to attend school in any school district, requiring records for such students to be timely transferred between school districts and requiring a transportation plan if the child remains in the school of origin.
ks:HB 2320.summary: Requires DCF to decide a foster student's school placement before a planned move or within two business days of an unplanned one; lets them attend any district or stay in their original school, with a transportation plan; schools transfer records within two business days.

ks:HB 2323.title: Establishing procedures for a civil action instituted by the commissioner of insurance related to fraudulent insurance acts, providing that expunged criminal records will be disclosed in any application for licensure as an insurance producer or public adjuster if the arrest, conviction or diversion is for a fraudulent insurance act and including automobile assigned claims plans in provisions related to fraudulent insurance acts.
ks:HB 2323.summary: As amended by the House committee, lets the insurance commissioner sue for insurance fraud in district court, proving it by a preponderance of the evidence, with civil penalties up to $10,000 per act, and requires producer and public adjuster applicants to disclose insurance-fraud arrests or convictions even if expunged.

ks:HB 2327.title: Establishing procedures and requirements for the secretary of corrections to issue a certificate of employability to certain inmates.
ks:HB 2327.summary: Directs the corrections secretary to issue a certificate of employability on release to inmates who earned an education credential, had no major disciplinary violations in their final year, and met a required job skills assessment score.

ks:HB 2329.title: Changing the name of juvenile crisis intervention centers to juvenile stabilization centers, modifying the intake criteria for such centers, prohibiting certain rules and regulations for such centers, modifying the treatment and services provided by such centers, increasing the cumulative detention limit for juvenile offenders and criminal penalties for juvenile offenders who use a firearm in the commission of an offense or who are repeat offenders, providing for increased placement of offenders in non-foster home beds in youth residential facilities, requiring the secretary of corrections to pay for the costs associated with such placements, authorizing the secretary to make expenditures from the evidence-based programs account of the state general fund moneys to contract for such beds and transferring moneys from such account of the state general fund to the department for children and families to provide juvenile stabilization services.
ks:HB 2329.summary: Renames juvenile crisis intervention centers as juvenile stabilization centers and changes their intake criteria and services. Directs the corrections secretary to contract for out-of-home placement beds, allows judges to send moderate-risk chronic offenders to juvenile correctional facilities, and changes detention length limits.

ks:HB 2331.title: Creating the crime of aggravated criminal desecration and providing penalties therefor, authorizing the disposition of the unclaimed remains of deceased persons by district coroners and providing exemptions from liability for such actions, establishing requirements for programs of continuing education for licensed embalmers and funeral directors and authorizing the use of the word "crematory" as part of the business name for businesses owned by the same person who owns a licensed crematory.
ks:HB 2331.summary: Creates the crime of aggravated criminal desecration (desecration meant to conceal a death or crime), lets coroners dispose of unclaimed cremated remains after notice, sets minimum continuing education for embalmers and funeral directors, and allows some licensed businesses to use "crematory".
