ks:HB 2332.title: Establishing a seal for the house of representatives and a seal for the senate and providing for the custody and use of each.
ks:HB 2332.summary: Establishes official seals for the Kansas House and the Senate, sets when they may be used, lets the Speaker and Senate President approve other uses, and revises a term describing the Great Seal of Kansas.

ks:HB 2333.title: Enacting the Kansas intellectual rights and knowledge act, providing a civil cause of action and penalties for violations of such act and authorizing students and student associations to exercise political and ideological beliefs, values and missions.
ks:HB 2333.summary: Allows non-commercial expressive activity on public college campuses unless it materially and substantially disrupts operations, bans free speech zones, and limits time, place and manner rules. Lets the Attorney General or an injured person sue colleges, and extends student-group protections to political and ideological groups.

ks:HB 2335.title: Providing for the hunter nation distinctive license plate.
ks:HB 2335.summary: Authorizes a Hunter Nation distinctive license plate from January 1, 2026, with Hunter Nation, Inc. setting a $25–$100 royalty at issuance and renewal, and allows transfer of the plate from a leased to a purchased vehicle.

ks:HB 2336.title: Providing for the apportionment of business income by the single sales factor and the apportionment of financial institution income by the receipts factor, deductions from income when using the single sales factor and receipts factor, the decrease in corporate income tax rates determining when sales other than tangible personal property are made in the state and excluding sales of a unitary business group of electric and natural gas public utilities.
ks:HB 2336.summary: Requires most multistate corporations to apportion Kansas income using only the sales factor from tax year 2027 with market-based sourcing, sets a corporate tax rate reduction from 2029 tied to receipts growth, and adds a deferred tax deduction for certain corporations.

ks:HB 2338.title: Authorizing the board of cosmetology to issue temporary location and temporary guest artist permits and establishing criteria therefor.
ks:HB 2338.summary: Lets the cosmetology board issue temporary location permits to practitioners licensed in other states and temporary guest artist permits for conventions, licensed establishments or other approved events, if their out-of-state licenses are in good standing.

ks:HB 2340.title: Providing for an exemption from remediation costs or other liability from prior commercial pesticide application by the United States army for owners of certain property located in Johnson county.
ks:HB 2340.summary: Bars state agencies from requiring owners of nonresidential former U.S. Army property in Johnson County to pay for investigating or cleaning up contamination from legally registered pesticides the Army applied before 2005.

ks:HB 2342.title: Authorizing the attorney general and the state gaming agency to receive certain additional criminal history records, updating criminal history record language related to the state bank commissioner, requiring the secretary of labor to conduct criminal history record checks on employees who have access to federal tax information and authorizing the secretary of commerce to conduct such checks on final applicants for and employees in certain sensitive positions.
ks:HB 2342.summary: As amended, lets the Commerce secretary request state and national criminal history checks from the KBI for final applicants and employees in sensitive Department of Commerce positions, with minimum standards on theft, fraud and felony convictions.

ks:HB 2343.title: Creating the no-impact home-based business fairness act, supporting the development and growth of such businesses by limiting the regulatory power of municipalities.
ks:HB 2343.summary: As amended by the House committee, creates the No-Impact Home-Based Business Fairness Act, allowing such businesses in residences, overriding deed restrictions and covenants entered on or after July 1, 2025 except clear homeowners association bylaws the business would likely violate, and limiting municipal permit requirements.

ks:HB 2346.title: Substitute for HB 2346 by Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development - Establishing the Kansas sports tourism grant program administered by the secretary of commerce to provide matching grants to communities for developing and continuing sporting events and providing for funding of such grants from the state economic development initiatives fund.
ks:HB 2346.summary: Creates the Kansas Sports Tourism Grant Program, run by the Secretary of Commerce, providing dollar-for-dollar matching grants for sports tourism events held in Kansas. Applications are due at least 90 days before an event, and a fee of up to $100 may be charged.

ks:HB 2347.title: Changing the culpability required for certain types of theft and increasing the criminal penalty for theft to a felony when the property is a motor vehicle of the value of at least $500, creating the crime of unlawful use of a laser pointer and providing criminal penalties therefor, modifying criminal use of a financial card to include certain conduct involving gift cards, increasing the criminal penalties for buying sexual relations, removing provisions regarding city ordinances prohibiting buying sexual relations, requiring certain offenders to complete an educational or treatment program regarding commercial sexual exploitation and requiring the attorney general to approve such programs in consultation with the office of judicial administration.
ks:HB 2347.summary: Changes the culpability for obtaining control of stolen property from 'knowing' to 'has reason to know', makes theft of a $500–$1,500 vehicle a felony, creates a laser pointer crime, and raises penalties for buying sexual relations, requiring AG-approved programs for certain offenders.

ks:HB 2349.title: Authorizing law enforcement officers to conduct investigations of violations of the scrap metal theft reduction act.
ks:HB 2349.summary: Authorizes Kansas law enforcement officers to investigate violations of the Scrap Metal Theft Reduction Act, and requires investigative reports be sent to the Attorney General whether or not local action follows.

ks:HB 2352.title: Requiring a duly ordained minister of religion to report certain abuse and neglect except when reporting would violate the penitential communication privilege and requiring training for persons obligated to report abuse and neglect.
ks:HB 2352.summary: Requires ordained ministers to report suspected child abuse or neglect unless doing so would violate the penitential communication privilege, and requires all mandated reporters to complete reporting training before July 1, 2027.

ks:HB 2357.title: Substitute for HB 2357 by Committee on Judiciary - Providing for expungement of certain court records and consideration of mediation in eviction actions in which the underlying rental agreement is governed by the residential landlord and tenant act.
ks:HB 2357.summary: Lets tenants in covered eviction cases file free electronic requests to expunge court records three years after judgment, with landlords able to object within 30 days, and requires courts to consider mediation in most eviction actions.

ks:HB 2359.title: Enacting the uniform adult guardianship and protective proceedings jurisdiction act and the uniform guardianship, conservatorship and other protective arrangements act.
ks:HB 2359.summary: Enacts the Uniform Adult Guardianship and Protective Proceedings Jurisdiction Act and a new Uniform Guardianship, Conservatorship, and Other Protective Arrangements Act, repealing existing Kansas guardianship and conservatorship statutes, effective January 1, 2026.

ks:HB 2364.title: Prohibiting certain health insurers from requiring cost-sharing for nonopioid prescription drugs or providing less favorable coverage for such drug than that for opioid or narcotic prescription drugs for the treatment of pain.
ks:HB 2364.summary: Bars health insurers from denying coverage of non-opioid pain drugs in favor of opioids or requiring patients to try an opioid first, and from putting non-opioid drugs at a formulary disadvantage through stricter criteria or utilization controls.

ks:HB 2365.title: Adding and removing certain substances in schedules I, III and IV of the uniform controlled substances act and making conforming changes to the criminal code definition of fentanyl-related controlled substances.
ks:HB 2365.summary: Adds substances to Kansas's controlled substance schedules, including 14 to Schedule I such as synthetic opioids, hexahydrocannabinol and 7-hydroxymitragynine from kratom, and adjusts fentanyl and cannabis language to match federal law.

ks:HB 2366.title: Expanding the scope of practice of naturopathic doctors, specifying continuing education requirements, increasing the required amount of professional liability insurance and modifying certain provisions relating to the licensure and regulations of naturopathic doctors.
ks:HB 2366.summary: Expands naturopathic doctors' scope of practice to include prescribing prescription-only drugs and testosterone, sets prescribing and recordkeeping rules, and adds them as covered providers under the Health Care Stabilization Fund.

ks:HB 2371.title: Amending the Kansas revised limited liability company act, the business entity transactions act and the business entity standard treatment act.
ks:HB 2371.summary: Updates the Revised Limited Liability Company Act, Business Entity Transactions Act and Business Entity Standard Treatment Act on document forms, signatures, delivery, filing fee limits, certificates, registration and resident agent changes.

ks:HB 2374.title: Creating the specialty practice student loan program and the specialty practice student loan repayment fund, allowing for the transfer of funds from the OBGYN and psychiatry medical student loan repayment funds to the specialty practice student loan repayment fund and abolishing the OBGYN and psychiatry medical student loan repayment funds.
ks:HB 2374.summary: Creates a specialty practice student loan program at the University of Kansas School of Medicine, offering loans to students who commit to full-time practice in an approved specialty in a service commitment area, and amends the Medical Student Loan Act.

ks:HB 2377.title: Providing that countywide retailers' sales tax is apportioned based on total assessed valuations of property taxes rather than property taxes levied.
ks:HB 2377.summary: Keeps the apportionment of countywide retailers' sales tax among cities and counties, where based on property tax levied, at current ratios from July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026. Population-based apportionment is unchanged.

ks:HB 2378.title: Establishing the removal of squatters act, providing a procedure to remove a squatter from a dwelling unit, requiring owners or agents of dwelling units to provide an affidavit to the county sheriff department or police department , requiring notice to vacate by the sheriff, establishing the crime of providing a false affidavit and establishing a civil cause of action for wrongful removal of a person from a dwelling unit, allowing attorney fees and punitive damages.
ks:HB 2378.summary: Creates a process for property owners or agents to file an affidavit asking law enforcement to remove unauthorized occupants from a dwelling, requires officers to serve a notice to vacate, makes a knowingly false affidavit a misdemeanor, and allows civil suits for wrongful removal.

ks:HB 2382.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2382 by Committee on Education - Requiring school districts to include a fetal development presentation as part of the curriculum for any course that addresses human growth, human development or human sexuality and authorizing the state board of education to establish the rate of compensation for members of the board.
ks:HB 2382.summary: Requires school districts teaching human growth, development or sexuality to include a fetal development presentation of at least three minutes, and lets the State Board of Education set board members' meeting compensation.

ks:HB 2390.title: Providing countywide retailers' sales tax authority for Jackson county for the purpose of supporting hospital services in the county.
ks:HB 2390.summary: Authorizes Jackson County commissioners to put a countywide 0.25 percent sales tax for hospital services to voters. The county keeps all proceeds and the tax expires ten years after collection begins.

ks:HB 2393.title: Authorizing the supreme court to impose a charge to fund the costs of non-judicial personnel through June 30, 2030.
ks:HB 2393.summary: Extends the Judicial Branch surcharge on docket fees through June 30, 2030, and removes outdated statutory references.

ks:HB 2396.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2396 by Committee on Assessment and Taxation - Authorizing the use of a protest petition to limit funding of a taxing jurisdiction by property tax revenues exceeding a certain amount, providing for a protest petition notice to be sent to taxpayers and modifying the content requirements of the revenue neutral rate hearing notice.
ks:HB 2396.summary: As amended by the House committee, limits property tax revenue after a successful protest petition to the prior year's level plus inflation, new construction and new bond payments, creates a fund paying cities and counties that meet the limit, and repeals revenue neutral rate notice and hearing requirements.

ks:HB 2400.title: Amending the definition of land devoted to agricultural use to include trail rides as a ranching activity to qualify as an agritourism activity.
ks:HB 2400.summary: Adds trail rides to the activities that count as agritourism under the Agritourism Promotion Act and as agricultural use of land for property valuation purposes.

ks:HB 2402.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2402 by Committee on Education - Requiring eligible boards of education to consider participation in the community eligibility provision, providing a financial hardship exception to such participation, requiring the state department of education to assist school districts seeking such participation, extending the application deadline for authorization to operate as a public innovative district from December 1 to May 1 and deeming such applications approved if not approved or denied within 45 days of submission.
ks:HB 2402.summary: Requires school boards with a school where at least 50 percent of students are directly certified for free lunch to annually consider joining the federal Community Eligibility Provision. Also moves Public Innovative District application deadlines, such as December 1 to May 1.

ks:HB 2408.title: Providing that leased ground owned by a county-recognized community land trust shall be considered as a factor in determining fair market value for property tax purposes.
ks:HB 2408.summary: Adds restrictions on the use of real estate on leased ground owned by a county-recognized community land trust to the factors considered in determining a property's fair market value for property tax.

ks:HB 2412.title: Requiring instruction to provide students with an understanding of communist, fascist and socialist regimes and ideologies and that students pass an American civics examination in order to graduate with a high school diploma.
ks:HB 2412.summary: Requires schools to teach about the negative impacts of communist, fascist and socialist regimes and ideologies, and makes passing a 20-question American civics exam, based on naturalization questions, a graduation requirement for students entering ninth grade from July 2026.

ks:HB 2416.title: Creating the Kansas motorsports venue protection act to provide immunity to motorsports venues from civil actions for nuisance, taking or similar legal theories.
ks:HB 2416.summary: Gives racetracks immunity from nuisance and taking lawsuits if the track existed before neighboring owners built or acquired residential or commercial property. Exceptions apply for violations of law or permits, and for tracks with no race in the prior four years.

ks:HB 2422.title: Providing that the theft of grain or hay is a severity level 6, nonperson felony.
ks:HB 2422.summary: Requires app stores to verify the age category of Kansas account holders and get parental consent before minors download or buy apps, and requires developers to check that data. The Attorney General enforces; most duties start January 1, 2027.

ks:HB 2427.title: Substitute for HB 2427 by Committee on Appropriations - Establishing the positions of the senate fiscal integrity auditor appointed by the president of the senate and the house of representatives fiscal integrity auditor appointed by the speaker of the house of representatives, providing for the duties of such fiscal integrity auditors including access to the state fiscal technology systems and software and reports and recommendations to certain legislative committees.
ks:HB 2427.summary: Creates two legislative fiscal integrity auditors, one appointed by the Senate President and one by the House Speaker, with access to state budgeting systems and agency fiscal records.

ks:HB 2433.title: Clarifying county authority over the transfer or appropriation of water by placing such authority, except for domestic use, with the chief engineer and water transfer hearing panel.
ks:HB 2433.summary: Bars counties from regulating the transfer or appropriation of water in ways that conflict with or duplicate the state chief engineer's authority, including permits and fees, while allowing zoning and sanitary rules for domestic wells.

ks:HB 2434.title: Substitute for HB 2434 by Committee on Appropriations - Making and concerning supplemental appropriations for fiscal year 2026 and appropriations for fiscal years 2027 and 2028 for various state agencies, authorizing certain capital improvement projects and fees, authorizing certain transfers.
ks:HB 2434.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for fiscal year 2026 and appropriations for later fiscal years for state agencies, authorizing certain transfers, capital improvement projects, and fees.

ks:HB 2435.title: Substitute for HB 2435 by Committee on Energy, Utilities and Telecommunications - Authorizing natural gas public utilities to recover certain growth-related investments in the gas system reliability surcharge, increasing the cap on the amount that the monthly fixed charge may be increased for residential customers and reducing the time for the state corporation commission to act on gas system reliability surcharge filings.
ks:HB 2435.summary: Lets natural gas utilities recover growth-related capital investments, such as lines connecting new customers, through the Gas System Reliability Surcharge, shortens the commission's review period from 120 to 90 days, and raises the cap on monthly residential charges.

ks:HB 2437.title: Establishing the save Kansas act, authorizing the use of additional resources for verifying voter registration records, imposing restrictions on websites that can accept and transmit voter registration applications, removing individuals disqualified for voting from such records and providing an open records request exemption for certain information related to such records.
ks:HB 2437.summary: Requires twice-yearly checks of voter rolls against the federal SAVE database, adds duplicate-registration, Social Security death-list and out-of-state driver's license checks, and requires quarterly reports on noncitizen benefit recipients. Limits online voter registration to .gov or state-approved websites.

ks:HB 2438.title: Imposing restrictions on websites that can accept and transmit voter registration applications.
ks:HB 2438.summary: Limits online voter registration to .gov websites or sites approved by the Secretary of State under data-protection criteria, and makes running an unapproved voter registration website a crime.

ks:HB 2440.title: Excluding owners of oil leases from having to file request for exemption with the board of tax appeals for property tax exemptions.
ks:HB 2440.summary: Allows county appraisers to approve the property tax exemption for low production oil leases without lease owners filing an application with the Board of Tax Appeals.

ks:HB 2444.title: Providing that jail credit when consecutive sentences are imposed shall not apply to more than one case, creating special sentencing rules when a felony is committed by certain offenders while on probation, parole or postrelease supervision for a prior felony and requiring secured minimum bonds for certain defendants who commit a new felony while on probation, parole, postrelease supervision or bond for a prior felony unless the court makes certain findings.
ks:HB 2444.summary: Allows jail credit on consecutive sentences to be applied only once, requires bond for misdemeanor and felony charges unless conditions are met or findings made, sets minimum appearance bonds for new felonies committed while under supervision, and creates a sentencing rule for certain repeat offenders.

ks:HB 2446.title: Deleting the requirement that the name of treasurers be listed in attributions for political advertising.
ks:HB 2446.summary: Removes the requirement to list the treasurer's name in paid-for attributions on political advertising, requiring only the sponsoring organization's chairperson's name.

ks:HB 2448.title: Requiring citizenship status be listed on driver's licenses.
ks:HB 2448.summary: Requires driver's licenses to list citizenship status and lets a person whose license lists them as a noncitizen but who claims to be a citizen obtain a provisional ballot.

ks:HB 2451.title: Prohibiting the use of public assets by government officers and employees to advocate for or against proposed amendments to the constitution of the state of Kansas and ballot questions submitted to qualified electors.
ks:HB 2451.summary: Bars government officers and employees from using public assets to promote or oppose changes to the Kansas Constitution or any ballot question, and requires a fiscal disclosure statement in publicly funded informational material about bond issues.

ks:HB 2453.title: Requiring applications for advance voting ballots be filed by the 14th day prior to election day, that advance voting in person be completed by 12:00 p.m. on the Sunday prior to election day, extending the time for transmittal of advance voting ballots to 22 days prior to an election and ending the time for voter registration at 23 days prior to election day.
ks:HB 2453.summary: Moves the mailed advance ballot application deadline to 14 days before an election, lets clerks mail ballots 22 days out instead of 20, requires mailed ballots to arrive by close of polls, and moves the voter registration cutoff from 20 to 25 days before.

ks:HB 2460.title: Modifying an exception to the Kansas open records act that authorizes certain individuals to have identifying information restricted from public access on public websites that identify home addresses or home ownership by providing that certain individuals who were employed for five or more years, certain elected officials and persons who reside at an address that is subject to restriction from public access may request to have such information restricted and removing an exception related to information or reports obtained and prepared by the office of the state bank commissioner.
ks:HB 2460.summary: Extends the exception letting people request that home address and ownership be kept off keyword-searchable public websites to legislators, statewide officers, state school board members, local elected officials and certain former officials, and removes an open-records exception for State Bank Commissioner money-transmission records.

ks:HB 2462.title: Requiring the secretary of health and environment to adopt rules and regulations that allow for the direct and indirect potable reuse of treated wastewater, providing additional requirements for applications to the water technical assistance fund and the water projects grant fund and extending the current expiration date of such funds.
ks:HB 2462.summary: Requires the health secretary to adopt rules by July 1, 2028 allowing direct and indirect potable reuse of treated wastewater, favoring affordable prescriptive treatment processes. Also changes the sunset, funding transfers and grant process for two state water funds.

ks:HB 2464.title: Extending the number of years that tax credits may be issued or earned for contributions to graduates of aerospace and aviation-related educational programs and employers of program graduates, the tax credits for contributions to the Eisenhower foundation and friends of cedar crest association and the sunset for the angel investor tax credit and providing for a minimum amount of such credits for investments in counties with a population of 50,000 or fewer.
ks:HB 2464.summary: Extends to 2031 the angel investor credit and the credits for aerospace graduates and employers, the Eisenhower Foundation and Friends of Cedar Crest. Reserves at least 25 percent of angel credits for investments in counties of 50,000 or fewer people, if enough are requested.

ks:HB 2466.title: Enacting the Kansas sports authority act, authorizing STAR bond projects in major amusement park areas and extending the expiration date of the STAR bonds financing act.
ks:HB 2466.summary: Creates the Kansas Sports Facilities Authority to build a stadium and related infrastructure for an NFL team's home games. Changes STAR Bonds law, extending it to July 1, 2031, and modifies the authorized uses of the Attracting Professional Sports Fund.

ks:HB 2467.title: Prohibiting past convictions or sanctions for failure to comply with a traffic citation that are more than five years old from being considered by courts and the division of vehicles in determining suspended or restricted driving privileges and eliminating certain notice requirements for the division of vehicles.
ks:HB 2467.summary: Bars the Division of Vehicles from considering a license suspension or restriction for failure to comply with a traffic citation that is more than five years old, retroactively, and ends a requirement to mail notices to people eligible for reinstatement.

ks:HB 2468.title: Electing to participate in the federal tax credit for individual contributions to scholarship granting organizations and increasing the aggregate tax credit limit on the tax credit for low income students scholarship program.
ks:HB 2468.summary: Has Kansas elect to take part in the federal tax credit for contributions to scholarship granting organizations for tax years after 2026, and raises the aggregate cap on the state's low-income scholarship tax credit program.

ks:HB 2470.title: Providing that certain municipalities may designate the entire municipality within a neighborhood revitalization area under the Kansas neighborhood revitalization act.
ks:HB 2470.summary: Clarifies that a municipality with fewer than 10,000 residents may designate its entire territory as a neighborhood revitalization area under the Kansas Neighborhood Revitalization Act.

ks:HB 2476.title: Permitting federal pesticide warning or labeling requirements to satisfy any state pesticide warning or labeling requirements.
ks:HB 2476.summary: Deems a pesticide label to satisfy state health or safety warning requirements if it matches the most recent federal health assessment or EPA carcinogenicity classification, without barring claims unrelated to warnings or labeling.

ks:HB 2477.title: Requiring the Kansas department of agriculture to publish a map on the department's official website that shows the location of all applied for diversions of water, including requested changes in the point of diversion by more than 300 feet, and expanding the current individual notice requirement to apply to all landowners that are within half a mile of such applied for diversions or changes.
ks:HB 2477.summary: Requires the Division of Water Resources to publish a map of applied-for water diversions and proposed point-of-diversion changes, requires individual notice to landowners within half a mile, and ends notice to water right owners when a water conservation area is established.

ks:HB 2478.title: Requiring that advanced practice registered nurses and registered nurse anesthetists submit to a criminal history check upon application for a nursing license.
ks:HB 2478.summary: Requires applicants for advanced practice registered nurse and registered nurse anesthetist licenses to be fingerprinted for state and national criminal history record checks.

ks:HB 2479.title: Authorizing electronic monitoring with victim notification as a condition of release prior to trial for certain offenders charged with a domestic violence offense, domestic battery, stalking or violation of a protective order, modifying the culpable mental state required to commit the crime of breach of privacy and increasing the criminal penalties for certain violations of such crime, modifying the elements of the crime of blackmail related to threatened dissemination of any image, video or other recording of another identifiable person who is nude or engaged in sexual activity, describing who is a person in a position of authority for a school for the crime of unlawful sexual relations and increasing the penalties for the crimes of endangering a child and aggravated endangering a child if the child is less than six years of age.
ks:HB 2479.summary: Requires courts to consider ordering electronic monitoring with victim notification as a release condition for people charged with domestic violence offenses, domestic battery, or stalking, and sets rules for its use.

ks:HB 2481.title: During the period of the FIFA 2026 world cup, prohibiting certain limitations by municipalities on short-term rental or vacation properties and requiring timely rental permit processing, modifying the definition of transient guest for transient guest tax purposes and authorizing expanded sales of alcoholic beverages by cities and counties.
ks:HB 2481.summary: Lets counties and cities allow alcohol sales 23 hours a day during the FIFA 2026 World Cup. From May 15 to July 25, 2026, requires transient guest tax on short-term rentals and bars cities and counties from limiting the number of rental permits.

ks:HB 2482.title: Removing the requirement that the state board of education use a certain exam provider to deliver certain college entrance and career readiness exams and requiring the board to provide for such exams using any provider.
ks:HB 2482.summary: Replaces required ACT exams in state law with a nationally recognized college entrance exam for grades 11 and 12, an aligned pre-college exam for grade 9, and a career readiness assessment leading to a credential for grade 11, effective July 1, 2027.

ks:HB 2485.title: Authorizing the chief executive officer of the board of regents to negotiate and settle repayment obligations arising under financial aid programs administered by the board, providing requirements for agreements between postsecondary educational institutions and school districts for postsecondary courses taught in secondary schools, directing the governor to approve short-term workforce training programs for Pell grant eligibility, modifying requirements under the every child can read act and prohibiting Kansas promise scholarship awards for remedial hours.
ks:HB 2485.summary: Authorizes the Board of Regents to negotiate and settle service scholarship repayment obligations, and bars scholarship recipients who owe repayment from receiving more scholarship funds.

ks:HB 2487.title: Defining teacher and paraprofessional for purposes of eligibility for a scholarship under the Kansas education opportunity scholarship program.
ks:HB 2487.summary: Defines "employed in Kansas as a teacher or paraprofessional" for the Education Opportunity Scholarship as a public or nonpublic school employee whose main duties are classroom instruction or support in grades pre-K-12, certified by a school administrator to the Board of Regents.

ks:HB 2489.title: Requiring school districts to provide fentanyl abuse education programs and maintain supplies of naloxone in each school.
ks:HB 2489.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to issue guidance and school districts to teach fentanyl abuse prevention to students in grades 9 through 12, and requires districts to keep a stock supply of naloxone.

ks:HB 2491.title: Requiring state agencies to make quarterly reports to the secretary of state with the names and addresses of noncitizens receiving public benefits.
ks:HB 2491.summary: Requires state voter registration agencies that provide public assistance to report quarterly to the Secretary of State the identifying details of each noncitizen benefit recipient, including name, address, birth date, and alien registration number.

ks:HB 2497.title: Prohibiting the assessment of a prepayment penalty against any party more than six months after the execution of a note evidencing a home loan made primarily for personal, family or household purposes secured by a real estate mortgage.
ks:HB 2497.summary: Limits the ban on prepayment penalties more than six months after signing to home loans made for personal, family or household purposes, which lets lenders charge prepayment penalties on business-purpose home loans.

ks:HB 2501.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2501 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Providing for immunity from civil liability to federal firearms licensees for returning a firearm to the firearm owner at the termination of a firearm hold agreement, removing the criminal prohibition against firearm suppressors and shotgun barrel length qualification requirements and providing enhanced penalties for certain felonies committed while using a firearm suppressor or short-barrel shotgun.
ks:HB 2501.summary: Sets rules for firearm hold agreements, where a licensed dealer stores an owner's firearm, including dealer civil immunity. Removes suppressors and the 18-inch shotgun barrel minimum from state weapons crimes; raises the sentence one level when either is used in a nonperson or drug felony.

ks:HB 2502.title: Requiring the Kansas department of wildlife and parks to offer discounted resident senior combination hunting and fishing passes to residents of this state who are 65 years of age or older and removing the expiration date for Kansas kids lifetime combination hunting and fishing licenses.
ks:HB 2502.summary: Requires the wildlife and parks department to offer a discounted resident senior combination hunting and fishing pass to residents 65 or older, priced at no more than one-eighth of the lifetime combination license fee.

ks:HB 2503.title: Repealing the mail ballot election act.
ks:HB 2503.summary: Repeals the Mail Ballot Election Act and all provisions authorizing elections conducted exclusively by mail ballot, without changing advance voting by mail in primary, general, or special elections.

ks:HB 2504.title: Prohibiting cities and counties from restricting the discretion of landlords not to rent residential or commercial property on grounds including prospective tenants receipt of housing assistance or eviction or criminal history, and permitting cities and counties to prohibit discrimination by landlords on the basis of receipt of veterans benefits.
ks:HB 2504.summary: Bars cities and counties from adopting rules that stop landlords from refusing tenants paying with housing assistance, limit use of credit, eviction or criminal history, or limit security deposits, while allowing bans on discrimination based on veterans benefits.

ks:HB 2505.title: Providing an exception for Kansas department of wildlife and parks records regarding the location of any species that is threatened, endangered or in need of conservation from the disclosure requirements of the Kansas open records act.
ks:HB 2505.summary: Exempts from the Kansas Open Records Act wildlife department records giving the precise location of threatened, endangered or conservation-need species, except for requests by landowners or their lessees or designees about their own property.

ks:HB 2507.title: Removing the requirement for migratory waterfowl stamps to be validated by a signature across the face of each such stamp and increasing the fees for such stamps, authorizing the adoption of certain rules and regulations related to fees, registrations and other charges by the department of wildlife and parks and providing an exception from the disclosure requirements of the Kansas open records act for department of wildlife and parks records regarding the location of any species that is threatened, endangered or in need of conservation.
ks:HB 2507.summary: Raises the cap on the resident migratory waterfowl habitat stamp fee from $8 to $15 and sets the nonresident fee at $100 to $200. Ends the stamp signature requirement and no longer requires disclosing precise locations of protected species, except to landowners.

ks:HB 2509.title: Allowing licensed physical therapists to perform certain capillary blood tests, adding advanced practice registered nurse to the definition of healthcare provider for purposes of the healthcare provider insurance availability act, adding an advanced practice registered nurse position to the board of governors of the healthcare stabilization fund and requiring advance practice registered nurses to maintain professional liability insurance as a condition of active licensure.
ks:HB 2509.summary: Adds advanced practice registered nurses to the Health Care Stabilization Fund from January 2028, adds an APRN seat to its governing board, and lets licensed physical therapists perform certain capillary blood tests.

ks:HB 2511.title: Permitting moneys received from agricultural production on a state-owned property to be used for the management of all state-owned properties.
ks:HB 2511.summary: Allows money from agricultural production on state-owned wildlife and parks land, held in separate property accounts, to be used for habitat management costs on all state-owned properties, not only the property that earned it.

ks:HB 2513.title: Making and concerning supplemental appropriations for fiscal year 2026 and appropriations for fiscal years 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030 for various state agencies, authorizing certain capital improvement projects and fees, authorizing certain transfers.
ks:HB 2513.summary: Sets state agency spending for fiscal years 2026 through 2030, including about $27.8 billion in fiscal year 2026 and $26.8 billion in fiscal year 2027 from all funds, and funds a new Office of Early Childhood.

ks:HB 2515.title: Establishing the Kansas legal tender act and providing for an income tax subtraction modification for sales of specie.
ks:HB 2515.summary: Creates the Kansas Legal Tender Act, treating U.S.-issued gold and silver coin as legal tender not taxed as personal property, and lets taxpayers subtract net gains from selling gold and silver coin or bullion from Kansas taxable income from tax year 2025.

ks:HB 2518.title: Enacting the Kansas transparency in consumer legal funding act.
ks:HB 2518.summary: Creates the Kansas Transparency in Consumer Legal Funding Act, setting contract rules for companies advancing money to people in lawsuits: plain language, a 10-business-day cancellation right, and nothing owed if the lawsuit yields no recovery, absent fraud or breach.

ks:HB 2519.title: Continuing in existence certain exceptions to the disclosure of public records under the Kansas open records act.
ks:HB 2519.summary: Continues in existence five exceptions to the Kansas Open Records Act, including those covering driver's license emergency contacts, local child death review records, reinsurance certification applications, and elder abuse team materials.

ks:HB 2520.title: Increasing the number of allowed residents in a home plus facility from 12 to 16.
ks:HB 2520.summary: Raises the maximum number of residents in a Home Plus adult care facility from 12 to 16, and requires facilities serving more than 12 after July 1, 2026 to keep written plans for meeting residents' needs and emergencies.

ks:HB 2521.title: Expanding the Kansas tort claims act to include child placement agencies that contract with the secretary for children and families.
ks:HB 2521.summary: Treats child placement agencies with an active contract with the Department for Children and Families as governmental entities under the Kansas Tort Claims Act, for claims arising on or after July 1, 2026. The provision expires July 1, 2029.

ks:HB 2522.title: Permitting highway construction and maintenance vehicles in road construction zones to display flashing amber, white or green lights at all times or flashing white and blue lights on stationary trailers under certain conditions and prohibiting the use of a mobile telephone while operating a motor vehicle in a school zone or a road construction zone.
ks:HB 2522.summary: As passed by the House, permits highway construction and maintenance vehicles to display flashing amber, green or white lights at all times in road construction zones, and white and blue lights on stationary trailers at night when part of the road is closed.

ks:HB 2524.title: Permitting the secretary for children and families to license family foster homes when certain persons reside in such home and creating an appeal process for family foster homes when licenses are not granted.
ks:HB 2524.summary: Allows DCF to license a family foster home where a resident placed there as a child in DCF custody has a past conviction or adjudication, generally if under 26 and no safety concerns; allows appeal to the Secretary if a license is not granted.

ks:HB 2527.title: Prohibiting certain sex offenders from entering onto school property or attending school activities, prohibiting courts from assigning a defendant to work release if the defendant is required to register as a sex offender for certain crimes and prohibiting the secretary of corrections from granting an inmate leave from confinement except for specified purposes if theinmate is required to register as a sex offender for certain crimes or is serving a sentence for certain crimes that require registration as a sex offender.
ks:HB 2527.summary: Makes it a felony for registered sex offenders whose offense was committed at age 18 or older against a victim under 16 to enter school property or attend school activities. Also bars work release for certain registrants.

ks:HB 2528.title: Requiring all state board of nursing actions related to certain nonpractice violations be void, allowing for late license renewal for professional, practical and advanced practice registered nurses, setting fees for late license renewal, limiting unprofessional conduct to acts related to the practice of nursing, prohibiting the board from taking retaliatory action against a licensee based on certain lawful actions and creating a civil cause of action for violation thereof, requiring termination of current board members on January 1, 2027 and requiring the governor to appoint interim board members subject to senate confirmation and requiring the board to issue refunds for overpayment or duplicate payment.
ks:HB 2528.summary: Voids certain nursing board disciplinary actions from 2005 onward tied to licensure renewal and lapsed-license violations, adds a grace period and late renewal process for nursing licenses, and changes the definition of unprofessional conduct.

ks:HB 2530.title: Substitute for HB 2530 by Committee on Education - Providing for the transferability of credentials earned through ACT workkeys career readiness assessments towards a degree.
ks:HB 2530.summary: Requires postsecondary institutions to adopt policies accepting platinum, gold or silver ACT WorkKeys credentials, or similar career readiness credentials, as transferable credit toward a postsecondary technical degree, based on the American Council on Education National Guide.

ks:HB 2533.title: Enacting the occupational therapy licensure compact, respiratory care interstate compact, esthetics licensure compact and athletic trainer licensure compact to provide interstate practice privileges.
ks:HB 2533.summary: Enacts four interstate licensure compacts, for occupational therapy, respiratory care, esthetics and athletic trainers, giving licensed practitioners in member states privileges to practice in Kansas.

ks:HB 2534.title: Requiring school districts to provide fentanyl abuse education programs and maintain a supply of naloxone in all schools, requiring the department of education to establish guidelines for active shooter drills conducted by public and accredited nonpublic elementary and secondary schools, regulating active shooter simulations in such schools and modifying the requirements for student cohorts and achievement goals in school district at-risk student accountability plans.
ks:HB 2534.summary: Enacts the Respiratory Care Interstate Compact, letting licensed respiratory therapists in member states practice in other member states, including Kansas, and creating a commission to administer it.

ks:HB 2536.title: Requiring proposed guardians for certain adults who have a cognitive impairment or are diagnosed with a neurological condition to complete training approved by the secretary for aging and disability services prior to appointment as a guardian.
ks:HB 2536.summary: Bars a court from appointing a guardian for an adult with Alzheimer's, dementia or a similar condition until the proposed guardian files an affidavit of completing state-approved training; the court may waive training if in the adult's best interest.

ks:HB 2537.title: Increasing the penalties for the crime of sexual extortion when an offender is 18 years of age or older and the victim is less than 18 years of age or a dependent adult, creating the crimes of aggravated sexual extortion causing great bodily harm and aggravated sexual extortion causing death and requiring the attorney general to prepare and provide educational materials and information concerning such crimes.
ks:HB 2537.summary: Expands sexual extortion to cover threats to distribute sexual or nude images to obtain anything of value, raises penalties when the offender is over 18 and the victim is a minor or dependent adult, and creates aggravated offenses for great bodily harm and death.

ks:HB 2539.title: Authorizing library boards to change from being appointed members to elected members and requiring that the members of the Eudora community library district board of directors be elected to such positions.
ks:HB 2539.summary: Lets a library board, by resolution or a petition of 25 percent of electors, put to voters whether its board members are appointed or elected, and changes how Eudora Community Library District board members are chosen.

ks:HB 2540.title: Exempting contingent deferred annuities from certain requirements of the standard nonforfeiture law for individual deferred annuities act and authorizing the commissioner of insurance to establish nonforfeiture benefits for such contingent deferred annuities through rules and regulations.
ks:HB 2540.summary: Exempts contingent deferred annuities from the standard nonforfeiture law for individual deferred annuities and authorizes the Commissioner of Insurance to adopt rules on nonforfeiture benefits for them.

ks:HB 2552.title: Requiring criminal presentence investigation reports and journal entries to be completed and submitted in the form and manner prescribed and approved by the Kansas sentencing commission.
ks:HB 2552.summary: Requires presentence investigation reports and certain journal entries to be completed and submitted in the form and manner set by the Kansas Sentencing Commission, and bars courts from recognizing those documents if submitted in any other form.

ks:HB 2553.title: Providing for the Kansas PBS distinctive license plate and discontinuing the issuance of certain distinctive and educational institution license plates.
ks:HB 2553.summary: As passed by the House, creates a PBS Kansas distinctive license plate available from January 1, 2027, with a $25 to $100 royalty for use of the logo set by Kansas Public Telecommunications Service, Inc.

ks:HB 2555.title: Requiring grant applications, expenditure information, reports and other documentation concerning the rural health transformation program to be presented and provided to the state finance council, house of representatives committee on appropriations, senate committee on ways and means and legislative budget committee.
ks:HB 2555.summary: Requires Rural Health Transformation Program grant applications, expenditure records and quarterly grantee reports to go to the State Finance Council, and to the House Appropriations, Senate Ways and Means and Legislative Budget committees.

ks:HB 2557.title: Enacting and joining with other states in the interstate compact for the placement of children and authorizing the administration and implementation of the compact.
ks:HB 2557.summary: Enacts the Interstate Compact for the Placement of Children, replacing the current compact in state law, to govern placements of children across state lines.

ks:HB 2560.title: Concerning postsecondary education; authorizing the state board of regents to sell and convey certain real property in the city of Manhattan, Riley county, Kansas, on behalf of Kansas state university, granting authority to state educational institutions regarding transactions involving contracts, easements and the procurement of goods and services, exempting the state educational institutions from statutes governing such transactions and authorizing legislators to request copies of certain documents.
ks:HB 2560.summary: Authorizes sale of specified Kansas State University property in Manhattan by July 1, 2028, with proceeds to a KSU housing fund, and lets state universities adopt board-approved policies exempting them from certain contract, easement and procurement statutes.

ks:HB 2562.title: Permitting the issuance of a special license plate or permanent or temporary placard for a person with a disability based on documentation of satisfactory proof of disability from a physical therapist.
ks:HB 2562.summary: Adds licensed physical therapists to the practitioners who may certify to the Division of Vehicles that a person has a disability, for special license plates or placards.

ks:HB 2564.title: Providing for the election of alternative payment methods by a dental provider and allowing such payment method to remain in force for the duration of a contract with a dental benefit plan.
ks:HB 2564.summary: Requires a dental benefit plan to get a dentist's express written acceptance before paying claims by credit card or electronic funds transfer, keeps the chosen method in effect until changed, and limits certain fees on automated clearing house payments.

ks:HB 2568.title: Authorizing the adoption of certain rules and regulations related to fees, registrations and other charges by the department of wildlife and parks.
ks:HB 2568.summary: Authorizes the wildlife and parks department to adopt proposed permanent rules on motor vehicle permit, camping, utility, and other fees and registrations described in its January 16, 2026 economic impact statement.

ks:HB 2571.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2571 by Committee on Local Government, Transparency and Ethics - Increasing the cost threshold for when a county shall use the public bidding process in awarding a construction contract.
ks:HB 2571.summary: As passed by the House, requires two municipalities whose territory abuts opposite sides of the same road, street or highway to enter a cost-sharing agreement allocating improvement and maintenance duties, and bars material road improvements the agreement does not authorize.

ks:HB 2573.title: Amending statutes concerning the Kansas board of accountancy; relating to licensure requirements for certified public accountants.
ks:HB 2573.summary: Creates an added path to CPA licensure: an accountancy bachelor's degree, two years of work under a licensed CPA, and passing the exam. Also replaces the substantial-equivalency standard for out-of-state CPAs with new recognition provisions.

ks:HB 2574.title: Removing the expiration on certain cybersecurity requirements, modifying the duties of chief information security officers and cybersecurity programs, requiring assessment of executive branch agency compliance with cybersecurity requirements, providing for consideration of such compliance by the legislature during the budget process and creating the judicial branch technology oversight council.
ks:HB 2574.summary: Sets up information technology and cybersecurity administration for each branch of state government and certain elected offices, creates legislative and judicial technology oversight councils, and removes delayed versions of statutes to eliminate sunset provisions enacted in 2024.

ks:HB 2587.title: Authorizing a licensed private psychiatric hospital to maintain a stock supply of emergency medication kits for pharmaceutical emergencies.
ks:HB 2587.summary: Requires driver's licenses to show the holder's citizenship status, and requires a provisional ballot for a person who shows a license listing them as a noncitizen at a polling place and claims to be a citizen.

ks:HB 2588.title: Providing for statewide electrician licensing by the state fire marshal.
ks:HB 2588.summary: Creates the Electrician Licensing Act, moving electrician licensing from cities and counties to the State Fire Marshal on July 1, 2027, with licenses for contractors, master, journeyman and residential electricians and set experience and schooling hours.

ks:HB 2589.title: Prohibiting the secretary for children and families from accepting anonymous reports of child abuse or neglect, requiring the secretary to inform anonymous reporters of such prohibition and other pertinent information regarding reporting child abuse and neglect and allowing law enforcement agencies to accept anonymous reports of child abuse or neglect.
ks:HB 2589.summary: Bars the Department for Children and Families from accepting anonymous child abuse or neglect reports and requires it to tell anonymous reporters so, except it must pass reports of serious physical harm or sexual abuse needing action to law enforcement.

ks:HB 2590.title: Enacting the Kansas community property trust act to authorize the use of community property trusts during the marriage of settlor spouses and amending the Kansas uniform trust code to allow trustees to reimburse settlors of grantor trusts, authorize the use of designated representatives for trusts and permit the terms of a governing instrument to expand, restrict or eliminate certain general rules applicable to fiduciaries, trusts and trust administration.
ks:HB 2590.summary: Creates the Kansas Community Property Trust Act, letting spouses place property in a trust that is treated as community property during the marriage, and amends the Kansas Uniform Trust Code.

ks:HB 2591.title: Authorizing financial institutions to report suspected financial exploitation of an adult account holder to a designated agency, notify any adult designated as a trusted contact by such account holder of suspected financial exploitation and place a temporary hold on certain transactions or disbursements. Enacting the virtual currency kiosk consumer protection act, providing definitions, and establishing requirements for virtual currency kiosk operators. Prohibiting the office of the state bank commissioner or any other state agency from becoming a receiver for a technology-enabled fiduciary financial institution that becomes insolvent or declares bankruptcy. Providing that earned wage access service registrants are subject to the Kansas financial institutions information security act, and eliminating certain stipulations relating to the payment of negotiable instruments on Saturday afternoons or holidays.
ks:HB 2591.summary: Lets financial institutions set up trusted-contact programs, report suspected financial exploitation of adults and delay suspicious transactions; sets rules for virtual currency kiosk operators; bars state receivership of certain fiduciary institutions; covers earned wage access registrants under data security law.

ks:HB 2593.title: Requiring that a political subdivision hold an open meeting to discuss a contingency fee contract for legal services before approving such contract and requiring the attorney general to approve such contracts.
ks:HB 2593.summary: Requires a city, county or other local government to hold a noticed open meeting before approving a contingent-fee contract for legal services, and requires Attorney General approval of the contract. The Attorney General must report to the Governor and Legislature on contracts not approved.

ks:HB 2595.title: Substitute for HB 2595 by Committee on Agriculture and Natural Resources - Enacting the attorney training program for rural Kansas act, providing stipends to law students who meet certain requirements and agree to practice law in rural areas and providing loan forgiveness to lawyers who meet certain requirements and practice law in rural areas, coordination between the department of commerce and the office of judicial administration.
ks:HB 2595.summary: Creates the Attorney Training Program for Rural Kansas, with a law student training and stipend program and incentives for attorneys and KU and Washburn law students to practice in rural counties (all except five metro counties). Program ends July 1, 2031.

ks:HB 2596.title: Permitting the secretary of corrections to enter into certain contracts for the production of manufactured or modular homes for a pilot program at the Hutchinson correctional facility under the prison-made goods act.
ks:HB 2596.summary: Lets the corrections secretary run a pilot program at Hutchinson Correctional Facility contracting for manufactured or modular home production. Private contractors must provide a recognized construction certification program and pay all costs; nonprofits may not seek a property tax exemption.

ks:HB 2601.title: Establishing a registry for child abuse and neglect to be maintained by the secretary for children and families, providing for registration and expungement processes that include administrative hearings and opportunities for subsequent appeals, requiring reports of abuse or neglect to include information regarding a custody dispute concerning the child who is the subject of the report and directing the secretary to submit a report to the legislature on such information.
ks:HB 2601.summary: Creates a child abuse and neglect registry kept by the Department for Children and Families, with notice, an administrative hearing and appeals before a person is listed, and requires abuse reports to include any known custody dispute involving the child.

ks:HB 2602.title: Establishing requirements for a portable benefit plan for independent contractors, determining types of contributions to such plans and providing a subtraction modification for Kansas income tax purposes.
ks:HB 2602.summary: Sets requirements for portable benefit plans for independent contractors, administered by banks, credit unions or similar firms, covering health, disability, life or income replacement insurance or retirement. Lets hiring parties contribute and provides Kansas income tax subtractions for contributions.

ks:HB 2603.title: Prohibiting regulation of battery-charged security fences by municipalities.
ks:HB 2603.summary: Bars local governments from requiring extra permits or fees, or adding installation or operating conditions, for battery-charged security fences on non-residential property that meet the bill's definition. Other alarm-system regulation stays allowed.

ks:HB 2604.title: Including gross vehicle weight in the definitions for classes of commercial motor vehicles for drivers' license purposes and modifying the definition of commercial motor vehicle and creating a definition of air mile and gross vehicle weight in the Kansas uniform commercial drivers' license act.
ks:HB 2604.summary: Adds gross vehicle weight to the definitions of class A, B and C commercial vehicles, aligns Kansas commercial driver's license and registration definitions with federal rules, and defines an "air mile" for the farm CDL exemption.

ks:HB 2606.title: Modifying the definition of conviction in the Kansas uniform commercial drivers' license act.
ks:HB 2606.summary: Changes the definition of "conviction" in the Kansas Uniform Commercial Driver's License Act to align with the definition in federal commercial driver's license standards.

ks:HB 2609.title: Enacting the supported decision-making agreements act to provide a statutory framework for allowing an adult to receive decision-making assistance from one or more other adults, requirements for decision-making agreements and duties related thereto.
ks:HB 2609.summary: Creates the Supported Decision-Making Agreements Act, letting an adult sign an agreement with one or more adult supporters who help them make and communicate decisions and obtain records. Supporters act as fiduciaries and keep information confidential.

ks:HB 2610.title: Limiting the use of a summons instead of a warrant for the arrest of a defendant to misdemeanor crimes and requiring that any bond set on a warrant issued after a failure to appear in response to a summons shall not allow release on the defendant's own recognizance.
ks:HB 2610.summary: Requires a warrant, not a summons, for complaints alleging a felony, and bars release on one's own recognizance for bond set on a warrant issued after failing to appear on a summons.

ks:HB 2613.title: Providing for the crime victims compensation board to establish fees chargeable for conducting examinations of persons who may be victims of sexual assault, authorizing the board to adopt rules and regulations to administer such fees and to use moneys in the crime victims compensation fund for the payment of such fees and allowing certain exceptions to the confidentiality of records and information given to the board.
ks:HB 2613.summary: Makes the Crime Victims Compensation Board, not the county, pay sexual assault examination fees, with the Board setting the fees by rule and payment limited to eligible victims. Also adds exceptions to the confidentiality of records given to the Board.

ks:HB 2614.title: Allowing certain exceptions to the confidentiality of records and information given to the crime victims compensation board.
ks:HB 2614.summary: Adds exceptions to the confidentiality of Crime Victims Compensation Board records: disclosure to law enforcement, prosecutors and DCF for child abuse or neglect investigations, and to law enforcement for false or fraudulent records. Exceptions expire July 1, 2031.

ks:HB 2615.title: Designating a portion of United States highway 75 as the Brig Gen George H Wark memorial highway, a portion of United States highway 56 as the Bill Tucker memorial highway and redesignating a current portion of the purple heart/combat wounded veterans highway for United States highway 75.
ks:HB 2615.summary: Designates a portion of US-56 in Morton County as the Bill Tucker Memorial Highway and a portion of US-75 in Montgomery County as the Brig Gen George H Wark Memorial Highway, with signs funded by donations.

ks:HB 2618.title: Requiring the state board of education to report to the legislature on federal moneys received by the state, ending certain educational reporting requirements and applying expiration dates to other educational reporting requirements.
ks:HB 2618.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to report to the Legislature twice a year on federal education funds received, and sunsets or repeals various other reports by the board and the state education department.

ks:HB 2622.title: Modifying the municipal lease-purchase protest petition requirements.
ks:HB 2622.summary: As passed by the House, changes the protest petition threshold forcing an election on a county, school district or community college lease-purchase from 5 percent of voters in the last secretary of state race to 3 percent of registered voters.

ks:HB 2624.title: Authorizing the disorganization of a county fire district by the board of county commissioners when such district contains no territory.
ks:HB 2624.summary: Lets a board of county commissioners disorganize a county fire district on its own motion when the district has no remaining territory. Current law requires a landowner petition and a four-year wait.

ks:HB 2626.title: Directing the capitol preservation committee to develop and approve plans for a registry kiosk of Kansas military forces killed in action or who died of wounds incurred during active duty to be placed within the state capitol, enacting the safeguarding American veteran empowerment (SAVE) act to limit compensation for assisting in veterans benefits matters, establishing the Kansas military affairs commission and prescribing the powers and duties thereof, expanding veterans preference in government employment to include current members of the national guard and such members' eligible spouses and permissive preference in private employment to include current servicemembers and such members’ eligible spouses.
ks:HB 2626.summary: Expands veteran's preference in government hiring to certain National Guard and reserve members and eligible spouses, creates a Capitol kiosk listing Kansas military members killed in service, creates a Kansas Military Affairs Commission, and limits fees for help with veterans benefits claims.

ks:HB 2627.title: Expanding permissive preference in private employment to include current servicemembers and eligible spouses.
ks:HB 2627.summary: Lets private employers give hiring preference to current Kansas National Guard and reserve members and eligible spouses of servicemembers, in addition to veterans, under the existing permissive preference law.

ks:HB 2633.title: Increasing the service charge fee for each license, permit, stamp or other issue of the department of wildlife and parks to an amount of not to exceed $2.00 and, in the case of each migratory waterfowl habitat stamp, an amount of not to exceed $1.00.
ks:HB 2633.summary: Raises the cap on service charges for wildlife and parks licenses and permits from $1 to $2 (from $0.50 to $1 for the waterfowl habitat stamp) and lets sellers add a fee covering the cost of the payment method used.

ks:HB 2635.title: Enacting the pregnancy center autonomy and rights of expression act to protect the ability of private pregnancy centers to provide life-affirming care.
ks:HB 2635.summary: Bars state and local governments from requiring pregnancy centers to perform, refer for or counsel in favor of abortion, provide abortion-inducing drugs, or post materials promoting abortion or information on obtaining one.

ks:HB 2639.title: Changing the name of juvenile crisis intervention centers to juvenile stabilization centers, modifying the intake criteria and treatment provided at such centers and transferring moneys from the evidence-based programs account of the state general fund for use at such centers.
ks:HB 2639.summary: Renames juvenile crisis intervention centers as juvenile stabilization centers, requires family-focused services and access to faith-based services, changes admission criteria, and transfers Evidence-based Programs Account money to the Department for Children and Families for these centers.

ks:HB 2642.title: Removing obsolete reference to global intangible low-taxed income provided for under the federal internal revenue code in determining Kansas adjusted gross income.
ks:HB 2642.summary: Repeals obsolete language on global intangible low-taxed income from the Kansas income tax subtraction for certain internationally sourced income.

ks:HB 2644.title: Requiring a county appraiser to adjust the value of personal property mobile homes, residential and commercial property upon final determination or obtain a fee simple appraisal if the appraised value exceeds 5% increase over five years.
ks:HB 2644.summary: Extends to residential property and personal property mobile homes a rule that county appraisers must adjust values after a final valuation appeal or order a fee simple appraisal if value rises over 5 percent, and lengthens the period from two to five years.

ks:HB 2647.title: Authorizing the Kansas department of transportation to establish a statewide conduit system for fiber optic transmissions of broadband connections.
ks:HB 2647.summary: Establishes a Statewide Conduit System for fiber optic broadband run by the Department of Transportation, a Kansas Broadband Revolving Fund, and a fee schedule for entities installing or using the system, with annual reports to the Governor and legislative committees.

ks:HB 2651.title: Limiting the use of a summons instead of a warrant for the arrest of a defendant to misdemeanor crimes and requiring that any bond set on a warrant issued after a failure to appear in response to a summons shall not allow release on the defendant's own recognizance.
ks:HB 2651.summary: Requires a warrant, not a summons, for felony complaints, and bars release on a defendant's own recognizance for bonds set on a warrant issued for failing to appear after a summons.

ks:HB 2652.title: Requiring the clerk of the appellate courts to publish monthly a list of cases of the supreme court and court of appeals in which a decision has not been entered and filed within six months of submission and a list of cases in which a petition for review has not been granted or denied within six months of submission.
ks:HB 2652.summary: Requires the Clerk of the Appellate Courts to publish monthly a list of cases undecided or with petitions for review unresolved six months after submission, post it on the Supreme Court website, and send it to legislative leaders, the Attorney General and the Governor.

ks:HB 2655.title: Authorizing the chief judge of each municipal court to establish a specialty court program, providing for expungement when a person has completed the requirements of such program, authorizing judges to waive the fee in expungement cases by reviewing and granting a poverty affidavit and requiring judges to waive the fee for petitions for expungement of municipal arrest records in certain cases.
ks:HB 2655.summary: Lets municipal court chief judges establish specialty court programs, and lets people who complete a program petition to expunge the related conviction and arrest records, filing a poverty affidavit instead of paying the fee.

ks:HB 2663.title: Modifying the requirements for student cohorts and achievement goals for school district at-risk accountability plans.
ks:HB 2663.summary: Changes at-risk student accountability plan cohorts: one cohort becomes fourth-graders, cohorts may be defined by state assessment subgroups or at-risk eligibility, and improvement is required in either English or math rather than both.

ks:HB 2688.title: Providing that a nondisclosure agreement shall not be judicially enforceable in a dispute involving childhood sexual abuse or human trafficking allegations or claims.
ks:HB 2688.summary: Makes nondisclosure agreements unenforceable in court in legal actions involving childhood sexual abuse or human trafficking claims, declares them void as against public policy, and makes victims' identifying information confidential. Applies to agreements made before or after the law.

ks:HB 2700.title: Establishing the Kansas digital right-to-repair act to provide the right for persons who purchase digital electronic equipment to obtain the legal authorization and necessary documentation and parts from original equipment manufacturers to diagnose, maintain and repair such equipment.
ks:HB 2700.summary: Creates a digital right-to-repair law requiring manufacturers to give independent repair providers and owners the parts, tools and documentation they offer authorized repairers, for digital electronic equipment with a wholesale price of at least $50.

ks:HB 2702.title: Providing that applicants for a physician assistant license submit to a criminal record check, providing for the collaboration between physicians and physician assistants and requiring the revocation of a physician assistant license under certain circumstances.
ks:HB 2702.summary: Sets collaboration requirements between physician assistants (also called physician associates) and physicians, and allows the Board of Healing Arts to require fingerprints and a criminal history check from physician assistant license applicants.

ks:HB 2703.title: Enacting the Kansas health insurance affordability transparency act to require a report specifying the financial impact to covered individuals resulting from the passage of certain health insurance legislation.
ks:HB 2703.summary: Creates the Kansas Health Insurance Affordability Transparency Act, requiring the Department of Insurance, at a legislator's request, to report on the financial impact to covered individuals of proposed health insurance legislation.

ks:HB 2711.title: Modifying and updating procedures for dissolution of cities of the third class.
ks:HB 2711.summary: Changes the process for dissolving third-class cities: on a petition of a majority of electors, the council must put the question on the next primary or general election ballot, held at least 60 days after the petition is submitted.

ks:HB 2712.title: Increasing the authority for a countywide retailers' sales tax and providing for the dedicated apportionment of special purpose tax revenues up to 2%, limiting special purpose city and countywide retailers' sales taxes to 10 years and requiring certain reporting to the department of revenue for administration of such tax.
ks:HB 2712.summary: Lets county commissioners put countywide sales taxes of up to 3 percent to voters: up to 1 percent for general purposes and 2 percent for special purposes, in 0.05 percent increments, with notice requirements.

ks:HB 2719.title: Providing an exception to the rules and regulations filing act for technical amendments, creating a process for certain rules and regulations to receive priority status in the adoption process, removing references to revival of rules and regulations, clarifying that the department of the budget is not required to approve proposed rules and regulations mandated by the federal government, adding references to department of corrections rules and regulations that are not subject to the act and requiring an agency submit a proposed rule and regulation to the joint committee on administrative rules and regulations prior to presentation of a bill to the legislature for ratification.
ks:HB 2719.summary: Lets agencies adopt technical amendments, such as corrected cross-references and updated titles, to existing rules without new rulemaking. Sets priority status for some rules, drops references to rule revival, and requires agencies to submit proposed rules to the rules committee before seeking ratification bills.

ks:HB 2727.title: Providing for the plaintiff to elect to limit recovery in claims brought for violations of the woman's-right-to-know act and making the laws providing for medical malpractice screening inapplicable when such election is made.
ks:HB 2727.summary: Lets a plaintiff suing under the Woman's-Right-to-Know Act's informed consent provisions elect to limit recovery to $5,000 in statutory damages, amounts paid to the abortion provider, and attorney fees. If elected, the medical malpractice screening panel laws do not apply.

ks:HB 2729.title: Requiring the Kansas department of health and environment to provide forms and notices to physicians pursuant to the woman's-right-to know act.
ks:HB 2729.summary: Requires abortion informed-consent information to be provided on a form supplied by the Kansas health department, in paper or electronic form. Requires the Act's informed consent and medication abortion reversal notice signs to state they come from the department.

ks:HB 2731.title: Substitute for HB 2731 by Committee on Welfare Reform -Requiring the department of health and environment in coordination with the Kansas department for aging and disability services to seek federal approval to establish continuous medicaid eligibility for certain individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities who are receiving services through a home and community based services waiver, requiring the secretary for children and families and the secretary of health and environment to enter into data-matching agreements with state agencies to verify eligibility for food and medical assistance, directing the department of health and environment to submit certain data to the centers for medicare and medicaid services, prohibiting certain public assistance program waivers or exemptions without legislative approval, prohibiting self-attestation for purposes of determining eligibility for public assistance programs, limiting retroactive enrollment in the medical assistance program, increasing the age limit for able-bodied adults without certain dependents and prohibiting certain exemptions from work requirements under the food assistance program.
ks:HB 2731.summary: Requires Kansas to seek federal approval for continuous Medicaid eligibility for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities on home-based waivers, sets data-matching for food and medical assistance, and bars unverified self-attestation of income, residency and similar facts unless federal law requires.

ks:HB 2732.title: Directing the state registrar of vital statistics to provide death certificates to survivors of deceased veterans with a service-connected disability that state in such certificates the relationship between the cause of death and the service-connected disability of such veterans.
ks:HB 2732.summary: Requires the state registrar to keep a confidential roster of Kansas veterans with service-connected disabilities, and directs death certificate certifiers to determine whether the cause of death was related to a service-connected disability.

ks:HB 2733.title: Requiring any person who is candidate or who has been elected to certain offices shall be and must remain a resident of the state or the appropriate district.
ks:HB 2733.summary: Adds residency requirements for candidates and holders of district attorney, six statewide offices, State Board of Education, school board, community college trustee and township or road district offices; failing to remain a qualified elector there creates an immediate vacancy.

ks:HB 2736.title: Requiring hospitals to screen all patients for eligibility for such hospital's financial assistance program or charity care policy.
ks:HB 2736.summary: Requires non-disproportionate share hospitals to screen all uninsured patients, within 90 days of discharge and before billing, for charity care discounts or financial assistance eligibility; a qualified third-party vendor may do the screening.

ks:HB 2737.title: Enacting the taxpayer agreement act to provide for an alternative method of tax increment financing of municipal economic development projects through taxpayer agreements.
ks:HB 2737.summary: Creates the Taxpayer Agreement Act, letting cities that can use tax increment financing instead enter taxpayer agreements with property developers and issue bonds under them, after getting written consent from existing mortgage or deed of trust holders.
