ks:HB 2738.title: Directing the secretary for children and families to request or update a pending waiver application from the supplemental nutrition assistance program that would allow the state to prohibit the purchase of food commonly marketed, advertised or recognized as candy and soft drinks.
ks:HB 2738.summary: Directs the children and families secretary to request a federal waiver barring purchase of candy and soft drinks with SNAP benefits, to re-request it yearly if denied, and to implement it within six months if granted.

ks:HB 2739.title: Relating to housing code requirements, removing the definition of apartment houses from chapter 31 of the Kansas Statutes Annotated, providing requirements for adoption of the international fire code, 2024 edition, and providing that certain state accessibility standards are not applicable to moderate income housing program and Kansas investor tax credit housing act projects.
ks:HB 2739.summary: Removes apartment houses from State Fire Marshal fire safety rules and repeals the definition of apartment house. Exempts housing financed through two state housing programs from accessibility standards and creates a limited exception to review requirements for Fire Prevention Code updates.

ks:HB 2740.title: Adopting compounding standards established by the United States pharmacopeia and allowing for exemptions from such standards.
ks:HB 2740.summary: Adopts U.S. Pharmacopeia standards 795, 797 and 825 for drug compounding as in effect July 1, 2027, and lets the Board of Pharmacy set exemptions or waivers from them. Takes effect July 1, 2027.

ks:HB 2745.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2745 by Committee on Assessment and Taxation - Providing a protest petition to contest certain increases in property tax revenues and continuing reimbursements from the taxpayer notification costs fund for an additional five years.
ks:HB 2745.summary: Lets voters petition against local budgets whose property tax revenue exceeds last year's plus inflation (capped at 3 percent). If 10 percent of registered voters sign, the budget is disapproved and limited to prior-year property taxes. Moves the school budget deadline to October 1.

ks:HB 2747.title: Specifying that courts shall consider certain factors in determining whether a prior violation of law is comparable to any act described in certain driving under the influence crimes when calculating a person's criminal history score under the Kansas sentencing guidelines act.
ks:HB 2747.summary: Requires courts to consider the offense's name, elements and similarity to the closest Kansas offense when deciding whether an out-of-state or local violation counts as DUI in criminal history scoring. Known as "Sidnee's Law."

ks:HB 2758.title: Directing the capitol preservation committee to develop and approve plans for a registry kiosk of Kansas military forces killed in action or who died of wounds incurred during active duty to be placed within the state capitol.
ks:HB 2758.summary: Requires the Capitol Preservation Committee to approve plans for a permanent kiosk in the Capitol listing Kansas military forces killed in action or dead of wounds, funded only by private gifts through a new fund.

ks:HB 2760.title: Enacting the esthetics licensure compact to provide interstate practice privileges for estheticians.
ks:HB 2760.summary: Enacts the Esthetics Licensure Compact, an agreement among member states that lets licensed estheticians practice in other member states through a multistate licensing system while states keep their own licensing authority.

ks:HB 2761.title: Enacting the speech-language pathology assistant act to provide for the licensure of speech-language pathology assistants.
ks:HB 2761.summary: Creates the Speech-Language Pathology Assistant Licensure Act, providing for state licensure of assistants who work under a supervising speech-language pathologist, defining their scope of practice and qualifications, with licenses expiring after two years.

ks:HB 2762.title: Modifying the crime of unlawful sexual relations to describe who is a person in a position of authority for a school.
ks:HB 2762.summary: Defines a "person in a position of authority for a school" for the crime of unlawful sexual relations to include non-student volunteers, service providers and contractors (or their employees) delegated authority to interact with students. The offense remains a severity level 5 person felony.

ks:HB 2763.title: Requiring school districts to provide elementary students with a certain amount of daily recess, prohibiting limiting or withholding recess for disciplinary reasons, requiring a Kansas state fitness test and designating required recess time as part of the school term.
ks:HB 2763.summary: Requires public school districts to give elementary students 30 minutes of organized recess daily from 2027-28, bars withholding recess as discipline unless a student is an immediate threat, and requires an annual state physical fitness test for grades 1 through 12.

ks:HB 2767.title: Establishing the Kansas military affairs commission and prescribing the powers and duties thereof.
ks:HB 2767.summary: Creates the Kansas Military Affairs Commission in the governor’s office, with voting and nonvoting members, as the continuation of the Governor’s Military Council.

ks:HB 2769.title: Requiring members of governing bodies of subordinate service taxing areas to be residents of such taxing areas.
ks:HB 2769.summary: Requires voting members of an appointed governing body of a subordinate service taxing area to live in that area when it levies a property tax or sets a budget; nonresident members serve as nonvoting.

ks:HB 2773.title: Providing for the apportionment of business income by manufacturers of alcoholic liquor depending on whether the taxpayer is a qualifying Kansas investor or a general manufacturer.
ks:HB 2773.summary: Requires alcoholic liquor manufacturers with at least $5 million in Kansas property and over $2 million in Kansas pay to use single sales factor apportionment for corporate income tax from 2027. Other such manufacturers keep the three-factor formula.

ks:HB 2781.title: Authorizing the state historical society to acquire the junior officers' quarters at Fort Dodge and provide for the use, preservation, improvement, control and maintenance thereof.
ks:HB 2781.summary: Authorizes the state historical society to acquire the Junior Officers' Quarters at Fort Dodge from the Office of Veterans Services, requires it to maintain the site as a historical landmark, and lets it adopt rules for its use and upkeep.

ks:HB 2788.title: Establishing the business enterprise program oversight task force to review state administration of priority placement for blind vendors on state property, allowing audits on the administration of such program, abolishing the vending facilities account outside the state treasury, establishing the business enterprise program fund in the Kansas department for children and families in the state treasury and transferring moneys from the vending facilities account to the business enterprise program fund.
ks:HB 2788.summary: Creates a task force to study and recommend changes to the state's Business Enterprise Program for blind vendors, requires fiscal and performance audits of the program, and renames its advisory committee the Committee of Blind Vendors.

ks:HB 2793.title: Enacting the Kansas sports authority act to establish a sports authority to provide for the construction, financing and management of certain sports facilities and sports facility infrastructure and create venues for professional sports and other events.
ks:HB 2793.summary: Creates the Kansas Sports Facilities Authority, a state-created body with 11 voting members, to build and manage a sports facility and related infrastructure for a National Football League team’s home games.

ks:HB 2798.title: Substitute for HB 2798 by Committee on Higher Education Budget - Granting authority to state educational institutions regarding transactions involving contracts, easements and the procurement of goods and services, exempting the state educational institutions from statutes governing such transactions and authorizing legislators to request copies of certain documents.
ks:HB 2798.summary: Lets Kansas's six state universities adopt Board of Regents-approved policies on contracts, easements, procurement, and surplus property, exempting them from the state statutes that currently govern those transactions.

ks:HCR 5001.title: Making application to the congress of the United States to call a convention of the states to establish term limits for members of congress.
ks:HCR 5001.summary: Applies to Congress under Article V of the U.S. Constitution to call a convention of the states limited to proposing a constitutional amendment setting term limits for members of Congress.

ks:HCR 5004.title: Proposing an amendment to section 1 of article 5 of the constitution of the state of Kansas to require individuals to be citizens of the United States, at least 18 years of age and a resident of the voting area in which such person seeks to vote in order to vote in this state.
ks:HCR 5004.summary: Proposes amending the Kansas Constitution to state that a person is a qualified elector only if they are a U.S. citizen, at least 18, and a resident of the voting area, subject to any residency exception.

ks:HCR 5008.title: Proposing to amend section 1 of article 11 of the constitution of the state of Kansas to value residential real, commercial and industrial real property and mobile homes property based on the fair market value or average fair market value of the residential portion and providing the legislature the authority to establish valuation limits for any classes or subclasses of property.
ks:HCR 5008.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, from tax year 2028, taxing residential, commercial, industrial and farm-building property at the lesser of fair market value or average fair market value, and letting the Legislature set valuation limits for property classes.

ks:HCR 5011.title: Proposing to amend section 1 of article 11 of the constitution of the state of Kansas to provide that valuations of residential property, commercial and industrial real property and mobile homes personal property shall be determined based on the lesser of the fair market value or the average fair market value.
ks:HCR 5011.summary: Proposes a Kansas constitutional amendment limiting yearly growth in taxable value of real property and residential mobile homes to 4 percent, with exceptions for new construction, class changes and other listed events.

ks:HCR 5013.title: Urging Congress to give state insurance regulators authority over Medicare Advantage plans.
ks:HCR 5013.summary: Urges Congress to give state insurance regulators authority over Medicare Advantage plans and to let states enforce their own marketing and consumer disclosure laws on those plans.

ks:HCR 5022.title: Making application to the congress of the United States to call a convention of the states to establish term limits for members of congress.
ks:HCR 5022.summary: Applies to Congress under Article V of the U.S. Constitution to call a convention of the states limited to proposing a constitutional amendment setting term limits for members of Congress.

ks:HCR 5031.title: Ratifying and providing for the continuation of the state of disaster emergency declaration issued on February 9, 2026, for Douglas, Johnson and Wyandotte counties.
ks:HCR 5031.summary: Ratifies the governor's February 9, 2026 disaster emergency declaration for Douglas, Johnson and Wyandotte counties, issued over 2026 FIFA World Cup impacts, and continues it through July 30, 2026.

ks:HCR 5033.title: Ratifying and providing for the continuation of the state of disaster emergency declaration issued on February 24, 2026, for certain counties.
ks:HCR 5033.summary: Ratifies the Governor's February 24, 2026 wildfire disaster emergency declaration for 77 counties and extends it through March 25, 2026; without ratification it would last no more than 15 days.

ks:SB 1.title: Exempting the state of Kansas from daylight saving time but providing for moving to permanent daylight saving time upon an act of Congress requiring such move.
ks:SB 1.summary: As amended, exempts Kansas from daylight saving time and adopts permanent standard time if Missouri does the same, and moves Kansas to permanent daylight saving time if federal law adopts it.

ks:SB 10.title: Providing property tax exemptions for certain personal property including watercraft, marine equipment, off-road vehicles, motorized bicycles and certain trailers.
ks:SB 10.summary: As amended, exempts from property taxes beginning in tax year 2026 items such as watercraft, off-road vehicles not used on highways, golf carts, motorized bicycles and scooters, light personal-use trailers, and aircraft.

ks:SB 104.title: Granting the Shawnee county board of county commissioners the discretion to create a citizens commission on local government.
ks:SB 104.summary: Lets, rather than requires, counties with 170,000 to 200,000 residents create a citizens commission on local government. Only Shawnee County currently falls in that range.

ks:SB 105.title: Requiring the governor to appoint a person to fill vacancies in the offices of United States senator, state treasurer and commissioner of insurance from a list of names approved by the legislature.
ks:SB 105.summary: Creates a 12-member Joint Committee on Vacancy Appointments to recommend three candidates for vacancies in the U.S. Senate, state treasurer and insurance commissioner offices. Requires the governor to appoint one, who must have been registered in the prior officeholder's party for six years.

ks:SB 114.title: Authorizing nonpublic and virtual school students to participate in ancillary public school activities and making it unlawful for the Kansas state high school activities association and school districts to discriminate against such students based on enrollment status.
ks:SB 114.summary: Lets nonpublic and virtual school students in KSHSAA activities also take part in district events and programs directly related to the activity, and lets school boards set policies for other district events.

ks:SB 117.title: Expanding the property tax exemption for Strother field airport property.
ks:SB 117.summary: Expands the property tax exemption for Strother Field Airport to property owned by the political subdivisions that make up the airport commission, whenever acquired, if used for aviation purposes, aviation commerce or to raise revenue for the airport.

ks:SB 121.title: Authorizing the commissioner of insurance to select and announce the version of certain instructions, calculations and documents in effect for the upcoming calendar year and cause such announcement to be published in the Kansas register, allowing certain life insurers to follow health financial reports and adopting certain provisions from the national association of insurance commissioners holding company system regulatory act relating to group capital calculations and liquidity stress testing.
ks:SB 121.summary: Requires the insurance commissioner to announce by December 1 which version of national insurance calculations and instructions applies next year, adds certain self-funded health plans to those exempt from the Insurance Code, and amends risk-based capital and holding company provisions.

ks:SB 126.title: House Sub for SB 126 - Establishing an advance universal newborn screening program, providing for the reimbursement of certain treatment services and extending the transfer of moneys to the Kansas newborn screening fund, increasing state financial assistance for local health departments under certain circumstances and increasing the annual assessment rate on hospital providers.
ks:SB 126.summary: Updates newborn screening as the Advance Universal Newborn Screening Program with screening, follow-up and treatment products, raises minimum state aid to local health departments from $7,000 to $12,000, and raises the hospital provider assessment, extending it to larger critical access and rural emergency hospitals.

ks:SB 128.title: Creating an exception to certain mandatory reporting obligations for licensed social workers when working under the supervision of an attorney and permitting an attorney to require a licensed social worker to keep ethical obligations of attorney-client privilege while working under the supervision of such attorney.
ks:SB 128.summary: Exempts licensed social workers supervised by an attorney from mandatory abuse reporting when the suspicion of harm to a child or vulnerable adult arises solely during representation of a client or prospective client.

ks:SB 13.title: Eliminating requirements for filings, registrations and licenses related to labor organizations, educational facility agreements, annual tax reports, river bank easements and bonded warehousemen with the secretary of state.
ks:SB 13.summary: Removes several Secretary of State filing requirements, including labor organization bylaws and reports, Regents reciprocal facility agreements, certain Revenue Department tax reports, stream bank easements and bonded warehouseman filings.

ks:SB 135.title: Providing precedence of child-related orders issued under the protection from abuse act.
ks:SB 135.summary: Rewrites the Protection from Abuse Act section on child-related orders to refer to an "order issued in any action," without changing which order takes precedence.

ks:SB 138.title: Requiring search warrants to be issued only on the statement of facts sufficient to show probable cause made by a law enforcement officer.
ks:SB 138.summary: Allows only law enforcement officers, rather than any person, to give the sworn statement of facts supporting probable cause for a search warrant.

ks:SB 14.title: Providing for continuous state budgets until amended, lapsed or eliminated by the legislature, temporary reallocations and establishing conditions and limitations.
ks:SB 14.summary: Carries existing appropriations into each next fiscal year unless the Legislature changes them, lets the Secretary of Administration lapse unneeded executive-branch continuing appropriations, and allows temporary transfers between funds.

ks:SB 146.title: Requiring the secretary for aging and disability services and the city of Osawatomie to execute and record an amendment to the original deed for conveyance of certain real property in Miami county that amends the reversionary interest of the state of Kansas to July 1, 2046.
ks:SB 146.summary: Directs the aging and disability services secretary to amend the Osawatomie deed so the state's reversion right over land not used for economic development moves from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2046.

ks:SB 156.title: Increasing the reimbursement amount of money that the secretary of corrections may make to inmates for losses for personal injury or property damage or loss caused by negligence and requiring notice to the secretary for claims exceeding the reimbursement maximum.
ks:SB 156.summary: Raises the limit on inmate property-loss or injury claims the Secretary of Corrections may reimburse from $500 to $750, and requires inmates to give notice of the nature, time, date and place of claims above $750.

ks:SB 157.title: Requiring search warrants to be issued only on the statement of facts sufficient to show probable cause made by a law enforcement officer, warrants issued for failure to appear to be provided to a compensated surety, bond forfeiture to be set aside in certain circumstances and remission if the defendant is returned to custody in certain circumstances and prohibiting a compensated surety from making loans for certain portions of the required minimum appearance bond premium.
ks:SB 157.summary: Allows only law enforcement officers to give the sworn statements supporting probable cause for search warrants. Also requires courts to give failure-to-appear warrants to the bail bond surety on request, changes when bond forfeitures are set aside, and requires partial bond return in some cases.

ks:SB 161.title: Requiring legislative approval prior to any state agency seeking or implementing a public assistance program waiver or other authorization from the federal government that expands eligibility for any public assistance program or increases cost to the state or making certain changes in services for persons with intellectual or developmental disabilities..
ks:SB 161.summary: As amended, bars state agencies, on or after July 1, 2025, from seeking federal public assistance waivers that expand eligibility or raise state costs, or changing disability-service funding, day services or case management, without legislative approval (or Legislative Coordinating Council approval when not in session).

ks:SB 166.title: Enacting the fostering competitive career opportunities act to remove postsecondary degree requirements from state employment considerations.
ks:SB 166.summary: Prohibits state employers from basing hiring decisions solely on lack of a postsecondary degree unless a degree is justifiably necessary. Requires job postings to list baseline requirements and any assessments that can show competence. Excludes legislative and judicial branch employers.

ks:SB 175.title: Updating the definition of athletic trainer and providing an exemption for those licensed in another state, District of Columbia, territory or foreign country to practice in Kansas.
ks:SB 175.summary: Broadens the definition of athletic training to cover sports, exercise, fitness and recreational activity, exempts out-of-state athletic trainers who travel with a visiting team and serve only its members, and changes license application requirements.

ks:SB 179.title: Establishing a child income tax credit.
ks:SB 179.summary: As introduced, creates a refundable state income tax credit for each child under six, from $600 at Kansas adjusted gross income up to $25,000 down to $25 above $350,000, starting in tax year 2025 and adjusted for cost of living.

ks:SB 18.title: Providing for the hunter nation distinctive license plate.
ks:SB 18.summary: Authorizes a Hunter Nation license plate starting January 1, 2026, for passenger vehicles and trucks up to 20,000 pounds. Hunter Nation, Inc. sets a royalty of $25 to $100, paid at issuance and renewal.

ks:SB 181.title: House Substitute for SB 181 by Committee on Appropriations - Making and concerning appropriations for fiscal year 2027 for various state agencies, authorizing certain capital improvement projects and fees and authorizing certain transfers.
ks:SB 181.summary: Limits annual growth in State General Fund spending and transfers to the prior year's amount adjusted for Midwest CPI and Kansas population growth, starting in FY 2027, with the limit certified each year by the State Treasurer.

ks:SB 184.title: Amending the Kansas drycleaner environmental response act to modify the penalties for violations of the act, the required deductible rate for corrective actions, the environmental surcharge rate, the solvent fee and the delinquency penalty related to environmental surcharges and solvent fees.
ks:SB 184.summary: Raises the drycleaner cleanup fund deductible from $5,000 to $10,000 and the drycleaning surcharge from 2.5 to 5 percent, and lets the health and environment secretary impose penalties up to $10,000 per violation under the Drycleaner Environmental Response Act.

ks:SB 186.title: Modifying elements in the crimes of sexual exploitation of a child, unlawful transmission of a visual depiction of a child and breach of privacy, prohibiting certain acts related to visual depictions in which the person depicted is indistinguishable from a real child, morphed from a real child's image or generated without any actual child involvement, prohibiting dissemination of certain items that appear to depict or purport to depict an identifiable person, requiring affidavits or sworn testimony in support of probable cause to be made available to law enforcement, requiring the statement of facts sufficient to show probable cause justifying a search warrant to be made by a law enforcement officer, requiring that certain prior convictions be considered when bond is being set for certain sex offenses and specifying minimum requirements and conditions for such bond; relating to appearance bonds, requiring warrants for failure to appear to be given to sureties, allowing bond forfeiture to be set aside in certain circumstances and requiring remission in certain circumstances and prohibiting a compensated surety from making a loan for certain portions of the minimum appearance bond premium required.
ks:SB 186.summary: As amended by the House committee, requires probable-cause affidavits for warrants to be made available to law enforcement, requires magistrates to determine prior convictions when setting bond for certain sex offenses, and sets a $750,000 minimum bond if a prior sexually violent conviction is found.

ks:SB 193.title: Sub for SB 193 by Committee on Public Health and Welfare - Exempting law enforcement agencies who do not provide emergency opioid antagonists pursuant to the statewide protocol from the requirement to procure a physician medical director.
ks:SB 193.summary: Exempts law enforcement agencies from the Statewide Opioid Antagonist Protocol's requirement to use a physician medical director or pharmacist, unless the agency uses an opioid antagonist dispensed under the protocol.

ks:SB 194.title: Providing that covenants, conditions or restrictions established between January 1, 1948, and December 31, 1958, that restrict the use of real property owned by state educational institutions for only single-family residence purposes and contain discriminatory provisions to restrict ownership or tenancy by race are against public policy and therefore void.
ks:SB 194.summary: Voids covenants set between 1948 and 1958 that limit property owned by Board of Regents institutions to single-family residences and contain race-based restrictions on ownership or tenancy.

ks:SB 197.title: House Substitute for Substitute for SB 197 by Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development - Setting visitor origin requirements for STAR bond projects and providing for enforcement of such requirements, expanding transparency of such projects, authorizing the Kansas development finance authority to issue bonds for such projects, making certain other changes and extending the expiration date of the STAR bonds financing act.
ks:SB 197.summary: Creates the No-Impact Home-Based Business Fairness Act, allowing qualifying home businesses in residential dwellings. Bars cities and counties from requiring permits, licenses, variances or rezoning for them, while allowing health, safety, legal-compliance and tax regulations. Excludes animal breeding and short-term rentals.

ks:SB 199.title: Designating the existing fallen firefighters memorial within the Kansas firefighters museum in Wichita as the official fallen firefighters memorial of the state of Kansas and replacing the Kansas firefighters memorial advisory committee with the Kansas firefighter memorial council; defining the fireworks sales season for seasonal retailers of consumer fireworks, providing for year-round sales by permanent retailers of consumer fireworks, requiring permanent retailers to register with the state fire marshal.
ks:SB 199.summary: Allows year-round fireworks sales by retailers registered with the State Fire Marshal, designates the Wichita Fallen Firefighters Memorial as the state's official memorial, and replaces the advisory committee with a Kansas Firefighter Memorial Council.

ks:SB 2.title: Validating the election results for the bond issuance question submitted by the board of education of USD 200, Greeley county, at a special election held on May 21, 2024.
ks:SB 2.summary: Declares valid the May 21, 2024 election approving up to $4.6 million in bonds for USD 200 (Greeley County). Limits the website-posting requirement for bond election notices to counties whose election office has a website.

ks:SB 20.title: Enacting the Kansas consumer prescription protection and accountability act and providing for regulation and registration of pharmacy benefits managers.
ks:SB 20.summary: Regulates pharmacy benefit managers: requires them to charge plans what they pay pharmacies, use the monthly NADAC drug cost survey, and reimburse pharmacies at least NADAC plus a $10.50 dispensing fee. Also sets audit, reporting and examination rules.

ks:SB 21.title: Amending the Kansas parimutuel racing act regarding qualifications for an organization license, the definition of horsemen's associations and horsemen's nonprofit organizations and the distribution of certain tax revenues.
ks:SB 21.summary: Removes location limits for horsemen's groups seeking horse racing licenses, bars them from operating historical horse race machines, delays their live racing until March 2028 (except at Eureka Downs), and redirects State Racing Fund money.

ks:SB 211.title: Modifying member appointments to the wildlife and parks commission, authorizing the commission to direct the secretary to develop or report on rules and regulations and allowing members to submit potential rules and regulations to the commission.
ks:SB 211.summary: As amended, changes Wildlife and Parks Commission appointments to four regional seats appointed by the governor, one at-large member each from the House speaker and Senate president, keeps the attorney general's at-large member, and changes how proposed rules are developed.

ks:SB 213.title: Prohibiting nonresidents from hunting migratory waterfowl during certain times and places and increasing fees for migratory waterfowl habitat stamps.
ks:SB 213.summary: Bars nonresidents from hunting migratory waterfowl on state lands and certain federal reservoirs and refuges except on Sundays, Mondays and Tuesdays, with exceptions for walk-in areas, navigable rivers and the light goose conservation order.

ks:SB 216.title: Establishing the Kansas paid sick time act, setting accrual, usage and employer obligations regarding earned paid sick time and making it unlawful for employers to retaliate against employees exercising rights under the act.
ks:SB 216.summary: As introduced, creates the Kansas Paid Sick Time Act, requiring employers to let employees earn paid sick time at their regular pay, carry over up to 80 hours, and use it for health and safety reasons, with anti-retaliation protections.

ks:SB 218.title: Increasing the Kansas minimum wage of employees.
ks:SB 218.summary: As introduced, raises the Kansas minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour on January 1, 2026, then adjusts it each year for cost of living starting in 2027.

ks:SB 22.title: Requiring title agents to make their audit reports available for inspection instead of submitting such reports annually, requiring the amount of surety bonds filed with the commissioner of insurance to be $100,000 and eliminating the controlled business exemption in certain counties.
ks:SB 22.summary: Lets title insurance agents keep annual audit reports available on request instead of filing them with the insurance commissioner, requires a $100,000 surety bond or letter of credit regardless of county size, and removes the controlled business exemption in counties of 10,000 or fewer people.

ks:SB 222.title: Prohibiting deference to a state agency's interpretation of a statute, rule or regulation or document by a state court or an officer hearing an administrative action.
ks:SB 222.summary: As amended, bars state courts and administrative hearing officers from deferring to a state agency's interpretation of statutes, rules and binding documents, requiring them to decide meaning de novo while allowing them to consider the agency's view.

ks:SB 229.title: House Substitute for SB 229 by Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development - Providing amendments, suspensions or repeals of employment security law provisions should follow specified review procedures by the legislature, authorizing the secretary of labor to recognize and approve employer-sponsored supplemental unemployment benefit plans if such plans meet specific criteria and integrating such plans into the employment security law, updating and reorganizing statutory language, enhancing federal conformity by incorporating references to federal laws and guidelines, updating temporary unemployment provisions and providing for eight weeks of temporary unemployment benefits, eliminating debt relief provisions for negative balance employers and other updates to the employment security law.
ks:SB 229.summary: Ends the unemployment insurance provision that writes off and forgives part of the negative balances of certain employers' accounts.

ks:SB 23.title: Requiring agents and insurers to respond to inquiries from the commissioner of insurance within 14 calendar days and authorizing certain rebate pilot programs to exceed one year in duration.
ks:SB 23.summary: Specifies that agents and insurers must answer Insurance Department inquiries within 14 calendar days, adds an insurer's failure to respond as grounds to deny, suspend or revoke a license, and lets the commissioner extend one-year pilot or testing periods for value-added products.

ks:SB 232.title: Establishing the born to invest act and requiring the office of vital statistics to provide data to the office of the state treasurer for distribution of informational materials regarding certain government-administered savings accounts.
ks:SB 232.summary: Requires the Office of Vital Statistics to give the State Treasurer data on children born in Kansas, and lets the Treasurer send families information on federal Trump Accounts for children born from 2025, 529 college savings accounts and ABLE accounts.

ks:SB 237.title: Authorizing law enforcement officers to conduct investigations of violations of the scrap metal theft reduction act.
ks:SB 237.summary: Authorizes Kansas law enforcement officers to investigate violations of the Scrap Metal Theft Reduction Act and requires investigative reports to be sent to the Attorney General.

ks:SB 24.title: Expanding the postsecondary educational institutions eligible to participate in the Kansas promise scholarship program and increasing the maximum annual appropriation limit.
ks:SB 24.summary: From July 1, 2026, lets nationally accredited Kansas institutions recognized by the Board of Regents and eligible for federal Title IV aid join the Kansas Promise Scholarship, and raises the program's maximum appropriation from $10 million to $15 million.

ks:SB 241.title: Providing that restrictive covenants in certain contracts are enforceable and not considered a restraint of trade in certain circumstances.
ks:SB 241.summary: Makes certain written restrictive covenants, such as non-solicitation and notice-of-termination agreements, not a restraint of trade and presumed enforceable. Requires courts to modify overbroad covenants and enforce them as modified.

ks:SB 244.title: House Substitute for SB 244 by Committee on Judiciary - Requiring the designation of multiple-occupancy private spaces in public buildings for use by only one sex and imposing criminal and civil penalties for violations, defining the term "gender" to mean biological sex at birth for purposes of statutory construction, directing the division of vehicles to invalidate and reissue driver's licenses when necessary to correct the gender identification on such licenses and directing the office of vital statistics to invalidate and reissue birth certificates when necessary to correct the sex identification on such certificates.
ks:SB 244.summary: Requires public buildings to designate restrooms, locker rooms and similar shared spaces for one sex, with civil and criminal penalties; defines gender as biological sex at birth; and invalidates, then corrects, driver's licenses and birth certificates issued earlier that list a different sex.

ks:SB 250.title: Enacting the right to try for individualized treatments act to permit a manufacturer to make an individualized investigative treatment available to a requesting patient.
ks:SB 250.summary: Creates the Right to Try for Individualized Treatments Act, letting manufacturers at eligible facilities provide individualized investigational drugs, biologics or devices to patients with life-threatening or severely debilitating illnesses, with consent rules and liability exemptions.

ks:SB 254.title: Prohibiting aliens who are unlawfully present in the United States from receiving any state or local public benefit in accordance with applicable federal law.
ks:SB 254.summary: Bars people unlawfully present in the U.S. from state or local public benefits, except those federal law requires. Requires applicants 18 or older to prove lawful presence, agencies to verify through the federal SAVE program, and bars reduced in-state tuition for them.

ks:SB 259.title: Providing that future personal and corporate income tax rate decreases be contingent on exceeding tax receipt revenues.
ks:SB 259.summary: As amended, lowers state income and privilege tax rates when state general fund tax receipts exceed the FY 2024 amount adjusted for inflation, as determined each year by the budget director by August 15.

ks:SB 260.title: House Subsitute for SB 260 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Relating to campaign finance; concerning a vacancy in the joint candidacy of the governor and lieutenant governor; relating to reasons for withdrawal of candidacy from national, state and local offices; relating to the election of the board of directors of certain irrigation districts; specifying when such elections may be conducted by the mail ballot election law; relating to the crime of corrupt political advertising; removing the requirements that treasurers be listed in political advertising attributions; clarifying campaign finance reports regarding vendor information.
ks:SB 260.summary: Changes election and campaign finance law: lets some local candidates withdraw for severe medical hardship, sets rules for a vacancy in the Governor and Lieutenant Governor joint candidacy, changes paid-for attributions and vendor expenditure rules, and sets irrigation district board elections.

ks:SB 263.title: House Substitute for SB 263 by Committee on Education - Establishing standards and requirements for active shooter drills conducted by public and accredited nonpublic elementary and secondary schools and regulating active shooter simulations.
ks:SB 263.summary: Creates the Student Safe at School Act: requires 24-hour parent notice and opt-out for active shooter drills, bans active shooter simulations in grades K-8 except certain law enforcement exercises, and has the education department write best-practice guidelines.

ks:SB 269.title: Providing that future income tax and privilege tax rate decreases be contingent on exceeding revenue estimates and retaining a certain amount in the budget stabilization fund.
ks:SB 269.summary: Makes future state income and privilege tax rate cuts depend on General Fund receipts exceeding the inflation-adjusted FY 2024 amount, and bars cuts when the Budget Stabilization Fund is under 15 percent of prior-year tax revenue.

ks:SB 27.title: Eliminating the requirement that the commissioner submit certain reports to the governor and removing certain specific entities from the definition of person for the purpose of enforcing insurance law.
ks:SB 27.summary: Removes the requirement that the insurance commissioner send an annual report to the governor, requiring publication on the department website instead, and narrows the definition of person used in enforcing insurance law.

ks:SB 271.title: Updating income eligibility requirements for the state children's health insurance program and requiring the Robert G. (Bob) Bethell joint committee on home and community based services and KanCare oversight hold meetings each quarter.
ks:SB 271.summary: Bases children's health insurance (CHIP) eligibility at 250% of the current federal poverty guidelines instead of the 2008 level, requires sliding-scale premiums, and requires the KanCare oversight joint committee to meet at least quarterly.

ks:SB 28.title: Updating public adjuster and insurance agent statutes pertaining to suspension, revocation, denial of licensure and licensure renewal.
ks:SB 28.summary: Lets the insurance commissioner check the status of related licenses when reviewing insurance agent and public adjuster applications, suspend or revoke public adjuster licenses for not answering inquiries within 15 business days, and sets criteria for reviewing criminal convictions.

ks:SB 281.title: House Substitute for Substitute for SB 281 by Committee on Education - Requiring school districts to prohibit the use of personal electronic communication devices during school hours, prohibiting any employee of a school district from using social media to directly communicate with any student for official school purposes.
ks:SB 281.summary: Requires public school districts, and permits accredited nonpublic schools, to adopt policies banning student cell phone use during the school day, with phones turned off and stowed, sets enforcement procedures, and provides indemnity for lost or damaged devices.

ks:SB 284.title: Enacting the defense of drug delivery act to prohibit manufacturer interference relating to 340B drug distribution.
ks:SB 284.summary: Creates the Defense of Drug Delivery Act, barring limits on delivery of 340B discount drugs to covered entities and manufacturer demands for extra health information, with attorney general rules, civil penalties and pharmacy board complaint investigations.

ks:SB 29.title: Substitute for SB 29 by Committee on Public Health and Welfare - Removing the authority of the county or joint board of health or local health officer to prohibit public gatherings when necessary for the control of infectious or contagious disease.
ks:SB 29.summary: Requires the health secretary to have probable cause under oath before restricting people's movement to stop disease spread, allows civil suits over health orders, limits local boards to recommending against gatherings, and ends officials' power to order law enforcement help.

ks:SB 299.title: Requiring the supreme court nominating commission to release certain records under the Kansas open records act.
ks:SB 299.summary: Bars the Kansas Supreme Court and its Nominating Commission from adopting rules that keep the Commission’s records confidential, making them open, but allows background check and sensitive financial information on applicants to stay closed.

ks:SB 30.title: Providing for occupational licensing annual reports by agencies to the joint committee on administrative rules and regulations and requiring that adoption of new occupational licenses and material changes to existing occupational licenses by a state agency be approved by the legislature by ratification.
ks:SB 30.summary: Requires the Legislature to ratify, by enacting a bill, new occupational licenses and material changes to existing ones proposed by covered state agencies. Requires those agencies to report annually to the rules and regulations committee. Several health licensing boards are exempt.

ks:SB 300.title: Providing for the apportionment of business income by manufacturers of alcoholic liquor depending on whether the taxpayer is a qualifying Kansas investor or a general manufacturer and removing obsolete reference to global intangible low-taxed income provided for under the federal internal revenue code in determining Kansas adjusted gross income.
ks:SB 300.summary: Requires alcoholic liquor manufacturers with at least $5 million in average Kansas property and over $2 million in Kansas pay to apportion corporation income tax by sales alone starting 2027; others keep the three-factor formula. Repeals obsolete GILTI language.

ks:SB 303.title: House Substitute for SB 303 by Committee on Taxation - Decreasing the rate of ad valorem tax imposed by a school district, discontinuing certain sales tax exemptions, imposing sales tax on certain sales of lottery tickets, imposing an excise tax on all sports wagers as a rate of 2% of the amount wagered, creating the property tax relief fund and providing for transfers therefrom to the state school district finance fund and creating the sports wagering privilege tax refund fund.
ks:SB 303.summary: As passed by the Senate, authorizes Labette, Leavenworth, Lincoln and Sheridan counties to put additional countywide sales taxes to voters for fire departments, emergency management, county facilities and a law enforcement center. Proceeds stay with the county.

ks:SB 304.title: Establishing the born to invest act and requiring the office of vital statistics to provide data to the office of the state treasurer for the distribution of informational materials regarding certain government-administered savings accounts.
ks:SB 304.summary: Creates the Born to Invest Act, requiring the State Treasurer to publish information on Section 529, ABLE and 530A savings accounts and the Office of Vital Statistics to give the Treasurer newborn data for mailing informational materials.

ks:SB 317.title: Providing additional requirements for applications to the water technical assistance fund and the water projects grant fund, including the requirement that applicants demonstrate the availability of a 25-year water supply, prohibiting grants for issues related to water rights that are impaired by another other water right, prioritizing applications based on various criteria and mandating annual submissions on September 15.
ks:SB 317.summary: Requires Water Technical Assistance Fund grant applications to include a preliminary engineering report, and requires at least half of annual transfers to the fund to go to municipalities with fewer than 8,000 residents when enough applicants exist.

ks:SB 32.title: Reducing insurance company premium tax rates and discontinuing remittance and crediting of a portion of the premium tax to the insurance department service regulation fund.
ks:SB 32.summary: Lowers the insurance company premium tax rate from 2.0 to 1.98 percent beginning with tax year 2026, and stops transferring part of the tax to the Insurance Department Service Regulation Fund starting January 1, 2026.

ks:SB 321.title: Designating certain bridges on U.S. highway 69 and 18th street expressway in Johnson county as the Representative Robert M Tomlinson memorial bridge, a bridge on interstate 135 in Sedgwick county as the Don Snyder memorial bridge, a portion of interstate 35 as the deputy Sam Smith memorial highway, a portion of U.S. highway 36 as the undersheriff Brandon Gaede memorial highway, a portion of K-49 highway as the Pvt Michael E Gerber memorial highway and redesignating a current portion of the 35th infantry division memorial highway for interstate 35.
ks:SB 321.summary: Designates memorial bridges in Johnson and Sedgwick counties and memorial highways in Franklin, Sumner and Phillips counties, with signs to be placed once donations cover costs. Removes a segment of I-35 from the 35th Infantry Division Memorial Highway.

ks:SB 322.title: Removing the authority of the state board of pharmacy to authorize individuals to access the prescription monitoring program database by rules and regulations.
ks:SB 322.summary: Removes the State Board of Pharmacy's authority to set, by rule, the list of people allowed to access the K-TRACS prescription monitoring database.

ks:SB 325.title: Creating the vehicle services modernization task force, providing limitations on expenditures of county treasurer motor vehicle fee funds and authorizing county treasurers to charge certain increased fees for vehicle registration transactions.
ks:SB 325.summary: Creates a 15-member Vehicle Services Modernization Task Force, limits use of the county treasurer special fund for registration costs, renames certain vehicle registration fees, and lets counties raise a transaction fee to no more than $10 in 2027 through 2029.

ks:SB 327.title: Changing the requirement that the Robert G. (Bob) Bethell joint committee on home and community based services and KanCare oversight meet in January and April to meeting at least once each quarter.
ks:SB 327.summary: Requires the Bethell joint committee on home and community based services and KanCare oversight to meet once each quarter, with two consecutive days in the third and fourth quarters, instead of one day in January and April.

ks:SB 328.title: Permitting a pharmacist to distribute pre-measured doses of epinephrine to a school for emergency medication kits.
ks:SB 328.summary: Allows pharmacists to distribute epinephrine delivery systems, not only auto-injectors, to schools for emergency medication kits.

ks:SB 329.title: Requiring the county appraiser to submit a single property appraisal report at the valuation appeal hearing before the regular division of the state board of tax appeals.
ks:SB 329.summary: Requires county appraisers to submit a single-property appraisal report, rather than a mass appraisal, at valuation appeal hearings before the regular division of the State Board of Tax Appeals.

ks:SB 33.title: House Substitute for Substitute for SB 33 by Committee on Taxation - Providing that countywide retailers' sales tax is apportioned based on total assessed valuations of the county and cities within the county rather than property taxes levied.
ks:SB 33.summary: Lets county commissioners put countywide sales taxes of up to 3 percent to voters, with limits of 1 percent for general and 2 percent for special purposes, and leaves special-purpose revenue with the county rather than shared with cities.

ks:SB 331.title: Eliminating certain stipulations relating to the payment of negotiable instruments on Saturday afternoons or holidays.
ks:SB 331.summary: Repeals a Kansas statute on payment of negotiable instruments, such as checks, and provides that financial institutions may pay them on Saturdays or legal holidays.

ks:SB 334.title: Facilitating nursing workforce development by providing education levels for instructors at nursing schools as a requirement for state approval.
ks:SB 334.summary: Requires nursing school faculty to hold a nursing degree at least one level above the degree of the program they teach, bars the Board of Nursing from requiring more advanced credentials, and lets the Board grant exemptions to schools with hiring hardships.

ks:SB 335.title: Requiring public construction contracts to include a mutual waiver of consequential damages.
ks:SB 335.summary: Requires public construction contracts to include a mutual waiver of consequential damages, such as rental expenses, lost use, income, financing and reputation for the owner, and office expenses and lost profit for the contractor.

ks:SB 339.title: Requiring school districts to provide elementary students with a certain amount of daily recess, prohibiting limiting or withholding recess for disciplinary reasons, requiring a Kansas state fitness test and designating required recess time as part of the school term.
ks:SB 339.summary: Requires public schools to give grades K-8 at least 30 minutes of daily organized recess starting in 2027-28, bars withholding recess as discipline except for immediate threats, and directs the State Board to set a state fitness test.

ks:SB 340.title: Prohibiting promise scholarship awards from being used to fund corequisite courses.
ks:SB 340.summary: Bars Kansas Promise Scholarship awards from paying for remedial hours offered as part of a corequisite course.

ks:SB 344.title: Authorizing animal shelters to place certain animals needing treatment or care in foster homes and requiring shelters to display photographs of animals at a location other than the shelter during a holding period.
ks:SB 344.summary: Allows animal shelters to place newborn animals needing care in foster homes with their photos displayed during the holding period, and requires the Division of Animal Health to keep inspection records at least five years instead of three.

ks:SB 348.title: Exempting any electric public utility that is a not-for-profit wholly owned subsidiary of an electric cooperative public utility from the jurisdiction of the state corporation commission.
ks:SB 348.summary: Exempts not-for-profit electric utilities wholly owned by an electric cooperative from Kansas Corporation Commission regulation, while letting customers petition the commission to review rate changes if 5% of customers, or 3% of a rate class, sign.

ks:SB 35.title: Discontinuing the state property tax levies for the Kansas educational building fund and the state institutions building fund and providing for financing therefor from the state general fund.
ks:SB 35.summary: Ends the statewide property tax levies for state educational buildings (1.0 mill) and state institutions buildings (0.5 mill) from tax year 2026, replacing them from FY 2027 with General Fund transfers of $56.0 million and $25.0 million.

ks:SB 353.title: Designating an official Kansas railroad hall of fame and establishing the Kansas railroad hall of fame selection committee.
ks:SB 353.summary: Creates the Kansas Railroad Hall of Fame, sets up a selection committee and a process for choosing honorees, and designates the Great Plains Transportation Museum in Wichita as its official site and repository.

ks:SB 355.title: Regulating the manufacture, wholesale and distribution of electronic cigarettes in this state and establishing licensure of electronic cigarette manufacturers.
ks:SB 355.summary: Requires electronic cigarette manufacturers selling in Kansas to be licensed by the Director of Taxation, regulates e-cigarette products like other nicotine products, and bans selling products marketed and advertised to minors.

ks:SB 356.title: House Substitute for SB 356 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Authorizing the adoption of administrative rules and regulations concerning sports wagering by the Kansas racing and gaming commission.
ks:SB 356.summary: Authorizes the Kansas Racing and Gaming Commission to adopt the listed proposed permanent rules on sports wagering that were described in an economic impact statement approved February 13, 2025.

ks:SB 358.title: Requiring individuals convicted of certain felonies to be held without bond in the county jail until sentencing.
ks:SB 358.summary: Requires people convicted of off-grid felonies, level 1-4 nondrug felonies, or level 1-2 drug felonies to be held in county jail without bond until sentencing, revoking any existing bond.

ks:SB 36.title: Increasing the cap on the amount of moneys disbursed by the division of conservation to conservation districts and providing an increased matching basis for state moneys disbursed to conservation districts based on amounts allocated by the board of county commissioners for such districts.
ks:SB 36.summary: Raises the cap on state funding per conservation district from $25,000 to $50,000, and raises the state match from $1 to $2 for each $1 of county funding. Moves the district certification deadline from September 1 to November 1.

ks:SB 360.title: Enacting the Kansas consumer prescription protection and accountability act and providing for regulation and registration of pharmacy benefits managers.
ks:SB 360.summary: Creates the Kansas Consumer Prescription Protection and Accountability Act regulating pharmacy benefit managers, requiring pharmacy reimbursement at no less than national average drug acquisition cost plus a $10.50 dispensing fee, and setting audit and reporting rules.

ks:SB 361.title: Electing to participate in the federal tax credit for individual contributions to scholarship granting organizations.
ks:SB 361.summary: Makes Kansas participate in the federal tax credit for individual contributions to scholarship granting organizations for tax years after 2026, directs the State Treasurer to give the federal government the required list of eligible organizations, and bars state rules stricter than federal law.

ks:SB 362.title: Requiring the office of each state officer to keep and maintain records of information concerning all travel locations and expenses of the state officer that were paid or reimbursed by the state during each fiscal year and provide such records of information upon request by a member of the public.
ks:SB 362.summary: Requires the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State, State Treasurer and Insurance Commissioner to keep yearly records of state-paid travel locations and expenses, available to the public on request.

ks:SB 363.title: Requiring the department of health and environment (KDHE) to seek federal approval for continuous medicaid eligibility for certain individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities receiving services through a home and community based services waiver, directing state agencies to report to certain legislative committees on Kansans losing public assistance program eligibility, requiring the Kansas department for children and families and KDHE to enter into data-matching agreements with state agencies to verify eligibility for food and medical assistance and KDHE to submit certain data to the centers for medicare and medicaid services, prohibiting certain public assistance waivers or exemptions without legislative approval and self-attestation for purposes of determining eligibility for public assistance, requiring quarterly eligibility redeterminations for medical assistance and providing exceptions for certain individuals, limiting retroactive enrollment in medical assistance, immediately terminating eligibility for medical assistance upon confirmation of death of the enrollee, increasing the age limit for able-bodied adults without certain dependents and prohibiting certain exemptions from work requirements under the food assistance program.
ks:SB 363.summary: Sets data-matching and eligibility verification requirements for public assistance programs, requires quarterly and annual legislative reports, and directs KDHE to seek federal approval for continuous Medicaid eligibility for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities on home and community based waivers.

ks:SB 364.title: Requiring the department of wildlife and parks to offer a discounted resident senior combination hunting and fishing license to residents of Kansas who are 65 years of age or older and increasing the maximum age to qualify for the Kansas kids lifetime combination hunting and fishing license and decreasing the maximum fee and removing the expiration of such license.
ks:SB 364.summary: Requires the wildlife department to offer a resident senior combination hunting and fishing license for Kansans 65 or older, at a fee no more than one-eighth of the general lifetime combination license, and changes the Kansas kids lifetime license.

ks:SB 366.title: House Substitute for Senate Bill 366 by Committee on Transportation - Prohibiting the use of a mobile telephone while operating a motor vehicle in school or construction zones and providing penalties thereof and permitting the display of certain lighting in road construction zones by vehicles and trailers engaged in highway construction and maintenance operations.
ks:SB 366.summary: Bans using a mobile phone, other than hands-free, in school zones with reduced speed limits and in posted road construction zones with workers present, with exceptions for emergency uses, and allows certain warning lights on highway construction vehicles.

ks:SB 368.title: Enacting the health care sharing ministries tax deduction act to provide a subtraction modification for qualified health care sharing expenses paid by a qualified individual and certain qualified health care shares received by a qualified individual.
ks:SB 368.summary: Creates a state income tax subtraction for health care sharing ministry contributions and amounts received, capped at $5,000 for an individual or $10,000 for joint filers, for ministries meeting listed requirements such as 501(c)(3) status.

ks:SB 372.title: Enacting the app store accountability act to regulate app store and developer operations with respect to minors, create requirements for age verification and parental consent and provide for enforcement under the Kansas consumer protection act and through a private cause of action.
ks:SB 372.summary: Creates the App Store Accountability Act: requires app stores to verify the age category of Kansas account holders, and applies requirements to app stores and developers regarding minors, enforced through the Consumer Protection Act and a private right to sue.

ks:SB 374.title: Permitting a municipal judge to initiate a psychiatric or psychological examination to determine competence, setting forth relevant procedures and requiring further consideration of evaluation and treatment during the course of competency proceedings for defendants charged with the most serious offenses.
ks:SB 374.summary: Requires the court to order the prosecutor in the criminal case to start involuntary commitment when a defendant is not competent within six months of treatment, limits outpatient treatment for felony defendants, and creates competency procedures for municipal courts.

ks:SB 375.title: Enacting the proxy advisor transparency act, requiring proxy advisors to make certain disclosures when recommending an action against company management, authorizing the attorney general to investigate and take enforcement actions against violators and establishing a private right of action for a declaratory judgment or injunctive relief.
ks:SB 375.summary: Requires proxy advisors that recommend against company management to tell clients and the company's board whether the recommendation rests on a written financial analysis, and to share it on request. The Attorney General enforces. Exempts small charities and banks.

ks:SB 379.title: Authorizing the state 911 board to establish a statewide program for emergency medical dispatch and telecommunicator cardiopulmonary resuscitation, medical direction and quality assurance services.
ks:SB 379.summary: Requires the State 911 Board to set up a statewide emergency medical dispatch and telecommunicator CPR program, with common protocols, medical direction and quality assurance for 911 centers, and creates a fund for it.

ks:SB 380.title: Requiring retail electric suppliers to provide fair, reasonable and nondiscriminatory rates and services to entities that provide electric vehicle charging services.
ks:SB 380.summary: Requires retail electric suppliers that run public fast charging stations to offer fair, reasonable, non-discriminatory rates and services to others providing similar services, without giving their own stations an unreasonable advantage. Excludes stations built before July 1, 2026; expires 2036.

ks:SB 381.title: Requiring instruction to provide students with an understanding of communist and socialist regimes and ideologies and that students pass an American civics examination in order to graduate with a high school diploma.
ks:SB 381.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to develop, and school districts to teach, instruction on the negative impacts of communist and socialist ideologies and regimes in grades K-12, and requires a 100-question civics exam to graduate.

ks:SB 382.title: Providing for the administration of statewide assessments to virtual school students by such students' virtual schools, adding third parties who contract with school districts to the definition of special teacher, providing for special education state aid reimbursement for certain qualified teachers, authorizing nonpublic schools to permit nonaccredited private elementary or secondary school students to participate in certain activities and authorizing foreign exchange students who reside with a host family to enroll in and attend the resident school district of the host family.
ks:SB 382.summary: Lets nonpublic schools allow students from non-accredited private schools to take part in activities governed by the state high school activities association. Also changes foreign exchange student open enrollment, special education aid for contracted teachers, and virtual school testing.

ks:SB 384.title: Extending the application deadline for authorization to operate as a public innovative district from December 1 to May 1 and deeming applications approved if not approved or denied within 45 days of submission.
ks:SB 384.summary: Moves the public innovative district application deadline from December 1 to May 1, shortens state board review windows from 90 to 45 days, and treats applications as approved if not acted on in time.

ks:SB 387.title: Requiring school districts to verify the household gross earned income of each student who qualifies for free meals under the national school lunch program and requiring legislative authorization to receive special assistance payments under federal law.
ks:SB 387.summary: Requires school districts to verify each year the household income of at-risk students who are not directly certified through other benefit programs, and to get legislative approval before using the Community Eligibility Provision.

ks:SB 39.title: Establishing the Kansas legal tender act and providing for an income tax subtraction modification for sales of specie.
ks:SB 39.summary: As amended, creates the Kansas Legal Tender Act, recognizing U.S.-issued gold and silver coin as legal tender, exempts sales and exchanges of gold and silver specie from tax, and adds a state income tax subtraction for net gains from selling specie.

ks:SB 390.title: House Substitute for SB 390 by Committee on Agriculture and Natural Resources - Prohibiting certain additives in food provided by schools as part of certain federal food service programs and permitting federal pesticide warning or labeling requirements to satisfy any state pesticide warning or labeling requirements.
ks:SB 390.summary: Bars schools serving reimbursable or free or reduced-price meals from serving food containing listed additives, including brominated vegetable oil, titanium dioxide and several FD&C dyes, from school year 2027-28, with inspection certification and corrective action plans.

ks:SB 391.title: Prohibiting cities and counties from adopting or enforcing any ordinance or resolution that requires landlords to lease housing to tenants receiving financial assistance from or through the housing choice voucher program or any other housing assistance program or that otherwise restricts a landlord's ability to consider the income source of a prospective tenant.
ks:SB 391.summary: Bars cities and counties from adopting or enforcing local rules that stop landlords from refusing housing-voucher payments, restrict tenant screening criteria, cap security deposits, or require a right of first refusal for tenants; voids such rules adopted before July 1, 2026.

ks:SB 392.title: House Substitute for SB 392 by Committee on Elections - Establishing reasons for withdrawal of candidacy from national, state and local offices, concerning vacancies in the joint candidacy of the governor and lieutenant governor, requiring driver's licenses to reflect citizenship status, requiring provisional ballots be provided to persons showing a driver's license reflecting noncitizenship, require state agencies required by federal law to provide voter registration services to provide quarterly reports to the secretary of state listing noncitizens receiving public benefits.
ks:SB 392.summary: As passed by the Senate, lets school board, city and community college candidates withdraw for severe medical hardship or no longer living in the district, and ends the filling of vacancies in a joint Governor and Lieutenant Governor candidacy.

ks:SB 393.title: Authorizing any county or city to allow the sale of alcoholic beverages 23 hours a day, seven days a week for the duration of the FIFA 2026 world cup.
ks:SB 393.summary: Lets counties and cities allow alcohol sales from 6 a.m. to 5 a.m. the next day, from June 11 through July 19, 2026, during the FIFA World Cup. Applies to licensed retailers and on-premises sellers in places that opt in.

ks:SB 396.title: Reorganizing the Clearwater cemetery district in Sedgwick county to remove Ohio township.
ks:SB 396.summary: Authorizes the Clearwater Cemetery District board to remove Ohio Township from the district by resolution, effective January 1, 2026, and sets procedures for board membership after the change.

ks:SB 398.title: Requiring a proponent to demonstrate that it is more likely than not that certain specialized knowledge will help the trier of fact to understand evidence before certain qualified witnesses may testify.
ks:SB 398.summary: Changes the Kansas Rules of Evidence on expert testimony so the party offering an expert must show it is more likely than not that the expert's specialized knowledge will help the judge or jury, and that the testimony rests on sufficient facts and reliable methods.

ks:SB 4.title: Requiring the return of advance voting ballots by 7:00 p.m. on the day of the election.
ks:SB 4.summary: Requires mailed advance voting ballots to be received by 7:00 p.m. on election day, instead of up to the third day after the election, starting January 1, 2026.

ks:SB 402.title: Modifying the definition of household income for the homestead property tax refund act, providing for one homestead property tax refund claim form and providing an eligibility exception for claimants who are required to live away from the homestead by reason of health or other hardship, increasing the homestead appraised value thresholds for certain homestead refund claim provisions, extending the period of time to file homestead claims and providing for an increase in the maximum refund allowed, providing that a person shall not lose eligibility for a homestead property tax refund claim or the SAFESR tax credit if the appraised valuation of the homestead subsequently exceeds the applicable threshold after qualifying in a previous tax year and modifying the household income threshold, providing a cost-of-living adjustment for purposes of the SAFESR tax credit and prohibiting tax sales of residential property for certain qualifying individuals for taxes owed on residential property.
ks:SB 402.summary: Combines the Homestead and Tax Freeze property tax relief forms, changes the Homestead income definition to Kansas adjusted gross income of household members, and raises the Homestead and Tax Freeze home value limit from $350,000 to $375,000.

ks:SB 403.title: Providing for the pheasants forever, quail forever and delta waterfowl distinctive license plates.
ks:SB 403.summary: Authorizes Pheasants Forever and Quail Forever license plates from July 2026 and Delta Waterfowl plates from January 2027. Bans frames or objects that affect a license plate's visibility, and clarifies the definition of conviction in the commercial driver's license act.

ks:SB 404.title: House Substitute for SB 404 by Committee on Transportation - Creating the vehicle services modernization task force, providing limitations on expenditures of the county treasurer motor vehicle fee funds and authorizing county treasurers to charge certain increased fees for vehicle registration transactions.
ks:SB 404.summary: Creates a Vehicle Services Modernization Task Force, limits uses of the county treasurers' vehicle fee fund, renames certain registration fees, and lets counties raise a transaction fee to no more than $10 in 2027 through 2029.

ks:SB 406.title: Directing the governor to approve eligible programs for workforce Pell grants and providing requirements for the state workforce development board with regard to eligibility, approval and financing of such programs.
ks:SB 406.summary: Requires the Governor, with the state workforce development board, to approve eligible workforce training programs for federal Workforce Pell Grants, and requires the board to set up eligibility approval and appeals processes and coordinate with other workforce programs.

ks:SB 407.title: Authorizing the adoption of certain rules and regulations related to hazardous waste monitoring and permit application fees by the Kansas department of health and environment.
ks:SB 407.summary: Authorizes the health and environment department to adopt rules KAR 28-31-10 and 28-31-10b on hazardous waste monitoring and permit application fees, as required for rules with costs of $1 million or more.

ks:SB 410.title: Providing that earned wage access service registrants are subject to the Kansas financial institutions information security act.
ks:SB 410.summary: Makes earned wage access service registrants subject to the Kansas Financial Institutions Information Security Act, and clarifies that financial institutions doing money transmission without a Money Transmission Act license are also covered.

ks:SB 412.title: Imposing a duty on a conservator to notify certain entities and persons of any court order commanding performance or safekeeping of a conservatee's estate assets.
ks:SB 412.summary: Requires a conservator, within 15 days of a court order commanding performance or safekeeping of the conservatee's estate assets, to notify the entities and people the conservator has identified as holding those assets.

ks:SB 413.title: Prohibiting counsel from suggesting an amount of damages for noneconomic loss in civil actions.
ks:SB 413.summary: Bars lawyers in civil cases from suggesting an amount of damages for non-economic loss, whether as a dollar figure, range, formula, units of time, or comparison to unrelated objects or values.

ks:SB 415.title: Making certain violations of the residential landlord and tenant act subject to the remedies and enforcement provisions of the Kansas consumer protection act.
ks:SB 415.summary: Subjects a landlord's intentional action or failure to act that causes a dwelling to be declared uninhabitable by a code enforcement agency to Kansas Consumer Protection Act remedies, enforceable only by the attorney general or a county or district attorney.

ks:SB 418.title: Enacting the by-right housing development act to provide a streamlined permit approval process for by-right housing developments, allowing third-party review of new residential construction development documents and inspection of improvements, requiring political subdivisions to allow certain building provisions for certain single-family residences of a certain size, excluding owner initiated rezoning to a single-family residential district from protest petition provisions and providing for all land within the corporate limits of a city that is zoned for any type of residential use to be considered zoned for single-family residential use.
ks:SB 418.summary: Creates a streamlined approval process requiring local authorities to approve qualifying single-family homes, townhouses and accessory dwelling units as of right, without discretionary review, if they meet zoning criteria and, for townhouse projects, have at most 12 attached units.

ks:SB 419.title: Enacting the Kansas intellectual rights and knowledge act, providing a civil cause of action and penalties for violations of such act and authorizing students and student associations to exercise political and ideological beliefs, values and missions.
ks:SB 419.summary: Creates the Kansas Intellectual Rights and Knowledge Act, setting limits on public colleges and universities regarding non-commercial expressive activity on campus, and lets the attorney general or an affected individual sue a college that violates it.

ks:SB 42.title: Providing for the establishment of a web-based online insurance verification system for the verification of evidence of motor vehicle liability insurance, eliminating the requirement that the commissioner of insurance submit certain reports to the governor and requiring certain reports be available on the insurance department's website, removing certain entities from the definition of person for the purpose of enforcing insurance law, requiring that third party administrators maintain separate fiduciary accounts for individual payors and prohibiting the commingling of funds held on behalf of multiple payors, requiring the disclosure to the commissioner of insurance of any bankruptcy petition filed by or on behalf of such administrator pursuant to the United State bankruptcy code, requiring title agents to make their reports available for inspection upon request of the commissioner of insurance instead of submitting such reports annually, standardizing the amount of surety bonds filed with the commissioner of insurance at $100,000 and eliminating the small business exemption in certain counties.
ks:SB 42.summary: Requires the Insurance Commissioner to create one web-based system to verify motor vehicle liability insurance, requires insurers to cooperate, and requires third-party administrators to keep a separate fiduciary account for each payor.

ks:SB 422.title: Reorganizing certain provisions that apply to foreign insurance companies seeking authorization to do business in Kansas, authorizing the suspension or revocation of a nonresident agent's license without notice and opportunity for a hearing following notification to the commissioner of insurance that such nonresident agent no longer holds a home state license and requiring agents and public adjusters to respond to inquiries from the commissioner.
ks:SB 422.summary: Allows the Insurance Department to revoke a nonresident agent's license without a hearing 30 days after learning the agent lost a home state license, and requires agents and public adjusters to answer Commissioner inquiries within 14 calendar days.

ks:SB 425.title: Increasing the maximum annual registration fee limit for seed retailers and wholesalers and authorizing a late fee for registrations renewed after the registration deadline.
ks:SB 425.summary: Raises the maximum annual registration fee for seed retailers from $30 to $50 and for seed wholesalers from $300 to $400, and authorizes late fees of $25 or $50 for seed retailers, wholesalers and live plant dealers.

ks:SB 426.title: Enacting the Kansas transparency in consumer legal funding act.
ks:SB 426.summary: Creates the Kansas Transparency in Consumer Legal Funding Act, setting contract requirements for companies that fund consumers' lawsuits, including plain language, disclosures and a 10-business-day right to cancel by returning the money.

ks:SB 427.title: Clarifying that the chairperson and vice chairperson of the senate committee on confirmation oversight shall have access to review tax information from the department of revenue and Kansas bureau of investigation background checks on persons appointed to state offices who are subject to senate confirmation.
ks:SB 427.summary: Lets the chair and vice chair of the Senate Committee on Confirmation Oversight review KBI background checks and Department of Revenue tax information on appointees needing Senate confirmation, with the information kept confidential other than conviction data.

ks:SB 430.title: Adding mitragynine to schedule I of the uniform controlled substances act and reconciling multiple amendments to certain statutes in the Kansas criminal code.
ks:SB 430.summary: Adds mitragynine, the main active compound in kratom, to Schedule I of the Uniform Controlled Substances Act and reconciles overlapping amendments to the theft and expungement statutes.

ks:SB 431.title: Establishing the remote practice of pharmacy, requiring certain conditions for such practice and limiting activities performed under such practice.
