ks:SB 431.summary: Allows pharmacies to employ pharmacists, interns and technicians to work remotely, requiring a posted notice of remote work, records, and remote practice areas free from third-party observation using pharmacy-provided devices.

ks:SB 434.title: House Substitute for SB 434 by Committee on Taxation - Establishing the veterans' valor property tax relief act providing an income tax credit or refund for eligible individuals and discontinuing the sales tax exemption for purchases made by certain qualifying military veterans.
ks:SB 434.summary: Creates a refundable income tax credit of 50% of property taxes paid on the home of Kansas veterans with a total service-connected disability rating, beginning tax year 2026, and repeals a sales tax exemption for certain disabled veterans set to start July 1, 2026.

ks:SB 435.title: Providing procedures, standards and requirements for the deposit and investment of public moneys, creating the public moneys fee fund and authorizing the state treasurer to assess a fee to operate the public moneys pooled method, making and concerning appropriations for fiscal year 2027 for the office of the state treasurer, authorizing a certain transfer from the state general fund to the public moneys fee fund, modifying investment standards for the board of trustees of the Kansas public employees retirement system of moneys certified by the state treasurer as equivalent to the aggregate net amount received for unclaimed property and authorizing investments in certain foreign governments and the KPERS board of trustees to elect the vice chairperson of the board, requiring newly affiliated KP&F employers to contribute at the actuarial required rate for past and future service and repealing certain working after retirement statutes for state and local elected officials.
ks:SB 435.summary: Changes rules for investing public moneys through the State Treasurer's pooled method, with a fee fund and $250,000 appropriation; lets KPERS trustees elect their vice chair; requires all KP&F employers to pay the actuarial rate; repeals some post-retirement work statutes.

ks:SB 436.title: Increasing the cost threshold for when a county shall use the public bidding process in awarding a construction contract.
ks:SB 436.summary: Repeals the ban on local governments requiring contractors to provide leave, benefits or above-minimum wages, and raises the threshold for counties to use public bidding on construction from $25,000 to $100,000.

ks:SB 439.title: Enacting the utility railroad crossing act and establishing a process and limitations for utilities to interact with railroad right-of-way.
ks:SB 439.summary: Creates the Utility Railroad Crossing Act, setting a process and limits for utilities to place, maintain, and relocate facilities that cross or run parallel to railroad rights-of-way.

ks:SB 44.title: Declaring antisemitism and antisemitic acts to be against public policy and establishing a statutory definition of such terms.
ks:SB 44.summary: Declares antisemitism against state public policy and defines it using the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance working definition as of May 26, 2016, plus listed examples, without limiting First Amendment rights.

ks:SB 448.title: Permitting the use of expedited partner therapy to treat a sexually transmitted disease.
ks:SB 448.summary: Allows health care providers to treat the sexual partner of a patient diagnosed with a sexually transmitted disease without examining the partner, if the partner is unlikely to be examined and was exposed within the prior 60 days.

ks:SB 45.title: Substitute for SB 45 by Committee on Education - Requiring the state board of education to calculate graduation rates for all school districts for purposes of accreditation using an alternative calculation.
ks:SB 45.summary: Sets a statutory four-year adjusted cohort graduation rate calculation for school accreditation, excluding certain students who transferred in or out, and repeals the separate calculation for virtual schools.

ks:SB 450.title: Authorizing the secretary of administration to grant a monetary award to a state employee who reports activity that constitutes fraud, waste or abuse of funds in any program administered by a state agency.
ks:SB 450.summary: Creates a reward of 10 percent of state savings, after costs, for a state employee who reports fraud, waste or abuse in a state-administered program to the secretary of administration, with limits on awards.

ks:SB 451.title: House Substitute for SB451 by House Committee on Elections - Clarifying when contributions may be accepted for the primary and general elections, prohibiting the use of public assets by government officers and employees to advocate for proposed amendments to the constitution of the state of Kansas and ballot questions submitted to voters, requiring campaign finance treasurer reports to include the products and services provided by vendors, requiring reporting of small contributions to the public disclosure commission.
ks:SB 451.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires campaign finance reports on payments to advertising agencies, public relations firms or consultants who pay vendors to also show the products and services each vendor provided.

ks:SB 454.title: Enhancing the criminal penalty for committing certain crimes in the context of transnational repression and requiring the development of transnational repression recognition and response training.
ks:SB 454.summary: Raises the sentencing severity level by one (life imprisonment for level 1) for offenses committed with intent to commit transnational repression for a foreign principal, and requires the KBI Director to develop related training by July 1, 2027.

ks:SB 459.title: Removing the prisoner review board from the supervision of the secretary of corrections, changing the appointing authority and creating qualifications for the members of the board and requiring parole hearings to be postponed if proper notice of the public comment session is not made to the victim.
ks:SB 459.summary: Makes the Prisoner Review Board independent of the corrections secretary, with five Senate-confirmed members: three appointed by the governor and two by the attorney general. Requires postponing parole hearings if the victim did not get proper notice of the public comment session.

ks:SB 462.title: Prohibiting persons who engaged in wrongful conduct from recovering damages in certain civil actions, prohibiting certain public nuisance claims, providing that only the attorney general may file claims regarding public nuisances that are not wholly contained in one political subdivision unless the attorney general delegates authorization to file such claims and requiring special injury for certain public nuisance actions.
ks:SB 462.summary: Bars public nuisance claims based on product design, sale or marketing of lawful products, on lawfully authorized conduct, or on aggregated individual injuries. Also bars people engaged in wrongful conduct from suing for negligence or collecting damages related to that conduct.

ks:SB 463.title: Prohibiting certain persons from recovering damages in certain civil actions and creating requirements for actions involving negligent security.
ks:SB 463.summary: Bars people engaged in wrongful conduct, including certain crimes and intentional or reckless torts, from recovering negligence damages tied to that conduct, and sets requirements for negligent security lawsuits.

ks:SB 47.title: Requiring school districts to publicly list the names and email addresses of current school board members, authorizing local school board members to add new items to board meeting discussions, ask questions or engage in discussion with members of the public and access school property, authorizing members of the public to address school boards at board meetings and authorizing payment of annual dues to any not-for-profit organization that provides services to member school districts.
ks:SB 47.summary: As amended, requires school districts to post board members' names and email addresses online, requires public comment time at regular meetings and budget hearings, and lets board members enter district buildings during school hours and activities.

ks:SB 473.title: Authorizing Audubon of Kansas to convey certain property in Wabaunsee county and requiring any deeds or conveyances related to such property be reviewed and approved by the state historical society.
ks:SB 473.summary: Allows Audubon of Kansas to convey real estate in Wabaunsee County, removes the language barring it from conveying real estate, and requires the state historical society to review and approve any deeds or conveyances first.

ks:SB 480.title: Reviving repealed statutes related to estates of absentees and requiring nonresident fiduciaries to appoint an agent residing in this state.
ks:SB 480.summary: Revives repealed Probate Code statutes on estates of absentees, including trustee appointment and presumption of death, and requires agents of nonresident fiduciaries to be Kansas residents.

ks:SB 481.title: Permitting a municipal judge to initiate a psychiatric or psychological examination to determine competence and setting forth relevant procedures.
ks:SB 481.summary: Allows municipal judges to order a psychiatric or psychological examination, completed within 60 days, when a defendant may be incompetent to stand trial. Statements made in the examination cannot be used as evidence against the defendant.

ks:SB 487.title: Requiring the Kansas bureau of investigation to implement a statewide offender registration system for agencies who register offenders under the offender registration act, providing for a petition to determine that an offender is indigent and authorizing a notice to appear to be issued for a violation of the act involving nonpayment of a fee.
ks:SB 487.summary: Directs the KBI to provide, from July 1, 2028, a statewide offender registration system at its own cost, replacing paper forms with data entry; adds a technology fee of up to $10; lets offenders petition a court to be declared indigent for registration fees.

ks:SB 497.title: Adding kratom to schedule I of the uniform controlled substances act and making conforming amendments to the definition of fentanyl-related controlled substance in the criminal code.
ks:SB 497.summary: Adds 7-hydroxymitragynine and mitragynine, kratom compounds, to Schedule I of the Uniform Controlled Substances Act, and makes matching changes to the criminal code's definition of fentanyl-related controlled substance.

ks:SB 498.title: Providing income tax credits for the retail sale of higher ethanol blends of fuel and expenditures for lockable gun and ammunition storage and discontinuing income tax credits for qualified alternative-fueled motor vehicle property or fueling station expenditures, agritourism liability insurance, assistive technology contributions, declared disaster capital investment, environmental compliance, owners promoting employment across Kansas and swine facility improvement.
ks:SB 498.summary: Creates income tax credits for 2026 through 2028 of $0.05 per gallon for retail sales of E15 or higher ethanol blends (capped at $2.5 million a year) and for lockable gun and ammunition storage purchases, and ends or repeals certain other credits.

ks:SB 5.title: Prohibiting the use of funds provided by the United States government for the conduct of elections and election-related activities unless approved by the legislature.
ks:SB 5.summary: Bars election officials and government agencies from accepting or spending federal money for election administration unless authorized by state appropriation or law, with an exception for election security funds.

ks:SB 50.title: Establishing uniform interest rate provisions for service scholarship programs administered by the Kansas board of regents, authorizing the board of regents to recover the costs of collecting such repayment and charge fees for administration costs, requiring eligible students to enter into agreements with the board of regents as a condition to receiving a grant under the adult learner grant act and sunsetting the low-income family postsecondary savings accounts incentive program in 2028 and reducing the number of audits required for such program.
ks:SB 50.summary: As amended by the House committee, sets a uniform interest rate equal to the federal PLUS loan rate, with no interest before repayment is due, for Board of Regents scholarships and aid that require repayment, and lets the Board charge collection costs and application fees.

ks:SB 502.title: Authorizing the adoption of administrative rules and regulations concerning sports wagering by the Kansas racing and gaming commission.
ks:SB 502.summary: Authorizes the Kansas Racing and Gaming Commission to adopt the proposed permanent sports wagering rules described in the economic impact statement approved by the Division of the Budget on February 13, 2025.

ks:SB 51.title: House Substitute for SB 51 by Committee on Legislative Modernization - Authorizing the chief information security officer to receive audit reports, updating statutes related to services provided by the chief information technology officer and authorizing the office of information technology services to provide certain services to political subdivisions and hospitals.
ks:SB 51.summary: Lets the state's executive branch chief information technology officer set IT strategy and standards and contract with local governments and certain hospitals to provide IT and cybersecurity services, with fees going to the state treasury. Lets the state cybersecurity office receive IT audit reports.

ks:SB 513.title: Directing the Kansas department for children and families to develop, procure and implement software to provide direct child care subsidy payments to child care providers.
ks:SB 513.summary: Directs the Department for Children and Families to request vendor information by January 1, 2027 on a child care subsidy payment system supporting direct payments to providers, report by June 30, 2027, then issue a request for proposals, subject to appropriations.

ks:SB 515.title: Authorizing nonpublic schools to permit nonaccredited private elementary or secondary school students to participate in certain activities for such nonpublic schools.
ks:SB 515.summary: Lets nonpublic schools allow students from nonaccredited private schools to take part in Kansas State High School Activities Association activities, and sets a moratorium on interscholastic competitions and practices during certain time periods.

ks:SB 517.title: Expanding the every child can read act reporting requirements and amending the Kansas blueprint for literacy to provide certain requirements for the state board of education, the state board of regents and school districts with regard to literacy education and reporting.
ks:SB 517.summary: Adds a statewide universal reading screening tool and new district data reporting to the Every Child Can Read Act, moves the annual report due date to October 1, and shifts literacy goals to joint responsibility of the state education and regents boards.

ks:SB 52.title: Enacting the Kansas film and digital media industry production development act, providing a tax credit and sales tax exemption to incentivize film, video and digital media production in Kansas, establishing a program to be administered by the secretary of commerce for the purpose of developing such production in Kansas and requiring the secretary of commerce to issue reports to the legislature regarding the program.
ks:SB 52.summary: As amended, creates the Kansas Film and Digital Media Production Development Act, with a sales tax exemption and nonrefundable income tax credits for approved film production projects, administered by the Commerce secretary.

ks:SB 521.title: Providing for income tax credits for payment of employee's child care related expenses and certain employer contributions to expand community child care availability.
ks:SB 521.summary: Changes the income tax credit for employer child care expenses to 75 percent of qualifying costs and adds a refundable credit for employer contributions to groups that expand community child care, capped at $100,000 per taxpayer for both credits combined.

ks:SB 524.title: Requiring banks to enter into a written agreement with the state treasurer to be a depository of public moneys, increasing the market value of securities necessary to secure the deposit of public moneys, providing procedures for when a depository fails to follow the requirements of the state treasurer, modifying certain definitions, authorizing the state treasurer to assess a fee to operate the public moneys pooled method, creating the public moneys fee fund and providing exceptions to the public moneys pooled method if accounts are subject to conflicting federal law.
ks:SB 524.summary: Requires depositories of local government money to sign a written agreement with the State Treasurer, raises required security from 100 to 102 percent of deposits, lets the Treasurer assess a fee into a new fund, and exempts accounts under conflicting federal law.

ks:SB 53.title: Providing that the attorney members of the board of trustees of a county law library in certain counties shall be appointed by the chief judge of the judicial district and allowing such board to authorize the chief judge to use certain fees for the purpose of facilitating and enhancing functions of the district court of the county.
ks:SB 53.summary: Replaces election with appointment by the judicial district's chief judge for attorney members of county law library boards (outside Douglas, Johnson and Sedgwick counties), and lets boards also authorize using certain court-case library fees for district court functions.

ks:SB 54.title: Substitute for SB 54 by Committee on Judiciary - Limiting discovery and disclosure of third-party litigation funding agreements and requiring reporting of such agreements to courts.
ks:SB 54.summary: Requires parties in civil cases to give the court a copy of any third-party litigation funding agreement for private review, and to file a sworn statement within 30 days. Excludes agreements giving the funder no profit beyond repayment plus up to 11.1 percent interest.

ks:SB 55.title: Prohibiting the assignment of benefits under certain property and casualty insurance contracts and defining such assignment of benefits as an unfair method of competition and unfair or deceptive act or practice.
ks:SB 55.summary: Prohibits soliciting or accepting assignment of post-loss benefits under residential property insurance policies to or from persons providing services like repairs, voids such assignments, and exempts those made to federally insured financial institutions, mortgagees and later property buyers.

ks:SB 58.title: Modifying the requirements and allocations for multi-year flex accounts.
ks:SB 58.summary: Changes rules for multi-year flex accounts, which let groundwater right holders exceed yearly water limits within a five-year total. Revises definitions, eligibility conditions and allocations.

ks:SB 6.title: Prohibiting the use of ranked-choice voting methods for conducting elections.
ks:SB 6.summary: Bans ranked-choice voting in federal, state, county and municipal elections and voids any local ordinance, resolution or regulation adopted before July 1, 2025 that uses it.

ks:SB 63.title: Enacting the help not harm act, restricting use of state funds to promote gender transitioning, prohibiting healthcare providers from providing gender transition care to children whose gender identity is inconsistent with the child's sex, authorizing a civil cause of action against healthcare providers for providing such treatments, requiring professional discipline against a healthcare provider who performs such treatment, prohibiting professional liability insurance from covering damages for healthcare providers that provide gender transition treatment to children and adding violation of the act to the definition of unprofessional conduct for physicians.
ks:SB 63.summary: Bans health care providers, with listed exceptions, from giving minors puberty blockers, high-dose hormones or surgery for gender transition, bars state funds including Medicaid from paying for them, and bars state facilities and certain state employees from promoting social transition, such drugs or surgery.

ks:SB 64.title: Adjusting certain internal KPERS act statutory references, extending the time for filing administrative appeals and updating provisions relating to compliance with the federal internal revenue code.
ks:SB 64.summary: As amended, extends from 30 to 60 days the time a KPERS member has to request a hearing on an adverse board decision, and updates KPERS law for federal retirement rules and outdated statutory cross-references.

ks:SB 65.title: House Substitute for SB 65 by House Committee on Elections - Removing cities, counties, school districts and community colleges from the mail ballot election law; authorizing the election of directors by irrigation districts by mail ballot; requiring qualified electors deliver advance ballots unless otherwise provided by federal law.
ks:SB 65.summary: As passed by the Senate, allows elections for irrigation district boards of more than 35,000 acres to be held by mail ballot on the first Tuesday in March, with terms of two, three or four years set by the board.

ks:SB 66.title: Substitute for SB 66 by Committee on Local Government, Transparency and Ethics - Requiring annual filing of the statement of substantial interests by elected or appointed city or county officials, providing that officials of governmental subdivisions other than cities or counties file statements of substantial interests if any change in substantial interests occurred and requiring governmental officials with a substantial interest in a real estate development project to verbally disclose such interest prior to participating in any discussion, review or action on a proposed zoning change or permit.
ks:SB 66.summary: Requires certain local officials to file annual statements of substantial interests, requires verbal public disclosure of certain substantial interests, and changes what information is collected about people viewing those statements.

ks:SB 67.title: Substitute for SB 67 by Committee on Public Health and Welfare - Authorizing registered nurse anesthetists to prescribe, procure and administer drugs consistent with the registered nurse anesthetist's education and qualifications.
ks:SB 67.summary: Allows certified registered nurse anesthetists to prescribe durable medical equipment and to prescribe, procure and administer drugs consistent with their education, while barring them from performing abortions or prescribing drugs for abortion.

ks:SB 69.title: Extending by five years the loan repayment program and income tax credit for rural opportunity zones.
ks:SB 69.summary: As amended, extends the Rural Opportunity Zone student loan repayment program and tax credit to July 1, 2031, lets counties offer homebuyer down payment help or child care reimbursement instead, and widens credit eligibility.

ks:SB 7.title: Increasing the statutory limits on bonds issued by a township based on township population and purpose of the bond issuance.
ks:SB 7.summary: Raises township bond caps from 1 percent of assessed valuation to 5 percent for townships of over 5,000 and under 10,000 people, and 10 percent above that. Raises the fire department bond cap from 0.5 to 5 percent and maximum term to 20 years.

ks:SB 70.title: Prohibiting fees for electronic copies of records under the open records act, exempting from disclosure formally closed investigations with no found violations, requiring county or district attorneys to file reports of violations with the attorney general in October instead of January, determining the membership calculation of subordinate groups under the open meetings act, requiring public bodies or agencies that live stream meetings to ensure that the public is able to observe and providing for a five minute deviation to resume an open meeting at the conclusion of executive sessions.
ks:SB 70.summary: As amended, bars per-page fees for electronic copies of public records, limits the $0.25 per page fee to printed copies, exempts from disclosure closed civil-law investigations that found no violation, and changes complaint reporting dates and some public meeting procedures.

ks:SB 71.title: Increasing the criminal penalties for buying sexual relations, removing provisions regarding city ordinances prohibiting buying sexual relations, requiring certain offenders to complete an educational or treatment program regarding commercial sexual exploitation and requiring the attorney general to approve such programs in consultation with the office of judicial administration.
ks:SB 71.summary: Makes every violation of buying sexual relations a severity level 9 person felony, raises the minimum fine from $1,200 to $2,000, and requires certain offenders to complete an Attorney General-approved educational or treatment program.

ks:SB 76.title: Requiring employees of school districts and postsecondary educational institutions to use the name and pronouns consistent with a student's biological sex and birth certificate and authorizing a cause of action for violations therefor.
ks:SB 76.summary: As amended, bars school district employees from addressing a minor with a pronoun or title inconsistent with biological sex, or a name other than the birth-certificate name, without written parental permission; bars adverse job action against school or college employees, or discipline of students, for declining to do so.

ks:SB 77.title: Requiring state agencies to provide notice of revocation of administrative rules and regulations to the public and removing abolished and inactive state agencies from the agency review requirement.
ks:SB 77.summary: Requires state agencies to give written notice to businesses, local governments and other known stakeholders before expedited revocation of a rule, and removes abolished or inactive agencies from the five-year rule review requirement.

ks:SB 78.title: Requiring postsecondary educational institutions to regularly review and update accreditation policies, prohibiting accrediting agencies from compelling such institutions to violate state law and providing a cause of action for violations thereof.
ks:SB 78.summary: Requires colleges and universities to review their accreditation policies and, by December 31, 2025, identify eligible accreditors so they can freely choose among them. Bars accrediting agencies from compelling institutions to violate state law.

ks:SB 79.title: Directing the secretary for children and families to request a waiver from supplemental nutrition assistance program rules that would allow the state to prohibit the purchase of candy and soft drinks with food assistance.
ks:SB 79.summary: Directs the Department for Children and Families to request a federal waiver to bar buying candy and soft drinks with SNAP food assistance, and to bar those purchases if approved. If denied, it must reapply each year.

ks:SB 8.title: Requiring drivers to proceed with due caution when passing stationary vehicles displaying hazard warning lights.
ks:SB 8.summary: Requires drivers approaching a stopped vehicle with hazard lights, flares or caution signals to proceed with caution and, if safe, change lanes away; otherwise reduce speed. Adds a $75 fine for unlawful passing of a stationary vehicle.

ks:SB 82.title: Providing tax credits for expenditures for lockable gun and ammunition storage and the retail sale of higher ethanol blends of fuel, discontinuing the tax credit for qualified alternative-fueled motor vehicle property or fueling station expenditures, repealing the agritourism liability insurance, assistive technology contributions, declared disaster capital investment, owners promoting employment across Kansas and swine facility improvement tax credits and expanding the eligibility for applicable expenses under the child day care services assistance tax credit.
ks:SB 82.summary: Revises employer child care tax credits, creates credits for higher-ethanol fuel sales (five cents per gallon) and lockable gun and ammunition storage purchases for 2026 through 2028, and ends or repeals several other tax credits.

ks:SB 84.title: Enacting the supported decision-making agreements act to provide a statutory framework for allowing an adult to receive decision-making assistance from one or more other adults, requirements for decision-making agreements and duties related thereto.
ks:SB 84.summary: Creates the Supported Decision-making Agreements Act, letting an adult sign an agreement with one or more adult supporters who help them make and communicate decisions and obtain records. Supporters act as fiduciaries and keep information confidential.

ks:SB 85.title: Directing the secretary for children and families to review and compare data for public assistance program eligibility.
ks:SB 85.summary: As amended, requires the children and families secretary to make data-matching agreements with state and federal agencies to check food assistance eligibility, and to post certain noncompliance and fraud investigation findings on the department's website.

ks:SB 87.title: Expanding student eligibility under the tax credit for low income students scholarship program, increasing the amount of the tax credit for contributions made pursuant to such program and providing for aggregate tax credit limit increases under certain conditions.
ks:SB 87.summary: As amended, widens eligibility for the Tax Credit for Low Income Students Scholarship program to students meeting any one of several criteria, adds foster care, military and first-responder-parent criteria, and raises the credit cap from $10 million to $15 million.

ks:SB 88.title: Requiring the state long-term care ombudsman and regional ombudsman to receive training in memory care.
ks:SB 88.summary: Requires the state long-term care ombudsman to include dementia care training for regional ombudsmen, designated employees and volunteers, covering the needs and rights of residents with dementia and strategies for their care.

ks:SB 89.title: Authorizing the animal health commissioner to adopt rules and regulations to administer the poultry disease control act and to establish an annual participation fee for participation in the national poultry improvement plan, a certification fee for persons performing testing and diagnostic services and a testing fee per visit to each location participating in the plan.
ks:SB 89.summary: Amends the Poultry Disease Control Act and sets fees: up to $50 to join the National Poultry Improvement Plan, up to $50 for certifying testers, and up to $100 per location visit for testing and diagnostic services.

ks:SB 9.title: House Substitute for SB 9 by Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development - Prohibiting foreign principals from acquiring interests in real estate in proximity to military installations, state agencies and local government from purchasing drones or critical components of drones from foreign principals or that are manufactured in countries of concern and foreign principals from receiving benefits from economic development programs.
ks:SB 9.summary: Bars foreign principals of countries of concern from acquiring real property within 100 miles of military installations (the Governor may approve expansions), requires registration of holdings, and bars agencies from buying drones with components from those countries.

ks:SB 92.title: Extending the expiration date for provisions that authorize an electric utility to not offer parallel generation service to certain large load customers and exempt certain large load customers from the determination of the utility's peak demand.
ks:SB 92.summary: Extends from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2027 the provision that leaves the added demand of new or expanded large facilities served at 34.5 kilovolts or higher out of a utility's historic peak demand calculation.

ks:SB 97.title: Requiring vehicle dealers to apply for a dealer inventory-only title for certain used nonhighway vehicles that a vehicle dealer obtains.
ks:SB 97.summary: Requires vehicle dealers that acquire used all-terrain, work-site utility or recreational off-highway vehicles, or certain motorcycles, to apply to the county treasurer for a dealer inventory-only title, with a $10 fee and a bill of sale or title.

ks:SB 98.title: Providing for the route 66 association of Kansas distinctive license plate.
ks:SB 98.summary: Exempts qualified firms' purchases for building and operating a qualified data center from sales tax, including land, buildings, equipment, lease payments, installation labor and contractor purchases.

ks:SCR 1602.title: Encouraging the governor to fully cooperate with federal enforcement of immigration laws.
ks:SCR 1602.summary: Urges the Governor to fully cooperate with and assist federal immigration law enforcement, including deportations, and to use lawful authority, such as the Kansas National Guard, to help secure the border.

ks:SCR 1603.title: Proposing to amend section 1 of article 11 of the constitution of the state of Kansas to value residential real property, commercial and industrial real property and mobile homes personal property based on the fair market value or average fair market value and providing that the legislature may provide by law for the freezing of property tax valuations for owner-occupied residential property of qualifying seniors.
ks:SCR 1603.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, starting in tax year 2028, letting the Legislature limit valuation increases for any classes or subclasses of property. Needs two-thirds of each chamber, then goes to voters in November 2026.

ks:SCR 1604.title: Making application to the United States congress to call a convention of the states for the purpose of proposing amendments to limit the federal government.
ks:SCR 1604.summary: Applies to Congress for a convention of the states limited to amendments on federal fiscal restraints, limits on federal power and jurisdiction, and term limits for members of Congress and federal officials, continuing until two-thirds of states apply.

ks:SCR 1609.title: Proposing to amend the Kansas Constitution to repeal section 12 of article 15, regarding membership and nonmembership in labor organizations.
ks:SCR 1609.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for voters to decide, that repeals section 12 of article 15 of the Kansas Constitution, which bars denying employment based on membership or nonmembership in a labor organization.

ks:SCR 1611.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to provide for direct election of supreme court justices and abolish the supreme court nominating commission.
ks:SCR 1611.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the August 4, 2026 ballot, replacing appointment of Kansas Supreme Court justices through the nominating commission with direct election of justices.

ks:SCR 1615.title: Honoring the life and legacy of Charlie Kirk and recognizing October 14 as Charlie Kirk Free Speech Day.
ks:SCR 1615.summary: Condemns the assassination of Charlie Kirk and recognizes October 14 each year as Charlie Kirk Free Speech Day in Kansas, encouraging the governor and residents to observe it.

ks:SCR 1616.title: Proposing to amend section 1 of article 11 of the constitution of the state of Kansas to limit property tax assessed value increases for real property in any subclass and personal property classified as mobile homes.
ks:SCR 1616.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment limiting yearly growth in taxable assessed value of real property and residential mobile homes to 3 percent, with exceptions such as new construction and reclassification, if approved by two-thirds of each chamber and voters.

ky:HB 139.title: AN ACT relating to elections and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 139.summary: Lets the State Board of Elections share data with other agencies to remove ineligible voters, bars buying voting systems that tabulate from barcodes or QR codes, and changes several election deadlines and procedures.

ky:HB 142.title: AN ACT relating to depredating wildlife and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 142.summary: Sets rules for landowners, tenants and designees to take or trap wildlife damaging property, including destruction tags and 24-hour reporting, and lets the Fish and Wildlife Commission set an extra 7 to 10 day antlerless deer season in overpopulated areas.

ky:HB 311.title: AN ACT relating to railroad crossings.
ky:HB 311.summary: Requires railroads to remove obstructive vegetation 250 feet each way at public grade crossings by January 1, 2029; railroads may petition the Transportation Cabinet for waivers. After 30 days' notice, the cabinet or local government removes it and bills the railroad.

ky:HB 504.title: AN ACT making appropriations for the operations, maintenance, support, and functioning of the Judicial Branch of the government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and its various officers, boards, commissions, subdivisions, and other state-supported activities.
ky:HB 504.summary: Overrides the Governor's line-item vetoes of the Judicial Branch budget, which appropriates money for the Judicial Branch's operating and capital projects and sets general provisions and a budget reduction or surplus expenditure plan.

ky:HB 519.title: AN ACT relating to identity documents.
ky:HB 519.summary: Lets license and ID card applicants choose a communication disorder notation, removable on request, with no proof or fee required. A Senate amendment also ends the four-year license option and lets renewal occur any time within a year of expiration.

ky:HB 567.title: AN ACT relating to open records.
ky:HB 567.summary: As passed by the Senate, lets records custodians require a government photo ID showing an address, or other proof, of Kentucky residency; counts requests from licensed attorneys for certain clients as resident requests; and lets planning commissions add a nonvoting military installation representative.

ky:HB 6.title: AN ACT relating to administrative regulations and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 6.summary: Redefines "major economic impact" as combined costs of $500,000 or more over two years, and after March 31, 2025 bars agencies from promulgating regulations unless they certify an exception, such as no major economic impact or an emergency.

ky:HB 652.title: AN ACT relating to critical facility mapping and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 652.summary: Moves administration of the school mapping data program to the Kentucky 911 Services Board and assigns responsibility for mapping data accuracy walk-throughs.

ky:HB 658.title: AN ACT relating to limited commercial driver's licenses and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 658.summary: Directs the Transportation Cabinet to extend limited farm-related commercial driver's license terms to the federal maximum; from July 1, 2027, lets county officials in counties without a regional licensing office issue renewal and duplicate licenses and IDs by agreement, with a $25 convenience fee.

ky:HB 669.title: AN ACT relating to child welfare.
ky:HB 669.summary: Requires the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to check whether each child in its custody gets or qualifies for Social Security or veterans benefits, and creates the Success Sequence Savings and Disbursement Plan, requiring financial training before a child accesses part of saved benefits.

ky:HB 676.title: AN ACT relating to the Kentucky statewide health data utility.
ky:HB 676.summary: Directs Legislative Research Commission staff to study creating a Kentucky statewide health data utility and report to a legislative health committee by December 1, 2026.

ky:HB 727.title: AN ACT relating to education and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 727.summary: Changes many education statutes, including class-size and caseload rules for exceptional children and school board training topics; lets a legislative subcommittee temporarily authorize new state education reports; repeals the summer learning camp and teacher computer purchase laws.

ky:HB 78.title: AN ACT relating to firearms liability protections and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 78.summary: Limits civil lawsuits against firearm and ammunition makers, sellers and trade associations over criminal misuse of their products, preempts local laws imposing such liability, and gives the Attorney General enforcement authority.

ky:HB 826.title: AN ACT relating to education.
ky:HB 826.summary: Requires at least 85% of Office of Adult Education general funds to go to adult education programs, requires a paper-test option for the high school equivalency exam, and removes the McConnell Center from developing a required American civics course.

ky:HB 869.title: AN ACT relating to fiscal matters and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 869.summary: As passed by the Senate, creates a refundable economic development credit for approved incentive projects based on a four-tier county ranking, raises skills training credit caps to $5,000 or $4,000 per trainee, and creates a heritage community revolving fund.

ky:HJR 24.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to withdraw all waiver applications that have been submitted to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to establish a community engagement program, and declaring an emergency.
ky:HJR 24.summary: Directs the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to withdraw, within five days, its Medicaid waiver applications for a community engagement program, including the one filed June 25, 2025.

ky:HJR 81.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION authorizing the release of funds and declaring an emergency.
ky:HJR 81.summary: Authorizes the state budget director to release $52,502,260 in General Fund money to the Kentucky Infrastructure Authority for 17 listed water and wastewater projects under the Kentucky WWATERS program.

ky:SB 124.title: AN ACT relating to sick leave for school district personnel.
ky:SB 124.summary: Lets school district employees use sick leave for religious holidays not on the school calendar, and lets districts pay employees before retirement for accrued sick leave above 15 days at up to 30% of the daily wage.

ky:SB 127.title: AN ACT relating to actuarial costs of annual leave payments in the Teachers' Retirement System.
ky:SB 127.summary: As amended, makes the state pay Teachers’ Retirement System actuarial costs of annual leave accrued through July 31, 2026, plus up to 5 days yearly for school districts and some state schools; last employers pay rest. Credits leave for retirement only if accrued before August 1, 2026 with employers already paying it.

ky:SB 129.title: AN ACT relating to unemployment insurance.
ky:SB 129.summary: Ends the 0.075% employer unemployment insurance rate reduction after 2026 and sets a 0.0115% reduction from 2027, adjustable yearly up to 0.025%, suspended if the upgrade fund reaches $15 million or the trust fund does not exceed its 2022 balance.

ky:SB 133.title: AN ACT relating to the fiscal reporting of local entities.
ky:SB 133.summary: Raises the receipts or spending thresholds that set audit requirements for special purpose governmental entities, lets entities with two straight unqualified audit opinions move to an audit every four years, and allows agreed-upon-procedures engagements for some, starting July 2027.

ky:SB 147.title: AN ACT relating to vital records.
ky:SB 147.summary: Raises the maximum fee for certifying vital records from $5 to $10 and for a certified birth record from $10 to $15, adds fee waivers for line-of-duty death certificates and declared disasters, and changes how certified copies are requested.

ky:SB 156.title: AN ACT relating to child marriage.
ky:SB 156.summary: Removes the exception letting 17-year-olds marry with court permission, so marriage and marriage licenses are barred under age 18. Lawful marriages entered into before the effective date remain valid.

ky:SB 160.title: AN ACT relating to child-care centers and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 160.summary: Lists factors the Cabinet for Health and Family Services must consider before issuing a plan of correction or suspending or revoking a child-care center license, and requires two weekly support contacts, one in person, for centers on a six-month preliminary license.

ky:SB 197.title: AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 197.summary: Amends the state budget bills to add supplemental appropriations for various programs and projects, with conditions attached.

ky:SB 214.title: AN ACT relating to agriculture and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 214.summary: Allows the Department of Agriculture to accept nonfederal grants and funds from any public or private source, and creates a Kentucky Urban Youth Agriculture Initiative run jointly by the Kentucky State University and University of Kentucky extension services.

ky:SB 261.title: AN ACT relating to pedestrian swinging bridges.
ky:SB 261.summary: Allows fiscal courts and cities to spend public funds to care for and maintain pedestrian swinging bridges open for recreation, and limits liability for owners of land leased to a local government that maintains such a bridge.

ky:SB 281.title: AN ACT relating to grandparent visitation.
ky:SB 281.summary: Requires clear and convincing evidence of compelling factors before granting grandparent visitation over a fit parent (a lower standard applies if a non-parent has custody), lists best-interest factors, and removes the presumption favoring visitation when the child's parent has died.

ky:SB 312.title: AN ACT relating to court-ordered transports.
ky:SB 312.summary: Allows certified court security officers to transport people detained or in custody as ordered by a court, including outside the court facility, to arrest while transporting or supervising them, and to transport people ordered into involuntary hospitalization.

ky:SB 324.title: AN ACT relating to the entertainment industry.
ky:SB 324.summary: Lets unused portions of the $75 million annual film tax credit cap carry into the next year, adds video games, music videos and commercials to eligible productions, and raises minimum qualifying spending for some productions.

ky:SB 37.title: AN ACT relating to state symbols.
ky:SB 37.summary: Names the Treeing Walker Coonhound state dog, cats and dogs adopted from or living in Kentucky shelters or rescues official state pets, the eastern spotted skunk state nongame mammal, and the eastern hellbender state amphibian.

ky:SB 59.title: AN ACT relating to prohibited uses of tax dollars and resources.
ky:SB 59.summary: Extends the ban on using public money to advocate on ballot questions to public resources such as staff, facilities and websites. Sets fines of $500, then $1,000, then a Class A misdemeanor; exempts educational television and employees acting on personal time.

ky:SB 65.title: AN ACT relating to deficient administrative regulations and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 65.summary: Declares six proposed administrative regulations (Medicaid outpatient pharmacy, tobacco and vapor licensing, online insurance verification, controlled substance monitoring, relative caregiver services) null and void and bars agencies from reissuing similar ones through June 1, 2027. Takes effect immediately as an emergency.

ky:SB 66.title: AN ACT relating to the operation of a motor vehicle.
ky:SB 66.summary: Bars driving with clonazepam, cyclobenzaprine or fentanyl detected in the blood, removes blood-test refusal as an aggravating circumstance, and says refusing a preliminary breath test cannot be used in court or cause a license suspension.

ky:SB 70.title: AN ACT relating to the Public Pension Oversight Board.
ky:SB 70.summary: Adds the State Treasurer and a House and Senate state-government committee chair or vice chair to the Public Pension Oversight Board from January 2027, drops one gubernatorial appointee, and extends an annual pension report to line-of-duty death benefits.

ky:SB 9.title: AN ACT relating to teacher benefit provisions and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 9.summary: Has the state pay costs of unused sick leave counted in teachers' retirement pay (balances through June 2025 plus up to 12 days a year), with the last employer paying the rest, and requires districts to offer up to 30 paid maternity days by 2030.

ky:SB 94.title: AN ACT relating to motor vehicle dealers.
ky:SB 94.summary: Sets rules for how motor vehicle manufacturers must compensate dealers for warranty work, including time allowances, labor rates, parts markups, and payment procedures and deadlines.

ky:SB 98.title: AN ACT relating to welding safety.
ky:SB 98.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires structural steel welding on projects whose specifications cite AWS D1.1 or D1.5 to use welders certified by an accredited testing facility and meet those standards, effective January 1, 2027. Exempts homeowner or farmer welding on their own premises.

ky:SCR 66.title: A CONCURRENT RESOLUTION urging the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville to explore opportunities to participate in federal nuclear-related programs and to expand their curricula to offer courses and degree paths to train the workforce that will construct and operate the next generation of nuclear energy facilities.
ky:SCR 66.summary: Urges the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville to explore participating in the U.S. Department of Energy's Nuclear Energy University Program and to expand courses and degree paths training the nuclear energy workforce.

ky:SJR 116.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the University of Kentucky, the University of Louisville, and Eastern Kentucky University to coordinate a search for actionable solutions to physician shortages and to explore and expand health care opportunities in medically underserved areas in collaboration with community, state agency, professional associations, and other stakeholders.
ky:SJR 116.summary: Directs the University of Kentucky, University of Louisville and Eastern Kentucky University to coordinate a search for solutions to physician shortages and report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027.

ky:SJR 54.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Department for Libraries and Archives and the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to cooperate in exploring ways to increase enrollment in Dolly Partonâs Imagination Library Program.
ky:SJR 54.summary: Directs the Department for Libraries and Archives and the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to explore ways to increase enrollment in Dolly Parton's Imagination Library and report by November 1, 2026.

ky:SJR 62.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Division of Water to provide recommendations and clear guidance on how local governments can more easily access jurisdictional streams and waterways for cleanup after a flood.
ky:SJR 62.summary: Directs the Division of Water to report to the Legislative Research Commission by December 15, 2026 on how state and local governments can more easily access public waterways after flooding for debris removal and cleanup.

ky:SJR 74.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Legislative Research Commission and state agencies to collaborate to create a statewide fiscal map of substance use disorder programs and funding sources.
ky:SJR 74.summary: Directs the Legislative Research Commission and state agencies to create a statewide fiscal map of substance use disorder programs and funding sources, post it online, and report to the General Assembly by October 30, 2026.

ky:SJR 75.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Public Service Commission to explore measures that would address affordability and the provision of essential utility services and declaring an emergency.
ky:SJR 75.summary: Directs the Public Service Commission to open administrative cases to identify ways to make utility service more affordable for low- and fixed-income customers and to report to the Legislative Research Commission by September 1, 2027.

la:HB 1.title: APPROPRIATIONS: Provides for the ordinary operating expenses of state government for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 1.summary: Appropriates $46.2 billion for state government operating expenses in fiscal year 2026-27, including $11.7 billion in state general fund money, and transfers $850 million from the Revenue Stabilization Fund to several funds.

la:HB 1005.title: INDIGENT DEFENSE: Provides relative to the office of the state public defender (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1005.summary: Replaces references to the Louisiana Public Defender Board with the office of the state public defender, whom the governor appoints with Senate confirmation to a two-year term. District public defenders who contract with the office are independent contractors.

la:HB 1007.title: DISTRICTS/SPECIAL: Creates the Faubourg Nouveau Marigny Improvement District in Orleans Parish
la:HB 1007.summary: Creates the Faubourg Nouveau Marigny Improvement District in Orleans Parish, run by a five-member board, to fund beautification and streetscape projects. Allows a voter-approved parcel fee, such as up to $100 a year for improved residential parcels.

la:HB 1017.title: RETIREMENT/FIREFIGHTERS: Prohibits certain post-divorce earnable compensation in the Firefighters' Retirement System from being included in a former spouse's portion of community property (EN NO IMPACT APV)
la:HB 1017.summary: Excludes from a former spouse's share of community property any raise in a full-time firefighter's earnable compensation, made after the community ends, that was conditional on passing a written exam and working test.

la:HB 1018.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE PERMT: Provides relative to limitations on the issuance of certain alcoholic beverage permits
la:HB 1018.summary: Bars new high and low alcohol permits for small premises under 5,000 square feet in Louisiana House District 2 from August 1, 2026 through 2027. Exempts downtown Shreveport, Bossier City and purchases of existing licensed premises.

la:HB 1028.title: MEDICAID: Requires the Louisiana Department of Health to increase the reimbursement rates for nonemergency medical transportation providers (EN +$2,601,174 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 1028.summary: Requires the Department of Health to set Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation rates of at least $14.50 per trip and $2.10 per mile, with a multi-passenger rate method. Limits rides outside the home or neighboring parishes unless medically necessary.

la:HB 1029.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE PERMT: Provides relative to limitations on the issuance of certain alcoholic beverage permits
la:HB 1029.summary: As passed by the House, extends the ban on new Class B and C high- and low-alcohol permits in Louisiana House District 3 from the end of 2026 to the end of 2032. Exempts national chains, defined as companies operating in 10 or more states.

la:HB 1043.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the civil jurisdictional amounts for the First and Second Parish Courts
la:HB 1043.summary: Raises the civil jurisdictional limit of the First and Second Parish Courts of Jefferson Parish from $20,000 to $50,000.

la:HB 1049.title: PUBLIC MEETINGS: Provides relative to public meetings (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1049.summary: Lets school boards set reasonable rules on public comment, requires public meeting notices to be posted so the public can read them, and requires draft minutes to go to members five business days before approval.

la:HB 1050.title: MTR VEHICLE/DRIVER LIC: Modifies provisions relative to certain requirements for commercial driver's licenses
la:HB 1050.summary: Revises commercial driver's license rules: removes the tractor-trailer restriction on Class A licenses earned in other vehicles, removes the "straight vehicle" definition, and repeals vision standards for intrastate driver waivers.

la:HB 1051.title: PROPERTY/VACANT SUBSTAND: Provides relative to the demolition of certain dilapidated property in the city of Shreveport
la:HB 1051.summary: Requires Shreveport commercial property owners who received an insurance payment for fire damage to demolish the structure if the city finds it dilapidated and dangerous, applying retroactively to Jan. 1, 2023.

la:HB 1052.title: CHILDRENS CODE: Provides relative to confidentiality policies and procedures pertaining to work product created, received, or maintained by child advocacy centers and multidisciplinary investigative teams
la:HB 1052.summary: Requires each multidisciplinary child abuse investigative team and child advocacy center to adopt a written confidentiality policy limiting shared information to authorized participants for investigation, assessment, prosecution and treatment, and covers team work product.

la:HB 1056.title: PROPERTY/PUBLIC: Authorizes the transfer of certain state property in Natchitoches Parish
la:HB 1056.summary: Authorizes the president of the Board of Elementary and Secondary Education and the commissioner of administration to transfer about 1.16 acres of state property in Natchitoches Parish, excluding mineral rights, which the state keeps.

la:HB 1062.title: SCHOOLS: Provides relative to the membership, powers, and duties of the board of directors of the Special School District
la:HB 1062.summary: Changes the Special School District board: ends the one-member-per-health-region appointment rule, requires annual nominee lists by Aug. 1, has the board authorize the superintendent to select textbooks, and requires annual superintendent evaluations.

la:HB 1076.title: HEALTH/BEHAVIORAL: Repeals the termination of the Louisiana Behavior Analyst Board
la:HB 1076.summary: Repeals the July 1, 2028 termination date of the Louisiana Behavior Analyst Board, keeping the board and behavior analyst licensing in place.

la:HB 1081.title: PORTS/HARBORS/TERMINALS: Provides for the Louisiana Ports and Waterways Investment Commission (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1081.summary: Moves the Louisiana Ports and Waterways Investment Commission from the governor's office to the Office of Multimodal Commerce within the Department of Transportation and Development.

la:HB 1082.title: CIVIL/VENUE: Provides for venue with respect to the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System
la:HB 1082.summary: As passed by the House, requires lawsuits involving the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System to be filed in the district court of the judicial district where the employer is located, instead of East Baton Rouge or the system's domicile parish.

la:HB 1084.title: STUDENT/TUITION: Provides relative to tuition and mandatory fees for public postsecondary education institutions
la:HB 1084.summary: Authorizes each public college and university to set and adjust tuition and fees for all programs, with increases capped at 10% per year and no cap on reductions, starting January 1, 2027.

la:HB 1095.title: NURSING HOMES: Provides for alternative power sources at nursing facilities
la:HB 1095.summary: Creates a rebate program, capped at $2 million total, for certain nursing facilities that install solar energy systems, and clarifies that nursing facilities must keep fuel or an alternative power source stored on site.

la:HB 1098.title: LIABILITY/CIVIL: Provides with respect to a limitation of liability for aerospace entities
la:HB 1098.summary: As passed by the House, bars nuisance, trespass and similar claims against aerospace flight entities over noise, vibration, light, exhaust and other flight-related disturbances. Exceptions include gross negligence, violating federal license conditions and falling debris beyond normal risk.

la:HB 1100.title: SMALL BUSINESS: Repeals requirements for enriching bread and flour sold in this state
la:HB 1100.summary: Repeals the state requirement that bread and flour sold in Louisiana be enriched with vitamins, along with the related labeling, exemption and Department of Health inspection provisions.

la:HB 1117.title: INSURANCE: Provides relative to certain insurer contractual payments and prescriptive period
la:HB 1117.summary: As passed by the House, provides that an insurer's payment under its contract is not an acknowledgment of debt and does not interrupt the time limit for suing on the policy.

la:HB 1126.title: LEGISLATIVE EXPENSES: Makes appropriations for the expenses of the legislature for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 1126.summary: Appropriates $94.5 million in state general funds for the expenses of the Legislature and legislative agencies for fiscal year 2026-2027, including $33.0 million for the House and $28.1 million for the Senate.

la:HB 1129.title: PROPERTY/PUBLIC: Provides relative to the selling of state-owned surplus movable property (EN SEE FISC NOTE SG EX)
la:HB 1129.summary: Gives preference to in-state auctioneers over out-of-state ones when the commissioner of administration sells surplus state movable property, if service quality is equal and cost is within 10 percent.

la:HB 1139.title: MENTAL HEALTH: Requires certain behavioral health services for patients receiving treatment pursuant to an emergency certificate
la:HB 1139.summary: Requires a health care facility that admits a patient on an emergency certificate to have a licensed professional conduct a behavioral health evaluation and contact the patient's behavioral health provider for treatment history within 72 hours.

la:HB 1153.title: ENVIRONMENT/ENFORCEMENT: Authorizes parishes and municipalities to declare bans on burning
la:HB 1153.summary: Lets parish and municipal governments issue burn bans during elevated fire risk, requires lifting them when risk ends, requires parishes to publish notice in the official journal, and sets fines of $500 to $2,500 for violations.

la:HB 1161.title: PROPERTY/PUBLIC: Authorizes the transfer of certain state property in Lafourche Parish
la:HB 1161.summary: Authorizes the transportation and development secretary to transfer certain Lafourche Parish property to the city of Thibodaux and certain Jefferson Parish property to the city of Gretna, reserving mineral rights to the state.

la:HB 1162.title: INSURANCE CLAIMS: Provides relative to the verification of contractors
la:HB 1162.summary: Requires insurers to verify a contractor's license with the state licensing board before paying a property-repair claim that names the contractor as payee, and shields insurers from bad-faith penalties for delays caused by failed verification if they notify the insured within five business days.

la:HB 1182.title: OCCUPATIONAL THERAPISTS: Provides relative to the rules governing Occupational Therapists and Occupational Therapy Assistants
la:HB 1182.summary: Requires occupational therapy license applicants to pass the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy exam, replaces references to the American Occupational Therapy Association with that board, removes a license waiver for certain state employees, and raises most license fees.

la:HB 1186.title: BUILDING CODES: Provides relative to the Uniform Construction Code and inspector licensing
la:HB 1186.summary: Replaces the Uniform Construction Code Council with a Uniform Construction Code Commission that adopts the state building code and licenses inspectors.

la:HB 1189.title: WILDLIFE & FISHERIES: Provides for charter boat fishing guide licenses
la:HB 1189.summary: Requires freshwater charter boat fishing guides operating on U.S. waters in Louisiana to hold a U.S. Coast Guard captain's license, and renames the nonresident saltwater guide license a nonresident charter boat fishing guide license.

la:HB 119.title: CRIME: Provides relative to unlawful conduct involving images of another person created by artificial intelligence (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 119.summary: Raises penalties for disseminating or selling AI-created images of a person (up to five years if under 17), creates a crime of possessing such images of people under 17, and adds up to two consecutive years when an educator's victim is a student.

la:HB 1193.title: CONTRACTS/BIDS: Provides for Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity construction phase contracts (EN SEE FISC NOTE SD EX See Note)
la:HB 1193.summary: Lets the Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity construction contracts for coastal protection projects, using single or multiple awards and low bid, best value or qualification-based selection.

la:HB 1194.title: AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES: Provides with respect to the Healthy Food Retail Act (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1194.summary: Expands the Healthy Food Retail Act to cover food deserts, defined as low-income census tracts with many residents far from a supermarket, and other food access projects, with priority for projects showing demand and long-term sustainability.

la:HB 1195.title: AMUSEMENTS/SPORTS: Provides relative to the Louisiana State Athletic Commission
la:HB 1195.summary: Changes State Athletic Commission rules: cuts the maximum rounds in a boxing contest from 20 to 12, raises the maximum fine on licensees from $1,000 to $5,000 and on unauthorized events from $500 to $5,000, and adds cease and desist authority.

la:HB 1199.title: INSURANCE/HEALTH: Provides relative to health insurance coverage for genetic testing and the treatment of SCN2A-associated medical conditions (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1199.summary: Requires health plans, starting Jan. 1, 2027, to cover genetic testing and medically necessary treatment for SCN2A-associated conditions when ordered by a treating provider, while allowing nondiscriminatory prior authorization.

la:HB 1201.title: ELECTED OFFICIALS/COMP: Provides with respect to the compensation of statewide elected officials and legislators (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 1201.summary: Lets legislators claim per diem and mileage for up to 10 days a month of official business, extends the $1,000 monthly housing allowance to all legislators, and adds inflation adjustments and allowances for statewide elected officials other than the governor.

la:HB 1203.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to parent-driven learning microschools
la:HB 1203.summary: Defines parent-driven learning microschools as parent groups teaching mixed-age children in homes or community spaces. Provides that using a building for one does not change its zoning, building code or fire safety status, and exempts microschools from state registration and early learning center licensing.

la:HB 1223.title: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT: Establishes the Louisiana Clinical Trial Competitiveness and Patient Access Act
la:HB 1223.summary: Creates the Louisiana Clinical Trial Competitiveness and Patient Access Act: lets Louisiana Economic Development market voluntarily provided clinical-trial capabilities, and has research entities use an external central review board for Phase II and III trials unless the sponsor requests otherwise or the entity head excepts.

la:HB 1228.title: HEARING AID DEALERS: Relative to the Louisiana Board of Hearing Aid Dealers
la:HB 1228.summary: Changes hearing aid dealer rules: ends their role collecting taxes, requires a seller email on sales contracts, lets buyers cancel by notifying the seller in person, by mail or by email, and revises licensing requirements.

la:HB 1230.title: COMMERCIAL REGULATIONS: Provides relative to the Louisiana Money Transmission Act
la:HB 1230.summary: Repeals the Sale of Checks and Money Transmission Act and enacts the Louisiana Money Transmission Act, setting licensing, exemption, supervision and examination rules for money transmitters under the financial institutions commissioner, including multistate examinations.

la:HB 1231.title: MEDICAID MANAGED CARE: Provides relative to Medicaid coverage for continuous glucose monitoring devices for individuals with certain conditions (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1231.summary: Changes Medicaid coverage of continuous glucose monitoring to cover diabetes, including gestational diabetes, for people who require insulin or have level 2 or 3 hypoglycemia, rather than only those needing insulin more than twice daily.

la:HB 1234.title: CRIMINAL/PENALTIES: Provides relative to penalties for hit-and-run driving (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 1234.summary: Requires at least two or five years of a hit-and-run sentence, depending on the offense level, to be served without parole, probation or suspension when the victim is a pedestrian or bicyclist.

la:HB 1236.title: INSURANCE: Provides relative to pharmacy benefit managers reimbursements (EN +$2,265,844 SG EX See Note)
la:HB 1236.summary: Changes how pharmacy benefit managers reimburse pharmacies, requiring a formula with a professional dispensing fee of at least $9 applied retroactively to January 1, 2026, and barring managers from recovering that fee from pharmacies.

la:HB 1237.title: RETIREMENT/STATEWIDE SYS: Provides relative to the Municipal Police Employees Retirement System and the Firefighters' Retirement System (EN SEE ACTUARIAL NOTE FC)
la:HB 1237.summary: Requires a police chief or mayor to sign and notarize a police officer's affidavit opting out of the municipal police retirement system, repeals partial-dissolution payments for police departments, and changes the payment formula and triggers for fire departments.

la:HB 1243.title: SEWERAGE/N O WATER BD: Provides relative to the Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans
la:HB 1243.summary: Removes the state-law makeup of the New Orleans Sewerage and Water Board, including its selection committee and quorum rule, and lets the board's composition follow the city charter, with the city council setting appointment and term rules by ordinance.

la:HB 1249.title: HEALTH/SCHOOL CLINICS: Provides relative to school-based health center services provided to students (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 1249.summary: Bars school employees from preventing a student from using medically necessary school-based health center services when a parent, guardian or adult student consents, and requires school policies that avoid delays or extra barriers for licensed providers.

la:HB 1252.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the city court system in Avoyelles Parish (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 1252.summary: Assigns Avoyelles Parish wards to the Marksville and Bunkie city courts, which share concurrent jurisdiction with the 12th Judicial District Court over misdemeanors, civil disputes under $50,000 and juvenile matters, for cases filed from January 1, 2027.

la:HB 1256.title: PROPERTY/UNCLAIMED: Provides with respect to abandoned digital assets
la:HB 1256.summary: Adds digital assets to the unclaimed property law, presuming them abandoned three years after the owner's last sign of interest. Holder notices must warn that the asset may be liquidated without a response; the state generally waits three years after receiving it to liquidate.

la:HB 129.title: HIGHWAYS: Designates certain portions of Louisiana highways
la:HB 129.summary: Designates a stretch of Louisiana Highway 1 in Shreveport as the "Virginia Green Evans Memorial Highway" and directs signage if local or private money covers its cost, up to $750 per sign.

la:HB 153.title: COURTS/CRIMINAL: Provides with respect to the collection of criminal court fines and fees
la:HB 153.summary: Bars reporting criminal fines and fees debt to credit bureaus or consumer reporting agencies. Does not apply to traffic law violations under Title 32 or municipal law violations. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 159.title: CRIMINAL/SENTENCING: Creates a pretrial incarceration alternative pilot program in Caddo Parish (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX See Note)
la:HB 159.summary: Lets the Caddo Parish Sheriff run a pretrial pilot program, starting by January 1, 2027, using electronic monitoring instead of jail for eligible defendants, with court and district attorney approval.

la:HB 166.title: JUVENILES: Removes Vermilion Parish as a member of the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District
la:HB 166.summary: Removes Vermilion Parish from the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District and cuts the district commission from 11 to 10 members.

la:HB 167.title: PUBLIC SFTY/CORRECTIONS: Provides for the issuance of certain documentation to inmates before their release from incarceration (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 167.summary: Requires the corrections department to give felony inmates released to a Louisiana residence documentation for job searches and, with the Office of Motor Vehicles, to start ID paperwork nine months before release and issue those without current ID a six-year special ID card.

la:HB 180.title: PROPERTY/EXPROPRIATION: Provides relative to expropriation by private entities
la:HB 180.summary: Defines "foreign adversary" and "agent of a foreign adversary" for the law on expropriation by private entities, presuming control when a person holds at least 50% of an entity's voting interests or profits.

la:HB 2.title: CAPITAL OUTLAY: Provides for the comprehensive Capital Outlay budget
la:HB 2.summary: Sets the capital outlay budget for fiscal year 2026-27, with about $3.17 billion in cash and authority for about $11.5 billion in general obligation bonds for listed projects.

la:HB 210.title: ETHICS/CODE: Provides for restrictions on payments from nonpublic sources
la:HB 210.summary: Bars statewide elected officials from being paid for lobbying, consulting or advising. Applies retroactively an existing exception letting school board and local governing authority members work for employers doing business with their government, except where an ethics body has issued a final decision.

la:HB 211.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the creation, administration, and eligibility requirements of the Homelessness Court program (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 211.summary: Lets district courts create Homelessness Court programs with probation conditions, and creates the crime of unauthorized camping on public property, punishable by up to $500, six months in jail, or both. Offenders may qualify for court programs.

la:HB 226.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Provides relative to requests for admissions
la:HB 226.summary: Replaces the rule that a request for admission is deemed admitted after 30 days without a written answer with a requirement for a Rule 10.1 conference first, except for default judgments.

la:HB 227.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Provides that filings may be made on letter size rather than legal size paper
la:HB 227.summary: Allows court filings, electronic or paper, on letter size or legal size paper, and removes full dates of birth from the personal information barred from civil and criminal court filings.

la:HB 258.title: ETHICS/DUAL OFFICEHOLDG: Provides for exceptions to the dual officeholding laws for volunteer firefighters and judicial branch employees
la:HB 258.summary: As passed by the Senate, adds dual officeholding exceptions for volunteer firefighters, unpaid advisory committee members and judicial branch employees serving on boards, and bars full-time appointed officers and employees from serving on boards not required by law for their duties.

la:HB 291.title: INSURANCE/HEALTH: Prohibits health insurers from taking adverse payment or contracting actions against participating facilities based solely on another provider's network status (EN INCREASE  EX See Note)
la:HB 291.summary: Bars health insurers from reducing payments to, or suspending or ending contracts with, a participating licensed health care facility solely because a nonparticipating provider was involved in a patient's care; the Office of Group Benefits is exempt.

la:HB 3.title: CAPITAL OUTLAY: Provides for the Omnibus Bond Act
la:HB 3.summary: Authorizes a five-year capital improvement program, repealing certain prior bond authorizations, creating new ones, and providing for bond authorization and sale by the State Bond Commission.

la:HB 302.title: TOBACCO/TOBACCO PRODUCTS: Prohibits the sale of vapor products near schools
la:HB 302.summary: Bars the sale or storage of vapor products within 300 feet of a school where a municipal or parish ordinance provides, measured along sidewalks unless the local government chooses straight-line measurement for new permits.

la:HB 312.title: APPROPRIATIONS/SUPPLEML: Makes supplemental appropriations for Fiscal Year 2025-2026
la:HB 312.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for fiscal year 2025-26, adding about $301.8 million in state general fund money, including $144.3 million from surplus toward the state employees' retirement system's unfunded liability.

la:HB 314.title: REVENUE SHARING: Provides for the Revenue Sharing Distribution for Fiscal Year 2026-2027
la:HB 314.summary: Distributes $90 million in state revenue sharing to parishes in fiscal year 2026-27, with 80% allocated by population and 20% by number of homesteads, paid in three installments.

la:HB 316.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to student literacy (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 316.summary: Adds adolescent literacy instruction to special and secondary education teacher programs, and requires schools to assess grade 4-8 students who scored below mastery in English, notify parents of reading deficiencies, and provide interventions and reading improvement plans.

la:HB 324.title: JUDGES: Provides relative to judicial salaries (EN +$6,690,757 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 324.summary: Raises salaries of Louisiana Supreme Court, appeals court and district court judges by $10,723 to $12,129 from July 1, 2026, and by 2.7% from July 1, 2027, with the 2026-27 increase paid from judiciary reserves.

la:HB 325.title: TOPS: Provides relative to TOPS-Tech (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 325.summary: Lets part-time students receive TOPS awards in some cases. For TOPS-Tech, adds a third eligibility criterion of nine early college credit hours, and students qualify by meeting two of three criteria, for 2026-2027 graduates onward.

la:HB 337.title: GAMING: Provides relative to charitable bingo and the issuance of special licenses
la:HB 337.summary: Increases the number of special bingo sessions a licensed charitable organization may hold each year under a special license from two to four.

la:HB 342.title: EDUCATION/SPECIAL: Provides that a local education agency shall have the burden of proof in any special education due process hearing relative to the appropriateness of a student's current or proposed program or placement (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 342.summary: Requires the local education agency to carry the burden of proof, by a preponderance of the evidence, in special education due process hearings on whether a student's program or placement is appropriate.

la:HB 352.title: STUDENTS: Provides relative to behavioral health services for public school students (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX)
la:HB 352.summary: Requires school boards to post behavioral health service policies online and in handbooks, requires in-classroom services where medically necessary, sets a service-delivery review meeting within 21 days of a parent's treatment plan, and bars recording other students during virtual supervision.

la:HB 36.title: JUVENILES: Removes Evangeline Parish as a member of the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District
la:HB 36.summary: Adds parish presidents in certain parishes as joint appointing authorities for the Acadiana Regional Juvenile Justice District commission, and requires approval by every board member and each member parish's governing authority before a tax measure goes on the ballot.
