md:HB 849.title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Freeze in Enrollment - Exceptions and Waitlist
md:HB 849.summary: Bars Child Care Scholarship enrollment freezes from covering certain groups such as children with enrolled siblings and homeless children, and requires a waitlist with priority enrollment for certain applicants.

md:HB 862.title: Railroads - Required Crew for Movement of Freight
md:HB 862.summary: Bars freight trains sharing a corridor with high-speed passenger or commuter trains from running with fewer than two crew; fines up to $10,000 for a willful violation, $25,000 within 3 years of a prior one; needs similar laws in New York, Pennsylvania and Virginia.

md:HB 866.title: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing - Extension
md:HB 866.summary: Extends the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to December 31, 2028, and moves its report deadline to December 1, 2028.

md:HB 882.title: Consumer Health Information - Termination Date and Mandatory Funding for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub - Repeal
md:HB 882.summary: Makes the Consumer Health Information Hub's duties apply only to the extent funding is available, ends the required budget appropriation for the Hub, and removes the termination date on consumer health information provisions.

md:HB 889.title: Wicomico County - Property Tax Credit - Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.
md:HB 889.summary: Authorizes Wicomico County and its towns to grant property tax credits for property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. that is used for development, rehabilitation and transfer to private owners.

md:HB 894.title: Land Use - Transit-Oriented Development - Alterations (Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act)
md:HB 894.summary: Makes transit-oriented developments designated on or after October 1, 2026 at stations with hourly rail service automatic enterprise zones unless the locality opts out, generally bars minimum parking requirements within 0.25 mile of such stations, and prioritizes State-owned land near stations for infrastructure loans.

md:HB 914.title: Worcester County - Board of License Commissioners - Membership
md:HB 914.summary: Increases the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members appointed by the Governor, with terms staggered; takes effect June 1, 2026.

md:HB 919.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program - Established
md:HB 919.summary: Creates a Maryland Higher Education Commission grant program for minorities living in historically redlined neighborhoods and underrepresented communities to pursue Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal training.

md:HB 936.title: Montgomery County Public Schools - Jane E. Lawton Local Food Procurement MC 7-26
md:HB 936.summary: Requires Montgomery County public schools to publish the dollar amount of school-meal food bought from certified local farms and invasive-species providers in 2026-27, then set target increases for later school years and a plan to meet them.

md:HB 951.title: Real Property - Recordation and Land Records - Revisions
md:HB 951.summary: Repeals the margin requirement for printed deeds and other instruments offered for recording, and requires circuit court clerks to date each change or correction made to the general alphabetical index.

md:HB 991.title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class HC (Health Club) License - Hours of Sale
md:HB 991.summary: Extends the closing time for beer and wine sales by Harford County Class HC (health club) licensees from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m.

md:SB 101.title: Higher Education - Loan Repayment and Scholarships for Correctional Officers
md:SB 101.summary: Expands the state police officer and probation agent scholarship and loan repayment programs to include correctional officers, with the same eligibility and service requirements, and renames the programs.

md:SB 12.title: Residential Rental Apartments - Air-Conditioning Requirement
md:SB 12.summary: Requires landlords of apartment buildings with 10 or more units to provide air conditioning from June 1 to September 30, capable of keeping habitable spaces at 80 degrees or below, in new units, units that had or required it since 2025, and some renovated units.

md:SB 13.title: Alcoholic Beverages - License Fee Refund Requirements - Alterations
md:SB 13.summary: Extends alcoholic beverages license fee refunds for license holders called into the armed forces to those called into the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Corps and Public Health Service.

md:SB 140.title: Criminal Law - Benefits Exploitation
md:SB 140.summary: Bars knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting or obtaining a person to take their government benefits (such as Medicaid, SNAP or Social Security) through deception, coercion or other means, and bars profiting from or aiding that conduct. Penalties scale with the value involved.

md:SB 148.title: Income Tax - Credit for 9-1-1 Specialist Retirement Income (Supporting Our 9-1-1 Specialists Act)
md:SB 148.summary: Creates a nonrefundable income tax credit for tax years 2026 through 2028 equal to 4.75% of the first $15,000 of retirement income from 9-1-1 specialist service, capped at $700, with $250,000 in total credits certifiable per year.

md:SB 16.title: Child Support - Earnings Withholdings Limits
md:SB 16.summary: Caps child support earnings withholding at 35% of disposable earnings for obligors whose income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty level for one person, and lets employees contest withholding amounts.

md:SB 168.title: Study to Evaluate Blockchain-Based Real Property Lease and Title Recordation and Verification
md:SB 168.summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to study using blockchain to record and verify property ownership and leases, including for squatting disputes, and report by December 31, 2026.

md:SB 169.title: Hospitals - Emergency Pregnancy-Related Medical Conditions - Procedures
md:SB 169.summary: Requires hospitals that find a patient has an emergency pregnancy-related condition to stabilize the patient, including by terminating the pregnancy when the treating practitioner finds it medically necessary, or transfer them; bars retaliation against certain staff; sets civil penalties up to $25,000-$50,000 per violation.

md:SB 182.title: Adult Protective Services - Modifications
md:SB 182.summary: Changes adult protective services law by adding an online reporting portal, requiring investigators to assess risk of harm and find abuse indicated, not indicated or undetermined, repealing the 10-day deadline for emergency investigations, and revising definitions.

md:SB 187.title: Correctional Services - Comprehensive Rehabilitative Prerelease Services - Female Incarcerated Individuals (Monica Cooper Prerelease Act)
md:SB 187.summary: Requires the women's prerelease unit to become a facility in Baltimore City for incarcerated women within 36 months of release, resets deadlines (opening by September 2031), adds public-benefits screening to services, and requires annual Correctional Ombudsman progress reports.

md:SB 194.title: Income and Property Tax Incentives - Members and Veterans of the Space Force - Application
md:SB 194.summary: Creates one definition of "active military, naval, air, or space service" and applies it to property tax benefits for disabled veterans, disabled service members and surviving spouses, and to the job creation tax credit's definition of qualified veteran employee.

md:SB 198.title: Prince George's Community College - Aerospace and Aviation Systems Technology Programs - Feasibility Study
md:SB 198.summary: Requires Prince George's Community College to study aerospace and aviation systems technology training programs and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2027, with $100,000 in the fiscal 2028 budget for the study.

md:SB 204.title: Public Schools - Maryland Civic Excellence Program - Established
md:SB 204.summary: Creates the Maryland Civic Excellence Program in the State Department of Education to recognize public high school students' civic readiness and engagement, with the State Board of Education setting criteria by regulation and local school systems opting in.

md:SB 242.title: Modernizing Civil Relief for Service Members Act
md:SB 242.summary: Lets active service members and spouses who relocate to Maryland on service orders practice under another state's license for the orders' duration after applying, and removes the 1-year post-discharge limit from the "eligible veteran" definition in licensing laws.

md:SB 244.title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
md:SB 244.summary: Revises and recodifies the State's Medicaid laws as a nonsubstantive revision, with technical and stylistic changes and updated terminology.

md:SB 252.title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership
md:SB 252.summary: Increases the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12 members.

md:SB 253.title: Baltimore County Public Library - Collective Bargaining - Supervisory Employees
md:SB 253.summary: Lets supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library form or join employee organizations and bargain collectively, and authorizes bargaining units for library employees.

md:SB 263.title: Education - Dependent Children of Active Service Members - Advance Enrollment Procedures
md:SB 263.summary: Requires county superintendents to let a dependent child of an active service member advance enroll, including by fee-free remote registration, and requires boards to avoid delays in services for children with disabilities. Directs the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to publish enrollment information.

md:SB 276.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Orthoses and Prostheses (So Every Body Can Move Act)
md:SB 276.summary: Requires Medicaid and certain insurers to cover orthoses starting January 1, 2027, and clarifies that required prosthesis coverage includes all prostheses a provider finds medically necessary for daily living, work or physical activities.

md:SB 285.title: Higher Education - Scholarships for Correctional Officers
md:SB 285.summary: Expands the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program to include correctional officers and students in certificate programs, and renames the program.

md:SB 292.title: County Boards of Education - Student Transportation - Sunset Repeal and Study
md:SB 292.summary: Repeals the sunset on a 2021 law letting county school boards transport students in vehicles other than Type I or II school vehicles when none can reasonably be provided, and requires a State Department of Education regulation review and report by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 30.title: Baltimore County - Property Tax Credit - Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
md:SB 30.summary: Lets Baltimore County grant a 100% property tax credit on real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 in Middle River, for tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

md:SB 309.title: Sales and Use Tax - Precious Metal Bullion or Coins - Exemption
md:SB 309.summary: Expands the sales and use tax exemption for precious metal bullion and coins by repealing the minimum sale price and Baltimore Convention Center sale requirements, and revises the definition so value depends primarily on metal content.

md:SB 311.title: Education - The Blueprint for Maryland's Future - Revisions
md:SB 311.summary: Extends the current low-income student count method for compensatory education and concentration of poverty grants through fiscal 2028, adds teacher certification options, and delays the National Board Certification requirement for licensed principals from 2029 to 2034.

md:SB 322.title: Courts - Jury Service - Disqualification
md:SB 322.summary: Changes jury disqualification: a person convicted of a crime punishable by over a year is disqualified while serving the sentence, including parole or probation. Also disqualifies those convicted of perjury, witness or jury intimidation, or fraud crimes. Repeals the pardon provision.

md:SB 324.title: Higher Education - Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Direct Admission Program and Study
md:SB 324.summary: Creates a direct admission program at participating public senior colleges starting 2028-2029, offering conditional admission with a waived application fee to high school students who meet set requirements, including college and career ready standards and a minimum GPA.

md:SB 325.title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)
md:SB 325.summary: Requires housing development applications to be judged only under laws in effect when a complete application is submitted, and gives approved projects vested development rights for 5 years or a locally set period, whichever is longer.

md:SB 339.title: Maryland School for the Deaf - Membership of Board of Trustees - Alterations
md:SB 339.summary: Reduces the Maryland School for the Deaf Board of Trustees from 19 to 13 members, raises the minimum number of deaf members from 6 to 7, and sets a phase-out of six members.

md:SB 366.title: Motor Vehicles - Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program - Establishment
md:SB 366.summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to create, by October 1, 2027, a pilot program requiring drivers whose accumulated points would trigger license suspension or revocation to use an aftermarket intelligent speed assistance device that prevents exceeding the speed limit, under a restricted license.

md:SB 378.title: Public Libraries - Young Readers Matching Grant Program, Funding, and Services
md:SB 378.summary: Increases state per-capita aid to public library systems and regional resource centers starting in fiscal 2028, changes the services libraries must offer, and raises the Young Readers Grant Program's mandated funding from $350,000 to $450,000.

md:SB 379.title: Recovery Residence Grant Program - Funding
md:SB 379.summary: Extends through fiscal year 2030 the requirement to include $500,000 in the state budget for the Recovery Residence Grant Program.

md:SB 398.title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners - Alterations
md:SB 398.summary: Increases the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members, requires the Governor to appoint them from lists recommended by county legislators, limits two per legislative district, and requires a conflict-of-interest policy.

md:SB 400.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Entertainment Permits
md:SB 400.summary: Renames Anne Arundel County music, entertainment and dancing permits as background, general and full entertainment permits, changes what each allows, and requires outdoor entertainment under the general and full permits to be at least 100 feet from residentially zoned property.

md:SB 401.title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners and Part-Time Inspectors - Compensation
md:SB 401.summary: Raises annual salaries for the chair, part-time inspectors and other members of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and includes cost-of-living increases given to nonrepresented county employees.

md:SB 410.title: Public Libraries - State Library Resource Center - Funding
md:SB 410.summary: Raises per capita State aid for the State Library Resource Center starting in fiscal 2028, by 10 cents per capita that year, rising to 57 cents in fiscal 2032.

md:SB 414.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Consumption-Only Nonprofit Swim Club License
md:SB 414.summary: Creates a $100 annual consumption-only license for nonprofit swim clubs in Anne Arundel County, letting members and guests bring their own alcohol to designated events, up to five days a year between 2 p.m. and 10 p.m.

md:SB 42.title: Reduction Facilities and Veterans Service Organizations - Hydrolyzed and Soil Remains - Immunity
md:SB 42.summary: Extends civil-liability protection for good-faith transfers or receipt of unclaimed veterans' remains to hydrolyzed and soil remains, covering funeral establishments, reduction operators, crematories and veterans service organizations.

md:SB 420.title: Public Institutions of Higher Education - Pregnant and Parenting Students - Plan and Reporting
md:SB 420.summary: Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to collect data on students' parental status from every public college, and extends pregnant and parenting student support plan requirements to community colleges.

md:SB 426.title: Public Information Act - Divorce Records
md:SB 426.summary: Requires custodians to deny public inspection of divorce records, including applications, financial records, settlements and custody orders, except to people in interest, their lawyers, or by court order; final divorce decrees remain open.

md:SB 428.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Collaborative Care Model - Cost Sharing Prohibition
md:SB 428.summary: Bars the Maryland Department of Health from charging copayments, coinsurance or deductibles for collaborative care model services, requires insurers to cover them, and orders a study on ending cost sharing.

md:SB 441.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Golf Course License and Sports Activity Venue Licenses
md:SB 441.summary: Creates in Anne Arundel County a Class C GC golf course license for beer, wine and liquor and two sports activity venue licenses (beer and wine, or beer, wine and liquor), all for on-premises consumption.

md:SB 442.title: Real Property - Landlord and Tenant - Procedures for Failure to Pay Rent, Breach of Lease, and Tenant Holding Over
md:SB 442.summary: Requires landlords to give tenants written notice at least 6 days before a warrant of restitution is executed, and lets tenants recover damages and attorney's fees for violations. Applies only to cases filed after the effective date.

md:SB 448.title: Carroll County - Public Facilities Bond
md:SB 448.summary: Authorizes the Carroll County Commissioners to borrow up to $27 million through general obligation bonds for public facilities, including water and sewer projects and loans to volunteer fire departments.

md:SB 450.title: Carroll County - Office of Permits and Inspections - Denial of Commercial Permit or License for Unpaid Personal Property Taxes
md:SB 450.summary: Lets the Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections deny or refuse to renew a commercial license or permit for unpaid personal property taxes, unless the applicant shows evidence of disputing the amount, and allows issuance once the taxes are shown to be paid.

md:SB 459.title: Procurement - Advertising - Maryland News Organizations (Local News for Maryland Communities Act of 2026)
md:SB 459.summary: Requires state procurement units to direct 50% of advertising contract dollars to Maryland news organizations, except advertising aimed outside Maryland for tourism, recruitment or investment, and to prioritize outlets serving underserved communities.

md:SB 461.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program - Heat and Eat Program - Study
md:SB 461.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study how many households lose automatic utility allowance eligibility in the SNAP Heat and Eat program under the 2025 federal budget law, and report findings and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

md:SB 467.title: Maryland Child Care Credential Program - Extension of Funding
md:SB 467.summary: Requires the Governor to include $5,687,000 a year in the budget for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program in fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:SB 469.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
md:SB 469.summary: Lowers from 3% to 1% the cap on the private passenger auto assessment allocation percentage that supports the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund, and lets the fund, with Insurance Commissioner approval, run a premium-limiting affordability program for low-income policyholders; effective July 2027, ends June 30, 2029.

md:SB 48.title: Education - Public School Construction - Alterations
md:SB 48.summary: Revises public school construction rules, requiring county boards to get State Superintendent approval for certain actions, letting the Interagency Commission set funding eligibility rules, creating an appeal process, and changing report due dates and debt service reimbursement provisions.

md:SB 486.title: School Health and Wellness Personnel Assessment and Maryland Council
md:SB 486.summary: Requires the health and education departments to assess the school health and wellness workforce each year, and adds a school nurse to the Maryland Council on Advancement of School-Based Health Centers.

md:SB 496.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Coverage for the Treatment of Obesity - Authorization
md:SB 496.summary: Allows Medicaid, starting January 1, 2027, to cover obesity treatment, including behavioral therapy, bariatric surgery and FDA-approved weight-management medication, and lets the Health Department seek federal approval for that coverage.

md:SB 497.title: Property Tax - City of Hagerstown and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. - Exemption
md:SB 497.summary: Exempts City of Hagerstown-owned property used mainly for public social, recreational or entertainment purposes from State, county and municipal property tax, and makes that exemption and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility's exemption retroactive to fiscal 2024, with refunds.

md:SB 501.title: Washington County - Property Tax Credit - Platoon 22, Incorporated
md:SB 501.summary: Requires Washington County and its municipalities to grant a 100% property tax credit on real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated and used to provide housing to veterans.

md:SB 503.title: Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program - Funding
md:SB 503.summary: Requires the Governor to include $450,000 in the budget for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program in each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:SB 507.title: Public Schools - Individuals With Disabilities - Accessibility and Emergency Planning
md:SB 507.summary: Requires each school system's safety evaluation to identify disability-accessibility issues, and its annual report to list times a school facility became inaccessible to a student with a disability in a way that could impede evacuation. The report is confidential, except to legislators on request.

md:SB 509.title: Higher Education - Workforce Pell Grant Program - Implementation
md:SB 509.summary: Sets up Maryland's Workforce Pell Grant process: the Governor, consulting the Workforce Development Board, may approve short-term career programs for federal Pell Grants; the board and MHEC may charge application fees, and the board must collect institution data.

md:SB 521.title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period
md:SB 521.summary: Extends enrollee notice and 90-day continued-care rights from primary care providers to behavioral health providers leaving a network, requires notice of intent to terminate a contract, and gives individual-market enrollees a special enrollment period when their provider is terminated.

md:SB 530.title: Aging-in-Place Programs - Grants - Multigenerational Third Places (Village Multigenerational Third Places Act)
md:SB 530.summary: Lets the Department of Aging give grants to nonprofits and area agencies on aging for events at multigenerational third places that support social connection among people in aging-in-place programs.

md:SB 532.title: Higher Education Institutions - Over-the-Counter Contraception - Access and Reporting
md:SB 532.summary: Requires public four-year colleges to report annually on over-the-counter contraception access, adds reporting items for community colleges, and requires community colleges to give students access to all over-the-counter contraception methods.

md:SB 535.title: County Boards of Library Trustees - Membership - Student Member
md:SB 535.summary: Lets a county library board of trustees select a high school junior or senior as a student member, with a one-year term; the student member may vote on policy matters.

md:SB 58.title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions
md:SB 58.summary: Lets local governments grant a property tax credit on real property converted from a retail gas station to certain retail, residential or mixed uses, only if underground storage tanks have been permanently closed.

md:SB 597.title: Higher Education - Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership
md:SB 597.summary: Creates the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership within the University System of Maryland to coordinate AI workforce, business and research efforts, with a strategic plan due December 1, 2026. Also creates an AI public services fellowship and, conditionally, an AI incubation lab.

md:SB 6.title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Nontenure Track Faculty
md:SB 6.summary: Gives collective bargaining rights to nontenure-track faculty at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University and St. Mary's College, and creates a separate bargaining unit for them.

md:SB 607.title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Public Safety Retirement Income - Amount
md:SB 607.summary: Phases in an increase in the Maryland income tax subtraction for public safety retirement income from $15,000 to $20,000 by 2030, rising $1,000 each year starting in 2026.

md:SB 636.title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Revisions
md:SB 636.summary: Repeals the deadline for Baltimore City Class A license holders to pay the fee for Sunday sales, and changes the deadline for showing proof that personal property taxes owed to the city and State are paid.

md:SB 637.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Fund Producer Commission Rate
md:SB 637.summary: Lowers the minimum commission the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund pays producers on private passenger auto policies from 10% to 5% of premium, and bars commissions on policies the Fund writes directly.

md:SB 646.title: Public School System Contracts - Prohibited Provisions
md:SB 646.summary: Bars public school system contracts from including specified terms, such as unfunded indemnification, binding arbitration, out-of-state venue, liability caps, or terms the other party can change unilaterally; such terms are void. Excludes collective bargaining agreements and existing contracts.

md:SB 657.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program - Established
md:SB 657.summary: Creates a Higher Education Commission grant program for minority residents of historically redlined and underrepresented communities to complete Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) training, aimed at closing appraisal gaps and diversifying the appraisal field.

md:SB 668.title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards
md:SB 668.summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and requires the Governor to include budget appropriations to it, at least equal to fiscal 2027's for fiscal 2028-2030 and $500,000 above fiscal 2030's for fiscal 2031, for grants to local management boards.

md:SB 681.title: Worcester County - Board of License Commissioners - Membership
md:SB 681.summary: Increases the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members appointed by the Governor, with terms staggered; takes effect June 1, 2026.

md:SB 700.title: Wicomico County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B (Golf Course) License - Hours of Sale
md:SB 700.summary: Lets Wicomico County Class B golf course license holders begin selling beer, wine and liquor at 7 a.m. instead of 10 a.m., Monday through Sunday.

md:SB 72.title: Health Occupations Boards - English Proficiency Requirements and Licensure by Endorsement for Nursing
md:SB 72.summary: Bars health occupations boards from requiring more proof of English proficiency from applicants holding an unrestricted license in another state that required it, and changes English proficiency and endorsement rules for nursing and pharmacy.

md:SB 728.title: Higher Education - Student Financial Assistance - Alterations to Scholarship Programs
md:SB 728.summary: Extends Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship eligibility to Delmar, Maryland residents who graduate from Delmar High School in Delaware, and widens the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship to cover surviving transportation workers and more relatives, for total cost of attendance.

md:SB 729.title: Real Property - Access to Counsel in Evictions Program - Expansion
md:SB 729.summary: Extends the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program to residents of mobile home parks, giving them legal representation in repossession actions and requiring outreach, an informational pamphlet and annual reporting that cover them.

md:SB 739.title: Climate Change, Homeowner's Insurance, and Emergency Management - Study
md:SB 739.summary: Requires the University System of Maryland to study how climate change affects homeowner's insurance availability and cost and emergency preparedness, and report recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027, including on flood insurance programs.

md:SB 747.title: Condominiums - Unit Owner Responsibility for Damage or Destruction and Mandatory Insurance Coverage
md:SB 747.summary: Changes a condo owner's liability for damage originating in their unit from up to $10,000 of the council's insurance deductible to the least of repair cost, deductible or $25,000, and requires residential condominium unit owners to carry insurance and show proof annually.

md:SB 76.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class C (Veterans' Organization) Licenses - Membership
md:SB 76.summary: Changes the Anne Arundel County Class C (veterans' organization) alcohol license to cover clubs composed of members who served in the uniformed services, not just the armed forces, adding veterans who served in NOAA and the Public Health Service.

md:SB 760.title: Real Property - Recordation and Land Records - Revisions
md:SB 760.summary: Repeals the margin requirement for printed deeds offered for recordation and requires circuit court clerks to date each change or correction made to the general alphabetical index.

md:SB 765.title: Property Taxes - Tax Sales, Legacy Protection Program, and Tax Credits
md:SB 765.summary: Extends State Tax Sale Ombudsman services to estates and heirs of deceased homeowners, creates a Legacy Protection Program with $250,000 a year from the state and $500,000 from counties, and gives eligible heirs homeowners' and homestead tax credits for up to three years.

md:SB 769.title: University System of Maryland - Academic Facilities Bonding Authority
md:SB 769.summary: Approves $26 million of University System of Maryland academic facility projects and $24 million of facility renewal projects, authorizing $50 million in bonds, which are not State debt.

md:SB 791.title: Correctional Services and Criminal Procedure - Immigration Enforcement - Prohibitions (Community Trust Act)
md:SB 791.summary: Adds a provision stating that the bill's section on law enforcement agents may not be construed to bar an agent from participating in a joint task force that includes the Department of Homeland Security.

md:SB 794.title: Health Insurance - Special Enrollment Period for Pregnancy - Coverage Effective Date
md:SB 794.summary: Lets a person who enrolls in health coverage during a pregnancy special enrollment period choose coverage starting the month pregnancy is confirmed or the month after plan selection, for plans issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2027.

md:SB 802.title: Garrett County - Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2026
md:SB 802.summary: Creates a Garrett County Special Event Permit for winery licensees, adds a substitute board member, lets catering-option licensees sell alcohol at events on unlicensed or temporarily licensed premises, and requires license applicants to state citizenship or, for noncitizens, show immigration status complies with federal law.

md:SB 803.title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 3 Wineries and Class 4 Limited Wineries - Alterations
md:SB 803.summary: Expands the definition of pomace brandy that Class 4 limited wineries may make and sell, and lets Class 3 wineries buy bulk wine from Class 4 limited wineries, which may sell and deliver it.

md:SB 807.title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 8 Farm Brewery Licenses
md:SB 807.summary: Creates a Class 10 farm distillery license, open to Class 8 farm brewery holders, to distill and sell spirits made on the licensed farm, requires farm brewery and distillery holders to engage in agritourism, and changes brewery food service and zoning exceptions.

md:SB 808.title: Prince George's County - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems - School Bus Stops
md:SB 808.summary: Allows stop sign cameras within 100 feet of school bus stops in Prince George's County, operating weekdays 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., through June 30, 2029.

md:SB 809.title: Supporting Our Caregiver Infrastructure Program - Feasibility Study
md:SB 809.summary: Requires the University of Maryland, College Park to study the feasibility of a program giving caregivers universal monthly payments for each dependent they care for, with a final report by July 1, 2028.

md:SB 839.title: Medical Assistance Programs - Drug Dispensing - Cost-of-Dispensing Survey
md:SB 839.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the in-State Medicaid cost-of-dispensing survey for pharmacies at least once every three years, beginning in 2026, and report results to the General Assembly.

md:SB 851.title: Anne Arundel County - Property Tax Credit - Rural Legacy Program
md:SB 851.summary: Authorizes Anne Arundel County to grant, by local law, a property tax credit for real property in a Rural Legacy Area whose owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program.

md:SB 852.title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages – Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
md:SB 852.summary: Lets Anne Arundel County barbershop and beauty salon license holders serve each customer up to 1.7 ounces of liquor per visit for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine.

md:SB 864.title: Higher Education - Tuition Exemption for Foster Care Recipients - Eligibility
md:SB 864.summary: Lowers from 13 to 8 the age on or after which a person must have lived in an out-of-home placement to qualify for the foster care tuition and mandatory fee exemption at public colleges. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

md:SB 865.title: Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance – Extension and Alteration of Membership and Duties
md:SB 865.summary: Extends the auto insurance affordability workgroup to June 30, 2027, changes its membership, and adds duties to develop specific recommendations to reduce premiums, including on territorial rating. Requires an updated report by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 890.title: Insurance - Captive Insurers - Premium Receipts Tax Study
md:SB 890.summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to study the use, regulation and taxation of captive insurance companies by entities in the State and report findings and recommendations by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 892.title: Health Occupations, Public Health, and Insurance - Menopause - Provider Training Coverage Requirements, Policy Initiatives, and Access to Care
md:SB 892.summary: Requires health insurers to cover evaluation and management of menopause symptoms, directs the Department of Health to identify provider training programs for which health boards grant continuing education credit, and changes the Advisory Council on Health and Wellness.

md:SB 897.title: Cecil County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
md:SB 897.summary: Changes the Cecil County license quota to count only Class A licenses, at 1 per 2,000 registered voters, and allows the board to issue at least two Class A licenses in each election district.

md:SB 898.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Behavior Technicians - Reimbursement
md:SB 898.summary: Requires Maryland Medicaid to reimburse registered behavior technicians for applied behavior analysis services to recipients with autism spectrum disorder, and bars requiring certification as a condition of reimbursement, except that certification may be required within 150 days of starting.

md:SB 941.title: Department of Housing and Community Development - Severe Health and Safety Risk Properties - Intervention Plan
md:SB 941.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to develop a plan, due August 31, 2027, to identify and intervene in severe health and safety risk rental properties of 50 or more units, and to publish a list of them.

md:SB 974.title: Caroline County - Alcoholic Beverages - Inspector
md:SB 974.summary: Requires the Caroline County alcoholic beverage license board's inspector to be either someone the board appoints or the county codes administrator, who currently fills the role.

md:SB 982.title: Mutual Insurance Holding Companies - Conversion to Mutual Insurers
md:SB 982.summary: Lets a mutual insurance holding company that owns all of a reorganized stock insurer convert to a mutual insurer under a plan approved by a board majority and at least 75% of members voting, then by the Insurance Commissioner.

me:HO 21.title: House Order Relating to the Censure of Speaker of the House Ryan Fecteau
me:HO 21.summary: Censures the Speaker of the House for conducting business after 9 p.m. without a two-thirds vote to dispense with House Rule 501, and requires a public apology.

me:HO 8.title: House Order, to Require the House Committee on Ethics to Convene to Consider Allegations Against Representative Lucas Lanigan of Sanford
me:HO 8.summary: Orders the House Committee on Ethics to convene to investigate allegations against a representative charged with domestic violence aggravated assault, and to report back within one month of convening.

me:HP 130.title: Joint Order, to Amend Joint Rule 208 to Eliminate All but Certain Concept Drafts
me:HP 130.summary: Amends Joint Rule 208 to eliminate concept-draft bills other than certain kinds, such as unified budget bills and uniform or model acts.

me:HP 367.title: Joint Order Allowing Reports of Ought Not to Pass to Be Made After the Committee Vote
me:HP 367.summary: Amends Joint Rule 310 so a committee member absent at a vote may register a vote with the clerk that creates an additional Ought Not to Pass report, which need not be voted on at the same work session as the majority report.

me:HR 1.title: HOUSE RESOLUTION RELATING TO THE CENSURE OF REPRESENTATIVE LAUREL D. LIBBY OF AUBURN BY THE MAINE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
me:HR 1.summary: Censures a state representative over a Facebook post naming a minor athlete and criticizing transgender students' participation in high school sports, and requires a public apology to the House and the people of Maine.

me:HR 2.title: HOUSE RESOLUTION TO RESCIND THE RESTRICTIONS ON THE VOTING AND SPEAKING PRIVILEGES OF REPRESENTATIVE LAUREL D. LIBBY OF AUBURN
me:HR 2.summary: Rescinds, effective upon adjournment of the First Special Session, the restrictions on one representative's voting and speaking privileges that followed her censure.

me:LD 100.title: An Act to Increase the Expenditure Limit for the Informal Bidding Process for the Selection of Professional, Architect and Engineer Services
me:LD 100.summary: Raises from $25,000 to $50,000 the cost limit for the informal bidding process the Bureau of General Services uses to select professional, architect and engineer services.

me:LD 1002.title: An Act to Protect Children's Identification by Requiring Public Schools to Use the Name and Gender Specified on a Child's Birth Certificate
me:LD 1002.summary: As introduced, requires public school and charter school staff to refer to a minor student by the name and gender on the student's official birth record unless a parent gives written permission otherwise or legal change documents are provided.

me:LD 1003.title: An Act Establishing the Retirement Benefit Improvement Fund
me:LD 1003.summary: As amended, transfers the General Fund surplus remaining each year after higher-priority transfers into a nonlapsing fund that pays for cost-of-living adjustments on a larger part of retirees' benefits, with annual status reports to the Legislature.

me:LD 1007.title: An Act to Update the State's Informed Consent Laws Regarding Drug-induced Abortion
me:LD 1007.summary: As introduced, requires a health care professional obtaining informed consent for a drug-induced abortion to give the patient specific information on the potential ability of qualified professionals to reverse its effects.

me:LD 1009.title: An Act to Restore Full Civil Rights to Possess Firearms to Persons Previously Convicted of Certain Nonviolent Felony Crimes
me:LD 1009.summary: As amended, lets a person with a single Class B or C felony conviction ask a District Court to restore firearm rights 10 years after completing the sentence, excluding crimes such as robbery, arson and offenses involving firearms; requires a background check.

me:LD 1011.title: An Act to Change the Residency Requirements for State Funding for Student Tuition at the Maine School of Science and Mathematics
me:LD 1011.summary: As introduced, changes Maine School of Science and Mathematics free tuition eligibility from the student having lived in Maine 6 months to the student's parent or guardian being a Maine resident at the start of the school year.

me:LD 1012.title: An Act to Fund the Operations of the University of Maine Cooperative Extension Tick Laboratory
me:LD 1012.summary: As amended, directs the State Liquor and Lottery Commission to start an instant lottery game by July 1, 2026 to raise money for the University of Maine Cooperative Extension Tick Laboratory Operations Fund.

me:LD 1013.title: An Act to Protect Taxpayers by Requiring Referenda on Significant Municipal Debt
me:LD 1013.summary: Requires a municipality to hold a voter referendum in November to approve any bond of $10,000,000 or more.

me:LD 1016.title: An Act to Establish the Manufactured Housing Community and Mobile Home Park Preservation and Assistance Fund
me:LD 1016.summary: Creates a fund at the Maine State Housing Authority to support resident ownership of mobile home parks, financed by a $10,000-per-lot fee on sales of such parks, with buyers whose net worth is under $50,000,000 exempt.

me:LD 1017.title: An Act to Include Food Provided or Served at Emergency Shelters in General Assistance Reimbursement
me:LD 1017.summary: Includes the cost of food provided or served at emergency shelters in the Department of Health and Human Services' reimbursement of general assistance costs to municipalities.

me:LD 102.title: An Act to Notify the Public of Juveniles Who Are Wanted Persons
me:LD 102.summary: Lets the Corrections Commissioner publicly release certain juvenile information to find a juvenile who escaped a corrections facility and poses a serious risk, and creates a working group to study apprehending juveniles with warrants.

me:LD 1020.title: An Act to Repeal the Laws Providing for the Construction of a Connector to Gorham and to Resell Land Taken Under Those Laws to Previous Property Owners
me:LD 1020.summary: Repeals the laws authorizing the Maine Turnpike Authority to build a connector to Gorham.

me:LD 1021.title: An Act to Remove Certain Cost-of-living Adjustment Restrictions for Retired Members of the Law Enforcement Bargaining Unit Who Are 65 Years of Age or Older
me:LD 1021.summary: Removes the limit on the retirement benefit subject to cost-of-living adjustments once a retired law enforcement officer or probation or parole officer reaches age 65.

me:LD 1022.title: An Act to Protect and Increase Access to Justice in Civil Legal Matters for Persons with Low Incomes
me:LD 1022.summary: Increases ongoing state funding for civil legal services for low-income and elderly people through the Maine Civil Legal Services Fund, sets an annual minimum, and requires biennial public hearings on funding and an annual commission report.

me:LD 1024.title: An Act to Expand the List of Crimes That Do Not Qualify for Immunity Under Maine's Good Samaritan Laws Concerning Drug-related Medical Assistance
me:LD 1024.summary: As introduced, adds firearm possession by a prohibited person, trafficking in scheduled drugs and unlawfully furnishing scheduled drugs to the crimes that do not qualify for Good Samaritan immunity in drug-related medical assistance cases.

me:LD 1027.title: An Act to Strengthen the Law Regarding Relief for Improvident Transfers of Title
me:LD 1027.summary: Requires, instead of allowing, a court that finds undue influence over an elderly dependent person in a property transfer to award attorney's fees and costs against the person who exercised it or a transferee who paid less than full value.

me:LD 1032.title: An Act Regarding Court Security
me:LD 1032.summary: As introduced, requires the State Court Administrator to contract for court security when a lack of security disrupts more than 2% of a court's scheduled time in a month, offering the contract first to the county sheriff's office.

me:LD 1034.title: An Act to Decriminalize Personal Possession of Therapeutic Amounts of Psilocybin for Adults
me:LD 1034.summary: Establishes the Commission to Study Pathways for Creating a Psilocybin Services Program in Maine, which reports findings and recommended legislation by November 4, 2026.

me:LD 1036.title: An Act to Protect Recipients of Public Assistance from Housing Discrimination
me:LD 1036.summary: As introduced, adds status as a recipient of public assistance, including medical assistance and housing subsidies, to Maine's housing discrimination law, covering inquiries, sales, rentals, evictions and loans, and bars refusing to rent to recipients because of that status.

me:LD 1044.title: An Act to Clarify the Qualifying Use of Tax Increment Financing for Extension of a Development District
me:LD 1044.summary: Clarifies that a tax increment financing district can qualify for a 20-year extension by using revenue for affordable housing, transit-oriented development, or both, and removes the requirement that transit-oriented development be in a designated transit district, area, corridor or node.

me:LD 1048.title: An Act to Require Certain Notice Requirements for Whistleblower Protections
me:LD 1048.summary: Requires public utilities and competitive electricity providers to send employees, affiliated interests and utility contractors an annual plain-English notice of their legal protections for giving testimony or information to legislative committees, the Public Utilities Commission and the Public Advocate.

me:LD 1049.title: An Act to Eliminate the Duty to Inform a Law Enforcement Officer When Carrying a Concealed Handgun Without a Permit
me:LD 1049.summary: As introduced, repeals the requirement that a person carrying a concealed handgun without a permit tell a law enforcement officer about it during an arrest, detainment or routine traffic stop, and the penalty for failing to do so.

me:LD 1059.title: An Act to Establish the Process for the Selection of Delegates for a Convention Called Under the United States Constitution, Article V
me:LD 1059.summary: Sets a process for the Legislature to choose 5 commissioners, with required qualifications, to represent Maine at an Article V convention, limits their authority to the subject of the state applications, and creates an advisory committee that can recall them.

me:LD 1062.title: An Act to Eliminate Background Checks for Private Sales of Firearms
me:LD 1062.summary: As introduced, ends the requirement that firearm sales resulting from an advertisement go through a licensed dealer for a background check, limiting the law to dealer sales at gun shows.

me:LD 1063.title: An Act to Require Competitive Procurement of Electricity from Generators Fueled by Municipal Solid Waste in Conjunction with Recycling
me:LD 1063.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to direct investor-owned transmission and distribution utilities to contract for energy and renewable energy credits with generators fueled by municipal solid waste in conjunction with recycling.

me:LD 1067.title: An Act to Improve the Process for Mobile Home Owners to Purchase Their Mobile Home Park
me:LD 1067.summary: As introduced, raises from 51% to 60% the share of mobile home owners who must give written support before an owners' group makes an offer to buy the park, and limits association contacts about the purchase to 3.

me:LD 1077.title: An Act to Exempt Drinking Water from Sales and Use Tax
me:LD 1077.summary: As introduced, adds packaged drinking water to the "grocery staples" definition, exempting it from sales and use tax.

me:LD 1078.title: An Act to Support Maine's Public Health Objectives by Increasing Access to Hypodermic Apparatus Exchange Programs
me:LD 1078.summary: Allows certified syringe service programs to operate mobile sites within parameters preapproved by the Maine CDC and to deliver hypodermic apparatuses within their service area.

me:LD 1080.title: An Act Prohibiting Public Utilities from Requiring Deposits Based Solely on a Residential Customer's Income
me:LD 1080.summary: Bars a public utility from requiring a deposit based solely on income from a residential applicant who was not a customer in the prior 30 days, and requires the Public Utilities Commission to start rulemaking.

me:LD 1088.title: An Act to Enact the Maine Consumer Data Privacy Act
me:LD 1088.summary: As introduced, creates the Maine Consumer Data Privacy Act, effective July 1, 2026, regulating how businesses collect, use, sell and delete residents' personal data and limiting collection to what is reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes.

me:LD 1089.title: An Act to Permanently Fund 55 Percent of the State's Share of Education by Establishing a Tax on Incomes of More than $1,000,000
me:LD 1089.summary: Imposes a 2% income tax surcharge on Maine taxable income above $1,000,000 for single filers ($1,500,000 for heads of households, $2,000,000 for joint filers), with the revenue going to a fund for public prekindergarten through grade 12 education.

me:LD 109.title: Resolve, Directing the Maine Arts Commission to Study Federal and National Efforts to Protect Artists from Copyright Infringement by Artificial Intelligence Companies and Users and to Monitor Educational Use
me:LD 109.summary: Directs the Maine Arts Commission to study federal and national efforts to protect artists from AI copyright infringement and to monitor educational use of copyrighted work, with $25,000 in one-time funding.

me:LD 1097.title: An Act to Provide De-escalation and Behavior Intervention Training for School Personnel
me:LD 1097.summary: Requires school units to give administrators, teachers and education technicians at least 4 hours of de-escalation and behavior intervention training every third year starting 2026-2027, and the Department of Education to develop training best practices.

me:LD 1105.title: An Act Concerning Displaced Civilian Federal Firefighters in Maine
me:LD 1105.summary: Requires the Department of Labor to maintain a database of civilian federal firefighters in Maine displaced by a federal military installation closure or reduction in force and share it with municipalities that have fire departments.

me:LD 1107.title: Act to Create a Working Group to Support Tax Expenditure Evaluation Efforts
me:LD 1107.summary: Replaces a concept draft by removing the requirement of expedited review for tax expenditures meant to serve broad policy goals, requiring a legislative committee to adjust review categories twice a year, and creating a task force on centralizing tax expenditure data.

me:LD 1109.title: An Act to Reduce Gun Violence Casualties in Maine by Prohibiting the Possession of Large-capacity Ammunition Feeding Devices
me:LD 1109.summary: As introduced, makes it a Class D crime to knowingly manufacture, import, buy, possess, sell or transfer a magazine or similar device holding more than 10 rounds, with exemptions.

me:LD 1113.title: An Act Regarding Fairness in Sentencing for Persons Under 26 Years of Age
me:LD 1113.summary: Requires courts sentencing for Class A, B or C crimes to consider the person's age when the conduct occurred, in addition to other sentencing factors.

me:LD 1117.title: An Act to Strengthen Maine's Workforce Through Certified Preapprenticeship Training Programs
me:LD 1117.summary: Allows Maine Apprenticeship Program grants to cover preapprenticeship costs such as fees, tools and support services, directs at least 51% of funding to certified programs meeting set criteria, and directs the Department of Labor to study similar programs.

me:LD 112.title: An Act to Promote Opportunities by Establishing a Student Wage
me:LD 112.summary: Sets the minimum hourly wage for employees who are secondary school students at 50% of the state minimum wage for at least 2 years, unless the employee graduates.

me:LD 1123.title: An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related Services for Public Schools
me:LD 1123.summary: Provides ongoing funds for 2 Public Service Coordinator I positions to give technical assistance and help local school districts obtain MaineCare reimbursements.

me:LD 1126.title: An Act Requiring Serial Numbers on Firearms and Prohibiting Undetectable Firearms
me:LD 1126.summary: As amended in committee, bars possessing, importing or transferring firearms, frames and receivers without serial numbers, with exceptions such as antiques and curios or relics; lets licensed dealers imprint serial numbers; and bars making, selling or knowingly possessing undetectable firearms.

me:LD 1131.title: An Act to Reform the Process by Which a Person May Petition an Agency to Adopt or Modify Rules Under the Maine Administrative Procedure Act
me:LD 1131.summary: Changes the number of voter signatures needed to petition an agency to adopt or modify a rule from 150 to 1% of votes cast for Governor in the last gubernatorial election, and classifies such rules as major substantive rules.

me:LD 1133.title: An Act to Allow Electric Vehicle Charging Stations by Condominium and Residential Associations
me:LD 1133.summary: As amended, voids declaration or bylaw provisions of an association of unit owners that prohibit or unreasonably restrict installing or using an electric vehicle charging station in a parking space, starting January 1, 2026, and lets unit owners apply to the board to install one at their cost.

me:LD 1134.title: An Act to Prohibit Males from Participating in Female Sports or Using Female Facilities
me:LD 1134.summary: As introduced, bars state-funded schools and colleges from letting a person whose sex assigned at birth is male join female-designated competitive athletics or use female-only facilities.

me:LD 1138.title: An Act to Reduce Pollution Associated with Transportation in Alignment with the State's Climate Action Plan
me:LD 1138.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation and Maine Turnpike Authority to assess whether capacity expansion projects raise greenhouse gas emissions or per-capita vehicle miles traveled, and to alter scope or design to ensure a neutral or lower impact.

me:LD 1145.title: An Act to Protect Residents Living in Mobile Home Parks
me:LD 1145.summary: Clarifies that a mobile home owners' group or association has first option to buy a park by matching the price and substantially equivalent terms of an offer the owner intends to accept, and gives it 90 days after a purchase agreement to secure financing.

me:LD 1146.title: An Act Regarding the Required State of Mind Relating to Robbery
me:LD 1146.summary: Requires that threatening to use force, or placing a person in fear of imminent force, be done intentionally or knowingly for the act to count as robbery.

me:LD 1147.title: An Act Regarding the Required State of Mind Relating to the Threatening Display or Carrying of a Concealed Weapon
me:LD 1147.summary: As introduced, requires a person to act intentionally or knowingly to be criminally liable for displaying a weapon in a threatening manner or carrying one concealed.

me:LD 1148.title: An Act to Improve Access to Absentee Ballots for Municipal Elections for Uniformed Service Voters and Overseas Voters
me:LD 1148.summary: Directs the Secretary of State to study digital access to local absentee ballots for uniformed service and overseas voters in municipal elections held with statewide elections, update its website to say local ballots come from the voter's municipality, and report by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 115.title: An Act to Assess Impact Fees on Megayachts
me:LD 115.summary: As introduced, charges megayachts of 150 feet or more an impact fee of $10 per foot over 150 feet per day, up to 30 days, in slips in municipalities that collect slip fees, funding harbor and transit infrastructure.

me:LD 1154.title: An Act to Require That Informed Consent for Abortion Include Information on Perinatal Hospice
me:LD 1154.summary: Requires a health care professional, before an abortion where the fetus has a lethal anomaly diagnosis, to inform the woman of perinatal hospice services and give her a provider list; if she declines, she must certify that in writing.

me:LD 1159.title: An Act to Prohibit Businesses from Refusing to Accept Cash for In-person Payments
me:LD 1159.summary: Bars municipalities and other governmental entities that charge a credit card fee on in-person retail purchases from refusing cash payment for those goods or services.

me:LD 1164.title: An Act to Create Economic Opportunity for the Wabanaki Nations Through Internet Gaming
me:LD 1164.summary: Lets each federally recognized tribe in Maine run internet gaming under a Gambling Control Unit license, taxing adjusted gross receipts at 18% and splitting the revenue among state funds.

me:LD 1169.title: An Act Regarding Employer Payments for the Paid Family and Medical Leave Benefits Program
me:LD 1169.summary: Lets an employer whose private paid family and medical leave plan is approved request a refund of premiums paid if the plan was in place by January 1, 2025, with the department refunding within 90 days plus interest.

me:LD 117.title: An Act to Provide Funding for Sexual Assault Services
me:LD 117.summary: As amended in committee, appropriates $1,230,000 for 2025-26 and $1,830,000 for 2026-27 to the Department of Health and Human Services for sexual assault services.

me:LD 1181.title: An Act Regarding the Designation of Short-term Rental Units as Commercial or Residential in Use
me:LD 1181.summary: Allows a municipality to adopt a regulation letting, but not requiring, its assessor to assign land use codes designating short-term rental units as commercial or residential in use.

me:LD 1184.title: An Act to Require Municipal Reporting on Residential Building Permits, Dwelling Units Permitted and Demolished and Certificates of Occupancy Issued
me:LD 1184.summary: Requires municipalities with 4,000 or more residents to report annual housing data to the state by January 31, including building permits, units permitted and demolished, certificates of occupancy and affordability, with 90% reimbursement of added local costs.

me:LD 1185.title: An Act to Prohibit Persons Under 18 Years of Age from Marrying
me:LD 1185.summary: Bars issuing a marriage license to anyone under 18, eliminating the current allowance for 17-year-olds.

me:LD 1187.title: An Act to Require Certain Mental Health Data to Be Included in Uniform Crime Reports
me:LD 1187.summary: Requires the Maine CDC's annual report on firearm fatalities and hospitalizations to include the number of assessments performed, the number of people referred for mental health treatment, and aggregate demographic data that does not identify individuals.

me:LD 1189.title: An Act to Allow an Attorney for the State to Determine Whether to Charge Certain Class E Crimes as Civil Violations
me:LD 1189.summary: As amended in committee, lets the attorney for the State charge certain Class E crimes as civil violations with penalties up to $1,000, unless an arrested defendant objects. Excludes election-law crimes, crimes eligible for probation, and those with mandatory license suspension.

me:LD 1200.title: An Act to Prohibit the Sale of Items Intended to Be Used to Inhale Nitrous Oxide for Recreational Purposes
me:LD 1200.summary: Bars knowingly selling or distributing a device containing nitrous oxide for inhaling it to cause intoxication, with exceptions for sales to certain dentists, pharmacists and physicians, and sets civil fines of $250 to $1,000 by offense.

me:LD 1202.title: An Act to Establish the African American Studies Advisory Council and Provide Funding to Support African American Studies
me:LD 1202.summary: Creates the African American Studies Advisory Council to set a baseline measure of how school units implement African American studies, and lets the State Board of Education adopt rules requiring an African American studies component for teacher certification if it finds them necessary.

me:LD 1204.title: An Act to Support Direct Access Worker Employment by Removing Certain Employment Disqualifications
me:LD 1204.summary: As introduced, removes aggravated cultivating of marijuana from the offenses that disqualify a person from working as a direct access worker for a personal care agency.

me:LD 1210.title: An Act to Regarding Renewable Electricity Generation by Hydropower Projects
me:LD 1210.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection, when deciding hydropower permits and water quality certifications, to weigh the project's effect on state renewable energy and economic goals and its benefits against effects on wildlife habitat and aquatic life.

me:LD 1211.title: An Act Regarding Certain Definitions in the Sales and Use Tax Laws Affecting Rental Equipment and Automobiles Used in Transporting Goods
me:LD 1211.summary: Exempts from sales and use tax grants of up to 7 days to use sports or recreational equipment valued under $100 a day and used only on the grantor's premises.

me:LD 1217.title: An Act Regarding the New Markets Tax Credit and the Maine New Markets Capital Investment Program
me:LD 1217.summary: Creates a second tax credit authority ("program 2") for allocations made on or after Jan. 1, 2026, with an application process; the amendment changes program participant qualifications and investment deadlines.

me:LD 1219.title: An Act to Increase State Funding for the Campuses of the University of Maine System and to Raise the Minimum Hourly Wage for Employees of the System
me:LD 1219.summary: Provides ongoing funds for a 4% increase in funding to the University of Maine System in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27.

me:LD 122.title: An Act to Update Certain Laws Regarding Extended Care and Adoption
me:LD 122.summary: Updates extended foster care and adoption laws: requires annual court reviews for ages 18 to 20, lets youth, the department or the court request a review, and extends transition grants to people enrolled in training programs.

me:LD 1220.title: An Act to Allow Chiropractors to Treat Dogs and Equids
me:LD 1220.summary: Lets licensed chiropractors apply to the Board of Chiropractic Licensure for authority to treat animals, with training, exams, 22 hours of animal-specific continuing education before each renewal, only trained species, and a veterinarian's referral or medical clearance.

me:LD 1226.title: An Act to Protect Consumers by Licensing Residential Building Contractors
me:LD 1226.summary: Requires residential general contractors to be licensed, creates a Residential Construction Board to administer licensing, and sets penalties for violations, with funding appropriated.

me:LD 1228.title: An Act to Clarify Certain Terms in the Automotive Right to Repair Laws
me:LD 1228.summary: Replaces the independent entity under Maine's automotive right-to-repair law with a Motor Vehicle Right to Repair Commission that monitors manufacturer compliance, and clarifies equipment, diagnostic and repair access, and enforcement provisions.

me:LD 1230.title: An Act to Abolish the 72-hour Waiting Period for a Gun Purchase
me:LD 1230.summary: As introduced, repeals the requirement that a firearm seller wait 72 hours before delivering a purchased firearm to the buyer.

me:LD 125.title: An Act to Increase the Total Amount of Credits Authorized Under the Maine Seed Capital Tax Credit Program
me:LD 125.summary: Increases from $5,000,000 to $10,000,000 the maximum annual tax credit certificates the Finance Authority of Maine may issue under the Maine Seed Capital Tax Credit Program for investments from 2027.

me:LD 1251.title: Resolve, to Reduce the Cost of Energy in Maine and Further Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions Through Energy Contracts
me:LD 1251.summary: Directs the Public Utilities Commission to seek information on energy cost reduction and storage contracts and on replacements for natural gas, and negotiate with gas utilities and adjacent states and provinces, reporting by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 1254.title: An Act to Expand the Licensing of Outpatient Surgical Facilities
me:LD 1254.summary: Removes the exclusion of physician and dental private offices, and of facilities existing mainly to perform pregnancy terminations, from the definition of ambulatory surgical facility, so those whose primary purpose is outpatient elective surgery need a license.

me:LD 1257.title: An Act Regarding Labeling of Genetically Engineered Food Products
me:LD 1257.summary: As amended, bans the sale or distribution of cell-cultured meat, defined as food made from cultured animal cells, with civil fines up to $100 for a first offense and $200 for each later one.

me:LD 1258.title: An Act to Include Qualified Out-of-state Electric Vehicle Providers and Clarify Provisions Regarding Electric Bicycles Under the Electric Vehicle Fund
me:LD 1258.summary: Allows electric vehicles bought or leased from out-of-state authorized dealers that meet in-state requirements to qualify for the Electric Vehicle Fund incentive, and clarifies eligibility rules for electric bicycle incentives.

me:LD 1263.title: An Act Regarding Penalties for Fentanyl Trafficking When That Trafficking Results in an Overdose Causing Serious Bodily Injury of a Person
me:LD 1263.summary: Creates the Class A crime of aggravated trafficking in a scheduled drug when fentanyl powder the defendant trafficked contributes to another person's serious bodily injury, without requiring that the injury result from an overdose.

me:LD 1265.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Public Employee Market Pay Studies and Comprehensive Reviews of the Classification Plan for State Service Positions
me:LD 1265.summary: Requires the Bureau of Human Resources to issue a request for proposals and contract with an outside contractor for state employee market pay studies and job classification plan reviews, with $2,000,000 in one-time funding.

me:LD 1266.title: Resolve, Directing the Attorney General to Convene a Working Group to Propose a Plan for Expanding the Reach of Treatment Courts
me:LD 1266.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Behavioral Health to convene a working group on expanding adult drug, family and veterans treatment courts and report recommendations to the Judiciary Committee.

me:LD 127.title: An Act to Strengthen Legislative Oversight of Government Agencies and Programs by Reaffirming the Legislature's Access to Confidential Records
me:LD 127.summary: Requires the Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability director to brief the Government Oversight Committee every two years on confidentiality policies, and lets the director share a confidential copy of a final report with it before public release, after the agency review period.

me:LD 1270.title: An Act to Establish the Department of Energy Resources
me:LD 1270.summary: Eliminates the Governor's Energy Office and creates a cabinet-level Department of Energy Resources that takes over its functions, including energy policy oversight, solar and storage programs, and competitive energy solicitations.

me:LD 1273.title: An Act to Make Paid Family and Medical Leave Voluntary
me:LD 1273.summary: As introduced, repeals the paid family and medical leave benefits program with refunds of contributions, and creates a voluntary program for employers of 50 or more employees that employees of nonparticipating employers may also join.

me:LD 1277.title: An Act Regarding Controlled Substances Prescription Monitoring Activities
me:LD 1277.summary: Removes anabolic steroids from the definition of controlled substance in the state's prescription monitoring program.

me:LD 128.title: An Act to Support Permitting of Certain Multifamily Housing Developments Under the Site Location of Development Laws
me:LD 128.summary: Allows lots with single detached structures of up to 4 dwelling units, with or without an accessory unit, to count under the higher 15-lot threshold for subdivisions under site location of development laws, and excludes their land from the 20-acre calculation.

me:LD 1281.title: An Act to Address the Safety of Nurses and Improve Patient Care by Enacting the Maine Quality Care Act
me:LD 1281.summary: Creates the Maine Quality Care Act, setting minimum direct care registered nurse staffing levels by patient care unit in hospitals, freestanding emergency departments and ambulatory surgical facilities, with staffing calculation, anti-retaliation, record-keeping and civil-penalty enforcement provisions.

me:LD 1283.title: An Act to Allow Employees Covered Under the Maine Retirement Savings Program to Elect to Enroll and Unenroll in a Payroll Deduction for an Individual Retirement Account
me:LD 1283.summary: Changes the Maine Retirement Savings Program payroll-deduction IRA from automatic enrollment with opt-out to enrollment only when a covered employee elects to join, and requires participants to ensure their account information is up to date.

me:LD 1288.title: An Act to Amend Certain Provisions of Maine's Drug Laws Regarding Heroin, Fentanyl and Cocaine
me:LD 1288.summary: As introduced, adds heroin and fentanyl powder (2 grams or more) to trafficking and smaller amounts to furnishing, adds cocaine base thresholds including 32 grams for aggravated offenses, and removes heroin and fentanyl powder from the evidentiary inference provisions.

me:LD 1292.title: An Act to Codify the Maine Turnpike Authority's Contributions to the Highway Fund with Regard to the Sensible Transportation Policy Act
me:LD 1292.summary: As introduced, requires the Maine Turnpike Authority to pay into the Highway Fund each quarter any revenue and reserves above its operating, reserve and debt service needs and legislatively approved project allocations.

me:LD 1294.title: An Act to Expand the Dependent Exemption Tax Credit
me:LD 1294.summary: Doubles the dependent exemption tax credit for a child or dependent under age 6 and phases out refundability of the credit based on income; the amendment adds an appropriations section.

me:LD 1298.title: An Act Establishing Alternative Pathways to Social Worker Licensing
me:LD 1298.summary: Creates an alternative path to social work licensure for applicants who tried and failed the State Board of Social Worker Licensure exam, requiring a consultation agreement and a competency attestation instead of passing the exam.

me:LD 1299.title: An Act to Prohibit the Unsecured Storage of Handguns in Motor Vehicles
me:LD 1299.summary: Prohibits storing a handgun in an unoccupied motor vehicle unless it is out of sight in a locked hard-sided container and the vehicle is locked, with exceptions; civil fines of $200 to $500, or $500 to $1,000 for repeat violations.

me:LD 1307.title: An Act to Suspend the Remittance Obligation for Paid Family and Medical Leave Private Plan Users
me:LD 1307.summary: As introduced, suspends employer paid family and medical leave premiums until January 1, 2026 (employers may keep paying) and directs the Labor Department to set rules by November 1, 2025 for expedited approval of private plans, waiving premiums while applications are pending.

me:LD 1318.title: An Act to Enhance Data Collection Requirements Related to Immigration Status and Asylum Seekers to Safeguard Services for Legal Residents
me:LD 1318.summary: As introduced, requires the Office of New Americans to collect data on the immigration status of people it serves and on outcomes of asylum claims.

me:LD 132.title: Resolve, to Establish the Commission to Study the Constitution of Maine
me:LD 132.summary: As introduced, creates a Commission to Study the Constitution of Maine to review the Constitution and pending constitutional resolutions and report to the Judiciary Committee by November 4, 2026.

me:LD 1321.title: An Act to Reform Net Energy Billing by Establishing Limitations on the Programs' Duration and Compensation
me:LD 1321.summary: As introduced, limits net energy billing to distributed generation resources under a set size and number of customers, and limits the duration and compensation of net energy billing programs.

me:LD 1328.title: An Act to Create Housing and Recovery Services for LGBTQIA+ Individuals
me:LD 1328.summary: Requires the Maine State Housing Authority to run a competitive bid to award a new fund to acquire or operate two recovery residences, one in a community of 20,000 or more and one smaller, led by people trained in culturally appropriate, trauma-informed services.

me:LD 1329.title: An Act to Identify United States Citizenship Status on Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards
me:LD 1329.summary: Requires driver's licenses and nondriver identification cards to state whether the holder is a U.S. citizen, a noncitizen or an asylum seeker.

me:LD 1330.title: An Act to Clarify That a Business's License or Subscription to Use Software Is Not Considered a Lease for the Purposes of Sales and Use Tax
me:LD 1330.summary: As introduced, says leases, licenses and subscriptions to use or access software are not leases or rentals for sales tax when the user is a business.

me:LD 1331.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine Regarding When the Governor May Call the Legislature into Session
me:LD 1331.summary: Proposes amending the Maine Constitution so that if the Legislature has adjourned without day, the Governor may not convene it until 90 days after adjournment.

me:LD 1333.title: An Act to Make Changes to the Paid Family and Medical Leave Benefits Program
me:LD 1333.summary: As introduced, changes the paid family and medical leave program, including a 120-day employment requirement before taking leave, a 30-day limit on retroactive applications, and requiring available unpaid leave to be taken at the same time as paid leave.

me:LD 1337.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Human Rights Act Regarding Female Athletes and Safety in Women's Single-sex Shelters
me:LD 1337.summary: As introduced, exempts privately run emergency shelters and temporary residences for women in fear for their safety from the Human Rights Act's public accommodation definition, and says its education provisions do not affect female athletes' Title IX rights.

me:LD 1343.title: An Act to Protect the Right to Harvest Wildlife
me:LD 1343.summary: Declares that people in Maine have a right to harvest fish and wildlife by hunting, fishing or trapping for their own nourishment, sustenance, health or well-being, subject to applicable laws and rules.

me:LD 1349.title: An Act to Require Legislative Approval for a Contract to Operate the Juniper Ridge Landfill
me:LD 1349.summary: Bars the Bureau of General Services from entering into or renewing a contract to operate the Juniper Ridge Landfill unless a majority vote of the Legislature approves it.

me:LD 1353.title: An Act Regarding Required Landings in the Menhaden Fishery
me:LD 1353.summary: Authorizes up to 350 commercial menhaden licenses for people who landed 20,000 pounds or more in 2019, 2020 or 2021, with a one-to-one exit ratio, and directs the Department of Marine Resources to develop an entry plan for priority groups, reporting by January 1, 2027.

me:LD 1358.title: An Act to Reduce Electricity Rates by Removing Limitations on the Ownership of Generation by an Affiliate of an Investor-owned Transmission and Distribution Utility
me:LD 1358.summary: Allows an affiliate of an investor-owned transmission and distribution utility to own generation assets under conduct standards set by the Public Utilities Commission, and removes the bar on such affiliate assets taking part in long-term contracts.

me:LD 1364.title: Resolve, Authorizing a Study on the Impacts and Risks of Lead-based Ammunition
me:LD 1364.summary: As amended, directs the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to evaluate, over three years from Nov. 1, 2025, its efforts to educate hunters on non-lead ammunition, including a review of other states' lead ammunition laws.

me:LD 1365.title: An Act to Allow Consumption of Adult Use Cannabis in Locally Approved Hospitality Lounges
me:LD 1365.summary: As introduced, lets municipalities, and local governments in unorganized areas, license cannabis hospitality lounges where adults 21 and older may consume cannabis without separate state licensing or Office of Cannabis Policy oversight, and allows smoking cannabis there.

me:LD 1366.title: An Act to Amend Certain Provisions of the Drug Laws Related to Cocaine Base
me:LD 1366.summary: Removes possession of more than 4 grams of cocaine base from the drug-possession offenses that carry Class B penalties for people with prior drug convictions, and removes the 32-gram cocaine base threshold from aggravated importation of cocaine.

me:LD 1372.title: An Act to Establish a Special Committee to Review Routine Technical Rules
me:LD 1372.summary: As introduced, creates a Special Committee on Regulatory Review of six senators and six representatives, split evenly between the two largest parties, to review routine technical rules and approve, change or reject them.

me:LD 1386.title: An Act to Provide Emergency One-time Relief from the Wild Blueberry Tax for Sellers in Maine and Partial Relief for Processors and Shippers
me:LD 1386.summary: As introduced, exempts sellers of Maine-harvested wild blueberries from their half of the 1.5-cent-per-pound wild blueberry tax for 2025, while processors and shippers still pay their half, 0.75 cents per pound.

me:LD 1394.title: An Act to Support Maine's Electric Vehicle Adoption Goals by Providing an Exclusion for Electric Vehicles from Certain Requirements of the Right to Repair Law
me:LD 1394.summary: As introduced, lets manufacturers exclude electric vehicles from right-to-repair telematics requirements if they annually certify to the Department of Environmental Protection that federal security and privacy standards are met and meet an electric vehicle availability threshold set by rule.

me:LD 1395.title: An Act Regarding Human Trafficking Prevention Instruction and Dissemination of and Access to Obscene Material in Schools
