me:LD 1395.summary: Requires school and college digital library databases offered to K-12 students to block child pornography and obscene material, with schools withholding payment from noncompliant providers. Removes a public-school educational exception from the law on obscene matter for minors.

me:LD 14.title: An Act to Provide Indigenous Peoples Free Access to State Parks
me:LD 14.summary: Waives admission fees at state-owned parks, historic sites, camping areas and beaches for members of federally recognized tribes in Maine who present qualifying tribal identification.

me:LD 1401.title: An Act to Repeal the Provisions of Law Requiring Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance Policies to Cover the Cost of Towing and Storing Certain Vehicles
me:LD 1401.summary: Repeals the requirement that motor vehicle liability policies cover up to $500 per accident in towing and storage charges when law enforcement has the vehicle towed after an accident.

me:LD 1405.title: An Act to Amend Laws Governing the Public Utilities Commission Concerning Participant Funding
me:LD 1405.summary: Removes the Public Utilities Commission's authority to use administrative penalties for intervenor funding and to give participants in nonadjudicatory proceedings funding similar to intervenors.

me:LD 1411.title: An Act to Modify the Laws Regarding Driver's License Applications
me:LD 1411.summary: Makes failing to get a Maine license within 30 days of becoming a resident a traffic infraction, with a $150 to $500 fine after 90 days, instead of a crime, and waives the Social Security number requirement for anyone ineligible, without requiring written proof.

me:LD 1414.title: An Act to Support and Sustain Maine's Child Care Workforce
me:LD 1414.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to raise Child Care Affordability rates for infants and toddlers to 20% above rates for children 36 months and older by January 1, 2027, and to create grants of up to $10,000 to plan overnight child care.

me:LD 142.title: An Act to Prohibit Financial Institutions from Charging Multiple Fees for Attempted Withdrawals Involving Insufficient Funds
me:LD 142.summary: Directs the Bureau of Financial Institutions to issue written guidance by January 1, 2026 to state-chartered financial institutions and credit unions on charging multiple fees for attempted withdrawals involving insufficient funds.

me:LD 1420.title: Resolve, to Establish the Commission to Ensure a Just and Equitable Energy Transition for Maine's Workforce
me:LD 1420.summary: Establishes a commission on a just and equitable energy transition for Maine's workforce, with utility, non-union employer and Public Advocate members added, and requires its report by December 15, 2025.

me:LD 1423.title: An Act to Improve Recycling by Updating the Stewardship Program for Packaging
me:LD 1423.summary: Changes the packaging stewardship program definitions of "producer" and "toxicity," exempts a producer's first 15 tons of perishable food packaging, and lets the stewardship organization recommend changes to producer payment schedules.

me:LD 143.title: An Act to Improve Women's Health and Economic Security by Funding Family Planning Services
me:LD 143.summary: Requires the State Controller to transfer up to $3,000,000 of General Fund surplus at the close of fiscal year 2024-25 to the Maine CDC to fund a single grantee managing statewide family planning services.

me:LD 1431.title: An Act to Implement an Interstate Voter Registration Cross-check Program
me:LD 1431.summary: As introduced, authorizes the Secretary of State to cross-check voter registration lists with other states to identify duplicate registrations, and to contract with a private data provider, barring disclosure of voter data not publicly accessible.

me:LD 1432.title: An Act to Remove Consideration of Gender Identity from the Maine Human Rights Act
me:LD 1432.summary: As introduced, removes gender identity from the grounds on which the Maine Human Rights Act bars discrimination, and repeals a related definition.

me:LD 1435.title: An Act to Allow a Municipality or Locally Recognized Lake Association to Post Certain Information on the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife's Information Kiosks Located at State Boat Launch Facilities
me:LD 1435.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to give municipalities, lake associations and similar nonprofits reasonable space on state boat launch kiosks to display information on water quality and invasive species.

me:LD 1437.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Specify the Qualifications of Electors in State and Local Elections
me:LD 1437.summary: Proposes amending the Maine Constitution to allow only U.S. citizens to vote in state, county, municipal or other local elections.

me:LD 1439.title: An Act to Protect the Health and Welfare of Children in Public Schools by Requiring Parental Consent for Certain Tests, Analyses and Diagnoses
me:LD 1439.summary: As introduced, bars school administrative units from conducting student evaluations that test or diagnose intellectual, emotional, behavioral, psychological or physical development without first obtaining parental consent.

me:LD 1457.title: Resolve, to Allow the Maine Turnpike Authority to Conduct a Pilot Program to Implement Automated Speed Control Systems in Highway Work Zones
me:LD 1457.summary: Allows the Maine Turnpike Authority to run a pilot of automated speed cameras at up to 3 Turnpike work-zone locations, with advance warning signs, notices to vehicle registrants, and deletion of images showing faces within one business day.

me:LD 1461.title: An Act to Prohibit School Boards from Implementing or Enforcing Mask Mandates
me:LD 1461.summary: As introduced, bars a school board from implementing or enforcing a policy that requires a school administrative unit to adopt a mask mandate.

me:LD 1462.title: An Act to Promote Artisans and the Creative Economy
me:LD 1462.summary: Bars municipalities from prohibiting the vending of expressive matter such as written material and visual art, but allows time, place and manner restrictions that meet listed conditions, such as health, safety or access requirements.

me:LD 1463.title: An Act to Prohibit the Auctioning of State Surplus or Forfeited Firearms
me:LD 1463.summary: Bars the State from selling surplus or forfeited firearms and requires them to be destroyed, except firearms assigned to a state employee, who may buy that firearm on leaving employment.

me:LD 1466.title: An Act Related to Excusing a School from Making Up Missed Days When It Cannot Operate During a Declared State of Emergency
me:LD 1466.summary: As introduced, requires the Commissioner of Education to exempt a school from making up missed days when it is in an area under a gubernatorial state of emergency and could not operate, without requiring a waiver application.

me:LD 1467.title: An Act to Ensure Accountability for Repairs Conducted by Independent Repair Facilities on Motor Vehicles Under Warranty
me:LD 1467.summary: As introduced, requires independent repair shops to cover the costs to consumers, manufacturers and dealers of correcting their improper repairs on vehicles under manufacturer warranty, with failure to reimburse treated as an unfair trade practice.

me:LD 147.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Provide for the Popular Election of the Secretary of State
me:LD 147.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment providing for popular election of the Secretary of State every two years, beginning in 2026, in the manner used for legislators.

me:LD 1471.title: An Act to Require Energy Efficiency Disclosure Statements and Energy Efficiency Standards for Certain Rental Housing in the State
me:LD 1471.summary: As amended, beginning January 1, 2030, lets a tenant end a lease on 30 days' written notice if the landlord did not give the required signed energy efficiency disclosure statement, and bars the landlord from keeping any fee or security deposit for that termination.

me:LD 1473.title: An Act to Require Utilities to Monitor Meters for Natural Gas Leaks
me:LD 1473.summary: Requires gas utilities to assess every natural gas main and meter for leaks at least every three years and report leak numbers, locations and actions to the Public Utilities Commission, which publishes the reports online.

me:LD 1474.title: An Act to Strengthen the Teaching of Wabanaki Studies in Maine Schools
me:LD 1474.summary: Creates a Wabanaki studies specialist in the Department of Education, lets the State Board of Education adopt rules requiring a Wabanaki studies component for teacher certification, and requires the department to begin reviewing Wabanaki studies curricula in 2026.

me:LD 1476.title: An Act to Support Maine's Homeless Shelters by Imposing a Fee for Booking Hotels, Short-term Rentals and Recreational Vehicle Camping Reservations
me:LD 1476.summary: Imposes a $2 fee, beginning January 1, 2026, on rentals of lodging place living quarters and recreational vehicle camping sites, with revenue going to the Department of Health and Human Services for homeless shelter operations.

me:LD 1477.title: An Act to Provide an Exemption from Pilotage Requirements for Passenger Ferry Service Between Bar Harbor, Maine and Yarmouth, Nova Scotia
me:LD 1477.summary: Provides ongoing General Fund money to the Department of Economic and Community Development to pay for pilotage services for the Bar Harbor to Yarmouth, Nova Scotia ferry.

me:LD 1488.title: An Act Regarding Cannabis Testing and the Manufacture of Cannabis and Hemp Products
me:LD 1488.summary: As amended, changes cannabis testing rules so using concentrate in vape cartridges or flower and trim in prerolls does not count as further processing requiring extra testing, and drops the bill's shared-equipment provision.

me:LD 149.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Provide for the Popular Election of the Attorney General
me:LD 149.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment providing for popular election of the Attorney General every two years, beginning in 2026, in the manner used for legislators.

me:LD 1494.title: Resolve, Directing the Office of Procurement Services to Study Adapting the Procurement Process to the State Climate Action Plan
me:LD 1494.summary: Directs the Office of Procurement Services to study adapting state procurement to the climate action plan with state agencies, excluding quasi-independent bodies and Public Utilities Commission energy procurements, and report by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 1496.title: An Act to Ensure Ongoing Access to Medications and Care for Chronic Conditions and Conditions Requiring Long-term Care by Changing Requirements for Prior Authorizations
me:LD 1496.summary: Limits prior authorization rules for chronic conditions: approvals last for the treatment's duration or one year, whichever is longer, carriers may not require renewal more than every 3 years, and the limits cover related diagnostic procedures and tests.

me:LD 1498.title: An Act to Address Maine's Housing Crisis by Limiting Municipal Impact Fees on Housing Development and Transferring Oversight of the Housing Opportunity Program to the Maine Office of Community Affairs
me:LD 1498.summary: As amended, requires municipalities with impact fee ordinances to maintain a public policy on how developers' shares are set and to encumber fees within 360 days of receipt, and moves the Housing Opportunity Program to the Office of Community Affairs.

me:LD 150.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Provide for the Popular Election of the Treasurer of State
me:LD 150.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment providing for popular election of the Treasurer of State every two years, beginning in 2026, in the manner used for legislators.

me:LD 1505.title: An Act to Phase out the Sales and Use Tax
me:LD 1505.summary: Reduces the sales tax rate by one-half of a percentage point every two years starting January 1, 2026 until it reaches 0%, with use tax rates falling in step.

me:LD 1507.title: An Act to Require General Public Notification of Oil Terminal Facility Transfer Activities
me:LD 1507.summary: As amended, requires licensed petroleum storage facilities with aboveground tanks over 39,000 gallons to post warning signs about hazardous air pollutants and flammable vapors at intervals of 100 feet or less along publicly accessible property boundaries.

me:LD 1517.title: An Act to Replace Participation Thresholds with Approval Thresholds in Certain School, Municipal and County Measures
me:LD 1517.summary: As amended, lowers the vote turnout required for certain school, municipal and county measures, measured against the last governor's-race vote total (for example, 50% to 25% for school unit withdrawal, 30% to 15% for charter changes); some provisions count only votes in favor.

me:LD 1519.title: An Act to Create a Stewardship Program for Electronic Smoking Devices and Related Products
me:LD 1519.summary: Requires producers of electronic smoking devices to submit a stewardship plan for collecting unwanted devices, requires retailers selling them to join as collection sites within 3 years of plan approval, and sets a minimum $2 incentive per returned device (up to 2 a day).

me:LD 152.title: An Act to Amend the Freedom of Access Act to Require a Specific Time Frame for Agencies to Comply with Requests for Public Records
me:LD 152.summary: Requires agencies and officials to comply with a Freedom of Access Act public records request within 30 days after it is made, rather than within a reasonable time.

me:LD 1522.title: An Act to Establish the Maine Eviction Prevention Program
me:LD 1522.summary: Creates the Maine Eviction Prevention Program at the Maine State Housing Authority, paying up to $800 a month to a participant's landlord for up to 12 months, with $10,000,000 in ongoing yearly funding.

me:LD 1535.title: An Act to Reduce Illegal Cannabis Operations by Requiring Permits for High Electrical Usage
me:LD 1535.summary: As amended, replaces the permit bill with a resolve directing the Public Utilities Commission to facilitate at least one stakeholder meeting on high-electrical-usage permits for cannabis operations and report to the Energy, Utilities and Technology Committee by January 15, 2026.

me:LD 1536.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Bail
me:LD 1536.summary: As introduced, reverses the changes made to the Maine Bail Code by Public Law 2021, chapter 397.

me:LD 1539.title: An Act to Create a State Employee Compensation Stabilization Fund
me:LD 1539.summary: Creates a State Employee Compensation Stabilization Fund to raise state employee salaries toward market parity, funded by 5% of the General Fund surplus, and cuts the share going to the Budget Stabilization Fund from 80% to 75%.

me:LD 1543.title: An Act to Establish the Maine Green Schools Network
me:LD 1543.summary: Creates the Maine Green Schools Network in the Department of Education to support school environmental projects and educator training; participants may be invited subject to available funds, and the network reports to the Legislature by November 4, 2026.

me:LD 1549.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine Regarding the Use and Oversight of Transportation-related Revenues
me:LD 1549.summary: As introduced, proposes a constitutional amendment requiring at least 60% of automobile-related sales and use tax revenue to go to the Highway Fund starting July 1, 2027, for all modes of transportation.

me:LD 1553.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Require a Supermajority of the Legislature to Approve Raising Taxes
me:LD 1553.summary: As introduced, proposes a constitutional amendment barring state tax rate increases and new state taxes unless approved by direct initiative or by a two-thirds vote of each House.

me:LD 1563.title: An Act to Establish Content Standards for Legislation
me:LD 1563.summary: As introduced, requires all legislation to be fully drafted before introduction, not an abstract or concept, and bars referral to a committee of any bill not drafted so it could become law if unamended.

me:LD 1566.title: An Act to Provide Compensation to Individuals with Lived Experience Serving on Advisory Boards, Commissions, Councils and Similar Groups
me:LD 1566.summary: Lets board members representing lived experience on certain advisory boards receive compensation up to the legislative per diem, plus expenses, if not otherwise paid by an employer or the entity they represent; the amendment adds a one-time $5,000 appropriation.

me:LD 1571.title: An Act to Modify Certification Standards for Full-time Teachers in Public Charter Schools and for Educational Technicians
me:LD 1571.summary: As amended, requires full-time public charter school teachers to hold a teaching certificate starting August 1, 2026, and from that date cuts from 5 to 3 years the retirement-benefit period allowed for reissuing a lapsed educational technician certificate.

me:LD 1576.title: An Act to Extend a One-year Lobbying Prohibition to Partisan and Nonpartisan Staff of the Legislature
me:LD 1576.summary: Extends the one-year ban on lobbying by former executive branch employees to former legislative branch employees, partisan and nonpartisan, beginning January 1, 2026.

me:LD 1582.title: An Act to Clarify the Prohibition on the Sale of Beverages in Plastic Containers
me:LD 1582.summary: Defines "closure device" in the law that bars selling beverages in plastic containers whose basic structure also includes aluminum or steel.

me:LD 1585.title: Resolve, to Direct the Maine State Housing Authority to Amend Its Rules Governing the Fuel Assistance Program Regarding Benefit Payments for Wood Fuel
me:LD 1585.summary: As introduced, directs the Maine State Housing Authority to change its fuel assistance rules so benefit payments for wood fuel are paid directly to vendors before delivery.

me:LD 1586.title: An Act to Amend the Regional School Unit Budget Validation Referendum Law
me:LD 1586.summary: Requires the question on a regional school unit budget validation referendum to include the dollar amount of the budget.

me:LD 1587.title: An Act to Establish Greater Alignment of Penalties for Certain Labor Law Violations
me:LD 1587.summary: Lets the Director of Labor Standards investigate suspected violations of certain labor laws, order penalties, issue levy notices for unpaid amounts, and requires employers to post notices of violation in the workplace.

me:LD 1593.title: An Act to Require Certain Public Entities to Define Their Use of the Term "Equity"
me:LD 1593.summary: As introduced, requires the State, local governments and educational institutions that make a decision based on advancing equity to post on a public website the definition of "equity" and the metrics they used.

me:LD 16.title: An Act to Establish Separate Prosecutorial Districts in Downeast Maine
me:LD 16.summary: Reduces Prosecutorial District Number 7 to Hancock County and creates a new Prosecutorial District Number 9 for Washington County.

me:LD 160.title: An Act to Eliminate REAL ID Requirements in Maine
me:LD 160.summary: Repeals the law letting the Secretary of State issue, on request, driver's licenses and nondriver ID cards that meet federal REAL ID Act standards, and repeals the related fee provisions.

me:LD 161.title: Resolve, Directing the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to Convene a Stakeholder Group Tasked with a Comprehensive Overhaul and Modernization of the State Subdivision Laws
me:LD 161.summary: Directs the Maine Office of Community Affairs to convene a working group with two other state departments to recommend an overhaul and modernization of Maine's subdivision laws, with a final work plan due November 4, 2026.

me:LD 1611.title: An Act to Decrease the Retirement Contributions Required for Teachers and State Employees
me:LD 1611.summary: Gradually lowers required member contributions to the Maine Public Employees Retirement System from 7.65% to 6.2% of earnable compensation between July 1, 2027 and July 1, 2032, with the State paying resulting higher employer costs for teachers.

me:LD 1620.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Regulating the Testing of Adult Use Cannabis and Adult Use Cannabis Products
me:LD 1620.summary: As introduced, requires cannabis testing rules to set a 100,000 colony-forming units per gram yeast and mold limit, makes licensees with 10 consecutive passing batch tests eligible for audit testing, and requires the state to publish anonymized test results online.

me:LD 1624.title: An Act to Provide Funding for Summer School Programming
me:LD 1624.summary: Provides ongoing funding to school administrative units for summer school and credit recovery programs, including units already offering them, with priority for units with student poverty rates of 25% or higher.

me:LD 1626.title: An Act to Improve Professional Development for Educational Technicians and School Support Staff
me:LD 1626.summary: Requires school administrative units to give educational technicians and support staff annual training on topics including emergency procedures, confidentiality, reporting duties and discipline policies, plus training on student disabilities for educational technicians.

me:LD 1629.title: An Act to Require Legislative Committees to Provide Equal Time to Each Member of the Public Who Testifies
me:LD 1629.summary: As introduced, requires joint standing and select committees to give each person who testifies at a public hearing equal time to testify.

me:LD 163.title: An Act to Require Health Insurance Coverage for Federally Approved Nonprescription Oral Hormonal Contraceptives and Nonprescription Emergency Contraceptives
me:LD 163.summary: Requires health plans to cover FDA-approved nonprescription oral hormonal and emergency contraceptives without a prescription beginning January 1, 2026, and requires yearly enrollee notice and monitoring by the Bureau of Insurance.

me:LD 1636.title: Resolve, to Study Changing the Start of the State Fiscal Year to October 1st
me:LD 1636.summary: Creates a working group to study moving the state fiscal year from a July 1 to June 30 year to an October 1 to September 30 year, and the effects on the state, counties, towns and school units.

me:LD 1643.title: An Act to Establish the Maine Life Science Innovation Center
me:LD 1643.summary: Establishes the Maine Life Sciences Innovation Center within the Maine Technology Institute, with nine voting members appointed by the Governor plus the economic development commissioner as a nonvoting member, to support life sciences research, entrepreneurship and workforce development, and requires an interim report.

me:LD 1647.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Human Rights Act to Provide Additional Remedies for Educational Discrimination
me:LD 1647.summary: Lets a court award compensatory damages up to $100,000 in cases of intentional educational discrimination under the Maine Human Rights Act, if the institution had actual notice, and funds two positions at public college systems.

me:LD 1649.title: Resolve, to Establish the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study the Operations of the Legislature
me:LD 1649.summary: As amended, creates a commission to study and recommend ways to modernize the Legislature and improve its effectiveness.

me:LD 165.title: An Act to Allow School Boards to Expel or Suspend Students Regardless of Grade Level
me:LD 165.summary: As introduced, allows a school board to expel or authorize suspension of a student of any grade level.

me:LD 1655.title: An Act to Allow the Keeping of Chickens on Private Residential Property
me:LD 1655.summary: Bars counties and municipalities from prohibiting a person from keeping chickens on their residential property. Defines chicken as a domesticated bird raised for meat or eggs, excluding fully mature males.

me:LD 1656.title: An Act to Facilitate Compliance with Federal Immigration Law by State and Local Government Entities
me:LD 1656.summary: As introduced, bars state and local government entities and law enforcement agencies from adopting policies that restrict immigration-information sharing or assistance with federal immigration enforcement; sets Attorney General review, with a $500 daily fine for entities that keep a policy after a court injunction.

me:LD 1657.title: An Act to Expand the Use of Tax Increment Revenue for Affordable Housing by Adding Authorized Project Costs
me:LD 1657.summary: As introduced, adds costs of developing, buying, selling, financing and operating affordable housing, and of municipal loan or grant programs for qualifying buyers, to the authorized uses of tax increment revenue.

me:LD 166.title: An Act to Prohibit the Sale of Tobacco Products in Pharmacies and Retail Establishments Containing Pharmacies
me:LD 166.summary: Makes pharmacies and retail stores containing a pharmacy ineligible for a retail tobacco license and makes their tobacco sales a civil violation with fines up to $2,000 per offense, effective April 1, 2026.

me:LD 1662.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Regarding Zoning and Land Use Restrictions to Limit Certain Requirements to Municipalities with Populations of More than 10,000
me:LD 1662.summary: As introduced, limits certain zoning rules on dwelling units and accessory dwelling units in residential areas to municipalities with populations over 10,000.

me:LD 1664.title: An Act to Repeal the Dirigo Business Incentives Program
me:LD 1664.summary: As amended, changes the Dirigo business incentives program so that workforce reductions caused by Department of Transportation vehicle weight or passage restrictions do not count as a layoff.

me:LD 1665.title: An Act to Provide Property Tax Relief to Maine Families
me:LD 1665.summary: As amended, raises the property tax fairness credit benefit base for tax years from 2025, including to $4,250 for filers 65 or older, raises the credit cap to $2,000 for some households with children, and creates a state working group to study simplifying the credit.

me:LD 1666.title: An Act to Include in the Ranked-choice Election Method for General and Special Elections the Offices of Governor, State Senator and State Representative and to Make Other Related Changes
me:LD 1666.summary: Extends ranked-choice voting to general and special elections for Governor, State Senator and State Representative, with technical wording changes, and states the winner is the candidate with a plurality of votes.

me:LD 1667.title: Resolve, to Allow Hemphill Farms, Inc. to Sue the State
me:LD 1667.summary: As introduced, authorizes Hemphill Farms, Inc., of Presque Isle to sue the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry for damages from actions it claims the department took.

me:LD 1668.title: An Act Regarding the Voting Requirement to Extend the Date for Adjournment of the Legislature
me:LD 1668.summary: Lowers the vote needed to extend a regular legislative session past its statutory adjournment date from two-thirds to a majority of members present and voting.

me:LD 1672.title: An Act to Allow Participation in the Adult Use Cannabis Tracking System to Be Voluntary
me:LD 1672.summary: Directs the Office of Cannabis Policy to provisionally adopt rules by Jan. 9, 2026 for an alternate method of tracking adult use cannabis that licensees may use instead of the state tracking system.

me:LD 1684.title: An Act to Exclude from Eligibility for a Community Confinement Monitoring Program a Person Serving a Sentence for Certain Domestic Violence Crimes
me:LD 1684.summary: As amended, adds Office of Victim Services input and, for prisoners incarcerated for crimes against family, household members or dating partners, domestic violence risk assessments to community confinement transfer reviews; lets the commissioner require participants to keep paying victim restitution.

me:LD 1696.title: Resolve, to Study Maine's Absolute Dominion and Beneficial Use Laws Relating to Water Rights
me:LD 1696.summary: Creates a commission to study Maine's absolute dominion and beneficial use groundwater laws and recommend changes, reporting to the Environment Committee by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 1697.title: An Act to Increase Penalties to Deter Violations of the Laws Regarding Improper Pesticide Use
me:LD 1697.summary: Raises the maximum fine for violating pesticide laws and rules from $1,500 to $10,000, or to $50,000 for an unauthorized application from which the violator benefited substantially.

me:LD 1704.title: An Act to Prohibit a School Administrative Unit from Adopting a Policy That Allows a Student to Use a Restroom Designated for Use by the Opposite Sex
me:LD 1704.summary: As introduced, bars school administrative units from adopting policies that let a student use a restroom matching gender identity when it is designated for a sex differing from the student's sex assigned at birth.

me:LD 1705.title: An Act Regarding Adult Education Funding and Oversight
me:LD 1705.summary: Requires the Department of Education to assess adult education needs each year and report to the Legislature, including the full funding each adult education program is eligible for and a plan to reach 100% funding.

me:LD 1707.title: An Act to Require a Person to Be a United States Citizen to Receive State or Local Financial Assistance and to Ensure Municipal Compliance with Federal Immigration Laws
me:LD 1707.summary: As introduced, bars the State and municipalities from giving financial assistance to non-citizens (except school general purpose aid), and makes municipalities ineligible for state aid if they conflict with a federal immigration-information law or bar local police from gathering immigration-status information.

me:LD 1712.title: An Act to Amend the Paid Family and Medical Leave Benefits Program to Balance Support of Businesses and Employees
me:LD 1712.summary: As introduced, changes the paid family and medical leave program, including listing undue-hardship conditions for employers to deny leave without Department of Labor review and requiring employers to deduct 50% of the payroll premium from employee wages.

me:LD 1715.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Amend the Appointment and Confirmation Process for Certain Judicial, Civil and Military Officers
me:LD 1715.summary: As amended in committee, proposes a constitutional amendment letting the Senate confirm the Governor's nominations of certain judicial, civil and military officers by majority vote.

me:LD 1716.title: An Act to Require Family Life Education to Include a Human Growth and Development Curriculum
me:LD 1716.summary: As introduced, requires schools offering comprehensive family life education to include, by grade 3, a lesson on pregnancy and fetal development with an ultrasound video and a fertilization-to-birth video, and lets the Attorney General sue to enforce it.

me:LD 1719.title: An Act Regarding Superintendent Agreements for Transfer Students
me:LD 1719.summary: Sets added procedures for student transfers between school units: both superintendents review a parent's evidence and decide within 30 days, with appeals to the Commissioner of Education and State Board of Education.

me:LD 1723.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Manufactured Housing Communities to Prevent Excessive Rent and Fees Increases
me:LD 1723.summary: Requires manufactured housing community owners to give written notice of lot rent or fee increases and to join mediation, paid by the owner, if at least 51% of households request it.

me:LD 1726.title: An Act to Enhance the Coordination and Effectiveness of Integrated Distribution Grid Planning
me:LD 1726.summary: As amended, directs the Governor's Energy Office to seek consistent energy forecasting; adds advanced conductors, grid-enhancing technologies and low-voltage sensors to utility grid plan filings; lets the PUC use filings in competitive solicitations; orders PUC reviews.

me:LD 173.title: An Act to Exempt Certain Watercraft from Registration Requirements
me:LD 173.summary: As introduced, exempts canoes, kayaks and rowboats equipped with a motor under 100 horsepower from boat registration requirements.

me:LD 1730.title: An Act Regarding the Beneficial Electrification Policy of the State
me:LD 1730.summary: Exempts retail customers' installation of plug-in solar and battery systems that offset on-site electricity use from certain requirements, subject to safety standards and capacity limits, and bars using those systems for net energy billing.

me:LD 1731.title: An Act to Increase the Influence of the Maine State Ferry Advisory Board on the Funding and Operations of the Maine State Ferry Service
me:LD 1731.summary: As introduced, requires the Maine State Ferry Service to consult the Ferry Advisory Board on budgets, planning and major operational decisions, consider its recommendations and report to it regularly; requires the board to review the service annually and report to the Legislature by January 15.

me:LD 1734.title: An Act to Exempt Over-the-counter Medicines from the Sales and Use Tax
me:LD 1734.summary: Exempts over-the-counter medicines and drugs labelled per FDA requirements from the sales tax, including antacids, contraceptives, cough, cold and allergy products and opioid antagonists, for sales on or after January 1, 2026.

me:LD 1736.title: An Act to Increase the Supply of Child Care Services Through the Use of Contracts
me:LD 1736.summary: Requires the Office of Child and Family Services to contract directly with child care providers for slots for children under 3, children with disabilities and children in underserved areas, and allows other priority groups.

me:LD 1738.title: An Act to Establish the Biohazard Waste Disposal Grant Program to Support Public Health Efforts in the State
me:LD 1738.summary: Creates a Biohazard Waste Disposal Grant Program at the Maine CDC to fund community collection and disposal of used hypodermic needles; municipalities that receive opioid settlement funds and apply must match the amount requested from their settlement allocation.

me:LD 174.title: An Act to Restore Religious Exemptions to Immunization Requirements
me:LD 174.summary: Reinstates exemptions from immunization requirements based on sincere religious belief for students at all school levels, nursery school employees, and health care practitioners.

me:LD 1743.title: An Act to Allow Municipalities to Prohibit Firearms Within Their Municipal Buildings and Voting Places and at Their Municipal Public Proceedings
me:LD 1743.summary: Lets a municipality limit or prohibit possession of firearms in its buildings, voting places and public proceedings, with civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; exempts law enforcement officers and requires posted notice.

me:LD 1748.title: An Act to Enhance Businesses' Understanding of Labor Standards and Grow Maine's Energy Economy Through a Training Program
me:LD 1748.summary: Replaces the bill with a requirement that the Department of Labor work with state energy entities to develop a fact sheet and guide on state labor laws for developers of assisted energy projects of 1 megawatt or more, who must attest they reviewed it.

me:LD 1749.title: Resolve, Directing the Department of Corrections to Study Achieving Gender Equality
me:LD 1749.summary: Directs the Department of Corrections to study gender inequality in its programs, services, facilities and policies and to recommend solutions to the Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee by Dec. 3, 2025.

me:LD 1750.title: An Act to Require the Attorney General to Create and Update Biennially a Model Residential Lease
me:LD 1750.summary: Requires the Attorney General to create and post a model residential lease reflecting current law, including required disclosures, and update it every two years.

me:LD 1751.title: An Act to Improve the Growth Management Program Laws
me:LD 1751.summary: As introduced, changes municipal growth management laws by updating terminology and procedures and requiring comprehensive plans to include a needs assessment, local goals and a future land use plan.

me:LD 1754.title: An Act to Provide for the Direct Shipment of Spirits to Consumers
me:LD 1754.summary: Allows distilleries, rectifiers and out-of-state spirits makers to ship spirits directly to Maine consumers, similar to wine shipping, and lets registered fulfillment providers ship for them; the amendment adds registration and pricing rules.

me:LD 1759.title: An Act to Allow Firefighters to Be Eligible for State College Funding
me:LD 1759.summary: As introduced, reduces one-time funding for the free community college program in fiscal year 2025-26 by $800,000 and gives $800,000 one-time to the Maine Fire Service Institute.

me:LD 1765.title: An Act to Ensure Affordability and Stability in Housing for Mobile Home Park Residents
me:LD 1765.summary: Requires more information from applicants for a manufactured housing community license and directs the Office of Policy Innovation and the Future to complete tasks on affordable housing and report to the Housing committee by Dec. 31.

me:LD 1766.title: An Act to Incorporate Probate Judges into the Maine Judicial Branch
me:LD 1766.summary: Replaces part-time elected county probate judges with full-time state judges appointed by the Governor and confirmed by the Legislature: 4 judges in York, Kennebec, Somerset and Aroostook counties from January 1, 2029, and 9 statewide from January 1, 2031.

me:LD 1768.title: An Act to Protect Residents of Mobile Home Parks by Amending the Real Estate Transfer Tax
me:LD 1768.summary: Exempts sales of mobile home parks to their residents from the real estate transfer tax and adds maintaining affordability in mobile home parks to the purposes of the Housing Opportunities for Maine Program.

me:LD 1771.title: An Act to Strengthen Oversight of Kennels by Changing the Licensing Authority from Municipalities to the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
me:LD 1771.summary: Moves kennel licensing from municipalities to the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, sets criteria for refusing or revoking facility licenses, exempts kennel licensees from individual dog license fees, and requires licensees to pay for background checks.

me:LD 1777.title: An Act to Clarify Tariff Rates for Nonresidential Customers Participating in Net Energy Billing with a Distributed Generation Resource
me:LD 1777.summary: Amends the committee amendment to the net energy billing bill: removes the "mechanical completion" definition, applies the kilowatt-hour credit program to resources with an agreement on December 31, 2025, and bars new agreements with front-of-meter resources after that date.

me:LD 1784.title: An Act to Require Police Departments to Publish and Make Accessible Their Policies and Procedures and Require Training of Officers
me:LD 1784.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to publish their required policies and procedures online or in printed form and to train officers on them; allows a reasonable fee for paper copies and bars release of confidential investigative records.

me:LD 1787.title: An Act to Strengthen the Maine Clean Election Act
me:LD 1787.summary: Raises the Maine Clean Election Act seed money contribution limit for participating gubernatorial candidates to $250 per individual.

me:LD 179.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Bail Code to Eliminate the Class E Crime of Violation of Condition of Release
me:LD 179.summary: As introduced, repeals the Class E crime of violating a condition of bail release, leaving the Class C crime for violating conditions of release in place.

me:LD 1792.title: An Act Regarding the Energy Policy of the State
me:LD 1792.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission, by Oct. 1, 2025, to set a rate design for each investor-owned transmission and distribution utility that groups certain customer classes for recovering post-restructuring stranded costs; takes effect as an emergency.

me:LD 1802.title: An Act to Implement the Recommendations of the Maine Commission on Public Defense Services to Clarify When an Indigent Criminal Defendant Is Entitled to Counsel at State Expense
me:LD 1802.summary: Defines when there is a risk of imprisonment entitling an indigent defendant to state-paid counsel, including when the prosecutor will seek jail, the accused is held in custody beyond 24 hours, or bail conditions apply.

me:LD 1804.title: An Act Concerning Funding and Oversight of Transportation Matters
me:LD 1804.summary: As introduced, gives the transportation committee oversight of the Highway Fund, sets minimum funding for bridges, highway lights and multimodal transportation, raises from 40% to 60% the automobile-related sales tax share going to the Highway Fund, and funds State Police solely from the General Fund from 2027-28.

me:LD 1806.title: An Act to Create a Residential Rental Unit Registry
me:LD 1806.summary: As introduced, requires owners of residential rental units to register them annually with the Secretary of State and bars serving a nonpayment termination notice on an unregistered unit, with a civil penalty of 3 times the monthly rent.

me:LD 1810.title: An Act to Formalize a Process for Reviewing the Conduct of Judges and Justices
me:LD 1810.summary: As amended, creates a commission to review the Supreme Judicial Court's rules on judicial discipline and report findings and recommendations to the Judiciary Committee by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 1816.title: An Act to Establish a Statewide Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Kit Tracking System and Conduct an Inventory of Existing Forensic Examination Kits in the Possession of Law Enforcement
me:LD 1816.summary: As introduced, directs the Department of Public Safety to run a statewide tracking system for all completed sexual assault forensic exam kits, requires agencies to inventory their kits by June 1, 2026, and extends a health care law kit storage period from 8 to 20 years.

me:LD 1819.title: An Act Regarding the Brunswick Naval Air Station Job Increment Financing Fund
me:LD 1819.summary: Sends 100% of the remaining tax increment and base benefit shares into the Brunswick Naval Air Station Job Increment Financing Fund through January 2035, and splits fund reimbursements 75% to the redevelopment authority and 25% to Southern Maine Community College.

me:LD 182.title: An Act to Require the Department of Health and Human Services to Establish MaineCare Reimbursement Rates for the Maine Veterans' Homes on a Per Resident Basis
me:LD 182.summary: As amended, requires MaineCare to pay Maine Veterans' Homes facilities a daily rate per MaineCare resident, set by the department and adjusted annually for inflation, and appropriates funding.

me:LD 1821.title: An Act to Ensure Responsible Business Practices by Licensed Firearms Dealers
me:LD 1821.summary: As introduced, requires firearm dealers to meet state security standards, background-check and train employees, keep records, report thefts, annually certify compliance (false certification is a Class C crime), and post notices on child safety, background checks and suicide prevention.

me:LD 1822.title: An Act to Enact the Maine Online Data Privacy Act
me:LD 1822.summary: Enacts the Maine Online Data Privacy Act, letting residents access, correct, delete and opt out of sale or targeted-advertising use of their personal data held by businesses, and limiting collection of sensitive data; as amended, takes effect September 1, 2027.

me:LD 1823.title: An Act to Promote Transparency in the Criminal Justice System by Requiring the Posting of Criminal Case Decisions
me:LD 1823.summary: As introduced, requires the Attorney General and court clerks to post the final decision of each criminal case on their public websites within 60 days of final disposition.

me:LD 1838.title: An Act to Provide Opportunities and Sustainable Revenue for Maine Farms, Agricultural Fairs, Wabanaki Tribes and Veterans' Homes
me:LD 1838.summary: As introduced, allows licensed tribes, commercial tracks, off-track betting facilities and certain beano organizations to operate electronic terminals for historical horse race wagers, electronic beano and virtual sealed tickets, with 25% of net terminal income distributed to named funds and municipalities.

me:LD 184.title: Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Study the Foreclosure Process
me:LD 184.summary: As introduced, creates a 7-member commission to study foreclosure laws, rules and timelines, including how they affect availability of foreclosed properties for affordable housing and the role of mortgages sold on the secondary market.

me:LD 1840.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Medical Use of Cannabis Act
me:LD 1840.summary: As amended, bars the Office of Cannabis Policy from requiring registrant attestations on forms unless the law authorizes them, lets caregivers sell or furnish medical cannabis at their premises, trade shows and by delivery, and adds gross sales to its annual report.

me:LD 1847.title: An Act to Institute Testing and Tracking of Medical Use Cannabis and Cannabis Products Similar to Adult Use Cannabis and Cannabis Products, Dedicate a Portion of the Adult Use Cannabis Sales and Excise Tax to Medical Use Cannabis Programs and Create a Study Group
me:LD 1847.summary: As amended, requires mandatory testing of harvested medical cannabis, except for certain caregivers; creates cannabis testing facility registration; requires inventory reporting and six-year record retention; and allows $100 per-batch testing reimbursements to qualifying registrants.

me:LD 1849.title: An Act to Establish a Minimum Age at Which Conduct Constitutes a Juvenile Crime and to Confer Jurisdiction to the Juvenile Courts Over Any Criminal Offense Under Maine Law Committed by a Juvenile
me:LD 1849.summary: As introduced, sets 11 as the minimum age for juvenile crimes (none for murder, felony murder and manslaughter) and makes any Title 12 or 29-A offense a juvenile crime when committed by a juvenile. The committee amendment adds license-suspension rules for juvenile motor vehicle offenses.

me:LD 1853.title: An Act to Establish an Educational Tax Credit Program to Help Parents Pay for Nonpublic School Tuition and Fees
me:LD 1853.summary: As introduced, creates a refundable tax credit equal to 70% of the cost of publicly funded education for parents of eligible students enrolled in nonpublic schools, delayed until 2027-2028 for currently enrolled students.

me:LD 1858.title: An Act to Promote Local Seafood in Schools
me:LD 1858.summary: Changes the Local Foods Fund in the Department of Education to match $1 for every $2 a school unit spends on food, including seafood, from in-state producers, with a state maximum of $10,000 per unit ($11,000 if it sends a food service employee to training).

me:LD 1859.title: An Act to Improve Access to Child Care and Early Childhood Education by Establishing Regional Resource Hubs
me:LD 1859.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to contract for two early childhood resource hubs by July 1, 2026, helping families find child care and early education programs and training child care workers, with annual reports starting in 2028.

me:LD 186.title: An Act to Clarify the Public Utilities Commission's Authority to Establish Time-of-use Pricing for Standard-offer Service
me:LD 186.summary: Clarifies that the Public Utilities Commission may use time-of-use pricing for standard-offer service, requires it to report to the Legislature's utilities committee before an adjudicatory proceeding setting such rates, and to seek to avoid negative impacts on certain residential customers.

me:LD 1865.title: Resolve, to Create a Tax Incentive Pilot Project to Encourage Businesses to Adopt a 4-day Workweek
me:LD 1865.summary: Directs the Department of Economic and Community Development to run a Four-day Workweek Pilot Project ending by December 31, 2029, and makes participating employers eligible for the wellness program tax credit.

me:LD 1867.title: An Act to Prohibit Financial Institutions from Using Merchant Category Codes to Identify or Track Firearm Purchases or Disclose Firearm Purchase Records
me:LD 1867.summary: Bars financial institutions from assigning merchants a firearms code and payment card networks from requiring or permitting its use. The Attorney General may investigate, must allow a chance to correct violations, and may sue for an injunction; takes effect Jan. 1, 2026.

me:LD 1868.title: An Act to Advance a Clean Energy Economy by Updating Renewable and Clean Resource Procurement Laws
me:LD 1868.summary: Changes renewable and clean energy procurement laws, setting 2040 goals of 90% renewable and 10% clean electricity, defining Class III clean resources including nuclear and qualifying hydroelectric, and letting the Public Utilities Commission coordinate procurement with other states.

me:LD 187.title: An Act to Prohibit Labor Organizations from Imposing Mandatory Service Fees on Nonmembers
me:LD 187.summary: Removes the authorization for a union serving as bargaining agent to charge represented non-members a service fee for representation expenditures.

me:LD 1870.title: An Act to Establish a Climate Superfund Cost Recovery Program to Impose Penalties on Climate Polluters
me:LD 1870.summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Protection to assess the State's costs from greenhouse gas emissions from 1995 through 2024 and report the results by January 1, 2028.

me:LD 1871.title: An Act to Permit Sealing Criminal History Record Information of Victims of Sex Trafficking or Sexual Exploitation
me:LD 1871.summary: Lets a person move to seal criminal records for any conviction where they show they were a victim of sex trafficking or sexual exploitation and the crime was a substantial result of it.

me:LD 1872.title: An Act to Reinvest in the Pension Funds of the Maine Public Employees Retirement System
me:LD 1872.summary: Transfers General Fund money each year from 2028-29 through 2032-33 to a nonlapsing fund for retirement benefit improvements for retired state employees and teachers, capped at $185,000,000 a year.

me:LD 1873.title: An Act to Require Age Verification for Online Obscene Matter
me:LD 1873.summary: As introduced, requires businesses that knowingly publish obscene matter online to verify users are of age by reasonable methods and bars them from keeping users' identifying information after verification.

me:LD 1879.title: An Act to Support Maine's Agricultural Economy by Increasing Revenue from the Corporate Income Tax and Providing Property Tax Exemptions
me:LD 1879.summary: Imposes an extra 1.07% tax on corporate income over $3.5 million, bringing the top rate to 10%, with revenue directed to agricultural purposes in a set order of priority.

me:LD 1881.title: An Act to Ensure the Rights of Parents of Minor Children in Education
me:LD 1881.summary: As introduced, gives parents the right to access their minor child's school health and education records and instructional materials, to preview health questionnaires, and to refuse noneducational assignments, and bars policies preventing staff from informing parents about a student's well-being.

me:LD 1884.title: Resolve, to Increase the Number of Kennebec County Commissioners
me:LD 1884.summary: As introduced, proposes a referendum in November 2026 asking Kennebec County voters to increase the number of county commissioners from 3 to 5.

me:LD 1886.title: An Act Regarding Penalties for Violation of the Law Governing Distracted Driving When the Violation Results in the Death or Significant Injury of Another Person
me:LD 1886.summary: Applies existing penalties for motor vehicle violations that cause another person's death to violations that cause serious bodily injury to another person.

me:LD 189.title: An Act to Increase Availability and Affordability of Mental Health Care and Substance Use Disorder Services by Removing the Certificate of Need Requirement
me:LD 189.summary: Eliminates the certificate of need requirement for health care facilities providing mental and behavioral health care and substance use disorder detoxification and treatment services.

me:LD 1892.title: An Act to Establish Procedures for School Construction Projects
me:LD 1892.summary: Raises the maximum debt service limit for school construction projects to $188.8 million in fiscal 2028, rising to $206.3 million in 2031, creates a School Construction Accelerator Fund for heating, cooling and roof repairs, and transfers $50 million yearly to the School Revolving Renovation Fund.

me:LD 1893.title: An Act to Establish an Independent Office of the Child Advocate
me:LD 1893.summary: Replaces the child welfare ombudsman program with an independent Office of the Child Advocate, led by a five-year-term Child Advocate who reviews complaints about state services to children, investigates, and makes recommendations.

me:LD 1894.title: An Act to Address Consumer Grocery Pricing Fairness
me:LD 1894.summary: Establishes a commission to study grocery supply-chain terms and conditions that affect product availability and prices, independent grocers and local products, and to report findings and recommended legislation by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 1897.title: An Act Regarding Sun-grown Cultivation in the Medical Use and Adult Use Cannabis Industries
me:LD 1897.summary: Raises the limit for medical cannabis caregivers who grow mature plants only outdoors (March to December) to 150 mature plants or 2,500 square feet of canopy, up from 30 or 500, with an annual registration fee; defines outdoor and indoor adult use cultivation.

me:LD 1899.title: An Act to Eliminate Taxation on Health Care Spending
me:LD 1899.summary: Creates a state income tax deduction for medical and dental expenses of the taxpayer, spouse and dependents that federal law allows, even below the federal threshold, to the extent not covered by insurance or otherwise deducted.

me:LD 19.title: An Act to Change the Definition of "Oversized ATV" in the Laws Governing the Registration of All-terrain Vehicles
me:LD 19.summary: Raises the minimum weight of an "oversized" all-terrain vehicle from 2,000 to 2,950 pounds and removes the bill's emergency clause.

me:LD 1900.title: An Act to Bring Parity to the State's Recognition of the Wabanaki Nations' Authority to Provide Electric Power Districts and Child Support Enforcement
me:LD 1900.summary: Lets the Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians and the Mi'kmaq Nation form tribal power districts to provide electricity on their trust lands, and extends certain child support enforcement tools to the Houlton Band and the Maliseet Tribal Court.

me:LD 1902.title: An Act to Support Nonprofit Organizations by Authorizing the Operation of Electronic Lucky Seven Devices and Similar Sealed Ticket Games
me:LD 1902.summary: Authorizes the Gambling Control Unit to license eligible organizations to operate electronic lucky seven devices, limits their number, location and operation, and requires distributors of the devices to be licensed.

me:LD 1908.title: An Act to Require the Cooperation of Original Manufacturers of Electronic Devices to Facilitate the Repair of Those Devices by Device Owners and Independent Repair Providers
me:LD 1908.summary: Requires manufacturers of digital electronic equipment to give independent repairers and owners repair documentation, parts and tools on fair terms from 2028, and bars software parts pairing in newer consumer electronics; excludes vehicles, medical devices and game consoles; bars suits by owners and repairers.

me:LD 1911.title: An Act to Automatically Seal Criminal History Record Information for Certain Crimes
me:LD 1911.summary: Requires the judicial branch, starting January 1, 2028, to automatically seal records of eligible Class D and E convictions 5 years after conviction and of nonconvictions 6 months after case closure, phases in sealing of older cases, and funds added court positions.

me:LD 1917.title: An Act to Allow the Sealing of Criminal History Record Information Related to Convictions for Conduct That Is No Longer a Crime in the State
me:LD 1917.summary: Adds convictions for conduct that is no longer a crime to the convictions eligible for sealing, and clarifies which entities, including licensing boards, may receive sealed records, how they may use them, and an applicant's duty to disclose them.

me:LD 1918.title: An Act to Clarify the Criminal History Record Information Act with Respect to Criminal Charges Dismissed as the Result of a Plea Agreement
me:LD 1918.summary: Clarifies that a charge dismissed under a plea agreement is not confidential if the defendant is convicted of another charge in it, allows evidence of a deferred-disposition guilty plea, and clarifies which entities may receive sealed records. The first two take effect April 1, 2027.

me:LD 1920.title: An Act to Prohibit the Sale of Potentially Intoxicating Hemp Products to a Person Under 21 Years of Age
me:LD 1920.summary: Bars selling potentially intoxicating hemp products to anyone under 21, requires child-resistant, tamper-evident packaging for them except beverages, salves and topicals, and bars hemp product labels or packaging that violate federal trademark law or could be mistaken for a different trademarked product.

me:LD 1921.title: An Act to Create a Statewide Housing Resolution Board
me:LD 1921.summary: Replaces a proposed Housing Resolution Board with a commission to study ways to cut the cost and time of litigation over housing development projects, meeting up to 6 times in 2026 and reporting to the Legislature.

me:LD 1923.title: An Act to Update Juvenile Justice System Reporting Requirements and to Direct the Department of Corrections and the Department of Health and Human Services to Study Modifying the Long Creek Youth Development Center
me:LD 1923.summary: Requires the Departments of Corrections and Health and Human Services to convene a working group on changing the use of Long Creek Youth Development Center, and requires monthly online publication of juvenile justice data starting August 15, 2026.

me:LD 1928.title: An Act to Prohibit Lodging Establishments from Providing Single-use Plastic Containers
me:LD 1928.summary: Bars lodging establishments from providing shampoo, soap and similar products in single-use plastic containers under 6 ounces, starting 2030 for those with 50 or more units and 2032 for smaller ones; exempts stand-alone cabins, cottages or apartments (12 or fewer units, one owner).

me:LD 1930.title: An Act Regarding Acts of Violence Committed Against a Pregnant Woman
me:LD 1930.summary: As introduced, defines "person" and "human being" to include an unborn child in Criminal Code provisions on murder, manslaughter and assault, with exceptions for the mother, lawful medical procedures and lawfully prescribed medication.

me:LD 1934.title: An Act to Promote Responsible Outdoor Lighting
me:LD 1934.summary: Requires public outdoor lighting installed or replaced beginning Oct. 1, 2026 to meet standards on brightness, shielding and color temperature, with exemptions such as ski, emergency, temporary and certain roadway lighting; lets municipalities adopt ordinances.

me:LD 1937.title: An Act to Require Hospitals and Hospital-affiliated Providers to Provide Financial Assistance Programs for Medical Care
me:LD 1937.summary: Requires hospitals to provide free care to state residents with family income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, and sets rules for hospital financial assistance programs, including a 45-day eligibility decision.

me:LD 1940.title: An Act to Revise the Growth Management Program Laws
me:LD 1940.summary: Changes the state growth management program for local land use planning, adding a state goal for orderly growth that preserves rural character, and revising how towns create growth plans and how the Office of Community Affairs writes rules.

me:LD 1941.title: An Act to Implement Recommendations of the Commission to Examine Reestablishing Parole
me:LD 1941.summary: Renames the State Parole Board the Maine Parole Board, expands it from 5 to 7 members including at least one formerly incarcerated person, and makes people sentenced to Department of Corrections custody after May 1, 1976 eligible for parole.

me:LD 1942.title: An Act to Modify Taxes Applying to Adult Use Cannabis, Hemp and Hemp Products
me:LD 1942.summary: Imposes, from January 1, 2027, a 14% sales tax on potentially intoxicating hemp products and a $143-per-pound excise tax on cannabis in prerolled cigarettes that cultivators sell to other licensees, and moves cultivation facility excise tax return due dates from the 15th to month end.

me:LD 1948.title: An Act to Fund MaineCare
me:LD 1948.summary: Provides one-time funding for the MaineCare program in fiscal year 2024-25 and withdraws the one-time MaineCare funding provided in Public Law 2025, chapter 2, Part D.

me:LD 1949.title: An Act Regarding Energy Fairness
me:LD 1949.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to consider residential affordability, publish utility credit and collection data, review electric delivery rate components, and develop an energy-burden affordability metric, with reports due in 2027.

me:LD 195.title: An Act to Create the Small Business Capital Savings Account Program
me:LD 195.summary: Creates the Small Business Capital Savings Account Program, letting certified small farm, fishing and wood-harvesting businesses deduct contributions to accounts for capital expenditures from 2026 through 2029; withdrawals not used for capital expenditures are taxable.

me:LD 1951.title: An Act to Promote Food Processing and Manufacturing Facility Expansion and Create Jobs
me:LD 1951.summary: Removes the in-state headquarters requirement for the food processing facility expansion tax credit, allows 12 months after start-up to employ 40 full-time workers, raises the credit from 1.8% to 2% from 2027, and doubles the approval cap to $200 million.

me:LD 1955.title: An Act to Increase Child Care Affordability and Early Childhood Educator Stability
me:LD 1955.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to submit a long-term plan for the Child Care Affordability Program's financial sustainability by December 15, 2026, allows it to accept donations or grants, and sets ongoing program funding of $15,000,000.

me:LD 1956.title: An Act to Amend the Law Governing the Competitive Skills Scholarship Program and Establish the Community Workforce Connections Program
me:LD 1956.summary: Ends the peer workforce navigator pilot, creates the Community Workforce Connections Program starting January 1, 2026 for unemployed and underemployed people, and adds a cohort delivery model and eligibility and appeal changes to the Competitive Skills Scholarship Program.

me:LD 1957.title: An Act to Promote Film Production in Maine
me:LD 1957.summary: Repeals the certified visual media production tax credit, raises and caps reimbursements under the visual media production reimbursement program, changes the definition of qualifying expenses, and requires applicants to withhold a percentage of payments to entities hiring out one individual's services.

me:LD 1960.title: An Act to Exempt Electronic Smoking Devices or Other Tobacco Products Containing Ingestible Hemp from the Tax Imposed on Tobacco Products
me:LD 1960.summary: Exempts tobacco products that contain hemp from the state tax on tobacco products.

me:LD 1962.title: An Act to Establish the Corrections Ombudsman
me:LD 1962.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Corrections to notify the Governor and legislative leaders of a board of visitors vacancy within 5 days, and lets members of the legislative corrections committee access all areas of correctional facilities and Long Creek except during certified emergencies.

me:LD 1963.title: An Act to Protect and Compensate Public Utility Whistleblowers
me:LD 1963.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to set up a process for whistleblowers to report utility conduct and lets it award them a percentage of sanctions it imposes based on their information, with protection from retaliation.

me:LD 1966.title: An Act to Improve Access to Community Solar Programs in the State
me:LD 1966.summary: Requires utilities with over 50,000 customers to itemize administrative charges on bills, directs the Public Utilities Commission to set billing disclosure rules for shared-savings net energy billing, and to solicit bids for up to 4 megawatts of small distributed generation serving low- and moderate-income customers.

me:LD 1967.title: Resolve, to Establish the Maine Home Energy Navigator and Coaching Pilot Program
me:LD 1967.summary: Directs the Governor's Energy Office and the Office of Policy Innovation and the Future to design a pilot program of community-based energy coaching for homeowners and renters, and to report on the design by February 1, 2026.

me:LD 1968.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Regarding Legislative Reimbursement
me:LD 1968.summary: As introduced, removes set dollar amounts for legislators' meal and housing allowances and has the Legislative Council set them, capped at the federal per diem rate.

me:LD 197.title: Resolve, to Direct the Governor's Energy Office to Conduct a Study Regarding the Future of Electric Transmission Infrastructure in the State
me:LD 197.summary: Directs the Governor's Energy Office to study the State's future electric transmission infrastructure needs with a stakeholder group, hold at least three stakeholder meetings, and report by September 1, 2026.

me:LD 1971.title: An Act to Protect Workers in This State by Clarifying the Relationship of State and Local Law Enforcement Agencies with Federal Immigration Authorities
me:LD 1971.summary: As amended in committee, bars law enforcement agencies from using money or personnel to stop, detain or arrest people for immigration enforcement, including solely on a hold request; allows information sharing under federal law, some joint task force work, and immigration interviews backed by a court order.

me:LD 1974.title: An Act to Affirm Parental Rights
me:LD 1974.summary: Declares parents the joint natural guardians of their minor children with joint rights to their care, custody and control, and states that a parent's liberty to direct a child's upbringing, education and care is a fundamental right.

me:LD 1975.title: An Act to Eliminate the ConnectMaine Authority by Repealing the Advanced Technology Infrastructure Act
me:LD 1975.summary: Directs the Maine Connectivity Authority to review the laws on the ConnectMaine Authority and recommend changes to move its functions to the Maine Connectivity Authority by October 1, 2027, with a report due January 15, 2027.

me:LD 1979.title: Resolve, Directing the Department of Corrections to Convene a Working Group to Examine the Establishment of a Program to Award Earned Time Credit for Educational Achievement to Persons Who Are Incarcerated
me:LD 1979.summary: Directs the Department of Corrections to convene a working group on awarding earned time credit for educational achievement to incarcerated people and to report findings by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 1987.title: An Act to Fund Collective Bargaining Agreements with Executive Branch Employees and Continue the Voluntary Employee Incentive Program
me:LD 1987.summary: Funds the cost items in state collective bargaining agreements for executive branch employees from the General Fund and Highway Fund, and requires salary schedules to follow agreements ratified by December 31, 2025.

me:LD 1988.title: An Act to Address Funding Needs for State Employees Affected by Federal Funding Disruptions
me:LD 1988.summary: As introduced, allows the State Controller to transfer up to $2,500,000 from the General Fund operating capital reserve to cover layoff obligations for state employees affected by federal funding disruptions, with any unobligated balance returned by June 30, 2026.

me:LD 199.title: An Act to Change the Limits on Candidates' Communications with Voters at the Polls
me:LD 199.summary: Allows a candidate at a voting place to say aloud the office they seek that day and their party or designation as listed on the ballot, if not trying to influence votes.

me:LD 1993.title: An Act to Increase the Annual Cap on Funds Assessed for the Safety Education and Training Fund
me:LD 1993.summary: Raises the cap on the Safety Education and Training Fund assessment on workers' compensation benefits from 1% to 1.25%, and requires an efficiency review of the Labor Department's safety training programs.

me:LD 1995.title: An Act to Require the Maine Office of Community Affairs to Establish a Technical Assistance Materials Hub
me:LD 1995.summary: Requires the Maine Office of Community Affairs to build and maintain a technical assistance materials hub on its website, with planning, climate resilience, housing and development materials for communities.

me:LD 1999.title: An Act to Exclude Agricultural Leases from the Definition of "Subdivision" Under the Planning and Land Use Regulation Laws
me:LD 1999.summary: As amended, excludes from the definition of "subdivision" leases of land used primarily for farming or ranching that do not convey fee simple ownership or allow permanent residential dwellings; housing construction for migrant or seasonal farm workers is not excluded.

me:LD 2003.title: An Act to Improve Localization of Emergency Broadcast Messaging
me:LD 2003.summary: Provides $600,000 in one-time funds in fiscal year 2026-27 for Maine Public Broadcasting Corporation radio equipment to localize public safety information and emergency alert messages.

me:LD 2004.title: An Act to Enhance Support of Local Nutrition Incentive Programs by Modifying the Eligibility Requirements of the Fund to Address Food Insecurity and Provide Nutrition Incentives
me:LD 2004.summary: Removes the word "federal" from references to food and nutrition assistance programs in the law on the Fund To Address Food Insecurity and Provide Nutrition Incentives, covering its purpose, application priority and reporting provisions.

me:LD 2007.title: An Act Regarding the Prohibition of Online Sweepstakes Games
me:LD 2007.summary: Bans operating, promoting or supporting casino-style online sweepstakes games that use dual-currency payment, as a civil violation with $10,000 to $100,000 fines and as unlawful gambling; requires revoking the license of any gambling licensee found in violation.

me:LD 2011.title: An Act to Remove the MaineCare Program from the Prescription Drug Benefit Provisions in the Maine Insurance Code
me:LD 2011.summary: Removes the MaineCare program from the definition of "carrier" in the Insurance Code law governing health plans' prescription drug benefits.

me:LD 2017.title: An Act to Update Certain Statutes Governing School Nutrition
me:LD 2017.summary: Changes school meal laws by making the state's online free and reduced-price meal application optional, letting other eligibility agencies receive applications, and removing an alternative breakfast delivery exemption and related rulemaking requirements.

me:LD 2018.title: An Act to Amend the Requirements Governing Self-insurance Plans in the Paid Family and Medical Leave Benefits Program
me:LD 2018.summary: Bars the Department of Labor from allowing multiple employers to pool risk in self-insured paid family and medical leave plans, while letting them share legal, accounting and third-party administrator costs. Applies retroactively to April 1, 2025.

me:LD 2036.title: An Act to Clarify the Approval Process for and the Operation of the Commingling Program for the Management of Beverage Containers
me:LD 2036.summary: Conditions the October 1, 2026 deadline for the beverage container commingling program to switch from sorting by brand to by material on 90% of deposit initiators supplying sales data by June 30, 2026; applies retroactively to January 1, 2025.

me:LD 2037.title: An Act to Update the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative Allowances
me:LD 2037.summary: Sets Maine's base annual carbon dioxide emissions budget under the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative for 2027 and later years, falling from 2,065,595 tons in 2027 to 221,314 tons from 2037, and repeals carbon offset project category provisions.

me:LD 2038.title: An Act to Require Maine Transmission and Distribution Utility Participation in a Regional Transmission Organization
me:LD 2038.summary: Requires transmission and distribution utilities to participate in a regional transmission organization, excepting consumer-owned utilities and utilities in northern Maine's separately administered electricity market.

me:LD 2040.title: An Act to Survey Food Insecurity in Maine
me:LD 2040.summary: Directs the Commissioner of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to study ways to measure food insecurity and progress on the state plan to end hunger by 2030, and to publish the results online.

me:LD 2051.title: An Act to Ensure Access to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in Maine
me:LD 2051.summary: Establishes eligibility for the state Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program for people who lost federal eligibility under the 2025 federal budget law (Public Law 119-21), and clarifies current state eligibility language.

me:LD 2054.title: An Act to Clarify the Laws Regarding Moose Hunting Permits for Hunting Outfitters
me:LD 2054.summary: Makes technical corrections to the committee amendment on moose hunting lodge permits, including keeping the outfitter share of all moose permits at 2% rather than 5% and conforming references to the lodge-permit drawing.

me:LD 2056.title: An Act to Provide Additional Financing Options to Consumers in the State
me:LD 2056.summary: As amended, exempts purchases of new, never-titled automobiles from the rule that consumer credit payments be substantially equal, letting a scheduled payment exceed other payments by up to 36%.

me:LD 2057.title: An Act to Support Rehabilitation and Development of Affordable Manufactured Housing Communities
me:LD 2057.summary: Removes the requirement that Maine State Housing Authority make construction loans only if a financial institution participates, lets it make construction loans for programs under Title 30-A, chapter 201, and repeals separate bonding limits for those loans.

me:LD 2058.title: An Act to Require Municipal and County Jails to Be Available at All Times for Detention of Persons Arrested on Criminal Charges by Maine Law Enforcement Officers
me:LD 2058.summary: Keeps the requirement that municipal and county jails be available to hold people arrested by any law enforcement officer, but adds an exception for people detained solely for civil immigration violations.

me:LD 2059.title: An Act to Provide Required Funding for the Reimbursement of Assigned Counsel and to Develop the Public Defender Office for Cumberland County
me:LD 2059.summary: Provides one-time funding to the Maine Commission on Public Defense Services to cover shortfalls in paying court-assigned defense lawyers in fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27.

me:LD 206.title: An Act to Protect Maine Businesses by Eliminating the Automatic Cost-of-living Adjustment to the Minimum Hourly Wage
me:LD 206.summary: Sets the minimum hourly wage at $14.65 and removes the annual cost-of-living adjustment.

me:LD 2062.title: An Act to Enhance the Safety of Public Transit Bus Operators Through the Installation of Vehicle Security Barriers
me:LD 2062.summary: Requires urban transit providers in towns over 20,000 people to install driver security barriers on large heavy-duty buses by August 1, 2029, and creates a state fund for grants to buy and install them.

me:LD 2064.title: An Act to Expand Access to Early Childhood Nutrition by Establishing a Grant Program for Public Preschools
me:LD 2064.summary: Creates a Department of Education grant program for school units to contract with off-site public preschools to provide meals meeting child care nutrition standards, with grants capped at the federal school lunch per-student rate plus up to $10,000 for infrastructure.

me:LD 2066.title: An Act to Establish the Child Care Employment Award
me:LD 2066.summary: Creates the Child Care Employment Award, giving child care subsidies, paid directly to the provider, for children of staff at licensed child care facilities, with $3,000,000 in funding and a Department of Health and Human Services position to run it.

me:LD 2067.title: An Act to Include Certain Community Mental Health Workers Under the 1998 Special Plan for Retirement
me:LD 2067.summary: As amended, adds Department of Health and Human Services Community Response Workers who provide crisis outreach and services to adults with developmental or intellectual disabilities, employed on or after August 1, 2026, to the 1998 Special Plan of the state retirement system.

me:LD 2071.title: An Act to Expand Access to Vaccines Approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration by Allowing Pharmacists to Prescribe, Dispense and Administer Vaccines and Require Insurance Coverage
me:LD 2071.summary: Lets pharmacists give flu and COVID-19 vaccines to anyone over 6 months, and other FDA-licensed vaccines recommended by CDC advisers or pediatric, family physician or obstetric groups to adults, or to ages 3 to 17 with a prescription; lets pharmacy interns vaccinate minors.

me:LD 2077.title: An Act to Reduce the Cost of Purchasing a Home by Providing Grants to Reduce Mortgage Rates
me:LD 2077.summary: Requires the Maine State Housing Authority to run a program giving buyers whose income is within federal first-time-homebuyer limits grants of up to $15,000 per purchase to lower a mortgage rate or serve as a down payment on an owner-occupied single-family home.

me:LD 2078.title: An Act to Establish the Electricity Cost Fairness Refundable Tax Credit
me:LD 2078.summary: Exempts all sales and delivery of residential electricity from sales tax beginning July 1, 2026; current law exempts only some, such as the first 750 kilowatt hours per month.

me:LD 2079.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Municipal Reporting on Residential Buildings
me:LD 2079.summary: Changes the annual housing data that municipalities of 4,000 or more residents report to the Maine Office of Community Affairs, moving the deadline to March 31 and revising the building-type categories, and encourages smaller towns to report.

me:LD 208.title: An Act to Eliminate the 72-hour Waiting Period on Firearm Purchases
me:LD 208.summary: As amended, replaces the repeal with a resolve directing the attorney general to monitor the case Beckwith v. Frey (1st Cir.) and update the judiciary committee by January 15, 2027.

me:LD 2080.title: An Act to Protect Consumers by Prohibiting the Use of Credit Cards in Sports Wagering
me:LD 2080.summary: Bars sports wagering and internet gaming operators from accepting wagers paid for with a credit card, and requires the Gambling Control Unit's rules to ensure credit cards are not used to place wagers.

me:LD 2088.title: An Act to Increase Access to Primary Care Provided by Physician Associates
me:LD 2088.summary: Removes the requirement that a physician associate who is the principal clinical provider in a practice without a physician have a practice agreement with a physician, and makes consultations with physicians optional.

me:LD 2089.title: An Act to Amend the Law Governing Agricultural Labor Housing Standards
