me:LD 2089.summary: Makes it optional rather than required for the Bureau of Labor Standards to adopt rules on the health, safety and welfare of agricultural workers living in employer-provided housing, and removes the requirement that the rules match federal migrant and seasonal worker housing regulations.

me:LD 2094.title: An Act to Authorize a General Fund Bond Issue to Support Maine's Agricultural and Forestry Sectors
me:LD 2094.summary: Authorizes a $45,000,000 general fund bond issue to support Maine's agricultural and forestry sectors.

me:LD 2097.title: An Act to Modify the Law Governing Revocation of a Code Enforcement Officer's Certification
me:LD 2097.summary: Replaces court revocation of code enforcement officer certificates with a complaint process run by the Maine Office of Community Affairs, using a review committee, and lets its division director discipline certificate holders. Makes complaints confidential and lets certifications be extended up to 24 months.

me:LD 2098.title: An Act to Update Certain Higher Education Statutes and Laws
me:LD 2098.summary: Repeals the correspondence school statutes, requires degree-granting institutions to pay an application fee, and lets the state board recommend degree-granting authority without added review in some cases. The committee amendment also broadens College of the Atlantic's degree-granting authority.

me:LD 2099.title: An Act to Amend Certain Eligibility Requirements for Secondary Students Receiving State Subsidies for Postsecondary Courses
me:LD 2099.summary: Lowers the minimum high school grade average for state-subsidized college courses from 3.0 to 2.0 through July 2028, adjusts the school recommendation rule, and requires a report on the changes and on lifetime credit caps for early college students.

me:LD 21.title: An Act to Update the Provision of Law Concerning Student Codes of Conduct in Order to Reflect Best Practices Regarding Behavioral Threat Assessment and Response
me:LD 21.summary: Requires school boards' student codes of conduct to include policies and procedures to identify, assess and respond to students who may pose a threat of violence, reflecting best practices in behavioral threat assessment.

me:LD 2100.title: An Act to Update the Laws Regarding Fuel Gas Detector Requirements
me:LD 2100.summary: As amended, limits the multifamily fuel gas detector requirement to buildings of 3 or more units, moves business, mercantile and assembly occupancies from 2026 to 2027, and adds day care, educational, health care and correctional occupancies from 2028.

me:LD 2102.title: An Act to Clarify and Strengthen the Government Shutdown Loan Guarantee Program
me:LD 2102.summary: Changes the Government Shutdown Loan Guarantee Program to allow lenders an origination fee of up to the lesser of $60 or 1%, raise the claim-stop threshold from 10% to 50% of loans, and require notice once payouts reach $200,000.

me:LD 2104.title: An Act to Clarify Contractual Rights of Personal Sports Mobile Dealers
me:LD 2104.summary: Requires personal sports mobile manufacturers to allocate new vehicles to dealers fairly by model, bars requiring substantial dealership renovations without written supply assurances, clarifies what counts as coercion of dealers, and replaces the warranty reimbursement rules.

me:LD 2106.title: An Act to Prohibit the Disclosure of Nonpublic Records Without Proper Judicial Review
me:LD 2106.summary: Bars public schools, state postsecondary institutions, state institutions and state libraries from voluntarily letting law enforcement enter nonpublic areas or access protected records for immigration enforcement; requires them to adopt Attorney General model policies, which the Attorney General publishes within 60 days.

me:LD 2107.title: An Act to Establish the Maine Nonprofit Security Grant Program
me:LD 2107.summary: Establishes the Maine Nonprofit Security Grant Program in the Maine Emergency Management Agency, funding security improvements at nonprofit-owned or occupied property against hate crimes and terror attacks, with $1,500,000 appropriated for fiscal year 2026-27.

me:LD 2109.title: An Act to Define "Public Education" and Clarify That a Private School Receiving Approval for Public Tuition Must Be Located in the State
me:LD 2109.summary: Defines "public education" and requires private schools approved for public tuition to be located in Maine, while letting out-of-state schools keep tuition for students already enrolled until they finish secondary school.

me:LD 2114.title: An Act Regarding Public Preschool Programs Serving Children Who Are 3 Years of Age
me:LD 2114.summary: Expands public preschool programs to include 3-year-olds, allows state start-up funding for programs serving 3-year-olds with identified disabilities, and lets 3-year-olds without disabilities enroll where offered, without counting them for state subsidy.

me:LD 2115.title: An Act to Protect Private Wells from Hazardous Substances
me:LD 2115.summary: Creates a Well Contamination Response Fund at the Department of Environmental Protection with $1,000,000 a year in General Fund money starting in 2026-27 for PFAS contamination work, including in private wells.

me:LD 2116.title: An Act to Make Permanent the Affordable Housing Income Tax Credit
me:LD 2116.summary: Extends the sunset date of the affordable housing income tax credit to December 31, 2036.

me:LD 2121.title: An Act to Enhance the Safety of Judicial and Elected Officials, Constitutional Officers and the State Auditor by Allowing Certain Personal Information to Be Removed from Designated Public Records
me:LD 2121.summary: Directs the Secretary of State to convene a working group on safety of judges and elected officials and run a 2-year pilot giving participating judges and legislators a service that removes their personal information from public websites.

me:LD 2122.title: An Act to Prevent Negative Impacts from Federal Funding Changes to and Fund Eligibility Determinations and Outreach for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program
me:LD 2122.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to run a system to reduce SNAP eligibility errors, give community groups at least $750,000 a year for SNAP outreach, employ a state outreach coordinator, and keep a contingency fund for SNAP benefits.

me:LD 2125.title: An Act to Sustain Access to Children's Residential Care Services
me:LD 2125.summary: Provides $1,000,000 for an emergency sustainability fund for children's residential treatment providers at risk of closing a facility or beds.

me:LD 2127.title: An Act to Increase the Cap on Bonds Issued by the Maine State Housing Authority to Reflect Current Housing Production Needs in the State
me:LD 2127.summary: Raises from $3 billion to $4 billion the cap on outstanding principal of certain Maine State Housing Authority mortgage purchase bonds.

me:LD 213.title: An Act to Increase the Sales Commission of Retailers Selling Lottery Tickets
me:LD 213.summary: As introduced, requires lottery rules to give licensed retailers a sales commission of at least 10% on each instant game ticket and each draw or terminal-generated game ticket sold.

me:LD 2132.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Emergency Medical Services Act of 1982 to Require Compliance with the Statewide Trauma-incidence Registry and Make Certain Technical and Other Changes
me:LD 2132.summary: Requires emergency medical services educators and training centers to be licensed, adds civil fines for unlicensed practice, limits the existing criminal penalty to intentional, knowing or reckless violations, and has the state trauma advisory committee evaluate trauma care, reporting by September 1, 2027.

me:LD 2136.title: An Act to Support Victims of Trafficking in Maine in Response to Federal Funding Cuts
me:LD 2136.summary: Provides $317,000 in one-time General Fund money for the Department of Health and Human Services to support the Preble Street anti-trafficking program, replacing delayed federal funding.

me:LD 2140.title: An Act to Reduce Household Energy Costs in Response to Federal Cuts
me:LD 2140.summary: Requires the Efficiency Maine Trust to set up a demand response program encouraging electricity customers to cut use during peak periods, with outreach to renters and low-income customers, and to report on its cost-effectiveness by February 28, 2028.

me:LD 2143.title: An Act Facilitating the Reconstruction or Replacement of Storm-damaged Commercial Fisheries Facilities and Infrastructure
me:LD 2143.summary: Lets owners seeking a local variance to repair or replace a substantially damaged dock, pier or wharf for a functionally dependent use skip the requirement to show their land cannot otherwise yield a reasonable return.

me:LD 2145.title: An Act to Decrease Offsets to Disability Retirement Benefits
me:LD 2145.summary: Raises the cap on combined disability retirement and workers' compensation benefits for state employees and teachers, and removes the Social Security offset for certain local-district disability retirees whose applications predate October 1, 1989.

me:LD 2146.title: An Act to Increase Access to Critical Vaccinations
me:LD 2146.summary: Requires the Maine Vaccine Board to consider vaccines recommended by pediatric, family physician and obstetric groups for its Universal Immunization Program, lets it request state funding for children's vaccines, and shields pharmacists from negligence liability for vaccines given per state or those groups' guidelines.

me:LD 2147.title: An Act to Provide Funding to Improve the College and Career Readiness of Certain Students in Androscoggin and Oxford Counties
me:LD 2147.summary: Provides one-time funds for the University of Maine System to offer academic support and college and career preparation to eligible students at six high schools formerly served by River Valley Upward Bound, with a report due December 1, 2027.

me:LD 2148.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Health Insurance Premium Cap for State Employees
me:LD 2148.summary: Limits increases in total premiums for active and retired state employee health insurance, for fiscal years ending after June 30, 2026, to the Consumer Price Index percentage increase plus 10%, excluding the fully insured Medicare Advantage prescription drug plan.

me:LD 2149.title: An Act to Protect Affordability in Mobile Home Parks and Manufactured Housing Communities
me:LD 2149.summary: Raises from $50 million to $75 million the net worth exemption from the transfer assessment fee on sales of manufactured housing communities and mobile home parks, and exempts purchases from family members or family trusts.

me:LD 215.title: An Act to Establish a Program to Assist Residents of Large Recovery Residences
me:LD 215.summary: Requires municipalities to cap housing assistance for residents of recovery residences with 26 or more beds at 70% of the cap for smaller ones, with the state reimbursing 100%, and directs DHHS to convene a stakeholder group and report by February 1, 2026.

me:LD 2150.title: An Act to Establish Procedures for Restricting Access to State Property, Access to State Services and Communication with or Through State Entities
me:LD 2150.summary: As amended, requires a state entity restricting a person’s access to state property or services, or communication with it, to give written notice stating the factual basis and how to challenge it; directs State Police to report on notices by January 15, 2028.

me:LD 2151.title: An Act to Improve Access to Affordable Prescription Drugs in Underserved Areas
me:LD 2151.summary: Directs the health department to grant $3,563,763 by December 15, 2026 to nine federally qualified health centers to expand retail or mobile pharmacies in rural and underserved areas; the Maine Primary Care Association reports on use by February 15, 2027.

me:LD 2155.title: An Act to Clarify Certain Laws Governing Licenses for the Sale of Liquor by Manufacturers
me:LD 2155.summary: Bars the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations from suspending, revoking or not renewing manufacturing facility licenses issued before May 23, 2025 solely because owners hold more on-premises retail licenses than allowed, replacing a temporary 24-month pause; bars selling or transferring them.

me:LD 2156.title: An Act to Provide for the 2026 and 2027 Allocations of the State Ceiling on Private Activity Bonds
me:LD 2156.summary: Allocates the state ceiling on tax-exempt private activity bonds for calendar years 2026 and 2027 among the state-level issuers of tax-exempt bonds.

me:LD 2157.title: An Act to Prohibit the Unauthorized Use of Drones on or over the Premises of Correctional Facilities and Jails
me:LD 2157.summary: Makes intentionally or knowingly flying a drone over a correctional facility or jail without authorization a civil violation with a fine of at least $500, and a Class D crime for repeat violations.

me:LD 2159.title: An Act to Require School Buses to Be Equipped with and to Use School Bus Crossing Arms
me:LD 2159.summary: Requires all school buses to have technology preventing the door from closing on people, with operators keeping it in working order; a violation is a traffic infraction. Added to a committee amendment requiring use of school bus crossing arms.

me:LD 2162.title: An Act to Regulate and Prevent Children's Access to Artificial Intelligence Chatbots with Human-like Features and Social Artificial Intelligence Companions
me:LD 2162.summary: Bars AI chatbot operators from making chatbots with human-like features available to minors starting February 15, 2027, requires systems to detect and respond to minors' stated intent to harm themselves or others, and allows enforcement by the Attorney General and private lawsuits.

me:LD 2164.title: An Act to Assist Communities with Converting Vacant School Buildings into Housing
me:LD 2164.summary: Creates a Vacant School Housing Conversion Program within the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority to assist municipalities in converting vacant school buildings into housing, plus a Maine School Conversion Fund with a $5 million appropriation for 2026-27.

me:LD 2165.title: An Act to Change Supervisory Authority over the Capitol Police
me:LD 2165.summary: Removes the State Police Lieutenant position that supervises the Bureau of Capitol Police and lets the Commissioner of Public Safety decide whether the Capitol Police chief or the State Police chief supervises the bureau.

me:LD 2172.title: Resolve, Regarding Legislative Review of Portions of Chapter 33: Rule Governing Physical Restraint and Seclusion, a Major Substantive Rule of the Department of Education, State Board of Education
me:LD 2172.summary: Authorizes final adoption of portions of the Department of Education's Chapter 33 rule on physical restraint and seclusion in schools, a provisionally adopted major substantive rule.

me:LD 2173.title: An Act to Update the Laws Regarding Housing Developments and Accessory Dwelling Units
me:LD 2173.summary: As amended, changes housing and land use laws: accessory dwelling unit sprinkler rules, rate-of-growth ordinance limits in designated growth areas, a 55-foot cap on affordable housing height allowances, and lot size and density limits; delays application to July 1, 2027.

me:LD 2175.title: Resolve, Regarding Legislative Review of Portions of Chapter 115: The Credentialing of Education Personnel, a Major Substantive Rule of the Department of Education, State Board of Education
me:LD 2175.summary: Allows the Department of Education's educator credentialing rule to be adopted only if it establishes a Mathematics Specialist Certificate, grade-level specifications for teachers of children with disabilities, and extends grade 7-12 certificates to grades 6-12.

me:LD 2176.title: An Act to Create a Right to Judicial Review Under the Maine Civil Rights Act for Persons Erroneously Detained
me:LD 2176.summary: Adds disclosure of private information to the definition of harassment, raises from $100 to $250 the penalty for a landlord entering a tenant's home without reasonable notice, and bars landlords from disclosing tenants' personal information without consent, with a $1,000 penalty.

me:LD 218.title: An Act to Make Student Transfer Agreements Renew Automatically Except in Certain Circumstances
me:LD 218.summary: As introduced, ends the annual superintendent review of student transfers between school units and renews transfers automatically each year unless attendance is irregular, the student is disruptive or does not use best efforts in class, or the transfer is no longer in the student's best interest.

me:LD 2189.title: An Act to Require Prior Notification of Closures of Labor and Delivery Units and Changes in Maternity or Newborn Care Services by Hospitals as Recommended by the Commission to Evaluate the Scope of Regulatory Review and Oversight over Health Care Transactions That Impact the Delivery of Health Care Services in the State
me:LD 2189.summary: Requires hospitals to notify the state Department of Health and Human Services at least 120 days before ending maternity or newborn care services or changing their level of care, with contact, emergency-plan and notification details.

me:LD 219.title: An Act to Limit Hypodermic Apparatus Exchange Programs to a One-for-one Exchange
me:LD 219.summary: Limits certified hypodermic apparatus exchange programs to exchanging one apparatus per participant for each one that participant returns.

me:LD 220.title: An Act to Establish the Hope and Inclusion Scholarship Program in Order to Provide Funding for Students Attending Certain Private Schools and Students Receiving Home Instruction
me:LD 220.summary: Creates the Hope and Inclusion Scholarship Program, in which parents of qualified private school and home-instruction students receive accounts funded by shifting 90% of the state and local essential programs and services funding for each student.

me:LD 2200.title: An Act to Prohibit Noncompete Clauses for Health Care Professionals as Recommended by the Commission to Evaluate the Scope of Regulatory Review and Oversight over Health Care Transactions That Impact the Delivery of Health Care Services in the State
me:LD 2200.summary: Requires enforceable noncompete agreements between employers and health care practitioners to recognize an individual's right to choose their own practitioner, and extends a current-law provision on physician noncompetes to all health care practitioners.

me:LD 2203.title: An Act to Limit Rates Charged to Low-income Electricity Consumers
me:LD 2203.summary: Bars competitive electricity providers from charging low-income-assistance customers a generation rate above the standard-offer rate that would otherwise apply, and lets the Public Utilities Commission adopt implementing rules.

me:LD 2207.title: An Act Regarding the Statute of Limitations for Certain Sexual Offenses Committed Against Minors
me:LD 2207.summary: Eliminates the statute of limitations for prosecuting aggravated sex trafficking and commercial sexual exploitation of a minor when the victim was under 18, for conduct on or after September 1, 2026 or not yet time-barred.

me:LD 2208.title: An Act to Offset Federal Cuts to Health Insurance for Certain Maine Families and Seniors
me:LD 2208.summary: Creates a $50 million Rural Health Stabilization Fund (hospitals accepting money must limit price growth and charges to 200% of Medicare), a $17.3 million premium subsidy fund and a $105 million MaineCare Federal Response Fund, and provides $40 million for the reinsurance association.

me:LD 2209.title: Resolve, to Direct the Department of Health and Human Services to Develop Innovative Models for the Delivery of Dental Services to Expand Access to Oral Health Care Throughout the State
me:LD 2209.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to consider a hub-and-spoke model for dental services, and to explore dental specialist residencies and expanded dental therapist training in Maine.

me:LD 2211.title: An Act Implementing the Recommendations of the Automotive Right to Repair Working Group
me:LD 2211.summary: Replaces the automotive right-to-repair independent entity with a Motor Vehicle Right to Repair Commission, sets a September 1, 2027 deadline for owner-authorization access platforms, and lets the Attorney General seek injunctions and civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation.

me:LD 2212.title: An Act Making Supplemental Appropriations and Allocations from the General Fund and Other Funds for the Expenditures of State Government and Changing Certain Provisions of the Law Necessary to the Proper Operations of State Government for the Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2027
me:LD 2212.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for state government for fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27, sets the K-12 education cost and state share, updates state tax conformity to the federal code, and creates an Affordability Payment Program of $300 payments to eligible recipients.

me:LD 2216.title: An Act to Establish the Maine Blue Economy Center
me:LD 2216.summary: Establishes the Maine Blue Economy Center within the Maine Technology Institute, requires an interim report within 60 days after its board is appointed, and provides $500,000 for start-up costs.

me:LD 2217.title: An Act Related to the Electronic Tagging of Deer
me:LD 2217.summary: Phases in electronic deer registration from 2027 to 2030, removes seal fees for registering bear, deer, moose and turkey, raises some hunting license fees by $2 (residents) or $4 (nonresidents), and suspends for a year the licenses of hunters who fail to register a deer.

me:LD 222.title: An Act to Establish a Take-back and Disposal Program for Firefighting and Fire-suppressing Foam to Which Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances Have Been Added
me:LD 222.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection to design and, by July 1, 2027, run a take-back and disposal program for PFAS-containing firefighting foam, collecting it from people who voluntarily request it.

me:LD 2220.title: An Act to Establish the Maine Home Energy Navigator and Coaching Resource Hub
me:LD 2220.summary: Establishes the Maine Home Energy Navigator and Coaching Resource Hub in the Department of Energy Resources to provide training materials for community energy coaching programs, with a one-time $100,000 appropriation in fiscal year 2026-27.

me:LD 2222.title: An Act to Establish Municipal Cost Components for Unorganized Territory Services to Be Rendered in Fiscal Year 2026-27
me:LD 2222.summary: Sets the state and county service costs charged as the property tax for Maine's unorganized territory in fiscal year 2026-27, and provides a one-time prepayment to Washington County's unorganized territories, to be recovered by June 30, 2027.

me:LD 2224.title: An Act to Reduce Certain Costs Associated with Residential Construction
me:LD 2224.summary: Directs the State Fire Marshal to update fire alarm standards to the 2025 NFPA 72 edition and study residential sprinkler and limited-use elevator costs, and directs the building codes board to begin rulemaking removing elevator smoke-partition and 2-way video communication requirements.

me:LD 2225.title: An Act to Support Municipal Enforcement of Residential Construction Laws, Codes and Regulations
me:LD 2225.summary: Adds an off-site construction standard to the Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code, adds industrialized housing to code enforcement officer training, and directs the Maine Office of Community Affairs to run a 3-year pilot supporting regional code enforcement by municipalities.

me:LD 2226.title: An Act to Amend the Essential Programs and Services School Funding Formula
me:LD 2226.summary: Changes the school funding formula’s regional adjustment to a nationwide cost-of-living index from 2027-28, adjusts local ability to pay by 10% for relative income, bars cutting the subsidy tied to those changes until 2030-31, and orders a formula study due January 15, 2027.

me:LD 2229.title: An Act Regarding Municipal Inspection of the Electrical and Plumbing Components of a Manufactured Home
me:LD 2229.summary: As introduced, allows electrical and plumbing installations made during manufactured housing construction without a state license if supervised or inspected by a master electrician or plumber, and ends duplicate municipal inspections of that work.

me:LD 2230.title: An Act to Invest in the Construction of Industrialized Housing
me:LD 2230.summary: Creates an Industrialized Housing Incentive Program giving grants to industrialized housing manufacturers, changes the Housing Opportunity Program's information duties, and has the economic development department design a construction extension partnership program.

me:LD 2231.title: An Act to Support Owners of Manufactured Housing, Mobile Homes and Tiny Homes
me:LD 2231.summary: Bars manufactured housing community owners from raising lot rent more than once a year, treats demanding nondisclosure agreements in mediation as bad faith, changes minimum lot sizes for new or expanded communities, and allows title cancellation for homes permanently affixed to real property.

me:LD 2232.title: An Act to Increase County Jail Funding
me:LD 2232.summary: Requires an annual $30 million appropriation to the County Jail Operations Fund, adjusted yearly by the Consumer Price Index, and lowers the share county jails must spend on community corrections and pretrial release programs from 25% to 20%.

me:LD 2240.title: Resolve, Regarding Legislative Review of Chapter 10: Significant Wildlife Habitat, a Late-filed Major Substantive Rule of the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
me:LD 2240.summary: Authorizes the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to finally adopt Chapter 10: Significant Wildlife Habitat, a major substantive rule submitted outside the legislative rule acceptance period.

me:LD 2242.title: Resolve, Regarding Legislative Review of Portions of Chapter 6: Standards Relating to Prescriptive Authorities and Collaborative Relationship for Naturopathic Doctors, a Late-filed Major Substantive Rule of the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation
me:LD 2242.summary: Authorizes the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation to finally adopt portions of its rule on prescriptive authority and collaborative practice for naturopathic doctors, which was submitted outside the legislative rule acceptance period.

me:LD 226.title: An Act to Protect the Cultural Resources and Historical Heritage of Sears Island in Searsport by Extending Conservation Easement Protections
me:LD 226.summary: Directs the Department of Transportation, with the Maine Coast Heritage Trust, to extend the conservation easement to all Sears Island lands not already under a permanent buffer easement.

me:LD 229.title: An Act to Bring Fairness in Income Taxes to Maine Families by Adjusting the Tax Brackets and Tax Rates
me:LD 229.summary: Changes Maine income tax brackets beginning in 2026, adding higher brackets with top rates of 7.75% and 8.95%, and adjusts the indexing dates.

me:LD 233.title: An Act to Prohibit Biological Males from Participating in School Athletic Programs and Activities Designated for Females When State Funding Is Provided to the School
me:LD 233.summary: As introduced, bars state-funded schools and colleges from letting a person whose sex assigned at birth is male take part in athletic programs designated for females.

me:LD 234.title: An Act to Eliminate Ranked-choice Voting
me:LD 234.summary: Repeals ranked-choice voting in primaries for President, U.S. Senate, U.S. House, Governor and the Legislature, in general and special elections for Congress, and in presidential elector elections.

me:LD 241.title: An Act to Authorize the Public Utilities Commission to Approve Rate Adjustments for Low-income Water Utility Ratepayers
me:LD 241.summary: Allows the Public Utilities Commission to approve a water utility's low-income discount or credit program for residential ratepayers if cost-effective, and bars the commission from requiring a utility to start such a program.

me:LD 244.title: An Act to Provide Safe, Short-term Housing to Indigent Individuals Recently Released from Correctional Facilities
me:LD 244.summary: As amended, directs the Department of Corrections to contract with a community organization for a transitional housing pilot and run a second one in southern Maine for adults recently released, with one-time funding and reports due January 1, 2026 and 2027.

me:LD 246.title: An Act to Establish the Option of Sentencing Alternatives for Primary Caregivers
me:LD 246.summary: Requires a court sentencing a defendant convicted of an offense to consider a sentencing alternative other than imprisonment because the defendant is the primary caregiver of a minor, dependent person or incapacitated adult.

me:LD 252.title: An Act to Withdraw from the National Popular Vote Compact
me:LD 252.summary: Repeals the National Popular Vote for President Act and updates other election laws to match.

me:LD 253.title: An Act to Prevent the MaineCare Program from Covering Abortion Services
me:LD 253.summary: Repeals the law requiring the Department of Health and Human Services to cover abortion services for MaineCare members and to pay with state funds for services Medicaid does not cover.

me:LD 255.title: An Act to Support Mobile Home Residents in Purchasing Their Mobile Home Parks
me:LD 255.summary: Provides $3,000,000 in one-time funding for the manufactured and mobile home park preservation and assistance program.

me:LD 259.title: An Act to Establish the Criminal Records Review Commission in Statute
me:LD 259.summary: Creates the Criminal Records Review Commission, with legislators, state commissioners and organization representatives, to review laws and procedures on criminal history record information and make recommendations; legislator members receive a per diem and expenses.

me:LD 260.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Establish That All Maine Residents Have Equal Rights Under the Law
me:LD 260.summary: Proposes amending the Maine Constitution to bar the State and its subdivisions from denying equal rights based on actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, ancestry or national origin.

me:LD 264.title: An Act to Remove the 12-month Waiting Period for the Maine Resident Homestead Property Tax Exemption
me:LD 264.summary: Removes the requirement of 12 months' prior ownership of a homestead (or shareholding in a housing cooperative) to qualify for the Maine resident homestead property tax exemption; the amendment adds an appropriation to reimburse municipalities.

me:LD 265.title: An Act to Prohibit the Maine National Guard from Combat Deployment Absent an Act of the United States Congress
me:LD 265.summary: Prohibits sending Maine's state military forces into foreign combat without a congressional declaration of war or action for an enumerated constitutional purpose, while allowing the Governor to deploy them for civil missions in the U.S.

me:LD 266.title: An Act to Require the Updating of Voter Registration Signatures
me:LD 266.summary: Makes a voter's signature valid for 5 years from its last update beginning January 1, 2026, and requires municipal registrars to notify voters whose signatures expire and give them an update form.

me:LD 270.title: Resolve, Regarding Legislative Review of Portions of Chapter 850: Health Plan Accountability, a Major Substantive Rule of the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation, Bureau of Insurance
me:LD 270.summary: Authorizes final adoption of portions of the Bureau of Insurance's Chapter 850 health plan rule only if two changes are made: written appeal and grievance decisions must attest to reviewers' credentials and independence and name a contact person, instead of naming reviewers.

me:LD 271.title: Resolve, Regarding Legislative Review of Chapter 12: Fees for Kickboxing Contests and Authorized Participants, a Major Substantive Rule of the Combat Sports Authority of Maine
me:LD 271.summary: Authorizes final adoption of Chapter 12, the Combat Sports Authority's major substantive rule setting fees for kickboxing contests and authorized participants. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.

me:LD 274.title: An Act Making Unified Allocations from the Highway Fund and Other Funds for the Expenditures of State Government and Changing Certain Provisions of the Law Necessary to the Proper Operations of State Government for the Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2025, June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2027
me:LD 274.summary: Sets Highway Fund and other transportation spending for 2025-26 and 2026-27 and raises the authorized TransCap revenue bond from $200 million to $250 million.

me:LD 277.title: An Act to Repeal the Law Prohibiting Places of Business from Being Open to the Public on Sunday
me:LD 277.summary: Limits to between 7 a.m. and noon the hours that grocery stores with no more than 10,000 square feet of customer selling space may open on Thanksgiving Day, under a committee amendment authorizing those stores to open that day.

me:LD 278.title: An Act to Eliminate the Tobacco Products Tax on Certain Products That Contain Nicotine
me:LD 278.summary: As introduced, removes from the tobacco products tax definition products that contain nicotine but no tobacco, while leaving specifically listed items such as electronic smoking devices taxable.

me:LD 281.title: An Act to Provide Support for Certain Maine Discovery Museum Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics Educational Programming Throughout the State
me:LD 281.summary: Provides ongoing funds to the Maine Discovery Museum for the Maine Science Festival, the Maine Invention Convention and the Science Around ME program.

me:LD 287.title: An Act to Require and Encourage Safe and Interconnected Transportation Construction Projects
me:LD 287.summary: Authorizes the Department of Transportation to prioritize funding for projects that support walkable, mixed-use, infill and affordable housing goals, and requires reports on funded projects to the legislature in January 2027 and 2028.

me:LD 29.title: Resolve, to Require the Department of Transportation to Implement the Recommendations of the Lower Road Rail Use Advisory Council
me:LD 29.summary: Directs the Department of Transportation, subject to funding, permits and municipal agreements, to remove inactive state-owned rail track on the Lower Road and the Calais Branch and replace it with interim trails.

me:LD 291.title: An Act to Eliminate the Lodging Tax on Campground Sites and Revert to Using the Current Sales Tax
me:LD 291.summary: Excludes campground site rentals from the 9% lodging tax starting Jan. 1, 2026, making them subject to the general sales tax rate, currently 5.5%.

me:LD 297.title: An Act Regarding the Management of Oversized Bulky Waste from Wastewater Treatment Plants
me:LD 297.summary: Replaces the bill with changes to construction and demolition debris recycling deadlines for certain solid waste facilities and to rules on oversized bulky waste residue disposed in state-owned landfills.

me:LD 299.title: An Act to Support Investment in Agriculture
me:LD 299.summary: Authorizes a $45 million bond, subject to voter approval, for agricultural and forestry funds, adds livestock stress and hay losses to Farmers Drought Resilience Program grants, and adds two members to the agriculture investment advisory board.

me:LD 30.title: Resolve, Directing the Department of Transportation to Implement the Recommendations of the Portland to Auburn Rail Use Advisory Council Regarding the Rail Line from Portland to Yarmouth
me:LD 30.summary: Directs the Department of Transportation, subject to funding, permits and municipal agreements, to remove inactive state-owned railroad track on the Berlin Subdivision between Portland and Auburn and replace it with an interim bicycle and pedestrian trail.

me:LD 301.title: An Act to Allow the Public Utilities Commission to Establish Performance-based Metrics and Rate-adjustment Mechanisms for a Public Utility in Any Proceeding
me:LD 301.summary: Allows the Public Utilities Commission to establish or authorize rate-adjustment mechanisms or quantitative metrics for a utility's operations and activities in a proceeding for a general rate increase.

me:LD 303.title: An Act to Repeal the Law Prohibiting Unauthorized Paramilitary Training
me:LD 303.summary: Repeals the law prohibiting unauthorized paramilitary training.

me:LD 307.title: An Act Regarding Energy, Utilities and Technology
me:LD 307.summary: Requires the Department of Energy Resources to convene a Maine Data Center Coordination Council to report by February 1, 2027, and bars permits for data centers of 20 megawatts or more before November 1, 2027.

me:LD 309.title: An Act to Allow a Political Party to Determine How That Party's Nominee Is Selected in a Primary Election
me:LD 309.summary: Allows a political party to decide at its state convention whether its primary uses ranked-choice voting or an alternate method set in party rules, with notice to the Secretary of State by October 1 of the prior year.

me:LD 32.title: An Act to Repeal the Laws Regarding Net Energy Billing
me:LD 32.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to designate, rather than appoint, an interconnection ombudsman and clarifies which activities the commission's interconnection ombudsman fund may pay for.

me:LD 324.title: An Act to Increase Reading Proficiency in Public Schools
me:LD 324.summary: Appropriates funds to the Department of Education to continue the early literacy grant program and math instruction grants, and lets the department partner with a national foundation to use private resources.

me:LD 328.title: An Act Requiring the State to Pay a Retired State Employee's or Retired Teacher's Premium for Medicare Part B Under Medicare Advantage
me:LD 328.summary: As amended, requires the State to pay 100% of the Medicare Part B premium under the Medicare Advantage plan for retired state employees and teachers not eligible for Medicaid, beginning January 1, 2026, and appropriates funds for it.

me:LD 331.title: Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely Reimbursement Under MaineCare Regarding Hospital Cost Reports
me:LD 331.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to change MaineCare hospital rules to reimburse at least 75% of a hospital's as-filed cost report settlement within 90 days of receipt, using existing resources.

me:LD 332.title: An Act to Establish Mandatory Minimum Sentences for Gross Sexual Assaults Against Children and Aggravated Sex Trafficking of Children
me:LD 332.summary: As introduced, requires a prison term of at least 25 years, none suspended, for gross sexual assault of a child under 12 and for aggravated sex trafficking of a child under 12, and life imprisonment for repeat gross sexual assault of a child under 12.

me:LD 335.title: An Act to Safeguard Reproductive Rights
me:LD 335.summary: As later amended in committee, creates a fund to give one provider a grant to manage statewide family planning services, requires state grants to Title X grantees whose federal funding is reduced or withdrawn, and requires state-funded MaineCare payment for providers barred from federal Medicaid payment.

me:LD 338.title: An Act to Increase the Size and Balance of Jury Pools
me:LD 338.summary: Adds registered voters and recipients of state unemployment compensation to the source lists for selecting jurors in each county, starting January 1, 2028. The committee version also added public assistance recipients; a later amendment removed them.

me:LD 339.title: Resolve, to Provide Funds to the Maine Indian Education School District to Develop a Wabanaki-centered Curriculum
me:LD 339.summary: As introduced, provides $100,000 per year to the Maine Indian Education school district to develop and pilot a Wabanaki-centered curriculum for Native American high school students and share it with state-approved schools.

me:LD 34.title: An Act to Increase the Minimum Salary for Teachers
me:LD 34.summary: Sets minimum teacher salaries of $45,000 in 2026-27, $47,500 in 2027-28 and $50,000 in 2028-29, including in the unorganized territory, with added state aid for qualifying school units and the funding-adjustment repeal date moved to July 1, 2030.

me:LD 340.title: An Act Regarding Speedy Trials
me:LD 340.summary: Creates the Maine Speedy Trial Act, setting time limits to start a criminal trial by filing date and crime class, and for a new trial after a mistrial. Defendants may waive the right after being advised by the court.

me:LD 342.title: An Act to Include Nuclear Power in the State's Renewable Portfolio Standard
me:LD 342.summary: Counts electricity from a nuclear power plant built after January 1, 2025 as a renewable resource and renewable capacity resource, making it a Class I resource under the portfolio requirements for competitive electricity providers.

me:LD 343.title: An Act to Direct the Public Utilities Commission to Seek Informational Bids Regarding Small Modular Nuclear Reactors in the State
me:LD 343.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to request informational bids on establishing a small modular nuclear reactor in Maine by October 1, 2026, and every 3 years after, and to report triennially starting January 15, 2027.

me:LD 364.title: An Act to Promote Economic Development in Maine
me:LD 364.summary: Directs the Maine Office of Community Affairs to develop legislation moving manufactured housing regulation from the Manufactured Housing Board to the office, and to seek federal approval as the state administrative agency, with legislation and a report due by January 1, 2027.

me:LD 365.title: An Act to Respond to the Housing Affordability and Accessibility Crisis in Maine
me:LD 365.summary: Replaces a concept draft with a moratorium on sales of mobile home parks with more than 25 lots until 91 days after the First Special Session adjourns; it does not apply if residents have not said they support buying, or for sales between family members.

me:LD 371.title: An Act to Expand Hydroelectric Development by Removing the 100-megawatt Cap
me:LD 371.summary: Removes the 100-megawatt cap for in-state hydroelectric generators in the definitions of renewable capacity resource and renewable resource, and requires hydropower project permit applicants to hold a public meeting and summarize public input.

me:LD 372.title: An Act to Protect Maine People from Inflation by Exempting Gold and Silver Coins and Bullion from the State Sales and Use Tax
me:LD 372.summary: Exempts sales of gold and silver coins and bullion from Maine's sales and use tax; a committee amendment limits this to coins, bars or rounds valued primarily by their weight, purity and content.

me:LD 373.title: An Act to Establish "Welcome Home" as the Official State Anthem
me:LD 373.summary: Designates "Welcome Home," as written, recorded and performed by Gordon Thomas Ward, as Maine's official state anthem.

me:LD 38.title: An Act Requiring Photographic Identification for Voting
me:LD 38.summary: As introduced, requires photo identification to vote in person (Maine driver's license or ID card, passport, military ID, or photo concealed-handgun permit; college IDs excluded) and offers a free voter photo ID card from the Secretary of State.

me:LD 380.title: An Act to Amend Certain Laws Regarding Gender-affirming Health Care Services
me:LD 380.summary: As introduced, repeals the 2023 law (Public Law 2023, chapter 648) covering people who seek, provide or assist with gender-affirming and reproductive health care, and restores the law in effect before it.

me:LD 384.title: An Act to Prevent Student Homelessness
me:LD 384.summary: Creates a Student Homelessness Prevention Program within the Department of Education to give direct financial assistance to families to help students keep stable permanent housing.

me:LD 385.title: An Act to Protect Communications by Alleged Victims Regarding Sexual Assault, Sexual Harassment, Sexual Misconduct, Cyberbullying or Discrimination from Litigation
me:LD 385.summary: Adds, to communications protected from lawsuits under the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act, those made without malice by a person with a reasonable basis to file a complaint about sexual assault, sexual harassment, sexual misconduct, cyberbullying or discrimination the person experienced.

me:LD 389.title: Resolve, to Increase Transparency and Evaluate Emergency Response Through a COVID-19 Review Commission
me:LD 389.summary: Establishes a COVID-19 Review Commission to review the state's COVID-19 response, including executive orders, related contracts, health data, and agency policies and rules, and to report its findings.

me:LD 395.title: An Act to Restore Access to Federal Laws Beneficial to the Wabanaki Nations
me:LD 395.summary: Establishes a working group to recommend how to extend federal laws that benefit Indian tribes to the Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians, Mi'kmaq Nation, Passamaquoddy Tribe and Penobscot Nation, reporting to the judiciary committee by December 2, 2026.

me:LD 396.title: An Act to Provide for a Later Starting Time for High Schools
me:LD 396.summary: As amended, directs the Department of Education to create a School Start Time Fund and grant program for school units to plan staggered start times that let secondary schools start later than elementary schools.

me:LD 402.title: An Act to Move the Natural Areas Program from the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife and to Amend the Law Governing Administration of the Bureau of Resource Management Within the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
me:LD 402.summary: Moves the Natural Areas Program from the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, creates a Natural Areas Conservation Fund, and requires a report on the transfer by January 15, 2027.

me:LD 405.title: An Act to Define "Solitary Confinement" for the Laws Governing Jails and Correctional Facilities
me:LD 405.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Corrections to report to the Legislature's criminal justice committee each instance of a prisoner kept in their cell at least 22 hours in 24, with the number of prisoners, duration and reason.

me:LD 406.title: An Act to Repeal the Laws Providing for Paid Family and Medical Leave and to Reimburse Taxpayers
me:LD 406.summary: As introduced, repeals the paid family and medical leave benefits program, requires the Department of Labor to refund employer and self-employed contributions, and transfers the program's fund balance to the General Fund.

me:LD 407.title: An Act to Prohibit the Use of Aqueous Film-forming Foam at the Former Brunswick Naval Air Station
me:LD 407.summary: Directs the Midcoast Regional Redevelopment Authority to shut off systems containing aqueous film-forming foam and remove loose foam from its properties by December 31, 2025, and fully purge the systems by December 31, 2026.

me:LD 411.title: An Act to Amend the Law Governing the Disposition of Forfeited Firearms
me:LD 411.summary: Directs the Attorney General to update rules so auction proceeds of forfeited firearms go to the Safe Homes Program Fund, except 12% the Department of Administrative and Financial Services may retain and proceeds from firearms forfeited to a law enforcement agency's own department.

me:LD 418.title: An Act to Remand Individuals with Pending State Probation Violations to the Department of Corrections Following Initial Proceedings
me:LD 418.summary: As introduced, requires that a person charged with a probation violation who is denied bail or cannot make bail be held in Department of Corrections custody until the court proceedings are resolved.

me:LD 419.title: An Act to Increase the Transparency and Accountability of the Maine Information and Analysis Center
me:LD 419.summary: Creates an auditor of the Maine Information and Analysis Center in the Attorney General's office to check that the center operates lawfully, requires de-identified public reports, and keeps the identity of people who file complaints confidential.

me:LD 421.title: An Act to Eliminate Barriers to Reentry into the Community After Incarceration by Repealing Certain Driver's License Suspension Provisions
me:LD 421.summary: Repeals the Criminal Code provisions that let a court suspend a person's driver's license for up to 5 years when a motor vehicle was used to facilitate certain drug trafficking, furnishing, cultivating or importation offenses.

me:LD 422.title: An Act to Require the State to Obtain Municipal Approval Before Placing Noncitizens in the Municipality
me:LD 422.summary: Prohibits the State from placing noncitizens in a municipality without its prior authorization and lets the municipality limit the number of noncitizens placed there.

me:LD 424.title: An Act Concerning the Concealed Carrying of a Handgun by an Individual Who Is 18 Years of Age but Under 21 Years of Age
me:LD 424.summary: As introduced, lowers from 21 to 18 the age at which a person not otherwise barred from carrying a firearm may carry a concealed handgun without a permit, replacing the exception for 18-to-20-year-old service members and veterans.

me:LD 427.title: An Act to Prohibit Mandatory Parking Space Minimums in State and Municipal Building Codes
me:LD 427.summary: Bars municipalities from requiring more than one off-street parking space per dwelling unit in residential developments in growth areas, and requires them to let developers meet parking rules through off-site agreements within 0.25 miles.

me:LD 428.title: An Act Regarding the State Forensic Service
me:LD 428.summary: Requires the State Forensic Service to send mental examination reports to courts electronically, and requires entities to provide requested records electronically, if feasible, on the day they are mailed; takes effect Jan. 1, 2028.

me:LD 429.title: An Act to Track Certain Information Regarding and Seek Federal Reimbursement for Medical Care Provided to Asylum Seekers
me:LD 429.summary: As introduced, requires hospitals to collect patients' immigration status (patients may decline) and report quarterly the aggregate cost of care for asylum seekers, and directs the health department to report annually and seek federal Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement for that cost, starting in 2027.

me:LD 436.title: An Act to Prohibit State Agencies from Promoting the COVID-19 Vaccination to Children
me:LD 436.summary: Bars state agencies, including through MaineCare, from promoting COVID-19 vaccination to anyone under 18.

me:LD 437.title: An Act Directing the Department of Education to Develop Pilot Programs to Place Child Care Facilities in Selected School Administrative Units
me:LD 437.summary: Directs the Department of Education to study placing child care facilities in public schools and set up pilot programs in at least 4 school administrative units, serving children of school staff, with funding appropriated.

me:LD 439.title: An Act to Preserve Maine's Sporting Heritage and Enhance Sporting Opportunities for Maine's Youth by Allowing Maine's Youth to Hunt on Sunday
me:LD 439.summary: As introduced, allows holders of junior hunting licenses, and licensed hunters under 18 enrolled in secondary school, to hunt wild animals and birds on Sundays.

me:LD 444.title: An Act to Lower Energy Costs by Repealing the Law Setting Out the State's Goals for Consumption of Electricity from Renewable Resources
me:LD 444.summary: Repeals the law setting the state's renewable energy goals and removes cross-references to those goals elsewhere in law.

me:LD 451.title: An Act to Require Testing of Solar and Wind Energy Developments for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances Contamination
me:LD 451.summary: Requires solar and wind energy developments to test for PFAS contamination, and if the Department of Environmental Protection finds the development reasonably caused it, removes its eligibility as a renewable resource and for net energy billing.

me:LD 455.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Require a Statewide Popular Election of the Secretary of State, the Treasurer of State and the Attorney General for 4-year Terms
me:LD 455.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment providing for statewide popular election of the Secretary of State, Treasurer of State and Attorney General, beginning in 2032 and every four years after, in the manner used for legislative elections.

me:LD 457.title: An Act to Fund Climate Resiliency Projects Related to the Repair of Campus Infrastructure Used for Active Transportation and Outdoor Recreation
me:LD 457.summary: Provides one-time funds to encourage private and federal investment in climate resiliency repairs of historic structures on the Southern Maine Community College campus.

me:LD 461.title: An Act to Fund Rural Patrol Services in Washington County
me:LD 461.summary: Provides funding for 4 State Trooper positions and related costs to conduct rural patrols in Washington County.

me:LD 468.title: An Act to Address Food Insecurity by Helping Maine Residents Access Locally Produced Food
me:LD 468.summary: Provides funding to the Fund To Address Food Insecurity and Provide Nutrition Incentives, to be used to match private and public contributions.

me:LD 470.title: An Act to Require School Administrative Units to Adopt Mentoring Programs for Teachers and to Improve Existing Programs
me:LD 470.summary: As amended, directs the Department of Education to review teacher mentoring programs in public schools, including whether teachers with emergency, conditional or new certificates have mentors, and report by February 15, 2026.

me:LD 477.title: An Act to Enhance Public Safety in Rural Counties by Providing State Police Patrol and Policing Services
me:LD 477.summary: Provides funding for 15 State Trooper positions, 9 State Police Corporal positions and related costs for rural counties and to support county sheriff departments.

me:LD 48.title: An Act to Update References to the United States Internal Revenue Code of 1986 Contained in the Maine Revised Statutes
me:LD 48.summary: Updates Maine tax-law references to the federal Internal Revenue Code as amended through December 31, 2024, for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024.

me:LD 482.title: An Act to Expand Educational Opportunities and Broaden Educational Services for Students Enrolled in Equivalent Instruction Programs
me:LD 482.summary: Applies one set of standards for public school participation to all equivalent instruction programs, removes the superintendent written-approval requirement to enroll in or audit courses, and lets programs agree to use library, museum, theater and church facilities.

me:LD 486.title: An Act to Remove the Duty of an Individual Exercising Self-defense to Safely Retreat or Abstain from Performing Certain Acts upon Demand
me:LD 486.summary: Removes the duty to retreat safely, or to comply with a demand to stop an act one is not obliged to perform, before using deadly force in self-defense.

me:LD 487.title: Resolve, Directing the Northern New England Passenger Rail Authority to Apply for Federal Funding for the Purpose of Identifying the Rail Corridor Connecting Portland to Orono as an Intercity Passenger Rail Corridor
me:LD 487.summary: Directs the Northern New England Passenger Rail Authority to apply in 2025 for federal corridor program funding to designate a Portland-Auburn-Lewiston-Waterville-Bangor-Orono route as an intercity passenger rail corridor.

me:LD 488.title: An Act to Protect Coastal Property by Allowing Property Owners to Protect Their Existing Dwellings
me:LD 488.summary: Authorizes the DEP to permit fortification of a residential building in or over a coastal sand dune system or coastal wetland, if specified conditions are met.

me:LD 492.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Provide for Parental Rights
me:LD 492.summary: Proposes amending the Maine Constitution so minor children's rights are held by their parents or guardians until adulthood or emancipation, and government may not infringe parents' authority over upbringing, education and care absent abuse, neglect or a minor's criminal acts.

me:LD 493.title: An Act to Expand Testing for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances to Private Drinking Water Wells
me:LD 493.summary: Requires landlords of residential buildings on private drinking water wells to test for PFAS, requires sellers of such property to disclose a water test showing PFAS, and adds PFAS to the state's uniform private-well testing recommendations.

me:LD 495.title: An Act to Require Rules Designed to Reduce Climate Change to Include Estimates of the Reduction in Adverse Climate Effects and of the Cost to Consumers
me:LD 495.summary: Requires the DEP, when adopting rules to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to estimate the climate effects prevented and the costs consumers would bear.

me:LD 497.title: An Act Regarding the Department of Environmental Protection
me:LD 497.summary: Requires Department of Environmental Protection rules on significant vernal pools to define critical terrestrial habitat and a protection zone within 100 feet of the pool, bar disturbance there where practicable, and apply the same protections across property boundaries.

me:LD 499.title: An Act to Prohibit Geoengineering
me:LD 499.summary: Prohibits engaging in, authorizing or funding geoengineering, defined as deliberate large-scale intervention in natural systems to counteract climate change, with exemptions for some DEP-authorized research; violations are a Class E crime with a $10,000 daily fine.

me:LD 5.title: An Act to Clarify the Law Regarding Prior Authorization for Air Ambulances
me:LD 5.summary: Limits the ban on requiring prior authorization for urgent air ambulance transport to nonprofit air ambulance providers, retroactive to August 9, 2024.

me:LD 500.title: An Act to Ensure Access to Safe Drinking Water from Household Wells in Rural Areas by Expanding Testing
me:LD 500.summary: Requires a program, set up by July 1, 2027, offering free PFAS testing of household well water for low-income residents, and adds PFAS to the state's private-well testing recommendations. Clarifies that homeowners with contaminated wells qualify for housing authority treatment grants.

me:LD 508.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Require Constitutional Officers to Be Elected by Popular Election
me:LD 508.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment for direct popular election, beginning in 2026, of the Secretary of State, Treasurer of State and Attorney General, as is done for legislators.

me:LD 512.title: An Act to Provide Educational Opportunities for Students in Secondary Schools with 200 or Fewer Students
me:LD 512.summary: Lets a secondary student from a district with 200 or fewer secondary students enroll in another district's secondary school if accepted, with the home district paying tuition at the per-pupil rate, capped at the state maximum tuition rate.

me:LD 513.title: An Act to Allow the Spouse of a School Board Member to Serve as a Stipend Employee Within the School Board's Jurisdiction
me:LD 513.summary: Allows a school board to let a board member's spouse serve as a stipend employee and volunteer, and allows a written nepotism policy for stipend positions. The provisions repeal July 1, 2028.

me:LD 515.title: An Act to Reverse Recent Changes Made to the Law Governing Net Energy Billing and Distributed Generation
me:LD 515.summary: As introduced, repeals 2019 net energy billing and distributed generation provisions and directs the Public Utilities Commission to restore its net energy billing rule to be substantially similar to the March 29, 2017 version.

me:LD 517.title: An Act to Protect the First Amendment Rights of Individuals in the State
me:LD 517.summary: As amended in committee, requires campaign communications containing synthetic media (deceptive or materially altered candidate images, audio or video) to carry a manipulated-or-altered disclosure; exempts satire and parody; sets civil penalties up to 500% of the expenditure.

me:LD 522.title: Resolve, Directing the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to Study the Extent of Workforce Gender Segregation in the State
me:LD 522.summary: Directs the Permanent Commission on the Status of Women to study occupational and workforce segregation by gender in Maine and any related disparities in safety or compensation, and report its findings.

me:LD 524.title: An Act to Reduce Trafficking in the State
me:LD 524.summary: Renames sexually explicit material crimes as child sexual abuse material crimes and extends them to AI-generated or altered images of an identifiable child, or obscene images appearing to depict a minor; defines minor as under 16 except where compulsion is involved.

me:LD 525.title: An Act to Strengthen Maine Citizens' Second Amendment Rights by Allowing the Discharge of Firearms on Private Property That Is Within 500 Feet of School Property in Certain Circumstances
me:LD 525.summary: As introduced, exempts a person acting under the laws on use of force in defense of premises from the ban on discharging a firearm within 500 feet of a school.

me:LD 532.title: An Act to Protect Health Care Workers by Addressing Assaults in Health Care Settings
me:LD 532.summary: Replaces the bill with a resolve directing the Commissioner of Health and Human Services to convene a working group on assaults on health care workers in health care facilities and report by Jan. 1, 2026.

me:LD 535.title: An Act to Authorize Judicial Disposition of a Juvenile Adjudicated of Murder or a Class A Crime to a Term of Commitment Extending Beyond the Juvenile's 21st Birthday
me:LD 535.summary: Allows a court to sentence a juvenile adjudicated of murder or a Class A crime to commitment beyond age 21, after weighing set factors, with transfer to an adult correctional facility at 21.

me:LD 536.title: An Act to Establish Net Neutrality
me:LD 536.summary: Requires internet service providers to offer net neutral broadband service in Maine, while allowing plans that differ in speed, data limits or income-based eligibility if all lawful traffic is treated equally. Violations fall under the Unfair Trade Practices Act, without private lawsuits.

me:LD 537.title: An Act to Prohibit the Doxing of a Minor and to Authorize a Related Civil Action
me:LD 537.summary: As amended, bars knowingly or recklessly disclosing a minor's personal identifying information that causes stalking, physical harm, serious property damage or reasonable fear for the safety of the minor or a close relation; allows civil damages, brought through a representative, and protection from harassment orders.

me:LD 538.title: An Act to Amend Maine's Prescription Drug Labeling Law by Allowing the Removal of the Name of a Prescriber of Mifepristone, Misoprostol and Their Generic Alternatives
me:LD 538.summary: Allows, at the prescriber's request, labels on mifepristone, misoprostol and their generics to show the prescriber's health care facility instead of the prescriber's name.

me:LD 54.title: An Act to Require Employers to Disclose Pay Ranges and Maintain Records of Employees' Pay Histories
me:LD 54.summary: Requires employers with 10 or more employees to state the pay range in job postings and give a position's pay range to employees on request, and to keep position and pay history records for 3 years after employment ends.

me:LD 542.title: An Act Regarding Municipal Property Tax Levy Limits
me:LD 542.summary: Limits annual growth in municipal property tax levies to average personal income growth plus new-property growth, with exceptions for specified circumstances and local votes, for municipal fiscal years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

me:LD 544.title: An Act to Create Parity in the Taxation of Medicine by Exempting Sales of Cannabis for Medical Use
me:LD 544.summary: Adds sales of cannabis to people certified for medical use to the sales tax exemption for medicines sold on a doctor's prescription.

me:LD 549.title: An Act to Establish a Statewide Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Kit Tracking System and Update Certain Requirements Regarding Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Kits
me:LD 549.summary: As amended, creates a statewide tracking system for sexual assault forensic exam kits, requires law enforcement agencies to inventory their kits by June 1, 2026, and requires crime lab analysis of kits completed after January 1, 2027 when the assault is reported.

me:LD 551.title: An Act to Restore Balanced Emergency Powers
me:LD 551.summary: As introduced, requires emergency orders that infringe private rights to be narrowly tailored and limited in scope and duration, and requires the Governor to convene the Legislature if an emergency would last over 30 days, needing a two-thirds vote of each House to extend.

me:LD 555.title: An Act to Create a Separate Department of Child and Family Services
me:LD 555.summary: As introduced, creates a Department of Child and Family Services and moves child and family services and child welfare functions to it from the Department of Health and Human Services.

me:LD 556.title: An Act to Preserve Heating and Energy Choice by Prohibiting a Municipality from Prohibiting a Particular Energy System or Energy Distributor
me:LD 556.summary: Bars municipalities from prohibiting individuals or businesses from using their chosen heating or energy system, or hiring the provider or distributor they choose, unless a state law authorizes the prohibition.

me:LD 56.title: An Act to Remove the 5 Cent Fee for Bags in Retail Stores
me:LD 56.summary: Removes the 5-cent fee retailers must charge when providing a recycled paper bag or reusable plastic bag at the point of sale.

me:LD 577.title: An Act to Address Student Hunger and Nutrition Through Expanded Access to Free Milk in Schools
me:LD 577.summary: Requires public and tuition-approved private schools with at least 60% publicly funded students to maximize federal school meal reimbursements to receive state funding, directs the Department of Education to annually share meal program options, and funds eligible schools.

me:LD 579.title: An Act to Include Certain Mental Health Workers Under the 1998 Special Plan for Retirement
me:LD 579.summary: Adds Department of Health and Human Services employees in specified nurse job classifications to the 1998 Special Plan for state retirement, effective October 1, 2026.

me:LD 580.title: An Act to Protect Maine Consumers by Prohibiting Fees Charged for Receiving Paper Statements from Financial Institutions and Credit Card Issuers
me:LD 580.summary: Removes the depository-institution exemption from the law barring businesses from penalizing customers who opt out of electronic billing statements, so banks and credit unions may not penalize customers who choose paper statements.

me:LD 582.title: An Act to Require Health Insurance Carriers to Provide Coverage for Blood Testing for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances
me:LD 582.summary: Requires health plans issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2027 to cover PFAS blood testing recommended by a provider as medically necessary under National Academies clinical guidelines.

me:LD 584.title: An Act to Make the Director of the Office of Cannabis Policy an Appointed Position Subject to Confirmation by the Legislature
me:LD 584.summary: As introduced, makes the Director of the Office of Cannabis Policy a Governor-appointed position subject to legislative committee review and confirmation by the Legislature, with the appointment due within 60 days of the law's effective date.

me:LD 585.title: An Act to Use Certain Regional Transmission Organization Payments for Beneficial Electrification to Reduce Electricity Rates
me:LD 585.summary: Removes the time limit on directing forward capacity market payments to beneficial electrification, and adds electric vehicles to heat pumps as an eligible use of those funds.

me:LD 587.title: An Act to Require Cardiac Emergency Response Plans and Athletic Emergency Action Plans for Schools and School-sponsored Athletic Events
me:LD 587.summary: As amended, beginning in the 2026-27 school year, requires school administrative units to adopt a policy providing access to automated external defibrillators at all school-sponsored events, including how a person can access one.

me:LD 588.title: An Act to Enact the Agricultural Employees Concerted Activity Protection Act
me:LD 588.summary: As introduced, gives agricultural employees the right to confer with coworkers, employers and outside groups about work conditions, bars employer interference and retaliation, and lets the Maine Labor Relations Board process complaints.

me:LD 589.title: An Act to Make Agricultural Workers and Other Related Workers Employees Under the Wage and Hour Laws
me:LD 589.summary: Requires agricultural employers to pay at least the state minimum wage starting January 1, 2026, with annual cost-of-living increases from 2027, to keep hours and wage records, and sets remedies and penalties for violations.

me:LD 59.title: An Act to Ban the Drug Tianeptine
me:LD 59.summary: As introduced, adds tianeptine to the list of Schedule W drugs.

me:LD 592.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Crime of Endangering the Welfare of a Child
me:LD 592.summary: Replaces the bill with a resolve directing the Office of Child and Family Services to convene a working group to study the laws on endangering the welfare of a child, including a felony level when serious bodily injury results.

me:LD 594.title: Resolve, Directing the State Auditor to Audit All State Agencies
me:LD 594.summary: As introduced, requires the State Auditor to audit all state agencies and report on each one's staffing, budget and budget growth, jurisdiction, projects, and share of the state biennial budget.

me:LD 598.title: An Act to Require Minimum Pay for Reporting to Work
me:LD 598.summary: Requires employers with 10 or more employees to pay a worker whose shift is cancelled or cut after reporting the lesser of two hours' pay or the shift's pay, unless the employer documented a good-faith effort to give notice; excludes seasonal and union-covered public employees.

me:LD 599.title: An Act to Codify the Federal Salary Threshold for Overtime Pay
me:LD 599.summary: Adds a $58,656 salary level and the 35th percentile of weekly earnings in the lowest-wage census region to the amounts, the highest of which an executive, administrative or professional employee must earn to be exempt from overtime, starting January 1, 2026.

me:LD 6.title: An Act to Allow Persons to Label Their Wild Animal Traps with Their Online Identification Number Issued by the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
me:LD 6.summary: Allows a person to label wild animal traps with their trapping online licensing identification number from the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife instead of their full name and address.

me:LD 60.title: An Act to Allow Employees to Request Flexible Work Schedules
me:LD 60.summary: Lets employees request a flexible work schedule in writing. Employers must consider requests and give a written reason for any denial, but need not grant them. Employers may not retaliate against employees for making a request.

me:LD 601.title: An Act to Remove State-imposed Referendum Requirements Regarding Nuclear Power
me:LD 601.summary: Removes the requirement for voter referendum approval before constructing nuclear power plants, building or operating low-level radioactive waste facilities, or entering interstate or federal waste compacts.

me:LD 607.title: An Act to Require the Approval of Superintendent Agreements Regarding Transfers of Students Between School Administrative Units
me:LD 607.summary: As introduced, requires superintendents to approve a student's transfer between school administrative units when the parent approves and the receiving unit has the physical space and staff to enroll the student.

me:LD 61.title: An Act to Regulate Employer Surveillance to Protect Workers
me:LD 61.summary: Requires employers to notify employees before using electronic surveillance and bars audiovisual monitoring in homes and personal vehicles unless required for the job. Requires written notice to employees yearly and exempts personal care services settings.

me:LD 612.title: An Act to Require the Department of Health and Human Services to Review Medicaid, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and Electronic Benefits Transfer Card Transactions and Lottery Operations
me:LD 612.summary: As introduced, requires DHHS to deduct five years of Medicaid and SNAP benefits from lottery winners' prizes, and to end benefits of recipients whose EBT transactions are solely out of state for 90 days and who no longer live in Maine or do not respond.

me:LD 613.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Death with Dignity Act to Ensure Access by Qualified Patients
me:LD 613.summary: Lets an attending physician waive part of the waiting periods for end-of-life medication requests if it is in the patient's best interests given the patient's condition, as long as the total waiting period is at least 7 days.

me:LD 618.title: An Act to Allow Minors Under 16 Years of Age to Work Until 9 p.m. During the School Year and Until 10 p.m. During Summer Vacation
me:LD 618.summary: Allows minors under 16 to work until 9 p.m. during the school year and until 10 p.m. during summer vacation.

me:LD 633.title: An Act Concerning the Restoration of Electricity During Emergencies for Certain Medically Vulnerable Individuals Who Rely on Electronic Medical Apparatuses
me:LD 633.summary: Requires investor-owned transmission and distribution utilities to include in their emergency response plans procedures to identify, and conduct outreach to, customers with a documented need for electricity for essential medical equipment.

me:LD 635.title: Resolve, to Direct the Attorney General to Drop the Lawsuit Filed Against Big Oil Companies Concerning Climate Change
me:LD 635.summary: Directs the Department of the Attorney General to dismiss and withdraw from the case State of Maine v. BP, PLC et al., pending in the U.S. District Court, District of Maine.

me:LD 639.title: An Act to Improve Training Opportunities for Law Enforcement Officers
me:LD 639.summary: Removes the requirement that the structured law enforcement training program of the Maine Criminal Justice Academy be a residential program.

me:LD 644.title: An Act to Expand Employment Opportunities for Minor Students by Eliminating Certain Work Limitations
me:LD 644.summary: Repeals limits on the hours and times 16- and 17-year-olds may work, the ban on employing minors under 17 during school hours, and the related work-hour record-keeping requirements.

me:LD 648.title: An Act to Expand the Supervised Community Confinement Program
me:LD 648.summary: Makes a prisoner eligible for supervised community confinement after serving 2/3 of the term or 20 years, whichever is first, if the crime was committed before age 26 and the prisoner meets minimum-custody criteria.

me:LD 66.title: An Act to Expand Access to the Maine Wage Assurance Fund
me:LD 66.summary: Raises from 2 to 4 the maximum weeks of unpaid wages, plus equal liquidated damages, that the Maine Wage Assurance Fund can pay former employees of closed or bankrupt employers.

me:LD 660.title: An Act to Provide Transparency and Public Access to Public School Curricula
me:LD 660.summary: As introduced, requires school units to implement approved curriculum without change, post three years of enrollment and performance data, and create an online portal for student information and curriculum materials, and restricts certain class offerings and materials.

me:LD 662.title: An Act to Fund Military Sexual Trauma Liaisons
me:LD 662.summary: Moves $200,000 a year from the Medical Use of Cannabis Fund to a military transition-to-civilian-life fund and $285,000 a year to a new program funding housing and support for unhoused veterans and military sexual trauma survivors.

me:LD 666.title: An Act to Prevent Domestic Violence by Providing Adequate Funding Support for Court-ordered Certified Domestic Violence Intervention Programs
me:LD 666.summary: Provides ongoing state funding for certified domestic violence intervention programs.

me:LD 670.title: An Act to Address Coercive Control in Domestic Abuse Cases
me:LD 670.summary: Expands the definition of abuse in protection from abuse laws to include compelling a person by coercion to engage in, or refrain from, conduct they have a right to refrain from or engage in.

me:LD 671.title: An Act to Abolish the Maine Income Tax and Establish a Zero-based Budget
me:LD 671.summary: Eliminates the Maine income tax starting January 1, 2026, and requires a state report on needed law changes. Also creates a budgeting system in which agencies face zero-based budgeting every 8 years, with review requirements in between.

me:LD 677.title: An Act to Update the Statutory Definition of "Machine Gun" and Prohibit Possession of a Rapid-fire Device
me:LD 677.summary: Expands the definition of machine gun to include parts designed to convert a weapon, and makes knowingly possessing a rapid-fire device without authority a Class D crime.

me:LD 68.title: An Act to Amend the State Tax Laws
me:LD 68.summary: As introduced, changes state tax laws, including excluding watercraft leases and rentals from the nonresident sales tax exemption, replacing the automatic extension for business equipment exemption applications with a good-cause extension, and clarifying that casual sales tax covers casual rentals.

me:LD 681.title: An Act Regarding Public Higher Education Funding in the State
me:LD 681.summary: As introduced, requires the Legislature to raise Maine Maritime Academy's state funding share of operating costs by 5% each year until it matches the lower of the university or community college systems' shares, and creates a higher education funding study commission.

me:LD 69.title: An Act to Repeal the Law Restricting the Use of Certain Plastic, Paper and Single-use Bags
me:LD 69.summary: Repeals the law restricting the use of recycled paper bags, reusable plastic bags and single-use carry-out bags.

me:LD 695.title: An Act Regarding the Laws of the State of Maine
me:LD 695.summary: Creates a Legislator Residential Security Program and Fund, run by the Legislative Council's executive director, to pay for home security systems for sitting legislators who request them, subject to available funds.

me:LD 696.title: An Act to Bolster the Maine Teacher Residency Program
me:LD 696.summary: Provides an ongoing appropriation of $500,000 per year for the Maine Teacher Residency Program at the University of Southern Maine.

me:LD 697.title: An Act to Direct the Maine Prescription Drug Affordability Board to Assess Strategies to Reduce Prescription Drug Costs and to Take Steps to Implement Reference-based Pricing
me:LD 697.summary: Changes the Prescription Drug Affordability Board's duties to assessing strategies for lowering drug costs and spending growth, adds a Maine Health Data Organization director to the board and an insurer member to its advisory council, and requires a review of upper payment limits.

me:LD 698.title: An Act to Sustain Emergency Homeless Shelters in Maine
