me:LD 698.summary: Provides $4,473,000 in one-time General Fund money for emergency homeless shelter operations in 2025-26, paid for by redirecting $2,982,000 from the Housing Opportunities for Maine Fund and $1,491,000 from the Housing First Fund.

me:LD 70.title: An Act to Fund Free Health Clinics
me:LD 70.summary: Provides $50,000 a year in one-time General Fund money in 2025-26 and 2026-27 to the Maine CDC for the state's free health clinics, distributed by a formula based on clients served and a base amount per clinic.

me:LD 700.title: An Act to Promote Student Enrollment and Degree Completion in the University of Maine System by Awarding Waivers of Tuition and Fees to Eligible Students
me:LD 700.summary: Requires the University of Maine System to waive tuition and fees for eligible full-time students, covering costs left after Pell Grants and other aid except merit scholarships, subject to available funding.

me:LD 702.title: An Act to Designate January 6th as A Day to Remember and to Preserve the Accounts of Witnesses to the Events of January 6, 2021
me:LD 702.summary: Designates January 6 each year as A Day to Remember, with the Governor issuing an annual proclamation about the events of January 6, 2021 in Washington, D.C.

me:LD 703.title: An Act to Establish a Health Care Gap Year Program for Recent College Graduates
me:LD 703.summary: Provides $250,000 in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27, as one-time funds, for a health care gap year program that incentivizes recent college graduates to work in critical health care positions, particularly in underserved and rural communities.

me:LD 704.title: An Act to Clarify Performance Standards for Quarries
me:LD 704.summary: Requires quarry operators otherwise exempt from the quarrying law who plan blasting to notify people within 1,000 feet before each blast under a notification plan, by phone, in writing, newspaper notice or other means.

me:LD 708.title: An Act to Allow for Rescission of a Site Location of Development Permit When a Development Is Decommissioned
me:LD 708.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Environmental Protection to rescind, on the permittee's request, a site location of development permit for a non-subdivision development once it is fully decommissioned to the department's satisfaction, and defines "fully decommissioned."

me:LD 713.title: An Act Regarding Taxation
me:LD 713.summary: Excludes data centers that begin operating on or after August 1, 2026 from the Dirigo business incentives program and the business equipment tax exemption, and directs a state study of data center incentives due November 4, 2026.

me:LD 717.title: An Act to Amend the Maine Criminal Code Governing Restitution to Include the Costs of All Analyses of Suspected Illegal Drugs
me:LD 717.summary: Removes the limit that drug-analysis costs count as restitution only when the defendant is convicted of trafficking and the court finds the conduct was profit-motivated.

me:LD 72.title: An Act to Designate the Spring Peeper as the Official State Amphibian
me:LD 72.summary: Designates the spring peeper as Maine's official state amphibian.

me:LD 723.title: An Act Requiring the Maine Criminal Justice Academy to Develop a Nonresidential Basic Law Enforcement Training Program
me:LD 723.summary: As amended, directs the Maine Criminal Justice Academy trustees to convene a working group to study a nonresidential law enforcement training program and report to the Legislature's criminal justice committee by January 1, 2026.

me:LD 724.title: An Act to Recognize Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as State Holidays
me:LD 724.summary: Establishes Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as state holidays, with the Governor designating the specific date of each holiday every year.

me:LD 725.title: An Act to Advance Equitable Energy Policy in Maine
me:LD 725.summary: Directs the Efficiency Maine Trust to study, using a survey developed with an advisory group, the quality of jobs created by projects it funds and to report findings and recommendations to the legislature's labor committee.

me:LD 726.title: An Act to Protect Municipalities' Investment in Law Enforcement Officers
me:LD 726.summary: As introduced, doubles the training-cost payments a government employer owes the original employer when it hires a full-time officer within 5 years of the officer's academy graduation.

me:LD 73.title: An Act to Designate the Wood Turtle as the Official State Reptile
me:LD 73.summary: Designates the wood turtle as Maine's official state reptile.

me:LD 732.title: An Act to Prohibit Copyrights for Works of State Government
me:LD 732.summary: Bars copyright protection for works of the State except merchandise sold by a department or agency, while allowing the State to hold copyrights received by assignment or bequest or existing before the law takes effect.

me:LD 735.title: An Act to Protect Sand Dunes on Sears Island and to Establish Criteria for Legislation Regarding Land Development
me:LD 735.summary: Repeals laws allowing DEP to permit an offshore wind terminal on Sears Island’s coastal sand dune system and directing conservation of its northwest parcel; bars state authorization of development on the island without a committee’s certification that no sacred indigenous site is affected.

me:LD 738.title: An Act to Remove Barriers to Becoming a Lawyer by Establishing a Law Office Study Program
me:LD 738.summary: Lets bar applicants complete a four-year law office study program under a judge or attorney, instead of attending law school, before taking the bar exam; the amendment adds an appropriations section.

me:LD 739.title: An Act to Reimburse the City of Ellsworth for an Access Road to a New Court Facility in Hancock County
me:LD 739.summary: Provides one-time funding to the Judicial Department to reimburse the City of Ellsworth for 50% of the cost, up to $750,000, of building a public road to a planned Hancock County courthouse site.

me:LD 74.title: An Act to Update the System of Learning Results Review Timeline
me:LD 74.summary: Lengthens the Department of Education's review cycle for learning results content standards and performance indicators from 5 years to 7 years.

me:LD 740.title: An Act to Establish a Comprehensive Program to Divert Youth from the Criminal Justice System and Address Their Needs
me:LD 740.summary: Directs the Department of Corrections to convene a task force on safely diverting youth from formal court processing and improving community supervision, with a report due January 1, 2028.

me:LD 741.title: An Act to Increase Preparedness for Solar Power Adoption in Maine
me:LD 741.summary: As introduced, requires the Technical Building Codes and Standards Board to add Appendix CB of the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code to the state building code for new commercial buildings, excluding buildings permitted before July 1, 2026 or funded by Maine State Housing Authority.

me:LD 743.title: An Act to Increase the Availability and Affordability of Health Care by Eliminating Certificate of Need Requirements
me:LD 743.summary: Repeals Maine's certificate of need law, which requires state approval before introducing new health care services in a market area, and makes related changes in other statutes.

me:LD 746.title: An Act to Authorize a Local Option Sales Tax on Short-term Lodging to Fund Municipalities and Affordable Housing
me:LD 746.summary: Allows a municipality to adopt, by referendum, a 2% local option sales tax on short-term lodging, starting no earlier than Jan. 1, 2027, with 10% of revenue going to the Maine State Housing Authority for rural affordable housing.

me:LD 747.title: An Act to Provide Funds to Reduce Student Homelessness
me:LD 747.summary: Renames the homeless student subsidy program the rental assistance program for homeless students and provides $125,000 a year in ongoing General Fund money to the Maine State Housing Authority for it.

me:LD 749.title: An Act to Ensure That the Will of the Voters Is Reflected in Interim Appointments of United States Senators
me:LD 749.summary: Requires the Governor’s interim appointee to a U.S. Senate vacancy to be enrolled in the same party as the departing senator was at the last election, at the vacancy and at appointment, or to be unenrolled if the senator was.

me:LD 77.title: An Act to Stabilize and Sustainably Fund the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, Fisheries and Hatcheries Division by Increasing the Inland Fishing License Fees and Establishing the Inland Fisheries Conservation and Enhancement Fund
me:LD 77.summary: Creates an Inland Fisheries Conservation and Enhancement Program, changes inland fishing license fees from December 1, 2025, and lets the fish hatchery maintenance fund pay hatchery overtime and support additional state hatcheries.

me:LD 771.title: An Act to Include Possession of Compounds, Mixtures or Substances Containing a Detectable Amount of Certain Scheduled Drugs to Prove the Offense of Unlawful Trafficking of Scheduled Drugs
me:LD 771.summary: Defines amphetamine and methamphetamine in the Maine Criminal Code as any compound, mixture or preparation containing the drug in any quantity.

me:LD 775.title: An Act Requiring Voter Approval of Legislative and Gubernatorial Pay Increases
me:LD 775.summary: As introduced, requires pay raises for the Governor and legislators to be submitted to voters at the next November election before taking effect, excluding cost-of-living adjustments for legislators.

me:LD 783.title: An Act to Continue Support for the Maine Multicultural Center
me:LD 783.summary: Provides ongoing funds to the Maine Multicultural Center in Bangor for one or more positions to establish a comprehensive program for foreign-trained workers.

me:LD 784.title: An Act to Require Health Insurance Coverage for Specialized Risk Screening for First Responders
me:LD 784.summary: Creates a rebuttable presumption, in lawsuits over denied coverage, that a health insurer failed to use ordinary care in denying specialized risk screening for a first responder whose provider found it medically appropriate.

me:LD 785.title: An Act to Enact the Remaining Recommendations of the Task Force on Changes to the Maine Indian Claims Settlement Implementing Act
me:LD 785.summary: Lets the Mi'kmaq Nation elect a House representative from 2027, allows Wabanaki Nation members to subtract tribal employment pay from Maine income, and exempts certain manufactured housing sales on tribal land from sales tax.

me:LD 792.title: An Act to Fund Medical Research and Cancer Prevention
me:LD 792.summary: Provides one-time funding to the Christine B. Foundation for a research project on medically tailored groceries and dietitian counseling for cancer patients and their families.

me:LD 799.title: An Act to Report Gender Wage Gaps
me:LD 799.summary: As amended, requires employers with 250+ U.S. employees and one in Maine to report annually the number of male, female and nonbinary employees, median hourly pay by gender and the gender wage gap, and funds one Labor Department position.

me:LD 80.title: An Act to Designate the Seppala Siberian Sleddog as the Maine State Dog
me:LD 80.summary: Designates the Seppala Siberian Sleddog as the official state dog of Maine.

me:LD 810.title: An Act Regarding the Approval of Transmission Lines
me:LD 810.summary: Deems a high-impact electric transmission line to have the legislative approval required by law if it is approved for a contract after a competitive procurement run by the Public Utilities Commission or another state agency.

me:LD 813.title: An Act Regarding State Recognition of Native American Tribes
me:LD 813.summary: Creates a process for state recognition of Native American Indian tribes, with a 5-member Governor-appointed commission reviewing applications and making recommendations, and the Legislature deciding on recognition.

me:LD 818.title: An Act to Allow Expenditure of Maine Clean Election Act Funding for the Care of Candidates' Dependents
me:LD 818.summary: Allows Maine Clean Election Act candidates to use Clean Election Fund money for paid caregiving for a dependent family member of the candidate or spouse or partner, when the need exists only because of the campaign.

me:LD 82.title: An Act to Amend the Workers' Compensation Laws by Extending Indefinitely the Presumption Applying to Law Enforcement Officers, Corrections Officers, E-9-1-1 Dispatchers, Firefighters and Emergency Medical Services Persons Diagnosed with Post-traumatic Stress Disorder
me:LD 82.summary: Continues indefinitely the workers' compensation rebuttable presumption that post-traumatic stress disorder in law enforcement, corrections, 911 dispatch, firefighter and EMS workers arose from work, which is set to end October 1, 2025.

me:LD 820.title: RESOLUTION, Proposing an Amendment to the Constitution of Maine to Establish the Right to Hunt and Fish
me:LD 820.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment that the right to hunt and fish may not be infringed, subject to laws and rules on wildlife conservation, and that wildlife and fish are a common trust that may not be polluted, enforceable through legal proceedings.

me:LD 825.title: An Act to Prohibit Geoengineering, Including the Use of Cloud Seeding, Weather Modification, Excessive Radio Waves and Microwave Radiation
me:LD 825.summary: Bans geoengineering, defined as intentional large-scale intervention in natural systems including stratospheric aerosol injection and weather modification. The Department of Environmental Protection enforces it; violations are a Class C crime with a $500,000 fine per day.

me:LD 827.title: An Act to Allow the Sale of Polymer-coated Cookware That Is Authorized for Food Contact by the United States Food and Drug Administration
me:LD 827.summary: Allows the sale of cookware with a cooking surface containing the PFAS polytetrafluoroethylene, fluorinated ethylene propylene or perfluoroalkoxy alkane.

me:LD 828.title: An Act to Allow Chiropractors to Be Designated as School Health Advisors
me:LD 828.summary: Provides that a chiropractor may, within the scope of chiropractic practice, perform physical examinations of students for participation in athletic activities, including injured students seeking to resume participation.

me:LD 829.title: An Act to Standardize the Laws Regarding the Carrying of Concealed Handguns in State Parks
me:LD 829.summary: As introduced, removes the permit requirement for carrying a concealed handgun in state parks, Baxter State Park, the Allagash Wilderness Waterway and Acadia National Park for people not otherwise barred from having firearms.

me:LD 830.title: An Act to Protect Maine's Scenic Beauty by Requiring Solar Panel Fields to Be Hidden from View
me:LD 830.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Environmental Protection to find, before approving a solar energy development, that a barrier will conceal it from view from abutting properties.

me:LD 832.title: An Act to Provide Funds to Reduce the Debt of the Vassalboro Sanitary District
me:LD 832.summary: As introduced, provides one-time funding to the Vassalboro Sanitary District for debt reduction.

me:LD 837.title: An Act to Require the Office of the Public Advocate to Implement the State's Climate Action Plan
me:LD 837.summary: Requires the Public Advocate, when taking positions in proceedings, to use independent judgment so those positions are consistent with cost-effective implementation for ratepayers of the state's greenhouse gas emissions reduction obligations.

me:LD 838.title: An Act to Explore Public Financing and Ownership of Electric Transmission and Distribution Infrastructure
me:LD 838.summary: Creates a commission to study public financing of transmission, distribution, generation and energy storage projects, with findings and recommendations due December 2, 2026.

me:LD 847.title: An Act to Prohibit Housing Discrimination
me:LD 847.summary: Creates a commission to examine housing discrimination against renters using income-based assistance such as Section 8 vouchers, and ways to encourage landlords to rent to them, with a report to legislative committees.

me:LD 853.title: An Act to Replace the Minimum Hourly Wage with a Regionally Based Living Wage
me:LD 853.summary: As amended, replaces the $14.65 minimum wage from 2026 with a share of the MIT living wage for one adult, set by region: 80% in 2026, rising 5 points yearly to 100% in 2030, then 100% of the statewide figure.

me:LD 856.title: An Act to Phase Out the Income Tax
me:LD 856.summary: As introduced, phases out the Maine income tax over five years beginning in 2026 and requires state department budgets to be reduced proportionally.

me:LD 858.title: An Act to Ensure Behavioral and Mental Health Services Are Available to Students by Providing Grants to Schools That Contract for Those Services
me:LD 858.summary: Creates a grant program in the Department of Education for school units that contract with licensed providers for behavioral and mental health services not covered by MaineCare. Grants are based on school unit population and may not replace existing school staff.

me:LD 86.title: An Act to Update the Laws Regarding Education
me:LD 86.summary: Updates education laws: aligns the definition of homeless student with federal law, allows reorganizing community school districts without a private and special law, reflects Carson v. Makin on private-school tuition, and repeals the School Finance Act of 2003.

me:LD 868.title: An Act to Ensure Equity and Safety in Athletics, Restrooms, Changing Rooms and Housing at Elementary, Secondary and Postsecondary Schools
me:LD 868.summary: As introduced, requires public school and college teams to be designated male, female or coed, bars male students from female teams, and requires restrooms, changing rooms and sleeping quarters to be designated for one sex.

me:LD 87.title: An Act Regarding the State Workforce Board
me:LD 87.summary: As amended, renames the State Workforce Board the State Workforce Development Board, limits its membership to listed members, ends legislative review of other appointments, and requires legislative confirmation of its Governor-appointed chair, allowing interim chairs for up to 6 months.

me:LD 870.title: An Act Regarding the Membership of the Maine Land Use Planning Commission
me:LD 870.summary: As amended, increases the Maine Land Use Planning Commission from 9 to 11 members, with the Governor appointing 2 (one a tribal member) and the Senate President and House Speaker jointly appointing 1 at-large, and sets appointee qualifications.

me:LD 874.title: An Act to Provide Relief to Federal or State Employees Affected by a Federal Government or State Government Shutdown
me:LD 874.summary: Creates a program in which the Finance Authority of Maine repays defaulted loans of up to $6,000 that lenders make to workers affected by a federal or state shutdown, until payouts reach 10% of loans issued, with $250,000 transferred to fund it.

me:LD 877.title: An Act to Require Transportation Network Companies to Provide Fair Wages to Drivers
me:LD 877.summary: Creates a commission to study the employment practices and operations of transportation network companies in Maine, with a report to the labor committee by November 4, 2026.

me:LD 878.title: Resolve, to Study the Effects of 5G and Other Non-ionizing Radio Frequency Radiation-emitting Technology on Bird, Bee, Insect and Other Wildlife Populations and the Effects of Long-term Exposure on Children
me:LD 878.summary: Creates an independent commission to study effects of 5G and other non-ionizing radio frequency technology on wildlife and on children, reporting to two legislative committees by December 3, 2025.

me:LD 879.title: An Act to Increase Maximum Small Claim Limits for Home Construction Contracts
me:LD 879.summary: Raises the small claims limit to $25,000, excluding interest and costs, for claims involving a home construction contract.

me:LD 882.title: An Act to Protect Communication with Providers of Critical Incident Stress Management Peer Support
me:LD 882.summary: Extends confidentiality of communications with critical incident stress management providers to peer support providers for emergency responders, allows disclosure if required by law or if the provider reasonably believes the person is a danger, and sets peer support training standards.

me:LD 885.title: An Act to Allow Certain Persons with a Permit to Carry Concealed Handguns to Possess or Discharge a Firearm on School Property
me:LD 885.summary: Allows a person who is 21 or older, holds a concealed handgun permit and is not a student at the school to possess and discharge a firearm on school property.

me:LD 886.title: An Act to Regulate Medication Abortions
me:LD 886.summary: As introduced, prohibits buying abortion drugs online, requires a prescription and in-person oversight by a licensed health care professional for medication abortions, and requires the professional to give set information, including on the steps, risks and reversal.

me:LD 887.title: An Act to Make Manufacturers Responsible for Proper Disposal of Abortion Drugs and Require a Health Care Provider to Be Physically Present During a Chemical Abortion
me:LD 887.summary: As introduced, makes it a Class C crime for a prescriber to provide an abortion drug without examining the patient, being present, scheduling a follow-up within 7 days and providing a catch kit and waste bag; makes manufacturers responsible for disposal, with a $20,000 civil penalty.

me:LD 893.title: An Act to Exempt Nonprofit Agricultural Membership Organizations from Insurance Requirements
me:LD 893.summary: Exempts statewide nonprofit agricultural membership organizations that offer health care benefits to farmers from the health insurance definition if they meet requirements on eligibility, financial documentation, disclosure and a complaint process.

me:LD 894.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Paid Family and Medical Leave
me:LD 894.summary: Establishes the Bureau of Paid Family and Medical Leave in the Department of Labor, lets the department collect unpaid premiums by civil action or levy, makes buyers of a business liable for its unpaid premiums, and sets fines for lapsed private-plan coverage.

me:LD 895.title: An Act to Support Immersive Outdoor Education by Establishing the Outdoor School for All Maine Students Program
me:LD 895.summary: Creates the Outdoor School for All Maine Students Program at the University of Maine Cooperative Extension Service, which provides grants for outdoor education for students in grades 4 to 8, and sets up a dedicated fund.

me:LD 896.title: An Act to Provide Young Children Stable Access to Health Care
me:LD 896.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to seek a federal waiver by December 31, 2025 for continuous Medicaid eligibility from birth through age 5, and to adopt rules to implement it if approved.

me:LD 897.title: An Act Regarding the Calculation of Electric Rate Contracting Costs
me:LD 897.summary: Requires investor-owned transmission and distribution utilities to submit small-project planning studies to the Public Utilities Commission as well as the Public Advocate, and requires commission-solicited energy contracts to cut payments by the absolute value of any negative price times energy delivered.

me:LD 900.title: An Act to Protect State Retiree Pensions from Inflation
me:LD 900.summary: Requires the Maine Public Employees Retirement System board to automatically raise retirement benefits in fiscal year 2027-28 by the Consumer Price Index increase, up to 4%.

me:LD 901.title: Resolve, Directing the Maine State Housing Authority to Negotiate for the Purchase of or Acquire by Eminent Domain the Land and Buildings Commonly Known as the Bangor Mall
me:LD 901.summary: Requires the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority to work with the City of Bangor on a plan to redevelop the Bangor Mall with mixed uses including affordable housing, and report by January 15, 2026.

me:LD 911.title: An Act to Modify Ranked-choice Voting with Regard to Candidates Who Withdraw from an Election
me:LD 911.summary: Keeps an election ranked-choice when a candidate dies or is disqualified less than 70 days before a primary, or withdraws less than 70 days before a primary or general election, regardless of how many candidates remain.

me:LD 913.title: An Act to Prohibit Ticket Sellers from Prohibiting the Transfer of Tickets to Third Parties
me:LD 913.summary: Requires ticket sellers to disclose total prices and give refunds in set cases, bans speculative ticket sales, deceptive website addresses and bots, and limits resale marketplace charges to 10% of the original price; the Attorney General enforces.

me:LD 916.title: An Act to Promote Investment in Housing
me:LD 916.summary: Creates the Middle-income Housing Support Program and Fund at the Maine State Housing Authority, providing loans or grants for building or rehabilitating homes for renters at or below 120% of area median income and for owners at or below 180%.

me:LD 918.title: An Act to Allow a Qualifying Religious Organization to Self-insure for Automobile Insurance
me:LD 918.summary: Allows qualifying religious organizations to meet motor vehicle financial responsibility requirements through self-insurance, with certificates issued by the Secretary of State that members can use as proof when registering vehicles.

me:LD 919.title: An Act to Require Parental Permission for Certain Surveys and Questionnaires Administered to Minors in Schools
me:LD 919.summary: As introduced, bars public schools, public charter schools and private schools approved for tuition from giving a minor a survey or questionnaire that asks for or identifies the student's full name without written permission from a parent.

me:LD 92.title: An Act Regarding the Management of the Waste Components of a Solar Energy Development upon Decommissioning
me:LD 92.summary: Requires that waste components of a solar energy development be recycled or disposed of within 90 days of their physical removal from the development.

me:LD 93.title: An Act to Reduce Cost and Increase Access to Disease Prevention by Expanding the Universal Childhood Immunization Program to Include Adults
me:LD 93.summary: As amended in committee, expands the Universal Childhood Immunization Program to cover vaccines for adults, spreads program costs among payers through assessments, and takes effect July 1, 2026.

me:LD 930.title: An Act to Amend the Law Governing Items Identified as Prison Contraband
me:LD 930.summary: As amended, makes it a Class D crime for a person in official custody to make, obtain or possess an unauthorized mobile phone or handheld communication device not meant to commit another crime, and adds vaping devices to the Class E tobacco trafficking crime in adult correctional facilities.

me:LD 935.title: Resolve, Directing the Department of Environmental Protection to Report on Air and Soil Chemical and Metal Levels and on Soil Testing on Solar Panel Farm Sites
me:LD 935.summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Protection to report on levels of chemicals and metals in air and soil statewide, and on soil testing at solar farm sites before, after and during operation.

me:LD 939.title: An Act to Increase the Maximum Permissible Size of Recreational Campfires
me:LD 939.summary: Raises the maximum permitted size of a recreational campfire from 3 feet in diameter to 42 inches in diameter.

me:LD 952.title: An Act to Exempt Agricultural Employers and Employees from the Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Benefits Program
me:LD 952.summary: As introduced, removes agricultural employees from the paid family and medical leave program, requires the Department of Labor to refund employers' contributions, and requires employers to pass deducted premiums back to employees as wages.

me:LD 953.title: An Act to Change the Definition of "Machine Gun" in the Maine Criminal Code
me:LD 953.summary: As introduced, redefines "machine gun" in the Maine Criminal Code as a weapon that shoots, is designed to shoot or can readily be restored to shoot automatically more than one shot per trigger function, including frames, receivers, conversion parts and part groups that could be assembled into one.

me:LD 957.title: An Act to Integrate Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander History into the Statewide System of Learning Results
me:LD 957.summary: As amended, adds Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander history to required American history and Maine studies instruction, with state-developed teaching materials and a curriculum audit process, taking effect by July 1, 2029.

me:LD 958.title: An Act to Prohibit Eminent Domain on Tribal Lands
me:LD 958.summary: Bars taking Passamaquoddy, Penobscot, Houlton Band and Mi'kmaq trust land for public uses under state law, limited to lands held when the tribal governments certify approval; removes limits on Passamaquoddy and Penobscot reinvesting compensation for federal takings.

me:LD 96.title: An Act to Amend the Motor Vehicles and Traffic Law Governing Mandatory Driver's License Suspension for Refusing Testing for Drugs or a Combination of Drugs and Alcohol
me:LD 96.summary: As introduced, broadens drug-impairment testing law to cover impairment by any drug, replaces "drug recognition expert" with "law enforcement officer", and clarifies that the Secretary of State immediately suspends the license of a person who fails to submit to or complete the test.

me:LD 965.title: An Act to Require the Automatic Repealing of Agency Rules
me:LD 965.summary: As introduced, repeals agency rules automatically five years after adoption (rules adopted by January 1, 2026: January 1, 2030), allows Legislature-approved renewals up to five years, and requires new rules to name two existing rules not to be renewed.

me:LD 969.title: An Act to Increase Emergency Medical Services Provider Training Opportunities
me:LD 969.summary: Directs the Emergency Medical Services' Board to adopt rules allowing municipalities to conduct or host EMS licensing and relicensing training.

me:LD 973.title: An Act to Establish the Community Partnerships with Public School Systems Grant Program
me:LD 973.summary: As amended, creates a Department of Education grant program for partnerships between colleges, community action agencies and public school systems on mental health, public health and staff development, with $250,000 in one-time funding.

me:LD 978.title: An Act to Increase General Assistance Reimbursement for Municipalities and Indian Tribes
me:LD 978.summary: Raises the state reimbursement to municipalities and Indian tribes for general assistance costs from 70% to 75% of direct costs incurred on or after July 1, 2026.

me:LD 98.title: An Act to Include School Counselors in the Educators for Maine Program
me:LD 98.summary: As amended, adds school counselors to the Educators for Maine student loan and loan repayment program, defines school counselor, and requires repayment recipients to be employed as a teacher, school counselor or speech pathologist in a school in an underserved area.

me:LD 995.title: An Act to Provide Funding for Low-income Electric Ratepayer Assistance
me:LD 995.summary: Defines a low-income electric household as one eligible for a Maine State Housing Authority or means-tested DHHS assistance program with income up to 150% of the federal poverty level, and provides $7,500,000 in each of two fiscal years for electric ratepayer assistance.

me:LD 998.title: An Act Regarding an Employer's Authority to Prohibit an Employee from Storing a Firearm in the Employee's Vehicle
me:LD 998.summary: As introduced, extends the rule barring employers from prohibiting employees from keeping a locked, out-of-sight firearm in their vehicles to employees without a concealed-carry permit.

me:SC 1037.title: HCIFS - nomination of Dr. Patrick Connolly of Falmouth, for appointment to the Advisory Council on Affordable Health Care
me:SC 1037.summary: Would send the nomination of Dr. Patrick Connolly of Falmouth to the Advisory Council on Affordable Health Care back to the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee instead of proceeding to a confirmation vote.

me:SC 1067.title: SLG - nomination of Elizabeth Stivers of Yarmouth, for appointment to the State Civil Service Appeals Board
me:SC 1067.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Elizabeth Stivers of Yarmouth as a member of the State Civil Service Appeals Board.

me:SC 1080.title: ACF - nomination of Judith Camuso of Falmouth, for appointment to the Land For Maine's Future Board
me:SC 1080.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Judith Camuso of Falmouth as a member of the Land for Maine's Future Board.

me:SC 1081.title: ACF - nomination of Patrick C. Keliher of Alna, for appointment to the Land For Maine's Future Board
me:SC 1081.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Patrick C. Keliher of Alna as a member of the Land for Maine's Future Board.

me:SC 1101.title: HED - nomination of Jessica Fusco of Dedham, for appointment tof the Maine Space Corporation, Board of Directors
me:SC 1101.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Jessica Fusco of Dedham as a member of the Maine Space Corporation's Board of Directors.

me:SC 1102.title: HED - nomination of Erika Haskins of Scarborough, for appointment of the Maine Space Corporation, Board of Directors
me:SC 1102.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Erika Haskins of Scarborough as a member of the Maine Space Corporation's Board of Directors.

me:SC 1103.title: HED - nomination of Tami Gower of Wells, for appointment to the Finance Authority of Maine
me:SC 1103.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Tami Gower of Wells as a member of the Finance Authority of Maine.

me:SC 1104.title: HED - nomination of Juliet Browne, Esq. of Portland, for appointment to the Finance Authority of Maine
me:SC 1104.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Juliet Browne, Esq. of Portland as a member of the Finance Authority of Maine.

me:SC 1105.title: HED - nomination of Daniel Kleban of Cumberland Foreside, for appointment to the Finance Authority of Maine
me:SC 1105.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Daniel Kleban of Cumberland Foreside as a member of the Finance Authority of Maine.

me:SC 1106.title: HED - nomination of Martin Grohman of Biddeford, for appointment to the Maine Space Corporation, Board of Directors
me:SC 1106.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Martin Grohman of Biddeford as a member of the Maine Space Corporation's Board of Directors.

me:SC 1107.title: HED - nomination of Steven Levesque of Greenville, for appointment to the Maine Space Corporation, Board of Directors
me:SC 1107.summary: Would override the committee's recommendation to confirm Steven Levesque of Greenville as a member of the Maine Space Corporation's Board of Directors.

me:SC 1108.title: HED - nomination of Thomas Vaneck of Gloucester, for appointment to the Maine Space Corporation, Board of Directors
me:SC 1108.summary: Overrides the Housing and Economic Development Committee’s recommendation to confirm Thomas Vaneck of Gloucester, MA to the Maine Space Corporation Board of Directors.

me:SC 22.title: HCIFS - nomination of the Honorable Joan Cohen, Esq. of Portland, for appointment as the Commissioner of the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation
me:SC 22.summary: Decides whether to override the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee's recommendation that the Senate confirm Joan Cohen as Commissioner of Professional and Financial Regulation.

me:SC 94.title: JUD - nomination of the Honorable Lea-Anne Sutton of Gorham, for reappointment as a District Court Judge
me:SC 94.summary: Decides whether to override the Judiciary Committee's recommendation that the Senate confirm Lea-Anne Sutton's reappointment as a District Court judge.

me:SC 95.title: JUD - nomination of The Honorable Ann M. Murray of Bangor, for reappointment as a Superior Court Justice
me:SC 95.summary: Decides whether to override the Judiciary Committee's recommendation that the Senate confirm Ann M. Murray's reappointment as a Superior Court justice.

me:SC 999.title: JUD - all business which was placed before the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary during the Second Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature has been completed.
me:SC 999.summary: Places on file the Judiciary Committee's report that all business before it in the Second Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature is completed.

me:Senate motion.title: ADJOURN SINE DIE
me:Senate motion.summary: Adjourns the Senate sine die at the end of the second regular session of the 132nd Legislature.

me:SP 102.title: Joint Order, to Amend Joint Rule 308 to Allow Referencing of Bills by the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House at All Times
me:SP 102.summary: Amends Joint Rule 308 so the Senate Secretary and House Clerk refer bills to committees at all times, not only when the Legislature is out of session, subject to approval of the Senate President and House Speaker.

me:SP 173.title: JOINT RESOLUTION MAKING AN APPLICATION TO THE CONGRESS OF THE UNITED STATES CALLING AN ARTICLE V CONVENTION TO PROPOSE AN AMENDMENT ADDRESSING CAMPAIGN FINANCE REFORM
me:SP 173.summary: Applies to Congress to call an Article V convention limited to an amendment regulating money in elections, including overturning Citizens United, if Congress does not propose such an amendment by December 31, 2026.

me:SP 382.title: JOINT RESOLUTION COMMEMORATING WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH AND INTERNATIONAL WOMEN'S DAY
me:SP 382.summary: Designates March 2025 as Women's History Month and March 8, 2025 as International Women's Day in Maine, honoring the contributions of Maine women.

me:SP 519.title: Joint Order to Carry Over to the Next Special or Regular Session Matters Not Disposed of in the First Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature
me:SP 519.summary: Carries over to the next special or regular session of the 132nd Legislature all matters not finally disposed of in the first regular session, including nominations and Legislative Council determinations.

me:SP 789.title: Joint Order, to Waive the Requirement to Hold a Public Hearing on L.D. 1378, I.B. 2, An Act to Protect Maine Communities by Enacting the Extreme Risk Protection Order Act
me:SP 789.summary: Waives the public hearing requirement under Title 21-A, section 907 for the citizen-initiated Extreme Risk Protection Order Act, L.D. 1378.

me:SP 790.title: Joint Order, to Require the Legislative Council to Hold a Public Hearing on L.D. 1378, I.B. 2, An Act to Protect Maine Communities by Enacting the Extreme Risk Protection Order Act
me:SP 790.summary: Directs the Legislative Council to convene as a special committee and hold the required public hearing on the citizen-initiated Extreme Risk Protection Order Act, L.D. 1378, before the session adjourns.

me:SP 791.title: Joint Order, to Require the Adjournment Sine Die of the First Special Session of the 132nd Legislature
me:SP 791.summary: Orders the House and Senate to adjourn without day when they adjourn on Thursday, June 5, 2025.

me:SP 799.title: Joint Order, to Require the Joint Standing Committee on Appropriations and Financial Affairs to Report Out 2 Bills to the Senate
me:SP 799.summary: Recalls two bills from the Appropriations Committee to the Senate: L.D. 1140, an agricultural economy bond, and L.D. 1912, a housing bond.

me:SP 99.title: Joint Order, to Amend Joint Rule 214 to Require Approval of Memorials if Submitted After Cloture
me:SP 99.summary: Amends Joint Rule 214 so memorials submitted before cloture need no Legislative Council approval, while memorials submitted after cloture must meet the requirements of Joint Rule 205.

mi:HB 4011.title: Authorize the department of technology, management, and budget to convey or transfer state-owned property in Arenac County; to prescribe conditions for the conveyance or transfer; to provide for…
mi:HB 4011.summary: As introduced, authorizes the state to sell or transfer the roughly 118-acre former Standish Maximum Correctional Facility property in Arenac County by competitive sale, sale to a local government, transfer to another state agency or the Land Bank Authority, or trade.

mi:HB 4135.title: Property: conveyance of state property; conveyance of certain state-owned property in Jackson County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:HB 4135.summary: As introduced, authorizes the State Administrative Board to convey about 81 acres of state land in Jackson County, with Jackson County given first right to buy it for $1.00 within two years of enactment.

mi:HB 4301.title: Vehicles: emergency vehicles; definition of authorized emergency vehicle; expand. Amends secs. 2 & 698 of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.2 & 257.698).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4302'25
mi:HB 4301.summary: Adds vehicles owned by the Michigan Mutual Aid Box Alarm System and operated during an interlocal emergency to the definition of authorized emergency vehicle, and lets them use red, white, amber or green flashing lights.

mi:HB 4302.title: Vehicles: emergency vehicles; exception to commercial driver license for authorized emergency vehicles of Michigan Mutual Aid Box Alarm System; create. Amends sec. 312e of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.312e).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4301'25
mi:HB 4302.summary: Exempts Michigan Mutual Aid Box Alarm System employees and members who drive authorized emergency vehicles and meet firefighter driver-training standards from the commercial driver license vehicle group designation requirement.

mi:HB 4598.title: Crimes: organized; gift card fraud; provide for. Amends sec. 4 of 2012 PA 455 (MCL 752.1084).
mi:HB 4598.summary: Adds gift card fraud to Michigan's organized retail crime law: knowingly acquiring, tampering with, or using gift cards or redemption information with intent to defraud is a felony punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a $5,000 fine.

mi:HB 4599.title: Crimes: organized; certain definitions related to gift card fraud; provide for. Amends 2012 PA 455 (MCL 752.1081 - 752.1087) by adding sec. 3a.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4598'25
mi:HB 4599.summary: Defines "gift card," "gift card redemption information," "issuer," and "seller" for the organized retail crime law's gift card fraud provisions; takes effect only if House Bill 4598 is enacted.

mi:HB 4678.title: Agriculture: weights and measures; certain definitions; provide for. Amends 1964 PA 283 (MCL 290.601 - 290.635) by adding sec. 28g.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4679'25
mi:HB 4678.summary: As introduced, lets qualified equipment rental businesses sell motor fuel to refill rented equipment at a flat rate or per-gallon fee, if stated in the rental contract.

mi:HB 4679.title: Agriculture: weights and measures; certain definitions; provide for. Amends secs. 10 & 28c of 1964 PA 283 (MCL 290.610 & 290.628c).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4678'25
mi:HB 4679.summary: As introduced, says the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development need not inspect and test each qualified fuel dispenser, and treats testing requirements as met if the dispenser complies with HB 4678 and federal transportation rules.

mi:HB 4703.title: Insurance: health insurers; coverage for group prenatal care services; require. Amends 1956 PA 218 (MCL 500.100 - 500.8302) by adding sec. 3406ss.
mi:HB 4703.summary: As introduced, requires health insurance policies issued or renewed in Michigan on or after January 1, 2026 to cover group prenatal care services.

mi:HB 4793.title: Elections: school; requirement for school board members to file an acceptance of office; eliminate. Amends secs. 309 & 310 of 1954 PA 116 (MCL 168.309 & 168.310).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4794'25,  HB 4795'25
mi:HB 4793.summary: Eliminates the requirement that school board members file a written acceptance of office. Takes effect only if House Bills 4794 and 4795 are also enacted.

mi:HB 4794.title: Elections: school; requirement for community college board of trustee members to file an acceptance of office; eliminate. Amends secs. 156 & 157 of 1966 PA 331 (MCL 389.156 & 389.157).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4793'25
mi:HB 4794.summary: Eliminates the requirement that community college trustees file an acceptance of office, while keeping the oath of office. Takes effect only if House Bill 4793 is also enacted.

mi:HB 4795.title: Elections: school; requirement for intermediate school board members to file an acceptance of office; eliminate. Amends sec. 861 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.861).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4793'25
mi:HB 4795.summary: Eliminates the requirement that appointed members of a consolidating school district's board file an acceptance of office with the intermediate superintendent. Takes effect only if House Bill 4793 is also enacted.

mi:HB 5109.title: Vehicles: other; allocation to transportation administration collection fund; modify. Amends sec. 810b of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.810b).
mi:HB 5109.summary: Reduces by $1.7 million a year, for fiscal years 2027 through 2029, the amount the state treasurer may receive into the transportation administration collection fund, and deposits that $1.7 million in the general fund instead.

mi:HB 5120.title: Civil procedure: service of process; cost for service of process for personal protection orders; eliminate. Amends secs. 2559 & 2950 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2559 & 600.2950).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5121'25,  HB 6033'26
mi:HB 5120.summary: As passed by the House, requires courts issuing domestic-relationship personal protection orders to designate the law enforcement agency that serves them and give petitioners two or more copies free; service within 72 hours is at no cost while the Personal Protection Order Service Fund has money.

mi:HB 5121.title: Civil procedure: service of process; cost for service of process for personal protection orders; eliminate. Amends sec. 2950a of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2950a) & adds secs. 2950d & 2950p.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5120'25,  HB 6033'26
mi:HB 5121.summary: As passed by the House, creates the Personal Protection Order Service Fund, administered by State Police, to pay law enforcement for serving personal protection order documents, and sets service rules, including service within 72 hours and further attempts within 10 days if the first fails.

mi:HB 5317.title: Counties: boards and commissions; county parks and recreation commission membership; modify. Amends sec. 1 of 1965 PA 261 (MCL 46.351).
mi:HB 5317.summary: Lets counties under 100,000 population, beginning January 1, 2027, reduce the appointed members of a county parks and recreation commission from seven to four, and makes wording updates to the commission's membership rules.

mi:HB 5356.title: Vehicles: title; requirements for transfer of title by a dealer; provide for. Amends 14, 41a, 78, 217, 217c, 233, 233a, 233b, 234, 238, 239, 240, 248, 248a, 248j, 249, 250, 258, 801b, 806 & 810a of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.14 et seq.) & adds sec. 9b.
mi:HB 5356.summary: As passed by the House, revises Vehicle Code title, registration and salvage rules, including raising the police salvage-vehicle inspection fee cap from $100 to $125 and setting a $5,000 value threshold for ownership-bond rules for licensed new vehicle dealers.

mi:HB 5482.title: The management and budget act: amend section 242
mi:HB 5482.summary: Removes the requirement that an appropriation bill authorizing capital outlay projects include appropriations for projected State Building Authority rental payments for those projects.

mi:HB 5485.summary: As passed by the House, requires dam owners to register dams in 5 staggered rounds with asset management and compliance documents, creates a dam safety emergency fund, and creates a dam risk reduction grant program requiring owners to match at least 10%.

mi:HB 5514.title: Children: other; prohibition of use of certain restraint while transporting youths to certain youth residential treatment programs; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:HB 5514.summary: Bars youth transportation companies from using blindfolds, hoods, or mechanical restraints on youths headed to residential treatment programs, limits physical restraint to imminent serious harm, bars pickups from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m., and sets civil fines up to $1,000.

mi:HB 6007.title: Food: service establishments; delegation of certain duties and exemption of certain persons from licensure; modify. Amends secs. 3105, 3113, 3129, 3139, 4101, 4105, 5101 & 6103 of 2000 PA 92 (MCL 289.3105 et seq.).
mi:HB 6007.summary: Lets the state take back wholesale food-processing oversight from local health departments in some cases, adds licensing exemptions (such as minor-run lemonade stands), and requires 120 days' written notice before revoking a local health department's certification.

mi:HB 6033.title: Civil procedure: costs and fees; fees for service of process; revise. Amends sec. 2559 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2559).
mi:HB 6033.summary: As passed by the House, bars courts and police from charging personal protection order petitioners service fees while the Personal Protection Order Service Fund has money, lets police collect at least $50 per completed service from the fund, and raises other service-of-process fees.

mi:HB 6080.title: Education: teachers and administrators; certain professional development courses; prohibit. Amends sec. 1248 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1248).
mi:HB 6080.summary: Requires coursework counted as 'relevant special training' in teacher layoff, placement and promotion decisions to be degree-eligible credit from an accredited institution, shown on a transcript and letter-graded; pass/fail coursework is ineligible unless converted to a letter grade.

mi:HB 6127.title: Gaming: other; expenditures in the internet gaming fund; modify. Amends secs. 14 & 16 of 2019 PA 152 (MCL 432.314 & 432.316).
mi:HB 6127.summary: Raises the annual Internet Gaming Fund allocation to the first responder presumed coverage fund from $2.0 million to up to $7.0 million (half its claim and administrative costs), and allocates $1.0 million a year for tribal governments.

mi:HB 6130.title: Michigan trust fund act: amend section 12
mi:HB 6130.summary: Closes the Community District Education Trust Fund after September 30, 2026, moving any remaining money to the School Aid Fund, and removes the requirement that the general fund cover shortfalls in offsetting Detroit schools' foundation allowance costs.

mi:HB 6259.title: Criminal procedure: sentencing guidelines; sentencing guidelines for criminal sexual conduct; modify. Amends sec. 16y, ch. XVII of 1927 PA 175 (MCL 777.16y).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 6261'26,  HB 6262'26
mi:HB 6259.summary: As introduced, reclassifies second- and third-degree criminal sexual conduct in the sentencing guidelines as Class A felonies with a statutory maximum of life; takes effect only if HB 6261 and 6262 are enacted.

mi:HB 6260.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the first degree; modify. Amends sec. 520b of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520b).
mi:HB 6260.summary: As introduced, sets a 15-year mandatory minimum sentence for first-degree criminal sexual conduct, which already carries a maximum of life.

mi:HB 6261.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the second degree; modify. Amends sec. 520c of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520c).
mi:HB 6261.summary: As introduced, sets a 10-year mandatory minimum and raises the maximum from 15 years to life for second-degree criminal sexual conduct.

mi:HB 6262.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the third degree; modify. Amends sec. 520d of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520d).
mi:HB 6262.summary: As introduced, sets a 5-year mandatory minimum and raises the maximum from 15 years to life for third-degree criminal sexual conduct.

mi:HB 6263.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the fourth degree; modify. Amends sec. 520e of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520e).
mi:HB 6263.summary: As introduced, changes fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct from a misdemeanor to a felony, keeping the 2-year maximum prison term.

mi:HB 6282.title: Public employees and officers: ethics; moratorium on former legislators accepting employment with an entity that receives a grant from the utility consumer participation board; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:HB 6282.summary: Bars former legislators, for at least two years after leaving office, from taking jobs with entities that receive utility consumer participation board grants; violations are misdemeanors punishable by up to 90 days in jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both.

mi:HB 6302.title: Education: school districts; requirement to display an American flag in classrooms; provide for. Amends sec. 1347 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1347).
mi:HB 6302.summary: As passed by the House, changes the school flag rule so a U.S. flag in classrooms where students recite the Pledge of Allegiance must be displayed, hoisted, draped, or placed on a stand or post in a prominent location.

mi:HB 6309.title: Highways: memorial; portion of M-86; designate as the "Casey Rice Memorial Highway". Amends 2001 PA 142 (MCL 250.1001 - 250.2092) by adding sec. 116.
mi:HB 6309.summary: Designates M-86 in Branch County between US-12 and Arbogast Road as the "Casey Rice Memorial Highway."

mi:HR 373.title: A resolution to condemn socialism, the platform of the Democratic Socialists for America, and politicians who espouse socialist views, and to oppose the implementation of socialist policies in the state of Michigan and the United States.
mi:HR 373.summary: Condemns socialism, the platform of the Democratic Socialists for America, and politicians who espouse socialist views, and opposes socialist policies in Michigan and the United States.

mi:SB 102.title: Counties: employees and officers; request for transcript and abstract of paper or record; modify. Amends sec. 1 of 1895 PA 161 (MCL 48.101).
mi:SB 102.summary: Extends the capped-fee electronic records rule for county treasurers to records they possess, and treats a request for both winter and summer tax bill amounts as one request with a $2,000 maximum charge.

mi:SB 1132.title: Military affairs: other; Camp Grayling improvement fund; establish. Amends 1967 PA 150 (MCL 32.501 - 32.851) by adding secs. 388a, 388b, 388c, 388d, 388e & 388f.
mi:SB 1132.summary: Creates a Camp Grayling improvement fund for the site's fees, rents and other revenue, spendable by the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs on appropriation for improvements; authorizes site leases and contracts; and requires an annual report.

mi:SB 1134.title: Retirement: state employees; election process to transfer certain law enforcement officers to the Michigan state police retirement system; provide for. Amends sec. 55 of 1943 PA 240 (MCL 38.55) & adds secs. 50b, 50c, 50d, 64a, 64b & 64c.   TIE BAR WITH: SB 1133'26,  SB 1135'26
mi:SB 1134.summary: Lets state employees' retirement system Tier 2 participants in certain corrections positions, conservation officers, and state police motor carrier and properties security officers elect to join the state police retirement system effective January 2028, with elections due October 15, 2027.

mi:SB 198.title: Occupations: vehicles, dealers, and repair facilities; requirements for automobile dealer data collection; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:SB 198.summary: As introduced, bars vehicle manufacturers and third parties from accessing, sharing or using protected dealer data, including consumer and diagnostic data, without the dealer's written consent, and from limiting dealers' use of it.

mi:SB 217.title: Traffic control: accidents; penalties for moving violation causing physical injury or death to a vulnerable roadway user; enhance. Amends sec. 12e, ch. XVII of 1927 PA 175 (MCL 777.12e).   TIE BAR WITH: SB 0216'25
mi:SB 217.summary: As introduced, adds the new felonies for moving violations that seriously injure or kill vulnerable roadway users, such as pedestrians, to the sentencing guidelines; tied to SB 216.

mi:SB 373.title: Housing: landlord and tenants; limitations on fees charged to tenants; provide for. Amends sec. 3 of 1978 PA 454 (MCL 554.633).
mi:SB 373.summary: As introduced, bars a rental agreement from charging an extra fee on every allowed rent payment method, so an agreement allowing multiple methods must offer at least one without an added charge.

mi:SB 413.title: Health occupations: psychologists; licensure requirements for limited licensed psychologists; modify and modify membership of Michigan board of psychology. Amends secs. 18221, 18223, 18233 & 18237 of 1978 PA 368 (MCL 333.18221 et seq.).
mi:SB 413.summary: Raises supervised postgraduate experience for a Michigan limited psychology license from 1 year to 2 years (3,000 hours, or 4,000 for master's degrees granted from Aug. 31, 2027), starting 12 months after enactment; lets limited licensees practice unsupervised; adds two limited-license psychologists to the board.

mi:SB 433.title: State agencies (existing): health and human services; educational materials regarding health dangers for youth using high-potency THC and cannabis products; require the department to provide. Amends 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1 - 380.1852) by adding sec. 1509.
mi:SB 433.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Department of Health and Human Services to develop, by July 1, 2027, an annually updated notice on the dangers of tobacco, vapor, nicotine, THC cannabis and synthetic hemp products and on THC poisoning, which schools must give parents by October 1 each year from 2027-28.

mi:SB 478.title: Property: conveyance of state property; transfer of certain state-owned property in Livingston County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:SB 478.summary: Authorizes the State Administrative Board to transfer administrative jurisdiction of about 93 acres in Green Oak Township, Livingston County, from the Department of Corrections to the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs without payment.

mi:SB 569.title: Public health code: amend sections 5431, 5841, 13104, and 16315
mi:SB 569.summary: Transfers money to the General Fund each year from fiscal 2027 through 2029: $1 million of newborn screening fees, $220,000 from the parent participation fund, and $100,000 of body art facility license fees.

mi:SB 729.title: An act creating the state building authority with power to acquire, construct, furnish, equip, own, improve, enlarge, operate, mortgage, and maintain facilities for the use of the state or any of its…
mi:SB 729.summary: Exempts $485.1 million of State Building Authority bonds issued in June 2025 from counting against the authority's $2.7 billion debt cap, raising the effective cap to about $3.19 billion.

mi:SB 791.title: Highways: memorial; portion of I-475; designate as the "St. John Street Community Memorial Highway". Amends 2001 PA 142 (MCL 250.1001 - 250.2092) by adding sec. 124.
mi:SB 791.summary: As introduced, designates the portion of I-475 in Genesee County from Hamilton Avenue north to a quarter mile past Stewart Avenue as the "St. John Street Community Memorial Highway."

mi:SB 947.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 31502, 31503, 31504, 31505, 31506, 31507, 31508, 31509, 31510, 31511, 31513, 31515, 31516, 31517, 31518, 31520, 31521, and 31523
mi:SB 947.summary: Revises the dam safety law: extends state oversight to federally licensed dams, changes spillway capacity criteria and increases inspection frequency for high- and significant-hazard dams, creates 10-year dam registrations, and allows emergency orders to remove dams in imminent danger of failure.

mi:SB 988.title: Property tax: tax tribunal; number of days to appeal a claim for poverty exemption; modify. Amends sec. 53c of 1893 PA 206 (MCL 211.53c).
mi:SB 988.summary: Extends the deadline to appeal a board of review's denial of a poverty exemption to the Michigan Tax Tribunal from 30 to 35 days after the denial, and treats a mailed appeal as timely if postmarked by the deadline.

mn:HF 1082.title: Public safety; time extended to use appropriations; public safety officer and survivor benefits provided; sale or transfer of law enforcement vehicle, assault of hospital or clinic security guard, and grooming prohibited; crimes of impersonating a peace officer and theft modified; task forces and grant program established; MINNCOR policies modified; domestic violence case process modified; personal information protections provided to public safety officers; criminal penalties provided; reports required; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 1082.summary: Appropriates $1,314,000 for a clearance grant program and two task forces, transfers $12 million to the victims of crime account, and bars selling law enforcement vehicles to the public with police equipment or insignia, along with other public safety provisions.

mn:HF 1141.title: Housing finance and policy bill.
mn:HF 1141.summary: Appropriates $25 million to the Minnesota Housing Finance Agency from its investment earnings, authorizes $100 million in housing infrastructure bonds, and returns tax-forfeited land settlement money to the general fund and appropriates it for family homeless prevention.

mn:HF 1410.title: Correctional and peace officer disciplinary procedures modified.
mn:HF 1410.summary: Adds procedures for questioning correctional officers in discipline cases, including a signed complaint, witness lists, electronic recording, a union representative or attorney present, and damages from agencies that violate them; adjusts related peace officer definitions.

mn:HF 1606.title: Nudification technology access prohibited.
mn:HF 1606.summary: Bars owners of websites and apps from letting users nudify images or videos of identifiable people, or doing so for them, unless the service requires user technical skill; bans advertising such services; lets depicted people sue; allows attorney general penalties up to $500,000 per violation.

mn:HF 1849.title: Term limits provided for governor and lieutenant governor, and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 1849.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the 2026 ballot, limiting a person to being elected governor no more than twice and lieutenant governor no more than twice, counting terms from the 2026 election.

mn:HF 2133.title: Income tax; pass-through entity tax technical correction made.
mn:HF 2133.summary: Corrects the wording of the Minnesota income tax law on the credit for pass-through entity tax paid to another state, changing references from "section" to "subdivision" so the credit's expiration applies to that subdivision.

mn:HF 2358.title: Enhanced criminal penalty provided for violations of coercion crime.
mn:HF 2358.summary: Raises the maximum sentence for coercion by threatening a violation of the law on nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images to 10 years if a substantial factor in great bodily harm, and 15 years if in the victim's death.

mn:HF 2433.title: Education finance bill.
mn:HF 2433.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt a policy by June 30, 2027 and implement a local or state anonymous threat reporting system by July 1, 2028; changes fiscal year 2027 compensatory aid; provides grants and appropriates money.

mn:HF 2438.title: Taxation bill; financing and operation of state and local government provided.
mn:HF 2438.summary: Conforms Minnesota's income tax to most changes in federal Public Law 119-21, with exceptions such as a 1% floor on charitable deductions, and makes other state and local tax changes.

mn:HF 2484.title: Bonding bill; spending authorized to acquire and better land and buildings and for other improvements of a capital nature, new programs established and existing programs modified, report required, prior appropriations modified and canceled, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 2484.summary: Appropriates general fund money in fiscal year 2027 for capital improvements to land and buildings, establishes new programs and modifies existing ones, and modifies and cancels prior appropriations.

mn:HF 3067.title: Paraprofessional qualifications clarified.
mn:HF 3067.summary: Treats a paraprofessional who shows the required competencies as meeting federal qualification rules when the employing district or charter school validates it, and requires Department of Education guidance on validation by August 1, 2026.

mn:HF 3155.title: Gift card fraud included in organized retail theft.
mn:HF 3155.summary: Includes gift cards in the organized retail theft law and adds tampering with stolen merchandise or packaging to obtain value to the covered acts.

mn:HF 3298.title: Reimbursement program established for underground petroleum storage tank systems with pressurized single-walled steel piping.
mn:HF 3298.summary: Uses up to $4 million a year from the Petroleum Tank Fund to reimburse underground tank owners for 50% of the cost of replacing single-walled steel piping and equipment; the program expires in 2037.

mn:HF 3404.title: Criminal penalty for impersonating a peace officer increased, crime of impersonating a peace officer while possessing a firearm established, enhanced penalties established, persons presenting as peace officers required to fulfill duty to identify, and criminal penalties established.
mn:HF 3404.summary: Makes impersonating a peace officer a felony (up to 2 years; 10 with a firearm or recent prior), raises penalties for other crimes committed while impersonating, and requires officers to identify their agency, last name and ID number by uniform markings or on request.

mn:HF 3426.title: Environment and natural resources trust fund finance bill.
mn:HF 3426.summary: Appropriates about $102 million in fiscal year 2027 from the Environment and Natural Resources Trust Fund, sets rules for its community grant program, and adds requirements for approving emerging-issues spending.

mn:HF 3453.title: Kratom; legal age to possess kratom established as 21 years of age or older.
mn:HF 3453.summary: Raises from 18 to 21 the age below which selling kratom is a gross misdemeanor and possessing it is a misdemeanor, effective August 1, 2026.

mn:HF 3467.title: Commissioner of veterans affairs allowed to direct agency resources to veterans' initiatives, and reports required.
mn:HF 3467.summary: Lets the commissioner of veterans affairs direct nonmonetary agency resources to initiatives on veterans' food insecurity, homelessness, suicide prevention and similar issues, and requires an annual report each October 15.

mn:HF 3489.title: Licensing boards reporting required, criminal offense of grooming established, criminal penalties provided, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3489.summary: Creates the felony of grooming a child, extends felony solicitation offenses to people in authority over a minor and to school staff regarding students, requires police to notify licensing boards when a teacher is charged with listed offenses, and appropriates money.

mn:HF 3521.title: Exception to the hospital construction moratorium provided.
mn:HF 3521.summary: Adds an exception to the hospital construction moratorium for a project to add 85 licensed beds at an existing safety net, level I trauma center hospital in Ramsey County.

mn:HF 3522.title: Veterans; standards established for legislatively directed competitive and direct grants, honor guard detail provided, available benefits to veterans of the Secret War in Laos modified, eligibility for burial in state veterans cemeteries modified, Commanders Task Force established, pay for state active service modified, commissioner of veterans affairs allowed to temporarily close veterans homes, reports required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3522.summary: Sets standards for legislatively directed veterans grants, extends honor guard funeral payments to more groups, changes Secret War in Laos veteran benefits, state veterans cemetery burial eligibility and state active service pay, creates a Commanders Task Force, and appropriates money.

mn:HF 3544.title: Certain veterans or former members of the armed forces who have forfeited federal benefits made ineligible for state-funded benefits, services, or programs; and environmental hazards information and assistance program for veterans discontinued.
mn:HF 3544.summary: Bars veterans the federal VA has found to have forfeited federal benefits from state-funded veterans benefits and programs, adds a deputy commissioner for administration at the veterans department, and ends the environmental hazards information and assistance program.

mn:HF 3629.title: Program payment withholding provided for credible allegation of fraud, grant management provisions changed, and program integrity reports required.
mn:HF 3629.summary: Replaces agencies' 60-day payment withholding on a preponderance of fraud evidence with withholding during a credible allegation of fraud under investigation, with administrative reconsideration; changes grant rules; requires annual program integrity reports from Human Services and Children, Youth, and Families.

mn:HF 3676.title: Safe at Home program; protections, remedies, and various provisions provided and modified; and criminal penalties established.
mn:HF 3676.summary: Changes the Safe at Home address confidentiality program by barring discrimination against participants, adding a criminal penalty when a violation causes bodily harm, and adjusting legal-proceeding and driver's license address rules.

mn:HF 3709.title: Virtual-currency custody services allowed to be offered and performed.
mn:HF 3709.summary: As passed by the House, allows banks and credit unions to provide virtual-currency custody services if they follow safety-and-soundness and written-policy requirements and give the commissioner 60 days' written notice.

mn:HF 3718.title: Veterinary medicine and veterinary technology practice provisions modified.
mn:HF 3718.summary: Rewrites Minnesota's veterinary practice law, adding definitions for telemedicine, teletriage and the veterinarian-client-patient relationship, and changing rules on veterinary technicians, drug dispensing, record keeping, feed directive drugs, and donated drugs for animals.

mn:HF 3741.title: Educational assistance for veterans' children and spouses modified, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3741.summary: As introduced, expands Minnesota's educational assistance for veterans' children and spouses to those of prisoners of war and missing-in-action service members, requires state residency, requires colleges to report annually, and ends the single $750 veteran payment.

mn:HF 3769.title: Multiple levels of substance abuse care provided by the commissioner of corrections clarified in law, and access to mental health unit beds for incarcerated persons expanded.
mn:HF 3769.summary: Requires residential substance use treatment programs in certified state-operated juvenile correctional facilities to meet community treatment program standards, as adult programs already must, and expands incarcerated people's access to mental health unit beds.

mn:HF 3782.title: Chemical irritant used in buildings disclosure required, and commissioner of public safety required to develop a standard form.
mn:HF 3782.summary: Requires peace officers to notify building owners, and occupants of homes or apartments, when chemical irritants are used inside a building, requires agencies to share product information on request, and directs the Department of Public Safety to create a standard notice form.

mn:HF 3785.title: Definitions and registration requirements for motorized bicycles and motorcycles powered by electric motors modified, sellers required to have a dealer license, certain vehicles prohibited from using public roads, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3785.summary: Defines motorized bicycles with electric motors as over 750 and under 1,500 watts, lets them register as off-highway motorcycles, requires dealer licenses and electrical safety certification for sellers, lowers micromobility device limits to 20 mph and 100 pounds, and appropriates $30,000 for signage.

mn:HF 3825.title: Health occupations; licensing and scope of practice modified for acupuncture and herbal medicine practice, athletic training, mortuary science, social work, dentistry practice, marriage and family therapy, pharmacy practice, physical therapists, and advanced practice registered nurses; registration established for massage therapists and Asian bodywork therapists; licensure established for music therapists; unlicensed practice provisions modified; advisory councils established; civil penalties; reports required; fees imposed; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3825.summary: As passed by the House, changes licensing and scope of practice for acupuncture, athletic training, mortuary science, social work, dentistry, pharmacy and other health professions; creates registration for massage and Asian bodywork therapists and licensure for music therapists.

mn:HF 3827.title: Grants from Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to local law enforcement clarified as reimbursements, law related to recording of crimes updated, process for determining how certain criminal records are ineligible for sealing established, and court required to provide order for protection for access by law enforcement.
mn:HF 3827.summary: Turns public safety grants to local law enforcement into reimbursements, has the BCA superintendent prescribe the form for crime data, has court administrators make vulnerable adult protection order status available to officers, and requires the BCA to unseal records later found ineligible for expungement.

mn:HF 3875.title: Judiciary policy bill.
mn:HF 3875.summary: Lets district courts post notices on the judicial branch website when no suitable local newspaper exists, limits public-authority notice in dissolutions to cases with children, makes docketed restitution orders last until satisfied, and extends the child protection council's report deadline to December 15, 2026.

mn:HF 3900.title: Permanent school fund investment, management, and distribution policy modified; and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 3900.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment for the November 2026 ballot letting permanent school fund distributions be set by law instead of limited to interest and dividends; a companion law sets them at 4.5% of the fund's three-year average value.

mn:HF 3908.title: Ignition interlock program license revocation requirements modified, driver's license indicators classified as private data, and technical corrections made.
mn:HF 3908.summary: Changes driver's license rules, including making license indicators and designations private data, barring sharing of autism and mental health designations with federal agencies, and revising impaired-driving and ignition interlock provisions.

mn:HF 3970.title: Remedy to extinguish a joint interest in a contract for deed of a perpetrator of domestic abuse or sexual assault established.
mn:HF 3970.summary: Lets an unmarried person subjected to domestic abuse, sexual assault, sexual extortion or harassment by a contract-for-deed co-party ask a court to end the abuser's interest if the abuser has not lived there for six months and the petitioner made all payments.

mn:HF 4017.title: Unlawful shipment of infectious or pathological waste study required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 4017.summary: Requires the Pollution Control Agency to submit a study by January 15, 2027 on unlawful shipment of infectious or pathological waste to solid waste facilities, including a survey of waste generators, and appropriates $75,000 for it.

mn:HF 4052.title: Various provisions governing telephone company regulation, facilities and property, pricing plans, service classification, and reporting requirements.
mn:HF 4052.summary: Repeals many state telephone company rate, price and service regulations and requires telephone companies to notify residential customers of the price of all service options available to them.

mn:HF 4063.title: First aid kit requirements on school buses modified, USDOT numbers required for all school buses, and school buses authorized on public roads for training purposes.
mn:HF 4063.summary: Requires anyone providing school transportation with a school bus to apply for a USDOT number, allows school buses to be used on public roads for driver training, and requires first aid kits meeting national school transportation specifications in model year 2027 and newer vehicles.

mn:HF 4074.title: Retirement policy bill.
mn:HF 4074.summary: Changes public pension law, including lower contribution rates and higher postretirement adjustments for correctional service plan members, state aid for certain plans, firefighter relief association rules, and Secure Choice Retirement Program administration.

mn:HF 4075.title: Uniform procedure established for imposition, implementation, and oversight of firearm restrictions resulting from certain criminal convictions and judicial orders.
mn:HF 4075.summary: Creates a uniform process for surrendering firearms in child protection, domestic abuse, assault, harassment and pretrial release cases, and requires petitioners in child protection and domestic abuse cases to identify where the respondent's firearms are located.

mn:HF 4102.title: State Patrol compensation study requirements modified, and volunteer chaplains allowed within the state patrol.
mn:HF 4102.summary: Excludes State Patrol lieutenants from the 'patrol trooper' category, drops benefits from the law enforcement compensation survey and continues it every odd year through 2037, and allows volunteer chaplains to support the State Patrol.

mn:HF 4133.title: Homeowner's insurance policies specified exclusions prohibited when damage is done by a peace officer.
mn:HF 4133.summary: Bars homeowner's insurance from excluding damage from a peace officer's use of chemical irritants, smoke screens or diversionary devices when the homeowner is owed just compensation, and lets homeowners choose their mitigation contractor, effective January 1, 2027.

mn:HF 4138.title: Social media platform requirements established relating to accounts for minors, and enforcement mechanisms established for regulations on child social media accounts.
mn:HF 4138.summary: Requires social media platforms with 10,000 or more account holders or $1 billion in revenue to get verifiable parental consent for accounts of children 15 and under, bars addictive features and targeted ads on them, and allows private lawsuits and attorney general enforcement.

mn:HF 4151.title: Eligibility of certain applicants for licenses to serve as private detectives or protective agents modified.
mn:HF 4151.summary: Removes partnerships from private detective and protective agent licensing law and requires a corporate applicant's chief executive officer, chief financial officer, qualified representative and Minnesota manager to each meet licensing requirements.

mn:HF 4188.title: Commerce policy bill.
mn:HF 4188.summary: Makes commerce law changes on consumer protection, financial products, student loan servicing, insurance, securities and unclaimed property, modifies the Minnesota premium security plan, and eliminates the Prescription Drug Affordability Advisory Council.

mn:HF 4224.title: Notice requirements for water discharges modified.
