mn:HF 4224.summary: Changes the notice a sewage treatment works or domestic sewer owner must give after a discharge, to cover downstream users and Tribal governments along with the public and drinking water facilities.

mn:HF 4239.title: Noncampaign disbursements provided; data classification provided; complaints provided; and requirements for reports, written communications, and disclaimers modified.
mn:HF 4239.summary: Adds candidate security expenses to the definition of noncampaign disbursements, classifies certain campaign finance address data as not public, lets the board chair dismiss frivolous complaints, and modifies requirements for reports, written communications and disclaimers.

mn:HF 4240.title: Elections; various changes made related to election administration, absentee voting provisions modified, timelines modified, elected officials and candidates prohibited from betting on elections, technical and clarifying changes made, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 4240.summary: Requires notice of whether absentee voting starts 46 or 18 days before an election, requires the statewide voter registration system for most absentee voting from September 1, 2027, and bars candidates from wagering on prediction markets about their own election.

mn:HF 4252.title: Higher education finance and policy bill.
mn:HF 4252.summary: Makes higher education changes, including paid blood-donation leave for MnState employees, a ban on mandatory MnState student fees for athletic facilities not open to all students, written explanations before developmental courses, and supplemental appropriations.

mn:HF 4384.title: Abusive head trauma training requirements for child care providers modified.
mn:HF 4384.summary: As first engrossed, requires abusive head trauma training for child care centers, family child care license holders and helpers to be interactive rather than only reading or viewing material, effective January 1, 2027.

mn:HF 4492.title: Read Act modified, early literacy field experiences required for teacher candidates, high school diploma established for veterans, and rulemaking required.
mn:HF 4492.summary: Changes Read Act rules on screening, parent notice, literacy plans and training; requires early literacy field experience for teacher candidates; and requires schools to issue diplomas, on request, to Korean War and Vietnam War veterans who did not finish high school.

mn:HF 4502.title: Trusted contact program established to mitigate financial exploitation and fraud, and liability limited.
mn:HF 4502.summary: Lets financial services providers offer a trusted contact program, where customers name an adult the provider may contact in an emergency, if the customer is unresponsive, or about suspected fraud or exploitation, and limits providers’ civil liability.

mn:HF 4591.title: State government policy and finance bill.
mn:HF 4591.summary: Makes supplemental state government appropriations, including more money for the new Office of Inspector General and grants to public television and radio stations, along with state government policy changes.

mn:HF 4987.title: Ramsey County State-Aid Highway 96 portion designated as "Master Sergeant Nicole Amor Memorial Highway".
mn:HF 4987.summary: Designates a portion of Ramsey County State-Aid Highway 96 as "Master Sergeant Nicole Amor Memorial Highway," with signs erected once nonpublic money covers the costs.

mn:HF 5074.title: Claims against the state settlement provided, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 5074.summary: Appropriates fiscal year 2027 general fund money to pay claims against the state: $250,000, $350,000 and $4.5 million in wrongful-imprisonment awards to three people, and $4,570.40 to one person injured while incarcerated.

mn:HF 5084.title: Preborn child given recognized right to life, and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 5084.summary: As introduced, proposes a constitutional amendment for the 2026 ballot stating that a preborn child, defined as a living human from fertilization until live birth, has the right to life; it does not prohibit treatment to save the life or preserve the health of the pregnant individual.

mn:HF 5140.title: Ownership, possession, and sale of semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines regulated; provisions for possessing dangerous weapons in schools, negligently storing firearms, and reporting on law enforcement firearms discharge modified; ghost guns criminalized; other gun safety provisions modified; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 5140.summary: As introduced, bars dealers from selling semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines, requires owners to certify them with the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, bans ghost guns, re-enacts the binary trigger ban, changes extreme risk protection order law, and appropriates money.

mn:HF 5149.title: Law enforcement access to sensitive locations restricted, civil remedies established, concealing identity crime modified, scope of use of force investigations expanded, access to certain information limited.
mn:HF 5149.summary: As introduced, bars civil immigration arrests of parties, witnesses and companions at court proceedings, bars health care facility staff from admitting immigration agents without a judicial warrant, limits school disclosure of student immigration data, and creates a civil cause of action for constitutional violations.

mn:HF 719.title: Safe routes to school grant program funding provided, bonds issued, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 719.summary: Authorizes state bond sales and capital spending on public land and buildings, including $1 million for safe routes to school grants, authorizes conveyance of bond-financed property, and provides a temporary reduction in vehicle registration tax for 2027.

mn:SF 1943.title: Pet shops prohibition from selling cats and dogs
mn:SF 1943.summary: As amended by the House, appropriates about $191 million from the outdoor heritage fund for fiscal 2027, changes arts and cultural heritage fund grants, revises parks and trails commission and land acquisition rules, and authorizes certain state land conveyances.

mn:SF 2077.title: Omnibus Outdoor Heritage Fund, Legacy and Lands bill
mn:SF 2077.summary: Appropriates $191.1 million from the Outdoor Heritage Fund for fiscal 2027 and $80,000 to the Agricultural Utilization Research Institute for legal costs, changes state land and DNR licensing provisions, and extends unemployment benefits for certain iron ore mining workers.

mn:SF 2373.title: Omnibus Labor policy bill
mn:SF 2373.summary: Exempts minor league baseball players from minimum wage and overtime rules, changes construction code and licensing provisions, extends unemployment insurance for certain iron ore workers, and funds the Agricultural Utilization Research Institute.

mn:SF 2814.title: Disciplinary sanction matrix establishment
mn:SF 2814.summary: Lets the commissioner of commerce consider the Appraisal Foundation's Voluntary Disciplinary Action Matrix as non-binding guidance when setting a sanction for a real estate appraiser, while keeping discretion over each case.

mn:SF 3210.title: Disability accommodations as protection inclusion from discrimination
mn:SF 3210.summary: Adds to the Minnesota Human Rights Act policy statement that failing to engage in the process to determine a reasonable accommodation for people with disabilities may be an unfair discriminatory practice in employment, housing, public accommodations, public services and education.

mn:SF 3236.title: Helmets requirement for operators of electric-assisted bicycles under the age of 18
mn:SF 3236.summary: Requires operators of electric-assisted bicycles under 18 to wear helmets, sets operation and sale requirements for motorized bicycles, and creates a motorized bicycle safety coordinator in the Department of Public Safety.

mn:SF 334.title: Human Services Systems Modernization Advisory Council and Legislative Commission on Human Services Systems; creation
mn:SF 334.summary: Creates a Human Services Systems Modernization Advisory Council, a Legislative Commission on Human Services Systems, and a modernization fund that gets general fund transfers, up to a $50 million balance, when the budget closes above forecast, with required reports.

mn:SF 3602.title: Uniform Electronics Estate Planning Documents Act Establishment
mn:SF 3602.summary: Enacts the Uniform Electronic Estate Planning Documents Act, recognizing electronic records and signatures on estate planning documents other than wills, such as trusts, and setting rules for notarization, witnessing, retention, paper-copy certification and evidence.

mn:SF 3637.title: Optometrists prescribing of certain window glaze materials authorization clarification provision
mn:SF 3637.summary: Lets optometrists, as well as physicians, provide the statement of medical need that allows vehicle window glazing darker than the usual light-transmittance limit.

mn:SF 3720.title: 2026 recommendations adoption of the Workers' Compensation Advisory Council
mn:SF 3720.summary: Changes workers' compensation law, including raising maximum legal fees and permanent partial disability compensation, adding amounts owed when an insurer leaves the reinsurance association, and changing how an insolvent member's liabilities are handled.

mn:SF 3887.title: Watershed districts, watershed management organizations, and towns permission to self-insure for certain employee health benefits
mn:SF 3887.summary: Adds towns, watershed districts and watershed management organizations to the local governments that may self-insure employee health benefits, alone with over 100 employees or jointly with others that together have over 100.

mn:SF 3888.title: Tow trucks permission to use variable message signs
mn:SF 3888.summary: Allows tow trucks to display a portable variable message sign while doing emergency service on or near a highway, if the sign meets state traffic control manual standards.

mn:SF 3891.title: Permission to donate eggs past their quality assurance date
mn:SF 3891.summary: Lets charitable food assistance programs distribute donated eggs up to 30 days past their quality assurance date if they are in original packaging, graded, kept refrigerated and labeled "Donated Eggs - Not for Resale."

mn:SF 3958.title: Disaster assistance contingency account reporting date modification
mn:SF 3958.summary: Moves the annual disaster assistance contingency account spending report's due date from January 15 to January 31.

mn:SF 3967.title: Due date of the pediatric hospital-to-home transition pilot program report modification
mn:SF 3967.summary: As amended, bars health plans from imposing quantity limits on home care nursing coverage for people also on medical assistance, bars the commissioner from making payments to defray the cost (both retroactive to January 1, 2026), and requires plans to use the defined term “home care nursing services.”

mn:SF 4059.title: Omnibus Supplemental Finance Bill
mn:SF 4059.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for education, state government, environment, jobs, public safety and corrections, creates a battery stewardship program, authorizes certain state land sales, and changes peace officer compensation provisions.

mn:SF 4171.title: Vacating tenants submetered utility service final billing provision and payment of rent by tenants provisions modifications
mn:SF 4171.summary: Lets landlords bill vacating tenants an estimated final utility charge, requires another way to pay if a landlord's online payment platform is down, bars naming a tenant's minor child in eviction suits, and adds assault on the landlord, employees or contractors to expedited-eviction grounds.

mn:SF 4244.title: Miscellaneous technical corrections to laws and statutes
mn:SF 4244.summary: Makes miscellaneous technical corrections to Minnesota laws, fixing erroneous, obsolete and omitted text and references and removing redundant, conflicting or superseded provisions.

mn:SF 4282.title: Various agency forecast adjustments
mn:SF 4282.summary: Adjusts fiscal year 2026 and 2027 education, human services and Metro Mobility appropriations to match the February 2026 forecast, and changes K-12 programs, including new aid for Tribal contract schools and extended restroom grants.

mn:SF 4339.title: Certain excavation notice system governing requirements modification and electronic positive response requirement inclusion provision
mn:SF 4339.summary: Defines "electronic positive response" and requires underground facility operators to send one through the notification center before the locate period ends, for excavation and boundary survey notices; the center must make it available to the excavator.

mn:SF 4401.title: Omnibus Cannabis bill
mn:SF 4401.summary: Makes changes to Minnesota's cannabis law, including creating a cannabis macrobusiness license, streamlining adult-use and medical cannabis rules, requiring endorsements for authorized activities, changing labeling rules, and letting hemp license holders also hold cannabis licenses.

mn:SF 4476.title: Omnibus Human Services supplemental appropriations
mn:SF 4476.summary: Makes human services supplemental budget changes, including Medicaid continuity of care, long-term care facility rules, background studies, behavioral health, electronic visit verification, and appropriations for the Department of Human Services and other agencies.

mn:SF 4515.title: Certain prize and ticket limits modification
mn:SF 4515.summary: Raises the maximum price of a lawful gambling paddlewheel ticket from $2 to $5, caps merchandise prizes for paddle tickets at $200 fair market value, and excludes gift cards redeemable for cash from merchandise prizes.

mn:SF 4612.title: Omnibus Health and Human Services supplemental appropriations
mn:SF 4612.summary: Makes health and children and families supplemental budget changes, including Department of Health, hospital stabilization, health licensing board, medical assistance fraud prevention and child care licensing provisions, plus forecast adjustments and agency appropriations.

mn:SF 476.title: Omnibus Human Services policy bill
mn:SF 476.summary: Changes human services policy on state direct care and treatment, the Department of Health, aging and disability services, behavioral health, housing supports and maltreatment of vulnerable adults; removes housing stabilization supports provisions and requires release of an Optum report.

mn:SF 4760.title: Omnibus Public Safety policy bill
mn:SF 4760.summary: Makes public safety policy changes on data practices, domestic violence, victim rights, impaired driving, identity theft and corrections; makes running a prediction market as a business a felony; bars selling law enforcement vehicles with police equipment or insignia to the public.

mn:SF 5073.title: Omnibus Agriculture, Broadband, and Rural Development policy and supplemental appropriations
mn:SF 5073.summary: Changes agriculture policy, including farm down payment assistance, seed potato rules, fees and reports; allows eggs to be donated past their quality assurance date; and modifies prior appropriations.

mn:SF 5200.title: Miscellaneous oversights, inconsistencies, ambiguities, unintended results, and technical errors correction
mn:SF 5200.summary: Makes technical corrections to 2026 laws, setting effective dates for a Supreme Court child protection council provision (June 15, 2026) and direct primary care agreement provisions (August 1, 2027), and fixing wording in election precinct summary statement law.

mo:SB 1.title: Relating to county officials
mo:SB 1.summary: Replaces duplicate versions of six county-official statutes with single versions, covering county officials' salary schedules, sheriff, coroner and public administrator pay, and county auditor property inventories.

mo:SB 10.title: Relating to construction regulation
mo:SB 10.summary: Removes expiration and sunset dates from many state laws, including the Show MO Act and Entertainment Industry Jobs Act tax credits, CASA and diaper bank credits, the pharmacy tax, the Medicaid managed care allowance, and parts of the SAFE Act.

mo:SB 1000.title: Relating to the division of tourism supplemental revenue fund
mo:SB 1000.summary: Repeals the formula for depositing general revenue into the Division of Tourism Supplemental Revenue Fund, leaving a fund of appropriations and gifts for the tourism division whose year-end balance does not revert to general revenue.

mo:SB 1001.title: Relating to homeownership
mo:SB 1001.summary: Changes real estate laws, including delinquent property tax sales, land banks, nuisance property rules in large cities, sewer district liens, vacant-property LLCs, and limits on institutional buyers of single-family homes, residential sale-leasebacks and wholesalers.

mo:SB 1002.title: Relating to school board elections
mo:SB 1002.summary: Moves school board elections in districts mostly in counties of 400,000 to 500,000 people to November of even-numbered years from 2028 with four-year terms, lets candidates choose to list a party, and puts school tax and bond proposals on those ballots.

mo:SB 1003.title: Relating to military affairs
mo:SB 1003.summary: As an amendment, lets counties, by ordinance or voter-approved referendum, give 100%-disabled veterans a property tax credit equal to increases in their homestead's real property tax liability above their initial credit year.

mo:SB 1012.title: Relating to the use of artificially generated content
mo:SB 1012.summary: Declares artificial intelligence systems non-sentient and bars them from legal personhood, marriage, owning property or holding executive positions, requires notice when AI interacts with consumers, regulates companion chatbots, and requires disclaimers on certain AI-generated political ads depicting false speech or conduct.

mo:SB 1015.title: Relating to assisted outpatient treatment
mo:SB 1015.summary: Creates court-ordered assisted outpatient treatment: certain physicians, mental health program directors, guardians and health agencies may petition probate courts for orders requiring adults with mental illness, who meet set criteria, to take part in outpatient services.

mo:SB 1019.title: Relating to hospitals
mo:SB 1019.summary: Raises the share of available funds that boards of city hospitals under chapter 96 may invest from 25% to 50%, gives hospital districts a 50% authority, adjusts limits on hospital activities in some counties, and revises the Missouri Lyme Disease Eradication Act.

mo:SB 1023.title: Relating to a sales tax for public libraries
mo:SB 1023.summary: Adds more counties, defined by population, whose public library districts may impose a library sales tax; changes urban library district budget-approval timing; and repeals an expired county civil filing surcharge.

mo:SB 1032.title: Relating to an income tax exemption for certain dependents
mo:SB 1032.summary: Allows a $2,400 state income tax deduction, starting in 2027, for each child a taxpayer gives birth to or adopts during the year, even if the federal exemption amount is zero; it cannot be combined with the regular dependent deduction for that child.

mo:SB 1033.title: Relating to regulation of air quality
mo:SB 1033.summary: Starting July 1, 2027, ends reversion of some Natural Resources Protection Fund balances and transfers 5% of state sales tax revenue from electric power distribution to the air permit fee account; exempts older farm vehicles from emissions inspections and certain cotton gins from air modeling.

mo:SB 105.title: Relating to nonnative invasive plants
mo:SB 105.summary: Requires nursery dealers to swear they will not knowingly import, sell, transport, distribute or propagate certain invasive plants, such as Japanese honeysuckle starting in 2027 and Callery pear and burning bush starting in 2029.

mo:SB 1067.title: Relating to civil actions based on public expression
mo:SB 1067.summary: Replaces the state's special-motion-to-dismiss law for public hearing speech with the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act, extending it to government proceedings and public-concern speech: motion within 60 days, other proceedings paused, fees to a prevailing mover.

mo:SB 1087.title: Relating to driver's licenses
mo:SB 1087.summary: Requires limited driving privilege applications to state travel times, routes and purposes, adds worship and essential-business trips as qualifying purposes, and lets courts and the director set route and schedule limits.

mo:SB 1092.title: Relating to social workers
mo:SB 1092.summary: Reduces from five to three years the social work practice experience required to serve as a qualified supervisor of clinical, baccalaureate or advanced macro social worker applicants.

mo:SB 110.title: Relating to Kappa Alpha Psi Week in Missouri
mo:SB 110.summary: Designates January 5 each year as Kappa Alpha Psi Day in Missouri to commemorate the fraternity's founding.

mo:SB 111.title: Relating to the designation of September as ovarian cancer awareness month
mo:SB 111.summary: Designates September each year as Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month in Missouri and encourages activities to raise awareness of the disease.

mo:SB 1119.title: Relating to the appointment and duties of commissioners to attend an Article V convention
mo:SB 1119.summary: Sets how Missouri picks commissioners to an Article V convention: one commissioner and one alternate per congressional district, chosen by the General Assembly, bound by its instructions and an oath, at least one-third not legislators.

mo:SB 1135.title: Relating to child maintenance orders for certain persons convicted of driving while intoxicated
mo:SB 1135.summary: Requires a court, on a surviving parent's or guardian's petition, to order a person convicted of an intoxicated-driving offense that killed a child's parent to pay child maintenance, generally until the child turns 18, or up to 21 if in school.

mo:SB 1142.title: Relating to series limited liability companies
mo:SB 1142.summary: Lets anyone apply to the Secretary of State for a certificate of good standing for an LLC or an individual LLC series, and requires each series to be separately listed and searchable on the Secretary's business website by January 31, 2027.

mo:SB 1233.title: Relating to the licensing of accountants
mo:SB 1233.summary: Changes licensing laws for many professions, including accountants, architects, engineers, respiratory therapists and pharmacists, and moves interior designers from a registration council to licensure under the architects' and engineers' board.

mo:SB 125.title: Relating to port authorities
mo:SB 125.summary: Modifies which projects qualify for Waterways and Ports Trust Fund appropriations, including projects on land owned by a city not within a county and managed by a port authority, or in a navigable river adjacent to it.

mo:SB 1328.title: Relating to blood donor awareness month
mo:SB 1328.summary: Designates January as Blood Donor Awareness Month in Missouri and recommends observing it with activities that raise awareness of blood donation.

mo:SB 133.title: Relating to underground facilities
mo:SB 133.summary: Changes the underground facility damage-prevention law, requiring most new buried facilities to be installed with a detectable locating device and relieving excavators of liability for damage caused by incorrect location information from facility owners.

mo:SB 1351.title: Relating to urban school districts
mo:SB 1351.summary: Treats a student as present when accompanying a parent to vote in urban school districts, excusing one absence per election, and sets annual school board elections with three-year terms in districts mostly within cities of 105,000 to 125,000 people.

mo:SB 1383.title: Relating to agricultural education
mo:SB 1383.summary: Authorizes the education department to make the elementary agricultural education pilot an ongoing program starting in 2027-28, open to public elementary schools that elect to join, with its evaluation published on the department's website.

mo:SB 1408.title: Relating to the speed limit on certain roads of this state
mo:SB 1408.summary: Raises the uniform speed limit on rural interstates and freeways from 70 to 75 miles per hour and raises the maximum limit the state may set on state roads to 75.

mo:SB 1421.title: Relating to the unlawful use of unmanned aircraft in certain areas
mo:SB 1421.summary: Makes two parts of the bill take effect immediately: authority for certified peace officers to mitigate credible drone threats, and a revised drone offense over open-air venues (now 500-person capacity, was 5,000) and critical infrastructure.

mo:SB 145.title: Relating to the taxation of certain businesses
mo:SB 145.summary: Bars municipalities from imposing a license tax on enterprises owned by a person aged 18 or younger, and bars constitutional charter cities over 350,000 residents from licensing, taxing or regulating such enterprises.

mo:SB 1470.title: Relating to the duties and functions of the joint committee on legislative research
mo:SB 1470.summary: Revises laws on the Joint Committee on Legislative Research, allowing laws and resolutions to be published in electronic form, ending free printed copies to legislators and officials, and changing the committee's membership.

mo:SB 1477.title: Relating to motorcycle auxiliary lighting
mo:SB 1477.summary: Allows motorcycles to use auxiliary lighting of any color instead of only amber and white, if nonblinking and directed at the engine and drive train, and changes professional sports team license plate provisions.

mo:SB 150.title: Relating to the career -tech certificate program
mo:SB 150.summary: Changes workforce and education laws, including lowering the minimum age for adult high schools to 18, creating a STEM career awareness program and a Career-Tech Certificate Program, and changing student aid, loan repayment and licensing rules.

mo:SB 152.title: Relating to campaign finance
mo:SB 152.summary: Bars ballot-measure committees from knowingly accepting contributions from foreign nationals, requires committees to get a non-foreign-national affirmation from donors giving over $2,000, and lets the attorney general investigate and sue over violations.

mo:SB 1544.title: Relating to the designation of infrastructure
mo:SB 1544.summary: Creates state designations, including Blood Donor Awareness Month in January, Missouri Black Bear Awareness Day on April 22, Ulysses S. Grant Day on April 27, and Frankie Muse Freeman Day on November 24, and names highways and bridges.

mo:SB 1553.title: Relating to incentives for producing certain critical materials and pharmaceuticals
mo:SB 1553.summary: Creates a nonrefundable tax credit of 20% to 25% of project costs of $5 million or more, capped at $40 million a year, for nontraditional defense contractors producing critical materials or pharmaceuticals, and extends the manufacturing sales tax exemption to such production.

mo:SB 156.title: Relating to Chris Sifford Day in Missouri
mo:SB 156.summary: Designates August 6 each year as Chris Sifford Day in Missouri.

mo:SB 1572.title: Relating to the board of trustees of the police retirement system of St
mo:SB 1572.summary: Bars public pension systems from spending funds to support or oppose ballot measures or candidates; also changes the St. Louis police retirement board, a public school retirement board voting rule, and provisions of the state employees' retirement plan.

mo:SB 1576.title: Relating to a commission for the study of trade with Ireland
mo:SB 1576.summary: Creates the nine-member Missouri Ireland Trade Commission in the Department of Economic Development to study ways to advance trade, investment, and academic and business exchanges between Missouri and Ireland.

mo:SB 1586.title: Relating to solid waste management
mo:SB 1586.summary: Requires sellers of land containing a landfill to disclose the sale to the Department of Natural Resources; cuts solid waste districts' share of remaining Solid Waste Management Fund revenue from 61% to 51% and sets aside 10% for the department's work on abandoned disposal sites.

mo:SB 160.title: Relating to student associations at public institutions of higher learning
mo:SB 160.summary: Bars schools (pre-K to 12) receiving state aid from discriminating based on hair texture or protective hairstyles associated with a race or origin, bars public colleges from adverse action against belief-based student groups over viewpoint or leadership requirements, and changes hazing and degree laws.

mo:SB 1613.title: Relating to Frankie Muse Freeman day
mo:SB 1613.summary: Designates November 24 each year as Frankie Muse Freeman Day in Missouri.

mo:SB 1629.title: Relating to underground facilities
mo:SB 1629.summary: Exempts all storm water sewers, regardless of installation depth, from the requirement that new underground facilities installed after August 28, 2025 carry a detectable underground location device.

mo:SB 163.title: Relating to an income tax deduction for certain National Guard duties
mo:SB 163.summary: Adds income from National Guard state active duty or state emergency duty orders, for tax years beginning 2026, to the military income that is fully deductible from Missouri taxable income.

mo:SB 1652.title: Relating to the office of missing and murdered African American women and girls
mo:SB 1652.summary: Creates the Phoenix Alert System to notify law enforcement and media of missing African American women and girls, creates an office on the issue within the Department of Public Safety, and makes knowingly false reports triggering an alert a class A misdemeanor.

mo:SB 166.title: Relating to cardiac emergency response plans
mo:SB 166.summary: Requires each public school, starting in 2026-27, to adopt a cardiac emergency response plan with AEDs on campus and at athletic venues, annual drills, and CPR and AED-certified staff such as coaches and nurses; creates no cause of action against schools.

mo:SB 1694.title: Relating to incentives for downtown redevelopment
mo:SB 1694.summary: Reopens the downtown redevelopment incentive program, letting the Department of Economic Development approve up to four new municipal applications from Aug. 28, 2026 until the end of 2032, and changes how revenue from relocated out-of-state businesses is counted.

mo:SB 218.title: Relating to mental health treatment courts
mo:SB 218.summary: Changes court laws, including expanding the Judicial Privacy Act to more court-related officers, adding circuit judgeships, changing juror pay, letting families request confidential misdemeanor records of deceased people, and revising treatment court provisions.

mo:SB 22.title: Relating to ballot summaries prepared by the general assembly
mo:SB 22.summary: Raises the word limit for legislature-written ballot summaries from 50 to 100, changes ballot title challenge deadlines and procedures, and lets the attorney general appeal preliminary injunctions that block state laws or regulations.

mo:SB 221.title: Relating to judicial review of agency determinations
mo:SB 221.summary: Bars courts and hearing officers from deferring to a state agency's reading of a law or rule, requiring de novo interpretation, with any remaining doubt in actions involving a state agency resolved toward limiting agency power.

mo:SB 266.title: Relating to assessment of virtual school students
mo:SB 266.summary: Allows virtual schools to give statewide assessments in a virtual setting at an assigned time, with camera proctoring and a ten-to-one student-to-proctor goal; excludes college and workforce readiness tests from national providers.

mo:SB 271.title: Relating to powers of fire protection district boards
mo:SB 271.summary: Changes laws on fire protection and ambulance districts, including board training, ambulance district audits at least every three years, EMS advisory council size, ambulance license standards, and a bar on county fire rules covering farm buildings.

mo:SB 3.title: Relating to department of revenue fee offices
mo:SB 3.summary: Raises the fees department of revenue fee offices may charge for registrations, titles and licenses, such as from $6 to $9 for a title or annual registration and from $12 to $18 for a biennial registration.

mo:SB 348.title: Relating to state designations
mo:SB 348.summary: Designates commemorative days and awareness months, such as John Donaldson Day on February 20 and Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month in September, names numerous state highways, bridges and interchanges in honor of individuals, and designates official city titles and historic trails.

mo:SB 35.title: Relating to tax credits for downtown revitalization
mo:SB 35.summary: Creates state tax credits from 2026 for downtown revitalization: 25% of costs of converting office buildings to mainly residential use and 30% of upper-floor housing costs in main street districts, carried back three years, forward ten, and transferable.

mo:SB 360.title: Relating to assessment of public elementary and secondary schools
mo:SB 360.summary: Replaces the state school accountability report card with annual data dashboards published by districts and charter schools, limits statewide assessments to federal requirements, and bars using results to classify school districts.

mo:SB 38.title: Relating to discrimi natory practices
mo:SB 38.summary: Bars public and private prekindergarten, elementary and secondary schools that receive state aid from discriminating based on hair texture or protective hairstyles, such as braids, locks, twists and afros, commonly associated with a race or origin.

mo:SB 396.title: Relating to consolidated public library districts
mo:SB 396.summary: Changes the deadline for a consolidated public library district board to approve its budget from June 30 to the last day of the fiscal year before the budget year.

mo:SB 4.title: Relating to utilities
mo:SB 4.summary: Changes utility regulation, including electric rate-setting rules, capacity and integrated resource planning, time-of-use rate opt-outs, discounts for large new customers, hot and cold weather shutoff rules, advanced meters, and Public Counsel funding.

mo:SB 40.title: Relating to the CTF medical alert system
mo:SB 40.summary: Creates a task force on missing and murdered African American women and girls to study causes of violence against them, data tracking and policing practices, and report annually; it expires December 31, 2027 unless extended.

mo:SB 43.title: Relating to child protection
mo:SB 43.summary: Changes child-protection laws, including raising the age for enticement of a child to under 17, allowing more children's out-of-court statements as evidence, creating a legal representation commission and a program for youth with severe behavioral needs, and requiring restitution payments for trafficking offenses.

mo:SB 466.title: Relating to agricultural tax credits
mo:SB 466.summary: Removes the 2028 sunset dates for agricultural tax credits, including the wood energy producer, meat processing facility, biodiesel, urban farm and specialty agricultural crop credits.

mo:SB 47.title: Relating to class actions
mo:SB 47.summary: Rewrites the Missouri Supreme Court class action rule, setting requirements for certifying a class, notice to class members, class counsel, attorney's fees and appeals of certification orders.

mo:SB 49.title: Relating to allowing public schools to employ or accept chaplains as volunteers
mo:SB 49.summary: Allows school districts and charter schools to employ chaplains or accept them as screened volunteers; requires membership in a Defense Department-listed religious-endorsing organization and background checks; bars registered sex offenders.

mo:SB 59.title: Relating to an income tax deduction for certain survivor benefits
mo:SB 59.summary: Adds Missouri income tax subtractions for first responders' retirement benefits starting in 2026, for up to $500 of unreimbursed educator expenses starting in 2025, and for up to $500 of first-responder compensation.

mo:SB 63.title: Relating to participation of certain students in nontraditional educational settings
mo:SB 63.summary: Bars school districts and charter schools from preventing home-schooled, family-paced education, and virtual-school students from joining district events such as athletics and fine arts, subject to eligibility rules, and replaces the home-school declaration of enrollment with parent notice to drop a child from district rolls.

mo:SB 66.title: Relating to the age of marriage
mo:SB 66.summary: Bars marriage licenses for anyone under age 18, removing the current allowance for 16- and 17-year-olds with parental consent, and requires applicants to show proof of age.

mo:SB 68.title: Relating to school safety
mo:SB 68.summary: Changes many K-12 education laws, including school emergency operations plans, lead testing of school drinking water, active shooter training, reading instruction, teacher and substitute certification, statewide assessments, and school funding rules.

mo:SB 71.title: Relating to college tuition for first responders
mo:SB 71.summary: Creates the Public Safety Recruitment and Retention Act for first responder tuition, changes local government retirement systems, lets licensing agencies require fingerprint checks, changes second-degree burglary and vehicle-entry offenses, and creates a nonprofit security task force and fund.

mo:SB 79.title: Relating to health care benefits provided by certain organizations
mo:SB 79.summary: Allows expedited partner therapy for more sexually transmitted infections, requires health plans covering hormonal contraceptives to reimburse supplies of up to 90 days (180 for generics), lets farm bureaus and similar organizations offer self-funded health benefits, and changes MO HealthNet and prenatal testing rules.

mo:SB 81.title: Relating to water preservation in the state of Missouri
mo:SB 81.summary: Changes public safety laws, including fireworks display permits and fire marshal inspections of sellers, fingerprint background checks by many licensing boards, line-of-duty compensation, and childhood sexual abuse lawsuit rules.

mo:SB 82.title: Relating to water resources
mo:SB 82.summary: Requires a state permit to export Missouri water out of state, exempting bottled water and uses within 30 miles of the border, and restricts withdrawals for export through pipelines.

mo:SB 834.title: Relating to mortgage modifications
mo:SB 834.summary: Creates the Missouri Residential Sale Leaseback Protection Act, requiring a buyer to give a home seller a written disclosure 14 days before signing and barring title transfer for 30 days after; also enacts the Uniform Mortgage Modification Act.

mo:SB 835.title: Relating to garnishments
mo:SB 835.summary: Raises the homestead exemption from $15,000 to $40,000 and other exemptions from attachment, sets three circuit judges in the 25th circuit, changes execution and garnishment procedures, and replaces the anti-SLAPP law with the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act.

mo:SB 838.title: Relating to the renewable energy standard
mo:SB 838.summary: As an amendment, bars an electrical corporation from demanding any service charge based on construction-work-in-progress costs for a nuclear power generating facility.

mo:SB 863.title: Relating to statewide activities associations
mo:SB 863.summary: Creates a five-member Interscholastic Athletic Oversight Commission, starting in 2027-28, to hear appeals of activities association decisions on transfer eligibility for athletic purposes and on contests and contest procedures.

mo:SB 878.title: Relating to the duties of a pharmacist
mo:SB 878.summary: Lets pharmacists dispense ivermectin and hydroxychloroquine without a prescription under board of pharmacy protocols, requires health plans with maternity benefits to cover prescribed home blood pressure monitors for pregnant and postpartum women, and bars carriers and pharmacy benefit managers from discriminating against 340B entities.

mo:SB 889.title: Relating to repealing expired, terminated, sunset, and obsolete statutes
mo:SB 889.summary: Repeals or edits more than 200 Missouri statute sections to remove expired, terminated, sunset and obsolete provisions.

mo:SB 890.title: Relating to obsolete administrative entities
mo:SB 890.summary: Eliminates or merges obsolete state boards, moving workforce development duties to the Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development and life sciences research grants to the Department of Economic Development, and requires reports on inactive entities.

mo:SB 895.title: Relating to professional licensing
mo:SB 895.summary: Changes professional licensing, including converting interior designer registration to licensure under the architects' chapter, creating a temporary license for people with three years of out-of-state experience in unlicensed occupations, and changing physician and social worker licensing rules.

mo:SB 903.title: Relating to telecommunications infrastructure
mo:SB 903.summary: Makes knowingly possessing copper, brass, aluminum, fiber or telecommunications material a class E felony unless the person is an owner, utility, telecom provider, scrap dealer or other listed authorized person; sets graded penalties for reckless damage to critical infrastructure and updates the facility definition.

mo:SB 905.title: Relating to a training program for Missouri rangers
mo:SB 905.summary: Directs the POST commission to create a Missouri Rangers training program of up to 160 hours with a fitness test; rangers employed by schools get limited arrest powers on school property and may carry firearms if the school authorizes.

mo:SB 913.title: Relating to tax credits
mo:SB 913.summary: Extends the end dates of several tax credits and programs, including those for meat processing, biodiesel, wood energy, urban farms and specialty agricultural crops, from 2028 to 2033, and creates a railroad track and rail infrastructure tax credit.

mo:SB 914.title: Relating to sewage regulation
mo:SB 914.summary: Changes on-site sewage rules to base the state standard on soil properties and soil evaluations by registered evaluators instead of percolation rates, and has the health department set construction permit application requirements and fees.

mo:SB 916.title: Relating to liability of private contractors
mo:SB 916.summary: Creates a statutory cause of action against Department of Transportation contractors and engineers, replacing common-law claims, for periods before construction starts and after the department accepts the work; makes the department solely liable then; bars requiring contractors to indemnify the state.

mo:SB 937.title: Relating to the conveyance of certain state property
mo:SB 937.summary: Authorizes the governor to sell or convey state-owned property, and grant one easement, in 17 separate transfers, including in Harrisonville, Springfield, Jefferson City, Joplin and Kirksville.

mo:SB 938.title: Relating to land surveying
mo:SB 938.summary: Raises the county recorder user fee on recorded instruments from $4 to $6, increasing the share kept in the recorder's fund from $2 to $3 and the portion credited to the state land survey fund from $1 to $2.

mo:SB 944.title: Relating to compensation for the attorney of the sheriff of the city of St
mo:SB 944.summary: Lets the St. Louis city sheriff set the pay of the sheriff's attorney, replacing the current $3,000 to $15,000 yearly range.

mo:SB 945.title: Relating to court filing surcharges
mo:SB 945.summary: Repeals an expired provision that let certain first-class counties add a $10 civil case filing surcharge through 2019; the $15 general limit, or $20 in Jackson County, St. Louis and some other circuits, stays.

mo:SB 953.title: Relating to the expenditure of moneys in certain funds by the department of natural resources
mo:SB 953.summary: Changes Department of Natural Resources programs, including dropping the income-source restriction on Clean Water Commission members, giving holders of Army Corps reservoir storage rights to their return flows, and changing emissions inspection fee and Natural Resources Protection Fund provisions.

mo:SB 959.title: Relating to the Missouri geospatial advisory council
mo:SB 959.summary: Establishes the Missouri GIS Advisory Council within the Office of Administration to advise the state on a statewide geospatial data infrastructure, with members from state agencies and other subject-matter experts.

mo:SB 974.title: Relating to compensation for services rendered in veterans benefits matters
mo:SB 974.summary: Bars compensation for referring veterans to benefits help or for services on claims filed within one year of release from active duty, requires written contingent-fee agreements, and creates a Cybersecurity Mission Act for the National Guard and a living organ donor program for Guard members.

mo:SB 975.title: Relating to ambulance districts
mo:SB 975.summary: Lets county commissions provide for at-large election of ambulance district directors, sets first elections on the next regular election date, changes how board vacancies are filled, and sets a consolidation process with a vote only if enough voters object.

mo:SB 977.title: Relating to application of foreign law
mo:SB 977.summary: Bars state and local government from enforcing rules of the World Health Organization, United Nations or other international bodies, and voids court rulings and contracts applying foreign law that denies parties fundamental rights.

mo:SB 98.title: Relating to the fraudulent use of accounts with a financial institution
mo:SB 98.summary: Changes banking and finance laws, including a Virtual Currency Kiosk Consumer Protection Act, a new offense of financial institution account fraud, trusted contacts for bank customers, campaign cash-contribution rules, and some income tax credit and filing provisions.

mo:SB 991.title: Relating to interior designers
mo:SB 991.summary: Replaces the registered interior designer title with licensed interior designer, moves regulation to the board for architects, engineers, land surveyors and landscape architects, and defines licensed practice by interior alteration or construction projects.

mo:SB 999.title: Relating to abortion
mo:SB 999.summary: Revises assault and stalking offenses; creates cyberharassment, cyberstalking, intimate digital depiction and sadistic online exploitation offenses; requires providers to give a child born alive after an abortion the same care as other children born alive; makes knowingly killing such a child first-degree murder, not second-degree.

mo:SCR 1.title: Relating to the Inaugural Committee
mo:SCR 1.summary: Directs the Senate and House leaders to appoint a 36-member committee, half from each chamber, to plan the General Assembly's role in the January 13, 2025 inauguration of state executive officials.

mo:SCR 2.title: SCR 2
mo:SCR 2.summary: Commemorates the 30th anniversary of the Srebrenica genocide, designates July 11, 2025 as Srebrenica Genocide Remembrance Day in Missouri, and honors victims, survivors and the state's Bosnian community.

mo:SCR 3.title: Relating to missions of institutions of higher education
mo:SCR 3.summary: Approves Missouri Southern State University's mission change, adding health and life sciences and immersive learning experiences to its existing statewide mission in international or global education.

mo:SJR 40.title: Relating to sheriffs
mo:SJR 40.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment requiring most counties to elect a sheriff as chief law enforcement officer, listing the sheriff's duties and allowing removal only by a quo warranto writ brought by the attorney general.

mo:SJR 87.title: Relating to sheriffs
mo:SJR 87.summary: Submits to voters an amendment requiring most counties to elect a sheriff to a four-year term as chief law enforcement officer, with set duties such as jailing felons and attending circuit court, removable only by quo warranto writ initiated by the attorney general.

mo:SJR 95.title: Relating to creation of a sovereign wealth fund for the state of Missouri
mo:SJR 95.summary: Submits to voters an amendment creating the Show-Me Prosperity Fund, invested in S&P 500 index funds. Once its earnings can replace the revenue, appropriations capped at 3% of its five-year average value may be used solely to eliminate state income, sales, corporate and other taxes.

ms:HB 1.title: Appropriation; Department of Human Services to establish and implement youth diversion program.
ms:HB 1.summary: Revises the purpose of an existing $1.5 million Capital Expense Fund appropriation to the Department of Human Services so it funds establishing and implementing the youth diversion program.

ms:HB 2.title: Appropriation; Department of Human Services of.
ms:HB 2.summary: Appropriates $12 million to renovate and expand the Oakley Youth Development Center, $7.5 million for statewide youth diversion programs, and $10 million to the Department of Public Safety for secured youth detention facilities in North and South Mississippi.

ms:SB 2001.title: The Mississippi Youth Court Reform Act of 2026; enact.
ms:SB 2001.summary: Creates youth court divisions in chancery courts, abolishes county-court youth divisions unless counties opt out, opens youth court hearings to the public with exceptions, authorizes expungement of delinquency records, and creates a Family Services Forum.

mt:HB 182.title: Provide grant funding for senior citizen centers
mt:HB 182.summary: Creates a senior citizen center grant program, with up to $5 million in grants to nonprofits for construction, repair and equipment, with matching funds required for grants of $25,000 or more.

mt:HB 2.title: General Appropriations Act
mt:HB 2.summary: Appropriates money to state agencies for the two-year period ending June 30, 2027.

mt:HB 202.title: Generally revise laws related to the unlawful use of aircraft for hunting
mt:HB 202.summary: Adds game birds to species protected from aircraft-assisted hunting, lengthens the waiting period after aircraft use, bans possessing drones while hunting, and raises fines to $3,000-$10,000.

mt:HB 259.title: Revise fish and wildlife  commission techniques for gray wolf management
mt:HB 259.summary: Requires the Fish and Wildlife Commission to apply different gray wolf management techniques by region, and allows infrared and thermal scopes when hunting wolves on private land outside daylight hours.

mt:HB 283.title: Revise laws for hunting licenses lotteries
mt:HB 283.summary: Lets the Fish and Wildlife Commission issue its one annual male mountain sheep license and one Shiras moose license by lottery as well as by auction.

mt:HB 339.title: Fund 6th graders in middle school at high school ANB rates along with 7th and 8th graders
mt:HB 339.summary: Funds 6th graders in accredited middle school or junior high programs at the midpoint between elementary and high school per-student rates, as 7th and 8th graders are, and adds funding for career and technical education.

mt:HB 340.title: Establish Montana's BEST program to bolster educator support and training
mt:HB 340.summary: Creates the Montana B.E.S.T. program giving training and support to teachers in their first three years, including mentor stipends, with a $1 million a year appropriation.

mt:HB 368.title: Generally revise water supply requirements for coal-fired generating units
mt:HB 368.summary: Creates the Town of Colstrip Water Infrastructure Mitigation Account, funded with $2 million a year of coal severance tax revenue, to pay for a town water supply if the nearby coal-fired generating unit closes and the town cannot access water.

mt:HB 4.title: Appropriations by budget amendment
mt:HB 4.summary: Appropriates money normally handled by budget amendment to state agencies for fiscal 2025, lets some appropriations continue into 2026 and 2027, and provides for fund transfers.

mt:HB 419.title: Implementing cost reporting for certain Medicaid service provider types
mt:HB 419.summary: Establishes a standardized cost reporting process for certain Medicaid service providers and appropriates $600,000 in state and $600,000 in federal funds for the related rate-adequacy report.

mt:HB 456.title: Provide best beginnings scholarships to child care workers
mt:HB 456.summary: Expands the Best Beginnings child care scholarship program to child-care workers at licensed day-care centers and registered family or group day-care homes with household income under twice the state median, appropriating $5.5 million a year.

mt:HB 499.title: Extend the grow your own grant program
mt:HB 499.summary: Extends the Grow Your Own grant program, makes postsecondary institutions eligible, revises high school credit requirements, and appropriates $500,000.

mt:HB 5.title: Long-range building appropriations
mt:HB 5.summary: Appropriates money for major repair and capital development projects for the biennium ending June 30, 2027, and raises certain long-range building program value thresholds from $150,000 to $300,000.

mt:HB 511.title: Provide grant funding for firefighting training facilities
mt:HB 511.summary: Creates a firefighting training facility grant program, with up to $5 million in grants to local firefighting authorities for construction, repair and equipment, requiring one-to-one matching funds.

mt:HB 551.title: Eliminate reduced-price copayments for school lunch and breakfast
mt:HB 551.summary: Creates a state program, funded at $600,000 a year, to replace funding for school districts that eliminate reduced-price copayments for school lunch and breakfast.

mt:HB 585.title: Revise provider rate laws for physical therapists, speech-language pathologists, and occupational therapists
mt:HB 585.summary: Sets Medicaid fees for physical, speech-language and occupational therapist services as a conversion factor ($39.56 in fiscal 2026) times relative value units; the department may raise the factor later in line with the medical care price index.

mt:HB 610.title: Revise preauthorization laws relating to healthcare
mt:HB 610.summary: Bars the health department from requiring Medicaid prior authorization for FDA-approved antipsychotic drugs, for approved uses, for members 18 and older.

mt:HB 628.title: Revise early literacy targeted intervention laws
mt:HB 628.summary: Expands the early literacy targeted intervention program to include scholastic literacy and lets school districts opt in to enrolling on-target students, up to one per five eligible students, in some interventions.

mt:HB 643.title: Revise reimbursement costs to detention centers holding inmates in state custody
mt:HB 643.summary: Redefines the 'actual costs' counties charge for holding other agencies' inmates as the greater of a private-facility daily rate less 10% or $82, and appropriates $6 million to reimburse counties for holding people awaiting mental evaluation or placement.

mt:HB 722.title: Provide a retention period for electronic communications after a public employee's employment ends
mt:HB 722.summary: Requires public agencies to keep a public employee's email account communications for at least one year after the employee's last day of employment.

mt:HB 762.title: Require the department of fish, wildlife, and parks to publish a report on river usage
mt:HB 762.summary: Requires the Department of Fish, Wildlife and Parks to publish a biennial river-use report, paid from the state park account, and appropriates $2.6 million.

mt:HB 810.title: Revise tenant landlord laws
mt:HB 810.summary: Specifies acceptable forms of rent payment (cash, check, electronic or other agreed forms) and bars landlords from charging extra fees based on payment type, except to recoup an electronic bank fee for electronic payments.

mt:HB 831.title: Increase elderly homeowner and renter income tax credit
mt:HB 831.summary: Increases the elderly homeowner and renter income tax credit, changes the definition of household income and the credit phaseout, and adds an inflation adjustment to the phaseout income level.

mt:HB 832.title: Establish PTSD nonmedication therapy training grant program
mt:HB 832.summary: Creates a grant program to train providers in posttraumatic stress disorder therapies that do not use medication, appropriating $600,000.

mt:HB 850.title: Provide licensing and regulation of community health workers
mt:HB 850.summary: Requires community health workers to be licensed by the Department of Labor and Industry; applicants must be 18 or older, complete a training program and supervised experience or show equivalent experience, and pay fees, with requirements set by rule.

mt:HB 860.title: Provide for veterinary training loan program
mt:HB 860.summary: Creates a veterinary training loan program giving loans up to $100,000 to students who commit to practicing in underserved Montana areas, with repayment if they do not, and with forgiven loans not counted as income.

mt:HB 861.title: Provide statewide access to a K-12 digital toolkit
mt:HB 861.summary: Appropriates money for statewide access to a K-12 digital toolkit, $1.1 million a year to the Office of Public Instruction and $750,000 a year to the Department of Labor and Industry.

mt:HB 901.title: Create a fire department health and safety grant program
mt:HB 901.summary: Creates a fire department health and safety grant program funded by charitable donations, with grants up to $10,000 per department and a $10 application fee.

mt:HB 924.title: Generally revise state finance laws
mt:HB 924.summary: Creates the Montana Growth and Opportunity Trust funded by transfers of volatile revenue, accounts for property tax relief, water development, local bridges and early childhood, a property tax credit for certified primary residences, and pension and housing funds.

mt:HB 952.title: Authorizing governor to enter into agreements with tribal governments relating to marijuana
mt:HB 952.summary: Authorizes the governor to enter agreements with tribal governments on marijuana regulation and appropriates $1,000.

mt:SB 167.title: Provide funding for noxious weed trust
mt:SB 167.summary: Transfers $10 million from the general fund to the noxious weed management trust fund and requires one-quarter of the fund's interest and income to stay in the trust fund.

mt:SB 188.title: Revising solar energy policy laws
mt:SB 188.summary: Requires utilities to interconnect shared solar facilities of 50 kilowatts to 5 megawatts and to give subscribing customers on-bill credits, and distinguishes shared solar subscribers from net metering customers.

mt:SB 232.title: Revise state procurement laws related to entitles that are exempt from the RFP process.
mt:SB 232.summary: Applies the Montana Procurement Act to the Board of Investments, except for purchases of securities, and changes the act's list of exempt contracts.

mt:SB 244.title: Revise laws related to health insurance coverage of behavioral health screening
mt:SB 244.summary: Requires individual health insurance policies, HMOs, state employee plans and certain multiple employer plans to cover optional behavioral health screenings and assessments at no out-of-pocket cost to the insured.

mt:SB 394.title: Provide for workers' compensation coverage of PTSD for first responders
mt:SB 394.summary: Allows firefighters, law enforcement officers and emergency care providers to file workers' compensation claims for posttraumatic stress disorder when diagnosed under the DSM and arising from their employment.

mt:SB 40.title: Revise supreme court public records laws by opening deliberations and files to the public
mt:SB 40.summary: Requires the Montana Supreme Court to record its closed deliberation meetings and keep a written record, and makes both available to the public after the case is final, though the court may redact confidential information.

mt:SB 410.title: Provide for Montana genomic security act
mt:SB 410.summary: Bars Montana medical and research facilities from using genetic sequencers or software made by a foreign adversary, bans storing Montanans' genetic data outside the U.S., and requires written consent for remote access from outside the U.S.

mt:SB 422.title: Generally revise laws relating to insurance coverage relating to cancer
mt:SB 422.summary: Bars health insurers that cover advanced or metastatic cancer from requiring an insured person to fail, or prove a history of failing, a different drug before covering an FDA-approved prescription drug that follows national cancer guidelines.

mt:SB 424.title: Revising the disabled veteran property tax assistance program
mt:SB 424.summary: Extends the disabled veteran property tax assistance program to veterans rated 80% to 90% disabled, with property tax rate multipliers of 70% to 90% depending on income.

mt:SB 437.title: Revise definition of sex in Montana law
mt:SB 437.summary: Defines sex in state law by reproductive anatomy as male or female only, defines male, female, man, woman, father and mother on that basis, and says "gender" used alone is a synonym for sex rather than gender identity.

mt:SB 472.title: Revise penalties for violations under 310 permit process
mt:SB 472.summary: Raises the daily civil penalty for violating the 310 stream-permit law from $500 to $5,000, with total limits of $100,000 for a first violation and $250,000 for a second, none after; exempts forest practices allowed under state law.

mt:SB 536.title: Revise contractor gross receipts tax
mt:SB 536.summary: Lets 100%-employee-owned (ESOP) contractors claim refunds of the contractor's gross receipts tax credit, extends the credit carryforward from 5 to 7 years, and lets the credit offset certain real property taxes.

mt:SB 537.title: Generally revise marijuana tax laws
mt:SB 537.summary: Changes how marijuana tax revenue is divided, including 20% to a new habitat legacy account, 31% to law enforcement grants and 6.5% to drug and alcohol prevention, and creates accounts for wildlife highway crossings and land and wildlife stewardship.

mt:SB 72.title: Provide presumptive eligibility for Medicaid coverage of home and community-based services
mt:SB 72.summary: Allows presumptive Medicaid eligibility for certain home and community-based services for people with physical disabilities and older adults after a screening and functional assessment, once per 12 months, with a full application due within 30 days.

mt:SB 96.title: Establish working animal protection act
mt:SB 96.summary: As introduced, bars local governments from enacting ordinances or resolutions that ban, or create an undue hardship for, the use of working animals or animal enterprise in commerce or service.

nc:HB 1035.title: Various Local Election Changes III.
nc:HB 1035.summary: Moves municipal elections to even-numbered years for all municipalities in Catawba and McDowell Counties and several towns starting in 2028, and New Bern in 2030. Also extends some town officers' terms from two to four years and changes New Bern's election method.

nc:HB 1040.title: Pitt-Greenville Airport Authority Changes.
nc:HB 1040.summary: Changes Pitt-Greenville Airport Authority law so the county and city split costs in proportions they set jointly instead of half each, drops the voter-approval limit on using property taxes, and requires both governing bodies to approve land purchases.

nc:HB 1089.title: Const. Amend. Property Tax Levy Limit.
nc:HB 1089.summary: Puts a constitutional amendment on the November 3, 2026 ballot requiring the legislature to pass general laws limiting how much local property tax levies may increase, with possible exceptions.

nc:HB 1094.title: Ferry Division Audit/DOT Omnibus.
nc:HB 1094.summary: Requires a state audit of the DOT Ferry Division and a study of DMV funding, lets drivers renew licenses at any time before expiration, extends the insurance-lapse notice response time from 10 to 30 days, and sets utility relocation reimbursement rules.

nc:HB 1104.title: Improve Involuntary Commitment Process and Enhance Public Safety.
nc:HB 1104.summary: Changes involuntary commitment law, including outpatient commitment criteria and treatment plans; sets capacity restoration services for defendants found incapable to proceed; and orders studies of commitment and of behavioral health care in jails.

nc:HB 1123.title: UNC Omnibus and Capital Contracting Law Changes.
nc:HB 1123.summary: Authorizes four University of North Carolina capital projects financed by bonds, requires 12 months of state residency for admission to the NC School of Science and Mathematics, and changes public construction contract and architect thresholds.

nc:HB 1126.title: 2026 Department of State Treasurer Administrative/Technical/Clarifying Changes.
nc:HB 1126.summary: Amends the Treasurer department bill to make its changes to unclaimed property notices to apparent owners effective December 1, 2026, and its changes to abandoned property reports effective then for property presumed abandoned on or after that date.

nc:HB 116.title: Columbus Co. Bd. of Ed. Partisan.
nc:HB 116.summary: Makes Columbus County school board elections partisan, with five members on staggered four-year terms from residency districts, elected by voters outside the Whiteville city school unit.

nc:HB 1173.title: Jaleeyah's Law.
nc:HB 1173.summary: Changes the definitions of criminal gang member and gang leader, makes it a crime for a gang member to use or carry a firearm during a serious felony, and raises criminal court costs by $30 for costs assessed on or after December 1, 2026.

nc:HB 1220.title: Various Local Provisions IX.
nc:HB 1220.summary: Makes local changes, including repealing Stedman's charter ban on alcohol sales, letting the Madison County sheriff make cross-state law enforcement agreements with three Tennessee sheriffs, and revising the Stanley town manager and council appointment powers.

nc:HB 1222.title: Record Development Approval Votes/Brunswick.
nc:HB 1222.summary: Requires Brunswick County commissioners to make final decisions on special use permits and subdivisions of 25 or more lots by recorded vote, and to require traffic impact analyses for certain projects, outside municipal jurisdictions.

nc:HB 1237.title: Appointments and Corrections.
nc:HB 1237.summary: Appoints and reappoints people to numerous state boards and commissions on recommendations of the Senate leader and House Speaker, and corrects earlier appointments.

nc:HB 133.title: NC Farmland and Military Protection Act.
nc:HB 133.summary: Bars foreign parties tied to adversarial governments from acquiring or holding interests in agricultural land or land within 50 miles of a military installation. Holdings before April 1, 2027 may continue but must be registered; later acquisitions must be sold within one year.

nc:HB 162.title: Parking Lot Reform/Stormwater Control.
nc:HB 162.summary: Bars most local governments outside the coastal area from requiring a minimum number of off-street parking spaces, and lets local governments offer optional incentives for extra stormwater controls. Also changes stormwater rules for existing impervious surface.

nc:HB 169.title: Haywood/Cherokee/Leland Occupancy Tax Modifications.
nc:HB 169.summary: Raises Haywood County's occupancy tax authority from 2% to 6%, changes Cherokee County Tourism Development Authority membership and terms, and removes the nonprofit lodging exemption from Leland's occupancy tax.

nc:HB 198.title: ABC Omnibus of 2026.
nc:HB 198.summary: Allows the ABC Commission to borrow up to $310 million for a new warehouse, creates a service business permit for complimentary malt beverages and wine, lets on-premises permit holders sell up to six original-container drinks per patron at once, and makes other alcohol permit changes.

nc:HB 206.title: DPS/Other Changes.
nc:HB 206.summary: Lets the Air National Guard accept a 50-year land license at Stanly County Airport, raises Crime Victims Compensation weekly caps from $300 to $400, and lets emergency management transfer donated travel trailers to local governments, nonprofits or survivors.

nc:HB 240.title: Currituck/New Hanover Beach Towns/Jacksonville Occupancy Tax.
nc:HB 240.summary: As passed by the House, revises and consolidates the Town of Davidson's charter, setting a mayor and five commissioners, nonpartisan elections in odd-numbered years, and a council-manager form of government.

nc:HB 258.title: Worker Safety Act of 2026.
nc:HB 258.summary: Requires retaliatory employment discrimination complaints filed with the Commissioner of Labor to include ten listed items, gives respondents seven days to submit a defense, and bars considering extraneous material submitted with complaints.

nc:HB 3.title: Various Local Election Changes II.
nc:HB 3.summary: Makes Pitt County school board elections partisan; moves Monroe to even-year partisan elections; moves Pamlico County towns and Simpson to even-year elections; puts partisan Currituck school board elections to a November 2026 vote; changes Cabarrus commissioner vacancy rules.

nc:HB 301.title: Social Media and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety.
nc:HB 301.summary: Requires addictive social media platforms to bar children under 14, require parental consent for ages 14 and 15, and verify age with anonymous or standard methods, with Attorney General enforcement; also adds public school AI literacy standards and AI use policies.

nc:HB 308.title: 2026 Criminal Law Changes.
nc:HB 308.summary: Raises penalties for assault causing serious bodily injury and for strangulation, splits indecent liberties with a child into separate offenses by age and conduct, creates offenses for retail theft tools and approaching a first responder after a warning, and makes other criminal law changes.

nc:HB 315.title: Prohibit Litigation Investments/Amend Workers' Compensation Benefits.
nc:HB 315.summary: Makes it unlawful to provide or engage in litigation investment in civil cases, doubles the maximum workers' compensation payments for disfigurement and loss of body parts, and raises the minimum weekly total-disability rate from $30 to $50.

nc:HB 328.title: Regulate Hemp-Derived Consumables.
nc:HB 328.summary: Creates a licensing and regulation system for hemp-derived consumables, bans sales to people under 21 and sales without a license, requires child-proof exit packaging, and removes school discretion to allow such products on campus.

nc:HB 332.title: Nash/Rocky Mount Occupancy Tax Changes.
nc:HB 332.summary: Repeals Nash County's additional 2% room occupancy tax on October 1, 2026, and creates Rocky Mount District R, covering the city's part of the county, which may levy its own occupancy tax of up to 2% with a tourism authority.

nc:HB 34.title: Strengthen Medicaid Provider Controls.
nc:HB 34.summary: Creates a DHHS Provider Enrollment Credentialing Committee to decide provider enrollment and termination, extends criminal history checks to provider owners, operators and managing employees, and lists grounds for denying or ending Medicaid enrollment, such as false claims.

nc:HB 349.title: Modify Health Care Powers of Attorney/Advance Directives.
nc:HB 349.summary: Lets a health care power of attorney or advance directive be validated by two witnesses or a notary rather than both, and allows electronic filing with the Secretary of State's registry without notarization, adding a HIPAA waiver.

nc:HB 356.title: Various Civil and Insurance Law Changes.
nc:HB 356.summary: Makes insurance and civil law changes, including delaying inexperienced-driver insurance rules to January 1, 2027, revising insurance education licensing, and letting the Commissioner of Banks investigate licensed mortgage businesses.

nc:HB 368.title: Revise Child Passenger Restraint Systems Law.
nc:HB 368.summary: Requires children under 8 and under 57 inches tall to use a height- and weight-appropriate child restraint, rear-facing from birth until the manufacturer's limits, in the rear seat unless an exception applies. Applies to offenses from December 1, 2025.

nc:HB 369.title: Parking Lot Reform/Stormwater Control.
nc:HB 369.summary: Bars local rules requiring minimum off-street parking space counts or spaces over 9 by 20 feet (except handicap, parallel, diagonal), and lets stormwater-permitted local governments require redevelopers to capture up to 50% of runoff or offer incentives, excluding small residential projects.

nc:HB 372.title: Home-Based Business Fairness Act.
nc:HB 372.summary: Bars cities from prohibiting no-impact home-based businesses or requiring permits for them, while allowing narrowly tailored restrictions for health and safety and residential compatibility.

nc:HB 376.title: Various On-Site Wastewater and Well Provisions.
nc:HB 376.summary: Changes on-site wastewater contractor certification and board rules, lets certified private evaluators verify septic installations and issue site-denial letters, and repeals local health-board private well permitting rules except testing standards and fees.

nc:HB 377.title: 2026 Court Changes.
nc:HB 377.summary: Changes court laws, including when juvenile records may be disclosed, giving any attorney of record access to the trial file in indigent appeals, assigning superior court judges to districts with a county over 1 million people, and Judicial Standards Commission definitions.

nc:HB 381.title: On-Site Wastewater System Amendments.
nc:HB 381.summary: Lets makers of advanced pretreatment wastewater systems seek innovative-system status through a nationally recognized certification body's approval, requires DHHS to verify testing data (at least 55 datasets over 26 weeks) and installation plans, and defines advanced pretreatment.

nc:HB 433.title: State Fiscal Recovery Fund/NC Pandemic Recovery Office Revisions.
nc:HB 433.summary: Lets the state budget director reclassify unspent State Fiscal Recovery Fund balances to other eligible government services, allows the Pandemic Recovery Office to reallocate those funds, and extends the date that office ceases operating to May 1, 2027.

nc:HB 437.title: Establish Drug-Free Homeless Service Zones.
nc:HB 437.summary: Makes selling or delivering controlled substances in a signed drug-free homeless service zone (a funded service facility and the area within 100 feet) a Class E felony, and makes operators who intentionally allow it a Class H felony.

nc:HB 481.title: Pay Exceptions/Special Separation Allowance.
nc:HB 481.summary: Changes the special separation allowance for retired officers so a break in service due to retirement pay does not affect eligibility if the officer returns within 45 days, and stops payments on reemployment in certain state positions.

nc:HB 517.title: Modify Nonprofit Corporations Act/Charitable Organizations.
nc:HB 517.summary: Changes the nonprofit corporation law: allows new kinds of mergers and asset sales, requires annual reports to the Secretary of State, allows domestication, requires new nonprofit boards to have at least 3 natural persons, and aligns charity disclosures with federal rules.

nc:HB 536.title: Physical Therapy Practice Act Modifications.
nc:HB 536.summary: Lets the Board of Physical Therapy Examiners restrict licenses and discipline therapists for departing from recognized practice and ethics standards, and changes Board removal rules and the definition of physical therapy.

nc:HB 56.title: 2026 Budget Technical Corrections.
nc:HB 56.summary: Makes technical and clarifying changes to the 2026 budget act and other acts, including Hurricane Helene fund transfers, school facility funding cross references, and the principal salary schedule.

nc:HB 562.title: Budget Technical Corrections Modifications.
nc:HB 562.summary: Adjusts the 2026 budget act: redirects several directed grants, moves authorization of the America's Semiquincentennial license plate into GS 20-63, delays an insurance regulatory charge change to 2027, and appropriates $225,000 for State Fire Marshal and $300,000 for Labor Department positions.

nc:HB 565.title: Limit Use of AI Medicaid/Commercial Insurance.
nc:HB 565.summary: As amended in committee in April 2025, adds an organ and tissue donation election to North Carolina income tax return forms for resident taxpayers and spouses, and lets the Department of Revenue share elections with the DMV and organ procurement organizations.

nc:HB 727.title: Limit Medicaid Reimb. for Facility Fees.
nc:HB 727.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to stop Medicaid from reimbursing facility fees unless the service is provided at a hospital's main building or nearby structures, a facility with an emergency department, or an ambulatory surgical facility.

nc:HB 747.title: 2026 Wildlife Resources Changes.
nc:HB 747.summary: Makes locations of rare species confidential when disclosure risks harm, creates wildlife-themed license plates, changes out-of-state boat numbering rules, and requires one elk permit by raffle and one by auction for the 2027 hunting season.

nc:HB 83.title: Revise Laws on Minors/Human Trafficking.
nc:HB 83.summary: Removes the under-16 limit from the felony of giving obscene material to a minor when the person is 18 or older and at least four years older, lets courts order sex offender registration for such offenses, and orders a human trafficking reporting study.

nc:HB 832.title: Education Omnibus.
nc:HB 832.summary: As amended by the Senate, makes K-12 changes, including adding English Language Arts to advanced courses with automatic enrollment for top test scorers, removing limits on school units contracting with private providers, creating a Community Eligibility meal incentive program, and changing principal licensing.

nc:HB 834.title: State Board of Elections Administrative Changes.
nc:HB 834.summary: Amends the absentee-ballot statute in the elections bill so ballots transmitted to county boards under that statute or under federal law are counted, and requires State Board rules implementing it to be consistent with federal law.

nc:HB 87.title: Educational Choice for Children Act (ECCA).
nc:HB 87.summary: Opts North Carolina into the federal tax credit for donations to scholarship granting organizations, and directs the State Education Assistance Authority to list qualifying organizations and carry out the state's participation.

nc:HB 920.title: Virtual Currency Kiosk Consumer Protection Act.
nc:HB 920.summary: Sets rules for virtual currency kiosks, requiring operators to give customers risk and fee disclosures, capping fees at 12% of the transaction, and directing the Commissioner of Banks to develop fraud rules, effective January 1, 2027.

nc:HB 936.title: Robocall Solicitation Modifications.
nc:HB 936.summary: Applies state telephone solicitation rules to robocalls and text messages, requires prior express written consent for solicitations, bans impersonating government officials in them, and counts civil penalties per violation within a single solicitation.

nc:HB 958.title: Election Law Changes.
nc:HB 958.summary: Changes election law, including shortening early voting for primaries and runoffs, requiring county boards to remove deceased voters within a week of receiving federal lists, and making other-state voter data non-public.

nc:HB 96.title: Expedited Removal of Unauthorized Persons.
nc:HB 96.summary: Lets a property owner start an expedited court process to remove an unauthorized person occupying residential property, with a hearing no later than 48 hours after service.

nc:HJR 1241.title: Honor Louis Milford Pate Jr.
nc:HJR 1241.summary: Honors the life of Louis Milford Pate Jr., a state senator and former House member, and extends the General Assembly's sympathy to his family.

nc:HJR 2.title: Adjourn 2026 First Extra Session Sine Die.
