nd:SB 2037.title: AN ACT to create and enact three new sections to chapter 27-20.4 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to juvenile court petitions, fitness to proceed in juvenile court proceedings, and collateral consequences the juvenile court may order; to amend and reenact sections 12.1-04.1-01, 12.1-04.1-20, and 12.1-17-01.2, subsection 2 of section 12.1-17-07.2, section 12.1-20-01, subsections 2 and 6 of section 12.1-31-03, sections 12.1-32-15 and 15.1-09-33.4, subsection 6 of section 27-20.2-01, subsection 3 of section 27-20.2-09, subsection 5 of section 27-20.4-11, subsection 1 of section 27-20.4-18, subsection 1 of section 27-20.4-20, and section 62.1-02-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to lack of criminal responsibility, court jurisdiction, distribution of intimate images without consent, domestic violence, criminality of a child regarding sex offenses, sale and use of tobacco by an individual under the age of twenty-one, child registration requirements, restitution, probation of a delinquent child, extracurricular activities for students, and persons not allowed to possess a firearm; to repeal sections 27-20.4-12, 27-20.4-13, and 27-20.4-19 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to delinquency; to provide an appropriation; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2037.summary: Lets children ten or older be assessed for lack of criminal responsibility, sets one-year court jurisdiction over a juvenile not adjudicated for that reason, appropriates $300,000 for evaluations, and revises other juvenile justice provisions.

nd:SB 2051.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 43-30-16 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to fees charged by the North Dakota private investigative and security board; to provide for a performance audit of the North Dakota private investigative and security board; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2051.summary: Raises maximum fees the Private Investigative and Security Board may charge, for example from $150 to $225 for an individual license, and requires a performance audit of the board.

nd:SB 2070.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 50-10.2-01, 50-10.2-02, and 50-10.2-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the rights of health care facility residents.
nd:SB 2070.summary: Revises resident rights in nursing, basic care and assisted living facilities, lets residents use their own technology and virtual-monitoring devices, and changes the rules for in-room recording devices, including consent, notice and costs.

nd:SB 2082.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subsection 2 of section 37-17.1-07.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the state's hazardous chemical fee system.
nd:SB 2082.summary: Replaces the fixed $25 per-chemical hazardous chemical fee with fees set by the homeland security director, caps per-chemical increases after January 1, 2026 at $5 a year with a year's notice, and raises the maximum annual fee per facility from $475 to $950.

nd:SB 2086.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 4.1-33 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to pesticide certification standards; and to amend and reenact sections 4.1-33-01 and 4.1-33-03, subdivision b of subsection 1 of section 4.1-33-12, section 4.1-33-13, subsection 1 of section 4.1-33-16, and subsection 5 of section 4.1-33-20 of North Dakota Century Code, relating to pesticide control.
nd:SB 2086.summary: Incorporates federal Environmental Protection Agency pesticide certification standards into state law and requires the state pesticide control board to adopt those standards in its rules for certifying pesticide applicators.

nd:SB 2093.title: A BILL for an Act to amend and reenact subdivision u of subsection 2 of section 57-38-30.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an income tax deduction for retired law enforcement personnel benefits; and to provide for retroactive application.
nd:SB 2093.summary: Raises the income thresholds of the 0%, 1.95% and 2.5% state income tax brackets for individuals, estates and trusts starting with tax year 2025, and extends the retired peace officer benefits deduction to surviving spouses, retroactive to tax year 2024.

nd:SB 2112.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 25-04-00.1, 25-04-02, 25-04-04, 25-04-04.1, 25-04-05, 25-04-05.1, 25-04-08, 25-04-08.1, 25-04-14, and 25-04-17 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the life skills and transition center; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide for a department of health and human services study; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2112.summary: Lets the Life Skills and Transition Center serve eligible people with developmental disabilities in crisis, and noneligible minors for up to 90 days (extendable 90 more). Requires six-month reports and a study of alternatives to placement there.

nd:SB 2113.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 50-06 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to certified community behavioral health clinics and the financing of health and human services; to amend and reenact section 12.1-04-06, subsection 4 of section 20.1-03-04, sections 25-03.1-03.1 and 25-03.1-04, subsection 3 of section 25-03.1-08, section 25-03.1-10, subsection 3 of section 25-03.1-11, subsection 1 of section 25-03.1-19, subsection 2 of section 25-03.1-26, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 26.1-36-08, subdivisions c and d of subsection 2 of section 26.1-36-09, subsection 9 of section 43-12.1-04, subsection 6 of section 43-41-02, subdivision b of subsection 1 of section 44-04-18.30, sections 50-06-01, 50-06-01.4, 50-06-01.7, 50-06-05.1, 50-06-05.2, 50-06-05.3, 50-06-05.4, 50-06-05.5, 50-06-06.2, 50-06-06.5, and 50-06-06.13, subsections 1 and 3 of section 50-06-15, sections 50-06-33 and 50-06-41.3, subsection 1 of section 50-06-42, subsection 1 of section 50-06-42.1, and sections 50-06-46, 50-06.2-01, 50-06.2-02, 50-06.2-03, 50-06.3-02, and 50-06.3-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the powers and duties of the department of health and human services, treatment hearing timelines, and membership of the cross-disability advisory council; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2113.summary: Requires state certification of certified community behavioral health clinics, creates a health and human services operating special fund, renames regional human service centers as state-operated behavioral health clinics, and changes treatment hearing timelines and other behavioral health laws.

nd:SB 2129.title: AN ACT to create and enact ten new sections to chapter 43-29 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the practice of veterinary medicine, veterinary technology, and recognized animal services; to amend and reenact section 43-29-01.1, subsection 1 of section 43-29-02, sections 43-29-03, 43-29-04, 43-29-05, 43-29-05.1, 43-29-06, 43-29-07, 43-29-07.1, 43-29-07.2, 43-29-07.3, 43-29-08.1, 43-29-13, 43-29-14, and 43-29-15, subsection 2 of section 43-29-16, sections 43-29-16.1 and 43-29-17, and subsection 2 of section 43-29-19 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the practice of veterinary medicine and veterinary technology; to repeal sections 43-29-09, 43-29-10, 43-29-11, and 43-29-12.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the practice of veterinary medicine and veterinary technology; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2129.summary: Revises veterinary practice law, covering veterinarian-client-patient relationships, veterinary telemedicine, accreditation standards for veterinary schools, veterinary technician duties and licensing, and recognized animal services.

nd:SB 2155.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subsection 5 of section 20.1-03-11 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to gratis antelope licenses.
nd:SB 2155.summary: Limits free antelope licenses for landowners and operators of 150 or more acres to one-half of the licenses in a hunting unit, and lets unsuccessful applicants be entered in the lottery for remaining licenses.

nd:SB 2159.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 15-11-40 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to projects the state energy research center is permitted to pursue.
nd:SB 2159.summary: Allows the state energy research center at UND to pursue research or projects on above-ground exploration, storage, treatment or disposal of high-level radioactive waste only if approved by the Industrial Commission in consultation with the high-level radioactive waste advisory council.

nd:SB 2160.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 54-52.1-01, 54-52.1-02, and 54-52.1-03.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to health insurance benefits coverage provided by the uniform group insurance program; to provide an appropriation; to provide for a statement of legislative intent; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2160.summary: Requires the state employee health plan to meet federal rules for non-grandfathered large-employer plans starting January 1, 2027, and appropriates $1.44 million from the general fund and $1.85 million from other funds toward resulting premium increases.

nd:SB 2180.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 44-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the opportunity to provide public comment at a meeting of a public entity.
nd:SB 2180.summary: Requires regular meetings of city, county, township, school, park and water resource district boards to include time for public comment, which boards may limit by time per speaker or by agenda topic. Speakers must give their name and address in writing.

nd:SB 2186.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 14-09 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to interference with court-ordered parenting time; to create a child custody review task force; to provide for a legislative management report; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2186.summary: Requires courts that find a parent intentionally interfered with parenting time to order make-up time, unless clear and convincing evidence shows otherwise, of at least the time lost and up to double it, within two years. Creates an interim custody review task force.

nd:SB 2188.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 54-63.1-03 and 54-63.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the membership of the clean sustainable energy authority and the clean sustainable energy fund line of credit; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:SB 2188.summary: Adds the Department of Water Resources director as a nonvoting advisor, making the Clean Sustainable Energy Authority 18 members (nine voting, nine nonvoting), and extends the energy fund's line-of-credit access and repayment date from June 30, 2025 to 2029.

nd:SB 2213.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-13 and two new sections to chapter 15.1-21 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to mathematics curriculum, professional development, screening and intervention, related administrative rules and reporting requirements, and mathematics instructor competency; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide for a department of public instruction mathematics screening pilot program; to provide an appropriation; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2213.summary: Requires teaching candidates for elementary and secondary math to show competence in explicit math instruction, and sets math curriculum, professional development and screening requirements, a screening pilot program and a funding appropriation.

nd:SB 2225.title: A BILL for an Act to provide an appropriation to the department of commerce for a housing for opportunity, mobility, and empowerment program; to provide for a legislative management report; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2225.summary: As amended, appropriates $5 million from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the Department of Commerce for slum and blight removal grants to political subdivisions in communities under 4,500 people, requires dollar-for-dollar nonstate matching funds, and requires a report by June 30, 2026.

nd:SB 2226.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 54-61-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the commission on legal counsel for indigents; to provide an appropriation; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2226.summary: Presumes an incarcerated person indigent for setting release conditions at an initial appearance, effective January 1, 2026, and appropriates $463,644 to the indigent defense commission for counsel at initial appearances through June 2027.

nd:SB 2230.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 16.1-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the secretary of state's duty to distribute educational and informational materials before an election; to provide an appropriation; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2230.summary: Requires the secretary of state to distribute information on each statewide ballot measure, including a summary, fiscal impact and an analysis of voting for and against, to active voters at least 45 days before the election. Appropriates $600,000.

nd:SB 2232.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 50-25.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an exemption for postpartum exposure to controlled substances and alcohol; to amend and reenact sections 50-25.1-16 and 50-25.1-17 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to reporting requirements for prenatal exposure to controlled substances and alcohol abuse and toxicology test requirements; and to repeal section 50-25.1-18 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to reporting requirements for prenatal exposure to alcohol misuse.
nd:SB 2232.summary: Exempts mandated reporters from reporting prenatal or postpartum substance use or alcohol misuse while they provide or coordinate care or treatment, unless the woman stops care, fails to follow treatment, or continues use. Makes physicians' toxicology tests and test-result reports optional.

nd:SB 2241.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new chapter to title 15.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the authorization and administration of public charter schools; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:SB 2241.summary: Creates public charter schools in North Dakota, authorized and overseen by the superintendent of public instruction through charter performance agreements. Sets open enrollment with a lottery when oversubscribed, and requires reports to legislative management.

nd:SB 2251.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 54-10-01, subsection 5 of section 54-10-14, and sections 54-10-22 and 54-10-27 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to audits conducted by the state auditor and charges for audits.
nd:SB 2251.summary: Bars the State Auditor from charging audit fees to institutions under the state board of higher education, except for cost recovery on federal programs, and lets the auditor refer public-records requests about submitted information back to the submitting entity.

nd:SB 2262.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 15.1-01-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the authority for the kindergarten through grade twelve education coordination council to enter contracts; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:SB 2262.summary: Lets the K-12 Education Coordination Council contract for studies, and appropriates $60,000 from the general fund to the superintendent of public instruction for those contracts in 2025-27.

nd:SB 2267.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new chapter to title 23.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to onsite wastewater treatment systems; to amend and reenact sections 23-35-02 and 23-35-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the powers and duties of the boards of health and public health units; to repeal sections 23-35-02.2 and 23-35-02.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the onsite wastewater recycling technical committee; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide a penalty; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:SB 2267.summary: Creates a state license for septic-system installers, gives the Department of Environmental Quality exclusive rulemaking authority over septic permitting and inspection (conflicting local ordinances are void), and sets civil penalties up to $12,500 per violation. Public health units must inspect within one business day.

nd:SB 2276.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 61-16.1-11, 61-16.1-15.1, and 61-16.1-59 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the joint exercise of powers of joint water resource boards, mandating the formation of joint water resource boards for projects affecting two or more counties, and proceedings to confirm special actions.
nd:SB 2276.summary: Requires water resource districts in five major river basins to form joint water resource boards, and requires a joint board for projects spanning counties; sets mediation and state appeal steps for board disputes and allows court action against uncooperative boards.

nd:SB 2282.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 57-38 and new subdivision to subsection 7 of section 57-38-30.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an income tax credit for child care contributions provided by qualified employers; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2282.summary: Creates an income tax credit for employers equal to 50% of child care contributions made for employees, counting up to $1,000 per employee, for tax years after 2024; the employer must offer an equal contribution to all employees with child care costs.

nd:SB 2291.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 30.1-28 and two new sections to chapter 30.1-29 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to removal, resignation and death of a guardian, notices in a guardianship, notices in a conservatorship, and confidentiality of reports; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 23-12-13, subsection 1 of section 25-03.1-18.1, subsection 1 of section 27-20.1-17, sections 30.1-01-06 and 30.1-28-03.1, subsection 3 of section 30.1-28-03.2, section 30.1-28-04, subsection 1 of section 30.1-28-05, section 30.1-28-07, subsection 1 of section 30.1-28-09, sections 30.1-28-10.1, 30.1-28-12, 30.1-28-12.1, 30.1-28-12.2, and 30.1-29-05, subsection 6 of section 30.1-29-07, subsection 2 of section 30.1-29-08, sections 30.1-29-13 and 30.1-29-18, subsection 3 of section 30.1-29-19, subsection 1 of section 30.1-29-20.1, subsection 2 of section 30.1-29-22, and subsection 5 of section 30.1-29-25 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to incapacitated persons, court-authorized involuntary treatment, guardianship of a child, guardianship of an incapacitated person, and protection of property of persons under disability and minors; and to repeal sections 30.1-26-01, 30.1-28-08, and 30.1-28-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to visitors in a guardianship proceeding and appointment of successor guardians.
nd:SB 2291.summary: Revises guardianship and conservatorship law, adding procedures for removing, replacing, or ending a guardian's service, notice requirements after appointment, and confidentiality rules for reports.

nd:SB 2294.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 19-24.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to qualifying nonresident medical marijuana patients; to amend and reenact subsection 3 of section 19-24.1-01, subsection 4 of section 19-24.1-01, subsection 8 of section 19-24.1-01, subsection 26 of section 19-24.1-01, subsection 47 of section 19-24.1-01, and sections 19-24.1-03, 19-24.1-11, and 19-24.1-37 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to allowable amounts of usable medical marijuana, medical marijuana recordkeeping, cannabinoid edible products, patient qualifications, and disclosure of information.
nd:SB 2294.summary: Lets nonresidents with a valid out-of-state medical marijuana card get a 60-day North Dakota registry card, makes registry cards valid for two years, raises the application fee cap from $25 to $40, and changes the rules for cannabinoid edible products.

nd:SB 2297.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subsection 3 of section 23-06.5-03 and section 23-12-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the determination of incapacity and informed consent of incapacitated patients and minors.
nd:SB 2297.summary: Changes who may give informed consent for incapacitated adult patients, adding an interdisciplinary team of at least three health care professionals as a last option, and requires written certification of incapacity for a health care directive to take effect.

nd:SB 2307.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 12.1-27.1-01 and two new sections to chapter 12.1-27.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the definition of a public library, required safety policies and technology protection measures, and the state's attorney's review of public libraries, school districts, and state agencies for compliance with statutes protecting minors from explicit sexual material; to amend and reenact subsection 5 of section 12.1-27.1-01, subsection 2 of section 12.1-27.1-03.1, and sections 12.1-27.1-03.5 and 12.1-27.1-11 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to obscenity control; to provide for a report to the legislative management; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2307.summary: Bars public libraries and school districts from keeping explicit sexual material in any area easily accessible to minors, not just children's collections, and requires K-12 online library databases to filter it. Adds state's attorney review with funding withholding; sets 2026 deadlines.

nd:SB 2308.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 23.1-01, a new section to chapter 54-07, and two new sections to chapter 61-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to standards for well drilling and installation of water well pumps, pitless units, and monitoring wells, a boards review task force, a water well contractors advisory board, and requirements for firms engaged in water well work, installation of water well pump and pitless units, monitoring well work, and drilling of geothermal systems; to amend and reenact section 6-09-43, subdivision j of subsection 2 of section 15.1-01-04, sections 15.1-07-33 and 23-35-02.2, subsection 1 of section 50-06-01.4, sections 52-02-02 and 52-02-08, subsection 1 of section 54-07-01.2, sections 54-54-05, 54-59-26, 54-59-27, 54-59-34, 54-59-36, 54-59-37, 54-59-39, 61-03-01.3, 61-04.1-03, 61-04.1-08, 61-04.1-09, 61-04.1-12, 61-04.1-14, 61-04.1-15, 61-04.1-16, 61-04.1-17, 61-04.1-18, 61-04.1-19, 61-04.1-20, 61-04.1-21, 61-04.1-33, 61-04.1-34, 61-04.1-37, 61-04.1-38, and 61-04.1-39, and subdivision a of subsection 2 of section 65-02-03.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the wastewater recycling treatment guide, boards and commissions, the unemployment insurance advisory council, gubernatorial appointments, the committee on aging, health information technology advisory committee, statewide longitudinal data system committee, atmospheric resource board, the department of health and human services, the council on the arts, the state engineer, the superintendent of public instruction, job service North Dakota, and workforce safety and insurance coordinating committee; to repeal chapter 8-11.1, sections 12-48-06.1, 15.1-37-05, 15.1-37-06, and 15.1-37-08, chapter 17-07, sections 19-24.1-38, 19-24.1-39, and 23-35-02.3, chapters 34-16 and 43-35, sections 50-06-05.6, 50-06.4-10, 50-11.1-25, 50-11.1-26, 50-11.1-27, 52-02-07, 54-34.3-10, 54-54-10, 54-59-25, 54-59-33, 54-59-35, 54-59-38, 54-60-25, 55-01-13, 55-01-14, 61-04.1-04, 61-04.1-05, 61-04.1-06, 61-04.1-07, and 61-04.1-10, and chapter 61-36 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to occupational and professional boards, the midwest interstate passenger rail compact, prison industry advisory committee, energy policy commission, medical marijuana advisory committee, onsite wastewater recycling technical committee, state board of water well contractors, committee on aging, brain injury advisory council, early childhood council, unemployment insurance advisory council, commission on the status of women, health information technology advisory committee, poet laureate nominating board, rural development council, America 250 commission, atmospheric resource board, and Devils Lake outlet management advisory committee; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2308.summary: Repeals statutes for a number of state boards and committees, creates a boards review task force and a water well contractors advisory board, and sets requirements for firms doing water well work.

nd:SB 2327.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 4.1-01.1-07 and 4.1-01.1-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to uses of the agriculture diversification and development fund and committee; to provide an appropriation; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:SB 2327.summary: Changes how the agriculture diversification and development fund and committee operate, including grants for infrastructure for value-added agriculture businesses, and transfers $15 million to the fund for 2025-27.

nd:SB 2330.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-09 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to human trafficking and exploitation prevention and awareness education for students at public schools and tribal schools.
nd:SB 2330.summary: Requires school districts and tribal-run schools to adopt a human trafficking education policy, give schoolwide education to students in grades six, ten and twelve each year, and offer optional workshops or materials to parents.

nd:SB 2339.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new chapter to title 49 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to strict liability and a wildfire mitigation plan of a qualified utility; and to provide for a report.
nd:SB 2339.summary: Bars courts from applying strict liability to electric utilities in wildfire damage lawsuits. Lets utilities file wildfire mitigation plans, updated every two years, and treats following a plan as a rebuttable presumption of reasonable care.

nd:SB 2340.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study to evaluate the evolving fire service operational and response needs of the state.
nd:SB 2340.summary: Directs the Legislative Management to study the state's fire service needs, including regional response teams, training, wildland-urban interface fire codes, and funding less dependent on local property tax, and report to the next Legislature.

nd:SB 2354.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact the new section to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, as created by House Bill No. 1160, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, relating to the use of personal electronic devices in schools providing prekindergarten, elementary, or secondary education.
nd:SB 2354.summary: Amends the school phone law: devices must be turned off, stowed away and inaccessible during instructional time, medical and individualized-plan exceptions remain, and districts must communicate the policy and publish it in handbooks.

nd:SB 2374.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 26.1-30, two new sections to chapter 26.1-39, a new section to chapter 26.1-44, and a new subsection to section 26.1-46-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to mandatory arbitration endorsements for property insurance, managed repair programs, civil remedy actions against property insurers, notice of property insurance claims, and surplus lines insurance policies; to amend and reenact sections 26.1-02-05, 26.1-25-02.1, 26.1-25-16, 26.1-26-04.1, 26.1-44-03, 26.1-46-01, 26.1-46-08, and 26.1-46-08.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to exceptions to unauthorized insurance transactions, exceptions for large commercial risks in fire, property, and casualty insurance rates, surplus lines insurance, risk retention groups and purchasing groups, restrictions on insurance purchased by purchasing groups, and purchasing group taxation and fees; to repeal section 26.1-44-03.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an exemption from search requirements for licensed surplus line producers; to provide for a legislative management report; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2374.summary: Sets property insurance rules: policies may require arbitration only with the insured's separate written acceptance; bad-faith claims need a prior court judgment for breach of contract; reopened claims need notice within one year of loss. Also changes surplus lines and risk retention rules.

nd:SB 2375.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 43-28 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to joint negotiations by dental providers with dental insurers.
nd:SB 2375.summary: Lets dental providers and dental insurers enter voluntary non-fee joint negotiations after notifying the attorney general, who has 90 days to decide whether to authorize them, weighing factors such as market power and anticompetitive risk.

nd:SB 2380.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 51-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a commercial entity's liability for publishing or distributing sexual material harmful to a minor; to provide a penalty; and to provide for application.
nd:SB 2380.summary: Makes a commercial entity that knowingly publishes sexual material harmful to minors on a website where it is over one-third of content liable if it does not verify users are 18 or older; bars keeping identifying data; allows civil suits for damages and injunctions.

nd:SB 2385.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new chapter to title 23 and a new section to chapter 47-32 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to receivers for mobile home parks and a defense to an eviction from a mobile home; to amend and reenact sections 23-10-03, 23-10-04, 23-10-06, 23-10-06.2, 23-10-12, and 47-10-28 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to licensure and regulation of mobile home parks; and to provide a penalty.
nd:SB 2385.summary: Lets courts place a mobile home park whose license was revoked under a receiver, changes mobile home park licensing and inspection rules, and lets tenants defend an eviction by showing the landlord violated certain mobile home park tenant protections.

nd:SB 2387.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 12.1-34 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the rights of sexual violence survivors.
nd:SB 2387.summary: Gives victims of listed sexual offenses rights to consult an advocate during forensic exams (communications privileged), to have private counsel present when speaking with police, to a free copy of the police report, and to an attorney general rights document.

nd:SB 2390.title: AN ACT to create and enact three new sections to chapter 54-40.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a rural catalyst committee, grant program, and fund; to amend and reenact section 54-40.1-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to definitions for regional planning councils; to provide an appropriation; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:SB 2390.summary: Creates a rural catalyst committee, grant program and fund through the Department of Commerce, with grants requiring at least a dollar of non-state matching funds for each state dollar.

nd:SB 2397.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 57-51.1-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a limited exemption for development incentive wells; to amend and reenact sections 57-51-02.6, 57-51-05, and 57-51.1-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the temporary exemption for oil and gas wells employing a system to avoid flaring, an exemption from gross production tax for gas produced from certain enhanced oil recovery projects, and the definition of development incentive well; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2397.summary: Changes oil and gas tax exemptions, including the temporary exemption for wells that avoid flaring, an exemption from gross production tax for gas from certain enhanced oil recovery projects, and a limited exemption for development incentive wells.

nd:SB 2399.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 50-24.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to medical assistance reimbursement of psychiatric residential treatment facilities; to provide for a legislative management report; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:SB 2399.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to amend Medicaid reimbursement rules for psychiatric residential treatment facilities' direct care costs, capping therapeutic leave days at $500 per day, and to report by October 1, 2026.

nd:SB 2401.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subdivision to subsection 2 of section 12-60-24 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to criminal history record checks by the board of occupational therapy practice; to amend and reenact section 43-17-27.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to physician continuing education requirements; to provide a statement of legislative intent; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2401.summary: Allows the Board of Occupational Therapy Practice to run criminal history record checks on applicants and licensees, and requires physicians to complete at least one hour of continuing education on nutrition and metabolic health each renewal cycle.

nd:SB 2402.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 43-15 and a new subsection to section 43-48-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the prescriptive authority of pharmacists and therapeutic substitution; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 26.1-36.11-01 and section 43-15-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the scope of practice of pharmacists; to repeal section 43-15-25.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to approved laboratory tests; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2402.summary: Lets pharmacists independently prescribe listed drugs and devices, such as for lice, cold sores and motion sickness, and for flu, strep or COVID after a positive test; allows therapeutic substitution with exceptions, with prescriber notice within 24 hours.

nd:SB 2403.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 6-09-47 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a medical facility emergency operating loan program under the medical facility infrastructure loan fund; to provide an appropriation; to provide a transfer; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2403.summary: Creates a Bank of North Dakota emergency operating loan program for nonprofit hospitals in cities under 2,500 people, with loans up to $5 million at no more than 2% interest, and transfers $5 million from the general fund to fund it.

nd:SB 2404.title: AN ACT to provide appropriations to the information technology department and public service commission; to provide contingent loan authorization; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2404.summary: Appropriates $1.5 million to the information technology department to bring state websites into compliance with federal digital accessibility rules, and $325,000 to the Public Service Commission for federal lawsuit intervention, with contingent loan authority if that is not enough.

nd:SB 2405.title: A BILL for an Act to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.9, section 57-20-09, and subsection 1 of section 57-55-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the order of application of the primary residence credit and discount for early payment of tax; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2405.summary: Removes the requirement that the 5% early-payment discount be applied before the primary residence property tax credit, so the credit is applied before the discount, for real estate and mobile home taxes.

nd:SB 2406.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact chapter 44-04.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to prohibiting agencies from entering nondisclosure agreements concerning data centers and industrial projects; to provide a penalty; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2406.summary: Bars state and local agencies from signing nondisclosure agreements with developers of data centers and industrial projects, voids such agreements, and bars approvals of projects whose developer signed one.

nd:SB 2407.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation to the state historical society for the North Dakota military museum project; to amend and reenact section 55-01-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to jurisdiction of the heritage center; to repeal subsection 3 of section 6 of chapter 17 of the 2025 Session Laws, relating to a donation pledge requirement to access funding from the strategic investment and improvements fund; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to authorize a line of credit; to provide for a report; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2407.summary: Allows the State Historical Society to borrow up to $20 million from the Bank of North Dakota for the military museum project through June 30, 2027, and repeals a donation pledge requirement for related state funding.

nd:SB 2408.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact subdivision lll of subsection 3 of section 19-03.1-05 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the scheduling of kratom alkaloids and kratom alkaloid derivatives as a schedule I controlled substance; to amend and reenact section 19-03.1-22.3 and subsection 7 of section 19-03.1-23 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to penalties for the use and possession of kratom alkaloids and kratom alkaloid derivatives; to provide a penalty; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2408.summary: Lists kratom alkaloids and their derivatives as schedule I controlled substances and makes ingesting them an infraction for a first offense and a class A misdemeanor for later offenses.

nd:SCR 4007.title: A concurrent resolution to amend and reenact section 9 of article III and section 16 of article IV of the Constitution of North Dakota, relating to requiring each resolution adopted by the legislative assembly proposing a constitutional amendment and each initiative petition and measure proposing a constitutional amendment to be comprised of a single subject.
nd:SCR 4007.summary: Proposes constitutional amendments requiring each legislatively referred and each citizen-initiated constitutional amendment to cover a single subject, with the secretary of state barring multi-subject initiative petitions from circulating. Would go to voters in June 2026.

ne:LB 1075A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 1075A.summary: Appropriates $12,000 for FY2025-26 and $25,000 for FY2026-27 from the Accountability and Disclosure Commission Cash Fund to that commission to carry out LB 1075, which changes election, campaign finance, local government and unclaimed property laws.

ne:LB 1101A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 1101A.summary: Appropriates $7,500 for FY2026-27 from the Judges Expense Fund to the Public Employees Retirement Board to carry out LB 1101, which changes Judges Retirement Act contribution rates and benefits.

ne:LB 1181.title: Change provisions relating to the rights of victims of certain crimes
ne:LB 1181.summary: Revises victims' rights statutes and definitions, changes prosecuting attorneys' duties relating to plea agreements, including consulting victims and recording it, and repeals sections 29-119 and 29-120.

ne:LB 1236A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 1236A.summary: Appropriates $25,000 a year for fiscal years 2026-27 and 2027-28 from the Nebraska Statutes Distribution Cash Fund to the Legislative Council to carry out LB 1236, which changes how the Legislative Journal, session laws and statutes are published and distributed.

ne:LB 1261A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 1261A.summary: Appropriates $4,750 in each of fiscal years 2026-27 and 2027-28 from the Nebraska Power Review Fund to the Power Review Board to carry out LB 1261, which bars consumer-owned utilities from using eminent domain on certain privately owned generation facilities.

ne:LB 13.title: Require the Department of Health and Human Services to file a state plan amendment relating to child care
ne:LB 13.summary: Amends LB 13 to set a July 1, 2026 deadline for the Department of Health and Human Services to file a state plan amendment paying child care providers by enrollment or authorized hours rather than attendance.

ne:LB 215A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 215A.summary: Appropriates $122,000 for FY2025-26 and $125,966 for FY2026-27 from the General Fund to the Board of Parole to carry out LB 215, which as introduced adopts the Clean Slate Act sealing certain criminal records.

ne:LB 304A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 304A.summary: Appropriates $3,157,170 from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund for FY2026-27 to the Department of Health and Human Services to carry out LB 304.

ne:LB 316.title: Prohibit conduct relating to hemp other than cannabidiol products and change provisions of the Nebraska Hemp Farming Act and the Uniform Controlled Substances Act
ne:LB 316.summary: Amends LB 316 to replace its text with the Nebraska Consumable Hemp Control Act: a commission licenses retailers of consumable hemp products, sales to anyone under 21 are barred, and a 3 percent excise tax applies to first sales to retail licensees.

ne:LB 365.title: Require coverage of self-measure blood pressure monitoring services under the Medical Assistance Act
ne:LB 365.summary: Requires Nebraska Medicaid, by January 1, 2027, to cover and reimburse self-measure blood pressure monitoring for pregnant and postpartum women, including training on home devices, separate readings, daily collection, and sending readings to a provider.

ne:LB 417.title: Provide for administration of the Nebraska Promise Program by the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska, adopt the College Promise Act, and change provisions relating to the Quality Education Accountability Act
ne:LB 417.summary: As amended in committee, creates the Nebraska Promise Program covering University of Nebraska tuition left after Pell and other grants for residents with family income under $65,000 or Pell eligibility, and a College Promise Act waiving community and state college resident tuition under $65,000.

ne:LB 596.title: Change requirements for legal publications and notices required by law, provisions of the Open Meetings Act, county inventories, warrants, and discharge records, storage requirements for certain records, petitions to change names, marriage license and record fees, reports of abandoned property, and the Nebraska Hall of Fame and eliminate a penalty for certain public officials and provisions relating to the registration of farm, ranch, or home names
ne:LB 596.summary: Amends LB 596 to require the Nebraska Hall of Fame Commission to name one living Nebraskan to the Hall of Fame before June 30, 2027, with a record in public service, collegiate athletics leadership and volunteer youth mentorship.

ne:LB 758.title: Change provisions relating to nontestamentary transfers on death, and evidence of ownership to obtain a certificate of title and provide a method for a beneficiary charitable organization to receive property or information
ne:LB 758.summary: Lets a 501(c)(3) charity that is a decedent’s beneficiary claim the property, or information about it, from its holder by affidavit; allows suit if the holder does not comply within 30 to 45 days; accepts the affidavit as vehicle-title ownership evidence.

ne:LB 781.title: Adopt updates to federal law relating to motor vehicles and motor carriers and change civil penalties against certain motor carriers
ne:LB 781.summary: Adopts updates to federal motor vehicle and motor carrier law in Nebraska statutes, updates federal references, and changes the dollar amounts of civil penalties against certain motor carriers.

ne:LB 798.title: Change provisions relating to the composition of the planning commission of a city of the second class or village and allow a city of the second class to elect council members by ward
ne:LB 798.summary: Lets a city of the second class elect some council members by ward and some at large, with at least two and no more than half at large, and lets second-class cities and villages have three-member planning commissions.

ne:LB 803A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 803A.summary: Appropriates $1.11 million for FY2026-27 and $986,400 for FY2027-28, plus $177,711 and $17,383, from the General Fund to the Department of Revenue to carry out LB 803, a property tax and income tax bill including a first-time home buyer savings account.

ne:LB 834.title: Change provisions relating to county assessors, the Property Tax Administrator, real property assessments, taxes levied in counties, delinquent taxes owed to counties, remission of sales and use taxes, and mobile homes
ne:LB 834.summary: Changes property tax administration: allows deputy county assessors, requires assessor certification exams, adds duties for the Property Tax Administrator, changes assessment and reporting deadlines, and provides mobile home certificates of title.

ne:LB 838A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 838A.summary: Appropriates $523,247 for FY2026-27 and $136,300 for FY2027-28 from the General Fund to the Department of Revenue to carry out LB 838, which among other things imposes an excise tax on certain remittance transfers.

ne:LB 912A.title: Appropriation Bill
ne:LB 912A.summary: Appropriates $187,151 from the General Fund and $40,000 from the Professional and Occupational Credentialing Cash Fund for FY2026-27, and $338,010 from the General Fund for FY2027-28, to the Department of Health and Human Services to carry out LB 912.

ne:LB 924.title: Change powers of learning community councils and authorized uses of learning community levies
ne:LB 924.summary: Changes the authorized uses of learning community levies and lets learning community coordinating councils partner with public and private entities to support increasing high school graduation rates.

ne:LB 935.title: Provide for court fees; change provisions relating to incentives for rural legal practice, protection orders, hearsay, sentencing, support order liens, and paternity proceedings; provide for no-contact periods for victims of certain assaults and civil actions for conduct relating to prohibited content or child exploitation devices; and provide for and change offenses involving mobile tracking devices, stalking, unlawful intrusion, operation of unmanned aircraft systems, and swatting
ne:LB 935.summary: Creates the offense of swatting with restitution, bars tracking people with mobile tracking devices without consent, changes stalking penalties, rural legal practice loan repayment rules and other court procedures, and allows civil actions over obscene and child sexual abuse materials.

nh:HB 1184.title: relative to the issuance of no trespass orders on municipal or school district property.
nh:HB 1184.summary: Lets public bodies issue emergency no-trespass orders for public property lasting up to 35 days, with longer orders needing a roll call vote, a one-year maximum, and a right to a hearing and appeal to superior court.

nh:HB 1267.title: prohibiting school district attorneys and non-school personnel from questioning students without their parent or guardian present.
nh:HB 1267.summary: Requires school boards and charter school trustees to adopt a policy barring non-school persons, and school-employed attorneys, paralegals or law enforcement, from questioning a minor student without written parental permission, and to ask adult students whether to notify parents; child-welfare inquiries excepted.

nh:HB 1336.title: relative to regulated conditional deposits.
nh:HB 1336.summary: Lets landlords accept a regulated conditional deposit of up to one extra month's rent from applicants missing screening criteria (credit-score minimums up to 650, income minimums up to 3 times rent, evictions, unpaid judgments, unverified references), with written notice and rescreening rights.

nh:HB 1369.title: relative to the manner of posting the warrant for town meetings.
nh:HB 1369.summary: Requires towns to post special meeting warrants by at least two of three methods (newspaper, public posting, town website), adds the website as a posting place for regular warrants, and requires website warrants to appear or be linked on the home page.

nh:HB 1422.title: relative to the time to petition for a new trial.
nh:HB 1422.summary: Removes the 3-year deadline for new-trial petitions by people with felony or class A misdemeanor convictions who are serving or affected by the sentence and allege innocence from newly discovered evidence; adds prima facie review and victim services. Effective January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 1442.title: permitting classification of individuals based on biological sex under certain limited circumstances.
nh:HB 1442.summary: Provides that classifying people by biological sex in multi-person restrooms and locker rooms, sports where strength, speed or endurance favors males, and prisons or involuntary treatment facilities is not unlawful discrimination; it does not require such separation.

nh:HB 1766.title: relative to cruelty to livestock.
nh:HB 1766.summary: Sets separate rules for animal cruelty cases involving livestock: officers may confiscate livestock only when someone is charged, or its life is in imminent danger, and the investigating officer must be accompanied by the state veterinarian, a designee, or a licensed veterinarian.

nh:HB 2026.title: relative to the state 10-year transportation improvement plan; relative to toll rate adjustments and periodic toll reviews for the New Hampshire turnpike system to support the 2027-2036 ten-year transportation plan; and relative to reconstruction of the Gregg Mill Road Bridge in the town of New Boston.
nh:HB 2026.summary: Adopts the 2027-2036 state ten-year transportation plan with added projects, raises cash and non-E-ZPass turnpike tolls and sets minimum E-ZPass rates from January 2027, repeals the E-ZPass discount, and transfers easements to New Boston for the Gregg Mill Road Bridge.

nh:HB 609.title: relative to the general court's authority over the sale, purchase, ownership, use, possession, transportation, licensing, permitting, taxation, and other matter pertaining to firearms, stun guns, Tasers, pepper spray devices, knives and other self-defense tools.
nh:HB 609.summary: As amended by conference committee, extends the local-rule bar to stun guns, Tasers, pepper spray and other self-defense tools, allows damages suits (actual or $1,000, if greater) by aggrieved people, and limits state agency rules to expressly authorized ones, lapsing July 1, 2029 unless renewed.

nh:SB 101.title: authorizing parents to enroll their children in any public school in the state.
nh:SB 101.summary: Lets parents enroll children in any public school in the state rather than only the assigned resident-district school, and exempts required assessments and school-sponsored events open to the general public from the parental consent requirement for recordings.

nh:SB 268.title: permitting classification of individuals based on biological sex under certain limited circumstances.
nh:SB 268.summary: Provides that classifying people by biological sex (male or female) is not unlawful sex or gender-identity discrimination, by public or private entities, in multi-user restrooms and locker rooms, sports where strength, speed or endurance favors males, and prisons and involuntary-commitment facilities; separation is not required.

nh:SB 431.title: relative to violations of the prohibition on teaching discrimination.
nh:SB 431.summary: As introduced, adds 'intentionally or knowingly' to the public-school ban on teaching, instructing or inculcating the listed discriminatory concepts; takes effect 60 days after passage.

nh:SB 434.title: relative to regulation of public school materials.
nh:SB 434.summary: Requires school boards to adopt a policy by November 1, 2026 for parent complaints about material that is obscene and harmful to minors, and a complaint procedure by November 1, 2027 with set deadlines for investigation, decision, written response and appeal to the school board.

nh:SB 439.title: relative to municipal data center zoning.
nh:SB 439.summary: As amended, allows data centers in commercial and industrial zoning districts, subject to local land use regulations, and lets planning boards adopt regulations with local legislative body approval.

nh:SB 441.title: relative to the financial responsibility for local assistance and enabling municipalities to request a hearing regarding the residency of an assisted person.
nh:SB 441.summary: As an amendment, requires a municipality intending to transport, or arrange transport of, a homeless person or someone showing addiction or substance-use incapacitation symptoms to another municipality for housing, shelter or treatment, where unrelated to a general assistance application, to first have a memorandum of understanding with it.

nh:SB 467.title: relative to the penalty for certain fentanyl-related offenses and establishing a mandatory minimum sentence for the crime of distribution of a controlled drug with death resulting.
nh:SB 467.summary: As introduced, sets mandatory minimum prison terms of 3.5 years for 20 grams or more and 7 years for 50 grams or more of a fentanyl-class drug, and 7 years where distribution causes a death, with court exceptions under set conditions. Effective January 1, 2027.

nh:SB 468.title: relative to enabling alternative treatment centers to operate a greenhouse cultivation location.
nh:SB 468.summary: Lets registered alternative treatment centers request state authorization to run a greenhouse cultivation location, with department rules on location and security, a plan to cut energy costs and patient prices, local zoning compliance, and local input.

nh:SB 475.title: relative to pet vendor foster homes, defining pet vendor foster facility, and relative to cruelty to livestock.
nh:SB 475.summary: Defines pet vendor foster homes and facilities, requires licensed pet vendors to report foster homes annually to the agriculture department, keeps those listings confidential, and sets separate procedures for confiscating livestock in animal cruelty cases.

nh:SB 481.title: relative to the sale of the Sununu youth services center property.
nh:SB 481.summary: Directs the Department of Administrative Services to take possession of the Sununu Youth Services Center property in Manchester and seek a buyer at not less than market value, with governor and council approval and proceeds going to the general fund.

nh:SB 535.title: defining residential breeder and imported animal for the purposes of animal transfers and removing references to commercial kennels.
nh:SB 535.summary: Defines "residential breeder" (breeds dogs or cats in the home, transfers up to 50 a year, no imported animals) and exempts them from state premises rules, defines "imported animal," and replaces "commercial kennel" references with "pet vendor."

nh:SB 552.title: permitting classification of individuals based on biological sex under certain limited circumstances.
nh:SB 552.summary: Provides that classifying people by biological sex, defined as male and female, is not unlawful discrimination in multi-user restrooms and locker rooms, sports where strength, speed or endurance favors biological males, and prisons and involuntary-commitment facilities. Does not require entities to separate by sex.

nh:SB 661.title: relative to pooled risk management programs.
nh:SB 661.summary: Repeals and reenacts the law on pooled risk management programs for local governments: lets the secretary of state require abatement of insufficient assets or seek receivership, requires pro rata member assessments for deficiencies, sets contingency reserve standards, and requires public disclosures.

nj:A 1072.title: Distributed battery storage program-direct BPU & electric utilities to establish
nj:A 1072.summary: Requires the Board of Public Utilities to create a distributed energy storage incentive program run by electric utilities, aiming for at least 1,000 MW of storage by 2030 and 2,000 MW more by 2032.

nj:A 1131.title: Veteran cremains, unclaimed-provide a central website registry
nj:A 1131.summary: Requires funeral directors to respond promptly when the Department of Veterans Affairs asks whether they hold unclaimed cremains of veterans or their eligible spouses or dependents, and has the death registry electronically notify the department of such deaths.

nj:A 1203.title: "Pet Insurance Act"-concerns
nj:A 1203.summary: Creates the Pet Insurance Act, setting rules for selling pet insurance in New Jersey, including disclosures of exclusions, limits on denying claims for preexisting conditions, separation of wellness programs from insurance, and producer training and licensing requirements.

nj:A 1205.title: Division of Developmental Disabilities-create and distribute satisfaction survey
nj:A 1205.summary: Requires the Division of Developmental Disabilities to survey clients of support coordination services and rate each support coordination agency out of five stars.

nj:A 1207.title: Ovulation enhancing drugs/medical svc-req Medicaid coverage, cert beneficiaries
nj:A 1207.summary: Requires Medicaid to cover oral ovulation-enhancing drugs and related office visits and tests for people aged 21 to 44 with infertility, limited to three treatment cycles per lifetime, if federal approval and funding are available.

nj:A 1211.title: Payment card scanning device-upgrade criminal penalties for use or possession
nj:A 1211.summary: Raises the criminal penalties for using or possessing a payment card scanning device and requires merchants to take reasonable safety measures to prevent scanning of payment cards.

nj:A 1295.title: Local government employee on paid leave-proh a different county from employing
nj:A 1295.summary: Bars a local government agency from employing a person in a full-time or part-time position while that person is on paid leave from a local government agency in another county or municipality.

nj:A 1323.title: Video surveillance w/ artificial intelligence capabilities-adopt policy on use
nj:A 1323.summary: Requires school boards and charter school boards of trustees that use AI-enabled surveillance systems, such as video, x-ray or body scanners, to adopt a policy covering what data is collected, how it is used and who can access it.

nj:A 1340.title: Consumer debt lawsuits-collect and publish statistical information
nj:A 1340.summary: Requires the Administrative Office of the Courts to collect and publish annual statistics on consumer debt lawsuits, including filings, pending cases, defendants with attorneys, judgments and default judgments.

nj:A 1375.title: Veterans-establishes special license plates
nj:A 1375.summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Commission to issue veteran license plates to honorably discharged veterans, with a $50 application fee and $10 annual renewal fee deposited in a fund appropriated to the Department of Veterans Affairs for veterans' benefits.

nj:A 1389.title: Domestic violence restraining orders-seizure of ammunition/firearm components
nj:A 1389.summary: Adds ammunition, firearm accessories and firearm components to the items that may be seized or surrendered under a domestic violence restraining order or after a domestic violence conviction.

nj:A 1400.title: Drinking water quality standards-supplier notify affected mun & school districts
nj:A 1400.summary: Requires public water systems to immediately notify, by phone and email, municipal governing bodies and the school districts, charter, nonpublic and higher education institutions they serve of any Tier 2 public notice violation, with contaminant levels, test dates, sample locations and suggested customer steps.

nj:A 1432.title: School bus monitoring systems-authorizes use
nj:A 1432.summary: Lets municipalities and school districts contract for cameras on school buses to enforce the law against passing a stopped school bus, with a $300 civil penalty and a notice of liability mailed to the registered owner within 90 days.

nj:A 1457.title: General Contractor Licensing Act-provides for licensure
nj:A 1457.summary: Creates a State Board of General Contractors to license general contractors, with standards, examinations and discipline set by the board, and requires general contractor businesses to register annually and employ a licensed general contractor.

nj:A 1468.title: Dam hazard classification, hazard potential-consider impact to natural resources
nj:A 1468.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection's dam hazard classification system to consider potential damage to natural resources, in addition to loss of life and property damage.

nj:A 1495.title: Affordable housing projects, cert-exempts sale of materials from sales & use tax
nj:A 1495.summary: Exempts from sales and use tax materials, supplies and services sold to contractors for housing sponsors' affordable housing projects where all units are for moderate-, low- or very-low-income occupants.

nj:A 1502.title: Patient and Provider Protection Act-concerns
nj:A 1502.summary: Requires pharmacy benefits managers to act in the best interests of the health carriers they contract with, bars misleading marketing, voids rebate deals excluding generics, and sets pharmacy reimbursement at NADAC plus the Medicaid dispensing fee (NADAC alone for affiliated pharmacies).

nj:A 1516.title: Unemployment compensation-exempt poll worker wages from affecting
nj:A 1516.summary: Excludes temporary poll worker pay of up to $1,000 a year from unemployment, disability and family leave insurance taxes and from counting as employment for unemployment benefits.

nj:A 1517.title: Native Seed Commission-establish; develop plan to increase production and use
nj:A 1517.summary: Creates an 11-member Native Seed Commission in the Department of Agriculture to develop a plan, reported within a year, to increase native seed production and its use in public projects and to keep native seeds commercially available at reasonable cost.

nj:A 1552.title: Limousine laws-revise penalties for certain violations
nj:A 1552.summary: Sets a $7,500 fine for a third or later limousine violation, such as operating without a license, adequate insurance or inspection, or over seating capacity, plus license suspension for six months or vehicle impoundment in some cases.

nj:A 1628.title: Cosmetology & hairstyling teachers-allow cert licensees teach in private schools
nj:A 1628.summary: Lets holders of barbering, beauty culture, manicuring, hair braiding or skin care licenses teach in private cosmetology and hairstyling schools, and bars teaching courses outside the scope of the teacher's license.

nj:A 1630.title: Local government employee on paid leave-proh a different county from employing
nj:A 1630.summary: Bars local government agencies from employing a person in a full-time or part-time position while that person is on paid leave from a local government job in another county or municipality.

nj:A 1657.title: Pub. school student mental health svcs-permit referral to private prof counselor
nj:A 1657.summary: Allows school counselors, student assistance coordinators, school psychologists and other district mental health staff to refer students to licensed professional counselors for mental health assessments and services. Bars referrals to counselors in which the employee or family has a significant beneficial interest.

nj:A 1669.title: Teachers, certain-remove obstacles to teacher certification
nj:A 1669.summary: Bars the State Board of Education from requiring a basic skills test such as the Praxis Core for most instructional certificates or for admission to preparation programs, and repeals the law creating an alternative certificate of eligibility.

nj:A 1672.title: Homestead prop tax reimbursement-make person receiving disab payments eligible
nj:A 1672.summary: Makes people with disabilities who receive payments under the federal Railroad Retirement Act eligible for homestead property tax reimbursement, as people receiving Social Security disability payments already are.

nj:A 1675.title: TPAF-extend membership, 7 yrs after discontinuance & 25 yrs for those laid off
nj:A 1675.summary: Extends from two to 10 years how long Teachers' Pension and Annuity Fund members can keep membership and tier after leaving service, and to 15 years for certain qualifying departures if contributions were not withdrawn; applies retroactively.

nj:A 1677.title: Electric sch buses-auth competitive contracting/extended terms, lease & purchase
nj:A 1677.summary: Lets school districts lease or lease-purchase electric school buses and charging equipment for terms up to the bus's service life, keeps the 10-year limit for fossil fuel buses, and lets the School Boards Association act as a government aggregator.

nj:A 1682.title: Student Learning Standards, Social Studies-provide instruction on labor movement
nj:A 1682.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt social studies standards on U.S. and New Jersey labor history, and schools to teach it in grades six through 12, including strikes, unionization drives and collective bargaining.

nj:A 1700.title: Perinatal anxiety-estab. awareness campaign, devel policies, promote recognition
nj:A 1700.summary: Directs the Department of Health to develop, if funds are available, a public awareness campaign on perinatal anxiety and, with health care facilities and professionals, policies to give patients information and screening for it during and after pregnancy.

nj:A 1715.title: John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act of New Jersey-establishes
nj:A 1715.summary: Establishes the John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act: election laws are construed liberally for voters, policies that unnecessarily abridge voting and methods that dilute protected classes’ votes are barred, and the Attorney General gets preclearance power over certain jurisdictions.

nj:A 1738.title: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. license plates-authorize creation
nj:A 1738.summary: Authorizes special Delta Sigma Theta Sorority license plates, with a $50 application fee and $10 annual renewal fee; after program costs, fee revenue goes to a fund for the sorority's programs.

nj:A 1790.title: Out-of-state contractors-estab registry, awarded public works contracts in State
nj:A 1790.summary: Requires the State Treasurer to keep a public online registry of out-of-state contractors awarded public works contracts in New Jersey, listing each project, trade name, owner and principal business address.

nj:A 1813.title: Smoking devices, electronic & tobacco products-prohibits delivery, under age 21
nj:A 1813.summary: Bars delivering electronic smoking devices or tobacco products to anyone under 21, and requires the signature of a resident aged 21 or older on delivery to a residence, with the same penalties as sales to under-21s; Postal Service employees are exempt.

nj:A 1815.title: Antenatal prenatal care clinics-DOH conduct survey on status
nj:A 1815.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Health to survey antenatal and prenatal care clinics, including recently closed ones, to evaluate maternity care services, availability, and where low- and moderate-income pregnant women receive care.

nj:A 1825.title: Health insurance step therapy protocols-establish certain guidelines concerning
nj:A 1825.summary: Sets requirements for step therapy protocols in the State Health Benefits Program, School Employees Health Benefits Program and Medicaid, including that clinical criteria rest on evidence-based practice guidelines endorsed by a multidisciplinary expert panel.

nj:A 1830.title: Ambulatory care facility-revise provisions of State law concerning licensure
nj:A 1830.summary: Removes the rule that bars a new license for an ambulatory care facility relocating to provide surgical services unless it moves within 20 miles or into a Health Enterprise Zone.

nj:A 1844.title: Child care centers, licensed-60 day notice required for tuition rate changes
nj:A 1844.summary: Requires licensed child care centers to give parents or guardians 60 days’ notice when proposing to raise or lower tuition by four percent.

nj:A 1848.title: Diet pills & dietary supplements, certain-proh. sale to persons under 18 years
nj:A 1848.summary: Bars selling over-the-counter diet pills and weight-loss or muscle-building dietary supplements to anyone under 18 unless with a parent or guardian, and requires an adult's signature for home delivery. Plain protein powders, drinks and foods are excluded.

nj:A 1872.title: Gardens, community-exempts composting on-site under certain conditions
nj:A 1872.summary: Exempts community gardens with on-site composting from certain Department of Environmental Protection permits if they take no more than 200 gallons of organic waste per week (more on lots of 5,000 square feet or larger) and use, give away or sell the compost.

nj:A 1873.title: Flood mitigation projects-prioritize funding for projects that include/allow for
nj:A 1873.summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Protection to give additional priority points to Blue Acres, clean water and drinking water project applicants whose projects include or allow on-site flood mitigation.

nj:A 1875.title: Title 26-consolidates & makes technical updates to certain definitions
nj:A 1875.summary: Moves definitions used across Title 26 (health and vital statistics laws) into one general definitions section and removes them from individual sections.

nj:A 1899.title: Drugs and vaccines-expand authority, pharmacy technician in administering
nj:A 1899.summary: Lets pharmacy technicians administer drugs to patients 18 and older in set circumstances, lets pharmacists, interns, externs and technicians give flu or COVID-19 vaccines to patients 5 and older (parental permission under 18), and drops pharmacist certification for administering prescription drugs.

nj:A 1921.title: Bias incident investigation standards-concerns AG guidelines
nj:A 1921.summary: Requires the Attorney General to maintain and periodically review bias incident investigation guidelines, which must require county and municipal law enforcement to report suspected bias incidents within 24 hours and county prosecutors to notify the Attorney General before seeking bias intimidation charges.

nj:A 1925.title: Professional license, Cosmetology & Hairstyling-modify languages; concerns exams
nj:A 1925.summary: Requires the Board of Cosmetology and Hairstyling to offer its exams in English, with the option of the four other most commonly spoken languages in New Jersey, in compliance with the state language-access law.

nj:A 1929.title: Career school, priv-clarifies law concerning requirements for closure
nj:A 1929.summary: Applies private career school closure rules, including filing teach-out plans with the Labor Commissioner, to schools licensed by the Board of Cosmetology and Hairstyling, and requires the board to develop a model teach-out plan.

nj:A 1948.title: VCCO-issue annual report to Governor and Legislature
nj:A 1948.summary: Requires the Victims of Crime Compensation Office to issue an annual report within six months of fiscal year end, covering applications, awards granted and denied, reasons, demographics and funding, to the Governor and Legislature.

nj:A 1959.title: Billing due date-proh. telecommunications/utility companies from charging prior
nj:A 1959.summary: Directs the Board of Public Utilities to bar telecommunications, electric, gas and cable companies from charging credit card or direct debit customers before the billing due date that applies to cash or check payers, unless the customer agrees or requests it.

nj:A 1970.title: Legionnaires's disease-DEP, DOH, DCA & public water systems prevent/control
nj:A 1970.summary: Requires surface-water public community water systems with over 100 connections to keep minimum disinfectant levels and report disruptions to DEP within 72 hours, requires Legionella water management programs at hospitals and other listed buildings, and requires investigating each reported Legionnaires’ case.

nj:A 1973.title: Endometriosis-estab. req, screen cert people who are pregnant & have given birth
nj:A 1973.summary: Directs the Health Commissioner and Board of Medical Examiners to require obstetric care providers to evaluate or refer patients diagnosed with preeclampsia who later show endometriosis symptoms, unless the patient refuses in writing, and to give them Department of Health endometriosis information.

nj:A 1996.title: Preeclampsia-estab req to screen people who are pregnant & have given birth
nj:A 1996.summary: Requires birthing centers, federally qualified health centers and prenatal or postpartum care practitioners to adopt policies for evaluating symptomatic patients for pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders such as preeclampsia, to give them information on warning signs, and to develop a treatment plan after a positive evaluation.

nj:A 1997.title: Student learning support-establish central registry, supplemental tutoring
nj:A 1997.summary: Directs the Department of Education to partner with a nonprofit to maintain a public, searchable registry of individuals and organizations offering free tutoring, listing contact information, subject expertise and availability.

nj:A 2001.title: Dialysis-related drugs & devices, cert-establish pharmacist licensing exemption
nj:A 2001.summary: Exempts drug manufacturers and wholesale distributors from the pharmacist-licensing requirement when they deliver FDA-approved dialysate drugs or devices for home dialysis to patients with end-stage renal disease, under conditions including a physician's order and sealed original packaging.

nj:A 2018.title: Integrated care facility-require publication of guide for licensure
nj:A 2018.summary: Requires the Department of Health and the Department of Human Services to publish online a guide to the steps health care facilities must take to be licensed for integrated general and behavioral health care, and to list a staff contact for questions.

nj:A 2027.title: Work First New Jersey Menstrual Hygiene Benefit Program-establishes;$2.5M
nj:A 2027.summary: Creates one-year pilot programs paying Work First New Jersey participants a monthly State benefit of $14 for menstrual hygiene products (ages 18 to 50) and $30 per child under 36 months for diapers, with a $2.5 million appropriation.

nj:A 2029.title: Vaping awareness campaign-concerns; devel guidelines, sch dist/instit higher ed
nj:A 2029.summary: Directs the Departments of Education and Health to develop and annually update guidelines for school districts and colleges to run on-campus anti-vaping awareness campaigns aimed at students.

nj:A 2078.title: Out-of-state contractors-estab registry, awarded public works contracts in State
nj:A 2078.summary: Requires the State Treasurer to maintain a public online registry of out-of-state contractors awarded New Jersey public works contracts, listing trade name, owner, address and project description.

nj:A 2090.title: Food waste-solid waste management district required to develop strategy plan
nj:A 2090.summary: Requires each solid waste management district to adopt a strategy, subject to Department of Environmental Protection approval, to cut food waste 50 percent from 2022 levels by 2035. Exempts food waste sent to landfills that supply gas to renewable energy facilities.

nj:A 2100.title: Educational research & svc corporation-broaden types of contracts may enter into
nj:A 2100.summary: Lets educational research and services corporations formed by colleges and universities act as lead agency or contracting unit for procuring any goods or services, rather than only educational technology.

nj:A 2102.title: Gardens, community-exempts composting on-site under certain conditions
nj:A 2102.summary: Exempts community gardens with on-site composting from Department of Environmental Protection permits if they accept no more than 200 gallons of food waste a week (more on larger lots) and use, give away or sell the compost.

nj:A 2104.title: Flood mitigation projects-prioritize funding for projects that include/allow for
nj:A 2104.summary: Directs the Department of Environmental Protection to give extra priority points to Blue Acres, clean water and drinking water funding applicants whose projects include or allow for on-site flood mitigation.

nj:A 2115.title: Human trafficking-pub. trans emp complete training course, handling & responding
nj:A 2115.summary: Requires New Jersey Transit, with the Commission on Human Trafficking, to provide a one-time training course for public transportation employees on handling and responding to suspected human trafficking, reviewed at least every two years.

nj:A 2127.title: Public utility meter reading fees-proh charging residents, multi-unit dwellings
nj:A 2127.summary: Bars electric and gas utilities from charging a multi-unit residential customer who opted out of a smart meter a meter-reading fee that exceeds the cost of that billing cycle's electricity or gas usage.

nj:A 2132.title: Access Link paratransit vehicle operators-announce stops for passengers
nj:A 2132.summary: Requires operators of paratransit vehicles to announce every scheduled stop, or use a recorded announcement system, as fixed-route operators are already required to do.

nj:A 2158.title: Public Svc Loan Forgiveness prog-concerning the provision of information about
nj:A 2158.summary: Requires colleges to give students with federal loan debt, and government employers to give employees, information about the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness program at set points.

nj:A 2159.title: Third-party litigation funding agreements-requires disclosure
nj:A 2159.summary: Requires parties to notify the court within 30 days of any third-party litigation funding agreement, lets courts review it privately and parties seek discovery of its terms in some cases, and sets responsibilities for litigation funders.

nj:A 2163.title: Veteran-DMVA notify cert organizations, names of deceased in veteran cemeteries
nj:A 2163.summary: Requires the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs to send monthly lists of people buried or cremated in State veteran cemeteries to veteran organizations and county and municipal officers, if a representative signs a waiver.

nj:A 2180.title: School buses, Type S-permits certain persons to operate
nj:A 2180.summary: Lets school boards, nonpublic schools and State agencies designate qualified school personnel to drive students to and from school (not only to activities) in vehicles seating eight or fewer; drivers must be 21 or older with a three-year license, checks and training.

nj:A 2195.title: Vaping awareness campaign-concerns; devel guidelines, sch dist/instit higher ed
nj:A 2195.summary: Directs the Department of Health to develop guidelines for school districts and colleges on anti-vaping awareness campaigns for students, to be reviewed annually.

nj:A 2196.title: Outdoor lighting fixtures-install or replace, at projects receiving State funds
