nj:A 5867.summary: Extends a barbering pilot program in Elizabeth, Passaic, Paterson and Perth Amboy by three years and lets people who barbered where no license exists qualify for a 120-day provisional permit.

nj:A 5877.title: Nursing homes-revise assessment imposed if permissible under federal law
nj:A 5877.summary: Changes the nursing home assessment cap from six percent of revenues to six percent or the maximum percentage federal law permits, whichever applies.

nj:A 5886.title: United States House of Representatives-revise process, filling vacancy from St.
nj:A 5886.summary: Requires the Governor to issue a writ of election within 10 days of a New Jersey U.S. House vacancy, and sets special primary and special election timing when at least 180 days of the term remain.

nj:A 5901.title: Preserv. farmland-auth construction/installation/operation, cert energy projects
nj:A 5901.summary: Lets owners of energy generation facilities apply to the State Agriculture Development Committee for approval to install transmission and distribution wires that cross preserved farmland to connect to the grid, and sets an application process.

nj:A 5902.title: Electric capacity & transmission-research and recommend certain action
nj:A 5902.summary: Requires the Board of Public Utilities to work with neighboring states to research and recommend actions such as contracting requirements for electricity suppliers or withdrawing from PJM's capacity market or transmission grid.

nj:A 5905.title: Parolee violates domestic violence restraining order-notify State Parole Board
nj:A 5905.summary: Requires prosecutors or law enforcement to notify the State Parole Board when a parolee is charged with violating a domestic violence restraining order, and sets how parolee status appears in the domestic violence central registry.

nj:A 5907.title: Automated license plate reader-concerns
nj:A 5907.summary: Bars knowingly sharing license plate reader data for interstate investigations seeking liability over reproductive health care services legal in New Jersey. Requires law enforcement to get an out-of-State agency's written declaration against such use before sharing. Sets civil penalties up to $1,000, then $5,000.

nj:A 5908.title: Early childhood ed-amend FY2026 approp act to revise various language provisions
nj:A 5908.summary: Amends language in the Fiscal Year 2026 Appropriations Act on Preschool Education Aid to match legislation changing how that aid is allocated.

nj:A 5935.title: Charter school-concerns enrollment, student placements, reporting, & athletics
nj:A 5935.summary: Sets charter school rules: a student placement liaison at public schools, no admission criteria beyond random selection, optional enrollment priority for teaching staff's children, a ban on counseling students to withdraw, exit reporting, and joining an interscholastic athletic association.

nj:A 5936.title: Charter schools-estab various req for school/board of trustees memb/mgt org
nj:A 5936.summary: Sets charter school requirements, including public notice and comment on applications and renewals, a financial plan and demonstration of need in applications, consolidation petitions, physical location rules, and rules for trustees and management organizations.

nj:A 5978.title: Real estate salesperson or broker-saleperson-clarifies current law, comm paid
nj:A 5978.summary: Clarifies that a real estate salesperson or broker-salesperson may accept commissions from a limited liability company or other entity they formed, without affecting their business affiliation with their broker.

nj:A 5987.title: Community Resources funding, certain-reassign distribution
nj:A 5987.summary: Amends the FY2026 budget to move $25,000 to American Legion Post #346 in Neptune Township from a post outside New Jersey, and $100,000 to Meals on Wheels of Ocean County from its prior name.

nj:A 6072.title: Caffeinated beverages, cert-req retail food establishments provide disclosures
nj:A 6072.summary: Requires retail food establishments to display a 'High caffeine' warning, or similar approved icon, next to beverages with at least 80 milligrams of caffeine per serving on menus, including drive-through menu boards.

nj:A 6107.title: Gubernatorial transition expenses of Governor-Elect-provide suppl approp;$250K
nj:A 6107.summary: Appropriates an additional $250,000 to the Department of the Treasury for the Governor-Elect's transition expenses, bringing the total for this purpose to $650,000 with the $400,000 already appropriated.

nj:A 6113.title: Paterson Great Falls Natl. Park-support stadium, entertainment, & tourism;$4M
nj:A 6113.summary: Appropriates a supplemental $4 million to Hinchliffe Stadium Partners for sports, entertainment and tourism infrastructure at Paterson Great Falls National Park, in addition to a $900,000 fiscal 2026 appropriation.

nj:A 6124.title: Hotel/motel occupancy fee-concerns revenue collected, Div of Travel & Touism;&1M
nj:A 6124.summary: Sets minimum annual appropriations from the hotel and motel occupancy fee starting in Fiscal Year 2027: $31.9 million for the arts council, $5.5 million for the Historical Commission, $17.6 million for tourism, $720,000 for the Cultural Trust.

nj:A 6129.title: NJ 2-1-1 Partnership-make supplemental approp to DHS for grant;$615K
nj:A 6129.summary: Appropriates $615,000 to the Department of Human Services for a grant to the NJ 2-1-1 Partnership, the sole administrator of the statewide 2-1-1 human services information and referral line.

nj:A 6149.title: School nursing services pilot program-establish
nj:A 6149.summary: Creates a three-year nonpublic school nursing pilot in one eligible county, letting a county consortium provide nursing services to nonpublic schools using the State nursing aid otherwise paid to the school district.

nj:A 6201.title: SHBP-remove language requiring achievement of cost savings
nj:A 6201.summary: Amends the FY2026 budget act to remove the language requiring $100 million in State Health Benefits Plan cost savings, including the fallback steps if the plan design committee cannot agree.

nj:A 6210.title: Firearms permit applications, cert-require fees be deposited into General Fund
nj:A 6210.summary: Requires firearms permit application fees paid to the State Police Superintendent, such as for a handgun purchase permit, purchaser ID card and carry permit, to go to the General Fund instead of the Victims of Crime Compensation Office account.

nj:A 6211.title: Criminal trespassing while carrying firearm-revise penalty
nj:A 6211.summary: Raises criminal trespass penalties when the person has a firearm, with or without a carry permit: to third degree for schools, dwellings and similar sites, fourth degree for research, utility and airport secured areas, and a disorderly persons offense where notice is posted.

nj:A 6213.title: Life guard pension benefits-concerns; make new pension plans permissive
nj:A 6213.summary: Lets fourth-class cities close existing lifeguard pension plans to new members, changes certain lifeguard pension benefits, and makes establishing new lifeguard pension plans optional rather than required.

nj:A 6219.title: FY2026 approp act-amend, reassign to Parkside Bus. & Community in Partnership
nj:A 6219.summary: Amends the FY2026 budget to move $500,000 appropriated to the City of Camden for capital projects to Parkside Business & Community in Partnership, a Camden nonprofit.

nj:A 6273.title: Historic preservation projects, certain-appropriate revenues for grants;$15.815M
nj:A 6273.summary: Appropriates $15,815,984 from dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the New Jersey Historic Trust for historic preservation grants to listed projects and administrative costs.

nj:A 6274.title: Development of lands, recreation & conservation purposes-appropriate;$55M
nj:A 6274.summary: Appropriates $55 million from dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection for capital and park development projects on State lands for recreation and conservation.

nj:A 6275.title: Acquisition of land, recreation & conservation purposes-appropriate;$44.4M
nj:A 6275.summary: Appropriates $44.4 million from dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection for State acquisition of land for recreation and conservation, including Blue Acres flood-prone property buyouts.

nj:A 6276.title: City of Newark, Ivy Hill Park-modify authorized use of certain State aid
nj:A 6276.summary: Reassigns $250,000 in FY2026 State aid for an Ivy Hill Park community center from the City of Newark to Essex County, which owns the park, and allows use for general park improvements. Adds no new appropriation.

nj:A 6283.title: Saving Our Diners & Protecting Our Past Act-provide certain tax incentives
nj:A 6283.summary: Creates a registry of historic diners and restaurants and exempts their on-premises prepared food and drink sales from sales tax for 12 months after approval; also allows corporation business and gross income tax credits.

nj:A 6298.title: Transformative projects under NJ Aspire Program, cert-concerns requirements
nj:A 6298.summary: Exempts certain transformative projects in a restricted county-seat municipality near a transit hub, college and health facility from the Aspire program's net positive benefit test, deems them of special economic importance, and requires a community benefits agreement.

nj:A 6306.title: Sports & entertainment projects, certain-authorize tax credits
nj:A 6306.summary: Authorizes $2.5 billion in tax credits, including up to $300 million for sports and entertainment projects, which must apply before June 30, 2027; the remainder is added to the Aspire and Emerge programs.

nj:A 6307.title: Film & digital media content production tax credit program-modifies cert req
nj:A 6307.summary: Changes the film and digital media production tax credit program, including which costs count as qualified production expenses, rules on out-of-state producer fees and script costs, the $125 million studio-partner enhancement, and credit recapture.

nj:A 6308.title: Safe Communities Act-require AG develop certain model policies
nj:A 6308.summary: Requires the Attorney General to develop model policies for hospitals, schools, shelters, courthouses and similar sites that bar assisting federal civil immigration enforcement or enforcement on premises; state agencies adopt them. A separate model policy is optional for places of worship.

nj:A 6310.title: Strengthening Trust Between Law Enforcement & Immigrant Communities-concerns
nj:A 6310.summary: Codifies the Attorney General's immigrant-trust directive: bars police from racially influenced policing and from stopping or detaining people solely over immigration status, and limits help to federal civil immigration enforcement, with exceptions.

nj:A 6313.title: Hospitals-estab pilot program to support certain services when relocating;$3M
nj:A 6313.summary: Creates a $3 million Department of Health pilot letting a hospital that relocates to former federal property keep a community access location, as a remote site under its license, at its original site in an underserved community.

nj:A 6316.title: Deferred compensation plan-estab financial advisory services for participants
nj:A 6316.summary: Requires the Treasury Department to contract with a vendor to offer low-cost individualized financial advisory services to State employees who participate in the State's deferred compensation plan.

nj:A 6319.title: FY2026 supplemental appropriations-make for various reasons
nj:A 6319.summary: Makes FY2026 supplemental appropriations, including $54 million in county aid, $26 million for events including the 2026 World Cup, $25 million for a supercomputer site, $10 million for Hudson County Schools of Technology, and $5 million each for food security research and Kean University.

nj:A 775.title: Fairness in Women's Sports Act-concerns student participation
nj:A 775.summary: As introduced, requires public and nonpublic schools and colleges to designate sports teams by biological sex at birth and bars male students from teams designated for females.

nj:A 794.title: Real property abandoned, vacant, or subject to unpaid taxes-permit mun to aquire
nj:A 794.summary: Lets a distressed municipality take vacant, abandoned or tax-delinquent property by paying fair market value or by eminent domain, instead of using the abandoned-property, tax-sale or in rem foreclosure laws.

nj:A 795.title: Violations, cert-permit 30-calendar day extention, bus. to address & resolve
nj:A 795.summary: Lets a State agency, for good cause, extend by 30 days the 60-day period in which a business can cure a first-time minor violation before fines are imposed.

nj:A 796.title: Electric public utilities-develop and apply special rules for cert data centers
nj:A 796.summary: Requires the Board of Public Utilities to set standards for serving large data centers (size threshold no higher than 50 megawatts); utilities then file tariffs assigning data-center costs to those customers, with financial guarantees and curtailment before residential customers.

nj:A 798.title: Business receive cert notices electronically-req St entities offer optional svc
nj:A 798.summary: Requires State entities that issue legally required notices to businesses to offer an optional electronic delivery service and to tell businesses about it within 60 days.

nj:A 804.title: Governor's annual budget message-report societal benf charge rev/expend included
nj:A 804.summary: Requires the Board of Public Utilities to report to the Governor and Legislature each January and October on societal benefits charge revenues and how they were allocated and spent on efficiency, energy assistance and electric vehicle incentive programs.

nj:A 817.title: Higher ed instit-estab. plans concerning cyber security & prev. of cyber attacks
nj:A 817.summary: Requires public colleges and universities to adopt and regularly update cyber security plans covering system monitoring, threat assessment, risk mitigation and incident response and recovery.

nj:A 913.title: Sickle cell anemia-authorize medical cannabis for treatment
nj:A 913.summary: Adds sickle cell anemia to the list of medical conditions that qualify a patient for the medical use of cannabis.

nj:A 936.title: Veterans and their spouses-waives certain prof. and occupational licensing fees
nj:A 936.summary: Waives initial application and license fees at State professional licensing boards for resident veterans, and their spouses or partners, who are licensed in another state with equivalent requirements and seek a New Jersey license by reciprocity.

nj:A 938.title: SJTA-provides representation of Burlington County
nj:A 938.summary: Adds Burlington County as a member county of the South Jersey Transportation Authority and changes the makeup of its board of commissioners by adding new members.

nj:A 947.title: Perinatal anxiety-estab. awareness campaign, devel policies, promote recognition
nj:A 947.summary: Requires prenatal and postnatal care providers to screen patients for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders, prenatal providers and birthing facilities to give patients information on them, and, if funded, the Health Commissioner to run a public awareness campaign.

nj:A 948.title: Antenatal prenatal care clinics-DOH conduct survey on status
nj:A 948.summary: Requires the Health Commissioner to survey antenatal and prenatal care clinics, including ones that recently closed or cut services, to assess availability of maternity care and inform certificate of need policy on closures.

nj:A 976.title: Courtesy license, temporary-allows for issuance for nonresident military spouses
nj:A 976.summary: Extends temporary courtesy licenses for nonresident military spouses in six licensed health and counseling professions from one year to two years, with a possible one-year extension.

nj:ACR 105.title: Joint Committee on Economic Justice & Equal Employment Opportunity-reconstitutes
nj:ACR 105.summary: Reconstitutes the Joint Committee on Economic Justice and Equal Employment Opportunity to continue studying those issues statewide, with authority to hold hearings.

nj:ACR 114.title: Plastics recycling marketplace-urges DEP and EDA to establish
nj:ACR 114.summary: As introduced, urges the Department of Environmental Protection to use State Recycling Fund money to research a plastics recycling marketplace, and urges the Economic Development Authority to encourage and fund establishing one.

nj:ACR 115.title: Universal School Meals Program Act of 2023-urges US Congress to pass
nj:ACR 115.summary: Urges the U.S. Congress to pass the Universal School Meals Program Act of 2023, which would provide free school meals to all students and reimburse schools for unpaid meal debt.

nj:ACR 138.title: Jersey Fresh program-honors 40th anniversary
nj:ACR 138.summary: Honors the 40th anniversary of the Jersey Fresh program, the State's agricultural marketing and quality grading program for New Jersey produce.

nj:ACR 144.title: Shrewsbury Borough-recognizes centennial
nj:ACR 144.summary: Recognizes the centennial of Shrewsbury Borough, incorporated by referendum on May 11, 1926.

nj:ACR 165.title: Concussion management teams-urge school districts to establish
nj:ACR 165.summary: Urges school districts to establish concussion management teams of school-based professionals to manage a student's care after a concussion.

nj:ACR 169.title: Newark Liberty Internat. Airport-urge Cong, approp emerg funds/increase staff
nj:ACR 169.summary: Urges Congress to appropriate emergency funds to modernize air traffic control infrastructure and increase staffing at facilities supporting Newark Liberty International Airport.

nj:AJR 103.title: John Basilone Day-designates September 22
nj:AJR 103.summary: Designates September 22 each year as John Basilone Day in New Jersey and asks the Governor to issue an annual proclamation.

nj:AJR 112.title: Suicide Prevention Week-designates calendar week that includes September 10th
nj:AJR 112.summary: Designates the week, starting Sunday, that includes September 10 each year as "Suicide Prevention Week" in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 120.title: Tardive Dyskinesia Awareness Week-designates first full week of May
nj:AJR 120.summary: Designates the first full week of May each year as Tardive Dyskinesia Awareness Week in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 126.title: Worker Safety Day-designates April 18 of each year
nj:AJR 126.summary: Designates April 18 of each year as "Worker Safety Day" in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 128.title: American Artist Appreciation Month-designates August
nj:AJR 128.summary: Designates August each year as “American Artist Appreciation Month” in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 139.title: Deaf Awareness Month/Deaf Awareness Week-desig. Sept. & last full week of Sept.
nj:AJR 139.summary: Designates September each year as Deaf Awareness Month in New Jersey and asks the Governor to issue an annual proclamation.

nj:AJR 159.title: Ruby Bridges Walk to Sch Day-designate November 14, each yr
nj:AJR 159.summary: Designates November 14 of each year as Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 166.title: National Museum of the American Latino-urges Congress to continue progress
nj:AJR 166.summary: Urges Congress to reinstate the 2008 commission exploring a National Museum of the American Latino and to advocate for creating it as part of the Smithsonian on the National Mall.

nj:AJR 169.title: Benjamin Franklin Bridge-commemorate 100th anniversary
nj:AJR 169.summary: Commemorates the 100th anniversary of the Benjamin Franklin Bridge, which opened July 1, 1926.

nj:AJR 170.title: Donate Life Month-designates month of April, each year
nj:AJR 170.summary: Designates April of each year as Donate Life Month in New Jersey, encouraging residents to register as organ donors.

nj:AJR 205.title: Eating Disorders Awareness Week-permanently designates last week in February
nj:AJR 205.summary: Permanently designates the last week in February as Eating Disorders Awareness Week in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 211.title: Six Triple Eight Day-designate May 18 each year in NJ
nj:AJR 211.summary: Designates May 18 of each year as Six Triple Eight Day in New Jersey, recognizing the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion, a World War II Army unit.

nj:AJR 215.title: Brian Sicknick Day-designate July 30 each year in New Jersey
nj:AJR 215.summary: Designates July 30 of each year as Brian Sicknick Day in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 229.title: Adequate food-recognize right
nj:AJR 229.summary: Recognizes a right to adequate food, defined to include nutrition, availability, physical and economic access, and water, and encourages State, county and municipal entities to act on it. States that it creates no private right of action.

nj:AJR 231.title: U.S. Hostage & Wrongful Detainee Day-designate March 9 each year
nj:AJR 231.summary: Designates March 9 of each year as U.S. Hostage and Wrongful Detainee Day.

nj:AJR 46.title: Hindu Heritage Month-designates January of each year
nj:AJR 46.summary: Designates October of each year as Hindu Heritage Month in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 47.title: National Adoption Day/Month-designate Saturday before Thanksgiving & November
nj:AJR 47.summary: Designates the Saturday before Thanksgiving as "National Adoption Day" and November as "National Adoption Month" in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 57.title: Menstrual Toxic Shock Syndrome Awareness Day-designate March 30th each yr
nj:AJR 57.summary: Designates March 30 of each year as Menstrual Toxic Shock Syndrome Awareness Day.

nj:AJR 59.title: Diabetes and Cardiovascular Disease Awareness Month-designates November
nj:AJR 59.summary: Designates November of each year as Diabetes and Cardiovascular Disease Awareness Month in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 62.title: Children's Mental Health Awareness Week-designates first week of May each year
nj:AJR 62.summary: Designates the first week of May each year as Children's Mental Health Awareness Week in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 63.title: Korean American Day-designates January 13
nj:AJR 63.summary: Designates January 13 of each year as Korean American Day in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 66.title: Korean War-commemorates 70th anniversary of armistice
nj:AJR 66.summary: Commemorates the 71st anniversary of the armistice that ended fighting in the Korean War on July 27, 1953.

nj:AJR 69.title: Cesar Chavez Day-designates March 31
nj:AJR 69.summary: Designates March 31 of each year as Cesar Chavez Day in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 86.title: First-Generation College Student Day-permanently designate November 8 each year
nj:AJR 86.summary: Permanently designates November 8 of each year as First-Generation College Student Day in New Jersey.

nj:AJR 89.title: Hate and bias crimes-condemns hate in all forms
nj:AJR 89.summary: Declares the Legislature's rejection and condemnation of hatred, hate-based violence and bias-based discrimination, and recognizes that the Governor and Attorney General should continue assisting hate crime victims and improving security and preparedness.

nj:AR 107.title: Paratransit trans network, existing-utilize & fund, disab vet to medical centers
nj:AR 107.summary: Urges the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to use and fund existing paratransit networks to take disabled veterans to and from its New Jersey medical centers.

nj:AR 108.title: Inpatient hospital facility-establish at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst
nj:AR 108.summary: Urges the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to establish an inpatient hospital facility at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst.

nj:AR 111.title: Loneliness-recognizes as public health crisis
nj:AR 111.summary: As introduced, recognizes loneliness as a public health crisis in New Jersey.

nj:AR 117.title: Affordable Connectivity Program-urges Congress to permanently fund
nj:AR 117.summary: As introduced, urges the U.S. Congress to permanently fund the Affordable Connectivity Program, the federal broadband subsidy for low-income households.

nj:AR 120.title: Streamlined Sales/Use Tax Agreement-create definition, oral health care products
nj:AR 120.summary: Urges the Streamlined Sales Tax Governing Board to amend the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement to add a definition for oral health care products.

nj:AR 122.title: Alabama Supreme Court ruling-condemn; reaffirm freedom, reproductive care svcs
nj:AR 122.summary: Condemns the Alabama Supreme Court ruling in LePage v. Mobile Infirmary Clinic and pending federal bill H.R. 431, and reaffirms access to reproductive health care in New Jersey, including in vitro fertilization.

nj:AR 127.title: Arizona Supreme Court-condemns ruling in banning abortions in the state
nj:AR 127.summary: Condemns the Arizona Supreme Court ruling in Planned Parenthood v. Mayes that an 1864 abortion ban is enforceable, and reaffirms New Jersey residents' freedom to access reproductive health care services.

nj:AR 128.title: Taiwan Relations Act-Commemorates 45th anniversary of enactment
nj:AR 128.summary: Commemorates the 45th anniversary of the Taiwan Relations Act and the 35th anniversary of the New Jersey-Taiwan sister state relationship.

nj:AR 131.title: Public assistance programs-urges federal govt to raise federal poverty line
nj:AR 131.summary: As introduced, urges the federal government to raise the federal poverty line used to determine eligibility for public assistance programs.

nj:AR 138.title: LGBTQIA+ Pride Month-designates June 2024 in NJ
nj:AR 138.summary: Designates June 2024 as LGBTQIA+ Pride Month in New Jersey and urges public officials and residents to mark it with appropriate activities.

nj:AR 141.title: Artificial intelligence/content sharing platforms-prevent/remove harmful content
nj:AR 141.summary: Urges generative artificial intelligence and content-sharing platforms to make voluntary commitments to prevent and remove harmful content, including deceptive manipulated media known as deepfakes and cheapfakes.

nj:AR 147.title: Bump stocks-condemn US Supreme Court decision, reaffirms dangerous firearm
nj:AR 147.summary: Condemns the U.S. Supreme Court ruling in Garland v. Cargill, which held ATF exceeded its authority in banning bump stocks, and reaffirms New Jersey's commitment to its own law prohibiting the sale and possession of bump stocks.

nj:AR 148.title: Reproductive freedom & full access to health care-affirms commitment, protecting
nj:AR 148.summary: Condemns Republican members of Congress for not supporting S. 3612, a federal bill on access to in vitro fertilization, and reaffirms New Jersey's commitment to reproductive health care access, including IVF.

nj:AR 150.title: Gambling advertisements-urges prohibition to certain individuals
nj:AR 150.summary: Urges sports wagering licensees, casino licensees and internet gaming affiliates not to target known problem gamblers with personalized VIP marketing, and urges Major League Baseball and other leagues and players associations to reject such programs.

nj:AR 152.title: Breakfast Bowl-expresses support & recognizes food insecurity efforts
nj:AR 152.summary: Expresses support for the "Breakfast Bowl" football game between Montclair State University and Rowan University and recognizes the two schools' efforts on food insecurity.

nj:AR 153.title: Haskin Shellfish Research Laboratory-recognize the scientific advancements
nj:AR 153.summary: Recognizes the scientific work of Rutgers University's Haskin Shellfish Research Laboratory, including its development of new oyster strains.

nj:AR 154.title: Semiquincentennial of Declaration of Independance-prov joint session in honor
nj:AR 154.summary: Urges Congress to hold a joint session at Independence Hall in Philadelphia on July 2, 2026, in honor of the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

nj:AR 156.title: Per- & polyfluoroalkyl substances-offer legal remedies to victims exposed
nj:AR 156.summary: Asks Congress to pass legislation supporting research on PFAS exposure and offering legal remedies against manufacturers for people exposed to PFAS chemicals.

nj:AR 157.title: US Postal Svc. & its employees-honor contributions to American democracy
nj:AR 157.summary: Honors the U.S. Postal Service and its employees for their historic role in American democracy.

nj:AR 158.title: September 11, 2001-commemorate 25th anniversary
nj:AR 158.summary: Commemorates the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks.

nj:AR 164.title: Bruce Springsteen's 75th birthday-recognize and celebrate
nj:AR 164.summary: As introduced, recognizes and celebrates Bruce Springsteen's 75th birthday.

nj:AR 165.title: Proporty tax relief, proportional-enact fed leg providing, vet permanent disab
nj:AR 165.summary: As introduced, urges the President and Congress to enact federal legislation providing proportional property tax relief for honorably discharged veterans with a permanent service-connected disability.

nj:AR 166.title: Miss America Pageant-return to Atlantic City
nj:AR 166.summary: Urges the Miss America Pageant to return to Atlantic City in 2025 and every year after.

nj:AR 167.title: Assembly Select Committee on Ballot Design-establish
nj:AR 167.summary: Creates an Assembly Select Committee on Ballot Design, with 12 members (six appointed by the Speaker and six by the Minority Leader), to review research on primary and general election ballot design.

nj:AR 173.title: Unidentified drones-urge federal govt to investigate, operating in NJ airspace
nj:AR 173.summary: As introduced, urges the federal government to investigate sightings of unidentified drones operating in New Jersey airspace.

nj:AR 180.title: Forest mgt-engage alternative practices, periods of drought when burning unsafe
nj:AR 180.summary: Urges the Department of Environmental Protection, Pinelands Commission and Highlands Council to use alternative forest management practices during droughts when prescribed burning is unsafe.

nj:AR 186.title: Congressman William J. Pascrell, Jr.-honors life
nj:AR 186.summary: Honors the life and legacy of Congressman William J. Pascrell Jr., who died August 21, 2024, and urges New Jersey's members of Congress to join the Congressional Brain Injury Task Force he co-founded.

nj:AR 194.title: LGBTQ+ Pride Month-designate June 2025 in New Jersey
nj:AR 194.summary: Designates June 2025 as LGBTQ+ Pride Month in New Jersey and urges officials and residents to commemorate it with appropriate activities.

nj:AR 208.title: Year of Black History & 250 yrs of American independance-urge Gov. to desig 2026
nj:AR 208.summary: Urges the Governor to designate 2026 as the Year of Black History in New Jersey, marking 100 years of Black history observance and the nation's 250th anniversary of independence.

nj:AR 82.title: Xylazine-urges DOH to increase public awareness on effects
nj:AR 82.summary: Urges the Department of Health to take steps to inform the public of the dangers of xylazine, a veterinary tranquilizer linked to overdose deaths, when used as a recreational drug.

nj:AR 95.title: Tax code-urges to exclude all discharged student loans from federal income tax
nj:AR 95.summary: Urges Congress to amend the tax code to permanently exclude all forms of discharged student loans from federal income tax.

nj:S 1016.title: State agency websites-make accessible to people w/disabilities on mobile devices
nj:S 1016.summary: Sets Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 Level AA, or a newer version where the State agency finds it practicable, as the accessibility standard for State agency websites, which must also work on mobile devices.

nj:S 1017.title: Victim of sexual assault-establish right to notify developments in criminal case
nj:S 1017.summary: Gives sexual assault victims the right to be told if a DNA profile of an assailant was obtained, entered into a data bank, or matched to a profile in a data bank.

nj:S 1029.title: Invasive plant species-prohibits sale distribution or propagation without permit
nj:S 1029.summary: Bans the sale, distribution, import, export and propagation of listed invasive plant species, in phases after enactment, and creates an Invasive Species Council in the Department of Environmental Protection.

nj:S 1042.title: Protecting Against Forever Chemicals Act-concerns perfluoroalkyl/polyflouroalkyl
nj:S 1042.summary: Bans selling cosmetics, carpets, fabric treatments and food packaging with intentionally added PFAS beginning two years after enactment, requires labeling of PFAS in cookware, creates a PFAS source reduction program, and appropriates funds. The Division of Consumer Affairs enforces the sales bans.

nj:S 1067.title: Mental health-direct DHS to conduct landscape analysis of available services
nj:S 1067.summary: Directs the Department of Human Services to conduct a landscape analysis of mental health services available to people who are deaf or hard of hearing, with an 11-member advisory committee it appoints, and to report the findings.

nj:S 1087.title: Birthing options-midwives/physicians required to provide pregnant women w/info.
nj:S 1087.summary: Requires certified nurse midwives and obstetric physicians to give each pregnant patient written, evidence-based information on all available birthing options, in English and the seven most common other languages in the State.

nj:S 1090.title: Political violence-create crime; estab review board & training for law enforce
nj:S 1090.summary: Creates the crime of political violence, covering listed offenses such as homicide, assault and arson committed because of a victim's political participation or expression, graded one degree higher than the underlying crime, and requires training for law enforcement and prosecutors.

nj:S 1097.title: Health insurance-require carriers provide coverage for planned home childbirth
nj:S 1097.summary: Requires health insurers, State and school employee health plans, and Medicaid/NJ FamilyCare to cover planned home childbirth, including health care providers, doula services, equipment and medical supplies.

nj:S 1107.title: FY2026 approp act-amend, reassign to Parkside Bus. & Community in Partnership
nj:S 1107.summary: Amends the FY2026 budget to move $500,000 appropriated to the City of Camden for capital projects to Parkside Business & Community in Partnership, a Camden nonprofit.

nj:S 1148.title: Veterans professional/occupational license/certification-profession board issue
nj:S 1148.summary: Requires professional and occupational licensing boards to license veterans and service members who hold an equivalent license in good standing elsewhere and an honorable or general discharge, and to evaluate equivalent military training.

nj:S 1188.title: Behavioral health care treatment-lowers age minors can consent from 16 to 14
nj:S 1188.summary: Lowers from 16 to 14 the age at which a minor can consent to temporary outpatient behavioral health treatment under a licensed professional's supervision, excluding medication.

nj:S 1193.title: Restaurant reservations-concerns third-party restaurant reservation service
nj:S 1193.summary: Bans third-party restaurant reservation services from advertising, listing, promoting or selling reservations for a restaurant without a written agreement with it, with civil penalties up to $500 per violation, accruing daily, and lawsuits by affected restaurants or customers.

nj:S 1230.title: Electioneering-proh within 25 feet of person at polling place or ballot drop box
nj:S 1230.summary: Bars electioneering within 25 feet of a person waiting in line farther than 100 feet from a polling place or ballot drop box, extends tampering and obstruction offenses to drop boxes, and classifies electioneering as a disorderly persons offense.

nj:S 1237.title: Telemarketers making sales calls-required to display their name and phone number
nj:S 1237.summary: Requires telemarketers making sales calls to transmit their name and phone number to recipients' caller ID, or the seller's name and customer service number instead.

nj:S 1253.title: Unemployment benefits-concerns eligibility
nj:S 1253.summary: Allows an employee who quits a job after receiving another job offer that is then rescinded through no fault of the employee to collect unemployment benefits, and extends the allowed gap before the new job starts from seven to 10 days.

nj:S 1270.title: Human trafficking prosecution-elim statute of limitation, extend for civil cases
nj:S 1270.summary: Eliminates the five-year statute of limitations for human trafficking prosecutions and for victims' civil suits, and removes the time limit for prosecuting aggravated criminal sexual contact.

nj:S 1277.title: Affordable and senior citizen housing-establishes centralized directory
nj:S 1277.summary: Requires each municipality to report quarterly to the Department of Community Affairs on its affordable housing units, including affordable senior citizen and veteran units, for a directory published on the department's and NJ Housing Resource Center websites. Takes effect February 15, 2027.

nj:S 1279.title: Youth Detention Task Force-create
nj:S 1279.summary: Creates a 26-member Youth Detention Task Force to assess youth detention in New Jersey and recommend whether county facilities, Youth Justice Commission facilities, or another system would best serve young people.

nj:S 1281.title: Apparel, added perfluoroalkyl/polyfluoroalkyl-proh sale/manufacture/distribution
nj:S 1281.summary: Bans selling, making or distributing apparel and diaper products containing intentionally added PFAS beginning two years after the effective date, exempting protective equipment, military clothing and motorcycle or off-highway vehicle protective gear.

nj:S 1310.title: For-profit debt adjusters-eligible for licensing to conduct business in State
nj:S 1310.summary: Lets for-profit debt adjustment companies be licensed in New Jersey, where only nonprofits are now allowed, if they hold no consumer funds and are FTC-regulated; annual reports on consumers, fees and debt settled may be required; effective 180 days after enactment.

nj:S 1312.title: EMT and paramedic certification cards-MVC accept as ID verification program
nj:S 1312.summary: Lets applicants for permits, driver licenses, non-driver IDs and power vessel licenses submit a Department of Health EMT or paramedic certification card for two points under the Motor Vehicle Commission's Six-Point Identification Verification Program.

nj:S 1313.title: Businesses owned by LGBTQ+ persons-establishes certification program
nj:S 1313.summary: Authorizes the Department of the Treasury to certify businesses owned by LGBTQ+ people, like its certification of minority- and women-owned businesses, codifying a program created by executive order.

nj:S 1320.title: Licensed public adjusters-require cert information be included in cert contracts
nj:S 1320.summary: Requires public adjusters to use a written, signed contract listing license numbers, services, compensation and a notice of a three-business-day right to cancel; adjusters must keep an original on file for State inspection.

nj:S 1322.title: Credit reports-consumer reporting agencies provide a free report 3 times a year
nj:S 1322.summary: Requires consumer reporting agencies to provide a consumer a free credit report three times in any 12-month period on request, instead of once.

nj:S 1323.title: Aspire Program, NJ-revises various requirements
nj:S 1323.summary: Revises New Jersey Aspire redevelopment tax-credit program rules, including eligible project costs, a maximum eligibility period of 10 years, which municipalities count as government-restricted, and what qualifies as a special mission non-profit project.

nj:S 1325.title: Portable electronics insurance-authorize electronic delivery of documents
nj:S 1325.summary: Allows portable electronics insurers to deliver notices and documents by email, and requires another delivery method if an email likely was not received or the address is no longer valid.

nj:S 1340.title: Physical education/sport programs-permit students to opt out during Ramadan
nj:S 1340.summary: Requires the Education Commissioner, with the Health Commissioner, to develop guidance for public schools on accommodating students who fast for religious or medical reasons, including flexibility in physical education, athletics and exams, and communication with parents.

nj:S 1343.title: County fire academy course-req districts award high school graduation credits
nj:S 1343.summary: Lets students aged 16 to 18 who complete a county fire academy course and commit to two years of volunteering with their local fire department earn credit toward high school health, safety and physical education requirements.

nj:S 1370.title: Mercury free-new flooring for schools and child care centers be certified
nj:S 1370.summary: Prohibits construction permits for flooring work in schools, community centers and child care centers unless flooring materials identified by the Health Department as mercury sources are certified mercury-free by the manufacturer, with options for existing mercury-containing floors.

nj:S 1385.title: Lisa's Law-4 yr. pilot prog for electronic monitoring of domestic viol offenders
nj:S 1385.summary: Creates a four-year pilot in Ocean County letting courts order electronic monitoring, with the victim's consent, of people convicted of contempt of a domestic violence order, with notice to victims; appropriates $2.5 million.

nj:S 1388.title: Health club svcs contracts-proh limiting liability, injury caused by negligence
nj:S 1388.summary: Bans health club contracts from limiting the club's liability for injuries caused by the negligence of its owner, operator, agents or employees, with violations penalized under the Consumer Fraud Act, up to $10,000 for a first offense.

nj:S 1395.title: Limited liability company-allow to terminate alternate names
nj:S 1395.summary: Lets limited liability companies terminate a registered alternate name before the five-year registration ends, except companies that operate as residential landlords, which may not.

nj:S 1400.title: Uniform Partition of Heirs Prop Act-provide alt process, prop w/multiple owners
nj:S 1400.summary: Creates the Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act, setting an alternative court process for partition actions on jointly owned property inherited from a relative, with extra requirements before such property can be sold.

nj:S 1403.title: Employer/contractor, work for public body-register & submit payroll to DOLWD
nj:S 1403.summary: Requires employers and contractors doing work for public bodies to submit certified payroll records to the Department of Labor and the public entity; those not required to register under the Public Works Contractor Registration Act are exempt from registering.

nj:S 1411.title: Economic conditions, various-req stress testing on State's ability to prov svcs
nj:S 1411.summary: Requires the Treasury Department to conduct and publish, every third year, a stress test of the State's ability to maintain services under various economic conditions, and include it in the Governor's budget message.

nj:S 1420.title: Secondary mortgage loan payments-concerns requirements
nj:S 1420.summary: Exempts reverse mortgage transactions from the requirement that second mortgage loan payments be made in substantially equal installments over equal periods.

nj:S 1421.title: School performance reports-require info. about positive placement of graduates
nj:S 1421.summary: Requires school performance reports to include the number of graduates who obtain placement after high school, including apprenticeships.

nj:S 1422.title: Depreciation-allow alternative method, connection w/new affordable housing devel
nj:S 1422.summary: Lets taxpayers deduct, over 10 years, eligible property costs of building new affordable housing developments they own, under the corporation business tax and gross income tax.

nj:S 1425.title: Firearm trafficking offenses-expands culpability requirements
nj:S 1425.summary: Extends the fourth-degree crime of violating firearms regulatory provisions from knowing to knowing or reckless violations. Extends the second-degree crime for dealers selling a firearm meant for a disqualified person to cases where the dealer reasonably should have known.

nj:S 1430.title: Affordable housing voucher program-expand funding for homeownership expenses
nj:S 1430.summary: Requires the Department of Community Affairs to set aside part of State Rental Assistance Program funding for a program like the federal Section 8 homeownership program, letting voucher holders apply assistance to down payments and mortgage-related costs.

nj:S 1433.title: Benjamin Moore & the Sappers Company Memorial Hwy-desig bridge, Crosswicks Creek
nj:S 1433.summary: Names the Interstate 295 North bridge over Crosswicks Creek the "Benjamin Moore and the 693rd Sapper Company Memorial Highway," with no public funds used for signs.

nj:S 1439.title: Prosthetic appliance, additional-req health benefit coverage, cert circumstances
nj:S 1439.summary: Requires health coverage for an additional orthotic or prosthetic appliance for physical and recreational activities when a physician finds it necessary, reimbursed at Medicare rates, and covers appliances from licensed podiatrists.

nj:S 1441.title: School Plastics Upcycling Grant Program-establishes in DEP;$5M
nj:S 1441.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection to run a School Plastics Upcycling Grant Program, giving schools grants in proportion to the plastics they collect to buy furnishings made from upcycled plastic, starting with a three-year pilot.

nj:S 1445.title: Military service-req instit of higher ed readmit student, enrollment interrupted
nj:S 1445.summary: Requires public colleges to readmit undergraduates who withdrew for uniformed service, with the same academic status, on written request for the next semester, without charging an application or other fee.

nj:S 1446.title: Homebuyers, first generation & first-time-modify down payment assistance program
nj:S 1446.summary: Modifies the Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency's down payment assistance loan program for first-generation and first-time homebuyers, including who qualifies as first-generation (such as certain emancipated or unaccompanied homeless youth), and raises the maximum loan from $15,000 to $20,000.

nj:S 1447.title: Historic Trust, NJ-transfer to DCA & make cert changes to trustees & powers
nj:S 1447.summary: Moves the New Jersey Historic Trust from the Department of State to the Department of Community Affairs, requires trustees to have five years' experience in listed fields, and expands its power to charge fees.

nj:S 1458.title: DMVA mobile application-req to develop, provide guidance on available resources
nj:S 1458.summary: Gives the Commissioner of Veterans Affairs authority, and directs the commissioner to endeavor, to provide veterans and their families information on State and federal veterans' programs and benefits through a mobile application.

nj:S 1487.title: State-administered federal rental assistance-req. application option enhancement
nj:S 1487.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Community Affairs to establish, obtain or arrange a non-internet application method for housing, shelter and rental assistance programs the department administers, to the extent federal law permits, starting January 1, 2027.

nj:S 1493.title: Occupational therapy-update requirements for licensure
nj:S 1493.summary: Requires the Division of Consumer Affairs to set continuing competence requirements for renewing occupational therapy licenses, expands the definition of occupational therapy services, limits council terms, and names the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy to give exams.

nj:S 1526.title: Senior citizen or veteran identity theft-increase penalties
nj:S 1526.summary: Raises penalties for identity theft by one degree when a victim is a senior citizen or veteran, such as making a first offense under $500 a third-degree crime instead of fourth-degree.

nj:S 1533.title: Beach fees-municipalities charge reduced or no fee, children ages 12 to 17
nj:S 1533.summary: Lets municipalities charge no beach fee or a reduced fee to children aged 12 to 17 and to honorably discharged veterans regardless of length of service or disability.

nj:S 1548.title: Student sun protection-adopt policies on sunscreen use & sun-protective clothing
nj:S 1548.summary: Requires school districts to adopt a policy on students' use of sunscreen and sun-protective clothing outdoors at school. The policy may require parental permission and may not require a doctor's note.

nj:S 1576.title: Farm pesticide collection and disposal program-establish
nj:S 1576.summary: Creates a voluntary Department of Agriculture program to collect and dispose of unused pesticides, herbicides and fertilizers from commercial farms, with one collection event a year, generally a 2,000-pound yearly limit per participant, and a $1 million appropriation.

nj:S 1577.title: Roadways surrounding State capital complex-requires maintenance
nj:S 1577.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to maintain, including paving and snow plowing, sections of West State Street, West Lafayette Street, Barrack Street and Memorial Drive around the State capitol complex in Trenton.

nj:S 1602.title: Discrimination of basis of height or weight-prohibits under Law Against Discrim.
nj:S 1602.summary: Prohibits discrimination based on height or weight under the Law Against Discrimination, with exceptions for bona fide occupational qualifications in employment and safety reasons in public accommodations.

nj:S 1631.title: Discrimination of basis of height or weight-prohibits under Law Against Discrim.
nj:S 1631.summary: Prohibits discrimination based on height or weight under the Law Against Discrimination, with exceptions for bona fide occupational qualifications in employment and for safety reasons in public accommodations.

nj:S 1636.title: Voter registration-changes MVC procedures
nj:S 1636.summary: Revises Motor Vehicle Commission voter registration: standard license applicants must select or decline registration, notices let people request removal of a registration, and eligible people scheduled for release from incarceration are offered registration with their non-driver ID but registered only after release.

nj:S 1644.title: Real property & improvements, certain-sell as surplus, Twp. of Hillsborough
nj:S 1644.summary: Authorizes the State Treasurer to sell surplus property at 1600 Brooks Boulevard in Hillsborough to the Borough of Manville for $870,000, or by internet auction with that minimum bid.

nj:S 1759.title: Property tax credit option-increase for certain individuals
nj:S 1759.summary: Raises from 18 percent to 30 percent the share of rent treated as property taxes under the Property Tax Deduction Act, and raises the optional property tax credit from $50 to $250.

nj:S 1773.title: School performance reports-require info. about positive placement of graduates
nj:S 1773.summary: Requires school performance reports (report cards) to include the number of students who achieve placement after high school graduation, including in apprenticeships.

nj:S 1783.title: Cursive handwriting in public schools-requires instruction
nj:S 1783.summary: Requires school districts to include cursive handwriting instruction in the curriculum for grades three through five, with activities and materials helping students read and write legibly in cursive by the end of grade five.

nj:S 1815.title: Coordination Among Nonprofit Social Service Organizations-establish Task Force
nj:S 1815.summary: Creates a 17-member Task Force on Coordination Among Nonprofit Social Service Organizations to recommend ways to share services, form alliances to reduce duplication, and standardize expense reporting.

nj:S 1819.title: Student discipline records-req nonpublic school transfer to public school
nj:S 1819.summary: Requires nonpublic schools to send a transferring student's disciplinary records, and information received from courts or law enforcement about charged offenses, to the public school district within 14 days of its written request.

nj:S 1838.title: Bringing Veterans Home Initiative-codifies
nj:S 1838.summary: Codifies the Bringing Veterans Home initiative, directing the Department of Community Affairs' Office of Homelessness Prevention to set up six regional hubs, use State data on veteran homelessness, publish a standard referral form, and help veterans access housing and benefits.

nj:S 188.title: Delinquency complaint, alleged-req juvenile appear before court, where occurred
nj:S 188.summary: Requires juveniles accused of first- through third-degree offenses to appear in the county where the alleged incident occurred, rather than the county of their home, which is the current default venue.

nj:S 1896.title: Dredging control reserve fund-authorizes municipalities to establish
nj:S 1896.summary: Allows municipalities to create a dredging control reserve fund, into which unspent dredging budget balances may lapse, to pay for later dredging-related costs.

nj:S 1927.title: Veteran's gross income tax exemption-extends to deceased veteran spouses
nj:S 1927.summary: Lets the spouse of a deceased veteran keep claiming the $6,000 veterans' gross income tax exemption in later years until the spouse remarries.

nj:S 1962.title: Residents of long-term care facilities-provide certain protections
nj:S 1962.summary: Bars owners, officers and employees of long-term care facilities, and others who benefit financially from them, from serving as attorney-in-fact for a resident, though family members may still serve; such powers of attorney are void.

nj:S 1965.title: Pharmaceutical services in long-term care facilities-regulates provision
nj:S 1965.summary: Codifies Department of Health rules for pharmaceutical services in long-term care facilities, including a consultant pharmacist and a pharmacy and therapeutics committee, and adds a requirement aimed at preventing conflicts of interest.

nj:S 1989.title: Human trafficking-expands crime to include individuals who benefit financially
nj:S 1989.summary: Applies the mandatory 20-year minimum prison term and $25,000 minimum fine for human trafficking to any participant who benefits financially and to anyone trafficking minors for coerced labor or services.

nj:S 199.title: State House Complex-requires environmental sustainability plan
nj:S 199.summary: Requires the State Capitol Joint Management Commission to adopt and carry out an environmental sustainability plan for the State House Complex, covering energy efficiency, water conservation, carbon reduction, green building principles and annual performance reporting.

nj:S 2019.title: HIV prophylaxis-authorizes pharmacists to dispense w/out individual prescription
nj:S 2019.summary: Allows pharmacists to dispense HIV preexposure and postexposure prophylaxis without an individual prescription, under a standing order from the state health commissioner, and requires prescription benefits coverage for it.

nj:S 2024.title: Fiscal Year 2024-makes supplemental appropriations;$37.430M
nj:S 2024.summary: Adds $37.43 million in supplemental fiscal year 2024 appropriations and cuts $24 million from existing ones, a net increase of $13.43 million, and adjusts budget language provisions.

nj:S 2026.title: State budget, fiscal year 2026-State funds $58.782B and federal funds$31.007B
nj:S 2026.summary: Appropriates $58.78 billion in State funds and $31.01 billion in federal funds for the Fiscal Year 2026 State budget.

nj:S 2038.title: Institution's website-req. pub institution of higher ed post certain infomation
nj:S 2038.summary: Requires four-year public colleges to post average time to degree for each bachelor's degree, county colleges to post student outcome measures for associate degrees, and public institutions to post their annual fiscal monitoring report and required audits.

nj:S 2051.title: Domestic violence victim-req law enforcement officer conduct danger assessment
nj:S 2051.summary: Requires officers to administer the ODARA domestic violence risk assessment, or another approved tool, with an alleged victim's consent, and to facilitate services; an elevated-risk score requires notifying the victim and charging the defendant by complaint-warrant.

nj:S 2082.title: Summative evaluations, certain education professionals-revises schedule
nj:S 2082.summary: Creates a 13-member New Jersey Educator Evaluation Review Task Force to study the TEACHNJ Act evaluation system for teachers and administrators and make recommendations, and clarifies collection of student growth data.

nj:S 2141.title: Cryptocurrency automatic teller machines-prohibits
nj:S 2141.summary: Bans any business from owning, controlling, installing or managing a cryptocurrency ATM in New Jersey.

nj:S 216.title: Aquaculture products-concerns promotion through Jersey Fresh Prog;$25K
nj:S 216.summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to promote State-produced fish and shellfish from aquaculture through the Jersey Fresh Program, with a quality grading system, and appropriates $25,000 a year for that purpose.

nj:S 2160.title: Alcoholic beverage licenses-allow seasonal retail holder, exchange for full-year
nj:S 2160.summary: Lets holders of a seasonal retail alcohol consumption license convert it to a plenary license within 24 months, with municipal approval, for a fee paid to the municipality of 43 percent of the average local plenary license price, or $350,000 in specified cases.

nj:S 2167.title: School breakfast and lunch nutrition standards-public schools comply
nj:S 2167.summary: Requires public and nonpublic schools in the federal school lunch and breakfast programs to follow USDA nutrition standards, including for competitive foods, and any more stringent federal standards adopted later.

nj:S 2181.title: School employees, public-eliminates requirement for State residency for 3 years
nj:S 2181.summary: Lets school districts and charter schools hire out-of-state residents for three years without meeting the State residency requirement, if the job was advertised to residents for three months; hires must become residents within three years.

nj:S 2188.title: Legionnaires's disease-DEP, DOH, DCA & public water systems prevent/control
nj:S 2188.summary: Requires state agencies and operators of large public water systems and certain buildings to take steps against Legionnaires' disease, including maintaining minimum chlorine disinfectant levels, distribution system maintenance plans and best management practices set by the DEP.

nj:S 219.title: Affordable housing programs-estab guidelines for creditworthiness determinations
nj:S 219.summary: Bars landlords from using credit scores when screening affordable housing applicants who hold a State or federal tenant-based subsidy, allowing negative credit history only for repeated missed payments of the tenant share of rent.

nj:S 2200.title: Fruit and vegetable donations-provides CBT and income tax credits for value
nj:S 2200.summary: Creates a three-year pilot tax credit for commercial farm operators who donate fruits or vegetables to in-State charities, equal to 50 percent of wholesale value, up to $5,000 per tax period, against corporation business or gross income tax.

nj:S 2236.title: Jury duty-exempts nursing mothers
nj:S 2236.summary: Exempts nursing mothers from jury duty when the child is one year old or younger.

nj:S 224.title: Recyclable products-prohibit sale/distribution/import unless widely recycled
nj:S 224.summary: Amends a recyclability-claims bill: DEP contracts with a nonprofit recycling group to maintain a list of items by curbside eligibility and run an annual education program, funded by up to 2% of the State Recycling Fund; caps higher-education grants at 3%, not 5%.

nj:S 2243.title: Menstrual products-req instit of higher education develop menstrual equity plan
nj:S 2243.summary: Requires the president of each public college or university to develop a plan for menstrual equity within six months, covering needs, product access, distribution locations and projected costs.

nj:S 226.title: Shipping box size-proh use of box greater than 2 times volume of product shipped
nj:S 226.summary: Bars large online retailers and major retailers from shipping products in a box more than twice the product's volume, with civil penalties of $250 to $500 per offense.

nj:S 2260.title: Legally protected health care activities-secure protections, patient & provider
nj:S 2260.summary: Creates a crime and civil action for interfering by obstruction, intimidation, threat or property damage with reproductive health care services, defined to include abortion and gender-identity care; widens existing limits on state cooperation with other states’ investigations and extradition to cover that care.

nj:S 2275.title: Hair products, cert-bans carcinogens & cert toxicants, chemicals & compounds
nj:S 2275.summary: Requires manufacturers of synthetic-fiber hair products to test for carcinogens, reproductive toxicants and volatile organic compounds, certify the results, and give the certification to buyers.

nj:S 2283.title: Psilocybin Behavioral Health Access & Svcs Act-auth production/use of psilocybin
nj:S 2283.summary: Creates a Department of Health pilot program for psilocybin therapy at up to three hospitals, one each in the northern, central and southern regions, with an advisory board, required data reporting, and a $6 million appropriation to a new research fund.

nj:S 2284.title: Office of Resilience in DCF-establishes
nj:S 2284.summary: Puts into law the Office of Resilience in the Department of Children and Families, led by an executive director, to coordinate Statewide initiatives on adverse childhood experiences, training and trauma-informed services.

nj:S 229.title: Institutions of higher education-collect & report employment data for cert grad
nj:S 229.summary: Requires colleges and universities to publish employment outcomes and earnings data for graduates of the three most recent academic years, using the New Jersey Statewide Data System, with their other consumer information.

nj:S 2310.title: Employment listings-requires transparency concerning compensation
nj:S 2310.summary: Requires employers to disclose pay (or a pay range) and a general description of benefits in advertised job and transfer postings, and to make reasonable efforts to announce advertised promotion opportunities to affected employees before deciding.

nj:S 2311.title: Criminal history background check-require for licensure, cert. health care prof.
nj:S 2311.summary: Requires criminal history background checks before initial licensing for applied behavior analysts, creative arts and activities therapists, and dietitians and nutritionists.

nj:S 2331.title: Equitable Outcomes in Child Support Collection Act-estab procedures, collection
nj:S 2331.summary: Removes the provisions making legally responsible persons liable to reimburse the state for maintenance costs of children in resource family homes under DCPP care, and voids existing related child support debts, judgments, warrants and liens.

nj:S 2332.title: Guardianship of minor-allow complaint, filed six months before reaching age 18
nj:S 2332.summary: Allows a guardianship complaint for a minor expected to need a guardian at age 18 to be filed up to 180 days before the 18th birthday; any resulting judgment takes effect no earlier than age 18.

nj:S 2335.title: Latino/Hispanic Americans-req sch dist prov instruction on history/contributions
nj:S 2335.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt social studies standards on Latino and Hispanic history, and school districts to teach it in grades kindergarten through 12.

nj:S 2339.title: Parkinson's disease-establishes State registry
nj:S 2339.summary: Requires the Department of Health to create a Statewide Parkinson's disease registry, with hospitals, facilities and practitioners required to report each diagnosed case; registry information is generally confidential.

nj:S 2344.title: Child Care Facilities Improvement Program-limit grants funded, licensed centers
nj:S 2344.summary: Removes language in the Child Care Revitalization Act requiring that $54.5 million in federal facility improvement grants fund registered family child care homes.

nj:S 2346.title: Code Red alert-creates to shelter at-risk individuals during hot weather
nj:S 2346.summary: Creates a three-year pilot in which the five counties with the highest homeless populations may receive $500,000 grants to run Code Red alert plans, declared on a heat advisory or Air Quality Index of 151 or higher; appropriates $2.5 million.

nj:S 2347.title: Accessory dwelling units & municipal land use regulations-concerns development
nj:S 2347.summary: Allows accessory dwelling units on property zoned for single- or two-family homes, requires municipalities to follow state model ordinances, and requires decisions on complete applications within 60 days or they are deemed approved.

nj:S 2368.title: Portable solar generation devices, cert-exempt, interconnection & net metering
nj:S 2368.summary: Exempts plug-in portable solar devices of up to 1,200 watts from interconnection agreements and net metering requirements, and requires landlords (for tenants who pay their own electricity), homeowners' associations and municipalities to allow their use, barring municipal permits.

nj:S 2373.title: First responders diagnosed w/post-traumatic stress disorder-prov emp protections
nj:S 2373.summary: Bars public employers from firing, harassing or retaliating against paid first responders for taking leave tied to a qualifying work-related PTSD diagnosis.

nj:S 2376.title: Students w/epilepsy & seizure disorder-ensure all staff trained every 5 years
nj:S 2376.summary: Requires school boards of education to train all staff they employ in the care of students with epilepsy and seizure disorders once every five years.

nj:S 2386.title: Vol emerg service organizations members-prov income tax credit, personal veh use
nj:S 2386.summary: Creates a refundable gross income tax credit, up to $500 ($1,000 for joint filers), reimbursing unpaid volunteer fire and first aid members for personal vehicle mileage used on active duty.

nj:S 2428.title: Eagleton Science and Politics Fellowship Program-codifies; makes approp.
nj:S 2428.summary: Codifies the Eagleton Science and Politics Fellowship Program at Rutgers, placing at least four doctoral-level scientists, engineers or health professionals yearly in the Legislature and executive branch, and appropriates $360,000 plus at least $520,000 annually.

nj:S 2435.title: Emerg Medical Technician Training Fund-revise requirements concerning reimb elig
nj:S 2435.summary: Lets any agency or organization seek reimbursement from the Emergency Medical Technician Training Fund for unreimbursed training costs of volunteer EMTs, even if the squad charges for basic life support services.

nj:S 2437.title: Criminal contempt violations, certain-provide legal representation
nj:S 2437.summary: Directs the Office of the Public Defender to provide legal representation to indigent defendants charged with contempt for violating domestic violence restraining orders, when the offense is a fourth-degree crime or disorderly persons offense.

nj:S 2456.title: School bus transporting student w/ disabilities-call 911, life-threatening emerg
nj:S 2456.summary: Requires school bus drivers and aides to call 911 during a potential life-threatening emergency on the bus and report the call to the Department of Education, and requires districts or contractors to keep records and provide training.

nj:S 2457.title: Armed Forces of US or National Guard-permit excused absence, student enlisted
nj:S 2457.summary: Allows students in grades 11 and 12 up to three excused absences a year for college or technical school visits and up to three for military recruitment activities, without those absences affecting transcripts or perfect-attendance status.

nj:S 2470.title: Prosecutors Part of PERS-permit service credit for judicial clerk service
nj:S 2470.summary: Lets county prosecutors buy Prosecutors Part pension credit for prior State judicial clerk service, lifts the law-practice bar for retired judges serving as appointed prosecutors, raises county prosecutor salaries to $204,166.50 retroactive to January 2024, and sets a separate presiding Appellate Division judge salary.

nj:S 2491.title: Respite care-increase maximum number of monthly service hours funded through DCF
nj:S 2491.summary: Increases the maximum respite care funded by the Department of Children and Families to up to 90 hours over a 90-day period for eligible families.

nj:S 2493.title: Special care nursing facilities-estab rate, neurologically impaired adult unit
nj:S 2493.summary: Sets a minimum NJ FamilyCare rate of $1,100 a day, or the facility's FY 2022 rate if higher, for special care nursing facilities with a certificate of need for a neurologically impaired young adult unit as of July 1, 2023, starting January 1, 2024.

nj:S 2495.title: Cosmetologist-hairstylist & hair braider-req training, include on textured hair
nj:S 2495.summary: Requires cosmetology, barbering and hair braiding school curricula and licensing exams to include working with textured hair, without increasing the required training hours.

nj:S 2496.title: Office of New Americans-establish in Department of Human Services
nj:S 2496.summary: Codifies the Office of New Americans, created by a 2019 executive order, in the Department of Human Services as a central source of expertise and data on immigrants and refugees, to administer services and advise state agencies.

nj:S 2498.title: Common application and web portal, substitute teachers-establish and maintain
nj:S 2498.summary: Requires the Education Commissioner, within funds appropriated, to create within 12 months an educator job web portal listing public and approved private special-education school openings with links to school applications, plus a virtual applicant profile system. Allows a private vendor contract.

nj:S 2531.title: Police presence at public sch/sr resid center-permit being used as polling place
nj:S 2531.summary: Allows plain-clothes police officers at a school or senior residential center used as a polling place when it requests them, and requires schools used as polling places to adopt security plans keeping voters from reaching or interacting with students.

nj:S 2551.title: Epinephrine-requires law enforcement officers to carry
nj:S 2551.summary: Requires law enforcement officers in departments that make epinephrine auto-injectors available to complete an approved training program and give their employer the certificate, and lets departments stock the devices in vehicles or medical kits.

nj:S 2565.title: Victims and witnesses testify-permits via close circuit television
nj:S 2565.summary: Lets all victims and witnesses of human trafficking, not just those involving sexual activity, testify by closed-circuit television, and lets the judge allow it without a formal motion.

nj:S 2594.title: Dam restoration/repair & inland waters projects-approp. $28.670M bond act monies
nj:S 2594.summary: Appropriates $28,670,924 in 2003 and 1992 bond act money for loans to 17 listed dam restoration and repair projects and inland waters projects, including administrative costs.

nj:S 2606.title: Mental health rehab services-requires Medicaid reimbursement provided
nj:S 2606.summary: Requires Medicaid to reimburse mental health rehabilitation services provided through Clubhouse International-accredited clubhouse programs, without precluding coverage of other prescribed mental health services.

nj:S 261.title: Compassion for Community Cats Law-spaying/neutering stray/feral cats; estab fund
nj:S 261.summary: Requires, with limited exceptions, cats to be spayed or neutered before adoption from shelters and rescues, and trapped community cats to be sterilized, ear-tipped and rabies-vaccinated before release; creates a fund for municipal and county grants.

nj:S 2611.title: Menstrual products-req instit of higher education provide, all campus buildings
nj:S 2611.summary: Requires each public higher education institution to convene a menstrual equity task force that, within six months, submits a plan including estimated need and locations for free menstrual product distribution.

nj:S 2644.title: Reading intervention program-req sch dist implement, students in certain grades
nj:S 2644.summary: Requires school districts to offer a reading intervention program to students in kindergarten through grade three, with progress monitoring and instruction in phonics, fluency, vocabulary and comprehension.

nj:S 265.title: Multiple dwellings-prov priority status to cert residents moving to lower floors
nj:S 265.summary: Requires owners of multiple dwellings of three or more floors to give senior and mobility-limited residents priority and right of first refusal for same-size units on lower floors; condos and co-ops are excluded.

nj:S 2652.title: Sexual exploitation or abuse of children-revises statutory terms
nj:S 2652.summary: Replaces the term "child pornography" and related uses of "pornography" in state law with terms such as "child sexual abuse or exploitation material."

nj:S 2697.title: Motor vehicles, certain-permit to display both amber and green warning lights
nj:S 2697.summary: Permits snow and ice removal vehicles owned by the State, bi-state agencies or local governments, or contracted by the Department of Transportation, to display green warning lights along with amber lights during hazardous operations.

nj:S 2782.title: Licensed or regulated professionals, cert-concerns independent contractor status
nj:S 2782.summary: Provides that certain licensed professionals, including insurance producers and registered securities agents, may be treated as independent contractors if they work under a written agreement describing them as such.

nj:S 2783.title: Travel Insurance Act-concerns
nj:S 2783.summary: Establishes the Travel Insurance Act, setting licensing rules for travel insurance producers, applying premium tax to certain travel insurance premiums, and codifying how travel insurance is sold and administered.

nj:S 2786.title: Contracts, State-proh enter into, limits ability to install & run cert software
nj:S 2786.summary: Requires State contracts to license software designed for generally available desktop or server hardware without limiting the agency's ability to install or run it on hardware of its choosing.

nj:S 2788.title: Farmland preservation purposes-appropriate CBT revenues;$128.241M
nj:S 2788.summary: Appropriates $128.241 million from farmland preservation funds to the State Agriculture Development Committee for buying development easements and farmland, and for grants to counties, municipalities and nonprofits for farmland preservation.

nj:S 2791.title: State tax refunds and unemployment insurance benefits-provide payment options
nj:S 2791.summary: Requires State agencies to give State employees, taxpayers and unemployment claimants the option to receive payments by paper check, and requires unemployment claimants to choose a payment method in writing.

nj:S 2792.title: Farmland preservation purposes-approp, CBT revenues & Preserv Fund;$500K
nj:S 2792.summary: Appropriates $500,000 to the State Agriculture Development Committee for a municipal planning incentive grant for farmland preservation in Washington Township, Warren County, from dedicated corporation business tax revenue and the 2009 Farmland Preservation Fund.

nj:S 2793.title: Farmland preservation purposes-approp, CBT revenues & Preserv Fund;$1.723M
nj:S 2793.summary: Appropriates $1.723 million to the State Agriculture Development Committee for farmland preservation, funding grants to one nonprofit of up to 50 percent of the cost of easements or purchases on five farms.

nj:S 2810.title: SPRS, member of board of trustees-remove req, 2 members be private citizens
nj:S 2810.summary: Removes the requirement that two Governor-appointed members of the State Police Retirement System board of trustees be private citizens who are neither active nor retired members of the system.

nj:S 2816.title: Electric infrastructure improvement plans-req pub utilities submit & implement
nj:S 2816.summary: Requires each electric utility to file a plan with the Board of Public Utilities within 120 days of enactment for reopening distribution circuits closed to new renewable energy installations, and to report interconnection performance metrics.

nj:S 2822.title: Workers' compensation-revises law, increase contingency attorney fee cap
nj:S 2822.summary: Raises the cap on attorney contingency fees in workers' compensation cases from 20 percent to 25 percent.

nj:S 2825.title: Alcoholic beverage licenses, addl-removes time limitation on issuance
nj:S 2825.summary: Removes the five-year time limit on municipalities in the Fort Monmouth redevelopment area issuing or transferring special alcoholic beverage consumption licenses.

nj:S 2837.title: School dist additional spending, budget yr-authorize to submit separate proposal
nj:S 2837.summary: Lets school districts without a board of school estimate ask voters at a special school election for permission to raise additional taxes for the next budget year beyond the district's authorized levy.

nj:S 2840.title: Conservation restrictions, certain-directs DEP lift as condition of CAFRA permit
nj:S 2840.summary: As introduced, directs the Department of Environmental Protection to lift a CAFRA permit conservation restriction on land needed for expanding a school for special needs children, if a similar restriction covers land at least twice as large within 20 miles.

nj:S 286.title: Low-income person-permits local units & authorities to reduce water/sewer fees
nj:S 286.summary: Allows local governments and authorities that run water, sewer or stormwater systems to reduce fees for low-income residents, with eligibility procedures, applicant documentation, and a set-aside of funds to offset the lost revenue.

nj:S 2864.title: Professional athletes-establishes working hours, certain minors employed
nj:S 2864.summary: Lets 14- and 15-year-olds employed as professional athletes work until 11:30 p.m. of any day, with written parental permission stating permitted hours.

nj:S 2869.title: Immigrant workers-establishes penalties for employers that coerce workers
nj:S 2869.summary: Imposes civil penalties on employers that coerce employees over immigration status: up to $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 for a second and $10,000 for each later violation.

nj:S 2875.title: Health benefits plans-make certain changes to calculation of min loss ratio req
nj:S 2875.summary: Requires the 80 percent minimum loss ratio for individual and small-employer health plans to be calculated using a three-year rolling average, and directs the Department of Banking and Insurance to issue rules for that calculation.

nj:S 2876.title: John R. Elliott Memorial Interchange-desig Hwy Route 42 & Hwy Route 295
nj:S 2876.summary: Designates the interchange between Route 42 and Interstate 295 as the John R. Elliott Memorial Interchange, with no public funds used for signs; private contributions may pay for them.

nj:S 2886.title: Insulin manufacturer assistance programs-req pharmacies prov cert info regarding
nj:S 2886.summary: Requires pharmacies to post a Department of Health notice about insulin manufacturer assistance programs on their website and at points of sale, and to give a department pamphlet to anyone who asks. Takes effect 12 months after enactment.
