nj:S 290.title: Tenants, sr citizens & certain with disabilities-extend protected tenancy period
nj:S 290.summary: Extends the protected tenancy period for senior citizen tenants and tenants with disabilities in converted buildings to the tenant's lifetime, rather than ending 40 years after the conversion recording.

nj:S 2912.title: Civics education-req. instrution on voting in curriculum, students in grade 12
nj:S 2912.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt social studies standards on voting, and school districts to teach grade 12 students about the importance of voting and voter registration, starting the first full school year after enactment.

nj:S 2930.title: Government records, access-makes various changes to process;$8M
nj:S 2930.summary: Changes the Open Public Records Act, including letting custodians deny duplicative requests, defining personal identifying information, setting response timelines, moving responsibility for violations to the agency, and restructuring the Government Records Council.

nj:S 2947.title: Mail-in ballot messengers-proh acceptance, offer, or provision of consideration
nj:S 2947.summary: Bars mail-in ballot messengers and bearers from accepting compensation other than transportation reimbursement, bars anyone from offering it, and allows employees and volunteers of certain nonprofits, hospitals, care facilities and veterans' homes to serve as messengers or bearers.

nj:S 2948.title: Fire escape inspections-performed by engineer or certified inspection company
nj:S 2948.summary: Limits installing, repairing, inspecting and maintaining fire escapes to registered design professionals or employees of certified fire escape contractors.

nj:S 2951.title: Tax law violation-monetary award, report violation by employer in construction
nj:S 2951.summary: Requires the Division of Taxation to pay whistleblowers generally 15 to 30 percent of proceeds collected when their information about a construction-industry employer's tax violations leads to an action or settlement.

nj:S 2952.title: Cooperative sober living residences & boarding houses-concerns State regulation
nj:S 2952.summary: Adds oversight of cooperative sober living residences: higher maximum penalties for licensing violations, a public state list of licensed residences, two unannounced inspections yearly, incident reporting, and multiple supervisors with one always present rather than a live-in supervisor.

nj:S 2953.title: LGBTQIA+ Pride Month-establish in New Jersey
nj:S 2953.summary: Designates June of each year as LGBTQIA+ Pride Month in New Jersey and requests the Governor to issue an annual proclamation encouraging public officials and residents to observe it.

nj:S 2959.title: MyNJHelps web-based platform-reformat as centralized online resource
nj:S 2959.summary: Directs the State Chief Technology Officer to expand the MyNJHelps platform within 365 days into a single online resource and single application covering all State public assistance programs, rather than only food, cash and NJFamilyCare benefits.

nj:S 2961.title: Public works contract-establishes minimum qualifications, persons employed
nj:S 2961.summary: Requires contractors registering for public works to certify that each journeyperson completing contract work has graduated from an apprenticeship program equivalent to the craft's union apprenticeship standards or has four years of documented tradesperson work verifiable by tax filings.

nj:S 2962.title: Contractor, prevailing wage project-provide orientation meeting to new employee
nj:S 2962.summary: Requires prevailing-wage contractors and subcontractors to give each new employee an orientation on wages and job classification and keep signed forms at least six years; not required for employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement.

nj:S 2969.title: Porperty tax levy cap-concerns retirement of county debt svc & amount raised
nj:S 2969.summary: Changes county property tax levy cap rules so that retiring county debt does not reduce the amount a county may raise.

nj:S 2996.title: Nurses, advanced practice-eliminates certain practice restrictions for
nj:S 2996.summary: Exempts advanced practice nurses from joint protocols with a physician when they have over 5,000 practice hours and provide primary or behavioral health care, excluding general obstetrics and cosmetic services.

nj:S 3006.title: Burglary of residence-upgrades to crime of second degree
nj:S 3006.summary: Creates the crime of home invasion burglary, a first-degree crime when a person enters a residence to commit an offense and injures someone or is armed with a deadly weapon, and residential burglary, a second-degree crime for entering a residence to commit an offense.

nj:S 3023.title: Long-term care facilities/acute care hospitals-prov cert protections, residents
nj:S 3023.summary: Bars long-term care facility owners, administrators, officers, employees, affiliates and anyone benefiting financially from a facility from acting as attorney-in-fact for a resident or applicant, except family members, and requires the Department of Health to create standard admission contracts.

nj:S 3041.title: Public works contracts-proh receiving when one member fails to pay wages
nj:S 3041.summary: Defines cooperative for the three-year bar on public works contracts for firms that failed to pay prevailing wages, and allows public works construction purchases through cooperative agreements only if competitively bid by a New Jersey contracting unit and subject to prevailing wage law.

nj:S 3052.title: Service members & dependants-concerns grade options at instit of higher ed
nj:S 3052.summary: Extends the grade options for a course a student cannot finish due to an unplanned military obligation to dependents of service members at public colleges, clarifies the existing options and adds new ones.

nj:S 3091.title: Doulas-requires DHS establish public awareness campaign
nj:S 3091.summary: Requires the Maternal and Infant Health Innovation Authority to run a public awareness campaign on doula and midwife services, contingent on funding, effective July 1, 2027.

nj:S 3097.title: Economic Redevelopment & Growth Grant prog-modifies req for cert projects
nj:S 3097.summary: Extends from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2028 the deadline for certain qualified projects in the Economic Redevelopment and Growth Grant program to submit a temporary certificate of occupancy, and changes the definition of project cost.

nj:S 3114.title: Law enforcement officer-reveal facial identity during cert public interactions
nj:S 3114.summary: Requires law enforcement officers, including federal officers, to show their faces during public interactions, with exceptions, and to present identification such as a uniform, ID, badge number or spoken name before arresting or detaining someone.

nj:S 3132.title: Telephones/wireless communication devices, secondhand dealers-impose cert req
nj:S 3132.summary: Requires secondhand dealers of cell phones and wireless devices to record each device's description and identifier plus a receipt, and to require two forms of identification, at least one with a photo, from sellers.

nj:S 3134.title: Commercial driver licenses and learner's permits-req MVC take certain action
nj:S 3134.summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Commission to check the federal drug and alcohol clearinghouse for commercial license and permit applicants and holders, deny issuance or renewal to prohibited drivers, and downgrade their existing licenses.

nj:S 3142.title: Personal injury protection coverage-proh. health insurance coverage as primary
nj:S 3142.summary: Ends the option to choose health insurance as primary coverage for personal injury protection, and makes the named insured's PIP coverage primary for the insured and resident relatives without their own policy.

nj:S 3152.title: Utility assistance program-concerns notification req, coronavirus 2019 pandemic
nj:S 3152.summary: Requires State agencies running utility assistance programs to keep public information current with a phone number, and requires utilities to put program and consumer-protection information on bills, overdue notices and websites.

nj:S 3153.title: Child in out of home placement-prohibits DCF from using federal benefits
nj:S 3153.summary: Bars the Department of Children and Families from using a child in out-of-home placement's property or benefits to offset the State's care costs, except to keep the child within federal SSI asset limits; requires an ABLE or trust account for eligible children.

nj:S 3156.title: School property, cert-permit to lease, fed qualified health centers w/o bidding
nj:S 3156.summary: Lets school boards lease school property to federally qualified health centers for a nominal fee without competitive bidding. A health center sharing a building must be in a part separate from where students may be present, where federal law permits.

nj:S 3158.title: State tax refunds and unemployment insurance benefits-provide payment options
nj:S 3158.summary: Requires State agencies to give State employees, taxpayers and unemployment claimants the option to receive payments by paper check, and requires unemployment claimants to choose a payment method in writing.

nj:S 3173.title: Insurance liability cases-require insurance companies be named defendants
nj:S 3173.summary: Requires insurance companies sued in uninsured or underinsured motorist cases to be identified in litigation by their legal name, not an assumed or fictitious name.

nj:S 3179.title: Emergency operations plans, cert-req to be submitted to law enforce agencies
nj:S 3179.summary: Requires emergency operations plans for sports and entertainment facilities, movie theaters and places of worship to be filed electronically and include digital emergency mapping data, and lowers the place-of-worship seating threshold from over 500 to over 300.

nj:S 3183.title: Renewable energy incentive programs-modifies various provisions
nj:S 3183.summary: Modifies renewable energy incentive programs: allows co-location of solar facilities, lets 5-to-20 MW rooftop, landfill, contaminated-site and mining-site projects join community solar until 2028, and requires utilities to process interconnection applications for certain solar projects.

nj:S 3189.title: Angel Investor Tax Credit Act-increase tax credits, certain tech bus ventures
nj:S 3189.summary: Raises the Angel Investor tax credit from 20 to 35 percent of a qualified investment (40 percent with the additional credit), lowers the maximum employee count for eligible businesses from 224 to 149, and cuts the annual credit cap from $35 million to $25 million.

nj:S 3190.title: Delinquency complaint, alleged-req juvenile appear before court, where occurred
nj:S 3190.summary: Requires juveniles accused of first- to third-degree-level offenses to appear in the county where the incident occurred, and those accused of lesser offenses to appear in their home county unless the court finds good cause.

nj:S 3192.title: Real Estate Consumer Protection Enhancement Act-concerns
nj:S 3192.summary: Writes into law the duties that brokerage firms and buyer's, seller's, dual and designated agents and transaction brokers owe consumers in real estate deals, sets broker-agreement terms, and adds an hour of agency continuing education.

nj:S 3195.title: Food service businesses-proh providing single-use utensils and condiments
nj:S 3195.summary: Bars full-service restaurants with 10 or more seats from providing single-use utensils and condiments to on-site customers, and lets casual dining places provide them only on request. Sets a warning for a first violation, then $100 and $250 penalties.

nj:S 3199.title: New Jersey-Haiti Commission-establishes
nj:S 3199.summary: Creates a 13-member New Jersey-Haiti Commission in the Department of State to advise the Governor and Legislature on economic and cultural links with Haiti and on economic challenges facing the State's Haitian-American community.

nj:S 3219.title: Gubernatorial budget message to Legislature, Fiscal Year 2027-concerns
nj:S 3219.summary: Moves the deadline for the Governor's Fiscal Year 2027 budget message to the Legislature from the fourth Tuesday in February to Tuesday, March 10, 2026.

nj:S 3235.title: Intoxicating hemp products, certain-regulates production and sale
nj:S 3235.summary: Regulates the production and sale of intoxicating hemp products by treating them as cannabis items under the Cannabis Regulatory Commission, aligning definitions of hemp and total THC concentration.

nj:S 3237.title: Closed captioning, on televisions in State buildings-display
nj:S 3237.summary: Requires every television in a State-owned or leased building that is open to the public or public employees to display closed captioning whenever it is available, except older sets that cannot show captions.

nj:S 3245.title: High school student financial aid application-revises requirements
nj:S 3245.summary: Makes permanent the requirement that high school students complete a financial aid application to receive a diploma unless waived, and requires an annual report from the Higher Education Student Assistance Authority.

nj:S 3251.title: Infrastructure Bank-make various changes to enabling act
nj:S 3251.summary: Changes the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank's enabling act to define and allow cross-investment between its financing programs, clarify that the $10 billion debt limit counts outstanding debt, and allow loans and other assistance for wastewater, water supply and onsite wastewater projects.

nj:S 3275.title: Film and digital media content production tax credit program-revises
nj:S 3275.summary: Revises the film and digital media production tax credit program to cover wages of workers exempt from New Jersey income tax under reciprocity agreements, and makes unused Aspire and Emerge credits available to more program participants.

nj:S 3278.title: Glucagon & blood glucose tests-extends permission to administer to EMTs
nj:S 3278.summary: Directs the Health Commissioner to set standards for emergency medical technicians to be authorized to administer glucagon and blood glucose tests, and lets the commissioner modify, suspend or end that authorization when needed for public health, safety or welfare.

nj:S 3287.title: Real property interests, conservation purposes-prov gross income tax deduction
nj:S 3287.summary: Creates a gross income tax deduction for money received for selling real property interests, including bargain sales, for conservation purposes.

nj:S 3306.title: Health club svc-require notification to member, contract sold to new owner
nj:S 3306.summary: Requires a health club to notify members by mail or email at least 60 days, and again 30 days, before a change in ownership, including the new business name and when billing starts.

nj:S 3308.title: Grid supply solar fac, cert-implement cert improvements, interconnection process
nj:S 3308.summary: Requires electric utilities to approve Level 3 interconnection applications for grid supply solar or energy storage facilities of 20 megawatts or less, unless incomplete or unsafe, and to provide an initial feasibility study within 90 days.

nj:S 3309.title: Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act-establishes
nj:S 3309.summary: Establishes the Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act: the Motor Vehicle Commission adds an open-recall notice to registration renewals, and franchisors pay dealers at least 1.5% of a used vehicle's value monthly when recall parts are unavailable and a stop-sale is issued.

nj:S 3317.title: Senior residents-creates central registry & prov supply kits during emergencies
nj:S 3317.summary: Allows each county to set up a voluntary central registry of residents 65 and older who want extra help in emergencies, and to prepare emergency supply kits for registered seniors.

nj:S 3353.title: Housing resident farm employees, commercial farms-adopt agric mgt practice
nj:S 3353.summary: Directs the State Agriculture Development Committee to adopt an agricultural management practice allowing housing for resident farm employees on commercial farms, making that housing eligible for Right to Farm Act protection.

nj:S 3366.title: Special plates, firefighters & first aid or rescue squad members-eliminates fee
nj:S 3366.summary: Eliminates the $15 fee for special license plates for firefighters and first aid or rescue squad members, requiring annual renewal with proof of continued membership.

nj:S 3368.title: Lead-based paint hazards-concerns law protecting residential tenants
nj:S 3368.summary: Lets municipalities with a code enforcement agency either inspect rentals for lead-based paint in-house or hire certified contractors, allows shared-service agreements, and repeals the Department of Community Affairs inspection requirement for one- and two-family rentals.

nj:S 3371.title: Annuity policies and contracts-revises limits for net cash values to $250K
nj:S 3371.summary: Raises from $100,000 to $250,000 the amount the Life and Health Guaranty Association pays on annuity net cash surrender or withdrawal values when a member insurer is insolvent, effective immediately.

nj:S 3379.title: Semi-annual water & energy usage-req data center owners & operators submit
nj:S 3379.summary: Requires data center owners and operators to file semi-annual water and energy usage reports with the Board of Public Utilities for three years, with added performance data if the center receives State financial incentives.

nj:S 3384.title: Environmental infrastructure projects-appropriates funds to DEP for FY2025
nj:S 3384.summary: Appropriates federal and State money to the Department of Environmental Protection for the fiscal 2025 Environmental Infrastructure Financing Program, for loans to local governments and private water companies for water infrastructure projects.

nj:S 3385.title: Non-resid development fee info, certain-concerns deadline for mun to report
nj:S 3385.summary: Gives municipalities 180 days after the March 20, 2024 enactment of a related law to report to the Department of Community Affairs on non-residential development fees collected and spent, with retroactive effect on penalties.

nj:S 3386.title: Campaign funds-auth use for security expenses, candidate & immediate family
nj:S 3386.summary: Allows candidates and officeholders to spend campaign funds on reasonable security measures for themselves, household family members and staff, such as alarms, locks, security personnel and cybersecurity, but not firearms or ammunition.

nj:S 3387.title: NJ National Guard-concerns tuition benefits
nj:S 3387.summary: Lets a New Jersey National Guard member who qualifies for the Guard's tuition-free public college benefit transfer that benefit to a spouse or child.

nj:S 3388.title: Schedule II attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder prescr-allow pharm transfer
nj:S 3388.summary: Allows pharmacists to transfer Schedule II controlled substance prescriptions for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder to another pharmacist, in compliance with federal regulations.

nj:S 3389.title: Railroad safety-provides certain requirements
nj:S 3389.summary: Requires two crew members on trains carrying 200,000 gallons or more of petroleum or 20,000 gallons of other hazardous materials, with exceptions, and bars trains over 8,500 feet. Lets out-of-State trains with smaller crews pass through unless they stop to change cars.

nj:S 3399.title: Solar & photovoltaic energy generation facilities-requires end-of-life recycling
nj:S 3399.summary: Requires owners, producers, distributors or manufacturers of solar energy facilities to remove and recycle or refurbish them after use ends, starting 180 days after the Department of Environmental Protection publishes a finding that recycling is widely available; allows DEP rules and fees.

nj:S 3407.title: Clean energy prog-req payment of prevailing wage, finan through commercial prop
nj:S 3407.summary: Requires prevailing wage to be paid on projects financed through the Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) program by treating that financing as authority financial assistance.

nj:S 3412.title: Social media platforms, cert-take certain actions concerning user mental health
nj:S 3412.summary: Requires the Social Media Research Center to study addictive social media behavior among minors, including warning labels and ad disclaimers, and report within 18 months; the Health commissioner may then adopt rules.

nj:S 3416.title: Health insur carrier network adequacy standards-estab addl, cert specialists
nj:S 3416.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Banking and Insurance to adopt rules ensuring covered persons have reasonable, timely access to physician specialists, such as anesthesiologists, radiologists, pathologists and emergency physicians, at in-network hospitals and facilities.

nj:S 3418.title: Recently constructed structure, preserv farmland, cert-auth spec occasion events
nj:S 3418.summary: Allows permanent structures built in the past five years on preserved farmland to host special occasion events if a winery uses them mainly for tasting, sale or production, or if event revenue stays within 10 percent of farm revenue.

nj:S 3423.title: Career fire fighters-org & deployment consistant w/ certain national standards
nj:S 3423.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Community Affairs to adopt rules, and career fire departments to deploy firefighters, consistent with National Fire Protection Association standard NFPA 1710 (2020 edition).

nj:S 3426.title: Civil service firefighter applicants, certain-establish mentoring program
nj:S 3426.summary: Requires the Civil Service Commission to run a mentoring program, including a study group, for firefighter applicants from municipalities with median income at or below 250 percent of the federal poverty level.

nj:S 3432.title: Next New Jersey Program-establish for artificial intelligence investments
nj:S 3432.summary: Creates the Next New Jersey Program in the Economic Development Authority, offering tax credits to businesses primarily engaged in the artificial intelligence industry or large AI data centers.

nj:S 3445.title: NJ State Board of Cosmetology and Hairstyling-modifies membership
nj:S 3445.summary: Changes the State Board of Cosmetology and Hairstyling's membership: four licensed professionals, two beauty school owners or operators, and one licensed teacher replace the six licensed members, with textured-hair experience required for one of them.

nj:S 3446.title: Farmland Assessment Review Comm-estab, annually review & recommend changes
nj:S 3446.summary: As substituted, directs the State Farmland Evaluation Committee to adjust the minimum sales and income thresholds for land to qualify for farmland assessment, raises repeat-misrepresentation penalties to $15,000 and $20,000, creates an online application portal, and adds the State Forester to the committee.

nj:S 3447.title: Special Education Transportation Task Force-establish
nj:S 3447.summary: Creates a Special Education Transportation Task Force to study and recommend best practices for transporting students receiving special education, including responding to medical and behavioral emergencies.

nj:S 3451.title: 2026 FIFA World Cup-submit reports concerning human rights
nj:S 3451.summary: Requires State agencies, certain municipalities and other entities involved in hosting the 2026 FIFA World Cup to submit reports on how they carried out the commitments in the NY/NJ Human Rights Report.

nj:S 3452.title: Reproductive health care services-req health insurance & Medicaid coverage
nj:S 3452.summary: Requires health insurers, NJ FamilyCare, and state and school employee health plans to cover family planning and reproductive health care, including pregnancy termination, with cost-sharing only for some out-of-network care; religious employers may request an exclusion.

nj:S 3453.title: Therapy dog-estab pilot program to use in public elementary school wellness prog
nj:S 3453.summary: Creates a three-year pilot program in which two school districts in each of the southern, central and northern regions use therapy dogs in elementary school wellness programs to assess academic and health benefits.

nj:S 3455.title: Off-track wagering licenses-prov automatic renewal; modifies cert operating req
nj:S 3455.summary: Requires the Racing Commission to renew off-track wagering licenses when licensees file renewal forms and pay fees and the commission finds the legal qualifications met, and lets the commission set license terms of at least one year.

nj:S 3457.title: Out-of-School Time Advisory Commission-review certain programs
nj:S 3457.summary: Creates a 23-member Out-of-School Time Advisory Commission to review State policies, research and funding for before-school, after-school and summer programs, and to recommend models for program design and assessment.

nj:S 3463.title: Health care service firms-make certain changes to regulation
nj:S 3463.summary: Raises from $250,000 to $500,000 the Medicaid personal care billing level that triggers an audit of health care service firms, lets out-of-state accountants perform audits, and changes the report required of smaller firms.

nj:S 3466.title: Highlands Region-allocates annually CBT revenue for preservation of land;$7.5M
nj:S 3466.summary: Extends the Highlands Region special two-appraisal process for Green Acres and farmland purchases from June 30, 2024 to June 30, 2029, and requires annual State aid to Highlands municipalities hosting watershed lands that get no watershed moratorium offset aid.

nj:S 3470.title: Cyber-harassment, public servant or family member-upgrades to third degree crime
nj:S 3470.summary: Makes cyber-harassment of a public servant or a public servant's family member a third-degree crime, up from fourth degree. Requires the Attorney General to promote cyber-harassment education and prevention and to assist victims.

nj:S 3474.title: Lands for recreation and conservation purposes-appropriate to DEP;$10.067M
nj:S 3474.summary: Appropriates $10,067,905 from dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection: $9,588,905 for nonprofit grants to acquire or develop recreation and conservation land, and $479,000 for administration.

nj:S 3475.title: Veteran suicide prevention public service announcements-DVA receive vol contrib
nj:S 3475.summary: Lets the Department of Veterans Affairs accept public and private gifts, grants and donations for veteran suicide prevention public service announcements, held in a special nonlapsing State fund under rules to be developed.

nj:S 3482.title: Alcohol manufacturers-provide for inclusion on highway signs & for internet site
nj:S 3482.summary: Directs the Department of Transportation to add cideries, distilleries and meaderies to the eligible facilities in highway Tourist Oriented Directional Sign and Specific Service Sign programs, alongside wineries and breweries.

nj:S 349.title: Motor vehicles, overtaking cert pedestrians, bicycles & conveyances-concerns
nj:S 349.summary: Defines "personal conveyance" to include e-bikes, scooters, wheelchairs and skateboards, and broadens the definition of "pedestrian", in the law on motor vehicles overtaking pedestrians, bicycles and personal conveyances.

nj:S 3511.title: Debt Defeasance and Prevention Fund-estab process, auth future approp;$393.480M
nj:S 3511.summary: Appropriates $393.48 million from the Debt Defeasance and Prevention Fund for capital projects, including $70 million for Liberty State Park, and sets a process for authorizing future appropriations from the fund.

nj:S 3517.title: Division of State Police-expands rank and grade titles
nj:S 3517.summary: Lets the Superintendent of State Police change the ranks and grades of troopers, detectives, supervisors, managers and executive personnel without Attorney General approval, while keeping Attorney General approval for changes to specified command staff positions.

nj:S 3519.title: Properties, certain-provide monies for EDA to purchase, devel potential;$65M
nj:S 3519.summary: Appropriates up to $65 million from the General Fund for the Economic Development Authority to buy New Jersey Transit properties, and lets the authority use at least $35 million from its economic growth account to develop, rehabilitate and lease them.

nj:S 3522.title: Privacy Protection Act-concerns collection & sharing of certain personal info
nj:S 3522.summary: Bars State and local government entities and health care facilities from collecting immigration status, citizenship, birthplace, Social Security or taxpayer ID numbers unless needed for eligibility, services or licensure, restricts disclosing them, and limits sharing license plate reader data.

nj:S 3525.title: Financial institutions-allow mortgagor to make biweekly and bimonthly payments
nj:S 3525.summary: Requires financial institutions to let mortgagors in good standing make biweekly or semi-monthly mortgage payments and pay extra principal without penalty, and sets how payments are applied when an escrow analysis raises the payment.

nj:S 3528.title: Governor's Survivor Leader Advisory Council-estab; create report;$1M
nj:S 3528.summary: Requires the Commission on Human Trafficking to report to the Governor and Legislature on human trafficking risks tied to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, creates a Human Trafficking Survivor Leader Advisory Council, and appropriates $1 million.

nj:S 3530.title: Female Incarcerated Person's Rights Protection Act-establish
nj:S 3530.summary: Requires the Corrections Commissioner to add gender-responsive risk assessments to inmate classification, set up community supervision and reentry services, and train officers who supervise women annually. Creates a Division of Women's Services in the Department of Corrections.

nj:S 3561.title: Medical countermeasures, products, & therapeutics-permits procurement
nj:S 3561.summary: Allows the Department of Health to buy medical countermeasures, supplies and therapeutics directly under federal programs and approved federal contracts when the Commissioner finds it necessary for public health and safety.

nj:S 3562.title: Public Health Institute-provide for designation and establishment in New Jersey
nj:S 3562.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Health to designate one entity as New Jersey's Public Health Institute, under criteria the commissioner sets, to coordinate among national, State and local agencies.

nj:S 3587.title: Retail theft-concerns, establishes theft unit;$1M
nj:S 3587.summary: Makes retail theft changes: simple assault on store employees becomes aggravated assault, repeat offenders face extended terms, shoplifting values can be aggregated, online dealing in stolen goods is clarified, fostering stolen-goods sales becomes an offense, and gift card sales and notices are regulated.

nj:S 3602.title: Summer tuition and grants-makes FY2025 suppl approp;$20M
nj:S 3602.summary: Appropriates $20 million for summer tuition aid grants at 75 percent of the maximum award; as amended, sets a process to fund awards above 75 percent.

nj:S 3604.title: Sales & Use Tax and Corp Business Tax-elim transaction nexus requirement
nj:S 3604.summary: Removes the 200-transaction threshold, leaving only the $100,000 revenue threshold, for when out-of-state sellers must collect New Jersey sales tax and when corporations become subject to the Corporation Business Tax.

nj:S 3607.title: SPRS retirees, certain-extends accidential death benefit for survivors
nj:S 3607.summary: Extends accidental death benefits to survivors of State Police retirees with World Trade Center rescue, recovery or cleanup-related conditions, including retirees on ordinary disability, special or service retirement, and removes the July 8, 2019 death-date cutoff.

nj:S 3608.title: Restaurants & cert alcoholic retailers-conduct bus within desig outdoor space
nj:S 3608.summary: Lets restaurants and certain alcohol retailers and manufacturers use outdoor spaces they own or lease, adjacent or not, as extensions of their licensed premises for selling food and beverages, under premises expansion permits.

nj:S 3609.title: Raffles-allow licensed organizations to conduct remotely and advertise
nj:S 3609.summary: Directs the Legalized Games of Chance Control Commission to adopt rules within 180 days allowing licensed organizations to run and advertise remote raffles, removes prize value limits, and allows remote raffles on Sundays.

nj:S 3610.title: NJ FamilyCare-annually identify State funds available, evaluate program
nj:S 3610.summary: Requires state budget and human services officials to report yearly on unspent state funds available for NJ FamilyCare and child care subsidies, evaluate care quality, and list the 12 most urgent policy changes with their costs.

nj:S 3611.title: Mental health care resources for children-provides grant to study and map
nj:S 3611.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Families to give a $1 million grant to the NJ Health Care Quality Institute to study and map mental health care resources, eligibility rules and access barriers for children.

nj:S 3618.title: Wildlife Corridor Action Plan-establish;$90K
nj:S 3618.summary: Requires the Departments of Environmental Protection and Transportation to jointly develop a Wildlife Corridor Action Plan within 36 months, updated every 10 years, identifying wildlife corridors and wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots.

nj:S 3620.title: Energy Bill Watch program-estab & include cert info in bills and notices
nj:S 3620.summary: Requires electric and gas utilities with smart meters to run an Energy Bill Watch program that sends customers usage and cost updates on the 10th and 20th day of each billing cycle, with optional dollar alerts, and to show charge changes on bills.

nj:S 3621.title: Thoroughbred horse racing-reduce min number, annually required dates
nj:S 3621.summary: Lets the Monmouth Park and Meadowlands thoroughbred permit holders cut annual race dates from 141 to as few as 25 with horsemen's association consent or if State purse funding is under $5 million, or to 40 if it is $5-10 million.

nj:S 3622.title: Membership of county planning boards-concerns
nj:S 3622.summary: Lets the director of a county board of commissioners appoint a designee to serve on the county planning board, instead of requiring the director to serve personally.

nj:S 364.title: Fusion-adds to types of Class I renewable energies
nj:S 364.summary: Adds fusion energy to the types of power counted as Class I renewable energy under the Electric Discount and Energy Competition Act.

nj:S 3663.title: Reproductive health travel advisory-establishes
nj:S 3663.summary: Requires the Department of State to publish a Reproductive Health Travel Advisory placing each state in a blue, yellow or red tier based on its restrictions on reproductive health care, such as gestational limits and waiting periods.

nj:S 3670.title: Homeowner, cert impacted, Hurricane Ida-prov mortgage relief & foreclosure prot
nj:S 3670.summary: Requires mortgage servicers to grant one-year forbearance to certain homeowners affected by the remnants of Hurricane Ida who receive a Department of Community Affairs eligibility certification, and lets those homeowners seek a temporary court stay of foreclosure.

nj:S 3689.title: Limited liability company-allow to terminate alternate name
nj:S 3689.summary: Allows a limited liability company to terminate a registered alternate name before its five-year registration period ends, except an LLC operating as a residential landlord.

nj:S 3695.title: Cell phone & social media policy-develop by DOE & adopted in schools
nj:S 3695.summary: Requires the Education Commissioner to issue guidelines, and each public school to adopt a policy, prohibiting non-academic use of internet-enabled devices by students on school grounds during the school day, with authorized exceptions.

nj:S 3711.title: Clean Communities Prog Fd-make annual alloc, single-use plastic reduction;$500K
nj:S 3711.summary: Makes permanent the annual $500,000 allocation from the Clean Communities Program Fund to the Department of Environmental Protection for public outreach on the single-use plastics law, now limited to three years.

nj:S 3735.title: Police chiefs & fire depart chiefs-concerns mandatory retirement age
nj:S 3735.summary: Extends to April 30, 2027 the period in which police and fire chiefs who turn 65 may stay in the Police and Firemen's Retirement System, with written approval, until the end of the year they turn 67.

nj:S 3739.title: Electric supply equipment devel processes & standards, certain-establish
nj:S 3739.summary: Requires administrative approval by non-discretionary permit for qualifying electric vehicle charger and make-ready parking installations at existing gas stations, retail sites and buildings, exempting them from site plan and land use board approval.

nj:S 3746.title: Moose's Law-person w/animal cruelty conviction prohibits owning companion animal
nj:S 3746.summary: Bars people convicted of animal cruelty, for a court-set period, from working in animal-related businesses or owning or living with animals, and requires forfeiture of their animals to a shelter or co-owner.

nj:S 3750.title: Residential Facility Quality of Care Improvement Fund-enhance enforce auth
nj:S 3750.summary: Lets the Department of Human Services impose financial penalties on developmental disability service providers that violate licensing rules, and creates a Residential Facility Quality of Care Improvement Fund.

nj:S 3751.title: Child abuse or neglect-revise definition, include between 18 & 21, cert setting
nj:S 3751.summary: As introduced, extends the child abuse and neglect definition to people ages 18 to 21 who are abused, neglected or exploited by staff of an institution regulated by the Department of Children and Families that is responsible for their care.

nj:S 3754.title: Disability Mortality and Abuse Prevention Advisory Committee-estab; make approp
nj:S 3754.summary: Creates a temporary Disability Mortality and Abuse Prevention Advisory Committee in the Department of Human Services to review cases of abuse, neglect or death of adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, and makes an appropriation.

nj:S 3772.title: Board and lodging-concerns valuation, w/ respect to workers' compensation
nj:S 3772.summary: Changes the workers' compensation value of employer-provided board and lodging from $25 per week to market value, unless another amount was set at hiring. Excludes it from the benefit rate during total temporary disability if the worker keeps receiving it.

nj:S 3773.title: Employee leasing agreements-concerns req, report separations from employment
nj:S 3773.summary: Makes a client company of an employee leasing company, not the leasing company, solely responsible for reporting separations from employment and liable for penalties for failing to report.

nj:S 3776.title: Chronic Absenteeism Task Force-establish
nj:S 3776.summary: Establishes a 20-member Chronic Absenteeism Task Force to examine causes and data on chronic student absenteeism in public schools, including mental health and school climate, and research other states' practices.

nj:S 3787.title: Long Term Tax Exemption Law-concerns certain payments in lieu of taxes
nj:S 3787.summary: Requires municipal officials to notify the county finance officer when a long-term tax exemption annual service charge is received and send the county its 5% share within seven days. Requires notice of public hearings on financial agreements to go to the county.

nj:S 3800.title: Law Against Discrimination-enhance protections, military & military veterans
nj:S 3800.summary: As introduced, adds military service members and veterans as protected classes under the Law Against Discrimination and makes it an unlawful employment practice to deny reemployment to employees who take military leave.

nj:S 3802.title: Constr projects-utilize plastic materials, cert postconsumer recycled content
nj:S 3802.summary: Bars State-funded government construction projects, starting one year after enactment, from using plastic construction materials with under 10 percent postconsumer recycled content (15 percent for materials bought after two years). Exempts cases with a 20 percent cost increase, unavailable supply, structural-safety risks, or income-restricted housing.

nj:S 3815.title: US Postal Service postmark-estab public awareness campaign, fed rules;$100K
nj:S 3815.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to run a public awareness campaign on the federal Postal Service postmark rule and mail-in ballots, evaluate ballot drop box placement and use, and appropriates $100,000.

nj:S 3818.title: Borinqueneers license plates-authorize creation
nj:S 3818.summary: Authorizes Borinqueneers license plates honoring the Army's 65th Infantry Regiment, with a $50 application fee and $10 annual renewal fee; net fees go to a special fund.

nj:S 3819.title: Transmission-scale energy storage procurement-modifies cert requirements
nj:S 3819.summary: Extends from June 30, 2026 to December 31, 2026 the deadline for the Board of Public Utilities to approve at least 1,000 megawatts of transmission-scale energy storage incentive awards, and modifies Tranche 2 project maturity requirements to make more projects eligible.

nj:S 3824.title: Apartment Complex swimming pools-concerns safety measures
nj:S 3824.summary: Exempts apartment complex swimming pools restricted to tenants and their invited guests from first aid and lifeguard requirements, and applies the existing "No lifeguard on duty" sign requirement to them.

nj:S 3825.title: Securing Our Children's Future Fund-provide project grant, career/tech ed;$7.65M
nj:S 3825.summary: Appropriates $7.65 million from the Securing Our Children's Future Fund to the Cumberland County Technical Education Center to expand career and technical education.

nj:S 3838.title: Div of Pensions & Benefits-initiate temp transfer of funds, cert circumstances
nj:S 3838.summary: Lets the Pensions and Benefits director temporarily transfer money from the health benefits fund when the dependents premium or employer health benefits fund cannot cover 10 days of payments, capped at 30 days of payments and repaid within 120 days unless extended.

nj:S 3848.title: Alcoholic beverage licenses-concerns for sporting facilities
nj:S 3848.summary: Lets sporting facility alcohol license holders create up to five all-inclusive areas, with combined capacity of 500 people or five percent of facility capacity. Allows special permits for larger areas at national or international events.

nj:S 3850.title: County boards of elections-extend distance w/in which electioneering prohibited
nj:S 3850.summary: Lets county boards of elections extend the ban on electioneering near a polling place, room or ballot drop box from 100 to 200 feet after posting notice; violating an extended ban is a disorderly persons offense.

nj:S 3858.title: School bus transporting student w/ disabilities-call 911, life-threatening emerg
nj:S 3858.summary: Requires school bus drivers, aides and other personnel to call 911 during a potential life-threatening emergency on a bus, report the call to the Department of Education, and extends safety and disability training to all such personnel.

nj:S 3870.title: Nuclear facilities-modifies certain CAFRA permit review requirements
nj:S 3870.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection, in coastal permit review of a nuclear generation facility, to determine that its radioactive waste storage as well as disposal method is safe and meets Nuclear Regulatory Commission standards.

nj:S 3879.title: Environmental infra projects-amend list, projects eligible to receive loans
nj:S 3879.summary: Amends the list of environmental infrastructure projects the NJ Infrastructure Bank may lend for in fiscal year 2025, adding and removing projects and changing loan amounts, for a total of 227 projects and up to $2.47 billion.

nj:S 388.title: Multiple dwellings-prov priority status to cert residents moving to lower floors
nj:S 388.summary: Requires owners of multiple dwellings with three or more floors to give seniors and people with mobility disabilities first priority to move to a same-size unit on a lower floor, and to post a sign about it.

nj:S 3880.title: Hazard mitigation and resilience projects-amend list approved for funding
nj:S 3880.summary: Adds three projects, in Brick, Rochelle Park and Highlands, to the list of hazard mitigation projects the NJ Infrastructure Bank may fund in fiscal year 2025 under the Community Hazard Assistance Mitigation Program.

nj:S 3881.title: Environmental infrastructure projects-amend list approved for long-term funding
nj:S 3881.summary: Amends the fiscal year 2025 list of environmental infrastructure projects funded through the Department of Environmental Protection, adding and removing projects and changing loan amounts, for a total of 227 projects and up to $2.47 billion.

nj:S 3887.title: Lakes, certain State owned-req DEP provide public access for boats;$2M
nj:S 3887.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection to build, or contract with private marina owners for, public boat access to State- or county-owned lakes and reservoirs that allow boats.

nj:S 3889.title: Food waste reduction program-req public instit of higher ed develop on campus
nj:S 3889.summary: Requires each public college and university to run a campus food waste reduction program that sends unused food from dining halls and events to local food pantries, shelters and similar groups, and to file annual reports.

nj:S 3890.title: Food assistance programs-req public instit of higher ed provide information
nj:S 3890.summary: Requires public colleges to send students information on the federal SNAP food assistance program, plus details on campus and local food aid, with admission offers and at each semester's registration.

nj:S 3902.title: Armed Forces of US or National Guard-permit excused absence, student enlisted
nj:S 3902.summary: Gives grade 11 and 12 students up to three excused absences a year for college or technical school visits, and records military recruitment-related absences as excused and not counted against perfect attendance.

nj:S 3906.title: Tree Experts & Tree Care Operators Licensing Act-prov enforce & penal provisions
nj:S 3906.summary: Gives the Board of Tree Experts and the Department of Environmental Protection enforcement tools under the tree expert licensing law: compliance orders, civil actions, and administrative or civil penalties for violations.

nj:S 3910.title: Preschool aid and facilities requirements-make various changes to provision
nj:S 3910.summary: Establishes the “New Jersey Universal Preschool and Kindergarten Act,” revising early childhood education laws and requiring preschool expansion grants for districts lacking State-funded free preschool for three- and four-year-olds.

nj:S 3917.title: School funding law-makes various changes; modifies tax levy growth limitation
nj:S 3917.summary: Changes extraordinary special education aid to require its funding or reimbursement share to rise each year, adds public review steps to the Educational Adequacy Report, and creates an 11-member Special Education Funding Review Task Force.

nj:S 3921.title: Standardbred horse racing purse subsidies-reallocates to Meadowlands Racetrack
nj:S 3921.summary: Directs the Racing Commission to move purse subsidies allocated to Freehold Raceway overnight purses to Meadowlands overnight purses during periods when Freehold holds no live racing.

nj:S 3922.title: Historic Trust-approp CBT revenues, cert historic preserv projects;$18.518M
nj:S 3922.summary: Appropriates $18,518,738 in dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the New Jersey Historic Trust for grants to listed historic preservation projects and administrative costs.

nj:S 3928.title: Consumer contracts, certain-limits general application
nj:S 3928.summary: Limits a consumer contract for a service to that service alone, barring terms that make the contract govern the consumer's purchase of other products or services from the company or its affiliates.

nj:S 3931.title: Occupational therapy-update requirements for licensure
nj:S 3931.summary: Requires the Division of Consumer Affairs to set continuing competence requirements for occupational therapists and assistants to renew licenses, defines occupational therapy services, and updates the advisory council's terms and meeting schedule.

nj:S 3933.title: School Supervisor Mentorship Pilot Program-establish; approp $500K
nj:S 3933.summary: Creates a three-year School Supervisor Mentorship Pilot Program that supports first-year school supervisors through a one-year mentoring cycle under guidelines set by the Commissioner of Education.

nj:S 3934.title: Medicaid, eligible pregnant women-codifies coverage for 365-day period
nj:S 3934.summary: Extends, from 60 to 365 days after the pregnancy ends, how long an eligible pregnant woman stays a Medicaid qualified applicant despite income changes.

nj:S 3936.title: Capital & park devel projects-approp, recreation & conservation purposes;$60M
nj:S 3936.summary: Appropriates $60 million in dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection for capital and park development projects on state lands used for recreation and conservation.

nj:S 3939.title: Dual-use solar facilities-participate in community solar program
nj:S 3939.summary: Lets dual-use solar projects participate in the Community Solar Energy Program, allows different incentive levels by project type, and lets dual-use solar incentives stack.

nj:S 3944.title: Non-profit corporation alcoholic beverage theater licensees, cert-concerns
nj:S 3944.summary: Makes “disregarded entity” single-member LLCs of nonprofits eligible for the liquor licenses held by nonprofit art house movie theaters, and lets municipalities issue such licenses for certain community theaters.

nj:S 3945.title: Hemp products/intoxicating hemp beverages-revise restrict through November 2026
nj:S 3945.summary: Delays from April 13 to May 31, 2026 the compliance deadlines for sales of intoxicating hemp beverages by alcohol and cannabis licensees, and lets hemp producers exceed the THC limit until then for extracts in manufacturing.

nj:S 3946.title: Human Trafficking-expand crime & eliminates statue of limitations; approp $1M
nj:S 3946.summary: Expands the human trafficking crime to cover knowingly receiving anything of value or benefiting from a trafficking scheme, separates adult and child sex trafficking, makes attempt a first-degree crime, requires restitution to victims, and changes evidence rules and training.

nj:S 3947.title: Telemedicine & telehealth-extend permanently certain pay parity
nj:S 3947.summary: Extends from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027 the requirement that health plans pay telemedicine and telehealth services at the same rate as in-person services.

nj:S 3957.title: Newspapers-allow public bodies continue using, req public notices & legal ads
nj:S 3957.summary: Lets newspapers used for legal notices and public body advertisements in 2024 keep qualifying for that purpose from January 1 to March 1, 2025, with price caps and no fee or registration to view the notices.

nj:S 3961.title: School lunch & other payments-req board of ed offer no-fee option to parents
nj:S 3961.summary: Requires public schools, and nonpublic schools in federal meal programs, to offer a no-fee way to pay for school meals, and requires payment platforms contracted by schools to disclose their fees and the no-fee alternative.

nj:S 3969.title: Municipal Rehabilitation and Economic Recovery Act-extend recovery term
nj:S 3969.summary: Extends the economic recovery term under the Municipal Rehabilitation and Economic Recovery Act by five years, continuing the special governing procedures, economic benefits and added state oversight for a qualified municipality (Camden).

nj:S 3982.title: Individualized Education Program-concerns annual IEP team meeting
nj:S 3982.summary: Requires schools to give parents a written list of discussion items at least two business days before the annual IEP meeting, and requires the Department of Education to create an IEP Improvement Working Group.

nj:S 3990.title: Primary elections-extend early voting period
nj:S 3990.summary: Extends the early voting period for all primary elections to start seven days before the election, extends the deadline to appoint a challenger, and appropriates $6 million.

nj:S 3992.title: Planned real estate developments, cert-modifies capital reserve funding req
nj:S 3992.summary: Requires planned real estate development capital reserve funding plans to let the reserve fall to a zero balance during the 30-year projection, permits additional plans with higher minimums or escalating contributions, and defines "adequate" reserves.

nj:S 3993.title: Motor vehicle sales-change certain requirements for inspection of records
nj:S 3993.summary: Removes the requirement that electronic records of online motor vehicle sales be kept for immediate inspection, and requires the Motor Vehicle Commission to give dealers one business day's advance written notice before inspecting records.

nj:S 4010.title: Social services-provide for expansion at county colleges
nj:S 4010.summary: Requires the Council of County Colleges to work with county colleges to identify unmet basic needs among low-income students, and county colleges to work with county boards of social services to help students enroll in supports such as SNAP and TANF.

nj:S 4028.title: State construction contracts-limit amount of payment agency may withheld, to 2%
nj:S 4028.summary: Bars State agencies from withholding more than 2 percent of each partial payment to contractors on State construction projects, except for contractors terminated for cause in the prior five years.

nj:S 4057.title: Prot. Against Forever Chemical Act-exempt rug/fabric in vehicles from provisions
nj:S 4057.summary: Clarifies that rugs and fabric intended solely for use inside aircraft, cars, light trucks, vans, buses and other vehicles are not "carpet" under the Protecting Against Forever Chemicals Act, exempting them from it.

nj:S 4066.title: State-owned property-req annual report for potential as affordable housing
nj:S 4066.summary: Requires the Treasury Department to inventory unutilized State-owned property, with State entities reporting biennially, and to analyze its feasibility for low- and moderate-income housing.

nj:S 4107.title: Customer using debit card-proh seller providing service from charging surcharge
nj:S 4107.summary: Bans sellers from adding a surcharge when customers pay with a debit or gift card, requires disclosure of that ban by sellers who surcharge credit cards, and makes violations Consumer Fraud Act offenses.

nj:S 4113.title: Athletic Trainer Compact-enter NJ
nj:S 4113.summary: Enters New Jersey into the Athletic Training Compact, letting athletic trainers licensed in one member state practice in other member states under a multistate license, and sets up the compact's commission and rules.

nj:S 4116.title: Public meetings, certain-require public participation be allowed
nj:S 4116.summary: Requires county boards of commissioners, and boards or entities they create, to set aside time for public comment at all public meetings.

nj:S 4121.title: Community Security Initiatives, Jewish Federation of Southern NJ-assign funding
nj:S 4121.summary: Amends the fiscal year 2025 appropriations act so $1.5 million for Community Security Initiatives goes to the Jewish Federation of Southern New Jersey, to be divided equally among the State's Jewish Federations for security costs.

nj:S 4122.title: State lottery contributions-revise apportionment
nj:S 4122.summary: Lowers the minimum share of lottery proceeds dedicated to the Common Pension Fund L account from 30 to 27 percent starting State Fiscal Year 2026, with conditions that can restore the 30 percent minimum.

nj:S 4126.title: Perchloroethylene and trichloroethylene-prohibit certain uses
nj:S 4126.summary: Prohibits all uses of trichloroethylene (TCE) and all consumer and commercial uses of perchloroethylene (PCE), requires facilities using PCE to limit worker exposure, and directs DEP to adopt rules matching December 2024 federal EPA rules.

nj:S 413.title: Tenants, sr citizens & certain with disabilities-extend protected tenancy period
nj:S 413.summary: Extends the protected tenancy period under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act, which now expires 40 years after a building's conversion, to the lifetime of covered senior and disabled tenants.

nj:S 4135.title: Redevelopment projects, cert-provide allowance undertaken by instit of higher ed
nj:S 4135.summary: Changes the New Jersey Aspire incentive for research university redevelopment projects: counts research workspaces and dormitory space as project costs, requires developer capital of $30 million or 20 percent of cost, whichever is greater, and caps total credits at $90 million.

nj:S 4136.title: Public notices & legal advertisements-continue using newspapers
nj:S 4136.summary: Extends through June 30, 2025 the eligibility of newspapers that public bodies used, or were permitted to use, in 2024 for legal notices and advertisements, and requires those newspapers to submit subscription and other data.

nj:S 4144.title: Ignition interlock devices-clarifies installation for certain DWI offenses
nj:S 4144.summary: Lets a person required to forfeit driving privileges for a DWI offense install an ignition interlock device instead, earning one day of credit per two days installed, except for offenses causing serious bodily injury or involving drugs.

nj:S 4162.title: Affordable Power Purchase Agreements Extention Act-concerns
nj:S 4162.summary: Lets certain public entities extend existing renewable energy power purchase agreements, without public bidding, up to 30 years in total instead of the current 15-year limit.

nj:S 4166.title: Energy supply contracts, third party-req customer consent to material changes
nj:S 4166.summary: Requires a residential customer's express consent to material changes in a third-party electric or gas supply contract, but allows renewals without consent if price rises by no more than 20 percent, with notices and a 60-day no-fee cancellation right.

nj:S 4193.title: Fortifying Corn Masa Act-establish
nj:S 4193.summary: Requires corn masa flour made or sold in New Jersey to be fortified with 0.7 mg of folic acid per pound within one year, allows 0.4 mg per pound in wet masa products, and sets labeling rules.

nj:S 420.title: Voting period, early-concerns for regular municipal elections in May
nj:S 420.summary: Lets nonpartisan municipalities that have adopted early voting, by ordinance, extend early voting for May municipal elections to 7 days instead of the current 3.

nj:S 4217.title: Community Hazard Assistance Mitagation Prog projects, FY2027-expend cert sums
nj:S 4217.summary: Authorizes the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank to spend up to $13.1 million in FY2027 on low-interest loans to local governments for four hazard mitigation and resilience projects under the Community Hazard Assistance Mitigation Program.

nj:S 4219.title: Administration of employer payroll tax-concerns
nj:S 4219.summary: Requires certain employers to give municipalities with a local payroll tax more information on request, lets them keep up to 3 percent of collections for administration, and requires State wage data sharing with them. Exempts out-of-State work taxed by an out-of-State payroll tax.

nj:S 4220.title: Environmental infrastructure projects, FY2027-expend cert sums to make loans
nj:S 4220.summary: Authorizes the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank to spend up to $3.85 billion in FY2027 on loans to local governments and private water companies for listed clean water and drinking water infrastructure projects.

nj:S 4221.title: Environmental infrastructure projects, FY2027-appropriate funds to DEP
nj:S 4221.summary: Appropriates federal and State money to the Department of Environmental Protection for FY2027 loans to local governments and private water companies for listed clean water and drinking water infrastructure projects.

nj:S 4224.title: Officers of State Board of Medical Examiners, cert-estab education requirements
nj:S 4224.summary: Requires the State Board of Medical Examiners to elect a vice president as well as a president, secretary and treasurer, and requires the president and vice president to be an M.D., D.O. or podiatrist (D.P.M.).

nj:S 4254.title: Racing Commission, employees-eliminates five-year residency requirement
nj:S 4254.summary: Eliminates the requirement that New Jersey Racing Commission employees have been State residents for at least five years before employment.

nj:S 4263.title: Involuntary commitment-make permanent certain sunset provisions
nj:S 4263.summary: Extends the expiration of 2023 involuntary commitment provisions, including the 72-hour limit on holding patients without a court order, from 24 to 36 months; adds consent and court-order rules for continued holds, expands hospital reporting, and requires a follow-up study.

nj:S 4265.title: License plate-prohibit purposeful obstruction
nj:S 4265.summary: Bans driving with a purposely obstructed license plate and selling or possessing devices designed to obstruct plates, with fines up to $500 for a first offense and $750 for later offenses.

nj:S 4293.title: Water and energy usage-req owner or operator of data center submit report
nj:S 4293.summary: Requires data center owners or operators to submit quarterly water and energy usage reports to the Board of Public Utilities, which publishes them and coordinates with the Department of Environmental Protection.

nj:S 4307.title: New Jersey History Day Act-concerns
nj:S 4307.summary: Designates December 18 each year as New Jersey History Day, asks the Governor to proclaim it, and allows school districts to mark it with history instruction activities.

nj:S 4309.title: Online news publication-use circulation req to meet eligibility standards
nj:S 4309.summary: Counts an online news publication that meets county-wide or State-wide circulation requirements as meeting the municipal-wide requirement for publishing legal notices, and includes county visits in the visit calculation.

nj:S 4313.title: Off. Conklin-Off. Cady Memorial Overpass-desig overpass, Shelton Road, Route 287
nj:S 4313.summary: Designates the Stelton Road overpass on Interstate 287 as the "Officer Conklin-Officer Cady Memorial Overpass," honoring two South Plainfield police officers who died in the line of duty; public funds cannot pay for the signs.

nj:S 4373.title: Residential utility assistance programs-concerns req, consolidation application
nj:S 4373.summary: Requires the Division of Housing and Community Resources to sign memoranda of understanding with State agencies and Statewide nonprofit energy assistance organizations that run any utility assistance program, not only their own, so it joins the consolidated online application.

nj:S 4376.title: Department of Veterans Affairs-establish
nj:S 4376.summary: Creates a Department of Veterans Affairs as a principal state department, moving veterans' divisions and programs out of the Department of Military and Veterans' Affairs into a new Title 38B without adding new programs.

nj:S 4377.title: Transportation infrastructure projects, FY2026-expend certain sums to make loans
nj:S 4377.summary: Authorizes the NJ Infrastructure Bank to spend up to $53.45 million in fiscal 2026 on low-interest loans to local governments for 17 transportation projects, with up to $1 million in principal forgiveness for planning and design costs.

nj:S 4384.title: Alcoholic beverage retailers, cert-make permanent, allowing to sell & deliver
nj:S 4384.summary: Makes permanent the pandemic-era rules letting bars and restaurants sell sealed alcoholic beverages and cocktails for off-premises consumption and deliver them to adults at home.

nj:S 4387.title: Continuing education requirements-estab tracking sys, determine compliance
nj:S 4387.summary: Requires the Division of Consumer Affairs to develop, obtain, or contract with a vendor for an automated system letting licensing boards track licensees' continuing education credits and help determine compliance with renewal requirements.

nj:S 4390.title: End Date Ctr. Tax Credits Act-issue tax credits for energy storage projects
nj:S 4390.summary: Reduces by $250 million, the uncommitted amount, the tax credits available under the Next New Jersey Program for artificial intelligence and data center projects (the End Data Center Tax Credits Act).

nj:S 4400.title: National sports assc, league, or team-extend hours minor may work
nj:S 4400.summary: Lets 14- and 15-year-old professional athletes work past 11:30 p.m. when a workday that began earlier runs late because of return travel or a game delay, with written parental permission.

nj:S 4404.title: Alcoholic beverage licensing-make various revisions to the laws
nj:S 4404.summary: Revises alcoholic beverage licensing laws, including defining how craft manufacturers may arrange food vendors, clarifying that they may sell snacks and non-alcoholic drinks, and making other changes to licensee privileges.

nj:S 4406.title: Sentencing-clarifies under certain circumstances
nj:S 4406.summary: Lets a court sentence a defendant convicted of a first- or second-degree crime to the term for one degree lower when mitigating factors substantially outweigh aggravating ones and justice demands; restores language omitted by P.L.2025, c.328, retroactively.

nj:S 4407.title: Involuntary commitment-extend certain provisions
nj:S 4407.summary: Extends by eight months temporary involuntary commitment rules, including the 72-hour hold of involuntarily admitted patients without a temporary court order and the education of facilities and county assignment judges on facilities' duty to accept patients.

nj:S 4413.title: Sch-based Partnerships for Access & Resilience for Kids program-establish
nj:S 4413.summary: Creates the School-Based Partnerships for Access and Resilience for Kids pilot program at the Department of Children and Families, with school district mental health guidelines and a contract for a mobile mental health app.

nj:S 4420.title: Regional rehab. & reentry center authority-determine county share assessment
nj:S 4420.summary: Replaces a regional rehabilitation and reentry center authority's property tax assessment with direct payments from participating counties, based on each county's share of the average daily inmate population.

nj:S 4423.title: Open space acquisition & park development projects-appropriate $77.406M
nj:S 4423.summary: Appropriates $77.4 million from dedicated corporate business tax revenue and Green Acres funds to the Department of Environmental Protection, mostly for grants or loans to local governments to acquire open space and develop parks.

nj:S 4424.title: Grants, cert nonprofit entities-devel lands, recreation/conservation;$15.546M
nj:S 4424.summary: Appropriates $15.5 million in dedicated corporate business tax revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection, mostly for grants to nonprofits to acquire or develop land for recreation and conservation.

nj:S 4425.title: Farmland preservation-appropriate $64.787M
nj:S 4425.summary: Appropriates $64,787,327 from farmland preservation funds to the State Agriculture Development Committee to buy development easements and farmland, and to fund county, municipal and nonprofit farmland purchases.

nj:S 4426.title: Environmental infrastructure projects-appropriate funds to DEP in FY2026
nj:S 4426.summary: Appropriates federal and State money to the Department of Environmental Protection for fiscal year 2026 water infrastructure loans to local governments and private water companies, funding listed clean water and drinking water projects.

nj:S 4427.title: Farmland preservation-approp, grants to cert nonprofit organizations;$3.479M
nj:S 4427.summary: Appropriates $3,479,032 in dedicated corporation business tax revenue for farmland preservation grants to one nonprofit for four farms, and allows those grants to cover up to 80 percent of costs instead of 50 percent.

nj:S 4436.title: Hudson County Jail-authorize supplemental approp for general operating aid
nj:S 4436.summary: Requires Hudson County to return to the State, by June 30, 2026, unspent balances of $28.1 million in State appropriations for jail capital improvements, and authorizes general operating aid to the county of up to $28.1 million, not exceeding the amount returned.

nj:S 4439.title: NJ Fair Play Act-estab protections for student athletes, concerns name or image
nj:S 4439.summary: Bars four-year colleges from preventing athletes' name, image and likeness earnings, lets colleges pay them directly, bars athletic associations from penalizing such deals, bars deals for athletes under 21 tied to alcohol, tobacco or cannabis, and repeals the New Jersey Fair Play Act.

nj:S 4440.title: Public school buildings-require key boxes; appropriates $2.5M
nj:S 4440.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to install at least one exterior emergency-responder key box at each school building by June 30 of the 2026-2027 school year, subject to available funds, with State-borne costs and an exemption process.

nj:S 4451.title: Mun. master plan, land use plan & housing plan elements-clarifies requirements
nj:S 4451.summary: Requires municipal master plans to include a housing plan element covering the municipality's housing need and affordable housing, and requires the land use plan element to describe how it implements the housing plan.

nj:S 4467.title: Environmental infrastructure projects, FY2026-expend cert sums to make loans
nj:S 4467.summary: Authorizes the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank to spend up to $2.4 billion in fiscal year 2026 on loans to local governments and private water companies for listed clean water and drinking water projects.

nj:S 4472.title: Local bond ordinances-elim 5% down payment, hazard mitigation/resilience proj
nj:S 4472.summary: Exempts local governments from the five percent down payment requirement, and from local finance board approval of installment payments, for bond ordinances funding hazard mitigation and resilience projects.

nj:S 4476.title: Preschool education svcs, cert-permit awarding of contracts; extend to 3 yrs
nj:S 4476.summary: Lets school boards award preschool services contracts with licensed child care providers or Head Start programs by resolution without public bidding, and extends the maximum contract length to three years.

nj:S 4477.title: Mental health svcs-auth in resid substance use disorders treatment fac or prog
nj:S 4477.summary: Allows a licensed residential substance use disorder facility with a formal hospital affiliation and hospital clinical support to offer residential mental health treatment as a distinct program component.

nj:S 4495.title: Green Acres funds-fund cert projects, State-owned land by cert nonprofit org
nj:S 4495.summary: Allows Green Acres grants to fully fund projects by qualifying tax-exempt nonprofits on State-owned land, with matching funds required only at the department's discretion.

nj:S 4499.title: Insurance liability cases-require insurance companies be named defendants
nj:S 4499.summary: As amended, requires defendants to be properly identified in lawsuits for damages; an insurance company named as a defendant is referred to by its legal name rather than an assumed name, and the trier of fact is told that name.

nj:S 4501.title: Priv. on-site inspection agencies-permit owners/agents/other persons to contract
nj:S 4501.summary: Lets a construction owner or agent choose, for any reason, to hire an authorized private on-site inspection agency for a requested inspection, and allows separate inspection fees.

nj:S 4506.title: Minor league baseball players-exempt from cert St wage laws, cert circumstances
nj:S 4506.summary: Exempts minor league baseball players from State wage and hour laws and certain wage-payment recordkeeping rules, while a collective bargaining agreement that expressly governs their wages and working conditions is in effect.

nj:S 4509.title: Intoxicating hemp products, activities involving-prov addl licensing eligibility
nj:S 4509.summary: Redefines hemp to follow the federal definition and, from April 13, 2026, bars selling hemp products with synthesized cannabinoids or over 0.4 milligrams THC per container. Lets licensees sell intoxicating hemp beverages, limited to 5 milligrams THC per serving, until November 13, 2026.

nj:S 4510.title: Contested child custody cases, certain-clarifies procedures
nj:S 4510.summary: Bars custody courts from ordering therapy without proof of safety and effectiveness and good cause, lets children of sufficient age speak privately to the judge, and requires periodic therapist reports. Bars therapy cutting a child off from a safe, bonded parent.

nj:S 4511.title: Community Hazard Assistance Program-expend cert sums for projects, FY2026
nj:S 4511.summary: Authorizes the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank to spend up to $6,813,000 in fiscal year 2026 on low-interest loans to local governments for three listed hazard mitigation and resilience projects under the Community Hazard Assistance Mitigation Program.

nj:S 4513.title: Open space/recreation/floodplain prot/farmland/historic preserv-concerns funding
nj:S 4513.summary: Lets municipalities with an arts and culture trust fund deposit fiscal year 2027 open space, recreation, floodplain, farmland and historic preservation trust fund levy revenue, and unspent earlier deposits, into their current fund for general use.

nj:S 4514.title: Motor vehicle-concerns certain related funding to certain municipalities
nj:S 4514.summary: Lets municipalities of 200,000 or more with over 15 percent 2010-2020 population growth impose the mass transit access parking tax for transit operating costs and a rental car tax, and sends 10 percent of certain parking penalties to municipal court.

nj:S 4515.title: Rutgers University-authorize dual employment by certain employees
nj:S 4515.summary: Allows Rutgers managerial executives with oversight of areas covered by a health care affiliation agreement to be employed by both Rutgers and the affiliated contracting entity.

nj:S 4524.title: Farmland preservation purposes-approp CBT rev, planning incentive grants;$34M
nj:S 4524.summary: Appropriates $34 million in dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the State Agriculture Development Committee for county planning incentive grants covering up to 80 percent of farmland development easement costs.

nj:S 4530.title: Community solar program-require BPU revise targets
nj:S 4530.summary: Requires the Board of Public Utilities to open registration by October 1, 2025 for 3,000 megawatts of community solar projects, in addition to existing goals, and removes the goal of at least 150 additional megawatts per year.

nj:S 4531.title: Child tax credit-increase amount in taxable years 2026, 2027, and 2028
nj:S 4531.summary: Temporarily raises the child tax credit for children under six in 2026 through 2028, from $1,000 to $1,250 at the lowest income bracket and from $200 to $250 at the highest.

nj:S 4538.title: FY2026-make suppl approp;$358.811M; add & amend various provisions to Approp Act
nj:S 4538.summary: Supplements and amends the fiscal year 2026 appropriations act, including $135 million in transitional aid to localities, $40 million for 2026 FIFA World Cup host costs and $15 million for horse racing purse subsidies, and adds language provisions.

nj:S 4545.title: Epinephrine administration-expand mechanisms permitted in schools
nj:S 4545.summary: Replaces the requirement for pre-filled auto-injectors with "single unit dose epinephrine" mechanisms, allowing nasal spray and other forms for anaphylaxis emergencies in schools, colleges and youth camps.

nj:S 4551.title: Farmland preservation purposes-appropriate CBT revenues for grants;$3.750M
nj:S 4551.summary: Appropriates $3,750,990 in dedicated corporation business tax revenue for farmland preservation grants to the Land Conservancy of New Jersey, covering up to 50 percent of costs at eight farms.

nj:S 4566.title: Farmland preservation purposes-approp for municipal planning incentives;$500K
nj:S 4566.summary: Appropriates $500,000 in dedicated corporation business tax revenue for a farmland preservation municipal planning incentive grant to Oldmans Township, Salem County.

nj:S 4567.title: Open space acquisition/park devel/planning project/cert admin expenses;$107.999M
nj:S 4567.summary: Appropriates $107,999,000 in Green Acres and dedicated corporation business tax funds to the Department of Environmental Protection, including $102.7 million for local land acquisition and park development projects and $3 million for a new planning grant program.

nj:S 4569.title: Open space/park devel/planning projects/cert admin expenses, grants;$13.640M
nj:S 4569.summary: Appropriates $13.64 million in dedicated corporation business tax revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection, mostly for nonprofit open space and park grants, plus $1 million for a new planning grant program and $681,000 for administration.

nj:S 4618.title: Film/digital media production tax credit prog-concerns req and availability
nj:S 4618.summary: Extends the film and digital media production tax credit program to July 2049 and raises the credit for New Jersey studio partners from 35 to 40 percent, with additional credits capped so total credits do not exceed 45 percent of qualified expenses.

nj:S 4620.title: Old Courthouse asbestos remediation funding-assign distribution to Jersey City
nj:S 4620.summary: Redirects a $2 million State Fiscal Year 2025 appropriation for asbestos remediation at the Old Courthouse in Jersey City from Hudson County to the City of Jersey City.

nj:S 4632.title: Filtered drinking water stations & faucets-estab grant prog, public sch install
nj:S 4632.summary: Directs the Education Commissioner to create a School Lead Filters grant program, subject to appropriations, for buying and installing filtered bottle-filling stations and faucets in public schools, prioritizing schools with water quality problems.

nj:S 4654.title: Publication of required legal notices-provide on government Internet websites
nj:S 4654.summary: Requires State and local public entities to publish legally required notices on their official websites, free to the public with a homepage link, with most requirements mandatory from March 1, 2026.

nj:S 4676.title: Advanced transmission technologies-require BPU study potential deployment
nj:S 4676.summary: Requires the Board of Public Utilities to study whether electric utilities could deploy advanced transmission technologies, including costs, benefits, grid congestion, and other states' policies, and make recommendations.

nj:S 4678.title: Science/tech/engineering/mathematics grant prog-include retired teachers;$3.5M
nj:S 4678.summary: Expands the science, technology, engineering and math teacher grant program to let retired teachers and county college faculty teach in nonpublic schools, and allows teachers of other STEM subjects to qualify.

nj:S 4733.title: Palisades Interstate Park Comm.-make suppl approp, cert constr projects;$45M
