nj:S 4733.summary: Appropriates $45 million from Transportation Trust Fund capital reserves to the Palisades Interstate Park Commission for disaster recovery construction projects. Requires the commission to repay the Treasury the full $45 million regardless of any federal reimbursement.

nj:S 4737.title: Borough of Lodi, Bergen County-sell as surplus, cert property & improvements
nj:S 4737.summary: Authorizes the State Treasurer to sell the surplus Lodi Armory property in Bergen County to the county for $4.1 million, with the county leasing back about 6,000 square feet and up to 45 parking spaces to the State.

nj:S 4758.title: Reckless vehicular homicide-increase penalty when driving while intoxicated
nj:S 4758.summary: Raises reckless vehicular homicide to a first-degree crime when the driver is intoxicated or refuses a sobriety test and the death occurs in a highway construction or repair area or a designated safe corridor.

nj:S 4775.title: Mobile sport fishing permits-provide time period, purchased only by NJ residents
nj:S 4775.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Protection to sell mobile sport fishing permits so that only New Jersey residents can buy them during an initial 14-day period.

nj:S 4796.title: Environmental infrastructure projects-amend lists approved for long-term funding
nj:S 4796.summary: Amends the list of environmental infrastructure projects funded for fiscal 2026 by adding and removing projects and changing priorities and loan amounts, bringing the Department of Environmental Protection loan appropriation to up to $2.69 billion.

nj:S 4797.title: Environmental infrastructure projects-amend lists, eligible to receive loans
nj:S 4797.summary: Amends the list of environmental infrastructure projects eligible for fiscal 2026 NJ Infrastructure Bank loans, authorizing up to $2.69 billion in loans for 225 projects.

nj:S 4800.title: Limousine laws-revise penalties for certain violations
nj:S 4800.summary: Sets a $7,500 fine, six-month license suspension and vehicle impoundment for third and later limousine violations such as no license, no insurance, or too many passengers, and fines and impoundment for missing plates or inspection.

nj:S 4803.title: Bias incident investigation standards-concerns AG guidelines
nj:S 4803.summary: Requires Attorney General guidelines directing county and municipal police to report confirmed or suspected bias incidents to the state crime-reporting system within 24 hours and, in certain cases, to notify the Attorney General and county prosecutor.

nj:S 4809.title: Commission on Latino & Hispanic Heritage-revise cert membership requirements
nj:S 4809.summary: Removes master's degree requirements for some public members of the Commission on Latino and Hispanic Heritage and the requirement that members be organization spokespersons or leaders, requiring instead knowledge and experience in Latino or Hispanic studies or education.

nj:S 4812.title: Superstorm Sandy-impacted homeowners-concerns recovery & rebuilding prog
nj:S 4812.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Community Affairs to resume the Reconstruction, Rehabilitation, Elevation and Mitigation program and accept grant applications from Superstorm Sandy-impacted homeowners, to the extent uncommitted funds remain.

nj:S 4816.title: Certificate of need exemption list-expand
nj:S 4816.summary: Exempts certain hospitals providing inpatient maternity services from certificate of need requirements when raising their neonatal care designation from community perinatal center-basic to intermediate.

nj:S 4824.title: Borinqueneers Park-reassign approp for City of Perth Amboy to Education Alliance
nj:S 4824.summary: Reassigns an existing $350,000 FY2026 appropriation for Borinqueneer Park improvements from the City of Perth Amboy to the Borinqueneers Park Education Alliance, a nonprofit supporting a memorial to the 65th Infantry Regiment. Adds no new funding.

nj:S 4831.title: P.L.2021, c.489-extends certain provisions
nj:S 4831.summary: Extends from four to seven years the time that certain retired public pension members may be re-employed part-time by the Legislature, including those already re-employed under the current law.

nj:S 4832.title: Municipal homelessness-establish trust funds & adoption of housing plans
nj:S 4832.summary: Lets municipalities create homelessness trust funds by ordinance, funded partly by added fees on fines and penalties, and adopt homeless housing plans; five percent may cover administration, the rest funds housing grants.

nj:S 4833.title: Abandoned mine reclamation program-establish in DOT
nj:S 4833.summary: Creates an Abandoned Mine Reclamation Program in the Department of Transportation, which must draft a Statewide plan ranking mine projects and carry them out directly, by contract, or through grants.

nj:S 4835.title: Mail-in ballot-allow voter to cure due to envelope deficiencies or missing cert
nj:S 4835.summary: Requires county boards of elections to send voters a cure letter and new mail-in ballot for defects such as a missing inner envelope or an unsealed or tampered envelope, when the voter can be identified. Voters may instead vote in person by provisional ballot.

nj:S 4841.title: Home improvement & elevation contractors-clarifies licensure requirements
nj:S 4841.summary: Lets individuals working under the direction or supervision of a licensed home improvement or home elevation contractor perform that work without being licensed themselves; other individuals, unless exempt, must be licensed by the State board.

nj:S 4845.title: Municipal Stabilization & Recovery Act-extend certain provisions for 5 years
nj:S 4845.summary: Extends State oversight of municipalities under the Municipal Stabilization and Recovery Act until December 1, 2031, retroactive to December 1, 2025, and revises and expands the Local Finance Board's oversight powers.

nj:S 4847.title: Cannabis Regulatory Commission-make various changes to membership
nj:S 4847.summary: Sets Cannabis Regulatory Commission pay at $165,000 for the chair and $160,000 for members, has a majority of members rather than the Governor designate the chair, and lets members holding local office campaign and fundraise. Also amends other cannabis marketplace laws.

nj:S 4858.title: Veterans and Military Spouses Asset Protection Act-establish
nj:S 4858.summary: Exempts the primary and secondary homes of veterans, service members and military spouses from forced sale to pay debts, with exceptions for mortgages, government-owed taxes and judgments for fraud or misconduct, and adds protections for certain other assets.

nj:S 4864.title: Project labor agreements-enter into, cert local units for projects below $5M
nj:S 4864.summary: Allows municipalities, counties, school districts and fire districts to use project labor agreements on public works projects costing less than the $5 million threshold, without changing the existing threshold.

nj:S 4870.title: Defendants who are victims of abuse, certain-concerns sentencing
nj:S 4870.summary: Adds a sentencing factor for defendants who were victims of domestic violence or substantial abuse that contributed to their crime (other than murder or Megan's Law offenses), allowing reduced terms, and lets eligible people already convicted petition for resentencing.

nj:S 4871.title: Defendants who are victims of abuse, certain-concerns expungement process
nj:S 4871.summary: Lets people convicted of offenses other than murder or Megan's Law crimes ask the Superior Court to expunge convictions tied to domestic violence or abuse they suffered, unless the court finds expungement is not in the interest of justice or they were the primary aggressor.

nj:S 4877.title: Solid waste or soil & fill recyclable materials-modifies provisions for licenses
nj:S 4877.summary: Changes licensing rules for solid waste and soil and fill recycling businesses, including exempting intra-utility soil and fill transport from the soil and fill license law and lengthening the deadline to apply for a soil and fill license.

nj:S 4879.title: Division of State Police Internet Crimes Against Children Unit-suppl approp;$3M
nj:S 4879.summary: Appropriates $3 million to the State Police Internet Crimes Against Children Unit for training, equipment, vehicles, software licensing and staff mental health programs.

nj:S 4881.title: New Jersey City University-provide for merger with Kean University
nj:S 4881.summary: Authorizes Kean University to merge with New Jersey City University once conditions in their October 1, 2025 agreement are met, transfers NJCU's functions, powers and property to Kean, and appropriates $25 million to Kean.

nj:S 4894.title: Advisory Comm. on Immunization Practices-revise cert references in statutory law
nj:S 4894.summary: Requires insurers and Medicaid to cover immunizations recommended by the New Jersey Department of Health without cost sharing, with the department to consider CDC advisory committee and, as appropriate, medical society recommendations. Replaces State-law references to the CDC committee with the department.

nj:S 4904.title: Law enforce officer, St. or county investigator-permit probationary or temp appt
nj:S 4904.summary: As introduced, lets a licensed permanent law enforcement officer with basic police training certification hold a probationary or temporary State or county investigator appointment for up to 120 days while being trained and certified as a basic investigator.

nj:S 4905.title: Waterfront workers, certain-revise statutory definition
nj:S 4905.summary: Revises the statutory definition of certain waterfront workers who must be fingerprinted, so it meets federal requirements for the FBI to share criminal history records with State officials.

nj:S 4925.title: P.L.2022, c.9-expand provisions under certain circumstances
nj:S 4925.summary: Extends a law letting certain police and fire chiefs stay in the pension system past age 65 to deputy police chiefs serving on April 12, 2022 who were promoted to chief by April 30, 2023.

nj:S 4927.title: Suppl Graduate Medical Education Subsidy-increase, support addl acute care;$496K
nj:S 4927.summary: Increases the FY2026 Supplemental Graduate Medical Education Subsidy by $496,000 to add a 15th hospital with a residency program, leaving payments to the existing 14 hospitals unchanged.

nj:S 4928.title: Data center construction, certain-concerns wages paid
nj:S 4928.summary: Requires prevailing wages on construction of data centers with an electrical capacity of five megawatts or more, and sets contractor registration, insurance, bonding, certified payroll and safety requirements for that work.

nj:S 4932.title: Camden Coalition of Healthcare Providers-supplemental appropriation;$1.5M
nj:S 4932.summary: Appropriates $1.5 million for the Camden Coalition of Healthcare Providers: $1 million to the Department of Health for the Pledge to Connect behavioral health program and $500,000 to the Department of Community Affairs for the Housing First Program.

nj:S 497.title: James Francisco & Walter Schmidt Memorial Roadway-desig portion, Route 35
nj:S 497.summary: Names a portion of Route 35 in Laurence Harbor the James Francisco and Walter Schmidt Memorial Roadway, with signs paid for by private sources rather than public funds.

nj:S 4974.title: Votes at shareholder meetings-concerns
nj:S 4974.summary: Allows a corporation's bylaws to require that shareholder actions other than board elections be approved by a majority of shares present or represented by proxy and entitled to vote, instead of a majority of votes cast.

nj:S 5014.title: Contracts, State-proh enter into, limits ability to install & run cert software
nj:S 5014.summary: Requires State contracts to license software designed for generally available desktop or server hardware without limiting the agency's ability to install or run it on hardware of its choosing.

nj:S 5015.title: Ambulatory care facilities-changes, gross uniform receipts assessment charged
nj:S 5015.summary: Caps the annual ambulatory care facility assessment at $2 million per facility, starting the third quarter of Fiscal Year 2026, subject to any needed federal approval.

nj:S 5018.title: Real property & improvements, cert-auth St. Treasurer to sell, Twp. of Clinton
nj:S 5018.summary: Authorizes the State Treasurer to sell about 10 acres of the Mountainview Youth Correctional Facility in Clinton Township to Waste Management of New Jersey for $3.4 million, and another portion to Hunterdon County.

nj:S 5021.title: Centenary University-expand authorized use of grant funding
nj:S 5021.summary: Amends the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations act so a $1.5 million grant to Centenary University is no longer limited to capital improvements and can be used for general purposes.

nj:S 5026.title: High cost special education services, certain-appropriate $3.25M
nj:S 5026.summary: Allocates up to $10 million of existing school facilities funds for parking at Colin Powell Elementary School in Union City, and appropriates $3.25 million from the General Fund to Union City School District for high cost special education services.

nj:S 5031.title: Sports & entertainment projects, certain-authorize tax credits
nj:S 5031.summary: Authorizes $2.5 billion in additional tax credits, including up to $300 million for renovating arenas with 15,000+ seats operating 15+ years in a first-class city with an international airport, and the rest for Aspire and Emerge programs.

nj:S 601.title: Dylan's Law-req info be provided, approved personal flotation devices
nj:S 601.summary: Requires vessel registration applications to include information on the types of Coast Guard-approved life jackets, when each is required or recommended, and an applicant acknowledgment of having read it.

nj:S 684.title: Telecommunications & Internet service providers-terminate service contracts
nj:S 684.summary: Requires telecommunications, cable and internet providers to let a customer pause or cancel service without extra fees after admission to a long-term care facility, with billing not resuming for at least 90 days.

nj:S 685.title: Fleet Conversion Task Force-establish in DEP
nj:S 685.summary: Creates a 15-member Fleet Conversion Task Force in the Department of Environmental Protection to report within 18 months on converting commercial vehicle fleets to zero-emission vehicles.

nj:S 687.title: Jt. Blue Ribbon Task Force on Impacts of Climate Change on Prop. Insur-create
nj:S 687.summary: Creates a 17-member Joint Blue Ribbon Task Force to assess the current and predicted effects of climate change on residential and commercial property insurance.

nj:S 693.title: Van accessible parking spaces-prohibit mun. from requiring certain plan approval
nj:S 693.summary: Bars municipalities from requiring site plan or construction code approval solely for improving a commercial-zone parking lot to add up to five ADA-compliant van accessible parking spaces.

nj:S 699.title: Development easements-estab program, acquisition on privately-owned woodlands
nj:S 699.summary: Directs the State Agriculture Development Committee to set up a program to acquire development easements on private woodlands of 20 or more acres used for farming or forest products. Grants may cover up to 80 percent of local or nonprofit costs.

nj:S 712.title: Reproductive health travel advisory-establishes
nj:S 712.summary: Requires the Office of Information Technology to create a Reproductive Health Travel Advisory describing each state's restrictions on reproductive health care, such as gestational limits, waiting periods and insurance coverage bans.

nj:S 715.title: Rape kit tracking system-requires AG to establish
nj:S 715.summary: Requires the Attorney General to establish an internet-based system for tracking sexual assault forensic evidence (rape) kits from collection through lab submission to final disposition, usable by victims, law enforcement, health care and lab staff, and others the Attorney General approves.

nj:S 720.title: DCPP-require to consult with Division of Developmental Disabilities
nj:S 720.summary: Requires the child protection agency to make reasonable efforts to consult with the Division of Developmental Disabilities on a services plan when a court-ordered abuse or neglect services case involves a person eligible for that division's services.

nj:S 721.title: Investment metal bullion & cert investment coins-exempts from sales and use tax
nj:S 721.summary: Exempts sales of investment metal bullion and of investment coins with a fair market value of at least $1,000 from sales and use tax, excluding jewelry, art made of coins, commemorative medallions and precious metals fabricated for industrial or artistic uses.

nj:S 741.title: Real property & improvements-authorize to sell as surplus in City of Jersey City
nj:S 741.summary: Authorizes the State Treasurer to sell the surplus Holland Tunnel Service Garage property in Jersey City to the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey for $1.

nj:S 742.title: Bridge Rehab & Improvement & Rr Right-of-way Preserv Bond Act-approp funds
nj:S 742.summary: Reappropriates unspent 1989 Bridge Rehabilitation and Railroad Right-of-way Bond Act money to the Department of Transportation for bridge rehabilitation and rail right-of-way costs, including emergency repairs at the Commissioner's discretion.

nj:S 743.title: Habitat restoration, land acquisition, & oversight projects-appropriate $111.6M
nj:S 743.summary: Appropriates $111.6 million in natural resource damages settlement revenue to the Department of Environmental Protection for habitat restoration, land acquisition, restoration oversight and administrative costs, including grants or loans to local governments and nonprofits.

nj:S 787.title: Interdistrict public school choice prog-prov suppl transportation aid, cert dist
nj:S 787.summary: Provides supplemental State transportation aid to certain interdistrict school choice districts, and requires a court-directed choice district in a second-class city to transport students from sending districts.

nj:S 788.title: Volunteer first responders, cert-exemp from coverage, unemployment comp law
nj:S 788.summary: Exempts volunteer first responders who receive only expenses or a nominal fee from temporary disability and family leave insurance coverage and contributions, while keeping their services subject to unemployment compensation contributions.

nj:S 862.title: Pavement condition & conduct pavement lifecycle analysis-DOT prov, annual report
nj:S 862.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation's annual roadway pavement report to include the number of pothole repairs, the cost and tonnage of materials used, and the number and cost of pothole damage claims, and to be posted online.

nj:S 871.title: County fire instructors-estab. elig. enrollment in PERS & subsequent retire benf
nj:S 871.summary: Grants PERS eligibility and service credit to county fire instructors enrolled before November 1, 2008 who meet service and salary conditions, and service credit to those ruled ineligible in the past five years if they repay returned contributions and interest.

nj:S 877.title: Electric utilities, municipal-exempt from regulation by BPU
nj:S 877.summary: Exempts municipal electric utilities from Board of Public Utilities rate regulation when they charge customers outside city limits the same rates as inside, while the board keeps authority over service and reliability. Sets rules for rate comparisons and out-of-town customer feedback on rate increases.

nj:S 912.title: Postpartum information-establishes requirements and develop care plans
nj:S 912.summary: Requires health care professionals providing prenatal care to give each pregnant patient the chance to develop a personalized postpartum care plan, and to educate those who decline or lack one about the risks of foregoing postpartum care.

nj:SCR 110.title: Financial Plan of NJ Infrastructure Bank, FY2025-approve
nj:SCR 110.summary: Approves the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank's fiscal year 2025 financial plan, used to finance clean water and drinking water projects on the Department of Environmental Protection's eligibility lists.

nj:SCR 131.title: Financial Plan of NJ Infrastructure Bank, FY2026-approve
nj:SCR 131.summary: Approves the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank's fiscal year 2026 Financial Plan, which covers financing of clean water and drinking water projects on the Department of Environmental Protection's eligibility lists.

nj:SCR 135.title: Financial Plan of NJ Infrastructure Bank, FY2027-approve
nj:SCR 135.summary: Approves the New Jersey Infrastructure Bank's fiscal year 2027 Financial Plan, which finances clean water and drinking water projects on the Department of Environmental Protection's eligibility lists.

nj:SCR 137.title: Centennial of Township of Wyckoff-recognizes
nj:SCR 137.summary: Recognizes the centennial of the Township of Wyckoff.

nj:SCR 38.title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-urges to help decrease no. of fatalities
nj:SCR 38.summary: Urges the Governor to direct State departments and agencies to help reduce deaths from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

nj:SCR 93.title: Poverty Line Act of 2023-urges President and Congress to enact
nj:SCR 93.summary: Urges the President and Congress to enact the "Poverty Line Act of 2023," which would change how the federal poverty guidelines are calculated to reflect real costs and regional differences.

nj:SJR 100.title: Cleft and Craniofacial Awareness & Prevention Month-designates July each yr
nj:SJR 100.summary: Designates July of each year as "Cleft and Craniofacial Awareness and Prevention Month" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 102.title: Necrotizing Enterocolitis Awareness Day-designates May 17 of each year
nj:SJR 102.summary: Designates May 17 of each year as NEC Awareness Day in New Jersey, for necrotizing enterocolitis.

nj:SJR 103.title: Purple Heart State-declares New Jersey as
nj:SJR 103.summary: Declares New Jersey a "Purple Heart State" to honor service members wounded or killed in service.

nj:SJR 121.title: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Awareness Day-designating May 15 each year
nj:SJR 121.summary: As introduced, designates May 15 of each year as Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Awareness Day in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 122.title: Diverse Business Month-designates month of July
nj:SJR 122.summary: Designates the month of July each year as "Diverse Business Month" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 14.title: World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims-designates November 20th
nj:SJR 14.summary: Recognizes the third Sunday of November each year as "World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 140.title: Amyloidosis Awareness Month-designate month of March each year
nj:SJR 140.summary: Designates March as Amyloidosis Awareness Month in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 146.title: Robert 'Bob' Popovics Day-designate June 1 each year
nj:SJR 146.summary: Designates June 1 of each year as "Robert 'Bob' Popovics Day" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 154.title: PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s Reliability Pricing Model-direct BPU investigate
nj:SJR 154.summary: Directs the Board of Public Utilities to investigate PJM Interconnection's Reliability Pricing Model, and directs the State to work with neighboring states on affordable energy and urge PJM to adopt market reforms and speed review of new generation applications.

nj:SJR 158.title: Delaware and Raritan Canal Day-designate June 25 each year
nj:SJR 158.summary: Designates June 25 of each year as "Delaware and Raritan Canal Day" in New Jersey and asks the Governor to issue an annual proclamation.

nj:SJR 27.title: Roxie's Wish: Drowning Prevention Week for Children-desig third full week in May
nj:SJR 27.summary: Designates the third full week in May each year as "Roxie's Wish: Drowning Prevention Week for Children" and asks the Governor to issue an annual proclamation.

nj:SJR 29.title: Professional Engineers Mo. & Engineering Day-designate August & first Wednesday
nj:SJR 29.summary: Designates August as "Professional Engineers Month" and the first Wednesday in August as "Professional Engineering Day" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 30.title: International Widows' Day-designates June 23
nj:SJR 30.summary: Designates June 23 of each year as International Widows' Day in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 46.title: Paul Robeson Day-designates April 9 of each year
nj:SJR 46.summary: Designates April 9 of each year as "Paul Robeson Day" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 49.title: Menstrual Toxic Shock Syndrome Awareness Day-designate March 30th each yr
nj:SJR 49.summary: Designates March 30 of each year as "Menstrual Toxic Shock Syndrome Awareness Day" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 62.title: Menopause Awareness Month-designates September of each year
nj:SJR 62.summary: Designates October of each year as Menopause Awareness Month, October 11 as Perimenopause Day, and October 18 as Postmenopause Day in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 67.title: Children's Mental Health and Trauma Awareness-designates mo. of May
nj:SJR 67.summary: Designates May as "Children's Mental Health and Trauma Awareness Month" in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 70.title: Honor Your Hometown Weekend-designates last weekend in October
nj:SJR 70.summary: Designates the last weekend in October each year as “Honor Your Hometown Weekend” in New Jersey and asks the Governor to issue an annual proclamation encouraging its observance.

nj:SJR 71.title: Wounded Warrior Appreciation Week-designates first week in May of each year
nj:SJR 71.summary: Designates the first full week of May each year as Wounded Warrior Appreciation Week in New Jersey.

nj:SJR 76.title: Paraprofessional & School-Related Personnel in Our Schools Day-2nd Fri. of Dec.
nj:SJR 76.summary: Designates the second Friday in December each year as "PSRPs in Our Schools Day" to recognize paraprofessionals and school-related personnel.

nj:SJR 94.title: Tree of Life Remembrance Day-designates October 27th of each year
nj:SJR 94.summary: Designates October 27 of each year as "Tree of Life Remembrance Day" in New Jersey, to remember the victims of the 2018 Pittsburgh synagogue shooting.

nj:SJR 96.title: Nonprofit Day-designates August 17th in NJ, permanently
nj:SJR 96.summary: Designates August 17 of every year as “Nonprofit Day” in New Jersey.

nj:SR 18.title: PJM Interconnection region-obtain new zero- or low-emission sources of energy
nj:SR 18.summary: Urges states in the PJM Interconnection region to require data centers to get their electricity from new zero- or low-emission sources.

nj:SR 85.title: Greenhouse gas endangerment-condemn EPA rule finding
nj:SR 85.summary: Condemns the U.S. EPA rule rescinding the 2009 greenhouse gas endangerment finding and repealing greenhouse gas emission standards for light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and engines.

nm:HB 1.title: Feed Bill
nm:HB 1.summary: Appropriates $66.6 million from the general fund and cash balances for legislative session expenses and for legislative agencies' fiscal year 2027 budgets and interim expenses; takes effect on the governor's signature.

nm:HB 10.title: Rld Cannabis Enforcement
nm:HB 10.summary: Creates an Enforcement Bureau in the Regulation and Licensing Department, with peace-officer agents, to enforce the Cannabis Regulation Act; sets inspection, product embargo and seizure rules, felony penalties for tampering with embargoed or recalled products, and fines up to $10,000 per violation.

nm:HB 101.title: Firearm at Polling Place for Law Enforcement
nm:HB 101.summary: Adds two exceptions to the ban on firearms at polling places: commissioned law enforcement officers with arrest powers who are performing official duties, or who are acting under their agency's policies.

nm:HB 102.title: Violent Felonies for Meritorious Deduction
nm:HB 102.summary: Classifies homicide by vehicle and great bodily harm by vehicle as serious violent offenses for meritorious deductions, limiting prisoners convicted of them to four days a month instead of up to 30.

nm:HB 103.title: Cap Residential Property Tax Rates
nm:HB 103.summary: Lets the cap on annual residential property valuation increases keep applying after a zoning change, as long as the property stays residential, beginning tax year 2026.

nm:HB 104.title: Crimes Against Peace Officer Definitions
nm:HB 104.summary: Adds aggravated assault, assault with intent to commit a violent felony, battery and aggravated battery on a peace officer to the Victims of Crime Act definition of criminal offense, and corrects cross-references.

nm:HB 108.title: Watershed District Taxes and Directors
nm:HB 108.summary: Revises appointment of watershed district directors and requires a soil and water conservation district to levy a property tax at a watershed district's request, within existing rate limits and approval requirements.

nm:HB 109.title: Water Project Fund Changes
nm:HB 109.summary: Sets criteria for prioritizing water projects, including urgency of need, matching funds and readiness, and lets the New Mexico Finance Authority fund projects from the Water Project Fund without legislative approval until December 31, 2029.

nm:HB 11.title: Paid Family & Medical Leave Act
nm:HB 11.summary: As passed by the House, creates the Welcome Child and Family Wellness Leave Act: up to six weeks of paid family or medical leave within a 12-week limit per rolling 12 months, funded by employee and employer contributions, plus a $9,000 payment per child at birth or adoption.

nm:HB 111.title: Water Law Violation Maximum Penalty
nm:HB 111.summary: Raises penalties for certain water law violations to up to $3,400 per day, starts penalties at notice of violation, sets a penalty for water sold without a permit, and limits over-diversion penalties to repaying water.

nm:HB 113.title: Animal Welfare Program and Trust Fund
nm:HB 113.summary: Creates an Animal Welfare Program within the Department of Finance and Administration, funded through a new fund, to give grants for projects benefiting domestic cats and dogs, such as animal shelters, stray control, spay and neuter services, and animal cruelty enforcement.

nm:HB 117.title: Death Certificate by Physician Assistant
nm:HB 117.summary: Allows physician assistants to sign death certificates and changes the conditions under which deaths must be referred to the Office of the Medical Investigator.

nm:HB 12.title: Extreme Risk Firearm Protection Order Changes
nm:HB 12.summary: Lets law enforcement officers file petitions for extreme risk firearm protection orders based on information gathered in their official duties, and requires a person served with such an order to give up firearms immediately.

nm:HB 120.title: Limiting Student Restraint & Seclusion
nm:HB 120.summary: Changes school restraint and seclusion rules, including barring timeout as a disciplinary response to code of conduct violations and requiring school boards and charter governing bodies to report restraint and seclusion use, with notices to parents, to the Public Education Department.

nm:HB 124.title: New Americans Division in Wsd
nm:HB 124.summary: Creates the Office of New Americans in the Workforce Solutions Department, with annual reports from August 2027 on new Americans' economic impact and workforce numbers, and a study of the refugee resettlement program.

nm:HB 127.title: Medical Board Expedited Licensure
nm:HB 127.summary: As amended, requires the Medical Board to grant expedited licenses to qualified applicants and keep a telehealth registry of out-of-state physicians, lets it issue provisional licenses of up to two years to qualified international medical graduates, and repeals the telemedicine license.

nm:HB 128.title: Nmfa Local Solar Access Fund
nm:HB 128.summary: Creates a Local Solar Access Fund at the New Mexico Finance Authority to give grants to local governments, school districts, land grants and tribes for solar energy systems on public buildings and infrastructure, with most funding for rural entities.

nm:HB 13.title: Distribution System and Electrification Plans
nm:HB 13.summary: Requires electric utilities to file distribution system plans and beneficial electrification plans with the Public Regulation Commission, and lets them recover related costs; the committee amendment removes the proposed virtual power plant program.

nm:HB 131.title: Caregiver Background Checks
nm:HB 131.summary: Moves caregiver criminal history screening from the Department of Health to the Health Care Authority, adds human trafficking, assault of a peace officer, identity theft and animal cruelty to disqualifying felonies, and lets the agency disqualify caregivers posing an unreasonable risk.

nm:HB 132.title: Police Officer Workers Comp Conditions
nm:HB 132.summary: As amended, creates a workers' compensation presumption that police officers' noise-induced hearing loss and PTSD, and heart injury or stroke within 24 hours of a call, training or emergency, are job-caused.

nm:HB 137.title: Strategic Water Supply Act
nm:HB 137.summary: Creates the Strategic Water Supply Program and fund, letting the Office of the State Engineer and the Environment Department enter contracts or award grants for projects such as treating brackish water, with public notice and hearing requirements.

nm:HB 14.title: Earned Income Tax Credit
nm:HB 14.summary: Creates a 0.28 percent surtax on certain oil products when West Texas crude averages $55 or more a barrel, cuts the natural gas emergency school tax from 4 to 3.9 percent, and replaces the working families tax credit with an earned income tax credit.

nm:HB 140.title: Hazardous Waste Constituent" Definition
nm:HB 140.summary: Changes the Hazardous Waste Act to include discarded firefighting foam containing intentionally added PFAS, and directs the Environmental Improvement Board to adopt rules on PFAS designated as hazardous waste.

nm:HB 143.title: Lobbying Activity Reports
nm:HB 143.summary: As passed by the House, requires lobbyists and their employers to report to the Secretary of State, within 48 hours of lobbying, the legislation they support or oppose, and bars lobbyist expenditures over $50 on gifts, food or entertainment for officials during a prohibited period.

nm:HB 145.title: Additional Highway Project Bonding
nm:HB 145.summary: Authorizes the Transportation Commission to issue up to $1.5 billion in additional highway bonds backed by the state road fund and federal funds, and adds project identification and reporting requirements.

nm:HB 149.title: Supported Decision-Making Act
nm:HB 149.summary: Lets adults sign supported decision-making agreements naming supporters who help them understand and make their own decisions, with witness and notary requirements. Also redefines "harm to self" and "harm to others" in mental health commitment and outpatient treatment law.

nm:HB 15.title: Health Care Strategic Recruitment Program
nm:HB 15.summary: Creates a healthcare strategic recruitment program in which the Workforce Solutions Department helps recruit New Mexico public college graduates of the past 10 years, in healthcare shortage fields, who are not working in healthcare in the state.

nm:HB 153.title: Low-Carbon Construction Material Rebate Act
nm:HB 153.summary: Creates a Low-Carbon Construction Material Rebate Act run by the Environment Department, an Environmental Product Declaration Act, and a carbon reduction incentive program for industry.

nm:HB 154.title: Advanced Energy Product Definition
nm:HB 154.summary: Replaces a federal tax credit cross-reference in New Mexico's advanced energy equipment credits with a state list of eligible products, including solar, wind, battery and fusion components, processed critical minerals and inverters.

nm:HB 155.title: Gaming Control Board Director Qualifications
nm:HB 155.summary: Changes the qualifications for the Gaming Control Board's executive director to allow experience in a regulatory agency or the gaming industry, and removes the cap that limits the director's salary to the governor's salary.

nm:HB 157.title: New School Licenses
nm:HB 157.summary: Creates new licenses for school site administrators and superintendents with set qualifications, and requires the Public Education Department to set standards for and approve school administrator preparation programs.

nm:HB 158.title: Plans on Use of Certain Funds
nm:HB 158.summary: Requires state agencies to submit accountability and evaluation plans, covering goals, activities and evidence base, for programs funded from the Government Results and Opportunity Program Fund to budget and legislative finance officials.

nm:HB 159.title: Energy Project Siting & Military Bases
nm:HB 159.summary: Requires developers of wind, solar and other projects that file an FAA construction notice to notify the Military Base Planning Commission chair in writing within 30 business days, and send a copy of any FAA determination, military compatibility letter or unacceptable-risk finding within 30 days.

nm:HB 160.title: Stop, Look & Listen for Railroad Equipment
nm:HB 160.summary: Requires drivers at railroad crossings to stop a set distance from, and look for, other on-track equipment as well as trains.

nm:HB 161.title: State Park Day Passes for Veterans
nm:HB 161.summary: Provides each New Mexico veteran one day-use pass for unlimited entry to state parks and recreation areas and one camping pass for unlimited use of state-operated camping areas.

nm:HB 164.title: Lobbying Activity Reports
nm:HB 164.summary: Requires lobbyists or their employers to file a report with the Secretary of State within 48 hours of starting to lobby on legislation, disclosing the bill, the employer's position on it, and the employer's name.

nm:HB 165.title: Payment of Certain Irb Special Assessments
nm:HB 165.summary: Requires special assessments under the Improvement Special Assessment Act to be paid by the property owner, or by the lessee when the property is under an industrial revenue bond lease, and states that local governments are not responsible for paying them.

nm:HB 166.title: Limit Restrictions on Certain Fences
nm:HB 166.summary: Limits county and municipal regulation of battery-charged alarm fences outside exclusively residential zones, and sets standards including a 12-volt battery limit, a nonelectric fence at least 5 feet high in front, and warning signs every 30 feet.

nm:HB 167.title: Higher Ed. Payment for Certain Tests
nm:HB 167.summary: Requires the Higher Education Department to provide free high school equivalency tests to New Mexico residents who are at least 16, not enrolled in secondary school, lack a diploma or equivalency, and have passed a practice test.

nm:HB 169.title: Public Expression Protection Act
nm:HB 169.summary: Creates the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act, letting defendants in civil suits over testimony, petitioning or speech seek expedited dismissal, excluding suits against government units and certain sales-related communications.

nm:HB 17.title: Commission on Reduction of Grocery Costs
nm:HB 17.summary: Creates the Commission on Reduction of Grocery Costs to study grocery prices and develop strategies to lower consumer costs, with findings due November 15, 2025.

nm:HB 171.title: Pharmacy Custodial Care Facilities
nm:HB 171.summary: Lets licensed custodial care facilities that provide medically monitored withdrawal management obtain and possess dangerous drugs and controlled substances for that purpose under Board of Pharmacy rules, starting January 1, 2026.

nm:HB 172.title: New Mexico Red & Green Chile Month
nm:HB 172.summary: Designates August as Red and Green Chile Month in New Mexico.

nm:HB 174.title: Pharmacy Reimbursement for Certain Plans
nm:HB 174.summary: Requires state group health plans with a prescription drug benefit to pay community pharmacies a dispensing fee at least equal to what Medicaid pays, currently $10.30.

nm:HB 175.title: Forest & Watershed Buffer Projects
nm:HB 175.summary: Adds projects that create or maintain buffer zones in and around wildland and urban areas to the projects eligible for funding from the forest land protection revolving fund under the Forest and Watershed Restoration Act.

nm:HB 178.title: Nursing Practice Changes
nm:HB 178.summary: Changes the Nursing Practice Act by defining advanced practice registered nurses, clarifying nurses' scope for anesthetics and sedatives, expanding Board of Nursing powers, changing license fees and discipline procedures, and renaming diversion programs 'alternative to discipline' programs.

nm:HB 180.title: Use of Emergency Funds & Disasters
nm:HB 180.summary: As passed by the House, allows the appropriation contingency fund to pay for non-natural disasters, renames the federal reimbursement revolving fund the executive order for disasters fund for natural disasters or martial law, and ends certificates of indebtedness for National Guard and defense force costs.

nm:HB 181.title: State Trust Program Accountability Plan
nm:HB 181.summary: Requires the Department of Finance and Administration and Legislative Finance Committee to set instructions for agencies to submit accountability and evaluation plans, covering goals, evidence, performance measures and timelines, for appropriations from the government results and opportunity fund.

nm:HB 182.title: Judicial Retirement Changes
nm:HB 182.summary: Increases judicial retirement benefits for future service by reducing the service needed to qualify, raising the pension multiplier, and raising employer and employee contributions.

nm:HB 184.title: Investment of Conservation & Legacy Funds
nm:HB 184.summary: Changes the conservation legacy permanent fund so that, starting July 1, 2026, it distributes 5 percent of its average year-end value over the prior three calendar years (a two-year average at first) to the land of enchantment legacy fund.

nm:HB 19.title: Trade Ports Development Act
nm:HB 19.summary: As passed by the House, creates the Trade Ports Development Act, letting the state and local governments partner with private parties on trade port projects in designated districts, with grants and loans from a fund financed by motor vehicle excise and gross receipts tax revenue.

nm:HB 191.title: Wildfire Suppression & Preparedness Funds
nm:HB 191.summary: Creates a wildfire suppression fund and a post-wildfire fund, both administered by the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department, and requires an annual report to the Legislative Finance Committee on the funds and wildfire spending.

nm:HB 192.title: Digital Trunked Radio System Subscriber Fees
nm:HB 192.summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to report to the Legislative Finance Committee each December 1, starting in 2026, on subscriber fees and users of the digital trunked radio system.

nm:HB 193.title: Study Public Education System
nm:HB 193.summary: Lets the Legislative Education Study Committee study New Mexico's whole public education system, removing a limit that confined its higher education studies to teacher preparation programs.

nm:HB 195.title: Collection of Medical Malpractice Judgements
nm:HB 195.summary: Bars a plaintiff in a medical malpractice claim from collecting a judgment from an independent provider's personal income or assets if the provider was qualified under the Medical Malpractice Act or carried at least $1 million in per-occurrence insurance.

nm:HB 197.title: Expand "Silver Alert" Definition
nm:HB 197.summary: Expands the definition of a "Silver Alert" for missing persons to include people with cognitive decline or impairment.

nm:HB 198.title: Tax Changes
nm:HB 198.summary: Raises the threshold for public disclosure of delinquent tax installment agreements from $1,000 to $10,000, raises minimum refund interest from $1 to $10, and increases penalties and fines for failure to pay or file taxes and for tax fraud.

nm:HB 199.title: Tax Return Info for Lfc Evaluation
nm:HB 199.summary: Allows the Taxation and Revenue Department to share otherwise confidential tax data with the Legislative Finance Committee under a data-sharing agreement, for use in program evaluations.

nm:HB 2.title: General Appropriation Act of 2025
nm:HB 2.summary: Appropriates about $10.8 billion in recurring general fund spending for fiscal year 2026, about 6% above FY25, plus one-time special spending and a 4% average pay increase for state, higher education and public school employees.

nm:HB 20.title: Native American Designation on Licenses
nm:HB 20.summary: Lets members of federally recognized tribes request a Native American designation on their driver's license, documented by tribal identification, without naming a particular tribe, effective October 1, 2026.

nm:HB 200.title: New Homes for New Mexico Program
nm:HB 200.summary: Creates the New Homes for New Mexico Program, in which the Mortgage Finance Authority makes loans to buyers of starter homes of up to 1,800 square feet, with assistance up to $50,000 per household outside high-cost counties.

nm:HB 203.title: Use of State Devices for Cyfd Business
nm:HB 203.summary: Bars Children, Youth and Families Department employees from erasing data on department-issued devices, requires hourly backup of work-related electronic records by January 1, 2026, and requires keeping those records at least seven years after an employee leaves.

nm:HB 205.title: Cyfd Nominating Committee
nm:HB 205.summary: Creates a nominating committee to give the governor a list of candidates for secretary of Children, Youth and Families, requires a statewide multilevel response system, and enacts the Families First Act on foster care prevention services.

nm:HB 206.title: Crime Victim Reparation Additional Crimes
nm:HB 206.summary: Adds assault, battery, criminal sexual contact against adults, and robbery while armed with a deadly weapon to the offenses for which victims may receive payments under the Crime Victims Reparation Act.

nm:HB 208.title: Hunting & Fishing License Voter Registration
nm:HB 208.summary: As introduced, lets a qualified voter register to vote through the Department of Game and Fish when applying for a hunting or fishing license.

nm:HB 209.title: Sunshine Portal Fund Creation Links
nm:HB 209.summary: Requires the state Sunshine Portal to post website links to the statutory language that creates each state fund.

nm:HB 21.title: Land Grant-Merced Assistance Fund Changes
nm:HB 21.summary: Raises the 100 percent distribution ceiling in the land grant-merced assistance fund from $50,000 to $100,000 in annual audited revenue, and stops year-end fund balances from reverting to the general fund.

nm:HB 212.title: Per- & Poly-Flouroalkyl Protection Act
nm:HB 212.summary: Creates the PFAS Protection Act, phasing out sales of certain consumer and other goods with intentionally added PFAS, such as firefighting foam, on a set timeline and barring state purchase of such products from January 2027.

nm:HB 213.title: Expand Optometry Act
nm:HB 213.summary: Expands optometrists' scope of practice to include two laser procedures, for lens capsule clouding and glaucoma, requires board credentialing, and requires a board member credentialed in laser surgery by December 31, 2028.

nm:HB 214.title: Doula Credentialing & Access Act
nm:HB 214.summary: Creates the Doula Credentialing and Access Act: a voluntary Department of Health credential letting doulas enroll as Medicaid providers, an advisory council, hospital policies on doula access, and a Doula Fund.

nm:HB 217.title: Counseling Compact
nm:HB 217.summary: As introduced, enters New Mexico into the Counseling Compact, which eases interstate practice by licensed professional counselors.

nm:HB 218.title: Tax Changes
nm:HB 218.summary: As passed by the House, makes administrative changes to tax laws at the Taxation and Revenue Department's request, including clarifying conflicting statutes, repealing obsolete sections, and raising the cap for filing and paying less often than monthly from $200 to $500 owed.

nm:HB 219.title: Slot Canyon Riverlands State Park
nm:HB 219.summary: Directs the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department to develop, designate and operate the Slot Canyon Riverlands state park near the Broad Canyon Ranch study area in Doña Ana County.

nm:HB 22.title: Prohibit Credit Card Fee Tip Deductions
nm:HB 22.summary: Bars employers from deducting credit card processing fees from tips paid to tipped employees. Takes effect immediately upon signing.

nm:HB 220.title: Ignition-Resistant Construction
nm:HB 220.summary: Voids covenants, deed restrictions and homeowner association rules that prohibit or unreasonably limit ignition-resistant construction materials or fire-mitigating landscaping, except where required by building codes.

nm:HB 228.title: Local Restrictions on Certain Fences
nm:HB 228.summary: Limits county and city power over battery-charged security fences outside exclusively residential zones, barring bans and extra permits, and sets standards including a battery of no more than 12 volts, a non-electric perimeter fence at least 5 feet high, and warning signs every 30 feet.

nm:HB 230.title: Cannabis Testing Certain Employees
nm:HB 230.summary: Bars employers from randomly testing medical cannabis patients for cannabis; testing is allowed only on reasonable suspicion of impairment at work or after an accident, and a positive test alone does not show impairment. Directs the Health and Workforce Solutions departments to develop impairment guidelines.

nm:HB 233.title: Diabetic Foot Ulcer Equipment Coverage
nm:HB 233.summary: Requires health insurance plans to cover medically necessary treatment of active diabetic foot ulcers, including topical oxygen therapy, for policies created, modified or renewed after January 1, 2026.

nm:HB 234.title: Definition of Fentanyl
nm:HB 234.summary: As amended, defines fentanyl, for the trafficking sentence enhancements, as fentanyl or a controlled substance analog of fentanyl as defined in the Controlled Substances Act.

nm:HB 238.title: Middle & High School Professional Work Hours
nm:HB 238.summary: Allows up to 60 hours of teacher professional work time to count toward annual instructional hour requirements in middle and high schools, up from 30 hours.

nm:HB 24.title: Community Governance Attorneys Changes
nm:HB 24.summary: Changes the Community Governance Attorney Act's tuition waiver program for law students: shifts program outreach and contract administration to the UNM School of Law, raises the pay limit to an entry-level salary, and widens eligible legal providers.

nm:HB 240.title: Drinking Water System Grants & Loans
nm:HB 240.summary: Lets the New Mexico Finance Authority make grants as well as loans from the drinking water revolving loan fund, extends maximum loan repayment periods by 10 years, and requires annual reports on the fund.

nm:HB 242.title: Psychology Interjurisdictional Act
nm:HB 242.summary: Enacts the Psychology Interjurisdictional Compact, an agreement among states regulating telepsychology and temporary in-person practice by psychologists across state lines.

nm:HB 243.title: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact
nm:HB 243.summary: As introduced, enters New Mexico into the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact for streamlined physician licensing across states, and provides for appointing the state's compact commissioners.

nm:HB 244.title: Magistrate Judge Minimum Age
nm:HB 244.summary: Sets a minimum age of 28 at the time of election for magistrate judges.

nm:HB 247.title: Capital Outlay Changes
nm:HB 247.summary: Limits capital outlay reauthorizations to one extension of up to two years with 10 percent of the original funds encumbered, requires new projects of $100,000 or more to be on an infrastructure plan, and sets a process to freeze funds on inactive projects.

nm:HB 248.title: General Obligation Bonds
nm:HB 248.summary: Authorizes general obligation bonds of up to $21.6 million for senior centers, $19.3 million for libraries and $352.2 million for higher education, special and tribal schools, subject to voter approval at the November 2026 general election.

nm:HB 249.title: Unemployment & Emergencies & Disasters
nm:HB 249.summary: Lets the Workforce Solutions secretary waive the one-week waiting period for unemployment benefits during a federal or state emergency or disaster declaration.

nm:HB 251.title: Ed. Retirement Beneficiary Changes
nm:HB 251.summary: Lets a retired educator who named a spouse as beneficiary make a one-time irrevocable change to a new beneficiary with the spouse's notarized consent, and adds options after divorce.

nm:HB 252.title: Kinship Caregiver Support Pilot Program
nm:HB 252.summary: Creates a three-year Kinship Caregiver Support Pilot Program at the Aging and Long-Term Services Department for grandparents, other relatives and fictive kin raising children, with application criteria considering household income and children's needs. Takes effect on signature.

nm:HB 253.title: Public Education Changes
nm:HB 253.summary: Replaces the Statewide Cyber Academy Act with a Distance Learning Act setting standards and state evaluation for full-time online programs, bars rural population funding units for online students, and bars requiring students to enroll in them.

nm:HB 254.title: Avoided Gasses in Prc Cost Test
nm:HB 254.summary: Lets investor-owned electric utilities calculate the benefit of avoided greenhouse gas emissions beyond the utility cost test for efficiency programs, and requires the commission to count that benefit in its cost-effectiveness finding when a utility elects to.

nm:HB 255.title: Rename "Juvenile Corrections Act
nm:HB 255.summary: As passed by the House, renames the Juvenile Community Corrections Act the Juvenile Community Connections Act, extends short-term juvenile commitments from one year to 15 months and long-term from two years to 27 months, adds voluntary manslaughter to youthful-offender offenses, and creates a stipend pilot.

nm:HB 256.title: Defibrillators at School Athletic Events
nm:HB 256.summary: Extends school cardiac emergency response plans to school athletic activities and requires an automated external defibrillator to be clearly marked and easily accessible during each school athletic activity.

nm:HB 26.title: Ticket Resale at State and Nonprofit Events
nm:HB 26.summary: Extends the ban on ticket scalping, now limited to college athletic events, to events presented by the state, local governments or 501(c)(3) nonprofits; the penalty stays a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $500, jail under one year, or both.

nm:HB 260.title: Allowable Responses to Student Behavior
nm:HB 260.summary: As passed by the House, bans chemical, mechanical and prone restraint in public schools, limits seclusion to supervised confinement during imminent serious harm, allows physical restraint only when a student endangers self or others and lesser steps fail, and requires staff training and approved behavior plans.

nm:HB 269.title: Health Care Authority Visit Verification
nm:HB 269.summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to implement an open electronic visit verification system, compliant with federal law, for personal care and home health services.

nm:HB 270.title: Contributions to Apprentice & Training Pgms.
nm:HB 270.summary: Ends the exemption of street, highway, bridge, road and utility public works contracts from required contributions to apprentice and training programs, with a zero contribution for trades lacking an approved program, effective July 1, 2026.

nm:HB 281.title: Hair Braiding Licensure
nm:HB 281.summary: Exempts hair braiding from licensing under the Barbers and Cosmetologists Act and bars discipline of people who braid hair without a state license; braiding is defined to exclude cutting, coloring or chemically altering hair.

nm:HB 284.title: Free-Roaming Horses & Livestock Code
nm:HB 284.summary: Sets up rules for managing free-roaming horses under the Livestock Board, defining them, registering free-roaming horse experts and equine rescue facilities, and allowing civil fines of up to $1,000 per violation.

nm:HB 285.title: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Changes
nm:HB 285.summary: Changes the disabled veteran property tax exemption by clarifying occupancy requirements and how the exemption is determined for properties with multiple owners, and sets procedures for claiming the exemption and protesting decisions.

nm:HB 287.title: Permanent Health & Human Services Committee
nm:HB 287.summary: Expands the Legislative Health and Human Services Committee to 12 legislators, revises appointment procedures, and provides for a permanent director and staff, effective January 1, 2027, with no appropriation.

nm:HB 289.title: Geothermal Projects Development Fund
nm:HB 289.summary: Widens the types of entities that can receive grants from the geothermal projects development fund to include others in a competitive bidding process; the committee amendment removed the bill's $20 million appropriation.

nm:HB 295.title: Tax on Property Owned by Nm Reta
nm:HB 295.summary: Provides that real property owned by the Renewable Energy Transmission Authority, including transmission lines leased to and operated by non-exempt entities, is exempt from property tax, starting with the 2026 tax year.

nm:HB 296.title: Public Accountant Licensure Requirements
nm:HB 296.summary: Changes New Mexico's Public Accountancy Act: sets three education pathways to CPA certification, extends the exam completion window from 18 to 30 months, and replaces "substantial equivalency" with "comparable licensure requirements" for out-of-state and foreign CPAs.

nm:HB 297.title: School Personnel Computer Science Licensure
nm:HB 297.summary: Appropriates $250,000 to the Public Education Department for professional development for teachers seeking or keeping a computer science endorsement in fiscal years 2026 and 2027, and sets pathways for earning that endorsement.

nm:HB 298.title: Local Government Official Changes
nm:HB 298.summary: Changes Municipal Code rules for mayor-council cities, covering mayoral vacancies, appointments, mayoral powers, required organizational meetings after elections, and recusal of governing body members with conflicts of interest.

nm:HB 30.title: Teacher Residency Act Changes
nm:HB 30.summary: Sets the teaching resident stipend as a percentage of the minimum level one teacher salary based on the resident's qualifications, lets residents work at any public school afterward, and expects partner districts to offer jobs based on staffing needs and performance.

nm:HB 303.title: Utility Certificate of Public Convenience
nm:HB 303.summary: Changes when public utilities must obtain a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Public Regulation Commission: when they begin operating a plant, system or extension, instead of before construction; takes effect on the governor's signature.

nm:HB 306.title: Prohibit Certain Health Care Facility Fees
nm:HB 306.summary: Bars hospitals and health systems from charging patients directly facility fees for outpatient preventive care, vaccinations and telehealth from January 2027, except at rural hospitals; bars them for uninsured patients; requires fee notices, a standardized bill and reporting to the all-payer claims database.

nm:HB 308.title: Remove Mrgcd From Local Election Act
nm:HB 308.summary: Removes conservancy districts from the Local Election Act and sets separate election rules for them, moving their elections to October of odd-numbered years and letting district boards adopt rules for candidate filing, vote counting and canvassing. Takes effect on signature.

nm:HB 309.title: Valuation of Energy Storage Property
nm:HB 309.summary: Extends the cost-based property valuation method for electric plants to energy storage property such as batteries, with a floor of 20 percent of tangible property cost, beginning tax year 2027.

nm:HB 31.title: Ems Personnel Licensure Interstate Compact
nm:HB 31.summary: Enacts the Emergency Medical Services Personnel Licensure Interstate Compact, letting EMTs, paramedics and other EMS personnel practice across member states.

nm:HB 32.title: Counseling Licensure Compact
nm:HB 32.summary: Enacts the Counseling Compact, an agreement among states to let licensed professional counselors practice across state lines through mutual recognition of licenses.

nm:HB 323.title: Engineer Licensure
nm:HB 323.summary: Exempts rural electric distribution cooperatives from the Engineering and Surveying Practice Act, if their services are not offered to the public and are performed only on property they own, lease, operate, or hold an easement or right of way on.

nm:HB 33.title: Psychology Interjurisdictional Compact
nm:HB 33.summary: Enacts the Psychology Interjurisdictional Compact, an agreement among states regulating telepsychology and temporary in-person practice by psychologists across state lines.

nm:HB 330.title: Land Grant-Merced & Acequia Infrastructure
nm:HB 330.summary: Creates a land grant-merced and acequia infrastructure trust fund and two project funds, and sets aside a share of severance tax bond capacity for each project fund, administered by the Land Grant Council and Interstate Stream Commission.

nm:HB 332.title: Capital Outlay Reauthorizations
nm:HB 332.summary: Reauthorizes 380 capital outlay projects funded in earlier years, changing administering agencies, purposes or reversion dates, and takes effect immediately.

nm:HB 336.title: Certain Retirees Returning to Work
nm:HB 336.summary: Allows retired public employees to return to work with the state in any position that carries a duty to maintain public order and make arrests, including positions limited to specific crimes.

nm:HB 339.title: Housing Discrimination & Human Rights Act
nm:HB 339.summary: As passed by the House, adds source of income, including wages, Social Security and housing vouchers, as a protected category in the Human Rights Act, treats screening that omits some income sources as discrimination, and sends public and housing accommodation complaints to the Attorney General.

nm:HB 34.title: School Nurse Licensure Provisions
nm:HB 34.summary: Applies school nurse licensure provisions to charter schools, lets level two or three nurses evaluate level one nurses (districts without one defer to the Department of Health), lets three years of registered nursing experience qualify for level three, and drops the 9.5-month salary basis.

nm:HB 340.title: Dna of Certain Offenders in Codis
nm:HB 340.summary: Sets when the DNA of a person who dies after arrest but before felony charges may be entered in the CODIS database: automatically for those incarcerated at death, otherwise only on a district attorney's motion and court order.

nm:HB 343.title: Cyfd Plans of Safe Care for Certain Children
nm:HB 343.summary: Updates the Children's Code for plans of safe care for substance-exposed newborns, moving responsibility to the Department of Health and its CARA navigators, setting required plan components, and specifying actions CYFD takes for noncompliance.

nm:HB 346.title: Hemp Products & Synthetic Cannabinoids
nm:HB 346.summary: Bans the receipt, possession, advertising, marketing or sale of semi-synthetic and synthetic cannabinoids in New Mexico, moves hemp rulemaking to the Environmental Improvement Board, and requires rules for retail hemp extracts and finished products.

nm:HB 352.title: Close & Relocate Certain Magistrate Courts
nm:HB 352.summary: Eliminates the circuit magistrate courts in Hatch, Jal, Thoreau, Pojoaque and Estancia, and, beginning January 1, 2027, moves the Chama circuit magistrate court to Tierra Amarilla as needed.

nm:HB 357.title: Mi Via Waiver Pgm. Provider Gross Receipts
nm:HB 357.summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to exclude gross receipts taxes from Mi Via waiver participants' budgets and instead bill and reimburse providers' gross receipts taxes as a separate line item.

nm:HB 36.title: Board of Optometry Powers and Duties
nm:HB 36.summary: Expands the practice of optometry to include laser procedures on the lens capsule and for glaucoma treatment, and requires the Board of Optometry to set credentialing requirements; the committee version dropped paracentesis and drug-implant placement.

nm:HB 361.title: Emnrd Conversion of Certain Wells
nm:HB 361.summary: Allows the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department to authorize depleted oil and gas wells to be repurposed for energy storage or geothermal energy development, and requires the well to be plugged if the use is no longer viable.

nm:HB 365.title: Public Education Commission Staff
nm:HB 365.summary: Makes the Public Education Commission's charter school staff a separate State Charter Schools Office with a director chosen by the commission, replacing the Public Education Department's charter schools division, effective July 1, 2026.

nm:HB 368.title: High Wage Jobs Tax Credit "Threshold Job
nm:HB 368.summary: Changes the high-wage jobs tax credit's "threshold job" definition so a job must be held for at least 44 of the first 52 weeks of employment, rather than 44 weeks of a calendar year.

nm:HB 371.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:HB 371.summary: Creates a Land Grant-Merced and Acequia Infrastructure trust fund capitalized with up to $175 million a year of severance tax bond capacity, with annual distributions to two project funds beginning July 1, 2028.

nm:HB 372.title: Off-Highway Motor Vehicle Act Changes
nm:HB 372.summary: As amended, raises the recreational off-highway vehicle weight limit from a 1,750-pound gross vehicle weight rating to a 3,500-pound unladen dry weight, removes its engine-size limit, and ends the nonresident permit fee exemption for vehicles registered in another state.

nm:HB 38.title: Wheelchair Insurance Coverage
nm:HB 38.summary: Requires group health plans under the Health Care Purchasing Act, and insurers, to cover complex rehabilitation technology devices such as specialized wheelchairs, and makes certain denials of such devices for people with limb loss or mobility limitation an unfair and deceptive practice.

nm:HB 394.title: Clean Energy & Natural Resources Board
nm:HB 394.summary: Creates an Energy and Natural Resources Advisory Board that meets at least twice a year and advises the governor, the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources secretary and interim legislative committees.

nm:HB 398.title: Hmo & Contract Provider Exam Time Lines
nm:HB 398.summary: Adds group capital calculation reports and liquidity stress tests to the Insurance Holding Company Law and changes the minimum HMO and contract provider examination frequency from once every three years to once every five.

nm:HB 4.title: Health Care Affordability Fund Distributions
nm:HB 4.summary: Raises the share of the health insurance premium surtax going to the health care affordability fund from 55 to 80 percent on September 1, 2027, and to 100 percent on September 1, 2028, instead of the general fund.

nm:HB 402.title: Health Insurance Provider Info Loading
nm:HB 402.summary: Requires health insurance carriers to load approved dentists and dental hygienists into payment systems within 30 days of a complete credentialing application, or reimburse them, and directs the insurance superintendent to set a uniform credentialing process.

nm:HB 405.title: Volunteer Firefighter Svc. & Training
nm:HB 405.summary: Requires employers to give volunteer firefighter employees leave of up to 112 hours a year for training (30 days' notice) and up to 112 hours for emergency service; leave may be unpaid and cannot be a basis for firing, demotion or reduced seniority.

nm:HB 41.title: Public Project Fund Appropriations
nm:HB 41.summary: Appropriates $13.25 million from the public project revolving fund: $6.25 million to the drinking water revolving loan fund, $2 million to the local government planning fund and $5 million to the cultural affairs facilities fund.

nm:HB 413.title: Physician Assistant Licensure Compact
nm:HB 413.summary: As introduced, enters New Mexico into the Physician Assistant Licensure Interstate Compact, which recognizes physician assistant licenses across participating states.

nm:HB 426.title: Mobile Home Park Sale Notices
nm:HB 426.summary: Requires mobile home park owners to notify residents and the Mortgage Finance Authority of an offer they intend to accept, giving residents a chance to buy first if 51 percent signal intent within 75 days and secure financing within 90 more.

nm:HB 427.title: Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring
nm:HB 427.summary: As introduced, allows the water project fund to pay for real-time water quality monitoring projects, with grants capped at $500,000 and monitoring data reported to the Department of Environment.

nm:HB 43.title: Disability & Survivor Pensions Changes
nm:HB 43.summary: Clarifies public employee pension rules on disability and survivor pensions, gives state fire members service credit during workers' compensation leave, and makes related changes to Public Employees Retirement Act provisions.

nm:HB 431.title: Appointment of Watershed Boards
nm:HB 431.summary: Changes watershed district boards from elected to appointed by the supervisors of the involved soil and water conservation districts, gives minority-jurisdiction districts three added seats, and sets four-year terms.

nm:HB 433.title: Study Career & Tech Education
nm:HB 433.summary: Requires the Higher Education Department, with other state agencies, to study the availability of career and technical education courses and instructors and instructor pay, and to report findings and recommendations.

nm:HB 439.title: Public Safety Telecommunicator Cpr Training
nm:HB 439.summary: Requires public safety telecommunicators to be trained in telecommunicator CPR, the instructions given to bystanders during cardiac emergencies, as part of basic and annual training.

nm:HB 444.title: Transfer Athletic Commission Authority
nm:HB 444.summary: Transfers the New Mexico Athletic Commission's authority to the Regulation and Licensing Department, expands the commission from five to seven advisory members, eliminates the Medical Advisory Board and adds an event coordinator license.

nm:HB 448.title: Office of Housing Planning & Production
nm:HB 448.summary: Creates the Office of Housing Planning and Production, attached to the Department of Finance and Administration, to set a statewide housing strategy, give technical help to local governments and tribes, and track housing goals and data.

nm:HB 449.title: Higher Education Major Projects Fund
nm:HB 449.summary: Creates a higher education major projects fund run by the Higher Education Department for large instruction and research buildings, student housing and student life projects at public colleges, requiring institutions to provide matching funds from non-state sources.

nm:HB 450.title: Capital Outlay Projects
nm:HB 450.summary: Appropriates $1.2 billion for 2025 capital outlay projects, including $799.8 million from the general fund and $292 million from severance tax bonds, for state agency, judicial, higher education and local projects.

nm:HB 453.title: Housing Creditworthiness Assistance Program
nm:HB 453.summary: Adds a creditworthiness assistance program to the Affordable Housing Act, run by the Mortgage Finance Authority, with a fund for grants covering participants' unpaid rent and rental property damage; participants must complete budgeting and financial training.

nm:HB 456.title: Architect & Engineering Svcs. & Construction
nm:HB 456.summary: Raises limits on multiple-source contracts: single architectural or engineering contracts up to $2 million, construction contracts up to $30 million over as many as ten years, and construction purchase orders up to $7 million.

nm:HB 457.title: Geologic Carbon Dioxide Sequestration Act
nm:HB 457.summary: Creates a regulatory framework for geologic carbon dioxide sequestration under the Oil Conservation Division, with application and annual fees, pore-space ownership rules, tribal consultation, and a required community benefit plan for each project.

nm:HB 458.title: Carbon Dioxide Storage Stewardship Act
nm:HB 458.summary: Creates the Geologic Carbon Dioxide Long-Term Stewardship Act and fund, charges operators a fee of at least 10 cents per metric ton of carbon dioxide stored, and sets rules for certifying closure of sequestration projects.

nm:HB 468.title: Retiring of State Flags
nm:HB 468.summary: Allows a retired or unusable New Mexico state flag to be destroyed, preferably by burning, in a dignified ceremony that may be public under military or patriotic society direction, or private.

nm:HB 469.title: Border Authority & Director Requirements
nm:HB 469.summary: As introduced, changes the makeup of the Border Authority and sets minimum professional qualifications for its executive director, including managerial experience.

nm:HB 47.title: School Employee Insurance Programs
nm:HB 47.summary: Sets the school district and charter school minimum employer share of group insurance cost at 80%, ends their waivers from Public School Insurance Authority health, disability and term life plans in 2027, requires reference-based hospital pricing for state employee plans, and orders a sustainability study.

nm:HB 487.title: Protection of Hispanic Education
nm:HB 487.summary: Allows Hispanic Education Advisory Council members to receive per diem and mileage, requires biannual Hispanic education summits, adds the Higher Education Department and community groups as stakeholders, and adds preserving New Mexico's heritage Spanish language and culture to the act's purposes.

nm:HB 49.title: Closed Captioning Act
nm:HB 49.summary: Requires hotels, restaurants, theaters and other public accommodations to turn on closed captioning on TVs in public areas, with civil penalties of $1, $50 and $250 for first, second and third violations, and lets people harmed by violations sue.

nm:HB 493.title: Public Finance Accountability Act
nm:HB 493.summary: Creates the Public Finance Accountability Act, setting grantee eligibility criteria such as a recent public audit and fixes for audit weaknesses, and requiring a fiscal agent when a grantee's audit history does not qualify.

nm:HB 494.title: Tax Exemptions for Veterans
nm:HB 494.summary: Removes a provision letting disabled veterans and their unmarried surviving spouses claim property tax exemptions for the current year, so they apply within the usual 30-day window after the valuation notice.

nm:HB 5.title: Office of Child Advocate Act
nm:HB 5.summary: Creates an Office of the Child Advocate attached to the Attorney General to review and take complaints about the Children, Youth and Families Department, run a hotline, and report annually; the advocate is picked by a seven-member committee.

nm:HB 50.title: Social Work Licensure Interstate Compact
nm:HB 50.summary: Enacts the Social Work Licensure Interstate Compact, letting licensed social workers practice across member states, adds knowledge of New Mexico cultures to the scope of social work practice, and authorizes the board to require state and national criminal background checks for initial licenses.

nm:HB 518.title: Lgbtq+ Day
nm:HB 518.summary: As introduced, designates the fourth Tuesday of January in each odd-numbered year as "Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Expansive Day" in New Mexico.

nm:HB 519.title: African American Arts Center Directors
nm:HB 519.summary: Transfers operation, maintenance and staffing of the African American Performing Arts Center and Exhibit Hall from the State Fair Commission to a board of directors attached to the Cultural Affairs Department, along with related functions, staff, money and property.

nm:HB 532.title: Student Water Safety Guidance
nm:HB 532.summary: Requires school boards and charter schools to adopt water safety guidance for parents, including local swimming lesson options, and give it to parents at enrollment or by the tenth school day, starting in 2025-26.

nm:HB 54.title: Defibrillators in Every High School
nm:HB 54.summary: Requires schools to develop cardiac emergency response plans and to install an automated external defibrillator.

nm:HB 553.title: Timber Grading Act
nm:HB 553.summary: Creates a state certificate program for sawmill owners and employees to grade and label in-state structural timber, with certificates costing up to $250 and expiring after five years.

nm:HB 554.title: Residential Home Building Authorization
nm:HB 554.summary: Requires cities and counties, including home-rule municipalities, to allow accessory dwelling units on residential lots as a permitted use, and to allow multifamily housing in commercial zones and near passenger rail stations.

nm:HB 56.title: Medicaid Reimbursements for Birth Centers
nm:HB 56.summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to set Medicaid rates for birth-center services comparable to hospital rates for similar services, with annual increases matching hospital rate increases.

nm:HB 571.title: Building Housing Communities
nm:HB 571.summary: Creates a Department of Finance and Administration program giving a "building New Mexico community" award certificate to municipalities, including counties, that adopt department-approved strategies to increase housing affordability and accessibility; the department sets the strategies by rule.

nm:HB 586.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:HB 586.summary: Extends and recompiles the Health Care Consolidation Oversight Act, which would otherwise expire July 1, 2025, letting the Health Care Authority secretary review mergers and acquisitions that materially change control of a health care entity.

nm:HB 6.title: Irb Project Minimum Wage
nm:HB 6.summary: Requires projects funded by industrial revenue bonds issued by cities or counties to pay prevailing wages and fringe benefits set by the Workforce Solutions Department, for projects over $60,000.

nm:HB 60.title: Revise Certain Criminal Offense Definitions
nm:HB 60.summary: Adds aggravated assault, assault with intent to commit a violent felony, battery and aggravated battery against peace officers to crimes covered by the Victims of Crime Act, giving officers victims' rights such as court notification.

nm:HB 61.title: Aggravated Battery on Police Officer
nm:HB 61.summary: Raises aggravated battery on a peace officer causing injury not likely to cause death or great bodily harm from a third-degree to a second-degree felony, increasing the basic sentence from up to 3 years to up to 9 years.

nm:HB 618.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:HB 618.summary: Clarifies the Department of Information Technology's role in approving state agencies' information technology procurement and projects.

nm:HB 63.title: Public School Funding Formula Changes
nm:HB 63.summary: Replaces the at-risk index factor in the public school funding formula with a family income index and creates two English learner factors, one for current English learners and one for students who recently exited that status.

nm:HB 64.title: Expand Post-Secondary Tuition Eligibility
nm:HB 64.summary: Extends in-state tuition and state financial aid to students regardless of immigration status who attended state-recognized adult education courses for two semesters, earned income and filed New Mexico tax returns for two years, or applied for special immigrant juvenile status, in addition to current eligibility.

nm:HB 65.title: Cyfd Short-Term Stabilization Pilot Pgm
nm:HB 65.summary: Creates a three-year pilot program in seven counties giving children in state custody short-term stabilization services, in-home or home-like placements and enhanced foster care, run through contracts with clinical experts.

nm:HB 66.title: Workers' Compensation Changes
