nm:HB 66.summary: Raises the workers' compensation cap on a claimant's attorney fees from $22,500 to $30,000, then $32,000 in 2027 and $34,000 in 2029, and raises employer-advanced discovery costs from $3,000 to $3,500, $4,000 and $4,500 on the same schedule.

nm:HB 67.title: Reasonable Assurance for Higher Ed Employees
nm:HB 67.summary: Changes when school and college employees between terms are barred from unemployment benefits, requiring a five-part test of reemployment, including a job offer for the next term at the same or higher position and at least 90 percent of current pay.

nm:HB 69.title: Loan Forgiveness Multiplier Act
nm:HB 69.summary: Creates the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Multiplier Act, requiring colleges to credit adjunct instructors with at least 4.35 hours of work per credit hour when determining full-time status for federal loan forgiveness.

nm:HB 7.title: Apprenticeship Assistance Act Transfers
nm:HB 7.summary: Keeps the annual distribution from the workforce development and apprenticeship trust fund at $5 million instead of dropping to $3 million in FY27, and removes the tobacco settlement permanent fund from reserves to be exhausted first.

nm:HB 70.title: Prc Support Agency
nm:HB 70.summary: Separates the Public Regulation Commission from the agency that supports it, clarifies the agency's duties, requires Gift Act compliance, and creates a utility oversight fund from utility inspection and regulatory fees.

nm:HB 71.title: Early Childhood Ed & Care Fund Transfers
nm:HB 71.summary: Raises the minimum annual distribution from the early childhood education and care fund to the program fund from $250 million to $400 million.

nm:HB 73.title: Childhood Sexual Abuse Statute of Limitations
nm:HB 73.summary: Extends the deadline to sue a private party over childhood sexual abuse to the victim's 58th birthday, excludes suits against government, and revives time-barred claims for a three-year period.

nm:HB 74.title: Firefighter and Ems Provider Peer Support Act
nm:HB 74.summary: Allows public fire agencies to set up peer support programs for emergency service providers, with State Fire Marshal-approved training, confidential communications and limited liability for team members.

nm:HB 77.title: Annual Federal Snap State Outreach Plans
nm:HB 77.summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to develop an annual state outreach plan for the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and submit it to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

nm:HB 78.title: Prohibit Discrimination Against 340b Entities
nm:HB 78.summary: Bars drug manufacturers and their agents or affiliates from restricting the acquisition or delivery of 340B discounted drugs to contract pharmacies of federally qualified health centers and look-alikes, interfering with those pharmacies dispensing, or requiring the centers to submit claims or utilization data.

nm:HB 79.title: Audiology & Speech-Language Pathology Compact
nm:HB 79.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact for practice across member states, and adds state and federal criminal background checks for licensees.

nm:HB 8.title: Higher Ed. Major Projects Fund
nm:HB 8.summary: Creates a higher education major projects fund, run by the Higher Education Department, for instruction and general, Division 1 athletics, and student housing and student life projects; institutions must match with non-state funds.

nm:HB 80.title: Oil & Gas Conservation Tax Act Changes
nm:HB 80.summary: Raises the share of oil and gas conservation tax receipts sent to the oil and gas reclamation fund (50% in 2027, 75% in 2028, 100% from 2029 to 2037) and lets it fund up to $250,000 a year of energy education.

nm:HB 81.title: Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact
nm:HB 81.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Occupational Therapy Licensure Interstate Compact for practice across member states, and adds state and federal criminal background checks for occupational therapy licensees.

nm:HB 82.title: Physical Therapy Licensure Compact
nm:HB 82.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Physical Therapy Licensure Compact to ease interstate practice of physical therapy; takes effect immediately.

nm:HB 84.title: Employee Free Speech Act
nm:HB 84.summary: Creates the Employee Free Speech Act, barring employers from retaliating against employees who decline to attend or listen to employer meetings on political matters, with exceptions, and letting employees sue for damages and attorney fees.

nm:HB 88.title: Land Grant-Merced Assistance Fund Changes
nm:HB 88.summary: Raises the annual revenue levels that set land grants-mercedes' distribution percentages from the land grant-merced assistance fund (full distribution below $100,000, up from $50,000) and ends reversion of fund balances to the general fund.

nm:HB 89.title: Graduate Scholarship Act Changes
nm:HB 89.summary: Changes the Graduate Scholarship Act to require New Mexico residency and a bachelor's degree with a 3.0 GPA, prioritize students from groups underrepresented in graduate education, drop citizenship requirements, and cap awards at the full cost of tuition and fees instead of $7,200 a year.

nm:HB 9.title: Immigrant Safety Act
nm:HB 9.summary: Bars New Mexico public bodies from entering, extending or renewing agreements to detain people for federal civil immigration violations or to let local officers perform federal immigration functions, and requires existing such agreements to end at the earliest permitted date.

nm:HB 91.title: Public Utility Rate Structures
nm:HB 91.summary: Lets the Public Regulation Commission approve utility rates and programs that reduce the burden of energy costs on low-income customers.

nm:HB 93.title: Advanced Grid Technology Plans
nm:HB 93.summary: As passed by the House, lets public utilities seek approval of advanced grid technology projects, directs them to consider such technologies in integrated resource plans, lets utilities recover project costs through a tariff rider or base rates, and lets distribution cooperatives recover deployment costs.

nm:HB 95.title: Additional Second Judicial District Judgeship
nm:HB 95.summary: As passed by the House, adds one district judge in the Second Judicial District, raising it from thirty to thirty-one.

nm:HB 96.title: Space Commission Working Group
nm:HB 96.summary: As passed by the House, creates a five-member working group, appointed by the governor, lieutenant governor, House speaker and the House and Senate minority leaders, to study a space commission and draft a proposal for its structure and scope.

nm:HB 99.title: Medical Malpractice Changes
nm:HB 99.summary: Changes medical malpractice law by redefining "occurrence" as an injury or set of injuries from combined acts or omissions, extending hospital participation in the patient compensation fund, barring lump-sum payment of future medical costs, and setting new punitive damages procedures.

nm:HJM 2.title: Ipra Implementation Study Task Force
nm:HJM 2.summary: Asks the attorney general to convene a task force to study how the Inspection of Public Records Act is working and propose any legislative changes for the 2027 session.

nm:HJM 3.title: Per- & Polyfluoroalkyl Substances Report
nm:HJM 3.summary: Requests the Environment Department to report on implementing the PFAS Protection Act to interim committees by December 1, 2026, and give a final report to the governor and Legislature by August 1, 2027.

nm:HJM 5.title: Protections for Upper Pecos Watershed
nm:HJM 5.summary: Expresses the Legislature's support for a proposed federal action withdrawing specified upper Pecos watershed lands from mining and mineral leasing, and calls on Congress to pass the Pecos Watershed Protection Act. A memorial carries no force of law.

nm:HJR 1.title: Session Length, Subjects & Overrides, Ca
nm:HJR 1.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for voters in November 2026, limiting each regular legislative session to 45 days, removing limits on which bills may be considered in even-numbered years, and allowing consideration of veto overrides for bills from earlier sessions in the same biennium.

nm:HJR 12.title: College Boards of Regents Changes, Ca
nm:HJR 12.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for voters in November 2026, letting the Legislature add duties for college regents, stating their fiduciary duty, and allowing removal for incompetence, neglect, breach of duty or malfeasance in a district court action started by the board or Attorney General.

nm:HJR 2.title: Eliminate Pocket Vetoes, Ca
nm:HJR 2.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment making bills passed in the last three days of a session law if the governor does not veto them within 20 days after adjournment, and requiring a written explanation for any full or partial veto.

nm:HJR 5.title: Legislative Compensation, Ca
nm:HJR 5.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment setting legislators' pay at New Mexico's annual median household income, adjusted as that income changes, effective for members of the Fifty-Ninth Legislature if voters approve.

nm:HJR 6.title: Session Length and Bill Consideration, Ca
nm:HJR 6.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment splitting each biennium into two sessions of up to 45 days starting the second Tuesday in January, ending limits on bills in even-numbered years, and allowing veto overrides of earlier sessions' bills.

nm:HJR 7.title: Consideration of Bills in All Sessions, Ca
nm:HJR 7.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment removing restrictions on which bills may be considered in even-numbered-year sessions and allowing the Legislature to consider veto overrides of bills from earlier sessions.

nm:HM 1.title: New Mexico Food and Farms Day
nm:HM 1.summary: Proclaims January 29, 2025 "New Mexico Food and Farms Day" in the House of Representatives, recognizing community food and farm initiatives.

nm:HM 11.title: Nm Speech-Language & Hearing Assoc. Day
nm:HM 11.summary: Declares February 6, 2026 "New Mexico Speech-Language and Hearing Association Day" in the House of Representatives, recognizing the state's audiologists and speech-language pathologists.

nm:HM 12.title: 4-H Day
nm:HM 12.summary: Declares February 4, 2025 "4-H Day" in the House of Representatives, recognizing 4-H's contributions to the state.

nm:HM 13.title: Public Health Day
nm:HM 13.summary: Declares February 5, 2025 "Public Health Day" in the House of Representatives, recognizing New Mexico's public health organizations and county and tribal health councils.

nm:HM 14.title: Ffa Day
nm:HM 14.summary: Proclaims February 5, 2025 "FFA Day" in the House of Representatives, recognizing the contributions of the FFA.

nm:HM 15.title: Gallup/ Mckinley County Day
nm:HM 15.summary: Designates February 5, 2026 as Gallup/McKinley County Day in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 16.title: Victims of Violent Crimes, in Recognition
nm:HM 16.summary: Recognizes and honors victims of violent crime and asks that a copy be sent to the chair of the Crime Victims Reparation Commission.

nm:HM 17.title: American Indian Day
nm:HM 17.summary: Declares February 7, 2025 "American Indian Day" in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 18.title: Nm National Board-Certified Teacher Day
nm:HM 18.summary: Declares January 28, 2026 as New Mexico National Board-Certified Teachers Recognition Day in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 19.title: Nm Aviation & Aerospace Day
nm:HM 19.summary: Declares January 27, 2026 as New Mexico Aviation and Aerospace Day in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 2.title: Study Screen Use in Elementary Classrooms
nm:HM 2.summary: Asks the Legislative Education Study Committee to study screen use for instruction and assessment in elementary classrooms, and asks the Public Education Department to set daily screen-use guidelines.

nm:HM 21.title: Acequia Day
nm:HM 21.summary: Declares February 11, 2025 "Acequia Day" in the House of Representatives, honoring acequias' contributions to New Mexico's history, culture, economy and water management.

nm:HM 22.title: Family Day
nm:HM 22.summary: Declares February 12, 2025 "Family Day" in the House of Representatives, recognizing the importance of families in all their forms.

nm:HM 23.title: Excellence in Rio Rancho Day
nm:HM 23.summary: Declares February 20, 2025 "Excellence in Rio Rancho Day" in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 24.title: Study Restructuring Las Vegas Land Grant
nm:HM 24.summary: Asks the Department of Justice's Guadalupe Hidalgo treaty division and the Land Grant Council to study changes that would take management and appointment authority over the Las Vegas land grant from the district court, reporting by December 1, 2026.

nm:HM 25.title: Victims of Violent Crimes & Their Families
nm:HM 25.summary: Recognizes and honors victims of violent crime and their families.

nm:HM 26.title: State Agency Insect Workshop
nm:HM 26.summary: Invites state agencies, including Game and Fish, the State Land Office and Agriculture, to join an insect identification and education workshop run by UNM's Wild Friends Program and the Xerces Society, and share insect education materials.

nm:HM 27.title: Anti-Donation Clause Interim Committee Work
nm:HM 27.summary: Asks the Legislative Council to assign an interim committee to study how to implement the 2022 constitutional exception to the anti-donation clause for state aid to essential services such as internet, energy and water, and to propose legislation for 2026.

nm:HM 3.title: Honoring Nurses and Health Care Workers
nm:HM 3.summary: Honors and commends New Mexico nurses and health care workers for their service.

nm:HM 30.title: Public Education Governance Study
nm:HM 30.summary: Asks the Legislative Education Study Committee to study public education governance and convene a 2026 interim working group on whether and how to create a statewide education commission.

nm:HM 37.title: Mount Taylor as Cultural Property
nm:HM 37.summary: Affirms the House’s commitment to protecting Mount Taylor as a traditional cultural property and opposes uranium mining projects that threaten it; urges federal and state agencies to deny permits for uranium mining within its boundaries and asks Congress to change the 1872 Mining Act.

nm:HM 4.title: Study Higher Ed Health Insurance Costs
nm:HM 4.summary: Requests the Legislative Finance Committee to study options for extending health insurance to all public higher education educators and graduate student employees, with results requested by October 1, 2026.

nm:HM 40.title: Mexican American Chicano Heritage Day
nm:HM 40.summary: Declares February 2, 2026 as Mexican American Chicano Heritage Day in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 48.title: Valencia County Day
nm:HM 48.summary: Proclaims February 4, 2026 as Valencia County Day in the House of Representatives.

nm:HM 49.title: Unm Day
nm:HM 49.summary: Declares February 4, 2026 as UNM Day in the House of Representatives, recognizing the University of New Mexico's service to residents.

nm:HM 52.title: Short-Term Rental Work Group
nm:HM 52.summary: Asks state economic development, tourism and tax agencies to form a work group on short-term rentals' economic impact, taxation and regulation, and asks county assessors to pause reclassifying such properties as nonresidential until the study ends.

nm:HM 6.title: New Mexico Mesa Day
nm:HM 6.summary: Declares January 30, 2025 "New Mexico MESA Day" in the House of Representatives and recognizes New Mexico MESA, Inc. for preparing minority students for careers in math, engineering and science.

nm:HM 62.title: Impact of Hermit's Peak/ Calf Canyon Fire
nm:HM 62.summary: Recognizes the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon fire as the most destructive fire in state history and states that its claimants are entitled to full federal compensation.

nm:HM 66.title: Study Santa Teresa Border Crossing Fee
nm:HM 66.summary: Asks the Department of Transportation to study the feasibility of a border crossing user fee at the Santa Teresa port of entry, including legal authority, trade impacts, fee options and revenue.

nm:HM 8.title: Reverend Doctor Martin Luther King, Jr.
nm:HM 8.summary: Commemorates and honors the life and legacy of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.

nm:SB 1.title: Behavioral Health Trust Fund
nm:SB 1.summary: Creates a behavioral health trust fund managed by the State Investment Officer that, from July 1, 2026, pays 5 percent of its three-year average value each year into a program fund for behavioral health services run by the Health Care Authority.

nm:SB 100.title: Burglary Definition of Dwelling
nm:SB 100.summary: Defines "structure" for burglary and aggravated burglary as a protected space enclosed enough to confine people or property and carrying an expectation of privacy, which may include a partially enclosed extension of a dwelling.

nm:SB 101.title: Increase Certain Livestock Fees
nm:SB 101.summary: Raises the maximum fees the New Mexico Livestock Board may charge for services such as livestock inspections, last increased in 2004; a 50 percent fee applies to seasonal grazing moves under the same owner.

nm:SB 104.title: Removal of Wildlife Commission Members
nm:SB 104.summary: Allows removal of state wildlife commissioners only for incompetence, neglect of duty or malfeasance in office; the governor may start proceedings, commissioners get notice and a hearing, and the state supreme court has exclusive, final jurisdiction.

nm:SB 105.title: Social Work Licensure Compact
nm:SB 105.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Social Work Licensure Compact, letting licensed social workers practice across participating states, and lets the state board require criminal history checks for initial licensure.

nm:SB 109.title: Prc & Supporting Agency
nm:SB 109.summary: Separates the Public Regulation Commission from the agency that supports it, clarifies the agency's statutory duties, and makes cleanup changes to the Public Regulation Commission Act.

nm:SB 11.title: Anti-Distraction Policy in Schools
nm:SB 11.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt policies on student wireless communication devices during instructional hours, with exceptions such as assistive technology, by August 1, 2025, using Public Education Department guidelines.

nm:SB 111.title: Motor Vehicle Code "Personal Info
nm:SB 111.summary: Adds sex, gender identity, immigration status and national origin to the Motor Vehicle Code's definition of personal information, making them confidential.

nm:SB 112.title: Higher Ed Housing Facility Property Tax
nm:SB 112.summary: Exempts from property tax residential housing for the exclusive use of students or medical residents of a higher education institution, on land the institution owns and leases to a nonexempt entity to operate or help operate it, starting with tax year 2026.

nm:SB 113.title: Board & Commission Sunset Dates
nm:SB 113.summary: Extends the Board of Barbers and Cosmetologists, Board of Nursing Home Administrators, Board of Landscape Architects, Water Quality Control Commission and Coal Surface Mining Commission to a July 1, 2035 sunset date.

nm:SB 115.title: Public Project Revolving Fund Projects
nm:SB 115.summary: Authorizes the New Mexico Finance Authority to make Public Project Revolving Fund loans to 199 listed state and local government entities, and voids authorization for any entity that does not certify its intent to borrow by the end of fiscal year 2028.

nm:SB 118.title: Organ Donor License Box & Registry
nm:SB 118.summary: Requires the Motor Vehicles Division to create material explaining how to apply to be an organ donor and distribute it to state agencies by January 1, 2026.

nm:SB 119.title: Investment in Bioscience Companies
nm:SB 119.summary: Changes the Bioscience Development Act: makes the bioscience fund nonreverting, limits Bioscience Authority investments to New Mexico businesses meeting employee and salary minimums, requires co-investors, and bars investing in companies tied to board members' families.

nm:SB 120.title: No Behavioral Health Cost Sharing
nm:SB 120.summary: Removes the 2027 sunset on the ban on copayments, coinsurance and deductibles for in-network behavioral health services in group health plans, making the ban permanent.

nm:SB 122.title: Expand Prescription Drug Donation Program
nm:SB 122.summary: Lets any person donate unexpired prescription drugs to "eligible recipients", meaning licensed practitioners and facilities registered with the Board of Pharmacy, which oversees rules for redistribution.

nm:SB 123.title: Regional Transit District Law Enforcement
nm:SB 123.summary: Lets any regional transit district, not only those running commuter rail, employ district law enforcement officers who have peace officer powers on district property.

nm:SB 124.title: Superintendent of Insurance Subpoenas
nm:SB 124.summary: Lets the superintendent of insurance issue civil investigative subpoenas before a notice to show cause, and seek a district court order compelling compliance if a person ignores a subpoena without valid reason.

nm:SB 126.title: Increase Rural Service Fund Allocations
nm:SB 126.summary: Raises the amount of the state rural universal service fund allocated to the broadband program from $30 million to $40 million, and raises the fund's obligation cap from $30 million to $40 million.

nm:SB 127.title: Movie Exemption From Barber & Cosmetic Act
nm:SB 127.summary: Exempts makeup artists and hairstylists working on theatrical or cinematic productions from licensing under the Barbers and Cosmetologists Act, and adds commissioned Air Force officers to the exempt list.

nm:SB 128.title: Certain Characters on License Plates
nm:SB 128.summary: Bars the Motor Vehicle Division from issuing special license plates with characters it finds offensive, obscene, vulgar, sexually explicit, or promoting drugs, alcohol, violence or gangs, and lets it refuse plates that are hard to tell apart.

nm:SB 13.title: State-Tribal Education Compact Schools Act
nm:SB 13.summary: Creates the State-Tribal Education Compact Schools Act, letting the Public Education Department enter up to five pilot compacts with tribes and pueblos for language- and culture-based schools, with an application process and exemptions from some state curriculum and assessment rules.

nm:SB 132.title: Doit Software Replacement Plan & Funding
nm:SB 132.summary: Lets the Department of Information Technology use its equipment replacement revolving fund to buy software as well as hardware and equipment, and repeals a 2008 provision for initial transfers into the fund.

nm:SB 133.title: Educational Retirees Returning to Work
nm:SB 133.summary: Raises the yearly earnings limit for educational retirees who return to work with an affiliated employer from $15,000 to $25,000 and extends the allowed time from 36 to 60 months without suspending retirement benefits.

nm:SB 135.title: Reimbursement for Certain Legislators
nm:SB 135.summary: Exempts legislators from the bar on out-of-state travel reimbursement for elected officials who did not file for reelection or lost a primary or general election, replacing the exemption that required a three-fourths Legislative Council vote.

nm:SB 137.title: Rename Enhanced 911 Act
nm:SB 137.summary: Updates the 911 system for Next Generation 911 (text, video, data), raises the monthly 911 surcharge from $0.51 to $1.00 per line, and renames the Enhanced 911 Act and fund.

nm:SB 14.title: Health Professional Advisory Committee
nm:SB 14.summary: Changes the Health Professional Loan Repayment Program: names eligible licensed health professions, offers physicians awards of up to $300,000 over four years, directs at least half of funds to physicians, and requires awardees to be U.S. citizens.

nm:SB 142.title: Grid Modernization Roadmap
nm:SB 142.summary: Requires the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department to consult the Public Regulation Commission on the grid modernization roadmap, lets school districts and charter schools apply for grants, and widens the definition of grid modernization.

nm:SB 143.title: Update Certain Agricultural Fees
nm:SB 143.summary: Raises the commercial feed fee from 15 to 25 cents per ton and lets certain agricultural fees rise with inflation (CPI-U) through fiscal year 2031.

nm:SB 145.title: Audit Changes
nm:SB 145.summary: Changes the Audit Act by adjusting which entities are audited, having the Department of Finance and Administration engage a statewide federal single audit starting in 2028, and appropriating $50,000 to the State Auditor for audit software.

nm:SB 146.title: Educational Opportunity for Military Children
nm:SB 146.summary: Corrects a reference to a United States Code provision in the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children.

nm:SB 15.title: Volunteer Ems & Firefighter Tax Credits
nm:SB 15.summary: Creates a $1,000 refundable income tax credit for volunteer firefighters and volunteer EMS providers who volunteer at least 52 times a year, capped at $4 million per credit type, for tax years 2025 through 2034.

nm:SB 151.title: Corporate Income Tax Changes
nm:SB 151.summary: Decouples corporate income tax from three 2025 federal provisions from 2027, creates credits for local news organizations, local news printers and physicians, adds a gross receipts deduction for affordable multifamily housing construction, extends the high-wage jobs credit, and funds a 1 percent pay raise.

nm:SB 152.title: Low-Income Telecomm. Assistance Program
nm:SB 152.summary: Creates a low-income telecommunications assistance program funded by the state rural universal service fund, capped at $10 million in year one and $45 million after, and repeals the Low-Income Telephone Service Assistance Act.

nm:SB 155.title: Determination of Embezzlement Penalty
nm:SB 155.summary: Sets embezzlement penalties by adding up the value taken from any one victim over any consecutive 12-month period.

nm:SB 158.title: Reporting of Economic Development Incentives
nm:SB 158.summary: Requires the Economic Development Department to report annually to the Legislature on Local Economic Development Act and Job Training Incentive Program results, including public support, investment, jobs, wages and economic impact.

nm:SB 159.title: Independent Theater Beer & Wine Licenses
nm:SB 159.summary: Creates an independent theater license letting theaters serve beer and wine during screenings and events, limited to two 12-ounce beers or two six-ounce glasses of wine per customer per event, with server permits required.

nm:SB 16.title: Non-Major Party Voters in Primary Elections
nm:SB 16.summary: Lets voters who declined to designate a party affiliation choose a participating major party's ballot in a primary election, without changing their voter registration unless they request it.

nm:SB 161.title: Background Checks for Dma Employees
nm:SB 161.summary: Requires state and national fingerprint background checks for Department of Military Affairs employees and volunteers who supervise minors in its youth programs, paid by the person checked; current staff have six months.

nm:SB 162.title: Severance Tax Permanent Fund Investments
nm:SB 162.summary: Replaces the 11 percent cap on severance tax permanent fund money the State Investment Council may put into the New Mexico Private Equity Investment Program with a $700 million cap.

nm:SB 163.title: Tribal Regalia at School Events
nm:SB 163.summary: Allows public school students enrolled in, or eligible for enrollment in, a federally recognized tribe, nation or pueblo to wear tribal regalia at graduation ceremonies and other school events; takes effect immediately.

nm:SB 166.title: Harm to Self & Others Definition
nm:SB 166.summary: Redefines "harm to self" as inability to meet basic needs with a likelihood of death or serious injury, and "harm to others" as recent serious violence with high risk of recurrence, dropping extreme property destruction; clarifies crisis triage centers as evaluation sites.

nm:SB 168.title: Travel Insurance Act
nm:SB 168.summary: Creates the Travel Insurance Act, setting responsibilities for travel insurance sellers and administrators, classifying travel insurance as inland marine for rate and form filing, and declaring cancellation fee waivers are not insurance.

nm:SB 169.title: Strategic Economic Development Site Readiness
nm:SB 169.summary: Creates the Strategic Economic Development Site Readiness Act, a site readiness fund, and an advisory committee to help the Economic Development Department select and fund business sites; tribes and pueblos qualify as public partners.

nm:SB 17.title: Stop Illegal Gun Trade Act
nm:SB 17.summary: Creates the Stop Illegal Gun Trade and Extremely Dangerous Weapons Act: sets dealer security, training and recordkeeping rules, and from July 1, 2026 bars dealers from selling magazines over 10 rounds, .50 caliber rifles, certain gas-operated semiautomatic firearms and machine guns.

nm:SB 170.title: Nmfa Definitions, Funds & Rates
nm:SB 170.summary: Adds rural electric cooperatives to entities that may borrow from the Public Project Revolving Fund, suspends legislative authorization of fund projects until June 30, 2028, and lets utilities recover costs of energy resources for certified economic development projects through rates.

nm:SB 172.title: Technology Readiness Grt Credit
nm:SB 172.summary: Extends the sunset of the technology readiness gross receipts tax credit for national laboratories from fiscal year 2028 to 2036 and raises each lab's annual cap from $1 million to $2 million in FY28, rising to $5 million from FY31 on.

nm:SB 175.title: Child Care Facility Loan Fund Changes
nm:SB 175.summary: Expands the child care facility revolving loan fund to cover creating and expanding facilities, including employer-run ones, lets the early childhood department and Finance Authority contract for services with providers meeting set conditions, and prioritizes high-poverty communities and nontraditional-hour care.

nm:SB 179.title: Electronic Disclosure for Rental Agreements
nm:SB 179.summary: Allows rent-to-own sellers to give required price and payment disclosures electronically, instead of on a tag or card, for items offered online.

nm:SB 18.title: Clear Horizons & Emissions Codification
nm:SB 18.summary: Writes into law statewide greenhouse gas reduction targets of 45 percent by 2030, 75 percent by 2040 and 100 percent by 2050 below 2005 levels, and directs the Environmental Improvement Board to adopt rules, emission limits for large sources, and fees.

nm:SB 180.title: Self-Service Storage Rental Changes
nm:SB 180.summary: Changes the Self-Service Storage Lien Act: calls the renter an "occupant," requires a phone number and email in rental agreements, lets occupants name an alternate contact for lien notices, and extends the default period before sale to 60 days.

nm:SB 186.title: Multifamily Housing Valuation
nm:SB 186.summary: Lets owners of multifamily housing choose among valuation methods for property tax: the existing 3 percent annual cap, a 40 percent valuation cap, or, for new construction, the lower of market value or construction and land cost.

nm:SB 19.title: Boards of Regents Training Requirements
nm:SB 19.summary: Requires the Higher Education Department to provide 10 hours of training to regents at New Mexico public colleges in their first six months, and to track each regent's compliance.

nm:SB 193.title: Acequia & Ditch Infrastructure Fund Transfer
nm:SB 193.summary: Doubles the annual transfer from the irrigation works construction fund to the acequia and community ditch infrastructure fund from $2.5 million to $5 million, effective July 1, 2026.

nm:SB 197.title: Ems System Improvement Projects Funding
nm:SB 197.summary: Lets municipalities and counties issue bonds, pledging Emergency Medical Services Fund distributions, to buy EMS equipment and vehicles, and lets the state treasurer redirect distributions to the New Mexico Finance Authority for related loans.

nm:SB 199.title: Administration of Local Dwi Grant Program
nm:SB 199.summary: Raises by $500,000 the liquor excise tax revenue available to administer the Local DWI Grant Program and lowers by the same amount the money available for grants to counties and municipalities.

nm:SB 2.title: State Highway Project Bonds
nm:SB 2.summary: Authorizes the Transportation Commission to issue up to $1.5 billion in additional highway bonds, capped at $290 million a year, and raises the weight-distance tax 35 percent and vehicle registration fees 25 percent, with a new fee on electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.

nm:SB 20.title: Increase Cigarette & Tobacco Products Taxes
nm:SB 20.summary: Raises the tax on e-liquid and other tobacco products to 40 percent, up from 12.5 percent on e-liquid and 25 percent on other products, and taxes closed-system cartridges at 40 percent. Sends 35 percent of the revenue to a new nicotine prevention fund.

nm:SB 202.title: Standardize State Investment Fund Language
nm:SB 202.summary: Changes state investment and budget statutes: separates permanent funds from other state investment funds, adjusts how consultants are assigned, changes agency budget reversion timing, and repeals a temporary transition provision for the State Investment Council.

nm:SB 21.title: Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Act
nm:SB 21.summary: Changes the Water Quality Act to move surface-water discharge regulation from the Oil Conservation Division to the Environment Department, sets new permit and enforcement rules, creates a fund for neglected contaminated sites, and lets the state take over federal discharge permitting (NPDES) from the EPA.

nm:SB 213.title: Yielding to Transit Buses
nm:SB 213.summary: Requires drivers to yield to a transit bus merging from a designated stop when an illuminated yield sign is displayed on its rear; violation is a $25 penalty assessment misdemeanor. Transit operators are not required to install the signs.

nm:SB 219.title: Medical Psilocybin Act
nm:SB 219.summary: Creates the Medical Psilocybin Act, with an advisory board and a program allowing limited use of psilocybin for patients whose clinicians recommend it, with the Department of Health setting qualifying conditions.

nm:SB 220.title: Publication of Legal Settlement Terms
nm:SB 220.summary: Requires state agencies and public schools to post the terms of legal settlement agreements on the sunshine portal within 30 days, and provides for loss prevention review teams and reports.

nm:SB 221.title: Additional Unfair Insurance Claims Practice
nm:SB 221.summary: Adds a prohibited unfair claims practice barring insurers from treating a policyholder inquiry as a claim when no coverage applies, no payment is made and there is no fraud.

nm:SB 226.title: Truck Tractor Max Speed Limit
nm:SB 226.summary: Sets a maximum speed limit of 65 miles per hour for truck tractors on New Mexico highways and adds a $250 penalty assessment for exceeding it.

nm:SB 23.title: Oil & Gas Royalty Rate Changes
nm:SB 23.summary: Raises the maximum oil and gas royalty rate on premium state trust land in the Permian Basin from one-fifth to one-fourth of production value for leases issued on or after July 1, 2025.

nm:SB 235.title: Microgrid Oversight Act
nm:SB 235.summary: Creates the Microgrid Oversight Act, requiring the Public Regulation Commission to enforce renewable and zero-carbon standards for microgrids with targets reaching 100 percent zero-carbon by 2045, annual reporting, and power to halt noncompliant operations. Applies to investor-owned utilities.

nm:SB 236.title: Look Twice for Motorcycle License Plate
nm:SB 236.summary: Extends the Look Twice for Motorcycles special registration plate to motorcycles, with a $40 initial fee for motorcycles; revenue covers plate production and the rest goes to the motorcycle training fund.

nm:SB 240.title: Capital Outlay Projects
nm:SB 240.summary: Appropriates about $1.3 billion from severance tax bonds, the general fund and other state funds for 1,344 capital outlay projects statewide.

nm:SB 241.title: Child Care Assistance Program Act
nm:SB 241.summary: Creates the Child Care Assistance Program Act, putting the program into statute with eligibility rules, allowing waiting lists and co-payments above 600 percent of poverty, and allowing transfers of up to $700 million from the early childhood fund.

nm:SB 242.title: Advancing the Science of Reading Act
nm:SB 242.summary: Creates the Advancing the Science of Reading Act: requires new teacher licensure candidates to show structured literacy competency, requires approved reading instructional materials, and bans balanced literacy as a teaching method in public schools and teacher preparation programs.

nm:SB 246.title: Massage Therapy Practice Changes
nm:SB 246.summary: Creates licensing for massage therapy establishments under the Massage Therapy Board, with minimum standards, inspections at any time, and an inactive status for unrenewed licenses; also requires new and renewed massage therapist licenses to include a current photo of the holder.

nm:SB 247.title: Publication of Certain Educational Info
nm:SB 247.summary: Requires the Public Education Department to publish statewide, district and school test proficiency rates before September 1 each year, including breakdowns by race, gender, ethnicity, tribal affiliation, socioeconomic status and special education status.

nm:SB 249.title: Health Care Provider Gross Receipts
nm:SB 249.summary: Requires managed care organizations to reimburse health care providers for applicable gross receipts taxes on Medicaid-contracted services and to document the tax amount separately from the Medicaid reimbursement.

nm:SB 254.title: Cybersecurity Act & Office Changes
nm:SB 254.summary: Renames the Cybersecurity Office the Office of Cybersecurity, lets it develop minimum cybersecurity controls for entities on state-operated or state-owned telecommunications networks rather than agency-operated or -owned ones, and changes the advisory committee's membership.

nm:SB 259.title: Professional Fundraiser Requirements
nm:SB 259.summary: As introduced, requires professional fundraisers to file a financial report with the attorney general within 90 days of a campaign, requires third-party solicitors to file periodic financial reports, and requires collection receptacles to display charity and operator contact information.

nm:SB 261.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:SB 261.summary: Removes most exceptions to the ban on carrying firearms at polling places, including for concealed handgun license holders and most officers, leaving exceptions for officers requested by election officials, people inside a private vehicle, and officers whose office is in the same building.

nm:SB 264.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:SB 264.summary: Bars ordering or bringing U.S. troops or armed persons to polling places or within 50 feet of ballot drop boxes from 28 days before an election through election day, except to repel armed enemies; makes violations a fourth-degree felony and allows civil actions.

nm:SB 267.title: Housing Application Fees
nm:SB 267.summary: Caps rental screening fees at $50, requires listings to disclose rent and fees in plain language, cuts the maximum late fee from 10 to 5 percent of rent, and requires 60 days' notice of fee increases.

nm:SB 273.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:SB 273.summary: Appropriates about $11.9 million in FY27 to local governments, including Torrance County and Estancia, for revenue lost under the law barring local governments' new contracts with private immigration detention facilities, plus $9.7 million (FY26) and $24 million (FY27) to state agencies.

nm:SB 274.title: Board of Finance Approval for Land Sales
nm:SB 274.summary: Raises approval thresholds for selling public property: State Board of Finance approval from $25,000 to $150,000, legislative approval from $100,000 to $550,000, and disposal of obsolete property without higher approval from $5,000 to $30,000.

nm:SB 278.title: Coronary Artery Calcium Screening Insurance
nm:SB 278.summary: Bars cost sharing for coronary artery calcium screening for insured people aged 50 to 65 at intermediate risk of heart disease, and excludes catastrophic plans and high-deductible savings-account plans until the deductible is met.

nm:SB 280.title: Nmmi in Capital Outlay Act
nm:SB 280.summary: Adds the New Mexico Military Institute to the Public School Capital Outlay Act as one of the constitutional special schools.

nm:SB 283.title: Cyfd & Use of Federal Benefits
nm:SB 283.summary: Requires CYFD to check within 60 days whether a child in custody is eligible for federal benefits, apply for them, and serve as representative payee only if no other candidate is available; bars using benefits to pay for the child's care.

nm:SB 29.title: Math Requirements for Teaching License
nm:SB 29.summary: Requires six hours of math methods courses for elementary licensure and secondary math endorsement, for licenses issued from July 2028. From 2027-28, requires districts and charter schools to make math professional learning plans, screen grades K-3 in math and give support plans to struggling students.

nm:SB 290.title: Raise Marriage License Fees
nm:SB 290.summary: Raises the county clerk's marriage license fee from $25 to $55, and splits each fee: $15 to the county general fund, $20 to the children's trust fund, and $20 retained by the county clerk.

nm:SB 299.title: Notice of Vacant Legislative Office
nm:SB 299.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to notify the governor, the presiding officer of the legislator's chamber and county commissioners within five days of a notice of legislative vacancy.

nm:SB 3.title: Behavioral Health Reform & Investment Act
nm:SB 3.summary: Creates a behavioral health executive committee and has regions draft behavioral health plans, coordinated by the courts' administrative office. Directs funding to gaps in those plans, requires a single Medicaid enrollment and credentialing process, and requires a needs analysis every two years.

nm:SB 30.title: Reporting of Induced Abortions
nm:SB 30.summary: Repeals the requirement that induced abortions performed in New Mexico be reported to the state registrar within five days.

nm:SB 302.title: Gaming Control Board Access Background Checks
nm:SB 302.summary: Requires fingerprints, criminal history and financial history from gaming license and work permit applicants, and background investigations, including ten years of business and financial disclosures, for contractors seeking unescorted access to Gaming Control Board facilities.

nm:SB 303.title: Gaming Machine Standards
nm:SB 303.summary: Removes the requirement that gaming machines meet Nevada and New Jersey standards, requiring instead that they meet standards set by New Mexico law.

nm:SB 305.title: Quality Foster Parent Task Force
nm:SB 305.summary: Creates a task force, convened by the Children, Youth and Families Department, to study foster parent recruitment and retention and ways to reduce children's office stays, reporting by July 1, 2026.

nm:SB 306.title: Higher Ed Regional Distinction
nm:SB 306.summary: As introduced, ends the distinction between regionally and nonregionally accredited private postsecondary institutions and changes "registration" to "licensure" in the Post-Secondary Educational Institution Act.

nm:SB 31.title: Zero-Interest Natural Disaster Loans
nm:SB 31.summary: Creates zero-interest loans from the Department of Finance and Administration to local governments and electric cooperatives awaiting FEMA funds after a federally declared disaster, repaid by reimbursement, plus a natural disaster revolving fund.

nm:SB 315.title: State Bread
nm:SB 315.summary: Declares the tortilla the official state bread of New Mexico.

nm:SB 318.title: Firearms in Unfair Practices Act
nm:SB 318.summary: Applies the Unfair Practices Act to firearms, destructive devices and accessories, adds online marketplace and third-party seller rules, and raises the attorney general's civil penalty from $5,000 to $30,000 per violation.

nm:SB 327.title: Lowrider Capital License Plate
nm:SB 327.summary: Creates a "lowrider capital of the world" special registration plate with an initial fee of $50 ($40 for motorcycles) and a $20 renewal, with most of the money going to the Department of Cultural Affairs for museum exhibits on lowrider history.

nm:SB 33.title: Wildfire Prepared Act
nm:SB 33.summary: Creates the Wildfire Prepared Act, with a wildfire prepared fund and program in the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department that gives grants to New Mexico residents who own homes, and adds duties and members to the Fire Planning Task Force.

nm:SB 343.title: Teacher Salary Rates Changes
nm:SB 343.summary: Removes the vocational-license exceptions to minimum salaries for level one, level two and level three-A teachers and changes "K-5 plus" program references to "K-12 plus".

nm:SB 345.title: Teacher & Instructional Support Licensure
nm:SB 345.summary: Adds a teacher portfolio option for level 1 teacher licensure and lets the Public Education Department grant level 2 and 3-A licenses to experienced instructional support providers licensed in other states.

nm:SB 35.title: Create Addition 1st District Judgeship
nm:SB 35.summary: Creates one additional district judgeship in each of the First and Second Judicial Districts, bringing them to eleven and thirty-one judges, and takes effect immediately.

nm:SB 353.title: Search & Rescue Emergency Responses
nm:SB 353.summary: Sets response protocols for federal, state, local and tribal agencies in search and rescue emergencies, requires standard notification criteria and search-and-rescue training for emergency personnel and 911 answering points, and adds tribes to the Search and Rescue Act.

nm:SB 357.title: Essential Services Development Act
nm:SB 357.summary: Creates the Essential Services Development Act to allow state support for infrastructure projects, mainly in residential areas, for broadband, energy, water and wastewater services.

nm:SB 36.title: Sensitive Personal Information Nondisclosure
nm:SB 36.summary: Bars state agency employees from disclosing sensitive personal information to outsiders except in listed cases, and bars Taxation and Revenue Department and Traffic Safety Bureau employees from disclosing driver and vehicle records to enforce the federal Immigration and Nationality Act, except its felony provisions.

nm:SB 364.title: Law Enforcement Qualifications
nm:SB 364.summary: Adds authorization to work from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services as an alternative to U.S. citizenship for appointment as peace officers, special deputy sheriffs and marshals, state police members, and law enforcement certification.

nm:SB 37.title: Strategic Water Reserve Fund
nm:SB 37.summary: Creates a strategic water reserve fund capped at $15 million, with excess reverting to the general fund, and expands Interstate Stream Commission authority over water management, conservation and aquifer recharge.

nm:SB 375.title: Probation & Parole Changes
nm:SB 375.summary: Ends the requirement that parolees pay for parole services, releases minimum-risk probationers who met their obligations and served half their term, and revises how prisoners earn meritorious deductions, including after parole revocation.

nm:SB 376.title: State Employee Health Benefit Contributions
nm:SB 376.summary: Sets the state's share of employee health premiums at 80 percent, lets the Health Care Authority set reference-based hospital pricing, and allows the health care affordability fund to subsidize premiums for lower-income state employees and certain National Guard members.

nm:SB 377.title: Nm United License Plate
nm:SB 377.summary: Creates a New Mexico United special registration plate available from July 1, 2025, with a $50 initial fee and $20 annual renewal; most revenue goes to the Tourism Department to promote sports-related tourism.

nm:SB 38.title: Fees on Registered Pet Food
nm:SB 38.summary: Repeals the scheduled July 1, 2026 end of the spay and neuter program fee on registered pet food, so the fee continues to be collected.

nm:SB 383.title: Flood Recovery Bonds & Gross Receipts
nm:SB 383.summary: Lets municipalities issue flood recovery revenue bonds to rebuild, repair or harden property damaged by a flood, and creates a municipal flood recovery gross receipts tax to repay them.

nm:SB 387.title: Community School Fund & Framework
nm:SB 387.summary: Allows community school implementation grants to be "up to" $150,000 a year rather than a fixed amount, and renames the community schools fund for Dr. Jeannie Oakes.

nm:SB 39.title: Add Classes to Prior Authorization Drugs
nm:SB 39.summary: Bars prior authorization and step therapy for medications prescribed, on-label or off-label, to treat rare diseases or conditions affecting fewer than 200,000 people in the United States.

nm:SB 40.title: Driver Privacy and Safety Act
nm:SB 40.summary: Sets rules for automated license plate readers, barring sharing of data a user reasonably believes may be used for immigration enforcement or to investigate or prosecute protected health care activity, requiring use reporting, and allowing civil enforcement by the attorney general and district attorneys.

nm:SB 401.title: Broadband for Education
nm:SB 401.summary: Makes education technology infrastructure projects eligible for severance tax bond proceeds, letting the broadband office director certify up to $10 million a year of supplemental bonds; the provisions expire July 1, 2030.

nm:SB 41.title: Statute of Limitations for Certain Sex Crimes
nm:SB 41.summary: Eliminates the statute of limitations for second-degree criminal sexual contact of a minor, so prosecution can begin at any time, and updates related tolling provisions for offenses against children.

nm:SB 411.title: Physician Loan Repayment Act
nm:SB 411.summary: Creates the Physician Loan Repayment Act, with the Higher Education Department providing loan repayment of $75,000 a year for up to four years to physicians practicing in designated shortage areas.

nm:SB 417.title: Confirmatory Adoptions
nm:SB 417.summary: Changes the Adoption Act and Uniform Parentage Act for children born through assisted reproduction, excluding donors and presumed parents from the "alleged father" definition and providing for confirmatory adoption to confirm parentage.

nm:SB 425.title: Capital Outlay Reauthorizations
nm:SB 425.summary: Reauthorizes or reappropriates unspent balances of prior-year capital project appropriations, changing some purposes, agencies and expenditure deadlines and setting conditions for reversion of unspent balances.

nm:SB 426.title: Repeal Obsolete School Provision
nm:SB 426.summary: As introduced, repeals Section 22-14-20, which transferred functions of the New Mexico School for the Visually Handicapped to the Blind Administrative Unit of the Vocational Rehabilitation Division.

nm:SB 43.title: Parole Requirement Changes
nm:SB 43.summary: Changes the factors the parole board weighs for inmates serving life sentences, including risk, program participation and rehabilitation, adjusts board member per diem and mileage rules, and sets hearing scheduling.

nm:SB 434.title: Math & Reading Academic Support
nm:SB 434.summary: Requires schools to identify students in the bottom quartile in math or reading, notify parents, and provide high-impact tutoring within 30 days, at least three times weekly for ten weeks, in groups of four or fewer.

nm:SB 443.title: No Cholesterol-Lowering Drug Cost Sharing
nm:SB 443.summary: Bars health plans that cover cholesterol-lowering drugs from charging cost sharing for generics, and for second-line step therapy drugs if generics fail or cause intolerable reactions. Takes effect January 1, 2026.

nm:SB 45.title: County Health Care Assistance Fund Use
nm:SB 45.summary: Allows counties to use county health care assistance funds to cover premiums and out-of-pocket costs of public or private health coverage for medically indigent residents.

nm:SB 456.title: Permanent Courts & Justice Committee
nm:SB 456.summary: Creates a permanent joint interim Courts and Justice Committee of 10 legislators (five from each chamber) to study courts, justice programs and related law and report to the Legislative Council each December 15.

nm:SB 47.title: Santa Cruz De La Canada Land Grant
nm:SB 47.summary: Adds the Santa Cruz de la Canada Land Grant-Merced to the land grants governed by Chapter 49, Article 1 of state law.

nm:SB 48.title: Community Benefit Fund
nm:SB 48.summary: Creates a community benefit fund, run by the Department of Finance and Administration, for projects such as cutting building greenhouse gas emissions, reducing methane leaks and expanding electric grid capacity. The passed version contains no appropriation.

nm:SB 480.title: Student Graduation Reporting
nm:SB 480.summary: Requires the Public Education Department to compile directory information on students who have not graduated within four years of starting ninth grade and share it on request with higher education, adult education, workforce programs and public schools.

nm:SB 495.title: Higher Education Radio
nm:SB 495.summary: Allows the educational television equipment replacement fund to be spent at public schools and on radio equipment, and clarifies that the fund does not revert.

nm:SB 5.title: Game Commission Reform
nm:SB 5.summary: Renames the Department of Game and Fish the Department of Wildlife, changes how Game Commission members are chosen and removed, and raises most hunting and fishing license fees, including a $90 nonresident hunting license and a new $200 nonresident shed-antler license.

nm:SB 50.title: Law Enforcement Training Requirements
nm:SB 50.summary: Removes the legal requirement for in-service training of police officers on domestic abuse incidents, and for officers and telecommunicators on missing-person reports, while keeping domestic abuse content in basic training. Takes effect January 1, 2028.

nm:SB 507.title: Firearm Licenses & Transfers
nm:SB 507.summary: Changes the Concealed Handgun Carry Act: lets licensees carry any legally possessed handgun, cuts the minimum initial training course from 15 to six hours, drops the four-hour renewal and two-hour refresher courses, and sets rules for transferring out-of-state licenses.

nm:SB 510.title: Public Safety Changes
nm:SB 510.summary: Makes many criminal law changes: widens the human trafficking definition to include debt-based labor, adds penalties for drug trafficking that results in a death, creates a "stash house" crime, and changes pretrial release and competency evaluation procedures.

nm:SB 52.title: Public Office Travel Reimbursement
nm:SB 52.summary: Sets mileage reimbursement for public officers and employees, including legislators on interim committee travel, at the U.S. General Services Administration standard rate, replacing the IRS rate and the 88-cent airplane rate.

nm:SB 53.title: Prescribing Psychologist Psychotropics
nm:SB 53.summary: Adds prescribing psychologists with at least four years of independent experience prescribing psychotropic drugs to the definition of "independently licensed prescribing clinician," allowing them to supervise other prescribing psychologists.

nm:SB 55.title: Solar Market Income Tax Credit
nm:SB 55.summary: Raises the solar market development income tax credit from 10 to 30 percent of system costs and the per-taxpayer annual cap from $6,000 to $15,000, for systems bought and installed on or after March 1, 2026.

nm:SB 57.title: Medical Provider Patient Ipra Info
nm:SB 57.summary: Exempts from the Inspection of Public Records Act records containing personal identifying or sensitive information about the practice of public-body-employed medical providers who perform abortion-related services.

nm:SB 58.title: Extend Property Tax Exemption Period
nm:SB 58.summary: Extends the property tax exemption for metropolitan redevelopment project property acquired by a municipality from seven to up to fourteen years, with matching payment-in-lieu-of-tax periods, and raises the maximum for certain pre-1986 projects from ten to fourteen years.

nm:SB 59.title: Public Works Minimum Wage Definitions
nm:SB 59.summary: Adds off-site fabrication of heating, cooling, ventilation and exhaust ducts for public works projects to the project "site", extending the Public Works Minimum Wage Act to those workers.

nm:SB 6.title: Fostering Connections Pgm Eligibility
nm:SB 6.summary: Makes youth who were in state custody but not court-adjudicated, or under voluntary placement agreements, eligible for the Fostering Connections Program, which supports eligible young adults until age 22.

nm:SB 63.title: Retirement of State Flag
nm:SB 63.summary: Allows a no-longer-usable New Mexico state flag to be destroyed, preferably by burning, in a dignified ceremony, public or private, which may be directed by military personnel or a patriotic society.

nm:SB 64.title: Create Office of Special Education
nm:SB 64.summary: Creates an Office of Special Education within the Public Education Department, sets its duties, and moves dyslexia, private training center and residential treatment center laws into the Special Education Act.

nm:SB 66.title: Criminal Offender Employment Exemptions
nm:SB 66.summary: Exempts the Early Childhood Education and Care Department, Health Care Authority, Children, Youth and Families Department and Public Education Department from the Criminal Offender Employment Act, letting them set their own rules on criminal history for child care, caregiver and school jobs.

nm:SB 7.title: Storm Water Service as Municipal Utility
nm:SB 7.summary: Lets municipalities set up and run storm water systems as municipal utilities and charge reasonable fees to benefiting property owners, with a deposit required if the municipality chooses.

nm:SB 70.title: Add Racketeering Crimes
nm:SB 70.summary: Adds sexual exploitation of children, criminal sexual penetration and contact, dog fighting, cockfighting, bringing contraband into prisons and human trafficking to the offenses that count as racketeering.

nm:SB 72.title: Nonprofit Condo Assoc. Remote Business
nm:SB 72.summary: Allows nonprofit condominium associations and nonprofit corporations to hold meetings, vote and count quorum by simultaneous remote electronic means, and allows electronic meeting notice if the recipient agrees.

nm:SB 73.title: Require Bicycle Stops for Safety
nm:SB 73.summary: Lets bicyclists treat red lights as stop signs and stop signs as yield signs: proceed through a red light after stopping if safe, and pass a stop sign without stopping if no one is approaching. Takes effect July 1, 2025.

nm:SB 75.title: Educational Retirement Changes
nm:SB 75.summary: Changes the Educational Retirement Act: unclaimed member contributions go to the educational retirement fund, disabled members over 60 keep an annuity adjustment, allowed service must be paid for within 90 days, and member data may be shared with the Public Employees Retirement Board.

nm:SB 78.title: Certified Nurse Anesthetist Role
nm:SB 78.summary: Changes the standard of care for certified registered nurse anesthetists to national nurse anesthesia guidelines and allows them to work independently, without supervision, or in collaboration with other providers under facility policies.

nm:SB 8.title: Veterinary Medical Loan Repayment Pgm
nm:SB 8.summary: Creates the Veterinary Medical Loan Repayment Program, which repays education loans for food-animal veterinarians who work in designated underserved areas under contracts with the Higher Education Department, with selection criteria and a dedicated fund.

nm:SB 81.title: Nm Property Insurance Pgm. Assoc. Board
nm:SB 81.summary: Creates the New Mexico Property Insurance Program Association board, which establishes a state FAIR Plan for property insurance, submits a plan of operation to the Superintendent of Insurance, and reports annually.

nm:SB 82.title: Public School Capital Outlay Changes
nm:SB 82.summary: Extends through fiscal year 2027 the one-third reduction in local shares for some school districts and one-half for certain small districts in public school capital outlay, and removes some criteria for adjusting a district's local share.

nm:SB 85.title: Campaign Finance Changes
nm:SB 85.summary: Expands Campaign Reporting Act definitions of expenditures and donations, requires reporting of electronic communications and independent expenditures, changes reporting deadlines, and bars candidates from repaying their own interest-bearing loans with contributions.

nm:SB 88.title: Medicaid Trust Fund & State Supported Fund
nm:SB 88.summary: Directs general fund reversions above $110 million to the Medicaid trust fund until it reaches $2 billion, and allows trust fund money to support Medicaid if federal funding cuts would reduce coverage or benefits.

nm:SB 9.title: Pipeline Safety Act Violations Civil Penalty
nm:SB 9.summary: Changes daily and maximum civil penalties for gas and oil pipeline safety violations to match federal pipeline penalty levels, roughly doubling them.

nm:SB 92.title: Horse Racing & Jockey Insurance Fund
nm:SB 92.summary: Redirects the jockey and exercise rider insurance premium tax receipts from the general fund into a new fund and appropriates them to the Racing Commission to pay for that insurance.

nm:SB 96.title: Regulated Child Care Zoning Requirements
nm:SB 96.summary: Bars local zoning rules, fees and taxes that treat child care homes differently from private residences, allows licensed child care centers by right in commercial, mixed-use and multifamily zones, and limits homeowner association rules and fees that apply only to child care homes.

nm:SJM 1.title: Forest Restoration & Economic Development
nm:SJM 1.summary: Asks the energy and economic development departments to study and recommend ways to build a wood-products industry to speed forest restoration, reporting by September 1, 2025.

nm:SJM 2.title: Frontier Areas Task Force
nm:SJM 2.summary: Asks the governor to appoint a task force to study the needs of sparsely populated frontier areas and community-operated infrastructure networks for shared services, reporting by November 1, 2025.

nm:SJM 3.title: Higher Ed Bilingual Ed Faculties & Degree
nm:SJM 3.summary: Asks the Higher Education Department to work with four state universities to develop a joint bachelor's degree in elementary bilingual multicultural education and to review scholarship needs.

nm:SJR 1.title: School Election Timing, Ca
nm:SJR 1.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment to remove the requirement that school elections be held at different times from partisan elections, for voters to decide.

nm:SJR 11.title: School Elections Timing, Ca
nm:SJR 11.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment removing the requirement that school elections be held at different times from partisan elections, for voters to decide at the next general election.

nm:SJR 7.title: Santa Fe Property Exchange
nm:SJR 7.summary: Ratifies and approves the General Services Department's exchange of five state-owned parcels in Santa Fe's midtown campus for one city-owned parcel.

nm:SM 14.title: Mt Taylor Cultural & Environmental Integrity
nm:SM 14.summary: Expresses the Senate's opposition to uranium mining that threatens Mount Taylor's cultural property status, urges federal and state agencies to deny permits for uranium mining within its boundaries, and asks Congress to amend the 1872 General Mining Act.

nm:SM 16.title: Data on Parenting Students in Higher Ed.
nm:SM 16.summary: Asks the Higher Education Department to convene a task force to study and draft legislation for collecting data on parenting students in higher education.

nm:SM 17.title: Sexual Assault Exam Kit Task Force
nm:SM 17.summary: Asks the public safety secretary and the New Mexico Coalition of Sexual Assault Programs to convene a task force on sexual assault exam kits and report on progress clearing the backlog.

nm:SM 19.title: New Mexico Meat, Cheese & Produce in Schools
nm:SM 19.summary: Asks the state agriculture and public education departments to convene a work group to plan for half of the beef, cheese and milk served in public schools to come from, and be processed by, New Mexico producers, reporting by November 1, 2025.

nm:SM 2.title: Pediatric Palliative Care Medicaid Benefit
nm:SM 2.summary: Asks the Health Care Authority to develop a Medicaid state plan amendment creating a pediatric palliative care benefit that allows palliative and curative treatment at the same time.

nm:SM 20.title: Statewide Youth Violence Summit
nm:SM 20.summary: Asks the Department of Health to convene a statewide youth violence summit and develop a statewide approach to youth violence, including expanded community violence prevention and intervention services.

nm:SM 21.title: Study Overdose Prevention Centers
nm:SM 21.summary: Asks the Department of Health to study the efficacy of overdose prevention centers and the statutory and regulatory framework needed to create them, and to report to legislative committees by November 1, 2026.

nm:SM 22.title: Study Cyfd Funds & Domestic Violence
nm:SM 22.summary: Asks the Legislative Finance Committee to convene a working group to study state and federal funds the Children, Youth and Families Department administers for domestic violence services.

nm:SM 27.title: Impact of Radiation Exposure
nm:SM 27.summary: Acknowledges harm to New Mexico downwinders and uranium workers, recognizes the expanded federal Radiation Exposure Compensation Act, and asks state agencies to conduct outreach and education about it.

nm:SM 3.title: State Agency Insect Workshop
nm:SM 3.summary: Asks state agencies to participate in a workshop on insect identification, ecology, monitoring and management, and to share educational materials.

nm:SM 31.title: Pera Work Group
nm:SM 31.summary: Asks the Legislative Finance Committee to create a work group to study the Public Employees Retirement Association fund, including cost-of-living adjustments, solvency and unfunded liability.

nm:SM 6.title: Name Roswell Bypass for Nancy Lopez
nm:SM 6.summary: Asks the Department of Transportation to consider naming the U.S. 285 bypass in honor of Nancy Lopez.

nm:SM 9.title: Continue & Improve 520 Language
nm:SM 9.summary: Acknowledges 520-certified Native American language and culture instructors and asks the Legislative Education Study Committee to convene a working group on the 520 certificates and recommend improvements.

nv:AB1.title: Voids certain regulations relating to the development and disposal of land in the Fort Mohave Valley.
nv:AB1.summary: Voids the regulations on development and disposal of land in the Fort Mohave Valley adopted by the Colorado River Commission and requires the Legislative Counsel to remove them from the Nevada Administrative Code.

nv:AB10.title: Revises provisions relating to local improvement projects. (BDR 22-407)
nv:AB10.summary: Includes water and sewer systems owned by common-interest communities in neighborhood improvement projects, exempts them from dissolution of the improvement district, and limits the effect of owner protests against such projects.

nv:AB102.title: Revises provisions relating to emergency medical services. (BDR 40-345)
nv:AB102.summary: Lets district boards of health in health districts with a county of 100,000 to 700,000 residents vote to regulate emergency medical services, makes people 16 or older eligible for attendant licenses and EMT certification, and lets EMT trainees ride in ambulances without an attendant license.

nv:AB103.title: Revises provisions relating to housing authorities. (BDR 25-554)
nv:AB103.summary: Lets cities, towns and the county in a county of 100,000 to 700,000 people form a regional housing authority with seven commissioners, and lets housing authorities set rents to help meet their purposes.

nv:AB104.title: Revises provisions relating to water. (BDR 48-383)
nv:AB104.summary: Creates in statute the Nevada Conservation and Recreation Program, including a voluntary program to buy or accept donations of groundwater rights through 2035, which the State Engineer then retires from use, and revises other water provisions.

nv:AB105.title: Revises provisions governing firearms. (BDR 15-64)
nv:AB105.summary: Bars firearms in or within 100 feet of an entrance to an election site, except for officers, hired security, guns in vehicles and nearby private property. Violation is a gross misdemeanor; a category D felony if done to disrupt, interfere with or monitor the election.

nv:AB107.title: Revises provisions relating to foster care. (BDR 38-339)
nv:AB107.summary: Exempts marijuana possession convictions, where not for sale and more than 5 years old, from provisions barring a person from operating, working in or living in a foster home.

nv:AB108.title: Makes an appropriation to the Outdoor Education and Recreation Grant Program Account.
nv:AB108.summary: Appropriates $250,000 in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27 from the General Fund to the Outdoor Education and Recreation Grant Program Account.

nv:AB11.title: Revises provisions governing the Department of Taxation. (BDR 32-285)
nv:AB11.summary: Requires the Department of Taxation to submit its proposed budget and legislation to the Tax Commission at a January meeting in odd-numbered years instead of a June meeting in even-numbered years.

nv:AB110.title: Revises provisions relating to the designation of certain highways. (BDR 35-148)
nv:AB110.summary: Designates State Route 163 as the Colorado River Highway and the bridge linking it to Bullhead City, Arizona, as the Donald J. Laughlin Memorial Bridge, and requires the Department of Transportation to place markers.

nv:AB111.title: Revises provisions relating to certain traffic violations. (BDR 43-161)
nv:AB111.summary: Makes violating the rules against driving on a divided highway a misdemeanor instead of a civil infraction.

nv:AB112.title: Removes an exemption from provisions providing certain employees with the right to use sick leave to assist family members. (BDR 53-318)
nv:AB112.summary: Removes the exemption for employees under collective bargaining agreements from private employers' sick-leave rule for family members' medical needs, not applying during the current term of agreements entered before October 1, 2025.

nv:AB114.title: Revises provisions relating to county fair and recreation boards. (BDR 20-740)
nv:AB114.summary: Changes how Washoe County's fair and recreation board is chosen: all board members, not just three, appoint the six interest-based members, and the board elects its chair from among all its members.

nv:AB116.title: Revises provisions relating to food delivery service platform providers. (BDR 52-898)
nv:AB116.summary: Bars food delivery platforms from facilitating, and restaurants from accepting, online orders unless the restaurant holds any required local business license for its address, with civil penalties up to $100 per order for violating restaurants.

nv:AB117.title: Revises provisions relating to special license plates. (BDR 43-48)
nv:AB117.summary: Creates a Las Vegas Aces special license plate with a $10 replacement fee, exempts it from certain special-plate limits, and lets new vehicle dealers accept registration applications from people wanting special plates.

nv:AB119.title: Revises provisions relating to paramilitary activity. (BDR 36-191)
nv:AB119.summary: Lets the Attorney General investigate and seek injunctions against armed private paramilitary activity, and creates a civil action for damages by injured people. A private paramilitary organization is three or more people under a command structure functioning or training as a combat or security unit.

nv:AB12.title: Revises requirements for obtaining judicial review of a decision of the Board of Review concerning a claim for unemployment benefits. (BDR 53-309)
nv:AB12.summary: Requires strict compliance with the existing 45-day deadline to serve an unemployment-benefit judicial review petition on the Employment Security Division administrator, bars courts from excusing it, and makes missed service deprive the court of jurisdiction.

nv:AB121.title: Revises provisions governing landlords and tenants. (BDR 10-166)
nv:AB121.summary: Requires landlords to offer tenants at least one rent payment method meeting set requirements, caps online payment fees at the portal operator's own fee, limits prospective tenant fees, and lets tenants sue landlords for certain violations.

nv:AB123.title: Revises provisions relating to elections communications. (BDR 24-733)
nv:AB123.summary: Makes it a misdemeanor, and a gross misdemeanor for repeat offenses, to threaten bodily injury or property damage to a candidate or their family. Lets candidates report threats to the Secretary of State, who investigates and refers cases with reasonable suspicion to the Attorney General.

nv:AB125.title: Revises provisions relating to public bodies. (BDR 18-909)
nv:AB125.summary: Requires a schedule of public body meetings to be posted on the State's official website location used for meeting notices.

nv:AB128.title: Creates the Public Records Task Force.
nv:AB128.summary: Creates a Public Records Task Force to evaluate issues with public records requests and report recommendations to legislative committees ahead of the 2027 session.

nv:AB131.title: Provides an exemption from property taxation for accessory dwelling units rented or leased to certain tenants. (BDR 32-694)
nv:AB131.summary: Exempts from property tax an accessory dwelling unit rented to a Housing Choice Voucher tenant on a lease of 12 months or more, on the same parcel as the owner's primary residence, compliant with zoning and community rules; one unit per parcel.

nv:AB132.title: Revises provisions relating to water. (BDR 48-586)
nv:AB132.summary: Raises the size limits for wildlife water guzzlers exempt from water-appropriation rules to 40,000 gallons of capacity and a half mile of pipe, from 20,000 gallons and a quarter mile.

nv:AB133.title: Revises provisions governing public financial administration. (BDR 20-537)
nv:AB133.summary: Requires county treasurer offices to stay open until at least 5 p.m., and sets tax-delinquency notice and property reconveyance deadlines at the treasurer's close of business instead of 5 p.m.

nv:AB136.title: Revises provisions relating to animals. (BDR 50-168)
nv:AB136.summary: Requires businesses that sell public access to live animals to post a sign giving the local animal control phone number for reporting suspected cruelty, with an administrative penalty for failing to post it. Accredited zoos and aquariums are exempt.

nv:AB137.title: Revises requirements for the advertising of a sale of personal property to satisfy the lien of an owner of a facility for storage. (BDR 9-183)
nv:AB137.summary: Changes storage unit lien sale advertising to require newspaper notice once in the week before the sale, allows internet posting where no newspaper exists, and drops the requirement to describe the property.

nv:AB14.title: Revises provisions relating to certain public officers. (BDR 20-453)
nv:AB14.summary: Requires county commissioners, clerks, recorders, sheriffs, treasurers, assessors, district attorneys, public administrators, constables and Carson City supervisors to be registered voters in Nevada, with an exception for current officeholders.

nv:AB140.title: Revises provisions governing driver authorization cards. (BDR 43-200)
nv:AB140.summary: Changes driver authorization cards from a four-year expiration to one set by Department of Motor Vehicles regulations, which must match driver's license periods where federal law allows.

nv:AB142.title: Revises provisions relating to industrial insurance. (BDR 53-876)
nv:AB142.summary: Adds civilian employees of law enforcement agencies who respond to and investigate crime scenes to the first responders eligible for industrial insurance coverage of stress-related mental injuries, and defines law enforcement agency and public safety agency.

nv:AB144.title: Revises provisions relating to “Indigenous Peoples Day” in Nevada. (BDR 19-7)
nv:AB144.summary: Moves Indigenous Peoples Day from August 9 to the second Monday in October, and requires the Governor to issue an annual proclamation encouraging its observance.

nv:AB148.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-770)
nv:AB148.summary: Changes the mail-ballot distribution deadline for in-state active voters from 20 days before an election to between the fifth and fourth Monday before it, and requires sample ballots to be sent before that deadline.

nv:AB15.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicaid fraud. (BDR 18-446)
nv:AB15.summary: Lets the Attorney General's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit subpoena people to testify under oath and answer written interrogatories, and revises Medicaid false-claims lawsuit rules to match federal law.

nv:AB150.title: Revises provisions relating to the criminal justice system. (BDR 15-157)
nv:AB150.summary: Extends criminal threat, assault and battery penalties and address-confidentiality options to tribal judicial personnel, and adds public defenders and certain court personnel to the "officer" definition for enhanced assault and battery penalties.

nv:AB153.title: Revises provisions relating to the education of incarcerated persons. (BDR 16-234)
nv:AB153.summary: Requires Department of Corrections programming staff to inform offenders about financial planning and the FAFSA and offer help completing it, with annual reporting.

nv:AB155.title: Revises provisions relating to public employees. (BDR 23-612)
nv:AB155.summary: Adds the ratio of pupils per licensed teacher and per specialized instructional support staff to mandatory subjects of collective bargaining. A school district bound by a bargained ratio need not consider State Board of Education recommendations.

nv:AB156.title: Revises provisions governing the members of the board of trustees of school districts. (BDR 34-689)
nv:AB156.summary: Gives appointed trustees on school boards in districts over 75,000 pupils the same duties and rights as elected trustees, lets them take part in filling vacancies and serve as officers, and sets 12-year term limits, salary changes and work-session rules.

nv:AB160.title: Creates the Nevada-Ireland Trade Commission. (BDR 18-650)
nv:AB160.summary: Creates a nine-member Nevada-Ireland Trade Commission to study and recommend to the Board of Economic Development ways to advance trade, investment and exchanges with Ireland, and creates a state account to hold its grants and gifts.

nv:AB161.title: Makes revisions relating to hospice care. (BDR 40-656)
nv:AB161.summary: Gives hospice patients a right to required care, requires informed written consent for treatment, and requires notice on admission of how to file a complaint with the Division of Public and Behavioral Health.

nv:AB163.title: Enters into the Counseling Compact. (BDR 54-129)
nv:AB163.summary: Enters Nevada into the Counseling Compact, letting licensed professional counselors from member states practice in Nevada, and authorizes sharing information with the Compact's database.

nv:AB164.title: Revises provisions relating to the Account for Student Indemnification. (BDR 34-544)
nv:AB164.summary: Raises the Student Indemnification Account balance at which private postsecondary schools stop paying the $5 per-student quarterly fee from $250,000 to $750,000.
