nv:AB165.title: Revises provisions relating to outdoor education. (BDR 35-633)
nv:AB165.summary: Creates an Outdoor Education Council in the Division of Outdoor Recreation to set standards and award designations to schools with qualifying outdoor education programs and to name an Outdoor Educator of the Year, with a nonmonetary award.

nv:AB167.title: Revises provisions relating to the use of corrective room restriction. (BDR 5-769)
nv:AB167.summary: Requires the 24-hour review of a detained child held in corrective room restriction to be done by facility staff and to assess whether a mental health screening, evaluation or treatment referral is appropriate.

nv:AB168.title: Revises provisions relating to bicycles. (BDR 43-598)
nv:AB168.summary: Requires bicyclists to stop at stop signs and steady red lights, with exceptions to proceed when safe or cautiously, and makes a violation a civil infraction.

nv:AB169.title: Revises provisions relating to health insurance. (BDR 57-735)
nv:AB169.summary: Requires health insurance policies and health plans to cover speech-language pathology as treatment for stuttering for people under 26, and bars certain limits on that coverage.

nv:AB17.title: Revises provisions relating to writs of garnishment. (BDR 3-416)
nv:AB17.summary: Requires writs of garnishment naming the State of Nevada as garnishee to be served on the Division of Human Resource Management instead of the State Controller.

nv:AB171.title: Revises provisions relating to the State Quarantine Officer. (BDR 51-985)
nv:AB171.summary: Lets the State Quarantine Officer suspend cage-free egg sale requirements for up to 120 days per suspension, no more than twice a year, during an event disrupting the national egg supply.

nv:AB174.title: Revises provisions relating to telecommunication providers. (BDR 58-128)
nv:AB174.summary: Removes the exclusion of satellite voice service from the definition of alternative voice service, letting satellite providers count when a landline provider of last resort seeks relief from its service obligation.

nv:AB176.title: Revises provisions relating to contraception and family planning services. (BDR 40-177)
nv:AB176.summary: Creates the Right to Contraception and Family Planning Services Act, barring state and local limits that single out and substantially burden reproductive health care unless the government shows a compelling interest by the least restrictive means; exempts abortion laws and public schools; allows court claims.

nv:AB177.title: Makes various changes relating to audiology, fitting and dispensing hearing aids and speech-language pathology. (BDR 54-199)
nv:AB177.summary: Creates licenses for speech-language pathology assistants, revises the scope of practice for audiologists, hearing aid specialists and speech-language pathologists, raises maximum board fees, and removes the endorsement audiologists need to fit and dispense hearing aids.

nv:AB18.title: Revises provisions relating to the electronic filing of certain documents. (BDR 5-469)
nv:AB18.summary: Requires certain electronically filed court documents to carry the filer's electronic signature as defined in the Nevada Electronic Filing and Conversion Rules.

nv:AB183.title: Revises provisions relating to optometry. (BDR 54-151)
nv:AB183.summary: Expands the Board of Optometry from four to five members, sets procedures for summary license suspension, requires proof of passing the national optometry exam for licensure by endorsement, and revises the definition of pharmaceutical agent.

nv:AB184.title: Revises provisions relating to interscholastic activities. (BDR 34-186)
nv:AB184.summary: Bans athletic recruitment in school sports, makes recruited pupils ineligible, requires school classification changes and association policies to be adopted by regulation, and bars certain adverse actions against those who advocate for or against a policy.

nv:AB185.title: Revises provisions relating to child care. (BDR 10-187)
nv:AB185.summary: Bars homeowners' association boards and governing documents from prohibiting a unit owner from operating a licensed child care facility for 5 to 12 children, while allowing conditions consistent with child care licensing requirements. Excludes age-restricted communities.

nv:AB188.title: Revises provisions relating to the Public Employees' Benefits Program. (BDR 23-673)
nv:AB188.summary: Requires the Public Employees' Benefits Program board to report every even-numbered year on retirees' comparable insurance costs, and limits how it can cap or revert retiree health reimbursement arrangement balances for Medicare and TRICARE retirees.

nv:AB189.title: Revises provisions relating to notaries public. (BDR 19-879)
nv:AB189.summary: As introduced, defines oath and affirmation, treats them as equal in legal effect, and lets notaries administer either in writing, orally or by other equivalent means.

nv:AB19.title: Revises provisions relating to the Statewide Substance Use Response Working Group. (BDR 40-442)
nv:AB19.summary: Adds the Executive Director of the Department of Indigent Defense Services and four Attorney General appointees to the Statewide Substance Use Response Working Group, and requires the health department designee to come from its Division of Public and Behavioral Health.

nv:AB192.title: Makes various changes relating to real property. (BDR 10-971)
nv:AB192.summary: Enacts the Uniform Easement Relocation Act, letting owners seek court approval to relocate certain easements, and the Uniform Mortgage Modification Act.

nv:AB193.title: Revises provisions relating to certain victims of crime. (BDR 16-984)
nv:AB193.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to give domestic violence victims, on written request, a free copy of reports about the violence, with personal identifying information redacted as appropriate.

nv:AB194.title: Prohibits the release of certain balloons that are lighter than air under certain circumstances. (BDR 15-338)
nv:AB194.summary: Bans intentionally releasing balloons filled with lighter-than-air gas, with exceptions such as hot air balloons, certain research balloons and indoor releases, and allows civil penalties sought by the Attorney General or local attorneys.

nv:AB196.title: Revises provisions governing psychology. (BDR 54-164)
nv:AB196.summary: Lets the psychology board authorize licensed psychologists to delegate certain tests to unlicensed "psychometrists," bars complaints filed 3 or more years after the alleged act, and repeals firm registration with the board.

nv:AB197.title: Enacts provisions strengthening certain protections for certain activities under the First Amendment. (BDR 19-136)
nv:AB197.summary: Requires governments to keep confidential personal information identifying people as donors, members or volunteers of nonprofits, and bars them from requesting or releasing it, with exceptions.

nv:AB198.title: Establishes provisions relating to certain inflatable devices. (BDR 52-49)
nv:AB198.summary: Requires businesses that operate inflatable bounce houses and water slides to hold licenses and at least $1,000,000 in insurance or bond, keep inspection logbooks, and stop use when an inspection finds a hazard.

nv:AB2.title: Revises provisions relating to alcoholic beverages. (BDR 32-24)
nv:AB2.summary: Exempts holders of nonrestricted gaming licenses, and certain affiliates, from the rule requiring liquor retailers to pay wholesalers by electronic funds transfer, and applies the same exemption to some restricted licensees.

nv:AB20.title: Revises provisions relating to the Department of Motor Vehicles. (BDR 43-305)
nv:AB20.summary: Lets the DMV use individual symbols for different medical conditions on driver's licenses, and requires it to send insurance-verification requests and registration-suspension notices electronically to owners who choose electronic notice.

nv:AB201.title: Revises provisions relating to the sealing of certain records. (BDR 3-843)
nv:AB201.summary: Expands automatic sealing of eviction case court files, including when a landlord does not timely oppose a tenant's motion or an appeal ends in certain ways, and covers files from unjustified lockouts.

nv:AB202.title: Revises provisions relating to claims for dental care. (BDR 57-573)
nv:AB202.summary: Lets dentists, as well as physicians, make decisions denying coverage of recommended care, and extends complaint-resolution and external-review rights to people with dental-only coverage.

nv:AB204.title: Revises provisions relating to medical debt. (BDR 52-135)
nv:AB204.summary: Bars health care entities and collection agencies from using arrest, liens or foreclosure on real property that includes a primary residence, federal tax refund garnishment, or bank account seizure to collect medical debt. Delays extraordinary collection actions until 180 days after the first bill.

nv:AB205.title: Revises provisions governing sexual education. (BDR 34-597)
nv:AB205.summary: Changes parental consent for the school course on HIV, reproductive health and sexual responsibility from opt-in to opt-out, requiring a refusal form sent by four weeks after school starts or four weeks before the course begins, whichever is earlier.

nv:AB207.title: Revises provisions governing the submission of certain information to the Commissioner of Insurance relating to mental health parity and addiction equity. (BDR 57-853)
nv:AB207.summary: Requires insurers to file mental health parity compliance data through the national electronic filing system and makes the filings public records, except consumers' personal information and trade secrets, which stay confidential.

nv:AB209.title: Provides immunity from criminal liability for engaging in prostitution or solicitation for prostitution. (BDR 15-781)
nv:AB209.summary: Gives a person who engages in prostitution or solicitation immunity from criminal liability for it when they seek emergency or medical assistance and the evidence was obtained as a result.

nv:AB21.title: Revises provisions relating to unemployment compensation. (BDR 53-308)
nv:AB21.summary: Eliminates the Employment Security Division's annual September solvency calculations for the Unemployment Compensation Fund, and counts the first 180 days instead of 90 of next-year authorized spending when computing the yearly transfer from the administration fund.

nv:AB211.title: Revises provisions relating to substandard properties. (BDR 20-811)
nv:AB211.summary: Requires local governments to order repair of residential multifamily rental properties that substantially endanger residents, and lets courts declare them substandard, appoint receivers, and order owners to pay costs.

nv:AB212.title: Revises provisions relating to early childhood education.
nv:AB212.summary: Renames and extends the Virtual Early Childhood Family Engagement Pilot Program from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2027, requires annual reports from its nonprofit administrator, and makes an appropriation to continue it.

nv:AB213.title: Revises provisions governing public works projects. (BDR 28-816)
nv:AB213.summary: Requires workers doing custom fabrication on public works to be paid prevailing wages, and requires bidders using preferences on public works in counties of 100,000 or more to certify nonstandard materials will be custom fabricated in Nevada.

nv:AB215.title: Revises provisions relating to employment. (BDR 53-132)
nv:AB215.summary: Lowers the weekly work-hour cap for 14- and 15-year-olds from 48 to 40 hours, and bars work between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m. before a school day for unemancipated high school students aged 16 to 18, with exceptions.

nv:AB217.title: Revises provisions relating to law enforcement on school property. (BDR 34-201)
nv:AB217.summary: Bars school districts, public schools and their employees from letting federal immigration officials onto school grounds, or giving pupil records to federal, state or local immigration enforcement officers, without a court order or warrant. Knowing violations bring discipline first, then misdemeanor charges.

nv:AB220.title: Authorizes the issuance of identification cards by the Department of Health and Human Services to persons experiencing homelessness under certain circumstances. (BDR 38-671)
nv:AB220.summary: Authorizes the Department of Health and Human Services to issue identification cards to Nevada residents experiencing homelessness without another license or ID, sets application, name-change and expiration rules, and lets certain local governments accept the cards.

nv:AB221.title: Exempts certain offices of physicians and other health care facilities from certain permitting requirements relating to anesthesia and sedation. (BDR 40-672)
nv:AB221.summary: Exempts physician offices and other health care facilities from the state anesthesia/sedation permit when they only administer sedation to dental patients under a dentist permit, so dual-licensed physician-dentists need one permit instead of two.

nv:AB223.title: Revises provisions relating to the habitability of rental property. (BDR 10-684)
nv:AB223.summary: Lets tenants file a verified complaint for expedited relief when a landlord fails to fix habitability problems, and revises rental agreement content, rent payment rules, tenant remedies, and amounts recoverable for unlawful landlord acts or missing disclosures.

nv:AB224.title: Provides for the issuance of bonds to assist certain school districts in financing capital improvements.
nv:AB224.summary: Requires the State Board of Finance to issue up to $100,000,000 in general obligation bonds for the school capital improvements fund, with proceeds granted to school districts in counties with fewer than 15,000 residents.

nv:AB226.title: Revises provisions relating to economic development. (BDR 32-690)
nv:AB226.summary: Requires businesses applying for certain state transferable tax credits or tax abatements to certify they will collaborate with their community and submit a community benefits agreement within two years of approval.

nv:AB227.title: Revises provisions governing adoption. (BDR 11-928)
nv:AB227.summary: Rewrites and reorganizes Nevada's laws on agency, identified, close-family, confirmatory and readoption adoptions of children, revises adult adoption provisions, and directs the Division of Child and Family Services to adopt regulations.

nv:AB230.title: Enacts the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact. (BDR 54-568)
nv:AB230.summary: Enacts the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, letting audiologists and speech-language pathologists licensed in one member state practice in other member states, including by telehealth, if they meet licensing, notice, fee and reporting requirements.

nv:AB231.title: Requires certain service contracts to impose certain duties upon the provider of the service contract. (BDR 57-655)
nv:AB231.summary: Requires home warranty service contracts to obligate the provider to restore covered goods within 14 business days of notice, and air conditioners, furnaces and heaters within 5 business days, with a lodging per diem allowance if the provider misses the 5 days.

nv:AB232.title: Makes changes to the computation of credit for service for certain members of the Public Employees' Retirement System. (BDR 23-402)
nv:AB232.summary: Gives school district employees and higher-education professional staff who work under 12 months a year, in the public retirement system, a full year of service credit for 900 or more hours over at least 8 calendar months, replacing full-time work for the full year.

nv:AB234.title: Requires Medicaid coverage for screening for certain forms of cancer. (BDR 38-893)
nv:AB234.summary: Requires Nevada Medicaid to cover screening for lung, colorectal and prostate cancer.

nv:AB235.title: Revises provisions relating to health care providers. (BDR 20-844)
nv:AB235.summary: Lets reproductive health care providers, gender-affirming care providers, employees and volunteers of reproductive health facilities, and their spouses, domestic partners and minor children ask courts to keep their personal information in county records confidential, and ask for an alternate address on their driver’s license.

nv:AB236.title: Revises provisions governing the selection of members to certain state boards and councils performing duties related to education. (BDR 34-78)
nv:AB236.summary: Changes the Governor's appointment of teachers to the State Board of Education and two education councils to use nominee lists from the teacher organizations representing the most teachers in a large school district and in all other districts, instead of the Nevada State Education Association.

nv:AB237.title: Authorizes any county to create the office of registrar of voters. (BDR 20-363)
nv:AB237.summary: Lets any county create the office of registrar of voters, removing the current requirement that the county have a population of 100,000 or more.

nv:AB238.title: Enacts the Nevada Studio Infrastructure Jobs and Workforce Training Act.
nv:AB238.summary: Authorizes film tax credits for productions at the Summerlin Production Studios Project, raises the cap on other film credits from $10 million to $25 million a year from July 2028 to 2043, has Clark County create a district funding prekindergarten, and creates workforce training grants.

nv:AB239.title: Revises provisions relating to business entities. (BDR 7-669)
nv:AB239.summary: Revises Nevada corporation and LLC law, including reverse stock split votes, a new holding-company reorganization process, bench-trial provisions in articles of incorporation, and making dissent rights the exclusive remedy for stockholders who may dissent.

nv:AB241.title: Revises provisions relating to housing. (BDR 22-65)
nv:AB241.summary: Requires counties and cities to allow multifamily and mixed-use housing with residential use by right on commercially zoned land, but not industrial land, and voids conflicting local rules.

nv:AB244.title: Enacts prohibitions relating to the use of disposable foodware containers containing polystyrene foam by certain food dispensing establishments. (BDR 40-685)
nv:AB244.summary: Bans food dispensing establishments with 10 or more Nevada locations from using polystyrene foam disposable foodware starting October 1, 2025, with a civil penalty up to $100 a day, and bans all food dispensing establishments from using it starting January 1, 2029.

nv:AB245.title: Revises provisions relating to firearms. (BDR 15-648)
nv:AB245.summary: Makes it a gross misdemeanor for anyone under 21 to possess a semiautomatic shotgun or semiautomatic centerfire rifle, with exceptions (military, law enforcement, some range and hunting use); makes selling one to under-21s a felony; extends child-access and unsafe-storage offenses to under-21s.

nv:AB248.title: Ratifies the Physical Therapy Licensure Compact. (BDR 54-566)
nv:AB248.summary: Enters Nevada into the Physical Therapy Licensure Compact, letting physical therapists and assistants licensed in a member state practice in other member states if they meet the compact's requirements.

nv:AB249.title: Revises provisions relating to fiscal notes. (BDR 17-932)
nv:AB249.summary: Changes the fiscal statement on bill summaries from "Yes" to "May have Fiscal Impact", adds a State Highway Fund statement, and lets the Fiscal Analysis Division extend the local-government fiscal note deadline by up to 7 days.

nv:AB25.title: Revises provisions relating to offenders. (BDR 16-296)
nv:AB25.summary: Limits guaranteed annual pelvic exams and mammograms for incarcerated women to those over a set age or recommended by a provider, and lets notaries verify an inmate's identity by prison ID card or a signed declaration.

nv:AB250.title: Revises provisions relating to certain debt. (BDR 52-599)
nv:AB250.summary: Makes coerced debt, meaning consumer debt resulting from domestic violence, trafficking, abuse, fraud or similar conduct against the debtor, an affirmative defense in civil actions to collect a consumer debt.

nv:AB251.title: Revises provisions relating to the inspection of meat and poultry. (BDR 51-154)
nv:AB251.summary: Removes the fixed-facility requirement for custom meat and poultry processing establishments and requires regulations letting them slaughter certain animals commercially for intrastate sale, and letting mobile processing units do so for interstate or intrastate sale.

nv:AB256.title: Directs the Legislative Commission to appoint a Regional Rail Transit Advisory Working Group to conduct an interim study relating to regional rail transit.
nv:AB256.summary: Directs the Legislative Commission to appoint a working group to study regional rail transit across Nevada and submit a plan and report to a legislative interim committee.

nv:AB258.title: Revises provisions relating to brokerage agreements. (BDR 54-741)
nv:AB258.summary: Requires real estate brokerage agreements to be in writing by removing oral contracts from the legal definition of a brokerage agreement.

nv:AB259.title: Establishes provisions governing prescription drugs. (BDR 40-165)
nv:AB259.summary: Bars buying or seeking reimbursement for a drug in Nevada at a price above the federal Medicare maximum fair price. Certain federally regulated health coverage providers are exempt but may elect to be covered.

nv:AB26.title: Revises provisions relating to dams. (BDR 48-261)
nv:AB26.summary: Exempts the State Engineer and assistants from liability for damages from certain dam failures tied to inspections or enforcement, and applies dam plan-approval and permit rules to reconstruction or alteration of dams.

nv:AB262.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-362)
nv:AB262.summary: Lets election trainees and election, voting and counting board officers choose to work unpaid, and removes the bars on voter registration agencies employing, and county clerks appointing as field registrars, people with theft or fraud felony convictions.

nv:AB263.title: Revises provisions relating to homelessness. (BDR 20-96)
nv:AB263.summary: Requires counties of 700,000 or more people (currently Clark) to notify the Department of Transportation before cleaning up a homeless encampment near a state right-of-way, and lets the Department consult outreach teams and join the clean-up.

nv:AB266.title: Makes revisions relating to breastfeeding. (BDR 40-595)
nv:AB266.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to post a Medicaid breastfeeding coverage fact sheet and a list of local lactation services, and to run a lactation education program. Bars public accommodations from denying service because a person is breastfeeding.

nv:AB269.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 18-618)
nv:AB269.summary: Adds speech-language pathologists, physical therapists, marriage and family therapists, drug counselors, behavior analysts, problem gambling counselors and public health professionals to the student loan repayment program for providers in underserved communities; extends eligible areas to adjacent census tracts.

nv:AB270.title: Revises provisions relating to architects, professional engineers and land surveyors. (BDR 54-773)
nv:AB270.summary: Removes the requirement that engineer and land surveyor applicants pass or waive the fundamentals exam before the principles and practices exam, and cuts the experience needed to waive the fundamentals exam from 15 to 10 years.

nv:AB277.title: Revises provisions relating to the confidentiality of information relating to the tax on the net proceeds of minerals in this State. (BDR 32-616)
nv:AB277.summary: Allows the Department of Taxation to disclose its otherwise confidential records related to computing gross yield and net proceeds of mineral extraction.

nv:AB278.title: Designates the month of July as Muslim American Heritage Month. (BDR 19-924)
nv:AB278.summary: Designates July each year as Muslim American Heritage Month in Nevada and requires the Governor to issue an annual proclamation encouraging its observance.

nv:AB28.title: Revises provisions related to transportation. (BDR 22-463)
nv:AB28.summary: Extends to December 31, 2028 the deadlines for regional transportation commissions to recommend, and county commissioners to put to voters, an added retail sales tax for transportation projects.

nv:AB280.title: Revises provisions relating to housing. (BDR 10-337)
nv:AB280.summary: Requires landlords to return certain application fees, bars application fees for minors in a household, requires fee and tenant-rights appendices in rental agreements, and limits rent increases to 5% through 2026 for existing tenants aged 62 or older or on Social Security.

nv:AB281.title: Revises provisions relating to the state militia. (BDR 36-398)
nv:AB281.summary: Clarifies that Nevada militia members on state active duty are treated as on duty 24 hours a day for each day of that duty for industrial insurance purposes.

nv:AB282.title: Revises provisions relating to billing for health care. (BDR 40-785)
nv:AB282.summary: Requires medical facilities and providers who receive notice of a medical bill error to review it and refund overpayments, allows discipline for noncompliance, and directs the Consumer Health Advocate to help patients with billing errors.

nv:AB283.title: Revises provisions governing certain actions and proceedings relating to real property. (BDR 3-819)
nv:AB283.summary: As introduced, replaces the summary eviction procedures for non-commercial tenants: a landlord applies by affidavit of complaint and serves the tenant, who must answer within 7 judicial days, instead of the tenant filing an affidavit to contest.

nv:AB284.title: Requires the Director of the Department of Health and Human Services to seek to establish certain rates of reimbursement under Medicaid for certain devices to treat epilepsy.
nv:AB284.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to ask federal approval for Medicaid reimbursement of at least 82 percent of cost for vagus nerve stimulation devices for epilepsy and replacement parts, separate from implantation costs, and makes an appropriation.

nv:AB286.title: Provides for a pilot program to assess the competency of applicants for a license to teach through alternative assessment methods. (BDR 34-836)
nv:AB286.summary: Lets Nevada higher education institutions run a pilot program, selecting up to 100 participants a year, assessing teaching-license applicants through alternative methods; completers are exempt from certain competency tests. The pilot expires July 1, 2029.

nv:AB289.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-320)
nv:AB289.summary: Authorizes the Board of Regents to establish a course of study in financial literacy in the Nevada System of Higher Education.

nv:AB29.title: Revises provisions relating to motor vehicle fuel. (BDR 51-271)
nv:AB29.summary: Requires fuel pumps to display specified information, sets labeling rules for ethanol flex fuel and biodiesel, requires price changes on signs and pumps in set order, and changes the diesel tax-exclusion wording size.

nv:AB291.title: Revises provisions relating to records of criminal history. (BDR 14-676)
nv:AB291.summary: Bars courts from considering a proceeding whose records were sealed when deciding whether to seal records of a conviction for another offense.

nv:AB296.title: Revises various provisions relating to motor vehicles. (BDR 43-231)
nv:AB296.summary: Requires the DMV, if it offers online registration, to contract with a licensed lender to offer installment loans for registration fees and taxes, with charges capped at 15 percent of the amount financed and no loans under $250. Also allows digital license plates.

nv:AB299.title: Revises provisions relating to prostitution. (BDR 15-1080)
nv:AB299.summary: Requires arrest on probable cause of customers engaging in or soliciting prostitution outside licensed brothels, raises the minimum first-offense fine to $800 and the civil penalty to $600, and allows sealing records two years after dismissal.

nv:AB3.title: Revises provisions relating to public office. (BDR 24-21)
nv:AB3.summary: Lets public officers ask that their personal information in certain government records be kept confidential, lets them request an alternate address on their driver's license, and allows campaign funds to pay for personal security.

nv:AB30.title: Revises provisions relating to records of defendants who have been found incompetent. (BDR 14-293)
nv:AB30.summary: Lets the state behavioral health administrator request records from local detention facilities, as already allowed for state prisons, to help evaluate and treat defendants found incompetent.

nv:AB301.title: Revises provisions relating to community development. (BDR 25-1047)
nv:AB301.summary: As passed by the Senate, raises the maximum annual pay for board members of general improvement districts with sewer, garbage and water powers from $9,000 to $14,500.

nv:AB302.title: Establishes provisions relating to facility dogs. (BDR 4-489)
nv:AB302.summary: Lets a court allow a minor or vulnerable witness to use a facility dog during testimony after making required findings, and allows the dog into courthouses and related county or city buildings, with exclusion allowed for misconduct.

nv:AB303.title: Revises provisions governing public works. (BDR 28-866)
nv:AB303.summary: Exempts contracts for privately owned broadband, telecommunication or fiber optic services from public works laws, and requires contractors on certain broadband public works to submit worker records to the Nevada State Infrastructure Bank board.

nv:AB304.title: Establishing certain notification and reporting requirements concerning pilot programs that research transcranial magnetic stimulation or electromagnetic brain pulse treatment.
nv:AB304.summary: Requires practitioners or entities running pilot programs on transcranial magnetic stimulation or electromagnetic brain pulse treatment to notify the Legislative Counsel Bureau before starting, report quarterly, and file a final report.

nv:AB305.title: Limits the amount a provider of health care may charge for filling out certain forms associated with certain leaves of absence. (BDR 54-665)
nv:AB305.summary: Bars health care providers from charging more than $30 to complete a certification form for federal family and medical leave, adjusted yearly for inflation by the Department of Health and Human Services.

nv:AB306.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-569)
nv:AB306.summary: Requires county clerks, between the end of early voting and general election day, to open at least 10 mail ballot drop box locations in counties of 700,000 or more and 5 in counties of 100,000 to 700,000, each open at least 7 hours daily.

nv:AB309.title: Revises provisions relating to certain orders for protection against domestic violence. (BDR 3-885)
nv:AB309.summary: Requires temporary domestic violence protection orders served on in-custody respondents to explain they may contest an extended order by written response, and lets the court hold the hearing and grant the order without them if they do not respond.

nv:AB315.title: Requires applications to participate in Medicaid as a provider to be accompanied by a certain verification. (BDR 38-659)
nv:AB315.summary: Requires a Medicaid provider application to include verification of the signer's identity and signature, by notarized oath or affirmation or an electronic identity verification system.

nv:AB319.title: Makes revisions relating to providers of health care. (BDR 54-791)
nv:AB319.summary: Changes Nevada medical licensing: treats doctors trained in the UK, Australia, New Zealand and equivalent countries like U.S. or Canadian graduates, revises exam and postgraduate training rules, raises a false-application fine, and requires licensees to keep an email address on file.

nv:AB320.title: Revises provisions related to the administration of justice. (BDR 1-810)
nv:AB320.summary: Bars courts from penalizing a defendant who is denied courtroom entry solely for lacking formal attire, and lets the Division of Parole and Probation create a pilot program for parolee and probationer job training and employment.

nv:AB321.title: Revises provisions relating to offenders. (BDR 16-1015)
nv:AB321.summary: Allows the Department of Corrections to create a forestry-training transitional housing program for certain minimum-security offenders denied parole only for lack of housing, and requires a program to hire former conservation camp firefighters in the Division of Forestry.

nv:AB325.title: Revises provisions relating to artificial intelligence. (BDR 36-393)
nv:AB325.summary: Requires emergency management plans to ensure final emergency response and resource decisions are not made by artificial intelligence, and bars public utilities from deciding disaster service reductions or shutdowns based solely on AI.

nv:AB326.title: Revises provisions relating to the designation of hospitals as centers for the treatment of trauma. (BDR 40-153)
nv:AB326.summary: Bars a trauma center from claiming a specific level of trauma care unless the state has designated it at that level, and authorizes the Board of Health to set designation levels, including level IV for certain critical access hospitals.

nv:AB329.title: Revises provisions relating to victims of crime. (BDR 16-1050)
nv:AB329.summary: Sets a 60-month filing deadline for crime victim compensation applications, or 60 months after age 21 for those injured as minors, and lets the Director waive the deadline for good cause without requiring a police report.

nv:AB331.title: Makes an appropriation to the Division of Public and Behavioral Health of the Department of Health and Human Services for a grant program to expand the biennial survey administered pursuant to the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System developed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention of the United States Department of Health and Human Services.
nv:AB331.summary: Appropriates $220,000 in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27 to the Division of Public and Behavioral Health for grants to higher-education institutions to expand the biennial Youth Risk Behavior Survey.

nv:AB333.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 49-833)
nv:AB333.summary: Ends the state's lease of land to Washoe County, requires a new lease of the county's building complex, and has the state Department of Agriculture run the remaining land as the Nevada State Fairgrounds.

nv:AB334.title: Revises provisions relating to oral health. (BDR 54-800)
nv:AB334.summary: Bars the Board of Dental Examiners from requiring dental hygienists applying by endorsement to have practiced in another state for a set period, voiding the current 5-year rule.

nv:AB335.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-837)
nv:AB335.summary: Requires each school district to designate an administrator for English learner support and requires school improvement plans to include methods for closing achievement gaps and, in schools with many English learners, goals for them.

nv:AB336.title: Revises provisions relating to state purchasing. (BDR 27-458)
nv:AB336.summary: Allows the 5 percent Nevada-business and veteran-owned-business preferences in state purchasing to be combined and eliminates the inverse preference imposed on out-of-state bidders from states that favor their own businesses.

nv:AB342.title: Designates the month of March as “Women Veterans History Month.” (BDR 19-459)
nv:AB342.summary: Designates March each year as Women Veterans History Month in Nevada and requires the Governor to issue an annual proclamation encouraging its observance.

nv:AB343.title: Makes revisions relating to health care. (BDR 40-988)
nv:AB343.summary: Requires hospitals to publish standard charge and shoppable service price lists, bars collecting medical debt that accrued while out of compliance, and requires health care entities to give certain information before collecting medical debt.

nv:AB344.title: Revises provisions relating to the judiciary. (BDR 38-155)
nv:AB344.summary: Replaces the title "master" with "judicial officer" for court-appointed officials in family, juvenile and other proceedings, and creates a process to transfer child welfare cases between Nevada courts requiring a joint hearing and a finding that transfer is in the child's best interests.

nv:AB345.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-97)
nv:AB345.summary: Requires the Board of Regents to post a public data dashboard by September 1, 2026 on high school graduates entering Nevada higher education, remedial enrollment and time to graduation, and to adopt a policy on low-cost course materials and study student food insecurity.

nv:AB346.title: Establishes provisions governing the prescribing, dispensing and administering of medication designed to end the life of a patient. (BDR 40-600)
nv:AB346.summary: Lets an adult patient diagnosed as terminally ill by two practitioners request a prescription for medication to end their own life, after two verbal requests and one signed written request, and sets requirements for prescribing it.

nv:AB347.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial administration. (BDR 31-936)
nv:AB347.summary: Raises from $200,000 to $500,000 the value of each gift or nongovernmental grant that a state agency may accept.

nv:AB348.title: Revises provisions relating to the Legislature. (BDR 17-931)
nv:AB348.summary: Sets member terms for the Interim Retirement and Benefits Committee, adds review of the Legislators' Retirement System, and eliminates the required biennial budget stress test by the Fiscal Analysis Division.

nv:AB35.title: Revises provisions relating to pornography involving minors. (BDR 15-448)
nv:AB35.summary: Replaces "child pornography" and related terms in the Nevada Revised Statutes with "child sexual abuse material," and sets that as the preferred term in statutes and the administrative code.

nv:AB350.title: Revises provisions relating to cemeteries. (BDR 40-874)
nv:AB350.summary: Requires a cemetery authority to get a district court order before disinterring remains from all or part of a cemetery, and ends county commissioners' rule-making over cemetery upkeep, setting owner duties directly.

nv:AB351.title: Revises provisions relating to the jurisdiction of the juvenile court over certain offenses. (BDR 5-494)
nv:AB351.summary: Gives juvenile court limited jurisdiction over people 21 or older charged for certain acts committed at ages 13 to 17, with a hearing on dismissal or transfer to district court, applying to offenses on or after October 1, 2013.

nv:AB352.title: Revises provisions relating to businesses. (BDR 51-890)
nv:AB352.summary: Creates a Department of Agriculture license for cottage cosmetics operations, meaning home-based makers selling cosmetics to individuals with gross sales of $100,000 or less per year, and exempts them from Commissioner of Food and Drugs licensing and inspection.

nv:AB354.title: Revises provisions relating to the Nevada State Board on Geographic Names. (BDR 26-718)
nv:AB354.summary: Changes the Nevada State Board on Geographic Names by replacing the Historical Society seat with a Division of Museums and History seat and making federal land-agency representatives nonvoting members.

nv:AB355.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-937)
nv:AB355.summary: Carries unspent balances in two school capital improvement funds forward instead of reverting to the General Fund, and allows rural-district grants matching gifts, grants or interest for capital projects on tribal land.

nv:AB356.title: Revises provisions relating to collective bargaining agreements. (BDR 23-935)
nv:AB356.summary: Requires the Governor to include in the proposed state budget, where practicable, money for pay terms agreed in collective bargaining agreements, and to report to the Legislature the reason when it is impracticable.

nv:AB36.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicaid. (BDR 38-291)
nv:AB36.summary: Puts into statute the 90-day deadline for Medicaid providers to request a hearing on an action against them, with an exception for extenuating circumstances, and directs regulations defining appealable actions and those circumstances.

nv:AB360.title: Revises provisions relating to testing for sexually transmitted diseases. (BDR 40-745)
nv:AB360.summary: Requires physician assistants and advanced practice nurses to screen pregnant patients for syphilis, and requires certain facilities to use rapid point-of-care tests for unscreened pregnant women, document refusals and adopt testing policies.

nv:AB361.title: Revises provisions relating to public mass transportation. (BDR 22-1066)
nv:AB361.summary: Requires regional transportation commissions in counties of 100,000 or more to install safety infrastructure such as barriers and panic buttons for transit operators, and post signs about penalties for crimes against operators.

nv:AB365.title: Eliminates provisions requiring the University of Nevada, Reno, School of Medicine to establish a program relating to the medical use of cannabis. (BDR 19-758)
nv:AB365.summary: Repeals the requirement that the University of Nevada, Reno, School of Medicine run a program evaluating and researching medical use of cannabis.

nv:AB366.title: Revises provisions relating to housing. (BDR 25-814)
nv:AB366.summary: Revises the Nevada Supportive Housing Development Fund and makes an appropriation to it, and requires the Governor to explain in the executive budget if no money is requested for the supportive housing grant program.

nv:AB367.title: Makes various changes related to language access in elections. (BDR 24-364)
nv:AB367.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to post voting materials and election information online in certain languages, run a toll-free language interpretation line, and employ a language access coordinator.

nv:AB368.title: Revises provisions governing electronic communication devices in locations where certain services are provided. (BDR 40-878)
nv:AB368.summary: Extends the right to install an electronic communication device in a patient's room, now limited to skilled nursing facilities, to residents of assisted living and other listed care facilities, under the same conditions.

nv:AB369.title: Revises provisions governing certain orders for protection against domestic violence. (BDR 3-824)
nv:AB369.summary: Lets police rely on a paper or digital copy of an out-of-state domestic violence protection order, or the respondent's own statement, and sets a notice-and-compliance process when service of the order cannot be confirmed.

nv:AB37.title: Revises provisions related to housing. (BDR 25-257)
nv:AB37.summary: Renames the Housing Advocate the Housing Liaison, requires an annual report on the low-income housing database, caps database costs paid from the affordable housing account at 6 percent of yearly deposits instead of $175,000, and adds affordable-housing income tiers.

nv:AB375.title: Revises provisions relating to intoxicating liquor. (BDR 32-1049)
nv:AB375.summary: Lets counties and cities authorize restaurants licensed to serve alcohol to sell sealed alcoholic drinks for off-premises consumption and deliver them, directly or through a delivery service. Requires the Department of Taxation to set a surcharge of up to 50 cents per such sale.

nv:AB376.title: Revises provisions relating to insurance. (BDR 57-1009)
nv:AB376.summary: Creates a four-year program letting insurers test property insurance products with exemptions from insurance rules, allows flex-rated property insurance rate filings, and revises wildfire coverage, reciprocal insurer, captive insurer and common-interest community insurance rules.

nv:AB377.title: Revises provisions relating to real property. (BDR 32-923)
nv:AB377.summary: Requires the property transfer declaration-of-value form to let owners claim the primary-residence or qualifying rental property tax abatement, and lets owners claim these abatements on that form.

nv:AB38.title: Revises various provisions relating to housing. (BDR 43-521)
nv:AB38.summary: Revises state regulation of manufactured and mobile homes, factory-built housing and commercial coaches, changes landlord disclosures and lot-maintenance rules in manufactured home parks, and requires buyers of mobile home parks to notify the Housing Division.

nv:AB380.title: Revises provisions relating to mobile crisis teams. (BDR 39-1062)
nv:AB380.summary: As introduced, removes location and sponsor requirements for mobile crisis teams and requires each team to include a behavioral health professional plus a law enforcement officer, emergency medical provider or person with behavioral health expertise.

nv:AB381.title: Revises provisions related to animals. (BDR 50-793)
nv:AB381.summary: Lets officers humanely destroy an animal treated cruelly on a court order or veterinary recommendation, ends court-ordered auctions of such animals, removes the agricultural-land exemption from seizure rules, and raises some animal cruelty penalties to category B felonies.

nv:AB383.title: Establishes provisions relating to programs of high-impact tutoring. (BDR 34-767)
nv:AB383.summary: Allows the State Board of Education to set criteria for vendors providing high-impact tutoring to schools, covering tutoring frequency, pupil selection, methods, tutor qualifications, materials, progress data and pupil data privacy.

nv:AB384.title: Requires the Chair of the Juvenile Justice Oversight Commission to solicit input regarding certain subjects relating to juvenile justice. (BDR 5-1053)
nv:AB384.summary: Requires the chair of the Juvenile Justice Oversight Commission to gather input on juvenile justice topics and report yearly to the Legislature on actions taken, findings and recommendations.

nv:AB387.title: Revises provisions governing guardianship of minors. (BDR 13-869)
nv:AB387.summary: Changes minor guardianship procedures: who must be served and how, required petition contents, when a preliminary care plan and budget are needed, and appointment of attorneys for minors through established legal service programs.

nv:AB388.title: Revises provisions relating to employment. (BDR 23-1027)
nv:AB388.summary: Raises paid family leave for state executive-branch workers from 8 to 12 weeks, eligible after 90 days instead of 12 months, with wage-based pay. Also requires private and local-government employers with 50 or more employees to provide 12 weeks of paid family leave.

nv:AB39.title: Revises provisions governing charter schools. (BDR 34-259)
nv:AB39.summary: Defines the Authority's nine appointed members as voting members who must be at least 21, limits meeting calls and quorum to voting members, and requires a charter school teacher or administrator member's school to be in good standing under its charter.

nv:AB391.title: Revises provisions governing annual reports of accountability of public schools. (BDR 34-1074)
nv:AB391.summary: Requires school districts, charter school sponsors and the State Board of Education to include in annual accountability reports the achievement of students with more than 10 absences before testing, reported by student group.

nv:AB392.title: Revises provisions relating to interlocal agreements and contracts with tribal governments. (BDR 22-1059)
nv:AB392.summary: Lets a county government negotiate with tribal governments on cooperative agreements, which must be conditional interlocal agreements that do not require waiving tribal sovereign immunity and that the county may end on 90 days' notice in certain cases.

nv:AB394.title: Authorizes the Board of Regents of the University of Nevada to require certain institutions to adopt emergency response plans related to opioid overdoses. (BDR 34-95)
nv:AB394.summary: Authorizes the Board of Regents to require Nevada System of Higher Education institutions to adopt opioid overdose response plans covering education and opioid antagonist distribution, and bars plans that require training to obtain or administer an antagonist.

nv:AB396.title: Revises provisions relating to housing. (BDR 22-232)
nv:AB396.summary: Requires counties of 100,000 or more and cities of 60,000 or more to adopt ordinances letting owners add accessory dwelling units, allows them on any residentially zoned parcel if none is adopted by January 1, 2026, and changes common-interest community rules.

nv:AB397.title: Revises provisions relating to higher education. (BDR 34-653)
nv:AB397.summary: Changes tuition-waiver rules: requires FAFSA or an alternative aid form and satisfactory academic progress instead of a GPA minimum, requires waivers for qualifying unaccompanied homeless youth, revises Native American student eligibility, and repeals a natural-materials analysis requirement.

nv:AB398.title: Revises provisions governing compensation for certain employees of public schools. (BDR 34-189)
nv:AB398.summary: Requires the Department of Education, with appropriated money, to award school districts extra pay for hard-to-fill positions such as teachers at certain Title I schools or in shortage subjects; appropriates $45 million in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27; requires biennial district reports.

nv:AB4.title: Revises provisions relating to public safety. (BDR 15-31)
nv:AB4.summary: Changes criminal law on assault, battery, stalking, child sexual abuse material, domestic violence and DUI, adds theft-related property damage offenses, and changes juvenile justice, record sealing, pretrial release and opioid use disorder provisions.

nv:AB40.title: Revises various provisions relating to environmental hazards. (BDR 46-265)
nv:AB40.summary: Lets the Division of Environmental Protection issue orders for mining reclamation violations and lien property of mining permit holders and solid waste facility operators, requires permits and financial-responsibility rules for solid waste facilities, and changes mining permit and hazardous waste rules.

nv:AB402.title: Creates a pilot program authorizing the installation and use of automated traffic enforcement systems in temporary traffic control zones. (BDR 43-184)
nv:AB402.summary: Creates a pilot program letting transportation agencies install automated speed cameras in temporary traffic control zones, with a public information campaign first, officer review before any civil citation, and limits on how image data is stored and shared.

nv:AB404.title: Revises provisions relating to alcoholic beverages. (BDR 52-651)
nv:AB404.summary: Lets brew pub operators sell other alcoholic beverages bought from licensed wholesalers and at up to two retail liquor stores they control, with a 1,000-foot distance from gaming establishments for new licenses.

nv:AB405.title: Revises provisions relating to agriculture.
nv:AB405.summary: Directs the Council on Food Security to study food insecurity in Nevada during the 2025-2026 interim and develop strategies to coordinate statewide efforts to address it.

nv:AB406.title: Makes various changes relating to health. (BDR 34-674)
nv:AB406.summary: Bars public schools from using artificial intelligence for school counselor, psychologist or social worker mental health duties, and bars AI providers from offering systems programmed to provide mental health care or implying they are qualified to, with exceptions.

nv:AB407.title: Enacts provisions relating to the repair of certain devices. (BDR 52-50)
nv:AB407.summary: Requires manufacturers of powered and manual wheelchairs, mobility scooters and similar devices to provide independent repairers and owners with documentation, parts and tools on fair and reasonable terms, and bars retaliation against authorized repairers.

nv:AB409.title: Revises provisions relating to special license plates. (BDR 43-1058)
nv:AB409.summary: Requires veterans' outreach special plates for Space Force veterans and their spouses, parents and children, creates special plates for recipients of the Air Force Cross, Coast Guard Cross, Distinguished Service Cross or Navy Cross, and lets personalized plates combine with certain military special plates.

nv:AB41.title: Revises provisions relating to the state militia. (BDR 36-267)
nv:AB41.summary: Lets the Adjutant General appoint a Deputy Adjutant General from the Army or Air National Guard in the unclassified service, and removes the Chief of Staff for Army from unclassified service.

nv:AB411.title: Revises provisions relating to prescription drugs. (BDR 54-1100)
nv:AB411.summary: As introduced, requires the label on a mifepristone or misoprostol prescription (or generic) to show the prescribing health care practice's name instead of the practitioner's name, when the prescribing practitioner requests it.

nv:AB414.title: Revises provisions relating to occupational safety and health. (BDR 53-666)
nv:AB414.summary: Requires employers with more than 15 workers at a large facility (10,000+ square feet, exposed to outdoor elements most of each shift) to include in their written safety program measures to reduce worker exposure to greenhouse gases, other gases and poor air quality.

nv:AB415.title: Revises provisions governing the towing of motor vehicles. (BDR 43-821)
nv:AB415.summary: Raises the scrap-value limit for vehicle junk certificates from $200 to $500, and lets a notice affixed to an abandoned, unregistered junk-appraised vehicle give the owner 7 days to remove it, with a right to request an expedited justice court hearing.

nv:AB416.title: Revises provisions concerning access to certain library materials. (BDR 34-925)
nv:AB416.summary: Bars school boards, charter schools and staff from removing, hiding, labeling or defacing school library materials to limit pupil access, with similar rules for public libraries; lets a parent seek court removal of obscene material; creates felonies for coercion or retaliatory release of personal information.

nv:AB417.title: Revises provisions relating to public safety. (BDR 43-647)
nv:AB417.summary: Requires officers investigating illegal speed contests or trick driving to inspect a vehicle they have reasonable cause to believe violates equipment or safety rules, allows citing the owner, and has courts order registration cancelled after impoundment unless the owner passes an inspection.

nv:AB418.title: Revises provisions relating to animals. (BDR 20-849)
nv:AB418.summary: Requires each county and city to adopt an ordinance requiring owners or operators of kennels, pet rescues and pet businesses to complete a pet-handling training course and renew it every two years.

nv:AB42.title: Revises provisions governing the adoption of regulations for the administration of certain programs of public assistance. (BDR 38-289)
nv:AB42.summary: Lets the Medicaid administrator adopt, change or repeal regulations or policies on 3 business days' notice instead of 30 when required for legal compliance or expanding benefits, and allows retroactive rules when necessary for compliance.

nv:AB420.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-538)
nv:AB420.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools that use school police to publish an annual report on officers' use of force, starting by the 2026-2027 school year.

nv:AB422.title: Revises provisions relating to the Civil Air Patrol. (BDR 36-190)
nv:AB422.summary: Gives employees who volunteer with the Nevada Wing of the Civil Air Patrol job-protected leave, which employers may treat as unpaid, of up to 10 workdays per federal fiscal year for emergency training and 30 for missions; allows suits for lost wages and benefits.

nv:AB426.title: Revises provisions relating to the organization of large school districts. (BDR 34-1048)
nv:AB426.summary: Changes local school precinct rules in large districts (currently Clark County): principals must email budgets to organizational teams 3 days before approval votes, give an itemized expenditure report, and send agendas to parents; principals cannot be elected team members in other roles.

nv:AB427.title: Revises provisions relating to public financial administration. (BDR 31-739)
nv:AB427.summary: Changes eligibility for investments by the State Treasurer's venture capital corporation from specified industries to those consistent with the State Plan for Economic Development, limited to businesses seeking early- or middle-stage investment.

nv:AB428.title: Requires certain health plans to include coverage for fertility preservation services. (BDR 57-915)
nv:AB428.summary: Requires public and private health plans, including Medicaid, to cover medically necessary fertility preservation services for insureds diagnosed with breast or ovarian cancer when the cancer or its treatment may cause infertility. Religiously affiliated insurers may opt out with notice.

nv:AB429.title: Revises provisions relating to natural resources. (BDR 10-679)
nv:AB429.summary: Allows any person, including a state or local government, to create, convey, modify or end a conservation easement in the same manner as other easements.

nv:AB43.title: Revises provisions relating to public works. (BDR 28-465)
nv:AB43.summary: Creates a permanent program letting Clark County, large cities in it, and certain sewer districts award job order contracts for minor construction on existing public works, with data reporting requirements.

nv:AB430.title: Exempts persons engaged in the provision of payroll processing services from provisions governing money transmission. (BDR 55-1072)
nv:AB430.summary: Exempts businesses that only provide payroll processing services from Nevada's money transmission licensing rules and repeals the duties set for payroll processors.

nv:AB433.title: Revises provisions relating to public safety.
nv:AB433.summary: Creates the Purple Ribbon Task Force on Firefighter and Peace Officer Wellness to review state wellness policies and report recommendations to the 2027 Legislature's government affairs committees.

nv:AB434.title: Prohibits certain employment practices. (BDR 53-188)
nv:AB434.summary: Bars employers from penalizing or threatening employees who decline meetings or communications meant to convey the employer's views on religious or political matters, with exceptions including religious organizations, and provides a remedy.

nv:AB439.title: Revises provisions concerning the purchase or acquisition of certain unmanned aerial vehicles or other related equipment and services under certain circumstances. (BDR 44-896)
nv:AB439.summary: Lets public and law enforcement agencies buy drones and related equipment or services from prohibited-list vendors if the vendor stores data only in the U.S. out of certain third parties' reach, the Department of Public Safety first finds compliance, and federal law allows.

nv:AB44.title: Prohibits manipulating the price of an essential good or service in this State. (BDR 52-503)
nv:AB44.summary: Makes manipulating the price of an essential good or service an unlawful restraint of trade, defined as knowing deceptive practices that raise prices beyond supply and demand and above the five-year average increase, with no private lawsuits.

nv:AB441.title: Revises provisions governing the Nevada Educational Choice Scholarship Program. (BDR 32-6)
nv:AB441.summary: Changes how tax credits for donations to scholarship organizations are requested and awarded, with applications May 1 to June 1 and priority to prior-year recipients, then siblings, then others, and requires scholarship organizations to be domestic nonprofits.

nv:AB442.title: Revises provisions relating to grants. (BDR 31-589)
nv:AB442.summary: Requires state grant-making entities to give written notice to nonprofits when a payment is more than 30 days late, lets the Office of Federal Assistance coordinate with grant-making entities, and revises the State Plan for Maximizing Federal Assistance, effective July 1, 2026.

nv:AB444.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 18-772)
nv:AB444.summary: Requires state agencies to notify chambers of commerce and trade associations, where practicable, about proposed regulations affecting small businesses, and to list them and the number of affected small businesses in the impact statement.

nv:AB445.title: Revises provisions relating to libraries. (BDR 34-1071)
nv:AB445.summary: Makes school and public library staff immune from criminal or civil liability for certain good-faith acts providing access to library materials or helping pupils and patrons access them.

nv:AB448.title: Revises provisions relating to insurance for vision care. (BDR 57-983)
nv:AB448.summary: Sets rules for vision benefit managers, including insurers and administrators: bars controlling providers' professional judgment, employing providers, recouping payment for eligible enrollees' care, varying reimbursement by providers' supplier choices, or requiring participation in any specific plan to join a network.

nv:AB449.title: Revises provisions governing public utilities. (BDR 58-888)
nv:AB449.summary: Raises the limits for simplified rate changes for water and sewer utilities to 4,000 persons served and $4 million in sales, and raises the revenue-increase limit for letter-of-advice rate changes from $15,000 to $100,000.

nv:AB45.title: Revises provisions relating to certain public bodies. (BDR 18-504)
nv:AB45.summary: Replaces the named Victim Information Notification Everyday System with a victim notification system in the Attorney General's office, and extends the Committee on Domestic Violence's duties to sexual assault.

nv:AB450.title: Revises requirements to obtain a license as a marriage and family therapist or clinical professional counselor by endorsement. (BDR 54-335)
nv:AB450.summary: Requires, rather than allows, the licensing board to grant out-of-state marriage and family therapists and clinical counselors a license by endorsement, and drops the requirement of proof of no investigation by the other state's regulator.

nv:AB451.title: Provides immunity from civil liability to certain persons returning a firearm under certain circumstances. (BDR 3-1057)
nv:AB451.summary: Gives licensed firearm dealers and local law enforcement agencies civil immunity for acts arising from agreements to hold an owner's firearm at least 21 days, with exceptions for gross negligence, reckless or unlawful conduct, and returning it to someone known to be dangerous or prohibited.

nv:AB452.title: Revises provisions relating to public utilities. (BDR 58-572)
nv:AB452.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to open investigatory dockets on a possible mechanism for sharing purchased fuel and power costs between electric utilities and customers, and requires utilities to refund overcharges.

nv:AB454.title: Enacts a Smart Heart Law for public and private schools. (BDR 34-1029)
nv:AB454.summary: Requires school coaches, managers and athletic trainers to be certified in CPR, and requires school emergency plans to include a response to cardiac emergencies, with committees allowed to include a medical professional.

nv:AB457.title: Requires the Joint Interim Standing Committee on Revenue to conduct a study concerning certain changes to provisions governing taxation.
nv:AB457.summary: Requires the Joint Interim Standing Committee on Revenue to study in 2025-2026 whether to treat certain businesses that rent Nevada real property as a single entity for the commerce tax, and to report recommendations.

nv:AB458.title: Revises provisions governing energy. (BDR 58-228)
nv:AB458.summary: Lets users of solar-powered affordable housing systems take part in net metering, sets requirements for related tariffs, contracts, tenant notices and contractors, and applies certain public works rules to related construction.

nv:AB46.title: Revises provisions relating to privileges applicable to information obtained from records and other property of public utilities and certain other entities. (BDR 58-310)
nv:AB46.summary: Provides that a legal privilege is not waived when privileged confidential information is disclosed or made available to the Public Utilities Commission and others authorized to access it.

nv:AB460.title: Revises provisions relating to child welfare. (BDR 13-1060)
nv:AB460.summary: Lets a parent or guardian complete a form nominating a guardian for a minor, requires courts to consider it, allows filing it in the Nevada Lockbox, and ends the Secretary of State's fee for registering documents there.

nv:AB461.title: Revises provisions governing health care. (BDR 38-156)
nv:AB461.summary: Replaces Nevada's health care power of attorney provisions with the remaining provisions of the Uniform Health-Care Decisions Act and requires a state program educating residents about long-term care planning.

nv:AB462.title: Revises provisions relating to economic development. (BDR 22-823)
nv:AB462.summary: Adds industrial parks to the Inland Port Authority Act, allows tax increment areas to repay bonds for port and park projects, requires school districts to designate career-pathways coordinators, creates a Career Pathways Oversight Committee, and revises Teacher Academy and teacher tuition-reimbursement rules.

nv:AB463.title: Revises provisions relating to prior authorization. (BDR 57-825)
nv:AB463.summary: Requires insurers to answer prior authorization requests within 2 business days (up to 7 calendar days if national rules allow), bars private insurers from requiring it for outpatient substance use treatment and diabetic test strips, and deems requests approved if a private insurer breaks them.

nv:AB465.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-927)
nv:AB465.summary: Makes school districts, charter schools and Nevada System of Higher Education institutions immune from civil liability for harassment by pupils, employees or contractors if they established, published and enforced a harassment policy with complaint protocols and supportive measures within 3 days.

nv:AB466.title: Revises certain notice requirements imposed on an insurer who issues a policy of portable electronics insurance. (BDR 57-797)
nv:AB466.summary: Removes the requirement that portable electronics insurers send electronic notices under Insurance Commissioner regulations, and applies the rule requiring a switch to another delivery method when electronic notices fail.

nv:AB467.title: Revises provisions relating to forensic mental health. (BDR 14-842)
nv:AB467.summary: Allows contracting with a community organization to run a competency-treatment facility in a county jail (counties of 100,000+, with sheriff's consent), allows programs outside forensic facilities for incompetent defendants, and requires Child and Family Services facilities to accept children placed by juvenile court order.

nv:AB471.title: Revises provisions governing remote sales of certain tobacco products. (BDR 32-846)
nv:AB471.summary: Taxes remote sales of cigars and pipe tobacco to Nevada consumers by out-of-state sellers above certain sales thresholds, based on the seller's cost, and requires those sellers to be licensed, file monthly reports and keep records.

nv:AB472.title: Revises provisions relating to educational personnel. (BDR 34-529)
nv:AB472.summary: Bars school districts from contracting with J-1 teacher exchange program sponsors or recruiters that charge more than $10,000 in total fees and costs per participant; existing contracts are exempt until renewed or extended.

nv:AB474.title: Requires the establishment and carrying out of a program to supplement the available food supply for certain persons in certain circumstances. (BDR 38-1103)
nv:AB474.summary: Requires, if money is available, the Division of Welfare and Supportive Services to run a program that identifies surplus food and distributes it at a discount to SNAP recipients, with a plan to cut food waste and improve access for seniors.

nv:AB475.title: Makes appropriations to Clark County, the City of Reno and the Nevada Rural Housing Authority for eviction diversion programs.
nv:AB475.summary: Appropriates $15,000,000 from the General Fund to Clark County, plus amounts to the City of Reno and the Nevada Rural Housing Authority, for eviction diversion programs.

nv:AB476.title: Makes an appropriation to the University of Nevada, Las Vegas.
nv:AB476.summary: Appropriates $500,000 in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27 to UNLV for pro bono legal services and experiential legal education at the William S. Boyd School of Law.

nv:AB477.title: Revises provisions relating to the counting of incarcerated persons for purposes of the apportionment of the population for certain election districts. (BDR 16-1134)
nv:AB477.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to record each inmate's last pre-prison address, whether 18 or older, and race or ethnicity for the State Demographer, and counts certain inmates with unknown or out-of-state addresses in a unit not tied to any census block.

nv:AB478.title: Revises provisions governing construction times in counties and cities. (BDR 20-1091)
nv:AB478.summary: Requires counties with 700,000 or more people (currently Clark) and their cities that restrict construction start times to let work on projects over 300 feet from a residential unit begin at 5 a.m., April 1 to September 30; voids ordinances that do not.

nv:AB479.title: Revises provisions relating to the taxation of agricultural real property. (BDR 32-426)
nv:AB479.summary: Treats land used for solar power combined with farming (agrivoltaics) as agricultural use for property tax purposes, but only for land that qualified for the agricultural use assessment before July 1, 2025.

nv:AB48.title: Revises provisions relating to bullying. (BDR 34-462)
nv:AB48.summary: Requires school administrators to screen reports of race discrimination or bullying to assess whether it likely occurred before investigating, and lets districts move the perpetrator to another school on a parent's request.

nv:AB480.title: Revises provisions relating to discrimination in housing. (BDR 10-1101)
nv:AB480.summary: Adopts the disparate impact standard in Nevada's fair housing law, allowing liability for housing practices that have a discriminatory effect on a group even without discriminatory intent, unless the practice is necessary for a substantial legitimate interest.

nv:AB483.title: Provides for priority review of certain applications for licensure to practice health professions. (BDR 40-354)
nv:AB483.summary: Requires health licensing boards, including Clark County's district health board and boards for medical, dental and nursing professions, to set up priority review of initial license applications from applicants who will practice mainly in historically underserved communities.

nv:AB484.title: Revises provisions relating to the collection of data concerning providers of health care. (BDR 40-806)
nv:AB484.summary: Requires health care provider license renewal data to also include the provider's sex, other jurisdictions where licensed, use of telehealth, and the types of patients served.

nv:AB486.title: Makes various changes related to transportation. (BDR 35-678)
nv:AB486.summary: Changes Department of Transportation rules: revises deputy director degree and experience requirements, raises the threshold for required highway project cost-benefit analyses from $25 million to $50 million, and adds wildlife-collision and wildlife-crossing information to project analyses and reports.

nv:AB487.title: Directs the Joint Interim Standing Committee on Natural Resources to conduct a study during the 2025-2026 interim concerning the sale of cats and dogs by retail pet stores in this State.
nv:AB487.summary: Bans retail pet stores from selling or otherwise transferring ownership of dogs or cats, makes violation by an operator a misdemeanor, and lets a court bar the person from selling dogs or cats as a breeder or dealer for up to one year.

nv:AB488.title: Revises provisions relating to criminal convictions of certain victims. (BDR 14-873)
nv:AB488.summary: Expands the offenses for which a human trafficking victim may petition to vacate a conviction and seal records to any state crime or local ordinance violation, applying retroactively.

nv:AB489.title: Revises provisions relating to civil actions. (BDR 3-1141)
nv:AB489.summary: Lets heirs and personal representatives sue for damages for a homicide death at any time, with no two-year limit, if a preponderance of evidence shows homicide. Applies retroactively and revives previously time-barred claims.

nv:AB49.title: Revises provisions relating to educational personnel. (BDR 34-519)
nv:AB49.summary: Lets districts and charter schools hire teachers licensed in another state for up to 1 year pending a Nevada license, requires rules letting school nurses and social workers work while endorsements are pending, and ends the State Board of Education's power to disapprove Commission regulations.

nv:AB490.title: Revises provisions relating to the venue for certain proceedings. (BDR 24-870)
nv:AB490.summary: Lets petitions for judicial review and challenges to initiative or referendum petitions be filed in any qualified district court, not only the First Judicial District Court. Qualified courts must offer electronic filing and access; others need five or more judges.

nv:AB491.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-570)
nv:AB491.summary: Requires clerks to give the Secretary of State requested election-cycle data, or a written timeline, within two working days; requires most elected state and local officeholders to be registered to vote where they must reside; makes candidacy declarations public electronically.

nv:AB493.title: Revises provisions relating to the collection, disposal and retirement of certain types of waste. (BDR 40-424)
nv:AB493.summary: Requires owners of leased or output-purchased residential solar systems to file end-of-life disposal plans, utility-scale solar retirement plans to cover decommissioning and land restoration, and solar recycling facilities to report materials received, recycled and recovered.

nv:AB494.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-1136)
nv:AB494.summary: Requires state agencies to report on funding and state-law options if specified federal laws on special education, student privacy, civil rights or health privacy are repealed, and lets them adopt substantially similar regulations.

nv:AB496.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-997)
nv:AB496.summary: Requires county clerks to post a downloadable alphabetical list of registered voters monthly, adds voter initials and a phone number space to mail ballot return envelopes, and requires online posting of mail and provisional ballot information.

nv:AB497.title: Revises provisions relating to campaign finance. (BDR 24-996)
nv:AB497.summary: Excludes nonprofits, businesses registered with the Secretary of State and all labor unions from the definition of committee for political action, lets committees use account money for certain purposes, and lets defeated candidates carry unspent contributions to a later election.

nv:AB498.title: Revises provisions relating to motor clubs. (BDR 57-696)
nv:AB498.summary: Removes the requirement that motor clubs give members their in-state place of business, and lets nonresident club agents be licensed if their home state requires no license.

nv:AB5.title: Enacts the Nevada Studio Infrastructure Jobs and Workforce Training Act.
nv:AB5.summary: Creates the Nevada Studio Infrastructure Jobs and Workforce Training Act, offering film infrastructure transferable tax credits for productions at the Summerlin Production Studios project, and funds film workforce education and training.

nv:AB50.title: Revises provisions relating to victims of a mass casualty incident. (BDR 20-466)
nv:AB50.summary: Lets counties set up a confidential electronic database of mass casualty victims for reunification and long-term support, and requires hospitals in those counties to report victim information to it and to ask victims about long-term services.

nv:AB500.title: Provides for the licensure and regulation of payments banks. (BDR 55-999)
nv:AB500.summary: Creates licensing and regulation by the Commissioner of Financial Institutions of payments banks, which may handle money transmission, deposit accounts and merchant acquiring but may not make loans.

nv:AB501.title: Authorizes certain pupils to receive academic credit for completing certain outdoor recreational activities. (BDR 34-1142)
nv:AB501.summary: Lets school boards and charter schools give middle and high school students academic credit toward promotion or graduation for approved outdoor recreational activities done outside school hours.

nv:AB502.title: Revises provisions relating to public works. (BDR 28-401)
nv:AB502.summary: Extends from 10 to 30 days the window for contractors to request apprentices before starting public works, and requires reporting identifying information about public works to the Labor Commissioner.

nv:AB503.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 15-394)
nv:AB503.summary: Sets penalties for tampering with critical infrastructure, bars possessing or buying used utility wire without proof of lawful ownership or a qualifying business, and sets recordkeeping and reporting rules for scrap metal processors.

nv:AB504.title: Establishes certain deceptive trade practices relating to the sale of or an offer to sell certain hemp products. (BDR 56-867)
nv:AB504.summary: Requires sellers of hemp products for human consumption who hold no cannabis license to post signs saying the location is not licensed for cannabis, bars false or misleading advertising about licensing or the product, and makes violations deceptive trade practices.

nv:AB506.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 18-934)
nv:AB506.summary: Eliminates or redirects many required reports to the Interim Finance Committee from state agencies, school districts and local governments, and ends the education evaluation bureau's odd-year report to the Legislative Commission.

nv:AB507.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial administration. (BDR 31-933)
nv:AB507.summary: Clarifies that the $75,000 threshold for Interim Finance Committee approval applies to any proposed revision of expense categories in a work program, and bars splitting a revision into separate requests to avoid approval.

nv:AB509.title: Revises provisions relating to the access of public rights-of-way by broadband providers. (BDR 58-664)
nv:AB509.summary: Bars broadband providers from using local public rights-of-way after July 1, 2026 without an agreement with the local government, and caps the compensation in such agreements at 2 percent of annual gross revenue from local broadband service.

nv:AB510.title: Makes various changes to the regulation of accountancy. (BDR 54-695)
nv:AB510.summary: Replaces the education and work-experience requirements in statute for CPA certificates with requirements the Board of Accountancy sets by regulation.

nv:AB511.title: Revises provisions relating to insurance. (BDR 57-697)
nv:AB511.summary: Changes insurance reimbursement rules for chiropractors, acupuncturists, psychologists, therapists, social workers, podiatrists, drug and alcohol counselors and certain nurses so the provider who treated the insured, not the insured, is entitled to reimbursement.

nv:AB512.title: Revises provisions relating to casualty insurance. (BDR 57-1089)
