nv:AB512.summary: Writes into statute which casualty policies are covered by, and which insurers are exempt from, the ban on liability policies that reduce limits by defense costs, and adds legal expenses insurance to casualty insurance.

nv:AB513.title: Revises provisions relating to chiropractic physicians and chiropractic assistants. (BDR 54-630)
nv:AB513.summary: Lets the chiropractic board issue temporary chiropractic assistant certificates, valid up to 15 business days, to people licensed in another jurisdiction, and changes board membership, license qualifications, fees and unprofessional conduct rules.

nv:AB514.title: Makes revisions relating to mental health care. (BDR 38-350)
nv:AB514.summary: Requires Medicaid to cover rehabilitative residential mental health care for certain recipients, creates licensing and regulation for providers as facilities for the dependent, adds them to Long-Term Care Ombudsman oversight, and appropriates money to the Division of Health Care Financing and Policy.

nv:AB515.title: Revises provisions relating to adoption assistance programs. (BDR 38-355)
nv:AB515.summary: Provides that unspent adoption-assistance grant money never reverts to the General Fund but must be used under federal rules, appropriates General Fund money for reinvesting adoption savings, and requires a study and plan for that reinvestment.

nv:AB518.title: Revises provisions relating to the interstate placement of children. (BDR 11-807)
nv:AB518.summary: Adopts a revised version of the Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children, which governs sending children to other states for foster care, adoption or juvenile justice placement.

nv:AB519.title: Creates a separate chapter of the Nevada Revised Statutes governing certain agencies and organizations that provide nonmedical services. (BDR 40-805)
nv:AB519.summary: Moves the laws on home personal care agencies, nonmedical personal care employment agencies and intermediary service organizations into a new chapter of the Nevada Revised Statutes, substantially keeping their licensing and regulation the same.

nv:AB52.title: Revises provisions relating to the payment of claims under policies of health insurance. (BDR 57-367)
nv:AB52.summary: Requires private health insurers and plan administrators to approve or deny and pay claims within 21 days if filed electronically or 30 days otherwise, bars denials without a reasonable basis, requires annual compliance reports, and extends administrative penalties to more insurer types.

nv:AB520.title: Revises provisions relating to adoption. (BDR 11-356)
nv:AB520.summary: Requires background checks for people who operate or provide services to children at child-placing agencies, allows certain adoption registry disclosures without a natural parent's consent in extenuating circumstances, and allows remote attendance at adoption hearings.

nv:AB521.title: Revises provisions relating to the protection of children. (BDR 40-1099)
nv:AB521.summary: Requires applicants, licensees, and certain employees and contractors of certain medical facilities and intermediary service organizations to authorize a Statewide Central Registry check for substantiated child abuse or neglect reports from the prior 5 years.

nv:AB523.title: Revises provisions relating to transportation. (BDR 57-1138)
nv:AB523.summary: Lowers minimum insurance for rideshare companies and autonomous vehicle providers from $1,500,000 to $1,000,000, and bars vicarious liability claims against rideshare and delivery network companies for acts of drivers or rideshare passengers.

nv:AB527.title: Authorizes the installation and use of school bus infraction detection systems on school buses. (BDR 43-421)
nv:AB527.summary: Lets school districts install cameras on school buses to detect drivers passing stopped buses, with a peace officer reviewing the evidence before a civil infraction citation is issued, and sets citation and hearing procedures.

nv:AB529.title: Revises provisions governing facilities for the generation of electricity. (BDR 58-427)
nv:AB529.summary: Requires certain wholesale electricity generation facilities within a cooperative or municipal utility's territory to buy their operating power from it, follow its rules and rates, and allow it to meter them.

nv:AB530.title: Revises provisions relating to the imposition by certain counties of additional taxes on fuels for motor vehicles. (BDR 32-783)
nv:AB530.summary: Lets a large county's commissioners continue annual fuel tax increases after 2026 by adopting an ordinance with a two-thirds board vote by December 31, 2026, replacing the required voter approval at the November 2026 election.

nv:AB533.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-756)
nv:AB533.summary: Lets a student attend a public school outside their assigned attendance zone if the school has room in their grade and approves them, requires district policies and an appeals process, and creates transportation grants for such students.

nv:AB534.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-975)
nv:AB534.summary: Makes many election law changes, including renaming certain provisional ballots "conditional ballots," revising voter registration updates, mail ballot and registration deadlines, risk-limiting audits and polling place conduct rules, and creating a Voter Access Grant Program.

nv:AB535.title: Revises provisions relating to the sales tax exemption for organizations created for religious, charitable or educational purposes. (BDR 32-812)
nv:AB535.summary: Sets factors the Department of Taxation and Tax Commission consider for a nonprofit's sales and use tax exemption, requires a full explanation and appeal procedure for denials, and requires a report to the Legislature every odd-numbered year.

nv:AB539.title: Authorizes the Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation to establish a career coaching program for certain pupils in certain circumstances. (BDR 18-418)
nv:AB539.summary: Allows the Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, to the extent money is available, to run a program placing career coaches in middle and junior high schools to help pupils explore career pathways.

nv:AB540.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 25-1036)
nv:AB540.summary: Creates the Nevada Attainable Housing Account, with $133,000,000 appropriated, to fund attainable housing projects through an annual allocation plan, with matching funds required, and creates a Nevada Attainable Housing Council to advise on its use.

nv:AB541.title: Revises provisions relating to indigent petitioners. (BDR 3-1153)
nv:AB541.summary: Requires costs of indigent postconviction habeas petitions to be paid from money appropriated to the Department of Indigent Defense Services instead of the Office of State Public Defender, with any Reserve for Statutory Contingency Account allocation going to the department.

nv:AB542.title: Revises provisions relating to offenders.
nv:AB542.summary: Extends the reversion date of a Department of Corrections offender-tracking appropriation to September 17, 2027, and delays the revised sentence-credit method to crimes committed on or after July 1, 2026, adding credit for exceptional meritorious service.

nv:AB543.title: Revises provisions relating to the lease of certain state real property for certain purposes and the sale of agricultural products produced on such real property. (BDR 26-1133)
nv:AB543.summary: Allows the Division of State Parks to lease grazing rights and sell agricultural products from state land it administers, with proceeds deposited in the state parks maintenance account and used in the region collected.

nv:AB544.title: Revises provisions relating to certain licenses issued by the Division of Public and Behavioral Health of the Department of Health and Human Services. (BDR 40-1118)
nv:AB544.summary: Makes medical facility and facility-for-the-dependent licenses expire one year after issuance instead of on December 31, renewable annually.

nv:AB545.title: Increases certain fees relating to emissions testing. (BDR 40-1150)
nv:AB545.summary: Raises the emissions-testing compliance form fee from $150 to $175 per set of 25 and from $6 to $7 per form for fleet stations, which also raises the linked first-issuance fee for certain special license plates.

nv:AB547.title: Revises provisions relating to public employment. (BDR 23-994)
nv:AB547.summary: Requires state hiring authorities to treat relevant federal government work experience as equivalent to Nevada state experience, and bars requiring a bachelor's degree for state jobs except in limited circumstances.

nv:AB55.title: Revises provisions relating to motor vehicle crashes. (BDR 43-250)
nv:AB55.summary: Requires blood samples from deceased crash victims to be tested for commonly misused substances as well as alcohol, drops the 8-hour draw limit, and requires police crash reports to go through the state electronic reporting system within 10 days of the crash or death.

nv:AB550.title: Revises provisions governing incompetent criminal defendants. (BDR 14-1120)
nv:AB550.summary: Limits prosecutors' commitment motions, in category A or certain category B felony cases where the defendant is found incompetent with no substantial probability of attaining competence, to people previously ordered to competency treatment; requires serving the motion on the Division of Public and Behavioral Health.

nv:AB551.title: Requires a background investigation of employees, prospective employees, contractors and prospective contractors of certain governmental agencies. (BDR 38-1122)
nv:AB551.summary: As introduced, requires background investigations, including fingerprints and proof of work eligibility, of employees and contractors of the Division of Welfare and Supportive Services; current employees must submit information by January 1, 2026.

nv:AB552.title: Revises provisions relating to the Trust Fund for Child Welfare. (BDR 38-1124)
nv:AB552.summary: Ends the requirement that the Division of Child and Family Services deduct the cost of publicly funded services from a child's separate account in the Trust Fund for Child Welfare.

nv:AB553.title: Transfers the Division of Emergency Management of the Office of the Military to the Office of the Governor. (BDR 18-1126)
nv:AB553.summary: Moves the Division of Emergency Management from the Office of the Military to the Office of the Governor and renames it the Office of Emergency Management, updating related statutory references and duties.

nv:AB554.title: Revises provisions relating to the Grant Matching Account. (BDR 18-1227)
nv:AB554.summary: Provides that money remaining in the Grant Matching Account at fiscal year end does not revert to the General Fund and carries forward.

nv:AB555.title: Establishes provisions relating to the coverage of prescription insulin drugs under certain policies of health insurance. (BDR 57-1167)
nv:AB555.summary: Caps cost-sharing at $35 for a 30-day supply of prescription insulin under certain private health insurance policies.

nv:AB556.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicaid. (BDR 38-1117)
nv:AB556.summary: Creates a Beneficiary Advisory Council that includes current or former Medicaid recipients, renames the Medical Care Advisory Committee the Medicaid Advisory Committee, requires at least 25 percent of its members to serve on the Council, and requires quarterly meetings and staggered terms.

nv:AB558.title: Makes appropriations to restore the balances in the Stale Claims Account, the Emergency Account and the Contingency Account.
nv:AB558.summary: Appropriates $4,616,752 to the Stale Claims Account, $17,000 to the Emergency Account and $25,730,726 to the Contingency Account from the General Fund to restore their balances.

nv:AB559.title: Makes a supplemental appropriation to the Office of the Extradition Coordinator within the Office of the Attorney General for an unanticipated shortfall related to extradition costs.
nv:AB559.summary: Appropriates $1,518,208 from the State General Fund to the Attorney General's Office of the Extradition Coordinator to cover an unanticipated shortfall in extradition costs.

nv:AB56.title: Revises provisions relating to the licensing of certain providers of health care. (BDR 54-255)
nv:AB56.summary: Changes continuing education and fee rules for physicians, physician assistants and osteopathic physicians, including raising osteopathic continuing education from 35 to 40 hours, and sets grounds for osteopathic board discipline and license denial.

nv:AB560.title: Makes a supplemental appropriation to the Division of Child and Family Services of the Department of Health and Human Services for an unanticipated shortfall related to the Rural Child Welfare budget account.
nv:AB560.summary: Appropriates $444,325 from the General Fund as a supplemental appropriation to the Division of Child and Family Services for a shortfall in the Rural Child Welfare budget account.

nv:AB561.title: Makes a supplemental appropriation to the Division of Forestry of the State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources for an unanticipated shortfall related to firefighting costs.
nv:AB561.summary: Appropriates $20,733,824 from the State General Fund to the Division of Forestry to cover an unanticipated shortfall in firefighting costs.

nv:AB562.title: Makes appropriations to the Office of the Secretary of State for costs associated with the voter registration and elections management system and connectivity of automatic voter registration agencies.
nv:AB562.summary: Appropriates $27,004,162 for continued replacement of the state voter registration and elections management system, $748,800 for consulting services for it, and $3,487,364 to connect automatic voter registration agencies.

nv:AB563.title: Makes an appropriation to the Office of the State Controller for the costs of certain consulting services.
nv:AB563.summary: Appropriates $1,110,000 from the General Fund to the Office of the State Controller for consulting services on preparing the state's annual financial report.

nv:AB564.title: Makes an appropriation to the Fleet Services Division of the Department of Administration for the replacement and purchase of vehicles.
nv:AB564.summary: Appropriates $13,131,324 from the General Fund to the Fleet Services Division for replacing and purchasing vehicles.

nv:AB565.title: Makes an appropriation to the Supreme Court of Nevada for the costs of the implementation of a statewide trial court electronic filing system.
nv:AB565.summary: Appropriates $5,175,367 from the General Fund to the Supreme Court of Nevada to implement a statewide trial court electronic filing system.

nv:AB566.title: Makes appropriations to and authorizes the expenditure of money by the Division of Museums and History of the Department of Tourism and Cultural Affairs for certain vehicles, tools and repairs.
nv:AB566.summary: Appropriates $75,781 and authorizes spending $323,067 of other money for the Division of Museums and History to buy vehicles, a tractor and locomotive tools and repair a sign at the Nevada State Railroad Museums in Boulder City and Carson City.

nv:AB567.title: Makes an appropriation to the Nevada System of Higher Education for safety and security equipment and enhancements.
nv:AB567.summary: Appropriates $11,000,000 from the General Fund to the Nevada System of Higher Education for safety and security equipment and enhancements.

nv:AB568.title: Makes appropriations to the Nevada System of Higher Education for operational and instructional expenses.
nv:AB568.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Nevada System of Higher Education for operations and instruction, including about $22.4 million for UNR, $23.6 million for UNLV, and smaller amounts for law, dental and extension programs.

nv:AB569.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Veterans Services for certain vehicles and equipment.
nv:AB569.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Veterans Services for replacing vehicles, a mower, security equipment and a dump truck at the southern and northern Nevada veterans memorial cemeteries, buying a tracked loader, and a video conference system.

nv:AB57.title: Revises provisions relating to the Nevada Intrastate Mutual Aid System. (BDR 36-263)
nv:AB57.summary: Gives the State Forester Firewarden authority over intrastate mutual aid for wildfire suppression, makes the Firewarden co-chair of the Intrastate Mutual Aid Committee with the emergency management chief, and has both jointly appoint its members.

nv:AB570.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Corrections for various purposes relating to certain technology, training and equipment.
nv:AB570.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Corrections for medical and dental equipment, vehicles, buses and transport vans, refrigerator trucks, computer hardware and software, furniture, and equipment and training for correctional officers.

nv:AB571.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Education for certain surveys, offsets to decreases in federal grant funding, professional development costs, information technology projects, programs, grants and studies.
nv:AB571.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Education for educator surveys, charter authority offsets for reduced federal grants, Canvas licenses, a multi-tiered system of supports framework ($3 million a year), a new school performance framework, seal programs, grants and studies.

nv:AB572.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Corrections for the replacement and purchase of certain equipment and furniture.
nv:AB572.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Corrections for replacing and purchasing equipment and furniture at conservation camps, including a dishwasher, laundry equipment, water heaters, boilers, office chairs and small equipment.

nv:AB573.title: Makes an appropriation to the Department of Education to carry out the Incentivizing Pathways to Teaching Grant Program.
nv:AB573.summary: Appropriates $8,710,708 from the General Fund to the Department of Education for the Incentivizing Pathways to Teaching Grant Program.

nv:AB574.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Corrections for the purchase and replacement of equipment and furniture at High Desert State Prison.
nv:AB574.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Corrections to buy and replace equipment and furniture at High Desert State Prison, including security, culinary, laundry, medical and automotive equipment.

nv:AB575.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Public Safety for the replacement of computer hardware, equipment and associated software, vehicles and furniture and for information technology projects and a recruiting campaign.
nv:AB575.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Public Safety for computer hardware, vehicles, furniture, equipment, a parole and probation records system, Nevada Criminal Justice Information System modernization and support, and an $840,926 recruitment campaign.

nv:AB576.title: Makes appropriations to the Nevada Highway Patrol Division of the Department of Public Safety for the purchase and replacement of motorcycles, vehicles and equipment.
nv:AB576.summary: Appropriates State Highway Fund money to the Nevada Highway Patrol for replacing fleet vehicles, motorcycles, portable radios, mobile data computers, event recorders, drones and scales, and buying flares, ammunition, first aid kits and other equipment.

nv:AB577.title: Makes appropriations to the State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources for a certain new website and database and for the replacement of vehicles and computer hardware and associated software.
nv:AB577.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources for a Sagebrush Ecosystem Technical Team website and database ($257,400), vehicle replacements and computer hardware.

nv:AB578.title: Makes appropriations to the State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources for the replacement of computer and information technology equipment, vehicles and other equipment and for certain projects.
nv:AB578.summary: Appropriates money to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, including $6,000,000 for Shared Stewardship Agreement conservation projects, $2,048,082 for deferred maintenance, and vehicle and equipment replacements for forestry and conservation camps.

nv:AB579.title: Makes an appropriation to the Department of Education for the replacement of the information technology system for educator licensure.
nv:AB579.summary: Appropriates $1,472,641 from the General Fund to the Department of Education to replace the educator licensure information technology system.

nv:AB58.title: Revises various provisions relating to gaming. (BDR 41-297)
nv:AB58.summary: Has the Gaming Control Board Chair administratively approve games instead of Board recommendation and Commission approval, requires the 2,500 square feet for restricted gaming licenses to be indoor space, and repeals rules on cash-access service providers and global risk management.

nv:AB581.title: Makes supplemental appropriations to the Department of Corrections for an unanticipated shortfall related to operating, travel, information services, personnel services, training, transportation, maintenance, utilities and inmate-driven expenses.
nv:AB581.summary: Appropriates money from the State General Fund to several Department of Corrections budget accounts, including $2,929,232 for Northern Nevada Correctional Center, to cover shortfalls in operating, personnel, utility and inmate-related costs.

nv:AB582.title: Revises provisions relating to the Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship Program. (BDR 31-1226)
nv:AB582.summary: Increases from 3 to 13 percent the cap on Endowment Account money the State Treasurer may spend on the Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship Program, tied to expected tobacco settlement revenue.

nv:AB583.title: Establishes for the 2025-2027 biennium the subsidies to be paid to the Public Employees' Benefits Program for insurance for certain active and retired public officers and employees.
nv:AB583.summary: Sets the State's share of group insurance premiums for active state employees, and the base state and local government share for retirees' coverage and Medicare plan medical expenses, in the Public Employees' Benefits Program for 2025-2027.

nv:AB585.title: Revises provisions relating to bill draft requests. (BDR 17-1137)
nv:AB585.summary: Reduces the number of bill draft requests legislators may make before a session, splits them between two deadlines, and requires legislators to supply enough detail to draft each request or withdraw it, or lose requests next time.

nv:AB586.title: Makes supplemental appropriations to the Aging and Disability Services Division of the Department of Health and Human Services for an unanticipated shortfall related to costs associated with certain provider payments.
nv:AB586.summary: Appropriates money from the State General Fund to the Aging and Disability Services Division for provider-payment shortfalls, including $3,930,266 for the Rural Regional Center and $4,257,914 for the Desert Regional Center developmental services.

nv:AB588.title: Revises provisions relating to members of the Assembly of the Nevada Legislature. (BDR 17-1235)
nv:AB588.summary: Replaces the terms Assemblyman and Assemblywoman with Assemblymember throughout state law and removes a provision letting a female member use Assemblywoman on official stationery.

nv:AB589.title: Establishes requirements to protect the privacy of certain information and genetic material. (BDR 19-1241)
nv:AB589.summary: Limits state and local agencies' collection and disclosure of autism-related data, and sets crimes and civil liability for unauthorized genetic testing, disclosure of a person's genetic information, and selling or transferring a person's DNA sample without consent.

nv:AB59.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 45-300)
nv:AB59.summary: Among other wildlife-law changes, extends game wardens' peace officer powers to all Nevada laws, widens the feeding ban from big game to wild mammals and game birds, and sets the higher trophy-animal civil penalty for moose.

nv:AB590.title: Makes appropriations to and authorizes the expenditure of money by the Office of the Military for certain projects, programs, equipment and contractual costs.
nv:AB590.summary: Appropriates money to the Office of the Military for Nevada National Guard facility maintenance projects, a $4,164,800 payment tied to ending a federal agreement, and other projects and equipment.

nv:AB591.title: Makes various changes regarding state financial administration and makes appropriations for the support of the civil government of the State.
nv:AB591.summary: Appropriates money from the State General Fund and State Highway Fund to support state government agencies in fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27, and makes other changes to state financial administration.

nv:AB592.title: Revises provisions relating to the compensation of state employees.
nv:AB592.summary: Sets maximum annual salaries for listed state officers, employees and medical positions by agency, and revises compensation provisions for Senate and Assembly employees.

nv:AB593.title: Makes appropriations to the Interim Finance Committee for costs associated with the implementation of the Enterprise Resource Planning System.
nv:AB593.summary: Appropriates $53,434,995 from the General Fund and $12,534,135 from the State Highway Fund to the Interim Finance Committee for the Office of Finance's Enterprise Resource Planning System.

nv:AB594.title: Revises provisions relating to taxation. (BDR 32-1130)
nv:AB594.summary: Lets the Department of Taxation send notices electronically, lets the Board of Economic Development deny or reduce abatements and tax credits, and moves the sales and use tax remittance deadline to the 20th of the following month for periods starting in 2026.

nv:AB595.title: Revises provisions governing fiscal information for legislative measures. (BDR 17-1239)
nv:AB595.summary: Defines the "Executive Budget" used in bill-summary fiscal statements and the fiscal-note exemption as the proposed budget the Governor submits to the Legislature under state law.

nv:AB596.title: Makes appropriations and authorizations for certain compensation and benefits for state employees represented by a bargaining unit.
nv:AB596.summary: Appropriates money for retention incentives, annual leave cash-outs, tool allowances and other items in state collective bargaining agreements, gives certain employees 1 percent raises in each of 2025-26 and 2026-27, and voids agreement provisions requiring money the Legislature did not appropriate.

nv:AB597.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-1245)
nv:AB597.summary: Allows voters registered without a party affiliation to vote in a major party's primary by requesting a partisan ballot, by mail or in person, and removes the notice that automatically registered voters cannot vote in partisan primaries.

nv:AB598.title: Revises provisions relating to the development of certain parcels of state land.
nv:AB598.summary: Exempts Campus for Hope Foundation development of state land at the Southern Nevada Adult Mental Health Services Campus for a qualified project or children's behavioral health cottages from Public Works Division oversight and public works law, though prevailing wage applies to qualified-project contracts.

nv:AB60.title: Revises provisions relating to certain behavioral health services. (BDR 39-434)
nv:AB60.summary: Requires people who call themselves certified prevention specialists to be certified, bars minors from providing or supervising peer recovery support services, and requires substance use prevention coalitions to employ or contract with certified prevention specialists.

nv:AB600.title: Revises provisions relating to legislative affairs. (BDR 17-1251)
nv:AB600.summary: Directs sales proceeds from food and items in legislative buildings to the Legislative Fund, states every state entity belongs to one of three branches and that statute organization is not a branch determination, and places a parcel under legislative control if purchased.

nv:AB63.title: Revises provisions relating to civil actions for wrongful conviction. (BDR 3-440)
nv:AB63.summary: Defines "incarcerated" as confined in a local detention facility, jail or prison for wrongful-conviction suits, and subjects any other court-awarded relief to the $100,000 yearly cap; applies to actions filed on or after the effective date.

nv:AB64.title: Revises provisions relating to public meetings. (BDR 19-445)
nv:AB64.summary: Narrows the Open Meeting Law exclusion for attorney consultations to receiving legal advice and deliberating on it, and changes the in-person location requirement for remote meetings to those adjudicating certain contested cases or holding regulation workshops or hearings.

nv:AB65.title: Revises provisions relating to guardianship. (BDR 13-470)
nv:AB65.summary: Renames the State Guardianship Compliance Office the State Guardianship Office, lets it hire needed accountants and investigators, bars fees for investigators' document copies, and lets courts appoint minor guardians for special immigrant juvenile status, ending by age 21.

nv:AB69.title: Removes the prospective expiration of the Nye County Sales and Use Tax Act of 2007.
nv:AB69.summary: Removes the October 1, 2027 expiration of the Nye County Sales and Use Tax Act of 2007, allowing the public safety sales tax to continue past that date.

nv:AB70.title: Revises provisions related to energy. (BDR 58-454)
nv:AB70.summary: Lets counties require renewable energy facilities on federal land seeking tax abatements to reimburse up to $50,000 of environmental review costs, and bars counties from permit requirements that make such facilities impractical or from applying any moratorium to them.

nv:AB72.title: Revises provisions relating to notaries public and document preparation services. (BDR 19-485)
nv:AB72.summary: Lets the Secretary of State adopt a code of professional responsibility for notaries and sanction violators, lets notaries refuse to notarize if they doubt a signer's capacity or voluntariness, and revises bond rules for document preparation services.

nv:AB73.title: Establishes requirements for certain communications relating to an election. (BDR 24-487)
nv:AB73.summary: Requires communications for or against candidates or parties that include synthetic media, when made or paid for by a person, candidate or political committee, to disclose the image, video or audio was manipulated; lets a depicted candidate seek an injunction if it is missing.

nv:AB76.title: Revises provisions relating to cannabis. (BDR 56-286)
nv:AB76.summary: Makes various changes to cannabis regulation, including using hearing officers for Cannabis Compliance Board discipline, letting the Board issue subpoenas in unlicensed-activity cases, and revising licensing, testing laboratory, packaging and advertising rules.

nv:AB79.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 24-483)
nv:AB79.summary: Sets a $5,000 contribution limit for non-recall special elections, requires candidates to file a notice of intent to run, clarifies campaign funds may pay ordinary and necessary expenses, and lets the Secretary of State impose administrative fines for campaign finance violations.

nv:AB8.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial administration. (BDR 31-378)
nv:AB8.summary: Lets the Division of State Parks deposit accumulated money of $10,000 or more within 10 working days instead of by the next working day.

nv:AB81.title: Exempts the State of Nevada from provisions of federal law relating to daylight saving time. (BDR 19-23)
nv:AB81.summary: Exempts Nevada from the federal daylight saving time requirement, keeping the state on Pacific Standard Time year-round.

nv:AB82.title: Requires the Governor to proclaim certain days of observance. (BDR 19-60)
nv:AB82.summary: Requires the Governor to proclaim Diwali Day, Eid al-Fitr Day, Vaisakhi Day and Vesak Day each year in Nevada.

nv:AB83.title: Designates “Larry Itliong Day” as a day of observance in this State. (BDR 19-99)
nv:AB83.summary: Requires the Governor to proclaim October each year as Larry Itliong Day in Nevada.

nv:AB86.title: Revises provisions relating to forestry. (BDR 47-377)
nv:AB86.summary: Removes the requirement to obtain a State Forester Firewarden logging permit, and related reseeding and certificate-copy requirements, for a "cutting operation."

nv:AB88.title: Revises provisions relating to juvenile justice. (BDR 5-495)
nv:AB88.summary: Removes the requirements that a district attorney give written approval, and that the child make certain admissions, before a juvenile court dismisses a petition and refers the child to a probation officer for informal supervision.

nv:AB89.title: Imposes certain requirements relating to unclothed searches of children at certain juvenile justice facilities. (BDR 5-496)
nv:AB89.summary: Requires juvenile detention and commitment facilities to adopt policies that prohibit unclothed searches of children except in certain circumstances and set rules for any such search.

nv:AB90.title: Revises provisions relating to juvenile justice. (BDR 5-497)
nv:AB90.summary: Adds regional facilities for treatment and rehabilitation of children to the facilities covered by the Juvenile Justice Bill of Rights, and requires the same court findings before committing a child to such a facility as for state detention facilities.

nv:AB91.title: Revises provisions relating to parole. (BDR 16-500)
nv:AB91.summary: Lets the Parole Board grant second-look review to people with category A or B felony convictions who have served 10 years of the minimum term and pose no significant, articulable public safety risk. Extends youth-offense parole eligibility from under age 18 to under 25.

nv:AB92.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-101)
nv:AB92.summary: Requires government-occupied buildings open to the public with available rooms to let major-party state and county committees use them free in presidential election years and for precinct meetings in other years, except higher-education system buildings, restoring a rule repealed in 2021.

nv:AB93.title: Revises provisions relating to public employees. (BDR 53-160)
nv:AB93.summary: Adds school police, juvenile probation officers, municipal court bailiffs and deputy marshals, city and town marshals, and other category I-III peace officers to the "police officer" definition used for occupational disease and related benefits. Appropriates money for annual physicals for certain Public Safety staff.

nv:AB96.title: Revises provisions relating to master plans. (BDR 22-397)
nv:AB96.summary: Requires master plans in counties of 100,000 or more people (Clark and Washoe) to include a heat mitigation element, with strategies such as public cooling spaces, public drinking water and shade over paved surfaces.

nv:AB97.title: Revises provisions relating to public safety. (BDR 14-499)
nv:AB97.summary: Requires criminal justice agencies to submit crime data to the state repository through the FBI's National Incident-Based Reporting System.

nv:AB98.title: Creates a day of observance for labor leader, Dolores Huerta. (BDR 19-642)
nv:AB98.summary: Requires the Governor to proclaim April 10 each year as Dolores Huerta Day in Nevada.

nv:AJR1.title: Proposes to amend the Nevada Constitution to revise certain provisions relating to property taxes.
nv:AJR1.summary: Proposes amending the Nevada Constitution so real property gets no age-based improvement adjustment or partial tax abatement in the first fiscal year after a sale or transfer, with later age adjustments figured as if improvements were new at sale.

nv:AJR10.title: Urges the Federal Government to release federally managed land in Nevada for housing.
nv:AJR10.summary: Urges the President and Congress to pass the Southern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act, which releases certain federally managed land to Nevada and local governments for housing.

nv:AJR11.title: Urges Congress to enact the Protecting the Right to Organize Act.
nv:AJR11.summary: Urges Congress to enact the Richard L. Trumka Protecting the Right to Organize Act of 2025, relating to employees' rights to collectively bargain.

nv:AJR14.title: Condemns the January 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol and denounces the use of presidential pardons and commutations to absolve the rioters.
nv:AJR14.summary: Condemns the January 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol, including the assault on law enforcement officers, and denounces the use of presidential pardons and commutations for participants in the riot.

nv:AJR6.title: Urges Congress to extend the Social Security Fairness Act.
nv:AJR6.summary: Urges Congress to extend the Social Security Fairness Act, which repealed the Government Pension Offset and Windfall Elimination Provision, so it applies to benefits from December 2013 forward, and urges the President to sign it.

nv:AJR7.title: Proposes to amend the Nevada Constitution to revise provisions relating to the compensation of certain elected officers.
nv:AJR7.summary: Proposes a Nevada Constitution amendment creating a Citizens' Commission on Compensation for Certain Elected Officers to set pay and benefits for legislators and statewide constitutional officers, replacing the Legislature's authority to change those salaries by law.

nv:AJR8.title: Proposes to amend the Nevada Constitution to provide for the establishment of a business court.
nv:AJR8.summary: Proposes a Nevada Constitution amendment requiring the Legislature, as money allows, to provide for a business court with exclusive original jurisdiction over business disputes seeking equitable or declaratory relief, with judges appointed by the Governor from three nominees chosen by a commission.

nv:AJR9.title: Urges Congress to enact legislation to prohibit officers and agents of the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement in the United States Department of Homeland Security from entering schools and places of worship for the purposes of enforcing federal immigration laws.
nv:AJR9.summary: Urges Congress to enact legislation barring Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers and agents from entering schools and places of worship to enforce federal immigration law.

nv:SB1.title: Revises provisions governing the short-term lease of a passenger car. (BDR 43-26)
nv:SB1.summary: Allows, rather than requires, short-term passenger car rental companies to require proof of minimum liability insurance as a condition of renting a car.

nv:SB10.title: Revises provisions relating to real property. (BDR 10-38)
nv:SB10.summary: Caps at 1,000 per year the residential units that corporations, investment vehicles, LLCs and their affiliates may buy in Nevada, requires them to register with the Securities Division and report purchases, and voids purchases over the cap.

nv:SB100.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-197)
nv:SB100.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to adopt regulations on timely completion of election duties, requires officials to say whether they can meet deadlines, and sets notice and enforcement steps when a county or city official misses one. Also requires state approval of voting system vendors.

nv:SB101.title: Revises provisions relating to wildlife. (BDR 45-555)
nv:SB101.summary: Applies the ban on wasting edible portions of game to all big game mammals, including mountain lions and black bears, and removes the carnivore exception from the ban on taking only a head or hide.

nv:SB102.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-90)
nv:SB102.summary: Makes creating or serving in a false slate of presidential electors, or conspiring to, a category D felony, and submitting false election documents with intent to defraud a category C felony. Bars those convicted of the elector offense from election or appointment to public office.

nv:SB104.title: Makes appropriations to the Other State Education Programs Account for allocation to certain nonprofit organizations for the creation and maintenance of school gardens and to certain other nonprofit organizations.
nv:SB104.summary: Appropriates $200,000 in each of two fiscal years for nonprofit-run school garden programs, plus $250,000 for Mob Museum expansion planning, $100,000 for the Nevada Judicial Resource Center on Firearms and $250,000 to Raise the Future.

nv:SB106.title: Revises provisions relating to the operation of vessels. (BDR 43-371)
nv:SB106.summary: Makes it a misdemeanor to operate a vessel faster than 5 nautical miles per hour within 600 feet of the Lake Tahoe shoreline, and updates outdated Tahoe Regional Planning Agency ordinance references.

nv:SB108.title: Revises provisions governing the Account for the Channel Clearance, Maintenance, Restoration, Surveying and Monumenting Program. (BDR 48-88)
nv:SB108.summary: Raises to $500,000 the balance below which the State Engineer may request Contingency Account money for the channel clearance and monumenting grant program, counting only uncommitted money in the program's account.

nv:SB11.title: Revises provisions relating to the payment of extended unemployment benefits. (BDR 53-306)
nv:SB11.summary: Reduces weekly and total extended unemployment benefits by the same percentage as any federal sequestration cut to the state's federal extended-benefit payments.

nv:SB113.title: Revises provisions relating to parking privileges for persons with disabilities. (BDR 43-660)
nv:SB113.summary: Lets occupational therapists and physical therapists, in addition to physicians, physician assistants and advanced practice nurses, certify disability for disabled parking placards and plates, and lets their supervised staff complete the certification.

nv:SB114.title: Revises provisions governing certain landlords. (BDR 10-125)
nv:SB114.summary: Requires landlords of premises with more than 50 units (30 in smaller counties) intended for older residents to require criminal background checks of job applicants, set key-control policies and keep a key log, enforceable by civil action.

nv:SB115.title: Makes various changes relating to bilingual education. (BDR 34-790)
nv:SB115.summary: Requires Commission on Professional Standards regulations to include an endorsement requirement for teaching bilingual education (already in regulation), and lets school districts and charter schools pay a $2,500 yearly stipend to endorsed teachers, or those working toward it, in those programs.

nv:SB116.title: Revises provisions relating to the compensation of elected county officers. (BDR 20-92)
nv:SB116.summary: Sets elected county officers' base pay for 2025-26 and after using a formula tied to prior salaries or 3 percent above their highest-paid employee, and lets boards of county commissioners add a 2 percent cost-of-living increase.

nv:SB117.title: Revises provisions relating to services for veterans. (BDR 37-795)
nv:SB117.summary: Requires the Director of Veterans Services to give agencies, resource centers and programs serving veterans existing informational materials on applying to upgrade the character of a discharge or change its narrative reason.

nv:SB119.title: Revises provisions relating to the NV Grow Program.
nv:SB119.summary: Renames the NV Grow Program's administering division, requires it to post an annual report on assistance provided and participating businesses' growth, lowers the minimum revenue to qualify from $50,000 to $35,000, and appropriates $1.2 million.

nv:SB12.title: Revises provisions relating to the Office of the Chief Information Officer within the Office of the Governor. (BDR 19-280)
nv:SB12.summary: Renames the Office of the Chief Information Officer the Governor's Technology Office, renames its units, moves the Information Security deputy chief to the unclassified service, and has the Chief Information Officer replace the Administration director on the Information Technology Advisory Board.

nv:SB120.title: Revises provisions relating to the administration of justice. (BDR 1-711)
nv:SB120.summary: Bars courts from charging interest or fees on payment plans for fines and assessments, and from ordering defendants with publicly appointed attorneys to repay the cost of that representation, repealing the current repayment authority.

nv:SB121.title: Revises provisions governing common-interest communities. (BDR 10-80)
nv:SB121.summary: Bars homeowner associations from requiring back yard landscaping sooner than 24 months after a first purchase from the builder (allowing a thin rock layer after 12 months), charging late fees sooner than 30 days past due, or reporting past-due obligations to credit agencies.

nv:SB124.title: Revises provisions relating to health care. (BDR 54-38)
nv:SB124.summary: Lets the Board of Medical Examiners issue limited medical licenses to qualified foreign-trained physicians, who practice under supervision and can earn an unrestricted license after 2 years of full-time practice in good standing, with an annual report to the Legislature.

nv:SB125.title: Revises provisions relating to services provided to victims of crime. (BDR 16-631)
nv:SB125.summary: Lets government entities share certain confidential information with the statewide crime victim assistance center for the limited purpose of providing support services to crime victims.

nv:SB128.title: Makes changes related to health care. (BDR 57-87)
nv:SB128.summary: Bars health insurers from relying solely on artificial intelligence or automated tools to deny, modify or reduce prior authorization for care, and requires approval of covered care unless a qualified clinician finds it unnecessary or experimental.

nv:SB13.title: Revises provisions relating to the disposition of bail. (BDR 14-471)
nv:SB13.summary: Lets a court dispose of bail as agreed by all parties when no formal action is brought or the case is dismissed.

nv:SB130.title: Provides for the issuance by the State Contractors' Board of a restricted license. (BDR 54-628)
nv:SB130.summary: Lets the State Contractors' Board issue restricted licenses for work like that allowed under the B-7 residential remodeling subclass, with experience, a business course and bonding required, and a path to a full license after two years.

nv:SB132.title: Makes an appropriation to the Nevada Clean Energy Fund for securing and implementing grants for qualified clean energy projects.
nv:SB132.summary: Appropriates $500,000 from the General Fund to the Nevada Clean Energy Fund to secure and implement grants for qualified clean energy projects, with expenditure reports to the Interim Finance Committee.

nv:SB133.title: Makes an appropriation to the Nevada Center for Civic Engagement to support civics education programs.
nv:SB133.summary: Appropriates $250,000 in each of two fiscal years to the Nevada Center for Civic Engagement for K-12 civics programs and expanded adult civics education.

nv:SB135.title: Makes an appropriation to Communities In Schools of Nevada to provide integrated student support services.
nv:SB135.summary: Appropriates $1 million from the General Fund to Communities In Schools of Nevada for integrated student support services, with reports to the Interim Finance Committee.

nv:SB137.title: Requires the establishment of a program relating to medical emergencies. (BDR 40-702)
nv:SB137.summary: Requires the Division of Public and Behavioral Health to run a program to improve how Nevadans respond to medical emergencies, including increasing trained volunteers and notifying people in an emergency where volunteers and other resources are located.

nv:SB138.title: Makes revisions governing health care for pregnant women and newborn children. (BDR 40-580)
nv:SB138.summary: Requires hospitals with birthing services to screen pregnant patients for presumptive Medicaid eligibility, directly or by contract, and to notify parents of qualifying newborns about Supplemental Security Income and Medicaid. Also sets rights for parents of newborns in neonatal intensive care.

nv:SB140.title: Revises provisions governing certain programs of treatment established by the juvenile court. (BDR 5-62)
nv:SB140.summary: Expands the juvenile court treatment program now available for children with autism spectrum disorders to children diagnosed with or suspected of having neurobehavioral disorders from prenatal alcohol or controlled substance exposure.

nv:SB141.title: Revises provisions relating to local facilities for detention. (BDR 16-241)
nv:SB141.summary: Requires the sheriff, police chief or town marshal running a county, city or town jail to develop a policy on supervision, housing and medical and mental health care of transgender, gender non-conforming, non-binary and intersex prisoners, and allows staff cultural-competency training.

nv:SB142.title: Revises provisions governing property that is exempt from execution. (BDR 2-707)
nv:SB142.summary: Requires the Department of Taxation to adjust limits on property exempt from creditor seizure, such as homestead equity, by the regional CPI on April 1, 2026 and every 3 years. Also revises the exempt share of wages and sets a $5,000 bank account exemption.

nv:SB147.title: Creates the Southern Nevada Regional Planning for Economic Resiliency Pilot Program.
nv:SB147.summary: Creates a Southern Nevada pilot program, run by the Regional Transportation Commission with an advisory committee, to evaluate regional planning for infrastructure, transit and economic development and report a regional infrastructure plan to a legislative committee.

nv:SB15.title: Revises various provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 30-464)
nv:SB15.summary: Removes the August requirement for debt management commission annual meetings, bars county treasurer offices from closing before 5 p.m., sets delinquent-tax deadlines at the treasurer's close of business, ends school associate superintendent reports to counties, and cuts franchise-notice postings.

nv:SB155.title: Revises provisions governing peace officers. (BDR 23-326)
nv:SB155.summary: Lets people legally authorized to work in the U.S. who have worked as peace officers in another state be employed as Nevada peace officers starting January 1, 2026, and bars the state standards commission from requiring U.S. citizenship for them.

nv:SB156.title: Revises provisions relating to the prevention of gun violence. (BDR 18-958)
nv:SB156.summary: Requires the Attorney General to appoint a Special Counsel for the Prevention of Gun Violence to advise on gun violence prevention, collect gun-law arrest and prosecution data, and optionally run a grant program for prevention initiatives.

nv:SB157.title: Revises provisions relating to the testing of cannabis and cannabis products. (BDR 56-962)
nv:SB157.summary: Requires, rather than allows, the Cannabis Compliance Board to adopt testing regulations, including testing of representative samples of each cannabis lot by an independent lab, with lots defined by maximum weight per harvest batch.

nv:SB16.title: Revises provisions relating to contractors. (BDR 54-254)
nv:SB16.summary: Lets the Contractors' Board refuse a license for up to a year to unlicensed people who bid on jobs of $1,000 or more, and makes interfering with a Board investigation or proceeding grounds for discipline and unlawful.

nv:SB160.title: Revises provisions relating to the Nevada Equal Rights Commission. (BDR 18-82)
nv:SB160.summary: Moves the Nevada Equal Rights Commission from the Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation to the Attorney General's office, which appoints its members and administrator, and requires the Commission to publish a summary of the EEOC appeal process.

nv:SB161.title: Revises provisions relating to local government employees. (BDR 23-34)
nv:SB161.summary: Lets school districts and teacher unions that mutually agree submit unresolved contract issues to binding arbitration near the start of a school year or after an agreement expires, and sets how the arbitrator is chosen and rules.

nv:SB162.title: Revises provisions relating to state financing. (BDR 31-789)
nv:SB162.summary: Requires an entity, as a condition of accepting a state appropriation, to agree to comply with civil rights and employment laws that apply to it.

nv:SB165.title: Establishes provisions relating to behavioral health. (BDR 54-145)
nv:SB165.summary: Creates licensing for behavioral health and wellness practitioners under the Board of Psychological Examiners, bars unlicensed practice of behavioral health promotion and prevention, creates a confidentiality privilege, and requires Medicaid to cover their services.

nv:SB166.title: Revises provisions relating to housing. (BDR 57-713)
nv:SB166.summary: Expands the ban on insurers refusing, cancelling or raising rates over a dog's breed to cover multi-family dwellings and cases where breed is not the sole basis; requires supportive housing grant recipients to let tenants keep at least one pet.

nv:SB167.title: Prohibits the importation and sale of household cleaning products for which animal testing was performed. (BDR 52-892)
nv:SB167.summary: Bars manufacturers from selling household cleaning products in Nevada if animal testing was done on or after January 1, 2030, with exceptions for legal requirements, foreign regulators, lack of alternative methods, and earlier testing.

nv:SB168.title: Revises provisions relating to cannabis. (BDR 56-553)
nv:SB168.summary: Limits Cannabis Compliance Board hold orders to products that fail requirements and pose a substantial health hazard, lets production facilities handle usable cannabis, excludes seeds from usable cannabis, and bars rules requiring extra wholesale labels or duplicate label information.

nv:SB169.title: Prohibits a third-party reservation service platform provider from engaging in certain activities. (BDR 52-627)
nv:SB169.summary: Bars online reservation platforms from listing or selling reservations at an establishment without a written agreement authorizing it, makes violations a deceptive trade practice subject to civil enforcement only, and exempts document preparation services.

nv:SB17.title: Revises provisions relating to specialty courts. (BDR 14-474)
nv:SB17.summary: Narrows who qualifies for misdemeanor preprosecution diversion by excluding certain charges and prior convictions, and confirms district, justice and municipal courts may run substance use treatment programs, with provisional referral pending assessment.

nv:SB170.title: Revises provisions relating to industrial insurance. (BDR 53-632)
nv:SB170.summary: Requires, starting July 1, 2026, firefighters outside the state executive branch, and volunteer firefighters, to get employer-paid cancer screenings at coverage start and annually, and sets examiner and test requirements for physical exams of covered firefighters, arson investigators and police officers.

nv:SB171.title: Enacts a shield law to protect the transgender community. (BDR 54-12)
nv:SB171.summary: Bars health licensing boards from disciplining or denying licenses over medically necessary gender-affirming care lawful in Nevada, bars the Governor from extraditing people charged in other states over such care (with exceptions), limits state help with out-of-state proceedings, and has boards study reciprocal licensing.

nv:SB172.title: Prescribes certain rights for agricultural workers. (BDR 53-959)
nv:SB172.summary: Requires a meal period of at least a half hour for agricultural employees working 5 continuous hours, applies limits on valuing employer-provided lodging and meals as wages to them, and creates an Agricultural Workers' Bill of Rights.

nv:SB173.title: Establishes provisions relating to the environment. (BDR 52-585)
nv:SB173.summary: Makes utensils and condiments in delivery orders opt-in, bans manufacturers from selling carpets, cosmetics, food packaging and certain other products with intentionally added PFAS from 2026, sets aside redevelopment revenue for shade landscaping, and requires formaldehyde testing of hair products in Clark County.

nv:SB175.title: Revises provisions governing the treatment of certain military credentials in the licensure and hiring of educational personnel. (BDR 34-663)
nv:SB175.summary: Requires rules letting Junior ROTC-certified service members and veterans receive a teaching endorsement for JROTC, and makes school districts count active service members' Joint Services Transcripts as credit toward licensure.

nv:SB177.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-942)
nv:SB177.summary: As passed by the Senate, lets principals suspend homeless or foster-care students for five days or less without weighing that status; on the sixth school day, requires a meeting on whether it caused the conduct and, if so, ends the suspension and adds support.

nv:SB179.title: Revises provisions relating to discrimination. (BDR 18-35)
nv:SB179.summary: Requires the Nevada Equal Rights Commission, when investigating alleged housing, employment or public accommodation discrimination based on religious creed, to consider whether it was motivated by antisemitism, defined by the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance 2016 working definition.

nv:SB180.title: Revises provisions relating to motor carriers. (BDR 58-963)
nv:SB180.summary: Requires certain freight-only motor carriers to file liability insurance or a bond of at least $1,000,000 from January 1, 2026, $1,250,000 from 2028 and $1,500,000 from 2030.

nv:SB181.title: Provides for the issuance of special license plates indicating support for Nevada State University. (BDR 43-787)
nv:SB181.summary: Creates Nevada State University special license plates, with a $35 initial and $10 renewal fee plus additional fees of $25 and $20 shared by the university's athletics programs and its foundation.

nv:SB182.title: Revises provisions relating to the staffing of health care facilities. (BDR 40-33)
nv:SB182.summary: Sets maximum patient-to-nurse ratios for hospitals in counties of 100,000 or more people, adds technical and service staffing committees beside nurse committees, requires compliance records, bars retaliation for reports, and allows discipline for violations.

nv:SB183.title: Revises provisions relating to caseworkers of agencies which provide child welfare services. (BDR 38-710)
nv:SB183.summary: Bars child welfare agencies from assigning more than 30 children in agency custody to a caseworker providing permanency services, except to keep siblings together or temporarily under an agency emergency policy.

nv:SB185.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicaid reimbursement for care of disabled or chronically ill children. (BDR 38-760)
nv:SB185.summary: Requires Medicaid to reimburse family members who provide personal care services to a Medicaid recipient under 18 who has a disability or chronic illness preventing them from doing daily activities unaided, and appropriates money for it.

nv:SB188.title: Establishes procedures to assist certain persons with limited English proficiency in accessing health care in certain circumstances. (BDR 40-41)
nv:SB188.summary: Requires health facilities and providers to take reasonable steps so language barriers do not block patients with limited English proficiency from care, including free, accurate and timely interpretation or translation, codifying similar federal rules.

nv:SB189.title: Provides for the licensure and regulation of genetic counselors. (BDR 54-69)
nv:SB189.summary: Requires genetic counselors to be licensed by the Board of Medical Examiners, with education, exam and American Board of Genetic Counseling certification requirements and temporary licenses, and makes unlicensed practice a felony.

nv:SB19.title: Authorizes the Governor to enter into certain interstate fire compacts. (BDR 47-381)
nv:SB19.summary: Ratifies the Great Plains Wildland Fire Protection Compact and the Northwest Wildland Fire Protection Agreement, letting Nevada exchange firefighting aid with member states, and directs the Governor to notify those states.

nv:SB191.title: Revises provisions relating to court reporters and court reporting firms. (BDR 54-14)
nv:SB191.summary: Replaces fixed statutory fees for certified court reporters and court reporting firms with fees set by Board regulation, starting at current amounts and adjustable between 90 and 125 percent. Also raises state district court reporters' pay for certain services.

nv:SB192.title: Revises provisions relating to public health. (BDR 40-86)
nv:SB192.summary: Requires hospitals and birthing centers to provide sign language interpreters to birthing patients and allow a doula present, requires insurers to cover doulas, limits race-based health formulas to board-approved lists, and requires assessments for some children leaving child welfare custody.

nv:SB193.title: Establishes a pilot program to reduce interest rates on mortgage loans to certain eligible borrowers. (BDR 25-42)
nv:SB193.summary: Creates a pilot program to buy down the interest rate on 30-year fixed-rate mortgages for first-time homebuyers with household income up to 160 percent of the county median.

nv:SB194.title: Revises provisions governing the short-term lease of a passenger car. (BDR 43-715)
nv:SB194.summary: Requires short-term car rental companies to require proof of qualifying insurance, lets them sell or refer temporary insurance policies at no more than the standard market rate, and says doing so is not an unfair practice.

nv:SB196.title: Authorizes a heavy equipment rental company to charge a recovery fee to offset taxes levied on certain heavy equipment. (BDR 32-19)
nv:SB196.summary: Lets heavy equipment rental companies charge renters a recovery fee of up to 2 percent of the rental charge to offset property taxes on the equipment, shown separately on invoices and kept in a separate account.

nv:SB198.title: Revises requirements relating to payment of wages and compensation to certain employees. (BDR 53-557)
nv:SB198.summary: Requires bonuses, profit sharing, fringe benefits and retirement matching contributions owed to an employee who is fired, resigns or quits to be paid on the regular payday rather than immediately or within 7 days, and revises the late-payment penalty.

nv:SB2.title: Revises provisions relating to legislative affairs. (BDR 17-30)
nv:SB2.summary: Clarifies that sales proceeds from food and items in legislative buildings go to the Legislative Fund, that the Revised Statutes' organization does not assign agencies to a branch of government, and that a Carson City parcel is legislative property; appropriates money for legislative security.

nv:SB20.title: Revises provisions relating to judicial administration. (BDR 14-476)
nv:SB20.summary: Lets justice courts record jury trials with sound equipment instead of requiring a court reporter, requires keeping recordings of certain criminal proceedings at least 5 years, and exempts public-assistance data from jury lists where federal law bars its use.

nv:SB201.title: Prohibits certain restrictions on the display of religious or cultural items under certain circumstances. (BDR 10-122)
nv:SB201.summary: Restricts homeowner associations and landlords from prohibiting residents from displaying items tied to sincerely held religious or cultural beliefs, with certain exceptions.

nv:SB202.title: Revises provisions relating to real property. (BDR 15-729)
nv:SB202.summary: Makes it a crime to procure or offer a false rental agreement to commit housebreaking or unlawful occupancy, expands unlawful occupancy to any dwelling, defines squatters as non-tenants, and shortens the occupant's reentry and property-storage periods.

nv:SB203.title: Revises provisions relating to the pari-mutuel system of wagering. (BDR 41-608)
nv:SB203.summary: Lets horse racing tracks contract directly with race book, sports pool or gambling game operators instead of using disseminators, repeals the disseminator licensing scheme, and has operators of systems register with the Gaming Control Board rather than hold Commission licenses.

nv:SB207.title: Requires the establishment of a program of all-inclusive care for the elderly. (BDR 38-763)
nv:SB207.summary: Moves authority to establish a program of all-inclusive care for the elderly (PACE) from the Aging and Disability Services Division to the Department of Health and Human Services, which must establish it, and appropriates money for it.

nv:SB208.title: Revises provisions governing certain surcharges imposed by a county. (BDR 20-677)
nv:SB208.summary: Lets counties use the 911 telephone-system surcharge for the part of a facility housing and dedicated to the emergency call system, and raises the fund-balance cap that triggers surcharge reductions to $15,000,000 in counties of 700,000 or more.

nv:SB21.title: Revises provisions relating to outdoor recreation. (BDR 35-266)
nv:SB21.summary: Lets the Division of State Parks administrator name a designee to the Outdoor Recreation advisory board, and expands outdoor education grants to cover recreational infrastructure for pupils and projects improving public access to outdoor recreation.

nv:SB210.title: Revises provisions relating to fees collected by constables and sheriffs for certain services. (BDR 20-540)
nv:SB210.summary: Raises fees constables and sheriffs charge for services, such as serving a summons from $17 to $26, eviction service from $21 to $26, and mileage from $2 to $3 per mile.

nv:SB213.title: Revises provisions relating to the crime of unlawful dissemination of an intimate image. (BDR 15-776)
nv:SB213.summary: Expands the crime of unlawfully disseminating an intimate image to cover realistic digital and computer-generated images, removes the exception for public figures, and exempts violators under age 18.

nv:SB215.title: Revises provisions relating to wildlife. (BDR 45-576)
nv:SB215.summary: Requires the Board of Wildlife Commissioners to adopt rules for free salvage permits that let people collect wildlife killed in vehicle collisions, and allows barring those permits if any Nevada wildlife tests positive for chronic wasting disease.

nv:SB217.title: Makes revisions relating to reproductive health care. (BDR 40-24)
nv:SB217.summary: Bars governments from limits that single out and substantially burden assisted reproduction, shields providers from liability solely for providing it, declares a pre-implantation embryo not a human being under state law, and requires plans for groups over 50 to cover infertility treatment.

nv:SB218.title: Enacts the Uniform Antitrust Pre-Merger Notification Act. (BDR 52-938)
nv:SB218.summary: Enacts the Uniform Antitrust Pre-Merger Notification Act, requiring companies that file federal merger notices and have a Nevada base or certain Nevada sales to send the same filing to the Attorney General.

nv:SB225.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-361)
nv:SB225.summary: Requires each candidate who files to appear on a presidential preference primary ballot to pay a $1,000 filing fee.

nv:SB226.title: Revises provisions relating to legislative affairs. (BDR 17-365)
nv:SB226.summary: Makes the Public Lands and Sunset subcommittees stand-alone interim committees, lets Public Lands request four bills and requires three meetings outside Clark and Washoe counties and Carson City, and moves governmental purchasing review to the Government Affairs committee.

nv:SB229.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-680)
nv:SB229.summary: Lowers the GPA needed for the State Seal of Financial Literacy to 3.0, revises how students show financial literacy proficiency, and requires financial literacy instruction starting in kindergarten.

nv:SB231.title: Establishes provisions relating to the collection and destruction of unused drugs. (BDR 54-564)
nv:SB231.summary: Sets requirements for DEA-registered collectors that maintain secure drug take-back bins, limits Board of Pharmacy discipline for compliant collectors, and allocates $500,000 from the opioid settlement fund to the Board to help with destruction.

nv:SB233.title: Revises provisions relating to agriculture.
nv:SB233.summary: Requires the Council on Food Security to study long-term funding for the Home Feeds Nevada Agriculture Food Purchase Program, and appropriates $800,000 to the Nutritious Food Purchase Account to run the program.

nv:SB235.title: Revises provisions relating to wildlife. (BDR 45-113)
nv:SB235.summary: Lets people take shed antlers, skulls or heads, or bones from the carcass of tag-required wildlife for non-commercial purposes without the required tag under certain circumstances.

nv:SB24.title: Provides for the certification and regulation of emergency medical responders. (BDR 40-292)
nv:SB24.summary: Puts emergency medical responder certification into state law, under the same bodies that certify EMTs and paramedics, and makes it a misdemeanor to claim to be one without certification.

nv:SB240.title: Revises provisions relating to state business licenses. (BDR 7-126)
nv:SB240.summary: Lowers the state business license fee to $100 from July 1, 2027 for sole proprietorships, LLCs and partnerships with not more than 50 employees.

nv:SB241.title: Revises provisions relating to juvenile probation. (BDR 5-493)
nv:SB241.summary: Limits juvenile probation to 18 months regardless of how many unlawful acts a child committed, unless an exception applies, and lets the court end probation for a child who has not paid full restitution but met other conditions.

nv:SB245.title: Makes various changes relating to education. (BDR 34-827)
nv:SB245.summary: Creates an Advisory Council on Civics Education in the Department of Education to help set criteria for the State Seal of Civics program, and revises the grade point average and exam requirements for earning the seal.

nv:SB246.title: Revises provisions relating to health insurance coverage for gynecological or obstetrical services. (BDR 57-205)
nv:SB246.summary: Extends the rule letting women get gynecological or obstetrical care without a referral to more plans, including Medicaid and the state employee plan, and lets women designate an OB-GYN as their primary care physician.

nv:SB25.title: Revises provisions relating to fire protection. (BDR 42-249)
nv:SB25.summary: Removes the State Forester Firewarden's duty to cooperate with the State Fire Marshal on vegetation fire prevention, drops the Fire Marshal Division's statutory sections, adds cannabis production facilities to the Marshal's oversight, and widens which fires the Marshal investigates.

nv:SB251.title: Revises provisions relating to psychological assistants, psychological interns and psychological trainees. (BDR 54-714)
nv:SB251.summary: Replaces registration of psychological assistants and psychological interns with provisional licenses from the Board of Psychological Examiners, and requires interns to have completed required doctoral coursework.

nv:SB256.title: Revises provisions relating to gaming. (BDR 41-146)
nv:SB256.summary: Requires people to forfeit to the State General Fund any profit from certain illegal gaming activities, in addition to existing penalties, and raises the penalty for certain unlawful wager-taking from a misdemeanor to a gross misdemeanor under some circumstances.

nv:SB257.title: Revises provisions relating to autism. (BDR 38-106)
nv:SB257.summary: Drops the required protocol and standardized instrument from the statewide autism assessment standard, lets any health care provider within their scope of practice assess and diagnose, and requires certain health plans to cover such diagnosis and treatment and accept diagnoses made under the standard.

nv:SB258.title: Revises provisions relating to industrial insurance. (BDR 53-594)
nv:SB258.summary: Caps the industrial insurer's lien on a worker's third-party recovery at the lesser of the lien minus half the recovery costs, or one-third of the recovery minus half the costs, and requires verified itemized cost statements.

nv:SB26.title: Revises provisions authorizing certain entities to obtain information relating to the records of criminal history of certain persons responsible for the safety and well-being of children, elderly persons or persons with disabilities. (BDR 14-248)
nv:SB26.summary: Lets organizations that care for children, elderly people or people with disabilities request criminal history checks on their independent contractors and vendors, and removes state-law wording that duplicates the federal definition of covered individuals.

nv:SB260.title: Revises provisions relating to air quality. (BDR 53-961)
nv:SB260.summary: Requires state regulations setting employer measures against wildfire smoke exposure at air quality index 150 to 199 and at 200 or more, setting an index level that bars outdoor critical tasks, and requiring a worker warning and reporting system.

nv:SB262.title: Revises provisions relating to graduate medical education. (BDR 18-120)
nv:SB262.summary: Moves the Graduate Medical Education Grant Program from the Governor's science office to the Department of Health and Human Services, and expands grants to residency programs training more residents than Medicare funds.

nv:SB263.title: Revises provisions relating to pornography involving minors. (BDR 15-520)
nv:SB263.summary: Extends the ban on preparing or distributing child sexual abuse material to computer-generated material, and makes a second or later violation a category A felony with a maximum of life imprisonment.

nv:SB266.title: Revises provisions governing the Student Loan Repayment for Providers of Health Care in Underserved Communities Program. (BDR 18-1064)
nv:SB266.summary: Adds marriage and family therapists and clinical, licensed or certified alcohol and drug counselors to the providers eligible for the Student Loan Repayment for Providers of Health Care in Underserved Communities Program.

nv:SB268.title: Revises provisions relating to insurance coverage for certain dental services. (BDR 57-329)
nv:SB268.summary: Codifies in statute the services dental hygienists with a public health endorsement may provide without dentist supervision, and requires health plans, including Medicaid, to cover those services when provided by endorsed hygienists employed by nonprofits, to the same extent as under dentist supervision.

nv:SB27.title: Revises provisions relating to museums. (BDR 33-281)
nv:SB27.summary: Renames the Nevada State Museum the Nevada State Museum Carson City, requires the Board of Museums and History to set policies and charges for Division services, and removes its say over certain museum programs and property.

nv:SB273.title: Revises provisions governing the confidentiality of the personal information of certain persons. (BDR 20-966)
nv:SB273.summary: Lets civilian employees supporting law enforcement agencies, and firefighters and retired firefighters, obtain court orders keeping their personal information confidential in assessor, recorder, Secretary of State and clerk records, and request an alternate address on their driver's license or ID card.

nv:SB274.title: Revises provisions governing state boards and commissions. (BDR 18-973)
nv:SB274.summary: Has the Legislative Commission chair appoint the Sunset Subcommittee's chair and vice chair, ends quarterly occupational-licensing board reports on criminal history petitions, and repeals the subcommittee's review of licensing criminal history rules.

nv:SB275.title: Revises provisions relating to domestic relations. (BDR 11-541)
nv:SB275.summary: Bars courts from ordering reunification treatment in certain circumstances or removing a child from a parent solely to repair the child's relationship with the other parent, and limits who may give expert evidence on alleged abuse in custody cases.

nv:SB276.title: Revises provisions relating to water. (BDR 40-750)
nv:SB276.summary: Requires cities, counties, water and wastewater districts and authorities to notify the Division of Environmental Protection of sewage or unauthorized discharges into state waters, requires the Division to notify affected Indian tribes, and requires giving tribes requested public records on incidents and water treatment policies.

nv:SB277.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-786)
nv:SB277.summary: Requires public schools in counties of 700,000 or more to employ a school social worker when money allows, immunizes districts from harassment liability if they publish an enforced prevention policy, and lets employed school staff complete counseling or psychology internships on the job.

nv:SB278.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-788)
nv:SB278.summary: Directs the Commission on Professional Standards in Education to consider improving access to licensure, ends local assessments for identifying reading deficiencies, ends school district and charter school reports on reading interventions, and sets when pupils can stop receiving reading services.

nv:SB279.title: Revises provisions relating to law enforcement. (BDR 23-1023)
nv:SB279.summary: Requires the written notice to a peace officer under investigation to describe the alleged acts or omissions with specificity, with the date, time and location of the alleged misconduct, and bars interviewing an officer as a witness on less than 48 hours' written notice.

nv:SB28.title: Revises provisions relating to municipalities. (BDR 22-411)
nv:SB28.summary: Adds affordable housing, multi-family housing, transit-oriented development, fixed guideway, high-capacity transit and transportation projects to those a tax increment area can fund, set in areas planned for transit-oriented development or other master-plan uses.

nv:SB280.title: Makes an appropriation to the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, School of Dental Medicine for cleft and craniofacial health care.
nv:SB280.summary: Appropriates $1,314,000 to the UNLV School of Dental Medicine for a cleft and craniofacial medical team that must hold monthly clinics and serve children under 3 and, if resources allow, older children with special needs.

nv:SB281.title: Revises provisions relating to certain foster care and behavioral health programs.
nv:SB281.summary: Requires a $2.5 million allocation from the opioid settlement fund to reimburse Clark and Washoe counties and the state child welfare division for programs for 18-to-22-year-olds leaving foster care; appropriates money for a jail-based behavioral health program and a UNR graduate certification.

nv:SB284.title: Revises provisions relating to child welfare. (BDR 38-747)
nv:SB284.summary: Requires child welfare agencies to determine whether children in their custody qualify for Social Security or Veterans Affairs benefits and apply for them, and repeals the trust funds that held such benefits to pay for the child's care.

nv:SB285.title: Revises provisions relating to apprenticeships. (BDR 53-91)
nv:SB285.summary: Requires an apprenticeship program covering more than one construction trade to have separate standards for each trade, and lets programs already approved under combined standards keep using them until they are voided or superseded.

nv:SB287.title: Revises provisions relating to public works. (BDR 28-949)
