nv:SB287.summary: Adds each worker's daily and weekly hours and overtime to the records public works contractors must keep, and lets joint labor-management committees inspect the otherwise confidential records of workers' license numbers.

nv:SB290.title: Revises provisions relating to regional transportation commissions. (BDR 22-743)
nv:SB290.summary: Lets designated security staff of a regional transportation commission remove from commission vehicles or property anyone using profane or indecent language, quarreling, annoying passengers, or refusing to leave after refusing to pay fare.

nv:SB291.title: Requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to establish procedures by which a victim of identity theft may obtain a new driver's license number. (BDR 43-39)
nv:SB291.summary: Requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to set procedures for identity theft victims to request a new unique driver's license number, and bars the Department from charging a fee for the change.

nv:SB292.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicare supplemental policies. (BDR 57-1069)
nv:SB292.summary: Requires insurers selling Medicare supplement policies in Nevada to let people under 65 who are on Medicare due to disability or end-stage renal disease buy the same policies offered to those 65 and older, with limits on their premiums and conditions.

nv:SB293.title: Revises provisions relating to intercollegiate athletics. (BDR 34-1088)
nv:SB293.summary: Removes bans on colleges enforcing rules against, compensating athletes for, or reducing scholarships over name, image and likeness pay, and lets athletes contract with institutions and athletic associations for it.

nv:SB294.title: Revises provisions relating to physician assistants. (BDR 54-965)
nv:SB294.summary: Requires the medical and osteopathic boards to adopt regulations letting one supervising physician oversee at least six physician assistants at once, up from the current limit of three.

nv:SB295.title: Revises provisions related to food establishments. (BDR 40-44)
nv:SB295.summary: Requires local health boards in counties of 100,000 or more (and cities in them) to publish multilingual guidance on sidewalk food vendor rules and to adopt vendor regulations, including on cart design and modular conveyances.

nv:SB297.title: Revises provisions relating to periods of observance. (BDR 19-803)
nv:SB297.summary: Designates October each year as Menopause Awareness Month and requires the Governor to issue an annual proclamation encouraging observance and calling for education and access to health care during menopause.

nv:SB298.title: Revises provisions relating to peace officers. (BDR 23-1031)
nv:SB298.summary: Adds denial of a seniority or pay increase, for purposes of punishment, to the actions treated as punitive against peace officers, and bars law enforcement agencies from imposing it during an investigation, with exceptions.

nv:SB299.title: Revises provisions relating to senior living communities. (BDR 40-1039)
nv:SB299.summary: Requires senior living community referral agencies to register with the Division of Public and Behavioral Health instead of being licensed by the State Board of Health, requires regulations for registration, and lets agencies operate without either until 120 days after those regulations take effect.

nv:SB3.title: Revises provisions relating to public assistance. (BDR 38-20)
nv:SB3.summary: Creates the Silver State General Assistance Program to give temporary cash or in-kind aid to eligible households during a governor-declared extraordinary circumstance, funded by transfers from the General Fund when a minimum balance remains.

nv:SB30.title: Revises provisions relating to prisoners. (BDR 16-252)
nv:SB30.summary: Removes the district judge from those who must receive pardon hearing notices and applications, lets district judges testify, drops court objection as a condition for expedited rights restoration, and requires releasing parole decision records for a named prisoner.

nv:SB300.title: Makes revisions relating to Medicaid. (BDR 38-110)
nv:SB300.summary: Requires Medicaid, where federal funding is available, to cover medication for opioid use disorder, and to cover services at federally qualified health centers from clinical professional counselors, alcohol and drug counselors and supervised master's-level interns.

nv:SB301.title: Revises provisions relating to public employees. (BDR 23-1024)
nv:SB301.summary: Allows state peace officers in the unclassified service (categories I, II and III) to bargain collectively with the Executive Department, adding them to the state employees covered by the collective bargaining law.

nv:SB303.title: Revises provisions relating to civil liability to persons using certain premises for recreational activity under certain circumstances. (BDR 3-1021)
nv:SB303.summary: Names the recreational-use liability law the Recreational Use of Land Statute and limits liability of the State, local governments and certain nonprofits for injuries on recreational premises such as designated trails, parks and washes that meet listed conditions.

nv:SB305.title: Revises provisions relating to interscholastic activities. (BDR 34-1007)
nv:SB305.summary: Requires the Nevada Interscholastic Activities Association to adopt regulations by October 1, 2025 for designating sanctioned sports, with priority for club sports, and shifts that authority to the Nevada Association of School Superintendents if it does not.

nv:SB309.title: Revises provisions relating to crimes. (BDR 43-906)
nv:SB309.summary: Raises the minimum jail or residential confinement term for second-offense DUI from 10 to 20 days, lowers the blood alcohol level triggering a substance use disorder evaluation from 0.18 to 0.16, and changes eligibility for treatment programs.

nv:SB31.title: Revises provisions relating to the adjudication of vested water rights. (BDR 48-260)
nv:SB31.summary: Clarifies that federal agencies need not submit proof of vested water right claims by December 31, 2027, and revises notices of pending water rights adjudications to require federal agencies to make proof of claim.

nv:SB311.title: Imposes certain requirements upon certain alarm companies. (BDR 52-730)
nv:SB311.summary: Requires alarm companies charging monthly monitoring fees to repair or replace a defective system within 5 business days of notice, or cancel and refund unearned money without penalty; violations are deceptive trade practices.

nv:SB312.title: Enacts provisions relating to the health of American Indians. (BDR 38-347)
nv:SB312.summary: Creates a Tribal Health Authority Council in the Department of Native American Affairs to adopt a plan to increase American Indians' health care access and request up to two bills; lets tribes determine presumptive Medicaid eligibility where federal law allows.

nv:SB315.title: Authorizes the Department of Transportation to enter into a progressive design-build contract for a certain project.
nv:SB315.summary: Authorizes the Department of Transportation to use progressive design-build contracts, covering preconstruction, final design and construction, for improvements to Interstate 80 East between Vista Boulevard in Sparks and USA Parkway in Storey County, and sets the procurement process.

nv:SB316.title: Revises provisions relating to insurance. (BDR 57-777)
nv:SB316.summary: Expands pharmacy benefit manager rules to cover pharmacist services, bars managers from steering people to affiliated pharmacies, requires fee disclosures and annual reports, sets civil penalties of $1,000 to $7,500 per violation, and caps insurer cost-sharing at the drug net price.

nv:SB317.title: Revises provisions relating to industrial insurance. (BDR 53-625)
nv:SB317.summary: Changes industrial insurance rules: lets insurers' legal representatives keep the required in-state office, replaces the $36,000 per-employee pay maximum in premium calculations for most employers, requires a drug formulary, and revises hearing, stress-injury and temporary partial disability provisions.

nv:SB318.title: Revises provisions relating to charter schools. (BDR 34-89)
nv:SB318.summary: Requires charter schools to give their sponsor notice of building projects costing over $100,000, plus competitive bidding documents and prevailing wage records.

nv:SB319.title: Requires the Washoe County Board of County Commissioners, Reno City Council and Sparks City Council to establish a board to study the creation of a county fire protection district within certain territory.
nv:SB319.summary: Requires Washoe County, Reno and Sparks to set up, by interlocal agreement, a board to study creating a county fire protection district to consolidate fire services in part of the area, and to report its findings.

nv:SB320.title: Revises provisions relating to crosswalks. (BDR 43-9)
nv:SB320.summary: Applies the 20-foot no-parking rule to unmarked as well as marked crosswalks, lets local governments set a greater distance if signed, and limits enforcement to warnings with posted notice through December 31, 2026.

nv:SB321.title: Revises provisions relating to public utilities. (BDR 58-1078)
nv:SB321.summary: Raises the maximum civil penalty for violating natural gas pipeline safety rules to match federal limits, now $272,926 per violation per day and $2,729,245 per related series, and removes the authority to deduct penalties from money the State owes the violator.

nv:SB322.title: Revises provisions relating to the Board of Regents of the University of Nevada. (BDR 34-764)
nv:SB322.summary: Requires each Board of Regents member to complete 6 hours of professional development training in the first and third year of each term, including annual training on the Open Meeting Law and eliminating bias.

nv:SB323.title: Revises provisions relating to offenders. (BDR 16-709)
nv:SB323.summary: Makes permanent the free daily phone call program for inmates at Florence McClure Women's Correctional Center, caps charges for inmate calls at actual cost, and requires phone contracts to follow federal refund rules.

nv:SB324.title: Establishes prohibitions relating to the sale of water in certain disposable plastic bottles in communities abutting the Lake Tahoe Watershed. (BDR 40-216)
nv:SB324.summary: Bans selling water in disposable plastic bottles of 4 liters or less in communities bordering the Lake Tahoe Watershed, with a warning, then fines of up to $100, $200 and $500 for repeat violations within a year.

nv:SB325.title: Authorizes certain counties and cities to establish a program relating to the adoption of certain animals. (BDR 20-1004)
nv:SB325.summary: Lets counties and cities that run or fund an animal shelter waive adoption fees for animals aged 6 months or older held 7+ days, one per veteran, law enforcement officer or first responder per 6 months, with identification and biennial reports to the Legislature.

nv:SB326.title: Requires certain public utilities to submit an annual report to the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada relating to the infrastructure of the public utility. (BDR 58-1084)
nv:SB326.summary: Requires small water and sewer utilities in counties of 700,000 or more that serve at least 250 people to file an annual infrastructure report with the Public Utilities Commission, including fire-protection water supply adequacy and water rights.

nv:SB327.title: Revises provisions relating to contractors. (BDR 54-1025)
nv:SB327.summary: Changes who may provide bonds required of contractor license applicants and licensees, replacing the requirement of an "A" or better debt rating with listing in U.S. Treasury Department Circular No. 570 as a certificate-holding company.

nv:SB329.title: Requires certain persons to complete training relating to elderly persons and persons with cognitive impairments. (BDR 40-1086)
nv:SB329.summary: Allows a large-county district board of health or the State Board of Health to require EMT and paramedic certification applicants to complete training on interacting with elderly and cognitively impaired people; the training does not raise their standard of care.

nv:SB330.title: Revises provisions relating to facilities for skilled nursing. (BDR 40-584)
nv:SB330.summary: Clarifies that a skilled nursing facility provides inpatient care, and requires cities and counties to use the state-law term for such facilities in their ordinances where those facilities exist or are referenced.

nv:SB334.title: Revises provisions relating to the employment of offenders. (BDR 16-1115)
nv:SB334.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to report to the Legislature each March 1 on inmate employment, including numbers eligible, employed and refusing work, pay, education, account deductions, and post-release employment.

nv:SB336.title: Establishes provisions relating to portable benefit accounts. (BDR 53-621)
nv:SB336.summary: Lets sole proprietors and independent contractors open portable benefit accounts for health coverage, medical costs, income replacement insurance, life insurance or retirement, and lets the businesses that hire them contribute, including by withholding a percentage of payments.

nv:SB338.title: Revises provisions relating to the sale of tickets to a live entertainment event. (BDR 52-590)
nv:SB338.summary: Requires live-event ticket sellers to clearly disclose the total ticket price, including mandatory fees, before showing or advertising prices, bars misrepresenting fees, requires refunds in certain cases, and repeals a narrower resale disclosure law.

nv:SB340.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 18-1008)
nv:SB340.summary: Lets a person or the adopting agency petition the Legislative Commission to suspend or nullify a regulation that exceeds statutory authority or legislative intent, and requires an oral public hearing on all proposed regulations when one is requested.

nv:SB343.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 49-972)
nv:SB343.summary: Renames the Agricultural Extension Department the University of Nevada Cooperative Extension, defines the State 4-H Camp's purpose, and changes State 4-H Camp Advisory Council appointments and term limits.

nv:SB344.title: Requires certain health insurance to cover certain screenings for certain genetic disorders. (BDR 57-1104)
nv:SB344.summary: Requires group health plans, fraternal benefit societies and Medicaid to cover noninvasive prenatal blood screening for fetal chromosomal abnormalities, without prior authorization.

nv:SB346.title: Makes various changes relating to guardianship. (BDR 13-217)
nv:SB346.summary: Requires guardianship petitions to attest that less restrictive alternatives were explained, has physicians assess whether such alternatives are sufficient, requires guardian reports to explain why they were not used, and allows ending a guardianship if the person has entered such an alternative.

nv:SB347.title: Revises provisions relating to mental health crisis holds. (BDR 39-8)
nv:SB347.summary: Allows officers to immediately seize a firearm from or near a person placed on a mental health crisis hold, and requires its return after treatment unless a protection-order application is filed or the person is legally barred from having it.

nv:SB348.title: Makes revisions relating to laboratory testing. (BDR 40-123)
nv:SB348.summary: Authorizes the State Public Health Laboratory to charge up to $150, or the Medicaid rate if lower, for newborn screening tests from 2026, and requires Medicaid to reimburse them separately from labor, delivery and newborn care.

nv:SB349.title: Revises provisions relating to anatomical gifts. (BDR 40-543)
nv:SB349.summary: Allows organ procurement organizations to transport, or arrange transport of, a deceased donor's body or part when medical equipment is needed to preserve suitability, and lets coroners require notice of such transport in their jurisdiction.

nv:SB35.title: Revises provisions governing certain offenses relating to prisoners. (BDR 16-444)
nv:SB35.summary: Raises penalties for prison staff, contractors and volunteers who commit sexual abuse of a prisoner from a category D to a category B felony and unauthorized custodial conduct to a category C felony, and broadens the intoxicant-smuggling ban.

nv:SB350.title: Revises provisions relating to the death penalty. (BDR 14-1110)
nv:SB350.summary: Changes the timing of executing death sentences, requiring the execution week to be 120 to 180 days after judgment (now 60 to 90) and, for new warrants, 120 to 180 days after the warrant (now 15 to 30).

nv:SB352.title: Revises provisions relating to health care. (BDR 57-712)
nv:SB352.summary: Adds race, color, national origin, sex, age, sexual orientation and disability to the bases on which insurers, including Medicaid, may not discriminate; bars providers from discriminating on those and gender identity; lets licensing boards adopt rules and discipline violators.

nv:SB353.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicaid.
nv:SB353.summary: Requires Medicaid to create a billing category and all-inclusive per diem rates for university-run training clinics for mental health professions, by October 1, 2025 if federal funding is available.

nv:SB358.title: Requires certain units of government of this State to accept certain forms of payment. (BDR 19-759)
nv:SB358.summary: Requires state and local government units to accept payment of fees, taxes and debts from businesses by debit card, credit card, check or electronic transfer, with certain exceptions, while allowing cash or money orders at their discretion.

nv:SB359.title: Makes various changes relating to drivers. (BDR 43-900)
nv:SB359.summary: Applies certain evidence rules to civil infraction hearings, lets cited people post a bond of up to the full penalty, allows counsel to appear for them, and requires dismissal if the officer neither appears nor submits a statement and no other sufficient evidence exists.

nv:SB36.title: Revises provisions relating to water. (BDR 48-384)
nv:SB36.summary: Requires retiring groundwater rights bought or donated under a new voluntary retirement program, creates an account for purchasing them, puts the Nevada Conservation and Recreation Program in statute, and lets water-system grants fund permanent water-right retirement.

nv:SB370.title: Revises provisions relating to manufactured housing. (BDR 43-754)
nv:SB370.summary: Requires the Housing Division to issue or deny a new certificate of title for a manufactured or mobile home within 45 days after application requirements are met, with written reasons for any denial, and to set up an expedited process by regulation.

nv:SB371.title: Revises provisions relating to crimes. (BDR 15-908)
nv:SB371.summary: Extends from 24 to 36 months how long a warning not to trespass remains valid for a misdemeanor trespass charge.

nv:SB372.title: Revises provisions relating to the care of children. (BDR 38-662)
nv:SB372.summary: Excludes from child abuse, neglect and parental-rights injury definitions a parent seeking mental health facility or hospital admission for a child whose behavioral health needs pose a risk to family safety, or bringing such a child into the home.

nv:SB373.title: Establishes requirements relating to multi-jurisdictional business licenses. (BDR 20-1073)
nv:SB373.summary: Requires Clark County and each incorporated city in it to adopt ordinances creating a multi-jurisdictional business license, with proposed business categories, and to integrate the application with the state business portal.

nv:SB374.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-752)
nv:SB374.summary: Requires schools to collect data on students in temporary alternative placement, requires school districts to provide staff training on student discipline and behavior, and has the Department of Education build a system to help address high levels of student discipline.

nv:SB375.title: Revises provisions relating to credit unions. (BDR 55-605)
nv:SB375.summary: Lets the Commissioner of Financial Institutions suspend credit union regulations for up to 90 days in emergencies or in the public interest, lowers required share par value from $5 to $1, and lets low-income credit unions issue shares to nonmembers.

nv:SB376.title: Revises provisions governing industrial insurance. (BDR 53-629)
nv:SB376.summary: Lets certain firefighters, arson investigators and police officers with occupational lung or heart disease claims see a physician of their own choice when the state panel has fewer than 12 available providers in the needed specialty, with reimbursement sought from the employer.

nv:SB378.title: Makes revisions relating to health care. (BDR 40-705)
nv:SB378.summary: Makes many health care changes, including licensing hospital-owned freestanding emergency facilities, requiring Medicaid value-based payments for them, Medicaid record audits, barring noncompete covenants for patient-facing providers, and requiring timely, fee-free release of health records.

nv:SB379.title: Revises provisions relating to commerce. (BDR 55-336)
nv:SB379.summary: Bars installment lenders from deceptive trade practices and adds disclosure and contract requirements for financiers of solar system loans, leases and power purchase agreements.

nv:SB38.title: Revises provisions relating to school emergency operations plans. (BDR 34-270)
nv:SB38.summary: Allows the Division of Emergency Management to share school emergency response plans with local public safety agencies when needed for terrorism, emergencies or preparedness, exempting this from the plan confidentiality rule.

nv:SB380.title: Revises provisions relating to autism spectrum disorders. (BDR 23-118)
nv:SB380.summary: Requires peace officer continuing education to include training on interacting with people with developmental disabilities, lets training cover autism spectrum disorders, and requires a Legislative Auditor audit of the Board of Applied Behavior Analysis licensing process.

nv:SB381.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 20-1076)
nv:SB381.summary: Lets sheriffs and constables appoint civil enforcement officers to serve and enforce notices and writs, allows online auctions of real property sold under execution, and changes constable certification, staff and firearm rules.

nv:SB382.title: Revises provisions relating to vehicles. (BDR 43-316)
nv:SB382.summary: Lets owners of farm trailers register them for five years and sets related fees and taxes, and lets autonomous vehicles carry marker lamps showing an automated driving system is operating.

nv:SB386.title: Revises provisions relating to massage therapy. (BDR 54-891)
nv:SB386.summary: Lets the Board of Massage Therapy license massage therapists, reflexologists and structural integration practitioners who have practiced legally in another state for 3 years and pass exams, and ends the requirement to alternate board meetings between northern and southern Nevada.

nv:SB387.title: Revises provisions relating to the prevention and early detection of lung cancer. (BDR 57-68)
nv:SB387.summary: Requires health insurance policies and plans that cover lung cancer treatment to also cover lung cancer screening under American Cancer Society or other nationally recognized guidelines, excluding Medicaid managed care organizations.

nv:SB389.title: Revises provisions relating to the administration of pharmacy benefits under Medicaid and certain other health plans. (BDR 38-240)
nv:SB389.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to contract with one state pharmacy benefit manager by January 1, 2030 to manage Medicaid and certain other prescription drug coverage, and sets contract and reimbursement requirements.

nv:SB39.title: Revises provisions relating to emergency management. (BDR 36-269)
nv:SB39.summary: Creates the Nevada Hazard Mitigation Revolving Loan Account, run by the Division of Emergency Management, to lend money to local and tribal governments for hazard mitigation projects, with prevailing-wage and competitive-bidding conditions.

nv:SB391.title: Revises provisions relating to real property. (BDR 10-84)
nv:SB391.summary: Caps purchases of residential real property by corporations, limited-liability companies and affiliates at 100 units statewide per calendar year, and requires a registry of those buyers kept by the Securities Division.

nv:SB393.title: Revises the Windsor Park Environmental Justice Act.
nv:SB393.summary: Changes the Windsor Park Environmental Justice Act relocation program for North Las Vegas homeowners: clarifies neighborhood boundaries and eligibility, lets some vacant-lot owners exchange lots, revises property and transfer taxes, extends appropriation reversion dates, and appropriates money.

nv:SB395.title: Revises provisions relating to autonomous vehicles. (BDR 43-61)
nv:SB395.summary: Requires a trained human operator with a commercial driver's license in autonomous vehicles over 26,000 pounds, and those with over two axles that carry eight or more passengers, from October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2035.

nv:SB4.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial and governmental administration.
nv:SB4.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations for state government operations for the 2025-2027 biennium, raises the maximum annual salary of the state Chief Information Officer, and changes the membership of the Commission on Innovation and Excellence in Education.

nv:SB400.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-108)
nv:SB400.summary: Requires districts to give a transferring child with a disability comparable services until a new plan is in place, and directs the Commission on Professional Standards to require a competency-tested endorsement to teach music or art, with some elementary school exceptions.

nv:SB403.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-611)
nv:SB403.summary: Creates a Subcommittee on Metrics under the Commission on Innovation and Excellence in Education to develop progress measures for schools, adds university education deans to the Commission, and appropriates money for a staff position and travel.

nv:SB404.title: Revises provisions relating to personal financial administration. (BDR 12-901)
nv:SB404.summary: Changes the priority order for appointing estate administrators, raises the summary administration limit from $300,000 to $500,000 and the set-aside-without-administration limit from $100,000 to $150,000, and sets a 2-year deadline for certain fiduciary breach actions.

nv:SB405.title: Creates the Transit-to-Trails Task Force. (BDR 35-382)
nv:SB405.summary: Creates the Transit-to-Trails Task Force to identify priority areas for using public transit to reach outdoor recreation sites and to seek federal and private grants, with a report due August 31 of each even-numbered year.

nv:SB406.title: Revises provisions relating to civil liability. (BDR 3-1022)
nv:SB406.summary: Gives the State, public colleges and their officers and employees immunity from civil liability for good-faith, health-related COVID-19 actions affecting spring 2020 semester services, in claims over tuition or fees; applies to actions filed since March 12, 2020, and expires June 30, 2030.

nv:SB407.title: Revises provisions relating to the Department of Indigent Defense Services. (BDR 14-492)
nv:SB407.summary: Makes the Indigent Defense Services Executive Director serve at the pleasure of the Board on Indigent Defense Services, generally removable only for good cause, and has the Executive Director appoint the State Public Defender instead of the Governor.

nv:SB408.title: Revises provisions relating to county hospitals and county hospital districts. (BDR 40-559)
nv:SB408.summary: Lets county hospitals and hospital districts employ medical and dental residents and fellows instead of interns, and lets hospital districts employ dentists and set their pay.

nv:SB409.title: Revises provisions relating to the reporting and investigation of child abuse or neglect. (BDR 38-357)
nv:SB409.summary: Extends immunity from civil and criminal liability to people who review or give medical opinions on photographs, x-rays or tests in child abuse investigations, and allows courts to award attorney's fees to mandatory reporters who win suits over such acts.

nv:SB41.title: Revises provisions relating to the taxation of cannabis establishments. (BDR 32-284)
nv:SB41.summary: Requires cannabis sellers to hold a separate cannabis tax permit from the Department of Taxation for each place of business starting January 1, 2027, and allows the Department to revoke or suspend permits for excise tax noncompliance.

nv:SB410.title: Revises provisions relating to public employees. (BDR 23-562)
nv:SB410.summary: Specifies that insurance benefits subject to mandatory bargaining between local governments and employee organizations include benefits for employees' covered dependents.

nv:SB414.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 23-1111)
nv:SB414.summary: Requires certain state employees appointed by constitutional officers outside the classified and unclassified service to file financial disclosure statements with the Secretary of State, with civil penalties for willful failure to file.

nv:SB416.title: Revises provisions relating to the statewide sobriety and drug monitoring program. (BDR 43-423)
nv:SB416.summary: Replaces the restricted driver's license for people in the 24/7 Sobriety and Drug Monitoring Program with a 24/7 privilege that lets them drive anywhere while complying with the program, and allows other approved alcohol testing methods.

nv:SB417.title: Revises provisions relating to public utilities. (BDR 58-1106)
nv:SB417.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to write rules letting natural gas utilities apply for alternative rate-making plans, sets what such plans must include, and revises the application and approval process for electric utilities' plans.

nv:SB418.title: Revises provisions relating to the collection of delinquent contributions by the Public Employees' Retirement System. (BDR 23-601)
nv:SB418.summary: Changes how the Public Employees' Retirement System collects delinquent employer contributions by specifying, for each type of public employer, who is notified and what payment source covers the debt, and no longer applies the procedure to late payroll reports.

nv:SB419.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial administration. (BDR 31-1011)
nv:SB419.summary: Removes data processing from services the Legislative Counsel Bureau and Budget Division provide the Economic Forum, lets the Bureau Director contract to assist it, and moves its odd-year revenue report deadline from May 1 to April 1.

nv:SB422.title: Revises provisions relating to voting. (BDR 24-954)
nv:SB422.summary: Sets the automatic voter registration deadline at 18 days before an election, changes ID and residency proof for same-day in-person registration, and requires weekend hours and no appointments at DMV offices in counties of 100,000 or more before registration deadlines and after elections.

nv:SB424.title: Revises provisions relating to emergency medical services. (BDR 38-561)
nv:SB424.summary: Requires the state Medicaid division to impose an assessment on private emergency medical transport providers, creates an account to spend the revenue on transport quality and access, and authorizes penalties and human trafficking training programs.

nv:SB426.title: Establishes provisions relating to the Lake Tahoe Basin Scenic Byway Corridor Recreation Safety Zone. (BDR 43-374)
nv:SB426.summary: Creates the Lake Tahoe Basin Scenic Byway Corridor Recreation Safety Zone on parts of four highways, where the Transportation Department and local law enforcement may restrict parking; the Department may charge parking fees on its land and contract with other governments for enforcement.

nv:SB427.title: Makes appropriations to certain institutions of the Nevada System of Higher Education for capital improvement projects.
nv:SB427.summary: Appropriates General Fund money for capital projects at Nevada System of Higher Education institutions, including $6.2 million for UNLV business school design and security upgrades, $6.2 million for UNR life sciences building design, and building repairs.

nv:SB428.title: Revises provisions relating to public office. (BDR 23-955)
nv:SB428.summary: Requires officeholders to swear additional oaths, including to relinquish office if they stop living in their district, lets voters challenge incumbents on that ground, and lets parties replace nominees who move away before the July deadline.

nv:SB43.title: Revises provisions relating to public health and safety. (BDR 40-264)
nv:SB43.summary: Lets the state environmental protection administrator designate which district boards of health act as solid waste authorities, based on capability and regulations, with current ones treated as designated; sets a similar designation for public water system oversight.

nv:SB431.title: Revises provisions relating to the excise tax on live entertainment. (BDR 32-692)
nv:SB431.summary: Extends the live entertainment excise tax to resales of admission, requires resellers to keep records, and requires facilitators of resales above set thresholds to collect and remit the tax.

nv:SB432.title: Revises provisions relating to privacy. (BDR 11-1020)
nv:SB432.summary: Makes family law proceedings presumptively open but lets courts close them or seal records for a compelling interest, repeals the mandatory divorce-closure statute, and makes willfully posting certain personal identifying information of another person without consent a category D felony.

nv:SB434.title: Creates a program to award grants to address shortages of providers of health care. (BDR 40-1107)
nv:SB434.summary: Creates a competitive Statewide Health Care Access and Recruitment Grant Program, funded by a state account, to support projects addressing shortages of health care providers.

nv:SB435.title: Revises provisions relating to nicotine products. (BDR 32-989)
nv:SB435.summary: Requires vapor product manufacturers to certify compliance with federal marketing authorization, and requires the Department of Taxation to keep a directory of compliant manufacturers.

nv:SB437.title: Enacts provisions relating to Internet consumer lenders. (BDR 55-951)
nv:SB437.summary: Lets internet-only consumer lenders get a Nevada lending license for an out-of-state office without an in-state license, exempts them from the one-business-per-office rule, and requires their loan contracts with residents to follow Nevada law.

nv:SB439.title: Revises provisions relating to alcoholic beverages. (BDR 52-1108)
nv:SB439.summary: Lets estate distilleries receive bulk spirits from non-affiliated suppliers for storage and bottling, and sell other alcoholic beverages at retail if properly licensed.

nv:SB44.title: Revises provisions relating to financial services. (BDR 54-258)
nv:SB44.summary: Requires listed financial service providers, including escrow agents, collection agencies, installment lenders and money transmitters, to follow federal customer-information safeguard rules and report breaches to state commissioners, and sets liquidity, governance and audit standards for large multistate mortgage servicers.

nv:SB440.title: Revises provisions relating to electricity. (BDR 10-950)
nv:SB440.summary: Adds disclosure and contract requirements for solar system purchase, lease and power purchase agreements, and lets a customer void a power purchase agreement if the solar company lacks the proper contractor's license.

nv:SB442.title: Requires the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada to establish certain reporting requirements. (BDR 58-429)
nv:SB442.summary: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to adopt rules making utilities publish a quarterly report of monthly residential service terminations, including aggregated customer data by zip code.

nv:SB443.title: Revises provisions relating to public works. (BDR 28-1112)
nv:SB443.summary: Requires prevailing wages on construction work for significant operational or capital projects awarded by public utilities, even when the work does not otherwise qualify as a public work, with some exceptions.

nv:SB444.title: Revises provisions concerning policies governing the use of certain electronic devices in schools. (BDR 34-855)
nv:SB444.summary: Requires school district policies on pupil electronic devices to cover electronic communication devices, use a progressive discipline scale, limit use during instruction, and include certain exceptions.

nv:SB445.title: Revises provisions relating to the privacy of data concerning pupils. (BDR 34-854)
nv:SB445.summary: Requires the Department of Education to move a student's data to an archive within a year after graduation or leaving school and remove personally identifiable information except birth date.

nv:SB447.title: Revises provisions relating to public works. (BDR 28-968)
nv:SB447.summary: Lets a party with legal standing sue a public body for a writ of mandamus requiring it to award certain public works contracts as the law provides, and lets the court award attorney's fees to the prevailing party.

nv:SB45.title: Revises provisions relating to educational programs. (BDR 34-275)
nv:SB45.summary: Changes career and technical education grant limits to depend on pupils in advanced courses, and requires work-based learning reports to use federal reporting information and groupings.

nv:SB450.title: Revises provisions relating to bailiffs and deputy marshals in certain courts. (BDR 1-1019)
nv:SB450.summary: Makes bailiffs and deputy marshals in counties of 700,000 or more (Clark County) county employees assigned to courts rather than appointed by judges, lets them serve process, and removes the bond requirement.

nv:SB451.title: Extends a property tax imposed to employ police officers with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department. (BDR 22-359)
nv:SB451.summary: Extends the 20-cent per $100 assessed value property tax for employing Las Vegas Metropolitan Police officers in unincorporated Clark County and Las Vegas from its June 30, 2027 expiration through June 30, 2057.

nv:SB452.title: Extends the date of reversion of certain previous appropriations made to the Office of Finance in the Office of the Governor.
nv:SB452.summary: Extends the date for returning two 2023 appropriations to the General Fund, $50 million for state office leases and furniture and $5 million for employee training, from September 19, 2025 to September 17, 2027.

nv:SB453.title: Makes an appropriation to restore the balance in the Reserve for Statutory Contingency Account.
nv:SB453.summary: Appropriates $9,835,522 from the General Fund to restore the balance in the Reserve for Statutory Contingency Account.

nv:SB454.title: Revises provisions governing the State Highway Fund. (BDR 35-1128)
nv:SB454.summary: Extends to June 30, 2027 the temporary increase in the share of State Highway Fund revenue that may cover vehicle fee collection and administration costs.

nv:SB455.title: Reorganizes certain divisions within the Department of Motor Vehicles. (BDR 43-1161)
nv:SB455.summary: Renames the Division of Field Services the Division of Customer Services, eliminates the Division of Central Services and Records, and renames the Administrative Services Division the Fiscal Operations Division at the Department of Motor Vehicles.

nv:SB457.title: Revises provisions relating to public safety. (BDR 15-1038)
nv:SB457.summary: Changes criminal law on assault, battery, stalking, pornography involving minors, domestic violence and DUI, requires compliance hearings after firearm relinquishment orders, adds theft-related property damage offenses, and changes juvenile justice, record sealing and pretrial release provisions.

nv:SB458.title: Makes a supplemental appropriation to the Office of the Secretary of State for an unanticipated shortfall related to travel, operating and information services expenses.
nv:SB458.summary: Appropriates $773,148 from the State General Fund to the Secretary of State's office to cover an unanticipated shortfall in travel, operating and information services expenses.

nv:SB459.title: Revises provisions relating to gaming salons. (BDR 41-1164)
nv:SB459.summary: Allows gaming salon regulations to permit table games, slot machines or other gambling games in any combination, and lets the licensee set slot-machine minimum wagers with Gaming Control Board approval instead of the current $500 minimum.

nv:SB46.title: Revises provisions governing gaming. (BDR 41-298)
nv:SB46.summary: Keeps Gaming Control Board and Commission jurisdiction over licensees after they leave a position, makes license surrenders effective only when accepted, lets the Board hold investigative hearings without majority concurrence, and lets regulators require suitability findings for tournament operators.

nv:SB460.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-16)
nv:SB460.summary: Makes wide-ranging education changes, including creating an Education Service Center and a Commission on Recruitment and Retention, providing for a Public Education Oversight Board, and revising school accountability, charter school, prekindergarten and Educational Choice Scholarship provisions.

nv:SB462.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial administration. (BDR 31-1156)
nv:SB462.summary: Revises adjustments to agency base budgets and changes the Rainy Day Account cap to 26 percent of the previous year's General Fund appropriations rather than the current year's.

nv:SB464.title: Enacts the Interstate Mining Compact. (BDR 46-1125)
nv:SB464.summary: Enacts the Interstate Mining Compact, lets the Governor name an alternate representative, gives the Governor and Legislature inspection rights over the Commission's books, and has the Division of Minerals pay annual dues.

nv:SB465.title: Revises provisions relating to certain criminal defendants. (BDR 14-1119)
nv:SB465.summary: Reduces from three to two the evaluators who assess competence of defendants committed for treatment, adding a third if they disagree, and replaces courts' power to include involuntary medication in commitment orders with a prosecutor's ability to seek a separate order.

nv:SB466.title: Revises provisions governing the authority of the State Department of Agriculture relating to food and water. (BDR 51-1121)
nv:SB466.summary: Moves permitting and regulation of food establishments, cottage food operations and farm-to-fork events from the state health division to the State Department of Agriculture and local health boards, and requires counties to pay the Department an assessment.

nv:SB467.title: Revises provisions relating to cybersecurity. (BDR 19-1149)
nv:SB467.summary: Moves the Nevada Office of Cyber Defense Coordination from the Department of Public Safety to the Office of the Chief Information Officer and merges it with the Office of Information Security.

nv:SB468.title: Makes an appropriation to the State Public Charter School Authority for the transportation of pupils enrolled in charter schools.
nv:SB468.summary: Appropriates $17 million from the General Fund to the State Public Charter School Authority for transporting charter school students, available through June 30, 2027.

nv:SB469.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Corrections for various purposes.
nv:SB469.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Corrections for replacing security, culinary, maintenance and other equipment and for deferred maintenance projects.

nv:SB470.title: Makes an appropriation to the Account for Charter Schools.
nv:SB470.summary: Appropriates $400,000 from the General Fund to the Account for Charter Schools.

nv:SB472.title: Makes appropriations to the Nevada System of Higher Education for expenditures related to instruction that are due to caseload adjustments at certain institutions within the System.
nv:SB472.summary: Appropriates about $4.86 million from the General Fund to the Nevada System of Higher Education for instruction costs tied to caseload adjustments at UNLV, Nevada State, the College of Southern Nevada, Western Nevada College and Truckee Meadows Community College.

nv:SB473.title: Makes appropriations to and authorizes the expenditure of money by the Department of Education for the replacement of computer hardware and associated software and office chairs.
nv:SB473.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Education budget accounts to replace computer hardware, software and office chairs.

nv:SB474.title: Makes an appropriation to the Nevada Gaming Control Board for the replacement of computer hardware and associated software.
nv:SB474.summary: Appropriates $938,490 in 2025-26 and $15,033 in 2026-27 to the Gaming Control Board to replace computer hardware and software.

nv:SB475.title: Makes appropriations to the Division of State Parks of the State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources for the purchase and replacement of vehicles, equipment, computer and information technology equipment and radios and for certain projects.
nv:SB475.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Division of State Parks for replacing vehicles, equipment, computers and radios, including $5.55 million for vehicles, and for certain projects.

nv:SB476.title: Makes appropriations to the Peace Officers' Standards and Training Commission for the replacement and updating of certain technology.
nv:SB476.summary: Appropriates $87,360 for computer hardware and software and $92,433 for a records management and tracking system to the Peace Officers' Standards and Training Commission.

nv:SB477.title: Makes an appropriation to and authorizes the expenditure of money by the Department of Taxation for the continued development and implementation of the Unified Tax System.
nv:SB477.summary: Appropriates $12,457,960 in 2025-26 and $15,281,906 in 2026-27 to the Department of Taxation for the Unified Tax System, and authorizes $5 million in other spending.

nv:SB478.title: Makes appropriations and requires the issuance of bonds for costs associated with the Judicial Department of State Government.
nv:SB478.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Judicial Department for court technology upgrades and requires issuing up to $9 million in state bonds to buy the Nevada Supreme Court Building in Las Vegas.

nv:SB479.title: Makes an appropriation to the Office of Economic Development in the Office of the Governor for the support of designated regional development authorities.
nv:SB479.summary: Appropriates $375,000 in each of two fiscal years to the Office of Economic Development to support designated regional development authorities.

nv:SB48.title: Revises provisions relating to planning and zoning. (BDR 22-413)
nv:SB48.summary: Moves the annual regional plan report in Washoe County from April to October 1, covering the prior fiscal year, and lets counties and cities under 700,000 population make planning commission members' terms match those of the governing-body member who recommended them.

nv:SB480.title: Makes an appropriation to the Office of Finance in the Office of the Governor for a loan to the Office of the Chief Information Officer within the Office of the Governor for the replacement of uninterruptible power supply equipment and related expenses.
nv:SB480.summary: Appropriates $790,902 in 2025-26 and $9,450 in 2026-27 as a loan to the Office of the Chief Information Officer for replacing uninterruptible power supply equipment, repaid from July 1, 2027.

nv:SB481.title: Makes a supplemental appropriation to the Division of Public and Behavioral Health of the Department of Health and Human Services for an unanticipated shortfall related to the costs of provider services in the Southern Nevada Adult Mental Health Services budget account.
nv:SB481.summary: Appropriates $1,647,791 from the General Fund to the Division of Public and Behavioral Health to cover a shortfall in provider service costs at Southern Nevada Adult Mental Health Services.

nv:SB484.title: Makes an appropriation to the Supreme Court of Nevada for the costs of upgrading the appellate court case management system.
nv:SB484.summary: Appropriates $2,162,178 from the General Fund to the Supreme Court of Nevada to upgrade the appellate court case management system.

nv:SB485.title: Makes an appropriation to the Supreme Court of Nevada for the costs of the implementation of a statewide trial court case management system.
nv:SB485.summary: Appropriates $4,700,954 from the General Fund to the Supreme Court of Nevada to implement a statewide trial court case management system.

nv:SB486.title: Makes appropriations to the Nevada Promise Scholarship Account and the Account for Pensions for Silicosis, Diseases Related to Asbestos and Other Disabilities.
nv:SB486.summary: Appropriates $10,718,696 to the Nevada Promise Scholarship Account and $1,000 to the Account for Pensions for Silicosis, Diseases Related to Asbestos and Other Disabilities.

nv:SB487.title: Makes an appropriation to the Office of the Secretary of State for costs associated with the business licensing system modernization project.
nv:SB487.summary: Appropriates $8,983,876 from the General Fund to the Secretary of State for the business licensing system modernization project, including contract staffing.

nv:SB488.title: Makes appropriations to the Office of the Secretary of State for the replacement of certain equipment and certain costs related to elections.
nv:SB488.summary: Appropriates to the Secretary of State $460,423 for computers and IT equipment, $1,462,864 for voter education, ballot translation and travel, and $26,000 for voter identity verification.

nv:SB489.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Corrections for the purchase and replacement of certain equipment and furniture.
nv:SB489.summary: Appropriates small General Fund amounts to the Department of Corrections for equipment purchases and replacement at Northern Nevada and Casa Grande transitional housing facilities.

nv:SB49.title: Revises provisions relating to consumer protection. (BDR 52-439)
nv:SB49.summary: Clarifies the Attorney General's authority to sue over deceptive trade practices, raises the administrative fine from $1,000 to up to $15,000 per violation, widens uses of the Consumer Protection Legal Account, and keeps agency records confidential when the Consumer's Advocate receives them.

nv:SB490.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Corrections for the purchase and replacement of equipment at certain prisons.
nv:SB490.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the Department of Corrections to replace and buy equipment at Ely State Prison, Lovelock Correctional Center and Florence McClure Women's Correctional Center.

nv:SB491.title: Makes appropriations to the Training Division of the Department of Public Safety for the replacement of equipment, computer hardware and associated software, beds and mattresses and for maintenance projects and services.
nv:SB491.summary: Appropriates money to the Public Safety Training Division to replace training equipment and officers' pistols, and for computer hardware, beds and mattresses, and maintenance projects, from the General Fund and State Highway Fund.

nv:SB492.title: Makes appropriations to the State Department of Agriculture for the purchase of software and the replacement of equipment.
nv:SB492.summary: Appropriates General Fund money to the State Department of Agriculture for veterinary software ($38,761) and for replacing equipment in its veterinary services ($51,485) and administrative services ($212,488) budgets.

nv:SB493.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Transportation for the replacement of the Nevada Shared Radio System.
nv:SB493.summary: Appropriates $2,865,572 from the General Fund and $15,039,943 from the State Highway Fund to the Department of Transportation to replace the Nevada Shared Radio System.

nv:SB494.title: Makes revisions relating to health and human services. (BDR 18-1116)
nv:SB494.summary: Creates the Nevada Health Authority to take over Medicaid, public employee health benefits, health care licensing and food establishment sanitation, and renames the Department of Health and Human Services the Department of Human Services.

nv:SB495.title: Revises provisions relating to health care. (BDR 40-1037)
nv:SB495.summary: Makes many health care changes, including creating an Office of Mental Health, requiring a biennial health care workforce needs assessment, and setting time limits for insurers and hospitals to process provider credentialing and privileging requests.

nv:SB496.title: Makes appropriations to the Department of Motor Vehicles for information technology system projects.
nv:SB496.summary: Appropriates State Highway Fund money to the Department of Motor Vehicles for information technology: moving a legacy system to a cloud platform ($13,780,212 in 2025-26; $9,792,437 in 2026-27) and continuing its modernization project ($33,903,370; $39,687,596).

nv:SB497.title: Eliminates a requirement concerning rates of reimbursement under Medicaid for applied behavioral analysis services. (BDR 38-1238)
nv:SB497.summary: Eliminates the requirement that Nevada Medicaid set reimbursement rates for applied behavior analysis services every two years comparable to other states' Medicaid rates; those rates are then set like other Medicaid services.

nv:SB498.title: Makes appropriations to the Nevada System of Higher Education to expand undergraduate and graduate nursing programs and for academic programming and building renovations at institutions within the System.
nv:SB498.summary: Appropriates $10 million in each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27 to the Nevada System of Higher Education to expand undergraduate and graduate nursing programs, for operating costs only, plus money for academic programming and building renovations.

nv:SB499.title: Revises provisions relating to state financial administration. (BDR 26-1237)
nv:SB499.summary: Allows below-market leases of state-owned housing to employees when an agency finds it beneficial, codifies a temporary General Fund advance for fire suppression, and creates an Out-of-State Fire Suppression Account with a $27,359,038 appropriation.

nv:SB5.title: Makes revisions relating to health care. (BDR 40-32)
nv:SB5.summary: Creates a competitive Statewide Health Care Access and Recruitment Grant Program, funded by a state account, to support projects addressing shortages of health care providers, and requires a biennial assessment of the state's health care workforce needs.

nv:SB500.title: Ensures sufficient funding for K-12 public education for the 2025-2027 biennium.
nv:SB500.summary: Sets estimated total public support per pupil at $13,889 for 2025-26 and $13,963 for 2026-27, apportions the State Education Fund for the biennium, and makes appropriations for base per-pupil funding, weighted funding and other education purposes.

nv:SB501.title: Authorizes expenditures by agencies of the State Government for the 2025-2027 biennium.
nv:SB501.summary: Authorizes state agencies to spend specified amounts of non-General Fund, non-Highway Fund money in fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27, and lets the State Public Defender collect up to set amounts from Humboldt and White Pine counties.

nv:SB502.title: Authorizes and provides funding for certain projects of capital improvement.
nv:SB502.summary: Appropriates about $99.5 million from the General Fund for state capital improvement projects in the 2025-2027 budget, authorizes related expenditures, and levies a property tax to support the Consolidated Bond Interest and Redemption Fund.

nv:SB503.title: Eliminates the Account for the Regulation and Supervision of Captive Insurers in the Fund for Insurance Administration and Enforcement. (BDR 57-1236)
nv:SB503.summary: Eliminates the Account for the Regulation and Supervision of Captive Insurers and sends its fees, assessments and tax revenue to the Fund for Insurance Administration and Enforcement, where they may be used for any of that fund's purposes.

nv:SB504.title: Revises provisions relating to the Extended Young Adult Support Services Program. (BDR 38-1123)
nv:SB504.summary: Changes the Extended Young Adult Support Services Program: widens who qualifies as a young adult, lets child welfare agencies petition courts to dismiss and reassume jurisdiction for federal funding, makes participation opt-out, and requires court review hearings every 6 months.

nv:SB507.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 18-1252)
nv:SB507.summary: Lets the Office of Nevada Boards, Commissions and Councils Standards charge licensing boards fees, removes the Commission on Postsecondary Education from its purview, specifies which authority sets taxicab technology fees, and lets transportation network companies connect taxicab carriers with passengers for a fee.

nv:SB52.title: Revises provisions relating to education. (BDR 34-273)
nv:SB52.summary: Requires school districts to report the percentage of English learner pupils, defines long-term English learner as over 6 years for that report, and lets third graders qualify for a reading promotion exemption by showing grade 3 mastery through a work portfolio.

nv:SB54.title: Requires Medicaid to provide coverage of certain services for persons experiencing homelessness. (BDR 38-412)
nv:SB54.summary: Requires Medicaid, from July 1, 2027 if federal funding is available, to cover medical respite care for people experiencing homelessness and directs state agencies to develop a model for providing it.

nv:SB6.title: Makes an appropriation to the Desert Research Institute of the Nevada System of Higher Education to support the Nevada State Cloud Seeding Program.
nv:SB6.summary: Appropriates $600,000 for each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27 to the Desert Research Institute to support the Nevada State Cloud Seeding Program, with expenditure reports to the Interim Finance Committee.

nv:SB60.title: Revises provisions governing crimes committed against older or vulnerable persons. (BDR 15-342)
nv:SB60.summary: Adds certain theft and deceptive trade practice crimes against people 60 or older or vulnerable persons to the crimes carrying an added consecutive sentence and a civil penalty the Attorney General can recover.

nv:SB62.title: Revises provisions relating to crimes. (BDR 16-507)
nv:SB62.summary: Expands crime victim compensation eligibility to people targeted because of certain actual or perceived characteristics, allows up to $1,000 per incident for property remediation, and appropriates money to the victims fund and human trafficking account.

nv:SB63.title: Revises provisions relating to the processing of certain data. (BDR 52-505)
nv:SB63.summary: Bars online services from processing children's personal data for certain purposes, sets rules for collecting and processing children's data, requires data protection assessments, and allows civil enforcement and penalties.

nv:SB66.title: Revises provisions governing certain postconviction petitions for a writ of habeas corpus. (BDR 3-441)
nv:SB66.summary: Requires habeas petitions challenging time-served calculations to be filed in the district court of the county where the petitioner is incarcerated or lives, or Carson City if the petitioner is outside Nevada.

nv:SB69.title: Revises provisions relating to economic development. (BDR 32-369)
nv:SB69.summary: Requires lead participants of $1 billion-plus projects in economic diversification districts, if the local government requires it, to agree to pay local service costs as a condition of state tax credits or abatements; makes negotiation records confidential.

nv:SB7.title: Revises provisions relating to occupational diseases. (BDR 53-36)
nv:SB7.summary: Makes the presumption that lung disease is job-related for qualifying police officers, firefighters and arson investigators apply without proof of exposure to smoke, fumes or gases, and applies it to claims already filed.

nv:SB71.title: Revises provisions relating to governmental administration. (BDR 27-366)
nv:SB71.summary: Requires local governments and the state Purchasing Division to post on their websites the kinds of goods and services they buy and how to request notice of solicitations. Also changes the purchasing commission's duties to promote local businesses.

nv:SB72.title: Revises the Charter of the City of Henderson.
nv:SB72.summary: Changes the Henderson charter: sets deadlines for special elections to fill vacancies, makes committee review of proposed ordinances optional, and allows installment sales of any city real property without requiring cost-based pricing for transfers to certain entities.

nv:SB74.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-482)
nv:SB74.summary: Makes many election law changes, including allowing mail ballots in certain emergencies, revising candidate eligibility and filing fee payment, changing ballot counting standards and election crimes, and requiring the Secretary of State to adopt a cyber-incident response plan.

nv:SB76.title: Revises provisions relating to securities. (BDR 7-486)
nv:SB76.summary: Creates a fund to compensate victims of securities fraud who are owed court-ordered restitution, administered by the Securities Division, with reimbursement required in some cases, and revises certain exempt securities and transactions.

nv:SB8.title: Revises provisions relating to employment. (BDR 53-35)
nv:SB8.summary: Adds federal Portal-to-Portal Act exclusions to Nevada wage law, so activities such as waiting time, preparatory and concluding activities, certain training and meetings, and travel time are not compensable working time.

nv:SB80.title: Revises certain provisions governing motor vehicles. (BDR 43-304)
nv:SB80.summary: As passed by the Senate, lets Department of Motor Vehicles theft investigators inspect identification numbers and its peace officers seek pen-register orders, bars tampering with or removing vehicle emission controls (with engine-swap exceptions), and ends the garage exemption for heavy-truck-only businesses.

nv:SB81.title: Revises various provisions governing education. (BDR 34-276)
nv:SB81.summary: Requires the Department of Education to survey school employees on working conditions and departing employees, requires school improvement plans to use the results, and changes the timing of school district fund balance transfers to the Education Stabilization Account.

nv:SB83.title: Requires the issuance of bonds for environmental improvement projects in the Lake Tahoe Basin.
nv:SB83.summary: Requires issuing up to $10.5 million in state general obligation bonds for Lake Tahoe Basin environmental improvement projects under the Environmental Improvement Program.

nv:SB84.title: Revises provisions relating to domestic violence. (BDR 40-488)
nv:SB84.summary: Requires that the curriculum and instructional materials in certified domestic violence treatment programs be evidence-based.

nv:SB85.title: Revises provisions relating to public safety. (BDR 43-490)
nv:SB85.summary: Makes permanent the requirements, set to expire February 1, 2026, that police record, keep and report traffic stop data, and revises related reporting duties of agencies and third-party analysts.

nv:SB87.title: Revises provisions relating to forensic medical examinations. (BDR 16-498)
nv:SB87.summary: Lets the compensation officer pay medical providers for sexual assault and strangulation forensic exams from the Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime, with counties paying any shortfall, and requires a maximum annual reimbursement rate per exam.

nv:SB88.title: Revises provisions relating to offenders. (BDR 16-491)
nv:SB88.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires the Director of Corrections to discharge outstanding medical debt owed to the Department by prisoners on release, including those released before July 1, 2025.

nv:SB89.title: Revises provisions relating to firearms. (BDR 15-174)
nv:SB89.summary: Bars buying, owning or possessing firearms for 10 years after conviction for an offense motivated by the victim's race, religion, disability, sexual orientation or similar characteristics, and permanently after a violent offense so motivated. Exempts firearms legally owned before July 2025 by those already convicted.

nv:SB9.title: Revises provisions relating to Medicaid. (BDR 57-290)
nv:SB9.summary: Requires insurers and other health coverage providers to answer Medicaid agency claim inquiries within 60 days, and bars denying a Medicaid agency claim solely for lack of prior authorization when the agency authorized the service.

nv:SB90.title: Makes an appropriation to the Department of Education for the provision of grants to organizations to provide certain supplies and materials to teachers and specialized instructional support personnel.
nv:SB90.summary: Appropriates $15 million to the Department of Education for grants to organizations that supply classroom materials to teachers and specialized instructional support personnel, with no more than $7.5 million spent in 2025-26.

nv:SB91.title: Establishes provisions relating to the use of diacritical marks in certain governmental records. (BDR 40-43)
nv:SB91.summary: Allows vital records and DMV-issued licenses and ID cards to record and display diacritical marks in a person's legal name.

nv:SB93.title: Establishes certain labor standards for the award of grants of federal money by a state agency for certain purposes. (BDR 18-556)
nv:SB93.summary: Requires state agencies awarding federal broadband grants to give 30 percent scoring weight to applicants certifying workforce standards, such as wage, safety and training commitments or a collective bargaining agreement.

nv:SB97.title: Makes revisions to the Silver State Health Insurance Exchange. (BDR 57-346)
nv:SB97.summary: Requires one Governor-appointed member of the Silver State Health Insurance Exchange board to be a member of a Nevada Indian tribe with expertise in tribal health care administration.

nv:SB99.title: Authorizes, under certain circumstances, certain governing bodies of a city or county to impose linkage fees on certain developers. (BDR 22-373)
nv:SB99.summary: Lets cities and counties in a region governed by an interstate planning agency (currently Lake Tahoe) charge linkage fees on larger new homes, additions and costly remodels to fund deed-restricted affordable housing.

nv:SCR8.title: Amends the Joint Standing Rules of the Senate and Assembly for the 83rd Session of the Legislature.
nv:SCR8.summary: Amends Joint Standing Rule 11 to change minority-party membership on the Legislative Commission, based on the minority's share of a House, and sets three members per party when a House is evenly divided.

nv:SJR1.title: Proposes to amend the Nevada Constitution to enact various requirements relating to the distribution and submission of mail ballots.
nv:SJR1.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment requiring county clerks to mail a ballot to each active registered voter, letting voters opt out, requiring polling places to accept mail ballots, and requiring mail ballot drop-off sites in the three days before elections.

nv:SJR10.title: Urges Congress to take certain actions relating to the therapeutic use of certain psychedelic compounds.
nv:SJR10.summary: Urges Congress and federal agencies to fund more research on psychedelic compounds, streamline research approval, allow compassionate use, reschedule several compounds, and shield state-compliant supervised adult use from federal prosecution.

nv:SJR7.title: Urges the Federal Government to recognize the unsuitability of Yucca Mountain as the site for a repository to store and dispose of spent nuclear fuel and high-level radioactive waste.
nv:SJR7.summary: Urges the President, Congress and federal agencies to recognize Yucca Mountain as unsuitable for a spent nuclear fuel repository, citing health, safety, economic and transportation concerns, and sends copies to federal officials.

nv:SJR8.title: Urges Congress to protect the public lands including and adjacent to Sunrise Mountain, Frenchman Mountain and the Rainbow Gardens Area.
nv:SJR8.summary: Urges Congress to give federal protection, such as national conservation area, recreation area or monument status, to public lands at and near Sunrise Mountain, Frenchman Mountain and the Rainbow Gardens Area.

nv:SJR9.title: Urges the Citizens' Stamp Advisory Committee and the Postmaster General of the United States Postal Service for the creation of a postage stamp commemorating John “Snowshoe” Thompson.
nv:SJR9.summary: Urges the Citizens' Stamp Advisory Committee and the U.S. Postmaster General to create a postage stamp commemorating John "Snowshoe" Thompson, a 19th-century mail carrier who crossed the Sierra Nevada on skis.

ny:B438.title: Provides for the election of eight Regents of the University of the State of New York
ny:B438.summary: Elects eight Regents of the University of the State of New York, re-electing four and electing four others, for terms of one to five years.

ny:C151.title: Provides for the election of eight Regents of the University of the State of New York
ny:C151.summary: Elects eight Regents of the University of the State of New York, re-electing four and electing four new members, with terms from one to five years.

ny:C978.title: Provides for the election of two Regents of the University of the State of New York
ny:C978.summary: Elects two Regents of the University of the State of New York for five-year terms starting April 1, 2026: one fifth Judicial District Regent re-elected and one at-large Regent elected.

ny:R1231.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for certain appropriations for services and expenses of additional grants-in-aid to certain school districts, public libraries and institutions
ny:R1231.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for additional grants-in-aid to school districts, libraries and nonprofit institutions in the 2019-20 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1232.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2022-2023 state fiscal year for grants in aid to certain agricultural organizations
ny:R1232.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for grants to agricultural organizations in the 2022-23 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1233.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for certain appropriations for the 2022-2023 state fiscal year for grants-in-aid to environmental conservation initiatives
ny:R1233.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for environmental conservation initiatives in the 2022-23 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1234.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2023-2024 fiscal year for services and expenses of human services and veterans community services organizations
ny:R1234.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for human services and veterans community services organizations in the 2023-24 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1235.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid to certain schools, libraries and not-for-profit institutions
ny:R1235.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2023-24 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1236.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid certain educational and not-for-profit institutions
ny:R1236.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1237.title: Establishes an itemized list of grantees for the 2024-25 state fiscal year for services and expenses, grants or reimbursement of expenses incurred by providers of community safety and restorative justice programs
ny:R1237.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for community safety and restorative justice programs in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1238.title: Sets forth an itemized list of grantees for the 2024-25 state fiscal year for services and expenses of senate priorities for housing initiatives
ny:R1238.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for Senate-priority housing initiatives in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1239.title: Sets forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2024-25 state fiscal year for the provision of community adult and youth mental health programs and services
ny:R1239.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for community adult and youth mental health programs in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R1240.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for certain appropriations for services and expenses of economic development and community services organizations
ny:R1240.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for economic development and community services organizations in the 2024-25 state budget.

ny:R1241.title: Establishes an itemized list of grantees for the 2024-25 state fiscal year for services and expenses of human services and veterans community services organizations
ny:R1241.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for human services and veterans community services organizations in the 2024-25 state budget.

ny:R1242.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for the New York state economic development assistance program
ny:R1242.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for the New York State Economic Development Assistance Program, funded since the 2008-09 state budget, amending a 2010 Senate resolution.

ny:R1243.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-2026 state fiscal year for community public health programs and services
ny:R1243.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for community public health programs in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1244.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-2026 state fiscal year for community adult and youth mental health programs and services
ny:R1244.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for community adult and youth mental health programs in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1245.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-2026 state fiscal year for community safety and restorative justice programs
ny:R1245.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for community safety and restorative justice programs in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1246.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-2026 state fiscal year for services and expenses of senate priorities for housing initiatives
ny:R1246.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for Senate-priority housing initiatives in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1247.title: Sets forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-2026 state fiscal year for services and expenses of economic development and community services organizations
ny:R1247.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for economic development and community services organizations in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1248.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-2026 state fiscal year for additional grants in aid for education
ny:R1248.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1249.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid to certain libraries
ny:R1249.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for a pilot program expanding social work services in libraries in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1250.title: Establishes a list of grantees for certain appropriations for the 2025-26 state fiscal year
ny:R1250.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for health programs in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1251.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for certain appropriations for the 2025-26 state fiscal year for grants or reimbursement of certain expenses by local governments
ny:R1251.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for legal services, gun violence prevention and other crime-prevention programs run by local governments and nonprofits in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R1722.title: Senate budget resolution in response to the 2026-2027 Executive Budget submission
ny:R1722.summary: Adopts the Senate's amended versions of the 2026-27 Executive Budget bills (S.9000 series) as the New York State Senate's budget proposal, with a report on changes to agency funding and proposals.

ny:R2343.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid for certain educational and not-for-profit institutions
ny:R2343.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2023-24 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2344.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2023-2024 fiscal year for services and expenses of human services and veterans community services organizations
ny:R2344.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for human services and veterans community services organizations in the 2023-24 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2345.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid certain educational and not-for-profit institutions
ny:R2345.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2346.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for certain appropriations for services and expenses of economic development and community services organizations
ny:R2346.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for economic development and community services organizations in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2347.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for aid for services and expenses of human services and veterans community services organizations
ny:R2347.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for human services and veterans community services organizations in the 2024-25 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.
