ny:R2348.title: Amending a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-26 state fiscal year for community adult and youth mental health programs and services
ny:R2348.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for community adult and youth mental health programs in the 2025-26 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2349.title: Amends a plan establishing itemized list of grantees for 2025-2026 providing community safety and restorative justice programs
ny:R2349.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for community safety and restorative justice programs in the 2025-26 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2350.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid for services and expenses of senate priorities for housing initiatives
ny:R2350.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for Senate-priority housing initiatives in the 2025-26 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2351.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for certain appropriations for services and expenses of economic development and community services organizations
ny:R2351.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for economic development and community services organizations in the 2025-26 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2352.title: Amends a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for additional grants in aid certain educational and not-for-profit institutions
ny:R2352.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2025-26 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2353.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2025-26 state fiscal year for services and expenses of human services and veterans community services organization
ny:R2353.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for human services and veterans community services organizations in the 2025-26 state budget.

ny:R2354.title: Amends a plan establishing itemized list of grantees for 2025-2026 providing community public health programs and services
ny:R2354.summary: Changes the itemized list of grantees for community public health programs in the 2025-26 state budget, amending an earlier Senate resolution.

ny:R2355.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2026-27 state fiscal year for additional grants in aid to certain school districts, public libraries
ny:R2355.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for additional grants to school districts, libraries, colleges and education and arts nonprofits in the 2026-27 state budget.

ny:R2356.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2026-27 state fiscal year for grants or reimbursement of certain expenses by local governments
ny:R2356.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for community public health programs in the 2026-27 state budget.

ny:R2357.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for a certain appropriation for the 2026-27 state fiscal year for services and expenses of human services and veterans community services organization
ny:R2357.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for human services and veterans community services organizations in the 2026-27 state budget.

ny:R2358.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for 2026-2027 providing Public Protection and Economic Development programs and services
ny:R2358.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for legal services, gun violence prevention and other public protection and economic development programs in the 2026-27 state budget.

ny:R2359.title: Establishes a plan setting forth an itemized list of grantees for 2026-2027 providing Public Health and Mental Health programs and services
ny:R2359.summary: Sets the itemized list of grantees for public health and mental health programs in the 2026-27 state budget.

ny:R488.title: Senate budget resolution in response to the 2025-2026 Executive Budget submission
ny:R488.summary: Adopts the Senate's amended versions of the 2025-26 Executive Budget bills (S.3000 series) as the New York State Senate's budget proposal, with a report on changes to agency funding and proposals.

ny:S2253.title: Relates to the establishment and the reporting of residential water cost indexes
ny:S2253.summary: Directs the Public Service Commission to set a formula for a residential water cost index, requires water systems with 1,000 or more customers to report it yearly, and requires an annual statewide comparison report.

ny:S2461.title: Authorizes the New York state and local employees' retirement system to accept an application for disability retirement benefits from Andrew Reilly, Jr.
ny:S2461.summary: As introduced, treats a former Town of Hempstead Sanitation District clerk as having applied for disability retirement within 30 days of his February 20, 2020 stroke, so the state retirement system can accept his late application.

ny:S2461-A.title: Authorizes the New York state and local employees' retirement system to accept an application for disability retirement benefits from Andrew Reilly, Jr.
ny:S2461-A.summary: Treats a former Town of Hempstead Sanitation District clerk as having applied for disability retirement within 30 days of his February 20, 2020 stroke, so the state retirement system can accept his late application. Employers bear the costs.

ny:S7663-A.title: Authorizes the assessor of Nassau county to accept an application for retroactive real property tax exempt status from Al-Muneer Foundation, Inc.
ny:S7663-A.summary: Allows the Nassau County assessor to accept a late property tax exemption application from the Al-Muneer Foundation, Inc. for a Uniondale parcel on the 2024-25 roll, with possible refund or cancellation of taxes.

ny:S9326-A.title: Authorizes the assessor of the town of Babylon to accept an application for exemption from real property taxes from Tiegerman Community Services, Inc.
ny:S9326-A.summary: Allows the Town of Babylon assessor to accept a late property tax exemption application from Tiegerman Community Services, Inc. for a North Babylon parcel, for a portion of the 2024-25 and all of the 2025-26 rolls, with possible refunds.

nyc:Int 0015-2026.title: Requirements and reporting for background checks for child care providers, employees, and volunteers.
nyc:Int 0015-2026.summary: As amended, bars the city health department from requiring a repeat background check for someone checked within five years for center-based child care, with exceptions, and requires annual public reports on checks received, completed and median processing time starting August 1, 2027.

nyc:Int 0055-2026.title: Signage describing certain constitutional and legal protections.
nyc:Int 0055-2026.summary: Requires the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs to develop plain-language, multilingual signs on access to city property and immigration enforcement with know-your-rights material, requires city agencies to post them, and has the Department of Education provide age-appropriate versions.

nyc:Int 0579-2026.title: An education and outreach campaign to enroll students in early childhood education programs.
nyc:Int 0579-2026.summary: As amended, requires the Department of Education to run an annual outreach campaign, starting by January 31, 2027, to enroll children in early childhood programs, prioritizing low-income families, and to report on it each year.

nyc:Int 0929-2026.title: A transparency report regarding New York city police department security perimeters adjacent to educational facilities.
nyc:Int 0929-2026.summary: Requires the NYPD to publish a transparency report on its plan to use security perimeters at entrances and exits of certain educational facilities, including steps to avoid curbing free speech: a proposed report within 45 days and a final report within 90 days.

nyc:Res 0524-2026.title: Resolution approving a modification (MN-8) pursuant to section 107(e) of the charter of the city of New York.
nyc:Res 0524-2026.summary: Approves a city budget modification (MN-8), requested by the Office of Management and Budget, that recognizes a net increase in revenue in the Fiscal 2026 expense budget.

oh:HB 105.title: Revise non-recourse litigation funding agreement regulations
oh:HB 105.summary: Requires consumer legal funding companies and commercial litigation financiers to register with the attorney general, sets disclosure rules for consumer funding agreements, bars referral fees to or from attorneys and health care providers, and bars deals with parties not domiciled in the United States.

oh:HB 173.title: Regards entities providing behind-the-meter utility services
oh:HB 173.summary: Regulates companies that resell electricity to tenants through submetering: requires registration with the Public Utilities Commission, disconnection protections, and a tenant bill at least 3% below the utility's standard service offer bill, and limits building conversions to submetering.

oh:HB 195.title: Revise the Ohio Uniform Commercial Code
oh:HB 195.summary: Updates the Ohio Uniform Commercial Code, including new rules on controllable electronic records and secured transactions, and changes billing for reimbursement of pay for retired judges serving as active judges.

oh:HB 20.title: Prohibit harassing or impeding an emergency service responder
oh:HB 20.summary: Bars approaching or staying within 15 feet of an emergency service responder, after a warning, while impeding or threatening them; raises penalties for obstructing official business involving responders; and specifies that heightened menacing penalties apply to probation officers.

oh:HB 210.title: Regards the sale of used catalytic converters
oh:HB 210.summary: Requires scrap metal dealers and others buying used catalytic converters to get specified proof of ownership and pay by traceable means, not cash, and lets the public safety director investigate dealers, suspend registrations, and fine unregistered dealers.

oh:HB 251.title: Regards drone use by law enforcement; aviation facilities
oh:HB 251.summary: Requires law enforcement to get a warrant to use drones to enter or view a home's interior when an in-person search would need one, lists warrantless uses, bars drones armed with lethal weapons, requires flight records, and bars public entities from acquiring foreign-adversary drones.

oh:HB 268.title: Regards filing for certificate of qualification for employment
oh:HB 268.summary: Changes the waiting period for a certificate of qualification for employment so, for felonies, the one-year wait runs from release from incarceration rather than from the end of all post-release supervision.

oh:HB 284.title: Require US-produced iron, steel be used on state-funded projects
oh:HB 284.summary: Extends the domestic-steel requirement for state-supported construction to iron, adds water, sewer and other infrastructure and maintenance work, covers projects with any state funds, and lets the funding state agency waive it in certain cases.

oh:HB 291.title: Create the Ohio International Trade Commission
oh:HB 291.summary: Creates the Ohio International Trade Commission, with legislators and regional representatives, to advance trade, investment, research and business exchanges between Ohio and up to eight designated regions.

oh:HB 292.title: Establish the Ohio Defense Commission
oh:HB 292.summary: Creates the Ohio Defense and Space Advisory Commission within the Department of Development and a Defense and Aerospace Industries Expansion Program under which the department may make grants, and appropriates $5 million for fiscal year 2027.

oh:HB 293.title: Designate NASA Day of Remembrance
oh:HB 293.summary: Designates the fourth Thursday of January as "NASA Day of Remembrance" in Ohio to honor NASA personnel who died in space exploration, including the Apollo 1, Challenger and Columbia crews.

oh:HB 297.title: Regards funds provided by county for Memorial Day expenses
oh:HB 297.summary: Raises from $500 to $1,000 the cap on county Memorial Day funds for each chartered veterans' organization post, and from $100 to $200 the cap for civic organizations receiving the funds when posts are extinct or unable to serve.

oh:HB 31.title: Require electronic recordings of all parole board hearings
oh:HB 31.summary: Requires electronic recordings of full parole board hearings and certain revocation hearings, makes recordings of full hearings public records excluding victim statements and identifying information, and gives prosecutors access to corrections health care records in certain parole and judicial release cases.

oh:HB 311.title: Designate EMS week in Ohio
oh:HB 311.summary: Designates the third full week of May as "EMS Week in Ohio."

oh:HB 314.title: Limit certain public record requests; allow contractor response
oh:HB 314.summary: Lets political subdivisions charge public records fees based on hours to produce (up to $200 for requests over 40 hours), lets offices ask a court to limit requests meant to harass or disrupt, and lets private contractors respond to voluminous requests.

oh:HB 319.title: Enact the Clinical Teaching Subsidy Reform Act
oh:HB 319.summary: Requires the chancellor of higher education to distribute a clinical teaching subsidy to six public medical schools, 90 percent by clinical-year enrollment and 10 percent on physician-retention performance metrics, with annual reporting.

oh:HB 377.title: Regards use of light-based medical devices for hair removal
oh:HB 377.summary: Lets advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants delegate and supervise light-based hair removal by nurses and laser hair removal professionals, allows off-site physician supervision of nurses with 40 hours of approved training, and caps supervision at five nurses and five professionals.

oh:HB 393.title: Require certain facilities assist inmates in obtaining ID cards
oh:HB 393.summary: Requires community-based correctional facilities, programs and halfway houses to help inmates obtain state identification cards before release, including verifying identity and submitting applications.

oh:HB 433.title: Alter amusement ride classification for inspection fee purposes
oh:HB 433.summary: Sets amusement ride inspection fees by ride type (large roller coasters rise from $1,200 to $4,000; inflatable rides $50 to $100 each), allows a medical exception for auctioneer licenses, and makes other changes to Ohio agriculture laws.

oh:HB 455.title: Regards the operation of public schools and the DEW
oh:HB 455.summary: Changes laws on the operation of public schools and the Department of Education and Workforce, State Board of Education appointments, and age and schooling certificates and work hours for people under 16, and repeals various education provisions.

oh:HB 459.title: Enact Katelyn's Law
oh:HB 459.summary: Creates a third-degree felony with no time limit on prosecution for moving or removing human remains to hide a crime, a death, its cause, or the remains; adds a five-year prison specification; exempts spontaneous miscarriage and stillbirth.

oh:HB 462.title: Regards student use of a nasal epinephrine delivery device
oh:HB 462.summary: Expands school, school district and camp epinephrine autoinjector provisions to all epinephrine delivery systems, including nasal sprays, and has the pharmacy board designate other FDA-approved devices by rule.

oh:HB 479.title: Regards physician supervision of imaging contrast administration
oh:HB 479.summary: Lets registered nurses and radiology staff give imaging contrast under physician supervision, creates an Ohio post-traumatic stress fund commission for public safety officers, and amends property tax, school construction and state budget provisions.

oh:HB 492.title: Prohibit interfering with motor vehicle-related arrests
oh:HB 492.summary: Expands the ban on resisting arrest by a peace officer to violations of Title XLV (vehicle, aircraft and watercraft laws) and equivalent ordinances, and bars operators and passengers suspected of such a violation from refusing to give name, address or birth date.

oh:HB 519.title: Prohibit specified actions with intent to steal a motor vehicle
oh:HB 519.summary: Makes possessing criminal tools a fourth-degree felony when an electronic vehicle-unlocking device or tool is involved. Temporarily cuts the state gasoline and diesel tax to near zero, levies a retail tax on that fuel afterward, and appropriates $725 million.

oh:HB 533.title: Revise list of vehicles that can commit vehicular homicide
oh:HB 533.summary: Adds more vehicle types to the list of vehicles whose operation can lead to vehicular homicide or vehicular assault charges.

oh:HB 54.title: Make appropriations for transportation for FY 2026-27 biennium
oh:HB 54.summary: Appropriates money for transportation programs for July 2025 through June 2027, and amends and repeals state laws on vehicles, traffic, driver licensing and highway administration.

oh:HB 541.title: Designate Deputy Daniel "Weston" Sherrer Memorial Highway
oh:HB 541.summary: Designates a portion of U.S. Route 42 in Morrow County as the Deputy Daniel "Weston" Sherrer Memorial Highway.

oh:HB 563.title: Regulate ticket sales
oh:HB 563.summary: Requires ticket resellers and online ticket marketplaces to include mandatory fees in the first displayed price, bars raising the price afterward, requires resale disclosures and proof of purchase, and bars imitating venue names or branding without permission.

oh:HB 585.title: Regards DoDD authority re: community capital assistance funds
oh:HB 585.summary: Directs the Department of Developmental Disabilities to adopt rules letting community capital assistance funds help county boards acquire housing, such as single-family homes, duplexes or manufactured homes, for people in supported living.

oh:HB 611.title: Issue medical marijuana processor cultivation, dispensary license
oh:HB 611.summary: Requires the Division of Cannabis Control to issue a dispensary license and a paired cultivator license, with up to 5,000 square feet of cultivation area, to processors licensed by December 7, 2023 that have no common ownership with a cultivator.

oh:HB 630.title: Regards police escorts for farm equipment, agricultural vehicles
oh:HB 630.summary: Creates an annual permit, fee up to $100, to operate farm machinery on limited access highways and freeways other than interstates, and bars the transportation director from requiring police escorts for permitted farm machinery moved under 10 miles on non-interstate state routes.

oh:HB 647.title: Regards publicly funded child care, the Child Care Cred Program
oh:HB 647.summary: As reported by a House committee, changes the publicly funded child care program, including rules on paying for absent days from July 1, 2027, and requires the attorney general to coordinate with the director of children and youth on investigating criminal or improper activity.

oh:HB 667.title: Enact the Reagan Tokes and Patrick Heringer Act
oh:HB 667.summary: Extends the 48-hour LEADS entry requirement for tier one offense warrants to warrants for certain people who break or fail to return to detention, sets GPS monitoring requirements for released offenders (zones, one vendor, law-enforcement access), and changes county T-CAP rules.

oh:HB 757.title: Enact the Rental Home Marketplace Guarantees Act
oh:HB 757.summary: Lets rental home marketplaces issue guarantees reimbursing hosts for renter damage without being regulated as insurance, if guarantee terms are posted and the guarantees are backed by a reimbursement insurance policy.

oh:HB 758.title: Regards SUDEP, epilepsy license designation, disability database
oh:HB 758.summary: Requires autopsies to check for sudden unexpected death in epilepsy when the coroner is told the person had epilepsy or a seizure history, and lets people with epilepsy enroll in the Disability Database and get an epilepsy designation on a driver's license or state ID.

oh:HB 80.title: Make appropriations for the Industrial Commission for FY 2026-27
oh:HB 80.summary: Appropriates about $53.1 million for fiscal year 2026 and $54.3 million for fiscal year 2027 for the Industrial Commission's operating expenses, rent and Attorney General payments.

oh:HB 852.title: Require appointed police chief to complete officer basic training
oh:HB 852.summary: Bars township and joint police districts, cities and villages from newly appointing a police chief or village marshal without peace officer basic training certification; allows an interim chief for up to six months, extendable for good cause, who must enroll in training.

oh:HCR 22.title: Encourage students to read the U.S. Declaration of Independence
oh:HCR 22.summary: Encourages Ohio students in grades one through twelve to read the U.S. Declaration of Independence in class during 2025-2026 for its 250th anniversary, and encourages schools to provide class time.

oh:HCR 3.title:
To delegate to the President of the Senate and the
Speaker of the House of Representatives authority to designate groups of members to prepare arguments for and against amendments to the Ohio Constitution proposed by the General Assembly; a person or persons to prepare an argument for any law, section, or item submitted to the electors by referendum petition; and a person or persons to prepare an argument against any constitutional amendment or law proposed by initiative
petition.
oh:HCR 3.summary: Delegates to the Senate President and House Speaker, during the 136th General Assembly, authority to name the members who write arguments for and against proposed constitutional amendments, and the people who write arguments on referendum and initiative petitions.

oh:HCR 32.title: Urge Congress to implement a zero-based budgeting process
oh:HCR 32.summary: Urges the U.S. Congress to adopt zero-based budgeting, in which each federal agency builds its budget from zero rather than from the prior year's funding.

oh:HCR 35.title: Urge Congress accelerate deployment of new energy infrastructure
oh:HCR 35.summary: Urges Congress to enact reforms to federal permitting policies to speed deployment of new energy infrastructure.

oh:HCR 8.title: Urge Congress to make the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent
oh:HCR 8.summary: Urges Congress to make the provisions of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent.

oh:SB 106.title: Regulate the ownership of electric vehicle charging stations
oh:SB 106.summary: Classifies electric vehicle charging stations as a competitive retail electric service, revises utility rate provisions for water service line replacement costs and reimbursements, and corrects provisions of Senate Bill 103.

oh:SB 162.title: Regards timing of health insurer recoupment from providers
oh:SB 162.summary: Shortens from two years to one year the time a health insurer has to recoup an overpayment from a provider, and gives providers 60 days instead of 30 to respond to an overpayment notice.

oh:SB 179.title: Verify veteran status of imprisoned individuals
oh:SB 179.summary: Requires jails and prisons to register with the federal Veterans Reentry Search Service and check each booked person's veteran status within three days, noting veterans on records.

oh:SB 19.title: Regards academic intervention, math improvement and intervention
oh:SB 19.summary: Changes academic intervention services in public schools, math improvement and intervention, approved diagnostic assessments, career-technical education for home-educated students, and community school quality designations.

oh:SB 219.title: Revise the law governing oil and gas wells
oh:SB 219.summary: Gives the Division of Oil and Gas Resources Management sole authority over in-state parts of cross-state wells, limits owners to ten expedited permits a year, sets a ten-year deadline for suits claiming a lease expired, and restricts uses of the Oil and Gas Well Fund.

oh:SB 223.title: Require ODNR discount program for veterans, service members
oh:SB 223.summary: Requires the Division of Parks and Watercraft to adopt rules giving veterans and service members with valid documentation a 25% discount on state park services and rentals, not merchandise.

oh:SB 262.title: Require construction contracts note variation from standard form
oh:SB 262.summary: Requires public authorities using an industry-standard construction contract form to mark any alterations by strike-through, underlining or cross-reference; unmarked alterations are void.

oh:SB 263.title: Regards professional employer organizations and Unemployment Law
oh:SB 263.summary: Lets professional employer organizations and alternate employer organizations choose to report shared employees' unemployment wages and contributions under their own account and experience rate, with the rate recalculated.

oh:SB 273.title: Enact the Keep Them Safe Act
oh:SB 273.summary: Lets gun owners store firearms with licensed dealers or law enforcement agencies that agree, with liability limits for them, and appropriates $10 million for Highway Patrol security for major-party candidates for governor and lieutenant governor and their families.

oh:SB 276.title: Ratify the Interstate Compact for School Psychologists
oh:SB 276.summary: Ratifies the Interstate Compact for School Psychologists, requires (rather than permits) massage therapist continuing education, has the Department of Education and Workforce maintain a list of success sequence curriculum resources, and lets students petition to join extracurricular activities at neighboring public schools.

oh:SB 315.title: Enact the Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act
oh:SB 315.summary: Adds Medicaid program integrity rules, changes Attorney General and Auditor of State authority, and requires Ohio's SNAP program to begin using chip-enabled EBT cards.

oh:SB 52.title: Designate Congressman David Hobson Memorial Highway
oh:SB 52.summary: Designates multiple memorial highways and creates multiple specialty license plates.

oh:SCR 20.title: Urge Congress accelerate deployment of new energy infrastructure
oh:SCR 20.summary: Urges Congress to change federal permitting and environmental review laws to speed construction of energy infrastructure such as pipelines and transmission lines, including by considering steps to limit court challenges that slow projects.

oh:SCR 3.title: Urge Fair Labor Standards Act changes for employees under 16
oh:SCR 3.summary: Urges Congress to amend the Fair Labor Standards Act to let people under 16 work between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m. during the school year with parent or guardian approval.

oh:SCR 5.title: Urge Presidential support for Medicaid work requirements
oh:SCR 5.summary: Urges the President to support the Ohio Department of Medicaid's request to impose work requirements on certain Medicaid recipients.

oh:SJR 5.title: Confirm the appointment of James Tressel as Lieutenant Governor
oh:SJR 5.summary: Confirms the nomination of James Tressel as Lieutenant Governor of Ohio by majority vote of each chamber.

ok:HB 1185.title: Firearms; prohibiting the destruction of historic military weapons; effective date.
ok:HB 1185.summary: Bars sheriffs' offices and campus police from destroying unclaimed weapons with historic military value, and bars agencies disposing of seized property from destroying such firearms; requires donation to a local congressionally chartered veterans' organization.

ok:HB 1370.title: Motor Fuel Tax Code; repealer; reduction in federal excise tax on gasoline or diesel fuel; emergency.
ok:HB 1370.summary: Repeals the Oklahoma statute (68 O.S. Section 500.4A) relating to reduction in the federal excise tax on gasoline or diesel fuel, and takes effect immediately.

ok:HB 1381.title: Alcoholic beverages; mixed beverage license; complimentary tasting; wholesalers; effective date.
ok:HB 1381.summary: As amended by the Senate, lets mixed beverage licensees give a guest 21 or older one free on-premises tasting drink per day, and bars brewers and manufacturers from forcing distributors or wholesalers to accept unordered product.

ok:HB 1687.title: Advance health care directives; creating the Uniform Health Care Decisions Act of 2026; establishing requirements for certain health care directives; effective date.
ok:HB 1687.summary: Creates the Uniform Health Care Decisions Act of 2026, setting rules for capacity, health care instructions, powers of attorney and default surrogates, and replaces the Oklahoma Advance Directive Act and Health Care Agent Act.

ok:HB 1752.title: Central purchasing; motor vehicles; requisition; Attorney General and District Attorneys Council exceptions; effective date.
ok:HB 1752.summary: Exempts the Attorney General's Office and the District Attorneys Council from the requirement to submit a requisition to the Office of Management and Enterprise Services before buying a vehicle.

ok:HB 2137.title: Criminal procedures; resumption of competency; administration of medication; notification; authorization; effective date.
ok:HB 2137.summary: Lets the state mental health department or a prosecutor ask a court to order medication to restore a defendant's competency to stand trial, with a hearing, appointed counsel and clear and convincing proof required before involuntary medication is ordered.

ok:HB 2166.title: Definitions and general provisions; newspapers; notices; publications; effective date.
ok:HB 2166.summary: Sets qualifications for a newspaper to carry legal notices in Oklahoma, creating a nonperiodical category that needs weekly print issues, at least 200 paid subscribers, 25% news content, a county office, annual audits and court petition.

ok:HB 2749.title: Medicaid; directing establishment of certain nursing facility add-on rate under specified conditions; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 2749.summary: Directs the Oklahoma Health Care Authority, subject to federal approval and available funds, to set a Medicaid add-on payment rate for nursing facilities that run multigenerational activities, and to write rules implementing it.

ok:HB 2894.title: Oklahoma Rural Jobs Act; cap on capital investment tax credits; authorizing and limiting additional participation in program under certain conditions.
ok:HB 2894.summary: Adds a second $15 million annual cap on Oklahoma Rural Jobs Act investment tax credits, for applications approved on or after the bill's effective date, and lets rural funds certified earlier receive certification on later applications.

ok:HB 2959.title: Schools; student abuse or neglect reporting; superintendents and administrators; school employees; law enforcement; interviews; investigations; duty to report; electronic communication; violations; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 2959.summary: Requires superintendents and school administrators to report suspected student abuse involving a school employee to law enforcement within 24 hours, before a school investigation, and bars formal interviews or discipline of the accused until law enforcement can interview, unless safety requires immediate action.

ok:HB 2961.title: Higher education; TSgt Marshal Dakota Roberts Gold Star Survivor Act; career and technology education; waiver of tuition and fees for the spouse and children of a Gold Star recipient; effective date.
ok:HB 2961.summary: Waives tuition, fees, and room and board at state higher education institutions, and tuition and fees at career technology districts, for spouses and children of Gold Star recipients killed in the line of duty, with Oklahoma residency conditions.

ok:HB 2979.title: Motor vehicles; creating the Talyn Bain Act; requiring the Department of Transportation establish school zones on certain state highways upon request; effective date.
ok:HB 2979.summary: Directs the Department of Transportation, on a local jurisdiction's request, to establish 45 mph school zones on qualifying parts of state highways, with the local jurisdiction paying for signage maintenance and operation.

ok:HB 3000.title: Professions and occupations; State Board of Cosmetology and Barbering; licenses and fees; extending sunset; modifying certain membership qualification under certain condition; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3000.summary: Extends the Board of Cosmetology and Barbering to July 1, 2031, resets its 11 seats to include a massage therapist and a member from law enforcement or trafficking-victim services, lets Service Oklahoma issue licenses from July 1, 2027, and ends the massage advisory board.

ok:HB 3004.title: Professions and occupations; Board of Examiners in Optometry; sunset; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3004.summary: Extends the sunset date of the Board of Examiners in Optometry from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2031.

ok:HB 3021.title: Schools; curriculum requirements for graduation; diploma pathway; State Department of Education; notice; seminar; English requirements financial literacy; alternate diploma; course availability; waiver; coursework; repealers; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3021.summary: Revises graduation requirements: lets an AP English seminar fulfill English, indigenous languages fulfill world language, and an AP course fulfill financial literacy; closes the college-prep pathway to students not already on it; requires a catalog of employer endorsements.

ok:HB 3262.title: Fees; criminal and juvenile proceedings; increasing sheriff's service fee; effective date.
ok:HB 3262.summary: Raises the maximum sheriff's fee for serving writs, warrants, orders and notices to $100, from $50 in criminal cases (inside or outside the county) and from $20 in juvenile cases.

ok:HB 3265.title: Retirement; Oklahoma Police Pension and Retirement System; term; psychologist; certification; salary; effective date.
ok:HB 3265.summary: Lets a psychologist certify mental disability applications for Oklahoma Police Pension and Retirement System disability benefits, and defines "mental health specialist" as a licensed psychiatrist, psychologist, counselor, therapist or behavioral practitioner.

ok:HB 3298.title: Civil procedure; Uniform Judicial Interview of Children Act; terms; scope; judicial officer; judicial interview; considerations; training; procedure; record; codification; effective date.
ok:HB 3298.summary: Creates the Uniform Judicial Interview of Children Act, letting a judge interview a child in custody, visitation, guardianship and similar civil cases when the judge finds it is in the child's best interest, on request or on the judge's own initiative.

ok:HB 3369.title: Food truck fire suppression; mobile food establishments; modifying mandate for automatic fire extinguishing system in food trucks; removing expiration date; effective date.
ok:HB 3369.summary: Removes the expiration date on the option for food trucks to use at least two portable fire extinguishers and annual employee fire safety training in place of an automatic fire extinguishing system.

ok:HB 3413.title: Public finance; annual estimate of funds needed; state agencies; contractors; consultant report; effective date.
ok:HB 3413.summary: Requires state agencies to report contractor and consultant use in budget submissions, including amounts, status and staffing purpose, to post consultant reports publicly, and lets agencies satisfy this by linking to their own contract data.

ok:HB 3431.title: Foreign government adversaries; alien and foreign government adversary ownership; foreign government adversary; mineral ownership; effective date.
ok:HB 3431.summary: Adds foreign terrorist organizations and Specially Designated Nationals to those barred from owning land in Oklahoma, and extends the bar for all covered persons to leasing land and to acquiring, owning or leasing critical minerals.

ok:HB 3462.title: Professions and occupations; plumbing licenses; definitions; examinations; qualifications; effective date.
ok:HB 3462.summary: Creates a residential journeyman plumber license limited to one- and two-family dwellings, with set experience requirements; sets a 70 percent passing score on plumbing exams; and cuts the wait to retake after repeated failures from 90 to 30 days.

ok:HB 3467.title: Education employees; maternity leave; adoption; purpose; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3467.summary: Allows covered school employees to take six weeks of paid maternity leave after adopting a child under age 4, and lets sick leave extending that leave also cover bonding with or caring for an infant.

ok:HB 3498.title: Business entities; Oklahoma General Corporation Act; Oklahoma Limited Liability Company Act; codification; effective date.
ok:HB 3498.summary: Amends the Oklahoma General Corporation Act to let corporations contract with shareholders on voting and other actions, creates safe harbors for conflict-of-interest transactions, and changes merger, conversion and inspection-request rules.

ok:HB 3500.title: Probate procedure; transfer-on-death deed; acceptance; timing; effective date.
ok:HB 3500.summary: Changes how beneficiaries accept real estate under a transfer-on-death deed, requiring each beneficiary to sign and record an affidavit with the death certificate, and sets a procedure and notice if the deed goes unclaimed.

ok:HB 3501.title: Alcoholic beverages; ABLE Commission; multiple licenses; manufacturing beverages; alternating proprietorship or premises; effective date.
ok:HB 3501.summary: Requires the ABLE Commission to issue multiple manufacturing licenses on the same premises to applicants in good standing with it and the Tax Commission, who hold federal approvals for alternating proprietorships and notify the commission. Does not cover distribution or wholesale licenses.

ok:HB 3521.title: Financial institutions; Oklahoma Money Transmission Modernization Act; Banking Commissioner; Oklahoma State Banking Board; licenses; felony; repealer; effective date.
ok:HB 3521.summary: Creates the Oklahoma Money Transmission Modernization Act, replacing existing money transmission laws with licensing, exemptions, safety and soundness requirements, and Banking Commissioner enforcement powers, and repeals sections of the Financial Transaction Reporting Act.

ok:HB 3581.title: Riots; penalties for participating; making certain acts unlawful; Governmental Tort Claims Act; exception; effective date.
ok:HB 3581.summary: Makes blocking public roads during a riot a Class D3 felony instead of a misdemeanor, sets felony penalties for assault and battery, aggravated assault and battery, and property damage in a riot, and removes immunity for riot losses where the government chose to allow it.

ok:HB 3644.title: Venous thromboembolism; creating the Blake Burgess Act; requiring certain hospital policies and training; establishing certain registry and reporting requirements; imposing certain requirements on assisted living centers; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3644.summary: Creates the Blake Burgess Act, requiring hospitals with emergency departments and ambulatory surgical centers to adopt policies for patients at risk of venous thromboembolism and train nonphysician staff annually. Emergency-department hospitals must report data to a statewide registry from July 1, 2027.

ok:HB 3649.title: Real property; Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services; trust; proceeds of sales; Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services Real Property Trust; permissible use of proceeds; descriptions of tracts of land; effective date.
ok:HB 3649.summary: Requires all proceeds from sales of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services Department land to be deposited in its Real Property Trust, expands allowed uses of the proceeds to infrastructure and capital projects benefiting persons it serves, and adds tracts that may be sold.

ok:HB 3650.title: Medicaid; extending certain termination dates; establishing certain reimbursement rates for multistate contracts; effective date.
ok:HB 3650.summary: Extends from July 2027 to July 2028 the minimum Medicaid reimbursement rates managed care entities must pay providers outside value-based arrangements, and sets pay for multistate-contract services at the lesser of the contract rate or the state fee schedule.

ok:HB 3660.title: Natural organic reduction; Class D1 criminal offenses; licenses; requiring certain records be maintained for certain time period; effective date.
ok:HB 3660.summary: Requires natural organic reduction facilities (conversion of human remains to soil) to be licensed within a funeral or embalming establishment, and creates Class D1 felonies for selling the remains, except by a licensed funeral director, or using the soil to grow food.

ok:HB 3661.title: Revenue and taxation; sales tax; exemptions; commercial forestry equipment; effective date.
ok:HB 3661.summary: Makes the sales tax exemption for commercial forestry equipment permanent by removing its January 2027 expiration date.

ok:HB 3673.title: Professions and occupations; term of license and registration certificates; renewal; prohibitions; reinstated licenses; application; continuing education requirements; effective date.
ok:HB 3673.summary: Bars renewal of electrical licenses expired over one year, allowing reinstatement instead by retesting or by applying, paying a $200 penalty and completing up to 24 hours of continuing education. Exempts licensees from continuing education for three years after passing the exam.

ok:HB 3718.title: Special education; Lindsey Nicole Henry Scholarships for Students with Disabilities Program; requiring certain meeting in certain time period; evaluations; exceptions; eligibility; calculation of scholarship; effective date.
ok:HB 3718.summary: Requires school districts to schedule a meeting within 15 school days of a parent's special education evaluation request and decide eligibility within 45 school days of signed consent. If the 45-day deadline is missed, the student is deemed eligible for a Lindsey Nicole Henry scholarship.

ok:HB 3764.title: Gang-related offenses; condition of membership; criminalizing certain acts related to foreign terrorist organizations; effective date.
ok:HB 3764.summary: Adds a Class B5 felony, with five years' prison added to other penalties, for gang-related offenses committed as a condition of membership in, in association with, on behalf of, or while knowingly supporting a State Department-designated foreign terrorist organization.

ok:HB 3767.title: Controlled dangerous substances; adding certain substances to Schedules I and IV; effective date.
ok:HB 3767.summary: Adds certain substances to Schedules I and IV of the state's list of controlled dangerous substances and changes the scope of certain definitions in the Anti-Drug Diversion Act.

ok:HB 3781.title: Insurance; rate may not be excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory; expiration; effective date.
ok:HB 3781.summary: Changes the state's insurance rate laws so rates in noncompetitive markets may be found excessive after actuarial review, adjusts rate filing timing, and sets hearing and disapproval procedures, effective July 1, 2027.

ok:HB 3800.title: Roofing contractors; Roofing Contractor Registration Act; definitions; violations; fees; fines; application; repealer; effective date.
ok:HB 3800.summary: Changes roofing contractor registration: adds residential roofers, requires each roofing firm to have a qualifying party, raises certain fines, creates a residential roofing endorsement with continuing education and a grandfathering period, and revises the roofing examiners committee's duties.

ok:HB 3831.title: Emergency management Services; recognizing Oklahoma Task Force 1 as the official deployment asset team; creating the Oklahoma Task Force 1 Revolving Fund; source; purpose; restrictions; codification; effective date.
ok:HB 3831.summary: Names Oklahoma Task Force 1 the official urban search-and-rescue and disaster deployment team (not for wildland firefighting) and creates a revolving fund, split equally between its Oklahoma City and Tulsa teams, to reimburse participating agencies.

ok:HB 3880.title: Tourism; commissions from tourism magazine and digital prints; additional employee compensation; effective date.
ok:HB 3880.summary: Extends sales commissions of up to 25% (total pay capped at 95% of the executive director's salary) from Oklahoma Today staff to any Tourism and Recreation Department employee who sells ads, sponsorships or products for department publications or promotions.

ok:HB 3940.title: Oklahoma National Guard; requiring certain compensation to be provided by the Oklahoma National Guard Supplemental Retention Pay Revolving Fund; effective date.
ok:HB 3940.summary: Requires Guard and State Guard personnel to be on active duty for state compensation, funds pay for full-time state employees in military roles at federal active-duty levels from a supplemental pay fund, and updates retirement and education benefit rules.

ok:HB 3941.title: Courts; secretary-bailiffs; salary; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3941.summary: Changes the secretary-bailiff salary from a flat $42,000 to the greater of $42,000 or 80% of the maximum salary for a level 5 law enforcement officer, starting in fiscal year 2027.

ok:HB 3970.title: Court reporters; duties and salaries; remote availability; transcripts; certifications;  continuing education; shorthand reporter examinations; methods; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3970.summary: Expands allowed court reporting methods, allows remote court reporter availability, sets rules for ordering transcripts, raises the annual court reporter salary from $53,000 to $65,000, and changes certification payments and continuing education requirements.

ok:HB 3972.title: Public finance; Ad Valorem Reimbursement Fund; school district revenue loss; state purchases; emergency.
ok:HB 3972.summary: Lets the Ad Valorem Reimbursement Fund repay counties for school district revenue lost when the state buys property for over $300 million on or after January 1, 2025, limited to the first two tax years after purchase.

ok:HB 3979.title: Public finance; Oklahoma Economic Development Pooled Finance Act; Infrastructure Pool; Economic Development Pool; caps; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 3979.summary: Raises the cap on pooled obligations the Authority may issue under the Oklahoma Economic Development Pooled Finance Act from $100 million to $125 million for each of the Infrastructure Pool and the Economic Development Pool.

ok:HB 3980.title: District Attorneys Council; Rural District Attorney Loan Repayment Assistance Program; Rural District Attorney Loan Repayment Assistance Program Revolving Fund; codification; effective date.
ok:HB 3980.summary: Creates a loan repayment program letting the District Attorneys Council pay up to $5,000 per 12 months, and $50,000 total, toward education loans of eligible assistant district attorneys. Those who leave designated high-need jurisdictions early repay pro rata. Creates a revolving fund.

ok:HB 3981.title: District Attorneys Council; District Attorney Locality Incentive Program; District Attorney Locality Incentive Program Revolving Fund; codification; effective date.
ok:HB 3981.summary: Lets the District Attorneys Council pay incentives, up to $50,000 over five years plus up to $10,000 per added two years, to full-time prosecutors in designated high-need localities. Those who leave early repay pro rata. Creates a revolving fund.

ok:HB 3996.title: Crimes and punishments; capital cases; Indigent Defense System to make certain payments and provide certain experts; effective date.
ok:HB 3996.summary: Requires the Oklahoma Indigent Defense System to contract with, and reasonably pay, experts as needed when representing indigent defendants seeking post-conviction relief in death penalty cases.

ok:HB 4095.title: 2-1-1 Collaborative; modifying powers and duties; modifying membership; specifying procedures for appointment, reappointment and removal of members; effective date.
ok:HB 4095.summary: Places the Oklahoma 2-1-1 Collaborative under Department of Human Services oversight, cuts its membership from 15 to 9, specifies 2-1-1 call center services, changes its duties, and sets rules for appointing and removing members.

ok:HB 4104.title: Crimes and punishment; Class B5 offenses; adding offenses; loitering; felony offenses; Sex Offenders Registration Act; adding offenses for registration; effective date.
ok:HB 4104.summary: Makes repeat clandestine watching, clandestine photographing for prurient purposes, and repeat or multi-victim private-area photographing Class B5 felonies, and adds these three offenses to sex offender registration.

ok:HB 4113.title: Voting access; modifying qualifications for convicted felons; effective date.
ok:HB 4113.summary: Revises voter registration eligibility for people with felony convictions: they must have completed any incarceration, parole, supervision or probation for the conviction and not be under such status for another felony; a commutation or pardon also restores eligibility on those terms.

ok:HB 4142.title: Crimes and punishments; unlawful use of bombs or explosive devices; modifying elements of certain crimes; effective date.
ok:HB 4142.summary: Expands the felony for unlawful use of bombs or explosive devices to cover conspiring to place them, and clarifies definitions.

ok:HB 4143.title: Motor vehicles; modifying damage amount requiring a written report of collision; effective date.
ok:HB 4143.summary: Raises from $300 to $3,000 the damage amount requiring a driver's written collision report, and from $500 to $3,000 the amount requiring an officer's report of public-roadway collisions. No report is required if parties exchange information and only vehicles are damaged.

ok:HB 4191.title: Revenue and taxation; Small Employer Quality Jobs Act; definitions; eligibility criteria; effective date.
ok:HB 4191.summary: Changes Small Employer Quality Jobs eligibility: sets two city-size tiers (under or over 50,000 people) with minimum new jobs of the greater of 5 jobs/5% or 10 jobs/10%, and lets employers qualify with over $500,000 in capital investment as an alternative to out-of-state sales.

ok:HB 4237.title: Criminal procedure; court costs and fees; requiring courts to offer certain hearing; cost waiver or reduction exceptions; determinations; effective date.
ok:HB 4237.summary: Requires courts that impose court financial obligations at sentencing to offer an ability-to-pay hearing. For delinquent defendants, the court must determine ability to pay at a cost hearing, and any waiver must occur in open court after the defendant is advised.

ok:HB 4268.title: Education; Teacher Effectiveness and Excellence Act; Growth-based Teacher Compensation Program; pilot program; eligibility; bonus program; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 4268.summary: Creates a three-year pilot paying performance bonuses to about 1,500 grade 4-8 English and math teachers based on student growth, and a $5,000-a-year National Board Certification bonus for five years, with an independent evaluation.

ok:HB 4275.title: Mental health; rules and standards for certification of behavioral health case managers; uniformity in rules and standards for certification for behavioral health case managers; certification as peer recovery support specialist; uniformity in rules and standards for certification for peer recovery support specialist; effective date.
ok:HB 4275.summary: Adds employees of tribes and tribal facilities to those eligible for state certification as behavioral health case managers and peer recovery support specialists.

ok:HB 4294.title: Health insurance; fair coverage; epilepsy; termination of coverage; devices; surgeries; effective date.
ok:HB 4294.summary: Requires health plans to cover people with epilepsy the same as others, bars dropping or refusing to renew coverage based on an epilepsy diagnosis, and requires coverage of medically necessary neurostimulation devices prescribed by a treating physician.

ok:HB 4298.title: Child care; directing establishment of certain master teacher ratios; authorizing certain fee subject to specified conditions; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 4298.summary: Directs Human Services to set master teacher ratios for two- to five-star child care facilities at the most permissive level not harming safety or care quality. With federal approval, lets subsidy-participating facilities charge families extra, capped with copayment at 10 percent of income.

ok:HB 4302.title: Children; Office of Juvenile System Oversight; authorizing the release of certain information for certain purposes; effective date.
ok:HB 4302.summary: Allows the Office of Juvenile System Oversight to give law enforcement a complainant's identity when needed to protect others' safety after the complainant communicates a threat of unlawful violence. Other disclosure still requires a court order.

ok:HB 4322.title: Professions and occupations; funeral director in charge; definitions; license requirements; effective date.
ok:HB 4322.summary: Changes the definition of funeral director in charge and removes the requirement that a funeral director in charge hold dual licenses.

ok:HB 4326.title: Oklahoma Higher Learning Access Program; modifying eligibility for certain students; clarifying application time period; modifying definition; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 4326.summary: Expands eligibility for the Oklahoma Higher Learning Access Program to certain adopted students and students in custody of a child-placing agency or tribe, removes the income limit for some of them, and extends the age by which students may qualify.

ok:HB 4338.title: Oklahoma Brine Development Act; modifications; modifying definitions; defining terms; Corporation Commission; emergency.
ok:HB 4338.summary: Places produced water used to extract its constituent elements under the Brine Development Act and other produced water under the Produced Water Recycling and Reuse Act, and lets the Corporation Commission regulate produced water units, generally sized to the drilling unit.

ok:HB 4342.title: Civil procedure; admissibility; evidence; disclosure; term; effective date.
ok:HB 4342.summary: Makes evidence of other acts of domestic violence or abuse by the defendant admissible in criminal cases involving such offenses, and requires the state to disclose it at least 15 days before trial, unless the court allows later for good cause.

ok:HB 4359.title: Schools; requiring statewide assessments to be held in the last four weeks of each school year; effective date; emergency.
ok:HB 4359.summary: Requires statewide student assessments for grades 3 through 8, beginning in 2026-2027, to be given within the last four weeks of the school year, excluding the Oklahoma Alternate Assessment Program for students with the most significant cognitive disabilities.

ok:HB 4408.title: State question 780 data; calculation of savings and averted costs from implementation of the Oklahoma Smart Justice Reform Act; Department of Corrections; Legislative Office of Fiscal Transparency; Administrator of the Courts; effective date.
ok:HB 4408.summary: Limits the State Question 780 crimes in annual data reports from Corrections and the Courts Administrator to former felonies now misdemeanors and offenses between old and new dollar thresholds, and gives the Legislative Office of Fiscal Transparency 30 days after receiving data to calculate savings.

ok:HB 4423.title: Oklahoma Health Care Authority; federal immigration reporting systems; requiring Authority to report certain applicants to the Attorney General; notification to Immigration and Customs Enforcement; effective date.
ok:HB 4423.summary: As passed by the House, requires the Oklahoma Health Care Authority to verify Medicaid applicants' immigration status through the federal SAVE system and notify the Attorney General when status does not indicate lawful presence; that office reviews cases and notifies ICE if presence is unverifiable.

ok:HB 4427.title: Adjunct teachers; annual report; qualifications; requirements; prohibiting adjunct teachers from teaching core curriculum subjects to certain grades; waiver; certificate; effective date.
ok:HB 4427.summary: Bars adjunct teachers from teaching core subjects in pre-K through fifth grade starting 2027-2028, except by waiver for those already employed who complete reading training. Limits adjunct employment to five years, extendable five more by waiver.

ok:HB 4428.title: Public finance; terms; Board of Trustees; votes; proxy proposal; pecuniary factors; exception; report; publish; effective date.
ok:HB 4428.summary: Requires public pension boards to vote shareholder proxies and engage companies solely on financial (pecuniary) factors, not environmental, social or political goals, and to publish an annual report of their proxy votes by March 1.

ok:HB 4431.title: Professions and occupations; Pharmacy Act; references; prescribing authority for certain persons; repealers; effective date.
ok:HB 4431.summary: Updates references in the Oklahoma Pharmacy Act and in prescribing authority for advanced practice nurses and certified midwives, changes physician assistant license application and jurisprudence exam procedures, and repeals duplicate versions of two sections.

ok:HB 4484.title: Motor vehicles; authorizing certain employees of the Corporation Commission to drive certain vehicles; effective date.
ok:HB 4484.summary: Allows Corporation Commissioners, division heads, emergency responders and field inspectors working assigned areas to use a state-owned or leased vehicle for travel between home and assigned work locations, as authorized by the Corporation Commission.

ok:HJR 1023.title: Workers' compensation; approving certain fee schedule; effective date; emergency.
ok:HJR 1023.summary: Approves the Workers' Compensation Commission's updated fee schedule of maximum rates paid to medical providers, effective July 1, 2026.

ok:HJR 1088.title: Joint Resolution; education state agencies; approving certain proposed permanent rules; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1088.summary: Approves proposed permanent rules filed by February 1, 2026 by education agencies, including the State Department of Education, the Regents for Higher Education, Teachers' Retirement System, Statewide Charter School Board and CareerTech.

ok:HJR 1090.title: Joint Resolution; energy and agricultural state agencies; approving certain proposed permanent rules; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1090.summary: Approves proposed permanent rules filed by February 1, 2026 by energy and agriculture agencies, including the Corporation Commission, Environmental Quality, Water Resources Board and Wildlife Conservation departments.

ok:HJR 1091.title: Joint Resolution; business and commerce state agencies; approving certain proposed permanent rules; disapproving in part certain proposed rule of the New Motor Vehicle Commission; excluding certain proposed rules; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1091.summary: Approves proposed permanent rules filed by February 1, 2026 by business and commerce agencies, such as the Insurance Department and Tax Commission, but disapproves part of a New Motor Vehicle Commission loaner vehicle rule and excludes Uniform Building Code Commission Chapter 20 changes.

ok:HJR 1093.title: Joint Resolution; state health-related agencies; approving certain proposed permanent rules; excluding certain rules; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1093.summary: Approves proposed permanent rules filed by February 1, 2026 by state health-related agencies, including Human Services, Mental Health, Nursing and Pharmacy boards, and most Health Care Authority rules except those listed.

ok:HJR 1095.title: Joint Resolution; general government state agencies; approving certain proposed permanent rules; excluding certain Office of Management and Enterprise Services proposed major rule changes; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1095.summary: Approves proposed permanent rules filed by February 1, 2026 by general government agencies, including Transportation, Veterans Affairs, Service Oklahoma, Securities and the State Election Board, except certain Office of Management and Enterprise Services major rules (OAC 260:75).

ok:HJR 1099.title: Joint Resolution; Oklahoma Health Care Authority; approving certain proposed permanent major rules; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1099.summary: Approves two proposed major rules of the Oklahoma Health Care Authority, OAC 317:30-5-47 and 317:30-5-47.7, submitted on or before February 1, 2026.

ok:HJR 1100.title: Joint Resolution; approving certain Office of Management and Enterprise Services proposed major rule changes; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1100.summary: Approves proposed major rule changes by the Office of Management and Enterprise Services in OAC 260:75, submitted on or before February 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1061.title: Oklahoma Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act; defining term. Effective date.
ok:SB 1061.summary: Defines "originated" loans, for the mortgage license renewal assessment based on loan volume, as loans closed in the mortgage broker's or lender's own name, excluding brokered loans, and updates references. Takes effect November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1090.title: Contracts; creating the Oklahoma Homeowner Repair Contract Protection Act. Effective date.
ok:SB 1090.summary: Gives homeowners five calendar days to cancel a home repair contract signed after in-person solicitation at their residence, by written notice sent by certified mail, under the Oklahoma Homeowner Repair Contract Protection Act.

ok:SB 1191.title: Oklahoma Energy Initiative Act; repealing Oklahoma Low Carbon Energy Initiative Board. Effective date.
ok:SB 1191.summary: Repeals the Oklahoma Low Carbon Energy Initiative Board.

ok:SB 1204.title: School employees; requiring school districts to provide paid bereavement leave to certain employees for certain purposes. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1204.summary: Requires school districts to give teachers and support employees three days of paid bereavement leave after the death of a spouse or child, including miscarriage, separate from miscarriage sick leave, and lets the paid maternity leave fund reimburse it.

ok:SB 1213.title: Prisons and reformatories; modifying provisions related to inmate earned credits. Effective date.
ok:SB 1213.summary: Removes the minimum time-incarcerated requirements for inmates to be placed in higher earned-credit class levels and changes how earned credits apply to certain inmates.

ok:SB 122.title: Motor vehicles; certification of existence of security; valid insurance. Effective date.
ok:SB 122.summary: As amended by the House, allows a licensed operator to accept physical proof of insurance, instead of the online verification system, when the operator determines it appears valid and sufficient to show the required vehicle security exists.

ok:SB 1224.title: Pardons and paroles; authorizing electronic notification to victims and victim representatives. Effective date.
ok:SB 1224.summary: Allows the Pardon and Parole Board to send required notices to crime victims or their representatives by email, as an alternative to first-class mail, if they have provided an email address.

ok:SB 1226.title: Motor vehicles; expanding criteria by which a person must remain at scene or make notification of certain accident. Effective date.
ok:SB 1226.summary: Extends the duty to stop and remain at the scene to accidents damaging property, not only driven or attended vehicles, and extends owner notification to damage to property along public or private roads or streets, not only highways.

ok:SB 1264.title: Crimes and punishment; Class A3 and B3 offenses; assault and battery; modifying certain definition; repealers. Effective date.
ok:SB 1264.summary: Raises maximum jail terms for assault from 30 to 90 days and for assault and battery from 90 days to six months, reclassifies related offenses, and removes one crime from the Class B3 felony list; effective November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1266.title: Notaries public; modifying allowable punishment for provision of certain legal advice. Effective date.
ok:SB 1266.summary: Adds up to one year in county jail, alone or with the existing fine of up to $1,000, to the penalty for notaries who, unless licensed or authorized, hold themselves out as having expertise in immigration or citizenship legal advice.

ok:SB 1277.title: Employment benefits; modifying conditions for disqualification; specifying work search actions. Effective date.
ok:SB 1277.summary: Requires unemployment claimants to complete three weekly work search actions, more if the Employment Security Commission requires, instead of applying for a minimum number of jobs. Lists qualifying actions such as applications, interviews, networking events and reemployment services.

ok:SB 1286.title: Elections; requiring certain political subdivisions to provide polling place. Effective date.
ok:SB 1286.summary: Requires political subdivisions that held a county-run election since January 1, 2023, and own or lease a facility in or near a precinct lacking a suitable polling place to provide a room free on the county election board secretary's written request.

ok:SB 1303.title: Workers' compensation; transferring property and records. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1303.summary: Terminates the Advisory Council on Workers' Compensation and transfers its property and records to the Workers' Compensation Commission.

ok:SB 1319.title: Corporation Commission; processes for cities and counties to seek certain reimbursement; fair market value; requiring application to request use of certain funds; creating the Remediation Assistance Revolving Fund. Emergency.
ok:SB 1319.summary: Sets a process for cities and counties to seek reimbursement from a new Remediation Assistance Revolving Fund after buying and removing homes contaminated by oil or brine. The Commission remediates using state plugging funds; the city or county then sells the property and returns proceeds.

ok:SB 1325.title: Protection from Domestic Abuse Act; requiring defendants charged with certain domestic violence offenses to use a Global Positioning System (GPS) device when released on bond. Effective date.
ok:SB 1325.summary: As passed by the Senate, requires defendants charged with domestic abuse by strangulation, with a deadly weapon, or after a prior domestic abuse adjudication to be on GPS monitoring at their own cost to be released on bail. Corrections lists approved GPS programs; the court may let the victim receive proximity alerts.

ok:SB 1326.title: Self-Service Storage Facility Lien Act; permitting electronic delivery and acceptance of rental agreements. Effective date.
ok:SB 1326.summary: Allows self-storage rental agreements to be delivered and accepted electronically, deems payment or continued use acceptance if the occupant does not sign within 30 days, and starts the 15-day wait before disposing of abandoned property from delivery of notice.

ok:SB 1338.title: Education; creating the Education Impact and Innovation Revolving Fund; providing for competitive grants pool; providing for use of grants. Effective date.
ok:SB 1338.summary: As amended, requires the State Department of Education to run competitive grants for proposals to improve education outcomes and creates the Education Impact and Innovation Revolving Fund. The State Board scores and ranks proposals, with identifying information removed, against a department rubric.

ok:SB 1360.title: Mathematics instruction; Oklahoma Math Achievement and Proficiency Act; teacher training; creating the Office of Mathematics Improvement; Director; screening instrument; funding. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1360.summary: Creates an Office of Mathematics Improvement in the State Department of Education, led by a director focused on K-5 math. Moves to 2027-2028 the year districts must use the statewide screening instrument, and changes how math funds are allocated to districts.

ok:SB 1380.title: Medicaid; requiring certain death record verifications; requiring certain denial or disenrollment of deceased individuals; prohibiting certain payments. Effective date.
ok:SB 1380.summary: Requires the Health Care Authority to check Social Security and state death records before approving Medicaid, deny applications of deceased people, verify enrollee deaths monthly from 2027, disenroll the deceased, stop payments after death and recoup them where allowed. Requires periodic State Auditor reviews.

ok:SB 1390.title: Gross production tax; modifying apportionment of collections for certain fiscal years; modifying apportionment limit. Effective date.
ok:SB 1390.summary: Extends through fiscal year 2032, instead of 2027, the current split of certain gross production tax revenue, one-third each to the tourism capital fund, conservation infrastructure fund and community water infrastructure fund.

ok:SB 1400.title: Sales tax exemption; combining certain exemptions for aircraft maintenance, manufacturing, and parts. Effective date.
ok:SB 1400.summary: Combines the sales tax exemptions for aircraft maintenance and manufacturing facilities with those for aircraft parts, and modifies certain exemptions.

ok:SB 1410.title: Agriculture; requiring operation of an Ag in the Classroom Education Program; requiring development of curriculum for K-12 programs. Effective date.
ok:SB 1410.summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to run an Ag in the Classroom Education Program with K-12 curriculum, and allows it to give incentives to participating teachers if funding is available.

ok:SB 1425.title: Health care; repealing provisions related to the Health Care Workforce Resources Board. Effective date.
ok:SB 1425.summary: Repeals the Oklahoma Health Care Workers and Educators Assistance Program and the Health Care Workforce Resources Act, which includes the Health Care Workforce Resources Board.

ok:SB 1437.title: Schools; creating the Donald J. Trump Physical Fitness Act. Effective date.
ok:SB 1437.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to set guidelines, including staff training, disability and medical exemptions, and a parent opt-out, for schools to give students the Presidential Fitness Test, which districts must then administer.

ok:SB 1448.title: Oklahoma Consumer Protection Act; modifying exemptions. Effective date.
ok:SB 1448.summary: Changes the Oklahoma Consumer Protection Act exemption for other regulators' oversight to actions required or authorized under specific state or federal laws or regulations they administer; actions regulated under Corporation Commission laws remain exempt.

ok:SB 1451.title: Voter registration; requiring certain information to be included on voter registration applications. Emergency.
ok:SB 1451.summary: Adds a prior-registration question to voter registration applications, treats an application as a request to cancel any prior registration, and requires notice to the other state's election official. Requires an annual report on those notices and cancellations.

ok:SB 1461.title: Oklahoma Educational Television Authority; extending sunset date.
ok:SB 1461.summary: Extends the sunset date of the Oklahoma Educational Television Authority from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2031 and clarifies language on its appointees.

ok:SB 1489.title: Students; directing compliance with the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act; requiring publication of certain information. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1489.summary: Adds special education law training to principal certification requirements, lets parents of children with disabilities review records five days before an IEP meeting and bring a person of their choice, and requires dispute-resolution information online.

ok:SB 1502.title: Long-term care; eliminating the Alzheimer-Dementia Disclosure Act Advisory Council. Effective date.
ok:SB 1502.summary: Eliminates the Alzheimer-Dementia Disclosure Act Advisory Council, which advises on state rules for dementia special care disclosures by long-term care facilities.

ok:SB 1531.title: Aerospace, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure; authorizing the Oklahoma Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics to take certain actions. Effective date.
ok:SB 1531.summary: Authorizes the Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics' unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility clearinghouse to invest in publicly owned infrastructure and partner with other states and industry to create regional or technical centers.

ok:SB 1534.title: Corporations; modifying requirements related to charitable organizations and solicitation of charitable contributions; prohibiting certain actions by charitable nonprofit corporations. Effective date.
ok:SB 1534.summary: Requires charitable organizations to list tax ID numbers on Secretary of State registrations, requires charitable nonstock corporation boards to have at least three members, bars loans to or guarantees for directors, and modifies which religious and educational groups are exempt from filing.

ok:SB 1543.title: Driving under the influence; authorizing aggregation of certain offenses; creating felony offense. Effective date.
ok:SB 1543.summary: Allows two or more DUI violations within one year to be aggregated and prosecuted as a single Class C2 felony, exempts certain cases from blood and breath test timing requirements, and repeals duplicate versions of the statute.

ok:SB 1546.title: Education; modifying eligibility under the Equal Opportunity Education Scholarship Act.
ok:SB 1546.summary: As amended, lets scholarship granting organizations and educational improvement grant organizations give capital improvement grants to schools, requires them to report such grants to the Tax Commission, and clarifies that public schools can spend grant money on improving reading and math scores.

ok:SB 1553.title: Medicaid; specifying certain qualifications for appeals; providing for recovery of certain costs. Effective date.
ok:SB 1553.summary: Specifies that a psychologist reviewing a Medicaid appeal meets the specialty requirement if currently licensed, with training and experience in testing for and treating the condition, sufficient to determine whether the service is medically necessary or clinically appropriate.

ok:SB 1555.title: Medicaid home- and community-based services; modifying certain definition. Effective date.
ok:SB 1555.summary: Replaces the IQ-based definition of "individual with intellectual disability" in Oklahoma's Medicaid home- and community-based services law with the Social Security Administration's listing criteria for intellectual disorder, effective November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1557.title: Applied behavior analysis; transferring licensure powers and duties to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists; requiring background check. Effective date.
ok:SB 1557.summary: Transfers licensing of behavior analysts and assistant behavior analysts to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, requires criminal history checks, and replaces the $100 fee cap with fees covering costs.

ok:SB 1562.title: Hospice; specifying certain penalties; defining term. Effective date.
ok:SB 1562.summary: Adds Health Department discipline and injunction authority for hospice solicitation or paid patient referrals, defines solicitation to include recruiting patients already enrolled in another hospice, and states that advertising and fair-market-value marketing payments are not prohibited.

ok:SB 1572.title: State Commissioner of Health; requiring Commissioner and Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services conduct a feasibility study to gather certain information. Emergency.
ok:SB 1572.summary: Directs the State Commissioner of Health, with the Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, to study consolidating the two agencies and report to the Governor and legislative leaders by March 1, 2027.

ok:SB 1589.title: Crimes and punishments; modifying scope of certain offense related to gambling. Effective date.
ok:SB 1589.summary: Adds online casino games, and geolocation providers, gaming suppliers, platform providers, promoters and media affiliates who support them, to the felony offense of conducting or supporting gambling games. Takes effect November 1, 2026.

ok:SB 1593.title: Higher education; removing language regarding the promulgation of rules and the presidential search process for the Board of Trustees for Oklahoma State University/Tulsa. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1593.summary: Removes the requirement that the Oklahoma State University/Tulsa Board of Trustees promulgate certain rules and adopt certain policies, along with the presidential search process language and other outdated language.

ok:SB 1595.title: Motor vehicles; prohibiting certain entities from providing certain recommendations; providing certain exception. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1595.summary: Bars state agencies and their contractors from recommending for or against a specific commercial driver training school or withholding student grants based on the school chosen, and lets affected schools or students sue.

ok:SB 1614.title: Teachers; modifying requirements of induction program; providing funding sources for program. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1614.summary: Makes the state teacher induction program state-supported, requiring districts to take part beginning in 2026-27, and allows it to be funded by appropriations, grants and philanthropic or nonprofit contributions.

ok:SB 1618.title: Criminal procedure; creating the Public Protection Act; conditions of release; public safety reports. Effective date.
ok:SB 1618.summary: Lets courts use a pretrial risk-assessment public safety report to help set release conditions, and requires one when the charge is a violent crime. The report cannot be the sole basis to grant or deny release and goes to defense and state counsel on request.

ok:SB 1630.title: Schools; allowing a school district or charter school to count certain day or number of hours toward certain requirement under certain circumstances. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1630.summary: Lets a school district or charter school count one virtual instruction day (six hours) toward the existing two-day (12-hour) virtual limit when a high school site holds statewide testing with limited space and staffing, if its board approves for non-testing students.

ok:SB 1632.title: Schools; directing career-readiness assessments and assessment-based credentials to be made available to certain students beginning in certain school year. Effective date. Emergency.
ok:SB 1632.summary: Shifts approval of career-readiness assessments and credentials from the Commerce Department to the State Department of Education, removes the funding condition, and makes the assessments available to grades 10 through 12 starting in the 2026-2027 school year.

ok:SB 1633.title: Higher education; removing language providing resident tuition eligibility for certain students. Emergency.
ok:SB 1633.summary: Removes language letting students who cannot document U.S. nationality or lawful immigration status qualify for in-state tuition, language on their eligibility for state scholarships and financial aid, and an exception to the bar on higher education benefits for certain students.

ok:SB 1651.title: State Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision; modifying various provisions related to physicians and allied health professionals. Effective date.
