sd:SB 37.summary: Appropriates money, mostly from the water and environment fund, to the Board of Water and Natural Resources for water grants and loans, including $11.4 million for consolidated water facilities, $3.4 million for solid waste, and regional water, hydrology and flood studies.

sd:SB 39.title: revise provisions relating to industrial hemp.
sd:SB 39.summary: Repeals state licensing of hemp growers, researchers and processors, so that only producers licensed by the USDA or a tribal program may grow hemp in South Dakota, effective January 1, 2027.

sd:SB 40.title: revise the compliance requirements for limitations on foreign ownership of agricultural land.
sd:SB 40.summary: Lets the attorney general fine up to 10 percent of a land interest's value for not filing with the state a copy of a federal foreign-ownership report; subjects a violating minority owner's inherited farmland share to forfeiture plus an equal-value penalty.

sd:SB 41.title: revise a provision related to criminal invasions of privacy, prohibit the creation and distribution of digitally fabricated material of an identifiable individual, and provide penalties therefor.
sd:SB 41.summary: Makes it a Class 5 felony to knowingly create or share digitally fabricated nude or sexual depictions of an identifiable person, without consent and with intent to self-gratify, harass or harm; also revises the existing invasion-of-privacy offense.

sd:SB 42.title: enhance the penalties for ingestion, possession with intent to deliver, and delivery of a controlled substance in a state correctional facility.
sd:SB 42.summary: Raises the felony class for delivering drugs or controlled substances to state prison inmates from Class 4 to Class 3, and makes ingesting a controlled substance a Class 5 felony for inmates and parolees.

sd:SB 43.title: address search and seizure provisions applicable to digital currency.
sd:SB 43.summary: Defines "digital currency" and includes it as property that can be searched for and seized under state search and seizure law.

sd:SB 44.title: establish investigative subpoena authority to gather business records in certain investigations.
sd:SB 44.summary: Lets the attorney general, with approval from a Hughes County judge, issue investigative subpoenas to electronic and internet providers for subscriber and account records in Division of Criminal Investigation cases on internet crimes against children or human trafficking.

sd:SB 45.title: revise a provision regulating delta-8 tetrahydrocannabinol, THC-O acetate, and hexahydrocannabinol for persons under the age of twenty-one and to provide a penalty therefor.
sd:SB 45.summary: Adds delta-9 THCA to the products it is unlawful to sell to anyone under 21 or for them to buy or possess, adds a prescription exception, and makes selling a Class 1 misdemeanor and other violations Class 2.

sd:SB 49.title: safeguard the integrity, privacy, and security of genetic data and provide a civil penalty therefor.
sd:SB 49.summary: Requires direct-to-consumer genetic testing companies to publish privacy notices and get a consumer's express consent to collect, use, share or retain genetic data and biological samples, with civil penalties for violations.

sd:SB 60.title: restrict ownership of real property interests by certain prohibited entities and to provide for enforcement.
sd:SB 60.summary: Bars certain "prohibited entities" from holding or acquiring real property interests in South Dakota while a military installation exists here, requires them to sell within two to three years, and lets the attorney general subpoena records and seek forfeiture.

sd:SB 69.title: make an appropriation for the purchase of a new Division of Highway Patrol airplane and mission equipment and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 69.summary: Appropriates $5 million from the general fund to the Department of Public Safety to buy a new Highway Patrol airplane and mission equipment and to install that equipment.

sd:SB 71.title: authorize the assumption of certain responsibilities and the waiver of sovereign immunity in connection with certain actions under federal environmental law.
sd:SB 71.summary: Lets the Department of Transportation take over the federal government's National Environmental Policy Act review duties for highway projects by agreement, waives the state's sovereign immunity from suit in federal court for those duties, and has the highway fund pay resulting damages and fees.

sd:SB 74.title: transfer moneys to the general fund from the budget reserve fund and the general revenue replacement fund, and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 74.summary: Transfers $80,854,355 from the budget reserve fund and $20,613,269 from the general revenue replacement fund to the general fund.

sd:SB 75.title: amend the type of entities eligible to participate in the cybersecurity services initiative.
sd:SB 75.summary: Changes a 2024 appropriation of $7 million for a cybersecurity services initiative run by the Attorney General so it can serve counties, municipalities, political-subdivision utilities and nonprofit drinking water and sewer utilities.

sd:SB 76.title: authorize loans from the South Dakota housing infrastructure fund for airport infrastructure.
sd:SB 76.summary: Lets the state housing authority make loans from the housing infrastructure fund of up to $15 million each to airports with scheduled air service in metropolitan areas of at least 125,000 residents, for airport infrastructure.

sd:SB 78.title: revise the General Appropriations Act for fiscal year 2026.
sd:SB 78.summary: Changes dollar amounts in the fiscal year 2026 General Appropriations Act for operating budgets of numerous state agencies and funds.

sd:SB 79.title: make an appropriation to the South Dakota Board of Technical Education to construct an advanced manufacturing laboratory space and classrooms on the campus of Southeast Technical College and to declare an emergency.
sd:SB 79.summary: Appropriates $6 million from the general fund for an advanced manufacturing lab and classrooms at Southeast Technical College, contingent on the college raising $18 million from other sources and no bonds being issued.

sd:SB 81.title: clarify the prohibition on injuring or harassing a service animal.
sd:SB 81.summary: Raises the penalty for harming, harassing or interfering with a service animal from a Class 2 to a Class 1 misdemeanor, drops the harness-and-control condition, and defines "service animal" as a dog trained for tasks directly related to a disability.

sd:SB 82.title: prohibit the misrepresentation of an animal as a service animal and to provide a penalty therefor.
sd:SB 82.summary: Makes it a Class 2 misdemeanor to intentionally misrepresent an animal as a service animal in a public accommodation to gain rights or privileges, and defines "service animal" as a dog trained to perform tasks related to a disability.

sd:SB 88.title: clarify the procedure for a potential condemnor to examine real property absent the property owner's permission.
sd:SB 88.summary: When an owner denies permission, limits a siting-permit project to a minimally invasive examination of the land, not a more invasive survey. Removes the $500 payment to the owner required for common-carrier projects.

sd:SB 90.title: expand the information required to be sent to the prescription drug monitoring program for each registry identification card holder.
sd:SB 90.summary: Adds physical address (none required if homeless) and registry card number to the name and date of birth the Department of Health sends the prescription drug monitoring program, and covers all cardholders, including nonresident ones.

sd:SB 96.title: authorize the imposition of a county option gross receipts tax to reduce owner-occupied property taxes.
sd:SB 96.summary: Allows counties, by ordinance, to impose a gross receipts tax of up to one-half percent on sales taxable under the state sales tax, with proceeds credited against county property taxes, starting with owner-occupied property.

sd:SB 98.title: prevent virtual currency kiosk fraud.
sd:SB 98.summary: Sets rules for licensed virtual currency kiosk operators, including a $1,000 daily and $10,000 thirty-day transaction limit per user, and adds reporting on transactions, refunds and suspicious activity to license renewal reports.

tn:HB 1493.title: Historical Sites and Preservation - As enacted, authorizes local historical boards to lease land owned or managed by such boards for agricultural purposes, with all proceeds received by the boards to be used for the preservation of historic sites and structures. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 11; Title 12; Title 29 and Title 43.
tn:HB 1493.summary: Allows local historical boards to contract with farmers to farm crops on historical-site land of five or more contiguous acres, and to harvest hay on smaller parcels, with proceeds used to preserve historic sites and structures.

tn:HB 1514.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, clarifies that the general assembly occupies the entire field of the regulation of shopping carts, including their purchase, use, taxation, manufacture, ownership, sale, storage, and transportation, to the exclusion of all county or metropolitan government laws, ordinances, resolutions, enactments, or regulations; prohibits a county or metropolitan government, or any agency, department, or official of a county or metropolitan government, from adopting an ordinance, resolution, or other regulation requiring a business to adopt a shopping cart policy of any nature or imposing a fee or fine on a business related to shopping carts. - Amends TCA Title 5, Chapter 1 and Title 6, Chapter 54.
tn:HB 1514.summary: Declares that the state alone regulates shopping carts and bars counties and metropolitan governments from requiring businesses to adopt shopping cart policies or imposing shopping cart fees or fines on them.

tn:HB 1572.title: Sunset Laws - As enacted, extends the department of children's services to June 30, 2028; requires the department to report back to the government operations committee by December 31, 2026, to update the committee on its progress in addressing the findings and observations set forth in the December 2025 performance audit report. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 29 and Title 37, Chapter 5.
tn:HB 1572.summary: As enacted, extends the Department of Children's Services' termination date to June 30, 2028, and requires it to report to a legislative committee by December 31, 2026 on its progress addressing the December 2025 state audit findings.

tn:HB 1652.title: Alcoholic Beverages - As enacted, establishes new premier type tourist resorts, restaurants, community theaters, clubs, retirement centers, premises, and commercial passenger boat companies that can offer liquor by the  drink; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 57.
tn:HB 1652.summary: As enacted, adds definitions of specific community theaters, recreational clubs, social clubs, marinas and other facilities, described by size, features and local population, so they can be licensed to serve liquor by the drink.

tn:HB 1667.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, authorizes municipalities and metropolitan governments to adopt a tiered system of monetary penalties for repeated violations of the same municipal ordinance by the same person or entity within a 12-month period. - Amends TCA Title 6 and Title 7.
tn:HB 1667.summary: As enacted, lets home rule cities, other municipalities and metropolitan governments set, by ordinance, tiered monetary penalties for repeated violations of the same ordinance by the same person or entity within 12 months, for acts on or after July 1, 2026.

tn:HB 1677.title: Licenses - As enacted, enacts the "Military Families Licensing Recognition Act."  - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 58; Title 62; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:HB 1677.summary: As amended, requires state licensing authorities to recognize covered out-of-state professional licenses, as defined in federal law (50 U.S.C. § 4025a), held by servicemembers and spouses who relocate to Tennessee, or to a neighboring state and work here, under military orders. Requires a website notice.

tn:HB 1681.title: Regional Authorities and Special Districts - As enacted, revises various provisions of the Real Estate Infrastructure Development Act of 2025. - Amends TCA Title 7; Title 9; Title 12; Title 13; Title 66; Title 67 and Title 68.
tn:HB 1681.summary: As amended, changes infrastructure development district law to let business improvement districts overlap them, allow bonds per development phase (30 years each), replace the 5 percent cap on administrative set-asides with actual costs, and set dissolution 30 years after the last assessment is first levied.

tn:HB 1690.title: Motor Vehicles - As enacted, prohibits the initial issuance of registration of a motor vehicle if the vehicle has not met the requirements of the Financial Responsibility Law of 1977, which provides insurance and financial responsibility requirements for motor vehicle operators; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 29; Title 55 and Title 56.
tn:HB 1690.summary: As enacted, bars initial vehicle registration without proof of insurance in force 30+ days (through June 30, 2029), raises coverage failure fees from $25 to $500 and $100 to $1,000, and caps noneconomic damages at $375,000 for uninsured owners suing after three noncompliance notices.

tn:HB 1706.title: Immigration - As enacted, creates certain offenses for a person who is unlawfully present in the United States to operate a commercial motor vehicle in this state and a direct employer of such person; requires the law enforcement agency of an officer who arrests a person who is unlawfully present in the United States to operate a commercial motor vehicle in this state to ensure that federal immigration authorities are notified; creates related civil actions for persons injured by an unlawfully present person's operation of a commercial motor vehicle. - Amends TCA Title 55, Chapter 50.
tn:HB 1706.summary: As enacted, creates Class A misdemeanors for unlawfully present people driving a commercial vehicle needing a CDL, and direct employers knowingly allowing it; has agencies notify federal immigration authorities of arrests; makes employers and officials who recklessly issue licenses liable for injuries.

tn:HB 1710.title: Immigration - As enacted, adds local governments to the entities that must verify that each applicant for public benefits is a United States citizen or lawfully present in the United States; authorizes certain investigations of violations of requirements for verification of citizenship or presence for public benefits; requires certain reporting related to such verification for benefits; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 1 and Title 4, Chapter 58.
tn:HB 1710.summary: As enacted, adds counties and cities to those verifying public-benefit applicants' lawful presence; requires government entities to report unlawfully present recipients to the state immigration enforcement division, with a Class A misdemeanor for intentional failure; lets the attorney general withhold state funds from noncomplying localities.

tn:HB 1759.title: Schools, Charter - As enacted, authorizes the establishment of adult public charter schools, which are defined as public charter schools that exclusively serve students who are 18 or older by providing instruction to such students in accordance with the rules for adult high schools promulgated by the state board of education to assist such students in obtaining course credit leading to the attainment of a high school diploma. - Amends TCA Title 4 and Title 49.
tn:HB 1759.summary: Authorizes adult public charter schools, serving only students 18 or older who lack a high school diploma, to open no earlier than the 2029-2030 school year, with a performance framework developed by the Department of Education.

tn:HB 1796.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, enacts the "Essential Governmental Employee Housing Act of 2026"; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 9; Title 12 and Title 67.
tn:HB 1796.summary: Lets AAA/Aaa-rated counties and cities acquire, lease or operate housing developments of 100 or more units for essential local government and school employees, with leases up to 55 years, and revises the definition of a regional retail tourism district.

tn:HB 1802.title: Firearms and Ammunition - As enacted, lowers the standard for the use of deadly force to protect property. - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:HB 1802.summary: As enacted, rewrites the property-defense law to justify deadly force by a person in their lawful residence, not committing a felony or Class A misdemeanor, against imminent arson, burglary, robbery or aggravated animal cruelty, when nothing else works and death, serious injury or grave sexual abuse threatens.

tn:HB 1817.title: Motor Vehicles - As enacted, revises law relative to out-of-service orders issued to commercial drivers and related penalties. - Amends TCA Title 55 and Title 65, Chapter 15.
tn:HB 1817.summary: As enacted, requires out-of-service orders and commercial license suspension, until the driver passes the written test in English, for commercial drivers unable to read and speak English as federal rules require (some hearing-exempt drivers excepted). Takes effect 90 days after notice that federal law allows it.

tn:HB 1844.title: Children - As enacted, revises various provisions governing surrendering custody of unwanted infants. - Amends TCA Title 36, Chapter 1, Part 1 and Title 68, Chapter 11, Part 2.
tn:HB 1844.summary: Lets ambulance stations staffed around the clock accept surrendered newborns, and sets rules for newborn safety devices, including continuous monitoring by staff and calling emergency services when an infant is retrieved.

tn:HB 1881.title: Education - As enacted, revises the assessment testing requirements for students who participate in the education savings account (ESA) program. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 9; Title 12; Title 48; Title 49 and Title 67.
tn:HB 1881.summary: As enacted, requires ESA students in grades 3-11 to take a nationally standardized achievement test or TCAP math and English tests each year; schools give results to parents and, from June 30, 2027, annually to the comptroller's research office.

tn:HB 1885.title: Gambling - As enacted, clarifies that gambling, the operation or possession of gambling devices, and the operation, conducting, or commercial promoting of online sweepstakes games and other forms of online or app-based gambling are unlawful and a violation of  the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act; expands the authority of the sports wagering council to investigate illegal gambling and gaming activity; expands the investigative authority of the attorney general to investigate unlawful activity within the purview of the attorney general. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 4, Chapter 49; Title 8, Chapter 6, Part 4; Title 40, Chapter 2 and Title 47.
tn:HB 1885.summary: Declares gambling, gambling devices and online or app-based gambling unlawful, treats violations as violations of the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act, and expands the attorney general's investigative powers.

tn:HB 1916.title: Real Estate Agents and Brokers - As enacted, exempts an affiliate broker or broker licensed under the Tennessee Real Estate Broker License Act from the additional licensure and classroom hours in training programs requirements for a vacation lodging service firm's designated agent; requires that vacation lodging services be under the supervision of the principal broker of an affiliate broker, broker, or firm. - Amends TCA Title 62, Chapter 13.
tn:HB 1916.summary: Exempts licensed brokers and affiliate brokers from additional licensure and classroom training hours otherwise required for firms providing vacation lodging services, if those services are supervised by the principal broker.

tn:HB 1946.title: Consumer Protection - As enacted, requires the Tennessee advisory commission on intergovernmental relations (TACIR) to conduct a study of the potential regulation of artificial intelligence systems and generative artificial intelligence chatbots in this state. - Amends TCA Title 29; Title 37 and Title 47.
tn:HB 1946.summary: Requires the Tennessee Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations to study possible regulation of artificial intelligence systems and generative AI chatbots in the state.

tn:HB 1951.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, enacts the "Grace Anne Sparks Coercive Suicide Prevention Law of 2026." - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:HB 1951.summary: Creates the Class D felony of coercive suicide: intentionally advising or encouraging another person to commit or attempt suicide within an imminent period, knowing that person has communicated intent to commit suicide.

tn:HB 1959.title: Pharmacy, Pharmacists - As enacted, enacts the "Freedom, Access, and Integrity in Registered Pharmacy (FAIR Rx) Act." - Amends TCA Title 63.
tn:HB 1959.summary: Creates the FAIR Rx Act, which bars any person or entity with over 5 percent ownership from owning or controlling a pharmacy together with both a health insurer and a pharmacy benefits manager, with civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation.

tn:HB 1966.title: Children's Services, Dept. of - As enacted, requires the commissioner to develop a statewide quality assurance program to ensure quality control through monitoring, evaluation, and feedback on the performance of the best practices in the service delivery system and utilizing both qualitative and quantitative data in outcomes-based approaches at the regional level. - Amends TCA Title 37, Chapter 5.
tn:HB 1966.summary: Requires the children's services commissioner to develop a statewide quality assurance program that monitors and evaluates service delivery using qualitative and quantitative data, with a state quality assurance committee and regional coordinators.

tn:HB 1967.title: Sentencing - As enacted, enacts the "James Bardsley, Jr. Life Protection Act." - Amends TCA Title 39, Chapter 13 and Title 55, Chapter 10.
tn:HB 1967.summary: Adds a mandatory one-year minimum sentence, served in full, and a $5,000 to $10,000 fine to the Class E felony for leaving a crash the driver knew or should have known caused a death; applies to offenses on or after July 1, 2026.

tn:HB 2000.title: Schools, Charter - As enacted, allows private postsecondary institutions, including those that are religiously affiliated, to operate a public charter school; allows such institutions to apply to the local board of education or directly to the Tennessee public charter school commission to open a public charter school and to give an enrollment preference to children of the institution's employees or members of its governing body in the same manner afforded to public institutions of higher education. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:HB 2000.summary: Allows regionally accredited private postsecondary institutions with a Tennessee campus, including religiously affiliated ones, to establish public charter schools.

tn:HB 2023.title: Victims' Rights - As enacted, authorizes a court clerk to increase the victims assistance assessment from $45 to $125, with the first $15 of each assessment being paid to the court clerk for processing and handling and the remaining amount being transmitted to the county in which the offense occurred for the exclusive use of the victims assistance program previously designated by the county legislative body. - Amends TCA Section 40-24-109.
tn:HB 2023.summary: Lets courts set the victims assistance assessment on convicted defendants at up to $125 instead of a flat $45, with the first $15 going to the court clerk and the rest to the county's victims assistance program.

tn:HB 2075.title: Mental Health & Substance Abuse Services, Dept. of - As enacted, enacts the "HOPE Treatment Act." - Amends TCA Title 9; Title 33; Title 53; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:HB 2075.summary: Creates the HOPE Treatment Act and an 11-member council on emerging behavioral health treatments, which may authorize and fund Tennessee institutions to join a multistate ibogaine clinical trial consortium; appointments are due by September 1, 2026.

tn:HB 2080.title: Lottery,  Corporation - As enacted, vacates and reconstitutes the board of directors of the Tennessee education lottery corporation; requires certain information maintained by the corporation to be subject to a public records request; terminates the lottery corporation on June 30, 2030. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 10 and Title 49.
tn:HB 2080.summary: Vacates the Tennessee education lottery board on July 1, 2026 and replaces it with nine directors, three each appointed by the governor and the two speakers, and subjects the lottery corporation to state public records and open meetings requirements.

tn:HB 2091.title: Tennessee Fish & Wildlife Commission - As enacted, establishes a statutory schedule of permit fees for the operation of off highway vehicles at North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area. - Amends TCA Title 70, Chapter 9.
tn:HB 2091.summary: Sets permit fees for off-highway vehicles at North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area, from $20 for a one-day resident permit to $300 for a nonresident annual permit, $40 for a sportsman supplement and $700 for a guide. Increases cannot take effect before 2030.

tn:HB 2097.title: TennCare - As enacted, extends the ground ambulance service annual assessment to June 30, 2027; changes the penalty imposed by the bureau on an ambulance provider for each day an assessment remains unpaid from $50 per calendar day to 5 percent of the principal amount owed per month for each month. - Amends TCA Title 71, Chapter 5, Part 15.
tn:HB 2097.summary: Extends the ground ambulance service assessment to June 30, 2027, and changes the penalty for unpaid assessments from $50 per day to 5 percent of the principal owed per month.

tn:HB 2102.title: County Government - As enacted, authorizes a county legislative body operating under the County Purchasing Law of 1957 to set the compensation for the director of accounts and budgets. - Amends TCA Title 5 and Title 8.
tn:HB 2102.summary: Lets a county legislative body operating under the County Purchasing Law of 1957 set the pay of the county's director of accounts and budgets.

tn:HB 2110.title: Health Care - As enacted, makes various changes to health-related laws, including, but not limited to, requiring the commissioner of health to prescribe conditions under which processed and verified claims data found on the UB-92 form are made available to the public; revising law relative to critical access hospitals, and revising law relative to certificates of need. - Amends TCA Title 33; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:HB 2110.summary: Changes health facility regulation: lets the Health Facilities Commission license burn units, neonatal intensive care units, MRI and PET services, sets a notice and eligibility process for critical access hospitals, and allows charging applicants and licensees site-visit costs.

tn:HB 2114.title: Newspapers and Publications - As enacted, requires the Tennessee advisory commission on intergovernmental relations (TACIR) to conduct a study to determine if newspapers of general circulation remain the most efficient and effective manner for governments to provide the public with transparent and accessible information. - Amends TCA Title 1, Chapter 3 and Title 8, Chapter 44.
tn:HB 2114.summary: Requires the Tennessee advisory commission on intergovernmental relations (TACIR) to study whether newspapers of general circulation remain the most efficient way for governments to give public notice, and report findings and recommendations to legislative committee chairs.

tn:HB 2140.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, makes various changes relative to the offense of organized retail crime. - Amends TCA Title 18; Title 38, Chapter 6, Part 1 and Title 39.
tn:HB 2140.summary: Changes the organized retail crime offense by counting theft value over 180 days instead of 90, adding use of masks or missing, altered or concealed license plates, and requiring a 30-day minimum sentence if a firearm, ammunition, firearm-related or anti-theft device was used or possessed.

tn:HB 2196.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, authorizes Putnam County and incorporated cities within the county to regulate sober living homes for recovery from alcohol, drug, and substance abuse to the extent such regulation complies with the Fair Housing Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act. - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 51, Part 26.
tn:HB 2196.summary: As enacted, changes the definition of 'local government' for regulating sober living homes to counties, and cities within them, with 2020 census populations of 366,200-366,300 or 79,800-79,900.

tn:HB 2204.title: Law Enforcement - As enacted, requires TACIR to conduct a study of the salaries and other benefits paid to state and local law enforcement officers in this state; authorizes the commissioner of safety to establish a hazardous duty designation for members of the highway patrol that may be used to authorize additional compensation for designated members. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 8; Title 9 and Title 38.
tn:HB 2204.summary: Requires TACIR to study salaries and benefits paid to state and local law enforcement officers, and lets the safety commissioner create a hazardous duty designation for highway patrol members that can support extra pay.

tn:HB 2207.title: Taxes - As enacted, provides that an application for an exemption from property taxation for property owned by a religious, charitable, scientific, or nonprofit educational organization that is filed within 180 days after the exempt use of the property began will be effective as of the date the exempt use began, if the application is made after May 20th of the year for which the exemption is sought, but prior to the end of the year; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 67.
tn:HB 2207.summary: Extends from 30 to 180 days the window for religious, charitable, scientific and nonprofit educational organizations to apply for a property tax exemption effective from the date exempt use began, and makes other tax administration changes.

tn:HB 2210.title: Natural Disasters - As enacted, enacts the "Local Disaster Displacement Tax Relief Act." - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 4; Title 58 and Title 67, Chapter 4.
tn:HB 2210.summary: Lets a county under a declared emergency authorize hotel operators and short-term rental marketplaces to waive hotel occupancy taxes, or reimburse taxes paid, for residents displaced from their homes, for up to 14 days.

tn:HB 2270.title: Children - As enacted, establishes the children's digital protection fund within the state treasury.  - Amends TCA Title 9, Chapter 4, Part 2.
tn:HB 2270.summary: Creates a children's digital protection fund in the state treasury to receive money from state legal claims over the effects of social media, online gaming and other digital technology on minors' mental health.

tn:HB 2290.title: Hospitals and Health Care Facilities - As enacted, requires each fertility clinic operating in this state to obtain a certificate from the department of health to perform assisted reproductive technology services. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 29; Title 36; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:HB 2290.summary: As enacted, requires each fertility clinic to hold a state health department certificate, renewed every two years, showing professional-society membership, an embryo transfer plan if it closes, and a passed lab inspection. Sets qualifications for clinical directors.

tn:HB 2301.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, makes revisions to the offense of adulteration of food, liquids, or pharmaceuticals.  - Amends TCA Title 39; Title 40 and Title 57.
tn:HB 2301.summary: Adds adulterating food, drink or medicine with intent to cause involuntary intoxication to the adulteration offense, punishable as a Class D felony.

tn:HB 2305.title: Teachers, Principals and School Personnel - As enacted, clarifies that certain individuals who have not completed the amount of clinical practice required by the educator preparation provider in which the individual is enrolled may receive a temporary clinical permit if all other requirements for the permit are satisfied; allows such an individual who is issued a temporary clinical permit to meet the clinical practice requirements of the EPP in which the individual is enrolled by combining the amount of clinical practice the individual completed  before being issued a temporary clinical permit with the amount of time the individual taught under the temporary clinical permit. - Amends TCA Title 49, Chapter 5.
tn:HB 2305.summary: Lets individuals who completed educator preparation coursework except clinical practice, whether or not they have begun it, receive a temporary clinical permit, and counts time taught under the permit toward the clinical practice requirement.

tn:HB 2309.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, makes revisions to law relative to offenses occurring at a house of worship. - Amends TCA Title 29 and Title 39.
tn:HB 2309.summary: Requires fines of at least double the damage for vandalism at houses of worship, sets felony penalties (Class E; Class C if repeat) for interfering with worship by force, threat or obstruction or for damaging one, and allows civil suits and attorney general actions.

tn:HB 2320.title: Regional Authorities and Special Districts - As enacted, revises the "Convention Center Authorities Act of 2009" as the "Convention Center and Agricultural Exposition Authorities Act." - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 89.
tn:HB 2320.summary: Renames the Convention Center Authorities Act the Convention Center and Agricultural Exposition Authorities Act, and adds agricultural exposition facilities to the projects such authorities may run, with fair operators able to appoint an extra board director.

tn:HB 2328.title: County Government - As enacted, applies the Neighborhood Preservation Act to Tipton County; authorizes Montgomery County and Tipton County to participate in the Tennessee Local Land Bank Program. - Amends TCA Title 5 and Title 13.
tn:HB 2328.summary: As enacted, applies the Neighborhood Preservation Act to Tipton County and authorizes Montgomery and Tipton counties to participate in the Tennessee Local Land Bank Program.

tn:HB 2359.title: Tobacco, Tobacco Products - As enacted, expands the definition of "consumable material" to include natural and synthetic liquid nicotine solutions and liquid nicotine analogues for purposes of the taxation of vapor products containing such material; requires the alcoholic beverage commission to issue the fines for the offense of selling or offering for sale a vapor product for retail sale in this state to anyone under 21. - Amends TCA Title 39, Chapter 17; Title 43; Title 57 and Title 67, Chapter 4, Part 10.
tn:HB 2359.summary: Expands the vapor product tax definition of consumable material to include natural and synthetic liquid nicotine solutions and liquid nicotine analogues, and specifies that the alcoholic beverage commission issues fines for selling vapor products to anyone under 21.

tn:HB 2381.title: Public Utilities - As enacted, requires a utility to provide material that is required for construction of utility infrastructure for the customer's or approved contractor's use at the same price as the utility paid for the material, if such material is available only from the utility; authorizes a customer or approved contractor installing utility infrastructure to install street lights; prohibits a utility from requiring a customer or approved contractor from installing street lights; prohibits certain fees for inspections and review of plans and designs from exceeding a combined total of 10% of the proposed cost of the project. - Amends TCA Title 7; Title 13, Chapter 7; Title 65 and Title 68.
tn:HB 2381.summary: Requires a utility to sell customers or approved contractors, at the price the utility paid, construction materials available only from the utility; lets them install street lights without requiring it; and caps combined inspection and plan-review fees at 10 percent of project cost.

tn:HB 2385.title: Sewage - As enacted, clarifies that a utility system providing waste water service must provide a connection if certain criteria are met. - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 35; Title 7, Chapter 82 and Title 68, Chapter 221.
tn:HB 2385.summary: Requires a utility providing wastewater service to connect a property owner on request when a gravity sewer line, or a reachable sewer force main, lies on or next to the owner's property.

tn:HB 2413.title: Children - As enacted, enacts the "Tennessee Child Care Red Tape Reduction Act." - Amends TCA Title 13, Chapter 7 and Title 71, Chapter 3.
tn:HB 2413.summary: Requires local governments to give child care agency permit applications the same priority as affordable housing applications, assigned for review within five business days, and makes the state fire marshal the only fire safety inspector for child care licensure.

tn:HB 2422.title: Education - As enacted, requires the department of education to implement a pilot program to evaluate whether administering fewer district- and state-mandated assessments results in students achieving greater academic success; adds an additional method by which a student who is not proficient in ELA, as determined by the student's achieving a performance level rating of “approaching” on the ELA portion of the student's most recent TCAP test, may be promoted. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:HB 2422.summary: Requires the Department of Education to run a pilot in up to 10 school systems testing whether fewer mandated assessments improve achievement, and lets a pilot third grader be promoted if they score within the 50th percentile on a state-approved reading screener.

tn:HB 2428.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, increases the penalty for assaulting a first responder from a Class A misdemeanor with a mandatory fine of $5,000 and a mandatory minimum of 30 days incarceration to a Class E felony with a mandatory fine of $10,000 and a mandatory minimum of 60 days incarceration. - Amends TCA Title 39 and Title 40.
tn:HB 2428.summary: Raises the penalty for assaulting a law enforcement officer or first responder from a Class A misdemeanor to a Class E felony, with a mandatory $10,000 fine and 60-day mandatory minimum incarceration.

tn:HB 2476.title: Public Funds and Financing - As enacted, revises law relative to pension plans and proxy advisors. - Amends TCA Title 9, Chapter 4.
tn:HB 2476.summary: As enacted, requires local government pension plans to invest and vote shares for financial reasons, report annually by September 1 on proxy advisor use and votes, and bars proxy advisory firms with conflicts of interest from advising those plans.

tn:HB 2485.title: Tennessee Investment in Student Achievement (TISA) - As enacted, requires the TISA review committee to study and include in its annual report recommendations for how this state may revise the ways in which it identifies economically disadvantaged students to ensure this state is accurately identifying the students in need of additional resources and recommendations for how this state may better support economically disadvantaged students through the TISA. - Amends TCA Title 49, Chapter 1 and Title 49, Chapter 3.
tn:HB 2485.summary: Requires the state's school funding formula review committee to study and recommend in its annual report how Tennessee identifies economically disadvantaged students and how the formula could better support them.

tn:HB 2491.title: District Attorneys - As enacted, eliminates the fraud and economic crimes fees and assessments in criminal prosecutions for counties that have enacted a $12.50 court cost to be used for supplemental funding for the district attorney general's office; requires existing funds in fraud and economic crimes prosecution fund to be remitted back to the county government of original assessment and collection. - Amends TCA Title 40, Chapter 3.
tn:HB 2491.summary: Stops enforcement of fraud and economic crimes fees in a county that enacts the $12.50 court cost for district attorney funding, and returns the fraud fund balance to the county of collection once the new cost's collections match it.

tn:HB 2502.title: Banks and Financial Institutions - As enacted, clarifies that the service of transmitting money from a location originating in this state to a location outside of the United States or its territories is a taxable service and that such a tax is generally levied on the amount of money transmitted; requires revenues generated from such a tax to be allocated to certain funds and purposes. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 38; Title 39; Title 45; Title 47; Title 49 and Title 67.
tn:HB 2502.summary: Taxes money transmission from Tennessee to places outside the U.S. by licensed transmitters at $10 per transaction plus 2% of amounts over $500, with revenue split among the general fund, TennCare hospital buybacks, child care, workforce housing, and teacher internships, starting January 1, 2027.

tn:HB 2503.title: Insurance, Health, Accident - As enacted, authorizes a health insurance entity to offer a short-term limited-duration plan and hospital indemnity coverage on the marketplace. - Amends TCA Title 3; Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 10; Title 12; Title 29; Title 35; Title 36; Title 37; Title 39; Title 40; Title 41; Title 42; Title 45; Title 47; Title 49; Title 50; Title 52; Title 53; Title 56; Title 58; Title 63; Title 67; Title 68 and Title 71.
tn:HB 2503.summary: Lets health insurers offer short-term limited-duration plans, with deductibles up to $10,000 and a $1 million maximum benefit, and hospital indemnity coverage on the marketplace, starting 30 days after federal law or rules allow it.

tn:HB 2509.title: Housing - As enacted, establishes the community workforce housing innovation pilot program to be administered by the Tennessee housing development agency; authorizes the agency to provide loans to an applicant for construction or rehabilitation of workforce housing in each of the three grand divisions; requires the housing to be affordable to natural persons or families who meet certain criteria. - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 53; Title 13; Title 48, Chapter 101, Part 3; Title 56 and Title 67.
tn:HB 2509.summary: Creates a pilot program in which the Tennessee Housing Development Agency makes loans for building or rehabilitating workforce housing for households earning over 80% and up to 150% of area median income, with applications due March 31, 2027.

tn:HB 2510.title: Taxes, Sales - As enacted, extends the deadline by which a county that borders at least three distressed rural counties must apply to be eligible to retain the sales and use tax generated from a commercial development district from December 31, 2026, to December 31, 2040; extends the deadline for the commissioner of finance and administration to approve a commercial development district from June 30, 2031, to June 30, 2041. - Amends TCA Title 67, Chapter 6.
tn:HB 2510.summary: Extends from December 31, 2026 to December 31, 2040 the deadline for eligible counties bordering three distressed rural counties to apply for commercial development district sales tax allocation, and extends the district approval deadline from June 30, 2031 to June 30, 2041.

tn:HB 2530.title: Boards and Commissions - As enacted, revises law regulating professions under the department of commerce and insurance. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 29, Part 2; Title 20, Chapter 9, Part 6; Title 55, Chapter 17, Part 1; Title 62, Chapter 13; Title 62, Chapter 18; Title 62, Chapter 2; Title 62, Chapter 20; Title 62, Chapter 27; Title 62, Chapter 35; Title 62, Chapter 4; Title 62, Chapter 6; Title 62, Chapter 76; Title 68, Chapter 102 and Title 68, Chapter 105.
tn:HB 2530.summary: As introduced, merges the land surveyors board into the architects and engineers board, ends interior designer and polygraph examiner licensing, lets contractors post a surety bond instead of a financial statement, and changes real estate broker licensing rules.

tn:HB 2533.title: Education - As enacted, makes various revisions to education law, including, but not limited to, prohibiting parents from using funds deposited in a participating student's IEA to make contributions to an achieving a better life experience account for purposes of the ABLE Act, and requiring the Title VI coordinator for a LEA or public charter school to investigate certain complaints of antisemitic discrimination and harassment reported to the LEA or public charter school before formally reporting the incidents and complaints to the Title VI coordinator designated by the department of education. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 29; Title 5, Chapter 21; Title 8, Chapter 50, Part 8; Title 49, Chapter 10, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 10, Part 14; Title 49, Chapter 11, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 11, Part 8; Title 49, Chapter 13; Title 49, Chapter 15, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 16, Part 2; Title 49, Chapter 17; Section 49-2-203; Title 49, Chapter 3, Part 1; Title 49, Chapter 5, Part 4; Title 49, Chapter 50, Part 10; Title 49, Chapter 50, Part 16; Title 49, Chapter 50, Part 18; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 10; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 15; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 22; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 23; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 30; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 34; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 42; Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 81; Title 49, Chapter 1, Part 2; Title 49, Chapter 1, Part 3 and Section 68-204-110.
tn:HB 2533.summary: Makes many education law changes, including barring parents from using individualized education account funds for ABLE accounts, requiring school Title VI coordinators to investigate antisemitism complaints first, and allowing charter schools to use remote instruction under the same rules as districts.

tn:HB 2539.title: Health Care - As enacted, makes revisions to health law, including, but not limited to, revising certain reporting requirements, requiring a person licensed by the board of examiners in psychology to complete certain suicide prevention training, defining palliative care, and clarifying certain rulemaking authority of health boards and the commissioner of health. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 8; Title 33; Title 36; Title 37; Title 48; Title 49; Title 52; Title 53; Title 55; Title 56; Title 62; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:HB 2539.summary: Makes health law changes: ends several annual controlled substance reports, requires licensed psychologists to complete suicide prevention training, redefines palliative care, and lets the health commissioner take over rulemaking a board has not started 60 days before a law takes effect.

tn:HB 2541.title: Salaries and Benefits - As enacted, expresses the public policy that the prevailing wage rate be paid to workers on non-state contracts for construction projects on public highways; makes other revisions to the Prevailing Wage Act for State Highway Construction Projects. - Amends TCA Title 12, Chapter 4, Part 4.
tn:HB 2541.summary: Revises the state highway prevailing wage law: limits "state contract" to written agreements, declares policy that the prevailing wage be paid on non-state public highway projects funded with federal or state highway funds, and lets the labor commissioner name a designee.

tn:HB 2542.title: Unemployment Compensation - As enacted, removes a requirement that work be deemed suitable for a claimant if certain criteria are met and a claimant's gross weekly wages equal or exceed certain threshold percentages of the claimant's weekly wage for insured work for the quarter of the base period when the claimant's wages were greatest. - Amends TCA Section 50-7-303.
tn:HB 2542.summary: Removes the rule that work counts as suitable for an unemployment claimant when it pays set percentages of the claimant's prior highest-quarter average weekly wage.

tn:HB 2552.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, requires a local government responsible for reviewing a development application, development plan, or a site inspection submitted by a developer for the purpose of developing real property in this state, within 60 business days of the submission, to approve the application, plan, or site inspection or add the submission to the next available agenda of either the planning commission or the governing body; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 7.
tn:HB 2552.summary: Requires local governments to approve a developer's application, plan, or site inspection, or put it on the next agenda, within 60 business days, or it is deemed approved; limits deficiency reports to two and sets deadlines for releasing completed-work bonds.

tn:HB 2592.title: Public Utility Commission - As enacted, requires, for an electric utility providing services outside the corporate limits of the home municipality, expansion of the utility board to provide representation on the board for such outside locality. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 12; Title 13; Title 54; Title 64; Title 65; Title 68 and Title 69.
tn:HB 2592.summary: As amended, requires electric utilities owned by, or in a county with, 350,000+ people to add voting board seats for the home county and for each outside county with a locality served by 3,500+ customers, if the county appoints.

tn:HB 2612.title: Driver Licenses - As enacted, requires driver license station staff to inquire of applicants whether the applicant would like a driver license that complies with the federal REAL ID Act of 2005 or does not comply with such act; makes other related revisions. - Amends TCA Title 55, Chapter 50.
tn:HB 2612.summary: Requires driver license station staff to ask applicants whether they want a REAL ID-compliant or non-compliant license, and to give them a printed document to sign listing the required documents and uses of each type.

tn:HB 2616.title: Open Meetings - As enacted, authorizes a governing body to conduct an executive session for the purpose of interviewing applicants for employment as director-level staff of the body without providing public notice of such session. - Amends TCA Title 8.
tn:HB 2616.summary: As enacted, allows a governing body to hold a closed executive session, without public notice, to interview applicants for director-level staff jobs. Deliberation and votes must occur in an open, noticed meeting.

tn:HB 2630.title: Bond Issues - As enacted, authorizes the state to issue and sell bonds. -
tn:HB 2630.summary: Authorizes the state to issue up to $438 million in general obligation bonds: $311 million for building projects and local grants through Finance and Administration, and $127 million for highways, bridges and buildings through Transportation.

tn:HB 2664.title: Stanton - Subject to local approval, revises the general powers of the town; revises provisions related to the town judge. - Amends Chapter 142 of the Private Acts of 1990.
tn:HB 2664.summary: Rewrites the section of the Town of Stanton's charter listing the town's powers, and revises provisions on the town judge, subject to local approval.

tn:HB 2666.title: Shelby County - Subject to local approval, changes the conditions under which the occupancy tax will no longer be levied; changes the allocation of the revenue from the occupancy tax if the tenant of the indoor sports facility no longer occupies such facility. - Amends Chapter 131 of the Private Acts of 1969; as amended.
tn:HB 2666.summary: Subject to a two-thirds county vote, ends Shelby County's hotel occupancy tax at the later of an NBA franchise no longer being a tenant of the indoor sports facility or June 30, 2050, and changes revenue allocation if the tenant leaves.

tn:HB 684.title: Human Services, Dept. of - As enacted, requires the commissioner to provide the commissioner of correction with a form application for food assistance for use by inmates who are preparing for release. - Amends TCA Title 71, Chapter 5, Part 3.
tn:HB 684.summary: Requires the human services commissioner to give the correction commissioner a food assistance application form for inmates preparing for release, including an option to decline to apply.

tn:HB 753.title: Taxes, Real Property - As enacted, establishes the process for property tax assessment and valuation of multi-unit rental housing that receives a federal, state, or local incentive based on low-income renter restrictions. - Amends TCA Title 7; Title 13; Title 48; Title 49; Title 67 and Title 68.
tn:HB 753.summary: As enacted, sets how multi-unit rental housing with government-restricted, low-income rents is valued for property tax, using net operating income adjusted for restricted rents and excluding housing tax credits, in localities that adopt it.

tn:HB 794.title: Utilities, Utility Districts - As enacted, establishes a process for a municipality that operates a sewerage system outside of its corporate boundaries and has imposed a moratorium on new sewer connections outside of its corporate boundaries for a period of five or more consecutive years to extend sanitary sewer service or allow sewer connection only to property located within an adjacency area if the property owner or developer agrees to pay, or the municipality assesses, a housing surcharge. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 12; Title 13; Title 29; Title 54; Title 64; Title 65; Title 68 and Title 69.
tn:HB 794.summary: As enacted, lets a city with a five-year-plus moratorium on new sewer connections outside its limits extend service only to adjacent property whose owner pays a housing surcharge (up to 3% of appraised value for single-family lots, 5% commercial), deposited in an affordable housing fund.

tn:SB 1232.title: Courts - As enacted, enacts the "Recovery Court Renewal Act." - Amends TCA Title 40, Chapter 32, Part 1.
tn:SB 1232.summary: As enacted, allows expunction of an offense committed at least ten years after a DUI conviction, for a person with one DUI conviction who completed a recovery court program and sentence and has no prior expunction. Excludes offenses involving a vehicle and alcohol or drugs.

tn:SB 1326.title: Taxes, Real Property - As enacted, provides that a collecting official or the division of property assessments is not required to request documentation verifying the income of an elderly person seeking tax relief if the applicant is at least 80 years old and meets certain other requirements. - Amends TCA Title 67, Chapter 5, Part 7.
tn:SB 1326.summary: As enacted, lets officials skip requesting income documentation from property tax relief applicants aged 80 or older who received relief the prior five years and whose income is under the limit; annual reapplication continues through a simplified form.

tn:SB 1490.title: Historical Sites and Preservation - As enacted, authorizes local historical boards to lease land owned or managed by such boards for agricultural purposes, with all proceeds received by the boards to be used for the preservation of historic sites and structures. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 11; Title 12; Title 29 and Title 43.
tn:SB 1490.summary: Allows local historical boards to contract with farmers to farm crops on historical-site land of five or more contiguous acres, and to harvest hay on smaller parcels, with proceeds used to preserve historic sites and structures.

tn:SB 1493.title: Computers and Electronic Processing - As enacted, requires TACIR to study artificial intelligence and submit a report to the governor and both speakers by January 31, 2027. - Amends TCA Title 29; Title 33; Title 39 and Title 47.
tn:SB 1493.summary: Requires the Tennessee Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations to study risks of artificial intelligence, including to children and chatbot use as emotional or health support, and report to the governor and legislative speakers by January 31, 2027.

tn:SB 1513.title: Sunset Laws - As enacted, extends the department of children's services to June 30, 2028; requires the department to report back to the government operations committee by December 31, 2026, to update the committee on its progress in addressing the findings and observations set forth in the December 2025 performance audit report. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 29 and Title 37, Chapter 5.
tn:SB 1513.summary: Extends the Department of Children's Services to June 30, 2028, and requires it to report by December 31, 2026 to the legislature's education, health, and general welfare joint evaluation committee on its progress addressing the December 2025 performance audit findings.

tn:SB 1585.title: Education - As enacted, revises the assessment testing requirements for students who participate in the education savings account (ESA) program. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 9; Title 12; Title 48; Title 49 and Title 67.
tn:SB 1585.summary: Lets education savings account students in grades 3 through 11 take a nationally standardized achievement test instead of TCAP math and English tests, and requires schools to give results to parents and, from 2027, to the comptroller's research office.

tn:SB 1587.title: Immigration - As enacted, creates certain offenses for a person who is unlawfully present in the United States to operate a commercial motor vehicle in this state and a direct employer of such person; requires the law enforcement agency of an officer who arrests a person who is unlawfully present in the United States to operate a commercial motor vehicle in this state to ensure that federal immigration authorities are notified; creates related civil actions for persons injured by an unlawfully present person's operation of a commercial motor vehicle. - Amends TCA Title 55, Chapter 50.
tn:SB 1587.summary: Creates Class A misdemeanors for unlawfully present people driving a commercial vehicle needing a CDL, and direct employers knowingly allowing it; has agencies notify federal immigration authorities of arrests; makes employers and officials who recklessly issue licenses liable for injuries.

tn:SB 1592.title: Municipal Government - As enacted, creates a process for continuing funding for a municipal LEA when the municipal legislative body and the governing body for the LEA cannot agree on a budget; provides a process for continuing funding of municipal operations when a municipal legislative body has not adopted a budget by the first day of a fiscal year. - Amends TCA Title 6, Chapter 56, Part 1 and Title 6, Chapter 56, Part 2.
tn:SB 1592.summary: Sets a city school district's budget at the minimum local match and maintenance of effort if the city and school board do not agree by August 31, and continues the prior year's city budget for two months, or three with comptroller approval.

tn:SB 1602.title: Sentencing - As enacted, enacts the "James Bardsley, Jr. Life Protection Act." - Amends TCA Title 39, Chapter 13 and Title 55, Chapter 10.
tn:SB 1602.summary: Enacts the James Bardsley, Jr. Life Protection Act: a driver who flees a fatal crash faces at least one year in prison served in full, plus a $5,000 to $10,000 fine, in addition to the Class E felony. Applies to offenses after July 1, 2026.

tn:SB 1620.title: Alcoholic Beverages - As enacted, establishes new premier type tourist resorts, restaurants, community theaters, clubs, retirement centers, premises, and commercial passenger boat companies that can offer liquor by the  drink; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 57.
tn:SB 1620.summary: Adds specifically described resorts, restaurants, a community theater, clubs, a retirement center, premises, and a boat company to those eligible to sell liquor by the drink, and lets restaurants in special historic districts qualify.

tn:SB 1665.title: Civil Procedure - As enacted, clarifies that the same immunities from civil liability, adverse action, and disciplinary action, and duties, that apply to this state, state employees, public schools, LEAs, public school students, public school teachers, public school employees, public school contractors, public institutions of higher education, public higher education students, public higher education faculty, public higher education employees, and public higher education contractors with regard to the use of a pronoun consistent with an individual's sex apply when using an honorific that is consistent with an individual's sex. - Amends TCA Title 8, Chapter 50; Title 49, Chapter 7, Part 24 and Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 51.
tn:SB 1665.summary: Extends existing pronoun rules to honorifics: same immunities from civil liability, adverse action and discipline for using a sex-consistent honorific, and same duties, for state employees and contractors, public schools, and public colleges and their employees, students and contractors.

tn:SB 1672.title: Public Funds and Financing - As enacted, creates the joint capital tourism board; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 9 and Title 67.
tn:SB 1672.summary: Creates a nine-member joint capital tourism board attached to the comptroller's office, with appointees of the governor and legislative speakers plus Davidson County tourism and convention officials, to guide handling of excess convention center tax revenue, and changes related taxes.

tn:SB 1681.title: Hospitals and Health Care Facilities - As enacted, prohibits a hospital emergency department, including a satellite emergency department, from denying to a woman who presents at such facility and purports or, if incapacitated, appears to be pregnant and experiencing active labor, other symptoms associated with active labor, or an emergency medical condition, an appropriate medical screening examination within the capability of the emergency department, including ancillary services routinely available to the emergency department, to determine whether or not an emergency medical condition or active labor exists; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:SB 1681.summary: Requires hospital emergency departments to give pregnant women in labor or with an emergency medical condition a medical screening exam, then provide stabilizing treatment or transfer, with informed-consent rules for refusal.

tn:SB 1692.title: Licenses - As enacted, enacts the "Military Families Licensing Recognition Act."  - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 58; Title 62; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:SB 1692.summary: Creates the Military Families Licensing Recognition Act, requiring state licensing authorities to comply with federal law for servicemembers and spouses with covered licenses who relocate under military orders to Tennessee, or to a neighboring state and seek to work here.

tn:SB 1700.title: Consumer Protection - As enacted, requires the Tennessee advisory commission on intergovernmental relations (TACIR) to conduct a study of the potential regulation of artificial intelligence systems and generative artificial intelligence chatbots in this state. - Amends TCA Title 29; Title 37 and Title 47.
tn:SB 1700.summary: Requires the Tennessee advisory commission on intergovernmental relations (TACIR) to study possible regulation of artificial intelligence systems and generative AI chatbots in the state and publish a report on its findings and recommendations.

tn:SB 1747.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, creates an offense of recklessly discharging a firearm into the air, ground, a body of water, or an object in close proximity to the person if the firearm is discharged at a place of public gathering or at a public event where there are at least 25 people in attendance at the time of the discharge; punishes the offense as a Class A misdemeanor; specifies certain exceptions to the offense. - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:SB 1747.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor to recklessly fire a gun into the air, ground, water, or a nearby object at a public gathering or event with 25 or more people, with exceptions for officers, military, hunting, shooting ranges, and defense against animals.

tn:SB 1748.title: Motor Vehicles - As enacted, revises law relative to out-of-service orders issued to commercial drivers and related penalties. - Amends TCA Title 55 and Title 65, Chapter 15.
tn:SB 1748.summary: Requires out-of-service orders and commercial license suspension, until the driver passes the written test in English, for commercial drivers unable to read and speak English as federal rules require (some hearing-exempt drivers excepted). Takes effect 90 days after notice that federal law allows it.

tn:SB 1762.title: Schools, Charter - As enacted, authorizes the establishment of adult public charter schools, which are defined as public charter schools that exclusively serve students who are 18 or older by providing instruction to such students in accordance with the rules for adult high schools promulgated by the state board of education to assist such students in obtaining course credit leading to the attainment of a high school diploma. - Amends TCA Title 4 and Title 49.
tn:SB 1762.summary: Authorizes adult public charter schools that serve only students 18 or older, follow state board rules for adult high schools to help students earn credits toward a diploma, and charge no registration, enrollment or tuition fees.

tn:SB 1771.title: Zoning - As enacted, authorizes certain counties to adopt a resolution prohibiting a municipality or regional zoning commission from exercising zoning authority outside of the boundaries of the municipality. - Amends TCA Title 5; Title 6; Title 7 and Title 13.
tn:SB 1771.summary: Lets a county legislative body, by resolution, bar municipalities and regional planning commissions from zoning outside municipal boundaries, voiding existing rules, and requires annexation declarations for development in urban growth boundaries. Covers counties under 341,500 residents, excluding metropolitan governments.

tn:SB 1772.title: Regional Authorities and Special Districts - As enacted, authorizes the Megasite Authority of West Tennessee and certain law enforcement agencies to enter into a written agreement authorizing sworn peace officers of the law enforcement agency to enforce certain traffic laws on one or more designated private megasite roadways identified in the agreement. - Amends TCA Title 54 and Title 64, Chapter 9.
tn:SB 1772.summary: Lets the Megasite Authority of West Tennessee sign written agreements allowing sworn officers of certain law enforcement agencies to enforce certain traffic laws on designated private megasite roads.

tn:SB 1773.title: Children - As enacted, revises various provisions governing surrendering custody of unwanted infants. - Amends TCA Title 36, Chapter 1, Part 1 and Title 68, Chapter 11, Part 2.
tn:SB 1773.summary: Adds ambulance stations with staff scheduled around the clock to the facilities that can accept a surrendered newborn, and requires newborn safety devices to be continuously monitored by a facility employee or medical professional.

tn:SB 1783.title: Driver Licenses - As enacted, requires driver license station staff to inquire of applicants whether the applicant would like a driver license that complies with the federal REAL ID Act of 2005 or does not comply with such act; makes other related revisions. - Amends TCA Title 55, Chapter 50.
tn:SB 1783.summary: Requires driver license station staff to ask applicants for a driver license whether they want a REAL ID compliant or non-compliant license and to have them sign a printed selection form; excludes renewals of REAL ID licenses.

tn:SB 1786.title: Real Estate Agents and Brokers - As enacted, exempts an affiliate broker or broker licensed under the Tennessee Real Estate Broker License Act from the additional licensure and classroom hours in training programs requirements for a vacation lodging service firm's designated agent; requires that vacation lodging services be under the supervision of the principal broker of an affiliate broker, broker, or firm. - Amends TCA Title 62, Chapter 13.
tn:SB 1786.summary: Exempts licensed brokers and affiliate brokers from additional licensure and classroom training hours otherwise required for firms providing vacation lodging services, if those services are supervised by the principal broker.

tn:SB 1793.title: Recycling - As enacted, establishes the office of cooperative marketing for recyclables and the recycling market development and diversion advisory council. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7 and Title 68, Chapter 211.
tn:SB 1793.summary: Expands the duties of the Office of Cooperative Marketing for Recyclables and creates an 18-member advisory council on recyclable-material markets that ends June 30, 2030 unless extended.

tn:SB 1814.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, creates a Class A misdemeanor offense of intentionally moving, altering, destroying, or removing a monument the person knows, or reasonably should know, is a property corner monument, historic land surveying monument, or geodetic control monument. - Amends TCA Title 39; Title 62, Chapter 18 and Title 66.
tn:SB 1814.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor to intentionally move without replacing, alter, destroy or remove a monument the person knows or should know is a property corner, historic survey or geodetic control monument, exempting transportation department employees and contractors on official duty.

tn:SB 1815.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, enacts the "Grace Anne Sparks Coercive Suicide Prevention Law of 2026." - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:SB 1815.summary: Creates the Class D felony of coercive suicide: intentionally advising or encouraging another person to commit or attempt suicide within an imminent period, knowing that person has communicated intent to commit suicide.

tn:SB 1826.title: Open Meetings - As enacted, authorizes emergency communications district boards of directors to participate in board meetings electronically under the open meetings law. - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 86, Part 3 and Title 8, Chapter 44, Part 1.
tn:SB 1826.summary: Lets emergency communications district boards of directors take part in meetings by electronic means under the open meetings law.

tn:SB 1847.title: Firearms and Ammunition - As enacted, lowers the standard for the use of deadly force to protect property. - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:SB 1847.summary: Rewrites the property-defense law to justify deadly force by a person in their lawful residence, not committing a felony or Class A misdemeanor, against imminent arson, burglary, robbery or aggravated animal cruelty, when nothing else works and death, serious injury or grave sexual abuse threatens.

tn:SB 1849.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, enacts the "Essential Governmental Employee Housing Act of 2026"; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 9; Title 12 and Title 67.
tn:SB 1849.summary: Creates the Essential Governmental Employee Housing Act of 2026, letting AAA-rated local governments acquire, lease, and operate developments of 100+ units for local government and school employees, funded by bonds or lease pledges, after comptroller approval. Also changes the retail tourism district definition.

tn:SB 1868.title: Children's Services, Dept. of - As enacted, requires a child placed in the custody of the department to remain in custody so long as necessary to complete treatment or services, which must be evidence-based and provided by a qualified provider; makes other changes to child custody law; creates a juvenile commitment review task force to examine system issues and service gaps for certain children committed to the custody of the department. - Amends TCA Title 37, Chapter 1, Part 1.
tn:SB 1868.summary: Keeps committed children in Department of Children's Services custody as needed to finish evidence-based treatment, capped at six months plus up to six more if services require custody or the child assaulted staff; creates a juvenile commitment review task force.

tn:SB 1874.title: Unemployment Compensation - As enacted, removes a requirement that work be deemed suitable for a claimant if certain criteria are met and a claimant's gross weekly wages equal or exceed certain threshold percentages of the claimant's weekly wage for insured work for the quarter of the base period when the claimant's wages were greatest. - Amends TCA Section 50-7-303.
tn:SB 1874.summary: As enacted, repeals the wage-percentage tests under which new work counts as suitable for an unemployment claimant based on its pay compared with the claimant's earlier wages.

tn:SB 1915.title: Immigration - As enacted, adds local governments to the entities that must verify that each applicant for public benefits is a United States citizen or lawfully present in the United States; authorizes certain investigations of violations of requirements for verification of citizenship or presence for public benefits; requires certain reporting related to such verification for benefits; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 1 and Title 4, Chapter 58.
tn:SB 1915.summary: Adds counties and cities to those verifying public-benefit applicants' lawful presence; requires government entities to report unlawfully present recipients to the state immigration enforcement division, with a Class A misdemeanor for intentional failure; lets the attorney general withhold state funds from noncomplying localities.

tn:SB 1992.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, creates a Class E felony offense when a person, for the purpose of deriving a pecuniary benefit, engages in conduct intended to influence the occurrence or nonoccurrence of an event while the person, or another acting in active concert with the person, is a party to a contract traded on a prediction-market by which the person will derive such pecuniary benefit directly from the settlement of that contract based on the occurrence or a nonoccurrence of the event. - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:SB 1992.summary: Creates a Class E felony for a person who holds a prediction-market contract and acts to influence whether an event occurs in order to profit from that contract.

tn:SB 2040.title: Pharmacy, Pharmacists - As enacted, enacts the "Freedom, Access, and Integrity in Registered Pharmacy (FAIR Rx) Act." - Amends TCA Title 63.
tn:SB 2040.summary: Enacts the FAIR Rx Act: from July 1, 2028, bars owning or controlling (over 5%) a pharmacy together with both a health insurer and a pharmacy benefits manager, with civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation. Exempts orphan and limited-distribution drugs.

tn:SB 2055.title: Local Education Agencies - As enacted, requires LEAs and public charter schools to allow a private pay provider who is under contract with a parent or legal guardian of a student with autism spectrum disorder or developmental delays who is enrolled in the LEA or public charter school, access to the student during the school day to provide the student with private pay services in educational settings as long as the educational settings in which private pay services are provided do not conflict with the student's educational placement; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 49; Title 68 and Title 71.
tn:SB 2055.summary: Requires public school districts and charter schools to let a parent-hired private provider give a student with autism or developmental delays applied behavior analysis on school grounds during the school day, coordinated with the student's IEP team.

tn:SB 2085.title: Victims' Rights - As enacted, authorizes a court clerk to increase the victims assistance assessment from $45 to $125, with the first $15 of each assessment being paid to the court clerk for processing and handling and the remaining amount being transmitted to the county in which the offense occurred for the exclusive use of the victims assistance program previously designated by the county legislative body. - Amends TCA Section 40-24-109.
tn:SB 2085.summary: Sets the victims assistance assessment on defendants who plead or are found guilty at $125, up from $45. Clerks keep the first $15 for processing and send $110 to the county's victims assistance program.

tn:SB 2102.title: Public Utility Commission - As enacted, requires, for an electric utility providing services outside the corporate limits of the home municipality, expansion of the utility board to provide representation on the board for such outside locality. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 12; Title 13; Title 54; Title 64; Title 65; Title 68 and Title 69.
tn:SB 2102.summary: Requires electric utilities owned by, or in a county with, 485,000+ people to add voting board seats for the home county (if 3,500+ customers outside the city) and each outside county with a locality served by 3,500+ customers, if the county appoints.

tn:SB 2136.title: Gambling - As enacted, clarifies that gambling, the operation or possession of gambling devices, and the operation, conducting, or commercial promoting of online sweepstakes games and other forms of online or app-based gambling are unlawful and a violation of  the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act; expands the authority of the sports wagering council to investigate illegal gambling and gaming activity; expands the investigative authority of the attorney general to investigate unlawful activity within the purview of the attorney general. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 4, Chapter 49; Title 8, Chapter 6, Part 4; Title 40, Chapter 2 and Title 47.
tn:SB 2136.summary: Declares gambling, gambling devices and online sweepstakes games unlawful (lawful licensed games excepted) and a Consumer Protection Act violation; lets the attorney general demand information in investigations of unlawful acts, and the sports wagering council investigate non-licensees.

tn:SB 2145.title: Orders of Protection - As enacted, allows a person to file a petition for a lifetime order of protection against a person who was convicted of certain offenses in another jurisdiction; provides that venue for such a petition is in the county where the respondent resides or, if the respondent is not a resident of this state, the county where the petitioner resides. - Amends TCA Title 36 and Title 39.
tn:SB 2145.summary: Lets a victim seek a lifetime order of protection against an offender convicted in another state of a comparable felony assaultive, homicide, kidnapping or sexual offense, filed in the respondent's county or, if the respondent lives out of state, the petitioner's county.

tn:SB 2162.title: Open Meetings - As enacted, authorizes a governing body to conduct an executive session for the purpose of interviewing applicants for employment as director-level staff of the body without providing public notice of such session. - Amends TCA Title 8.
tn:SB 2162.summary: As enacted, allows a governing body to hold a closed executive session, without public notice, to interview applicants for director-level staff jobs. Deliberation and votes must occur in an open, noticed meeting.
