wa:SB 6151.summary: Creates a Laboratory Accreditation Account to receive Ecology's lab accreditation fees, spendable after appropriation and fee rulemaking, to cover costs and clear the backlog of drinking water lab accreditations.

wa:SB 6162.title: Concerning property tax reform.
wa:SB 6162.summary: Exempts qualifying retired and disabled homeowners from the entire state property tax, raises income thresholds, and merges the two state levies into one state school levy set at $2.075355 per $1,000 for 2026.

wa:SB 6170.title: Adjusting monetary limits regarding contracting rules for state highway construction work and procurement.
wa:SB 6170.summary: Raises the cost limit for state highway work done by state forces to $100,000, sets an emergency limit of $160,000 adjusted annually for inflation from 2027, and sets the small-business contract cutoff at $160,000.

wa:SB 6182.title: Establishing an abortion savings program.
wa:SB 6182.summary: Creates an Abortion Savings Program: the Department of Health, subject to appropriation, awards operating grants to eligible abortion providers, abortion funds and other providers for patients lacking resources, funded by an annual per-coverage-month assessment on health carriers starting in 2027.

wa:SB 6188.title: Concerning the department of labor and industries' authority to enact rules related to regulating asbestos training.
wa:SB 6188.summary: Removes the limit on Labor and Industries asbestos certification rulemaking to federal-minimum rules, and instead requires rules based on best available evidence and industry standards that are the least burdensome necessary to address hazards.

wa:SB 6189.title: Changing the deadline for forming a public facilities district for regional aquatics and sports facilities.
wa:SB 6189.summary: Removes the deadline for contiguous cities, towns and counties that helped create a public facilities district to form an additional district for regional aquatics and sports facilities.

wa:SB 6194.title: Allowing payments to be made based on allowable costs for services provided by any rural hospital that is located on a federally recognized Indian reservation.
wa:SB 6194.summary: Makes rural hospitals on federally recognized Indian reservations eligible, from January 1, 2027, for Medicaid payments at 150 percent of the fee-for-service rate for inpatient and outpatient services, excluding psychiatric unit beds, regardless of managed care enrollment; expires January 1, 2029.

wa:SB 6197.title: Enforcing plumbing contractor requirements.
wa:SB 6197.summary: Changes the trigger for suspending a plumber's or plumbing contractor's license from three infractions in 36 months to five or more infractions in five years, for up to two years, ordered by the department, effective January 1, 2027.

wa:SB 6200.title: Concerning renters' and mobile home occupants' ability to install portable cooling devices.
wa:SB 6200.summary: Bars landlords from prohibiting tenants from installing portable air conditioners or heat pumps, with exceptions for existing heat pumps, code, safety or electrical limits, and for window units that block egress or cannot be secured.

wa:SB 6225.title: Authorizing bonds for transportation funding.
wa:SB 6225.summary: Authorizes up to $800 million in state bonds for highway projects, deposited in the Move Ahead Washington Account, raises the State Route 520 bond authorization by $500 million to $2.45 billion, and expires certain unused bond authority.

wa:SB 6226.title: Protecting the clinical autonomy of audiologists.
wa:SB 6226.summary: Lets licensed professionals use clinical judgment to choose telehealth or in-person care when fitting and dispensing hearing instruments, without limiting the board's authority to set standards of care, supervision, documentation and safety rules.

wa:SB 6228.title: Removing a tax exemption for the warehousing and reselling of prescription drugs. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Removing a tax exemption for the warehousing and reselling of prescription drugs and providing tax relief for critical access pharmacies.)
wa:SB 6228.summary: Repeals the 0.138 percent business tax rate for prescription drug wholesalers, setting 0.5 percent for 2027 and 0.35 percent from 2028, and creates a 0.138 percent rate for qualifying independent critical access pharmacies from 2027.

wa:SB 6231.title: Removing a tax exemption for the replacement of equipment for data centers.
wa:SB 6231.summary: Removes replacement servers from the data center sales and use tax exemption, ends new refurbishment certificates in rural counties from July 1, 2026 and expires existing ones that day, and ends the exemption for data centers refurbished after that date in counties over 800,000 residents.

wa:SB 6237.title: Concerning rental property disclosures of flooding history and flood risk.
wa:SB 6237.summary: Requires landlords, for leases entered into after 2026, to tell tenants the property may be in a flood hazard area, that the landlord's insurance does not cover tenants' belongings, and where to find county flood-risk information.

wa:SB 6246.title: Concerning emissions from emissions-intensive, trade-exposed facilities under the climate commitment act.
wa:SB 6246.summary: Fixes the industry classification codes for emissions-intensive, trade-exposed facilities under the cap-and-invest program as of January 1, 2026, and requires Ecology to recommend by December 1, 2026 how to schedule free allowance reductions for 2035-2050.

wa:SB 6248.title: Addressing travel insurance.
wa:SB 6248.summary: Creates rules for selling travel insurance, covering licensing and registration of sellers, consumer disclosures, premium tax, and classification of travel insurance under the inland marine line for rate and form filing.

wa:SB 6260.title: Implementing efficiencies and programming changes in public education.
wa:SB 6260.summary: Changes school funding rules: minimum bus lifetimes of 10 years (category A) and 15 years (C and D) for depreciation payments, reduced reimbursement for zero-emission buses, and Running Start funded enrollment capped at 1.2 or 1.3 FTEs instead of 1.4.

wa:SB 6269.title: Modernizing the definition of motor fuel in the motor fuel quality act.
wa:SB 6269.summary: Updates the motor fuel quality law's definition of motor fuel to cover products used for highway propulsion or transportation, and removes the separate definition of alternative fuel.

wa:SB 6302.title: Concerning misclassification in the finishing trades on public works projects.
wa:SB 6302.summary: Requires Labor and Industries to investigate possible misclassification when a contractor uses three or more independent contractors for drywall, flooring, tiling, painting or glazing work on a public works project, on referral by the owner, contractors, unions or workers.

wa:SB 6309.title: Providing for enhanced municipal permitting tools for high capacity transit projects.
wa:SB 6309.summary: Lets regional transit authorities apply for permits before acquiring the property or before a local land use decision, with notice to the owner, and build rail guideway facilities exceeding local height and setback limits while complying with local rules to the extent practicable.

wa:SB 6346.title: Establishing a tax on millionaires.
wa:SB 6346.summary: Amends the House striking amendment to exempt income derived by small forestland owners from the income tax it imposes.

wa:SB 6355.title: Concerning the electric transmission system.
wa:SB 6355.summary: Creates the Washington Electric Transmission Authority, a public body that works to expand electric transmission capacity, pursue upgrades to existing lines, and partner with utilities, tribes and neighboring states on transmission projects.

wi:AB 1.title: Relating to: an income tax subtraction for qualified tips and for qualified overtime compensation; state aid for school districts; surplus refund payments; increasing funding for special education and school age parents programs; state aid to technical colleges and the technical college district revenue limit; and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:AB 1.summary: As introduced, creates income tax subtractions for qualified tips and overtime pay, adds $85 million (2025-26) and $230 million (2026-27) for special education aid, raises technical college and school aid, and pays surplus refunds of up to $300 ($600 joint) by September 15, 2026.

wi:AB 100.title: Relating to: designating athletic sports and teams operated or sponsored by public schools or private schools participating in a parental choice program based on the sex of the participants.
wi:AB 100.summary: Requires public schools, independent charter schools and private choice schools to designate athletic teams as male, female or coed by biological sex (original birth certificate), bar male pupils from female teams, and designate locker rooms for one biological sex, with listed exceptions.

wi:AB 102.title: Relating to: designating University of Wisconsin and technical college sports and athletic teams based on the sex of the participants.
wi:AB 102.summary: As amended, requires University of Wisconsin and technical college athletic teams to be designated male, female or coed by biological sex (sex at birth per original birth certificate), bars male-sex students from female teams, and requires one-sex locker rooms, with exceptions and accommodations.

wi:AB 1027.title: Relating to: requiring information relating to the food stamp program to be compiled and provided to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
wi:AB 1027.summary: Changes FoodShare rules to match 2025 federal law, raising the work-requirement age cutoff from 50 to 65, narrowing the child exemption to under 14, limiting eligibility to qualified immigrants, and requiring DHS to share recipient data with USDA.

wi:AB 103.title: Relating to: school board policies related to changing a pupil’s legal name and pronouns.
wi:AB 103.summary: Requires school boards to adopt policies to change a pupil's name or pronouns in school records only on a parent's or adult pupil's notarized request, and bar staff from using a minor's name or pronouns not matching biological sex without a parent's notarized authorization.

wi:AB 1032.title: Relating to: the sale of property under Department of Natural Resources jurisdiction to prevent the spread of avian flu.
wi:AB 1032.summary: Allows the Natural Resources Board to sell state-owned land under Department of Natural Resources control that is adjacent to or within one mile of a commercial egg farm to prevent the spread of avian flu, waiving the usual conservation-need requirement.

wi:AB 1034.title: Relating to: name, image, and likeness rights for University of Wisconsin System student athletes; maintenance costs for University of Wisconsin–Madison intercollegiate athletic facilities; and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:AB 1034.summary: Lets the UW Board of Regents enter name, image and likeness compensation agreements with student athletes, requires athletes to disclose third-party deals, states they are not UW System employees because of those deals, and appropriates funds for UW athletic facility maintenance costs.

wi:AB 146.title: Relating to: requests for information from employers about unemployment insurance claims.
wi:AB 146.summary: Requires the Department of Workforce Development to give employers at least 12 business days to respond to an initial request for information about an unemployment insurance claim.

wi:AB 162.title: Relating to: workforce metrics.
wi:AB 162.summary: Requires state agencies running workforce programs to track and publicly report outcomes, such as employment after exit and median earnings, and requires mass-layoff notices to employees to include local workforce board contact information and a resource list if one exists.

wi:AB 165.title: Relating to: local guaranteed income programs.
wi:AB 165.summary: Bars cities, villages, towns and counties from spending public money on guaranteed income programs, meaning regular, unearned cash payments to individuals usable for any purpose. Programs requiring work or training are excluded.

wi:AB 168.title: Relating to: various changes to the unemployment insurance law.
wi:AB 168.summary: Requires DWD to use identity-proofing for unemployment claimants, run a call center with extended hours when calls surge, compare recipients with state and national databases at least weekly for fraud, and allows eight years to prosecute unemployment-benefit fraud.

wi:AB 169.title: Relating to: various changes to the unemployment insurance law.
wi:AB 169.summary: Lets employers report claimants who decline or ignore job interviews or offers or miss interviews; such a claimant fails the work search for that week unless the report is disregarded, for example after a prompt attempt to reschedule. Makes recovery of certain overpayments mandatory.

wi:AB 182.title: Relating to: changes to the low-income housing tax credit. (FE)
wi:AB 182.summary: Requires WHEDA to set aside 35 percent of state low-income housing tax credits for rural projects starting with its next allocation plan, and removes the requirement that projects be financed with tax-exempt bonds.

wi:AB 211.title: Relating to: exempting tobacco bars from the public smoking ban.
wi:AB 211.summary: Exempts tobacco bars opened on or after June 4, 2009 from the indoor smoking ban if only cigars and pipes are smoked, they are not retail food establishments, under-21s are barred, notice is posted, employees acknowledge secondhand smoke, and plans show air filtration.

wi:AB 219.title: Relating to: a tax credit for rail infrastructure modernization. (FE)
wi:AB 219.summary: Creates two income and franchise tax credits for short line and other railroads and local governments: 50 percent of qualifying track maintenance and new rail infrastructure spending, certified by WEDC, for tax years 2026 through 2030.

wi:AB 241.title: Relating to: required ratio of journeyworkers to apprentices in apprenticeship programs and contracts.
wi:AB 241.summary: Allows apprenticeship programs in construction trades to require up to two apprentices per journeyworker, up from one; the ratio for other trades stays at one, and the existing exception for collective bargaining agreements remains.

wi:AB 248.title: Relating to: vacancies in appointive state offices.
wi:AB 248.summary: Makes the expiration of a fixed term for an appointive state office create a vacancy, first applying to state officers appointed on January 1, 2027.

wi:AB 269.title: Relating to: delivery network couriers and transportation network drivers, Department of Financial Institutions’ approval to offer portable benefit accounts, providing for insurance coverage, modifying administrative rules related to accident and sickness insurance, and granting rule-making authority.
wi:AB 269.summary: Treats app-based delivery and rideshare drivers as non-employees for workers' compensation, minimum wage and unemployment if companies set no schedules, penalties or exclusivity; lets companies fund portable benefit accounts, with 4 percent contributions, for drivers earning $750 or more quarterly.

wi:AB 281.title: Relating to: the employment eligibility verification program and granting rule-making authority.
wi:AB 281.summary: Bars the state from contracting with employers that do not use E-Verify for all employees, and requires state and local governments to verify new hires through E-Verify.

wi:AB 308.title: Relating to: prohibiting funding for health services for unlawfully present individuals.
wi:AB 308.summary: Prohibits state, local and pass-through federal funds from paying for health care for people not lawfully present in the U.S., unless federal law requires payment or federal funds would be lost.

wi:AB 373.title: Relating to: creating a refundable individual income tax credit for the parent of a stillbirth and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:AB 373.summary: Creates a nonrefundable income tax credit for parents of a stillbirth: $2,000 for married joint filers, or $1,000 per parent for married separate and unmarried filers.

wi:AB 375.title: Relating to: modifications to the historic rehabilitation tax credit. (FE)
wi:AB 375.summary: Changes the state historic rehabilitation tax credit by dropping certain federal requirements for state-only claimants, having the state credit claimed when the federal credit is, and replacing the lifetime $3.5 million per-parcel limit with $3.5 million per 15 years.

wi:AB 39.title: Relating to: requiring state employees to perform their work at the offices of their employer.
wi:AB 39.summary: Requires state agencies to have employees work in person at agency offices for at least 80 percent of scheduled hours each month, exempting duties performed off site before March 2020 and the State of Wisconsin Investment Board.

wi:AB 450.title: Relating to: applicability of the commercial building code to certain buildings.
wi:AB 450.summary: Applies the commercial building code rules in effect August 1, 2025, which incorporated the 2015 International Building Code, to buildings whose plans are submitted by April 1, 2026, instead of the rules in effect when plans are approved.

wi:AB 454.title: Relating to: a workforce home loan program. (FE)
wi:AB 454.summary: Creates a workforce home loan fund run by WHEDA that makes interest-free second-mortgage loans to eligible buyers of newly constructed single-family homes, with 15- or 30-year terms (40 with payment deferral).

wi:AB 457.title: Relating to: the conditions under which a school district may adopt a resolution to exceed its revenue limit.
wi:AB 457.summary: Prohibits a school board from starting a referendum to exceed its revenue limit unless DPI certifies it has met financial reporting requirements; resolutions adopted without certification are void.

wi:AB 461.title: Relating to: an income tax subtraction for certain overtime compensation.
wi:AB 461.summary: Creates a state income tax subtraction matching the federal deduction for qualified overtime pay, starting with tax year 2025 and continuing after the federal deduction expires following 2028.

wi:AB 549.title: Relating to: manufactured home sales and certificates of title and modifying administrative rules of the Department of Safety and Professional Services related to manufactured home purchase contracts. (FE)
wi:AB 549.summary: Changes manufactured home rules: adds county to title applications, requires the Department of Safety and Professional Services to keep a public list of home communities, requires written purchase contracts from licensed sellers, and exempts people selling one home or fewer a year from dealer rules.

wi:AB 582.title: Relating to: dual enrollment programs, creating the Council on Dual Enrollment, and transfer of postsecondary course credits.
wi:AB 582.summary: Creates a Council on Dual Enrollment in the Department of Workforce Development to study high school college-credit pathways, and requires DWD to run a dual enrollment website and printed brochure.

wi:AB 601.title: Relating to: excluding certain event or sports wagers from the definition of “bet”.
wi:AB 601.summary: Excludes from the definition of an illegal bet sports wagers placed by a person in Wisconsin on a mobile device when the server is on Wisconsin tribal lands and the wager is under a tribal gaming compact originally entered before April 1, 1993.

wi:AB 602.title: Relating to: participating in the federal tax credit program for contributions to scholarship granting organizations.
wi:AB 602.summary: Requires the governor to elect Wisconsin into the federal tax credit for donations to scholarship granting organizations beginning in 2027, and requires the Department of Administration to send the U.S. Treasury an annual list of eligible organizations in the state.

wi:AB 614.title: Relating to: a teacher’s authority to manage the teacher’s class, parental notification of disruptive or violent behavior at school, and a school district’s code of conduct.
wi:AB 614.summary: Specifies teachers' authority over classroom discipline, changes when teachers may remove pupils, requires behavior plans before some return to class, and requires parent notification of disruptive or violent incidents, with limits for pupils with disabilities.

wi:AB 629.title: Relating to: police authority to disable drones threatening public safety and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 629.summary: Allows law enforcement officers authorized and trained under federal law to detect, warn, disrupt, seize or disable drones posing a credible safety threat, and makes using a weaponized drone that threatens public safety over a correctional institution a Class H felony.

wi:AB 663.title: Relating to: imposing certain prohibitions on foreign influence at University of Wisconsin System institutions. (FE)
wi:AB 663.summary: Bars UW System institutions from accepting grants from, or entering academic or research partnerships with, colleges or governments of China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba or Venezuela, except partnerships approved by the Board of Regents.

wi:AB 672.title: Relating to: penalty enhancer for crimes committed by a person acting as an agent of a foreign government or terrorist organization with the intent to silence or punish persons for their political view, criminalizing the enforcement of foreign laws without federal or state approval, and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 672.summary: Raises a crime's penalty class one level when committed as an agent of a foreign government or terrorist group to intimidate or silence dissidents and others, makes unapproved enforcement of foreign laws a Class E felony (three-year minimum prison term), and requires DOJ training.

wi:AB 673.title: Relating to: banning the use of genetic software from foreign adversaries in medical and research facilities, the storage of any human genome sequencing data within the borders of a foreign adversary, and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 673.summary: Bans medical and research facilities receiving state money from using genetic sequencers or analysis software made in China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia or Maduro-era Venezuela, and bars storing Wisconsin residents' genome data in those countries.

wi:AB 674.title: Relating to: prohibiting knowingly covering organ transplantation and related care under health insurance policies and the Medical Assistance program if the organ is transplanted in or originates from a country known to have participated in forced organ harvesting.
wi:AB 674.summary: Bars health insurance plans and Medical Assistance from knowingly covering organ transplants performed in, or using organs from, China or other countries the Department of Health Services designates as involved in forced organ harvesting, except life-saving posttransplant care.

wi:AB 699.title: Relating to: a long-term care insurance assessment and a long-term care insurance assessment tax credit. (FE)
wi:AB 699.summary: Creates a long-term care insurance account in the insurance security fund, with assessments split equally between life/annuity and health insurers, and a state tax credit of 20 percent of the assessment paid per year for five years.

wi:AB 700.title: Relating to: an appropriation for refundable long-term care insurance assessment credits and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:AB 700.summary: Provides a sum-sufficient appropriation to pay refundable long-term care insurance assessment credits created in a separate bill; the bill is void if that separate bill is not enacted.

wi:AB 73.title: Relating to: statutory recognition of specialized treatment court and commercial court dockets.
wi:AB 73.summary: Recognizes treatment courts and a commercial court docket in state law. Commercial cases such as business governance, securities and intellectual property disputes, some above dollar thresholds, go to judges selected by the chief justice; small claims and landlord-tenant cases are excluded.

wi:AB 757.title: Relating to: the appointment of certain employees of the University of Wisconsin System and faculty governance.
wi:AB 757.summary: Bars the UW Board of Regents from delegating limited appointments such as chancellors, requires it to approve and annually report their titles, salaries and descriptions, redefines faculty for shared governance, and bars faculty from limiting committee or program leadership by rank, tenure or degree.

wi:AB 759.title: Relating to: eligibility to receive occupational credentials for recipients of deferred action under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program. (FE)
wi:AB 759.summary: Allows people who first received DACA deferred action before the bill takes effect, and hold an unexpired work permit, to receive state occupational credentials if they meet other requirements; credentials last only while the work permit is valid.

wi:AB 793.title: Relating to: creating an Office of Internal Audit attached to the Department of Employee Trust Funds.
wi:AB 793.summary: Creates an Office of Internal Audit attached to the Department of Employee Trust Funds, with an internal auditor appointed by the Employee Trust Funds Board who reports directly to the board instead of the department secretary.

wi:AB 85.title: Relating to: recommendation to revoke extended supervision, parole, or probation if a person is charged with a crime.
wi:AB 85.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to recommend revoking a person's extended supervision, parole or probation whenever the person is charged with a crime while on release.

wi:AB 87.title: Relating to: restitution orders following a conviction for human trafficking and restoration of the right to vote to a person barred from voting as a result of a felony conviction.
wi:AB 87.summary: Requires courts to order immediate restitution from human trafficking defendants, with execution against property if unpaid, and conditions voting rights after a felony on also paying all fines, fees, surcharges and restitution and completing community service.

wi:AB 913.title: Relating to: subtraction for certain income of members of the National Guard and Reserves. (FE)
wi:AB 913.summary: Creates a Wisconsin income tax subtraction, starting with tax year 2026, for pay National Guard and reserve members receive for full-time training duty and for inactive-duty training.

wi:AB 957.title: Relating to: Internet crimes against children law enforcement and making an appropriation. (FE)
wi:AB 957.summary: Provides the Department of Justice $400,000 in each year of the 2025-27 budget period for Internet crimes against children law enforcement.

wi:AB 968.title: Relating to: virtual currency kiosks.
wi:AB 968.summary: Requires virtual currency kiosk operators to hold a money transmitter license, post fraud warnings, verify customer identity, limit each customer to $1,000 a day, refund fraud reported within 30 days, and keep kiosks five feet from ATMs.

wi:AJR 10.title: PROHIBIT GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND AGENCIES FROM CL
wi:AJR 10.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment barring the state and local governments from ordering places of worship closed or forbidding gatherings in them in response to a national, state or local emergency, including a public health emergency.

wi:AJR 102.title: PROHIBITING GOVERNMENTAL DISCRIMINATION-2ND CONS.
wi:AJR 102.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment barring state and local government from discriminating against or giving preferential treatment to any person or group based on race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin in public employment, education, contracting or administration.

wi:AJR 133.title: SUSPENSION OF RULES PROMULGATED BY STATE AGENCIES
wi:AJR 133.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment letting the legislature suspend any state agency rule by joint resolution adopted by a majority of all members of each house, without presentment to the governor.

wi:SB 10.title: Relating to: access to public high schools for military recruiters.
wi:SB 10.summary: Requires school boards and charter school governing boards to give military recruiters access to common areas of high schools, during the school day and at school-sanctioned events, though not to classrooms during instruction.

wi:SB 16.title: Relating to: participation in interscholastic athletics and application of the public records and open meetings laws to interscholastic athletic associations.
wi:SB 16.summary: Bars school districts from belonging to an interscholastic athletic association unless it elects to be covered by the state's public records and open meetings laws, with exceptions for records on individual referees or students.

wi:SB 176.title: Relating to: an income and franchise tax exemption for broadband expansion grants and for federal high-cost program funding for broadband expansion. (FE)
wi:SB 176.summary: As passed by the Senate, exempts from state income and franchise taxes broadband expansion grants from state, local, tribal or federal governments and federal high-cost universal service funding for broadband, and bars claiming this and the existing exemption for the same grant.

wi:SB 214.title: Relating to: registration of out-of-state health care providers to provide telehealth services.
wi:SB 214.summary: Lets out-of-state health care providers with active, unrestricted credentials and no recent discipline register with the Department of Safety and Professional Services to provide telehealth in Wisconsin, and requires them to carry malpractice insurance.

wi:SB 276.title: Relating to: challenges to the validity of administrative rules and making an appropriation.
wi:SB 276.summary: Requires a court that declares an administrative rule or guidance document invalid to award the challenging party reasonable attorney fees and costs.

wi:SB 277.title: Relating to: the expiration of administrative rules.
wi:SB 277.summary: Makes each administrative code chapter expire on January 1 of the seventh year after it takes effect unless the agency readopts it by notice or rule; the rules committee may extend a deadline by up to one year, with a second extension for some chapters.

wi:SB 289.title: Relating to: requirements for proposed administrative rules that impose any costs.
wi:SB 289.summary: Lowers the threshold at which an agency must halt a proposed rule from $10 million in expected two-year compliance costs to any amount, unless it removes the costs, offsets them with another rule that year, or a bill allows the rule.

wi:SB 291.title: Relating to: making certain child care expenditures eligible for the business development tax credit.
wi:SB 291.summary: Expands the refundable business development tax credit from child care capital expenditures to up to 15 percent of costs of providing child care for employees, including operating costs, reimbursements, reserved slots and dependent care account contributions.

wi:SB 36.title: Relating to: an income tax exemption for cash tips paid to an employee.
wi:SB 36.summary: Creates a Wisconsin income tax subtraction, for tax years 2025 through 2028, equal to the qualified tips deduction the taxpayer claims on their federal income tax return.

wi:SB 389.title: Relating to: the per pupil adjustment for school district revenue limits.
wi:SB 389.summary: Eliminates the $325 per pupil adjustment in the school district revenue limit formula beginning with the 2027-28 school year.

wi:SB 4.title: Relating to: agreements for direct primary care.
wi:SB 4.summary: Sets rules for direct primary care agreements, where patients pay providers a subscription fee for primary care. Requires written disclosure that the agreement is not insurance, bars fee-for-service billing of insurers for covered services, and limits when providers may refuse or end patients.

wi:SB 405.title: Relating to: a civil cause of action for a minor injured by a gender transition procedure.
wi:SB 405.summary: Lets a person injured by a gender transition procedure performed as a minor sue the provider before age 33. Defense: two years of documented perceived gender, two providers certifying it is the only treatment for any mental health concern, and consent of minor and parent.

wi:SB 417.title: Relating to: visitation of a long-term care facility resident or hospital patient during a communicable disease outbreak.
wi:SB 417.summary: Requires nursing homes, assisted living facilities and hospitals that limit visitors during a communicable disease outbreak to allow visits by clergy and an essential visitor in situations such as end of life or grief, with listed grounds for denial.

wi:SB 420.title: Relating to: prohibiting rights of nature ordinances.
wi:SB 420.summary: Bars cities, villages, towns and counties from enacting ordinances that give legal rights to natural resources to exist, be protected against pollution, or maintain a healthy ecosystem.

wi:SB 431.title: Relating to: discrimination based on arrest record under the fair employment law.
wi:SB 431.summary: Lets employers and licensing agencies refuse to hire or license a person because of any pending charge, not only criminal ones, that substantially relates to the job or licensed activity under the fair employment law.

wi:SB 432.title: Relating to: mandatory reporting requirements and referring cases of threatened or suspected child abuse to law enforcement.
wi:SB 432.summary: Requires county child welfare departments to refer all reports of threatened or suspected child abuse to police, and adds child welfare agency employees who work directly with children or handle cases to the mandatory reporter list.

wi:SB 480.title: Relating to: residential tax incremental districts. (FE)
wi:SB 480.summary: Lets cities, villages and certain towns create residential tax incremental districts for infrastructure serving owner-occupied one- and two-family homes within set lot, setback and size limits. Caps such districts at 3 percent of local property value and 20 years, with a 3-year extension.

wi:SB 482.title: Relating to: increasing the carryover period of the research income tax credit. (FE)
wi:SB 482.summary: Extends the carryover period for unused nonrefundable research income and franchise tax credits from up to 15 years to up to 50 years, applying retroactively to unexpired unused credits.

wi:SB 498.title: Relating to: free speech and academic freedom at University of Wisconsin System institutions and technical colleges, due process in disciplinary proceedings at University of Wisconsin System institutions and technical colleges, and causes of action against the Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System and technical college district boards.
wi:SB 498.summary: Sets free speech standards at University of Wisconsin System institutions and technical colleges, banning free speech zones and most permit requirements, allows civil suits for violations, and sets due process standards in student discipline.

wi:SB 532.title: Relating to: course fees at University of Wisconsin System institutions.
wi:SB 532.summary: Bars UW System institutions from charging a fee for fully online courses unless it covers added online costs or is also charged for the in-person equivalent, and requires institutions to disclose each course's format (in-person, online or hybrid) when listing courses.

wi:SB 533.title: Relating to: intentionally disarming a correctional officer and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 533.summary: Extends the Class H felony for disarming a peace officer to taking weapons or equipment, such as restraints, keys or radios, from correctional and juvenile correctional officers.

wi:SB 610.title: Relating to: increasing the maximum penalty for certain controlled substances offenses if the violation occurs near a homeless shelter and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 610.summary: Adds homeless shelter premises and the area within 1,000 feet of them to the places where the maximum prison term for delivering or possessing with intent to deliver certain controlled substances increases by five years.

wi:SB 622.title: Relating to: fees related to animal markets, animal dealers, animal truckers, and animal transport vehicles.
wi:SB 622.summary: Sets in statute the animal market, dealer, trucker and vehicle fees, plus livestock and other registration fees, at amounts DATCP set by rule in December 2024, and requires an annual report on fee revenue and spending.

wi:SB 652.title: Relating to: race-based higher education programs and requirements.
wi:SB 652.summary: Changes higher education programs for minority students to cover disadvantaged students instead, defined by a student's demonstrated economic and social disadvantage (personal narrative, net worth statement) without regard to race or sex, and repeals minority enrollment targets for a medical school and a dental school.

wi:SB 699.title: Relating to: alternative methods of providing pupil transportation services.
wi:SB 699.summary: Raises the number of passengers a non-school-bus vehicle may carry for school transportation from 9 to 14 besides the driver, and the emergency-exception threshold from 10 to 15 or more.

wi:SB 7.title: Relating to: prohibiting a foreign adversary from acquiring agricultural or forestry land in this state.
wi:SB 7.summary: Bars foreign-adversary governments and officials, citizens of foreign adversaries lacking U.S. permanent residency or a valid visa, and entities they own or control from acquiring Wisconsin real property after the effective date; interests held in violation are forfeited to the state.

wi:SB 76.title: Relating to:  dismissing or amending certain criminal charges and deferred prosecution agreements for certain crimes.
wi:SB 76.summary: Requires a prosecutor to get court approval to dismiss or amend charges for listed crimes, including domestic abuse, auto theft, sexual assault, crimes against children and certain firearm and driving offenses, and bars deferred prosecution agreements for them.

wi:SB 782.title: Relating to: intentionally sending false text messages to 911 and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 782.summary: Makes intentionally sending a false text message to 911 an offense, with the same penalties as a false 911 call: a $100 to $600 fine or up to 90 days in jail, and a Class H felony for repeats within four years.

wi:SB 799.title: Relating to: parental access to health records of minors.
wi:SB 799.summary: As amended by the Assembly, changes parents' access to minors' health records, removing the age-14 objection exception for developmentally disabled minors, allowing access to HIV test records, and requiring online access; also requires unanimous Milwaukee council votes to modify police and fire policies.

wi:SB 96.title: Relating to: exempting certain electric vehicle charging stations located at a residence from the electric vehicle charging tax. (FE)
wi:SB 96.summary: Exempts electricity delivered by any electric vehicle charger at a residence, whatever its level, from the state EV charging tax, retroactive to January 1, 2025, and clarifies the registration exemption covers all residential chargers.

wi:SJR 116.title: Relating to: prohibiting the governor from using the partial veto to create or increase any tax or fee (second consideration).
wi:SJR 116.summary: Proposes amending the state constitution to bar the governor from using the partial veto on an appropriation bill to create or increase any tax or fee. Second approval would send it to voters in November 2026.

wv:HB 4005.title: Skills to work
wv:HB 4005.summary: Replaces most of the state list of occupations barred for minors with federal Hazardous Occupation Order limits for ages 16 and up, limits under-16 work to federal exceptions, and changes Youth Apprenticeship student rules. Titled the Workforce Development Act of 2026.

wv:HB 4007.title: Relating to industrial access roads
wv:HB 4007.summary: Lets the Industrial Access Road Fund pay for signage and safety upgrades, sets a 90-day deadline for road-location decisions, raises per-county or municipality caps to $800,000 unmatched and $300,000 matched, and allows up to $3 million in added State Road Fund transfers.

wv:HB 4008.title: Relating to Business Ready Sites Program
wv:HB 4008.summary: Sets Certified Sites micro grants at up to $100,000 for sites of at least five acres and up to $250,000 for sites over 20 acres, replacing a $75,000 cap, and lets Business Ready Sites participants seek the fund with Commerce approval.

wv:HB 4009.title: Relating to the creation of the Portable Benefit Account Act
wv:HB 4009.summary: Allows hiring parties or independent contractors to fund voluntary portable benefit accounts for health, disability, life or retirement benefits. Allows state income tax subtractions for contributions from 2026, bars counting contributions in employment-classification decisions under several state laws, and authorizes rulemaking.

wv:HB 4022.title: CPS Allocation
wv:HB 4022.summary: Removes the rule that county child protective services staffing may not fall below the January 2023 level, lets the commissioner adjust county allocations to current referrals and caseloads, and requires the annual report to list allocation changes lasting over three weeks, with explanations.

wv:HB 4025.title: Exempting certain employees from the classified civil service system
wv:HB 4025.summary: Exempts new hires and promoted employees in the Departments of Health Facilities, Human Services and Health from the classified civil service system and state grievance procedures starting July 1, 2026. Secretaries may restore coverage where federal law requires; bars nepotism and favoritism in decisions.

wv:HB 4028.title: Relating to sales tax on construction materials
wv:HB 4028.summary: Exempts building materials and services bought by contractors for building or repairing public school facilities from state sales and use taxes, effective July 1, 2026, and defines related terms.

wv:HB 4053.title: To establish the blue envelope program.
wv:HB 4053.summary: Requires the State Police to create a Blue Envelope Program by January 1, 2027, giving drivers with autism, dementia, or intellectual or developmental disabilities envelopes to show officers. Bars keeping identifying information after distribution. The state does not warrant envelope contents.

wv:HB 4087.title: To create a West Virginia-Ireland Education Alliance.
wv:HB 4087.summary: Establishes the West Virginia-Ireland Education Alliance, adds education to the Ireland Trade Commission's membership interests, and sets up partnerships between state and Irish colleges. Grants require a four-year and a two-year state institution to collaborate.

wv:HB 4088.title: Relating to certified public accountants
wv:HB 4088.summary: Changes Certified Public Accountant licensing: sets education pathways (post-baccalaureate degree, bachelor's plus 30 credit hours, or bachelor's alone), requires one or two years of experience depending on pathway, and revises practice privileges for out-of-state CPAs and firm-name rules.

wv:HB 4089.title: Preservation of hair during chemotherapy.  Also known as the “Jessica Huffman Bill”
wv:HB 4089.summary: Requires health insurers, including public employee and Medicaid plans, to cover scalp cooling systems that preserve hair during cancer chemotherapy. Named Jessica Huffman's Law.

wv:HB 4106.title: Allowing constitutional carry for 18- to 20-year-olds
wv:HB 4106.summary: Lets people aged 18 to 20 who are U.S. citizens or legal residents and not prohibited from possessing firearms carry a concealed deadly weapon without a license; repeals the offense of carrying without a license for those under 21.

wv:HB 4126.title: To modify the funding distribution to the state park endowment fund and the State Parks Operational Fund
wv:HB 4126.summary: Directs 50 percent of Ohio River mineral-lease royalties deposited in the State Parks and Recreation Endowment Fund to park, forest and rail-trail operations from July 1, 2026, rising to 100 percent once the fund reaches $100 million.

wv:HB 4138.title: Relating to persons convicted of a crime
wv:HB 4138.summary: Requires a person on both the Central Abuse Registry and the sex offender registry to pay one $125 annual fee covering both, and requires sex offender registration for convictions of nonconsensual intimate-image disclosure (§61-8-28a) and §61-8-32 offenses.

wv:HB 4169.title: Relating to mental health examination requirements.
wv:HB 4169.summary: Expands who may sign the mental health examination certificate for petitions to regain firearm rights, adding physicians, licensed counselors, clinical social workers, psychiatric nurse practitioners and physician assistants; some must be authorized by a circuit court order.

wv:HB 4176.title: To allow youth and handicapped hunters to harvest a buck deer or doe during youth/handicapped special hunts
wv:HB 4176.summary: Removes Class XS resident senior license holders from the provision giving them the same privileges as youth hunters during special youth deer seasons.

wv:HB 4191.title: Relating to providing child care generally
wv:HB 4191.summary: Changes child care rules: pays licensed programs subsidies by monthly enrollment, ends subsidy for parents whose child averages under 8 days a month, requires electronic attendance filing, lets the Department of Human Services phase out aid gradually, and amends employer child care tax credits.

wv:HB 4196.title: To offer long-acting reversible contraception to patients receiving methadone and suboxone at the treatment facility for the methadone and suboxone
wv:HB 4196.summary: Requires medication-assisted treatment programs to offer long-acting reversible contraception to patients recovering from addiction, with non-coercive counseling and medical eligibility screening. Programs without a trained provider or equipment must refer patients elsewhere to receive it.

wv:HB 4215.title: Department of Health Rules Bundle
wv:HB 4215.summary: Authorizes the Department of Health, Office of Inspector General and Department of Health Facilities to adopt legislative rules, covering topics such as emergency medical services, lead abatement, nursing home and assisted living licensure, syringe services programs and certificate of need exemptions.

wv:HB 4245.title: Authorizing Certain Agencies of the Department of Revenue to Promulgate Legislative Rules
wv:HB 4245.summary: Authorizes Department of Revenue agencies to promulgate legislative rules, including rules on private clubs, residential mortgage lenders and loan originators, bank communication terminals, joint accounts, the Fintech Regulatory Sandbox Program and insurance producer fingerprinting.

wv:HB 4265.title: Relating to authorizing the Department of Agriculture to promulgate a legislative rule relating to registration forms and tags for registration, taxation, and control of dogs.
wv:HB 4265.summary: Authorizes miscellaneous state agencies and boards to adopt legislative rules, including Agriculture rules on dog registration, hemp and kratom derivatives, agritourism and milk, plus rules from the Board of Architects, Attorney General and State Auditor.

wv:HB 4335.title: Relating to Medicaid providers
wv:HB 4335.summary: Sets expedited Medicaid provider enrollment timelines, creates a uniform credentialing requirement and electronic-only submission form for managed care organizations with possible penalties, and repeals duplicate credentialing provisions.

wv:HB 4354.title: Relating to necessity allowance
wv:HB 4354.summary: Requires placement providers and child welfare workers to inventory the clothing and necessities of children removed from home, and requires the Bureau of Social Services to issue an initial clothing allowance of at least $375, paid by card or reimbursement.

wv:HB 4366.title: Relating to military interpersonal violence
wv:HB 4366.summary: Lets courts treat an unterminated military protective order as clear and convincing evidence of danger for emergency protective orders, and as reasonable cause for temporary personal safety orders. Requires officers arresting a service member for violating a registered order to notify the entering agency.

wv:HB 4390.title: Relating to the temporary payment to a kinship parent of a subsidy equal to that of a foster parent
wv:HB 4390.summary: Gives a kinship parent a temporary payment equal to a foster parent's, for up to six months while becoming certified, if background checks and home screening are satisfactory. Payment starts within 30 days of placement.

wv:HB 4395.title: Relating to investigations of allegations of child safety violations for school personnel.
wv:HB 4395.summary: Adds supervisors and administrators to principals as officials who must report alleged employee conduct jeopardizing student safety within 24 hours. Continues such investigations if the employee resigns or transfers, and expands the confidential state database of investigated school personnel.

wv:HB 4404.title: Increase the allowance for volunteer and part-volunteer fire companies and allowing fire departments to make an expenditure for educational and training supplies and fire prevention promotional materials
wv:HB 4404.summary: Raises from $500 to $5,000 per year the amount volunteer and part-volunteer fire companies may spend from fire-fund revenues on educational and training supplies and fire prevention promotional materials.

wv:HB 4412.title: Require certain websites to utilize age verification methods to prevent minors from accessing content
wv:HB 4412.summary: Requires commercial entities whose content is more than one-third material harmful to minors to verify visitors' ages by reasonable methods, creates civil liability and Attorney General enforcement with civil penalties, and exempts internet providers that only host or transmit others' material.

wv:HB 4416.title: Classifying forestry equipment for levy purposes
wv:HB 4416.summary: Classifies forestry equipment used in harvesting, processing or transporting forest products, when owned by the producer, as Class I property for property tax and exempts sales of forestry equipment from the consumers sales and service tax.

wv:HB 4418.title: Creating “The Tax Efficiency Act of 2026”
wv:HB 4418.summary: Creates the Tax Efficiency Act of 2026, authorizing the Tax Commissioner to design and implement an electronic data processing system for filing and collecting municipal business and occupation or privilege taxes.

wv:HB 4425.title: To repeal the provision allowing for students to transfer from one school to another without losing eligibility.
wv:HB 4425.summary: Repeals §18-2-25e of the Code, the section on athletic eligibility of students who transfer from one school to another.

wv:HB 4433.title: Prohibiting Human Smuggling and Trafficking
wv:HB 4433.summary: Creates crimes of human smuggling of an adult and of a minor, raises penalties for human trafficking offenses, allows civil asset forfeiture, and makes some offenders ineligible for parole. Exempts medical, mental health and legal services provided to unlawfully present people.

wv:HB 4437.title: To allow Gold Star parents to receive one free Gold Star vehicle registration for personal use.
wv:HB 4437.summary: Exempts a Gold Star parent from registration fees for one Gold Star Family license plate, defines "gold star parent," and clarifies the definition of "gold star spouse."

wv:HB 4452.title: To remove Mortmain restrictions on religious organizations
wv:HB 4452.summary: Repeals §35-1-8 of the Code, removing restrictions on property ownership by trustees of certain religious organizations.

wv:HB 4463.title: Relating to the Board of Sanitarians
wv:HB 4463.summary: Changes Board of Sanitarians rules by allowing online or in-person training, altering degree requirements, setting training time limits, letting registered sanitarians license qualifying individuals, and requiring reciprocity standards by May 1, 2026.

wv:HB 4464.title: Relating generally to Underground Facilities Damage prevention
wv:HB 4464.summary: Revises the underground utility damage prevention law, including definitions and Underground Facilities Damage Prevention Board enforcement. Lets operators and excavators agree in writing to extend the 48-hour response time after a one-call notification.

wv:HB 4474.title: Extending the Alzheimer’s Disease and Other Dementia Advisory Council sunset date.
wv:HB 4474.summary: Extends the sunset date of the Alzheimer's Disease and Other Dementia Advisory Council from 2026 to 2030.

wv:HB 4483.title: Relating to funeral service licensure and administration
wv:HB 4483.summary: Updates funeral service licensing law by clarifying definitions and credentials, revising apprenticeship standards, providing for renewal of emeritus licenses, and setting rulemaking and transition provisions.

wv:HB 4484.title: To expand each county commission’s ability to sell or lease property.
wv:HB 4484.summary: Lets counties sell property by sealed bid at no less than 1.5 times assessed or appraised value, or sell real property directly to private buyers at 75 percent or more of appraised value after public notice, as alternatives to auction. Offers are posted online.

wv:HB 4538.title: Regarding fines in DOH work zones
wv:HB 4538.summary: Increases fines for speeding, ignoring traffic-control instructions and violating distracted driving law in highway construction zones when workers are present, such as up to $500 for exceeding a posted limit by under 15 mph.

wv:HB 4546.title: Providing for biennial reporting instead of annual reporting for business organizations.
wv:HB 4546.summary: Lets businesses that elect biennial reporting pay certain Secretary of State fees every two years instead of annually, such as a $50 biennial attorney-in-fact fee in place of $25 per year.

wv:HB 4552.title: Relating to the law-enforcement powers of correctional officers
wv:HB 4552.summary: Classifies Division of Corrections and Rehabilitation correctional officers as law-enforcement officers, exempts those who finish division training from state certification requirements, and clarifies the commissioner's and officers' powers.

wv:HB 4561.title: Clarifying the sheriff’s authority to hire within their office.
wv:HB 4561.summary: Allows a county sheriff to appoint more than one chief deputy, with the advice and consent of the county commission.

wv:HB 4575.title: Making Supplemental Appropriation to State Board of Education
wv:HB 4575.summary: Appropriates $8 million of surplus General Revenue to the State Board of Education for a Hancock County Board of Education financial stability loan, transferred to the Temporary Shortfall Supplement Fund for county boards.

wv:HB 4577.title: Relating to driver’s licenses
wv:HB 4577.summary: Directs the Division of Motor Vehicles commissioner to seek reciprocal agreements with Ireland and Japan so their lawfully present citizens may drive in West Virginia on valid home licenses. Requires insurance compliance, allows fees, and says recognition does not register holders to vote.

wv:HB 4592.title: Relating to college campus safety
wv:HB 4592.summary: Requires each state higher education institution to create standardized campus safety mapping data in formats compatible with local public safety dispatch software, shared with public safety agencies, and exempts the data from public records law.

wv:HB 4599.title: Relating to the WV Cares background check variance process
wv:HB 4599.summary: Requires the director to decide background-check variance requests within 30 days (60 if filed with the application) instead of 60, requires rechecks 60 to 90 days before clearance expires, and requires notice of prior clearance within 10 days.

wv:HB 4606.title: Relating to the meaning of residence for the purpose of bail
wv:HB 4606.summary: Requires judicial officers to consider a defendant's West Virginia or U.S. residency, community ties and flight risk in misdemeanor release decisions and residency in setting bail, and bars magistrates from releasing defendants charged with listed felonies on their own recognizance.

wv:HB 4610.title: Safeguard the Right-To-Try Cutting-Edge Medicine Act
wv:HB 4610.summary: Expands the right-to-try law from terminal illness to life-threatening or severely debilitating illness, drops the clinical-trial access condition, adds individualized treatments made from one patient's genetic profile to covered products, and repeals the law's legislative findings.

wv:HB 4625.title: Relating to quit claim deeds
wv:HB 4625.summary: Changes real property transfer tax exemptions: removes exemptions for gifts to charitable associations and quitclaim deeds, and adds exemptions for no-consideration deeds to wholly owned LLCs, transfers between siblings, mineral deeds, and confirmatory deeds; also amends definitions.

wv:HB 4638.title: Relating to registration of voters and voluntary registration of organ donors
wv:HB 4638.summary: Adds an option on voter registration applications to register as an organ donor in a national registry. Lets the Secretary of State run or contract for a donor registry, provided the Center for Organ Recovery and Education reimburses all costs.

wv:HB 4696.title: Authorize the Department of Environmental Protection to deposit funds granted pursuant to federal programs
wv:HB 4696.summary: Lets the Department of Environmental Protection deposit federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and STREAM Act money into the Acid Mine Drainage Abatement and Treatment Fund and Reclamation and Restoration Fund, and other federal abandoned mine land money into related state funds.

wv:HB 4712.title: Increasing the criminal penalties for DUI causing death to be known as “Baylea’s Law.”
wv:HB 4712.summary: Adds a higher penalty for impaired driving with deliberate disregard for others' safety that causes a death: 5 to 30 years in prison, a $2,000 to $10,000 fine, lifetime license revocation, and a mandatory sentence. Names the changes "Baylea's Law."

wv:HB 4749.title: Relating to adding requirements to the foster child bill of rights
wv:HB 4749.summary: Adds three rights to the foster child bill of rights: children 13 or older get timely notice of hearings affecting them and the right to attend, and children may have hearing outcomes explained by their guardian ad litem or counsel.

wv:HB 4755.title: Adding Aggravated Vehicular Homicide to the list of qualifying offenses
wv:HB 4755.summary: Adds aggravated vehicular homicide, DUI causing serious bodily injury, third-offense DUI, and obstructing officers or emergency personnel causing death to the offenses that trigger enhanced sentences for repeat offenders.

wv:HB 4765.title: Teacher, School Personnel, and State Police Pay Raise
wv:HB 4765.summary: Raises salary schedules for West Virginia State Police members and forensic lab staff (effective July 1, 2026), public school teachers, and school service personnel (school year 2026-27).

wv:HB 4768.title: Relating to updating definitions to incorporate federal law changes to qualified higher education expenses for purposes of 529 accounts
wv:HB 4768.summary: Updates the definition of qualified higher education expenses for West Virginia 529 college savings accounts to match changes in federal law.

wv:HB 4784.title: Extending the Qualified Opportunity Zones until July 1, 2032.
wv:HB 4784.summary: Extends the corporate net income tax deduction for qualified opportunity zone business income, moving its end from tax years beginning January 1, 2024 to January 1, 2033. Covers businesses newly registered before 2033, for up to 10 years each, retroactive to January 1, 2024.

wv:HB 4798.title: Permitting teachers to wear a “mobile alert button” for emergency situations, to be known as “Alyssa’s Law.”
wv:HB 4798.summary: Requires the Board of Education to write a rule letting public schools adopt wearable panic alert devices if funded, requires school security data be accessible to local law enforcement, and creates the Alyssa Alhadeff School Safety Fund.

wv:HB 4799.title: To establish the cold case task force for the State of West Virginia
wv:HB 4799.summary: Creates a statewide Cold Case Task Force within the State Police with an executive board and director, authorizes interagency cooperation, establishes a Cold Case Task Force Fund, and requires Fusion Center information sharing.

wv:HB 4801.title: Defining Permissible expenditures for municipalities and counties
wv:HB 4801.summary: Adds demolition of unsafe and unsanitary structures, and planning for reuse or improvement of property owned by municipalities and county commissions, to the permitted uses of hotel occupancy tax revenue by counties and cities.

wv:HB 4819.title: Relating to use of criminal records as disqualification from authorization to practice a particular profession
wv:HB 4819.summary: Changes the test for denying initial licenses or certification of polygraph examiners, plumbers, HVAC workers, electricians, electrical inspectors and fire protection workers over a conviction: the crime must directly and specifically relate to the job, not just have a rational nexus.

wv:HB 4842.title: Relating to civil remedies for the unauthorized disclosure of intimate images.
wv:HB 4842.summary: Changes the civil remedies law on unauthorized sharing of intimate images to apply to sexual extortion, and makes each person found liable jointly and severally liable with any other defendants found liable.

wv:HB 4850.title: Providing online training for Executors/Executrix of an Estate
wv:HB 4850.summary: Requires the West Virginia State Bar, beginning January 1, 2028, to post free, prominently placed, accessible educational materials on the duties of executors and administrators of estates on its website.

wv:HB 4865.title: Providing for a program allowing election official trainees to be appointed as election officials
wv:HB 4865.summary: Lets election-appointing bodies set up a program to appoint junior or senior students as election officials, with grade-average, approval and training requirements and only one participant per political party per precinct. Students serving are not counted absent from school.

wv:HB 4869.title: Establish narrow, clearly bounded guaranteed-issue rights for Medicare Supplement policies in West Virginia.
wv:HB 4869.summary: Lets Medicare supplement policyholders replace a policy of 24+ months once a year, without health underwriting, with a same-or-lesser-benefit policy from the same or an affiliated insurer; guarantees issue to people 65 or older who lose Medicaid. Requires an annual premium trend report.

wv:HB 4881.title: Relating to obtaining title to abandoned or junked motor vehicles abandoned on the property or place of business of an automobile dealer
wv:HB 4881.summary: Removes the requirement that an abandoned vehicle's loan value be $9,500 or less, and its inflation adjustment, for a dealer, auction, repair shop, or towing company to obtain title to a vehicle abandoned on its property.

wv:HB 4951.title: Requiring MDs and DOs to complete continuing education
wv:HB 4951.summary: Requires physicians renewing their medical or osteopathic licenses to complete continuing medical education in nutrition, and authorizes rulemaking.

wv:HB 4976.title: To add definitions for special plates of Class G Vehicles
wv:HB 4976.summary: Lowers to 50 the applications an organization must collect before the state designs a special plate for Class G vehicles, keeping 100 for Class A, and applies the same split to discontinuing low-use plates.

wv:HB 4982.title: Make West Virginia Healthy Act of 2026
wv:HB 4982.summary: Re-establishes the statewide Healthy Lifestyles Program and expands the Office of Healthy Lifestyles' authority. Creates a fund and wellness programs, coordinates state agencies, requires physical fitness in schools, and requires a report; repeals the earlier Healthy Lifestyles article.

wv:HB 4983.title: Authorizing the Department of Commerce to promulgate a legislative rule relating to certification of a microgrid district or certification as a high impact data center
wv:HB 4983.summary: Authorizes Department of Commerce agencies to promulgate legislative rules as filed and modified, including rules on Tourism Development Districts and on certifying a microgrid district or high impact data center.

wv:HB 4990.title: Relating to crimes using gift cards
wv:HB 4990.summary: Creates misdemeanor and felony crimes for stealing, tampering with, or using false pretenses to obtain gift cards or redemption information with intent to defraud; values over $1,000 carry 1 to 10 years in prison, lower values up to one year in jail.

wv:HB 4995.title: Require the use of video cameras in certain special education classrooms
wv:HB 4995.summary: Changes rules for cameras in self-contained special education classrooms: parents get notice of camera interruptions, a judge may give them custody of recordings, administrators review recordings every 30 days instead of 90, and recordings may be used in staff discipline. Named Oscar's Law.

wv:HB 4996.title: Relating to bail in cases involving terroristic threats to schools or children
wv:HB 4996.summary: Creates a felony for intentionally communicating a threat of a violent crime that causes, or recklessly risks, severe public alarm, punishable by a $2,500 to $10,000 fine, 1 to 10 years in prison, or both; courts may bar living or working near the threatened site.

wv:HB 4999.title: Relating to crimes against athletic officials
wv:HB 4999.summary: Sets penalties for assault ($250 to $500 fine or up to six months in jail) and battery ($500 to $1,000 or up to a year) against athletic officials and participants. Lets schools ban convicted offenders from school sports events for a year or more.

wv:HB 5004.title: Relating generally to PANS and PANDAS.
wv:HB 5004.summary: Directs the Bureau for Public Health to add education on PANS and PANDAS, including warning signs, to existing public health programs for health care professionals and public outreach.

wv:HB 5012.title: Providing for in-year school personnel movement to meet school needs.
wv:HB 5012.summary: Lets a teacher dismissed for lack of need transfer to an unfilled vacancy by length of service, as an alternative to a preferred list, effective next school year. Permits reassignment after the second school month when population shifts leave staff without work; bars retaliatory transfers.

wv:HB 5015.title: Relating to the Respiratory Care Interstate Compact
wv:HB 5015.summary: Enacts the Respiratory Care Interstate Compact, letting licensed respiratory therapists practice across member states, and allows the Board of Respiratory Care Practitioners to run criminal history record checks.

wv:HB 5048.title: To ensure virtual instruction for foster students while in temporary placement facilities.
wv:HB 5048.summary: Requires foster children awaiting residential placement to keep receiving schooling through virtual learning, starting within three days of entering temporary care. The Department of Education trains the caretaker on the technology at its own expense.

wv:HB 5063.title: To permit the county commission to appoint a county commissioner to a convention and visitor’s bureau as a voting member
wv:HB 5063.summary: Lets a county commission appoint one of its commissioners to a convention and visitor's bureau as a voting member.

wv:HB 5065.title: Relating to hotel occupancy tax.
wv:HB 5065.summary: Specifies information online lodging marketplaces must record when collecting hotel occupancy tax, requires geofencing or similar tools and nine-digit postal codes so tax goes to the correct city or county, and names the county or municipal official who receives it.

wv:HB 5086.title: Relating to peer support services
wv:HB 5086.summary: Sets standards for peer support programs, bars licensing boards from disciplining licensees for certain peer support participation, and makes peer support communications privileged and creates a testimonial privilege.

wv:HB 5087.title: Relating to Interstate Cosmetology Licensure Compact.
wv:HB 5087.summary: Enacts the Interstate Cosmetology Licensure Compact, creating multistate licensure for cosmetologists, and lets the Board of Barbers and Cosmetologists require criminal history record checks when the compact requires.

wv:HB 5088.title: Relating to Natural Resource Police Officer Retirement
wv:HB 5088.summary: Raises the Natural Resources Police Officer Retirement System accrued benefit from 2.5% to 2.75% of final average salary per year of service for members retiring after July 1, 2029, and provides additional funding to the system.

wv:HB 5089.title: Relating to public school acceptance of student transcripts or other credentials
wv:HB 5089.summary: Requires public schools to accept public charter school transcripts and credentials, to record class, grade and source on each student's public school transcript, and to report to the Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability.

wv:HB 5110.title: Amend section providing for waiver of tuition and fees for senior citizens auditing certain college classes
wv:HB 5110.summary: Lowers the minimum age for the senior reduced-tuition program at state colleges from 65 to 60, extends it to metro-area students, and caps nonresident differential tuition in the no-credit option at 50% of the resident rate.

wv:HB 5168.title: To increase funding for EMS first responders.
wv:HB 5168.summary: Clarifies that certified microgrids and high-impact data centers must pay county fire and ambulance fees. Creates two county EMS funds and moves $12 million a year of State Lottery net profits to three EMS funds ($6 million salary fund, $3 million each new fund).

wv:HB 5182.title: Relating generally to authorizing security personnel employed by the State Treasurer to carry concealed weapons while performing his or her official duties
wv:HB 5182.summary: Lets the State Treasurer allow security personnel to carry concealed firearms on duty if authorized in writing, licensed, and trained and qualified annually like law-enforcement officers. Lets the Treasurer reimburse training costs; bars personal liability of the state and its employees for good-faith acts.

wv:HB 5212.title: Relating to financial aid for post-secondary education.
wv:HB 5212.summary: Changes higher education financial aid and workforce grant programs: lets the Learn and Earn program use block grants, and revises the medical student loan, health sciences and mental health provider loan repayment programs, including paying awards directly to loan servicers.

wv:HB 5214.title: Relating to drug testing of parents who have had abuse and/or neglect claims substantiated against them prior to reunification.
wv:HB 5214.summary: Requires drug testing, with lab confirmation, of parents found to have abused or neglected a child where substance use contributed or is ongoing, and bars reunification while a parent in the home tests positive without a valid prescription.

wv:HB 5227.title: Relating to Secretary of State annual reports, fees, and veteran-owned business logotypes
wv:HB 5227.summary: Allows businesses to file biennial reports with the Secretary of State at a set biennial fee, requires email addresses on reports, sets bad check fees, lets the Secretary waive late fees, and creates a veteran-owned business logotype.

wv:HB 5277.title: Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of Health Facilities-Welch Community Hospital, William R. Sharpe Jr. Hospital, and Mildred Mitchell-Bateman Hospital from the Unappropriated Surplus Balance
wv:HB 5277.summary: Adds fiscal year 2026 general revenue capital outlay, repairs and equipment appropriations: $1 million for Welch Community Hospital, $3.4 million for William R. Sharpe Jr. Hospital and $4.304 million for Mildred Mitchell-Bateman Hospital.

wv:HB 5288.title: Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of Agriculture-West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund from Special Revenue
wv:HB 5288.summary: Increases the fiscal year 2026 current expenses appropriation of the Department of Agriculture's West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund by $200,000.

wv:HB 5317.title: Supplemental Appropriation to the Department of Commerce - Division of Natural Resources from the Unappropriated Surplus Balance.
wv:HB 5317.summary: Appropriates $10 million from the General Revenue surplus balance to the Division of Natural Resources for capital outlay, repairs and equipment in fiscal year 2026.

wv:HB 5323.title: Relating to indexing of license and stamp fees
wv:HB 5323.summary: Removes the January 1, 2021 cutoff on indexing hunting and fishing license and stamp fees, so the Natural Resources director may keep proposing rule increases tied to the Consumer Price Index, rounded down to the nearest dollar.

wv:HB 5325.title: Creating an emeritus license status for retired  physicians, podiatric physicians and physician assistants who meet eligibility criteria.
wv:HB 5325.summary: Lets the medical board issue a free, honorary emeritus license, which does not allow practice, to a fully retired physician, podiatric physician or physician assistant who holds a current license and meets eligibility criteria.

wv:HB 5353.title: To bring virtual currency kiosks within the purview of money transmission licensure and create disclosure requirements and daily transaction limitations for new and existing customers.
wv:HB 5353.summary: Requires virtual currency kiosk operators to hold a money transmission license, with disclosures, paper receipts, a law enforcement contact, daily limits of $1,000 for new customers and $10,000 for existing ones, and refunds of fraudulent transactions in a new customer's first 10 days.

wv:HB 5354.title: Relating to authorizing legislative rules regarding higher education
wv:HB 5354.summary: Authorizes legislative rules for higher education bodies, including rules on administrative exemptions, the mental health loan program and the STAND program. Also authorizes repeal of rules on purchasing efficiencies and the Research Trust Fund program.

wv:HB 5366.title: Relating to rules governing the practice of law
wv:HB 5366.summary: Makes records gathered under Supreme Court rules for the West Virginia Judicial and Lawyer Assistance Program non-public and exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

wv:HB 5381.title: Relating to developing a comprehensive energy development policy and plan for the Office of Energy
wv:HB 5381.summary: Directs the Office of Energy to develop strategies for coal, gas, nuclear, hydropower, hydrogen and geothermal power and a state energy security plan, and lets it designate generation sites. Moves Coalfield Community Development into it and replaces the Coal Fired Grid Stabilization Act of 2023.

wv:HB 5382.title: Relating to the Neighborhood Investment Program.
wv:HB 5382.summary: Extends the Neighborhood Investment Program tax credit, ending the program on July 1, 2031, with no credit for contributions to certified projects made after that date. Taxpayers who already qualified keep their credits.

wv:HB 5401.title: Relating to voting in West Virginia elections while residing overseas
wv:HB 5401.summary: Changes absentee eligibility for U.S. citizens abroad, requiring a valid passport or other proof of citizenship and no registration elsewhere in the U.S., defines overseas voter categories, and bars citizens never domiciled in West Virginia from state and local elections; effective January 1, 2027.

wv:HB 5430.title: Relating to pharmaceutical benefits
wv:HB 5430.summary: Makes the Public Employees Insurance Agency subject to the Pharmacy Audit Integrity Act, requires a competitive bid for its cost containment vendor, limits pharmacy benefit manager charges, bars certain manager ownership structures, and orders a Medicaid pilot program and study.

wv:HB 5437.title: Creating the Vape Safety Act
wv:HB 5437.summary: Creates the Vape Safety Act, requiring a state license ($1,200 annual fee) for vape or smoke shops. Sets applicant qualifications, requires shops to be at least 300 feet from churches, schools and daycares, regulates signs and sales, and sets criminal and administrative penalties.

wv:HB 5438.title: To modify the foundation allowance to improve instructional programs.
wv:HB 5438.summary: Lets the Education Department retain up to $15 million a year from the school-aid allowance for a replacement budgeting and accounting system, adds science-of-reading teacher training to its retained-fund initiatives, and carries unused balances into the next year's budget.

wv:HB 5441.title: Reforming State Personnel System
wv:HB 5441.summary: Ends the separate personnel systems for Transportation, the State Tax Division and Social Services, terminates the State Personnel Board and moves its duties to the Division of Personnel, and exempts new and promoted Transportation employees from classified civil service from July 2026.

wv:HB 5444.title: Relating to increasing the amount of fees to be paid by parolees for supervision.
wv:HB 5444.summary: Raises the monthly fee parolees pay toward the cost of supervision, to an amount based on ability to pay and not to exceed $50 per month, and makes technical corrections.

wv:HB 5457.title: To allow partial credits for times of disability service in the CPRB for Troopers.
wv:HB 5457.summary: Gives State Police retirement system members one-half service credit for months in which they receive disability benefits, counted toward years of service for retirement, and defines disability service.

wv:HB 5458.title: Relating to professionals to be licensed by the West Virginia Board of Medicine
wv:HB 5458.summary: Revises Board of Medicine licensing rules, adds board membership and procedure provisions, repeals radiologist assistant and several licensure provisions, and creates a Genetic Counselors Practice Act requiring a license and criminal background check to practice genetic counseling.

wv:HB 5459.title: Relating to a tax on managed care organizations
wv:HB 5459.summary: Replaces the managed care organization tax's tiered per-member-month rates with a 2.5% tax on certified HMOs' gross premiums written in the state, starting July 1, 2027 and subject to federal approval. Excludes Medicare Advantage and certain public and federal employee plans.

wv:HB 5462.title: Relating to Mine Subsidence
wv:HB 5462.summary: Changes mine subsidence insurance: requires payments for a covered loss go first to property damage, gives the mine subsidence fund setoff rights, and bars lawsuits against insurers over claims reported to the Board of Risk and Insurance Management.

wv:HB 5466.title: Relating to Abuse Prevention Program
wv:HB 5466.summary: Renames batterer intervention programs "abuse intervention programs," replaces "batterer" with "participant," and allows classes in person or by live virtual platform, provided an in-person option is offered.

wv:HB 5480.title: Relating to establishing the West Virginia Youth Summer Employment and Career Readiness Program.
wv:HB 5480.summary: Creates the West Virginia Youth Summer Employment and Career Readiness Program, which awards grants to employer partners, requires annual reporting and rulemaking, and is funded through a special revenue account, grants and donations.

wv:HB 5484.title: Creating the crime of conspiracy to deny medical treatment to victim of sexual offense
wv:HB 5484.summary: Creates felonies, punishable by 5 to 15 years or a fine up to $50,000, for using force or threats to block medical care or forensic evidence collection after a sexual offense, for coercing a pregnant victim into an illegal abortion, or conspiring to do either.

wv:HB 5515.title: Relating to modernizing and updating workers’ compensation statutes.
