al:HB247.summary: Renames the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America" in state law and requires state and local entities and their employees to use the name where practicable.

al:HB30.title: Judge of probate of each county to conduct post-election audit
al:HB30.summary: Requires each county's probate judge to order a post-election audit of all ballots in one randomly selected precinct and race after each general election, with results reported to the Secretary of State and posted publicly.

al:HB343.title: General Retirement System for Employees of Jefferson County; removes provisions tying eligibility to participate in plan to civil service classification; provides for status of mandatory members and part-time employee members who join on or after October 1, 2025
al:HB343.summary: Makes eligible Jefferson County employees mandatory members of the county retirement system from October 1, 2025, regardless of civil service classification; part-time employees and full-time county officeholders stay optional members.

al:HB360.title: 2nd Amendment Sales Tax Holiday created; to exempt certain items from sales tax during the last weekend of August
al:HB360.summary: As introduced, creates an annual sales tax holiday, the last Friday through Sunday of August, exempting ammunition, firearms and hunting supplies from state sales and use tax; counties and municipalities may opt in for their own taxes.

al:HB363.title: Crimes; crime of disruption of a worship service, established; criminal penalty, provided
al:HB363.summary: Creates the Class C felony of disrupting a worship service: knowingly entering a church, mosque, synagogue or other religious property during a scheduled service, intending to disrupt it by rioting, disorderly conduct, harassing a participant, or blocking entry or exit.

al:HB392.title: Lauderdale County, Eleventh Judicial Circuit, district attorneys, annual supplemental compensation provided
al:HB392.summary: Gives the chief assistant district attorney and three assistant district attorneys of the Eleventh Judicial Circuit (Lauderdale County) $24,000 a year each in supplemental pay from the county general fund.

al:HB403.title: Crimes and offenses, establishment, development, management, and maintenance of Alabama Criminal Enterprise Database provided for
al:HB403.summary: Directs the Alabama State Law Enforcement Agency, subject to funding, to run a confidential statewide criminal enterprise database that criminal justice agencies may submit to and access.

al:HB463.title: Chilton County, Chilton County 911 Board of Commissioners, credit card or debit card purchases, creation of procedures authorized
al:HB463.summary: Authorizes the Chilton County 911 board to set procedures, including purchase limits, for its director to buy goods and services with a credit or debit card issued to Chilton County 911.

al:HB479.title: Voting, statewide voter registration database, identifying voter address changes, Electronic Registration Information Center removed as verification database
al:HB479.summary: Removes the Electronic Registration Information Center from databases used to find voters whose addresses changed, and requires the Secretary of State to run list maintenance through the Alabama Voter Integrity Database, comparing voter rolls to driver license, other-state, address-change, death and citizenship data.

al:HB495.title: Marion County, board of Marion County Public Water Authority further provided for
al:HB495.summary: Sets the Marion County Public Water Authority board at five directors from October 1, 2025: the county commission chair (ex officio) and one each appointed by the firefighters association, the county's mayors, its House members and its Senate members.

al:HB512.title: Fayette County, sheriff's compensation further provided for
al:HB512.summary: Keeps the Fayette County sheriff's current base salary until January 18, 2027, adds a $20,000 yearly expense allowance from October 1, 2025, and sets an $80,000 base salary from January 18, 2027 that replaces both.

al:HB544.title: Escambia County, powers, duties, appointment, and compensation of medical examiner further provided for
al:HB544.summary: Changes how Escambia County's medical examiner is chosen: a committee of the county commission chair, district attorney, sheriff and state chief medical examiner submits candidates, and the Region IV senior state medical examiner appoints one, with the department director's approval, to a six-year term.

al:HB559.title: Crimes and offenses; crime of loitering, exceptions further provided; mask usage policies on school campuses, authorized
al:HB559.summary: Exempts wearing a medical or surgical mask at a protest or public assembly, to follow health care provider guidance or a declared state of emergency, from the masked-loitering crime; lets school boards and public colleges set mask rules for protests on their property.

al:HB586.title: City of Cullman in Cullman County, corporate limits altered
al:HB586.summary: Adds specified parcels of land in Cullman County to the corporate limits of the City of Cullman.

al:HB598.title: Town of Pine Level in Autauga County, corporate limits altered
al:HB598.summary: Adds specified territory in Autauga County, along U.S. Highway 31 and Interstate 65, to the corporate limits of the Town of Pine Level.

al:HB7.title: Illegal immigration; procedures for arrest, detention, transportation of illegal aliens provided for; reporting requirements established
al:HB7.summary: Lets state and local law enforcement agree with federal agencies to enforce immigration law, requires jails to check inmates' immigration status and honor federal immigration detainers, and sets arrest, detention and transport rules for people in the country illegally.

al:HB78.title: Baldwin County, provides for court proceedings in branch courthouses
al:HB78.summary: Lets the presiding judge of the 28th Judicial Circuit (Baldwin County) authorize civil and criminal jury proceedings in branch courthouses, with approval of the clerk and trial judge, plus the sheriff and district attorney for criminal cases.

al:SB13.title: Public K-12 Schools, broadcast of the Star-Spangled Banner required weekly, proposed constitutional amendment
al:SB13.summary: As introduced, proposes a constitutional amendment requiring local school boards to adopt policies for each public K-12 school to broadcast a Library of Congress recording of the first stanza of The Star-Spangled Banner, or allow a school group's live performance, weekly.

al:SB133.title: Juvenile court, required to provide written notification to local superintendent or principal of private K-12 school if student charged with or adjudicated delinquent for certain serious crimes; authorized to provide written notice of charges for or adjudication of delinquency for lesser crimes
al:SB133.summary: As introduced, requires juvenile courts to notify a school district superintendent or private school principal when an enrolled child is charged with or adjudicated delinquent for an act that would be a Class A or B felony for an adult; allows notice for other crimes.

al:SB156.title: Sentencing; habitual felony offender act, resentencing procedures, established
al:SB156.summary: Lets people serving life without parole under the habitual felony offender act, sentenced before May 26, 2000, and with no homicide, sex, attempted murder or injury offenses, ask a court to reduce their sentence starting October 1, 2025.

al:SB26.title: Libraries; further provides for the appointment of local library boards
al:SB26.summary: Provides that county and municipal library board members serve at the pleasure of the appointing governing body, which may remove them at any time by a two-thirds vote.

al:SB303.title: Motor vehicles; off-road vehicles, operation requirements for use on public roads, provided
al:SB303.summary: Allows off-road vehicles on public roads in unincorporated areas with speed limits of 45 mph or less if they are registered, insured, and equipped, and operated by a licensed driver.

al:SB363.title: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs; Alabama Centralized Grant Management Database, established to maintain lists of available grants
al:SB363.summary: As introduced, creates a public online database in the Department of Economic and Community Affairs listing federal and state grants administered by state agencies, plus a voluntary registry of grant writers and technical assistance providers.

al:SB370.title: Tax increment districts, Major 21st Century Manufacturing Zone allowed to be located within a tax increment district without regard to size of district and further provides for use of ad valorem tax revenues collected within a district
al:SB370.summary: Lets a Major 21st Century Manufacturing Zone lie within a tax increment district of any size, and lets district property tax revenue reimburse a public entity's costs of acquiring land in the zone before the district was created.

al:SB55.title: Driver licenses, certain classes of driver licenses invalidated
al:SB55.summary: Invalidates driver licenses of a class issued only to people who did not provide proof of lawful U.S. presence, requires citations for drivers holding one unless they carry other proof, and removes the nonresident license exemption for such licenses.

al:SB77.title: International wire transfers; fee on wire transfers imposed; income tax credit for wire transfer fees paid, authorized; Securities Commission and Revenue Department to administer
al:SB77.summary: As introduced, requires money transmitters to charge $7.50 plus 1.5% of any amount over $500 on outgoing international wire transfers, funds sheriffs' immigration enforcement costs from the fees, and allows an income tax credit for fees paid, up to $5,000.

ar:HB1646.title: TO REQUIRE CERTAIN MATERIALS TO BE STORED IN LOCKED COMPARTMENTS WITHIN A DESIGNATED AREA.
ar:HB1646.summary: Requires K-5 school libraries to lock away "non-age-appropriate sexual content" (explicit instruction in, or promotion of, sexual ideology, behaviors or orientations unsuited to K-5 students), releasing it only with written parental approval; violations can bring unpaid suspension, then license suspension or revocation.

ar:SB211.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING INITIATIVE PETITIONS AND REFERENDUM PETITIONS; TO REQUIRE A CANVASSER TO SUBMIT AN AFFIDAVIT BEFORE SIGNATURES CAN BE COUNTED; AND TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY.
ar:SB211.summary: Requires petition canvassers to file an affidavit with the Secretary of State certifying compliance with canvassing, perjury, forgery and fraud laws; signatures from canvassers without one are not counted. Takes effect immediately.

al:SB187.title: Consumer protection, app store providers and developers required to take certain actions related to age verification and parental consent, Attorney General authorized to bring action for violations as deceptive trade practice, parents authorized to bring civil action
al:SB187.summary: Requires app stores to verify users' ages and get a parent's consent before minors download or buy apps, and developers to check age and consent data through the stores; makes knowing or reckless violations deceptive trade practices with Attorney General penalties up to $50,000 each.

ar:HB1793.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING THE USE OF POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL SUPPORTS IN PUBLIC SCHOOL DISTRICTS.
ar:HB1793.summary: Removes "positive behavioral support" from Arkansas's student-restraint law, repealing its definition and replacing it with "behavioral intervention" and a multi-tiered system of supports.

al:HB146.title: Youthful offender status, to prohibit a judge from granting youthful offender status to any person who is 16 years of age and older and charged with murder
al:HB146.summary: Bars youthful offender status for people who were 16 or older at the time of the offense and are charged with capital murder or intentional murder; they are charged, arrested and tried as adults.

al:HB280.title: Public nuisance, actions to abate or enjoin public nuisances further provided for
al:HB280.summary: Adds public colleges and universities to those that may sue to abate public nuisances. For nuisance events without a local permit, requires courts to order organizers and promoters to pay abatement costs, plus court costs and attorney fees; uninvolved property owners are not liable.

al:HB29.title: Unemployment compensation, unemployed individual required to contact an increased number of prospective employers for each week of unemployment claimed; further providing for the meaning of failure to seek or accept suitable work
al:HB29.summary: Raises the weekly work-search requirement for unemployment benefits from three to five prospective employers in counties of 20,000 or more residents; smaller counties stay at three. Deems missing a scheduled interview or skills test without notice, absent good cause, a failure to seek suitable work.

al:HB304.title: Motor vehicles; impoundment conditions and procedures, further provided; redemption procedures, further provided; issuance of local identification cards, restrictions provided
al:HB304.summary: Lets officers impound a vehicle when the driver cannot show a license and licensing cannot otherwise be verified; sets owner redemption requirements, requires sale of vehicles unclaimed after 60 days, and bars local government ID cards without driver-license-level proof of identity.

al:HB541.title: Primary Elections; require political party registration to vote in primary or primary runoff elections
al:HB541.summary: Requires voters, from 2027, to register a party affiliation to vote in countywide or statewide primaries and runoffs (requesting a party ballot at the polls counts); bars changing parties from 60 days before a primary until the general election; repeals the runoff crossover ban.

al:SB298.title: Class 3 Municipalities; minimum staffing requirements for law enforcement agencies, mandated; grace period, established; state assumption of oversight for violations, provided
al:SB298.summary: Requires Class 3 municipalities to keep 1.9 full-time officers per 1,000 residents, with a five-year grace period requiring annual 10 percent deficit reductions; after that, the State Law Enforcement Agency may assume oversight of noncompliant police departments and seek restitution of costs.

ar:HB1615.title: TO AMEND THE LAW CONCERNING RELIGIOUS NONDISCRIMINATION.
ar:HB1615.summary: Bars state government from discrimination against religious groups and people over beliefs about marriage or biological sex, and lets marriage officials seek recusal. Bars denying licenses or degrees over religious beliefs unless justified by a compelling interest and least restrictive means.

ar:HB1669.title: TO CREATE THE KEEP KIDS FIRST ACT; AND TO PROVIDE FOR PROTECTIONS FROM DISCRIMINATION FOR ADOPTION AND FOSTER CARE PROVIDERS ACTING IN ACCORDANCE WITH SINCERELY HELD RELIGIOUS BELIEFS.
ar:HB1669.summary: Bars state government from requiring child placement agencies to take part in placements that violate their religious or moral beliefs, or from discriminating against foster or adoptive parents over religious beliefs, including refusal of government sexual orientation or gender identity policies; allows claims and damages.

ar:SB444.title: TO AMEND THE MEDICAL ETHICS AND DIVERSITY ACT.
ar:SB444.summary: Expands the Medical Ethics and Diversity Act so medical workers may decline to take part in abortion, assisted suicide or gender transition services. Religious providers may make hiring and staffing decisions consistent with their beliefs; federally required emergency care is unaffected.

id:H 926.title: COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE DISTRICTS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the formation of community infrastructure districts.
id:H 926.summary: As introduced, allows counties to form community infrastructure districts, which finance publicly owned infrastructure, in areas outside a city's comprehensive plan.

il:HB 4327.title: AUDITOR GENERAL-340B AUDIT
il:HB 4327.summary: As amended, directs the Department of Insurance to study how 340B covered entities and drug manufacturers take part in the federal 340B drug discount program, requires insurers, pharmacy benefit managers and manufacturers to answer its requests, and puts resulting fines in a hospital capital fund.

il:HB 4418.title: EPA-STORMWATER-PLASTIC PELLET
il:HB 4418.summary: Requires the state EPA, one year after the effective date, to develop and begin implementing stormwater pollution prevention requirements in federal stormwater permits for certain regulated facilities, to control plastic pellets and other raw plastic materials in runoff.

il:HB 4587.title: CHILD CARE DIRECTORS
il:HB 4587.summary: As passed by the House, lets day care centers employ an interim conditional child care director for up to 12 months while the person finishes coursework, only if the center already has a fully qualified director, with at most two interim directors per qualified one.

il:HB 4758.title: JOB APPLICATION-DRIVER LICENSE
il:HB 4758.summary: Bars employers from stating in a job posting that applicants must have a driver's license unless driving is an essential function and a business necessity, and requires postings that do require one to briefly explain why. Effective January 1, 2027.

il:HB 4826.title: IDFPR-CONTINUING EDUCATION
il:HB 4826.summary: Bars licensed professionals from getting continuing education credit toward license renewal for courses that promote, teach or guide services or practices that state law or rule expressly prohibits. Effective January 1, 2027.

il:HB 5198.title: AFFORDABLE HOUSING-CILAS
il:HB 5198.summary: Changes the Affordable Housing Planning and Appeal Act to require non-exempt local governments to hold a public hearing before adopting affordable housing plans and to name specific lands and deadlines, and raises the exemption threshold from 10% to 25% affordable housing units.

il:HB 5228.title: WORK COMP-STATE LICENSURE
il:HB 5228.summary: As amended in the Senate, raises the workers' compensation burial benefit from $8,000 to $10,000, sets utilization-review rules (physician-made adverse decisions when a physician recommends care; 3-month certifications), and adds a charge to insurers' surcharge funding the Workers' Compensation Commission.

il:HB 5552.title: EDUCATION-VARIOUS
il:HB 5552.summary: Changes many School Code provisions, including replacing "foreign language" with "world language" and "ethnic school" with "community-based heritage language school," repeals the Community Service Education Act, and revises educator licensure and evidence-based funding provisions.

il:SB 3037.title: DARK SKY ACT
il:SB 3037.summary: Directs the Capital Development Board to adopt, by December 31, 2029, a commercial stretch energy code with outdoor lighting standards, including a light-trespass limit of 1.0 lux, under the Energy Efficient Building Act.

il:SB 3086.title: STATE PERMITTED INVESTMENTS
il:SB 3086.summary: Allows the State Treasurer to invest State money in pooled investment trusts registered as open-end investment companies whose voting trustees are officers or employees of a national labor federation.

il:SB 3465.title: CONSTRUCTION-SANITARY REQS
il:SB 3465.summary: Requires construction employers to provide minimum sanitary conditions for workers who menstruate and lactation accommodations on request, bars retaliation for requests or complaints, and sets penalties. Effective January 1, 2027.

il:SB 3565.title: PUB AID-TOWNSHIPS
il:SB 3565.summary: Allows townships to use public aid funds to run food banks, food pantries and in-kind aid programs for people who are poor, homeless or in immediate need, regardless of General Assistance eligibility.

il:SB 807.title: STATE GOVERNMENT-TECH
il:SB 807.summary: As passed by the Senate, changes the Grant Accountability and Transparency Act so the Illinois Stop Payment List names individuals and entities ineligible to receive state grant funds.

ks:HB 2020.title: Requiring a quarterly report from the director of the division of vehicles listing the names, addresses and alien registration numbers of certain noncitizens who have been issued a driver's license during such quarter.
ks:HB 2020.summary: Requires the Division of Vehicles to give the Secretary of State a quarterly list of noncitizens with driver's licenses, checked against voter rolls; county officials must remove matching noncitizens within five business days and notify them they can be reinstated with proof of citizenship.

ks:HB 2062.title: Providing for child support orders for unborn children from the date of conception, including the direct medical and pregnancy-related expenses of the mother as a factor in child support orders and providing for an income tax exemption for unborn and stillborn children, requiring courts to consider the value of retirement accounts in certain circumstances, authorizing payment from certain retirement accounts to pay child support arrearages and eliminating the exemption of pension and retirement moneys from claims to fulfill child support obligations.
ks:HB 2062.summary: Requires child support to run from conception and be limited to the mother's direct medical and pregnancy-related expenses, excluding elective abortion costs. Creates a $2,320 state income tax exemption for an unborn child starting in tax year 2025.

ks:HB 2109.title: Exempting public utilities from civil liability relating to the attachment, access, operation, maintenance or removal of law enforcement equipment on any utility pole or other structure that is owned or operated by the public utility.
ks:HB 2109.summary: Exempts public utilities from civil liability for law enforcement equipment placed on utility poles or other utility structures under an agreement with a police department or sheriff's office.

ks:HB 2164.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2164 by Committee on Judiciary - Prohibiting certain sex offenders from entering onto school property or attending school activities and creating criminal penalties for violation thereof.
ks:HB 2164.summary: As agreed in conference, requires 30 minutes of daily organized recess for elementary grades from 2027-28, directs the State Board of Education to create a state physical fitness test for grades 1-12, and bars 12 food additives, including certain dyes, from reimbursable school meals.

ks:HB 2284.title: Directing the department of administration to adopt written policies governing the negotiated procurement of managed care organizations to provide state medicaid services pursuant to a contract with the Kansas program of medical assistance.
ks:HB 2284.summary: Requires the Department of Administration to adopt written policies for negotiated procurement of Medicaid managed care contracts, including an appeals process decided by a 10-member committee of legislators.

la:HB 578.title: CIVIL/LAW: Provides for the Restoring Biological Truth Act
la:HB 578.summary: Changes references to "gender" to "sex" in many Louisiana laws and defines sex as an individual's biological sex, male or female, as observed or clinically certified at birth. Bars using "gender identity" or similar terms as substitutes for sex. Effective August 1, 2026.

me:LD 1023.title: Resolve, to Reestablish and Continue the Work of the Blue Economy Task Force
me:LD 1023.summary: Directs the Department of Economic and Community Development to convene a 23-member Blue Economy Task Force to recommend a Center for the Blue Economy and workforce training, with a one-time $100,000 General Fund appropriation.

me:LD 1174.title: An Act to Allow Gun Shops to Hold Firearms for Veterans of the United States Armed Forces and First Responders
me:LD 1174.summary: As introduced, lets gun shops hold firearms for veterans and first responders under a firearm hold agreement, requires contacting the owner every 6 months, and bars actions against shops for returning the firearm.

id:H 562.title: INSURANCE – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding cancellation and nonrenewal of certain policies.
id:H 562.summary: Raises to 60 days the notice commercial insurers must give to cancel an established policy (other than for nonpayment) or not renew it, up from 30 and 45 days, and sets 60 days for fire policies. Nonpayment cancellation notice stays at 10 days.

il:HB 5024.title: MUNI CD-DETENTION FACILITIES
il:HB 5024.summary: Bars locating, building or operating a facility that holds or processes people for immigration purposes, including deportation processing, within 1,500 feet of a school, day care, cemetery, park, forest preserve, public housing, private residence or place of worship.

ks:HB 2056.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2056- Requiring specific intent as an element of the crime of false representation of an election official; requiring that any person nominated for an elected office accept such nomination by signing a notarized statement of acceptance and restricting the number of nominations a person may accept to one nomination per election cycle.
ks:HB 2056.summary: Adds intent to make someone believe you are an election official to the crime of falsely representing one. For parties skipping primaries, requires nominees to sign a notarized acceptance, allows one nomination each, and moves voting-equipment testing from 5 to 30 days before elections.

ks:SB 452.title: Including federal law enforcement officers in the definition of law enforcement officer that is used in certain crimes and traffic provisions and clarifying that enforcement of a federal law is covered under the tort claims act.
ks:SB 452.summary: Creates the crime of staying within 25 feet of a first responder after a warning, if it distracts them or raises concern of harm. Applies certain traffic and criminal laws to federal officers and vehicles. Bars government liability for enforcing or not enforcing federal law.

me:LD 1120.title: An Act to Promote the Secure Storage of Firearms
me:LD 1120.summary: As introduced, replaces the crime of letting a child under 16 access a loaded firearm with Class D negligent storage when a minor or prohibited person uses the gun in a crime or threateningly (Class C if it causes death or serious injury), and requires dealers to post a firearm-risk warning.

mi:HB 4578.title: Make appropriations for the department of lifelong education, advancement, and potential for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:HB 4578.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $640 million for fiscal year 2025-26 for the Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential, which runs child care, early childhood, and postsecondary scholarship programs; about $3.5 million less than current-year funding.

mi:HB 4579.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 201 and 206
mi:HB 4579.summary: As passed by the House, sets fiscal year 2025-26 funding for Michigan's 28 community colleges at about $456.7 million, about $5.6 million (1.2%) below current-year funding.

mi:HB 4580.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 236 and 241
mi:HB 4580.summary: As passed by the House, sets fiscal year 2025-26 funding for public universities and student financial aid at about $2.26 billion, about $60 million (2.6%) below current-year funding, with about $1.94 billion from restricted funds and $325 million from the General Fund.

mi:HB 4582.title: Provide for the liability of possessors of real property for injuries to invitees.
mi:HB 4582.summary: Creates the premises liability act: property possessors must use ordinary care against unreasonable hazards they know or should know of, owe invitees no duty for open and obvious conditions (with exceptions), and courts may not adopt a reasonable-care standard.

mi:HB 4583.title: The general property tax act: amend sections 24f and 36
mi:HB 4583.summary: Requires, beginning January 1, 2027, local taxing units, including school districts, to submit proposals to impose a new millage or increase or renew an existing millage only at the November regular election.

mi:HB 4584.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 312, 641, and 821
mi:HB 4584.summary: Makes school ballot-question timing, school special elections, and May millage canvassing subject, from January 1, 2027, to the November-only millage election limit in HB 4583; takes effect only if HB 4583 is enacted.

mi:HB 4596.title: Mental health code: amend sections 1034 and 1044
mi:HB 4596.summary: Sets the deadline for dismissing charges against defendants found incompetent to stand trial at the later of 15 months after the incompetency finding or 15 months after admission to a state treatment facility.

mi:HB 4664.title: Michigan vehicle code: amend section 676b
mi:HB 4664.summary: Makes blocking or impeding traffic on a public street or highway while participating in an assembly on a highway a misdemeanor punishable by up to 93 days in jail, a fine up to $5,000, or both; other violations stay civil infractions.

mi:HB 4690.title: The Michigan penal code: amend section 479a
mi:HB 4690.summary: Sets minimum prison terms for fleeing and eluding police in a motor vehicle or vessel: 30 days (fourth degree), 1 year (third), 2 years (second), 5 years (first), with a fine allowed in addition; takes effect only if HB 4691 is enacted.

mi:HB 4691.title: Michigan vehicle code: amend section 602a
mi:HB 4691.summary: Sets minimum prison terms for fleeing and eluding police in a motor vehicle: 30 days (fourth degree), 1 year (third), 2 years (second), 5 years (first), with a fine allowed in addition; takes effect only if HB 4690 is enacted.

mi:HB 4706.title: Make, supplement, adjust, and consolidate appropriations for various state departments and agencies, the judicial branch, and the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; to…
mi:HB 4706.summary: As passed by the House, makes fiscal year 2025-26 appropriations for state departments, the judiciary, and the legislature totaling about $54.6 billion, including about $12.1 billion from the General Fund.

mi:HB 4707.title: Michigan election law: add section 642e.
mi:HB 4707.summary: Bans the state, cities, and townships from conducting elections using ranked choice voting, and voids any local law or ordinance authorizing it.

mi:HB 4720.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 795 and 795a
mi:HB 4720.summary: Bars the board of state canvassers from approving electronic voting systems acquired on or after January 1, 2026 that contain parts or equipment from entities with covered equipment or services on the Federal Communications Commission's list.

mi:HB 4747.title: Income tax act of 1967: amend section 30
mi:HB 4747.summary: Beginning in 2026, lets taxpayers deduct contributions to other states' 529 college savings programs and ABLE programs, not only Michigan's, up to $5,000 (single) or $10,000 (joint) a year.

mi:HB 4839.title: The social welfare act: add section 109z.
mi:HB 4839.summary: Prohibits Medicaid coverage of a brand name drug or biological product when a lower-cost generic or interchangeable equivalent exists, except in the circumstances listed in section 17755(3)(a) to (c) of the public health code.

mi:HB 4897.title: Skilled trades regulation act: amend section 939
mi:HB 4897.summary: Creates boiler installer license classes 2B through 6B and P, defines the boilers and work each may cover, requires Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs rules setting each class's requirements, and treats class 1B holders as class 2B.

mi:HB 4898.title: Skilled trades regulation act: amend section 941
mi:HB 4898.summary: Creates boiler repairer license classes I, III, IV, V, and P, defines the repair work each may perform, requires Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs rules setting each class's requirements, and treats class II holders as class III.

mi:HB 4907.title: Skilled trades regulation act: amend section 907
mi:HB 4907.summary: Requires the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs to let holders of a class 5B boiler installer or class IV boiler repairer license perform periodic maintenance and testing of boiler system controls and safety devices.

mi:HB 4914.title: Occupational code: amend section 2010
mi:HB 4914.summary: Lowers the share of a firm's principals who must be licensed for the firm to practice architecture, engineering, or surveying in Michigan from two-thirds to 51%.

mi:HB 4915.title: Public health code: add section 16149.
mi:HB 4915.summary: Bars the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs and health professional boards from adopting or enforcing rules requiring implicit bias training for licensure, registration, or renewal, and rescinds Administrative Code rule R 338.7004.

mi:HB 4917.title: Manufacturing milk law of 2001: amend section 157
mi:HB 4917.summary: Removes the requirement that only a grader approved by the Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development may grade butter.

mi:HB 4933.title: Occupational code: amend sections 303a and 411
mi:HB 4933.summary: Repeals Article 10 of the Occupational Code, which licenses personnel agencies and their agents, and repeals the related section of the State License Fee Act.

mi:HB 4949.title: An act to provide civil immunity to persons who operate or use certain sport shooting ranges; and to regulate the application of state and local laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances regarding…
mi:HB 4949.summary: Extends the noise-related civil, criminal, and nuisance protections for sport shooting ranges to ranges that are updated, upgraded, or expanded, if the changes follow generally accepted operation practices.

mi:HB 4951.title: Provide for the imposition and collection of excise taxes on certain sales of marihuana; to provide for the establishment of procedures for the collection, administration, and enforcement of those…
mi:HB 4951.summary: Imposes a 24% excise tax, starting January 1, 2026, on the wholesale price of marijuana sold or transferred to retail licensees; revenue goes mostly to the neighborhood road fund; takes effect only if HB 4183, 4961, and 4968 are enacted.

mi:HB 4961.title: Income tax act of 1967: amend sections 12, 30, 36, 607,
mi:HB 4961.summary: Directs up to $688 million in 2025-26, rising to $952 million by 2028-29, of income tax revenue to the neighborhood road fund, creates 2026-2028 deductions for qualified tips and overtime, and adjusts which federal tax code provisions Michigan follows.

mi:HB 4968.title: Insurance provider assessment act: amend sections 7, 11, and 17
mi:HB 4968.summary: Lets the Department of Health and Human Services continue the insurance provider assessment approved by federal officials on December 20, 2024; if that approval ends, it must propose a compliant structure raising no more than the April 2024 to March 2025 total.

mi:HB 4980.title: An act to regulate and license the selling, purchasing, possessing, and carrying of certain firearms, gas ejecting devices, and electro-muscular disruption devices; to prohibit the buying, selling…
mi:HB 4980.summary: Lets people apply for a concealed pistol license from a county clerk in any Michigan county, not only their county of residence, and requires the county clerk that issued a license to send its renewal notice.

mi:HB 5032.title: The revised school code: amend section 1361
mi:HB 5032.summary: Bars school districts from using State School Aid Act funds for bond election costs, requiring those costs to be paid by private donation, except administrative costs of a general November election.

mi:HB 5035.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: add section 2980.
mi:HB 5035.summary: Lets individuals injured by false representation in assisted reproduction sue for three times their damages plus attorney fees and costs, within three years of discovery; takes effect only if HB 5036 is enacted.

mi:HB 5036.title: The Michigan penal code: add section 219g.
mi:HB 5036.summary: Creates two felonies: knowingly giving false or misleading information about assisted reproduction (up to 5 years or $50,000), and a health professional using an embryo or gamete without the patient's written consent (up to 15 years or $100,000).

mi:HB 5037.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 24 of chapter VII
mi:HB 5037.summary: Sets a 15-year time limit to bring charges for the proposed assisted reproduction felonies; if DNA from an unidentified person is found, there is no limit until that person is identified, then 15 years.

mi:HB 5038.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 16l of chapter XVII
mi:HB 5038.summary: Adds the proposed assisted reproduction fraud felonies to the sentencing guidelines as Class E (5-year maximum) and Class C (15-year maximum) crimes against a person.

mi:HB 5055.title: Legislative sergeant at arms police powers act: amend section 2
mi:HB 5055.summary: Allows commissioned legislative sergeants at arms to enforce chamber rules and state law elsewhere in Michigan when necessary to provide security for, or investigate threats or crimes against, a legislative member.

mi:HB 5069.title: Food law: add section 7132.
mi:HB 5069.summary: Bans selling or offering for sale foods containing brominated vegetable oil, propylparaben, or the dyes Red 40, Green 3, Blue 1, Blue 2, or Yellow 6 starting January 1, 2029, unless the federal government bans them first.

mi:HB 5081.title: The revised school code: add section 1253.
mi:HB 5081.summary: Requires each school district, intermediate school district, and public school academy to employ by January 1, 2027 at least one teacher tasked with assisting pupils with dyslexia who has 30 hours of Orton-Gillingham training, plus 10 hours of annual professional learning.

mi:HB 5082.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 30321
mi:HB 5082.summary: Bars the state from charging a fee for wetland assessments requested by property owners or lessees, and requires the department to complete an assessment within 60 days of the request instead of within a reasonable time.

mi:HB 5145.title: The social welfare act: add section 10h.
mi:HB 5145.summary: Bars the state from accepting self-attestation of identity, income, and Michigan residency for public assistance applications and annual eligibility reviews, requiring documents such as a driver license, pay stub, or benefits letter.

mi:HB 5157.title: The Michigan penal code: add section 89a.
mi:HB 5157.summary: Creates a felony, punishable by life or any term of years, for illegally delivering a schedule 1 or 2 controlled substance other than marijuana that is consumed and causes serious injury.

mi:HB 5158.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 16d of chapter XVII
mi:HB 5158.summary: Classifies the proposed felony of delivering a schedule 1 or 2 controlled substance causing serious injury as a Class A felony against a person, with a maximum of life imprisonment.

mi:HB 5281.title: Regulate third-party litigation funding transactions; to require disclosures in those transactions; to establish the responsibilities of litigation funding companies and of attorneys; to require…
mi:HB 5281.summary: Creates the Third-Party Litigation Funding Transparency Act: sets disclosure requirements and a 36% annual charge cap for consumer litigation funding, bars certain company practices, and requires funding companies and commercial financiers to register with the Department of Insurance and Financial Services.

mi:HB 5298.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend section 3114
mi:HB 5298.summary: Adds limousines and certain other buses to the no-fault exceptions, so their passengers claim personal protection benefits through their own coverage rather than the vehicle's insurer, and defines "bus" and "limousine"; takes effect only if HB 5299 is enacted.

mi:HB 5299.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend section 3107c
mi:HB 5299.summary: Updates cross-references in the no-fault insurance coverage-level section and moves the rideshare vehicle definitions into it; takes effect only if HB 5298 or a Senate companion bill is enacted.

mi:HB 5314.title: An act to supplement the laws of the state relating to the powers and duties of the attorney general and the institution and prosecution of actions thereby on behalf of the state, to authorize…
mi:HB 5314.summary: Repeals the provision letting actions at law brought by the attorney general for the state be started in Ingham County circuit court, with process served anywhere in Michigan.

mi:HB 5316.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: amend section 1631
mi:HB 5316.summary: Removes the provision making the county containing the state capital a proper venue for actions the attorney general starts for the state, keeping it as a proper venue when no other venue provision applies.

mi:HB 5329.title: The management and budget act: add section 261g.
mi:HB 5329.summary: Bars public entities from contracting, starting one year after the law takes effect, to buy drones with software made in whole or part by entities on specified federal lists, including the Chinese military company list; takes effect only if HB 5330 is enacted.

mi:HB 5331.title: The management and budget act: add section 261g.
mi:HB 5331.summary: Bars public entities from buying (after two years) and operating (after five years) drones made in whole or part by companies on specified federal Chinese-military, sanctions, and export-control lists, with an exception during governor-declared emergencies.

mi:HB 5364.title: The revised school code: amend section 1278
mi:HB 5364.summary: Bars the State Board of Education from implementing or enforcing revisions to the recommended model core academic curriculum content standards unless the Senate and House approve them by concurrent resolution.

mi:HB 5388.title: The Michigan penal code: amend section 224d
mi:HB 5388.summary: Adds a solution of not more than 8% chlorobenzylidene malononitrile and 1% nonenamide to the substances allowed in legal self-defense spray or foam devices, with the existing use rules and penalties applying to it.

mi:HB 5450.title: Food law: amend section 3113
mi:HB 5450.summary: Prohibits counties, cities, villages, and townships from adopting rules or ordinances that impose or collect a fee, tax, or assessment for operating a mobile food establishment.

mi:HB 5456.title: Create a hyperbaric oxygen therapy grant program and pilot program for providing treatment to veterans with traumatic brain injuries or post-traumatic stress disorder; to provide for the powers and…
mi:HB 5456.summary: Creates the hyperbaric oxygen therapy pilot program act: a three-year Department of Health and Human Services pilot and grant program to help selected providers offer no-cost hyperbaric oxygen therapy to Michigan veterans with traumatic brain injury or PTSD.

mi:HB 5457.title: Create a hyperbaric oxygen therapy fund; and to provide for the administration of and distributions from the fund.
mi:HB 5457.summary: Creates the Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Fund to pay for grants and operation of the proposed hyperbaric oxygen therapy pilot program for veterans; the fund closes when the pilot ends.

mi:HB 5467.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 165, 169, 195, 198, 255, 260, 352, and 357
mi:HB 5467.summary: Allows party committees to replace a deceased, withdrawn, or disqualified candidate only if the vacancy occurs more than 55 days before the election, and removes language requiring already-printed ballots to be reprinted.

mi:HB 5472.title: Tobacco products tax act: amend section 6
mi:HB 5472.summary: Adds the largest unit of packaging, such as a shrink-wrapped pallet, to the shipping cases or containers that must bear the consignee's name and address for tobacco products shipped out of state.

mi:HB 5498.title: Require certain agencies to designate certain employees to certain positions to manage the issuance of permits.
mi:HB 5498.summary: Requires state departments that issue permits to sort them into subject areas by industry and assign an employee to manage permit issuance in each area, and bars departments from hiring additional full-time employees for this work.

mi:HB 5502.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 30305
mi:HB 5502.summary: Exempts wetlands created by any human activity not specifically intended to create a wetland from state wetland regulation, and puts the burden on the state environment department to prove a wetland was created in a non-exempt way.

mi:HB 5520.title: The revised school code: amend section 1280f
mi:HB 5520.summary: Starting with students in grade 3 in 2027-28, requires schools to keep back from grade 4 any student who scored not proficient in reading until they show proficiency by the state test, an approved alternative test or a work portfolio, with exceptions including good-cause exemptions.

mi:HB 5551.title: Skilled trades regulation act: amend section 1107
mi:HB 5551.summary: Exempts backflow preventer testing by individuals holding an active ASSE 5110 backflow tester certification, and backflow assembly testing on automatic fire suppression systems, from the plumber license requirement.

mi:HB 5575.title: The Michigan penal code: add section 409d.
mi:HB 5575.summary: Defines "first responder" for the proposed buffer-zone offense as law enforcement officers, corrections officers, firefighters and emergency medical personnel, and defines "harass" as intentionally causing substantial emotional distress through a course of conduct.

mi:HB 5576.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 16t of chapter XVII
mi:HB 5576.summary: Adds the proposed first-responder buffer-zone felonies to the sentencing guidelines: a violation causing injury is a Class G felony (up to 2 years), and one causing death is a Class C felony (up to 15 years).

mi:HB 5619.title: Make, supplement, adjust, and consolidate appropriations for various state departments and agencies, the judicial branch, and the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027; to…
mi:HB 5619.summary: Sets 2026-27 state spending across departments at about $51.6 billion, including $12.3 billion in general fund/general purpose money, in the version the House passed.

mi:HB 5648.title: The revised school code: amend section 1278a
mi:HB 5648.summary: Requires schools to grant high school credit to a 12th grader working at least 30 hours a week in an approved trade occupation, with documented training, employer safety and labor-law compliance, school monitoring and parental consent.

mi:HB 5650.title: Require the attorney general to submit reports related to certain litigation to certain committees of the legislature; to provide for the powers and duties of certain state governmental officers and…
mi:HB 5650.summary: Requires the attorney general to report every six months to House and Senate appropriations and oversight committees on litigation costing over $250,000, with a final report after the case ends; overdue reports can bring court orders and fines up to $1,000 a day.

mi:HB 5652.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: add section 2940a.
mi:HB 5652.summary: Bars owners or occupants of property within five miles of a racetrack from suing the track under nuisance, takings or other theories if the track was built before they acquired or improved the property; environmental and safety laws still apply.

mi:HB 5710.title: An act to provide for the regulation and control of public and certain private utilities and other services affected with a public interest within this state; to provide for alternative energy…
mi:HB 5710.summary: Changes how the Public Service Commission reviews utility long-term plans to prioritize reliability and affordability, removes greenhouse gas and environmental justice planning requirements, and ends the grant program for groups representing residential utility customers.

mi:HB 5711.title: Clean and renewable energy and energy waste reduction act: amend the title and sections 1, 3, 7, 9, 11, 75, 77, 83, 87, 101, 173, and 191
mi:HB 5711.summary: Repeals Michigan's clean energy (80% by 2035, 100% by 2040) and renewable energy (50% by 2030) standards and utility energy waste reduction savings requirements, and lowers the distributed generation program cap from 10% to 1% of peak load.

mi:HB 5719.title: Prosecuting attorneys coordinating office act of 1972: amend sections 2, 3, and 4
mi:HB 5719.summary: Moves the Prosecuting Attorneys Coordinating Office and its council from the attorney general's department to the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, removes the attorney general from the council, and adds a seat for a prosecutor from a county under 50,000 people.

mi:HB 5803.title: An act to provide for the protection of children through the licensing and regulation of child care organizations; to provide for the establishment of standards of care for child care organizations…
mi:HB 5803.summary: Excludes preschool programs and classrooms in public and nonpublic schools, including Great Start Readiness Program classes, from child care center licensing.

mi:HB 5806.title: Income tax act of 1967: add sections 281 and 678.
mi:HB 5806.summary: Allows a qualified taxpayer to claim the nonrefundable Housing Opportunity Tax Credit, as allocated on an eligibility certificate, against individual or corporate income tax starting January 1, 2027, under the MSHDA program created in HB 5805.

mi:HB 5807.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend sections 476a and 476b
mi:HB 5807.summary: Lets out-of-state insurers subtract the new housing opportunity tax credit they claim from the burden counted in Michigan's insurer retaliatory tax calculation, starting in 2027.

mi:HB 5810.title: The revised school code: add section 1278e.
mi:HB 5810.summary: Requires every school under a district or charter board to implement the Presidential Fitness Test, as reauthorized by federal Executive Order 14327, starting in the 2026-27 school year.

mi:HB 5812.title: The social welfare act: add section 14o.
mi:HB 5812.summary: As introduced, bars the Department of Health and Human Services from seeking, accepting or renewing federal SNAP work-requirement waivers without specific legislative authorization, and from using the state option to exempt people from those requirements.

mi:HB 5813.title: The social welfare act: add section 106c.
mi:HB 5813.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services, starting October 1, 2026, to report Michigan Medicaid's error rate and improper payment rate annually to House and Senate oversight committees and post it online.

mi:HB 5814.title: The social welfare act: add section 106c.
mi:HB 5814.summary: Limits retroactive Medicaid coverage starting January 1, 2027 to one month before application for the expansion population and two months for others, down from three months.

mi:HB 5815.title: Administrative procedures act of 1969: amend section 61
mi:HB 5815.summary: Requires courts to use independent judgment on whether an agency acted within its statutory authority in making rules, and bars deference to an agency's reading of an ambiguous statute.

mi:HB 5816.title: Administrative procedures act of 1969: amend sections 79 and 106
mi:HB 5816.summary: Requires hearing officers in contested cases, and courts reviewing final agency decisions, to review de novo, without deferring to the agency's determinations.

mi:HB 5817.title: Administrative procedures act of 1969: amend sections 39 and 45
mi:HB 5817.summary: Requires agencies to label proposed rules major (about $1 million or more annual impact) or nonmajor and file a regulatory impact analysis; major rules need legislative approval by resolution, and new rules are rescinded after five years unless extended once.

mi:HB 5818.title: Administrative procedures act of 1969: amend sections 3, 5, 33, 44, 46, 47, and 52
mi:HB 5818.summary: Replaces the Joint Committee on Administrative Rules with a new Joint Committee on Regulatory Oversight and Administrative Review of five House and five Senate members, which reviews existing and proposed nonmajor rules and can approve or disapprove them.

mi:HB 5819.title: The revised school code: amend section 1280f
mi:HB 5819.summary: Moves up by one year, to the 2026-27 school year, the deadline for schools to use reading materials that meet state literacy requirements.

mi:HB 5821.title: The revised school code: amend section 1280f
mi:HB 5821.summary: Caps the state's list of approved elementary reading curricula at 15, gives districts until 2027-28 to use them or locally developed materials, and requires the education department to set a process, with a 90-day review, to approve local curricula.

mi:HB 5845.title: Michigan election law: amend section 811
mi:HB 5845.summary: Requires data on electronic poll book flash drives used at an election to be preserved for 22 months, and allows erasing or reusing the drives only after that period.

mi:HB 5872.title: The general property tax act: amend section 27a
mi:HB 5872.summary: Beginning December 31, 2026, stops counting any conveyance of title or present interest in property as a "transfer of ownership," so sales no longer trigger the uncapping of the property's taxable value.

mi:HB 5873.title: Repeal 1993 PA 331, entitled “State education tax act,” (MCL 211.901 to 211.906).
mi:HB 5873.summary: Repeals the six-mill state education property tax that funds the School Aid Fund, states intent to replace the revenue from the general fund, and takes effect only if HB 5880, an excise tax on certain services, is also enacted.

mi:HB 5874.title: Repeal 1993 PA 330, entitled “State real estate transfer tax act,” (MCL 207.521 to 207.537).
mi:HB 5874.summary: Repeals the state real estate transfer tax, charged to sellers based on sale price and deposited in the School Aid Fund, states intent to replace the revenue from the general fund, and takes effect only with HB 5880.

mi:HB 5875.title: Recodified tax increment financing act: amend section 228a
mi:HB 5875.summary: As introduced, updates the tax increment financing act's exemption of authority property conveyances from transfer taxes to call the state real estate transfer tax act "former" law; takes effect only if HB 5874 and HB 5880 are also enacted.

mi:HB 5876.title: An act to establish the revenue collection duties of the department of treasury; to prescribe its powers and duties as the revenue collection agency of this state; to prescribe certain powers and…
mi:HB 5876.summary: As introduced, updates the revenue collection act's list of laws excluded from its tax settlement process to call the state real estate transfer tax act "former" law; takes effect only if HB 5874 and HB 5880 are also enacted.

mi:HB 5877.title: Estates and protected individuals code: amend section 3912
mi:HB 5877.summary: As introduced, updates the Estates and Protected Individuals Code section on purchasers from estate distributees to call the state real estate transfer tax act "former" law; takes effect only if HB 5874 and HB 5880 are also enacted.

mi:HB 5878.title: The general property tax act: amend section 19
mi:HB 5878.summary: Exempts from personal property tax, for taxes levied after 2026, all personal property not otherwise exempt, if owners file annual statements; local units report exemption data to Treasury. Takes effect only with HB 5879 and HB 5880.

mi:HB 5879.title: An act to provide for the regulation and control of public and certain private utilities and other services affected with a public interest within this state; to provide for alternative energy…
mi:HB 5879.summary: Requires electric and gas utilities to report to the Public Service Commission their savings from personal property tax exemptions, requires the commission to cut residential rates by that amount, and bars a general rate case filing for two years afterward.

mi:HB 5937.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 1301, 1305, 1307, 3112, and 30307
mi:HB 5937.summary: Cuts the time the environment department has to tell applicants whether certain permit applications are complete from 30 to 7 days, and sets the decision deadline for wetland permits at 30 days, or 90 if a hearing is held.

mi:HB 5938.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 30307
mi:HB 5938.summary: Lets wetland permit holders request changes without restarting the application, limits the department's own added changes to related ones notified within seven days, and cuts the hearing window after a completed application from 60 to 30 days.

mi:HB 5974.title: Medical records access act: amend sections 3 and 5
mi:HB 5974.summary: As introduced, removes the exception letting minors who lawfully obtained care without parental consent control access to those records, and bars providers from restricting a parent's or guardian's access to a minor's medical records, except as federal law provides.

mi:HB 6013.title: The social welfare act: add section 14n.
mi:HB 6013.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to monitor Bridge Card transactions and, subject to federal law, suspend a recipient's card used outside Michigan for over 90 consecutive days until they verify Michigan residency or eligibility.

mi:HB 6043.title: An act to provide for the protection of children through the licensing and regulation of child care organizations; to provide for the establishment of standards of care for child care organizations…
mi:HB 6043.summary: Writes the Tri-Share Child Care program into law under the Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential, letting employers take part by covering at least one-third of an employee's child care costs, creates a dedicated fund, and codifies the CareShare arrangement without state subsidy.

mi:SB 1041.title: Prohibit excessive pricing for certain lodgings during a declared state of emergency; to provide remedies and penalties; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local…
mi:SB 1041.summary: Bars lodging businesses from charging excessively increased prices during a declared emergency and 30 days after; allows attorney general suits, civil fines up to $10,000 (individuals) or $500,000 (others) per violation, and misdemeanor penalties.

mi:SB 1042.title: Prohibit excessive pricing for certain commodities and emergency services and supplies during a declared state of emergency; to provide remedies and penalties; and to provide for the powers and…
mi:SB 1042.summary: Bars businesses in the chain of distribution for building materials, food, goods, services, and emergency or medical supplies from charging grossly higher prices than for similar goods during or reasonably after a declared emergency; allows attorney general suits and civil and criminal penalties.

mi:SB 1043.title: Prohibit excessive pricing for certain energy products and services during a period of market disruption; to provide remedies and penalties; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state…
mi:SB 1043.summary: Bars businesses in the energy products and services chain of distribution from charging grossly higher prices than for similar products during a market disruption; allows attorney general suits and civil and criminal penalties.

mi:SB 1052.title: The medicaid false claim act: amend section 4
mi:SB 1052.summary: Exempts CMS-sponsored model arrangements and model patient incentives from counting as a kickback or bribe under the Medicaid False Claim Act, where a kickback is a felony punishable by up to four years in prison or a $30,000 fine.

mi:SB 106.title: Michigan vehicle code: add section 811kk.
mi:SB 106.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to develop, with the Michigan Pet Alliance, a fundraising license plate for companion animal welfare; plate donations go to a new Protecting Michigan's Pets Fund, paid quarterly to the Alliance.

mi:SB 111.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: add section 2950p.
mi:SB 111.summary: As introduced, lets people age 60 or older, vulnerable adults and people with developmental disabilities petition a circuit court for a protection order that can bar firearm purchase or possession, stalking conduct, harm to their animals, and control over their money or property.

mi:SB 1136.title: Publicly funded health insurance contribution act: amend the title and sections 3, 4, and 5
mi:SB 1136.summary: Raises annual caps on public employer health plan spending from 2027 to $8,258.54 per employee with single coverage, $17,271.17 plus-one and $22,523.34 family (from $5,500, $11,000 and $15,000), indexed yearly, and requires employers to pay at least 80% of plan costs.

mi:SB 1137.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: amend sections 4011, 4012, 4015, 4031, 4061a, 6023, 6027, 6059, and 6104
mi:SB 1137.summary: Generally exempts public assistance, unemployment, earned income tax credit, disability and workers' compensation money from garnishment, limits weekly wage garnishment to the lesser of earnings above 35 times minimum wage or 15% of garnishable earnings, and raises execution exemptions, including the homestead.

mi:SB 1138.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: amend section 5451
mi:SB 1138.summary: Raises Michigan's bankruptcy property exemptions, for example the motor vehicle from $2,775 to $15,000 and the homestead from $30,000 to $125,000, and adds exemptions such as crime-victim payments; applies to cases filed after the effective date.

mi:SB 1139.title: Provide for the establishment of history museum authorities; to provide for the powers and duties of a history museum authority; to authorize the levy and collection of a property tax by a history…
mi:SB 1139.summary: Creates the History Museum Authorities Act, letting any county form an authority that, with voter approval, may levy up to 0.2 mill for up to 10 years to fund a history museum owned by a city of over 500,000 people.

mi:SB 1140.title: Brownfield redevelopment financing act: amend section 2
mi:SB 1140.summary: Excludes the property tax levied by county history museum authorities from tax increment revenues that brownfield redevelopment authorities may capture.

mi:SB 1141.title: Recodified tax increment financing act: amend sections 201, 301, 402, 523, 603, 703, and 803
mi:SB 1141.summary: Excludes the property tax levied by county history museum authorities from tax increment revenues that tax increment financing authorities may capture.

mi:SB 129.title: Open meetings act: amend section 3a
mi:SB 129.summary: As introduced, lets an appointed (not elected) member of a public body with a disability attend and vote at meetings remotely as an accommodation, if physically in Michigan; it excludes state legislative bodies when formal votes are taken.

mi:SB 130.title: State license fee act: amend sections 9 and 25
mi:SB 130.summary: Changes application and license fees for cosmetologists and related professions, raises the annual license fee for cosmetology establishments and schools, and sets new fees for secondary cosmetology school facilities; it takes effect only with a companion bill allowing those facilities.

mi:SB 145.title: An act to regulate the time and manner of payment of wages and fringe benefits to employees; to prescribe rights and responsibilities of employers and employees, and the powers and duties of the…
mi:SB 145.summary: Bars employers from asking job applicants about past wages, benefits, credit score or credit history, with listed exceptions, and from policies that prohibit or discourage employees from disclosing their own wages.

mi:SB 147.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: amend section 2534
mi:SB 147.summary: Removes the March 1, 2025 end date on the yearly inflation adjustment of the rates newspapers may charge for publishing legal notices.

mi:SB 154.title: Prohibit certain conduct at or near a health facility and prescribe penalties; to provide remedies; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental officers and…
mi:SB 154.summary: Bars injuring, intimidating or interfering with, by force, threat of force or physical obstruction, people obtaining or providing reproductive health services, and damaging property of facilities that provide them; sets misdemeanor and felony penalties and allows civil suits.

mi:SB 155.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 13n of chapter XVII
mi:SB 155.summary: Adds the felony penalties created by a companion bill on interfering with access to health facilities to the state sentencing guidelines; it takes effect only with that bill.

mi:SB 157.title: Regulate pet cemeteries; to regulate the sale of pet cemetery merchandise and services; to provide for the powers and duties of certain local governmental officers and entities; and to prescribe…
mi:SB 157.summary: Creates the Pet Cemetery Regulation Act, requiring pet cemetery land to be dedicated and kept in that use, a $10,000 endowed care fund to establish one, local health department approval, and an endowed care fee on burial rights sales.

mi:SB 160.title: Enact the uniform premarital and marital agreements act; and to determine how and when a premarital or marital agreement is enforced.
mi:SB 160.summary: Enacts the Uniform Premarital and Marital Agreement Act: such agreements are enforceable only if signed by both parties with informed consent, financial disclosure and no duress, and are unenforceable if they adversely affect custodial rights or penalize seeking divorce.

mi:SB 163.title: Make appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026 for capital outlay to finance projects to demolish, construct, renovate, or equip buildings and facilities on state property…
mi:SB 163.summary: Appropriates for fiscal year 2025-26 for 24 capital outlay projects at universities, community colleges and state facilities (11 planning, 13 construction), using a $100 placeholder amount per project.

mi:SB 164.title: Make appropriations for the department of lifelong education, advancement, and potential for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 164.summary: Appropriates about $756.2 million in total funds for the Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 165.title: Make appropriations for the department of education for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 165.summary: Appropriates about $166.4 million in total funds for the Department of Education for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 166.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 6, 11, 11a, 11j, 11k, 11m, 11s, 11x, 11z, 12d, 15, 20, 20d, 21f, 21h, 22a, 22b, 22c, 22d, 22k, 22l, 22m, 22p, 24, 24a, 25f, 25g, 26a, 26b, 26c, 26d…
mi:SB 166.summary: Appropriates about $21.8 billion in total funds for K-12 school aid in 2025-26; requires districts to use half of foundation allowance increases for educator pay, lowers allowed virtual class days from 15 to 7, and changes preschool program rules.

mi:SB 167.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 236, 236c, 236j, 239, 241, 241a, 241c, 241e, 244, 247, 248, 254, 263, 263b, 264, 268, 269, 270, 270c, 275k, 276, 277, 278, 279, 280, 281, 282, 283…
mi:SB 167.summary: Appropriates about $2.41 billion in total funds for state universities in 2025-26, sets tuition restraint at 4.5% or $735, and lengthens eligibility delay for the MI Achievement Scholarship from 15 to 24 months.

mi:SB 168.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 201, 204, 206, 207a, 207b, 207c, 210, 210b, 210d, 216e, 217a, 217b, 217c, 222, 229a, and 230
mi:SB 168.summary: Appropriates about $506.5 million in total funds for community colleges in 2025-26 and sets tuition restraint at 4.5% or $227 for 2025-26 and 3.5% or $174 for 2026-27.

mi:SB 169.title: Make appropriations for the department of corrections for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 169.summary: Appropriates about $2.25 billion in total funds for the Department of Corrections for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 170.title: Make appropriations for the judiciary for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 170.summary: Appropriates about $395.3 million in total funds for the judiciary for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 171.title: Make appropriations for the department of agriculture and rural development for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 171.summary: Appropriates about $159.5 million in total funds for the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 172.title: Make appropriations for the department of natural resources for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 172.summary: Appropriates about $636.3 million in total funds for the Department of Natural Resources for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 173.title: Make appropriations for the legislature, the executive, the department of the attorney general, the department of state, the department of treasury, the department of technology, management, and…
mi:SB 173.summary: Appropriates about $5.43 billion in total funds for fiscal year 2025-26 for the legislature, executive, attorney general, state, treasury, technology, management and budget, and civil rights departments, and certain other state purposes.

mi:SB 174.title: Make appropriations for the state transportation department for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 174.summary: Appropriates about $6.91 billion in total funds for the state transportation department for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 175.title: Make appropriations for the department of military and veterans affairs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 175.summary: Appropriates about $291.6 million in total funds for the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 176.title: Make appropriations for the department of state police for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 176.summary: Appropriates about $1.02 billion in total funds for the Department of State Police for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 177.title: Make appropriations for the department of licensing and regulatory affairs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 177.summary: Appropriates about $657.1 million in total funds for the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 178.title: Make appropriations for the department of insurance and financial services for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 178.summary: Appropriates about $78.1 million in total funds for the Department of Insurance and Financial Services for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 179.title: Make appropriations for the department of labor and economic opportunity for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 179.summary: Appropriates about $2.11 billion in total funds for the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 180.title: Make appropriations for the department of health and human services for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 180.summary: Appropriates about $39.3 billion in total funds for the Department of Health and Human Services for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 181.title: Make appropriations for the department of environment, Great Lakes, and energy for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:SB 181.summary: Appropriates about $1.03 billion in total funds for the Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy for fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 184.title: Make, supplement, and adjust appropriations for various state departments and agencies, the judicial branch, and the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025; to provide for…
mi:SB 184.summary: Supplements fiscal year 2024-25 appropriations with about $705.7 million in total funds for various state departments, the judicial branch and the legislative branch.

mi:SB 204.title: The revised school code: add section 1258.
mi:SB 204.summary: Requires school districts, intermediate districts and public school academies to adopt a closure policy by July 31, 2026, including at least one month's notice to parents and employees and a public meeting, and allowing in-year closure only for health or safety emergencies.

mi:SB 213.title: Michigan strategic fund act: amend the title
mi:SB 213.summary: Requires the new Michigan Strategic Fund advisory board to develop a 10-year economic development strategic plan within a year, with yearly updates and annual reports from the Michigan Economic Development Corporation; takes effect with a companion bill.

mi:SB 214.title: Michigan strategic fund act: add sections 9a and 9b.
mi:SB 214.summary: Creates a Strategic Advisory Board within the Michigan Strategic Fund: the Governor appoints nonvoting members representing listed organizations and agencies in policy areas such as jobs, transit, housing and education, and each area elects four voting members; takes effect with a companion bill.

mi:SB 224.title: The Michigan penal code: amend section 224
mi:SB 224.summary: Bans manufacturing, selling or possessing a bump stock or multiburst trigger activator, devices that let a semi-automatic firearm fire repeatedly or faster per trigger pull; a violation is a felony punishable by up to five years in prison or a $2,500 fine.

mi:SB 225.title: An act to regulate and license the selling, purchasing, possessing, and carrying of certain firearms, gas ejecting devices, and electro-muscular disruption devices; to prohibit the buying, selling…
mi:SB 225.summary: Bars carrying a concealed pistol in the Capitol, Anderson House Office Building and Binsfeld Senate Office Building, except for serving legislators who hold a concealed pistol license.

mi:SB 226.title: The Michigan penal code: amend section 234d
mi:SB 226.summary: Bans possessing a firearm in the Capitol, Anderson House Office Building and Binsfeld Senate Office Building, except for serving legislators who hold a concealed pistol license.

mi:SB 246.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 11102, 11103, 11104, 11108, 11109, 11110, 11125, 11132, 11512, 11514b, 11525a, 62501, and 62509
mi:SB 246.summary: Requires the environment department to adopt a hazardous and radioactive waste management plan every five years, pauses new or expanded hazardous waste facility licenses until then, bars disposal of certain TENORM, requires financial responsibility proof from some disposal wells, and raises disposal fees.

mi:SB 247.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 62506a
mi:SB 247.summary: Charges operators of Class I commercial hazardous waste disposal wells a fee of 0.417 cents per gallon, adjusted yearly for inflation, with revenue funding administration and annual grants to local governments that host the wells.

mi:SB 276.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 43520, 43521, 43522, 43523a, 43523b, 43524, 43525b, 43525c, 43527a, 43527b, 43528, 43528a, 43528b, 43529, 43531, 43532, 43532a…
mi:SB 276.summary: Raises hunting, fishing and combination license fees, lets the Department of Natural Resources require a license or recreation passport fee to use state shooting ranges, creates complete licenses covering multiple privileges, and raises the base-license surcharge from $1 to $5.

mi:SB 277.title: General sales tax act: amend section 25
mi:SB 277.summary: Earmarks each year part of the 4% sales tax revenue, equal to amounts reported from license changes in a companion bill, to the game and fish protection account and its pheasant and cold-water subaccounts.

mi:SB 278.title: State housing development authority act of 1966: amend sections 58, 58b, and 58c
mi:SB 278.summary: Opens the Michigan Housing and Community Development Program to middle-income households, drops its downtown location requirement, and requires distribution by a formula reflecting economic distress, disability and accessible housing need.

mi:SB 285.title: Of marriage and the solemnization thereof: amend section 7
mi:SB 285.summary: Allows civil celebrants (age 18 or older), township supervisors and state legislators to solemnize marriages.

mi:SB 286.title: An act establishing the minimum ages for contracting marriages; to require a civil license in order to marry and its registration; to provide for the implementation of federal law; and to provide a…
mi:SB 286.summary: Replaces references to clergy and magistrates in the marriage license law with "marriage officiant," raises the fine for officiant violations from $100 to $500, and has witnesses sign rather than list residences on marriage certificates.

mi:SB 287.title: Of marriage and the solemnization thereof: amend section 16
mi:SB 287.summary: Makes a marriage performed by a person authorized under a companion bill valid regardless of whether that person actually had authority to solemnize it.

mi:SB 288.title: Open meetings act: amend section 8
mi:SB 288.summary: As introduced, lets a public body meet in closed session with its attorney about pending or potential litigation involving the body or a member, or the attorney's legal opinion, and removes the condition that open discussion would harm its litigating position.

mi:SB 29.title: Public health code: amend sections 2227, 2617, 2617a, and 2618
mi:SB 29.summary: Requires the health department to add inequity reduction to its disparities plan, post information on biased perinatal care including obstetric racism and violence, keep a maternal death review team, and report on maternal mortality and best practices.

mi:SB 296.title: Public health code: add section 21526.
mi:SB 296.summary: Bars hospitals from requiring registered nurses to work beyond scheduled or on-call hours from June 1, 2027, with exceptions such as declared emergencies, and requires eight off-duty hours after a 12-hour shift.

mi:SB 297.title: Public health code: amend section 20165
mi:SB 297.summary: Sets administrative fines on hospitals that violate the nurse mandatory overtime limits: $1,000 for a first violation, $2,500, $5,000, and $10,000 for a fourth or later, counting violations within 36 months of the first.

mi:SB 807.title: Create the secure retirement savings program to provide retirement savings options for certain employees; to provide for the powers and duties of certain governmental officers and entities; to…
mi:SB 807.summary: Creates a state-run automatic-enrollment payroll-deduction IRA program in the Department of Treasury for private-sector employees whose employers have not offered a qualified retirement plan in the prior two years; employees can opt out, and employers may set up their own plan instead.

mi:SB 808.title: Create the secure retirement savings board and prescribe its powers and duties.
