mi:SB 808.summary: Creates the Secure Retirement Savings Board within the Department of Treasury and sets its membership and appointment terms; the board would administer the automatic-enrollment retirement savings program proposed in Senate Bill 807.

mi:SB 81.title: Michigan indigent defense commission act: amend the title and sections 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 21, and 23
mi:SB 81.summary: Extends the Michigan Indigent Defense Commission to indigent youths in delinquency cases, adds a 19th commission member, bars youths from waiving counsel without advice on the consequences and a written record, and sets grants to local systems at 40% then three 20% installments.

mi:SB 82.title: Protect the safety of judges and certain other individuals; to protect certain information of judges and certain other individuals from disclosure; to provide for the powers and duties of certain…
mi:SB 82.summary: Creates the Judicial Protection Act, requiring public bodies and others to remove a judge's or family member's personal identifying information, such as home address and birth date, within five business days of a request, with civil suits allowed for noncompliance (Senate version).

mi:SB 860.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 3, 6, 11, 11a, 11j, 11k, 11m, 11s, 11x, 11aa, 12d, 12e, 15, 18, 18a, 19, 20, 20d, 21b, 21f, 21h, 22a, 22b, 22d, 22k, 22l,
mi:SB 860.summary: Sets 2026-27 K-12 school aid, raising the per-pupil foundation allowance 2.5% to $10,300 and merging at-risk and bilingual funding into a new weighted allowance that phases up over 15 years (Senate version).

mi:SB 877.title: Make, supplement, and adjust appropriations for various state departments and agencies, the judicial branch, and the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; to provide for…
mi:SB 877.summary: Makes supplemental 2025-26 appropriations totaling about $1.0 billion gross across state departments, including $596.7 million for health and human services and two budget stabilization fund appropriations totaling $350 million, with a net $52.6 million general fund reduction.

mi:SB 878.title: Make, supplement, adjust, and consolidate appropriations for various state departments and agencies, the judicial branch, and the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027; to…
mi:SB 878.summary: Appropriates about $63.0 billion in total, including $12.7 billion from the general fund, to state departments, the judicial branch and the legislative branch for fiscal year 2026-27 (Senate version).

mi:SB 903.title: The revised school code: add section 1280h.
mi:SB 903.summary: Requires districts and public school academies receiving weighted-allowance funding under the school aid act to use it for student achievement, including literacy, math and English language instruction, implement a multi-tiered system of supports, report annually to parents, and limit administrative spending to 2%.

mi:SB 913.title: Michigan trust fund act: amend section 7
mi:SB 913.summary: Removes the end date on the annual $75 million deposit of tobacco settlement revenue into the 21st Century Jobs Trust Fund, which under current law stops after fiscal year 2025-26.

mi:SB 961.title: Create a state voting rights act; to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental officers and entities; to provide for a court-appointed monitor under certain…
mi:SB 961.summary: Enacts the Michigan Voting Rights Act, prohibiting local governments and state agencies from election laws or practices that cause a voter-participation disparity for a protected class or impair its political participation, with a notice-and-remedy process, court-ordered remedies and expense reimbursement up to $50,000.

mi:SB 962.title: Create a voting and elections database and institute; to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental officers and entities; and to provide remedies.
mi:SB 962.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to contract with public universities by Nov. 5, 2027 to create a Voting and Elections Database and Institute for election research and training, with free access to at least 12 years of election data.

mi:SB 963.title: Provide for language assistance for elections; to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental officers and entities; to create the language access advisory council; and…
mi:SB 963.summary: Requires local governments to provide election language assistance when thresholds are met, such as, before 2030, over 5% of voting-eligible residents speaking one non-English language with limited English proficiency; the Secretary of State reimburses certain ballot-tabulation costs.

mi:SB 964.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 726, 736, and 751
mi:SB 964.summary: Requires local governments to notify the Secretary of State of changes to election methods, voter-removal programs and certain records requests, and lets voters unable to enter a polling place or early voting site request voting assistance from the clerk or precinct board.

mi:SB 966.title: State housing development authority act of 1966: amend section 22
mi:SB 966.summary: Lets the Michigan State Housing Development Authority run a housing opportunity tax credit program for low-income housing projects, capped at $42 million a year from 2027 and adjusted for inflation; each credit is the lesser of the federal credit or one-sixth of the reserved amount.

mi:SB 967.title: Income tax act of 1967: add sections 279, 679, and 821.
mi:SB 967.summary: Allows a qualified taxpayer to claim, against Michigan income tax, the state low-income housing tax credit proposed in Senate Bill 966, in the amount allocated to the taxpayer, beginning Jan. 1, 2027 (Senate version; that bill caps credits at $250 million a year).

mi:SB 968.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend sections 476a and 476b
mi:SB 968.summary: Allows an insurer to claim the state low-income housing tax credit, created in Senate Bill 966, against the deposit the Insurance Code requires of out-of-state insurers, starting Jan. 1, 2027.

mi:SB 973.title: Provide for the establishment of a state-based health insurance exchange as a nonprofit corporation; to create the board of exchange and prescribe its powers and duties; to provide for assessments…
mi:SB 973.summary: Creates the Michigan Health Insurance Exchange Act, establishing a 12-member board and a nonprofit corporation to run a state individual marketplace for qualified health plans, available by Jan. 1, 2028 and funded by fees on health carriers.

mi:SB 974.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend sections 1261, 1262, 1262a, and 1264
mi:SB 974.summary: Amends Insurance Code definitions in Section 1261 to match the state health insurance exchange that Senate Bill 973 creates.

mi:SB 975.title: The insurance code of 1956: add section 3406mm.
mi:SB 975.summary: Requires the director of the Department of Insurance and Financial Services to contract with the state health insurance exchange to certify qualified health and dental plans.

mi:SB 976.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend section 2212a
mi:SB 976.summary: Requires health insurers, at enrollment, to provide information required by the state health insurance exchange created in Senate Bill 973, as directed by the Department of Insurance and Financial Services.

mi:SB 977.title: The insurance code of 1956: add section 3406nn.
mi:SB 977.summary: Requires the Department of Insurance and Financial Services to apply for a state waiver to set up a state-based health reinsurance program and to report to the appropriations committees on the money needed to fund it.

mi:SB 978.title: The insurance code of 1956: amend section 3406o
mi:SB 978.summary: Repeals the Insurance Code section that lets insurers provide coverage for emergency and early prescription refills that meet specified requirements.

mn:HF 13.title: Duty to retreat before using reasonable force in defense of self or others eliminated.
mn:HF 13.summary: As introduced, provides that reasonable force may be used to resist or help another resist an offense against a person regardless of whether a reasonable possibility of retreat exists; effective Aug. 1, 2025.

mn:HF 1434.title: Age verification required for websites with material harmful to minors, enforcement by the attorney general provided, and private right of action created.
mn:HF 1434.summary: As introduced, requires commercial entities whose websites show harmful-to-minors material on 25% or more of pages viewed to verify Minnesota users are 18 or older and not retain identifying data; allows attorney general and parent lawsuits, with penalties up to $25,000 per violation.

mn:HF 1471.title: Copy of the landlord-tenant guide required at issuance or renewal of rental license.
mn:HF 1471.summary: Requires cities and towns that issue or renew a rental license or similar document to give the landlord a physical copy of the attorney general's landlord-tenant guide, or a link to it if issued electronically.

mn:HF 17.title: General fund cash bonding bill.
mn:HF 17.summary: Appropriates one-time general fund money in fiscal year 2026 for capital projects, including education, public safety, public facilities and housing; requires prevailing wages on funded projects; and cancels prior general fund appropriations listed in a 2025 cancellation report.

mn:HF 20.title: Data classification of certain data maintained by the attorney general clarified.
mn:HF 20.summary: As introduced, specifies that the categories of Attorney General office data classified as private, such as disciplinary proceeding records and consumer complaints, apply to data on individuals.

mn:HF 2442.title: Climate and energy finance bill.
mn:HF 2442.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 for energy programs, including about $15.3 million a year to the Department of Commerce, about $11.4 to $11.6 million a year to the Public Utilities Commission, and renewable development account spending.

mn:HF 2563.title: Legacy finance bill.
mn:HF 2563.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 from the outdoor heritage, clean water, parks and trails, and arts and cultural heritage funds, extends some prior appropriations, and changes reporting and accountability requirements.

mn:HF 2685.title: Athletic team designations based on biological sex at birth required.
mn:HF 2685.summary: As introduced, requires school-sponsored interscholastic, intramural or club athletic teams to be designated male, female or coed based on sex at birth, and limits female-designated teams to students who were female at birth.

mn:HF 3.title: Legislative auditor required to submit a report to the legislature related to an agency's implementation of legislative auditor recommendations, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3.summary: Requires the legislative auditor, as resources permit, to report yearly on whether audited entities implemented recommendations from the prior five years, requires an annual status report from the commissioner of management and budget, and appropriates money for both offices.

mn:HF 3023.title: Iron ore mining employees additional benefits adopted.
mn:HF 3023.summary: Provides up to 26 additional weeks of unemployment benefits, through June 19, 2026, to workers laid off from March 15 to June 16, 2025 by iron ore mining employers cutting 40% or more of their workforce, or by explosives suppliers to them.

mn:HF 3127.title: Expiration of the pass-through entity tax modified.
mn:HF 3127.summary: As introduced, sets the Minnesota pass-through entity tax election to expire for tax years after Dec. 31, 2027, replacing an expiration currently tied to a federal Internal Revenue Code provision.

mn:HF 32.title: Health insurers prohibited from requiring co-payments for children's mental health services.
mn:HF 32.summary: As introduced, prohibits health plan companies from requiring co-payments for mental health services for children under 18, except the minimum needed to keep high-deductible plans eligible for health savings accounts; applies to plans from Jan. 1, 2026.

mn:HF 3402.title: Possession of large-capacity ammunition magazines banned.
mn:HF 3402.summary: As introduced, bans manufacturing, importing, transferring, owning or possessing magazines that accept more than ten rounds, with exceptions for officers and military; owners must surrender, alter or remove them by July 1, 2027; violations are felonies.

mn:HF 3405.title: Bureau of Criminal Apprehension's Use of Force Investigations Unit required to conduct investigations of incidents involving federal agents.
mn:HF 3405.summary: As introduced, requires the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension's Use of Force Investigations Unit to investigate use-of-force deaths and criminal sexual conduct cases involving federal agents of DHS, ICE, CBP or USCIS, in addition to peace officers.

mn:HF 3412.title: Circumstances when a person may conceal their identity in public modified and specific exceptions for law enforcement officers created.
mn:HF 3412.summary: As introduced, adds exceptions to the misdemeanor for concealing identity in public for protection from smoke, gas or airborne toxins, and for officers acting undercover or on tactical teams where a mask reduces a known risk of facial disfigurement.

mn:HF 3493.title: Safe schools revenue increased; safe schools revenue available to charter schools, cooperative units, nonpublic schools, and Tribal contract schools made; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3493.summary: As introduced, makes safe schools aid of $36 per pupil unit available to charter schools, cooperative units, nonpublic schools and Tribal contract schools beginning in fiscal year 2027, and appropriates money.

mn:HF 16.title: Immigration law enforcement noncooperation ordinances and policies prohibited, use of immigration-related data provided, and county attorneys required to notify federal immigration authorities when an undocumented person is arrested for a crime of violence.
mn:HF 16.summary: As introduced, bars state and local government entities from restricting the sharing of immigration-status information with federal agencies, bars local ordinances limiting cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, and requires county attorneys to report undocumented people arrested on suspicion of a crime of violence to ICE even without charges.

mn:HF 3615.title: Cannabis laboratory testing requirements extended.
mn:HF 3615.summary: Extends from January 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 the period during which lower-potency hemp edibles and hemp-derived products without intoxicating cannabinoids may be tested by any ISO-accredited laboratory, not only licensed cannabis testing facilities.

mn:HF 3621.title: Fraud; payments to program participants withheld under certain circumstances.
mn:HF 3621.summary: Lets state agencies withhold program payments on a credible allegation of fraud under investigation, replacing the current 60-day, preponderance-of-evidence hold. Requires notice within five days, allows administrative reconsideration, and ends the hold when evidence is insufficient or legal proceedings finish.

mn:HF 3819.title: Licensing inspection requirements for child care providers modified, program integrity requirements for child care assistance program established, and report required.
mn:HF 3819.summary: As introduced, requires unannounced licensing inspections of child care centers, plus one more yearly for centers receiving $500,000 or more in assistance; providers receiving that much are subject to video monitoring with cameras installed. Providers must sign assistance bills under penalty of perjury.

mn:HF 3843.title: Report to the legislature recommending appropriations from the workforce development fund required.
mn:HF 3843.summary: As introduced, requires the Workforce Development Board to review nonprofit applicants and recommend which should receive workforce development fund appropriations, considering good standing, past state funding, staff size and executive pay, and past results; reports are due January 1 of odd-numbered years from 2027.

mn:HF 4378.title: Onetime emergency rental assistance aid for counties and Tribal governments established, claims administrator required to return unused funds, prior appropriation canceled, time period to correct delinquent rent temporarily extended, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 4378.summary: As introduced, provides $40 million one time to counties ($35.2 million) and Tribal governments ($4.8 million) for emergency rental assistance to households at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines, and temporarily sets 30 days to correct delinquent rent before an eviction action.

mn:SF 3596.title: Relating to taxation; aids to local governments; establishing a onetime emergency rental assistance aid for counties and Tribal governments; requiring the claims administrator to return unused funds; canceling a prior appropriation; temporarily extending time…
mn:SF 3596.summary: Provides $40 million one time to counties ($35.2 million) and Tribal governments ($4.8 million) for emergency rental assistance to households at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines, and temporarily sets 30 days to correct delinquent rent before an eviction action.

mn:HF 4487.title: Onetime property tax refund or credit provided, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 4487.summary: As introduced, provides a one-time refund of a share of 2026 property taxes on homes, apartments, farmland and certain other property, funded by a $4 billion general fund appropriation; unclaimed refunds become 2027 property tax credits.

mn:HF 4546.title: Human services and the Department of Children, Youth, and Families forecasted program adjustments made.
mn:HF 4546.summary: Adjusts 2026-27 forecasted program funding: adds $739.6 million (FY2026) and $775.0 million (FY2027) for human services, mainly Medical Assistance and MinnesotaCare, and reduces children, youth and families programs by $45.2 million and $36.5 million.

mn:HF 475.title: Joint Committee on Library of Congress of United States Congress requested to approve replacement of statue of Henry Mower Rice now on display in National Statuary Hall in the United States Capitol, and memorial resolution proposed.
mn:HF 475.summary: Asks the Joint Committee on the Library of Congress to approve replacing Minnesota's statue of Henry Mower Rice in the U.S. Capitol with one of Hubert H. Humphrey, with the Rice statue going to Rice County.

mn:HF 4907.title: Motor vehicle registration tax modified, and money transferred.
mn:HF 4907.summary: As introduced, lowers the passenger car registration tax rates from 1.54% to 1.25% and from 1.575% to 1.285% of vehicle price, lowers age-based percentages for years two to nine, and transfers general fund money to the highway user tax distribution fund.

mn:HF 5015.title: School safety plans enhanced, student discipline provisions modified, anonymous reporting systems enabled, safe schools revenue increased, school building and cybersecurity grant program modified, reports required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 5015.summary: As introduced, directs the School Safety Center to maintain a model school safety plan, encourages anonymous threat-reporting systems, increases safe schools revenue, and creates $50 million in school safety facility grants (up to $500,000 per school), canceling $50 million for a passenger rail project.

mn:HF 76.title: Rate recovery of executive pay limited for certain public utilities.
mn:HF 76.summary: As introduced, bars the Public Utilities Commission from letting ratepayers cover pay for a utility's ten highest-paid officers or employees above the governor's salary; applies to utilities with at least 300,000 Minnesota retail customers.

mn:HF 9.title: Tax finance and policy bill.
mn:HF 9.summary: Changes Minnesota's income, corporate, property and sales taxes, including making the research credit partially refundable, ending the data center electricity sales tax exemption, raising the cannabis products tax, and repealing the controlled substance tax.

mn:SF 1.title: Omnibus Higher Education policy and appropriations
mn:SF 1.summary: Sets higher education funding and policy for the Office of Higher Education, state colleges and universities, and the University of Minnesota, creates and changes scholarships and grants, requires a standard financial aid offer form, and changes sexual misconduct grievance processes.

mn:SF 17.title: Omnibus Jobs, Labor Economic Development policy and appropriations
mn:SF 17.summary: Sets the two-year budget for jobs, labor and economic development, funding the Departments of Employment and Economic Development and Labor and Industry, Bureau of Mediation Services, Explore Minnesota and Workers' Compensation Court of Appeals, and changes economic development and labor policy and fees.

mn:SF 2.title: Omnibus Energy, Utilities, Environment and Climate policy and appropriations
mn:SF 2.summary: Appropriates and transfers money for energy programs, makes changes to energy policy, and allows natural gas utilities to sell extraordinary event bonds under certain circumstances.

mn:SF 1671.title: Relating to civil law; requiring landlords to provide just cause for terminating tenancy
mn:SF 1671.summary: As introduced, requires landlords to have a listed ground, such as unpaid or repeatedly late rent, lease breach, owner or family move-in, leaving the rental market, renovation or a government order, before ending a tenancy or refusing to renew a lease.

nc:HB 105.title: Gaston County Board of Education Election Partisan.
nc:HB 105.summary: Makes Gaston County school board elections partisan, with nine members on staggered four-year terms: seven from residency districts and two elected countywide.

nc:HB 139.title: Baby Boxes/Newborn Safety Device.
nc:HB 139.summary: Lets 24-hour-staffed fire, rescue and emergency department buildings install temperature-controlled newborn safety devices where a parent can leave an infant up to 30 days old, with alarms, signage and annual state inspection.

nc:HB 171.title: Equality in State Agencies/Prohibition on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
nc:HB 171.summary: Bars state agencies from DEI programs in hiring, staffing or training, and bars state and local governments from using public money for DEI. Sets State Auditor compliance audits, removal of violating employees, civil penalties and lawsuits.

nc:HB 173.title: Various Local Provisions III.
nc:HB 173.summary: Bars Wake County municipalities from expanding extraterritorial jurisdiction through 2028, removes a parcel from Asheville, limits commercial moratoria in Taylortown, allows 40-year Asheboro and RDU airport leases, and sets the Catawba-Lincoln county line.

nc:HB 214.title: Faithful Article V Commissioner Act.
nc:HB 214.summary: Sets rules for North Carolina's delegates to a U.S. constitutional amendment convention: seven legislature-chosen commissioners, qualifications, an oath, and a Class I felony for exceeding their authority.

nc:HB 226.title: City of Greensboro/Deannexations.
nc:HB 226.summary: Removes three Greensboro parcels from the city limits, effective June 30, 2025.

nc:HB 244.title: Depoliticize Government Property Act.
nc:HB 244.summary: Limits flags flown or displayed at state and local government buildings to U.S., state, local government, military, POW/MIA, Honor and Remember, foreign nation, other state and tribal flags; employees who violate it face discipline, up to termination.

nc:HB 294.title: Jackson County Board of Education Election Partisan.
nc:HB 294.summary: Switches Jackson County school board elections from nonpartisan to partisan starting in 2026, with five members from residency districts on staggered four-year terms.

nc:HB 302.title: Pitt County Board of Education Election Partisan.
nc:HB 302.summary: Makes Pitt County school board elections partisan, with nine members from single-member districts on staggered four-year terms, starting with the 2026 elections.

nc:HB 305.title: Guilford County Sales Tax Distribution Mods.
nc:HB 305.summary: Lets Guilford County municipalities that levy no property tax receive 25% of their per-capita share of local sales tax proceeds, if their council adopts a resolution.

nc:HB 336.title: Town of Maggie Valley/Deannexations.
nc:HB 336.summary: Removes seven parcels from the Maggie Valley town limits, effective June 30, 2025.

nc:HB 38.title: Second Amendment Financial Privacy Act.
nc:HB 38.summary: Bars payment card networks from using firearms merchant codes, keeping records of state residents' firearm ownership, or discriminating against firearms merchants. Allows Attorney General penalties up to $5,000 and private suits for $10,000 per violation.

nc:HB 402.title: Limit Rules With Substantial Financial Costs.
nc:HB 402.summary: Makes state rules costing $20 million or more over five years take effect only if a General Assembly bill approves them. Requires two-thirds board votes for rules costing $1 million or more, and unanimity at $10 million or more.

nc:HB 412.title: Child Care Regulatory Reforms.
nc:HB 412.summary: Directs DHHS to develop a plan separating child care star ratings from subsidy requirements. Changes licensing standards, including lead-teacher group limits, staff qualifications and school-age care in school buildings, and creates a school-age care credential.

nc:HB 414.title: 1-to-1 Credit for Career and College Promise.
nc:HB 414.summary: Directs community colleges and the State Board of Education to develop courses that each give one high school credit and meet a graduation requirement, offered after a January 2028 report. Stops requiring Math III unless a student's career plan includes it.

nc:HB 439.title: Allow Concealed Carry of Knife.
nc:HB 439.summary: Allows people 18 or older to carry a concealed bowie knife, dirk, dagger, switchblade or similar blade if they carry ID and are not disqualified, for example by a felony conviction, fugitive status, drug addiction or a restraining order.

nc:HB 442.title: Restore Flounder/Red Snapper Season.
nc:HB 442.summary: Directs marine fisheries officials to set a recreational southern flounder season of at least six weeks (one fish per day), a 750,000-pound commercial flounder quota and a year-round red snapper season, and to finish a flounder stock assessment by July 1, 2026.

nc:HB 549.title: Clarify Powers of State Auditor.
nc:HB 549.summary: Exempts the State Auditor's office from certain state procurement rules, including IT procurement; lets the Auditor investigate improper activity by publicly funded entities; lets the Department of Revenue force-collect debts owed to state agencies.

nc:HB 568.title: 2025 Omnibus Labor Amendments.-AB
nc:HB 568.summary: Limits when Labor Department staff can be compelled to testify about workplace safety inspections, exempts rules identical to federal safety standards from notice-and-hearing steps, allows prehearing discovery, renames the elevator division a bureau, and revises employer notice posting.

nc:HB 58.title: Various Local Elections.
nc:HB 58.summary: Makes Asheboro school board elections partisan with seven members; creates seven Anson County commissioner districts; sets four-year Kittrell terms; applies a vacancy process to Caswell commissioners; lets Scotland County commissioners set school budgets at their discretion, ending the funding floor.

nc:HB 605.title: Definitions for Advanced Recycling.
nc:HB 605.summary: Defines recycled products to include products made from recyclable material through chemical recycling using mass balance attribution, and defines mass balance attribution and third-party certification system.

nc:HB 618.title: Ivermectin Access Act.
nc:HB 618.summary: Requires the State Health Director to issue a standing order by October 1, 2025, letting pharmacists dispense human-use ivermectin without a prescription, with civil and criminal liability immunity for the director and pharmacists.

nc:HB 1083.title: Voluntary Portable Benefits Plan Act.
nc:HB 1083.summary: Creates voluntary portable benefit accounts owned by independent contractors, which hiring parties, including app-based companies, may fund if the worker opts in. Contributions are not treated as evidence that the worker is an employee.

mn:SF 4367.title: Relating to local government; authorizing housing and redevelopment agencies to utilize certain long-term equity investment authority; modifying investment types in which a qualifying government may invest
mn:SF 4367.summary: Lets housing and redevelopment authorities and qualifying local governments invest in shares of an SEC-registered company holding at least 80% federally insured or guaranteed investment-grade securities and aimed in part at local multifamily housing.

mn:SF 916.title: Relating to education; restricting female sports team participation to the female sex
mn:SF 916.summary: Limits participation in elementary and secondary school sports teams restricted to girls to students of the female sex; if disputed, requires a physician's statement based solely on reproductive anatomy, natural testosterone level and chromosomes.

mi:HB 4156.title: The revised school code: amend sections 1278a and 1278b
mi:HB 4156.summary: Changes Michigan high school graduation requirements: makes algebra II one of several math options, lists courses that can fill math, arts and English credits, cuts the non-English-language requirement from 2 credits to 1, and adds a future-skills credit for students entering high school in 2029-30.

mi:HB 4158.title: The revised school code: amend sections 502, 503, 522, 552, and 1279g
mi:HB 4158.summary: Lets charter schools and school districts enrolled in the state school aid act's assessment pilot program use its state-administered assessment system in place of the M-STEP or Michigan merit exam, and makes other wording and deadline changes.

mi:HB 4159.title: The revised school code: amend section 1278
mi:HB 4159.summary: Requires the State Board of Education's recommended K-6 reading and writing standards to be based on the science of reading with a phonics-focused approach, and requires districts' K-6 reading and writing curriculum to follow them starting in the 2026-27 school year.

mi:HB 4160.title: Administrative procedures act of 1969: amend sections 32 and 45
mi:HB 4160.summary: Bars agencies from adopting rules stricter than the applicable federal standard unless the agency director finds a clear and convincing need or, for rules the federal government does not mandate, a statute authorizes it. The impact statement must give the facts. Exempts emergency rules.

mi:HB 4161.title: Make, supplement, adjust, and consolidate appropriations for various state departments and agencies, the judicial branch, and the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; to…
mi:HB 4161.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates $4.8 billion ($2.6 billion general fund) for 2025-26 to Corrections, Treasury and Technology/Management/Budget, the Judiciary, Military and Veterans Affairs, State Police and Transportation, and adjusts some 2023-24 appropriations.

mi:HB 4162.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 11 and 17b
mi:HB 4162.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates about $15.6 billion in total funds for K-12 school aid in 2025-26 and raises the per-pupil foundation allowance by $417 (4.3%), from $9,608 to $10,025.

mi:HB 4170.title: Income tax act of 1967: amend section 51
mi:HB 4170.summary: Lowers Michigan's individual income tax rate from 4.25% to 4.05% effective January 1, 2025, and makes any future revenue-triggered rate reduction permanent beginning with the 2026 tax year.

mi:HB 4180.title: General sales tax act: amend sections 6a and 6c
mi:HB 4180.summary: Exempts retail sales of motor fuel and aviation fuel from the state sales tax starting October 1, 2025. Part of a road-funding package that takes effect only if all its bills are enacted.

mi:HB 4181.title: Streamlined sales and use tax revenue equalization act: amend sections 3 and 5
mi:HB 4181.summary: Ends, starting October 1, 2025, the 6% specific tax on motor fuel and alternative fuel used by interstate motor carriers, along with the matching credit for fuel bought in Michigan. Takes effect only if the rest of the road-funding package is enacted.

mi:HB 4182.title: Use tax act: amend sections 6c and 21
mi:HB 4182.summary: Exempts motor fuel and aviation fuel from the state use tax starting October 1, 2025, and ends the required split of aviation-fuel use-tax revenue between two aviation funds.

mi:HB 4183.title: Motor fuel tax act: amend section 8
mi:HB 4183.summary: Sets Michigan's gasoline and diesel tax at 51 cents per gallon starting October 1, 2025, up from a 26.3-cent base rate adjusted annually for inflation, and changes how the January 1, 2026 inflation adjustment is calculated.

mi:HB 4184.title: Aeronautics code of the state of Michigan: amend sections 34 and 203
mi:HB 4184.summary: Raises Michigan's tax on aircraft fuel from 3 cents to 10 cents per gallon, sending 35% of the added 7 cents to the State Aeronautics Fund and 65% to the Qualified Airport Fund.

mi:HB 4185.title: General sales tax act: amend section 25
mi:HB 4185.summary: From 2025-26 on, requires an extra $755 million a year of 4% sales tax revenue to go to the School Aid Fund and $95 million a year to revenue sharing for cities, villages and townships.

mi:HB 4186.title: Michigan business tax act: amend sections 201 and 500
mi:HB 4186.summary: Raises the Michigan business tax rate from 4.95% to 30% for business activity from January 1, 2025, and lets taxpayers who elected to file under it switch to the corporate income tax, giving up remaining legacy credits.

mi:HB 4187.title: Income tax act of 1967: amend sections 623 and 695
mi:HB 4187.summary: Changes how corporate income tax revenue is distributed: after $50 million for housing, up to $2.2 billion a year goes 90% to local road agencies and 10% to the State Trunkline Fund; the rest goes to the general fund.

mi:HB 4192.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 3122
mi:HB 4192.summary: Charges licensed mobile home parks with 1,000 or fewer residents and campgrounds with 1,000 or fewer sites, if they would otherwise be group 1 facilities, the $1,800 groundwater discharge permit fee instead of $7,500.

mi:HB 4214.title: Michigan vehicle code: amend sections 601b and 682
mi:HB 4214.summary: Requires drivers to stop 20 feet or more from a school bus showing flashing yellow lights, if a safe stop is possible, and otherwise to slow and pass with caution; civil fines are $100 to $250, or up to $500 if camera-based.

mi:HB 4218.title: Mental health code: amend sections 100d and 756
mi:HB 4218.summary: Bars people employed by or serving in the health department's executive office from serving on the 12-member State Recipient Rights Advisory Committee; the director must replace any current member in that role within 30 days of the law taking effect.

mi:HB 4230.title: An act to provide for the classification of all public roads, streets, and highways in this state, and for the revision of that classification and for additions to and deletions from each…
mi:HB 4230.summary: Creates the Neighborhood Road Fund: $100 million a year through 2029-30 goes to repairing closed, restricted and critical bridges, and the rest is distributed to county road commissions and city and village road agencies by road mileage, for local road upkeep.

mi:HB 4238.title: The revised school code: add section 1346.
mi:HB 4238.summary: Bars public schools from agreements or grants with China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria or Venezuela that limit contracting freedom, let that country direct curriculum or values, or promote an agenda against U.S. security; cultural exchange deals need federal review first.

mi:HB 4246.title: Public health code: amend sections 16170a, 16222, 16231, 16238, and 17201
mi:HB 4246.summary: Enters Michigan into the Nurse Licensure Compact, letting nurses with a multistate license from a compact state practice in Michigan without a separate Michigan license.

mi:HB 4255.title: Public health code: amend sections 7401, 7410, and 7417
mi:HB 4255.summary: Sets minimum prison terms for manufacturing or delivering heroin, fentanyl, carfentanil and derivatives, from 5 years (under 50 grams) to 30 years (1,000 grams or more); sets 10 to 40 years for adults delivering to a minor, and 10 years for undisclosed-fentanyl sales.

mi:HB 4257.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 11502 and 11503
mi:HB 4257.summary: Defines anaerobic digestion and digestate in Michigan's solid waste law and makes the "disposal area" definition subject to a companion-bill provision exempting sites that manage digester material under its rules. Takes effect only if HB 4265 is enacted.

mi:HB 4265.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 11506 and 11568
mi:HB 4265.summary: Excludes digestate from registered anaerobic digesters from the definition of solid waste, and replaces the general-permit requirement for digesters using only off-site feedstock with 5-year registration ($750 fee, contingency plan), quarterly digestate testing and allowed-feedstock rules.

mi:HB 4284.title: An act to regulate and license the selling, purchasing, possessing, and carrying of certain firearms, gas ejecting devices, and electro-muscular disruption devices; to prohibit the buying, selling…
mi:HB 4284.summary: Cuts the concealed pistol license renewal fee from $115 to $30 and sends the full fee to the county concealed pistol licensing fund, instead of splitting it between the county ($36) and the state.

mi:HB 4338.title: Prohibit local units of government from enacting or enforcing any law, ordinance, policy, or rule that limits local officials, officers, or employees from communicating or cooperating with…
mi:HB 4338.summary: Bars cities, villages and townships from limiting officers' or employees' communication or cooperation with federal officials about immigration status; residents can sue and the attorney general must sue over violations, and courts must order policies changed and award damages and fees.

mi:HB 4339.title: Prohibit counties from enacting or enforcing any law, ordinance, policy, or rule that limits peace officers or local officials, officers, or employees from communicating or cooperating with…
mi:HB 4339.summary: Bars counties from limiting officers' or employees' communication or cooperation with federal officials about immigration status; residents can sue and the attorney general must sue over violations, and courts must order policies changed and award damages and fees.

mi:HB 4340.title: The social welfare act: add section 1d.
mi:HB 4340.summary: Bars people who are not U.S. citizens or federally defined qualified aliens from receiving services or grants or taking part in programs under the Social Welfare Act, except where federal law provides otherwise.

mi:HB 4341.title: State housing development authority act of 1966: add section 13.
mi:HB 4341.summary: Bars people who are not U.S. citizens or federally defined qualified aliens from receiving services or grants or taking part in programs under the State Housing Development Authority Act, except where federal law provides otherwise.

mi:HB 4342.title: Glenn Steil state revenue sharing act of 1971: amend section 21
mi:HB 4342.summary: Requires the state treasurer to withhold state revenue sharing payments from a city, village, township or county that enacts or enforces a policy violating the companion bills barring limits on cooperation with federal officials on immigration status, while the policy continues.

mi:HB 4350.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 40111a
mi:HB 4350.summary: Allows people to put out feed for wildlife and birds, despite Natural Resources Commission deer and elk feeding orders, if it is within 300 feet of a residence and totals no more than two gallons; requires feeding orders to follow federal disease-control standards.

mi:HB 4354.title: Michigan commission on law enforcement standards act: amend section 2
mi:HB 4354.summary: Adds law enforcement officers employed by a qualified authority under the municipal sewage and water supply systems act (1955 PA 233) to the officers covered by the Michigan Commission on Law Enforcement Standards act.

mi:HB 4356.title: Michigan election law: amend section 509bb
mi:HB 4356.summary: Requires the Secretary of State, after each November general election, to mail voters who have not voted in 8 years a card to confirm their address. If a notice is undeliverable and the voter stays inactive for two more general elections, the registration is cancelled.

mi:HB 4369.title: Food law: add section 7134.
mi:HB 4369.summary: Beginning July 1, 2028, bars public and nonpublic schools from providing, selling or making available to students foods containing brominated vegetable oil, potassium bromate, propylparaben, or the dyes Red 40, Green 3, Blue 1, Blue 2 or Yellow 6.

mi:HB 4375.title: Use tax act: amend section 2
mi:HB 4375.summary: Excludes the stated trade-in credit for a portable electronic device, traded toward a new or used one bought from a retailer, from the price subject to the state use tax. Takes effect only if its companion sales tax bill is also enacted.

mi:HB 4376.title: General sales tax act: amend section 1
mi:HB 4376.summary: Excludes the stated trade-in credit for a portable electronic device, traded toward a new or used one bought from a retailer, from the price subject to the state sales tax.

mi:HB 4390.title: Michigan vehicle code: amend sections 43b and 319b
mi:HB 4390.summary: Lets any peace officer, not only a certified drug recognition expert, give a roadside oral fluid (saliva) test to detect controlled substances, and adds "other bodily fluid" to the chemical-test provisions. Takes effect 90 days after enactment and only if HB 4391 is enacted.

mi:HB 4391.title: Michigan vehicle code: amend sections 625a, 625c, and 625g
mi:HB 4391.summary: Lets police require drivers to take a roadside oral fluid (saliva) test for controlled substances, as with the breath test; results can support an arrest, and refusing is a civil infraction (a misdemeanor for commercial drivers). Takes effect only if HB 4390 is enacted.

mi:HB 4421.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: add section 1506.
mi:HB 4421.summary: Bars Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy agents from entering private property without a warrant or the owner's or occupant's consent, and says the open fields doctrine does not apply to their searches.

mi:HB 4434.title: The code of criminal procedure: repeal sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 6a, and 6b of chapter VII
mi:HB 4434.summary: Repeals the Code of Criminal Procedure sections that let a judge, on a complaint or a prosecutor's request, conduct an inquiry into suspected crimes, compel witnesses to testify, and order the arrest of suspects.

mi:HB 4445.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 40102 and 40111a
mi:HB 4445.summary: Allows individuals to bait deer during deer open seasons, and defines deer or elk baiting separately from deer or elk feeding.

mi:HB 4466.title: Public health code: amend sections 16221 and 16226
mi:HB 4466.summary: Adds a final order or judgment under the companion bill barring gender-transition treatment of minors as a ground for health professional license discipline, with sanctions of revocation, permanent revocation or denial. Takes effect only if that bill is enacted.

mi:HB 4467.title: Prohibit chemical and surgical mutilation of minors; to provide remedies; and to provide for the powers of certain state officers and entities.
mi:HB 4467.summary: Bars health care professionals from giving minors puberty-blocking drugs, hormones above typical levels, or certain surgeries to alter the appearance of their sex or affirm a perceived sex inconsistent with their sex, with exceptions for sex-development disorders; allows lawsuits and attorney general enforcement.

mi:HB 4468.title: The insurance code of 1956: add section 3406ww.
mi:HB 4468.summary: Requires health insurers to cover side effects of an enrollee's gender transition treatment, annual monitoring, and treatment to reverse the transition, if the person was enrolled when the treatment occurred.

mi:HB 4469.title: Elliott-Larsen civil rights act: add section 405.
mi:HB 4469.summary: Says the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act does not bar K-12 schools subject to Title IX from basing athletics eligibility on an individual's biological sex as listed on the original birth certificate.

mi:HB 4486.title: Prohibit municipalities from imposing a ban on the use of natural gas or the installation of natural gas infrastructure; to provide for the powers and duties of certain local governmental officers…
mi:HB 4486.summary: Bars counties, cities, villages and townships from adopting or enforcing ordinances, resolutions or policies that prohibit using natural gas or propane or installing their distribution infrastructure; such provisions adopted after the bill takes effect are void.

mi:HB 4492.title: Improved workforce opportunity wage act: amend section 4d
mi:HB 4492.summary: Lets employers require tipped employees to share tips with other employees as long as each employee's tips still cover the gap between the tipped and general minimum wage, and removes the requirement that employees keep their tips and give written consent.

mi:HB 4515.title: The social welfare act: add section 14k.
mi:HB 4515.summary: Requires food assistance and cash assistance recipients' Michigan Bridge Cards to carry the photo and signature of the recipient and of other authorized users over 18, and requires the department to acquire the needed equipment.

mi:HB 4572.title: Make appropriations for the department of military and veterans affairs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:HB 4572.summary: Appropriates $152 million from the general fund for capital improvements at Selfridge Air National Guard Base, including shifting the runway and repairing the airfield, nearby roads, drainage and access to the base.

mi:HB 4576.title: Make appropriations for the department of education for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; and to provide for the expenditure of the appropriations.
mi:HB 4576.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates $133.2 million for the Department of Education in 2025-26, 19.2% below the current year, and removes authorization for 118 positions.

mi:HB 4577.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 11 and 17b
mi:HB 4577.summary: As passed by the House, appropriates $21.9 billion in total funds for 2025-26 school aid (up 5.5%), raises the per-pupil foundation allowance by $417 to $10,025, and adds per-pupil payments tied to school resource officer and mental health staff commitments.

mi:HB 4602.title: Michigan election law: amend section 794a
mi:HB 4602.summary: Requires secretary of state test-deck procedures to be replicable without proprietary systems, lets local election boards control their own test-deck process, and bars the secretary of state from restricting test-deck sources, giving one vendor exclusive control, or centralizing all ballot information with one vendor.

mi:HB 4750.title: Foster care and adoption services act: add section 8f.
mi:HB 4750.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to screen children in foster care for benefit eligibility within 60 days of entry and yearly, apply for benefits, and conserve at least 40% of benefits it manages at ages 14-15, 80% at 16-17, 100% at 18-20.

mi:HB 4765.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 493a, 493b, 495, 509gg, and 509ii
mi:HB 4765.summary: Requires the secretary of state to verify citizenship of voter registration applicants using state and federal Homeland Security databases; unverified applicants may vote only in federal elections until they provide proof, such as a license indicating citizenship.

mi:HB 4808.title: Open meetings act: amend section 3a
mi:HB 4808.summary: Allows the Children Trust Michigan state board to meet electronically in any circumstances, without the limit confining remote participation to members absent for military duty or a medical condition; takes effect only if SB 418, SB 421, and HB 4805 are enacted.

mi:HB 4824.title: Michigan liquor control code of 1998: amend sections 105 and 1115
mi:HB 4824.summary: Requires a supplier registering a multibranded product to appoint the wholesalers holding rights to its underlying brand, sets December 23, 2025 as the date for preserving distribution rights, and transfers $680,000 a year from the Sunday spirits-sales special fund to the general fund.

mi:HB 5315.title: Of certain state officers: amend section 28
mi:HB 5315.summary: Limits the attorney general's intervention in other courts in cases involving the state to when the governor or either legislative chamber requests it, removing intervention on the attorney general's own judgment.

mi:HB 5504.title: Create the state digital service office; to require reports; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state governmental officers and entities.
mi:HB 5504.summary: Creates a State Digital Service Office in the technology department for five years to promote modern software development practices and review software projects costing $1 million or more; its chief officer may block or redirect projects risking significant unnecessary costs.

mi:HB 5505.title: Create the digital oversight office; and to prescribe the powers and duties of the office, certain officials, and state agencies.
mi:HB 5505.summary: Creates a Digital Oversight Office in the legislature, led by an officer appointed by both chambers for three years, to investigate state agency IT projects and purchases and join or take over troubled projects, with access to agency records.

mi:HB 5515.title: The Michigan penal code: amend section 227
mi:HB 5515.summary: Limits the concealed-carry ban on double-edged nonfolding stabbing instruments and other dangerous weapons to those over 6 inches, and exempts fishing knives carried as such, as hunting knives already are; daggers, dirks and stilettos stay barred.

mi:HB 5536.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 30301, 30307, and 30308
mi:HB 5536.summary: Narrows the state wetland definition to features adjacent to, and continuously surface-connected with, waters of the United States, while provisions on local wetland ordinances keep the broader prior definition.

mi:HB 5537.title: The Michigan penal code: add section 473a.
mi:HB 5537.summary: Bans growing, synthesizing, selling, giving, importing or distributing kratom or synthetic variants like 7-OH, a misdemeanor with up to 90 days in jail, a $5,000 fine, or both; higher penalties for repeat offenses and sales to minors; FDA-approved kratom products are exempt.

mi:HB 5557.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 5503
mi:HB 5557.summary: Requires the state environment department to use the longest time period the federal Clean Air Act allows when calculating emission rates for an emissions inventory.

mi:HB 5574.title: The Michigan penal code: add section 409c.
mi:HB 5574.summary: Makes it a crime to violate a verbal warning not to approach a first responder and stay within 25 feet intending to impede, threaten or harass: a misdemeanor (60 days, $500), or a felony if the responder is injured (2 years) or killed (15 years).

mi:HB 5707.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 30103 and 30305
mi:HB 5707.summary: Exempts excavating or building a noncommercial residential pond under one acre, not connected to a lake, river or stream, on land zoned residential or agricultural, from state inland lake and stream permits and wetland permits.

mi:HB 5712.title: Of certain state officers: amend section 32
mi:HB 5712.summary: Makes attorney general opinions on legal questions submitted by the legislature or state officers advisory only, with no legal authority.

mi:HB 5727.title: Youth employment standards act: amend the title and sections 2, 5, 7, 10, 15, and 20
mi:HB 5727.summary: Replaces work permits and the state permit and registration system with employer-kept proof of age for minors, adds limits for under-16 workers of 8 hours a day when school is out and 6 days a week, and removes the bar on night-work and hazardous-work deviations.

mi:HB 5820.title: The revised school code: amend section 1531e
mi:HB 5820.summary: Starting July 1, 2026 (instead of September 30, 2027), requires teacher preparation programs for reading, language arts, special education or school psychologist candidates to offer instruction in evidence-based science-of-reading methods; the dyslexia instruction requirements keep the 2027 date.

mi:HB 5936.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 1307
mi:HB 5936.summary: Raises the payment the environment department owes applicants for missed permit deadlines from 15% to the full amount of the application fee and first periodic fee, as applicable, and requires each permit approval or denial to cite its statutory basis.

mi:HB 6038.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 30306
mi:HB 6038.summary: Limits when the environment department may require changes to a wetland permit application: only after a site visit made before the completeness-review period under section 1305 ends; it may not require changes after a later site visit.

mi:HB 5501.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 30311d
mi:HB 5501.summary: Requires the environment department to adopt wetland mitigation rules including expedited permit review, 1:1 ratios for wetlands relocated within a parcel, temporary mitigation credits and off-site mitigation near transportation projects; also sets statutory timing and financial-assurance requirements for mitigation.

mi:SB 109.title: Emergency management act: amend the title and sections 18 and 19
mi:SB 109.summary: Requires the Legislature to appropriate enough to keep the Disaster and Emergency Contingency Fund at $75 million, raises local disaster grant caps to $2.5, $5 or $10 million by population, creates a State Hazard Mitigation Fund, and requires annual reports.

mi:SB 132.title: Income tax act of 1967: add section 261.
mi:SB 132.summary: Allows a nonrefundable income tax credit, starting in 2026, of 50% of contributions to a certified community foundation's endowment fund, capped for individuals at $100 ($200 on a joint return).

mi:SB 134.title: Michigan consumer protection act: amend the title and sections 2, 4, 5, 10, and 15
mi:SB 134.summary: Sets specific civil fines for Consumer Protection Act violations targeting elders or vulnerable adults, lets the Attorney General (or a prosecutor with permission) serve a written demand for information before suing, and creates an enforcement and education fund financed by costs and proceeds.

mi:SB 30.title: Create the biased and unjust care reporting act; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state governmental officers and entities.
mi:SB 30.summary: Creates the Biased and Unjust Care Reporting Act, requiring the Department of Health and Human Services to collect and analyze reports of pregnancy and postpartum care that was biased, unjust or lacked informed consent, and report its prevalence without identifying providers.

mi:SB 310.title: An act to provide for the protection of children through the licensing and regulation of child care organizations; to provide for the establishment of standards of care for child care organizations…
mi:SB 310.summary: Puts the Tri-Share Child Care Program, which divides child care costs among employers, employees and the state, into law under the Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential (MiLEAP), and creates a Tri-Share Child Care Fund for it and Child Care Facilitator Hubs.

mi:SB 311.title: Require the adjustment of reimbursements made to child care providers under the child development and care program for inflation; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local…
mi:SB 311.summary: Requires annual inflation adjustment, using the Detroit-area consumer price index, of reimbursement rates paid to child care providers in the Child Development and Care Program, starting October 1, 2027, when the index shows an increase.

mi:SB 319.title: An act to prohibit strikes by certain public employees; to provide review from disciplinary action with respect thereto; to provide for the mediation of grievances and the holding of elections; to…
mi:SB 319.summary: Makes minimum staffing levels a required subject of collective bargaining for police and fire units covered by Public Act 312, but optional if the employer's revenue-sharing sales tax receipts or property tax collections fell from the prior fiscal year.

mi:SB 33.title: Estates and protected individuals code: amend sections 5507 and 5509
mi:SB 33.summary: Lets a patient advocate designation state which life-sustaining treatment the patient wants if pregnant, and removes the bar on a patient advocate withholding or withdrawing treatment that would result in a pregnant patient's death.

mi:SB 331.title: An act to regulate and license the selling, purchasing, possessing, and carrying of certain firearms, gas ejecting devices, and electro-muscular disruption devices; to prohibit the buying, selling…
mi:SB 331.summary: Bans making, selling or transferring firearms, frames or receivers without valid serial numbers, and bans possessing them after 18 months; limits unlicensed individuals to making five firearms a year and sets misdemeanor and felony penalties.

mi:SB 332.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 11b of chapter XVII
mi:SB 332.summary: Makes a second or later violation of the firearm serial-number prohibitions in Senate Bill 331 a Class E felony punishable by up to five years in prison.

mi:SB 34.title: Elliott-Larsen civil rights act: amend sections 201 and 301
mi:SB 34.summary: Adds pregnancy and lactating status to what counts as sex discrimination under the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act.

mi:SB 357.title: General sales tax act: amend section 25
mi:SB 357.summary: Replaces the School Aid Fund reimbursement calculation for revenue lost to certain sales tax exemptions with a fixed amount that rises each year with the Consumer Price Index.

mi:SB 358.title: Use tax act: amend section 21
mi:SB 358.summary: Replaces the School Aid Fund reimbursement calculation for revenue lost to certain use tax and property tax exemptions with a fixed amount that rises each year with the Consumer Price Index.

mi:SB 361.title: Deferred presentment service transactions act: amend section 22
mi:SB 361.summary: Updates a citation to the Identity Theft Protection Act in the Deferred Presentment Service Transactions Act to match the changes in Senate Bill 360, which it depends on.

mi:SB 362.title: The Michigan penal code: amend section 159g
mi:SB 362.summary: Updates a citation to the Identity Theft Protection Act in the Michigan Penal Code to match the changes in Senate Bill 360, which it depends on.

mi:SB 363.title: Of the statutes: amend section 9
mi:SB 363.summary: Updates a citation to the Identity Theft Protection Act in the Revised Statutes of 1846 to match the changes in Senate Bill 360, which it depends on.

mi:SB 364.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 10c of chapter II
mi:SB 364.summary: Updates a citation to the Identity Theft Protection Act in the Code of Criminal Procedure to match the changes in Senate Bill 360, which it depends on.

mi:SB 382.title: Create a financial aid program for certain residents of this state who attend certain postsecondary educational institutions in this state; to provide for the administration of the financial aid…
mi:SB 382.summary: Creates the Michigan Achievement Scholarship Act, moving the existing scholarship program out of the School Aid Act, and requires a public online dashboard of recipient completion data starting in fiscal year 2026-27.

mi:SB 383.title: Create a financial aid program for certain residents of this state who attend certain occupational training programs in this state; to provide for the administration of the financial aid program; to…
mi:SB 383.summary: Creates the Michigan Achievement Skills Scholarship Act, moving the existing program out of the School Aid Act, and bars training institutions from changing tuition or costs because a student receives the award.

mi:SB 4.title: The insurance code of 1956: add section 3406tt.
mi:SB 4.summary: Requires health insurers to comply with upper payment limits on prescription drugs that a state board could set under Senate Bill 3.

mi:SB 420.title: Open meetings act: amend section 3a
mi:SB 420.summary: Amends the Open Meetings Act to let the Children Trust Michigan Board meet electronically under any circumstance.

mi:SB 462.title: Youth tobacco act: amend the title and sections 1, 4, and 5
mi:SB 462.summary: Requires retailers and third-party facilitators of tobacco, vapor and nicotine product sales to hold a state license, sets fines and license sanctions, and requires regular compliance checks by the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs.

mi:SB 463.title: Youth tobacco act: amend section 2
mi:SB 463.summary: Ends penalties for people under 21 who possess, buy or attempt to buy tobacco, vapor or alternative nicotine products.

mi:SB 465.title: Youth tobacco act: add section 1i.
mi:SB 465.summary: Lets a retailer that lawfully sold nicotine or tobacco products before the licensing law and has a pending license application file an affidavit to keep selling without a license until the application is decided.

mi:SB 466.title: Age of majority act of 1971: amend sections 2 and 3
mi:SB 466.summary: Specifies that the Age of Majority Act does not apply to the Michigan Regulation and Taxation of Marihuana Act.

mi:SB 480.title: An act to provide for the protection of children through the licensing and regulation of child care organizations; to provide for the establishment of standards of care for child care organizations…
mi:SB 480.summary: Changes the child care licensing definition of "minor child" to remove limits on residents aged 18 or older in foster and group homes, and to include people 21 or younger placed by a court in a licensed facility or sentenced as juveniles.

mi:SB 49.title: Michigan occupational safety and health act: amend the title and sections 4, 13, 14, 14a, 14e, 14f, 14j, 14n, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 33, 35, 36, 37, 41, 45, 46, 52, 54,
mi:SB 49.summary: Moves Michigan occupational safety and health act duties from other departments to the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity, aligns state penalties with federal ones, exempts employer consultation reports from FOIA, and repeals a contingent penalty section.

mi:SB 5.title: The social welfare act: add section 109o.
mi:SB 5.summary: Requires Medicaid to comply with upper payment limits on prescription drugs that a state board could set under Senate Bill 3.

mi:SB 50.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 14b of chapter XVII
mi:SB 50.summary: Deletes Code of Criminal Procedure sentencing guidelines tied to a penalty section of the Michigan occupational safety and health act that Senate Bill 49 repeals.

mi:SB 515.title: An act to regulate relationships between landlords and tenants relative to rental agreements for rental units; to regulate the payment, repayment, use and investment of security deposits; to provide…
mi:SB 515.summary: Requires landlords to install at least one working carbon monoxide device in every rental unit with a fuel-fired appliance or adjacent to an enclosed garage, with a civil fine of up to $500 for violations.

mi:SB 517.title: The revised school code: amend section 1351a
mi:SB 517.summary: Changes what school districts may buy with borrowed money, notes or bonds for technology: bars consumables, out-of-warranty device repairs, and curriculum-specific software or training, replacing the current list of barred uses.

mi:SB 527.title: Revised judicature act of 1961: amend sections 151d and 321
mi:SB 527.summary: Transfers $1 million each year from the Juror Compensation Reimbursement Fund's unspent balance to the Court Equity Fund for state fiscal years 2027, 2028 and 2029, and directs certain fees collected for the juror fund to Court of Appeals operations instead of a probation program.

mi:SB 529.title: Michigan election law: add sections 483b, 544g, 590i, and 957a.
mi:SB 529.summary: Bars people paid to circulate petitions from being paid a fixed amount per signature collected or per completed signature sheet.

mi:SB 530.title: Michigan election law: add section 482g.
mi:SB 530.summary: Requires petition circulators to offer each signer the choice of having the petition summary read to them or reading it before signing.

mi:SB 531.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 482, 590h, 685, 957, and 958
mi:SB 531.summary: Counts only an elector's first valid signature when the same person signs a petition more than once, revises petition headings and warnings accordingly, and takes effect January 1, 2027.

mi:SB 533.title: Michigan election law: add section 931c.
mi:SB 533.summary: Sets civil fines of up to $1,000 for knowingly making false statements about an election to impede someone from voting, and up to $10,000 for an employer who employed such a person for election-related purposes, unless it shows no prior knowledge.

mi:SB 55.title: Make, supplement, and adjust appropriations for various state departments and agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2024; to provide for certain conditions on appropriations; and to…
mi:SB 55.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations of about $165.6 million ($61.5 million General Fund) for fiscal year 2023-24 across several departments, covering caseload adjustments, cost variances and unanticipated federal grants.

mi:SB 56.title: The state school aid act of 1979: add sections 11cc, 201i, and 236s.
mi:SB 56.summary: Adds supplemental school aid appropriations: a $3.3 million reappropriation of federal funds for the Community College Academic Catch-Up Program for 2023-24, and $100 placeholders for the 2024-25 K-12 and higher education budgets.

mi:SB 563.title: Aeronautics code of the state of Michigan: amend section 77
mi:SB 563.summary: Makes nonsubstantive wording changes to section 77 of the Aeronautics Code.

mi:SB 565.title: Michigan trust fund act: amend section 3a
mi:SB 565.summary: Requires money left in the Local Government Reimbursement Fund at fiscal year-end to lapse to the General Fund instead of staying in the fund.

mi:SB 566.title: Worker’s disability compensation act of 1969: amend sections 625 and 835
mi:SB 566.summary: Lets the Workers' Disability Compensation Agency set filing fees by administrative rule, bars charging for use of approved electronic record standards, and removes the current $100 fee per party for redemption agreements.

mi:SB 574.title: Michigan trust fund act: amend section 7
mi:SB 574.summary: Ends the required annual $17.5 million tobacco settlement deposit into the Countercyclical Budget and Economic Stabilization Fund, which would instead go to the Michigan Merit Award Trust Fund.

mi:SB 575.title: Revised municipal finance act: amend sections 303 and 319
mi:SB 575.summary: Raises municipal securities filing and late fees (for example, doubling the minimum qualified statement fee from $800 to $1,600) and requires annual inflation adjustment of the fees beginning January 1, 2026.

mi:SB 576.title: The management and budget act: add section 475.
mi:SB 576.summary: Creates the Energy Efficiency Revolving Fund, managed by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget, to support state projects that reduce Michigan's carbon footprint, and requires reporting to the Legislature.

mi:SB 577.title: Safe drinking water act: amend section 9
mi:SB 577.summary: Removes the October 1, 2025 end date on fees the environment department may charge for public water supply operator training and certification programs.

mi:SB 578.title: An act to provide for the classification of all public roads, streets, and highways in this state, and for the revision of that classification and for additions to and deletions from each…
mi:SB 578.summary: Requires the Department of Transportation to estimate the cost of local federal bridge load analysis, inspection and other mandates, and lets it pay them from the Movable Bridge Fund when no other funding exists.

mi:SB 579.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 301, 3101, 3104, 3110, 3118, 3120, 3122, 3132, 3306, 4104, 4112, 5519, 11108, 11109, 11123, 11153, 11509, 11512, 11525a, 11717b…
mi:SB 579.summary: Removes expiration dates on many environmental permit, registration and certification fees under the Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act, and requires annual inflation adjustment of the fees beginning January 1, 2026.

mi:SB 581.title: Recodified tax increment financing act: amend section 201
mi:SB 581.summary: Lets a municipality located on the mainland and one or more islands include separate areas, divided by water, in one downtown district for a downtown development authority.

mi:SB 707.title: Public health code: amend sections 16903 and 16909
mi:SB 707.summary: Replaces marriage and family therapist licensure requirements starting January 1, 2028, requiring 3,000 hours of supervised post-degree clinical experience (some by two-way video), and lets the licensing department adjust hour requirements by rule for Medicare provider eligibility.

mi:SB 721.title: Commercial redevelopment act: amend sections 9, 12a, 16, and 18
mi:SB 721.summary: Extends from December 31, 2025 to December 31, 2035 the date after which new commercial facilities exemption certificates may be issued, and lets applicants amend applications to correct errors.

mi:SB 722.title: Commercial rehabilitation act: amend sections 2, 6, 7, 14, and 16
mi:SB 722.summary: Extends the commercial rehabilitation tax exemption certificate sunset to December 31, 2035, lengthens the maximum certificate term from 10 to 12 years, and lets applicants submit amended applications to correct errors.

mi:SB 723.title: Brownfield redevelopment financing act: amend sections 2, 8a, 13c, 14a, and 16
mi:SB 723.summary: Removes the December 31, 2027 approval sunset for transformational brownfield projects, raises the cap on total tax capture from $1.6 billion to $3.5 billion, and adds affordable housing, milestone, profit-sharing and stock-buyback rules and a $300 million limit per new plan.

mi:SB 757.title: Regulate addictive feeds on addictive internet-based services or applications; to regulate covered operators; to provide for parental consent; to prohibit certain acts related to addictive…
mi:SB 757.summary: Enacts the SAFE Act, barring operators from giving minors addictive feeds without verifiable parental consent, limiting related notifications overnight and during school hours, and letting the Attorney General seek fines of up to $5,000 per violation.

mi:SB 758.title: Establish standards and practices relating to certain online services; to prohibit certain acts and practices by covered online service providers related to certain online services; to provide for…
mi:SB 758.summary: Enacts the Kids Code Act, barring online services from targeted advertising and profiling of minors, requiring high-privacy default settings and parental controls, and setting civil fines of up to $50,000 per violation from 2027.

mi:SB 759.title: Michigan consumer protection act: amend section 3
mi:SB 759.summary: Makes a violation of the Kids Code Act in Senate Bill 758 an unlawful practice under the Michigan Consumer Protection Act.

mi:SB 760.title: Regulate operators of certain chatbots; to regulate offering certain chatbots to minors; to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental officers and entities; to…
mi:SB 760.summary: Enacts the LEAD Act, barring chatbot operators from offering minors chatbots that act as confidants or encourage harm, requiring age verification, and allowing Attorney General fines up to $25,000 per violation and parent lawsuits.

mi:SB 78.title: An act to provide for setting aside the conviction in certain criminal cases; to provide for the effect of such action; to provide for the retention of certain nonpublic records and their use; to…
mi:SB 78.summary: Lets people ask a court to set aside otherwise ineligible felony convictions committed before age 18, if conditions are met including 15 years since release from incarceration; allows reapplying one year after denial and repeals the limit of one set-aside conviction.

mi:SB 792.title: Obsolete property rehabilitation act: amend sections 2, 6, 7, 14, 16, and 17
mi:SB 792.summary: Extends to December 31, 2036 the deadline for new obsolete property rehabilitation certificates, raises the yearly cap on school-aid millage exclusions from 25 to 45, and modifies certificate contents and project start rules.

mi:SB 793.title: An act to provide for the establishment of plant rehabilitation districts and industrial development districts in local governmental units; to provide for the exemption from certain taxes; to levy…
mi:SB 793.summary: Counts the start of an industrial facility project from its building or trade permit rather than demolition, and removes an applicant's right to appeal a local government's denial of an industrial facilities exemption certificate.

mn:HF 24.title: Born alive infant provisions modified.
mn:HF 24.summary: As introduced, changes the born-alive infant law so the recognition and protection sentence covers a born alive infant as a result of an abortion (currently any infant born alive), and the required measures change from caring for the infant to preserving the born alive infant's life and health.

mn:HF 3433.title: Possession of semiautomatic military-style assault weapons banned, and criminal penalties provided.
mn:HF 3433.summary: As introduced, bans transferring, owning or possessing semiautomatic military-style assault weapons; owners before Jan. 1, 2027 may keep theirs only by requesting BCA and local law enforcement certification by May 1, 2027, with secure storage and inspections. Violating the ban is a felony, up to five years.

mn:HF 3435.title: Access to school sites limited for federal officials.
mn:HF 3435.summary: As introduced, bars school district and charter school employees, except as state or federal law or a supported educational program requires, from letting DHS, ICE, CBP or USCIS agents enter a school site without ID, written purpose, judicial warrant and superintendent approval; ICE access is then limited to areas without students.

mn:SF 2689.title: Relating to consumer protection; adding and modifying provisions governing Medicaid fraud; providing the attorney general certain subpoena and enforcement authority; clarifying the classification of certain data maintained by the attorney general; providing…
mn:SF 2689.summary: As amended in committee, creates the crime of medical assistance fraud for intentionally submitting claims, cost reports or rate applications known to be partly false, with penalties up to 20 years and $100,000 by false amount, and expands attorney general subpoena authority to wage, insurance and financial records.

mn:SF 3699.title: Relating to immigration enforcement; restricting law enforcement access to sensitive locations; establishing civil remedies; modifying the concealing identity crime; expanding the scope of use of force investigations; limiting access to certain information
mn:SF 3699.summary: Creates a privilege from civil immigration arrest for people attending court proceedings and bars staff at health care facilities, schools, colleges and child care centers from allowing civil immigration enforcement entry without a judicial warrant. Adds civil remedies and changes the concealing-identity crime.

nc:HB 192.title: Defund Planned Parenthood & Cost Transparency.
nc:HB 192.summary: Directs the state Medicaid agency to disenroll Planned Parenthood Federation of America and associated entities as providers and engage others. Requires hospitals and surgical facilities to give written good-faith estimates for scheduled services on request, capping final bills at 5% above the estimate.

nc:HB 193.title: Firearm Law Revisions.
nc:HB 193.summary: Lets authorized nonpublic-school employees and volunteers with a concealed handgun permit and extra annual training carry firearms on campus; lets permit holders carry handguns at worship on shared school-church property; raises penalties for assaulting or threatening officials, adding local elected officers.

nc:HB 271.title: Cabarrus County Local Omnibus.
nc:HB 271.summary: Puts questions on the November 2025 ballot asking voters in Concord, Harrisburg, Midland and Mount Pleasant whether to change municipal elections from nonpartisan to partisan. Also changes how vacancies on the Cabarrus County commissioners' board are filled.

nc:HB 318.title: The Criminal Illegal Alien Enforcement Act.
nc:HB 318.summary: Expands the charges for which jails must try to determine legal status to any felony and impaired driving, adds a status inquiry at pretrial release, and changes how people with an ICE detainer and administrative warrant are held for transfer to ICE.

nc:HB 519.title: Parents' Medical Bill of Rights.
nc:HB 519.summary: Gives parents access to a minor child's medical records, with exceptions. Limits minors' own consent to pregnancy care and, from age 16, treatment of reportable diseases with a prescription of 10 days or less. Extends emergency no-consent treatment rules to physician assistants and nurse practitioners.

nc:HB 674.title: The Firearms Liberty Act.
nc:HB 674.summary: Allows lifetime concealed handgun permits, lets some lapsed permit holders renew without retaking the safety course, lets people under domestic violence protective orders store or sell guns through licensed dealers, and allows schools to keep defensive devices in biometric safes.

nc:HB 690.title: The Citizens Support Act.
nc:HB 690.summary: Directs state agencies and local housing authorities to stop providing State-funded benefits to noncitizens without legal permission, where federal law allows, and directs UNC, community colleges and the unemployment agency to verify legal status for in-state tuition, aid and unemployment benefits.

nc:HB 694.title: Regional Water Study/Interbasin Transfer Subbasin/Total Maximum Daily Load.
nc:HB 694.summary: Directs a UNC study of water and wastewater regionalization; folds the Haw River, Deep River and Contentnea Creek subbasins into the Cape Fear and Neuse basins, ending interbasin transfer certificates between them; and extends a 2020 nutrient offset rule to all Neuse local governments.

nc:HB 768.title: Emerg. Comm. Code Exempts/Sanitary Board/401.
