nc:HB 768.summary: Directs the Building Code Council to exempt certain apartments, hotels and motels from in-building emergency responder radio coverage requirements; requires certain sanitary district board vacancies be filled from the same residency district; sets deadlines for state review of certain Clean Water Act 401 certification applications.

nc:HB 781.title: Unauthorized Public Camping & Sleeping.
nc:HB 781.summary: Bars cities and counties from allowing regular public camping or sleeping on public property, except on sites a governing board designates by majority vote for up to one year and the state health department certifies, with safety, sanitation and behavioral-health standards.

nc:HB 805.title: Prevent Sexual Exploitation/Women and Minors.
nc:HB 805.summary: Defines male and female by biological sex in state rules; requires consent and age verification for online explicit images; bars state funds for prisoner gender transition care; sets a 10-year malpractice window for adult transition care; sets school sleeping quarters, religious excusal, library book rules.

nc:HB 859.title: Local Govts/Guaranteed Income Programs.
nc:HB 859.summary: Bars counties and cities from adopting or enforcing guaranteed income programs, defined as unconditional cash payments to individuals, unless state law expressly authorizes them.

nc:HB 870.title: Sedimentation Act and Other Environmental Changes.
nc:HB 870.summary: Requires General Assembly approval before state environmental agencies sign agreements with the U.S. EPA, and directs the Department of Environmental Quality to seek revisions to its sedimentation-control agreements to streamline requirements and to ask EPA to consult it on proposed federal rules.

nc:HB 913.title: Liability/Unfair/Deceptive Development Actions.
nc:HB 913.summary: Lets courts award attorneys' fees to people who win civil actions against local governments over development approvals, requires fees for intentional violations or delay, and requires punitive damages up to 10 times damages for flagrantly unfair or deceptive conduct meant to prompt a suit.

nc:HB 92.title: NC Digital Assets Investments Act.
nc:HB 92.summary: Allows the State Treasurer to invest up to 5% of certain state funds in digital assets after an independent assessment, and directs studies of retirement-plan investment in digital assets and a reserve for seized digital assets.

nc:HB 925.title: Consumers in Crisis Protection Act.
nc:HB 925.summary: Regulates companies that advance cash to consumers against expected lawsuit proceeds: requires registration with the Secretary of State, plain-language contracts and set disclosures, treats compliant deals as non-loans, and presumes the contracts are neither discoverable nor admissible in civil suits.

nc:HJR 379.title: Application for a Convention of the States.
nc:HJR 379.summary: Applies to Congress to call a convention of the states limited to proposing constitutional amendments on federal fiscal limits, limits on federal power and jurisdiction, and term limits for federal officials and members of Congress.

nc:SB 1080.title: Lower Taxes for All NC.
nc:SB 1080.summary: Puts a constitutional amendment on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot lowering the maximum state income tax rate from 7% to 3.5%, for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027.

nc:SB 227.title: Eliminating "Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)" in Public Education.
nc:SB 227.summary: Bars public school units from teaching or requiring affirmation of listed "divisive concepts" (such as one race or sex being inherently superior), from discriminatory practices, and from keeping diversity, equity and inclusion offices; requires annual compliance certification.

nc:SB 249.title: Realign Congressional Districts 2025.
nc:SB 249.summary: Changes the boundaries of North Carolina's congressional Districts 1 and 3, redrawing part of the state's U.S. House district map.

nc:SB 261.title: Energy Security and Affordability Act.
nc:SB 261.summary: Removes the 2030 target for electric utilities to cut carbon emissions 70% from 2005 levels, sets a Dec. 31, 2026 deadline for a plan toward 2050 carbon neutrality, and lets utilities recover baseload plant construction costs through base-rate increases outside general rate cases.

nc:SB 266.title: The Power Bill Reduction Act.
nc:SB 266.summary: Removes the interim carbon reduction target for electric utilities, allows alternative recovery of financing costs for baseload plants under construction, changes fuel-cost and performance-based ratemaking rules, and authorizes securitization of coal plant retirement costs.

nc:SB 370.title: Repeal Certificate of Need Laws.
nc:SB 370.summary: Repeals North Carolina's Certificate of Need law for health care facilities and services, effective January 1, 2026.

nc:SB 378.title: Align Medicaid Eligibility with Federal Law.
nc:SB 378.summary: Orders the Division of Health Benefits to disenroll Planned Parenthood and associated entities as Medicaid providers, end their Medicaid contracts, and engage other providers for services they provided.

nc:SB 449.title: Fiscal Responsibility and K-20 Technology Planning/Central Office Salary.
nc:SB 449.summary: Requires public schools, community colleges and UNC institutions to weigh long-term costs when buying technology, requires public schools to report device break/fix rates, and requires local school boards to publish total compensation and position data for central office employees.

nc:SB 472.title: Coastal Regulatory Reform.
nc:SB 472.summary: Sets timelines and procedures for state review of Clean Water Act 401 water quality certifications, creates permitting rules for upland basin marinas, and excludes certain man-made ditches from the Coastal Area Management Act.

nc:SB 493.title: Land Use Clarification and Changes.
nc:SB 493.summary: Requires commercial zoning to permit public school buildings by right or special use, phases out cities' extraterritorial planning jurisdiction by county population starting October 1, 2026, and clarifies that existing use rights survive approval of added uses.

nc:SB 50.title: Freedom to Carry NC.
nc:SB 50.summary: Lets U.S. citizens 18 or older who are not otherwise prohibited carry a concealed handgun without a permit, raises line-of-duty death payments to $150,000, and increases penalties for firearm assaults on law enforcement and other first responders.

nc:SB 558.title: Eliminating "Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)" in Public Higher Educ
nc:SB 558.summary: Bars UNC campuses and community colleges from endorsing or compelling belief in listed "divisive concepts," from discriminatory practices, and from keeping diversity, equity and inclusion offices; requires their governing boards to adopt policies implementing these rules.

nc:SB 599.title: Dental Board Reform.
nc:SB 599.summary: Changes the State Board of Dental Examiners from dentists elected by dentists to appointees of the Governor, legislative leaders and the Labor Commissioner, sets a 10-member board of six dentists, two hygienists and two public members, and limits service to two three-year terms.

nc:SB 655.title: Extend Certain Rights to Catawba Nation.
nc:SB 655.summary: Extends to the Catawba Indian Nation state laws now applying to the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, including full faith and credit for tribal court orders and tribal police authority on trust lands.

nc:SB 730.title: Ratepayer Protection Act.
nc:SB 730.summary: Sets rules for new data centers of 100 megawatts or more, including site assessments, closed-loop or liquid cooling with no evaporative cooling, electric contracts that shield other customers from costs, and a ban on local incentives; also delays a swine-waste energy requirement to 2029.

nc:SJR 763.title: Confirm Don van der Vaart/Utilities Commission.
nc:SJR 763.summary: Confirms Don van der Vaart as a member of the North Carolina Utilities Commission for a term from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2031.

nj:A 6309.title: Privacy Protection Act-concerns collection & sharing of certain personal info
nj:A 6309.summary: Bars state and local government entities and health care facilities from collecting immigration status, birthplace, SSN or ITIN unless needed for a service or benefit, limits disclosing it and license plate reader data, and requires consent, a warrant, or subpoena.

nj:S 170.title: School district spring break-requires Commissioner of Education recommend dates
nj:S 170.summary: Requires the Commissioner of Education to recommend dates each year on which school districts may close for spring break, and to inform districts of those dates by June 30 of the prior school year.

nj:S 4834.title: Motorized bicycles-regulate
nj:S 4834.summary: Creates an electric motorized bicycle category and redefines other bicycle classes, requires registration and licensing of electric motorized and low-speed electric bicycles, requires officers to report crashes to state agencies, and waives first-year fees for certain bicycles.

nm:SB 481.title: State Fairgrounds District Act
nm:SB 481.summary: Creates the State Fairgrounds District, a new governmental body with authority over planning, construction, redevelopment or demolition at the State Fairgrounds and nearby property, drawing on tax increment and redevelopment powers. Its board may buy adjacent private land.

nm:SB 83.title: Innovation in State Government Fund
nm:SB 83.summary: Creates an innovation in state government fund, run by the Department of Finance and Administration, to help agencies plan for net-zero emissions and climate policy. The passed version contains no appropriation.

nv:AB328.title: Creates certain commissions and subcommittees for the purpose of educating the general public concerning certain cultural affairs relating to African-Americans. (BDR 18-619)
nv:AB328.summary: Creates a Juneteenth Educational and Economic Commission, with its own fund, to educate the public about Juneteenth, and an interim legislative subcommittee to study historical discrimination against African-Americans in 2025-2026, including possible restitution to descendants of enslaved people.

nv:AB464.title: Revises provisions governing education. (BDR 34-235)
nv:AB464.summary: Bars state and local education bodies from repealing or blocking existing courses and standards on genocides and the history of ethnic groups, bars teachers from refusing to teach them, and bars adverse job actions against public employees over political, religious or social affiliation.

tn:HB 2574.title: DUI Offenses - As enacted, clarifies present law regarding the revocation of a person's driver license for an implied consent violation. - Amends TCA Section 55-10-407. HB2574 has been assigned Public Chapter Number 1046 by the Secretary of…
tn:HB 2574.summary: Sets the driver license suspension for refusing a chemical test at one year and six months for drivers with no prior DUI conviction, whether or not misdemeanor DUI is suspected. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

tn:SB 1900.title: Criminal Offenses - As enacted, increases the penalty for assaulting a first responder from a Class A misdemeanor with a mandatory fine of $5,000 and a mandatory minimum of 30 days incarceration to a Class E felony with a mandatory fine of…
tn:SB 1900.summary: Raises assault against a law enforcement officer or first responder from a Class A misdemeanor to a Class E felony, with a mandatory $10,000 fine and 60-day minimum sentence. Assault against a nurse stays a Class A misdemeanor with a $5,000 fine and 30-day minimum.

tx:HB 100.title: Relating to the purchase, adoption, and use of instructional materials by public schools
tx:HB 100.summary: Bars school districts from buying, adopting or using instructional materials on the State Board of Education's rejected list, and limits open education resources to materials not on that list. Applies beginning the 2025-26 school year.

tx:HB 1106.title: Relating to the definition of abuse or neglect of a child
tx:HB 1106.summary: Provides that a person responsible for a child's care does not commit abuse or neglect by refusing to affirm the child's perception of their gender, including refusing to use a preferred name or pronouns, or the child's expressed sexual orientation.

tx:HB 1107.title: Relating to applicability of civil service status to emergency medical services personnel in certain municipalities
tx:HB 1107.summary: Keeps civil service status for emergency medical services staff in cities of 460,000 or more that operated under a city manager form of government when adopting those rules, even if the city later changes its form of government.

tx:HB 111.title: Relating to the public information law
tx:HB 111.summary: Adds large nonprofit associations of local governments to the public information law, narrows the attorney-client exception to disclosure, and requires the attorney general to construe that exception narrowly.

tx:HB 1127.title: Relating to the promotion of breast-feeding and the prohibition against interference with or restriction of the right to breast-feed
tx:HB 1127.summary: Bars interference with a mother's right to breast-feed wherever she and her child are authorized to be, requires state agencies, where practicable, to adopt worksite breast-feeding policies, and lets a mother sue for injunctions, up to $500 daily damages and fees.

tx:HB 1128.title: Relating to the applicability to election judges of a prohibition on the carrying of a concealed handgun at a polling place
tx:HB 1128.summary: Exempts election judges, and early voting clerks serving as election judges, who hold handgun licenses from the ban on carrying a concealed handgun at polling places while performing their duties.

tx:HB 113.title: Relating to statutory construction
tx:HB 113.summary: Revises how courts read statutes: bars inquiry into legislators' intent, bars reliance on legislative history such as sponsor statements and committee reports, removes required deference to agency interpretations, and redefines "shall" and "must".

tx:HB 1147.title: Relating to the establishment by the Texas Workforce Commission of a workplace soft skills training pilot program
tx:HB 1147.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to run a pilot in Cameron County offering a six-week workplace soft skills course with a completion certificate, and to report on results by December 1, 2026. The program expires September 1, 2027.

tx:HB 1154.title: Relating to the establishment of a skilled labor task force by certain local workforce development boards
tx:HB 1154.summary: Requires local workforce boards in Gulf-bordering counties of 400,000 or more to create a 17-member skilled labor task force, which studies workforce training and skills gaps and recommends strategies to the Legislature and board.

nm:SB 535.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:SB 535.summary: As passed by the Senate, raises employer and employee workers' compensation administration contributions, and raises the telecommunications relay service surcharge from 0.33 to 1.66 percent, sending 80 percent of that surcharge revenue to a new fund for the 988 crisis line.

nv:AB499.title: Revises provisions relating to elections. (BDR 24-998)
nv:AB499.summary: Requires county clerks to run an online voter services portal and put a QR code for it on mail-ballot return envelopes. Skips signature checks when identifying numbers a voter writes on the envelope are confirmed accurate, and lets voters confirm signatures by email or text.

tn:SB 2403.title: Education - As enacted, makes various revisions to education law, including, but not limited to, requiring each public school to annually submit to the department of education a list of all local assessments administered to students,…
tn:SB 2403.summary: As amended by the House, requires public schools to report local assessments yearly, with the state posting them online, creates a nine-teacher TCAP review board, and requires each public school to offer a daily prayer period, with participation only after a signed consent form.

tx:HB 1056.title: Relating to the issuance of gold and silver specie and the establishment of a currency based on gold and silver; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 1056.summary: As passed by the Senate, recognizes gold and silver specie marked with its weight and purity as legal tender in Texas to the extent the U.S. Constitution allows, and lets the comptroller authorize electronic payment systems backed by bullion in the state depository. No one may be required to accept them.

tx:HB 1201.title: Relating to a pilot program to provide Medicaid coverage of doula services
tx:HB 1201.summary: Directs the Health and Human Services Commission to run a Medicaid pilot program, in two counties by September 1, 2026, that reimburses doula services. Rules set doula qualifications and covered services; the commission sets eligibility.

tx:HB 1203.title: Relating to the establishment of the office of food system security and resiliency in the Department of Agriculture and the management of the Texas food system security and resiliency planning council
tx:HB 1203.summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to create, by December 31, 2025, an office of food system security and resiliency to coordinate state food programs, plan regional food systems and promote local food markets, and to manage the state's food system planning council.

tx:HB 1249.title: Relating to authorizing the use of a writing portfolio assessment to assess writing performance for public school students
tx:HB 1249.summary: Lets a school district use a writing portfolio assessment instead of the non-multiple-choice portion of the grades 3-8 reading tests and English I and II end-of-course tests. Districts design it with a college or university and submit it to the Texas Education Agency for approval.

tx:HB 1276.title: Relating to a study of this state's response to plant disease or pest outbreaks
tx:HB 1276.summary: Requires Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service to study how the state identifies and responds to plant disease and pest outbreaks and report recommendations to state leaders by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 128.title: Relating to certain sister-city agreements between governmental entities and foreign countries and communities
tx:HB 128.summary: Bars Texas state agencies and local governments from sister-city agreements with China, Iran, North Korea, Russia or other designated countries, or their communities, and requires withdrawal from existing ones by October 1, 2025. Declares policy to encourage such agreements with U.S. allies, including Taiwan.

tx:HB 1295.title: Relating to a health literacy plan developed by the statewide health coordinating council and the inclusion of health literacy in the state health plan
tx:HB 1295.summary: Requires the statewide health coordinating council to develop and update, at least every two years, a long-range plan for improving health literacy, including a study of the economic impact of low health literacy and strategies such as plain-language patient instructions.

tx:HB 1359.title: Relating to a program to provide assistance for certain retail electric customers; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 1359.summary: Creates an income-based assistance fund and directs the Public Utility Commission to run bill-payment assistance for low-income electric customers in counties affected by an extreme weather emergency, plus one-time help for critical care residential customers facing disconnection.

tx:HB 1368.title: Relating to a notification requirement if a public school does not have a nurse, school counselor, or librarian assigned to the school during all instructional hours
tx:HB 1368.summary: Requires a public school with no full-time nurse, counselor or librarian for over 30 consecutive instructional days to notify parents in writing, bilingual where needed. Exempts districts and charter schools with fewer than 10,000 students.

tx:HB 1411.title: Relating to the use of personal leave during school holidays by certain school district employees
tx:HB 1411.summary: Lets school district employees who are not overtime-exempt and whose pay is not annualized use up to two paid personal leave days a year to be paid on school holidays when they would otherwise not be paid, starting with the 2025-26 school year.

tx:HB 1437.title: Relating to the task force on pollinator health
tx:HB 1437.summary: Requires the governor to create a task force on pollinator health to examine ways to add pollinator habitat, study other states' outreach and data-gathering, and identify ways to prevent habitat loss.

tx:HB 146.title: Relating to the required approval by the State Preservation Board of certain traffic changes near the state capitol
tx:HB 146.summary: Requires approval by four State Preservation Board members before a city can permanently reduce lanes, or close a lane for over 14 consecutive days, on Congress Avenue between the Congress Avenue bridge and 11th Street in Austin. Exempts special events and construction.

tx:HB 1499.title: Relating to the creation of an environmental product declaration grant program for manufacturers of ready-mixed concrete
tx:HB 1499.summary: Creates a Texas Commission on Environmental Quality grant program reimbursing small ready-mixed concrete makers, with under 100 employees or under $6 million in receipts, for environmental product declaration software, if they agree to use the declarations.

tx:HB 15.title: Relating to certain files maintained by a law enforcement agency regarding certain employees of the agency
tx:HB 15.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to keep a confidential file on each officer, holding records outside the personnel file, including misconduct allegations lacking sufficient evidence. Allows review by hiring agencies, the state licensing commission, and complainants and alleged victims; bars other release.

tx:HB 1573.title: Relating to a school district policy regarding custodian workloads
tx:HB 1573.summary: As reported by the House committee, requires each school district board to adopt and post a policy setting benchmarks for square feet a properly equipped custodian may be assigned per eight-hour shift, by school level, beginning in 2025-26.

tx:HB 158.title: Relating to a study on the use of surplus government property to provide housing to veterans and low-income families
tx:HB 158.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs to study the feasibility of using unused or underused federal, state and local property to house veterans, identify possible funding sources, and report by November 1, 2026.

tx:HB 1581.title: Relating to public school bilingual education programs, dual language immersion programs, and special language programs
tx:HB 1581.summary: Requires the education commissioner to develop training for school administrators on bilingual and dual language programs, and requires the Texas Education Agency to adopt rules for monitoring those programs, identifying deficient districts and providing technical assistance.

tx:HB 1646.title: Relating to the amount of an expenditure that may be paid by an emergency services district employee without board approval
tx:HB 1646.summary: Raises from $2,000 to $50,000 the amount an emergency services district employee may spend without board approval.

tx:HB 1661.title: Relating to election supplies and the conduct of elections; creating criminal offenses; increasing criminal penalties
tx:HB 1661.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor to intentionally under-supply ballots to a precinct or not resupply on request. Raises penalties to Class A misdemeanors for failing to deliver or obstructing election supplies, and to a state jail felony for revealing election data early.

tx:HB 1738.title: Relating to the repeal of the offense of homosexual conduct
tx:HB 1738.summary: Repeals Penal Code Section 21.06, an offense the statute calls "homosexual conduct," and removes references to that offense from two Health and Safety Code sections on HIV and sex education course materials.

tx:HB 175.title: Relating to establishing optional certifications for child-care providers participating in the Texas Rising Star Program and reimbursement rates for those providers
tx:HB 175.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to create optional certifications, including one for inclusion of children with disabilities, that raise a child-care provider's Texas Rising Star rating, and to run a grant program giving certified providers extra funding.

tx:HB 1781.title: Relating to the Texas Livestock and Rodeo Education and Continuation Grant Program
tx:HB 1781.summary: Creates a grant program to give money from a livestock and rodeo education fund to county fairs and local rodeos for facilities, event programs, salaries and public health and safety.

tx:HB 1784.title: Relating to measures to assist students enrolled at public institutions of higher education who are homeless or who are or were in foster care
tx:HB 1784.summary: Requires colleges and universities to designate a liaison for homeless students, and the Higher Education Coordinating Board to name one by January 1, 2026, extending existing support for students who were in foster care.

tx:HB 1788.title: Relating to continuing education for barbers and cosmetologists on identifying and assisting victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, and human trafficking
tx:HB 1788.summary: Requires barbers and cosmetologists to complete continuing education on identifying and assisting victims of sexual assault, domestic violence and human trafficking, under rules set by the licensing commission.

tx:HB 1794.title: Relating to the carrying of concealed handguns by handgun license holders on the premises of a polling place on the day of an election or while early voting is in progress
tx:HB 1794.summary: Allows licensed handgun holders to carry a concealed handgun into a polling place on election day or during early voting, unless state law bars handguns at that location.

tx:HB 1822.title: Relating to the jurisdiction of a juvenile court over certain persons and to the sealing and nondisclosure of certain juvenile records
tx:HB 1822.summary: Lets a juvenile court keep jurisdiction, regardless of age, over an incomplete proceeding delayed through no fault of the state, and lets courts seal records of people discharged from determinate-sentence probation who were not committed to the juvenile justice department or transferred.

tx:HB 1842.title: Relating to the sale of charitable raffle tickets by certain nonprofit wildlife conservation associations
tx:HB 1842.summary: Allows nonprofit wildlife conservation associations to sell charitable raffle tickets on their websites to previously identified supporters, without online animation of entries or drawings.

tx:HB 1846.title: Relating to the establishment of the Electric Truck Advisory Council
tx:HB 1846.summary: Creates an Electric Truck Advisory Council attached to the Department of Transportation to develop a statewide strategic plan for electric truck charging stations and advise on policies and incentives for electric trucks.

tx:HB 1955.title: Relating to the establishment of an early childhood mental health home visiting grant program
tx:HB 1955.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to run a grant program funding early childhood mental health home visiting services for high-need families, with preference for applicants experienced in home-based services.

tx:HB 2003.title: Relating to provision to the Texas Department of Transportation of information regarding certain high-speed rail projects
tx:HB 2003.summary: Requires entities proposing high-speed passenger rail (110 mph or more) to give the Department of Transportation yearly information on financing, finances, costs, schedule, ridership, route and foreign investment while the project is in the Texas Rail Plan; the department posts it online.

tx:HB 205.title: Relating to the eligibility for grants for alternative fueling facilities
tx:HB 205.summary: Exempts alternative fueling facilities run by certain transit authorities in counties over one million, in emission nonattainment areas, from the rule that grants go first to facilities agreeing to be open to the public.

tx:HB 2060.title: Relating to a study on the coverage of certain infants under Medicaid
tx:HB 2060.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to study its compliance with federal rules on Medicaid coverage for infants born to Medicaid-enrolled mothers, including separate applications and residency requirements.

tx:HB 2142.title: Relating to a study by the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs on the feasibility of using certain models to address homelessness in this state
tx:HB 2142.summary: As reported by the House committee, requires the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs to study a homelessness model using small dwelling units and partnerships with colleges, private entities and local governments, and report by December 31, 2026.

tx:HB 2145.title: Relating to the installation of electric vehicle charging stations at certain state-owned parking lots and garages
tx:HB 2145.summary: Allows the Texas Facilities Commission to authorize electric vehicle charging stations in state-owned parking lots and garages built on or after September 1, 2025, considering EV registrations, state employee EVs and lot usage, under guidelines requiring installation at no cost to the state.

tx:HB 2186.title: Relating to the regulation of elevator mechanics, elevator apprentices, and contractors; requiring an occupational registration
tx:HB 2186.summary: Requires registration with the state licensing department of elevator mechanics and apprentices, with mechanics showing completion of an approved training program or five years of experience.

tx:HB 222.title: Relating to the permissible uses of the school safety allotment under the Foundation School Program
tx:HB 222.summary: Adds training for educators in classroom behavioral management as an allowed use of school safety allotment funds.

tx:HB 223.title: Relating to exemptions to competitive requirements for purchases of certain services by a municipality
tx:HB 223.summary: Ends the exemption from city competitive bidding or proposal requirements for purchases of lobbying, government relations or similar services intended to influence state or federal lawmakers.

tx:HB 2234.title: Relating to the age of criminal responsibility and to certain substantive and procedural matters related to that age
tx:HB 2234.summary: Raises the age of criminal responsibility from 17 to 18 and moves 17-year-olds to the juvenile system. Applies to offenses on or after September 1, 2027.

tx:HB 2242.title: Relating to policy-making authority of constables for the purpose of a federal civil rights action
tx:HB 2242.summary: Makes a constable the final policymaker on law enforcement decisions for the county in federal civil rights lawsuits.

tx:HB 2243.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas Commission on Teacher Job Satisfaction and Retention
tx:HB 2243.summary: Creates a 13-member Texas Commission on Teacher Job Satisfaction and Retention, appointed by the governor, lieutenant governor and House speaker, to recommend ways to improve teacher job satisfaction and retention.

tx:HB 2249.title: Relating to the establishment of the Texas Teacher Recruitment Scholarship Program and the Texas Teacher Retention Incentive Program
tx:HB 2249.summary: Creates a conditional scholarship of up to $40,000 over four years for students in teacher-preparation bachelor's programs, who must work as educators in Texas public schools for five years or repay it.

tx:HB 2271.title: Relating to collecting and sharing capacity and enrollment information for certain day-care centers
tx:HB 2271.summary: Requires day-care centers and homes to report capacity and enrollment, by age group, to the Texas Workforce Commission monthly, and requires the commission to post it on its child care availability portal.

tx:HB 2282.title: Relating to the amount of the reimbursement fee paid by a defendant for a peace officer's services in executing or processing an arrest warrant, capias, or capias pro fine
tx:HB 2282.summary: Raises from $50 to $75 the fee a convicted defendant pays for a peace officer's work executing or processing an arrest warrant or capias, for offenses committed after the effective date.

tx:HB 2289.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to receive certain tax revenue derived from a hotel and convention center project and to pledge certain tax revenue for the payment of obligations related to the project
tx:HB 2289.summary: Adds a municipality through which the Comal River flows to those eligible to receive hotel and convention center project tax revenue and pledge it for related obligations.

tx:HB 2298.title: Relating to a health care facility grant program supporting the use of artificial intelligence technology in scanning medical images for cancer detection
tx:HB 2298.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to create a grant program helping hospitals and health facilities use artificial intelligence to scan medical images for cancer, with applicants providing at least 10 percent matching funds.

tx:HB 1240.title: Relating to certain governmental operations affecting the border region
tx:HB 1240.summary: Revises the county list defining the Texas-Mexico border region in the state strategic-planning law and applies that one list in education, health, transportation, water and other state laws that now define it differently. Takes effect September 1, 2026.

tx:HB 2200.title: Relating to the cremation of human remains by natural organic reduction
tx:HB 2200.summary: As amended, directs the Texas Funeral Service Commission to authorize natural organic reduction of human remains by rule, including rules on the process, facilities and vessels, and to adopt them by December 31, 2025.

tx:HB 2300.title: Relating to the distribution of hookahs; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 2300.summary: Creates a Class C misdemeanor for selling or providing a hookah to a person younger than 21, or to someone who will pass it to such a person, and makes retailer employees liable for sales they make.

tx:HB 2308.title: Relating to the establishment of the Texas Commission on Border Security and Illegal Immigration
tx:HB 2308.summary: Creates an 11-member advisory commission of state officials and legislators to review immigration issues, develop a list of border security infrastructure projects and a state plan, and advise the governor and legislature on border security legislation.

tx:HB 2341.title: Relating to the award of diligent participation credit to defendants confined in a state jail felony facility
tx:HB 2341.summary: Requires, rather than allows, diligent participation credit for time served in a state jail felony facility by people in education, vocational, treatment or work programs, and repeals the judge's finding on presumptive entitlement. Applies to offenses committed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:HB 2347.title: Relating to the adoption of a water conservation program by certain counties
tx:HB 2347.summary: Allows the commissioners court of certain Hill Country counties to adopt water conservation standards for new development in unincorporated areas, excluding agricultural operations. City rules prevail in conflicts, and the authority expires September 1, 2031.

tx:HB 2440.title: Relating to the authority of a state agency or the state's air quality state implementation plan to impose certain restrictions with respect to a motor vehicle, including a motor vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine
tx:HB 2440.summary: Bars state agencies from restricting the sale or use of motor vehicles based on their energy source or from prohibiting ownership of engine-powered vehicles, and bars the state air quality implementation plan from restricting vehicle purchases.

tx:HB 2442.title: Relating to an application for an early voting ballot by mail
tx:HB 2442.summary: Makes an application for an early voting ballot by mail count as an application for any resulting runoff election too, unless the applicant asks not to receive a runoff ballot.

tx:HB 2581.title: Relating to the information required for payment of services provided through the Thriving Texas Families Program
tx:HB 2581.summary: Requires providers seeking payment under the Thriving Texas Families Program to submit a state-prescribed form listing anonymized client IDs, interaction dates and locations, staff names, and itemized services, materials and referrals provided.

tx:HB 2669.title: Relating to the establishment of a reporting and education program for the dangers of balloons to livestock
tx:HB 2669.summary: Requires Texas A&M AgriLife Extension to set up a system for ranchers to report balloons on their land and livestock deaths from eating balloons, run an outreach program, and send an annual report to the legislature.

tx:HB 2701.title: Relating to construction standards for certain recreational vehicle parks and campgrounds
tx:HB 2701.summary: Requires recreational vehicle parks and campgrounds to meet National Fire Protection Association standards and bars governments from imposing stricter standards on sanitation, electrical, propane or fire safety. Existing parks must comply by September 1, 2026.

tx:HB 2731.title: Relating to the regulation of roadside vendors and solicitors in certain counties
tx:HB 2731.summary: Lets commissioners courts in counties over 500,000 people, and border counties over 200,000, regulate roadside vendors and solicitors in unincorporated areas, and removes the 40 mph road limit on that authority for border counties.

tx:HB 2783.title: Relating to automatic participation by certain county employees in deferred compensation plans provided by certain counties
tx:HB 2783.summary: Lets a county elect to enroll employees automatically in its deferred compensation plan at a 3 percent payroll contribution to a default investment, with employees free to opt out, change the amount or investment, or choose Roth contributions.

tx:HB 2786.title: Relating to the frequency with which an appraisal district is required to reappraise property for ad valorem tax purposes
tx:HB 2786.summary: Requires appraisal district plans in counties with 75,000 or more people to provide for reappraising all real and personal property every year, effective January 1, 2026.

tx:HB 2851.title: Relating to including nursing school applications in a consolidated application service
tx:HB 2851.summary: Requires consolidated application services for medical and dental schools, including the Texas Health Education Service at the UT System, to also include nursing school applications, beginning with fall 2027 admission, and sets up an advisory board to plan it.

tx:HB 2853.title: Relating to student union building fees at The University of Texas at El Paso
tx:HB 2853.summary: Raises the cap on the UT El Paso student union building fee from $30 to $150 per semester, with lower temporary caps through 2027; allows it to fund demolishing the existing building; bars increases of 10 percent or more without a student vote.

tx:HB 2858.title: Relating to the establishment of a temporary guest worker program in this state
tx:HB 2858.summary: Directs the governor to seek federal authorization and then allows a memorandum of understanding with a Mexican state for a temporary guest worker program, supplying legal workers on U.S. nonimmigrant visas to Texas businesses in high-need jobs.

tx:HB 3032.title: Relating to a study by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board in coordination with other state agencies on the feasibility of developing clinical sites for nursing students
tx:HB 3032.summary: Requires the Higher Education Coordinating Board and other agencies to study setting up clinical sites for nursing students at correctional and juvenile facilities, hospitals and health centers, and report by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 3045.title: Relating to a franchise tax exemption for corporations operating a spaceport for certain national defense purposes
tx:HB 3045.summary: Exempts from the franchise tax a corporation that operates an FAA-authorized spaceport and has a contract with the U.S. Department of Defense for spaceflight or launch services.

tx:HB 3053.title: Relating to municipal and county firearm buyback programs
tx:HB 3053.summary: Bars cities and counties from running or taking part in programs that buy firearms to remove them from circulation, reduce civilian ownership, or let people sell firearms without fear of prosecution.

tx:HB 3063.title: Relating to the civil prosecution of offenses involving certain municipal parking ordinances; authorizing a civil fine
tx:HB 3063.summary: Allows a city of 1.9 million or more people to make parking a vehicle in the front or side yard of a single-family home a civil offense, with fines imposed through an administrative hearing process.

tx:HB 3169.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to receive certain tax revenue derived from a hotel and convention center project and to pledge certain tax revenue for the payment of obligations related to the project
tx:HB 3169.summary: Adds a city of 130,000 to 1.3 million people located in three counties, each over 900,000 people, to the cities that may receive certain hotel and convention center project tax revenue and pledge it to pay project obligations.

tx:HB 3174.title: Relating to county and hospital district disease control pilot programs to reduce the risk of certain infectious and communicable diseases; authorizing fees
tx:HB 3174.summary: Allows Bexar, Dallas, El Paso, Harris, Nueces, Travis and Webb counties and their hospital districts to run disease control pilot programs, including anonymous exchange of used needles and syringes for new ones, disease education, and referrals to testing and treatment.

tx:HB 3178.title: Relating to the authority of certain counties to impose a hotel occupancy tax
tx:HB 3178.summary: Allows the commissioners court of the county where the Guadalupe River headwaters are located to impose a county hotel occupancy tax, which does not apply to hotels already taxed by a city.

tx:HB 321.title: Relating to implementing an express lane option under Medicaid and the child health plan program
tx:HB 321.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to use SNAP application data to determine children's eligibility for Medicaid and CHIP, enrolling a child once a parent or guardian is notified and gives consent.

tx:HB 3237.title: Relating to certain energy consumption goals for institutions of higher education and certain governmental entities
tx:HB 3237.summary: Extends the requirement that certain local governments, universities and state agencies set a goal of cutting electricity use at least 5 percent a year, from seven years starting in 2019 to six years starting September 1, 2025.

tx:HB 3241.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to receive certain tax revenue derived from a hotel and convention center project and to pledge certain tax revenue for the payment of obligations related to the project
tx:HB 3241.summary: Adds the county seat of a county with 600,000 or more people that is next to the county containing the State Capitol to the cities that may receive certain hotel and convention center project tax revenue.

tx:HB 3261.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain criminal defendants for an order of nondisclosure of criminal history record information
tx:HB 3261.summary: Lets people convicted of an offense committed before age 25 petition for nondisclosure of their criminal history two years (misdemeanor) or five years (felony) after finishing their sentence, excluding offenses barring community supervision and felonies with deadly-weapon findings.

tx:HB 3326.title: Relating to certain duties of a public institution of higher education in relation to the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program
tx:HB 3326.summary: Requires public colleges, for Public Service Loan Forgiveness certification only, to count adjunct faculty as working 3.35 hours per credit hour taught and as full-time at 30 average weekly hours, and to certify within 60 days.

tx:HB 3335.title: Relating to the authority of a county to dispose of surplus and salvage property to a civic or charitable organization
tx:HB 3335.summary: Changes the conditions for a county to donate surplus or salvage property to a civic or charitable group, dropping the finding that a sale would draw no bids and requiring that the county keep control to serve the public purpose.

tx:HB 3339.title: Relating to a study on maternal mortality and morbidity among Black women in this state
tx:HB 3339.summary: Requires the Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee and the Department of State Health Services to study maternal mortality and illness among Black women, compare rates with other races and ethnicities, and recommend steps to address disparities.

tx:HB 3441.title: Relating to the liability of vaccine manufacturers for advertising a harmful vaccine
tx:HB 3441.summary: Makes a vaccine manufacturer liable for actual damages, costs and attorney's fees if a vaccine it advertises in Texas harms someone, with suits allowed within three years.

tx:HB 3475.title: Relating to the establishment of a public law school in El Paso County
tx:HB 3475.summary: Allows a university system's governing board to establish a law school in El Paso County, subject to available funding, a Coordinating Board feasibility study on accreditation, and notice requirements.

tx:HB 349.title: Relating to civil liability for removing certain individuals or animals from a motor vehicle
tx:HB 349.summary: Gives a person civil immunity for entering a locked vehicle to remove a domestic animal if they reasonably believe imminent harm exists, notify police or 911 first, use minimal force, and stay until responders arrive.

tx:HB 3520.title: Relating to automobile liability insurance requirements for transportation network company drivers
tx:HB 3520.summary: Limits the higher insurance requirements for rideshare drivers on a prearranged ride to times when a rider is in the vehicle, for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.

tx:HB 3554.title: Relating to establishment of the Texas Rare Disease Advisory Council
tx:HB 3554.summary: Creates a 23-member Texas Rare Disease Advisory Council to advise the governor, state agencies and health care providers on improving outcomes for people with diseases affecting fewer than 200,000 people in the U.S.

tx:HB 3567.title: Relating to authorizing certain counties to impose a hotel occupancy tax and the use of revenue from that tax
tx:HB 3567.summary: Allows a county of over 125,000 people that borders the Red River and has a county seat over 100,000 to impose a hotel occupancy tax of up to 2 percent, expiring September 1, 2030.

tx:HB 3672.title: Relating to the creation of an extracurricular community education grant program
tx:HB 3672.summary: Requires the education commissioner to create a grant program for organizations providing after-school and summer community education programs for students, covering areas such as art, music, literacy, science, health and recreation.

tx:HB 3715.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to use certain tax revenue for hotel and convention center projects
tx:HB 3715.summary: Adds the largest city in a border county of at least 500,000 people, with no city of 500,000 or more, to the cities that may receive certain hotel and convention center project tax revenue.

tx:HB 3720.title: Relating to the construction of bridges in Harris County
tx:HB 3720.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Transportation to plan, design and build railroad grade-separation bridges in Harris County at Little York Road and Tidwell Road where they meet Hirsch Road.

tx:HB 3722.title: Relating to the protection of certain airspace designated for use by Department of Defense contractors
tx:HB 3722.summary: Bars constructing structures taller than 500 feet within five miles of an FAA-designated aerobatic training area used by a Defense Department aviation contractor, if designated by January 1, 2025.

tx:HB 3743.title: Relating to management-to-staff ratio for state agencies
tx:HB 3743.summary: Applies the limit of one management employee per 11 staff to all state agencies regardless of size, requires agencies to minimize management positions, and repeals the separate procedures requirement.

tx:HB 3826.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas Energy Efficiency Council
tx:HB 3826.summary: Creates the nine-member Texas Energy Efficiency Council within the Public Utility Commission to recommend statewide energy efficiency coordination, performance reporting, program monitoring, and use of federal funding.

tx:HB 2313.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to use certain tax revenue for certain qualified projects
tx:HB 2313.summary: Lets certain cities designate a hotel-tax project financing zone as a continuous area with exact boundaries, no larger than the three-mile-radius maximum, if designated by December 31, 2024, and adds one city over 250,000 people to those eligible for the project revenue.

tx:HB 2446.title: Relating to affidavits concerning cost and necessity of services in civil actions
tx:HB 2446.summary: Makes an affidavit supporting a medical bill or itemized statement of $50,000 or less sufficient evidence that the charge was reasonable or the service necessary, without supporting expert testimony.

tx:HB 247.title: Relating to the taxation of border security infrastructure
tx:HB 247.summary: Exempts from property tax, if voters approve a constitutional amendment, the added appraised value from border security infrastructure, such as walls or fences, built under an agreement or easement with the state or United States on property in counties bordering Mexico.

tx:HB 2715.title: Relating to the suspension and removal from office of certain elected officials of this state or a political subdivision of this state
tx:HB 2715.summary: Extends to all officers covered by the county removal-petition subchapter the process now used for prosecuting attorneys: the petition goes to the regional presiding judge, who assigns a district judge from outside the county and appoints a prosecutor from another district or county.

tx:HB 30.title: Relating to the repeal of provisions authorizing certain taxing units in the year following the year in which a disaster occurs to adopt an ad valorem tax rate that exceeds the voter-approval tax rate without holding an election to approve the adopted tax rate; making conforming changes
tx:HB 30.summary: Repeals the authority of non-school taxing units to exceed voter-approval tax rates without an election after a governor-declared disaster, and adds a disaster relief rate, covering debris removal and essential assistance costs, to the voter-approval rate formula for units in disaster areas.

tx:HB 3006.title: Relating to the purchase and installation of climate control systems at facilities operated by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice
tx:HB 3006.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, if the legislature provides funds, to contract for climate control at facilities lacking systems that hold 65 to 85 degrees, in three phases ending in 2028, 2030 and 2032, each capped at $100 million.

tx:HB 3142.title: Relating to school marshals, including eligibility for appointment as a school marshal, and licensure and training requirements
tx:HB 3142.summary: Allows school districts, charter schools, private schools and public junior colleges to appoint volunteers, not only employees, as school marshals: honorably discharged veterans, active-duty military, peace officers, reserve officers or retired peace officers certified through the state marshal training program.

tx:HB 3179.title: Relating to the authority of certain counties to impose a hotel occupancy tax
tx:HB 3179.summary: Allows commissioners courts of a county under 145,000 people containing part of Lake Ray Hubbard, and of the county where the Llano and James Rivers meet, to impose a county hotel occupancy tax. The Llano-James tax excludes hotels already taxed by a city.

tx:HB 3332.title: Relating to the creation of the Maverick County Regional Mobility Authority; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 3332.summary: Creates, if voters approve a constitutional amendment, the Maverick County Regional Mobility Authority without Transportation Commission approval, governed by three directors appointed by the Maverick County commissioners court, with other counties able to join.

tx:HB 3511.title: Relating to the interconnection of electric vehicles to the ERCOT power grid
tx:HB 3511.summary: Allows the Public Utility Commission to set standards for connecting electric vehicles in the ERCOT region and to let owners sell stored electricity in wholesale markets through a registered aggregator or load serving entity.

tx:HB 386.title: Relating to change order limits for certain construction contracts
tx:HB 386.summary: Raises from $1 million to $5 million the contract size above which change orders are capped at a 25 percent increase, caps smaller contracts at the greater of 50 percent or $1 million, and raises the official approval limit from $50,000 to $250,000.

tx:HB 3883.title: Relating to the eligibility of a Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) World Endurance Championship international automobile race for funding under the major events reimbursement program
tx:HB 3883.summary: Makes an FIA World Endurance Championship automobile race eligible for funding under the state's major events reimbursement program.

tx:HB 3892.title: Relating to county regulation of subdivision setbacks
tx:HB 3892.summary: Specifies that the existing bar on county limits on homes per acre in unincorporated areas covers minimum lot size, width, depth and setbacks, except certain Gulf-coast flood zones, and bars minimum road-frontage rules for roads platted after September 1, 2025.

tx:HB 3947.title: Relating to transportation planning by metropolitan planning organizations
tx:HB 3947.summary: Requires metropolitan planning organizations to consider the transportation needs of people who receive services from the Health and Human Services Commission or Workforce Commission in 10-year plans, and to show providers considered meeting those needs when requesting state funding.

tx:HB 3954.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to receive certain tax revenue derived from a hotel and convention center project and to pledge certain tax revenue for the payment of obligations related to the project
tx:HB 3954.summary: Adds a municipality of 10,000 to 75,000 residents, located in two counties including the State Capitol's county and hosting an annual German festival, to those entitled to certain hotel and convention center project tax revenue and allowed to pledge it.

tx:HB 3966.title: Relating to requiring owners or operators of commercial passenger bus services to provide certain notifications to residents concerning operations
tx:HB 3966.summary: Requires operators of scheduled intercity bus services using buses with 35 or more seats to publish newspaper notice, with a second-language notice in some cases, at least 90 days before opening a new Texas terminal, except in unforeseen emergencies.

tx:HB 3977.title: Relating to conditions of employment for firefighters employed by certain political subdivisions
tx:HB 3977.summary: Lets a majority of firefighters in certain local governments petition for an association's recognition as bargaining agent, subject to a governing-body vote; allows ratified written agreements on pay and conditions; bars firefighter strikes, with forfeiture of civil service and reemployment rights.

tx:HB 40.title: Relating to the Business Court
tx:HB 40.summary: Changes Business Court jurisdiction and procedure: lowers a $10 million amount-in-controversy threshold to $5 million, adds intellectual-property and trade-secret actions, removes the scheduled abolition of six divisions, and sends certain venue appeals to the Fifteenth Court of Appeals.

tx:HB 4070.title: Relating to the sale, design, and manufacture of orthodontic devices
tx:HB 4070.summary: Bars selling an orthodontic device, or related design or manufacture services, to a Texas patient without an in-person dental exam, diagnostic imaging review, a dentist's prescription, and counseling on treatment options and risks.

tx:HB 4076.title: Relating to prohibiting organ transplant recipient discrimination on the basis of vaccination status
tx:HB 4076.summary: Bars health care providers from denying organ transplant eligibility, services, referral or waiting-list priority based solely on vaccination status, unless a physician finds after individualized evaluation that it is medically significant to the transplant.

tx:HB 4166.title: Relating to an exemption for certain property owners from regulatory requirements for residential mortgage loan originators
tx:HB 4166.summary: Exempts an owner of residential real estate who makes a first-lien mortgage loan to the buyer from state mortgage lender licensing laws, if a sponsored licensed originator handles all origination activity.

tx:HB 4172.title: Relating to regulating charitable bingo and authorizing the establishment of a nonprofit corporation to advertise and promote charitable bingo
tx:HB 4172.summary: Lets bingo distributors accept returned defective, unordered or excess equipment; lets a qualifying statewide bingo association form a nonprofit for advertising; raises the operating-capital cap from $50,000 to $100,000 and the cash-prize fee threshold from $5 to $100.

tx:HB 4211.title: Relating to certain residential property interests controlled by certain entities
tx:HB 4211.summary: Sets rules for residential arrangements sold as interests in a managing entity: requires disclosure that buyers aren't buying real property, bars mandatory non-court dispute forums, transfer restrictions and resale fees, applies fair housing rules, and makes violations deceptive trade practices.

tx:HB 4279.title: Relating to the urban scholarship; enforcement and authorizing penalties
tx:HB 4279.summary: Requires local exchange companies to deliver reported unclaimed money to the urban scholarship fund instead of the comptroller, with the unclaimed-property penalty of 10 percent of value per day for late delivery.

tx:HB 4309.title: Relating to the filing fee for nomination by convention
tx:HB 4309.summary: Changes where candidates nominated by convention pay filing fees, from the secretary of state or county judge to the party's state or county chair, and repeals the requirement to deposit those fees in state or county funds.

tx:HB 4359.title: Relating to the review of school districts by the Sunset Advisory Commission
tx:HB 4359.summary: Requires the Sunset Advisory Commission to review and forensically audit two school districts each cycle, the lowest and highest instructional spenders per student in a chosen education service center region, and recommend changes.

tx:HB 4398.title: Relating to municipal permitting requirements for certain development projects supported with low income housing tax credit allocations
tx:HB 4398.summary: Requires cities over 100,000 residents to grant or deny building permits for low-income-housing-tax-credit projects in no more than half the time allotted for other residential permits, and to allow use of any accelerated review process.

tx:HB 4421.title: Relating to available resources of certain state agencies to support and sustain peer-recovery organizations in this state
tx:HB 4421.summary: Requires seven state agencies to identify funding, training or technical assistance available to peer-recovery organizations, and to report to the legislature by August 1 of each even-numbered year.

tx:HB 4443.title: Relating to the establishment by the Texas Workforce Commission of a pilot program to train workers for careers in energy-efficient technologies
tx:HB 4443.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to run a Dallas-Fort Worth pilot with junior colleges, technical institutes and employers to train students for energy-efficient technology jobs, including dual-credit courses and a certificate of completion.

tx:HB 4505.title: Relating to the establishment of the workforce housing capital investment fund program to fund the development of workforce housing in this state; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 4505.summary: Creates a workforce housing capital investment fund; the housing department contracts with a nonprofit to make zero-interest loans for building single-family homes, mainly for households earning 30 to 80 percent of area median income.

tx:HB 463.title: Relating to the automatic expunction of arrest records and files after certain controlled substance offense charges are dismissed
tx:HB 463.summary: Lets a drug defendant request a pretrial hearing on whether a substance contains a controlled substance, requires dismissal with prejudice if lab analysis finds none or the state provides none, and entitles the person to expunction if analysis finds none.

tx:HB 464.title: Relating to the establishment of a grant program to support the elimination of illegally disposed of scrap tires
tx:HB 464.summary: Requires the Commission on Environmental Quality to create, by January 1, 2027, a county grant program, funded from a new account, for prosecuting illegal scrap tire dumping, public information, and removing illegally dumped tires.

tx:HB 4696.title: Relating to the remote participation of certain persons in a proceeding for the issuance or modification of a protective order
tx:HB 4696.summary: Requires courts, on written request and absent good cause, to let a protective-order applicant or protected witness testify or take part remotely in hearings to issue or modify the order.

tx:HB 4742.title: Relating to the ability of a school district to request an appraisal of property by the appraisal district
tx:HB 4742.summary: Lets a school district require the appraisal office to reappraise all property at market value in a year the appraisal district does not reappraise, at the district's cost, with a deadline at least 30 days out.

tx:HB 475.title: Relating to Medicaid coverage and reimbursement for multisystemic therapy services
tx:HB 475.summary: Requires Medicaid to reimburse multisystemic therapy services and the Health and Human Services Commission to create a separate Medicaid provider type for multisystemic therapy providers.

tx:HB 4810.title: Relating to the continuation of the Trade Agricultural Inspection Grant Program
tx:HB 4810.summary: Extends the trade agricultural inspection grant program, moving the evaluation report deadline from January 15, 2025 to January 15, 2029 and the program's expiration from September 1, 2025 to September 1, 2029.

tx:HB 4811.title: Relating to the eligibility of the South by Southwest Conference and Festivals for funding under the Major Events Reimbursement Program
tx:HB 4811.summary: Makes the South by Southwest Conference and Festivals eligible for the major events reimbursement program and exempts it from the requirement that a competitive selection process considered out-of-state sites.

tx:HB 4838.title: Relating to conducting an assessment of language accessibility with respect to certain health and human services programs and 2-1-1 services provided by the Texas Information and Referral Network
tx:HB 4838.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to hire a language access coordinator to assess non-English speakers' access to its programs and 2-1-1 services and report findings within one year; the provisions expire June 1, 2027.

tx:HB 4944.title: Relating to the establishment of a grant program to provide financial assistance to counties for transportation assistance to indigent litigants
tx:HB 4944.summary: Creates a comptroller-run grant program, funded by appropriation, for counties that help indigent litigants with transportation to and from court proceedings.

tx:HB 5014.title: Relating to the rights of special forces veterans who hold a license to carry a handgun
tx:HB 5014.summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety to print "SPECIAL FORCES VETERAN" on the handgun license of a qualifying veteran who requests it and proves service and honorable discharge.

tx:HB 510.title: Relating to the issuance of a certified birth record to a homeless individual
tx:HB 510.summary: Requires registrars and county clerks to issue a homeless individual a certified birth record free on request, under verification and documentation rules set by the health commission, without requiring a physical address.

tx:HB 5115.title: Relating to the penalty for the crime of election fraud; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:HB 5115.summary: Expands the election fraud offense to cover knowingly or intentionally trying to count invalid votes or refuse valid ones, and raises the penalty from a Class A misdemeanor to a second degree felony (first degree for elected officials).

tx:HB 5134.title: Relating to eligibility to request a deposition before bringing a civil action
tx:HB 5134.summary: Allows a person to petition for a deposition to preserve testimony or investigate a potential claim, only if the person has sustained or expects actual damages; violators owe the deponent's attorney's fees.

tx:HB 5294.title: Relating to medical school admissions, coursework, academic standards, and employment decisions in this state
tx:HB 5294.summary: Requires medical schools to grade coursework A through F rather than pass/fail, consider a standardized test in admissions (not as sole criterion), and bars preferences based on race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin in admissions or employment.

tx:HB 538.title: Relating to student access to certain academic records; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 538.summary: Requires colleges to release a student's transcript on request unless financial obligations are unpaid, allows release to employers or schools for students out five years who made a good-faith effort to pay, and permits a uniform reasonable fee.

tx:HB 552.title: Relating to a study by the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service to determine standards for the appraisal for ad valorem tax purposes of certain agricultural land used to raise or keep bees
tx:HB 552.summary: Requires Texas A&M AgriLife Extension to study property tax appraisal standards for agricultural land used to raise bees and report by April 1, 2028.

tx:HB 5525.title: Relating to parole guidelines and procedures for inmates convicted of an offense committed when younger than 18 years of age
tx:HB 5525.summary: Requires the Board of Pardons and Paroles, by September 1, 2026, to adopt parole guidelines and procedures for inmates whose offense occurred before age 18, and to reconsider those previously denied parole.

tx:HB 5616.title: Relating to the Texas presidential library promotion program and fund
tx:HB 5616.summary: Requires the Texas Historical Commission to create a program that funds exhibit renovation, marketing and a mobile exhibit for the Lyndon B. Johnson, George H.W. Bush and George W. Bush presidential libraries, with a dedicated fund.

tx:HB 5623.title: Relating to the provision of loans and grants from the Texas Energy Fund for certain energy efficiency projects
tx:HB 5623.summary: Lets the Public Utility Commission use Texas Energy Fund money, without further appropriation, for grants to customers or nonprofits for energy efficiency projects such as weatherization and demand reduction.

tx:HB 5639.title: Relating to a veteran housing program established by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice
tx:HB 5639.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Criminal Justice to create a housing program dedicating cellblocks or dormitories to veteran inmates who opt in.

tx:HB 5658.title: Relating to the creation of the Craver Ranch Municipal Management District No. 1; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments and fees; granting a limited power of eminent domain
tx:HB 5658.summary: Creates the Craver Ranch Municipal Management District No. 1, which can issue obligations and impose assessments but not property taxes; eminent domain applies only if the bill passes by two-thirds of each house.

tx:HB 5677.title: Relating to the creation of the Pura Vida Municipal Management District No. 1; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes; granting a limited power of eminent domain
tx:HB 5677.summary: Creates the Pura Vida Municipal Management District No. 1, which can issue bonds, impose assessments and a sales and use tax, and, with voter approval, property taxes; eminent domain applies only if the bill passes by two-thirds of each house.

tx:HB 5682.title: Relating to the creation of the Colmena Ranch Municipal Management District No. 1; granting a limited power of eminent domain; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments and fees
tx:HB 5682.summary: Creates the Colmena Ranch Municipal Management District No. 1, which can issue bonds and impose assessments but not property taxes; eminent domain applies only if the bill passes by two-thirds of each house.

tx:HB 636.title: Relating to the implementation of a statewide homeless data sharing network to share real-time data on homelessness
tx:HB 636.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs, with the Texas Homeless Network, to set up a statewide network for sharing real-time homelessness data and to work with health plans to connect homeless individuals to services.

tx:HB 493.title: Relating to ineligibility to serve as a poll watcher
tx:HB 493.summary: Changes poll watcher ineligibility from a conviction for any offense tied to election conduct to a first or second degree felony or a felony tied to election conduct; requires the appointment certificate to include an affidavit of no such conviction.

tx:HB 5033.title: Relating to elimination of the motor vehicle emissions inspection and maintenance program
tx:HB 5033.summary: Excuses the state environmental commission and Department of Public Safety from implementing vehicle emissions inspections once Congress repeals or amends the federal Clean Air Act to end the requirement, or a U.S. constitutional amendment gives states authority over vehicle emissions.

tx:HB 5138.title: Relating to the duty of the attorney general to prosecute criminal offenses prescribed by the election laws of this state
tx:HB 5138.summary: Requires law enforcement to send the attorney general copies of probable-cause reports on Election Code offenses, and requires the attorney general to prosecute if the local prosecutor has taken no action within six months, subject to a local prosecutor's court objection.

tx:HB 5520.title: Relating to border protection and economic development services, programs, and other measures, including establishing an educational center and programs
tx:HB 5520.summary: Creates border-region grant programs for courts and higher education, directs governor's-office funds to border facilities and security infrastructure, sets Department of Public Safety border duties, extends the agricultural inspection grant program to 2029, and requires a loan-repayment plan for border-area health care professionals.

wi:SB 665.title: Relating to: establishing a statewide wolf population goal.
wi:SB 665.summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to set a statewide wolf population goal in its wolf management plan.

wi:SB 785.title: Relating to: including information about investigations of license holders in an online licensing portal maintained by the Department of Public Instruction.
wi:SB 785.summary: Requires the Department of Public Instruction to keep a free, public, searchable online licensing portal listing educators under investigation, investigation outcomes (including voluntary license surrenders), and revoked licenses.

wi:SB 94.title: Relating to: civil action for injury or damages resulting from riot or vandalism, participation in a riot, prohibiting certain limitations or restrictions on law enforcement responses to riot or vandalism activity, and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 94.summary: Makes urging others to riot a Class I felony and committing violence during a riot a Class H felony, allows civil suits for riot or vandalism damage, and bars officials from limiting police responses to riots.

wi:SJR 1.title: Relating to: the session schedule for the 2025-2026 biennial session period.
wi:SJR 1.summary: Sets the 2025-2026 legislative session schedule, including floor periods, dates bills go to the governor, and a session end of January 4, 2027; extends the executive budget deadline to February 20, 2025.

wi:SJR 2.title: VOTER IDENTIFICATION (SECOND CONSIDERATION)
wi:SJR 2.summary: Approves, on second consideration, a constitutional amendment requiring voters to present specified photo ID (state, federal, tribal or college), with provisional ballots for those without it, for the April 2025 ballot.

wi:SJR 88.title: Relating to: honoring the life and legacy of Charlie Kirk.
wi:SJR 88.summary: Honors the life and legacy of Charlie Kirk, mourns his assassination, and joins in prayer for his family and the nation.

wv:HB 4004.title: Creating the Recharge West Virginia Program
wv:HB 4004.summary: Creates the Recharge West Virginia Program: when funded, the Division of Economic Development may reimburse employers up to $10,000 per employee and $100,000 per year for upskilling training that earns a credential and a wage increase of at least 25%.

wv:SB 531.title: Establishing First Amendment Preservation Act
wv:SB 531.summary: Bars state agencies, including local governments, from contracting with companies that rate news sources for accuracy or bias, or with ad firms using them, for ad placement; requires bidders to certify this; also bars contracts tied to listed foreign adversaries or terror lists.

wv:SB 63.title: Creating Sustaining Opportunities for Academics in Rural Schools Act
wv:SB 63.summary: Changes public charter school law: gives charter schools first refusal on public schools a county board is closing, allows rural in-person charters and a second campus, and lets colleges apply for on-campus charter microschools.

mi:HB 4195.title: Michigan vehicle code: amend sections 50a, 51a, 232, 302, 303, 307, and 314
mi:HB 4195.summary: As introduced, removes citizenship and legal-presence requirements for driver's licenses, bars considering immigration status in deciding vehicle-code residency, and bars the Secretary of State from furnishing record lists for immigration enforcement.

mi:HB 4233.title: Of estates in dower, by the curtesy, and general provisions concerning real estate: amend the title and sections 35 and 36
mi:HB 4233.summary: Bars foreign principals tied to China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria or Venezuela's Maduro regime from acquiring Michigan agricultural land; existing holdings must be registered. Violations can bring a court-ordered sale; late registration, a fine up to $2,000.

mi:HB 4234.title: Of estates in dower, by the curtesy, and general provisions concerning real estate: amend the title and sections 35 and 36
mi:HB 4234.summary: Bars foreign principals tied to China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria or Venezuela's Maduro regime from acquiring real property within 20 miles of a military installation or key facility; existing owners may keep it but must register it. Violations can bring forced sale.

mi:HB 4241.title: Michigan strategic fund act: add section 7c.
mi:HB 4241.summary: Bars the Michigan Strategic Fund from knowingly giving incentives to entities controlled by, organized in, or based in China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria or Venezuela's Maduro regime, and requires recipients to swear they are not such entities.

mi:HB 4242.title: Public health code: amend sections 16213 and 20175a
mi:HB 4242.summary: Requires licensed health professionals, and health facilities and agencies, that keep patient records off-site or virtually, including through a records company, to ensure the records are physically maintained in a state or a Canadian province.

mi:HB 4256.title: The code of criminal procedure: amend section 13m of chapter XVII
mi:HB 4256.summary: Updates sentencing-guideline entries for manufacturing or delivering heroin, fentanyl or carfentanil to match the companion bill's penalties, raising the class for under 50 grams from D to B. Takes effect only if HB 4255 is enacted.

tx:HB 644.title: Relating to the civil liability of certain businesses in connection with allowing concealed handguns on the business premises
tx:HB 644.summary: Bars civil liability for a person controlling a business's premises, based solely on allowing a handgun license holder to enter with a concealed handgun, for damages from the holder's lawful carrying of it.

tx:HB 678.title: Relating to the inclusion of the National Sexual Assault Hotline on certain student identification cards issued by a public institution of higher education
tx:HB 678.summary: Requires public colleges and universities to print the National Sexual Assault Hotline contact information on student ID cards issued on or after the law takes effect, alongside the existing suicide-prevention and crisis-line numbers.

tx:HB 75.title: Relating to the release of defendants on bail, the duties of a magistrate in certain criminal proceedings, and the regulation of charitable bail organizations
tx:HB 75.summary: Requires a magistrate who finds no probable cause that an arrested person committed the offense to enter written findings supporting that finding in the record within 24 hours.

tx:HB 786.title: Relating to justice court security in certain counties
tx:HB 786.summary: Requires the commissioners court of a county with 3.3 million or more people to provide each justice court a metal detector and a constable, deputy constable or deputy sheriff at each public door, paid from county general revenue.

tx:HB 796.title: Relating to the Texas Sovereignty Act
tx:HB 796.summary: Creates a 12-member joint House-Senate committee to review federal actions and vote on whether each is unconstitutional. If both chambers and the governor approve, the action has no legal effect in Texas and state and local governments may not spend money enforcing it.

tx:HB 805.title: Relating to a study by the Public Utility Commission of Texas on the interconnection of electric transmission service facilities with the United Mexican States
tx:HB 805.summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study the effects of existing and possible new electric transmission connections between Texas and Mexico on networks and retail customers in both countries, and report to the legislature by September 1, 2026.

tx:HB 842.title: Relating to a study and report on burying power lines in the Gulf Coast region
tx:HB 842.summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to study, for areas within 150 miles of the Gulf Coast, the cost of burying overhead power lines, maintaining underground lines, and savings from fewer weather outages, and report by September 1, 2026.
