tx:HB 854.title: Relating to payment of the replacement cost of lost or damaged property under a homeowner's, renter's, or condominium owner's insurance policy
tx:HB 854.summary: Bars a homeowner's, renter's or condo insurer with replacement cost coverage from reducing an initial claim payment by more than 20 percent of its estimated repair cost minus the deductible; the rest is paid once completed repairs are documented. Applies from January 1, 2026.

tx:HB 869.title: Relating to the review and revision by the state's classification officer of information in the position classification plan regarding state information technology positions
tx:HB 869.summary: Requires the state's classification officer to review information technology job classifications at least every two years, aligning titles and descriptions with the private sector and emphasizing skills over degree and certification requirements.

tx:HB 871.title: Relating to the residential and commercial building codes of municipalities
tx:HB 871.summary: Updates the model residential and commercial building codes Texas cities adopt from the 2012 to the 2018 International Residential and Building Codes, for construction begun under agreements made on or after January 1, 2027; agricultural buildings stay under the 2012 codes.

tx:HJR 1.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment specifying the authority of the attorney general to prosecute a criminal offense prescribed by the election laws of this state
tx:HJR 1.summary: Proposes amending the Texas Constitution to give the attorney general concurrent jurisdiction with county and district attorneys to prosecute criminal offenses under state election laws.

tx:HJR 138.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment prohibiting the imposition of a carbon tax
tx:HJR 138.summary: Proposes amending the Texas Constitution to bar the legislature from taxing the carbon content of a fuel or the emission of carbon dioxide or other greenhouse gases from using, producing or consuming any good or service.

tx:HJR 218.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to authorize the use of money from the Texas energy fund for energy efficiency projects conducted to benefit retail electric customers
tx:HJR 218.summary: Proposes amending the Texas Constitution to let the Texas energy fund also finance energy efficiency projects conducted to benefit retail electric customers.

tx:HJR 34.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to authorize the legislature to exempt from ad valorem taxation the portion of the assessed value of a person's property that is attributable to the installation or construction in or on the property of border security infrastructure
tx:HJR 34.summary: Proposes amending the Texas Constitution to let the legislature exempt from property tax the market value added to real property in counties bordering Mexico by border security infrastructure and related improvements.

tx:HJR 98.title: Applying to the Congress of the United States to call a convention under Article V of the United States Constitution for the limited purpose of proposing one or more amendments to the constitution to impose fiscal restraints on the federal government, to limit the power and jurisdiction of the federal government, and to limit the terms of office of federal officials and members of Congress
tx:HJR 98.summary: Applies to Congress to call an Article V convention limited to proposing amendments that impose fiscal restraints on the federal government, limit federal power and jurisdiction, and limit terms of office for federal officials and members of Congress.

tx:SB 1008.title: Relating to state and local authority to regulate the food service industry
tx:SB 1008.summary: Bars counties, cities and public health districts from requiring food-business permits or charging fees beyond what the state health department requires or charges, with exceptions including reinspection fees up to $200 and fees up to 120 percent of the limit in the largest jurisdictions.

tx:SB 1024.title: Relating to the issuance of certain anticipation notes and certificates of obligation
tx:SB 1024.summary: Bars local governments from authorizing an anticipation note for a planned contract if a bond for the same purpose failed in the past five years or the note exceeds 5 percent of outstanding bonded debt, with exceptions such as disaster cleanup and court orders.

tx:SB 1026.title: Relating to the duty of the attorney general to prosecute criminal offenses prescribed by the election laws of this state
tx:SB 1026.summary: Gives the attorney general jurisdiction to prosecute Election Code crimes when a law enforcement probable-cause report goes to both the local prosecutor and the attorney general and six months pass without the local prosecutor starting a prosecution.

tx:SB 1059.title: Relating to the authority of the governing body of a home-rule municipality to submit a proposed charter amendment to the voters for approval if application of the provisions of the amendment would be contrary to state law
tx:SB 1059.summary: Bars the governing body of a home-rule city from submitting a proposed charter amendment to voters if applying it would be contrary to state law.

tx:SB 1065.title: Relating to a required provision in certain governmental entity contracts regarding the carrying of handguns by license holders; providing civil penalties
tx:SB 1065.summary: Requires contracts for use of government-owned or leased property to bar the contractor from prohibiting handgun license holders from entering or staying, unless state law bars carrying there. Violations carry civil penalties of $1,000 to $1,500 first, then $10,000 to $10,500.

tx:SB 1099.title: Relating to increasing the criminal penalty for certain offenses committed by an illegal alien
tx:SB 1099.summary: For certain listed felonies, raises the punishment one category, with a 15-year minimum for first-degree felonies, when the judge or jury finds beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant was in the United States illegally, as the bill defines it.

tx:SB 1137.title: Relating to group home consultant referrals; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 1137.summary: Bars group home consultants (people paid for referrals) from referring people to unlicensed or unpermitted group homes unless none is licensed in the region or the person cannot afford a licensed one, and requires telling them of known complaints first; a Class B misdemeanor.

tx:SB 1143.title: Relating to certain planning, notification, and evaluation requirements with respect to certain workforce development programs in this state
tx:SB 1143.summary: Requires local workforce development board plans to set specific goals and performance measures for people ages 14 to 24, and requires the Texas Workforce Commission to evaluate its federally funded youth workforce programs annually and report to the legislature.

tx:SB 1164.title: Relating to emergency detention of certain persons evidencing mental illness and to court-ordered inpatient and extended mental health services
tx:SB 1164.summary: Changes the standards for emergency mental health detention and court-ordered services, adding severe emotional distress and deterioration, or inability to recognize symptoms or treatment risks, as grounds alongside risk of serious harm, and revises the officer's detention notification form.

tx:SB 1183.title: Relating to electronic benefits transfer cards used by or for recipients of benefits under certain assistance programs
tx:SB 1183.summary: Requires benefit cards for cash assistance and SNAP to show the cardholder's name and photograph plus a fraud hotline number and reporting website, with photo exemptions for people 65 and older, under 19, blind, disabled, homeless or domestic violence victims.

tx:SB 1209.title: Relating to election dates
tx:SB 1209.summary: Ends the May uniform election dates so most elections are held in November, requires local governments to move their general elections to November by December 31, 2025, and requires elections and runoffs to be held on Tuesdays instead of Saturdays.

tx:SB 1241.title: Relating to the consideration of college entrance examinations for admission to certain public institutions of higher education and a study by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board regarding those examinations
tx:SB 1241.summary: Replaces the ACT and SAT score thresholds for admission to Texas public universities with scores the Higher Education Coordinating Board sets for designated exams, from fall 2028 admissions, and orders the board to study entrance exam scores.

tx:SB 1257.title: Relating to required health benefit plan coverage for gender transition adverse effects and reversals
tx:SB 1257.summary: Requires health plans, including Medicaid and CHIP, that cover or have covered gender transition procedures to cover their adverse consequences, annual follow-up testing, and treatment to manage, reverse or recover from the procedure, for plans issued or renewed from January 1, 2026.

tx:SB 128.title: Relating to hospital reporting requirements regarding suspected child abuse, exploitation, or neglect; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:SB 128.summary: Requires hospitals to report monthly to the state on child abuse reports made to child protective services, whether parents were told they may get an alternative opinion on treatment, and diagnostic codes used, with physician affidavits; late reports draw daily administrative penalties.

tx:SB 1281.title: Relating to certain criminal offenses involving mail or a mail receptacle key or lock; creating a criminal offense; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:SB 1281.summary: Expands the mail theft offense to cover taking mail anywhere, not only from a mailbox or premises, and with intent to steal a negotiable instrument; possessing mail from five or more addressees creates a rebuttable presumption of intent.

tx:SB 13.title: Relating to the use by a political subdivision of public funds for lobbying activities
tx:SB 13.summary: Bars cities, counties and other political subdivisions from spending public funds on registered lobbyists to lobby legislators, or on associations of local governments that hire them, with exceptions; residents can sue for injunctions and attorney's fees.

tx:SB 1307.title: Relating to a biennial health coverage reference guide developed by the Texas Department of Insurance
tx:SB 1307.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Insurance, consulting the Health and Human Services Commission, to publish a biennial public guide to health coverage covering definitions, coverage sources, consumer rights, shopping for plans, and how to resolve disputes.

tx:SB 1379.title: Relating to increasing the criminal penalties for forgery
tx:SB 1379.summary: Raises forgery from a Class A misdemeanor to a state jail felony and increases the penalty one degree for forged documents such as wills, deeds, checks, contracts, money and government records; also adjusts penalties by value obtained.

tx:SB 1396.title: Relating to prohibiting the adoption or use of national sex education standards in public schools
tx:SB 1396.summary: Bars the State Board of Education from adopting national sex education standards, bars human sexuality and sexually transmitted disease course materials from being based on them, and says school districts and charter schools cannot be required to offer them.

tx:SB 1401.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas Mental Health Profession Pipeline Program by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
tx:SB 1401.summary: Requires the Higher Education Coordinating Board to create a program encouraging colleges to offer guided pathways for community college students to transfer without losing credits and pursue degrees leading to licensure as psychologists, counselors, social workers and other mental health professionals.

tx:SB 1433.title: Relating to the assertion of legislative privilege by the attorney general in certain legal challenges to the constitutionality of state statutes
tx:SB 1433.summary: Lets the attorney general assert legislative privilege for the state or a state agency or official in lawsuits challenging state statutes, unless it creates a conflict, with 30 days afterward to show evidence of that representation.

tx:SB 1451.title: Relating to increasing the criminal penalty for the offense of stealing or receiving a stolen check or similar sight order
tx:SB 1451.summary: Raises the penalty for stealing or receiving a stolen check or similar sight order from a Class A misdemeanor to a state jail felony, for offenses committed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 1470.title: Relating to requiring the Department of Public Safety to share data for the purpose of maintaining the statewide voter registration list
tx:SB 1470.summary: Requires the secretary of state to use data on registered voters who apply for a license or ID in another state to flag voters with changed addresses, failed qualifications or multi-state registration, and requires the Department of Public Safety to share that data.

tx:SB 1498.title: Relating to civil asset forfeiture of digital currency or other similar property
tx:SB 1498.summary: Specifies that digital currency, non-fungible tokens and stablecoins can be forfeited as contraband under the civil asset forfeiture law, counts any increase in a digital currency's value before forfeiture as proceeds, and treats digital currency wallets as depository accounts.

tx:SB 15.title: Relating to certain files maintained by a law enforcement agency regarding certain employees of the agency
tx:SB 15.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to keep a confidential department file on each licensed officer, holding documents including unsubstantiated misconduct allegations; hiring agencies and the state law enforcement commission can review it, and otherwise it is disclosed only as required by law.

tx:SB 1534.title: Relating to a study and report by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board regarding health physics education in this state
tx:SB 1534.summary: Requires the Higher Education Coordinating Board, with the Texas Workforce Commission, to study gaps in health physics education and nuclear and radiological workforce needs, and report with recommendations by December 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1558.title: Relating to the liability of nonprofit entities contracted with the Department of Family and Protective Services or with a single source continuum contractor to provide community-based care or child welfare services
tx:SB 1558.summary: Treats nonprofits contracting for community-based care or child welfare services, and their staff, volunteers and caregivers, as charitable organizations under the Charitable Immunity and Liability Act, if insured; also limits liability for a worker's acts if background-check, reporting and training duties were met.

tx:SB 1563.title: Relating to county jailer training on interacting with veterans in the criminal justice system
tx:SB 1563.summary: Requires the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement, with the Texas Veterans Commission, to develop a training program for county jailers on interacting with veterans, and requires currently licensed jailers to complete it by August 31, 2027.

tx:SB 1596.title: Relating to the prohibition of short-barrel firearms
tx:SB 1596.summary: Removes short-barrel firearms from the Penal Code's list of prohibited weapons, ending the state offense of possessing, making, transporting, repairing or selling them, and repeals the definition of the term.

tx:SB 1626.title: Relating to censorship of or certain other interference with digital expression, including expression on social media platforms or through electronic mail messages
tx:SB 1626.summary: Lets a social media user who wins a suit over censorship by a large platform recover attorney's fees and actual or statutory damages, raises the covered-platform threshold from 50 million to 65 million U.S. users, and excludes newsfeeds, a platform's own homepage and non-common-carrier services.

tx:SB 1677.title: Relating to a study on prevention and reduction of diabetes-related amputation
tx:SB 1677.summary: Requires the Higher Education Coordinating Board to designate a top-tier research university to study preventing and reducing diabetes-related amputation, working with the health department, and report recommendations by September 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1717.title: Relating to the terminology used in statute, resolutions, rules, and other state publications to refer to the partially landlocked body of water on the southeastern periphery of the North American continent
tx:SB 1717.summary: Directs the legislature and state agencies to use "Gulf of America" instead of "Gulf of Mexico" in new and amended statutes, resolutions, rules and publications, and changes the term in existing Texas laws.

tx:SB 1718.title: Relating to the eligibility of the National Rifle Association's Annual Meetings and Exhibits or another annual event of the National Rifle Association for funding under the major events reimbursement program
tx:SB 1718.summary: Adds the National Rifle Association's annual meetings and exhibits, and other NRA annual events, to events eligible for the state major events reimbursement program, and lists the NRA as a site selection organization.

tx:SB 1727.title: Relating to procedures related to juvenile justice proceedings, the adjudication and disposition of cases involving delinquent conduct, and certain offenses or conduct committed by a child or by a person placed in or committed to certain juvenile facilities; changing the eligibility for community supervision
tx:SB 1727.summary: Bars community supervision for felonies committed at age 17 or older in juvenile custody, lowers from two to one the prior felony adjudications defining habitual felony conduct, and adds such custody felonies to cases prosecutors may refer to a grand jury for determinate sentences.

tx:SB 1728.title: Relating to the participation of certain juvenile justice entities in the Jobs and Education for Texans (JET) Grant Program
tx:SB 1728.summary: Allows the Texas Juvenile Justice Department, juvenile boards and juvenile probation departments to receive Jobs and Education for Texans (JET) grants from the Texas Workforce Commission for career and technical education programs.

tx:SB 1754.title: Relating to the authority of a taxing unit to enter into an agreement to exempt from ad valorem taxation a portion of the value of property on which a renewable energy facility is located or is planned to be located
tx:SB 1754.summary: Bars cities, counties and other taxing units from entering tax abatement or exemption agreements covering property of renewable energy facilities that sell power at wholesale, effective January 1, 2026, applying only to agreements entered after that.

tx:SB 1832.title: Relating to providing for an election by the parent of a student who was victimized by a public school employee to transfer the student to another public school campus or receive funding for the student to attend private school
tx:SB 1832.summary: Lets the parent of a student targeted by a school employee's offense, reported misconduct or grooming transfer the student to another campus or receive state funds equal to the district's per-student amount for private school or homeschooling.

tx:SB 1835.title: Relating to the maximum number of nonresident scholarship students permitted to pay resident tuition and fees at certain public institutions of higher education
tx:SB 1835.summary: Raises, for certain colleges, the cap on nonresident scholarship students charged resident tuition from 5 percent to 20 percent of enrollment where the area has below-average population growth and the school has capacity, and limits it to lawfully present students.

tx:SB 1851.title: Relating to the penalty for noncompliance with certain audit requirements by a municipality
tx:SB 1851.summary: Bars a city from adopting a property tax rate above its no-new-revenue rate if the attorney general finds it has not completed its required annual audit or filed its financial statement within 180 days of fiscal year end.

tx:SB 1861.title: Relating to the appointment of a special prosecutor by the court of criminal appeals for certain criminal cases
tx:SB 1861.summary: Lets a law enforcement agency that investigates an election-law offense send its report to the Court of Criminal Appeals, which must appoint a special prosecutor from outside the agency's area to decide whether to prosecute or request more investigation.

tx:SB 1863.title: Relating to the conduct of randomized county election audits
tx:SB 1863.summary: Requires the secretary of state to run randomized election audits after each November uniform election date, expands audited counties to 13 small and 3 large, and requires counties and political subdivisions to register and notify the state of elections.

tx:SB 1869.title: Relating to the procedures for modifying the schedules of controlled substances
tx:SB 1869.summary: Gives the state health commissioner 90 days, instead of 30, to object to federal changes to controlled substance schedules, and makes the commissioner's schedule decisions final unless the legislature changes them.

tx:SB 1870.title: Relating to municipal and county enforcement of drug and consumable hemp product laws; providing civil penalties
tx:SB 1870.summary: Adds constables to the local officials barred from adopting or enforcing policies of not fully enforcing state drug laws, extends the ban to consumable hemp product laws and ballot measures, and sets civil penalties of at least $25,000 for a first violation.

tx:SB 19.title: Relating to the use by a political subdivision of public funds for lobbying and certain other activities
tx:SB 19.summary: Bars political subdivisions from spending public funds to hire registered lobbyists to lobby legislators or to pay associations of governments that contract with them, with exceptions for officials, employees and sheriffs' associations; taxpayers or residents may sue for an injunction.

tx:SB 1924.title: Relating to the enforcement of certain criminal offenses on school property
tx:SB 1924.summary: Lets officers cite students for school offenses, bars a diploma until court-ordered community service, fines and costs are completed, and bars graduated sanctions before a complaint when the conduct posed an imminent threat to a teacher's safety or physically harmed a teacher.

tx:SB 1927.title: Relating to municipal regulation of the removal of an Ashe juniper tree
tx:SB 1927.summary: Bars cities from prohibiting, or charging a tree mitigation fee for, removal of an Ashe juniper on residential property, except in counties over two million people within 15 miles of an active military training base.

tx:SB 1936.title: Relating to the definition of an abuse unit for certain controlled substances under the Texas Controlled Substances Act
tx:SB 1936.summary: Changes the "abuse unit" definition for LSD-type drugs on unmarked paper from each quarter-inch square to each 10 milligrams of paper, rounded down to the nearest whole number.

tx:SB 1946.title: Relating to the creation of a family violence criminal homicide prevention task force
tx:SB 1946.summary: Requires the governor to create a Family Violence Criminal Homicide Prevention Task Force to analyze risk factors, advise agencies and nonprofits on training for professionals who work with survivors, and publish regional non-confidential data.

tx:SB 1999.title: Relating to protection for a public employee's or student's use of terms consistent with biological sex
tx:SB 1999.summary: Bars public schools, colleges and public employers from disciplining or retaliating against a student or employee who addresses someone in terms consistent with that person's biological sex, while leaving anti-bullying and harassment rules in place.

tx:SB 2004.title: Relating to the eligibility of the INDYCAR Grand Prix of Arlington for funding under the major events reimbursement program
tx:SB 2004.summary: Adds the INDYCAR Grand Prix of Arlington to the major events reimbursement program and lets it qualify through September 1, 2030 without a competitive site selection process, naming Penske Entertainment as a site selection organization.

tx:SB 2010.title: Relating to the authority of a political subdivision to establish and operate a guaranteed income program
tx:SB 2010.summary: Bars cities, counties and other local governments from creating or running guaranteed income programs of cash or equivalent payments to individuals, except short-term work-linked programs; existing programs may continue until January 1, 2026 or expiration.

tx:SB 2018.title: Relating to the strong families credit against certain taxes for entities that contribute to certain organizations
tx:SB 2018.summary: Creates a franchise tax credit, capped at $5 million a year in total, for contributions to nonprofits certified by the OneStar Foundation that serve at-risk families and do not provide abortion services or abortion information.

tx:SB 2043.title: Relating to prohibited retaliation against a physician or health care provider for reporting certain violations or taking certain actions with respect to the provision of health care services; providing a civil remedy
tx:SB 2043.summary: Bars hospitals, state agencies, medical schools and others from taking adverse action against a physician or health care provider for testifying, providing information, or protected speech, and lets the provider sue for an injunction and actual damages.

tx:SB 2069.title: Relating to the establishment of a work group to conduct a study on the feasibility of implementing an acute psychiatric bed registry
tx:SB 2069.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to set up a work group to study a statewide or regional registry of available inpatient psychiatric beds and report to legislative committees by November 1, 2027.

tx:SB 2078.title: Relating to the regulation of composting in certain counties; authorizing a civil penalty
tx:SB 2078.summary: Bars depositing food waste collected under a city's commercial composting ordinance at composting facilities in counties without such an ordinance, with a $1,000 civil penalty per violation and exceptions for farms, county-approved sites and existing facilities.

tx:SB 2111.title: Relating to legal representation of indigent persons in this state and to proceedings before a magistrate including the appointment of counsel for an indigent defendant
tx:SB 2111.summary: Changes indigent defense procedures: expands what managed assigned counsel programs cover and plan for, requires magistrates to appoint counsel or notify the appointing authority if an arrested person cannot understand, and lets counties appoint lawyers, including part-time public defender staff, solely for magistrate appearances.

tx:SB 2119.title: Relating to an exemption from certain immunization requirements for medical and veterinary students
tx:SB 2119.summary: Exempts medical and veterinary school students from required immunizations if they submit a conscience or religious-belief affidavit or a physician's statement that the vaccine would be harmful to their health.

tx:SB 2188.title: Relating to space flight activities
tx:SB 2188.summary: Makes space flight activities subject only to federal and state jurisdiction, barring cities and counties from banning or regulating them, and revises when certain coastal counties and cities may close beaches for launches.

tx:SB 2215.title: Relating to the enforcement against violations by a municipality of certain zoning laws
tx:SB 2215.summary: Lets a person harmed by a city's violation of the state zoning chapter sue the city for mandamus, declaratory or injunctive relief, waives the city's immunity from suit, and allows court costs and attorney's fees for the prevailing party.

tx:SB 2233.title: Relating to a prohibition on certain persons supporting terrorist activity at public institutions of higher education
tx:SB 2233.summary: Requires colleges to bar students and employees on nonimmigrant visas from publicly endorsing terrorist activity tied to an ongoing conflict; a first violation brings at least a one-year suspension, a second expulsion or firing, each reported to the federal Homeland Security Department.

tx:SB 2309.title: Relating to election integrity and security of ballot boxes, including by preventing fraud in the conduct of elections in this state; authorizing a penalty
tx:SB 2309.summary: Lets poll watchers follow ballot boxes and election materials to tabulation sites, requires counties of 100,000 or more to livestream video of areas holding voted ballots, with misdemeanor and felony penalties, and expands candidate presence at partial counts.

tx:SB 2330.title: Relating to payroll deductions for certain state and local government employee organizations
tx:SB 2330.summary: Bars the state and local governments from deducting labor organization or similar dues from employee pay, with exceptions including law enforcement, firefighter and emergency medical personnel organizations and charitable campaign donations.

tx:SB 2337.title: Relating to the regulation of the provision of proxy advisory services
tx:SB 2337.summary: Requires proxy advisors to disclose when advice is based on nonfinancial factors such as ESG or DEI, or differs between clients, makes violations deceptive trade practices, and lets affected parties seek declaratory or injunctive relief.

tx:SB 2340.title: Relating to examination of the records of filing entities and foreign filing entities by the attorney general; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 2340.summary: Lets the attorney general require filing entities to file written reports and examine people under oath in investigations, and makes concealing, destroying, altering or falsifying records to avoid compliance a misdemeanor with a fine up to $5,000 and up to a year in jail.

tx:SB 240.title: Relating to the designation and use of certain spaces and facilities according to biological sex; authorizing a civil penalty and a private civil right of action
tx:SB 240.summary: Requires state and local government restrooms, changing rooms and showers to be designated by biological sex, with exceptions; requires housing inmates by sex; limits women's family violence shelters to females and their minor children; sets civil penalties of $5,000, then $25,000.

tx:SB 2431.title: Relating to requiring foreign language credit opportunities for students enrolled in study abroad components or programs offered by certain institutions of higher education in this state
tx:SB 2431.summary: Requires public colleges and universities that offer a study abroad program where a language other than English is mainly spoken to give students an option to earn foreign language credit through it, under Coordinating Board rules. Applies from the 2026-2027 academic year.

tx:SB 2519.title: Relating to restrictions on the levy and use of certain ad valorem taxes and on the issuance of certain bonds supported by ad valorem taxes
tx:SB 2519.summary: Bars taxing units from transferring added maintenance-and-operations tax revenue from an automatic tax-rate election to a local government corporation to repay a public security. Bars cities, counties and those corporations from pledging such revenue for securities issued after the bill takes effect.

tx:SB 2529.title: Relating to the vote required by the governing body of a taxing unit to adopt an ad valorem tax rate that exceeds the voter-approval tax rate or authorize the issuance of tax bonds
tx:SB 2529.summary: Requires at least 60 percent of a political subdivision's governing body to vote to issue general obligation bonds. Requires 75 percent to adopt a tax rate above the voter-approval rate after voters rejected a higher rate the prior year, including for certain water districts.

tx:SB 2532.title: Relating to the calculation of the voter-approval tax rate for certain municipalities that receive municipal hotel occupancy tax revenue and other money from a local park board of trustees
tx:SB 2532.summary: Changes how the voter-approval property tax rate is calculated for Gulf-coast home-rule cities under 80,000 people that have a park board of trustees, reducing the rate by hotel occupancy tax revenue the city spent for purposes the law does not authorize.

tx:SB 2533.title: Relating to the accreditation of law schools in this state
tx:SB 2533.summary: Requires law schools at public, private and independent colleges in Texas to be accredited by an accreditor recognized by the U.S. Department of Education and the Texas Supreme Court.

tx:SB 2570.title: Relating to a legal justification for the use of force with a less-lethal force weapon by a correctional facility guard or a peace officer
tx:SB 2570.summary: Makes the use of less-lethal weapons by correctional guards and peace officers legally justified when reasonably necessary to do their duties and in substantial compliance with training. Defines less-lethal weapons to include projectile launchers, chemical sprays, striking devices and stun guns.

tx:SB 261.title: Relating to a prohibition on the offering for sale and the sale of cell-cultured protein for human consumption; providing civil and criminal penalties
tx:SB 261.summary: Bars offering for sale or selling cell-cultured protein, meaning food made from animal cells grown in a medium, for human consumption in Texas. The ban is enforced like other food-safety violations and expires September 1, 2027.

tx:SB 2615.title: Relating to restricting telework for employees of public institutions of higher education
tx:SB 2615.summary: Bars public colleges and universities from allowing employees to telework except in listed cases, such as illness, disability accommodation, certain nonteaching jobs, distance-education teaching, off-campus research, telehealth duties, and catastrophes like storms or epidemics. Applies from the 2025-2026 academic year.

tx:SB 2617.title: Relating to a policy adopted by a school district or open-enrollment charter school regarding the expression of dates
tx:SB 2617.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt a policy using the terms AD and BC when expressing dates in student instruction, and bars them from choosing curriculum materials that express dates otherwise. Applies from the 2026-2027 school year.

tx:SB 2619.title: Relating to certain accountability-related policies and procedures related to public schools, the availability of information regarding a board of trustees of a school district or governing body of an open-enrollment charter school, and the approval by the Texas Education Agency of training provided to a member of a board of trustees of a school district
tx:SB 2619.summary: Ends the terms of all trustees in districts rated F two years running, with seats filled by election; requires boards to review superintendent applicants' prior schools' performance; requires Texas Education Agency approval of trustee training; and creates annual performance percentile rankings of districts and charters.

tx:SB 2639.title: Relating to the designation of a property as a historic landmark and the inclusion of a property in a historic district or similar preservation district by certain municipalities
tx:SB 2639.summary: Requires historic designation impact statements to include repair costs and appraisals. In cities of 950,000 or more, bars historic designation without owner consent unless the city makes a compensation offer, with court-appointed commissioners assessing damages if the sides cannot agree.

tx:SB 269.title: Relating to required reports of certain vaccine-related or drug-related adverse events
tx:SB 269.summary: Requires physicians to report serious adverse events within a year of an experimental or emergency-use vaccine (to VAERS) or drug (to FDA MedWatch), excluding clinical trials. The Texas Medical Board takes corrective action for a first violation and disciplinary action for later ones.

tx:SB 2693.title: Relating to the role of advocacy and support groups in the juvenile justice system
tx:SB 2693.summary: Lets the Texas Juvenile Justice Department admit advocacy or support groups only if it finds that serves a child's best interest. Bars admission while the group has a federal complaint or lawsuit against the department pending, unless federal law or a court order requires it.

tx:SB 2742.title: Relating to the enforcement of electioneering prohibitions and the unlawful use of public funds for political advertising; imposing civil penalties
tx:SB 2742.summary: Sets civil penalties for independent school districts that electioneer (up to $1,000 per violation, each day separate) and for anyone who unlawfully uses public funds for political advertising ($1,000 to $1,500 a day). Lets the attorney general sue and bars officials from claiming official immunity.

tx:SB 2743.title: Relating to the prosecution of certain election offenses
tx:SB 2743.summary: Requires a judge to disqualify a district or county attorney who consistently refuses to prosecute election offenses and appoint an assistant attorney general instead. Lets county residents petition for disqualification or for referral of an election case to the attorney general.

tx:SB 2778.title: Relating to the amount of an expenditure that may be paid by an emergency services district employee without board approval
tx:SB 2778.summary: Raises from $2,000 to $50,000 the amount a bonded emergency services district employee may pay without board approval. Applies to purchases made after the bill takes effect.

tx:SB 2835.title: Relating to municipal regulation of stairway requirements in certain apartment buildings
tx:SB 2835.summary: Allows cities to permit single-stairway apartment buildings of up to six stories with no more than four units per floor, if they meet listed fire-safety conditions such as sprinklers in stairways, fire-rated stair enclosures and corridors, and limits on exit travel distance.

tx:SB 2847.title: Relating to innovations in core curriculum to accelerate the award of bachelor's degrees
tx:SB 2847.summary: Requires the Coordinating Board to form an advisory committee, equally from two- and four-year colleges, to review general education requirements and ways to condense them, with a report due November 1, 2026. Lets the board approve core curricula under 42 credit hours.

tx:SB 2858.title: Relating to state preemption of certain municipal and county regulation
tx:SB 2858.summary: Bars cities and counties from regulating conduct covered by the Election, Health and Safety, or Penal Codes unless a statute allows it, and voids such rules. Lets affected persons and the attorney general sue; the comptroller withholds sales tax revenue during the attorney general's suit.

tx:SB 2877.title: Relating to the penalty for the crime of election fraud; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:SB 2877.summary: Raises the penalty for election fraud from a Class A misdemeanor to a second-degree felony (first-degree for elected officials, third-degree for attempts). Adds offenses of counting votes known to be invalid or refusing to count votes known to be valid.

tx:SB 2920.title: Relating to the regulation of steroid use by students participating in athletic competitions sponsored or sanctioned by the University Interscholastic League
tx:SB 2920.summary: Provides that giving steroids to a minor student to transition the student's biological sex is not a valid medical purpose, so it does not exempt University Interscholastic League athletes from the steroid-use ban, testing and ineligibility rules.

tx:SB 2925.title: Relating to the establishment of the Task Force on Modernizing Manufacturing
tx:SB 2925.summary: Creates a 15-member Task Force on Modernizing Manufacturing, led by the Texas Economic Development and Tourism Office, with manufacturer, labor, education and agency members appointed by the governor, to study manufacturing in Texas. Report due October 1, 2026.

tx:SB 2972.title: Relating to expressive activities at public institutions of higher education
tx:SB 2972.summary: Limits campus free-expression protections at public colleges to enrolled students and employees, excludes defamation, harassment, incitement, obscenity and threats, and ends the traditional-public-forum rule for outdoor areas. Requires policies banning camping, certain face coverings, and expression from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m.

tx:SB 2995.title: Relating to the displacement of student financial aid at a public institution of higher education
tx:SB 2995.summary: Requires the Coordinating Board to write a financial aid displacement advisory explaining that private scholarships and other reasons can reduce other aid, and requires public colleges to include it or link to it in admission applications, with plain-language aid tips, starting 2025-2026.

tx:SB 3016.title: Relating to state preemption of municipal and county regulation on land use, structures, businesses, and related activities and municipal boundaries and annexation
tx:SB 3016.summary: Bars cities and counties from regulating fields occupied by state laws on land use, structures, businesses and annexation, and voids such rules. Lets affected persons and the attorney general sue; the comptroller withholds sales tax revenue during the attorney general's suit.

tx:SB 3037.title: Relating to the creation of La Cima Municipal Management District No. 1; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes; granting a limited power of eminent domain
tx:SB 3037.summary: Creates the La Cima Municipal Management District No. 1, with powers to provide improvements and services, borrow, issue bonds, impose property taxes, and contract for law enforcement. Eminent domain power applies only if the bill passes with a two-thirds vote in each house.

tx:SB 3039.title: Relating to the transfer of students in public higher education
tx:SB 3039.summary: Expands the annual transfer report public universities file to cover transfer goals, pathways, barriers and articulation agreements with junior colleges, beyond denied-credit courses. Requires rules making colleges publish uniform degree requirements, course prerequisites and minimum transfer requirements.

tx:SB 3047.title: Relating to the creation of the Pura Vida Municipal Management District No. 1; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes; granting a limited power of eminent domain
tx:SB 3047.summary: Creates three municipal management districts (Pura Vida, Rivers Market Place, Wolf Creek) with powers to provide improvements and services, issue bonds, and impose assessments and property taxes. Eminent domain power applies only if the bill passes with a two-thirds vote in each house.

tx:SB 318.title: Relating to the establishment of the election integrity division in the office of the attorney general
tx:SB 318.summary: Creates an election integrity division in the attorney general's office to investigate reports of election fraud and Election Code offenses in support of local prosecutors. Lets the division subpoena political subdivisions for documents or testimony and requires state law enforcement to assist.

tx:SB 324.title: Relating to requiring state contractors, political subdivisions of this state, and private employers to participate in the federal electronic verification of employment authorization program, or E-verify
tx:SB 324.summary: Requires state contractors and subcontractors, political subdivisions and private employers to register with and use the federal E-Verify program to check new employees; employer and local-government duties start January 1, 2027. Contractors that stop can be barred from state contracts for one year.

tx:SB 36.title: Relating to the homeland security activities of certain entities, including the establishment and operations of the Homeland Security Division in the Department of Public Safety
tx:SB 36.summary: Creates a Homeland Security Division in the Department of Public Safety to plan border security operations, run intelligence centers, manage the Operation Drawbridge camera program, and coordinate statewide homeland security planning and exercises with agencies and local governments.

tx:SB 37.title: Relating to the governance of public institutions of higher education, including review of curriculum and certain degree and certificate programs, a faculty council or senate, training for members of the governing board, and the establishment, powers, and duties of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board Office of the Ombudsman
tx:SB 37.summary: Requires public college governing boards to review general education curricula every five years and approve provost hires; lets boards overturn vice president and dean hires. Sets faculty senate rules, and creates a Coordinating Board ombudsman office to handle complaints.

tx:SB 383.title: Relating to the interconnection to the ERCOT power grid of certain coastal facilities for the provision of electric service
tx:SB 383.summary: Bars connecting wind power facilities in Texas Gulf waters within three marine leagues of the coast, or lines that connect directly to them, to the ERCOT power grid. Applies only to connections sought after the bill takes effect.

tx:SB 388.title: Relating to the legislature's goals for electric generation capacity in this state
tx:SB 388.summary: Changes the legislature's stated goal to 50 percent of ERCOT generating capacity installed after January 1, 2026 being dispatchable generation other than battery storage, replacing the natural gas goal, and replaces the natural gas credits program with a PUC-run dispatchable generation credits program.

tx:SB 39.title: Relating to civil liability of a commercial motor vehicle owner or operator
tx:SB 39.summary: Repeals exceptions that let claimants present employer negligence evidence, such as negligent entrustment, in the first phase of a bifurcated commercial truck crash trial once the employer stipulates its driver acted within the scope of employment. Keeps independent claims like negligent maintenance or loading.

tx:SB 406.title: Relating to the required inclusion of a person's sex on a birth certificate and prohibited change of sex on the birth certificate of certain persons
tx:SB 406.summary: Requires birth certificates to record a child's biological sex as male or female, except when it cannot be determined at birth. Bars changing the sex on a birth certificate except to fix a clerical error, fill a missing entry, or record a later-determined sex.

tx:SB 407.title: Relating to a health care facility's required policy for vaccine preventable diseases
tx:SB 407.summary: Requires health care facilities' vaccine policies to include exemptions for covered individuals for reasons of conscience, including religious belief, and bars facilities from rejecting such an exemption for any reason.

tx:SB 412.title: Relating to defenses to prosecution for certain offenses involving material or conduct that is obscene or otherwise harmful to children
tx:SB 412.summary: Replaces the scientific, educational, governmental and similar defenses to charges of selling or displaying harmful material to a minor, and the educational, medical, legislative and similar defenses to sexual performance by a child, with a defense for judicial or law enforcement officers on official duty.

tx:SB 268.title: Relating to the procedure for certain complaints against health care practitioners
tx:SB 268.summary: Requires a licensing board that receives a complaint about a practitioner licensed by a different board to forward it. Bars discipline unless the other board refers it back, for unlicensed practice of medicine, or within the receiving board's authority over a practitioner it also licenses.

tx:SB 2713.title: Relating to preventing discrimination in membership in a professional or trade association
tx:SB 2713.summary: Bars professional or trade associations from denying membership because of race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, national origin, or speech or assembly, except speech that incites crime, makes a specific threat of violence over listed traits, or is unlawful. Lets aggrieved people sue.

tx:SB 2880.title: Relating to abortion, including civil liability for distribution of abortion-inducing drugs; making conforming changes and harmonizing conforming provisions; authorizing a private civil right of action
tx:SB 2880.summary: Bars manufacturing, distributing, mailing or providing abortion-inducing drugs in Texas, with exceptions such as medical emergencies. Allows private suits for death or injury and qui tam suits with at least $100,000 in damages per violation; lets the attorney general sue over criminal abortion-law violations.

tx:SB 396.title: Relating to confirmation of a voter's residence by a voter registrar
tx:SB 396.summary: Adds a trigger for voter registrars to send residence confirmation notices: on November 30 after a general election, to voters not on the suspense list who have not voted in any election in the previous 25 months. Existing triggers remain.

tx:SB 495.title: Relating to the authority of the Texas Department of Insurance to adopt rules that implement or are based on certain environmental, social, and governance models, ratings, or standards
tx:SB 495.summary: Bars the insurance commissioner from requiring insurers to follow National Association of Insurance Commissioners rules or standards built on environmental, social and governance assessments unless a statute expressly authorizes them, and limits certain environment-related rules not authorized by statute.

tx:SB 505.title: Relating to processes to address election irregularities; providing a civil penalty
tx:SB 505.summary: Lets candidates, party chairs, election judges and ballot-measure committee heads request written explanations of apparent election irregularities from the county election authority, with escalation to a Secretary of State audit and a $500 civil penalty for each violation not remedied in 30 days.

tx:SB 511.title: Relating to prohibiting an officer or employee of this state or of a political subdivision of this state from distributing certain voter registration application forms; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 511.summary: Bars state and local officers and employees, on duty, from distributing voter registration forms to people who did not request them or contracting with vendors to do so with public funds. Class C misdemeanor (Class A for contracts); parties and candidates are exempt.

tx:SB 530.title: Relating to the accreditation of certain postsecondary educational institutions in this state or of certain programs offered by those institutions
tx:SB 530.summary: Removes references to the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools from Texas education law, substituting an institution's recognized accrediting agency or one designated by the Coordinating Board, and directs the board to ensure institutions are accredited to take part in federal student aid.

tx:SB 533.title: Relating to the election date for the authorization of the issuance of bonds or a tax increase
tx:SB 533.summary: Requires elections to issue bonds or other debt, or to raise taxes, to be held on the November uniform election date, and bars holding them as emergency elections. Applies to elections ordered on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 54.title: Relating to election procedures regarding accepting a voter with a residence address that is not current and the immediate effect of a voter's registration after the registrar's receipt of certain change of address notices
tx:SB 54.summary: Repeals the rule that an in-county change-of-address notice takes effect immediately, and lets voters who moved within their county vote in the precinct where they are registered without having to ask the registrar to update their registration address.

tx:SB 6.title: Relating to abortion, including civil liability for the manufacture and provision of abortion-inducing drugs, exemptions from the Texas Citizens Participation Act and Religious Freedom Restoration Act, authorizing civil and qui tam actions, amendments to the fee-shifting statute governing abortion litigation, immunity defenses and limits on state-court jurisdiction and relief, the parens patriae standing of the attorney general, and the jurisdiction of the Fifteenth Court of Appeals; providing for severability
tx:SB 6.summary: Lets private persons, but not government officials, sue those who manufacture, distribute, mail, prescribe or provide abortion-inducing drugs in Texas, with at least $100,000 in damages per violation. Excludes suits against the pregnant woman; exempts emergencies, ectopic pregnancy and other non-abortion uses.

tx:SB 9.title: Relating to the calculation of the voter-approval tax rate for certain taxing units
tx:SB 9.summary: Lowers from 1.035 to 1.025 the maintenance-and-operations multiplier in the voter-approval property tax rate for most taxing units, other than special units and cities or counties under 75,000 people, cutting allowed growth without a voter election from 3.5% to 2.5%.

tx:SB 617.title: Relating to hearing and public notice requirements regarding the conversion by a municipality of certain properties to house homeless individuals
tx:SB 617.summary: Bars a city from approving conversion of city-controlled property to house homeless people unless it holds a public hearing within one mile of the site at least 90 days earlier, with mailed notice to nearby residences and businesses. Residents may sue; emergency shelter is exempt.

tx:SB 618.title: Relating to the unlawful altering of election procedures; providing a civil penalty
tx:SB 618.summary: Directs the Secretary of State to investigate complaints that officials altered election procedures without legal authority and demand compliance. Officials who do not comply face civil penalties up to $1,000, then $5,000, per day; repeat non-elected violators may be removed.

tx:SB 619.title: Relating to protection of persons from participation in a health care service for reasons of conscience; providing a civil remedy; authorizing disciplinary action
tx:SB 619.summary: Lets health care providers decline to take part in a health care service for reasons of conscience, except emergency care and most life-sustaining treatment; bars liability and adverse action against them; requires facilities to adopt patient-access protocols; lets injured people file complaints or sue.

tx:SB 646.title: Relating to repayment of certain mental health professional education loans
tx:SB 646.summary: Raises caps on state loan-repayment assistance for mental health professionals, such as $160,000 to $180,000 for physicians; adds eligible professions, including school counselors; adds one-time $5,000 (needed-language fluency) and $10,000 (counties of 150,000 or fewer) amounts; counts public school service toward eligibility.

tx:SB 667.title: Relating to prohibiting certain state governmental entities from investing in certain Chinese-affiliated entities
tx:SB 667.summary: Requires the comptroller to list restricted Chinese-affiliated entities and bars state retirement systems and the permanent school fund from holding them, with at least half divested within 180 days of notice and all within 360, subject to fiduciary-duty exceptions.

tx:SB 689.title: Relating to employment practices regarding diversity and prohibiting the implementation of diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives by certain governmental entities
tx:SB 689.summary: Bars state agencies, counties, cities and special districts (not universities or school districts), except where federal law requires, from keeping diversity, equity and inclusion offices or requiring diversity statements; lets the attorney general seek mandamus; repeals state workforce diversity programs.

tx:SB 706.title: Relating to the recognition of a handgun license issued by another state
tx:SB 706.summary: Recognizes a valid handgun license from any other state in Texas, replacing the current requirement that the attorney general find the other state does background checks. The governor negotiates reciprocity agreements where required, and DPS lists states recognizing Texas licenses.

tx:SB 707.title: Relating to the authority of the legislature to determine that certain federal directives are unconstitutional and to prohibit certain government officers and employees from enforcing or assisting in the enforcement of the directive
tx:SB 707.summary: Lets the Legislature declare a federal directive unconstitutional by concurrent resolution and bar state and local officers and employees from enforcing or assisting it. Filing needs a two-thirds vote of the house; directives activating state military forces are excluded.

tx:SB 715.title: Relating to reliability requirements for certain electric generation facilities
tx:SB 715.summary: Extends ERCOT generation reliability requirements and penalties to eligible plants regardless of when their interconnection agreement was signed. Exempts resources able to run 24 continuous hours, including with batteries, and directs the PUC to consider rebating penalties to consumers.

tx:SB 760.title: Relating to an application for a ballot to be voted by mail submitted by certain residents of an assisted living facility, a nursing facility, or an intermediate care facility
tx:SB 760.summary: Requires early voting clerks to notify the state health commission when a mail-ballot application lists a long-term care facility address; the commission notifies the facility, which must tell the resident's guardian or agent, if any, within five business days. The commission audits 2.5% of facilities.

tx:SB 762.title: Relating to the display of flags in public schools; providing a civil penalty
tx:SB 762.summary: Bars public schools from displaying flags on school property other than listed ones, such as U.S., Texas, military, college, tribal, local-government and school flags. Parents may give notice of a violation; schools failing to report a fix within 10 business days owe $500 a day.

tx:SB 779.title: Relating to common law public nuisance claims
tx:SB 779.summary: Bars common-law public nuisance lawsuits over conditions authorized by government permits or rules, conduct already covered by a statutory cause of action or agency enforcement, or the making, sale or marketing of products. Combining many private injuries does not create a public nuisance.

tx:SB 781.title: Relating to certain files maintained by a law enforcement agency regarding certain employees of the agency
tx:SB 781.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to keep a separate confidential department file on each licensed officer, including misconduct allegations found unsubstantiated. Hiring agencies and the state law enforcement commission may view it; it is exempt from public information requests but subject to criminal-case discovery.

tx:SB 819.title: Relating to renewable energy generation facilities; authorizing fees
tx:SB 819.summary: Requires wind and solar facilities of 10 megawatts or more to get a PUC public-interest determination before connecting to transmission, with setbacks (solar 100 feet from property lines, wind twice turbine height), public notice, and automatic approval if undecided within 180 days.

tx:SB 825.title: Relating to an annual study on the economic, environmental, and financial impact of illegal immigration in this state
tx:SB 825.summary: Requires the governor's office to conduct an annual study of the economic, environmental and financial impact of illegal immigration in Texas, and to report results to the lieutenant governor and Legislature by December 1 of each even-numbered year.

tx:SB 870.title: Relating to the open carrying of a handgun by a uniformed school marshal
tx:SB 870.summary: Allows a school marshal wearing a uniform identifying them as a school marshal to openly carry a handgun on school premises, instead of only carrying concealed, for public, private and junior college school marshals.

tx:SB 875.title: Relating to prohibiting election activities committed by a member of the board of trustees or superintendent of an independent school district or on certain school district premises; creating criminal offenses
tx:SB 875.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor for school district trustees or superintendents to use district funds or resources, like email, to electioneer, and a Class B misdemeanor for a campus administrator to knowingly allow political signs over 48 hours outside voting periods.

tx:SB 912.title: Relating to the verification of health care practitioner continuing education compliance through the establishment of continuing education tracking systems
tx:SB 912.summary: Bars licensing boards from renewing a health care practitioner's license without verifying continuing education compliance, and requires each board to set up an electronic continuing education tracking system by September 1, 2026, or 2028 for the Department of Licensing and Regulation.

tx:SB 921.title: Relating to conducting an ex parte renewal of a recipient's Medicaid eligibility
tx:SB 921.summary: Bars the state from using information from other public assistance applications, such as SNAP, to automatically renew a person's Medicaid eligibility without their involvement, unless federal law requires it. Agencies may still act on reported changes in circumstances.

tx:SB 945.title: Relating to the adoption of political shareholder proposals by insurers and insurer holding companies
tx:SB 945.summary: Bars Texas-organized insurers and holding companies from including or implementing shareholder proposals that seek to limit insuring fossil fuel risks, require tracking or reducing greenhouse gas emissions, or limit insuring lawful businesses for environmental, social or political ends.

tx:SB 946.title: Relating to the prohibition on certain discrimination in the extension of credit to organizations based on social credit or value-based standards
tx:SB 946.summary: Bars lenders from denying or limiting credit to an organization based on social credit or ESG scores, diversity practices, or ties to religious institutions or industries like agriculture, fossil fuels or firearms, rather than a bona fide credit decision.

tx:SB 95.title: Relating to the administration of immunizations to children, including required written informed consent to those immunizations and civil liability for failure to obtain the consent; providing an administrative penalty
tx:SB 95.summary: Requires written informed consent before a provider immunizes a child, with liability up to $10,000 if consent is skipped and a reportable adverse reaction occurs. Bars providers from taking vaccine-maker payments for giving immunizations; penalty is the greater of $5,000 or ten times the payment.

tx:SB 964.title: Relating to the appearance of a personal identification certificate or driver's license issued to a person who is not a citizen of the United States
tx:SB 964.summary: Requires Texas IDs and driver's licenses issued to noncitizens to display the phrase "NOT ELIGIBLE TO VOTE" on the front, and to be oriented differently (vertically for licenses) from citizens' cards.

tx:SB 965.title: Relating to the right of a public school employee to engage in religious speech or prayer while on duty
tx:SB 965.summary: Bars school districts, charter schools and other state entities from infringing the right of a district or charter school employee to religious speech or prayer while on duty, unless necessary to further a compelling state interest by the least restrictive means.

tx:SB 973.title: Relating to the prohibition on posting on the Internet information held by an appraisal district regarding certain residential property
tx:SB 973.summary: Exempts certain items from the ban on posting appraisal records online: street-level exterior photos, aerial photos showing more than one separately owned building, and outline sketches. Bars reappraisal plans from preventing appraisals needed to meet market-value requirements.

tx:SB 974.title: Relating to the eligibility of a person employed by a school district as a teacher to serve on the appraisal review board of an appraisal district; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 974.summary: Allows school district teachers to serve on appraisal review boards, and makes it an offense for independent school district trustees or employees to contact a teacher member to influence their appraisal review board decisions.

tx:SB 985.title: Relating to the combination of certain election precincts
tx:SB 985.summary: Lets counties combine election precincts to avoid unreasonable costs when redistricting leaves precincts with fewer than 3,000 registered voters, removing the current limit to counties under 1.2 million that do not use countywide polling places.

tx:SCR 19.title: Authorizing the State Preservation Board to approve the construction of a Texas Life Monument at the State Capitol Complex
tx:SCR 19.summary: Authorizes the State Preservation Board to approve construction of a Texas Life Monument, a replica of a sculpture of a mother with an unborn child, at the Capitol Complex outside the historic Capitol grounds, subject to state law and board rules.

tx:SCR 27.title: Authorizing the burial of Guy Herman in the State Cemetery
tx:SCR 27.summary: Authorizes the burial of Travis County probate judge Guy Herman in the State Cemetery, provided the State Cemetery Committee approves his application for burial space.

tx:SCR 38.title: Recognizing the strategic importance of the Gulf of America to the economic and security interests of Texas and the United States
tx:SCR 38.summary: Recognizes the Gulf of America's importance to Texas and the U.S., affirms Texas' sovereignty over its 10-mile coastal zone, commends Trump Administration policies on energy, growth and state sovereignty, encourages federal-state collaboration, and opposes federal actions undermining Texas' control of coastal resources.

tx:SCR 42.title: Urging the state to adopt the policy to recognize two sexes, male and female
tx:SCR 42.summary: Declares it the policy of Texas to recognize two sexes, male and female, and states that Texas will use language and policies recognizing women as biologically female and men as biologically male.

tx:SCR 9.title: Urging Congress to propose and submit to the states for ratification the "Keep Nine" amendment to the U.S. Constitution
tx:SCR 9.summary: Urges Congress to propose a U.S. constitutional amendment, called the Keep Nine amendment, fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices, and to submit it to the states for ratification.

tx:SJR 1.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment requiring the denial of bail under certain circumstances for illegal aliens charged with certain offenses punishable as a felony
tx:SJR 1.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment requiring judges to deny bail to people in the U.S. unlawfully accused of listed offenses, such as murder, aggravated kidnapping, sexual assault and certain drug and weapon felonies, when a hearing finds probable cause.

tx:SJR 12.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment establishing a parent's right to direct a child's education
tx:SJR 12.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment giving parents the right to direct their child's education, including making choices within public schools, choosing private or home school, viewing teaching materials, attending school board meetings, and accessing the child's records.

tx:SR 5.title: Establishing rules of procedure to be observed by the Senate for the consideration of redistricting during the 89th Legislature
tx:SR 5.summary: Sets Senate procedures for congressional redistricting: a special committee, regional hearings with videoconference testimony, public notice 72 hours ahead for regional hearings (48 in called sessions) and 48 hours for bill hearings, and amendment-packet filing requirements for floor amendments changing districts.

tx:SR 708.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction on S.B. No. 2972
tx:SR 708.summary: Suspends Senate rules so the conference committee on SB 2972, on campus expressive activities, can change text not in disagreement: keeping 'content-neutral' in a provision on restrictions on expressive activities and removing an unnecessary 'and'.

tx:SR 715.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, H.B. No. 5246
tx:SR 715.summary: Suspends Senate rules so the conference committee on HB 5246 can add a provision, in neither chamber's version, letting the Texas Space Commission board, with city approval, order temporary closure of a highway, venue or other specified area in a municipality.

wi:AB 2.title: Relating to: requiring school boards to adopt policies to prohibit the use of wireless communication devices during instructional time.
wi:AB 2.summary: Requires each school board to adopt a policy by July 1, 2026 generally banning pupil use of phones and other wireless devices during instructional time, with exceptions for emergencies, health care, education plans and teacher-approved uses, and to submit it to DPI.

wi:AB 4.title: Relating to: required instruction in civics in the elementary and high school grades, high school graduation requirements, and private school educational program criteria.
wi:AB 4.summary: Requires schools to teach civics starting in 2027-28, including comparing communism, socialism and totalitarianism with representative democracy, and adds a half-credit civics requirement within high school social studies credits for 2030-31 graduates.

wi:AB 5.title: Relating to: requiring school boards to make textbooks, curricula, and instructional materials available for inspection by school district residents.
wi:AB 5.summary: Requires school boards to let district residents inspect adopted textbooks, curricula and instructional materials at no cost, within 14 days of a written request.

wi:AB 6.title: Relating to: requiring a school board to spend at least 70 percent of its operating expenditures on direct classroom expenditures and annual pay increases for school administrators.
wi:AB 6.summary: Requires school boards to spend at least 70 percent of operating expenditures on defined direct classroom costs, with state aid and property tax reductions if they fall short, and limits administrator pay raises to the average teacher raise.

wi:AB 24.title: Relating to: county sheriff assistance with certain federal immigration functions.
wi:AB 24.summary: Requires sheriffs to ask people jailed on felony offenses for proof of lawful presence, notify federal authorities when it cannot be verified, and honor federal detainers; counties whose sheriff fails to certify compliance lose 15 percent of shared revenue payments.

wi:AB 38.title: Relating to: an income tax exemption for cash tips paid to an employee.
wi:AB 38.summary: Creates a state income tax subtraction for qualified tips for tax years 2025 through 2028, matching the federal deduction for tips received in occupations that customarily receive them.

wi:AB 104.title: Relating to: prohibiting gender transition medical intervention for individuals under 18 years of age.
wi:AB 104.summary: Bans health care providers from performing or referring minors under 18 for medical treatment meant to align the body with a sex other than their biological sex, with exceptions, and requires licensing boards to revoke violators' licenses.

wi:AB 164.title: Relating to: various changes to the unemployment insurance law and federal Reemployment Services and Eligibility Assessment grants.
wi:AB 164.summary: Renames unemployment insurance as reemployment assistance, requires claimants to post a resume and make direct employer contacts, requires DWD to supply at least four job leads weekly, and requires it to continue the federal RESEA program.

wi:AB 167.title: Relating to: various changes to the unemployment insurance law and requiring approval by the Joint Committee on Finance of certain federally authorized unemployment benefits.
wi:AB 167.summary: Changes unemployment law by widening what counts as misconduct, requiring audits of at least 50 percent of work searches, and making federal benefit increases subject to Joint Finance Committee review.

wi:AB 223.title: Relating to: residency requirements for persons circulating nomination papers or recall petitions.
wi:AB 223.summary: Limits circulation of nomination papers to eligible Wisconsin voters, ending the current option for nonresident U.S. citizens (still allowed for president and vice president), and requires recall petition circulators to be Wisconsin electors.

wi:AB 226.title: Relating to: prohibiting school boards and independent charter schools from providing food containing certain ingredients in free or reduced-price meals.
wi:AB 226.summary: Bans public, charter and private choice schools from serving school meals containing brominated vegetable oil, potassium bromate, propylparaben, azodicarbonamide or red dye 3; private vendors may still serve such foods on school premises.

wi:AB 315.title: Relating to: the Warren Knowles-Gaylord Nelson stewardship 2000 program and a major land acquisitions program.
wi:AB 315.summary: Reauthorizes the Knowles-Nelson stewardship land conservation program through 2027-28, cutting yearly borrowing limits to $1 million for land acquisition and $9.25 million for development and local aid, and adds wildlife habitat grants.

wi:AB 320.title: Relating to: increasing certain court fees and surcharges and indexing those amounts for inflation.
wi:AB 320.summary: Raises court fees, surcharges and payments to witnesses and interpreters, expands state-reimbursed Milwaukee County district attorney staff, and requires interpreters in civil cases to appear by phone or video unless a party objects and the court orders otherwise.

wi:AB 377.title: Relating to: establishing English as the official state language, use of artificial intelligence or other machine-assisted translation tools in lieu of appointing English language interpreters, and use of English for governmental oral and written communication and for nongovernmental purposes.
wi:AB 377.summary: Makes English Wisconsin's official language, requires government communication in English with exceptions (including hospitals), and lets governments give AI or machine translation tools instead of appointing an interpreter, except for defendants accused of violent crimes.

wi:AB 385.title: Relating to: online credit card contributions and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 385.summary: Requires third-party groups taking online card donations for political committees to require card verification codes and U.S. billing addresses, with an exception for overseas citizens, and imposes a forfeiture equal to the contributions collected without those checks.

wi:AB 411.title: Relating to: creation of a farmland link program.
wi:AB 411.summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to run a farmland link program connecting landowners and farm operators with people seeking land for agriculture, with a public website and an annual report.

wi:AB 415.title: Relating to: use restrictions on state and local government electronic devices.
wi:AB 415.summary: Bars state agencies from using devices to access social media, software or generative AI controlled by foreign adversaries such as China and Russia, and requires state, legislative and court technology policies on such products, effective January 31, 2027.

wi:AB 446.title: Relating to: consideration of a certain definition of antisemitism for purposes of laws, ordinances, policies, or criminal penalty enhancers concerning discrimination based on race, religion, color, or national origin.
wi:AB 446.summary: Requires state and local governments to consider the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance's 2016 definition of antisemitism when judging discriminatory intent under anti-discrimination and hate-crime laws, without creating new penalties or limiting First Amendment rights.

wi:AB 453.title: Relating to: required approvals of rezoning requests related to residential development, contents of and consistency of local ordinances with local comprehensive plans, certain tax incremental district project costs related to residential development, and tax incremental district lifespan extension.
wi:AB 453.summary: Requires cities and villages to grant rezoning for residential development that meets plan, density and nearby-development conditions unless denial is needed to avoid overburdened public facilities or safety threats; also allows longer tax incremental district extensions for housing.

wi:AB 486.title: Relating to: permissible financial aid reductions in higher education.
wi:AB 486.summary: Bars colleges from cutting a student's institutional gift aid because of Wisconsin private scholarships up to $5,000 per semester, with exceptions for athletics rules and when total aid exceeds need or cost of attendance.

wi:AB 592.title: Relating to: professional development for science teachers.
wi:AB 592.summary: Requires DPI to work with nonprofits on professional development for K-12 science teachers in 2025-26 and 2026-27, unless the Joint Finance Committee has not supplemented the appropriation for it by June 1, 2026.

wi:AB 595.title: Relating to: compliance with the federal Help America Vote Act, voter registration data sharing agreements, removing ineligible voters from the official voter registration list, and fees for obtaining the official voter registration list.
wi:AB 595.summary: Requires matching the voter list against transportation, vital records and corrections data, directs the Legislative Audit Bureau to audit it for noncitizens, and requires removing ineligible voters from the list instead of marking them ineligible.

wi:AB 612.title: Relating to: the Warren Knowles-Gaylord Nelson stewardship 2000 program, a major land acquisitions program, and making an appropriation.
wi:AB 612.summary: Reauthorizes the Knowles-Nelson stewardship program through 2027-28 with a combined annual limit of $13.25 million, ends forestry account transfers to the capital improvement fund, and appropriates forestry account money directly for small land purchases, property development and grants.

wi:AB 613.title: Relating to: notifying parents if a pupil is removed from the classroom.
wi:AB 613.summary: Requires principals to notify parents of all pupils in a class, in writing and generally by 5 p.m. that day, when a pupil's removal reduces instructional time, and requires annual reporting of removals; exception for some pupils with disabilities.

wi:AB 617.title: Relating to: applying for and returning absentee ballots; use of central counting locations; election night reporting; court determinations of incompetency and ineligibility to vote; preelection tests of electronic voting equipment, and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 617.summary: Changes absentee voting by requiring fixed alternate ballot sites, ending central counting locations, moving the mail application deadline to seven days before elections, adding text notifications, and updating voter status after court incompetency rulings.

wi:AB 625.title: Relating to: pay for performance grant requirements.
wi:AB 625.summary: Requires the state to withhold 10 to 50 percent of homelessness grants for nine months, paying it only if recipients meet housing, employment or reduced-return-to-homelessness goals, and requires recipients to report data.
