wi:AB 640.title: Relating to: setting a maximum age for serving as a supreme court justice or judge of a court of record.
wi:AB 640.summary: Bars election or appointment of anyone aged 75 or older as a supreme court justice or judge of a court of record, other than as a temporary reserve judge.

wi:AB 644.title: Relating to: state aid for consolidated school districts.
wi:AB 644.summary: Raises consolidation aid for school districts consolidating in 2027 to 2029 to $1,500 per pupil in the first year and $650 per pupil in the second.

wi:AB 646.title: Relating to: requiring a school district consolidation study.
wi:AB 646.summary: Requires DPI to contract for a study of school districts covering boundaries, facilities, staffing and enrollment, with recommended consolidations, and to report it to the legislature.

wi:AB 647.title: Relating to: whole grade sharing grants for school boards.
wi:AB 647.summary: Requires DPI to pay four-year grants of $500 per pupil to school boards that enter whole grade sharing agreements, provided enough money is appropriated to cover prior grants.

wi:AB 648.title: Relating to: supplemental state aid for consolidated school districts.
wi:AB 648.summary: Creates aid for districts consolidated on or after July 1, 2026 whose levy rate exceeds the lowest merged district's: the rate gap times equalized value, falling 20 percent yearly and ending in year six; the bill provides no funding.

wi:AB 649.title: Relating to: supplemental funding for whole grade sharing grants, supplemental state aid for consolidated school districts, grants for feasibility studies of school district consolidation or whole grade sharing, and making an appropriation.
wi:AB 649.summary: Increases Joint Finance Committee supplemental funding by $2.7 million for grade sharing grants, $3 million for consolidated district aid, and $250,000 for consolidation feasibility studies.

wi:AB 652.title: Relating to: various changes to the unemployment insurance law.
wi:AB 652.summary: Raises the maximum weekly unemployment benefit from $370 to $395, lets employers report declined interviews or offers, reduces benefits by half of Social Security Disability payments instead of barring them, and adds a $5,000 penalty for failed attempts to claim benefits in another person's name.

wi:AB 1005.title: Relating to: admission to University of Wisconsin System institutions.
wi:AB 1005.summary: Requires University of Wisconsin-Madison undergraduate admission decisions, starting 2027-28, to be predominantly based on ACT, SAT or similar test performance or objective testing measures, except for applicants admitted through the guaranteed admission program.

wa:SGA 9109.title: CARMEN RIVERA
wa:SGA 9109.summary: Confirms Carmen Rivera as a member of the Sentencing Guidelines Commission.

wa:SGA 9144.title: YOLANDA KING-LOWE
wa:SGA 9144.summary: Confirms Yolanda King-Lowe as a member of the Washington State Women's Commission.

wa:SGA 9145.title: MALIA MULLEN
wa:SGA 9145.summary: Confirms Malia Mullen as a member of the Washington State Women's Commission.

wa:SGA 9147.title: GABRIEL VERDUGO
wa:SGA 9147.summary: Confirms Gabriel Verdugo as a member of the Pollution Control and Shorelines Hearings Board.

wa:SGA 9188.title: JAMES R. VOLLENDROFF
wa:SGA 9188.summary: Confirms James R. Vollendroff as a member of the Liquor and Cannabis Board.

wa:SGA 9203.title: PETER HOLMES
wa:SGA 9203.summary: Confirms Peter Holmes as a member of the Liquor and Cannabis Board.

wa:SGA 9220.title: DREW SHIRK
wa:SGA 9220.summary: Confirms Drew Shirk as Director of the Department of Revenue.

ia:SF 297.title: Relating to contracts entered into by state agencies and including applicability provisions
ia:SF 297.summary: Voids listed terms in state agency purchasing contracts, such as out-of-state venue, binding arbitration and jury-trial waivers, and deems Iowa law and courts to govern, with director waivers. Also limits each person to six events a year on Capitol grounds, with an official's recommendation.

ia:SF 303.title: Relating to county and city regulation of consumer fireworks
ia:SF 303.summary: Bars counties and cities from prohibiting or limiting the use of consumer fireworks on July 3, July 4 and December 31, while leaving local limits on other days.

ia:SF 393.title: Relating to discovery and postconviction procedure
ia:SF 393.summary: As introduced, bars discovery in postconviction relief cases without a court order or the parties' agreement, adds stricter limits on discovery involving crime victims, and requires parties to share subpoenaed evidence within three business days.

ia:SF 394.title: Relating to pesticides, by providing for tort liability
ia:SF 394.summary: Provides that an EPA-approved pesticide label, or one consistent with EPA health or cancer assessments, satisfies state-law warning and labeling duties, including common-law failure-to-warn claims, without barring other state-law claims.

ia:SF 407.title: Relating to the membership of district judicial nominating commissions
ia:SF 407.summary: As introduced, changes district judicial nominating commissions: the governor appoints six members instead of five, the senior district judge no longer serves on them, and members elect their own chairperson.

ia:SF 412.title: Relating to property law, including rent, rental agreements, notice requirements, and possession of property
ia:SF 412.summary: Changes rental and eviction law: allows notices by door posting plus email with the recipient's written consent, extends the peaceable-possession bar on eviction suits from 30 to 60 days, and requires sealing eviction court records in set cases.

ia:SF 418.title: Relating to sex and gender, including those and related terms for purposes of statutory construction, indications of a person’s sex on certain vital records, gender identity under the Iowa civil rights Act, and school curricula related to gender theory
ia:SF 418.summary: Defines sex in state law as male or female at birth, requires birth certificates and certain state data to record sex that way, and removes gender identity as a protected category from the Iowa Civil Rights Act.

ia:SF 445.title: Relating to early childhood education and care, including by modifying provisions related to the statewide preschool program, the child development coordinating council, programs for at-risk children, the responsibilities of the department of education, the early childhood Iowa initiative, and the state child care assistance program, establishing the child care continuum partnership grants pilot program within the departme nt of health and human services, making appropriations and reducing ap...
ia:SF 445.summary: Lets approved community-based providers join the state preschool program, ends the child development coordinating council and moves its duties to the Department of Education, makes some child care workers eligible for child care assistance, and creates a child care continuum partnership grants pilot.

ia:SF 459.title: Prohibiting the use of ranked choice and instant runoff voting in elections in this state
ia:SF 459.summary: As introduced, bans ranked choice and instant runoff voting for casting or counting ballots in any Iowa election, including local government elections.

ia:SF 487.title: Relating to employer recordkeeping and auditing requirements for purposes of unemployment insurance and including applicability provisions
ia:SF 487.summary: As introduced, requires employers to keep unemployment-insurance records for three years and directs the Department of Workforce Development to audit employer records in the field, with advance notice and a pre-audit interview.

ia:SF 507.title: Restricting county and city diversity, equity, and inclusion programs
ia:SF 507.summary: As introduced, bars counties and cities from keeping diversity, equity and inclusion offices or staff, or from requiring or giving preference based on diversity, equity and inclusion statements.

ia:SF 514.title: Relating to temporary orders of child custody in dissolution proceedings
ia:SF 514.summary: As introduced, requires courts to award temporary joint physical care of a child to both parents during divorce custody proceedings unless a rebuttable presumption exists against one parent; a judge finding joint care inappropriate must give reasons.

ia:SF 571.title: Relating to defense subpoenas in criminal cases, and providing penalties
ia:SF 571.summary: As introduced, requires criminal defendants to get court approval to subpoena documents or evidence, granted only on proof of compelling need for material, exculpatory, admissible evidence that excludes others' private information, and requires sharing results with the prosecutor within five business days.

ia:SF 579.title: Relating to local civil rights commissions and local civil rights agencies
ia:SF 579.summary: Sends local civil rights complaints involving a local government to the state Office of Civil Rights, lets any party move unresolved complaints there after 12 months, makes city commissions optional for cities of 29,000 or more, and sets two-year commissioner terms.

ia:SF 595.title: Related to the regulation of construction, including state building codes, contractor licensing, and stormwater management requirements
ia:SF 595.summary: Requires state building code rule proposals to include a report on estimated effects on home construction costs, and bars cities and counties from requiring licenses or fees for general contractors and subcontractors or imposing construction-site stormwater rules stricter than plat approval.

ia:SF 606.title: Relating to electronic filing of sales and use tax returns, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 606.summary: Requires monthly sales and use tax returns to be filed electronically, with exceptions the director may allow, and treats a return not filed in the department's specified electronic format as invalid.

ia:SF 615.title: Relating to work requirements for the Iowa health and wellness plan, public assistance programs, an information technology fund, the public assistance modernization fund, and the Medicaid for employed people with disabilities program, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 615.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to seek federal approval to require Iowa Health and Wellness Plan members to work at least 80 hours a month, with listed exemptions, and to align work rules across public assistance programs.

ia:SF 633.title: Relating to forest and fruit-tree reservations by establishing a program fee and including contingent effective date provisions
ia:SF 633.summary: Creates an annual per-acre fee, starting in 2026, on property tax-exempt forest and fruit-tree reservations: $2 in the owner's home county, $3 in an adjacent county, and a rate based on local farmland taxes elsewhere, paid to the county.

ia:SF 644.title: Relating to and making appropriations to the justice system, providing for properly related matters including indigent defense and representation, the corrections capital reinvestment fund, and a corrections federal receipts fund, and including effective date and retroactive applicability provisions
ia:SF 644.summary: Appropriates FY2025-26 money for the Department of Justice, corrections, public safety and other justice agencies, raises court-appointed attorney hourly rates by $2 (to $88 for class A felonies), and creates a corrections federal receipts fund.

ia:SF 645.title: Relating to and making appropriations for the economic development of the state, including to the economic development authority, Iowa finance authority, department of workforce development, and the state board of regents and certain regents institutions, and extending the repeal date for the housing renewal pilot program
ia:SF 645.summary: Appropriates FY2025-26 money for the Economic Development Authority, Iowa Finance Authority, Department of Workforce Development and certain Regents institutions, and extends the Housing Renewal Pilot Program's repeal date from July 1, 2025 to 2028.

ia:SF 647.title: Relating to and making appropriations to the education system, including the funding and operation of the department for the blind, department of education, and state board of regents, and including contingent effective date provisions
ia:SF 647.summary: Appropriates FY2025-26 money for the Department for the Blind, Department of Education and Board of Regents, including $1 million for a Center for Intellectual Freedom, and creates a court reporter equipment grant program and separate tuition-grant funds.

ia:SF 648.title: Relating to and making appropriations to the judicial branch including judicial officer salaries and interpreter or translator fees, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 648.summary: Appropriates FY2025-26 money for the Iowa judicial branch, sets judicial salary rates (for example $201,609 for each supreme court justice), and has the court revolving fund pay interpreter and translator costs and fees.

ia:SF 75.title: Relating to county supervisors, concerning county supervisor representation plans and county supervisor vacancies, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 75.summary: Requires counties with a Regents university main campus to elect supervisors by district (plan three), moves supervisor representation-plan special elections from August to November, and fills vacancies by special election in counties of 125,000 or more or with such a campus.

ky:HB 10.title: AN ACT relating to executive branch operations and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 10.summary: Requires Attorney General approval of executive settlements over $1 million within 180 days before a governor's inauguration, sets 24-month probation for some staff moved into classified jobs in the prior 18 months, extends Senate confirmation to more appointees, and requires preserving transition records.

ky:HB 103.title: AN ACT relating to water fluoridation programs.
ky:HB 103.summary: Makes water fluoridation optional, letting each regulated water system's governing body decide whether to take part; existing programs continue until it ends them, and its decision binds the systems it supplies. Grants liability immunity for those decisions.

ky:HB 136.title: AN ACT relating to corrections.
ky:HB 136.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to report data on time served and on people released on supervision, and to procure a new inmate communications contract by January 1, 2026.

ky:HB 137.title: AN ACT relating to air quality monitoring.
ky:HB 137.summary: Requires air-quality enforcement to use EPA-approved data collection methods, or methods producing defensible data the EPA accepts, and bars data from other methods in enforcement proceedings.

ky:HB 16.title: AN ACT relating to water fluoridation programs.
ky:HB 16.summary: Makes water fluoridation optional, letting each regulated water system's governing body decide whether to take part; existing programs continue until it ends them, and its decision binds the systems it supplies.

ky:HB 189.title: AN ACT relating to pedestrians.
ky:HB 189.summary: Bars sitting, standing or remaining stationary on state-maintained rights-of-way not designated for pedestrians, with emergency and utility-worker exceptions; lets local governments authorize limited exceptions and the Transportation Cabinet set minimum standards.

ky:HB 196.title: AN ACT relating to coal mining.
ky:HB 196.summary: Replaces the rule of two technicians on every coal-mine production shift with tiers by miners on the shift: one emergency technician for 10 or fewer, two for 11 to 50, more underground above 50; drops the nonproduction-shift requirement.

ky:HB 216.title: AN ACT relating to the Kentucky Office of Agricultural Policy and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 216.summary: Provides that the executive branch ethics code does not bar Department of Agriculture employees outside the Office of Agricultural Policy from applying for or receiving funds, awards or contracts that office administers, retroactive to March 12, 2021.

ky:HB 241.title: AN ACT relating to education and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 241.summary: For the 2024-25 school year, lets districts meet 1,062 instructional hours instead of 170 attendance days, lets the education commissioner grant up to five disaster relief days or waive up to five attendance days, and caps virtual-program teacher loads.

ky:HB 257.title: AN ACT relating to the education assessment and accountability system.
ky:HB 257.summary: Lets districts develop local indicators of school quality, removes the on-demand writing and editing assessments, replaces the school climate and safety rating indicator with chronic absenteeism, and orders a middle school advanced-math study by November 1, 2026.

ky:HB 312.title: AN ACT relating to concealed firearms and deadly weapons.
ky:HB 312.summary: Requires State Police to issue provisional concealed-carry licenses, valid until age 21, to people aged 18 to 20 who meet set criteria, and sets how they convert to standard licenses.

ky:HB 314.title: AN ACT relating to the Kentucky Communications Network Authority and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 314.summary: Attaches the Kentucky Communications Network Authority to the Finance Cabinet under the Commonwealth Office of Technology's executive director, abolishes its advisory group and executive director position, and replaces most of its board members.

ky:HB 346.title: AN ACT relating to air quality programs and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 346.summary: Provides that emergency stationary engines do not subject sources holding state-origin or non-major permits to emissions fees, requires refunds of 2023 fees paid contrary to that, and bars new or reassessed 2023 fees.

ky:HB 355.title: AN ACT relating to real property appraisers.
ky:HB 355.summary: Renames the Real Estate Appraisers Board the Real Property Appraisers Board and expands it from five to seven members, sets a one-year deadline for lawsuits and complaints against appraisers, and changes continuing education and licensing rules.

ky:HB 379.title: AN ACT relating to postsecondary education.
ky:HB 379.summary: Repeals several postsecondary education statutes, sets contract and collection rules for the Department of Revenue collecting debts owed to public colleges, requires Northern Kentucky University to administer the Center for Mathematics, and requires preliminary discussion of university president evaluations in closed session.

ky:HB 387.title: AN ACT relating to veterinarians and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 387.summary: Adds one livestock veterinarian and one equine veterinarian to the Controlled Substances Prescribing Council, removing one physician and one nurse, and exempts veterinarians from reporting controlled-substance prescribing to any governmental entity except the Board of Veterinary Examiners.

ky:HB 392.title: AN ACT relating to state-operated mental health facilities.
ky:HB 392.summary: Makes the Cabinet for Health and Family Services responsible for emergency and other outside medical care of patients in state-operated mental health facilities. The Senate version also requires prisoners and jail inmates to be housed by original biological sex.

ky:HB 399.title: AN ACT relating to interference with a legislative proceeding.
ky:HB 399.summary: Creates first- and second-degree crimes of interference with a legislative proceeding, states they do not bar assembly in traditional public forums, allows arrests for them, and requires officers to remove violators from a legislative building at the request of presiding officers or committee chairs.

ky:HB 424.title: AN ACT relating to employment at public postsecondary education institutions.
ky:HB 424.summary: Requires boards of the six comprehensive universities to appoint presidents, lets boards delegate faculty hiring and removal to presidents, removes contract-length limits, allows removal of employees for failing performance requirements, and requires faculty evaluations at least every four years.

ky:HB 45.title: AN ACT relating to campaign finance.
ky:HB 45.summary: Sets reporting and donor-certification rules for political issues committees and independent expenditures, bars foreign nationals from funding ballot-measure campaigns, creates privacy rights for donations to tax-exempt groups, and lets legislators use campaign funds to contribute to other candidates, parties or caucus committees.

ky:HB 455.title: AN ACT relating to elections.
ky:HB 455.summary: Creates a Unit of Election Investigations and Security within the Attorney General's office, sets its powers, duties and procedures, and requires an annual report to the Legislative Research Commission.

ky:HB 468.title: AN ACT relating to civil rights.
ky:HB 468.summary: Changes the Kentucky Civil Rights Act so people can sue over employment and public accommodation discrimination without first filing with the Human Rights Commission, narrows the commission's adjudication role, and lets it sue within 180 days on probable cause.

ky:HB 490.title: AN ACT relating to employment at public postsecondary education institutions and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 490.summary: Allows public postsecondary institutions to remove faculty members for bona fide financial reasons and requires governing boards to set the removal process under specified parameters.

ky:HB 520.title: AN ACT relating to law enforcement records.
ky:HB 520.summary: Exempts law enforcement investigative records from public inspection when disclosure could pose an articulable risk of harm to the agency or its investigation by revealing the identity of informants or witnesses not otherwise known.

ky:HB 546.title: AN ACT relating to transportation, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 546.summary: Creates a Local Assistance Road Program for rehabilitating local roads, capping state funding at $500,000 per project with a local match based on county population, and requires a memorandum with Indiana to use tolling revenue for the I-69 Ohio River Crossing.

ky:HB 566.title: AN ACT relating to the Kentucky Horse Racing and Gaming Corporation and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 566.summary: Restructures the Kentucky Horse Racing and Gaming Corporation: adds board seats for charitable gaming and quarter horse interests, requires annual outside audits, creates quarter horse and purse funds, expands its authority over charitable gaming, and bars reducing charitable games approved as of July 1, 2025.

ky:HB 569.title: AN ACT relating to designation of special judges and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 569.summary: Lets any person submit an affidavit to the Attorney General that an assigned judge cannot impartially preside; the Attorney General decides if impartiality may reasonably be questioned and may send it to the Chief Justice, who decides whether to appoint a special judge.

ky:HB 607.title: AN ACT relating to consolidated local governments.
ky:HB 607.summary: Changes rules for consolidated local governments: sets ethics enforcement and redistricting controls, lets the council override local health and solid waste board regulations within 45 days, requires an appointed chief audit executive, and allows property to be taxed separately as land and improvements.

ky:HB 619.title: AN ACT relating to public postsecondary education.
ky:HB 619.summary: Expands the KCTCS board of regents to 17 members with four-year terms, sets eligibility rules, lets the Governor remove all appointed members for cause, and gives the board budget review and presidential qualification powers over the system.

ky:HB 627.title: AN ACT relating to insurance.
ky:HB 627.summary: Raises the weekly personal injury protection work-loss limit from $200 to $500, sets rules for paying medical expenses, gives the Attorney General concurrent jurisdiction over insurance fraud, and requires prosecutors to refer fraud reports to the insurance commissioner.

ky:HB 662.title: AN ACT relating to personally identifiable information.
ky:HB 662.summary: Bars government agencies from disclosing judges' and their families' personal information on written request, requires removal within 72 hours, creates a lawsuit for violations, and ends requirements that insurance denial letters include a name, license number or medical director signature.

ky:HB 694.title: AN ACT relating to Teachers' Retirement System benefit funding.
ky:HB 694.summary: Requires TRS retiree health employer funding to pay down pension liability once the retiree health fund is fully funded, restoring it below 95 percent funding, and bars the board from recommending funding cuts or reducing pre-65 retiree charges until both funds are fully funded.

ky:HB 695.title: AN ACT relating to the Medicaid program and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 695.summary: Requires legislative authorization before the Cabinet changes Medicaid eligibility, coverage or benefits, makes the community engagement waiver mandatory, creates a Medicaid Oversight and Advisory Board, reinstates behavioral health prior authorization rules as of January 1, 2020, and requires new managed care contracts by 2027.

ky:HB 710.title: AN ACT relating to licensees authorized to prescribe or dispense controlled substances.
ky:HB 710.summary: Removes the requirement that licensees and applicants convicted of a felony relating to prescribing or dispensing a controlled substance be permanently barred from licensure.

ky:HB 757.title: AN ACT relating to revenue measures and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 757.summary: Updates the sales tax standard for remote retailers, sunsets state tax increment financing programs, conforms to the federal tax code with exceptions, taxes fantasy contest providers and data brokering services, and sets cash rounding rules.

ky:HB 775.title: AN ACT relating to fiscal matters.
ky:HB 775.summary: Makes tax and incentive changes: lets the income tax rate fall in smaller steps from 2028, taxes cannabis-infused beverages, extends training incentives to 2037, adds tourism project incentives, and requires electronic filing by certain brewers.

ky:HB 85.title: AN ACT relating to sanitation districts.
ky:HB 85.summary: Sets controls on fees and charges sanitation districts may impose, lets people sue if charged for a service not provided within a five-year plan, and limits stormwater charges to properties within 1,000 feet of the stormwater improvement and inside a city under a co-permittee agreement.

ky:HB 904.title: AN ACT relating to gaming.
ky:HB 904.summary: Requires online gaming operators to deny accounts to people on a child support arrearage registry, sets licensing and fee rules for fantasy contest providers and an age-18 minimum for participants, and lets lottery and racing regulators issue regulations without the Governor's signature.

ky:HB 96.title: AN ACT relating to the postsecondary education working group and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 96.summary: Requires the five members each legislative chamber appoints to the postsecondary education working group to reflect party proportions in that chamber, and requires the group to convene every four calendar years beginning in 2026.

ky:HJR 30.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION authorizing the release of funds.
ky:HJR 30.summary: Authorizes the State Budget Director to release part of the money appropriated for 2024-25 and 2025-26 for the water and wastewater assistance fund for troubled or economically restrained systems, for certain projects.

ky:HJR 50.title: A JOINT RESOLUTION directing the Auditor of Public Accounts to study the applicable statutes, administrative regulations, and agency policies and processes that directly impact the opening and operation of licensed and certified child care services in the Commonwealth.
ky:HJR 50.summary: Directs the Auditor of Public Accounts to hire a vendor to study laws, regulations and agency policies affecting opening and operating licensed child care, with findings due to the Legislative Research Commission by December 1, 2027.

ky:SB 1.title: AN ACT relating to education.
ky:SB 1.summary: Changes duties of school boards and superintendents in the Jefferson County district: sets five-year strategic plans, requires board approval of three-year revenue and expense projections, caps superintendent transfers without board approval at $250,000 per quarter, and removes the limit on board meeting frequency.

ky:SB 100.title: AN ACT relating to the Energy Planning and Inventory Commission and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 100.summary: Attaches the Energy Planning and Inventory Commission administratively to the University of Kentucky Center for Applied Energy Research while keeping its independence, gives its executive director authority over staff and contracts, and lets the director intervene in Public Service Commission cases.

ky:SB 101.title: AN ACT relating to children.
ky:SB 101.summary: Requires local boards to expel students in grades 6 to 12 for at least 12 months for assaulting school personnel without just cause, requires employees to report intentional assaults to law enforcement unless a disability interfered, and sets misdemeanor penalties for failing to report.

ky:SB 152.title: AN ACT relating to education.
ky:SB 152.summary: Moves school-based decision making council duties to advisory councils and principals, has the advisory council give a nonbinding nomination for principal to the superintendent, requires principals to report annually to the local board, and lets local boards adopt a human sexuality curriculum.

ky:SB 154.title: AN ACT relating to elections.
ky:SB 154.summary: Removes Social Security cards and public benefits cards, which carry no photograph, from the documents a voter lacking required photo identification may use to establish identity.

ky:SB 173.title: AN ACT relating to legislative oversight of the Medicaid state plan and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 173.summary: Creates an annual legislative review process for the Medicaid state plan and the Kentucky Children's Health Insurance Program state plan.

ky:SB 183.title: AN ACT relating to the fiduciary duties owed to the state-administered retirement systems.
ky:SB 183.summary: Requires proxy advisers contracted with state retirement systems to document an economic analysis before voting on, or recommending a vote on, a shareholder proposal against the company board's recommendation.

ky:SB 195.title: AN ACT relating to participants in the legal system.
ky:SB 195.summary: Sets a rebuttable presumption that contractors followed plans once a highway project is accepted and limits their liability, sets a rebuttable presumption that unlawful driving substantially caused injuries claimed against contracting parties, and extends Safe at Home to prosecutors and public defenders.

ky:SB 198.title: AN ACT relating to operations in the Office of the Attorney General.
ky:SB 198.summary: Sets a 10-year limit on actions by the Attorney General, lets anyone submit an affidavit to the Attorney General that a judge cannot impartially preside, and limits fees and solicitation by people assisting with veterans' benefits claims.

ky:SB 199.title: AN ACT relating to pesticide labeling.
ky:SB 199.summary: Deems a pesticide registered with the Department of Agriculture or EPA and bearing an EPA-approved master label to carry sufficient warning in civil actions over a duty to warn.

ky:HB 495.title: AN ACT relating to healthcare services and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 495.summary: Bars Medicaid funds, unless federal law requires, for cross-sex hormones above amounts a healthy person of the same age and sex normally produces, and for gender reassignment surgery; voids Executive Order 2024-632 (on conversion therapy) and similar orders or regulations through January 1, 2028.

ky:HB 526.title: AN ACT relating to members of the bar.
ky:HB 526.summary: Bars requiring a lawyer to join or pay dues to any association beyond admission and discipline fees, absent annual written consent; repeals KRS 21A.160 on Supreme Court control of the state bar while restating the Court's power to govern the bar, effective July 1, 2027.

ky:HB 667.title: AN ACT relating to solid waste management service companies.
ky:HB 667.summary: Bars counties, waste management districts and those acting for them from compelling, requesting, acquiring, reviewing or possessing solid waste companies' confidential business information; exempts it from open records disclosure; and requires securing and returning or destroying it if obtained in violation.

ky:SB 132.title: AN ACT relating to the recruitment and retention of health care professionals and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 132.summary: Lets health care professionals and institutions refuse to participate in services that violate their conscience, bars discrimination and liability for doing so, limits sanctions by hiring and licensing authorities for First Amendment-protected speech, and creates a civil cause of action for those injured by violations.

ky:SB 151.title: AN ACT relating to prohibited uses of state tax dollars.
ky:SB 151.summary: Bars use of state tax dollars appropriated by the General Assembly to pay foreign nationals unlawfully in the U.S. for goods or services provided to a governmental entity or other person; directs the Office of Homeland Security to help enforce it.

md:HB 10.title: Legal Advertisement or Legal Notice - Publication in Newspaper or Newspaper in General Circulation - Digital Newspapers
md:HB 10.summary: Expands which publications count as a "newspaper" for legal notices to include print and digital or digital-only outlets covering local news in more than three counties. Digital publishers must keep a public archive of notices and be accessible in the relevant county or municipality.

md:HB 1016.title: Labor and Employment - Noncompete and Conflict of Interest Clauses - Employer Workforce Relocation and Out-of-State Employers
md:HB 1016.summary: Voids noncompete and conflict-of-interest clauses when an employer with over 30 mostly Maryland-based employees at hire later lacks its principal place of business or a majority of its employees in the state. Applies only to contracts signed after the effective date.

md:HB 102.title: Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program - Revisions
md:HB 102.summary: Delays the Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program's contribution start to January 1, 2027, and benefit payments to a date between January 1, 2027 and January 3, 2028. Changes definitions and administration, and delays self-employed enrollment until regulations are adopted by July 1, 2028.

md:HB 1020.title: Consumer Protection - Credit Reporting - Medical Debt (Fair Medical Debt Reporting Act)
md:HB 1020.summary: Bars credit reporting agencies from including medical debt in consumer reports and bars using such information in credit decisions. Prohibits medical providers from reporting medical debt to agencies, and requires hospitals to ask agencies to delete previously reported adverse information by November 1, 2025.

md:HB 1026.title: Business Regulation - Rounding Cash Transactions - Authorization
md:HB 1026.summary: Allows merchants to round cash transaction prices to the nearest five cents, rounding 1, 2, 6 and 7 cents down and 3, 4, 8 and 9 cents up. Exempts up to two cents of rounding from sales tax and overrides conflicting local rules.

md:HB 103.title: Consumer Protection - Consumer Contracts - Prohibited Waivers
md:HB 103.summary: Prohibits consumer contracts from waiving or limiting legal remedies authorized by federal or state law, though recovery of statutory or punitive damages may be capped at applicable insurance coverage limits. Applies only to future contracts and takes effect no earlier than October 1, 2026.

md:HB 1032.title: Baltimore City and Montgomery County - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems - Authorization MC 4-25
md:HB 1032.summary: Authorizes stop sign cameras in school zones in Baltimore City and Montgomery County through June 30, 2029. Vehicles recorded running stop signs face civil penalties up to $40 unless the driver was cited by police. Requires implementation reports.

md:HB 1037.title: Energy Resource Adequacy and Planning Act
md:HB 1037.summary: Creates a Strategic Energy Planning Office, funded by assessments on public service companies. Requires it to submit a wholesale energy markets and bulk power system risk report to the Governor and General Assembly by September 1, 2028, and every three years after.

md:HB 1042.title: Health Occupations - Structural Racism Training - Funding Sources
md:HB 1042.summary: States the General Assembly's intent that the structural racism training required for health occupation license renewal be developed and offered at no cost to the State, using external funding such as a grant to the Maryland Nurses Association.

md:HB 1045.title: Health Insurance, Family Planning Services, and Confidentiality of Medical Records - Consumer Protections - Updates
md:HB 1045.summary: Updates Maryland health insurance and family planning references to federal law. Adds gender-affirming care to the definitions of legally protected health care and sensitive health services for disclosure purposes. Gives the Insurance Commissioner and Commission on Civil Rights concurrent jurisdiction over health insurance discrimination.

md:HB 1046.title: Mechanical Repair Contracts - Technical Service Bulletins
md:HB 1046.summary: Prohibits mechanical repair contracts from excluding coverage solely for an issue identified in a vehicle manufacturer's technical service bulletin. Bars providers from denying a claim solely because the diagnosed issue appears in such a bulletin.

md:HB 1058.title: Youth Delinquency Prevention Fund - Establishment
md:HB 1058.summary: Creates the Youth Delinquency Prevention Fund, administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, to give grants to community programs, including youth service bureaus, for delinquency, youth suicide and substance use prevention and youth development.

md:HB 1048.title: Public Health - Chain Restaurants - Sodium and Added Sugars Warning Icons and Disclosure and Notice
md:HB 1048.summary: Requires chain restaurants, from January 1, 2027, to mark menu items with at least 1,150 mg of sodium or 25 grams of added sugar with warning icons, plus a notice that full nutrition information is available. Sets penalties; the health department writes rules.

md:HB 1061.title: State-Owned Property - Inventory and Disposition - Housing
md:HB 1061.summary: Requires the state to inventory all state-owned property for suitability for affordable or mixed-use housing and to develop proposals to donate or sell excess property for housing, prioritizing affordable housing. Requires the housing department to set housing construction goals by December 31, 2030.

md:HB 1067.title: Hunting - Lead and Lead-Based Ammunition - Phase-Out
md:HB 1067.summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to mandate nonlead ammunition for hunting all game by July 1, 2030, except where nonlead ammunition is not commercially available for a specific firearm. Sets a civil fine up to $750 for a first offense.

md:HB 1069.title: Election Law - Absentee Ballots - State and Federal Requirements
md:HB 1069.summary: Writes absentee ballot timeliness rules into statute. If federal law or courts set different deadlines for federal contests, requires counting nonfederal votes on ballots meeting state rules and notice to voters. Requires elections officials to call internet-delivered ballots "print-at-home ballots."

md:HB 1070.title: Department of Social and Economic Mobility - Workforce Opportunities Grant Program and Fund
md:HB 1070.summary: Creates a Workforce Opportunities Grant Program in the Department of Social and Economic Mobility, with competitive grants for job fairs and workforce events. Requires at least $500,000 in the Governor's budget for each of fiscal 2028 through 2030. Ends September 30, 2031.

md:HB 1076.title: Higher Education Institutions - Over-the-Counter Contraception - Access and Reporting
md:HB 1076.summary: Requires public four-year colleges and community colleges to report annually on campus over-the-counter contraception access, beginning September 1, 2026. Requires community colleges to give students access to all over-the-counter methods. The higher education commission reports to the legislature each October 1.

md:HB 1078.title: Prince George's County - Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters - Mandated Appropriation
md:HB 1078.summary: Requires the Governor to budget at least $200 million for site redevelopment and transportation improvements tied to relocating FBI headquarters to Prince George's County, if the federal General Services Administration applies for a related permit.

md:HB 1082.title: Health Insurance - Individual Market Stabilization - Establishment of the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program
md:HB 1082.summary: Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to create a State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program for individual-market plans, targeting people whose federal premium contribution percentages rise in 2026 and 2027 compared with 2025. Ends June 30, 2028, subject to a contingent termination provision.

md:HB 1085.title: Housing Authorities - Tax-Exempt Status - Modifications
md:HB 1085.summary: Extends a property tax exemption for nonprofit entities created by public housing authorities, now limited to Baltimore City, Howard County and Montgomery County, to such entities statewide. Applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.

md:HB 1098.title: Insurance - Automobile Insurance - Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund and Affordability Study
md:HB 1098.summary: Requires the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund to report risk-based capital like other insurers, keep capital above a set threshold, and use prior-approval rate changes in specified circumstances. Creates an Insurance Administration workgroup on auto insurance affordability, reporting by January 1, 2026.

md:HB 1104.title: Md Department of Health - AHEAD Model Implementation - Electronic Health Care Transactions and Population Health Improvement Fund
md:HB 1104.summary: Creates a Population Health Improvement Fund for the state's AHEAD health care model, which the Health Services Cost Review Commission may credit with a uniform amount assessed in hospital rates. Clarifies that electronic health care transaction data may support the model.

md:HB 1108.title: Labor and Employment - Greenhouse Workers - Collective Bargaining and Heat Protection
md:HB 1108.summary: Gives greenhouse workers collective bargaining rights, enforced through the Public Employee Relations Board. Requires employers to give paid rest breaks of at least five minutes per hour when the indoor heat index reaches 90 degrees Fahrenheit.

md:HB 1109.title: Public Health Reform Act
md:HB 1109.summary: Changes the membership, duties and staffing of the Commission on Public Health and extends its end date. Requires the health department to organize a Medical Reserve Corps, creates a Public Health Workforce Development Fund, and changes rules for local health departments.

md:HB 1090.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Maryland College Aid Processing System - Applications
md:HB 1090.summary: Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to add a question to the state financial aid application, by August 1, 2025, asking whether the applicant missed a meal in the past six months because of cost. Answering "yes" is not required for eligibility.

md:HB 1123.title: Correctional Services - Medical and Elder Parole
md:HB 1123.summary: Repeals gubernatorial approval of medical parole for people serving life terms and changes how the Parole Commission evaluates medical parole. Creates elder parole hearings for people 60 or older who served 20 or more years, with no recent major infractions.

md:HB 1135.title: Health Occupations - Pharmacists - Vaccination Orders
md:HB 1135.summary: Lets pharmacists order a vaccine for anyone age three or older without administering it. For patients under 18, requires pharmacists to tell the patient and caregiver about pediatric primary care visits and refer them to a pediatric provider when appropriate.

md:HB 114.title: Pesticide and Pest Control - Revisions to Pesticide Applicator's Law and Repeal of Obsolete Provisions
md:HB 114.summary: Ends commercial use of restricted-use pesticides by noncertified individuals under a certified applicator's supervision. Adds requirements for noncertified individuals applying restricted-use pesticides privately under a certified private applicator. Repeals provisions on cyclodiene termiticides and tributyltin antifouling paint.

ma:S2581.title: An Act to promote student learning and mental health
ma:S2581.summary: Requires each district to have a policy prohibiting student use of personal electronic devices during the school day, with exceptions for disability, health and emergencies, and to teach social media risks. Bars social media accounts for under-14s, and for ages 14-15 without parental consent.

ma:S3104.title: RESOLUTIONS RESPONDING TO THE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT’S ORDER OF MAY 7, 2026, AND ENHANCING GOVERNMENT TRANSPARENCY
ma:S3104.summary: Resolves that the Senate will voluntarily give the State Auditor records for four requests covering fiscal 2021-2024 budgets, audits, balance-forward transactions and settlements, without conceding the Senate may be audited, and reserves its right to object to any audit.

me:LD 1227.title: An Act to Repeal the Requirement That Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Equip Vehicles with a Standardized Data Access Platform
me:LD 1227.summary: As introduced, repeals the law requiring motor vehicle manufacturers to equip vehicles with a standardized data access platform.

me:LD 1255.title: An Act to Ensure In-state Tuition for Postsecondary Students Who Are Registered to Vote in the State and to Amend Eligibility Requirements for the Free Community College Tuition Program
me:LD 1255.summary: As introduced, treats students registered to vote in Maine as residents eligible for in-state tuition at any postsecondary institution offering it, and adds a free community college condition of Maine high school graduation or 2 years' residency before enrollment.

me:LD 1376.title: An Act to Increase the Acceptable Level of Alcohol in a Low-alcohol Spirits Product and to Increase Availability of Those Products
me:LD 1376.summary: As introduced, raises the maximum alcohol content of a low-alcohol spirits product from 8% to 15% by volume, lets malt liquor licensees sell it for on- and off-premises consumption, and lets in-state malt liquor wholesalers distribute it.

me:LD 1710.title: An Act Regarding the Authority to Transport Prisoners Confined in Jail and the Use of Physical Force with Respect to Prisoners and Persons Who Have Been Arrested
me:LD 1710.summary: As introduced, authorizes corrections and transport officers to transport prisoners to and from court and rewrites the law on officers' use of force in corrections. The minority amendment adds in-service training for officers who transport inmates; without it, force is not justified.

me:LD 1776.title: An Act to Establish the Interdisciplinary Advisory Board for the State House Complex
me:LD 1776.summary: As introduced, creates the Interdisciplinary Advisory Board for the State House Complex to work on occupational health and safety in the complex and to streamline communication among the Legislative Council, its facilities committee and the Bureau of General Services.

me:LD 1803.title: An Act to Amend the Laws Governing Optometric Practice
me:LD 1803.summary: As introduced, includes certain ophthalmic surgeries in the practice of optometry for optometrists meeting board credentialing, adds hydrocodone combination products to drugs optometrists may dispense, and removes language barring drug administration by injection or intravenously.

me:LD 1815.title: An Act to Require a Blood Test for Drugs for Drivers Involved in a Motor Vehicle Accident That Results in Serious Bodily Injury or Death
me:LD 1815.summary: As introduced, requires a driver to take a drug blood test when there is probable cause that a crash caused death or serious injury and the driver was drug-impaired; refusal brings a one-year license suspension, lifted if the driver shows no impairment or no negligence.

me:LD 2063.title: An Act to Clarify Activities Allowed Under the Natural Resources Protection Act
me:LD 2063.summary: As introduced, exempts hand planting of native and dune vegetation and certain corrective actions from Natural Resources Protection Act permits, and adds great ponds and some wildlife habitat to the Department of Environmental Protection's compensation program.

me:LD 2112.title: An Act to Authorize Municipalities to Form Community Choice Aggregation Programs to Procure Electricity
me:LD 2112.summary: Lets municipalities run community choice aggregation programs buying electricity for residential and small commercial customers, most of whom are enrolled automatically unless they opt out. Plans need approval by local voters, the municipal governing body and the Public Utilities Commission.

me:LD 2187.title: An Act to Update Certain Water Quality Standards and to Reclassify Certain Waters of the State
me:LD 2187.summary: Updates water quality standards and reclassifies some waters as the Board of Environmental Protection recommended. The minority amendment also upgrades the Androscoggin River from Gulf Island Pond Dam in Auburn to Worumbo Dam in Lisbon Falls from Class C to Class B in 2027.

me:LD 530.title: An Act Regarding Occupational Licensing Reform
me:LD 530.summary: Eliminates the rebuttable presumption that a bar applicant convicted as an adult of a crime punishable by a year or more in prison lacks the good moral character required for admission.

me:LD 682.title: An Act to Amend Certain Laws Regarding Abortions
me:LD 682.summary: As introduced, adds race, marital status and education to required abortion reports, allows post-viability abortions only when medically necessary for the mother's life or health or for a fatal fetal anomaly, and restores criminal penalties for unlicensed or post-viability abortions.

me:LD 855.title: An Act to Limit Eligibility Under the Maine Clean Election Act
me:LD 855.summary: As introduced, limits participation as a Maine Clean Election Act candidate to once every 15 years for either house of the Legislature.

me:SP 10.title: JOINT RESOLUTION MAKING SEPARATE APPLICATIONS TO THE CONGRESS OF THE UNITED STATES CALLING ARTICLE V CONVENTIONS TO PROPOSE AMENDMENTS ESTABLISHING TERM LIMITS FOR MEMBERS OF CONGRESS AND TERM LIMITS FOR JUSTICES OF THE UNITED STATES SUPREME COURT
me:SP 10.summary: Applies to Congress to call two Article V conventions, one limited to term limits for U.S. House and Senate members and one to staggered 18-year term limits for U.S. Supreme Court justices.

me:SP 100.title: Joint Order, to Amend Joint Rule 215 to Remove the Requirement for a 2/3 Vote
me:SP 100.summary: Amends Joint Rule 215 to remove the requirement of a 2/3 vote in each chamber for items asking for a U.S. constitutional convention under Article V.

me:SP 726.title: Joint Order to Amend Joint Rule 308
me:SP 726.summary: Amends Joint Rule 308 on assigning bills to committees, adding a process for committee chairs and leads to recommend a change of committee reference before a public hearing is scheduled.

mi:HB 4001.title: Workforce opportunity wage act: amend sections 4 and 4b
mi:HB 4001.summary: Repeals the Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act and amends the 2014 wage act to set the minimum wage at $12.00 from Feb. 21, 2025, rising to $15.00 by Jan. 1, 2029, while keeping the tipped minimum wage at its current level.

mi:HB 4024.title: Require that certain educational institutions in this state, when providing students with multiple occupancy restrooms, changing areas, and similar facilities, do so in a manner that ensures each…
mi:HB 4024.summary: Creates the Student Restroom Privacy Act, requiring public educational institutions to have multiple-occupancy restrooms and changing areas used according to sex as listed on the original birth certificate, with exceptions such as custodial work, maintenance and medical assistance.

mi:HB 4027.title: Michigan zoning enabling act: amend section 205
mi:HB 4027.summary: As introduced, removes language making local zoning ordinances subject to state certification of large wind, solar and storage facilities, and removes the provision treating certain renewable energy projects with special land use approval as prior nonconforming uses.

mi:HB 4028.title: Clean and renewable energy and energy waste reduction act: amend the title and section 13
mi:HB 4028.summary: As introduced, repeals the part of the clean energy act creating a Michigan Public Service Commission certification process for large wind, solar and energy storage facilities, which generally preempts local zoning of those facilities.

mi:HB 4039.title: Administrative procedures act of 1969: amend section 39
mi:HB 4039.summary: Requires state agencies to rescind at least two existing rules for each new rule they propose, and bars the Office of Administrative Hearings and Rules from approving a rule-making request that does not list the rules to be rescinded.

mi:HB 4066.title: The revised school code: add section 1290.
mi:HB 4066.summary: Requires school districts, intermediate districts and charter schools in interscholastic athletics to designate teams as female, male or coeducational by sex on the original birth certificate, and bars them from knowingly letting males join teams designated female only.

mi:HB 4073.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend section 1602
mi:HB 4073.summary: Bars Department of Natural Resources employees from entering private property without the owner's or lessee's permission or a warrant, removes officers' warrantless search and entry powers, and states the open fields doctrine does not apply to them.

mi:HB 4141.title: The revised school code: add section 1303a; and to repeal acts and parts of acts.
mi:HB 4141.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt a policy banning student phone use during instructional time, and also during breaks, lunch and recess for elementary and middle school students, with exemptions such as medical, school-issued and instructional devices.

wi:AB 66.title: Relating to: dismissing or amending certain criminal charges and deferred prosecution agreements for certain crimes.
wi:AB 66.summary: Requires court approval for prosecutors to dismiss or amend charges for domestic abuse, auto theft, sexual assault, crimes against children, certain firearm possession and reckless driving causing great bodily harm, and bars deferred prosecution agreements for those crimes.

wi:AB 662.title: Relating to: prohibiting state contracting with certain business entities and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 662.summary: Bars state agencies from contracting with businesses headquartered or incorporated in China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia or Maduro-led Venezuela, their subsidiaries, or sellers of their products; requires contractor certification and sets forfeitures of at least $250,000.

wi:AB 683.title: Relating to: prohibiting critical telecommunications infrastructure from including equipment manufactured by a foreign adversary.
wi:AB 683.summary: Bars state agencies and other operators from contracts or technology giving foreign-adversary-linked entities access to critical infrastructure, bars telecom providers from using FCC-banned equipment (removal, annual certification, fines), and bars foreign nationals from contributing to referendum committees.

wi:AB 737.title: Relating to: financing certain infrastructure by special charge approved by a neighborhood improvement district.
wi:AB 737.summary: Lets a municipality create a neighborhood improvement district, petitioned by all taxable property owners in it, that can request a special assessment on its properties to fund infrastructure for residential development.

wi:AB 75.title: Relating to: Department of Justice collection and reporting of certain criminal case data.
wi:AB 75.summary: Requires the Department of Justice to collect criminal case data from state courts, including charges, prosecutors, bail decisions, plea offers, dismissals and convictions, report it annually, and keep a searchable public database for 10 years.

wi:AB 840.title: Relating to: certain requirements related to data centers.
wi:AB 840.summary: Sets rules for large data centers (over 100 megawatts of demand or 20 gigawatt-hours of use): bars shifting their utility costs to other customers, requires renewable plants serving them to be on site, limits cooling water, and requires annual water reports and a reclamation bond.

wi:AB 870.title: Relating to: adopting changes to the federal Internal Revenue Code for state tax purposes and modifying administrative rules related to such changes.
wi:AB 870.summary: Conforms Wisconsin income and franchise tax law to the federal Internal Revenue Code as of December 31, 2025, changes charging-order rules for creditors of limited liability company members, and requires local government employees who operate heavy equipment on highway improvements to hold a state license.

wi:AB 878.title: Relating to: a tax credit for certain sales and use taxes paid on services sold through an amusement device.
wi:AB 878.summary: Creates an income and franchise tax credit for Milwaukee County and municipal sales taxes, and premier resort area taxes, paid on taxable services purchased through amusement devices.

wi:AB 91.title: Relating to: the requirement that first class cities and first class city school districts place school resource officers in schools.
wi:AB 91.summary: Requires Milwaukee Public Schools and the City of Milwaukee to split the cost of at least 25 school resource officers 50-50, agree on implementation within 30 days, and jointly certify compliance to the Joint Committee on Finance.

wi:AB 961.title: Relating to: warning labels for explicit content, creating an explicit content label warning surcharge, making an appropriation, and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 961.summary: Requires distributors of explicit content on digital platforms to show a warning label covering two-thirds of the screen for at least 10 seconds or until acknowledged, and to add metadata; sets forfeitures up to $2,500 per initial violation, enforced by the Department of Justice.

wi:AB 962.title: Relating to: app stores and app developers and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 962.summary: Requires app stores to verify users' age categories, link minors' accounts to a parent account, and get verifiable parental consent before a minor downloads or buys an app; sets duties for app developers; allows civil actions with forfeitures up to $7,500 per violation.

wi:AB 963.title: Relating to: social media accounts for minors and providing a penalty.
wi:AB 963.summary: Requires social media platforms with $1 billion or more in annual revenue to estimate users' ages, obtain parental consent for minors' accounts, default minors to private settings, and bar addictive features such as infinite scroll and autoplay for minors.

wi:AB 996.title: Relating to: contributions by the Department of Financial Institutions to Trump accounts.
wi:AB 996.summary: Requires the Department of Financial Institutions to contribute $1,000 to the Trump account of a child born and living in Wisconsin whose account received the federal Treasury payment, to the extent funds are available.

wi:AB 997.title: Relating to: funding for the Department of Financial Institutions for contributions to Trump accounts and making an appropriation.
wi:AB 997.summary: Makes the Department of Financial Institutions appropriation for contributions to Trump accounts (created in companion bill AB 996) a sum-sufficient appropriation; takes effect only if AB 996 is enacted.

wi:SB 106.title: Relating to: psychiatric residential treatment facilities, providing an exemption from emergency rule procedures, and granting rule-making authority.
wi:SB 106.summary: Allows the Department of Health Services to certify psychiatric residential treatment facilities for people under 21 and makes their services a Medical Assistance benefit, subject to federal approval.

wi:SB 108.title: Relating to: sharing minors’ safety plans.
wi:SB 108.summary: Requires the Department of Health Services to maintain a statewide portal for sharing safety plans, written in advance for minors at risk of a behavioral health crisis, among designated safety plan partners, using a standard template.

wi:SB 11.title: Relating to: allowing representatives of certain federally chartered youth membership organizations to provide information to pupils on public school property.
wi:SB 11.summary: Allows federally chartered youth membership organizations, such as Scout groups, to ask a public school's governing body to let them give information to pupils during the school day; the governing body or its designee may schedule a date and time, starting in 2026-27.

wi:SB 111.title: Relating to: transportation of minors for emergency detention.
wi:SB 111.summary: Makes the county that approves a minor's emergency detention responsible for transporting the minor to the facility and for the cost, and lets counties contract with law enforcement, ambulance services or private vendors.

wi:SB 146.title: Relating to: prohibiting persons who have been convicted of a violent crime from changing their name and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 146.summary: Bars people convicted of a violent felony, such as homicide, battery, kidnapping, stalking, human trafficking or sexual assault, from changing their name; violation is a Class H felony.

wi:SB 179.title: Relating to: applying the motor vehicle fuel tax supplier’s administrative allowance to diesel fuel, a motor vehicle fuel tax refund for evaporation losses, and making an appropriation.
wi:SB 179.summary: Lets motor fuel suppliers keep the 1.35 percent administrative allowance on diesel fuel tax, as for gasoline, lets retailers claim a refund of 0.5 percent of fuel tax paid for evaporation and shrinkage, and credits wholesaler distributors for the resulting tax reduction.

wi:SB 182.title: Relating to: emergency medical services education, tuition and materials reimbursement for emergency medical responders and emergency medical services practitioners, and a live 911 pilot program.
wi:SB 182.summary: Requires grants to technical colleges for emergency medical services courses, a Higher Educational Aids Board program reimbursing tuition and materials for initial EMS certification, and a pilot program funding live video communication with 911 centers.

wi:SB 184.title: Relating to: governmental restrictions based on the energy source of a motor vehicle or other device.
wi:SB 184.summary: Bars state agencies and local governments from restricting the use or sale of a motor vehicle or other device based on the energy source that powers it.

wi:SB 25.title: Relating to: court-issued criminal complaints in officer-involved deaths.
wi:SB 25.summary: Bars courts from issuing a criminal complaint against an officer in an officer-involved death after the district attorney found no basis to prosecute, unless new or previously unused evidence is presented.

wi:SB 270.title: Relating to: the right of appeal for complainants aggrieved by decisions of the Elections Commission concerning the conduct of election officials.
wi:SB 270.summary: Provides that a person who files an Elections Commission complaint may appeal in court whenever the commission dismisses it or denies the requested relief, whether or not the person suffered a legally recognized injury.

wi:SB 275.title: Relating to: statements of scope for administrative rules.
wi:SB 275.summary: Requires agencies to say in each rule scope statement whether it covers an emergency or permanent rule, limits each to one rule, and makes emergency rule scope statements expire after six months.

wi:SB 279.title: Relating to: grants to law enforcement agencies for data-sharing platforms.
wi:SB 279.summary: Requires the Department of Justice to award grants to law enforcement agencies to acquire data-sharing platforms that meet set criteria, such as real-time integration of common law enforcement data, removal of duplicate records and limits on who can access information.

wi:SB 371.title: Relating to: explaining pregnancy, prenatal development, and childbirth as part of a human growth and development instructional program.
wi:SB 371.summary: Requires school boards that teach about pregnancy in a human growth program to include, when age appropriate, a high-definition fetal ultrasound video, a week-by-week animation of fetal development and a presentation on each trimester, plus infant mental health and reading to young children.

wi:SB 384.title: Relating to: requirements for children born alive following abortion or attempted abortion and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 384.summary: Requires health care providers to give a child born alive after an abortion or attempt the same care as any child of that age and have it taken to a hospital, with felony penalties, and makes intentionally killing such a child a life-sentence felony.

wi:SB 394.title: Relating to: damage or graffiti to certain historical property and providing a penalty.
wi:SB 394.summary: Makes it a Class I felony to damage or graffiti any structure, plaque, statue, painting or other monument of commemorative or historical significance on public property or maintained by the state, a county or a municipality.

wi:SB 41.title: Relating to: school safety grants and making an appropriation.
wi:SB 41.summary: Requires the Office of School Safety in the Department of Justice to run a competitive grant program for public, private and tribal schools to improve building safety and train staff, with a $20,000 maximum award, and no grants after June 30, 2027.

wi:SB 467.title: Relating to: local wheel tax referenda.
wi:SB 467.summary: Requires approval by a majority of voters in a referendum at a regularly scheduled election for any municipal or county vehicle registration fee, including existing fees, which would need approval within 18 months.

ct:HB 8001.title: AN ACT CONCERNING THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT HEALTH CENTER JOINT VENTURE INITIATIVE.
ct:HB 8001.summary: Raises UConn 2000 bond authorizations by $390 million over five years and lets the money fund UConn Health Center subsidiaries or joint ventures to acquire, operate, and sell hospital systems; sale proceeds go to the General Fund.

ct:HB 8003.title: AN ACT CONCERNING TEMPORARY ADJUSTMENTS TO THE BUDGET RESERVE FUND AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS TO ADDRESS REDUCTIONS IN FEDERAL FUNDING.
ct:HB 8003.summary: Appropriates $500 million from the Budget Reserve Fund to the Office of Policy and Management to respond to federal funding cuts to WIC, SNAP, energy assistance, health care, school meals, child care and housing; legislative leaders may disapprove spending.

ct:SB 1453.title: AN ACT CONCERNING EMERGENCY NONPROFIT ASSISTANCE.
ct:SB 1453.summary: Moves $3 million from the General Fund to a new emergency nonprofit assistance account, if the April 2025 revenue statement shows a surplus, and awards grants of $62,500 to $800,000 to 24 named nonprofits plus $112,500 for administration.

ia:HF 1044.title: Relating to and making appropriations for state government administration and regulation, including the department of administrative services, auditor of state, ethics and campaign disclosure board, offices of governor and lieutenant governor, department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, department of insurance and financial services, department of management, Iowa public employees’ retirement system, public information board, department of revenue, secretary of state, treasurer of stat...
ia:HF 1044.summary: Appropriates money for fiscal year 2025-26 to state administration and regulation agencies, including Revenue, Secretary of State, Auditor and Insurance, and sends captive insurance premium taxes to the Captive Insurance Regulatory and Supervision Fund.

ia:HF 2102.title: Prohibiting the use of a language other than English for driver’s license examinations
ia:HF 2102.summary: Bars the Department of Transportation and third-party testers from using any language other than English to examine driver's license applicants, and removes driver's license examinations from the exceptions to Iowa's English-only rule for official documents.

ia:HF 2226.title: Relating to the bachelor of science in nursing program at the university of Iowa, including priority for admission and reporting requirements
ia:HF 2226.summary: Requires the Board of Regents to adopt policies that at least 70% of students accepted each year to the University of Iowa nursing bachelor's program be Iowa residents (defined as Iowa high school graduates) from fall 2027, give residents admission priority, and require annual reporting.

ia:HF 2244.title: Relating to social studies instruction provided to students enrolled in grades seven through twelve, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2244.summary: Requires at least one-half unit of civics and U.S. government in grade 7 or 8, raises the high school civics and U.S. government requirement from one-half to one unit, and applies the standards to charter and innovation zone schools, starting 2028-29.

ia:HF 2245.title: Relating to selection committees for presidents of regents institutions
ia:HF 2245.summary: Requires the Board of Regents to use a presidential selection committee, with five voting board members and four nonvoting members, to choose university presidents; candidate identities stay confidential unless all voting members agree to release them.

ia:HF 2246.title: Relating to education requirements, including continuing education requirements, for certain licensed professions
ia:HF 2246.summary: Bars licensing boards from requiring continuing education unrelated to the licensed profession, and directs the Iowa Supreme Court to do the same for attorneys and to drop the requirement of an ABA-accredited law school to sit for the bar exam.

ia:HF 2253.title: Relating to terminology involving a pregnant female
ia:HF 2253.summary: Changes the term "pregnant person" to "pregnant female" in Iowa Code provisions on crimes involving pregnant females.

ia:HF 2335.title: Relating to hunter education requirements
ia:HF 2335.summary: Lets people meet the hunter education requirement with an online course offered or approved by the DNR, accepts certifications from nationally recognized organizations, and makes an in-person field day optional.

ia:HF 2336.title: Relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the protected speech and expression rights of students enrolled in school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools and the duties of the department of education, and providing civil penalties
ia:HF 2336.summary: Bars school districts from penalizing students or student clubs for religious, political or ideological speech on the same terms as other students; requires annual distribution of federal prayer guidance; lets students sue districts, with a civil penalty of at least $5,000.

ia:HF 2361.title: Relating to general education requirements, core curricula, other functions of regents institutions, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2361.summary: Requires Regents universities to make undergraduates take introductory American history and American government courses (3+ credits each) for students enrolling from 2028-29, and sets up lecture and debate series at three civics centers.

ia:HF 2488.title: Prohibiting private institutions of higher education that participate in the Iowa tuition grant program from establishing diversity, equity, and inclusion offices
ia:HF 2488.summary: Bars private colleges in the Iowa tuition grant program from operating a diversity, equity and inclusion office; violations are reported to the attorney general, and colleges that neither correct nor rebut a report within 30 days lose tuition grant eligibility.

ia:HF 2510.title: Relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the social studies instruction provided to students enrolled in grades one through twelve and the educational programs provided by the institutions of higher education under the control of the state board of regents, and requiring education related to the holocaust for students and teachers in school districts
ia:HF 2510.summary: Sets required K-12 social studies content, requires grade 7-8 semester courses in civics, U.S. history and western civilization, sets high school units in those subjects, bars Regents credit for action civics or political activism courses, and bars use of the 2025 draft standards.

ia:HF 2527.title: Providing a limitation on civil or criminal liability for any alleged actual or potential effect on climate caused wholly or partly by a greenhouse gas emission
ia:HF 2527.summary: Bars civil and criminal liability for alleged climate effects of greenhouse gas emissions from agricultural, petroleum or renewable fuel sources, unless a court finds by clear and convincing evidence the defendant violated an emission statute or permit.

ia:HF 2529.title: Providing for the repair of a diesel exhaust fluid system that is part of farm equipment, and providing penalties
ia:HF 2529.summary: Requires farm equipment manufacturers to give owners and lessees the same diagnostic and repair information, parts and tools for diesel exhaust fluid systems that they give authorized repair providers; the attorney general enforces.

ia:HF 2539.title: Repealing certain programs and other matters relating to higher education
ia:HF 2539.summary: Repeals higher education programs and functions, including the College Bound Program, the Regents' Minority and Women Educators Enhancement Program, laboratory schools, and various purchasing, policy and reporting requirements.

ia:HF 2557.title: Allowing a person to raise, guide, and instruct a child in a manner consistent with the child’s sex
ia:HF 2557.summary: Exempts from the definition of child abuse raising a child consistent with the child's sex, including pronouns, mental health services and declining gender transition procedures, and adds similar language to foster licensing, custody, adoption and child endangerment provisions.

ia:HF 2584.title: Establishing drug-free homeless service zones, and providing penalties
ia:HF 2584.summary: Creates a crime of selling or transferring controlled substances within 300 feet of a homeless shelter or housing facility, adding a year to the sentence and barring probation. Makes it an aggravated misdemeanor for an operator to knowingly allow drug possession or use there.

ia:HF 2618.title: Eliminating the Iowa smart planning principles and other local comprehensive planning and development guidelines
ia:HF 2618.summary: As introduced, repeals the Iowa smart planning principles and the requirement that cities and counties consider them when developing or amending comprehensive plans and land development regulations.

ia:HF 2623.title: Relating to elections for school district and city officers, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2623.summary: As introduced, moves regular city and school district elections from odd-numbered to even-numbered years, on the November general election day, for elections held after November 2, 2027, and extends the terms of some current officers.

ia:HF 2640.title: Relating to the intentional emission of air contaminants into the atmosphere, including prohibitions and reporting requirements, and providing penalties
ia:HF 2640.summary: Prohibits releasing chemicals, substances, or apparatus into the atmosphere to affect temperature, weather, climate, or sunlight, or for any purpose not otherwise regulated by law. Makes it a class D felony, each day a separate offense, and exempts licensed aerial application of agricultural inputs.

ia:HF 2649.title: Establishing a pilot program that authorizes eligible community colleges to offer baccalaureate degrees
ia:HF 2649.summary: Creates a pilot program letting community colleges whose main campus is at least 50 miles from a regents or private university offering the same degree offer up to three bachelor's degrees, in listed fields tied to unmet workforce needs, with annual reports.

ia:HF 269.title: Prohibiting certain requirements for students and faculty at regents institutions relating to diversity, equity, inclusion, and critical race theory and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 269.summary: Bars regents universities from requiring students to take, or faculty to include or be trained in, diversity, equity, inclusion and critical race theory content as defined. Lets the regents exempt racial, ethnic and gender studies programs and the attorney general seek a court order.

ia:HF 2716.title: Relating to the supplemental nutrition assistance program; the medical assistance program; the special supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and children; and other public assistance programs under the purview of the department of health and human services
ia:HF 2716.summary: Directs the state to seek federal SNAP waivers on students' earned income, data verification, and benefit expungement; raises the Medicaid income limit for working people with disabilities to 300 percent of poverty; lets the state require 12 months of residency proof for public assistance.

ia:HF 2717.title: Relating to executive branch functions, including ratification of major administrative rules and certain other actions, other matters relating to the state rulemaking process, and terms of service of certain appointed members of certain boards, and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 2717.summary: Defines "major rules" (including those costing $1 million or more a year), expands the Administrative Rules Review Committee from 10 to 16 members and lets it delay rules for legislative approval, requires legislative ratification of Clean Air Act plan amendments, and changes some board terms.

ia:HF 2718.title: Relating to the seizure of firearms, providing penalties, and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 2718.summary: As introduced, bars state and local agencies from enforcing "red flag" laws and orders that seize firearms, or from taking federal money to do so, and makes an employing agency liable for officers' knowing violations, with a $50,000 civil penalty per occurrence.

ia:HF 295.title: Relating to accreditation of postsecondary educational institutions, prohibiting adverse action by accrediting agencies against certain postsecondary educational institutions for compliance with state law, providing remedies, and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 295.summary: As introduced, bars accrediting agencies from taking adverse action against public colleges for complying with state law, allows the attorney general to sue for damages and injunctions, and replaces Higher Learning Commission references in the Code with any federally recognized accreditor.

ia:HF 299.title: Relating to the provision of information relating to immunization exemptions
