ia:HF 299.summary: Requires information on immunization exemptions and their requirements in state vaccine recommendation communications, in school, child care and college communications about immunizations, and on school and child care websites and registration documents.

ia:HF 314.title: Authorizing the waiver of preplacement investigations and reports in certain adoption proceedings
ia:HF 314.summary: Lets a court waive the preplacement investigation and report in an adoption when the petitioner has been the child's legal guardian for the preceding 36 consecutive months and has complied with guardianship requirements, in addition to the current waiver for close relatives.

ia:HF 390.title: Relating to physical examinations of personnel working in licensed or registered child care facilities
ia:HF 390.summary: Lets child care facility staff get their initial physical exam within six months before or six months after starting work, with follow-up exams at least every three years from the initial exam.

ia:HF 395.title: Relating to approved courses of instruction for school bus drivers
ia:HF 395.summary: Requires school bus drivers to hold a commercial license with passenger and school bus endorsements, makes a state-approved driver course required only if the school district requires it, and counts federal entry-level driver training as an approved course.

ia:HF 398.title: Relating to the duties of the director of the department of corrections, the board of corrections, superintendents, and district directors
ia:HF 398.summary: Changes the Board of Corrections' role from approving to advising on the corrections director's budget, rules, and appointments of institution superintendents and district directors, and shifts some board duties to the director.

ia:HF 401.title: Providing for general education requirements for undergraduate students at regents institutions and including applicability provisions
ia:HF 401.summary: Requires regents universities to set general education requirements totaling at most 37 credit hours, including western and American heritage, and bars those courses from distorting historical events or teaching identity politics or that systemic racism or privilege is inherent in U.S. or Iowa institutions.

ia:HF 437.title: Establishing a center for intellectual freedom at the university of Iowa
ia:HF 437.summary: Establishes a center for intellectual freedom at the University of Iowa to teach and research ideas shaping the American constitutional order, offer free speech and civil discourse programming, and offer an American history and civil government course.

ia:HF 510.title: Relating to petitions for special elections to fill vacancies in city offices
ia:HF 510.summary: As introduced, lets a city council challenge in district court, within 10 days, a petition for a special election to fill a vacancy when under a year remains in the term; if the court finds an election unduly financially burdensome, the seat is filled by appointment.

ia:HF 522.title: Relating to the therapeutic classroom incentive program by authorizing the expenditure of moneys for certain nutritional items
ia:HF 522.summary: As introduced, adds to the support a therapeutic classroom may provide: vitamin and mineral supplements, whole foods such as eggs, full-fat dairy, beef and bacon, limits on artificial food additives, reduced screen use, and more natural light.

ky:SB 2.title: AN ACT relating to correctional facilities.
ky:SB 2.summary: Bars the use of public funds for cosmetic services or elective procedures for inmates, including cross-sex hormones and gender reassignment surgery, while letting a provider taper hormones if stopping at once would cause physical harm.

ky:SB 202.title: AN ACT relating to regulated beverages and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 202.summary: Creates licenses to distribute and sell cannabis-infused beverages (up to 5 mg of intoxicating cannabinoids per 12 oz), sold by the package to people 21 and older under the Alcoholic Beverage Control department, and makes other changes to alcohol licensing.

ky:SB 219.title: AN ACT relating to debts.
ky:SB 219.summary: Raises the cap on total proceeds from open payday (deferred deposit) loans from $500 to $600, adjustable yearly for inflation up to $850, and sets required contents for wage garnishment orders sent to employers.

ky:SB 224.title: AN ACT relating to land use.
ky:SB 224.summary: Gives applicants for building permits, development plans or subdivision plats a vested right to local development standards in effect on the application date, for set periods (up to 10 years, 15 if phased), with exceptions such as safety hazards.

ky:SB 245.title: AN ACT relating to the Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources Commission and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 245.summary: Requires a Fish and Wildlife Resources Commission member whose reappointment the Senate declines to confirm to vacate the seat when that legislative session adjourns.

ky:SB 251.title: AN ACT relating to the Department of Corrections.
ky:SB 251.summary: Lets the Department of Corrections set execution protocols and procedures by internal policy or memorandum rather than through administrative regulations.

ky:SB 257.title: AN ACT relating to the Office of the Auditor of Public Accounts.
ky:SB 257.summary: Creates an Office of Government Efficiency within the Auditor of Public Accounts to audit and review state agencies, lets the Auditor hire additional staff, and appropriates $4,861,500 in restricted funds for fiscal 2025-26.

ky:SB 262.title: AN ACT proposing an amendment to Section 256 of the Constitution of Kentucky relating to the submission of constitutional amendments to voters.
ky:SB 262.summary: Proposes amending Section 256 of the Kentucky Constitution so constitutional amendments can go to voters as a ballot question or summary of their substance and effect, rather than the full text appearing on the ballot.

ky:SB 278.title: AN ACT relating to the Department of Kentucky State Police.
ky:SB 278.summary: Requires the State Police commissioner to allow approved off-duty and secondary law enforcement work, including for public entities and ticketed events but not retail stores, weddings, private parties or businesses primarily selling alcohol for on-site consumption, and sets vehicle-use policies.

ky:SB 28.title: AN ACT relating to agricultural economic development and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 28.summary: Creates a six-member agricultural economic development board, chaired by the Agriculture Commissioner, to award grants and loans to agribusiness and alternative fuels projects, and directs the economic development cabinet to consult the Commissioner on such incentives.

ky:SB 291.title: AN ACT relating to recyclers and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 291.summary: Moves licensing of secondary metals recyclers and vehicle, machinery and material recyclers to the Motor Vehicle Commission, with annual renewal and background checks that bar licenses for recent theft or drug felony convictions for metals recyclers.

ky:SB 39.title: AN ACT relating to fish and wildlife and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 39.summary: Exempts private landowners from state fishing limits (creel, possession, size and method of take) and most stocking requirements for their own private lakes and ponds, defined as those not connected to or accessible by fish from public waters.

ky:SB 4.title: AN ACT relating to education and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 4.summary: Creates a four-year leadership program for new principals, cuts the Jefferson County school board from seven to five members with new election divisions, creates a Center of American Civics at UK, and makes UofL's McConnell Center an independent academic unit, among other changes.

ky:SB 41.title: AN ACT relating to the levy of an ad valorem tax rate.
ky:SB 41.summary: Sets separate property-tax recall rules: a school "nickel" tax (five cents) takes effect after 45 days unless voters petition, while other local rates raising revenue over 4% above the compensating rate are suspended until a voter election.

ky:SB 45.title: AN ACT relating to agritourism.
ky:SB 45.summary: Bars cities, counties and other local governments from restricting or unduly burdening agritourism activities that meet health, safety and zoning rules, and adds activities involving working animals to the definition of agritourism.

ky:SB 6.title: AN ACT relating to the Support Education Excellence in Kentucky Program.
ky:SB 6.summary: Counts state-paid teacher retirement and insurance (fringe benefit) costs in the school funding formula without distributing them to districts, and requires Department of Education reports to itemize each add-on in total and per pupil.

ky:SB 60.title: AN ACT relating to restoring religious liberty.
ky:SB 60.summary: Amends the state religious-freedom law to define "government action" and "substantially burden," apply it to existing and future laws, allow claims or defenses with attorney's fees, and waive governmental immunity under the section.

ky:SB 71.title: AN ACT relating to public library district boards of trustees.
ky:SB 71.summary: Changes how library district trustees are chosen: the library board recommends one person per vacancy directly to the county judge/executive, who with fiscal court approval may appoint that person or, if unacceptable, another, replacing state library department recommendations.

ky:SB 72.title: AN ACT relating to the recruitment and retention of health care professionals and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 72.summary: Allows health care professionals and institutions to refuse to take part in health services that violate their conscience, bars liability and discrimination for refusing, and bars retaliation for reporting violations; emergency treatment and sexual assault evidence duties remain.

ky:SB 75.title: AN ACT relating to concealed deadly weapons.
ky:SB 75.summary: Lowers from 21 to 18 the age to carry a concealed firearm or other deadly weapon without a license and to qualify for a concealed-carry license.

ky:SB 76.title: AN ACT relating to local occupational license fees and taxes.
ky:SB 76.summary: Raises from 300,000 to 500,000 the county population needed to authorize a school occupational tax rate above the 0.5% cap, by up to one-quarter of one percent, effective August 1, 2026.

ky:SB 77.title: AN ACT relating to ibogaine research in the Commonwealth.
ky:SB 77.summary: Creates an ibogaine research fund run by the Department of Agriculture to partner with a drug developer on clinical trials for opioid use disorder and other conditions, requiring matching funds, in-state trials and a state share of intellectual property proceeds.

ky:SB 79.title: AN ACT relating to state personnel.
ky:SB 79.summary: Bars state employees in all three branches from teleworking unless an emergency is declared, with exceptions and up to two telework days a month for some employees, and makes other changes to state personnel law.

ky:SB 8.title: AN ACT relating to public utilities and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 8.summary: Expands the Public Service Commission from three to five members (two attorneys, three with specified expertise) with Senate confirmation and four-year terms, makes it an independent department, and adds two commissioners to the electric siting board.

ky:SB 84.title: AN ACT relating to judicial review of state agency action.
ky:SB 84.summary: Bars courts from deferring to a state agency's interpretation of a statute or regulation, requires de novo review of agency legal interpretations, and bars agencies from interpreting the law expecting deference.

ky:SB 89.title: AN ACT relating to environmental protection and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 89.summary: Narrows the state definition of "waters of the Commonwealth" to federally defined navigable waters, open-throat sinkholes, certain springs and wellhead protection areas, and adds long-term water treatment financial assurance to coal mining bonds where required.

ma:H2026.title: Order relative to the adoption of permanent Joint Rules for the 194th General Court governing the 2025-2026 legislative sessions
ma:H2026.summary: Adopts the joint rules of the House and Senate for 2025-2026, covering joint committees, committee reporting deadlines and conference committee procedures.

ma:H5151.title: An Act relative to energy affordability, clean power and economic competitiveness
ma:H5151.summary: Requires the Department of Energy Resources to return at least 70% of alternative compliance payments to ratepayers in some years, creates an online utility bill dashboard, mandates discounted rates for low- and moderate-income customers, and orders an inspector general review of Mass Save.

ma:H5175.title: An Act relative to energy affordability, clean power and economic competitiveness
ma:H5175.summary: Restructures energy-efficiency programs into a statewide building decarbonization and energy efficiency investment plan, mandates discounted rates for low- and moderate-income customers, and sets management and operations audits of gas and electric distribution companies.

ma:H5469.title: An Act promoting transparency and public access in state government
ma:H5469.summary: Lets the State Auditor audit administrative functions of the House, Senate and joint legislative operations, sets a public-records process for legislative records, covers the governor's office under the public records law, and appropriates $250,000 each for implementation.

ma:H57.title: An Act making appropriations for fiscal year 2025 to provide for supplementing certain existing appropriations and for certain other activities and projects
ma:H57.summary: Appropriates $425 million for emergency shelter for homeless families, requires adult applicants to disclose criminal convictions and be checked against state records, and limits emergency housing assistance to six consecutive months with hardship extensions.

ma:H58.title: An Act making appropriations for fiscal year 2025 to provide for supplementing certain existing appropriations and for certain other activities and projects
ma:H58.summary: Appropriates $425 million for emergency shelter for homeless families, requires adult applicants to disclose convictions and pending serious charges, caps eligibility at six consecutive months with hardship waivers, and limits temporary respite stays to 30 days.

md:HB 303.title: Real Property - Regulation of Common Ownership Community Managers
md:HB 303.summary: Creates a State Board of Common Ownership Community Managers, appointed by the Governor within the Department of Labor, to regulate property management services for condominiums and homeowners associations. The board ends July 1, 2031 unless reestablished.

md:HB 324.title: County Boards of Education - Antibias Training for Members - Requirement (County Board Member Antibias Training Act)
md:HB 324.summary: Requires each county school board member to complete an antibias training program at least once during their term, delivered separately from the training given to school employees, starting July 1, 2025.

md:HB 33.title: Department of Service and Civic Innovation - Maryland Corps Program Service Year Option Pathways - Revisions
md:HB 33.summary: Changes Maryland Corps Program rules on participant reimbursement and eligibility, gives the Department of Service and Civic Innovation more flexibility in using program funds, and repeals the Executive Fellows Program.

md:HB 338.title: State Buildings and State Highways - Collection and Disposal of Yard Waste
md:HB 338.summary: Bars State employees and contractors from putting yard waste collected at State buildings and highways in single-use plastic containers, and requires it be taken to certain composting or mulching facilities when one is within 30 miles and able to accept it.

md:HB 343.title: Housing Development Projects - Housing Counseling Services
md:HB 343.summary: Requires recipients of certain State housing funds building or rehabilitating single-family homes for ownership to give prospective buyers information on HUD-certified housing counseling, and requires the Governor to appropriate $90,000 a year from fiscal 2028 for counseling partnerships.

md:HB 348.title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Safety Corridors
md:HB 348.summary: Allows the State Highway Administration to place speed cameras on highway segments designated safety corridors, with fine revenue first covering program costs and the rest going to the Transportation Trust Fund for highway safety and preservation.

md:HB 349.title: Prince George's County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Maryland Route 210 PG 306-25
md:HB 349.summary: Sets escalating speed camera penalties on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County, with maximum fines from $40 to $425 depending on how far over the limit a driver is.

md:HB 367.title: Health Occupations Boards - English Proficiency Requirements and Licensure by Endorsement for Nursing
md:HB 367.summary: Bars health occupations boards from requiring extra proof of English proficiency from applicants holding a valid, unrestricted license from another state that required such proof, and changes English proficiency rules for nursing and pharmacy boards and nursing licensure by endorsement.

md:HB 371.title: Prince George's County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Maryland Route 5 PG 308-25
md:HB 371.summary: Permanently authorizes speed cameras on Maryland Route 5 in Prince George's County; the county may recover program costs from fines and sends the rest to the State Highway Administration for highway and pedestrian safety improvements.

md:HB 380.title: Criminal Law - Prohibition on Sale of Contraceptives and Contraceptive Devices by Vending Machine in School - Repeal
md:HB 380.summary: Repeals the misdemeanor ban on selling contraceptives or contraceptive devices from vending machines at kindergarten, nursery, elementary, and secondary schools.

md:HB 382.title: Commercial Law - Broadband Access - Low-Income Consumer Programs (Maryland Broadband Opportunity and Fairness Act)
md:HB 382.summary: Requires broadband providers with 10,000 or more customers to report annually, starting November 15, 2027, to the Office of Statewide Broadband on the availability of a low-income consumer program.

md:HB 385.title: Consumer Protection - Automatic Tip Prompt Screen - Requirements
md:HB 385.summary: Requires businesses whose point-of-sale screens prompt for a tip to display a notice that the tip goes to employees and a zero or "no-tip" option, starting July 1, 2026, with exceptions for table or bar service and mobile or online purchases.

md:HB 39.title: Public Health - Repeal of Prohibition on Transfer of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (Carlton R. Smith Act)
md:HB 39.summary: Repeals the misdemeanor offense, punishable by up to three years in prison, a $2,500 fine, or both, of knowingly transferring or attempting to transfer HIV to another person.

md:HB 390.title: Affordable Housing Payment In Lieu of Taxes Expansion Act
md:HB 390.summary: Lets counties exempt rental housing from the county property tax if the owner keeps at least 25% of units affordable for at least 15 years under a payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement with the county.

md:HB 4.title: Restrictions on Use - Solar Collector Systems - Alteration
md:HB 4.summary: Changes when a restriction on solar panel installation is unreasonable: when it raises the system's cost by at least 5% or cuts its projected energy output by at least 10%, and sets what community associations may do about solar systems in common areas.

md:HB 40.title: Natural Resources - Fishing Licenses and Stamps - Alterations
md:HB 40.summary: Raises fees for senior sport fishing licenses, angler's licenses, and trout stamps, and ends the trout stamp exemption for senior sport fishing license holders.

md:HB 402.title: Common Ownership Communities - Oversight, Governing Document Database, and Local Commissions
md:HB 402.summary: Creates a Common Ownership Community Oversight Division in the housing department, requires associations to file governing documents for a public database, and sets rules for local common ownership commissions and dispute resolution.

md:HB 431.title: Civil Actions - Consumer Contracts - Limitations Periods
md:HB 431.summary: Makes void any consumer contract term that sets a shorter deadline to sue than State law otherwise allows, and makes a violation a violation of the Consumer Protection Act.

md:HB 432.title: Municipalities - Vagrancy - Repeal of Authority to Prohibit
md:HB 432.summary: Repeals the authority of Maryland municipalities to prohibit vagrancy.

md:HB 437.title: Transportation - Major Highway Capacity Expansion Projects and Impact Assessments (Transportation and Climate Alignment Act of 2026)
md:HB 437.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to assess greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle miles traveled for major highway expansion projects and to carry out multimodal programs and other activities to offset the emissions, starting July 1, 2026.

md:HB 451.title: Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council - Membership, Duties, and Sunset Repeal
md:HB 451.summary: Makes the Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council permanent by repealing its termination date, changes its membership and duties, and makes its annual report permanent.

md:HB 452.title: Outdoor Lighting - Guidance and Use of State Funds
md:HB 452.summary: Extends the ban on State funds for non-compliant outdoor lighting to State parks and trails, exempts sports field lighting, and caps color temperature at 3,000 Kelvin for State-funded lights other than those installed by the transportation department.

md:HB 467.title: Correctional Services - Maryland Parole Commission - Improvements in Transparency and Equity
md:HB 467.summary: Removes the Parole Commission's authority to permanently deny parole, entitles denied incarcerated people to later hearings at set intervals, and changes hearing, decision, recording, and appeal requirements.

md:HB 480.title: Transportation Network Companies - Deactivation of Operators
md:HB 480.summary: Requires transportation network companies such as ride-hailing services to keep and apply a written policy for deactivating drivers, including an internal appeal process, starting January 1, 2027.

md:HB 483.title: Business Regulation - Charitable Organizations - Audit and Review Thresholds
md:HB 483.summary: Raises the charitable contribution thresholds requiring an audit (from $750,000 to $1,000,000) or a review (from $300,000 to $400,000) with a charity's registration statement, starting July 1, 2026.

md:HB 490.title: Education - The Blueprint for Maryland's Future - Revisions
md:HB 490.summary: Changes Blueprint for Maryland's Future programs, including funding for low-income students, local flexibility in using concentration of poverty grants, teacher certification qualifications, the Expert Review Team program, and the educator career ladder.

md:HB 494.title: Health Insurance - Primary Care Investment Targets - Reimbursement and Reporting
md:HB 494.summary: Requires health insurers and HMOs to reimburse providers in ways that meet the State's annual primary care investment targets and to report their progress when filing premium rates.

md:HB 517.title: Workgroup on the Reorganization of the Maryland Transit Administration
md:HB 517.summary: Creates a workgroup to study reorganizing the Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland Transit Administration, reporting findings to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026, with draft legislation from the department.

md:HB 520.title: State Board of Physicians - Naturopathic Doctors - Scope of Practice, Renewals, and Professional Liability Insurance
md:HB 520.summary: Expands the scope of practice for naturopathic doctors to include prescribing and administering specified drugs and devices, repeals the formulary council, and adds grounds for discipline, with new notice duties on professional liability insurance.

md:HB 527.title: Maryland Transit Administration - Purple Line - Free Ridership and Promotional Materials and Services
md:HB 527.summary: Requires the Maryland Transit Administration to offer free Purple Line rides for the first month to residents within a quarter mile of the line, and free promotional help to nearby small businesses beginning October 1, 2025.

md:HB 53.title: Criminal Law - Nondomesticated Animal Prohibitions - Alterations
md:HB 53.summary: Adds zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies to Maryland's list of banned nondomesticated animals, with an exception for current owners, shortens a nonresident travel exception to 48 hours, and removes the exception for assistance animals for people with severe mobility disabilities.

md:HB 541.title: Department of Commerce - Nonprofit Organizations Navigator - Established
md:HB 541.summary: Establishes a nonprofit organizations navigator in the Department of Commerce to represent nonprofits on the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council, with the position ending June 30, 2027.

md:HB 543.title: Real Property - Landlord and Tenant - Family Child Care Homes
md:HB 543.summary: Bars landlords of single-family homes from preventing tenants from operating a family child care home, with exceptions, while allowing a security deposit up to two months' rent and preserving local zoning authority.

md:HB 578.title: Fish and Wildlife - Endangered and Threatened Species and Migratory Birds - Regulations, Lists, Petitions, Essential Habitats, and Takings
md:HB 578.summary: Changes Maryland's endangered and threatened species laws: defines "foreseeable future" and "harm," lets areas be designated essential habitats, requires authorization to take black vultures if federal protection ends, and requires review of Irreplaceable Natural Areas rules by July 1, 2033 and every 10 years.

md:HB 579.title: Criminal Procedure - U Nonimmigrant Status Petitions and Immigration Enforcement at Sensitive Locations
md:HB 579.summary: Changes the U visa certification process for crime victims: lets victims' attorneys or advocates request certification, shortens response deadlines, and requires written explanations for denials. Also requires federal officers to notify state or local officials of immigration enforcement actions at sensitive locations.

md:HB 592.title: Prohibited Possession of Firearms - Assisted Outpatient Treatment Respondents
md:HB 592.summary: Bars a person from possessing a regulated firearm, rifle or shotgun while subject to a court order to follow an assisted outpatient treatment program. Courts must promptly report such orders through a secure portal approved by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

md:HB 597.title: Montgomery County - Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program - Alterations MC 17-26
md:HB 597.summary: Changes Montgomery County's community choice aggregation pilot: the start date becomes the earlier of notice to the Public Service Commission or April 1, 2026. It extends the pilot from seven to nine years and moves report deadlines later.

md:HB 598.title: Physicians - Licensing - Internationally Trained Physicians and Licensed Physicians Residing in Other Jurisdictions
md:HB 598.summary: Lets the Maryland Board of Physicians, from January 1, 2028, issue non-renewable limited licenses of up to three years to foreign-licensed physicians meeting set requirements, with a pathway to full licensure. Also changes when out-of-state licensed physicians may practice without a Maryland license.

md:HB 599.title: Health - Licensure of Hospitals - Ownership Requirements
md:HB 599.summary: Requires hospitals licensed on or after October 1, 2026 to qualify as nonprofits under federal law, register as nonprofits with the state, and keep that status. Ownership of a licensed hospital may be transferred only to a nonprofit organization.

md:HB 601.title: Montgomery County - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - Gaithersburg and Rockville MC 5-26
md:HB 601.summary: Authorizes stop sign cameras on state and local roads in school zones in Gaithersburg and Rockville for three years, with civil penalties of up to $40. Both cities must report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2028.

md:HB 604.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026
md:HB 604.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment requiring the Governor to budget for state employee contracts and arbitration awards. If ratified, creates binding arbitration with a neutral arbitrator when state employee contract negotiations reach an impasse, and expands bargaining topics.

md:HB 622.title: Cannabis - Licensees - Dispensary Licenses, Micro Dispensary Employees, and Cannabis Agent Training Programs
md:HB 622.summary: Raises the micro dispensary employee cap from 10 to 20 and extends medical cannabis delivery by licensed dispensaries one year, to July 1, 2027. Renames the responsible vendor program the cannabis agent training program, with training at least every two years.

md:HB 624.title: Hospitals - Staffing Committees and Plans - Establishment (Safe Staffing Act of 2026)
md:HB 624.summary: Requires each hospital to follow its accreditor's and federal CMS Conditions of Participation staffing standards and set up a clinical staffing committee of managers and employees. The chief nurse executive drafts a staffing plan, which the committee finalizes and gives staff on request.

md:HB 625.title: Human-Relevant Research Fund - Collection of Contributions - Responsible Entity
md:HB 625.summary: Moves collection of required annual contributions from research facilities to the Human-Relevant Research Fund from the Department of Health to the Department of Agriculture. Facilities and payment amounts do not change; existing civil penalties still apply.

md:HB 627.title: Commission on Historic, Cultural, and Civic Contributions in Education - Establishment
md:HB 627.summary: Creates the Commission on Historic, Cultural, and Civic Contributions in Education to recommend, every four years, school calendar changes and updates to K-12 curriculum and teacher preparation on the history of diverse groups. A report on its effectiveness is due December 1, 2029.

md:HB 637.title: Pblc Hlth - Recommendations for Immunizations, Screenings, and Prvntv Srvcs - Phrmcst Admin and Rqrd Hlth Ins Cvrg (The Vax Act)
md:HB 637.summary: Requires the Secretary of Health to publish recommendations for immunizations, screenings and preventive services. Lets pharmacists give recommended vaccines to anyone age 7 or older, and changes health insurance coverage requirements for these services, applying to plans from January 1, 2027.

md:HB 638.title: Judges - Mandatory Retirement Age
md:HB 638.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment raising the mandatory retirement age for Maryland judges from 70 to 73 and setting 73 for orphans' court judges. Judges in office or elected on or before November 3, 2026 must still retire at 70.

md:HB 644.title: Vehicle Laws - Speed Monitoring Systems - Residential Districts
md:HB 644.summary: Lets all local jurisdictions, not just Anne Arundel, Montgomery and Prince George's counties, use speed cameras on residential-district roads with posted limits of 35 mph or less, subject to existing local legislation requirements.

md:HB 649.title: Advancing Equal Educational Opportunities for All Students in Maryland
md:HB 649.summary: Authorizes the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights to enforce bans on discrimination in educational institutions, sharing complaint jurisdiction with the State Superintendent of Schools. Also creates a private right to sue for discrimination in education.

md:HB 658.title: Maryland Department of Health - Forensic Review Boards and Community Forensic Aftercare Program
md:HB 658.summary: Writes the Community Forensic Aftercare Program into law within the Department of Health to monitor people found not criminally responsible who are on conditional release, and certain others. A community monitoring board makes recommendations and decisions on conditional release and out-of-state travel requests.

md:HB 660.title: Public Libraries - State Library Resource Center - Funding
md:HB 660.summary: Increases the per-person funding amount that must be provided to the State Library Resource Center beginning in fiscal 2028.

md:HB 663.title: Department of the Environment - Federal Environmental Policy - Reporting
md:HB 663.summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to report to the General Assembly by July 1, 2026 and every six months after on legally valid changes in federal environmental policy and the steps the state is taking in response. Ends May 31, 2029.

md:HB 666.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Required Coverage for Calcium Score Testing
md:HB 666.summary: Requires insurers, nonprofit health plans, HMOs and Maryland Medicaid to cover calcium score testing following the latest American College of Cardiology guidelines. Applies to plans issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.

md:HB 672.title: School Health and Wellness Personnel Assessment and Maryland Council
md:HB 672.summary: Requires the Health and Education departments to assess the school health and wellness workforce each year and report jointly to the General Assembly by December 1, 2027, then annually. Adds a school nurse to the Council on Advancement of School-Based Health Centers.

md:HB 687.title: Criminal Procedure - Evidence - Protecting Artists' Creative Expression (PACE Act)
md:HB 687.summary: Bars a defendant's creative expression, such as lyrics or art, from being admitted against them in criminal or juvenile cases unless the court makes specified findings. Juvenile courts may still admit it for mental health referrals or diversion.

md:HB 688.title: Intercepted Communications - Penalty
md:HB 688.summary: Reclassifies a violation of the state law on intercepting communications from a felony to a misdemeanor.

md:HB 701.title: Department of Natural Resources - Water Resources - Identification of Vernal Pools (Jack Cover Vernal Pool Wetlands Protection Act of 2026)
md:HB 701.summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to create and maintain a list of vernal pools, and to train designated Environment Department staff to identify them. The Environment Department notifies the Natural Resources Department of possible vernal pools it finds.

md:HB 716.title: Housing and Community Development - Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program Eligibility - Alterations
md:HB 716.summary: Changes the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program: counts the housing department as a public housing agency, lets it make up to 100% of its voucher units project-based, and alters eligibility criteria, inspection frequency and state assistance to local housing agencies.

md:HB 717.title: Natural Resources - Public Lands - Acquisition, Staffing, Operations, and Funding
md:HB 717.summary: Changes laws on the Department of Natural Resources' land: affiliated foundations, use of Program Open Space acquisition and local funding, management of newly acquired property, rules for acquiring property interests, and a Land and Property Management Program.

md:HB 718.title: Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission - Established
md:HB 718.summary: Re-establishes the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission to monitor federal changes to the Affordable Care Act, Medicaid, Medicare and related programs, assess their impact, and recommend state and local action. It reports annually and ends June 30, 2029.

md:HB 719.title: Natural Resources - State Boat Act - Alterations
md:HB 719.summary: Changes definitions, regulatory requirements, Waterway Improvement Fund funding limits and fees under the State Boat Act.

md:HB 728.title: Opioid Restitution Fund - Authorized Uses
md:HB 728.summary: Allows the Opioid Restitution Fund to pay operating and personnel costs of the Attorney General's Opioids Enforcement Unit for recovering opioid judgment and settlement money. The office must report annually starting October 1, 2025. Ends June 30, 2029.

md:HB 731.title: Wildlife - Protections and Highway Crossings
md:HB 731.summary: Creates the Maryland Connectivity Coalition to improve wildlife habitat connectivity and reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions. Requires local governments to consider wildlife movement in comprehensive plans, with planning, natural resources and highway agencies supplying information.

md:HB 734.title: Property Tax - Agricultural Use Assessment - Community Solar Energy Generating Systems
md:HB 734.summary: Extends from December 31, 2025 to December 31, 2030 the deadline for community solar projects to be approved to qualify for the agricultural use property tax assessment. Creates a pre-construction determination process for agrivoltaics projects, with an application fee.

md:HB 74.title: State Procurement - Security Services - Contract Modification
md:HB 74.summary: Requires state security services contracts over $2 million and lasting three years or longer to include a clause requiring an equitable contract adjustment, subject to chief procurement officer approval, when law changes or collective bargaining raise required pay or benefits.

md:HB 747.title: Environment - On-Site Wastewater Systems - Requirements for Inspection and Pumping Services and Extension of Sunset and Implementation Dates
md:HB 747.summary: Requires landlords, by July 1, 2028 and before each new tenant, to have septic systems inspected and pumped, and requires real estate sale contracts to make that a purchaser's condition. Delays on-site wastewater license sunset and regulation deadlines two years.

md:HB 765.title: Hospitals - Medical Debt Collection - Sale of Patient Debt
md:HB 765.summary: Lets hospitals sell patient debt to a government unit, its contractor, or a tax-exempt nonprofit solely to cancel it. Patients owe nothing on the sold debt. Payments to hospitals for the debt offset uncompensated care amounts. Ends June 30, 2028.

md:HB 769.title: State Board of Social Work Examiners - Provisional License to Practice Social Work - Established
md:HB 769.summary: Requires the Board of Social Work Examiners, from November 1, 2026, to issue provisional licenses to applicants who meet education and experience requirements but have not passed the licensing exam. A full license follows a satisfactory exam score.

md:HB 780.title: Urban State Highways - Speed Limits - Exemptions
md:HB 780.summary: Lets the State Highway Administration lower speed limits by 5 mph on certain urban highways without an engineering and traffic study. Speed cameras may not enforce the lowered limit for six months.

md:HB 785.title: Common Ownership Communities and Zoning Authorities - Operation of Family Child Care Homes - Limitations
md:HB 785.summary: Bars condominium, cooperative and homeowners association rules from prohibiting or restricting family child care homes or their use of common roads and sidewalks. Bars these associations and local governments from capping children below the state-authorized number. Excludes age-restricted housing.

md:HB 795.title: Federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program - Employee Certification and Awareness Materials
md:HB 795.summary: Requires public service employers certifying employment for federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness to count employees as full time using a method that maximizes full-time status, and not unreasonably delay certification. Directs the Student Loan Ombudsman to develop awareness materials that employers share.

md:HB 796.title: Real Property - Filing Fee for Residential Mortgage Foreclosure - Increase
md:HB 796.summary: Raises the filing fee for an order to docket or complaint to foreclose on a residential mortgage or deed of trust from $300 to $450.

md:HB 797.title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis
md:HB 797.summary: Bars employers from disciplining, firing or otherwise discriminating against fire and rescue employees because they hold a valid medical cannabis certification or test positive for cannabis while certified, subject to additional restrictions on applicability.

md:HB 80.title: Landlord and Tenant - Residential Leases - Fee Disclosures
md:HB 80.summary: Requires landlords to give prospective tenants information about fees and bars charging undisclosed mandatory fees. Lets tenants sue for violations. Counties and municipalities may adopt consistent local laws, and stricter local laws prevail.

md:HB 804.title: Department of Aging - Aging Resilience Fund - Establishment
md:HB 804.summary: Creates the Aging Resilience Fund, a special nonlapsing fund administered by the Secretary of Aging, made up of investment earnings, department fees and other accepted money, to support the Department of Aging's programs. The Governor may not reduce its budget appropriation.

md:HB 825.title: Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board - Membership - Alteration
md:HB 825.summary: Adds the Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, as a member of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board.

md:HB 83.title: Family and Law Enforcement Protection Act
md:HB 83.summary: Requires temporary protective orders in domestic violence cases to order the respondent to surrender firearms and not buy or possess any during the order. Adds duties for local law enforcement on firearm surrender and for commissioners to give petitioners information with interim orders.

md:HB 84.title: Transportation - Major Highway Capacity Expansion Projects and Impact Assessments (Transportation and Climate Alignment Act of 2025)
md:HB 84.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to assess greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle miles traveled for major highway capacity expansion projects, and to run multimodal programs and other activities offsetting those emissions.

md:HB 85.title: Corporations and Associations - Cooperative Limited Equity Housing Corporations - Establishment
md:HB 85.summary: Lets a Maryland nonstock corporation convert to a cooperative limited equity housing corporation under set procedures. Bars counties and municipalities from restricting such corporations. The housing department may set additional rules and create a grant program.

md:SB 822.title: Correctional Services - Maryland Parole Commission and Erroneously Convicted Individuals - Improvements in Transparency and Equity
md:SB 822.summary: Bars the Maryland Parole Commission from permanently denying parole, entitling denied individuals to later hearings at set intervals, and changes hearing notice, document-access and decision-timing rules. Bars counties from being parties to administrative proceedings for erroneously convicted individuals.

md:SB 829.title: Residential-in-Commercial-Zone Laws - Study (Bring Back Main Street Act)
md:SB 829.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study laws in other states that require local governments to allow apartments or mixed-use development in commercial zones, and to report findings and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

md:SB 831.title: Labor Law - Child Labor Penalties, Private Sector Employee Labor Relations, and State Employee Labor Standards
md:SB 831.summary: Allows civil penalties of up to $16,035 per child labor violation, bars executive-branch units from seeking federal wage-and-hour waivers, bars employer-formed employee groups outside federal labor law, and extends the Public Employee Relations Board to private employees if federal labor law is repealed or ceded.

md:SB 84.title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Graduate Assistants
md:SB 84.summary: Gives graduate assistants, fellows and postdoctoral interns at the University of Maryland, College Park and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County the right to bargain collectively, starting July 1, 2028.

md:SB 842.title: Electronic Smoking Devices - Seizure and Wholesaler Record-Keeping Requirements
md:SB 842.summary: Lets the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission seize unlawfully sold electronic smoking devices without a warrant, with a 30-day claim process for owners. Ends manufacturers' authority to sell directly to consumers online and adds wholesaler record-keeping rules.

md:SB 848.title: Public Health Abortion Grant Program - Establishment
md:SB 848.summary: Creates a state program of grants for organizations providing abortion care to people without sufficient resources, funded by moving excess money from insurers' segregated abortion-coverage accounts, with $2 million allocated by October 1, 2025.

md:SB 856.title: Mold - Landlord Requirements and Regulations (Maryland Tenant Mold Protection Act)
md:SB 856.summary: Requires landlords to give tenants a mold pamphlet, assess mold within 15 days of written notice, and remediate within 45 days (or a reasonable time if infeasible) after a positive assessment; directs the Department of the Environment to set mold standards by June 1, 2027.

md:SB 860.title: Department of Aging - Aging Resilience Fund - Establishment
md:SB 860.summary: Creates the Aging Resilience Fund, a nonlapsing special fund run by the Secretary of Aging to support the Department of Aging's mission, bars the Governor from reducing its appropriation, and requires an annual report by January 1.

md:SB 866.title: Public Health - Chain Restaurants - Disclosure and Notice to Customers of Sodium and Added Sugars
md:SB 866.summary: Requires chain restaurants with 20 or more locations, starting January 1, 2027, to post a menu notice that items may be high in sodium or sugar and that full nutrition information is available by QR code, online or on request.

md:SB 867.title: Cyber Maryland Program - Revisions
md:SB 867.summary: Moves the Cyber Maryland Program from the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to the Maryland Department of Labor, expands its activities, and replaces a $99,000 mandated appropriation with discretionary funding, including $3.1 million for fiscal 2026 grants.

md:SB 872.title: Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing - Rental Dwelling Unit - Definition
md:SB 872.summary: Expands the definition of a rental dwelling unit under Maryland's lead-paint law for rental housing built before 1978, dropping the word independent so units that have or have access to living, cooking and sanitation facilities are covered.

md:SB 877.title: Baltimore City - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - 41st Legislative District
md:SB 877.summary: Authorizes stop sign cameras in school zones in Baltimore City's 41st Legislative District, with civil penalties up to $40, and sends half of fine revenue to the city's local management board for youth programming in that district.

md:SB 887.title: County Boards of Education - Reappointment of Incumbent County Superintendent - Authorization
md:SB 887.summary: Allows a county school board, any time after the second year of a superintendent's term, to vote at a public meeting to reappoint the incumbent to a new four-year term, with action required by March 1 of the renewal year.

md:SB 893.title: Business Regulation - Rounding Cash Transactions - Authorization
md:SB 893.summary: Allows merchants to round cash transaction prices and change to the nearest five cents, excludes rounding amounts of up to two cents from sales tax, and overrides conflicting existing regulations, rules and local ordinances.

md:SB 901.title: Environment - Packaging and Paper Products - Producer Responsibility Plans
md:SB 901.summary: Requires producers of packaging and paper products to submit producer responsibility plans to the Department of the Environment by July 1, 2028 and, from a date the Department sets, bars selling or distributing covered materials in Maryland without an approved plan.

md:SB 904.title: Education - Public Schools - Professional Development
md:SB 904.summary: Requires the State Department of Education, by July 1, 2027, to design a system of paid, in-person professional development during weekday school hours for paraeducators and other education support professionals.

md:SB 909.title: Energy Resource Adequacy and Planning Act
md:SB 909.summary: Creates a Strategic Energy Planning Office, funded by assessments on public service companies, to report on wholesale energy market and bulk power risks by September 1, 2028 and every three years after, and adds reporting duties for state energy agencies.

md:SB 929.title: Workgroup on Mail-In Ballot Accessibility
md:SB 929.summary: Creates a workgroup to examine how requiring mail-in ballots to be returned on paper affects voters with disabilities and to evaluate accessible alternatives, with findings due December 31, 2025.

md:SB 93.title: Election Law - Absentee Ballots - Notice to Request Application
md:SB 93.summary: Requires local election boards to include a notice about requesting an absentee ballot application with specimen ballots and other voter mailings, with exceptions for permanent absentee voters, repeat mailings in one election, and vote-by-mail elections.

md:SB 930.title: Environment - Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program - Establishment
md:SB 930.summary: Creates a pilot program letting the Department of the Environment permit use of treated reclaimed water to recharge groundwater, accepting applications from January 2, 2026 to January 3, 2028 and issuing only one five-year permit.

md:SB 94.title: Commercial Law - Earned Wage Access - Revisions
md:SB 94.summary: Bars earned wage access providers and lenders from soliciting or accepting tips, requires returning any tip within seven days, and subjects earned wage access providers to the consumer protection and nondiscrimination rules that apply to other loans.

md:SB 947.title: Maryland Transit Administration Reform Act
md:SB 947.summary: Replaces the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission with two oversight boards for Baltimore-area transit and commuter service, sets their minimum staffing, and requires a study by December 1, 2026 on creating a rail authority.

md:SB 949.title: Election Law - Absentee Ballots - State and Federal Requirements
md:SB 949.summary: Sets in state law when absentee ballots count as timely, requires counting votes in non-federal contests on ballots meeting state rules if federal law or courts impose different timeliness rules, and calls internet-delivered ballots print-at-home ballots.

md:SB 96.title: Environment - Water Bottle Filling Stations - Requirement
md:SB 96.summary: Requires, from October 1, 2025, a water bottle filling station in new construction and renovated buildings wherever a drinking fountain is required, and when a drinking fountain is replaced during renovation.

md:SB 979.title: Local Government - Accommodations Intermediaries - Hotel Rental Tax - Collection by Comptroller and Alterations
md:SB 979.summary: Requires accommodations intermediaries with at least $100,000 in bookings or 200 transactions to remit local hotel rental tax to the Comptroller, who distributes it to localities and may keep up to 1.5%, starting July 1, 2027.

md:SB 997.title: Prince George's County - Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters - Mandated Appropriation
md:SB 997.summary: Requires the Governor to include at least $200 million in the budget for site redevelopment and transportation improvements for the FBI headquarters if the federal government applies for a permit to relocate it to Prince George's County.

sc:H 3007.title: Convention of the States
sc:H 3007.summary: Applies to Congress under Article V for a convention limited to proposing an amendment that bars federal appropriations above estimated revenues except in a national emergency, with conditions limiting the convention's scope.

sc:H 3008.title: Convention of the States
sc:H 3008.summary: Applies to Congress under Article V for a convention limited to proposing a term limits amendment for members of the U.S. House and Senate, with conditions barring any changes to the Bill of Rights or the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments.

sc:H 3045.title: Obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse
sc:H 3045.summary: Creates a felony for knowingly producing, distributing or receiving obscene visual depictions of minors in sexually explicit conduct (two to ten years) or possessing them (up to ten years), and adds the offense to the sex offender registry.

sc:H 3368.title: Income tax on overtime pay
sc:H 3368.summary: As amended in the Senate, updates the state's reference to the federal Internal Revenue Code to December 31, 2025 and lets taxpayers claim a refundable credit the next year, instead of amending a return, when later legislation lowers a prior year's tax.

sc:H 3558.title: Commissioners to Article V Convention
sc:H 3558.summary: Sets rules for commissioners who represent South Carolina at an Article V convention: the General Assembly names them in joint session, they must meet residency and other qualifications and take an oath, follow written instructions, and may be recalled.

sc:H 3815.title: House Rules revisions
sc:H 3815.summary: Changes House rules to delete the motion period, rename the Legislative Oversight committee, drop the April 10 crossover deadline, require streaming of committee meetings when feasible, and bar certain House officers from openly reflecting personal political beliefs.

sc:H 4042.title: Ivermectin
sc:H 4042.summary: Allows adults 18 and older to buy FDA-approved human-use ivermectin over the counter at pharmacies without a prescription, kept behind the counter, with Board of Pharmacy screening and information rules and dispensing bans when contraindications exist.

sc:H 4151.title: Juveniles
sc:H 4151.summary: Treats 16-year-olds charged with felonies carrying 30 or more years, first-degree burglary or attempted murder as adults, and extends adult treatment for 17-year-olds to weapons offenses and repeat felonies; remand to family court remains possible.

sc:H 4163.title: South Carolina High School Athletic Association
sc:H 4163.summary: Beginning June 30, 2027, bars public schools from joining or funding a high school athletic association unless its rules require a board with legislative appointees, Legislative Audit Council audits, legislative budget oversight, and set rules on private-school, charter and home-school athletes.

sc:H 4216.title: Income tax
sc:H 4216.summary: Sets individual income tax rates at 1.99% on the first $30,000 and 5.39% above, adds a state deduction in place of the federal standard deduction, and cuts rates further when projected income tax revenue grows at least 5%.

sc:H 4573.title: Charlie Kirk Memorial Highway
sc:H 4573.summary: Asks the Department of Transportation to name the part of U.S. Highway 76 in Laurens County from the Greenville County line to S.C. Highway 101 the "Charlie Kirk Memorial Highway" and erect signs.

sc:H 4764.title: Immigration
sc:H 4764.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies that run jails and other correctional facilities to enter written 287(g) agreements with federal immigration agencies (or request one annually) unless impractical, bars school resource officers from participating, and has SLED provide training.

sc:H 4982.title: President Donald J. Trump Highway
sc:H 4982.summary: Asks the Department of Transportation to name the part of future Interstate 73 serving Dillon, Horry, Marion and Marlboro Counties the "President Donald J. Trump Highway" and erect signs.

sc:H 5000.title: "Charlie Kirk Memorial Bridge"
sc:H 5000.summary: Asks the Department of Transportation to name the bridge over the Little River on U.S. Highway 378 between Huguenot Parkway and Holiday Road in McCormick County the "Charlie Kirk Memorial Bridge" and erect signs.

sc:H 5683.title: Redistricting, Congressional Districts
sc:H 5683.summary: Replaces the congressional district map with new boundaries for the seven U.S. House districts (by county, voting district and census block), repeals the current district statute, and holds a special U.S. House primary on August 18, 2026 that replaces the June 9 results.

sc:H 5709.title: Special Order, H. 5683
sc:H 5709.summary: Sets House debate rules for the congressional redistricting bill: immediate special-order consideration, one amendment per member, three-minute explanations, ten-minute speeches on second reading, and no debate on third reading.

sc:S 0012.title: Santee Cooper Joint Project Authorization
sc:S 0012.summary: Authorizes the Public Service Authority (Santee Cooper) to co-own, with Dominion Energy South Carolina, natural gas-fired generation and transmission facilities at or near the former Canadys coal plant in Colleton County, owning a share equal to its investment.

sc:S 0026.title: Watercraft Liability Insurance
sc:S 0026.summary: Requires owners of watercraft over 70 horsepower, personal watercraft and specialty propcraft to carry at least $50,000 in liability insurance, with owners certifying coverage at registration and penalties for violations.

sc:S 0062.title: Education Scholarship Trust Fund
sc:S 0062.summary: Changes the Education Scholarship Trust Fund: drops the prior public-school attendance requirement, ends the income limit and 15,000-student cap from 2027-28 so participation depends on appropriations, and raises the education department's administrative share from 2 percent to 7 percent.

sc:S 0214.title: State Commission for Community Advancement and Engagement
sc:S 0214.summary: Renames the Commission for Minority Affairs the State Commission for Community Advancement and Engagement, removes the requirement that most members be African American, refocuses it on rural and under-resourced communities, and deletes duties such as Voting Rights Act assistance.

sc:S 0256.title: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy Programs (C-PACE)
sc:S 0256.summary: Lets counties and cities create voluntary C-PACE programs in which owners of commercial, industrial, agricultural and multifamily property finance energy and other improvements through a special assessment lien on the property, with existing mortgage holders' consent required.

sc:S 0832.title: University Campus Events Zoning
sc:S 0832.summary: Bars counties and cities from restricting or requiring land-use approval for board-approved events on state-supported college campuses, while applying safety laws; requires public and neighborhood notice for certain outdoor events within 1,000 feet of residential neighborhoods.

sc:S 0883.title: Sine Die 2026
sc:S 0883.summary: Sets the 2026 sine die schedule: after May 14 each chamber recesses and meets on call only for budget reports, vetoes, appointments, U.S. House redistricting and similar matters, with final adjournment by Nov. 8, 2026.

sc:S 0933.title: Legislative compensation
sc:S 0933.summary: Sets legislators' annual pay at $15,000 plus a $32,500 in-district allowance, starting with the 128th General Assembly, adjusted every two years for inflation, capped at 5 percent.

ia:HF 805.title: Relating to the practice of dental assistants without registration by the dental board
ia:HF 805.summary: Allows a person to practice as a dental assistant without a certificate of registration if they complete a term of practical training under a dentist's supervision, and directs the dental board to adopt rules.

ia:HF 851.title: Relating to student nutrition, including by modifying the curricula provided to students enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve to include instruction related to nutrition, modifying provisions related to the agriculture, food, and natural resources component of the career and technical education instruction provided to students enrolled in grades nine through twelve, and modifying provisions related to school meal programs, and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 851.summary: Requires K-12 nutrition instruction emphasizing animal-based protein, dairy, vegetables, and fruit, adds food production to high school agriculture courses, and directs the education department to seek a federal waiver from school meal sodium, whole-grain, and produce rules to set Iowa-specific standards.

ia:HF 856.title: Prohibiting public entities and private educational institutions from engaging in certain activities relating to diversity, equity, and inclusion, creating a private cause of action, and including effective date provisions, amended by th e Senate, and moved that the House concur in the Senate amendment H–1298
ia:HF 856.summary: Bars state entities, including local governments and community colleges, from spending money on diversity, equity, and inclusion offices or officers, and bars private colleges from having such offices or lose tuition grant eligibility; lets the attorney general, students, alumni, or employees seek enforcement.

ia:HF 862.title: Concerning conflicts of interest involving a county attorney, and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 862.summary: Allows a county board of supervisors, by majority vote, to obtain outside counsel to represent the board or any other county official.

ia:HF 865.title: Modifying provisions related to the harassment or bullying of students enrolled in school districts or accredited nonpublic schools
ia:HF 865.summary: Redefines school harassment and bullying as repeated, targeted conduct creating an objectively hostile school environment, no longer requiring it be based on a student trait or characteristic, and strikes the definition of "trait or characteristic."

ia:HF 884.title: Authorizing school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools to employ chaplains, or engage volunteer chaplains, to provide services to students
ia:HF 884.summary: Allows school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools to employ chaplains, or engage unpaid chaplains, to support students without a state license; bars requiring students to use them or using a chaplain instead of a school counselor.

ia:HF 928.title: Relating to the recounting and contesting of elections, and providing penalties
ia:HF 928.summary: Has the state elections commissioner order requested recounts for statewide, legislative, and federal offices when margins are under set limits (0.15 percent for statewide and federal), lets candidates name five observers per county, and allows fines up to $25,000 for purposeful recount violations.

ia:HF 946.title: Relating to the enforcement of immigration laws, and providing penalties
ia:HF 946.summary: Makes a law enforcement officer or sheriff who knowingly fails to comply with Iowa's immigration enforcement law subject to attorney general investigation, with possible referral to the law enforcement academy council with a recommendation to revoke the officer's certification.

ia:HF 949.title: Concerning the duties of county commissioners and county auditors
ia:HF 949.summary: Raises from $1,000 to $50,000 the cost above which county election commissioners must take bids, allows informal bidding at or below that amount, and removes many county auditor duties and a bond-indexing requirement.

ia:HF 954.title: Relating to the conduct of elections, and including effective date and retroactive applicability provisions
ia:HF 954.summary: Makes election law changes, including banning ranked choice voting, basing political party status on vote share in the last three general elections, changing filing deadlines and affidavits of candidacy, and marking or canceling registrations of self-reported noncitizens.

ia:SF 140.title: Relating to satellite absentee voting stations
ia:SF 140.summary: Requires county election officials to reject petitions for a satellite absentee voting station on school property when a school bond or levy question is on that election's ballot.

ia:SF 175.title: Incorporating provisions related to pregnancy and fetal development into the human growth and development and health curricula provided by school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools to students enrolled in grades four through twelve
ia:SF 175.summary: Requires human growth and development instruction in grades 5 through 12 to include fetal development, an ultrasound video, and imagery of prenatal development from fertilization, and bars materials produced or provided by entities that perform or promote abortions.

ia:SF 180.title: Relating to the right to refuse certain medical services for reasons of conscience
ia:SF 180.summary: Lets individuals refuse, for reasons of conscience, medical services declared a countermeasure under the federal PREP Act or given an FDA emergency use authorization; bars employers and officials from penalizing them; and allows lawsuits for violations.

ia:SF 2070.title: Relating to the commission on uniform state laws
ia:SF 2070.summary: Restructures the commission on uniform state laws into three members appointed by the governor, House speaker, and Senate president, sets two-year terms, and requires the commission to report its expenses and recommended legislation.

ia:SF 2089.title: Relating to information provided to the department of workforce development during the fact-finding process for claims for unemployment benefits
ia:SF 2089.summary: Requires the workforce development department to let unemployment claimants and employers each give information before fact-finding, and respond to the other's information before the initial determination, without the other party present if either requests.

ia:SF 2157.title: Relating to malicious prosecution arising from civil actions between private parties
ia:SF 2157.summary: Creates a lawsuit for malicious prosecution against a private party who filed a civil case without probable cause and with a primary purpose other than a proper ruling, if the case was decided or dismissed in the original defendant's favor.

ia:SF 2274.title: Relating to the sale or offer for sale of certain firearm devices
ia:SF 2274.summary: Repeals the aggravated misdemeanor for selling or offering to sell a trigger-activating device that increases a firearm's rate of fire.

ia:SF 2293.title: Relating to the department of administrative services’ historical resource research center in Iowa City, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2293.summary: Ends the requirement that the Department of Administrative Services maintain a historical resource research center in Iowa City; the Des Moines center requirement stays.

ia:SF 2341.title: Relating to the approval and publication of meeting minutes of county boards of supervisors
ia:SF 2341.summary: Requires a county board of supervisors' proceedings to be approved before publication, by the board at its next meeting or by the chairperson beforehand, and the county auditor to furnish them for publication after approval.

ia:SF 2385.title: Relating to the Iowa communications network, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2385.summary: Directs the Department of Management to sell the Iowa Communications Network as soon as feasible, keeping service to current contracted users for at least 10 years, and ends limits on which entities the network may serve starting July 1, 2027.

ia:SF 2404.title: Requiring the department of education to develop and administer a pilot program that requires certain specified school districts to establish attendance centers for students requiring special education and students with behavioral issues
ia:SF 2404.summary: Requires a pilot in which one rural and one urban school district set up attendance centers for students with special education or behavioral needs; a district takes part only if it agrees and can fund it, or if the state does.

ia:SF 2432.title: Eliminating a city’s ability to create a city board of health or a city health department, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2432.summary: Bars cities from maintaining a city board of health or health department, with city public health services provided through the local board of health, and requires county boards of health to agree with county hospitals to share facilities and resources unless waived.

ia:SF 2434.title: Relating to local government, including the approval of action by ordinance, and including applicability provisions
ia:SF 2434.summary: Bars county and city departments and offices from adopting or enforcing internal policies or rules unless the governing body approves them by ordinance, and requires each ordinance to have a cost analysis posted on the official internet site; public safety agencies are exempt.

ia:SF 2439.title: Relating to fire protection sprinkler systems in certain residential properties
ia:SF 2439.summary: Requires the state building code to bar mandatory fire sprinkler systems in detached single-family homes of 6,500 square feet or less and in a series of attached single-family homes totaling 18,000 square feet or less, and bars local building rules from requiring them.

ia:SF 2442.title: Relating to county zoning ordinances governing residential buildings
ia:SF 2442.summary: Bars county boards of supervisors from restricting construction or development of residential buildings through zoning, allowing only regulations necessary for the safety of life or property.

ia:SF 2444.title: Creating regulations for cigar bars, modifying the smokefree air Act, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2444.summary: Exempts qualifying cigar bars from the smokefree air Act: venues barring anyone under 21, holding a class C alcohol license, selling only premium cigars, preparing no food, and earning at least 35 percent of revenue from premium cigars and related products.

ia:SF 2500.title: Relating to townships, including the appointment and duties of township officers, township budgets, and the provision of fire protection and emergency medical services to townships by cities, and including effective date provisions
ia:SF 2500.summary: Has county supervisors appoint township trustees and clerks, instead of voters electing them, in townships in counties under 75,000 population with valuation under $250 million; lets supervisors approve or reject their budgets; and requires cities serving townships to keep a rural fire protection fund.

md:HB 1142.title: Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures
md:HB 1142.summary: Creates a task force to study county and municipal revenue sources, including unused options and other states' approaches, and report recommendations by December 1, 2026. The task force ends June 30, 2027.

md:HB 1143.title: Public Health - Office of the Chief Medical Examiner - Perinatal Autopsies (Lung Float Test Ban)
md:HB 1143.summary: Bans medical examiners and authorized pathologists from using the lung float test in perinatal autopsies to tell stillbirth from live birth, for two years from October 1, 2026. Requires a state report by December 1, 2027 on whether the test is needed.

md:HB 1147.title: Correctional Services - Maryland Parole Commission - Improvements in Transparency and Equity
md:HB 1147.summary: Bars the Maryland Parole Commission from permanently denying parole, sets timelines for later hearings after each denial, and requires hearing recordings, written reports within 14 days, and public release of commissioners' reasons for votes.

md:HB 1148.title: Property Taxes - Tax Sales, Legacy Protection Program, and Tax Credits
md:HB 1148.summary: Lets heirs of deceased homeowners use the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, creates a Legacy Protection Program funded yearly by $250,000 from the State and $500,000 from counties, and lets heirs not yet on the title claim property tax credits for up to three years.

md:HB 115.title: Election Law - Individuals Released From State Correctional Facilities - Automatic Restoration of Voter Registration
md:HB 115.summary: Requires the corrections department to send the elections board monthly lists of people released from state prisons so their prior voter registrations are restored, with notice to each person on how to decline or update their address. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

md:HB 1150.title: Health Occupations - Pharmacists - Minor Conditions and HIV Prevention and Treatment (Rapid Testing and Preventive Care Act)
md:HB 1150.summary: Allows pharmacists to order, test for, and treat certain minor conditions under a state protocol, and replaces the nPEP standing order program with a state protocol for pharmacist-delivered HIV pre-exposure and post-exposure prevention medications.

md:HB 1156.title: Correctional Services - Maryland Parole Commission - Members and Hearing Examiners
md:HB 1156.summary: Raises the Maryland Parole Commission from 10 members to 15 to 20, has the Governor appoint from panel-nominated candidates, ends its authority to appoint hearing examiners, and has commissioners hear all parole and administrative release cases.

md:HB 1162.title: Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, or Refrigeration Contractors - Equipment Sales
md:HB 1162.summary: Bars selling heating, ventilation, air-conditioning or refrigeration equipment to anyone who is not a licensed contractor (or employer of one), a reseller to licensed contractors, or exempt from licensing. Sets civil penalties of up to $1,000, then $5,000.

md:HB 1166.title: Motor Vehicles - Dealers - Front Registration Plate Display
md:HB 1166.summary: Bars dealers from delivering a new vehicle to be registered in Maryland without front license plate mounting hardware, unless the buyer or lessee signs a statement declining it and acknowledging that not displaying a front plate is a misdemeanor with a fine up to $500.

md:HB 1173.title: Montgomery County - Speed Monitoring Systems - High-Risk Highways MC 17-25
md:HB 1173.summary: Allows speed cameras in Montgomery County on highways identified in a safety or Vision Zero plan as high-risk for serious or fatal crashes. Sets rules for how camera revenue is used, how cameras are evaluated, and where cameras may be placed.

md:HB 1198.title: Crctnl Services - Comprehensive Rehabilitative Prerelease Services - Female Incarcerated Individuals (The Monica Cooper Prerelease Act)
md:HB 1198.summary: Requires the women's prerelease unit to be in Baltimore City on a site of at least 3 acres, resets its construction deadlines to 2025 through 2027, and requires comprehensive rehabilitative services by July 1, 2026. Allows up to $500,000 in grant funds.

md:HB 12.title: Cannabis - Sale and Distribution - Tetrahydrocannabinol Offenses
md:HB 12.summary: Bans selling or distributing THC products that violate state rules or are advertised above the legal THC limit, with a $5,000 maximum fine for unlicensed violators. Lets the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission seize illegal products and issue citations.

md:HB 1207.title: Montgomery County - Board of Education - Student Member Compensation MC 7-25
md:HB 1207.summary: Lets the Montgomery County Board of Education's student member take compensation as a monthly stipend during the term, with any remainder as a scholarship afterward, and requires salary increases for elected members to take effect at the start of a term.

md:HB 1239.title: Fair Housing and Housing Discrimination - Regulations, Intent, and Discriminatory Effect
md:HB 1239.summary: Bars housing actions that have a discriminatory effect on protected classes in the sale or rental of a dwelling, regardless of intent, unless the action had no discriminatory intent, served a legitimate business necessity, and had no less discriminatory alternative.

md:HB 1246.title: Health Benefit Plans - Calculation of Cost-Sharing Contribution - Requirements
md:HB 1246.summary: Requires health insurers and HMOs, including when a pharmacy benefit manager covers the drugs, to count discounts, vouchers and other assistance toward a patient's prescription drug cost-sharing. Bars setting plan terms based on available assistance. Takes effect January 1, 2026.

md:HB 1248.title: Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace - Established
md:HB 1248.summary: Creates a workgroup on expanding part-time employment in state government, reporting findings by September 15, 2027. Requires the budget department to issue guidance to state agencies on part-time opportunities by December 31, 2027.

md:HB 1249.title: Certified Recovery Residences - Refusing Services to Individuals Receiving Medication-Assisted Treatment - Prohibition
md:HB 1249.summary: Requires certified recovery residences' standards to bar them from refusing services to a person because they receive medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder, or from requiring them to stop or change that treatment.

md:HB 1253.title: Department of Social and Economic Mobility - Established
md:HB 1253.summary: Creates the Department of Social and Economic Mobility as a principal Executive Branch department, makes it successor to the small business, cannabis social equity and transportation minority business offices, and lets the Governor transfer their positions and funds to it.

md:HB 1254.title: Education - Public Schools - Service Contracts
md:HB 1254.summary: Sets a state policy preferring public school employees over private contractors for school functions. Requires county boards seeking contracts to document alternatives and at least 20% projected savings, and submit them to the state education department, which audits the projected savings.

md:HB 1258.title: Estates and Trusts - Estate Administration - Publication of Notice
md:HB 1258.summary: Requires registers of wills to maintain one shared website for publishing estate notices, such as appointments of personal representatives, instead of publishing them in a newspaper of general circulation.

md:HB 1259.title: Zoning Authorities - Operation of Family Child Care Homes - Prohibitions and Requirements
md:HB 1259.summary: Bars local governments from denying or restricting licensed family child care homes, and requires them to treat these homes as a residential activity and a permitted use in residential zones. Takes effect June 1, 2026.

md:HB 1263.title: Public Health - Workgroup on Postoperative Cosmetic Care
md:HB 1263.summary: Creates a workgroup to study regulating postoperative cosmetic services by nonphysician practitioners, with interim and final reports due December 1, 2026 and December 1, 2027. It cannot create a licensing program without legislative approval.

md:HB 128.title: Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation - Total Assessed Cost of Greenhouse Gas Emissions - Study and Reports
md:HB 128.summary: Requires the Comptroller, with Commerce and the Environment department, to study the total cost of greenhouse gas emissions in Maryland and report to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1294.title: Commercial Law - Credit Regulation - Earned Wage Access and Credit Modernization
md:HB 1294.summary: Treats earned wage access products as loans under the Maryland Consumer Loan Law, requires licensing of providers, sets rules on tips, and restricts and requires disclosure of fees tied to these products.

md:HB 1310.title: Prescription Drug Repository Program - Out-of-State Pharmacies
md:HB 1310.summary: Allows out-of-state entities to take part in the Prescription Drug Repository Program, expands it to accept over-the-counter drugs, defines eligible patients, expands immunity provisions, and exempts donors and recipients from holding a wholesale distribution license.

md:HB 1363.title: Places of Public Accommodation - Captioning for Motion Picture Houses - Alterations
