md:HB 1363.summary: Lowers from eight to four the number of screens at which a theater must offer open-captioned screenings, and requires monthly reports to the Commission on Civil Rights and the Attorney General on which films used closed or open captioning, with dates and times.

md:HB 1367.title: Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care in Maryland
md:HB 1367.summary: Creates a Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care to envision and recommend a comprehensive health care system for Maryland, with reports due December 2027, 2028 and 2029. Takes effect only if private funding is secured by June 1, 2027.

md:HB 1378.title: Civil Actions - Child Sexual Abuse
md:HB 1378.summary: Lowers noneconomic damages and government liability caps to $700,000 and $400,000 for previously time-barred child sexual abuse claims filed from June 1, 2025, limits attorney fees in such cases to 20% of settlements or 25% of judgments, and requires Judiciary reports.

md:HB 1380.title: Health Care Facilities - Hospitals and Freestanding Birthing Centers - Perinatal Care Standards
md:HB 1380.summary: Requires the health department to adopt, by October 1, 2026, minimum perinatal care standards meeting the Maryland Perinatal System Standards for hospitals with obstetric services and freestanding birthing centers, which must meet them as a condition of licensure.

md:HB 1419.title: Electric Distribution System Support Services - Energy Storage and Data Use
md:HB 1419.summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to approve regulatory-asset accounting for utilities' costs of distribution system support programs when consistent with program goals, to evaluate other states' energy storage programs by January 1, 2026, and to design Maryland programs by June 1, 2026.

md:HB 1420.title: Registers of Wills - Appointment of Personal Representatives - Noncitizens
md:HB 1420.summary: Repeals the rule barring non-citizens from serving as personal representatives of an estate unless they are permanent residents and the decedent's spouse, ancestor, descendant or sibling.

md:HB 1433.title: Community Colleges - Collective Bargaining - Definition of Supervisory Employee
md:HB 1433.summary: Defines "supervisory employee" for community college collective bargaining so it excludes department heads and faculty below assistant dean, allowing those employees to bargain collectively. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

md:HB 1456.title: Consumer Protection - Residential Property Advertisement - Ownership Verification
md:HB 1456.summary: Bars platforms and other commercial entities from advertising residential property for sale or lease for others unless they verify the poster is the owner, the owner's agent, or legally selling the property. Violations are unfair trade practices.

md:HB 146.title: Environment - On-Site Wastewater Systems - Requirements for Inspection and Pumping Services and Implementation Dates
md:HB 146.summary: Requires landlords and purchasers of property served by septic systems to have them inspected and pumped by licensed professionals, starting July 1, 2028, and delays licensing of on-site wastewater workers from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028.

md:HB 1464.title: Motor Vehicles - Rental Fleet Vehicles - Registration
md:HB 1464.summary: Lets owners of five or more rental vehicles use an alternative registration with distinctive plates, no validation tabs, shared expiration dates, the annual fee set for rental vehicles under existing law, and a one-time initial fee of up to $8.50.

md:HB 1468.title: Cyber Maryland Program - Revisions
md:HB 1468.summary: Moves the Cyber Maryland Program from the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to the state labor department, expands its activities, lets the Governor budget $3.1 million in fiscal 2026 for grants and contracts, and changes the board's composition.

md:HB 15.title: Corporations and Assns - Limited Worker Cooperative Assns - Authorization (Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Assn Act)
md:HB 15.summary: Creates the Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Association Act, which lets an LLC elect to operate as a worker cooperative, and sets rules for its formation, operation and dissolution. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

md:HB 150.title: Child Care Centers - Certificated Staff Ratio Requirement - Alteration
md:HB 150.summary: Lets the state education department set the required ratio of staff certified in first aid and CPR at child care centers, instead of the current one per 20 children.

md:HB 1502.title: Baltimore City - AIDS Prevention Sterile Needle and Syringe Exchange Pilot Program - Revisions
md:HB 1502.summary: Renames Baltimore City's needle exchange pilot the HIV Prevention Syringe Services Program, changes its oversight committee, duties and data collection, and repeals the listed exceptions to staff and participants' immunity from certain paraphernalia charges.

md:HB 1516.title: Financial Institutions - Consumer Credit - Application of Licensing Requirements (Maryland Secondary Market Stability Act of 2025)
md:HB 1516.summary: Exempts from State consumer credit licensing a person who acquires a mortgage, mortgage loan or installment loan without otherwise making such loans, and creates a licensing workgroup to report recommendations by December 31, 2025.

md:HB 1521.title: State Board of Social Work Examiners - Membership and Examination Requirements
md:HB 1521.summary: Repeals the exam requirement for bachelor and master social work licenses, keeps it for certified and certified clinical social workers, and adds two consumer members to the State Board of Social Work Examiners, raising it from 12 to 14 members.

md:HB 153.title: Residential Rental Apartments - Air-Conditioning Requirement
md:HB 153.summary: Requires landlords of apartment buildings with four or more units to provide air conditioning from June 1 to September 30, capable of keeping habitable spaces at 80 degrees or below. Applies to new units from June 2026 and certain renovated units from October 2026.

md:HB 1530.title: Higher Education - Undocumented Students - Out-of-State Tuition Exemption Eligibility
md:HB 1530.summary: Reduces from three years to two the number of years an undocumented student or their parent or guardian must have filed Maryland income tax returns to qualify for in-state tuition rates at public colleges under the Dream Act.

md:HB 1533.title: Pblc Hlth - Cosmetic Prdcts - Enfrcmt & Pnlts for Prhbtd Ingredients (Crown & Care Act - Protecting Cmnts Frm Harmful Hair Chemicals)
md:HB 1533.summary: Makes anyone who manufactures or sells cosmetics with specified prohibited ingredients liable for civil damages for actual harm, treats violations as unfair trade practices, and lets the Department of Health investigate complaints and inspect premises.

md:HB 1541.title: Condominiums - Mandatory Insurance Coverage
md:HB 1541.summary: Requires owners of residential condominium units to carry insurance covering contents, loss of use, personal liability and other specified coverage, and lets the condominium council buy a policy and bill the owner if they do not.

md:HB 1578.title: State Procurement - Procurement Preferences - Reauthorization and Revisions
md:HB 1578.summary: Extends the Minority Business Enterprise procurement program five years, to July 1, 2031, replaces its legislative findings, and adds quarterly reporting requirements and a small-business certification review process.

md:HB 1582.title: Ed - Program of Educ Accountability - Alterations (Cmprhnsv Outcomes and Measures of Progress for Supporting Schls (COMPASS Act))
md:HB 1582.summary: Raises the maximum weight of academic indicators in school accountability scores from 65% to 70%, bars the State Board from relying on teacher evaluations in accountability indicators, and expands the allowed school quality indicators.

md:HB 159.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2025
md:HB 159.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for voter approval, requiring the Governor to fund State employee contract and arbitration terms in the budget; if ratified, sets binding arbitration for State employee bargaining impasses and expands bargaining topics.

md:HB 1617.title: Public Health - Health Innovation Zones - Establishment
md:HB 1617.summary: Lets a county's zoning authority designate health innovation zones in areas with high disease rates and few grocery stores, pharmacies and health care providers; requires incentives for those businesses, exempts them from local zoning, and requires Prince George's County to designate two zones.

md:HB 164.title: State Buildings and State Highways - Collection and Disposal of Yard Waste
md:HB 164.summary: Bars State employees and contractors from putting yard waste from State buildings and highways in single-use plastic containers, and requires disposal at in-State organics, wood waste or mulching facilities when one within 30 miles can accept it.

md:HB 18.title: Vehicle Laws - Noise Abatement Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - Inspection and Extension
md:HB 18.summary: Extends by two years, to 2028, the Montgomery and Prince George's County pilot programs using noise-monitoring cameras to record vehicles over legal sound limits, and applies existing image-inspection rules to those cameras.

md:HB 182.title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Penalties
md:HB 182.summary: Replaces the flat $40 maximum fine for speed camera citations with a scale rising with speed over the limit, from $40 at 12-15 mph over to $425 at 40 or more, and requires a workgroup on school-zone speed cameras.

md:HB 184.title: Nonpublic Schools - Transcripts - Prohibition on Punitive Measures Related to Student Debt
md:HB 184.summary: Bars nonpublic schools in State-funded education programs from refusing to issue a transcript, or taking other punitive steps over a transcript request, because the student owes the school a debt.

md:HB 193.title: Uninsured Employers' Fund - Additional Assessment on Awards and Settlements - Amount
md:HB 193.summary: Raises from 1.0% to up to 1.5% the additional assessment on workers' compensation awards and settlements that funds the Uninsured Employers' Fund, and requires a special monitor to review the fund's finances.

md:HB 194.title: Consumer Protection - Retail Sales - Payment or Reimbursement of Shipping Costs
md:HB 194.summary: Requires merchants to provide a prepaid return label or refund return shipping when a consumer receives a damaged, faulty or wrong item, within 30 days of receiving the return; violations are unfair trade practices.

md:HB 197.title: Public Schools - Restorative Practices Schools - Comprehensive Plan
md:HB 197.summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to develop a comprehensive plan for restorative practices schools, which a local board that creates one must use, and replaces "restorative approaches" with "restorative practices" in school discipline rules.

md:HB 199.title: Election Law - Notice to Permanent Absentee Voters
md:HB 199.summary: Changes when the State Board of Elections must send confirmation notices to permanent absentee voters, to a period between 120 and 90 days before an election, and changes what the Board does if it cannot reach a voter by their chosen method.

md:HB 201.title: Election Law - Absentee Ballots - Notice to Request Application
md:HB 201.summary: Requires local election boards to include a notice on how to request an absentee ballot application with specimen ballots and other mailings to voters, except for voters with permanent absentee status and vote-by-mail elections.

md:HB 207.title: Higher Education - Undocumented Students - Out-of-State Tuition Exemption Eligibility
md:HB 207.summary: Reduces from three years to two the number of years an undocumented student or their parent or guardian must have filed Maryland income tax returns to qualify for in-state tuition rates at public colleges under the Dream Act.

md:HB 208.title: Consumer Protection - False Advertising - Digital Goods
md:HB 208.summary: Bars sellers from advertising or offering digital goods for sale with wording suggesting unrestricted ownership unless specified license acknowledgments or disclosures are given; exempts subscriptions and goods whose access cannot be revoked.

md:HB 227.title: Maryland Environmental Service - Authorizations and Requirements - Alterations
md:HB 227.summary: Lets the Maryland Environmental Service treasurer delegate more duties to the deputy treasurer, raises the small-procurement threshold from $25,000 to $50,000, and updates public notice rules for service district rate changes.

md:HB 23.title: Property Taxes - Authority of Counties to Establish a Subclass and Set a Special Rate for Commercial and Industrial Property
md:HB 23.summary: Lets Baltimore City and counties create a commercial and industrial property subclass with a special tax rate, and requires a tax exemption or credit for the residential portion of mixed-use properties.

md:HB 233.title: Lbr and Employment - Mndtry Meetings on Religious or Political Matters - Employee Attendance and Participation (Md Worker Freedom Act)
md:HB 233.summary: Bars employers from penalizing employees or applicants who decline to attend or take part in employer meetings where the employer gives its opinion on religious or political matters.

md:HB 238.title: Maryland Heritage Area Authority and Heritage Areas - Alterations
md:HB 238.summary: Adds the Agriculture Secretary and State Superintendent of Schools to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority and changes its rules for grants and loans.

md:HB 240.title: Local Comprehensive Plans - Guidance Materials and Notification to the Department of Planning Floor Amendment Ready /913427/1
md:HB 240.summary: Requires local planning commissions to notify the Department of Planning when they begin reviewing their comprehensive plans, and requires the Department to provide guidance materials within 60 days.

md:HB 246.title: Video Tolls - Class G (Trailer) Vehicles - Liability
md:HB 246.summary: Makes the registered owner of a Class G (trailer) vehicle liable for a video toll if the towing vehicle's registered owner cannot be determined, and applies existing video-toll collection and penalty rules to trailer owners, from January 1, 2027.

md:HB 247.title: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program - Variances - Alterations
md:HB 247.summary: Changes Critical Area variance standards, including a rebuttable presumption that an existing accessory structure shows reasonable and significant use when a new one is requested, and bars local governments from accepting certain variance applications.

md:HB 25.title: Environment - Reservoir Augmentation Permit - Establishment
md:HB 25.summary: Creates a Reservoir Augmentation Program in the Maryland Department of the Environment and requires a permit to place reclaimed water into a reservoir used as a drinking water source.

md:HB 252.title: Environment - Lead Paint Abatement Services - Performance Bond and Liability Insurance
md:HB 252.summary: Lets the Maryland Department of the Environment require companies accredited for lead paint abatement to carry a performance bond or liability insurance.

md:HB 254.title: Supporting Inclusive Community Adaptation Act
md:HB 254.summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to involve communities in project planning, creates a climate resilience capital grant fund, and allows partial forgiveness of shore erosion control loans.

md:HB 256.title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Safety Corridors (Vulnerable Road User Protection Act of 2026)
md:HB 256.summary: Allows the State Highway Administration to place speed cameras on highway segments designated safety corridors, and to authorize local governments to do so, under rules similar to existing speed cameras.

md:HB 260.title: Public Financing Act - Fair Campaign Financing Fund - Distributions
md:HB 260.summary: Moves the earliest date for public campaign financing payments to gubernatorial candidates from January 1 of the election year to July 1 of the year before, and moves the January campaign finance report deadline from the third to the fourth Wednesday.

md:HB 277.title: Environment - Water Bottle Filling Stations - Requirement
md:HB 277.summary: Requires new construction and renovations, from October 1, 2025, to include a water bottle filling station wherever a drinking fountain is required, with exceptions.

md:HB 278.title: Human Services - Department of Aging and Commission on Aging (The Longevity Ready Maryland Act)
md:HB 278.summary: Requires the Secretary of Aging to lead implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, with updated plans every four years and annual reports, and changes the Commission on Aging's membership and duties.

md:HB 280.title: Health Insurance - Mental Health and Substance Use Disorders - Codification of Federal Requirements
md:HB 280.summary: Writes parts of the 2024 federal mental health parity rule into Maryland law, requiring health insurers to collect, evaluate and act on outcomes data for treatment limits and to offer comparable mental health and substance use benefits.

md:HB 286.title: Local Comprehensive Planning and State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy - Planning Principles
md:HB 286.summary: Replaces the 12 planning visions for local comprehensive plans, and the matching State growth policy, with eight planning principles.

md:HB 292.title: Cooperative Housing Corporations, Condominiums, and Homeowners Assns - Funding of Reserve Accounts and Preparation of Funding Plans
md:HB 292.summary: Changes reserve-fund rules for condominiums, co-ops and homeowners associations, extending the time to reach recommended funding from three to five years and allowing deviation after a declared financial hardship.

md:HB 293.title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center - External Data Sharing With Third-Party Data Centers for Multistate Reporting - Authorization
md:HB 293.summary: Lets the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center share individual student and workforce data with one third-party data center at a time for multistate research, under a written agreement and security standards.

md:HB 297.title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program - Sunset Repeal
md:HB 297.summary: Makes the young adult health insurance subsidy pilot program permanent by removing its June 30, 2026 end date, and makes the Health Benefit Exchange's operation of it optional, depending on funding.

md:HB 298.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Demographic Data Collection - Parental Status
md:HB 298.summary: Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to collect data on students' parental status from public colleges, which must add specified questions to their demographic forms, and to report the data to legislative committees each September.

md:HB 858.title: Mattress Stewardship Program - Establishment
md:HB 858.summary: Requires mattress producers to submit a stewardship plan to the Department of the Environment by July 1, 2027, funded by a per-mattress assessment, and bars producers and retailers from selling a brand whose producer is not implementing an approved program.

md:HB 861.title: Transportation Network Companies - Weekly Fare and Earnings Summary and Operator Data Reporting
md:HB 861.summary: Requires ride-hailing companies to give each driver a weekly summary of fares collected and driver earnings, and to report aggregated average fare, driver time and driver earnings data to the Public Service Commission each year.

md:HB 870.title: Environment - Permit Applications for New Buildings - Notice (Large Buildings for Tomorrow Act)
md:HB 870.summary: Requires local governments, starting July 1, 2026, to notify the Department of the Environment within 10 business days of accepting a permit application for a new building of 35,000 square feet or more, listing its address, type and planned energy sources.

md:HB 875.title: Public Safety - Distribution of Literature to Purchasers of Firearms and Ammunition
md:HB 875.summary: Requires the Department of Health to prepare literature on firearm safety, training, suicide prevention, mental health and conflict resolution that sellers must display at the point of sale and give to buyers; civil penalties of up to $500, then $1,000, go to the county.

md:HB 881.title: Family Investment Program - Child Support
md:HB 881.summary: Increases, starting in fiscal 2028, the share of child support passed through to families receiving Family Investment Program aid and disregarded when computing benefits, reaching 100% in fiscal 2031.

md:HB 905.title: Hospitals - Clinical Staffing Committees and Plans - Establishment (Safe Staffing Act of 2025)
md:HB 905.summary: Requires each hospital to set up a clinical staffing committee with equal management and employee members, which writes a staffing plan the hospital must implement each January 1 and review yearly.

md:HB 913.title: Baltimore City - Speed Monitoring Systems - Interstate 83
md:HB 913.summary: Raises the number of speed cameras allowed on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City from two to four, with only one per direction operating at a time, and removes the end date of the authorization.

md:HB 915.title: Motor Vehicles - Out-of-State Drivers - Automated Enforcement (Out-of-State Driver Accountability Act)
md:HB 915.summary: Requires county and municipal automated traffic enforcement programs to report quarterly to the state Vision Zero coordinator on each citation issued to a vehicle registered in another state, including whether it is paid or past due.

md:HB 917.title: Corporations and Associations - Maryland Securities Act - Filing Fees
md:HB 917.summary: Raises Maryland Securities Act filing fees from $100 to $250 for certain exempt in-state offerings and for initial notice filings of federal covered securities.

md:HB 930.title: Public Health Abortion Grant Program - Establishment
md:HB 930.summary: Creates a Public Health Abortion Grant Program and fund in the Department of Health to give operating grants to organizations providing abortion care to people without sufficient resources, funded by 90% of excess balances in insurers' segregated abortion-coverage accounts.

md:HB 933.title: Nursing Homes - Cost Reports
md:HB 933.summary: Requires the Department of Health to review nursing home Medicaid cost reports, including spending on contracted nursing care and direct-care staff pay, and report findings annually from October 1, 2025 through 2029.

md:HB 939.title: Maryland Commission for Women - Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control
md:HB 939.summary: Requires the Maryland Commission for Women to set up a collaborative that studies and recommends ways to expand coverage of over-the-counter birth control, with an interim report due January 1, 2026 and a final report December 1, 2027.

md:HB 969.title: Electric Vehicle Fuel Sold at Retail - Equipment Requirements, Units of Measure, and Fees
md:HB 969.summary: Requires electric vehicle charging stations to post a local contact, sell electricity by the kilowatt-hour, and charge customers only for energy delivered, while allowing separate itemized service fees.

md:HB 974.title: Health Insurance - Preventive Services - Enforcement Authority
md:HB 974.summary: Requires the Insurance Commissioner to enforce insurers' duty to cover specified preventive services without cost-sharing, based on recommendations and guidelines in effect on December 31, 2024.

md:HB 978.title: Baltimore County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Interstate 695 and Interstate 83
md:HB 978.summary: Allows the State Highway Administration to place up to eight speed cameras on Interstate 695 and six on Interstate 83 in Baltimore County, with fines going to its costs and road safety improvements; ends June 30, 2030.

md:HB 983.title: Election Law - Local Boards of Elections - Language Assistance Program
md:HB 983.summary: Creates a Language Assistance Program requiring local election boards in counties the State Board of Elections finds have a significant need to provide language help, including translator access for voters at early voting and polling places.

md:HB 984.title: Public Utilities - Electric Cooperatives - Rate Proceedings
md:HB 984.summary: Adds electric cooperatives to the Public Service Commission's "make whole" rate proceedings, requires a public hearing for them, and bases their review on debt service coverage rather than rate of return.

md:HB 988.title: Montgomery County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Maryland Route 200 (Intercounty Connector) MC 10-25
md:HB 988.summary: Allows the Maryland Transportation Authority to place speed cameras on Maryland Route 200 (the Intercounty Connector) in Montgomery County, with penalty revenue remitted to the Authority.

md:HB 993.title: Real Property - Short-Term Rentals
md:HB 993.summary: Bars counties and municipalities from banning short-term rentals solely because the operator is a tenant, while still allowing them to limit a tenant-operator to one rental property.

md:SB 10.title: State Highway Administration - Speed Monitoring Systems - Application Approval
md:SB 10.summary: Gives the State Highway Administration 120 days to approve or deny a county's speed camera application for a State highway within a municipality, deeming it approved if it does not act, and caps applications at 10 per 30 days.

md:SB 100.title: Election Law - Early Voting Centers - Bus Stops
md:SB 100.summary: Requires local fixed-route buses running within half a mile of an early voting center to let passengers board and exit at its entrance on voting days, where practicable; takes effect January 1, 2027.

md:SB 1023.title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis
md:SB 1023.summary: Bars employers of firefighters, emergency medical technicians and paramedics from disciplining or discriminating against them for holding a valid medical cannabis certification or testing positive while certified, and requires employers to report to the EMS Board any employee who reports to work impaired.

md:SB 108.title: Environment - Water Resources and Wetlands - Enforcement
md:SB 108.summary: Authorizes the Department of the Environment to impose administrative penalties of up to $5,000 per violation ($100,000 total) for violations of water appropriation and dam safety laws, and extends its corrective-order, notice and hearing procedures from water use to dam safety.

md:SB 11.title: Campaign Financing - Campaign Finance Reporting Deadline and Fair Campaign Financing Fund Distributions
md:SB 11.summary: Moves the earliest date for public campaign financing payments to gubernatorial candidates to July 1 of the year before the election, and moves the January campaign finance report deadline to the fourth Wednesday.

md:SB 113.title: Human Services - Department of Aging and Commission on Aging (The Longevity Ready Maryland Act)
md:SB 113.summary: Codifies the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, requires the Secretary of Aging to lead it and update it every four years starting July 1, 2029, and changes the Commission on Aging's membership and duties.

md:SB 120.title: Restrictions on Use - Solar Collector Systems - Alteration
md:SB 120.summary: Defines a restriction on solar panel installation as unreasonable if it raises installation cost by at least 5% or cuts expected energy output by at least 10%, and sets rules for community associations on common-area systems.

md:SB 121.title: Vehicle Laws - Noise Abatement Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - Inspection and Extension
md:SB 121.summary: Extends by two years, through June 30, 2028, the pilot letting counties cite vehicles exceeding noise limits using cameras, and bars public inspection of noise-camera images except by cited drivers and agencies.

md:SB 125.title: Vehicle Laws - Transfer of Used Vehicles - Repeal of Notarized Bill of Sale Requirement
md:SB 125.summary: Repeals the notarized bill of sale used to base the vehicle titling excise tax on the actual price of a used vehicle sold $500 or more below retail value; the published valuation is used instead.

md:SB 130.title: Environment - Water - Individual Submeters
md:SB 130.summary: Allows owners and managers of apartment houses and mobile home parks, and local housing authorities, to install individual water submeters; bars charging tenants more than the provider's actual charges, allocated by usage plus up to $1 a month, and sets record and billing rules.

md:SB 136.title: Collective Bargaining - Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission - Police Officers
md:SB 136.summary: Extends the State employees collective bargaining law to nonsupervisory police officers of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission who have arrest authority.

md:SB 141.title: Election Law - Election Misinformation, Election Disinformation, and Deepfakes
md:SB 141.summary: Bars knowingly or recklessly creating, using or spreading election deepfakes to produce materially false information with intent to impede voting or misrepresent election procedures (up to $5,000, five years), and requires the State elections administrator to publicize corrections of election misinformation.

md:SB 144.title: Corporations and Assns - Limited Worker Cooperative Assns - Authorization (Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Assn Act)
md:SB 144.summary: Creates the Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Association Act, letting a Maryland LLC elect to operate as a worker cooperative under rules for its formation, operation and dissolution; takes effect October 1, 2026.

md:SB 149.title: Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation - Total Assessed Cost of Greenhouse Gas Emissions - Study and Reports
md:SB 149.summary: Requires the Comptroller, with the Departments of Commerce and the Environment, to study the total cost of greenhouse gas emissions in Maryland and report to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

md:SB 153.title: Election Law - Campaign Finance Entities - Oversight and Control of Campaign Funds
md:SB 153.summary: Changes campaign finance law to let campaign finance entities designate authorized agents to carry out duties, bars candidates from making disbursements from the designated campaign account, and alters how campaign managers, chairs and treasurers are appointed.

md:SB 154.title: Access to Counsel in Evictions - Task Force and Special Fund
md:SB 154.summary: Extends through fiscal 2028 the $14 million annual transfer from unclaimed property proceeds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions fund, and moves staffing of the related task force to the Department of Housing and Community Development.

md:SB 160.title: Public Safety - Licensed Firearms Dealers - Notification Regarding Compromising Events
md:SB 160.summary: Requires licensed firearms dealers to notify State Police within 24 hours of a burglary, robbery or theft involving firearms or ammunition, or a compromised required security feature, and changes related penalties.

md:SB 162.title: Criminal Procedure - Motion to Reduce Duration of Sentence - Repeal of Sentencing Date Limitation
md:SB 162.summary: Removes the requirement that a person must have been sentenced before October 1, 2021 to seek a sentence reduction under the Juvenile Restoration Act.

md:SB 180.title: Evidence - Interception of Oral Communications - Fair Housing Testing
md:SB 180.summary: Makes it lawful for a fair housing tester to record an oral communication they are part of, in a government or nonprofit civil rights testing program, to gather evidence of fair housing violations; use of the recording is limited to enforcing fair housing laws.

md:SB 188.title: Maryland Transportation Authority - Revenue Bond Limit - Increase
md:SB 188.summary: Raises the Maryland Transportation Authority's revenue bond limit from $4.0 billion to $5.0 billion, subject to existing bond issuance requirements.

md:SB 197.title: Land Use - Comprehensive and General Plans - Alteration of Elements
md:SB 197.summary: Reorganizes the elements local governments must include in comprehensive plans so they match State planning principles and apply uniformly, and adds guidance and requirements for plans and specific elements.

md:SB 205.title: Health Insurance - Mental Health and Substance Use Disorders - Codification of Federal Requirements
md:SB 205.summary: Writes parts of the 2024 federal Mental Health Parity Rule into Maryland law, barring discriminatory standards in treatment limits and requiring insurers to collect outcomes data and offer mental health and substance use benefits on par with medical benefits.

md:SB 210.title: Maryland Transportation Authority - Tolls, Fees, and Other Charges - Temporary Adjustments
md:SB 210.summary: Raises from 180 to 300 days the maximum length of a Maryland Transportation Authority emergency status in which temporary toll and fee increases take effect immediately, with public notice and comment procedures starting afterward.

md:SB 214.title: Cannabis - Sale and Distribution - Tetrahydrocannabinol Offenses
md:SB 214.summary: Bans selling or distributing THC products that violate potency, packaging or labeling rules or are advertised with a prohibited THC amount; lets the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission seize products sold at unlicensed locations and officers issue citations (fine up to $5,000).

md:SB 215.title: Cannabis Reform - Revisions
md:SB 215.summary: Changes cannabis law by removing on-site consumption licenses from the second licensing round, extending dispensary medical cannabis delivery to July 1, 2026, and allowing a licensee to be sold to its employees through an employee stock ownership plan.

md:SB 218.title: State Superintendent of Schools - Prolonged State of Emergency - Authority to Declare
md:SB 218.summary: Lets the State Superintendent of Schools, instead of the Governor, declare a prolonged state of emergency when an event prevents in-person attendance for at least 14 consecutive school days, allowing virtual instruction.

md:SB 219.title: Uninsured Employers' Fund - Assessments and Special Monitor
md:SB 219.summary: Raises the maximum extra assessment on workers' compensation awards and settlements for the Uninsured Employers' Fund from 1.0% to 1.5%, raises its fund balance thresholds, and requires a special monitor of its finances.

md:SB 228.title: Maryland Environmental Service - Authorizations and Requirements - Alterations
md:SB 228.summary: Expands duties the Maryland Environmental Service treasurer may delegate to the deputy treasurer, raises its small procurement limit from $25,000 to $50,000, and updates public notice for service district rate changes.

md:SB 23.title: Green and Renewable Energy Efficiency for Nonprofits (GREEN) Loan Program and Fund - Establishment
md:SB 23.summary: Creates a no-interest loan program and fund at the Maryland Clean Energy Center for nonprofits' renewable energy systems and efficiency upgrades, funded by Strategic Energy Investment Fund transfers and optional budget appropriations in fiscal 2028 and 2029.

md:SB 231.title: State Government - Public Employee Relations Act - Alterations
md:SB 231.summary: Lets the Public Employee Relations Board appoint up to three deputy directors, who must be attorneys; drops the public-health condition for unions to meet new employees by video; and limits the 10-day minimum voting period to union elections held by mail or electronic voting.

md:SB 237.title: Election Law - Presidential Electors - Selection and Voting
md:SB 237.summary: Requires presidential elector nominees to pledge to mark ballots for their party's or unaffiliated candidate's ticket, sets procedures for substitute electors, and treats an elector who refuses to present a ballot or votes against the pledge as vacating the office.

md:SB 241.title: Election Law - Individuals Released From State Correctional Facilities - Automatic Restoration of Voter Registration
md:SB 241.summary: Requires the corrections department to send the elections board a monthly list of people released from state prisons, and requires the board to restore the registrations of those previously registered with in-state addresses, with a notice they can decline.

md:SB 248.title: Department of Service and Civic Innovation - Maryland Corps Program Service Year Option Pathways - Revisions
md:SB 248.summary: Changes Maryland Corps rules: replaces the $15 hourly pay floor with the applicable county or State minimum wage, makes the $6,000 completion award cash only, drops the three-years-since-graduation limit, and repeals the Executive Fellows Program.

md:SB 249.title: Tobacco Product Licensees - Additional Licensure for Electronic Smoking Devices
md:SB 249.summary: Requires holders of cigarette or other tobacco product licenses who want to make, distribute or sell electronic smoking devices to get a separate license, with some fee exemptions. Existing license holders are excluded until their licenses expire.

md:SB 255.title: Voting Rights Act of 2026 - Counties and Municipal Corporations
md:SB 255.summary: Bars county and municipal election methods that dilute the voting strength of race, color or language minority groups where voting is polarized; lets the Attorney General or others sue, and lets courts order remedies. Statewide elections are excluded.

md:SB 257.title: Election Law - Notice to Permanent Absentee Voters
md:SB 257.summary: Changes the timing of the State Board of Elections' mailing to permanent absentee voters: it must be sent between 120 and 90 days before an election, replacing the current schedule tied to when absentee ballots are sent.

md:SB 264.title: Plant Disease Control - Nurseries - Inspection, Certification, and Licensing Fees
md:SB 264.summary: Raises fees for nursery certification, broker and dealer licenses, and nursery inspections, and requires the Department of Agriculture to report annually on licensees, inspections, pests found and compliance agreements to legislative committees starting January 31, 2026.

md:SB 265.title: Environment - Reservoir Augmentation Permit - Establishment
md:SB 265.summary: Creates a Reservoir Augmentation Program requiring a Department of the Environment permit to place reclaimed water in drinking-water reservoirs, with program fees and penalties funding it, and extends the Indirect Potable Reuse pilot program's end date from 2028 to 2030.

md:SB 266.title: Local Comprehensive Planning and State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy - Planning Principles
md:SB 266.summary: Replaces the 12 planning visions for local comprehensive plans with 8 planning principles, makes the State planning policy consist of the same principles, and updates a cross-reference in criteria for State funding of certain transportation projects.

md:SB 274.title: Fair Housing and Housing Discrimination - Regulations and Discriminatory Effect
md:SB 274.summary: Bars housing practices with a discriminatory effect (disparate impact or reinforcing segregated housing patterns), regardless of intent, unless the practice lacked discriminatory intent, was necessary for a substantial, legitimate and nondiscriminatory interest, and no less discriminatory means existed.

md:SB 279.title: Baltimore City - Cigarettes, Other Tobacco Products, and Electronic Smoking Devices - Enforcement and Licensure
md:SB 279.summary: Lets special enforcement officers in Baltimore City agencies enforce tobacco and vape licensing law, and requires city license applicants to get a city licensure authorization, with none for initial applicants from October 1, 2026 to October 1, 2027.

md:SB 28.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026
md:SB 28.summary: Sets a neutral-arbitrator process for State employee collective bargaining, ending in a binding award of one side's last offer, with wage and funding terms subject to budget and legislative approval. Takes effect only if voters ratify a related constitutional amendment.

md:SB 293.title: County Boards of Education - Antibias Training for Members - Requirement (County Board Member Antibias Training Act)
md:SB 293.summary: Requires each county school board member to complete the county's antibias training at least once during their term, conducted separately from the employee training.

md:SB 295.title: Income Tax - Income Tax Reconciliation Program - Established (Maryland Fair Taxation for Justice-Involved Individuals Act)
md:SB 295.summary: Creates an Income Tax Reconciliation Program letting incarcerated people who could not file returns set up installment plans with waived interest and penalties for tax years 2025 through 2029, excluding people convicted of crimes committed while holding elected office.

md:SB 305.title: Qualifying Nonprofit Organizations - Incarcerated Individual Training and Reentry Grant Fund - Extension
md:SB 305.summary: Extends by one year, through fiscal 2029, the Governor's authority to budget $1 million annually for a grant to nonprofits that train formerly incarcerated individuals in automotive repair.

md:SB 31.title: School Construction and Housing - School Zones and Adequate Public Facilities Ordinances
md:SB 31.summary: Requires local school boards to report student residency and school zones annually and consult municipalities on facilities plans. Provides that a county adequate public facilities ordinance with a time limit on school-capacity restrictions may delay construction starts but not plan processing.

md:SB 327.title: Affordable Housing Payment In Lieu of Taxes Expansion Act
md:SB 327.summary: Lets counties exempt rental housing from property tax if the owner keeps at least 25% of units affordable for at least 15 years under a payment in lieu of taxes agreement.

md:SB 342.title: Voting Rights Act of 2025 - Counties and Municipal Corporations
md:SB 342.summary: Bars county and municipal election methods that dilute the voting strength of race, color or language minority groups where voting is polarized; lets the Attorney General or others sue, and lets courts order remedies. Statewide elections are excluded.

md:SB 343.title: State's Attorneys - Reconstitution of Task Force to Study Transparency Standards for State's Attorneys
md:SB 343.summary: Reestablishes a task force to study minimum transparency standards for State's Attorneys, staffed by Legislative Services, with annual reports starting December 31, 2025. The task force ends June 30, 2028.

md:SB 348.title: Hospitals and Freestanding Birthing Centers - High-Risk Pregnancies - Communication After Discharge
md:SB 348.summary: Requires hospitals and freestanding birthing centers to "contact" rather than call the birthing parent 24 to 48 hours after discharge from a high-risk pregnancy delivery, to evaluate their status and give information about postpartum complications.

md:SB 351.title: Private Passenger Motor Vehicle Insurance - Use of Programs That Measure the Operation of an Insured Vehicle
md:SB 351.summary: Bars private passenger auto insurers from requiring vehicle-monitoring programs or using their data to cancel, not renew or refuse to underwrite, requires disclosure and a data-correction process, and directs regulations limiting data collected by July 1, 2027. Applies from January 1, 2027.

md:SB 354.title: Business Regulation - Charitable Organizations - Audit and Review Thresholds
md:SB 354.summary: Raises the charitable contribution income levels requiring an audit with registration from $750,000 to $1 million, and a review from $300,000 to $400,000. Raises the documentation-substitute threshold to $400,000.

md:SB 356.title: Public Health - Repeal of Prohibition on Transfer of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (Carlton R. Smith Act)
md:SB 356.summary: Repeals the misdemeanor offense and penalty for knowingly transferring or attempting to transfer HIV to another person.

md:SB 365.title: Department of Commerce - Nonprofit Organizations Navigator - Established
md:SB 365.summary: Creates a nonprofit organizations navigator in the Department of Commerce to help nonprofits find and apply for State grants, adds the navigator as a nonvoting member of the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council, and repeals the Council's 2024 State Grants Ombudsperson study.

md:SB 373.title: State Personnel - BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department - Collective Bargaining and Arbitration Processes
md:SB 373.summary: Establishes binding arbitration for collective bargaining impasses for uniformed fire employees of the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department, with arbitrator wage decisions limited by the State budget.

md:SB 385.title: Pblc Hlth - Recommendations for Immunizations, Screenings, and Prvntv Srvcs - Phrmcst Admin and Rqrd Hlth Ins Cvrg (The Vax Act)
md:SB 385.summary: Requires the Secretary of Health to issue recommended immunizations, screenings and preventive services (with notice and comment for some), lets pharmacists give Secretary-recommended vaccines to people 7 and older, and changes insurance coverage requirements, applying from January 1, 2027.

md:SB 387.title: Food Rtlers & Thrd-Prty Food Delivery Service Prvdrs - Dynamic Pricing and Personal Data(Protection From Predatory Pricing Act)
md:SB 387.summary: Bars food retailers and third-party food delivery services from using dynamic pricing or personal data to raise prices for a consumer, or protected class data to deny benefits. Violations are unfair trade practices without a private right of action.

md:SB 389.title: Land Use - Transit-Oriented Development - Alterations (Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act)
md:SB 389.summary: Lets local governments elect enterprise zone status for certain transit-oriented development areas, bars minimum parking requirements within 0.25 miles of certain rail stations (with exceptions), and delays development excise taxes and impact fees on some residential projects.

md:SB 390.title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Statements and Certificates of Violations
md:SB 390.summary: Lets technicians employed by or contracted with an agency, not only law enforcement officers, sign speed camera citations and certify violations. Requires "reasonable training" on the system before certifying violation certificates.

md:SB 4.title: Charitable Organizations - Charitable Donation and Tax-Exempt Status - Revocation (Keeping Charities Nonpartisan Act of 2026)
md:SB 4.summary: Bars charities and private foundations, except certain religious organizations, from participating in political campaigns for or against candidates, with a warning first, then civil penalties up to $1,000, and up to two years' tax-exempt status loss for willful violations. Contingent on federal changes.

md:SB 41.title: Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board - Membership - Alteration
md:SB 41.summary: Adds the Comptroller or the Comptroller's designee as a member of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board.

md:SB 411.title: Hospitals - Clinical Staffing Committees and Plans - Establishment (Safe Staffing Act of 2026)
md:SB 411.summary: Requires hospitals to follow their accreditor's and Medicare staffing standards and form clinical staffing committees of managers and employees, with the chief nurse executive drafting a staffing plan the committee finalizes. State hospitals are excluded.

md:SB 417.title: Lbr and Employment - Mndtry Meetings on Religious or Political Matters - Employee Attendance and Participation (Md Worker Freedom Act)
md:SB 417.summary: Bars employers from disciplining or refusing to hire people who decline to attend or listen to employer-sponsored meetings about the employer's views on religious or political matters. The Labor Commissioner enforces and must produce a poster by November 1, 2026.

md:SB 425.title: Environment - Coal Combustion By-Products - Fees, Coordinating Committee, and Regulations
md:SB 425.summary: Changes the annual fee for coal combustion by-product generators to account for volume stored, requires excess fee revenue to fund reuse and cleanup, and creates a Statewide CCB Coordinating Committee staffed jointly by the Environment department and a Natural Resources research program.

md:SB 431.title: Registered Apprenticeship Investments for a Stronger Economy (RAISE) Act
md:SB 431.summary: Creates the Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development, a qualified intermediary program, and a Pay Per Apprentice program and fund; sets a minimum one-to-one journeyworker-to-apprentice ratio with deviations allowed; and repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee.

md:SB 432.title: Criminal Records - Expungement and Maryland Judiciary Case Search (Expungement Reform Act of 2025)
md:SB 432.summary: Changes waiting periods for expunging convictions, expands the misdemeanors eligible for expungement and the factors courts consider, and bars Maryland Judiciary Case Search from showing certain charges, such as stet charges over three years old.

md:SB 439.title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis The bill is on third reading for final passage.
md:SB 439.summary: Bars employers of fire and rescue public safety employees from disciplining or discriminating against them for holding a medical cannabis certification or testing positive for cannabis while certified, with exceptions for impairment, on-duty use and federal-law conflicts.

md:SB 444.title: Public Safety - Gun Buyback Programs - Destruction of Firearms
md:SB 444.summary: Requires gun buyback programs to destroy each surrendered firearm and its parts unless police determine it is stolen or evidence, with fines up to $10,000 per violation and dealer license revocation. Operating a program otherwise is a misdemeanor.

md:SB 447.title: Hospitals - Emergency Pregnancy-Related Medical Conditions - Procedures
md:SB 447.summary: Requires hospitals with emergency departments to stabilize patients with emergency pregnancy-related conditions or transfer them, including terminating a pregnancy when medically necessary to stabilize the patient. Bars retaliation against providers and employees and sets civil penalties.

md:SB 451.title: Adult Education - High School Diploma by Examination - Requirements and Study
md:SB 451.summary: Requires the Department of Labor to let people take all components of the high school diploma by examination in either English or Spanish, identify other languages for the GED test, and study offering it in more languages, reporting by December 1, 2026.

md:SB 475.title: Criminal Procedure - Evidence - Protecting Artists' Creative Expression (PACE Act)
md:SB 475.summary: Bars a defendant's creative expression, such as music, poetry or film, from being used as evidence in criminal or juvenile cases unless a court finds it was meant literally, closely tied to the offense, relevant, and more probative than prejudicial.

md:SB 487.title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Safety Corridors (Vulnerable Road User Protection Act of 2026)
md:SB 487.summary: Allows the State Highway Administration to use speed cameras on state highway segments it identifies as high risk to vulnerable road users, such as pedestrians and cyclists, and to permit local governments to do so.

md:SB 49.title: Consumer Protection - Automatic Renewals
md:SB 49.summary: Requires sellers to clearly disclose automatic renewal terms and cancellation methods before a consumer agrees, and to let consumers cancel through an easy mechanism. Violations are unfair or deceptive trade practices, with no private right of action.

md:SB 495.title: Opioid Restitution Fund - Authorized Uses
md:SB 495.summary: Allows the Opioid Restitution Fund to pay operating and personnel costs of the Attorney General's Opioids Enforcement Unit for investigations and enforcement tied to opioid judgments and settlements, through June 2029. Requires an annual report on the unit's investigations and lawsuits.

md:SB 504.title: Data Privacy - Consumer Data, Public Records, and Message Switching System (Data Privacy Act)
md:SB 504.summary: Changes Maryland's online data privacy, public records and law enforcement database laws on immigration enforcement. Bars selling consumer data to government units that supported civil immigration enforcement in the prior six months, and requires court warrants for certain data requests.

md:SB 520.title: Property Tax - Charter Counties - Application of County Tax Limitation
md:SB 520.summary: Allows a charter county council, other than Prince George's, to override its charter's property tax rate or revenue limit by simple majority to fund the approved county public safety budget.

md:SB 522.title: Home Builders - New Home Sales - Notice of Appliance Warranty Registration
md:SB 522.summary: Requires home builders to include in a new-home sales contract, and give buyers at closing, the registration date and remaining time on warranties for each appliance they registered, including the heating and cooling system.

md:SB 555.title: Public Information Act - Denials - Pending Litigation
md:SB 555.summary: Allows, but does not require, a public records custodian to deny inspection of records created for pending or reasonably anticipated litigation involving the State, a local government or their officers or employees, except court records and records of concluded litigation.

md:SB 56.title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center - External Data Sharing With Third-Party Data Centers for Multistate Reporting - Authorization
md:SB 56.summary: Allows the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center, if its governing board approves, to share individual-level student and workforce data with one third-party data center at a time for multistate research, under a written agreement and security requirements.

md:SB 566.title: Real Property - Filing Fee for Residential Mortgage Foreclosure - Increase
md:SB 566.summary: Raises the filing fee for foreclosing on residential property by mortgage or deed of trust from $300 to $450.

md:SB 585.title: Human-Relevant Research Fund - Collection of Contributions - Responsible Entity
md:SB 585.summary: Moves collection of required contributions to the Human-Relevant Research Fund from specified research facilities from the Department of Health to the Department of Agriculture. Facilities and payment amounts do not change.

md:SB 587.title: State Government - Maryland Reparations Commission
md:SB 587.summary: Creates the Maryland Reparations Commission to study and recommend benefits, including possible monetary compensation, for people of Black African origin whose ancestors were enslaved in Maryland or affected by what the bill calls inequitable government policies. Reports due January 1 and November 1, 2027.

md:SB 594.title: Cannabis - Advertising - Alterations
md:SB 594.summary: Changes cannabis advertising rules: allows dispensaries more exterior signage, changes how audience age is determined, requires regulations accepting event organizers' attestations on audience composition, and lowers the required ownership share for social equity applicants from 65% to 55%.

md:SB 599.title: Behavioral Health Crisis Response Grant Program - Funding
md:SB 599.summary: Requires the Governor to include $5 million in each budget from fiscal 2027 through 2029 for the Behavioral Health Crisis Response Grant Program.

md:SB 60.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Required Coverage for Calcium Score Testing
md:SB 60.summary: Requires insurers, health plans, HMOs and Maryland Medicaid to cover calcium score testing, per the latest American College of Cardiology guidelines, for people with at least three of four risk factors: diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, family history of early heart disease.

md:SB 600.title: Baltimore City - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems - Authorization of Pilot Program
md:SB 600.summary: Authorizes stop sign cameras in school zones in Takoma Park and parts of Baltimore City through June 30, 2029, with civil penalties up to $40. Lets those localities use fine revenue to recover implementation and administrative costs.

md:SB 606.title: Residential Real Property - Tenants' Right of First Refusal
md:SB 606.summary: Provides that after closing on a sale between an owner and a third party, liability for failing to follow a tenant's right of first refusal rests only on the owner and does not attach to the property.

md:SB 608.title: Criminal Procedure - U Nonimmigrant Status Petitions
md:SB 608.summary: Changes the U visa certification process for crime victims: lets a victim's attorney or advocate request it, bars denial solely because of elapsed time since the crime, cuts the response deadline from 90 to 45 days, and requires a written explanation of denials.

md:SB 63.title: Cooperative Housing Corporations, Condominiums, & Homeowners Assns - Funding of Reserve Accounts and Preparation of Funding Plans
md:SB 63.summary: Changes reserve funding rules for condominiums, co-ops and homeowners associations: requires a funding plan, extends from three to five years the time to reach recommended reserve levels, and allows deviation from funding requirements after a financial hardship determination.

md:SB 632.title: Crctnl Services - Comprehensive Rehabilitative Prerelease Services - Female Incarcerated Individuals (The Monica Cooper Prerelease Act)
md:SB 632.summary: Requires the women's prerelease unit to be in Baltimore City on at least 3 acres, directs the Department of General Services to seek proposals and award the construction contract, expands rehabilitative services for incarcerated women, and requires progress reports.

md:SB 648.title: Correctional Services - Medical Parole - Life Imprisonment
md:SB 648.summary: Repeals the Governor's power to disapprove a Parole Commission decision granting medical parole to a person serving a life sentence.

md:SB 65.title: Election Law - Campaign Finance - Exploratory Committees
md:SB 65.summary: Creates exploratory committees for potential candidates, covered by political committee rules but with no limit on donations. Also caps at $24,000 per election cycle transfers from certain officeholders' and caucus campaign committees to a party's State central committee.

md:SB 656.title: Pblc Hlth - Cosmetic Prdcts - Enfrcmt & Pnlts for Prhbtd Ingredients (Crown & Care Act - Protecting Cmnts Frm Harmful Hair Chemicals)
md:SB 656.summary: Makes a person who knowingly manufactures or sells cosmetics containing any of 24 listed ingredients liable for civil damages for actual harm, treats violations as unfair trade practices, and requires a plan for a special fund for related research and treatment.

md:SB 666.title: Maryland Community Action Agencies - Funding
md:SB 666.summary: Requires the Governor to include $250,000 in the budget each year for fiscal 2027 through 2030 for operating grants to community action agencies.

md:SB 673.title: State Procurement - Apprenticeship Program Accountability and Completion
md:SB 673.summary: Requires apprenticeship programs that supply apprentices on certain state contracts, once they have graduated a cohort, to have a completion rate of at least 25%, and limits the registered apprenticeship requirement to contracts worth $1 million or more.

md:SB 674.title: Maryland Commission for Women - Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control
md:SB 674.summary: Requires the Maryland Commission for Women to create a collaborative to study and recommend ways to advance coverage of over-the-counter birth control, with an interim report by January 1, 2026 and a final report by December 1, 2027.

md:SB 676.title: Health Care Facilities - Hospitals and Freestanding Birthing Centers - Perinatal Care Standards
md:SB 676.summary: Requires the Department of Health to adopt, by October 1, 2026, minimum perinatal care standards meeting or exceeding the Maryland Perinatal System Standards for hospitals with obstetrical services and freestanding birthing centers, as a condition of licensure.

md:SB 679.title: Nursing Homes - Cost Reports (Nursing Home Care Crisis Transparency Act)
md:SB 679.summary: Requires the Department of Health to review cost reports from Medicaid-participating nursing homes, including spending on contracted nursing and direct care wages, and report findings annually from October 1, 2025 through 2029.

md:SB 685.title: Election Law - Local Boards of Elections - Language Assistance Program
md:SB 685.summary: Creates a Language Assistance Program: where the State Board of Elections finds significant need (over 2% of voting-age citizens, or 4,000, share a non-English language with limited English), local boards must offer translators at early voting and polling places.

md:SB 69.title: Nonprofit Organizations Navigator - Termination Provision - Repeal
md:SB 69.summary: Makes the Department of Commerce's nonprofit organizations navigator position permanent by repealing its termination date.

md:SB 695.title: Labor and Employment - Uninsured Employers' Fund Board - Membership and Reserves
md:SB 695.summary: Expands the Uninsured Employers' Fund board from three to five members, changes member qualifications, and requires the board to establish reserves for potential losses.

md:SB 708.title: Sports Wagering - Independent Evaluation of Sports Wagering Content - Required
md:SB 708.summary: As amended in the House, repeals the ban on video lottery license applicants and holders making campaign contributions, alters video lottery proceeds distribution at certain facilities, and requires sports wagering licensees to use a licensed independent evaluator once three are licensed.

md:SB 740.title: Transportation Network Companies - Deactivation of Operators
md:SB 740.summary: Requires transportation network companies to keep and apply a written policy, including an internal appeal process, for deactivating drivers.

md:SB 750.title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Part-Time Faculty
md:SB 750.summary: Allows part-time faculty at the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland to bargain collectively.

md:SB 757.title: Economic Development - Local Sourcing Database
md:SB 757.summary: Requires the Department of Commerce to maintain a searchable online Maryland Local Sourcing Portal connecting businesses with local sources for tariff-affected goods and supplies, with annual reports, through September 2031.

md:SB 764.title: Education - Minimum Wage for Education Support Professionals - Report
md:SB 764.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to study education support professionals' wages and report by December 1, 2026 on the cost of a $25-per-hour minimum wage, by school system.

md:SB 789.title: Higher Education - Hunger-Free Campus Grant Program - Alterations
md:SB 789.summary: Allows private colleges to receive the state's hunger-free campus designation, but not grant funding under the Hunger-Free Campus Grant Program.

md:SB 790.title: Public Health Reform Act
md:SB 790.summary: Changes the Commission on Public Health's membership and duties, extends its termination date, creates a Public Health Workforce Development Fund, organizes the Medical Reserve Corps, and requires the Department of Legislative Services to develop a process to assess health equity impacts of legislation.

md:SB 811.title: Real Property - New Home Sales - Entry of Final Sale Price in Multiple Listing Service
md:SB 811.summary: Requires a developer, builder, broker or real estate agent to enter a new home's final sale price, within 30 days after the sale closes, into a database available to real estate professionals. Takes effect July 1, 2027.

md:SB 820.title: Municipalities - Enforcement of Ordinances and Resolutions
md:SB 820.summary: Raises the maximum fine a municipality may impose for a misdemeanor or municipal infraction from $1,000 to $5,000.

tx:SB 1|general appropriations bill.title: General Appropriations Bill
tx:SB 1|general appropriations bill.summary: Sets the state budget for the two fiscal years ending August 2026 and August 2027, appropriating about $176 billion for fiscal 2026 and $162 billion for fiscal 2027 from all fund sources to state agencies, courts, schools and universities.

tx:HB 3556|relating to certain structure.title: Relating to certain structures located near a National Wildlife Refuge
tx:HB 3556|relating to certain structure.summary: Requires anyone planning a structure taller than 575 feet in certain less-populous Gulf Coast counties with national wildlife refuges, or neighboring counties, to seek state wildlife department review 90 days ahead; the department may require measures to protect migratory birds, subject to an administrative appeal.

tx:SB 30|relating to recovery of health.title: Relating to recovery of health care-related damages in certain civil actions
tx:SB 30|relating to recovery of health.summary: Limits evidence of medical costs in injury and wrongful death suits to amounts insurers and patients actually paid; for uninsured care, allows benchmarks such as Medicare rates alongside billed charges, and requires claimants to disclose letters of protection and referral arrangements.

tx:SB 25|relating to health and nutritio.title: Relating to health and nutrition standards to promote healthy living, including requirements for food labeling, primary and secondary education, higher education, and continuing education for certain health care professionals; authorizing a civil penalty
tx:SB 25|relating to health and nutritio.summary: Requires warning labels on food products containing certain listed additives, for labels created from 2027, with attorney general penalties up to $50,000 a day per product; also requires daily physical activity for young students, a high school nutrition elective, and nutrition training for health professionals.

tx:HB 5111|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of campaign treasurer appointments and related matters and the content of and posting of information contained in a campaign treasurer appointment; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 5111|relating to the regulation of.summary: Sets eligibility rules for campaign treasurers, barring registered lobbyists, people already serving as another campaign's treasurer, and people convicted of certain election crimes; campaigns must replace an ineligible treasurer within 14 business days or face civil penalties.

tx:HB 1268|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas technology and innovation program
tx:HB 1268|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates a state program that gives grants to Texas-based businesses that win federal small business innovation research or technology transfer awards, matching or supplementing that federal money, limited to one grant per business each year.

tx:SB 2024|relating to a prohibition on.title: Relating to a prohibition on marketing, advertising, or selling certain e-cigarette products; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 2024|relating to a prohibition on.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor to sell or market vapes disguised as other products, packaged with celebrity names or similar features, made in China or another federally designated foreign adversary, or containing substances such as cannabinoids, alcohol or kratom.

tx:SB 17|relating to the purchase or acq.title: Relating to the purchase or acquisition of an interest in real property by certain aliens or foreign entities
tx:SB 17|relating to the purchase or acq.summary: Bars governments, companies and certain individuals tied to countries named as national security threats in recent federal intelligence assessments, or designated by the governor, from buying Texas real estate, with exceptions for U.S. citizens, permanent residents and some homes; violations can bring felony charges, fines and forced sale.

tx:SB 2185|relating to the bilingual edu.title: Relating to the bilingual education allotment under the public school finance system
tx:SB 2185|relating to the bilingual edu.summary: Lets the state approve extra per-student funding for school districts using approved alternative bilingual methods with dual-language immersion programs, capped at $10 million statewide per two-year budget, and allows bilingual program funds to pay teacher salaries, not only salary supplements.

tx:HB 610|relating to a severance paymen.title: Relating to a severance payment to a superintendent of a school district
tx:HB 610|relating to a severance paymen.summary: Bars school boards from giving a departing superintendent a severance payment larger than six months' salary and benefits, down from the one-year level that now triggers a cut in state school funding, and requires boards to report severance terms to the state.

tx:HB 5151|relating to the prohibition o.title: Relating to the prohibition of certain new mines, quarries, or rock crushing operations
tx:HB 5151|relating to the prohibition o.summary: Bars state environmental regulators from permitting new rock quarry or crushing facilities within four miles of certain lakes with national fish hatcheries or the entrance to a certain cavern state park, or two miles of a certain youth camp; sites permitted by Jan. 1, 2025, are exempt.

tx:HB 45|relating to the duty of the att.title: Relating to the duty of the attorney general to prosecute human trafficking criminal offenses
tx:HB 45|relating to the duty of the att.summary: Requires police to send the attorney general a copy of any probable-cause report on a human trafficking offense they give local prosecutors, and requires the attorney general to take over prosecution if the local prosecutor takes no action within 180 days.

tx:HB 4120|relating to allowing certain.title: Relating to allowing certain inmates to apply for benefits under certain public benefits programs to be provided at the time of discharge or release
tx:HB 4120|relating to allowing certain.summary: Expands an existing agreement between the state health and prison agencies so inmates are screened before release for eligibility for public benefits such as Medicaid, CHIP, TANF and SNAP, not just food assistance, so benefits can start at release.

tx:SB 10|relating to the calculation of.title: Relating to the calculation of the voter-approval tax rate for certain taxing units
tx:SB 10|relating to the calculation of.summary: Lowers from 3.5% to 2.5% the yearly growth in operating property tax revenue that cities and counties of 75,000 or more people, and certain other local taxing units, may adopt without voter approval, starting with 2026 taxes.

tx:SB 2703|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to regulate condominiums
tx:SB 2703|relating to the authority of.summary: Bars cities and counties from treating a condominium as a land subdivision or requiring a subdivision plat to create or change a condominium, for condominium declarations filed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 1883|relating to the approval of l.title: Relating to the approval of land use assumptions, capital improvement plans, and impact fees
tx:SB 1883|relating to the approval of l.summary: Requires a two-thirds vote of a local governing body to adopt impact fees on new development, bars raising an impact fee more than once every three years, and requires related plans to be public at least 60 days before hearing notice.

tx:SB 3059|relating to the preservation.title: Relating to the preservation, maintenance, restoration, and protection of the Alamo complex and surrounding area by the Alamo Commission
tx:SB 3059|relating to the preservation.summary: Moves management of the Alamo and surrounding grounds from the General Land Office to a five-member Alamo Commission made up of the governor, lieutenant governor, House speaker and two legislators, with the transfer completed by January 1, 2028.

tx:HB 2674|relating to prohibiting the r.title: Relating to prohibiting the regulation of homeschool programs
tx:HB 2674|relating to prohibiting the r.summary: Bars the Texas Education Agency, State Board of Education and other state-funded educational institutions from adopting any rule or policy that regulates a home school's educational program, starting with the 2025-2026 school year.

tx:SB 3070|relating to the abolishment o.title: Relating to the abolishment of the Texas Lottery Commission and the transfer of the administration of the state lottery and the licensing and regulation of charitable bingo to the Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation; creating criminal offenses
tx:SB 3070|relating to the abolishment o.summary: Abolishes the Texas Lottery Commission and moves the lottery and charitable bingo to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation; bans buying lottery tickets, or selling them for pay, by phone or app, and ends the lottery in 2029 unless renewed after review.

tx:SB 1233|relating to information regar.title: Relating to information regarding perinatal palliative care; creating an administrative penalty
tx:SB 1233|relating to information regar.summary: Requires a health care provider who diagnoses an unborn child with a life-threatening or life-limiting condition to give the pregnant woman state information on perinatal palliative care and a provider list; repeat violations carry a $1,000 administrative penalty.

tx:HB 1|relating to resident youth camp.title: Relating to resident youth camp emergency plans and preparedness; authorizing a civil penalty
tx:HB 1|relating to resident youth camp.summary: Requires licensed youth camps to adopt written emergency plans filed with the state health department, notify parents if any part of a camp is in a floodplain, give campers a safety orientation, and meet state-set minimum camper-to-counselor ratios for overnight stays.

tx:HB 4308|relating to the creation of i.title: Relating to the creation of industrial development districts in certain counties; providing authority to issue bonds; and providing authority to impose assessments, fees, or taxes
tx:HB 4308|relating to the creation of i.summary: Lets commissioners courts in counties of three million or fewer people create industrial development districts that can build improvements, offer loans and grants to businesses, issue bonds, and impose assessments, fees or taxes.

tx:HB 2|relating to public education and.title: Relating to public education and public school finance
tx:HB 2|relating to public education and.summary: Changes school funding and teacher pay, giving districts per-teacher money for raises to teachers with three or more years' experience of up to $8,000 in districts of 5,000 or fewer students and $5,000 in larger ones, and revising special education and teacher preparation funding.

tx:HB 3221|relating to certain employer.title: Relating to certain employer contributions to the Teacher Retirement System of Texas
tx:HB 3221|relating to certain employer.summary: Changes how employers' contributions to the Teacher Retirement System are calculated for charter school employees and districts exempt from the state minimum salary schedule, basing them on the state minimum salary like other public schools, starting in 2025-2026.

tx:SB 1957|relating to the eligibility o.title: Relating to the eligibility of a person to serve on a civilian oversight board
tx:SB 1957|relating to the eligibility o.summary: Bars anyone who has been convicted of, or placed on deferred adjudication for, a felony from serving on a city civilian oversight board that monitors or investigates police officers, firefighters or their departments.

tx:HB 5499|relating to towing fee studie.title: Relating to towing fee studies and the amount of nonconsent towing fees in certain political subdivisions; authorizing an increase in existing fees
tx:HB 5499|relating to towing fee studie.summary: Requires local governments that regulate nonconsent towing fees to study those fees every two years and update them within 30 days; in counties of 750,000 or more, fees default to the state rate if a local government fails to act.

tx:SB 1253|relating to the provision by.title: Relating to the provision by a political subdivision of credits against impact fees to builders and developers for certain water conservation and reuse projects
tx:SB 1253|relating to the provision by.summary: Requires local governments to give builders and developers credits against water and wastewater impact fees for facilities or products that conserve or reuse water, and lets the Hays Trinity Groundwater Conservation District charge a production fee of up to 30 cents per 1,000 gallons, rising 5% yearly.

tx:HB 3284|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas Commission on Marriage and Family
tx:HB 3284|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates a temporary seven-member state commission, appointed by the governor, lieutenant governor and House speaker, to study ways to encourage marriage and family formation and report recommendations to the Legislature by November 1, 2026; it expires at the end of 2026.

tx:HB 4|relating to the assessment of pu.title: Relating to the assessment of public school students, public school accountability and actions, and proceedings challenging the operations of the public school system
tx:HB 4|relating to the assessment of pu.summary: Requires the state to replace its current student testing system by the 2027-2028 school year with end-of-year tests plus optional beginning- and middle-of-year progress tests, revises school accountability ratings, and limits use of school funds to sue the state.

tx:HB 1006|relating to the amendment of.title: Relating to the amendment of restrictive covenants applicable to certain subdivisions
tx:HB 1006|relating to the amendment of.summary: Lets owners of at least 67% of lots in large subdivisions platted before 1965 that span several cities and counties vote by mailed ballot to amend deed restrictions for all or part of the subdivision.

tx:SB 38|relating to the eviction from r.title: Relating to the eviction from real property of certain persons not entitled to enter, occupy, or remain in possession of the premises
tx:SB 38|relating to the eviction from r.summary: Speeds up eviction suits against tenants and unauthorized occupants, requiring trials 10 to 21 days after filing, letting justice courts rule without a trial when no facts are genuinely disputed, and letting landlords use other officers if constables miss five-business-day service deadlines.

tx:SB 2878|relating to the operation and.title: Relating to the operation and administration of and practices and procedures related to proceedings in the judicial branch of state government, including court security, court documents and arrest warrants, document delivery, juvenile boards, and youth diversion, and to public office candidate eligibility; increasing a criminal penalty; authorizing fees
tx:SB 2878|relating to the operation and.summary: Makes wide-ranging changes to Texas courts, including creating and reorganizing courts, and revising rules on court security, court records and arrest warrants, juvenile boards, youth diversion and expunction of certain records; increases a criminal penalty and authorizes new fees.

tx:SB 3031|relating to the punishment fo.title: Relating to the punishment for the offense of aggravated assault
