tx:SB 3031|relating to the punishment fo.summary: Makes aggravated assault a first-degree felony when the attacker fires a gun from inside or while traveling to or from a vehicle and causes any bodily injury, property damage or fear of serious injury, rather than only serious injury.

tx:HB 4535|relating to covid 19 vaccine.title: Relating to COVID-19 vaccine administration requirements
tx:HB 4535|relating to covid 19 vaccine.summary: Requires health care providers to get written informed consent before giving a COVID-19 vaccine, including a parent's consent for minors, and to provide a state-developed information sheet on the vaccine's benefits, risks, expedited development and manufacturer liability; violators may face professional discipline.

tx:SB 2|relating to the establishment of.title: Relating to the establishment of an education savings account program
tx:SB 2|relating to the establishment of.summary: Creates a state-run education savings account program letting families use public money for private school and other approved education costs, generally about 85% of average per-student school funding, up to $30,000 for students with disabilities and $2,000 for homeschoolers, capped at $1 billion for 2025–2027.

tx:SB 6|relating to the planning for int.title: Relating to the planning for, interconnection and operation of, and costs related to providing service for certain electrical loads
tx:SB 6|relating to the planning for int.summary: Sets new state rules for connecting very large electricity users, generally those of 75 megawatts or more, to the Texas grid, requiring them to share connection costs, disclose duplicate requests and allow their power to be cut during grid emergencies.

tx:SB 857|relating to the authorized rem.title: Relating to the authorized removal of certain motor vehicles
tx:SB 857|relating to the authorized rem.summary: Lets police and state license and weight inspectors remove a vehicle from a highway, or order it moved, when the driver has no valid license, is driving with a suspended license, or lacks required liability insurance.

tx:SB 15|relating to size and density re.title: Relating to size and density requirements for residential lots in certain municipalities; authorizing a fee
tx:SB 15|relating to size and density re.summary: Bars large cities in big counties from requiring lots in new single-family subdivisions of five acres or more to exceed 3,000 square feet, 30 feet wide or 75 feet deep, and limits other small-lot rules, with exceptions near airports and military bases.

tx:HB 521|relating to accommodating vote.title: Relating to accommodating voters with a disability; creating criminal offenses
tx:HB 521|relating to accommodating vote.summary: Changes curbside voting rules: voters must sign a form before receiving a curbside ballot, electioneering is banned within 20 feet of curbside parking spaces, and people driving seven or more voters to the polls must sign a form, with failure a misdemeanor.

tx:SB 986|relating to procedures under t.title: Relating to procedures under the public information law, including expedited responses and charges for bad faith requests
tx:SB 986|relating to procedures under t.summary: Lets government offices with trained staff withhold requested public records without first seeking an attorney general ruling if they respond within 10 business days and allow appeals, and lets the attorney general charge offices that seek rulings in bad faith $1,000 plus $500 a day.

tx:SB 1610|relating to sexually violent.title: Relating to sexually violent predators, to the Texas Civil Commitment Office, and to the prosecution of the offense of harassment by sexually violent predators and other persons confined in certain facilities; amending certain sex offender registration requirements; increasing criminal penalties
tx:SB 1610|relating to sexually violent.summary: Sets a prison sentence of 25 years to life for felonies committed by people civilly committed as sexually violent predators, and changes rules on assaults and harassment involving civil commitment staff and facilities, sex offender registration and the state civil commitment office.

tx:SB 1637|relating to the prosecution o.title: Relating to the prosecution of the offense of deadly conduct
tx:SB 1637|relating to the prosecution o.summary: Removes the presumption of recklessness when an on-duty peace officer points a gun at someone, and exempts on-duty officers from the deadly conduct offense of firing at people when they reasonably believed the shooting was legally justified.

tx:HB 112|relating to the creation and o.title: Relating to the creation and operation of a science park district in certain counties that may impose assessments, fees, and taxes
tx:HB 112|relating to the creation and o.summary: Lets landowners in or next to counties of 800,000 or more people petition the state to create science park districts that can issue bonds for research and technology projects, and creates a seven-member governor-appointed commission to plan them.

tx:SB 13|relating to a school district s.title: Relating to a school district's library materials and catalog, the establishment of local school library advisory councils, and parental rights regarding public school library catalogs and access by the parent's child to library materials
tx:SB 13|relating to a school district s.summary: Requires school boards to approve library book purchases and donations, bars school library materials with harmful, indecent or profane content, gives parents access to records of books their child borrows, and requires a parent library advisory council when enough parents petition for one.

tx:SB 1188|relating to electronic health.title: Relating to electronic health record requirements; authorizing a civil penalty
tx:SB 1188|relating to electronic health.summary: Requires electronic health records of Texans to be stored in the United States, gives parents full access to their minor children's records, requires records to note biological sex as observed at birth, and lets doctors use artificial intelligence if they review results and tell patients.

tx:SB 1362|relating to prohibiting the r.title: Relating to prohibiting the recognition, service, and enforcement of extreme risk protective orders; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 1362|relating to prohibiting the r.summary: Bars state and local government entities from adopting or enforcing policies on extreme risk protective orders, court orders removing guns from people not criminally charged, unless state law allows, bars related federal grants, and makes serving or enforcing a non-Texas order a state jail felony.

tx:SB 650|relating to requiring the use.title: Relating to requiring the use of electronically readable information to verify a purchaser's age in the retail sale of alcoholic beverages
tx:SB 650|relating to requiring the use.summary: Requires most retailers selling alcohol for off-premises consumption to scan or manually enter a buyer's driver's license or ID data to verify age, with discipline for skipping scans starting September 2027, and shields sellers from discipline when a scan showed a valid ID.

tx:HB 229|relating to general definition.title: Relating to general definitions for and collection of governmental information regarding biological sex
tx:HB 229|relating to general definition.summary: Defines sex in state law as biological sex, either male or female, along with related terms like man, woman, mother and father, and requires government agencies that collect data on a person's sex to record each person as either male or female.

tx:SB 961|relating to fraud prevention a.title: Relating to fraud prevention and verifying eligibility for benefits under Medicaid
tx:SB 961|relating to fraud prevention a.summary: Requires the state to verify Medicaid applicants' income, residency, citizenship and other eligibility facts rather than accept their own statements, and to check for out-of-state food benefit purchases, lottery winnings and canceled voter registrations that could signal ineligibility.

tx:SB 2073|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of an appraisal district to purchase, finance the purchase of, or lease real property or construct or finance the construction of improvements to real property
tx:SB 2073|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets county appraisal districts buy, lease or build offices, and finance them, without local taxing units' approval of the financing, and treats building purchase proposals as approved when taxing units fail to act within 30 days.

tx:HB 3225|relating to the prohibition o.title: Relating to the prohibition of access by minors to sexually explicit materials in municipal public library collections; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 3225|relating to the prohibition o.summary: Bars city public libraries from keeping sexually explicit material in children's sections, requires parental consent and age checks before minors can borrow such material, and allows civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation.

tx:HB 6|relating to discipline in public.title: Relating to discipline in public schools
tx:HB 6|relating to discipline in public.summary: Changes public school discipline rules, keeping a three-day limit on out-of-school suspensions while removing the time limit on in-school suspensions, letting districts place expelled students in virtual programs, and requiring alternative-school placement for selling or giving others e-cigarettes.

tx:SB 11|relating to a period of prayer.title: Relating to a period of prayer and reading of the Bible or other religious text in public schools
tx:SB 11|relating to a period of prayer.summary: Lets school boards adopt a daily period for prayer and Bible or other religious text reading, open only to students and staff with signed consent, and requires every board to vote on whether to adopt such a policy within six months.

tx:SCR 52|returning house bill no 1240 t.title: Returning House Bill No. 1240 to the Senate for further consideration
tx:SCR 52|returning house bill no 1240 t.summary: Asks the House to return House Bill 1240 to the Senate for further consideration after the Senate had passed it and sent it back to the House.

tx:SB 7|relating to the oversight and fi.title: Relating to the oversight and financing of certain water infrastructure matters under the jurisdiction of the Texas Water Development Board
tx:SB 7|relating to the oversight and fi.summary: Changes how the Texas Water Fund is overseen and spent, converting an existing advisory committee into a Water Fund advisory committee, requiring progress reports, adding flood projects and new reservoirs to eligible projects, prioritizing rural wastewater projects, and letting the state water bank acquire out-of-state water.

tx:SB 1579|relating to the appointment o.title: Relating to the appointment of a receiver for and sale of certain parcels of land that are abandoned, unoccupied, and undeveloped in certain municipalities
tx:SB 1579|relating to the appointment o.summary: Lets certain cities in a border county with a large city declare long-abandoned, undeveloped, tax-delinquent parcels worth under $1,000 abandoned after a public hearing, so a court-appointed receiver can combine, replat and sell them, holding net proceeds for owners.

tx:HB 24|relating to procedures for chan.title: Relating to procedures for changes to a zoning regulation or district boundary
tx:HB 24|relating to procedures for chan.summary: Changes zoning protest rules: for changes allowing more housing, raises the neighbor protest threshold from 20% to 60% of nearby land and lets councils then approve by simple majority rather than three-fourths, exempts broad housing rezonings from protests, and requires website hearing notices.

tx:HB 1586|relating to an exemption from.title: Relating to an exemption from required immunizations for school enrollment
tx:HB 1586|relating to an exemption from.summary: Requires the state health department to post its school vaccine exemption form online for printing, rather than only mailing it on request, bars requiring personal information to get the form, and stops the department from tracking who obtains it.

tx:HB 514|relating to a maternal health.title: Relating to a maternal health care workforce campaign
tx:HB 514|relating to a maternal health.summary: Requires the state health department, using available resources, to run a public outreach campaign to increase maternal health care professionals, including doulas, focusing on rural and shortage areas, training, and recruiting professionals from racial or ethnic minority groups.

tx:SB 14|relating to reforming the proce.title: Relating to reforming the procedure by which state agencies adopt rules and impose regulatory requirements and the deference given to the interpretation of laws and rules by state agencies in certain judicial proceedings
tx:SB 14|relating to reforming the proce.summary: Creates a regulatory efficiency office in the governor's office to help agencies cut unneeded rules, requires rule notices to seek cost information and use plain language where practicable, makes rules voidable if required impact steps are skipped, and says courts need not defer to agencies' legal interpretations.

mn:SF 3045|omnibus state and local gover.title: Omnibus State and Local Government and Elections policy and appropriations
mn:SF 3045|omnibus state and local gover.summary: Sets the budget for the legislature, constitutional offices and state government agencies for fiscal 2026–27, raises some fees, and changes state personnel, licensing board, business filing fraud, local government, campaign finance and election laws, including absentee voting procedures.

mn:SF 1740|omnibus education policy prov.title: Omnibus Education policy provisions
mn:SF 1740|omnibus education policy prov.summary: Makes policy changes for kindergarten through grade 12 education, covering general education, academic programs, charter schools, special education, school health and nutrition, and the duties of state education agencies.

mn:HF 2432|judiciary public safety and c.title: Judiciary, public safety, and corrections policy and finance bill.
mn:HF 2432|judiciary public safety and c.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the courts, public safety and corrections agencies, public defenders and related boards, and changes criminal penalties, crime victim programs, financial fraud investigations, corrections, court, data practices, mortgage foreclosure and civil law provisions.

mn:HF 2435|health and human services fin.title: Health and human services finance bill.
mn:HF 2435|health and human services fin.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the Departments of Human Services, Health, and Children, Youth, and Families, and changes health, health licensing board, pharmacy benefit, health care, behavioral health, program integrity, economic support, child protection, and child care and early learning policies.

mn:SF 1832|omnibus jobs labor economic d.title: Omnibus Jobs, Labor Economic Development policy and appropriations
mn:SF 1832|omnibus jobs labor economic d.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the Department of Employment and Economic Development, Explore Minnesota, the Department of Labor and Industry and related labor agencies, and changes economic development, workforce and labor law provisions.

mn:SF 1750|common interest communities p.title: Common interest communities provisions modifications
mn:SF 1750|common interest communities p.summary: Changes rules for homeowners and condominium associations: caps late fees at the greater of $20 or 5%, generally caps fines at $100 per violation, gives owners hearing rights, limits foreclosures over fines, and bars local governments from requiring associations for new housing.

mn:HF 2446|agriculture and broadband dev.title: Agriculture and broadband development policy and finance bill.
mn:HF 2446|agriculture and broadband dev.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the Department of Agriculture, Board of Animal Health, Agricultural Utilization Research Institute and Office of Broadband Development, and changes livestock dealer licensing, food handler licensing, cottage food exemptions and some fees.

mn:HF 2434|human services finance bill.title: Human services finance bill.
mn:HF 2434|human services finance bill.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 human services funding, changes aging, disability, long-term care, substance use disorder treatment, housing support and health care programs, and converts Direct Care and Treatment, which runs state-operated treatment services, from a board-run agency into a state department led by a commissioner.

mn:HF 2431|higher education policy and f.title: Higher education policy and finance bill.
mn:HF 2431|higher education policy and f.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the Office of Higher Education, Minnesota State colleges and universities, and the University of Minnesota, including state financial aid grants, and changes higher education policy.

mn:HF 2115|human services policy bill.title: Human services policy bill.
mn:HF 2115|human services policy bill.summary: Changes human services policy on aging and disability services, Department of Health programs, state-run treatment services, behavioral health, and the Department of Human Services inspector general, and reorganizes laws on intensive mental health treatment services.

mn:HF 4|budget surplus return to state t.title: Budget surplus return to state taxpayers provided, and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 4|budget surplus return to state t.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment for the 2026 ballot creating a tax relief fund: forecast revenue above 105% of projected spending would go to the fund and be returned as one-time refunds or tax cuts to taxpayers with incomes under $1 million.

mn:SF 1959|omnibus veterans policy and a.title: Omnibus Veterans policy and appropriations
mn:SF 1959|omnibus veterans policy and a.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the Department of Military Affairs and Department of Veterans Affairs, changes veterans services and benefits, provides benefits to veterans of the Secret War in Laos, and orders a Capitol plaque honoring Gold Star and Blue Star families.

mn:SF 4504|relating to energy establishi.title: Relating to energy; establishing provisions regulating plug-in solar photovoltaic devices; expanding the ability of the commissioner of commerce to enter into energy research partnerships or compacts; providing for energy security planning; extending or…
mn:SF 4504|relating to energy establishi.summary: Exempts plug-in solar devices up to 1,200 watts from utility interconnection agreements, net metering and utility fees or approvals, though utilities may require registration; extends energy grant deadlines; lets the Minnesota Climate Innovation Finance Authority borrow money and sell loans; and changes heat pump rebate rules.

mn:HF 3732|employment and economic devel.title: Employment and economic development finance and policy bill.
mn:HF 3732|employment and economic devel.summary: Changes Department of Employment and Economic Development programs and some of its funding, Department of Labor and Industry policies, Explore Minnesota council and Northern Technology Initiative provisions, and repeals obsolete, long-unfunded state programs.

mn:SF 3236|relating to public safety req.title: Relating to public safety; requiring helmets for operators of electric-assisted bicycles under the age of 18; imposing requirements on the operation and sale of motorized bicycles; establishing a motorized bicycle safety coordinator; appropriating money
mn:SF 3236|relating to public safety req.summary: Requires riders under 18 to wear helmets on electric-assisted bicycles, redefines motorized bicycles and bars them from bike paths and sidewalks, sets electrical safety standards for their sale, and funds a state motorized bicycle safety coordinator and public education campaign.

mn:HF 3682|grantee fraud risk rating sys.title: Grantee fraud risk rating system and corresponding grants management required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3682|grantee fraud risk rating sys.summary: Requires the state Office of Grants Management to create a fraud risk rating system for grant recipients, with matching grant management requirements, starting July 1, 2027, and appropriates $71,000 in fiscal 2027 for the work.

mn:HF 3679|continuing operations of the.title: Continuing operations of the legislature provided in advance of the legislature becoming duly organized, chief clerk of the house of representatives and the secretary of the senate term of office provided to continue until a successor is elected and qualified, and mandatory reports required to be submitted to members of legislative committees electronically.
mn:HF 3679|continuing operations of the.summary: Lets the House chief clerk and Senate secretary keep legislative operations and staff running at the start of a new term until each chamber organizes, keeps them in office until successors are chosen, and requires agencies to send mandated reports to legislators electronically.

mn:HF 3589|voters permitted to briefly l.title: Voters permitted to briefly leave a polling place to address an unexpected need, at the discretion of the head election judge.
mn:HF 3589|voters permitted to briefly l.summary: Lets a voter who has received a ballot briefly leave the polling place for a demonstrated need and return to vote, at the head election judge's discretion; the original ballot is spoiled and a new one issued.

mn:HF 3609|disallowance of drug manufact.title: Disallowance of drug manufacturers from restricting delivery of 340B prescription drugs continued, enforcement provided, and expiration date removed.
mn:HF 3609|disallowance of drug manufact.summary: As introduced, removes the July 1, 2027 expiration of the state ban on drug manufacturers restricting delivery of discounted 340B drugs to contract pharmacies, and makes violations an unfair trade practice enforceable by the attorney general.

mn:SF 856|office of the inspector genera.title: Office of the Inspector General creation and appropriation
mn:SF 856|office of the inspector genera.summary: Creates a state Office of the Inspector General, effective 2027, to investigate fraud and misuse in executive branch agencies and programs; the governor appoints the inspector general after considering legislative commission recommendations, with three-fifths Senate confirmation. Appropriates about $8.7 million in fiscal 2027.

mn:HF 14|temporary moratorium on certain.title: Temporary moratorium on certain light rail transit expenditures established.
mn:HF 14|temporary moratorium on certain.summary: Temporarily bars the Metropolitan Council from spending on light rail project development, except the Southwest line and payments for prior work, and, as amended on the floor, requires a bus rapid transit study of the Blue Line extension corridor with a report by January 15, 2026.

mn:HF 25|women s pregnancy centers and m.title: Women's pregnancy centers and maternity homes grant program established, appropriations reduced, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 25|women s pregnancy centers and m.summary: Creates a state grant program for nonprofit pregnancy centers and maternity homes that help women carry pregnancies to term, barring grants to groups that provide or refer for abortions, and funds it with $4 million a year shifted from the Health Department's budget.

mn:HF 21|supermajority approval by each.title: Supermajority approval by each house of the legislature required to extend a peacetime emergency beyond 14 days.
mn:HF 21|supermajority approval by each.summary: Ends governor-declared peacetime emergencies after 10 days unless both legislative chambers approve an extension by three-fifths votes, bars redeclaring a rejected emergency, lets the legislature declare emergencies by three-fifths votes, and says emergency powers cannot infringe listed rights.

mn:HF 12|female sports team participatio.title: Female sports team participation restricted to the female sex.
mn:HF 12|female sports team participatio.summary: Limits participation on school sports teams designated for women or girls to students who meet the bill's genetic and reproductive definition of female, and requires the State High School League to adopt matching rules.

mn:HF 1233|women s athletics exemption c.title: Women's athletics exemption created in the Human Rights Act.
mn:HF 1233|women s athletics exemption c.summary: Adds a Human Rights Act exemption letting schools, colleges, businesses, nonprofits and youth sports groups limit women's and girls' athletics to people meeting the bill's definition of female, and bars government or athletic bodies from penalizing them for doing so.

mn:SF 4059|relating to state government.title: Relating to state government finance; appropriating and transferring money for prekindergarten through grade 12 education, higher education, agriculture, state government, environment and natural resources, energy, renewable development, jobs and economic…
mn:SF 4059|relating to state government.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations and transfers across education, higher education, state government, environment, energy, jobs, labor and public safety, and creates a battery stewardship program while changing Medicaid fraud, campaign finance, clemency, data practices and barber and cosmetology board laws.

mn:SF 3868|virtual currency kiosks prohi.title: Virtual currency kiosks prohibition provision
mn:SF 3868|virtual currency kiosks prohi.summary: Bans virtual currency kiosks in Minnesota starting August 1, 2026, requires operators to remove them from public places by December 31, 2026, and requires kiosk-only operators to pay out customers' money or cryptocurrency in dollars or to a wallet the customer chooses.

mn:SF 2370|omnibus cannabis policy bill.title: Omnibus Cannabis Policy Bill
mn:SF 2370|omnibus cannabis policy bill.summary: Changes cannabis and hemp rules: modifies medical cannabis, hemp edible potency limits and sales, creates a hemp edible wholesaler license, allows hemp edible delivery and city-held licenses, revises testing, labeling and licensing requirements, and changes expungement and resentencing for felony cannabis offenses.

mn:HF 2|health children and families fin.title: Health/children and families finance bill.
mn:HF 2|health children and families fin.summary: Sets fiscal 2026–27 funding for the Departments of Health, Human Services, and Children, Youth, and Families, and changes policies on public health, health licensing boards, pharmacy benefits, public health care programs, child protection, child care, behavioral health, background studies and program integrity.

mn:SF 4223|relating to elections modifyi.title: Relating to elections; modifying campaign finance reporting requirements; modifying disclaimer requirements; expanding disclosure requirements; modifying provisions related to noncoordinated expenditures; classifying certain street address data as private…
mn:SF 4223|relating to elections modifyi.summary: Changes campaign finance reporting, disclaimer and disclosure rules, including for noncoordinated spending, makes certain street address data private, changes rules on campaign spending for security, changes absentee voting and other election procedures and timelines, and bars certain betting on elections.

mn:SF 4555|relating to state government.title: Relating to state government; changing copy numbers for legislative manual; changing provisions for business filings, energy and water use in state facilities, enterprise sustainability, grant management, pharmacy benefit manager selection, historic site…
mn:SF 4555|relating to state government.summary: Makes many state and local government policy changes, including energy and water tracking for state buildings, grant management and fraud-training rules, limits on legislators' outside paid work, letting the Historical Society contract with any entity to run historic sites, and naming the toboggan the state sled.

mn:SF 2884|omnibus pension bill.title: Omnibus Pension bill
mn:SF 2884|omnibus pension bill.summary: Makes wide-ranging changes to Minnesota's public pension plans, including higher benefit formulas and post-retirement increases for state employees, a higher cap on increases for local government employees, benefit increases and state aid for public safety and teacher plans, and changes to the Secure Choice retirement savings program.

mn:HF 1143|expiration of aid accounts mo.title: Expiration of aid accounts modified, appropriations modified, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 1143|expiration of aid accounts mo.summary: Appropriates $100 million to reimburse schools for summer unemployment benefits paid to hourly school workers and extends that account by a year, cancels $77.2 million set aside for the Northern Lights Express passenger rail project, and reduces special education aid appropriations.

mn:SF 4067|relating to public safety reg.title: Relating to public safety; regulating the ownership, possession, and sale of semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines; modifying provisions for possessing dangerous weapons in schools, negligently storing firearms, and…
mn:SF 4067|relating to public safety reg.summary: Requires owners of semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines to certify them with the state, bars licensed dealers from selling them, bans untraceable ghost guns, tightens safe-storage and school weapon rules, expands extreme risk protection orders, and funds school safety and mental health programs.

mn:SF 4535|relating to economic developm.title: Relating to economic development; establishing a Minnesota business recovery loan program; canceling prior appropriations; appropriating and transferring money; requiring a report
mn:SF 4535|relating to economic developm.summary: Moves $100 million from the Minnesota Forward Fund into a loan program for Minnesota businesses that lost more than 30% of revenue from December 2025 to February 2026 amid increased immigration enforcement, allows up to 60% loan forgiveness, and funds a $250,000 economic impact study.

mn:HF 1|undocumented adult minnesotacare.title: Undocumented adult MinnesotaCare coverage repeal bill.
mn:HF 1|undocumented adult minnesotacare.summary: Ends MinnesotaCare health coverage for undocumented adults age 18 and older starting January 1, 2026, and until then caps their enrollment at the number enrolled when the law takes effect; undocumented children under 18 remain eligible.

mn:SF 2691|relating to housing providing.title: Relating to housing; providing standards for rent and utility payments, fees, and charges in manufactured home parks; requiring certain safety inspections; modifying provisions for sale of manufactured home parks; modifying penalties
mn:SF 2691|relating to housing providing.summary: Limits manufactured home park rent increases to one a year and presumes increases above 3% unreasonable, caps late fees at 8%, requires itemized utility bills and fee-free payment options, and lets residents offer to buy before a park is sold.

mn:HF 5|k12 education finance and policy.title: K12 education finance and policy bill.
mn:HF 5|k12 education finance and policy.summary: Sets K-12 education funding for fiscal 2026 and 2027 and changes policy on general education aid, teachers, reading instruction, charter schools, American Indian education, special education, school facilities and safety, school meals and libraries, and early childhood programs.

mn:SF 3769|relating to health care conti.title: Relating to health care; continuing to disallow drug manufacturers from restricting delivery of 340B prescription drugs; providing for enforcement; removing an expiration date
mn:SF 3769|relating to health care conti.summary: Makes permanent, by removing its July 1, 2027, expiration, the ban on drug manufacturers restricting delivery of discounted 340B drugs to contract pharmacies, and makes violations an unfair trade practice the attorney general can enforce.

mn:SF 3295|relating to state government.title: Relating to state government; modifying provisions relating to health-related occupations, the Department of Health, human services health care, behavioral health, the Department of Human Services Office of the Inspector General, the medication repository…
mn:SF 3295|relating to state government.summary: Makes wide-ranging health and human services policy changes covering health occupations, the Department of Health, public health care programs, behavioral health, the human services inspector general, the medication repository program, prescription drugs, direct primary care, emergency medical services, and children's programs.

mn:HF 3425|supportive housing provider g.title: Supportive housing provider grant funding provided, report required, and money appropriated.
mn:HF 3425|supportive housing provider g.summary: Directs $9 million of existing state supportive housing money to providers whose federal Continuum of Care grants have expired or will expire and face funding gaps, and requires grantees to report to the Housing Finance Agency every 90 days, which then reports to the Legislature.

mn:HF 3|human services finance bill.title: Human services finance bill.
mn:HF 3|human services finance bill.summary: Sets the human services budget for fiscal 2026 and 2027 and changes programs for older adults, people with disabilities, health care, substance use treatment, state-run Direct Care and Treatment, autism therapy services, and homelessness, and adds Department of Human Services program-integrity measures.

mn:HF 3295|open meeting law meeting broa.title: Open Meeting Law; meeting broadcasting through social media authorized.
mn:HF 3295|open meeting law meeting broa.summary: Lets local public bodies livestream open meetings on social media platforms that do not require an account to watch, bars comment features during the broadcast, and requires meeting notices to explain how to watch and how to submit public comments.

mn:SF 3298|relating to health occupation.title: Relating to health occupations; modifying licensing and scope of practice for acupuncture and herbal medicine practice, athletic training, mortuary science, physician assistant practice, social work, dentistry practice, marriage and family therapy, pharmacy…
mn:SF 3298|relating to health occupation.summary: Changes licensing and scope-of-practice rules for health professions including acupuncture, athletic training, mortuary science, physician assistants, social work, dentistry, pharmacy, physical therapy and advanced practice nurses, and creates state registration for massage therapists and licensure for music therapists.

mn:HF 3658|processes for applying for se.title: Processes for applying for, securing, and enforcing extreme risk protection orders modified.
mn:HF 3658|processes for applying for se.summary: Expands who can seek an extreme risk protection order, including more family members, law enforcement agencies and people seeking one against themselves, lets courts extend orders up to five years after violations or repeat orders, and changes rules for surrendering and disposing of firearms.

mn:SF 3432|safety and security measures.title: Safety and security measures appropriation
mn:SF 3432|safety and security measures.summary: Funds security for the Capitol, judges, legislators and constitutional officers along with public safety and corrections programs, changes Capitol security rules, creates emergency contact policies for elected officials, raises penalties for theft from vulnerable adults, and makes running sports, election and similar prediction markets a felony.

mn:SF 2216|omnibus commerce and consumer.title: Omnibus Commerce and Consumer Protections policy and appropriations
mn:SF 2216|omnibus commerce and consumer.summary: As passed by the House, funds the Commerce Department, the Office of Cannabis Management and related legislative work, creates an ombudsperson for homeowners associations and other common interest communities, changes private fund adviser registration fees, and creates a homeowners and commercial property insurance task force.

mn:SF 3|omnibus environment and natural.title: Omnibus Environment and Natural Resources appropriations
mn:SF 3|omnibus environment and natural.summary: Funds state environment and natural resources programs for fiscal 2026 and 2027, including environment trust fund projects, and changes game and fish rules, PFAS product restrictions, abandoned watercraft and grant programs, authorizes certain state land sales, and revises environmental permitting.

mn:SF 2298|omnibus housing and homelessn.title: Omnibus Housing and Homelessness Prevention policy and appropriations
mn:SF 2298|omnibus housing and homelessn.summary: Sets the Housing Finance Agency budget at $101.1 million for fiscal 2026 and $82.8 million for fiscal 2027, authorizes up to $50 million more in housing infrastructure bonds, and changes landlord-tenant rules and state housing programs.

mn:SF 2300|relating to employment modify.title: Relating to employment; modifying earned sick and safe time provisions
mn:SF 2300|relating to employment modify.summary: Changes the earned sick and safe time law: exempts employers with fewer than four employees, allows documentation requests after more than two consecutive days off instead of three, and lets employers with more generous leave apply the law to only up to 160 hours yearly.

mn:HF 2130|public safety various provisi.title: Public safety; various provisions modified relating to driver's license revocations, ignition interlock participation length, treatment or rehabilitation program, criminal penalties for participants who operate a vehicle not equipped with interlock device, criminal vehicular homicide offenders, judicial review of an extension, impounded and reissued license plate process, temporary driver's licenses, and criminal penalties; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 2130|public safety various provisi.summary: Lengthens driver's license revocations for certain impaired-driving offenses, changes required ignition interlock periods, requires interlock participants to finish treatment before full driving privileges return, makes driving a vehicle without the required device a crime, and makes criminal vehicular homicide offenders eligible for the program.

mn:SF 3967|relating to human services mo.title: Relating to human services; modifying the due date of the pediatric hospital-to-home transition pilot program report
mn:SF 3967|relating to human services mo.summary: Bars health plans from imposing quantity limits on their already-required coverage of home care nursing for people also on Medical Assistance, retroactive to January 1, 2026, bars state payments to defray that cost, and requires plans to use the term home care nursing services.

ky:HB 2|an act relating to medicaid maki.title: AN ACT relating to Medicaid, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 2|an act relating to medicaid maki.summary: Adds federally set community engagement requirements and cost-sharing to Medicaid, requires eligibility checks every six months, extends current managed care contracts through 2028, bars coverage of weight-loss drugs, and limits Medicaid benefits to those the legislature authorizes or federal law requires.

ky:HB 398|an act relating to occupationa.title: AN ACT relating to occupational safety and health.
ky:HB 398|an act relating to occupationa.summary: Bars Kentucky's workplace safety regulators from adopting or enforcing rules that are stricter than federal OSHA standards or not issued by federal regulators, sets deadlines for complaints and citations, bars citations more than six months after a violation, and bars fines for de minimis (minor) violations.

ky:HB 500|an act relating to appropriati.title: AN ACT relating to appropriations measures providing funding and establishing conditions for the operations, maintenance, support, and functioning of the government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and its various officers, cabinets, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, subdivisions, agencies, and other state-supported activities.
ky:HB 500|an act relating to appropriati.summary: Sets the executive branch budget, including operating and capital project spending, state employee pay and benefit policy, fund transfers, General Fund and Road Fund budget reduction and surplus spending plans, and tobacco settlement spending.

ky:HB 534|an act relating to elections.title: AN ACT relating to elections.
ky:HB 534|an act relating to elections.summary: Requires courts to send election officials a list of people convicted of felonies, including cases on appeal, and removal of those found ineligible from voter rolls by August 4, 2026; lets the elections board work with federal agencies to remove noncitizens; lets judicial candidates disclose party affiliation; and changes campaign finance rules.

ky:HB 369|an act relating to police depa.title: AN ACT relating to police department members.
ky:HB 369|an act relating to police depa.summary: Lets local police departments set, in their personnel policies, the one-year period over which officers covered by state law earn their annual leave.

ky:HB 503|an act making appropriations f.title: AN ACT making appropriations for the operations, maintenance, and support of the Legislative Branch of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.
ky:HB 503|an act making appropriations f.summary: Sets the Legislative Branch budget, including its operating budget, general provisions, and plans for budget reductions or spending of any surplus.

ky:SB 120|an act relating to education.title: AN ACT relating to education.
ky:SB 120|an act relating to education.summary: Requires school athletics consent forms and coach training to cover reporting of child abuse and neglect, bars seventh and eighth graders from boys' and coed high school varsity lacrosse, and requires schools with grades 6 through 12 to post child labor law summaries in school and online.

ky:SB 19|an act relating to permitted us.title: AN ACT relating to permitted uses of time during the school day.
ky:SB 19|an act relating to permitted us.summary: Requires a moment of silence or reflection at the start of each school day, sets a process for school boards to let students attend outside moral instruction, requires background checks for instructors and drivers, and counts those students as present for state funding.

ky:SB 263|an act relating to education.title: AN ACT relating to education.
ky:SB 263|an act relating to education.summary: Changes how the state board of education grants school districts waivers from education rules, creates expedited waivers and a 'school of innovation' pilot project and fund ending June 30, 2028, and requires Covington Independent Schools to seek innovation waivers by August 1, 2026.

ky:HB 335|an act relating to choking pre.title: AN ACT relating to choking prevention in schools.
ky:HB 335|an act relating to choking pre.summary: As introduced, requires schools that obtain an anti-choking device to train cafeteria staff and other expected users, and shields people from civil liability when giving emergency care with such a device or the Heimlich maneuver at public or private schools.

wv:HB 2008|executive branch reorganizati.title: Executive Branch Reorganization
wv:HB 2008|executive branch reorganizati.summary: Folds the Department of Economic Development into the Department of Commerce as a division, and places new hires and transferring employees in Commerce and that division in exempt civil service with no access to state grievance procedures starting July 1, 2025.

wv:HB 4958|to create the southern coalfi.title: To create the Southern Coalfield Resiliency and Revitalization Program
wv:HB 4958|to create the southern coalfi.summary: As passed by the House, creates a five-year Southern Coalfield Resiliency and Revitalization Program for Boone, Logan, McDowell, Mingo and Wyoming counties, with a council to coordinate existing state, local and university resources for economic development, annual reports, and outreach to businesses on existing tax credits.

wv:SB 745|relating to requirements for s.title: Relating to requirements for school nutrition programs
wv:SB 745|relating to requirements for s.summary: As passed by the Senate, bars 23 more food additives, including some preservatives and artificial sweeteners, from school meals starting August 2027, phases down added sugars to 5% of daily calories by 2029, requires online menu ingredient lists, and allows waivers if compliant products are unavailable or costlier.

wv:HCR 102|urging congress call a conven.title: Urging Congress call a convention of the states, under the authority reserved to the states in Article V of the United States Constitution, limited to proposing Amendments to the Constitution of the United States to create fiscal responsibility by and within the federal government.
wv:HCR 102|urging congress call a conven.summary: As introduced, urges Congress to call a convention of the states limited to proposing federal fiscal-responsibility amendments, calls for West Virginia and other states to sue to force that convention, and invites states to hold the convention in West Virginia's capital.

wv:HB 2755|to provide that the west virg.title: To provide that the West Virginia Board of Education may promulgate rules or policies to be submitted to the Legislature for review
wv:HB 2755|to provide that the west virg.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to submit new rules through the Legislature's education oversight commission to the Legislature, which may approve, amend or reject them; rules take effect as written if not acted on within 15 months. Sets deadlines after which board emergency rules expire.

wv:HB 5074|relating to changing the allo.title: Relating to changing the allocation of proceeds in the Medical Cannabis Program Fund.
wv:HB 5074|relating to changing the allo.summary: Directs $5 million of the medical cannabis fund to a court child protection pilot and $5 million to homelessness services in June 2026, sends the rest to general revenue, then splits fund revenue among cannabis regulators, testing, substance-abuse programs, university research, child protection and police grants.

wv:HB 2960|allowing the division of high.title: Allowing the Division of Highways to contract out snow removal to private companies on secondary roads in Monongalia and Preston counties.
wv:HB 2960|allowing the division of high.summary: Sets four snow-removal priority categories for state roads and requires the Division of Highways to run a two-year pilot seeking bids from private vendors to clear secondary roads in Monongalia and Preston counties; vendors get no liability immunity, and contracts can be ended for cause.

wv:HB 5537|repealing obsolete and outdat.title: Repealing obsolete and outdated sections of the Education code.
wv:HB 5537|repealing obsolete and outdat.summary: As first passed by the House, before Senate and later House amendments, repeals education code sections on teacher professional development, a behavior interventionist pilot program, use of school buildings as child care facilities, and the High School Graduation Improvement Act.

wv:HB 4198|e verify safe harbor act.title: E-Verify Safe Harbor Act
wv:HB 4198|e verify safe harbor act.summary: As passed by the House, requires all employers to register with E-Verify, check new hires' work authorization and keep records, gives employers who use E-Verify a legal defense, removes some criminal penalties, and sets escalating sanctions from warnings to state-contract bans and business-license revocation.

wv:SB 137|modifying parole eligibility f.title: Modifying parole eligibility for crime of second degree murder and voluntary manslaughter
wv:SB 137|modifying parole eligibility f.summary: Lengthens prison terms for second-degree murder to 15 to 60 years and voluntary manslaughter to 5 to 25 years, sets minimum time served before parole for each, and raises minimum time before parole for life sentences.

wv:HB 3017|compliance audits of tabulati.title: Compliance Audits of Tabulating Equipment
wv:HB 3017|compliance audits of tabulati.summary: As passed by the House, requires county commissions to inspect vote-counting machines before each election to confirm they cannot connect to the internet, report findings to the Secretary of State, and bars use of noncompliant machines; adds Secretary of State audits.

wv:SB 645|prohibiting surprise billing o.title: Prohibiting surprise billing of ground emergency medical services by nonparticipating providers
wv:SB 645|prohibiting surprise billing o.summary: Requires health insurers to pay out-of-network ground ambulance providers directly at 200% of the Medicare rate or the billed charge, whichever is less, for policies issued from 2027, and bars those providers from billing patients beyond normal cost-sharing.

wv:SB 182|relating to annexation by mino.title: Relating to annexation by minor boundary adjustment
wv:SB 182|relating to annexation by mino.summary: As introduced, removes the limit allowing a city only one annexation by minor boundary adjustment every two years, keeping the existing caps on how much a single adjustment can expand the city.

wv:HB 2576|nil protection act.title: NIL Protection Act
wv:HB 2576|nil protection act.summary: Lets public colleges pay student athletes for their name, image and likeness, share athletic revenue and help arrange deals, but not with state appropriations; bars athletic associations from penalizing schools or athletes for this, bans deals involving alcohol, gambling and similar products, and allows lawsuits.

wv:SB 748|creating safer communities act.title: Creating Safer Communities Act
wv:SB 748|creating safer communities act.summary: As passed by the Senate, lets county commissions, after voter approval in a referendum, levy a public safety sales or amusement tax of up to 1%, with proceeds limited to public safety, emergency services and school resource officers; some municipalities are excluded.

wv:SB 730|establishing forest carbon reg.title: Establishing Forest Carbon Registry
wv:SB 730|establishing forest carbon reg.summary: As amended in committee, creates a Forest Carbon Registry run by the Division of Forestry and requires developers, or landowners selling directly, to record forest carbon offset agreements with mapping data within 60 days, with fines of $2,500 and $5,000, then permanent business license suspension.

wv:HB 3279|relating to requirements for.title: Relating to requirements for WVU and WVSU Board of Governors
wv:HB 3279|relating to requirements for.summary: Expands West Virginia University's Board of Governors to 15 governor-appointed members, including WVU Tech and Potomac State graduates, specifies that elected faculty, student and staff board members serve as nonvoting advisers, and requires an agriculture or forestry member on the WVU and West Virginia State University boards.

wv:SB 677|increasing fees charged by com.title: Increasing fees charged by Commissioner of Securities for each offering
wv:SB 677|increasing fees charged by com.summary: Changes registration, notice-filing and offering fees paid under the state securities law, adds filing requirements for certain securities issuers, and changes how the State Auditor distributes the fee money.

wv:HB 5453|to modify the school aid fund.title: To modify the school aid funding formula.
wv:HB 5453|to modify the school aid fund.summary: As passed by the House, keeps the current school aid formula through 2028-29, then funds county school systems with a $6,100-per-student block grant, $8,600 per charter school student, and a supplemental fund for special-needs students and other extra costs.

wv:SB 928|relating to manufacture sale a.title: Relating to manufacture, sale, and distribution of low-proof spirit alcohol products
wv:SB 928|relating to manufacture sale a.summary: As passed by the Senate, defines low-proof spirit drinks of up to 15.5% alcohol in containers of 25 ounces or less, lets them be distributed and sold like nonintoxicating beer, bars distillers from self-distributing them, and taxes them at $1.25 per gallon.

wv:HB 3154|relating to advertising by li.title: Relating to advertising by licensed limited video lottery retailers and licensed limited video lottery operators
wv:HB 3154|relating to advertising by li.summary: Lets limited video lottery retailers and operators advertise consistent with other state gambling laws, with prior approval from the Lottery director, and voids existing rules that restrict their advertising.

wv:SB 460|relating to vaccine requiremen.title: Relating to vaccine requirements
wv:SB 460|relating to vaccine requiremen.summary: As passed by the Senate, adds religious and philosophical exemptions to school and child care vaccine requirements, lets a doctor's, physician assistant's or nurse practitioner's note grant medical exemptions without state review, bars excluding exempt children from extracurriculars or school events, and allows lawsuits.

wv:HB 3444|relating to inflammation of t.title: Relating to inflammation of the eyes of newborns.
wv:HB 3444|relating to inflammation of t.summary: Repeals state laws on preventing and reporting inflammation of the eyes of newborns, including the required preventive eye medication at birth and related duties and penalties.

wv:HB 3387|relating to the creation of a.title: Relating to the creation of a regional school district pilot program
wv:HB 3387|relating to the creation of a.summary: As amended in committee, lets the State Board of Education start a pilot program, from July 2025, merging up to three neighboring counties under or expected to be under state emergency control into a regional school district whose decisions override county school boards.

wv:SB 526|creating pharmacist prescribin.title: Creating Pharmacist Prescribing Authority Act
wv:SB 526|creating pharmacist prescribin.summary: Lets pharmacists prescribe certain non-controlled drugs after a positive rapid test for flu, COVID-19 or RSV, or to refill an expired epinephrine injector prescription, with physician notification and a 30-day supply limit within six months.

wv:HB 5669|prohibiting the home schoolin.title: Prohibiting the home schooling of children in certain circumstances
wv:HB 5669|prohibiting the home schoolin.summary: As amended in committee, bars county school boards from approving homeschooling for an enrolled student while a school-reported child abuse or neglect investigation of the child's parent, guardian or home instructor is pending; homeschooling must be allowed if the complaint is not substantiated within seven days.

wv:SB 927|clarifying commissioner of agr.title: Clarifying Commissioner of Agriculture's authority to regulate bees
wv:SB 927|clarifying commissioner of agr.summary: As introduced, makes the Agriculture Commissioner the sole regulator of beekeeping and apiaries, overriding local rules, and requires clear and convincing evidence of damage for lawsuits against nearby farm operations.

wv:HB 2511|relating to charitable bingo.title: Relating to charitable bingo and alcohol sales and consumption while such bingo is taking places
wv:HB 2511|relating to charitable bingo.summary: Allows alcohol and beer to be sold and consumed during charitable bingo games held on the premises of fraternal societies, veterans' organizations and volunteer fire departments.

wv:SB 565|relating generally to practice.title: Relating generally to practice of optometry
wv:SB 565|relating generally to practice.summary: Expands the scope of practice for optometrists, letting them perform certain procedures, including laser procedures, once they meet board training and certification requirements, and updates the optometry board's rulemaking authority.

wv:HB 2695|raleigh and mason counties ec.title: Raleigh and Mason Counties Economic Opportunity Development Districts
wv:HB 2695|raleigh and mason counties ec.summary: Lets Raleigh County and Mason County levy a special sales tax inside new economic development districts of about 1,600 and 150 acres, after a public hearing and state approval, and requires every county using such a tax to file a detailed annual report.

wv:HB 3174|requiring municipalities take.title: Requiring municipalities take actions when potential customers apply for water and sewer service.
wv:HB 3174|requiring municipalities take.summary: Requires city and public service district water and sewer systems to price line extensions for people who apply for service, extend service once applicants pay their share, and seek state grant funding at applicants' request, reimbursing applicants' contributions if grants cover the full cost.

wv:HB 2054|relating to liability of vend.title: Relating to liability of vendors in private farmers markets
wv:HB 2054|relating to liability of vend.summary: Revises state alcohol licensing rules, dropping joint-liability agreements required of vendors at private farmers markets, food courts and multi-vendor festivals, allowing self-pour machines for beer, cider and wine, expanding who may join outdoor drinking areas, and creating a nonprofit license.

wv:SB 576|authorizing fixed odds racing.title: Authorizing fixed odds racing in horse and dog racing
wv:SB 576|authorizing fixed odds racing.summary: Lets licensed sports betting operators take fixed-odds bets on horse and dog races, collects 10 percent of their net receipts with shares going to new race purse funds and racetracks, and bars owners, trainers, jockeys and racing officials from betting on their races.

wv:HB 2752|relating to motorcycle safety.title: Relating to motorcycle safety
wv:HB 2752|relating to motorcycle safety.summary: Allows a person operating a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle or moped to ride standing astride the vehicle with both feet on the footpegs or pedals, facing forward, instead of only sitting on the seat.

wv:HB 2719|campaign finance and reportin.title: Campaign finance and reporting
wv:HB 2719|campaign finance and reportin.summary: Lets corporations and membership organizations contribute to candidates, subject to the same $2,800 limits for a nomination and for an election that apply to individuals, and to political action committees up to $5,000, and requires campaigns to report these donors, with addresses above $250.

wv:HB 2351|relating to compensation for.title: Relating to compensation for panel attorneys
wv:HB 2351|relating to compensation for.summary: Raises pay for court-appointed attorneys representing people who cannot afford a lawyer, from $60 to $70 an hour for out-of-court work and $80 to $90 for in-court work, and requires yearly reports on guardians ad litem in child abuse and neglect cases.

wv:HB 2159|relating to the assessment of.title: Relating to the assessment of interest on overpayments by the Bureau for Medical Services
wv:HB 2159|relating to the assessment of.summary: Charges interest on overpayments owed back to state Medicaid programs, at the state's court judgment interest rate, starting 31 days after an overpayment is finalized, with the interest kept by the fund that made the payment.

wv:SB 746|allowing state board of educat.title: Allowing State Board of Education to delegate its Medicaid provider status to public charter schools
wv:SB 746|allowing state board of educat.summary: Lets the State Board of Education pass its Medicaid provider status to public charter schools so they can bill Medicaid for school health services, and adds charter schools to the board's annual Medicaid report and advisory committee's work.

wv:HB 3412|relating to exemptions from d.title: Relating to exemptions from disclosure of certain records; and exempting the legislative branch if it adopts its own rules.
wv:HB 3412|relating to exemptions from d.summary: As amended by the Senate, amends the state public records law to exempt private personal information and more internal and security records, extend the response deadline from 5 to 14 business days, allow search fees, and remove the presumption of access.

wv:SJR 9|citizenship requirement to vote.title: Citizenship Requirement to Vote in West Virginia Elections Amendment
wv:SJR 9|citizenship requirement to vote.summary: Asks voters at the 2026 general election to amend the state constitution so that only United States citizens who are citizens of West Virginia may vote in elections held in the state.

sc:H 4767|physician noncompete contract.title: Physician Noncompete Contract Prohibition
sc:H 4767|physician noncompete contract.summary: Voids noncompete clauses in physician contracts that limit where or how long a doctor may practice or bar treating former patients, while letting employers recoup certain bonuses and relocation costs from doctors who leave within three years; applies to new and renewed contracts.

sc:S 0287|electronic nicotine delivery s.title: Electronic Nicotine Delivery System Regulation
sc:S 0287|electronic nicotine delivery s.summary: Requires e-cigarette makers to certify their products' federal authorization status to be listed in an Attorney General directory, bans selling unlisted vaping products starting in 2027, bars labels and marketing aimed at children, and sets fines and seizure for violations.

sc:S 0052|driving under the influence.title: Driving under the influence
sc:S 0052|driving under the influence.summary: Makes DUI causing moderate injury a felony punishable by 90 days to 10 years in prison, creates reckless-driving offenses for causing injury, lengthens license suspensions for refusing alcohol tests, expands ignition interlock rules, and has circuit solicitors prosecute first and second DUI offenses.

sc:H 4759|intoxicating hemp beverages.title: Intoxicating Hemp Beverages
sc:H 4759|intoxicating hemp beverages.summary: Bans the sale and possession of hemp-derived THC products except hemp beverages, which are limited to 5 milligrams of THC per 12-ounce can, sold only to people 21 and older through licensed liquor stores, and taxed like liquor.

sc:H 4025|appropriations bill 2025 2026.title: Appropriations Bill, 2025-2026
sc:H 4025|appropriations bill 2025 2026.summary: Sets South Carolina's state budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025, appropriating money and providing revenue for the ordinary expenses of state government and setting rules for how the funds are spent.

sc:H 4817|insurance rate reduction and p.title: Insurance Rate Reduction and Policy Holder Protection Act
sc:H 4817|insurance rate reduction and p.summary: Moves the Insurance Fraud Division from the Attorney General to the Department of Insurance, bars roofing contractors from negotiating insurance claims or covering deductibles, creates a disaster-supply sales tax holiday, and raises tax credits for hurricane retrofits and high homeowners' insurance premiums.

sc:S 0222|utility terrain vehicle.title: Utility terrain vehicle
sc:S 0222|utility terrain vehicle.summary: Lets utility terrain vehicles be registered and driven on roads with speed limits of 55 mph or less by licensed drivers 17 and older, with a $10 fee every two years and insurance and safety rules; also allows golf carts near large athletic events.

sc:S 0244|tort reform.title: Tort Reform
sc:S 0244|tort reform.summary: Changes how fault is divided in injury lawsuits, letting juries assign fault to parties who settled and limiting joint liability; lowers bars' required liquor liability coverage to $500,000, requires alcohol server training, raises caps on suits against government, and doubles minimum auto insurance.

sc:H 5538|guarantee banking act.title: Guarantee Banking Act
sc:H 5538|guarantee banking act.summary: Bars banks with over $100 billion in assets and large payment processors from denying or ending services based on religion, protected speech, or factors that are not impartial and risk-based; requires written reasons on request; and treats violations as unfair trade practices.

sc:H 3276|sc hands free act.title: SC Hands-Free Act
sc:H 3276|sc hands free act.summary: Bars drivers from holding a phone or other mobile device or texting or watching video while driving, with hands-free exceptions; sets a $100 fine for a first offense and $200 plus two license points for repeat offenses, with only warnings for the first 180 days.

sc:H 4760|abortion inducing drugs.title: Abortion-Inducing Drugs
sc:H 4760|abortion inducing drugs.summary: Makes it a felony, punishable by up to five years, to provide a pregnant woman abortion-inducing drugs to cause an abortion, with exceptions for lawful medical care; makes mifepristone and misoprostol controlled substances, bars possession without a prescription except by pregnant women, and allows civil suits.

sc:H 4270|evictions.title: Evictions
sc:H 4270|evictions.summary: Requires eviction filings and records to be removed from public court indexes and publicly accessible files seven years after the case's final disposition or filing if no later filing is recorded, starting January 1, 2027.

sc:H 4757|parental rights.title: Parental Rights
sc:H 4757|parental rights.summary: Declares parents' right to direct their children's upbringing, education and health care a fundamental right; requires parental consent before most health care for minors under 18; requires school districts to adopt parental-rights policies; and lets parents file complaints and then sue.

mi:SB 596|the management and budget act.title: The management and budget act: add section 364.
mi:SB 596|the management and budget act.summary: Bars state agencies from spending money appropriated as legislator-requested spending items unless the legislator files a formal request, makes for-profit businesses ineligible, sets eligibility rules for nonprofits, and requires public online posting of each request and funded item.

mi:HB 5975|public health code amend sect.title: Public health code: amend section 5474
mi:HB 5975|public health code amend sect.summary: As introduced, requires a local health department or physician notified that a child under 3 has an elevated blood lead level to refer the child to the state's Early On program, and sets July 1 annual deadlines for state lead-poisoning reports to the Legislature.

mi:HB 4153|the revised school code amend.title: The revised school code: amend sections 501, 521, 551, 1231, 1233, 1311b, 1526, 1535a, and 1809
mi:HB 4153|the revised school code amend.summary: Lets school districts, intermediate districts and charter schools issue local teaching certificates, valid up to five years, to people with a degree in their subject and at least a 3.0 GPA; excludes special education and ends new certificates after July 1, 2035.

mi:SB 423|the general property tax act a.title: The general property tax act: amend sections 78g and 78q
mi:SB 423|the general property tax act a.summary: Removes the expiration dates on programs that let local governments reduce delinquent property taxes, interest and fees for property owners in hardship, and let county treasurers offer homeowners up to five-year agreements to pay back taxes and avoid foreclosure.

mi:SB 1135|state police retirement act o.title: State police retirement act of 1986: add sections 24c, 24d, 24e, and 24f.
mi:SB 1135|state police retirement act o.summary: Lets corrections, conservation and certain other state law enforcement officers who move into the state police pension plan buy credit for past state service at its actuarial cost, starting the purchase by October 15, 2027 and paying within four years.

mi:HB 5630|the state school aid act of 1.title: The state school aid act of 1979: amend sections 11, 201, and 236
mi:HB 5630|the state school aid act of 1.summary: Appropriates state funding for K-12 school aid, community colleges and public universities for the 2026-27 fiscal year, as part of the omnibus education budget bill later enacted as Public Act 25 of 2026.

mi:SB 691|michigan election law amend se.title: Michigan election law: amend sections 3, 52, 53, 92, 93, 132, 133, 162, 163, 192, 193, 253, 254, 345, 349, 370, 409a, 409b, 412, 424a, 432, 433, 467a, 467b, 510, 534, 535, 544c, 551, 559, 590b, 590c…
mi:SB 691|michigan election law amend se.summary: Moves Michigan's August primary election to May, allows primaries on the February regular election date, and shifts related election deadlines, including filing and party convention dates, starting January 1, 2028.

mi:HB 4240|prohibit public bodies from r.title: Prohibit public bodies from receiving gifts and grants from foreign actors under certain circumstances; to prohibit public bodies from entering into agreements with foreign actors under certain…
mi:HB 4240|prohibit public bodies from r.summary: Bars state and local agencies other than public schools and colleges from agreements or grants with China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela's Maduro government or Syria meeting listed conditions; requires disclosure of foreign gifts of $50,000+ and of foreign ties by applicants for $100,000+ grants or contracts.

mi:HB 4239|prohibit state institutions o.title: Prohibit state institutions of higher education from entering into agreements with foreign actors under certain circumstances; to prohibit state institutions of higher education from receiving grants…
mi:HB 4239|prohibit state institutions o.summary: Bars public universities and community colleges from agreements or grants with China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela's Maduro government or Syria that meet listed conditions, requires written agreements for foreign gifts, and requires twice-yearly reports of foreign gifts of $50,000 or more.

mi:SB 360|identity theft protection act.title: Identity theft protection act: amend sections 3, 12, and 12b
mi:SB 360|identity theft protection act.summary: Requires businesses and state agencies holding residents' personal information to keep security safeguards, notify affected residents of data breaches, and notify the attorney general of breaches affecting more than 100 residents, with civil fines up to $750,000.

mi:HB 4506|the code of criminal procedur.title: The code of criminal procedure: add section 25b to chapter IX.
mi:HB 4506|the code of criminal procedur.summary: As introduced, lets prosecutors seek life without parole, after a hearing, for people convicted of first-degree murder, terrorism and certain other crimes committed at ages 18 to 20, including past cases; otherwise requires a 35-to-50-year minimum and at least an 80-year maximum.

mi:SB 8|improved workforce opportunity w.title: Improved workforce opportunity wage act: amend sections 4, 4d, and 10
mi:SB 8|improved workforce opportunity w.summary: Sets Michigan's minimum wage at $12.48 on February 21, 2025, $13.73 in 2026 and $15.00 in 2027, with later inflation increases, and keeps a separate tipped wage rising from 38% to 50% of the minimum by 2031, replacing a scheduled phase-out of the tipped wage.

mi:SB 3|provide for a cost and affordabi.title: Provide for a cost and affordability review of certain prescription drug products; to create the prescription drug pricing board and prescription drug affordability stakeholder council and to…
mi:SB 3|provide for a cost and affordabi.summary: Creates a state prescription drug affordability board that reviews the cost of selected drugs and may set upper payment limits on drugs it finds unaffordable, enforceable by the attorney general, along with an advisory council and a dedicated fund.

mi:SB 579|natural resources and environm.title: Natural resources and environmental protection act: amend sections 301, 3101, 3104, 3110, 3118, 3120, 3122, 3132, 3306, 4104, 4112, 5519, 11108, 11109, 11123, 11153,
mi:SB 579|natural resources and environm.summary: Extends to October 1, 2029 the state environmental department's authority to collect permit and user fees for floodplains, wastewater and stormwater discharges, operator certification, hazardous waste handlers, and land and water permits.

mi:HB 4012|public health code amend sect.title: Public health code: amend section 20925
mi:HB 4012|public health code amend sect.summary: Lets ambulances provide emergency transport to a veterinary clinic for retired police dogs, as already allowed for police dogs injured on duty, when no people need transport or emergency help at the time.

nh:HB 53|permitting qualifying patients.title: permitting qualifying patients and designated caregivers to cultivate cannabis for therapeutic use.
nh:HB 53|permitting qualifying patients.summary: Lets registered therapeutic cannabis patients or their designated caregivers grow cannabis at a home location reported to the state, in a locked, enclosed space not open to public view, within a 50-square-foot canopy (100 if shared), with caregivers growing for only one patient.

nh:HB 707|second new title establishing.title: (Second New Title) establishing a solid waste site evaluation committee.
nh:HB 707|second new title establishing.summary: Creates a seven-member state committee to approve or deny sites for new solid waste facilities taking over 100,000 tons a year, gives state environmental regulators sole approval over landfill expansions, and pauses state permits for new capacity at other large disposal facilities until July 1, 2027.

nh:HB 2|relative to state fees funds rev.title: relative to state fees, funds, revenues, and expenditures.
nh:HB 2|relative to state fees funds rev.summary: Makes the law, fee and program changes that carry out the state budget for fiscal 2026 and 2027, including allowing video lottery terminals, adding Medicaid premiums for enrollees above set income levels, barring diversity, equity and inclusion programs in public entities, and changing education aid.

nh:HB 94|relative to coverage of circumc.title: relative to coverage of circumcision under the state Medicaid plan.
nh:HB 94|relative to coverage of circumc.summary: Bars the state Medicaid plan from covering circumcision of children unless it is medically necessary for a listed or physician-diagnosed condition, such as recurrent urinary tract infections or phimosis, starting January 1, 2026.

nh:HB 1|making appropriations for the ex.title: making appropriations for the expenses of certain departments of the state for fiscal years ending June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2027.
nh:HB 1|making appropriations for the ex.summary: Sets the state's operating budget for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, appropriating money for state departments and agencies for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 as agreed in the final House-Senate conference report.

nh:HB 254|relative to options for end of.title: relative to options for end of life care.
nh:HB 254|relative to options for end of.summary: As introduced, lets a mentally capable adult with a terminal illness and a prognosis of six months or less obtain a prescription for medication they take themselves to end their life, after two health care providers confirm eligibility, with a waiting period and penalties for misuse.

nh:HB 358|relative to exemption from imm.title: relative to exemption from immunization requirements on the basis of religious belief.
nh:HB 358|relative to exemption from imm.summary: Lets a parent or guardian claim a religious exemption from childhood vaccination requirements with only a signed written statement that the child has not been immunized because of religious belief, replacing the reference to a required form.

nh:HB 1072|relative to employer notice o.title: relative to employer notice of department of labor investigations.
nh:HB 1072|relative to employer notice o.summary: Requires the labor commissioner to give employers at least 30 days' notice before a visit or inspection and at least 30 days to answer document or interview demands, with exceptions for recent violators, imminent safety risks, likely evidence destruction, certain safety inspections and owner consent.

nh:SB 669|relative to on premises licens.title: relative to on-premises licenses for licensed barbershops and salons.
nh:SB 669|relative to on premises licens.summary: Splits the liquor license for barbershops and salons into two tiers: a $100 license to serve one free drink per customer appointment and a $480 license to sell one drink per appointment, and requires an annual state report on licenses and violations.

nh:HB 475|relative to the reductions fro.title: relative to the reductions from the default budget for official ballot town meetings.
nh:HB 475|relative to the reductions fro.summary: Changes how towns with official-ballot meetings calculate their default budget, reducing it for salaries and benefits of eliminated positions and of positions vacant since before the prior year's budget, and basing pay on actual salaries of filled positions.

nh:HB 356|veto override.title: Veto Override
nh:HB 356|veto override.summary: Lets school district voters decide by majority ballot vote to elect school district officers in partisan elections run under town partisan election rules, and to return to nonpartisan elections by the same kind of vote.

nh:HB 1704|permitting public employees t.title: permitting public employees to bargain individually with public employers without any intervention.
nh:HB 1704|permitting public employees t.summary: Lets most public employees negotiate pay, hours and grievances individually instead of through a union, excluding police, firefighters, emergency medical workers and corrections officers, and makes coercing employees to join or pay a union a misdemeanor with up to a $5,000 fine.

nh:HB 1336|new title relative to regulat.title: (New Title) relative to regulated conditional deposits.
nh:HB 1336|new title relative to regulat.summary: Lets landlords accept an extra deposit of up to one month's rent from applicants who fail disclosed screening criteria such as credit score, income, prior evictions, unpaid judgments or references, with written notice and a right to re-screening; also says advance rent need not be escrowed.

nh:SB 625|new title establishing a commi.title: (New Title) establishing a committee to study options for family members of intentional homicide victims where the department of justice does not file charges in a case.
nh:SB 625|new title establishing a commi.summary: Creates a legislative study committee on informing families of intentional homicide victims when no charges are filed and, as amended by the House, ends the state refugee resettlement program, bars state spending on refugee resettlement and drops hepatitis B from required childhood vaccines.

nh:SB 88|prohibiting state government en.title: prohibiting state government entities from including specified terms related to labor organization agreements in construction related contracts and grants.
nh:SB 88|prohibiting state government en.summary: Bars the state and its agencies from requiring, favoring or prohibiting agreements with labor organizations in state construction contracts and grants, or from treating contractors differently based on such agreements, with an exemption for imminent threats to public health or safety.

nh:HB 1643|relative to the report of a g.title: relative to the report of a guardian ad litem.
nh:HB 1643|relative to the report of a g.summary: Removes courts' authority to ask a guardian ad litem in a parenting case to propose how decision-making is divided, a parenting plan or a parenting schedule in the report, which must be filed by the final pretrial hearing.
