nh:HB 1706|repealing the refugee resettl.title: repealing the refugee resettlement program in the department of health and human services and prohibiting expenditure of state funds on refugee resettlement.
nh:HB 1706|repealing the refugee resettl.summary: Ends the state refugee resettlement program in the health and human services department, requires its contracts to be terminated, and bars state agencies from accepting or spending money on refugee resettlement, including payments to towns or nonprofit groups.

nh:SB 96|relative to mandatory disclosur.title: relative to mandatory disclosure by school district employees to parents.
nh:SB 96|relative to mandatory disclosur.summary: Requires credentialed educators to answer parents' written questions about material information on their child within 10 business days, limits when schools may withhold information, lets parents sue schools, and sets escalating penalties, including credential suspensions, for willful violations.

nh:SB 627|new title relative to toll rat.title: (New Title) relative to toll rate adjustments and periodic inflation-based toll reviews for the New Hampshire turnpike system to support the 2027-2036 ten-year transportation plan.
nh:SB 627|new title relative to toll rat.summary: Raises tolls at the Hooksett, Bedford, Hampton, Dover and Rochester turnpike plazas starting January 1, 2027, setting separate cash and E-ZPass rates such as $2.00 and $0.70 for cars at Hooksett, and offers free E-ZPass transponders for 210 days.

nh:HB 524|repealing the new hampshire va.title: repealing the New Hampshire vaccine association.
nh:HB 524|repealing the new hampshire va.summary: Repeals the state law that establishes the New Hampshire Vaccine Association, eliminating the association's chapter of state law entirely.

nh:HB 1477|relative to the permitting an.title: relative to the permitting and regulation of anchored seasonal floating platforms on public waters.
nh:HB 1477|relative to the permitting an.summary: Limits anchored seasonal floating platforms on public waters to owners of the adjacent shorefront, requires a $50 marine patrol permit and owner contact information on each platform, exempts government, conservation and aquaculture uses, and sets a $100 fine for operating without a permit.

nh:HB 1066|relative to warrant articles.title: relative to warrant articles authorizing lease agreements.
nh:HB 1066|relative to warrant articles.summary: Treats many local government lease agreements like borrowing, requiring a public hearing and three-fifths voter approval for leases over $500,000 that are not equipment leases, while smaller leases need a simple majority; cities are excluded.

nh:HB 1268|modifying definitions and req.title: modifying definitions and requirements relative to home education programs.
nh:HB 1268|modifying definitions and req.summary: Rewrites home education law, no longer requiring notice to the state except for public school access or withdrawal, repealing evaluation and record-keeping rules, keeping home education information confidential, and letting families sue people who knowingly make abuse reports motivated primarily by home education.

nh:HB 1313|repealing buffer zones for re.title: repealing buffer zones for reproductive health care facilities.
nh:HB 1313|repealing buffer zones for re.summary: Repeals the law that bars people from entering or remaining on a public way or sidewalk next to a reproductive health care facility, eliminating those buffer zones upon passage.

nh:HB 319|relative to the responsibility.title: relative to the responsibility of local school districts to provide transportation and meals for pupils in kindergarten.
nh:HB 319|relative to the responsibility.summary: Makes school district transportation for half-day kindergarten students optional rather than required, while districts must still transport full-day students in kindergarten through grade 8 who live more than two miles from school.

nh:SB 557|third new title making it ille.title: (Third New Title) making it illegal for liquor commission licensees to sell, distribute, furnish, offer for sale, advertise, manufacture, possess, or allow the ingestion, inhalation, smoking, or vaping of certain kratom products.
nh:SB 557|third new title making it ille.summary: Bars liquor licensees from selling, advertising, manufacturing, possessing, or allowing on-site use of chemically altered or synthetic kratom products, with license revocation for a second offense. Also changes how towns adopt or repeal the official-ballot form of town meeting.

nh:SB 101|new title authorizing parents.title: (New Title) authorizing parents to enroll their children in any public school in the state and creating a limited exemption from parental consent required for certain recordings under the parental bill of rights.
nh:SB 101|new title authorizing parents.summary: As amended by the House, requires each school district to adopt an open enrollment policy letting parents apply to any public school, subject to district-set capacity and limited denial grounds; the state pays aid to receiving schools, and no tuition is charged.

nh:HB 80|allowing a public body member s.title: allowing a public body member's presence at a meeting by electronic or other means of communication only if physical presence is unavoidable and providing that physical presence is necessary for voting.
nh:HB 80|allowing a public body member s.summary: Lets a member of a public body participate in a meeting remotely only when attending in person is unavoidable, instead of when it is not reasonably practical, and requires the reason to be recorded in the minutes.

nh:SB 508|relative to the zoning board o.title: relative to the zoning board of adjustments appeal period.
nh:SB 508|relative to the zoning board o.summary: Requires all grounds for an appeal to a zoning board of adjustment to be stated in the initial notice, and requires municipalities to accept revised development plans within 10 business days, generally limiting applicants to one round of revisions.

nh:SB 60|relative to advanced deposit ac.title: relative to advanced deposit account wagering.
nh:SB 60|relative to advanced deposit ac.summary: Licenses advance-deposit account betting on horse races, with operators paying the state 1.25 percent of New Hampshire residents' wagers. Also limits required childhood vaccines to seven listed diseases once three other rules expire in June 2026, ending the health commissioner's power to add others.

nh:HB 66|relative to material subject to.title: relative to material subject to disclosure under the right to know law.
nh:HB 66|relative to material subject to.summary: Lets any person, not only citizens, use the right-to-know law, requires mail or electronic delivery of records for requesters with New Hampshire ties or media members, adds draft documents shared with a quorum, and changes appeals of ombudsman rulings.

nh:SB 295|new title relative to educatio.title: (New Title) relative to education freedom accounts.
nh:SB 295|new title relative to educatio.summary: Removes the household income limit for education freedom accounts, caps enrollment at 10,000 students for 2025-2026, raising the cap 25 percent when prior-year enrollment exceeds 90 percent of it, and exempts current students, siblings, children with disabilities, and lower-income families from the cap.

nh:HB 1797|relative to eligibility for p.title: relative to eligibility for public assistance, including the New Hampshire employment program, family assistance program, and SNAP.
nh:HB 1797|relative to eligibility for p.summary: Bars the health department from seeking SNAP work-requirement waivers without legislative approval or loosening eligibility standards unless federal law requires, mandates regular data checks of recipients' income, incarceration, lottery winnings, and citizenship, and removes out-of-state-only users found nonresident or unresponsive.

nh:SB 409|relative to the penalties for.title: relative to the penalties for the offense of disobeying an officer.
nh:SB 409|relative to the penalties for.summary: Makes fleeing police a felony when it involves extreme speeding, wrong-way driving, ramming, other extremely hazardous driving, or a crash causing serious injury or death. Also raises government negligence liability limits, requires towns to indemnify employees, and sets due-process rules for public college discipline.

nh:HB 1217|permitting classification of.title: permitting classification of individuals based on biological sex under certain limited circumstances.
nh:HB 1217|permitting classification of.summary: As introduced, allows public and private entities to separate people by biological sex in multi-user bathrooms and locker rooms and in sports where strength, speed, or endurance generally gives males an advantage, and states that doing so is not unlawful discrimination.

nh:HB 1773|relative to food and drink pu.title: relative to food and drink purchased under SNAP, the Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program.
nh:HB 1773|relative to food and drink pu.summary: Directs the state health department to ask federal officials by January 1, 2027 for a waiver barring the purchase of sweetened drinks and candy with SNAP benefits, and to report annually on the waiver and its results.

nh:HB 232|relative to the rights of cons.title: relative to the rights of conscience for medical professionals.
nh:HB 232|relative to the rights of cons.summary: Requires health care institutions to notify employees who provide abortion services each year that they may request an accommodation for religious or moral objections to directly participating in abortions and may complain to the attorney general, who must report substantiated complaints annually.

nh:SB 263|criminalizing and creating a p.title: criminalizing and creating a private right of action for the facilitation, encouragement, offer, solicitation, or recommendation of certain acts or actions through a responsive generative communication to a child.
nh:SB 263|criminalizing and creating a p.summary: Makes it a crime for AI chat service operators to knowingly encourage a child toward imminent sexual conduct, illegal drug or alcohol use, self-harm, or violence, with civil liability of at least $1,000 per violation. Also lets landlords evict when leases of six months or longer end.

nh:HB 1661|relative to expanding the hou.title: relative to expanding the housing finance authority's community heroes program and makes an appropriation therefor.
nh:HB 1661|relative to expanding the hou.summary: As introduced, requires the housing finance authority to run a homebuying assistance program for essential workers such as health care workers, first responders, educators, and service members, appropriating $750,000 for fiscal 2027 and $1.5 million a year starting July 2028.

nh:HB 1491|relative to pooled risk manag.title: relative to pooled risk management programs.
nh:HB 1491|relative to pooled risk manag.summary: Creates a state regulatory system for risk pools formed by local governments, requiring insurance commissioner approval, minimum deposits, rate review, financial and capital reports, investment limits, and regular examinations, and exempts the pools from insurance premium taxes.

nh:HB 197|relative to payment by the sta.title: relative to payment by the state of a portion of retirement system contributions of political subdivision employers.
nh:HB 197|relative to payment by the sta.summary: As introduced, has the state pay 7.5 percent of local employers' retirement system contributions for teachers and for police and firefighters starting in fiscal 2026, lowering what cities, towns, and school districts pay.

nh:HB 433|making 17 the age of consent f.title: making 17 the age of consent for marriage if either party is active duty military and removing language regarding age waivers for marriage registration records, since age waivers are no longer issued in New Hampshire.
nh:HB 433|making 17 the age of consent f.summary: As introduced, lowers the marriage age to 17 when one party is an active-duty service member, the other is at least 17, and one is a state resident, requiring parental permission for a non-military 17-year-old. Removes outdated age-waiver language.

nh:HR 35|urging the prohibition of the i.title: urging the prohibition of the intentional release of polluting emissions, including cloud seeding and weather modification, to preserve the atmosphere of New Hampshire.
nh:HR 35|urging the prohibition of the i.summary: Declares in a House resolution that no person shall engage in geoengineering involving intentional release of polluting emissions in the state, including weather modification, and recommends that the environmental services commissioner notify federal agencies and post the resolution online.

nh:HB 280|relative to wage payments.title: relative to wage payments.
nh:HB 280|relative to wage payments.summary: Lets employers and employees decide how wages are paid, removing the list of approved payment methods and payroll card rules, while requiring written notice of the payment method at hiring and 90 days before any change.

nh:CACR 25|relative to the right to marr.title: relative to the right to marry. Providing that the right to marry is a fundamental civil right and that the state shall protect the right of every individual, regardless of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, or race, to marry and to have their ma
nh:CACR 25|relative to the right to marr.summary: As introduced, proposes a state constitutional amendment making marriage a fundamental civil right and barring the state from denying or limiting marriage based on sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, or race, for voters to decide in November 2026.

nh:HB 1610|allowing school districts to.title: allowing school districts to annually retain year-end unassigned general funds.
nh:HB 1610|allowing school districts to.summary: Lets school district voters authorize, one year at a time, keeping unspent year-end funds up to 3 percent of the budget for unusual circumstances, replacing open-ended authorizations, which it cancels, and dropping the hearing requirement before spending.

nh:HB 299|relative to the award of attor.title: relative to the award of attorneys' fees and costs in workers' compensation claims.
nh:HB 299|relative to the award of attor.summary: As introduced, entitles injured workers who win workers' compensation disputes at the labor department level to reimbursement of reasonable attorney fees and costs, including when insurers are ordered to pay, or pay just before a hearing on, disputed medical bills.

nh:SB 643|new title requiring municipali.title: (New Title) requiring municipalities to hold a public hearing and conduct a roll call vote when seeking to override a tax or spending cap.
nh:SB 643|new title requiring municipali.summary: Requires cities and council-run towns to hold a public hearing and roll-call vote before overriding a tax or spending cap and to print the vote on tax bills, and has the state revenue department check and enforce local budget caps.

nh:HB 59|relative to the assault of a fi.title: relative to the assault of a firefighter, emergency medical care provider, or law enforcement officer.
nh:HB 59|relative to the assault of a fi.summary: Makes knowingly injuring a police officer, firefighter, or emergency medical provider on duty, or an officer targeted because of the job, first-degree assault if the injury is serious and second-degree assault otherwise.

nh:HB 324|relative to prohibiting obscen.title: relative to prohibiting obscene or harmful sexual materials in schools.
nh:HB 324|relative to prohibiting obscen.summary: Bars schools from giving minor students material harmful to minors, requires school boards to adopt a parent complaint and appeal process, and lets aggrieved persons, the attorney general, or the education department sue schools not following it, for at least $1,000 per violation.

nh:HB 1635|modifying the requirements of.title: modifying the requirements of suicide prevention education policies in schools.
nh:HB 1635|modifying the requirements of.summary: As introduced, changes school suicide prevention training so staff complete it within 30 days of being hired and every two years after, instead of at least two hours every year.

nh:HB 377|relative to health care profes.title: relative to health care professionals administering hormone treatments and puberty blockers.
nh:HB 377|relative to health care profes.summary: Bans giving minors puberty blockers or cross-sex hormones for gender transition starting January 2026, except for treatment begun earlier or for disorders of sex development, allowing medical board discipline and lawsuits. Also creates an annual Children's Environmental Health Day proclamation.

nh:HB 1299|permitting classification of.title: permitting classification of individuals based on biological sex under certain limited circumstances and establishing that certain biological sex distinctions do not qualify as discrimination.
nh:HB 1299|permitting classification of.summary: Lets public and private entities separate people by biological sex in shared bathrooms and locker rooms, certain sports, and prisons and similar secure facilities without it counting as discrimination; government buildings that do so must also offer a single-occupancy bathroom open to all.

nh:HB 666|relative to adding restitution.title: relative to adding restitution payment for violations of the confidentiality of the library use records and adding library cards and membership status to the list of confidential matters.
nh:HB 666|relative to adding restitution.summary: Adds library cards and membership status to the library records that must be kept confidential, and requires a library or staff member who knowingly or recklessly discloses them to pay the affected person a $1,000 civil penalty and send a notarized apology.

nh:HB 451|establishing the paint product.title: establishing the paint product stewardship program.
nh:HB 451|establishing the paint product.summary: Requires paint manufacturers to set up and fund a state-approved program to collect and recycle leftover paint, paid for by a per-container fee built into paint prices, with voluntary drop-off sites at stores and towns; bars sales of paint not covered by an approved plan.

nh:HB 1448|prohibiting the use of the wo.title: prohibiting the use of the World Economic Forum materials within state curriculum.
nh:HB 1448|prohibiting the use of the wo.summary: Bars New Hampshire public schools from including lectures, lesson plans or other educational materials created or provided by the World Economic Forum in their curriculum.

nh:HB 1561|prohibiting nationals of the.title: prohibiting nationals of the People's Republic of China from attending state institutions of higher education.
nh:HB 1561|prohibiting nationals of the.summary: Bars nationals of the People's Republic of China from enrolling in master's or doctoral programs, taking part in research, or holding full-time jobs at New Hampshire's public colleges and universities, with penalties for individuals and institutions that violate the ban.

nh:HB 1442|limiting the use of certain f.title: limiting the use of certain facilities on the basis of sex and redefining the term "gender identity."
nh:HB 1442|limiting the use of certain f.summary: Defines female and male by biology, requires bathrooms and locker rooms in public schools and town-owned buildings to be used by sex, lets businesses open to the public do the same, houses inmates by sex, and bars citing gender identity to access single-sex spaces.

nh:SB 567|new title relative to the comp.title: (New Title) relative to the composition of the board of dental examiners.
nh:SB 567|new title relative to the comp.summary: Requires one of the six dentists on the board of dental examiners to be a general dentist, bars routine X-ray screening before a clinical exam, and lets dentists treat patients who decline X-rays if the patient signs a liability waiver.

nh:HB 1300|changing the state s congress.title: changing the state's congressional districts.
nh:HB 1300|changing the state s congress.summary: Drops the congressional redistricting plan and instead puts a question on every town's ballot each even-year November to cap school property taxes at last year's level plus inflation and new construction, and SAU central office budgets at 6 percent of district spending, if 3/5 of voters approve.

nh:HB 1358|new title establishing a comm.title: (New Title) establishing a commission to study transitioning all public schools to public charter schools.
nh:HB 1358|new title establishing a comm.summary: Creates an eight-member commission of legislators, the education commissioner and school representatives to study the feasibility and effects of converting all New Hampshire public schools into public charter schools, including funding less reliant on local property taxes, with a report due November 1, 2026.

nh:HB 1719|removing hepatitis b from the.title: removing Hepatitis B from the list of diseases for which immunization is required under state law.
nh:HB 1719|removing hepatitis b from the.summary: As introduced, removes hepatitis B from the list of diseases against which parents must have their children immunized under state law; the other required childhood vaccines are unchanged.

nh:HB 1515|repealing the child care gran.title: repealing the child care grant program administered by the department of health and human services.
nh:HB 1515|repealing the child care gran.summary: Repeals a 2025 requirement that the Department of Health and Human Services include full funding for certain child care workforce programs in its two-year budget request.

nh:HB 238|prohibiting collective bargain.title: prohibiting collective bargaining agreements from requiring employees join or contribute to a labor union.
nh:HB 238|prohibiting collective bargain.summary: As introduced, bars public and private employers from requiring workers to join or pay a labor union to keep a job, bans contract terms requiring it, and makes violations a misdemeanor punishable by up to a $1,000 fine and 90 days in jail, plus civil damages.

nh:HB 1374|new title modifying the proce.title: (New Title) modifying the procedures for withdrawal from a cooperative school district and the discontinuance of elementary and high schools and requiring the review of school district operating documents by school boards.
nh:HB 1374|new title modifying the proce.summary: Lets a withdrawing district's voters alone decide, by a 3/5 vote, to leave a cooperative school district, requires voters in all towns a school serves to approve closing it unless the host town keeps it open by agreement, and has boards review governing documents every three years.

nh:SB 222|relative to moving the state p.title: relative to moving the state primary date.
nh:SB 222|relative to moving the state p.summary: Moves New Hampshire's state primary from September to June beginning in 2026, and shifts related deadlines earlier, including the candidate filing period and the cutoff for changing party registration, from June to March.

nh:SB 408|relative to health insurance c.title: relative to health insurance coverage for prosthetics.
nh:SB 408|relative to health insurance c.summary: Requires group health insurers and the state employee health plan to cover prosthetic devices for adults, including activity-specific devices, which insurers may limit to one every five years, starting January 1, 2028; children already have this coverage.

nh:HB 282|increasing the maximum benefit.title: increasing the maximum benefits for first responders critically injured in the line of duty.
nh:HB 282|increasing the maximum benefit.summary: Doubles the two-year cap on total critical-injury benefits for first responders to $1 million, and also revises how state education adequacy grants are calculated and makes several changes to public employee retirement benefits and contributions.

nh:HB 1196|repealing the state housing c.title: repealing the state housing champion designation and grant program.
nh:HB 1196|repealing the state housing c.summary: As introduced, repeals the state's housing champion designation and grant program, along with its dedicated fund and related reporting requirements.

nh:HB 1449|limiting times vaccine clinic.title: limiting times vaccine clinics may operate at schools and requiring parents or legal guardians to be present with their child during the administration of vaccinations at such a clinic.
nh:HB 1449|limiting times vaccine clinic.summary: As introduced, bars public and charter schools from holding vaccination clinics during school hours and requires a parent or guardian to be present whenever a child is vaccinated at a school clinic; school nurses' existing duties are unaffected.

nh:HB 422|increasing penalties for viola.title: increasing penalties for violations of the shoreland and water quality protection act.
nh:HB 422|increasing penalties for viola.summary: As introduced, raises the maximum court penalty and administrative fine for violating the state's shoreland water quality protection law from $5,000 to $15,000 for violators who don't restore a site within a year of notice; existing doubling of fines for repeat violations still applies.

nh:HB 1108|relative to the offense of cr.title: relative to the offense of criminal threatening.
nh:HB 1108|relative to the offense of cr.summary: Provides that a person who displays a firearm or other lawful means of self-defense to deter conduct reasonably seen as likely to cause serious injury, death, theft, unlawful entry, or refusal to leave after a trespass notice does not commit criminal threatening, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 357|relative to the department of.title: relative to the department of health and human services' rulemaking authority regarding immunization requirements.
nh:HB 357|relative to the department of.summary: As introduced, limits required childhood vaccines to the diseases listed in state law and removes the health commissioner's power to require others by rule, letting existing rule-based requirements for chickenpox, hepatitis B and Hib expire June 30, 2026.

nh:HB 97|making an appropriation to the.title: making an appropriation to the department of environmental services for wastewater infrastructure projects.
nh:HB 97|making an appropriation to the.summary: As introduced, appropriates $15 million in each of fiscal years 2026 and 2027 to the Department of Environmental Services for wastewater projects approved by June 30, 2026, with unspent money carrying over.

nh:HB 1578|adds definitions and reportin.title: adds definitions and reporting requirements relative to education freedom accounts.
nh:HB 1578|adds definitions and reportin.summary: As introduced, requires the education freedom account program administrator to file quarterly public reports with education officials and legislative committees on applications, withdrawals, payments to each vendor, spending, reimbursements and student demographics, starting with the quarter ending September 30, 2026, and adds program definitions.

nh:SB 15|relative to establishing a mand.title: relative to establishing a mandatory minimum sentence for the crime of distribution of a controlled drug with death resulting.
nh:SB 15|relative to establishing a mand.summary: Replaces the bill's original drug-death mandatory minimum with a hard-labor sentencing option: juries in capital murder and aggravated felonious sexual assault cases against children under 13 may impose life at hard labor without parole by at least 9 of 12 votes, with medical exemptions.

nh:HB 583|relative to state participatio.title: relative to state participation in the Medicaid direct certification program for free and reduced price school meals.
nh:HB 583|relative to state participatio.summary: As introduced, directs the Department of Education, with help from the health department, to seek to join a federal pilot that uses Medicaid enrollment to automatically certify public school students for free and reduced-price meals.

nh:HB 1264|increasing the requirements o.title: increasing the requirements of the education freedom savings account oversight committee and modifying the purpose of the committee.
nh:HB 1264|increasing the requirements o.summary: As introduced, expands the legislative oversight committee for education freedom accounts to review student data, eligibility rules and spending, and requires it to meet at least monthly with meetings broadcast live and recorded on the legislature's website.

nh:SB 141|extending the time to petition.title: extending the time to petition for a new trial in certain cases.
nh:SB 141|extending the time to petition.summary: Lets people convicted of a felony or class A misdemeanor who are still serving or affected by their sentence petition for a new trial after the usual three-year limit if they allege newly discovered evidence, and makes library cards and membership status confidential records.

nh:SB 498|relative to children s mental.title: relative to children's mental health services for persons 18 years of age and younger.
nh:SB 498|relative to children s mental.summary: As introduced, creates a nonprofit children's behavioral health association that assesses health insurers, stop-loss carriers and plan administrators to fund intensive mental health services, such as in-home care and peer support, for privately insured children under 19 through a dedicated state fund.

nh:SB 653|enabling counties to change th.title: enabling counties to change the dates of their biennial budgets.
nh:SB 653|enabling counties to change th.summary: Lets counties, if commissioners agree and a majority of county voters approve, move their two-year budget to years without a state election, and revises how towns adopt, rescind and elect budget committees and how first cooperative school budget committee members are appointed.

nh:SB 106|relative to the participation.title: relative to the participation of customer generators in net energy metering.
nh:SB 106|relative to the participation.summary: Requires new net-metered generators over 1 and up to 5 megawatts, in service after January 1, 2026, to use at least 33 percent of their own output, except for low- and moderate-income customers, and lets projects on current alternative tariffs keep them through at least 2040.

nh:HB 1607|relative to the use and stora.title: relative to the use and storage of road salt.
nh:HB 1607|relative to the use and stora.summary: As introduced, bars storing road salt and other de-icing chemicals in ways or places that risk contaminating groundwater or surface water, and directs the Department of Environmental Services to adopt storage and handling rules, including stricter rules where de-icers have already affected water.

nh:HB 1810|relative to a road salt fee t.title: relative to a road salt fee to support certified winter road maintenance practices.
nh:HB 1810|relative to a road salt fee t.summary: As introduced, imposes a $4-per-ton fee on bulk road salt, salt mix and brine sold to New Hampshire businesses, organizations, municipalities and state agencies, paid yearly by bulk sellers into a fund that gives grants to the state, municipalities and businesses certified in winter salt-application programs.

nh:SB 204|relative to the responsibility.title: relative to the responsibility of local school districts to provide meals to students during school hours, reimbursing schools for meals provided to students at no cost, and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:SB 204|relative to the responsibility.summary: Lets school boards raise free school meal eligibility to 200 percent of the federal poverty level, with the state reimbursing half the gap between free and reduced or paid meal rates, and appropriates $107,000 for administration and $250,000 for reimbursements and application software.

nh:HB 75|legalizing cannabis for persons.title: legalizing cannabis for persons 21 years of age or older.
nh:HB 75|legalizing cannabis for persons.summary: Legalizes possession and use of cannabis for adults 21 and older without creating retail sales or taxes, removes cannabis from the state's controlled drug laws, makes public use and underage possession violations, and annuls past cannabis convictions.

nh:HB 741|allowing parents to send their.title: allowing parents to send their children to any school district they choose.
nh:HB 741|allowing parents to send their.summary: Requires every school district to accept students from other districts tuition-free, with the home district paying at least 80 percent of the receiving district's per-pupil cost; districts may refuse only for space limits, a prior expulsion, or documented discipline or absence problems.

nh:HB 148|permitting classification of i.title: permitting classification of individuals based on biological sex under certain circumstances.
nh:HB 148|permitting classification of i.summary: Lets public and private entities separate people by biological sex in shared bathrooms and locker rooms, in sports where strength, speed or endurance generally gives males an advantage, and in prisons, juvenile detention and mental health facilities, without violating state anti-discrimination law.

nh:HB 1793|prohibiting public colleges a.title: prohibiting public colleges and universities from regulating the possession or carrying of firearms and non-lethal weapons on campus.
nh:HB 1793|prohibiting public colleges a.summary: As introduced, bars public colleges and universities from regulating the possession or carrying of firearms and non-lethal weapons on campus, and lets people harmed by such rules sue the school for damages and court orders.

nh:HB 1820|requiring the department of e.title: requiring the department of education to administer the education freedom account program.
nh:HB 1820|requiring the department of e.summary: Moves administration of the education freedom account program from a scholarship organization to the Department of Education starting July 1, 2026, including approving applications, transferring funds to accounts and approving service providers.

nh:HB 624|establishing a local river man.title: establishing a local river management advisory committee grant program and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:HB 624|establishing a local river man.summary: Creates a Department of Environmental Services grant program giving local river management advisory committees up to $10,000 a year each, and appropriates $40,000 in each of fiscal years 2026 and 2027.

nh:HB 1495|allowing a reimbursement anti.title: allowing a reimbursement anticipation note to be used as collateral in certain circumstances.
nh:HB 1495|allowing a reimbursement anti.summary: Lets school districts borrow against expected state reimbursements and count the borrowed money as revenue when tax rates are set, after a public hearing, if it is spent only for the same purpose; the borrowing is exempt from debt limits.

nh:HB 378|relative to an employee s unus.title: relative to an employee's unused earned time.
nh:HB 378|relative to an employee s unus.summary: Requires employers with 15 or more workers that offer paid time off to pay out unused vacation, holiday and personal time, but not sick days, when a business closes or changes owners or a job ends with no expected return.

nh:CACR 22|relating to the compensation.title: relating to the compensation of the legislature. Providing that the present compensation per elected term for legislators is hereby abolished.
nh:CACR 22|relating to the compensation.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment for the November 2026 ballot ending the $200 per-term pay for legislators and $250 for presiding officers while keeping mileage reimbursement; it needs two-thirds voter approval.

nh:HB 104|relative to requiring an offic.title: relative to requiring an official declaration of war for the activation of the New Hampshire national guard in a foreign state.
nh:HB 104|relative to requiring an offic.summary: Bars releasing New Hampshire National Guard members from the state into active-duty combat unless Congress has declared war or formally called out the Guard under the U.S. Constitution, and requires the governor to comply.

nh:HB 709|allowing parents or guardians.title: allowing parents or guardians to admit their children into any school district where they pay any property or school district taxes.
nh:HB 709|allowing parents or guardians.summary: Lets a child's school district of residence be any New Hampshire district where a parent or guardian lives or pays property or school district taxes, if the parent lives in the state; divorced parents with joint custody may choose either parent's district by written agreement.

nh:SB 449|new title relative to relative.title: (New Title) relative to relative to the participation of large customer-generators in net metering and relative to energy storage in connection with net metering.
nh:SB 449|new title relative to relative.summary: Requires electric utilities to offer alternative net metering tariffs under a 2017 utility commission order, sets terms for industrial customer-generators between 1 and 5 megawatts, and allows energy storage with net metering under Department of Energy installation rules.

nh:HB 332|allowing for the establishment.title: allowing for the establishment of a village district to protect and remediate surface waters.
nh:HB 332|allowing for the establishment.summary: Adds protecting and cleaning up surface water quality to the purposes for which a village district may be formed, letting towns that share a body of water adopt consistent environmental policies.

nh:HB 1697|exempting certain firearms an.title: exempting certain firearms and firearm accessories manufactured and retained in New Hampshire from federal regulation.
nh:HB 1697|exempting certain firearms an.summary: Declares firearms and accessories made and kept in New Hampshire and marked "For N.H. Use Only" exempt from federal regulation, requires serial numbers and certificates of manufacture, and makes exporting them or removing the marking a misdemeanor.

nh:HB 1834|relative to the education fre.title: relative to the education freedom account enrollment cap.
nh:HB 1834|relative to the education fre.summary: Keeps the education freedom account enrollment cap at 10,000 students for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 school years, then raises it 25 percent in any later year when prior-year enrollment exceeded 90 percent of the cap.

nh:HB 1817|permitting all students the c.title: permitting all students the choice to attend the school district in which they reside.
nh:HB 1817|permitting all students the c.summary: Lets students in private, charter and home education programs and education freedom account students take courses, state tests and activities such as clubs and sports in their local public school district, under board policies no stricter than for district students.

nh:HB 1405|relative to the housing finan.title: relative to the housing finance authority's affordable housing guarantee program.
nh:HB 1405|relative to the housing finan.summary: Creates a Housing Finance Authority program guaranteeing 80 percent of principal on approved lenders' affordable housing loans, capped at $30 million per lender a year and $300 million outstanding, backed by the state's full faith and credit.

nh:HB 1337|repealing the new hampshire c.title: repealing the New Hampshire council on autism spectrum disorders.
nh:HB 1337|repealing the new hampshire c.summary: Repeals the New Hampshire council on autism spectrum disorders, along with its seat on the developmental services quality council and its consulting role in the blue envelope driver program, effective December 31, 2027.

nh:HB 1452|relative to parent taught dri.title: relative to parent-taught driver education as an alternative to traditional driver education programs.
nh:HB 1452|relative to parent taught dri.summary: As introduced, lets the safety commissioner waive the driver education course for license applicants under 18 if a licensed parent or guardian, or another responsible adult when there is none, provides equivalent classroom and behind-the-wheel instruction.

nh:SB 105|enabling towns to adopt budget.title: enabling towns to adopt budget caps.
nh:SB 105|enabling towns to adopt budget.summary: Lets towns adopt, by a three-fifths vote, a budget cap limiting yearly spending to the prior year's per-resident amount times population, adjusted by a set percentage or inflation index; exceeding the cap requires a three-fifths ballot vote.

nh:HB 274|relative to the verification o.title: relative to the verification of voter rolls annually.
nh:HB 274|relative to the verification o.summary: Requires local election officials to verify voter checklists every year starting in 2026 instead of every 10 years, removing voters who have not voted in five years and do not reregister after notice.

nh:HB 1484|establishing a state minimum.title: establishing a state minimum wage and providing for incremental increases.
nh:HB 1484|establishing a state minimum.summary: Sets a state minimum wage above the federal rate: $12 an hour starting September 1, 2026, $14 in 2027, $15.50 in 2028 and $17 starting January 1, 2029.

nh:HB 219|new title relative to changes.title: (New Title) relative to changes to the minimum electric renewable portfolio standards.
nh:HB 219|new title relative to changes.summary: Repeals the separate Class II (solar) requirement of the state's renewable portfolio standard and replaces inflation-adjusted alternative compliance payments with fixed rates of $42 for Classes I and III ($30 for Class I thermal) and $37 for Class IV.

nh:HB 1832|adding students with parents.title: adding students with parents on active military duty to the education freedom accounts priority guidelines.
nh:HB 1832|adding students with parents.summary: Adds students living in New Hampshire with a parent or guardian on active military duty to the priority groups for education freedom accounts, regardless of where the parent is stationed.

nh:HB 1487|creating an independent commi.title: creating an independent commission to propose redistricting maps for the legislature to consider.
nh:HB 1487|creating an independent commi.summary: Creates a nine-member commission, chosen partly by random draw from screened applicants, to propose advisory redistricting maps starting in 2031; if the legislature twice rejects a map, voters may ask the state Supreme Court to appoint a special master.

nh:SB 33|relative to the regulation of p.title: relative to the regulation of public school materials.
nh:SB 33|relative to the regulation of p.summary: Requires school boards by September 1, 2026, to post policies on materials students may not access and a process for parents to challenge material as harmful to minors or age-inappropriate, with principal decisions within 15 school days and appeals to the board.

nh:HB 1155|relative to the home educatio.title: relative to the home education advisory council.
nh:HB 1155|relative to the home educatio.summary: Repeals the home education advisory council and ends the requirement that the state board of education send proposed home education rules to the council for review.

nh:HB 749|requiring high schools to incl.title: requiring high schools to include instruction on the nature and history of communism.
nh:HB 749|requiring high schools to incl.summary: Requires public high schools to provide at least one hour of instruction on the nature and history of communism, either as a standalone activity or within an existing course, beginning September 1, 2025.

nh:HB 1376|new title relative to a paren.title: (New Title) relative to a parent's ability to raise their child in a manner consistent with the child's biological sex and relative to breast surgeries for minors.
nh:HB 1376|new title relative to a paren.summary: Provides that raising a child consistent with the child's biological sex, including related medical and mental health decisions, is not by itself abuse, neglect or child endangerment, and cannot disqualify adoptive or foster parents or count against a parent in custody cases.

nh:CACR 14|relating to qualifications fo.title: relating to qualifications for office. Providing that candidates of the office of governor, state senator, and state representative shall be citizens of the United States.
nh:CACR 14|relating to qualifications fo.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, requiring candidates for governor, state senator and state representative to be U.S. citizens; it would take effect only with two-thirds voter approval.

nh:CACR 24|relating to the right to educ.title: relating to the right to educate children. Providing that parents and guardians have a right to direct the education of their children.
nh:CACR 24|relating to the right to educ.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, declaring that parents and legal guardians, as children's primary educators, have a right to direct their children's education that shall not be infringed; it requires two-thirds voter approval.

nh:HB 1815|relative to education financi.title: relative to education financing.
nh:HB 1815|relative to education financi.summary: Defines the adequate education the state must fund as meeting state school approval standards in 11 subject areas, including English, math, science, social studies, arts, world languages, health, physical education, personal finance and computer science, and restates state education policy.

nh:SB 36|relative to the collection and.title: relative to the collection and reporting of abortion statistics by health care providers and medical facilities.
nh:SB 36|relative to the collection and.summary: Delays the start of required abortion-statistics reporting by health care providers and facilities from January 1, 2027 to July 1, 2027, and changes the reported item from estimated gestational age to gestational age when the abortion was performed.

nh:HB 1655|establishing a funding source.title: establishing a funding source for maintaining state owned dams.
nh:HB 1655|establishing a funding source.summary: Creates a $100 yearly fee on waterfront property, and a $50 fee on property with deeded water access, on water bodies formed by state-owned dams, with proceeds going to dam maintenance; current-use land and working farms are exempt.

nh:HB 1224|relative to the default budge.title: relative to the default budget for official ballot town meetings.
nh:HB 1224|relative to the default budge.summary: Changes how a town's default budget is calculated, requiring reductions for the salaries and benefits of eliminated positions and of positions left vacant since the prior budget, with an exception for certain vacant public safety jobs, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 1799|relative to required state fu.title: relative to required state funding for providing an opportunity for an adequate education.
nh:HB 1799|relative to required state fu.summary: Raises state adequacy aid from $4,100 to about $7,380 per pupil starting July 2027, increases extra aid for low-income, English-learner and special-education students, requires district plans to close achievement gaps, and creates a commission to study alternatives to property taxes.

nh:HCR 7|recognizing abortion as a criti.title: recognizing abortion as a critical component of comprehensive reproductive health care.
nh:HCR 7|recognizing abortion as a criti.summary: Recognizes abortion as a critical component of comprehensive reproductive health care and resolves that an individual's right to end a pregnancy before 24 weeks of gestation shall not be denied or infringed in New Hampshire.

nh:HB 1227|relative to the calculation o.title: relative to the calculation of the local tax cap.
nh:HB 1227|relative to the calculation o.summary: Changes the local tax cap formula so that new annual debt payments on bonds approved by the local legislative body are added to the capped tax base once repayment begins, and applies the change to existing tax caps without re-adoption.

nh:HB 50|relative to teaching discrimina.title: relative to teaching discrimination in public schools and discrimination in public workplaces.
nh:HB 50|relative to teaching discrimina.summary: Limits the state ban on teaching certain discriminatory concepts to teaching that targets racial groups, protects historical and objective scientific discussion, and limits lawsuits, human rights complaints and educator misconduct findings to intentional or knowing violations.

nh:HB 1132|prohibiting the display of ce.title: prohibiting the display of certain flags in public schools and public charter schools and establishing penalties for the display of prohibited flags.
nh:HB 1132|prohibiting the display of ce.summary: Bars public and charter schools from displaying flags or banners other than the U.S., New Hampshire and POW/MIA flags, with exceptions for instruction, school, military and town flags, and allows state fines up to $1,000 for repeated violations, starting September 1, 2026.

nh:HB 1083|requiring the disclosure of t.title: requiring the disclosure of the source of certain political donations in state elections.
nh:HB 1083|requiring the disclosure of t.summary: Requires anyone spending over $500,000 independently to support or oppose a candidate for governor, or over $50,000 on executive council or legislative candidates, to file the names and addresses of the original sources of those funds with the secretary of state.

nh:HB 1716|relative to the academic acco.title: relative to the academic accountability of education freedom accounts.
nh:HB 1716|relative to the academic acco.summary: Requires test results or teacher evaluations for students using education freedom accounts to be reported to the state education department, which must create a portfolio-review rubric and compile proficiency data for those students by grade and other categories.

nh:HB 392|directing the dissolution of t.title: directing the dissolution of the department of health and human services' office of health equity, department of environmental services' functions for civil rights and environmental justice, and the governor's council on diversity and inclusion.
nh:HB 392|directing the dissolution of t.summary: Dissolves the health department's office of health access, moving its language-access, disability, federally required and rural health programs elsewhere in the department, and bars spending on projects labeled "health equity" or, at the environmental agency, "environmental justice."

nh:SB 206|requiring public schools to ad.title: requiring public schools to adopt policies to limit the use of cell phones by students.
nh:SB 206|requiring public schools to ad.summary: Requires school boards and charter schools to adopt policies barring student use of cell phones and other personal devices from the first bell to dismissal, with exceptions for medical, disability or language needs, developed with parents and teachers and reviewed yearly.

nh:HB 712|limiting breast surgeries for.title: limiting breast surgeries for minors.
nh:HB 712|limiting breast surgeries for.summary: Bars physicians from performing breast surgery on anyone under 18 except to treat cancer, injury, infection, certain abnormal breast development or congenital deformities, expands the existing ban on gender surgery for minors, changes care-facility licensing rules and requires abortion-statistics reporting.

nh:HB 1557|modifying the state average e.title: modifying the state average expenditure per pupil relative to students in special education.
nh:HB 1557|modifying the state average e.summary: Lowers the point at which the state helps pay a student's special education costs from 3.5 times to 1.5 times the state average per-pupil cost, with the state covering 80 percent of costs above that level, starting July 1, 2026.

nh:CACR 4|relating to voting eligibility.title: relating to voting eligibility. Providing that only legal resident citizens who are at least 18 years of age or older who reside in the place they claim as a domicile shall be eligible voters.
nh:CACR 4|relating to voting eligibility.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, giving the right to vote to every "legal resident" 18 or older instead of every "inhabitant," and requiring voters to actually live where they claim domicile; needs two-thirds voter approval.

nh:HB 1378|relative to parental access t.title: relative to parental access to a minor child's electronic medical records.
nh:HB 1378|relative to parental access t.summary: Gives parents and legal guardians full access to their minor child's medical records, including online patient portals, except for care a minor may legally get without parental consent, protective-order or court-ordered limits, or a provider-documented likely risk of abuse or neglect.

nh:HB 1542|relative to renewable energy.title: relative to renewable energy fund compliance payments.
nh:HB 1542|relative to renewable energy.summary: As amended by the House on February 12, 2026, requires that alternative compliance payments electricity providers make to the state renewable energy fund be rebated to ratepayers per kilowatt-hour instead of funding renewable energy programs, starting July 1, 2026.

nh:HB 1709|relative to prohibiting the r.title: relative to prohibiting the rental of residential property to individuals unlawfully present in the United States.
nh:HB 1709|relative to prohibiting the r.summary: Makes it a misdemeanor for an unlawfully present immigrant previously convicted of a felony and deported or who left the country, as confirmed by federal authorities, to occupy or rent property, and directs sheriffs to arrest such people during evictions when safely possible.

nh:SB 100|relative to violations of the.title: relative to violations of the prohibition on teaching discrimination.
nh:SB 100|relative to violations of the.summary: Applies the state ban on teaching certain discriminatory concepts only to intentional or knowing conduct targeting racial groups, allows historical discussion, lets aggrieved people or the attorney general sue schools or file with the human rights commission, and treats educator violations as misconduct.

nh:HB 461|relative to department of safe.title: relative to department of safety and department of motor vehicle training and testing materials.
nh:HB 461|relative to department of safe.summary: Requires driver's license exams and related materials to be in English only, with American Sign Language allowed, bars translators and translation devices during exams, and stops the motor vehicle division from acquiring or distributing other-language materials, starting January 1, 2026.

nh:SB 603|relative to the funding of the.title: relative to the funding of the SNAP program by the department of health and human services.
nh:SB 603|relative to the funding of the.summary: Directs the state health department, through June 2027, to shift funds among its accounts as needed to cover any cut in federal funding for the SNAP food assistance program, with transfers of $100,000 or more needing legislative fiscal committee and executive council approval.

nh:HB 360|prohibiting public schools fro.title: prohibiting public schools from performing diagnostic tests or surgical procedures, or prescribing pharmaceutical drugs.
nh:HB 360|prohibiting public schools fro.summary: Bars public school physicians, nurses and other health care providers employed or contracted by a school district from performing surgical procedures or prescribing pharmaceutical drugs on school grounds.

nh:HB 771|relative to funding for open e.title: relative to funding for open enrollment schools.
nh:HB 771|relative to funding for open e.summary: Changes how open enrollment schools are funded: no tuition for students attending one in their own district, and sending districts pay receiving districts at least 80% of their average per-pupil cost. Requires districts to budget open enrollment tuition as a line item.

nh:SB 543|relative to long term care eli.title: relative to long-term care eligibility and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:SB 543|relative to long term care eli.summary: Requires the health department to grant provisional Medicaid eligibility for nursing facility care within 90 days of a long-term care application, paying contracted facilities for up to 18 months, with payments repaid after a final decision. Appropriates $1 and creates two positions.

nh:HB 1807|relative to information on ta.title: relative to information on tax rates and tax impact information on warrant articles.
nh:HB 1807|relative to information on ta.summary: Changes the format and content of the mandatory report to voters on school expenses, including 10-year inflation-adjusted graphs of per-pupil cost, teacher pay and administrator pay, and lists the top 10 administrator salaries. Requires school budget warrant articles to display specified tax information.

nh:HB 1831|repealing the education trust.title: repealing the education trust fund targeted aid cap.
nh:HB 1831|repealing the education trust.summary: Repeals the $3,750-per-pupil cap on additional targeted education aid for communities with 5,000 or more pupils. The fiscal note estimates about $9 million a year in added state aid starting in fiscal 2028, affecting only Manchester.

nh:SB 430|new title relative to mandator.title: (New Title) relative to mandatory disclosure by school district employees to parents and legal guardians.
nh:SB 430|new title relative to mandator.summary: Requires credentialed public school educators to answer parents' written requests for information about their child honestly and completely within 10 business days, unless barred by law or a response would risk abuse or neglect. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

nh:SB 481|new title relative to the sale.title: (New Title) relative to the sale of the Sununu youth services center property.
nh:SB 481|new title relative to the sale.summary: Directs the state administrative services department to take over and sell the Sununu Youth Services Center property in Manchester for at least market value, with Governor and Council approval. Sends sale proceeds to the general fund and allows requests for maintenance funding.

nh:HB 1555|relative to the administratio.title: relative to the administration and enforcement of the state fire code.
nh:HB 1555|relative to the administratio.summary: Has the state fire marshal hear appeals of local fire chief decisions, holding a hearing within 40 days and ruling within 30 days after, and lets the fire marshal approve or deny project-specific alternatives and modifications to the state building code in all municipalities.

nh:HB 1722|relative to consumer protecti.title: relative to consumer protections and energy classifications for large-use electric facilities.
nh:HB 1722|relative to consumer protecti.summary: Requires utility regulators to create a separate electric rate class for facilities such as data centers drawing 20 megawatts or more, with cost-based rates, contracts of at least 10 years, and protections against shifting costs to other customers.

nh:HB 1317|relative to patient privacy p.title: relative to patient privacy protections.
nh:HB 1317|relative to patient privacy p.summary: Bars state agencies, local governments and their contractors from collecting, keeping or sharing personally identifiable medical, disability or mental health data with the federal government or third parties, except with consent, when required by law, or to provide care or benefits.

nh:HCR 13|requesting congress to call a.title: requesting Congress to call a constitutional convention relative to implementing term limits for elected members of both houses of Congress.
nh:HCR 13|requesting congress to call a.summary: Applies to Congress, under Article V of the U.S. Constitution, for a convention of the states limited to proposing an amendment setting term limits for members of the U.S. House and Senate.

nh:HB 1387|repealing limiting liability.title: repealing limiting liability for certain design features of firearms.
nh:HB 1387|repealing limiting liability.summary: Repeals the state law that limits legal liability for certain design features of firearms.

nh:HB 630|preventing the dissemination o.title: preventing the dissemination of deepfake materials of political candidates before an election.
nh:HB 630|preventing the dissemination o.summary: As introduced, bars distributing deepfakes of candidates, election officials or parties within 90 days of an election unless labeled as manipulated, and lets depicted candidates and officials sue. Exempts news reports, satire, parody and platforms hosting others' content.

nh:SB 545|relative to financial eligibil.title: relative to financial eligibility for the Medicare savings program.
nh:SB 545|relative to financial eligibil.summary: Removes the asset limit for New Hampshire's Medicare savings program and, subject to federal approval, makes the Medicare Part D low-income subsidy for prescription drug costs available to residents through the program.

nh:SB 223|new title prohibiting student.title: (New Title) prohibiting student identification cards from being used as photo identification for purposes of obtaining a ballot.
nh:SB 223|new title prohibiting student.summary: Limits the photo identification voters may show to obtain a ballot to the forms specifically listed in state law, and repeals the requirement that the education commissioner give the secretary of state a list of certain schools.

nh:HB 1791|directing the department of e.title: directing the department of education to establish a grant program at the post-secondary educational level for individuals with developmental disabilities, and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:HB 1791|directing the department of e.summary: As introduced, creates a state grant program for public colleges to offer courses and support to students with developmental disabilities, with 25% of grants going to student scholarships, and appropriates $100,000 for fiscal 2028.

nh:HB 1002|repealing the solar energy sy.title: repealing the solar energy systems tax exemption.
nh:HB 1002|repealing the solar energy sy.summary: Repeals the optional local property tax exemption for solar energy systems, effective April 1, 2027.

nh:SB 586|requiring school districts to.title: requiring school districts to publish a school administrative unit audit report after the end of the fiscal year.
nh:SB 586|requiring school districts to.summary: Requires charter schools, school administrative units and districts not otherwise audited to get independent annual audits, file them with the education department within nine months of year-end and post them online; noncompliant entities lose state grants other than adequacy aid until they comply.

nh:HCR 12|calling upon the federal deleg.title: calling upon the federal delegation from New Hampshire to support Medicare for All, a universal health insurance program that guarantees all people the health care they need.
nh:HCR 12|calling upon the federal deleg.summary: Urges New Hampshire's congressional delegation to pass Medicare for All legislation offering every citizen and legal resident Medicare enrollment, with coverage including dental, vision, prescription drugs and long-term care and no deductibles, and moving Medicaid enrollees into Medicare.

nh:HB 1824|relative to school district f.title: relative to school district financial distress.
nh:HB 1824|relative to school district f.summary: As introduced, lets the education commissioner, with legislative fiscal committee approval, lend to insolvent school districts, lets towns give them emergency aid, raises districts' allowed reserve from 5% to 10%, and creates a revolving loan fund for cash-flow gaps before state aid arrives.

nh:HB 1022|relative to religious exempti.title: relative to religious exemption from immunization requirements.
nh:HB 1022|relative to religious exempti.summary: Sets the wording of the form parents or guardians sign to claim a religious exemption from childhood vaccination requirements, including a statement that they hold sincere religious beliefs requiring refusal of the vaccines.

nh:HB 1447|restricting the use of certai.title: restricting the use of certain public and private facilities on the basis of sex and establishing that such restriction does not qualify as discrimination.
nh:HB 1447|restricting the use of certai.summary: As introduced, requires the state and local governments to adopt policies separating restrooms, locker rooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by sex as shown on the original birth certificate, lets private entities do the same, and declares such policies not discriminatory.

nh:HB 667|veto override.title: Veto Override
nh:HB 667|veto override.summary: Requires public school health curricula to include showing a computer-generated animation or ultrasound video of early fetal development, including the heart, brain and other organs.

nh:SB 119|relative to medicaid pharmaceu.title: relative to Medicaid pharmaceutical services.
nh:SB 119|relative to medicaid pharmaceu.summary: Requires pharmacists to dispense brand-name drugs on the state Medicaid preferred drug list instead of generics, and lets pharmacists dispense ivermectin without a prescription under a prescriber's standing order, except to pregnant patients or those under 18.

nh:HB 521|authorizing online voter regis.title: authorizing online voter registration.
nh:HB 521|authorizing online voter regis.summary: Requires the secretary of state to set up online voter registration for applicants with a New Hampshire motor vehicle ID, verified against motor vehicle records; online registrants must submit an original signature before voting in their first election.

nh:HB 756|relative to establishing a blo.title: relative to establishing a blood lead level testing requirement for children entering daycare and public schools.
nh:HB 756|relative to establishing a blo.summary: Requires school and day care health forms for children 6 and under to include at least one blood lead test result, unless exempt, and requires schools and day cares to notify parents of untested children and provide lead information.

nh:HB 1786|relative to creating a state.title: relative to creating a state assessment on non-homestead luxury second homes to fund statewide housing development programs and address housing shortages and making appropriations therefor.
nh:HB 1786|relative to creating a state.summary: As introduced, creates a twice-yearly state charge on homes valued over $1 million that are not a primary residence, at $2.50 per $500 of value above $1 million, to fund housing programs. Appropriates money for housing and workforce training and expands housing investment tax credits.

nh:HB 665|relative to eligibility for fr.title: relative to eligibility for free school meals.
nh:HB 665|relative to eligibility for fr.summary: Makes school meals free for children in households earning up to 300% of the federal poverty guidelines, with the state paying districts' costs from the education trust fund.

nh:SB 272|relative to electric vehicle c.title: relative to electric-vehicle charging station funding.
nh:SB 272|relative to electric vehicle c.summary: Lets towns use revolving funds to install and maintain electric-vehicle charging stations, and bars parking in signed charging spaces unless the vehicle is charging, with a minimum $62 fine.

nh:HB 1735|permitting treatment of certa.title: permitting treatment of certain severe illness under the right to try act.
nh:HB 1735|permitting treatment of certa.summary: Expands the state's right-to-try law so patients with a chronic and debilitating illness, not only a terminal one, can seek investigational drugs, biologics or devices, including treatments made for one patient based on their genetic profile.

nh:SB 34|relative to parental consent fo.title: relative to parental consent for student participation in Medicaid to schools program.
nh:SB 34|relative to parental consent fo.summary: Requires schools to get a parent's written consent for each new service, defined as each new diagnosis code, provided to a student under the Medicaid to schools program, and adds legislative policy committee chairs to those receiving the program's annual report.

nh:HB 198|relative to legalizing certain.title: relative to legalizing certain quantities of cannabis and establishing penalties for the smoking or vaping of cannabis in public.
nh:HB 198|relative to legalizing certain.summary: As introduced, legalizes possession of up to 2 ounces of cannabis, 10 grams of concentrate, or products with up to 2,000 mg of THC by adults 21 and older, and sets a fine of up to $100 for first-offense public smoking or vaping.

nh:HB 1565|new title relative to the pen.title: (New Title) relative to the penalty for false reports of suspected abuse and neglect made to the division for children, youth, and families, relative to owner's project manager services for school building aid projects, and relative to long-term care eligibility and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:HB 1565|new title relative to the pen.summary: Makes knowingly false reports of child abuse or neglect a misdemeanor and lets people harmed sue, raises to $1.5 million the school building aid project size requiring an owner's project manager, hired before applying, and requires provisional Medicaid nursing home eligibility within 90 days of application.

nh:HB 1171|relative to eviction safeguar.title: relative to eviction safeguards for tenants whose Social Security payments are disrupted.
nh:HB 1171|relative to eviction safeguar.summary: As introduced, gives residential tenants who miss rent because their monthly Social Security benefits are unexpectedly halted a 90-day grace period to find other housing or funding, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 656|relative to the authority of l.title: relative to the authority of local school districts to accept federal grants.
nh:HB 656|relative to the authority of l.summary: Requires school boards to list expected state and federal funds, and any obligations attached to them, in their annual report, and to hold a public hearing before accepting unexpected funds of $20,000 or more.

nh:HB 687|relative to class action settl.title: relative to class action settlements and consent decrees.
nh:HB 687|relative to class action settl.summary: As introduced, sends money from class action judgments that cannot be distributed to class members to the state general fund, bars courts from redirecting it to other recipients, and limits attorneys' fees in these and consent decree suits to the Laffey Matrix rates unless a court decides otherwise.

nh:SB 99|relative to regional career and.title: relative to regional career and technical education agreements.
nh:SB 99|relative to regional career and.summary: Requires each regional career and technical education agreement to set up a program letting students who take a career course at a receiving school also take other classes there, with sending districts paying at least 80 percent of their per-pupil cost, prorated for part-time students.

nh:HB 1609|limiting the use of state cou.title: limiting the use of state, county, and municipal funds and property for construction and operation of certain immigrant detention facilities.
nh:HB 1609|limiting the use of state cou.summary: As introduced, bars the state, counties and towns from using public funds or property to build or convert immigrant detention facilities, or paying for privately owned ones, while still allowing agencies with 287(g) agreements to cooperate with federal immigration authorities.

nh:HB 1760|repealing the directive that.title: repealing the directive that the department of health and human services seek a waiver to establish pharmacy copayment and premium requirements under the state Medicaid plan and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:HB 1760|repealing the directive that.summary: As introduced, repeals laws requiring the state to seek higher Medicaid prescription copayments and to charge premiums in the Granite Advantage and children's health insurance programs, and appropriates general funds to cover the lost revenue.

nh:SB 221|relative to the verification o.title: relative to the verification of the checklist.
nh:SB 221|relative to the verification o.summary: Requires local supervisors to verify voter checklists every year starting in 2026 instead of every 10 years, and to remove voters who have not voted in the past five years, joined since the last state general election, or re-registered, after at least 30 days' notice.

nh:SB 97|relative to intra district publ.title: relative to intra-district public school transfers.
nh:SB 97|relative to intra district publ.summary: Lets parents request that their child transfer to another school within their home district, and requires the superintendent to approve the request when the requested school has room for the student.

nh:HB 1584|directing the department of h.title: directing the department of health and human services to provide notice of medical and religious exemptions from immunization requirements and relative to the form of such exemption.
nh:HB 1584|directing the department of h.summary: Requires the state health department to tell families that medical and religious exemptions from immunization requirements are available, and makes any signed written statement of religious objection sufficient for an exemption.

nh:HB 724|relative to lead paint poisoni.title: relative to lead paint poisoning prevention and remediation.
nh:HB 724|relative to lead paint poisoni.summary: As introduced, lowers the blood lead level that triggers a state investigation of a child's lead poisoning from 5 to 3.5 micrograms per deciliter, requires inspection of all units in a rental building with a lead hazard, and presumes pre-1978 housing contains lead.

nh:HB 273|relative to a parent s access.title: relative to a parent's access to their minor child's library records.
nh:HB 273|relative to a parent s access.summary: Lets parents or legal guardians see their minor child's library records of current borrowing of books and audio-visual materials, starting January 1, 2026.

nh:HB 348|relative to eligibility for lo.title: relative to eligibility for local assistance.
nh:HB 348|relative to eligibility for lo.summary: Lets towns require proof of residency, such as a lease or utility bill, for local general assistance, allows special consideration for non-residents fleeing abuse and up to 72 hours of emergency aid for non-residents, and sets a monthly aid limit of at least half the federal poverty level.

nh:HB 690|directing the department of en.title: directing the department of energy to investigate the state's withdrawal from ISO-New England and other strategy decisions that impact ratepayers in relation to New England's environmental policy.
nh:HB 690|directing the department of en.summary: Directs the state energy department to study New Hampshire leaving the regional grid operator ISO New England, including costs, reliability and legal barriers, and to report to legislative energy committees within one year.

nh:HB 1356|relative to the statute of li.title: relative to the statute of limitations for bringing a private right of action for violation of the statute prohibiting medical procedures and treatments intended to alter a minor's gender.
nh:HB 1356|relative to the statute of li.summary: Extends the deadline to sue over a violation of the state ban on medical procedures intended to change a minor's gender from 2 years to 10 years after the minor turns 18.

nh:HB 121|establishing local school dist.title: establishing local school district special education parent advisory councils.
nh:HB 121|establishing local school dist.summary: Revises local audit rules with fines up to $500 a day for late audits, ends the election of school district auditors, and lets the state board of education put a school district on probation, with the education department appointing an administrator if a remedial plan fails.

nh:HB 768|concur.title: Concur
nh:HB 768|concur.summary: Lets school districts without a public school at a student's grade level contract with any approved nonpublic school, including religious schools, to educate that student.

nh:SB 574|establishing a commission to s.title: establishing a commission to study the efficiency and structure of school administrative units.
nh:SB 574|establishing a commission to s.summary: Creates a 10-member commission to study the efficiency and structure of school administrative units, including options for consolidation and property tax relief, with a report due November 1, 2026.

nh:HB 112|new title requiring students i.title: (New Title) requiring students in the university and community college systems of New Hampshire to pass the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services civics naturalization test, take a course that covers fundamental American documents as part of
nh:HB 112|new title requiring students i.summary: Requires students entering the state university and community college systems on or after July 1, 2027 to pass the federal civics naturalization test, take a general education course covering founding American documents, or pass a civics competency test in order to graduate.

nh:HB 1803|rendering a recipient of an e.title: rendering a recipient of an education tax credit scholarship ineligible to receive education freedom account funds in the same program year.
nh:HB 1803|rendering a recipient of an e.summary: As introduced, bars students from receiving both education freedom account funds and an education tax credit scholarship in the same program year, or while holding a leftover balance from the other program, and limits virtual charter academy part-time funding to students in neither program.

nh:HB 1225|relative to the definition of.title: relative to the definition of adjusted gross income with respect to child support guidelines.
nh:HB 1225|relative to the definition of.summary: Adds certain taxes, including Social Security and Medicare taxes withheld from an employee's pay, to the amounts subtracted from gross income when figuring a parent's income for child support, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 691|prohibiting the addition of fl.title: prohibiting the addition of fluoridation chemicals to public water systems.
nh:HB 691|prohibiting the addition of fl.summary: As introduced, bans adding fluoride or fluoride-containing chemicals to public water systems and repeals the laws letting communities vote on fluoridation.

nh:HB 1043|relative to employer discreti.title: relative to employer discretion in offering minimum payment options to employees.
nh:HB 1043|relative to employer discreti.summary: Makes the requirement that employers pay at least two hours' wages to workers called in to work apply only when the employer has no different written pay policy.

nh:HB 381|exempting firearms and firearm.title: exempting firearms and firearm accessories manufactured for in-state use only from the National Firearm Act.
