nh:HB 381|exempting firearms and firearm.summary: Bars product liability lawsuits against firearm manufacturers based on whether a gun has certain features, such as a magazine disconnect, loaded chamber indicator, user recognition technology or external safety, except for manufacturing defects or warranty failures.

nh:SB 23|expanding the crime of endanger.title: expanding the crime of endangering the welfare of a child.
nh:SB 23|expanding the crime of endanger.summary: Expands child endangerment to include conduct that places a child under 18 in danger of serious bodily injury or death (class B felony) or causes such injury or death (class A felony), makes a pattern of repeated duty-of-care violations a class B felony, and drops the 'purposely' requirement.

nh:SB 501|relative to authorization of s.title: relative to authorization of seclusion or restraint during a personal safety emergency by a physician, physician associate, or advanced practice registered nurse.
nh:SB 501|relative to authorization of s.summary: Lets a physician, physician associate, or advanced practice registered nurse order seclusion or restraint of a patient during a personal safety emergency at New Hampshire Hospital and other designated receiving facilities.

nh:CACR 10|relating to the adoption of t.title: relating to the adoption of tax laws. Providing that no law shall establish or increase a state imposed tax unless adopted by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
nh:CACR 10|relating to the adoption of t.summary: As amended by the House, proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, barring the House of Representatives from adopting a tax on wages or other personal income of individuals; taxes on businesses are not affected.

nh:HB 1458|new title relative to the lic.title: (New Title) relative to the licensing of massage establishments and massage, reflexology, structural integration, and Asian bodywork facilities.
nh:HB 1458|new title relative to the lic.summary: Requires owners and operators of massage and bodywork establishments to be licensed, with fingerprint-based criminal background checks and disqualification for certain past convictions, and bars operating without proprietor and practitioner licenses, starting July 2027.

nh:HB 584|relative to public health safe.title: relative to public health, safety, and state sovereignty.
nh:HB 584|relative to public health safe.summary: Declares that the World Health Organization, United Nations, and World Economic Forum have no authority in New Hampshire, bars state and local enforcement of their rules or mandates, and lets people sue local governments that enforce policies based on them.

nh:HB 452|relative to the issuance of dr.title: relative to the issuance of drivers' licenses for aliens temporarily residing in New Hampshire.
nh:HB 452|relative to the issuance of dr.summary: Tightens rules for driver's licenses issued to noncitizens living in the state temporarily, bars renewals for noncitizens without proof of permanent residency, bars licenses for asylees until permanent residency is granted, and requires a distinct marking on such licenses.

nh:HB 1826|relative to the cost of an op.title: relative to the cost of an opportunity for an adequate education.
nh:HB 1826|relative to the cost of an op.summary: Raises state adequate education aid starting July 2027, increasing the base amount per pupil from $4,100 to $4,438 and raising extra aid for students from low-income families, English learners, and special education students.

nh:HB 1798|relative to the coverage of d.title: relative to the coverage of diapers under the state Medicaid plan.
nh:HB 1798|relative to the coverage of d.summary: Directs the state health department to seek federal approval for Medicaid to cover 100 diapers a month for a child's first year, with a target start of May 2027, and appropriates $100,000 for the effort.

nh:HB 672|concur.title: Concur
nh:HB 672|concur.summary: Creates a category of off-grid electricity providers that generate and sell power without connecting to the regulated electric grid, exempting them from utility regulation unless they connect to the grid, use public rights-of-way, or cross state lines.

nh:HB 651|modifying the base cost and di.title: modifying the base cost and differential aid costs of an adequate education.
nh:HB 651|modifying the base cost and di.summary: Raises state adequate education aid, increasing the base amount per pupil from $4,100 to about $7,356 and raising extra aid for low-income, English learner, and special education students, and requires the cost of adequacy to be updated every two years.

nh:HB 374|relative to clarifying referen.title: relative to clarifying references under local tax cap and budget laws.
nh:HB 374|relative to clarifying referen.summary: Revises local tax cap and school budget cap laws, setting out an optional cap formula adjusted for inflation and population or school enrollment, updating ballot question wording, and letting towns and districts vote on a new cap while the existing cap stays if it fails.

nh:SB 504|relative to the practice of ph.title: relative to the practice of pharmacy and the dispensing of certain medications by pharmacists.
nh:SB 504|relative to the practice of ph.summary: Changes pharmacy rules, including letting supervised pharmacy technicians give vaccines to adults and letting prescribers dispense up to 30 days of oral cancer drugs, and lets state-authorized centers provide experimental treatments that have passed early trials but lack full federal approval.

nh:HB 1331|enabling the town of derry to.title: enabling the town of Derry to absorb the Derry cooperative school district.
nh:HB 1331|enabling the town of derry to.summary: Lets the Derry town council, by amending the town charter, make the Derry Cooperative School District a town department, giving the council control over how the school budget is prepared and adopted.

nh:HB 1710|relative to procedures relati.title: relative to procedures relating to child abduction.
nh:HB 1710|relative to procedures relati.summary: Adopts the Uniform Child Abduction Prevention Act, letting courts order measures such as travel limits, passport surrender, bonds, or supervised visits when there is a credible risk a child will be abducted, and issue emergency warrants to take custody of the child.

nh:HB 1570|relative to governmental budg.title: relative to governmental budget authority for agreements for law enforcement agencies to participate in federal immigration enforcement.
nh:HB 1570|relative to governmental budg.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to get approval from their local budget authority before entering 287(g) immigration enforcement agreements, requires quarterly reports to that authority, lets it end the agreements based on cost, and withholds all state funds from agencies that do not comply.

nh:HB 1121|defining the cost of an adequ.title: defining the cost of an adequate education.
nh:HB 1121|defining the cost of an adequ.summary: Defines in law the specific items that make up the cost of an adequate education, such as teachers, principals, counselors, instructional materials, technology, building upkeep, and transportation.

nh:HB 145|relative to background checks.title: relative to background checks for licensed dietitians and adopting the dietitian licensure compact.
nh:HB 145|relative to background checks.summary: Requires fingerprint-based criminal background checks for people seeking a first state dietitian license, paid by the applicant, and joins an interstate compact that lets licensed dietitians practice in other member states.

nh:HR 19|encouraging state colleges and.title: encouraging state colleges and universities to invite more conservative speakers to campus for the purpose of increasing diversity of viewpoints.
nh:HR 19|encouraging state colleges and.summary: Encourages New Hampshire colleges and universities to invite more conservative speakers, along with speakers from across the political spectrum, condemns political violence and intimidation, and states it does not direct curricula or require any invitation.

nh:HB 520|relative to authorizing hearin.title: relative to authorizing hearing officers of the department of education to issue subpoenas.
nh:HB 520|relative to authorizing hearin.summary: Lets state Department of Education hearing officers issue subpoenas for witnesses and records when investigating possible misconduct by certified educators and in related hearings, with deadlines for compliance and a process to challenge a subpoena.

nh:SB 62|relative to law enforcement par.title: relative to law enforcement participation in a federal immigration program.
nh:SB 62|relative to law enforcement par.summary: Bars state and local governments from blocking police agencies from joining federal immigration enforcement agreements or impeding cooperation with federal immigration law, lets the attorney general seek fines against violators, and lets county jails hold people on federal immigration detainers for up to 48 hours.

nh:HB 224|relative to rebates to ratepay.title: relative to rebates to ratepayers from the renewable energy fund.
nh:HB 224|relative to rebates to ratepay.summary: Requires money paid into the state renewable energy fund, after administrative costs and certain set-asides, to be rebated to all retail electric customers per kilowatt-hour instead of funding renewable energy programs.

nh:HB 679|relative to immunization requi.title: relative to immunization requirements.
nh:HB 679|relative to immunization requi.summary: Provides that state childhood immunization requirements cannot require any vaccine that has not been shown in clinical trials to prevent transmission of disease.

nh:HB 504|relative to the state energy p.title: relative to the state energy policy.
nh:HB 504|relative to the state energy p.summary: Rewrites the state energy policy to promote affordable, reliable, diverse, and secure energy, favoring market-based approaches, limiting government support for one technology over another, and calling for removal of regulatory barriers.

nh:HB 284|requiring tax impact statement.title: requiring tax impact statements on municipal warrant articles.
nh:HB 284|requiring tax impact statement.summary: Requires towns to show an estimated tax impact per $1,000 of property value on their budget and on warrant articles that affect taxes, with yearly estimates for multi-year articles and a total tax impact summary on the warrant and, where used, the official ballot.

nh:HB 361|prohibiting mandatory mask pol.title: prohibiting mandatory mask policies in schools.
nh:HB 361|prohibiting mandatory mask pol.summary: Bars school boards and public charter schools from requiring students or the public to wear face masks on school property, with exceptions for safety equipment, specific instructional needs, sports gear, and students' individual education or disability plans.

nh:HB 1811|repealing statutory immunizat.title: repealing statutory immunization requirements for children.
nh:HB 1811|repealing statutory immunizat.summary: Repeals state immunization requirements for children, including vaccination requirements for school and child care enrollment and related exemption and record rules, making state vaccine recommendations advisory only.

nh:HB 317|new title allowing a superviso.title: (New Title) allowing a supervisor of the checklist to verify a person's identity, with identification, if they personally know that person.
nh:HB 317|new title allowing a superviso.summary: Lets a moderator, clerk, supervisor of the checklist, or selectman who personally knows a voter without photo ID verify the voter's identity by completing a witnessed attestation form, with the supervisor deciding whether the person may vote.

nh:HB 726|relative to the state minimum.title: relative to the state minimum hourly rate.
nh:HB 726|relative to the state minimum.summary: Raises the state minimum wage in steps from $10 an hour in September 2025 to $15 in January 2028, and raises the base wage for tipped workers from 45 to 50 percent of the minimum wage.

nh:HB 570|relative to membership of the.title: relative to membership of the prescription drug affordability board and the definition of public payor for purposes of board administration.
nh:HB 570|relative to membership of the.summary: As amended by the House, repeals the state prescription drug affordability board, the law that governs it, its administrative fund, and the salary listing for its executive director, effective July 1, 2025.

nh:HB 1219|relative to immunization requ.title: relative to immunization requirements in foster family homes.
nh:HB 1219|relative to immunization requ.summary: Bars foster care rules from requiring children or adults living in a foster home to get vaccines beyond the state's general immunization requirements, whether in vaccine type, number of doses or exemptions.

nh:HB 155|new title relative to business.title: (New Title) relative to business enterprise tax returns and appropriating funds to the department of health and human services for licensed nursing facilities.
nh:HB 155|new title relative to business.summary: Raises the receipts and value thresholds for filing a business enterprise tax return from $250,000 to $400,000, appropriates $2.5 million for nursing facility per-diem rates, and cuts the business enterprise tax rate automatically after certain business tax revenue surpluses.

nh:HB 491|establishing a committee to st.title: establishing a committee to study alternative funding methods for public education and how to reduce its reliance on local real estate property taxes.
nh:HB 491|establishing a committee to st.summary: Creates a committee of five House members and four senators to study other ways to fund public education and how to reduce reliance on local property taxes, and to recommend changes to revenue sources.

nh:HB 1252|requiring the department of m.title: requiring the department of motor vehicles to only administer the skills test for commercial driver's licenses in English and prohibiting the support of an interpreter for the administration of the skills test for commercial driver's licenses.
nh:HB 1252|requiring the department of m.summary: As passed by the House, requires commercial driver's license tests in English only, without interpreters except under federal exemptions, and makes drivers licensed in the past five years who tested in another language or with an interpreter retest in English within 90 days or lose their license.

nh:HB 1664|directing the department of n.title: directing the department of natural and cultural resources to remove the Hannah Duston Memorial in Boscawen.
nh:HB 1664|directing the department of n.summary: Directs the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources to remove the Hannah Duston Memorial and its historic marker in Boscawen, allowing them to be destroyed or stored, and requires that any later display present them in an accurate and objective manner.

nh:HB 1245|relative to voluntary portabl.title: relative to voluntary portable benefits plans for independent contractors.
nh:HB 1245|relative to voluntary portabl.summary: Lets businesses that hire independent contractors voluntarily contribute to contractor-owned portable benefit accounts for insurance or retirement, including through opt-in withholding, and bars those contributions from being used to classify the worker as an employee.

nh:HB 1822|relative to reporting of civi.title: relative to reporting of civil immigration detentions by state, county, and local law enforcement and correctional facilities.
nh:HB 1822|relative to reporting of civi.summary: Requires state, county and local law enforcement agencies and correctional facilities that hold people for civil immigration violations to report every six months how many were held and for how long, with the attorney general compiling the reports.

nh:HB 1048|relative to repealing the pro.title: relative to repealing the prohibition on the possession or sale of blackjacks, slung shots, and metallic knuckles except by or to minors.
nh:HB 1048|relative to repealing the pro.summary: Repeals the general ban on possessing or selling blackjacks, slung shots and metal knuckles, keeping it a violation only for people under 18 to carry them or for anyone to sell or give them to minors, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 613|relative to enabling local pol.title: relative to enabling local political subdivisions to vote and set a reduced default budget option.
nh:HB 613|relative to enabling local pol.summary: Requires city and town clerks to post public notice 90 to 180 days before an election that accessible voting machines will not be available unless a registered voter asks in writing at least 60 days ahead to use one.

nh:HB 123|enabling municipalities to tax.title: enabling municipalities to tax standing wood and timber on land used for carbon sequestration.
nh:HB 123|enabling municipalities to tax.summary: Applies the 10 percent timber yield tax to land enrolled to generate carbon offset credits, taxing owners each year on the net value of credits sold, and requires those owners to register their projects and report credit tonnage to a state registry.

nh:HB 1708|relative to statewide educati.title: relative to statewide education property taxes and other tax revenues.
nh:HB 1708|relative to statewide educati.summary: Raises the business profits tax rate from 7.5% to 8.5%, sends a growing share of that tax to the education trust fund, cuts the statewide education property tax in steps to $273 million starting July 2028, and provides grants for towns that lose aid.

nh:HCR 9|urging the united states to rej.title: urging the United States to reject compliance with the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive.
nh:HCR 9|urging the united states to rej.summary: Urges the federal government to reject compliance with the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive and asks other state legislatures to join in that request.

nh:HB 1499|relative to additional ground.title: relative to additional grounds for eviction under the landlord and tenant statute.
nh:HB 1499|relative to additional ground.summary: Lets landlords evict tenants who used someone else's identification to get or keep a rental, or when a tenant or occupant has certain convictions, including illegal entry into the U.S., recent felonies or offenses requiring sex offender registration, unless disclosed before the lease began.

nh:SB 72|establishing a parents bill of.title: establishing a parents' bill of rights in education.
nh:SB 72|establishing a parents bill of.summary: Creates a parental bill of rights listing parents' rights over their children's schooling, health care and records, bars public schools from infringing those rights except to prevent abuse, requires schools to adopt parent involvement policies, and lets parents sue for damages and legal fees.

nh:HB 1323|relative to parental alienati.title: relative to parental alienation.
nh:HB 1323|relative to parental alienati.summary: Defines parental alienation in family law, requires courts to weigh evidence of alienation or abuse in custody, guardianship, child protection and termination cases, allows custody orders to be changed when alienation harms a child, and requires attorney fees in contempt cases.

nh:SB 287|requiring applicants for absen.title: requiring applicants for absentee ballots to present a copy of their photo identification with their application.
nh:SB 287|requiring applicants for absen.summary: Requires people applying for an absentee ballot to verify their identity before receiving it by including a copy of an approved photo ID, having the application notarized, or showing photo ID to the city or town clerk.

nh:HB 723|repealing the multi use energy.title: repealing the multi-use energy data platform.
nh:HB 723|repealing the multi use energy.summary: Repeals the state law that established an online multi-use energy data platform, including its requirements, certification and cost-recovery provisions.

nh:HB 1062|authorizing the secretary of.title: authorizing the secretary of state to conduct random audits of the citizenship qualification of registered voters.
nh:HB 1062|authorizing the secretary of.summary: Lets the secretary of state run random, statistically sound audits of the citizenship of voters who registered using a citizenship affidavit, refers possible noncitizens to the attorney general, limits data sharing with outside parties, and requires a public report of findings.

nh:HB 1675|establishing a commission to.title: establishing a commission to investigate the New Hampshire Coalition Against Sexual and Domestic Violence and requiring funding only be provided for the direct services materially benefitting survivors of sexual and domestic assault.
nh:HB 1675|establishing a commission to.summary: Creates a legislative commission with subpoena power to investigate the New Hampshire Coalition Against Sexual and Domestic Violence, requires annual state audits of the coalition, limits state funding to direct services for survivors, and removes the coalition from seven state boards.

nh:HB 366|relative to school building ai.title: relative to school building aid for eligible projects.
nh:HB 366|relative to school building ai.summary: Ends the rule ranking school building aid applications that went unfunded the prior year, or that address critical needs, ahead of newer applications, funding projects only as appropriations allow and letting unfunded projects reapply in the next budget cycle.

nh:SB 228|relative to the limitations on.title: relative to the limitations on community customer generators.
nh:SB 228|relative to the limitations on.summary: Expands net metering and community solar by raising the single-meter size limit from 100 to 500 kilowatts, tripling the yearly cap on low-to-moderate income community solar to 18 megawatts, and changing rules for group hosts and municipal hosts.

nh:HB 1705|establishing an employee assi.title: establishing an employee assistance program for small town and volunteer first responders and making an appropriation therefor.
nh:HB 1705|establishing an employee assi.summary: Creates a fund run by the health department to enroll volunteer first responders, and full-time responders from towns with five or fewer paid first responders, in the state employee assistance program, and appropriates $114,000 through June 2027.

nh:CACR 21|relating to voting eligibilit.title: relating to voting eligibility. Providing that only legal residents who are at least 18 years of age or older who reside in the place they claim as domicile shall be eligible voters.
nh:CACR 21|relating to voting eligibilit.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, giving the right to vote to inhabitants who are U.S. citizens 18 or older, in the place where they are domiciled; it would take effect only with two-thirds voter approval.

nh:HB 1061|establishing a commission to.title: establishing a commission to study alternatives to incarceration for nonviolent offenders who are primary caregivers.
nh:HB 1061|establishing a commission to.summary: Creates a commission of legislators, state officials and governor's appointees to study alternatives to incarceration, such as home confinement or community supervision, for nonviolent offenders who are primary caregivers, with a report due November 1, 2026.

nh:HCR 1|calling for policymakers locall.title: calling for policymakers locally and nationally to fully consider all relevant information and factors pertaining to climate change before pursuing courses of action that could adversely affect any economy or environment.
nh:HCR 1|calling for policymakers locall.summary: States the House's support for proper consideration of all relevant data and perspectives as climate policy is developed at every level throughout the United States.

nh:HB 682|relative to the office of offs.title: relative to the office of offshore wind industry, the offshore and port development commission, and the office of energy innovation.
nh:HB 682|relative to the office of offs.summary: Renames the state's offshore wind office the Office of Energy Innovation and removes its offshore wind duties, repeals the offshore wind and port development commission and workforce training committee, and drops offshore wind references from other energy laws.

nh:HB 487|relative to providing employee.title: relative to providing employees with advance notice of the work schedule.
nh:HB 487|relative to providing employee.summary: Requires employers with 15 or more workers to give hourly employees their work schedules at least seven days before each pay period and to notify them of changes as soon as possible, and bars retaliation; health care facilities are exempt.

nh:HB 342|concur.title: Concur
nh:HB 342|concur.summary: Lets property owners build without a variance for minimum lot size or lot coverage when the building conforms to zoning and to neighborhood density, and lets governing bodies of non-charter towns and village districts create C-PACER energy districts after a public hearing.

nh:HB 646|requiring school districts to.title: requiring school districts to establish an online application for participation in the free and reduced price meal program.
nh:HB 646|requiring school districts to.summary: Requires school districts to offer online as well as paper applications for free and reduced-price school meals, and appropriates about $206,000 for a state staff position and $1 million for application software.

nh:CACR 11|new title relating to sheriff.title: (New Title) relating to sheriffs. Providing that there shall be no age limitation for a person to hold the office of county sheriff.
nh:CACR 11|new title relating to sheriff.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, to go to voters in November 2026, removing the requirement that county sheriffs leave office at age 70, while keeping the age limit for judges.

nh:HB 609|relative to the general court.title: relative to the general court's authority over the sale, purchase, ownership, use, possession, transportation, licensing, permitting, taxation, and other matter pertaining to firearms, stun guns, Tasers, pepper spray devices, knives and other self-defense
nh:HB 609|relative to the general court.summary: Gives the legislature exclusive authority over regulating firearms, ammunition, stun guns, Tasers, pepper spray, knives and other self-defense tools, voids conflicting local and agency rules, and lets people harmed by violations sue in superior court.

nh:HB 1130|relative to judicial performa.title: relative to judicial performance evaluations.
nh:HB 1130|relative to judicial performa.summary: Requires the supreme court to evaluate every judge and judicial referee at least once every three years using surveys, self-evaluations and courtroom observations, publish the results, report yearly, and allows discipline after two straight unsatisfactory evaluations.

nh:HB 295|making school building aid pro.title: making school building aid program funds nonlapsing.
nh:HB 295|making school building aid pro.summary: Makes money appropriated for state school building aid, which helps districts and chartered public schools pay for construction, carry over instead of expiring at the end of the budget period.

nh:HB 1596|relative to the collection of.title: relative to the collection of certain health care program premiums; funding for the university system of New Hampshire; and raising the tobacco tax.
nh:HB 1596|relative to the collection of.summary: As introduced, raises the cigarette tax from $1.78 to $2.80 per pack starting July 1, 2026, appropriates $18 million a year to the University System of New Hampshire, and ends premiums for children's health insurance and Granite Advantage coverage.

nh:HB 548|relative to licensing requirem.title: relative to licensing requirements for health care facilities that operate on a membership-based business model.
nh:HB 548|relative to licensing requirem.summary: Exempts membership-based and direct-pay health care facilities, other than nursing homes, from the state moratorium on new licenses and beds, exempts such intermediate care and rehabilitation facilities from the duty to serve patients regardless of payer, and creates a patients' bill of rights for them.

nh:HB 235|relative to amending the educa.title: relative to amending the educator code of ethics and code of conduct to include responsibility to parents.
nh:HB 235|relative to amending the educa.summary: Amends the New Hampshire educator code of conduct so that the educator's listed responsibility to students also includes responsibility to parents, as parents are defined in existing school law.

nh:HB 131|requiring school boards to dev.title: requiring school boards to develop and enact policies regarding personal cell phone use in schools.
nh:HB 131|requiring school boards to dev.summary: As amended by the House, rewrites school antibullying rules: requires new written policies, parent notice within 48 hours, investigations begun within five school days, and expanded state reporting, and redefines negligence for bullying lawsuits as failing to use a reasonable person's care.

nh:HB 207|relative to repealing the proh.title: relative to repealing the prohibition on the possession or sale of blackjacks, slung shots, and metallic knuckles except by or to minors.
nh:HB 207|relative to repealing the proh.summary: As introduced, repeals the general ban on carrying or selling blackjacks, slung shots and metal knuckles, keeping it only for people under 18 and for selling or giving them to minors, starting January 1, 2026.

nh:HB 1775|relative to utility ownership.title: relative to utility ownership of natural gas and nuclear power generation facilities.
nh:HB 1775|relative to utility ownership.summary: Lets electric utilities own or invest in natural gas and nuclear generating units of up to 5 megawatts each, capped at 10 percent of their peak load, and seek to recover those costs in rates with regulators' approval.

nh:HB 502|relative to complete corporate.title: relative to complete corporate reporting for unitary businesses under the business profits tax and revenues from the state education property tax.
nh:HB 502|relative to complete corporate.summary: As introduced, replaces the 'water's edge' business profits tax method with combined reporting for all parts of a unitary business, sends statewide education property tax revenue, less a 3 percent municipal share, to the education trust fund, and revises low- and moderate-income homeowner tax relief.

nh:HB 323|requiring the presentation of.title: requiring the presentation of a government-issued photographic means of identification in order to vote.
nh:HB 323|requiring the presentation of.summary: Requires voters to show a driver's license, state ID card, military ID or U.S. passport to vote, removing student IDs from the accepted list; IDs may be expired up to five years, or any length for voters 65 and older.

nh:SB 520|relative to breast surgeries f.title: relative to breast surgeries for minors.
nh:SB 520|relative to breast surgeries f.summary: Adds an exception allowing doctors to perform breast reduction surgery on a minor who chooses it, in consultation with her primary care physician, mainly to relieve pain, posture problems or physical discomfort that limits activity.

nh:SB 218|relative to absentee ballot ou.title: relative to absentee ballot outer envelopes.
nh:SB 218|relative to absentee ballot ou.summary: Requires people registering to vote by absentee ballot to send copies of documents proving citizenship, age, domicile and identity, and treats in-person absentee ballots as verified only when the voter shows a qualifying photo ID.

nh:HB 564|relative to the adoption of sc.title: relative to the adoption of school administrative unit budgets.
nh:HB 564|relative to the adoption of sc.summary: Changes how school administrative unit budgets are adopted: voters in member districts vote on the budget by paper ballot, it passes by majority of all votes cast, the prior year's budget applies if it fails, and the alternative adoption procedure is repealed.

nh:HB 10|establishing the parental bill.title: establishing the parental bill of rights.
nh:HB 10|establishing the parental bill.summary: Creates a parental bill of rights covering their children's education, records, curriculum and opt-outs, bars schools from infringing those rights except to prevent abuse, requires school board policies and notices, and lets parents sue for damages.

nh:HB 314|prohibiting the use of federal.title: prohibiting the use of federal, state, or local funds for lobbying activities.
nh:HB 314|prohibiting the use of federal.summary: Bars recipients of state or local public funds from using them to lobby, letting towns and cities allow it by ballot vote, requires lobbying recipients to keep public funds physically separate, and lets towns pay Municipal Association dues only after voters approve such lobbying, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HCR 4|relative to rejecting all offsh.title: relative to rejecting all offshore wind energy projects in the waters off the coast of New Hampshire and the Gulf of Maine.
nh:HCR 4|relative to rejecting all offsh.summary: Declares that the legislature rejects all offshore wind projects off New Hampshire's coast and in the Gulf of Maine until questions about their effects are fully vetted and it approves them, and urges neighboring ocean states to do the same.

nh:HB 511|relative to cooperation with f.title: relative to cooperation with federal immigration authorities.
nh:HB 511|relative to cooperation with f.summary: Requires police and jails to honor federal immigration detainers for inmates when safe, bars state and local governments from adopting sanctuary policies that limit cooperation, and lets the attorney general sue to block such policies, starting January 1, 2026.

nh:HB 352|prohibiting possession of a fi.title: prohibiting possession of a firearm at a polling place.
nh:HB 352|prohibiting possession of a fi.summary: As introduced, makes it a class A misdemeanor to carry a firearm or other deadly weapon within 100 feet of a polling place during an election, with exceptions for police and unloaded firearms secured in vehicles, and lets affected voters vote absentee.

nh:HB 510|relative to establishing certa.title: relative to establishing certain due process rights for students, student organizations, and faculty members facing disciplinary actions by state institutions of higher learning.
nh:HB 510|relative to establishing certa.summary: Gives students, student groups and faculty at public colleges facing suspension, expulsion or firing rights to advance notice, a hearing, a presumption of innocence, cross-examination, a lawyer at their own expense and an appeal, starting July 1, 2026.

nh:HB 203|relative to coast guard approv.title: relative to coast guard approved personal flotation devices while on New Hampshire state waters.
nh:HB 203|relative to coast guard approv.summary: As introduced, requires people in canoes, kayaks or rowing sculls on state waters to wear a Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device at all times from November 15 through May 15, except during official competitions.

nh:HB 208|relative to certification requ.title: relative to certification requirements for school nurses.
nh:HB 208|relative to certification requ.summary: Lets school boards, on a superintendent's nomination, appoint any registered nurse licensed by the state board of nursing as a school nurse, ending the separate education department certification requirement.

nh:HB 442|relative to prohibiting paymen.title: relative to prohibiting payment of subminimum wages.
nh:HB 442|relative to prohibiting paymen.summary: As introduced, ends the lower base wage for tipped workers who earn more than $30 a month in tips, requiring employers to pay them at least the standard minimum wage.

nh:SB 84|relative to zoning procedures c.title: relative to zoning procedures concerning residential housing.
nh:SB 84|relative to zoning procedures c.summary: Bars towns from requiring single-family lots larger than 88,000 square feet on most single-family land, 44,000 with public water and 22,000 with public sewer unless the town shows those systems lack capacity, starting July 1, 2026.

nh:CACR 12|relating to voting on broad b.title: relating to voting on broad-based taxes. Providing that a supermajority vote of the general court shall be required to enact any broad-bases taxes.
nh:CACR 12|relating to voting on broad b.summary: As amended by the House, proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, barring the House from adopting any tax on wages or other personal income of individuals, while still allowing taxes on businesses.

nh:HB 600|enabling ranked choice voting.title: enabling ranked-choice voting for municipal elections.
nh:HB 600|enabling ranked choice voting.summary: As introduced, lets cities and towns adopt ranked-choice voting for some or all local offices by voter approval, sets ballot design and round-by-round counting rules, requires public release of tabulation data, and lets political parties use it in caucus nominations.

nh:HB 1642|relative to extreme risk prot.title: relative to extreme risk protection orders.
nh:HB 1642|relative to extreme risk prot.summary: As introduced, lets police, family or household members, or intimate partners seek extreme risk protection orders barring a person found to pose a significant and ongoing risk of causing bodily injury from having firearms or ammunition for up to 12 months, with possible extensions.

nh:HB 223|relative to licensing requirem.title: relative to licensing requirements for health care facilities that operate within 15 miles of a critical access hospital.
nh:HB 223|relative to licensing requirem.summary: As introduced, ends the requirement that ambulatory surgical centers, emergency and walk-in care centers, birthing centers, dialysis centers and similar facilities notify a critical access hospital before opening within 15 miles of it, keeping the notice rule only for new hospitals.

nh:HB 349|relative to the practice of op.title: relative to the practice of optometry and authorization to perform ophthalmic laser procedures.
nh:HB 349|relative to the practice of op.summary: Lets optometrists certified by the state optometry board perform three eye laser procedures (capsulotomy, trabeculoplasty and peripheral iridotomy) after approved training and a set number of supervised procedures, with outcome reporting and signed patient consent.

nh:HB 368|prohibiting smoking and e ciga.title: prohibiting smoking and e-cigarettes in motor vehicles when a passenger is under 16 years of age.
nh:HB 368|prohibiting smoking and e ciga.summary: As introduced, bans smoking tobacco or using e-cigarettes in a motor vehicle while a child under 16 is inside, with a $100 fine, enforceable only when police stop a driver for another suspected violation.

nh:SB 134|relative to work requirements.title: relative to work requirements under the state Medicaid program.
nh:SB 134|relative to work requirements.summary: Requires applicants and enrollees in the state's expanded Medicaid program who are subject to federal work requirements to prove compliance with documents, including for the month before applying, checked at least quarterly; those who don't comply within 30 days of notice lose coverage.

nh:HB 189|defining clean energy and the.title: defining "clean energy" and the department of energy's 10-year state energy strategy to include new technology small-scale nuclear energy, renewable energy, and fuel diversity; and, removing references to the energy efficiency and sustainable energy board
nh:HB 189|defining clean energy and the.summary: Defines "clean energy" as low-greenhouse-gas sources including nuclear and renewables, makes clean energy and fuel diversity part of the state's 10-year energy strategy, and drops the energy efficiency and sustainable energy board from the strategy's review.

nh:HB 88|establishing community property.title: establishing community property trusts.
nh:HB 88|establishing community property.summary: Lets married couples create New Hampshire community property trusts with an in-state trustee, treating trust assets as owned equally by both spouses and dividing them in half at a spouse's death or at divorce.

nh:SB 284|relative to the required maxim.title: relative to the required maximum number of residential parking spaces.
nh:SB 284|relative to the required maxim.summary: Bars cities and towns from requiring more than one residential parking space per unit, replacing current 1.5-space limits that apply only to small workforce housing units and multifamily developments of 10 or more units.

nh:HB 365|relative to proof of united st.title: relative to proof of United States citizenship for indigent voters.
nh:HB 365|relative to proof of united st.summary: Requires election officials, at a voter's request, to try to confirm citizenship through state and federal records when the voter lacks proof; if that fails, lets indigent voters get vouchers for birth certificates, with $50,000 to reimburse towns.

nh:HB 623|relative to prohibiting corpor.title: relative to prohibiting corporations from purchasing single-family homes for a certain amount of time.
nh:HB 623|relative to prohibiting corpor.summary: As introduced, bars corporations and other entities from buying single-family or multi-family homes until they have been on the market 90 days, with development exceptions, requires such buyers to register with the state, and lets courts declare unlawful purchases escheated to the municipality or county.

nh:HB 106|establishing a commission to d.title: establishing a commission to determine the monetary costs of climate damage to the state of New Hampshire and the best means of recouping such costs.
nh:HB 106|establishing a commission to d.summary: As introduced, creates a commission of legislators, state officials, and business and environmental representatives to estimate the financial cost of climate damage to New Hampshire and identify ways to recover those costs, reporting by November 1, 2026.

nh:HB 68|making best interest placements.title: making best interest placements within the same school district mandatory in the absence of a valid reason to deny the placement.
nh:HB 68|making best interest placements.summary: Requires school superintendents to approve parents' requests to move a student to another school within the same district unless the request fails legal requirements, to give written reasons for denials within 10 days, and treats requests as approved if procedures aren't followed.

nh:HB 380|relative to penalties for crim.title: relative to penalties for criminal violations of the therapeutic use of cannabis.
nh:HB 380|relative to penalties for crim.summary: Repeals the separate criminal penalty for medical cannabis patients or caregivers who sell cannabis to non-patients and removes language calling such diversion a class B felony; sellers would still lose their registry cards and may face other penalties for illegal cannabis sales.

nh:HB 226|relative to the use of drug ch.title: relative to the use of drug checking equipment.
nh:HB 226|relative to the use of drug ch.summary: Legalizes drug checking equipment such as fentanyl and xylazine test strips by removing it from the definition of drug paraphernalia, shields people who use or distribute it from arrest, and bars using test results as criminal evidence.

nh:HB 190|relative to therapeutic cannab.title: relative to therapeutic cannabis possession limits.
nh:HB 190|relative to therapeutic cannab.summary: As introduced, raises the amount of therapeutic cannabis a registered patient or caregiver may possess, and the amount a patient may obtain in a 10-day period, from 2 ounces to 4 ounces.

nh:HB 133|modifying the new resident dri.title: modifying the new resident drivers' license transfer requirements, specifying when the division of motor vehicles shall send violation notices, and appropriating funds to the division for technological upgrades required for legal compliance.
nh:HB 133|modifying the new resident dri.summary: As introduced, requires new residents with out-of-state driver's licenses to notify the state if they leave within 60 days or their license expires, directs motor vehicle officials to send notices to people over 30 days past deadlines, and appropriates $40,000 for computer upgrades.

nh:HB 56|requiring a background check an.title: requiring a background check and mandatory waiting period during certain firearm transfers.
nh:HB 56|requiring a background check an.summary: As introduced, requires most private gun sales and transfers to go through a licensed dealer who runs a background check, sets a 72-hour waiting period before delivery, and exempts transfers between immediate family members and certain temporary transfers.

nh:SB 460|relative to the offense of loi.title: relative to the offense of loitering or prowling.
nh:SB 460|relative to the offense of loi.summary: Makes it a class B felony for tier III registered offenders whose victims were minors to knowingly be within 500 feet of schools, child care centers, public parks, playgrounds, public pools or school bus stops without a legitimate purpose, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 526|establishing a climate change.title: establishing a climate change and damage division in the department of environmental services.
nh:HB 526|establishing a climate change.summary: As introduced, creates a climate change and damage division in the department of environmental services, led by a governor-appointed director, to handle climate adaptation planning, research and data analysis, public education, and grants.

nh:HB 1178|relative to permissible windo.title: relative to permissible window tinting on motor vehicles.
nh:HB 1178|relative to permissible windo.summary: As introduced, allows aftermarket tinting on a vehicle's front side windows if it lets through at least 35 percent of light, and lets the state issue medical permits for similar tinting on the windshield or front side windows.

nh:HB 1478|requiring the department of e.title: requiring the department of environmental services to revise the rules for proposed new landfills.
nh:HB 1478|requiring the department of e.summary: Bars permits for new landfills where groundwater could reach a drinking well or surface water within five years, sets a minimum 1,500-foot setback and soil standards, requires denial of nonconforming applications, and directs regulators to revise landfill rules.

nh:HB 60|relative to the termination of.title: relative to the termination of tenancy at the expiration of the tenancy or lease term.
nh:HB 60|relative to the termination of.summary: As introduced, allows landlords to evict tenants when a lease or tenancy of six months or longer expires, if the landlord gives at least 60 days' written notice that the lease will not be renewed.

nh:HB 1464|relative to discrimination ha.title: relative to discrimination, harassment, and violence based on political affiliation or opinion.
nh:HB 1464|relative to discrimination ha.summary: As introduced, adds political affiliation or opinion to state employment anti-discrimination law, creates crimes for harassment and economic interference based on political views, and lets courts lengthen sentences for crimes motivated by a victim's political affiliation.

nh:HB 96|requiring new hampshire builder.title: requiring New Hampshire builders to use the 2021 Energy Building codes or a similar code that achieves equivalent or greater energy savings.
nh:HB 96|requiring new hampshire builder.summary: As introduced, updates the state building code to adopt the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code in place of the 2018 edition, or a similar code achieving equal or greater energy savings, effective July 1, 2025.

nh:HB 1460|prohibiting the sale of locat.title: prohibiting the sale of location and other sensitive data regarding children.
nh:HB 1460|prohibiting the sale of locat.summary: As introduced, bars businesses covered by the state's consumer data privacy law from selling location data and other sensitive data about children, starting January 1, 2027.

nh:HB 444|relative to a tenant s right t.title: relative to a tenant's right to notification prior to the sale of a multi-family home.
nh:HB 444|relative to a tenant s right t.summary: As introduced, requires owners of certain multi-family rental properties to give each tenant 60 days' notice and a chance to make a purchase offer before accepting an offer to sell the property.

nh:HB 617|relative to the homestead righ.title: relative to the homestead right.
nh:HB 617|relative to the homestead righ.summary: Raises the homestead protection from creditors to $1,000,000, from $120,000 for a single person or $240,000 for a married couple, covers mobile homes, housing cooperatives and condominiums, and requires the home to have been a primary residence for the prior 12 months.

nh:HB 649|removing the requirement for p.title: removing the requirement for physical safety inspections and on-board diagnostic tests for passenger vehicles and eliminating funding for the motor vehicle air pollution abatement fund.
nh:HB 649|removing the requirement for p.summary: As introduced, ends required physical safety inspections and on-board diagnostic emissions tests for passenger vehicles and repeals the motor vehicle air pollution abatement fund, starting January 1, 2026.

nh:HB 1279|second new title relative to.title: (Second New Title) relative to the use of physical force in defense of a person.
nh:HB 1279|second new title relative to.summary: Allows a person to use deadly force inside their home or its yard against someone likely to use unlawful force while committing a felony against another person, not only against themselves, starting January 1, 2027.

us:S.J.Res. 141|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 141; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to the withdrawal of the rule relating to "Debt Collection Practices (Regulation F); Deceptive and Unfair Collection of Medical Debt".
us:S.J.Res. 141|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's May 2025 withdrawal of its 2024 rule on deceptive and unfair collection of medical debt, so the withdrawal has no legal force or effect.

us:H.Res. 566|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the Senate amendment to the bill (H.R. 1) to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14
us:H.Res. 566|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House rules for a vote on agreeing to the Senate's changes to the budget reconciliation bill, allowing one hour of debate split between the Budget and Ways and Means committees and waiving procedural objections.

us:H.Res. 580|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bills (H.R. 4016) Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026; (H.R. 3633) CLARITY Act; (H.R. 1919) Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act; and (S. 1582) GENIUS Act
us:H.Res. 580|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate and amendment rules for the 2026 Defense Department spending bill, a bill regulating digital-commodity markets, a bill restricting the Federal Reserve's use of a central bank digital currency, and a Senate bill regulating payment stablecoins.

us:H.Res. 211|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolution (H.J. Res. 25); providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1156); providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1968); and for other purposes.
us:H.Res. 211|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for overturning an IRS rule on broker reporting of digital-asset sales, extending the deadline to pursue pandemic unemployment fraud, and stopgap government funding through September 2025, and pauses the clock on forced votes to end the February 1, 2025 national emergency.

us:H.Res. 282|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolutions S.J.Res. 18 and S.J.Res 28; providing for consideration of the bills H.R. 1526 and H.R. 22; and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 282|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for overturning two consumer bureau rules, a bill limiting federal district courts' power to issue injunctions, and a proof-of-citizenship voter registration requirement. It also tables two pending resolutions and blocks efforts to force votes on one of them.

us:H.Res. 436|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1) to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14
us:H.Res. 436|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House rules for considering the budget reconciliation bill, treating as adopted a revised version with changes from the Rules Committee, allowing two hours of debate and waiving procedural objections.

us:H.Res. 707|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bills H.R. 4922, H.R. 5143, H.R. 5140, H.R. 5125, H.R. 1047, H.R. 3015, and H.R. 3062; and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 707|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for four District of Columbia crime, policing and courts bills and three energy bills, extends provisions of three earlier House rules through March 31, 2026, and through then suspends expedited procedures for ending the national emergency declared July 30, 2025.

us:H.Res. 294|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolutions S.J. Res. 18 and S.J. Res. 28; providing for consideration of the bills H.R. 1526 and H.R. 22; and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 294|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for measures overturning two consumer bureau rules, a bill limiting district courts' injunction powers, and a bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote. It also adopts a rule on announcing paired votes from members' written lists.

us:H.J.Res. 117|relating to a national e.title: Relating to a national emergency by the President on July 30, 2025
us:H.J.Res. 117|relating to a national e.summary: As introduced, ends the national emergency the President declared on July 30, 2025, in Executive Order 14323, using the National Emergencies Act process that lets Congress terminate national emergencies by joint resolution.

us:H.Res. 377|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 276) Gulf of America Act, and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 881) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
us:H.Res. 377|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for a bill renaming the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America" and a bill restricting Homeland Security funding for colleges with ties to Confucius Institutes.

us:S.J.Res. 82|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J.Res. 82; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Office of the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services relating to "Policy on Adhering to the Text of the Administrative Procedure Act".
us:S.J.Res. 82|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Health and Human Services Department's March 2025 policy on adhering to the text of the Administrative Procedure Act, which the Government Accountability Office found to be a rule, so it has no legal force or effect.

us:H.Res. 489|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bills H.R. 884, H.R. 2056, H.R. 2096, S. 331, and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 489|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for bills barring noncitizens from voting in District of Columbia elections, requiring the District to comply with federal immigration laws, restoring bargaining over D.C. police discipline, and changing how fentanyl-related substances are scheduled as controlled drugs.

us:H.Res. 879|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolutions S.J. Res. 80, H.J. Res. 130, and H.J. Res. 131; providing for consideration of the concurrent resolution H. Con. Res. 58; providing for consideration of the bills H.R. 1949, H.R. 3109, H.R. 5107, and H.R. 5214; and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 879|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for measures overturning three Bureau of Land Management land-use and oil-leasing decisions, a resolution denouncing socialism, bills on energy exports and petrochemicals, and two District of Columbia bills on policing and pretrial detention and cash bail.

us:H.Res. 722|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 5371) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026; providing for consideration of the resolution (H. Res. 719) honoring the life and legacy of Charles “Charlie” James Kirk; and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 722|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for a stopgap government funding bill for fiscal 2026 and a resolution honoring Charlie Kirk, and shortens to January 31, 2026, earlier pauses on forced votes, including votes to end certain national emergencies.

us:H.Res. 499|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4) the Rescissions Act; and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 499|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for a bill canceling federal funding the President proposed rescinding on June 3, 2025, turns off the Impoundment Control Act's expedited procedures for bills on that request, and directs corrections to the House-passed budget reconciliation bill's text.

us:H.Res. 242|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolutions H. J. Res 24 and H. J. Res. 75; and providing for consideration of the bill H.R. 1048, and for other purposes
us:H.Res. 242|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for measures overturning two Energy Department efficiency standards for commercial coolers, refrigerators and freezers, and a bill tightening disclosure of colleges' foreign gifts and barring contracts with certain foreign entities.

us:H.Res. 458|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bills (H.R. 2483) the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act; (H.R. 2931) the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act; (H.R. 2966) the American Entrepreneurs First Act; and (H.R. 2987) the CEASE Act
us:H.Res. 458|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate and amendment rules for a bill renewing opioid prevention and treatment programs and three Small Business Administration bills on relocating offices from sanctuary jurisdictions, requiring loan applicants' citizenship documents, and limiting the number of small business lending companies.

us:H.Res. 354|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the joint resolutions H.J. Res. 60, H.J. Res. 78, H.J. Res. 87, H.J. Res. 88, and H.J. Res. 89
us:H.Res. 354|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for measures overturning a Glen Canyon motor vehicle rule, an endangered listing for the San Francisco Bay-Delta longfin smelt, and three EPA approvals of California vehicle emission standards.

us:S.J.Res. 187|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 187; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Modification to the Start of the Submission Period for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Reporting and Recordkeeping Under TSCA 8(a)(7)".
us:S.J.Res. 187|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the EPA's April 2026 rule changing the start of the submission period for PFAS chemical reporting and recordkeeping under the Toxic Substances Control Act, so the rule has no legal force or effect.

us:S.J.Res. 103|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to proceed to S.J. Res. 103; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Veterans Affairs relating to "Reproductive Health Services".
us:S.J.Res. 103|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Veterans Affairs Department's December 31, 2025 rule titled "Reproductive Health Services," so the rule has no legal force or effect.

us:S.J.Res. 190|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J.Res. 190; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Executive Office for Immigration Review relating to "Appellate Procedures for the Board of Immigration Appeals".
us:S.J.Res. 190|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns a February 2026 Justice Department rule that makes the Board of Immigration Appeals' review of immigration judges' decisions on the merits discretionary, sets new briefing deadlines and streamlines other appeal procedures, so the rule has no legal effect.

us:H.Res. 53|providing for consideration.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 471) the Fix Our Forests Act; and providing for consideration of the bill (S. 5) the Laken Riley Act
us:H.Res. 53|providing for consideration.summary: Sets House debate rules for a bill speeding environmental review of forest management to reduce wildfire risk, and for a bill requiring federal detention of immigrants charged with theft, limiting debate and amendments.

us:H.Res. 530|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bills H.R. 3944, H.R. 275, H.R. 875, and providing for consideration of the resolution H.Res. 516
us:H.Res. 530|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for the 2026 military construction and veterans affairs spending bill, bills on monthly reports of special interest border encounters and deporting immigrants for drunk driving, and a resolution condemning the June 2025 Los Angeles riots.

us:H.Res. 122|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 77) the Midnight Rules Relief Act
us:H.Res. 122|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for a bill letting Congress overturn multiple late-term "midnight" regulations from an outgoing administration in a single resolution, allowing one hour of debate.

us:H.Res. 405|providing for consideratio.title: Providing for consideration of the bills (H.R. 2240) Improving Law Enforcement Officer Safety and Wellness Through Data Act, (H.R. 2243) LEOSA Reform Act, and (H.R. 2255) Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act
us:H.Res. 405|providing for consideratio.summary: Sets House debate rules for three bills: one requiring reports on violent attacks against police officers, one changing concealed-carry rules for law enforcement officers, and one letting federal officers buy their retired service weapons.

us:S.J.Res. 197|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J. Res. 197; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services of the Department of Health and Human Services relating to "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, HHS Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters for 2027; and Basic Health Program".
us:S.J.Res. 197|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the federal health agency's 2027 rule setting payment parameters and standards for Affordable Care Act marketplace plans, including insurer user fees, broker rules, hardship exemptions and catastrophic-plan options, so the rule has no legal effect.

us:S.J.Res. 83|motion to discharge s j r.title: Motion to Discharge S. J. Res. 83 from the Committee on Foreign Relations; A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities that have not been authorized by Congress.
us:S.J.Res. 83|motion to discharge s j r.summary: As introduced, directs the President to end the use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities against groups designated as terrorist organizations on or after February 20, 2025, states where they operate, or drug-trafficking organizations, unless Congress declares war or specifically authorizes force.

us:S.J.Res. 99|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J.Res. 99; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services relating to "Removal of the Automatic Extension of Employment Authorization Documents".
us:S.J.Res. 99|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns an October 2025 immigration agency rule that ended the automatic extension of work permits for certain immigrants who had filed timely renewal applications, so the rule has no legal effect.

us:S.J.Res. 132|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 132; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to the withdrawal of the rule relating to "Examinations for Risks to Active-Duty Servicemembers and Their Covered Dependents".
us:S.J.Res. 132|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's 2025 withdrawal of its 2021 rule explaining its authority to examine lenders for violations of the Military Lending Act affecting active-duty service members and their families.

us:S.Res. 852|motion to discharge s res.title: Motion to Discharge S. Res. 852; A resolution requesting information on Israel's human rights practices pursuant to section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.
us:S.Res. 852|motion to discharge s res.summary: As introduced, requests that the Secretary of State give Congress, within 30 days, a statement on Israel's human rights practices, including information on alleged killings of U.S. citizens by Israeli forces or settlers since 2022, Americans held in Israeli prisons and detained Palestinian children.

us:S.J.Res. 95|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 95; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Interim Guidance Simplifying Application of the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax to Partnerships".
us:S.J.Res. 95|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns IRS interim guidance that simplifies how the corporate alternative minimum tax applies to partnerships, so the guidance has no legal effect.

us:S.Res. 532|motion to invoke cloture s.title: Motion to Invoke Cloture: S.Res. 532; An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
us:S.Res. 532|motion to invoke cloture s.summary: Allows the Senate to consider 97 pending executive-branch nominations, including assistant secretaries, U.S. attorneys and ambassadors, together as a single group instead of one at a time.

us:S.J.Res. 199|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J. Res. 199; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Health and Human Services relating to "Restoring Flexibility in the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF)".
us:S.J.Res. 199|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns a Department of Health and Human Services rule on the Child Care and Development Fund, titled "Restoring Flexibility in the Child Care and Development Fund" and published May 12, 2026, so that the rule has no force or effect.

us:S.Res. 195|motion to discharge s res.title: Motion to Discharge S. Res. 195; A resolution requesting information on El Salvador's human rights practices pursuant to section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.
us:S.Res. 195|motion to discharge s res.summary: Requests that the Secretary of State give two congressional foreign affairs committees, within 30 days, a report on El Salvador's human rights practices, including alleged torture, forced disappearances, denial of due process, conditions at the CECOT prison, and detained U.S. citizens and residents.

us:S.J.Res. 130|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 130; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to withdrawal of the rule relating to "Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2024-05: Improper Overdraft Opt-In Practices".
us:S.J.Res. 130|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's May 2025 withdrawal of its 2024 guidance on improper overdraft opt-in practices, so that the withdrawal has no legal force or effect.

us:S.J.Res. 107|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J. Res. 107; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Beginning of Construction Requirements for Purposes of the Termination of Clean Electricity Production Credits and Clean Electricity Investment Credits for Applicable Wind and Solar Facilities".
us:S.J.Res. 107|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns an IRS notice setting rules for when wind and solar projects count as having begun construction for purposes of the ending of clean electricity production and investment tax credits, so the notice has no legal force or effect.

us:S.J.Res. 139|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 139; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Air Plan Disapproval; Colorado; Regional Haze Plan for the Second Implementation Period".
us:S.J.Res. 139|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Environmental Protection Agency's January 2026 rule disapproving Colorado's regional haze plan for the second implementation period, so the disapproval has no legal force or effect.

us:S.Res. 616|motion to discharge s res.title: Motion to Discharge: S.Res. 616 from the Committee on Foreign Relations; A resolution requesting information on Honduras's human rights practices pursuant to section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.
us:S.Res. 616|motion to discharge s res.summary: As introduced, requests that the Secretary of State give Congress, within 30 days, a statement on Honduras's human rights practices, including alleged drug-trafficking ties, corruption and abuses under former President Juan Orlando Hernandez, and whether U.S. security assistance supported drug trafficking.

us:S.J.Res. 188|motion to proceed s j re.title: Motion to Proceed: S.J. Res. 188; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units: Final Repeal".
us:S.J.Res. 188|motion to proceed s j re.summary: Overturns the EPA's February 2026 rule repealing parts of its 2024 update to mercury and air toxics standards for coal- and oil-fired power plants, including a stricter particulate limit for existing coal plants, so the repeal has no force or effect.

us:S.Res. 412|motion to invoke cloture e.title: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Executive Calendar No. 2, S.Res. 412; An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
us:S.Res. 412|motion to invoke cloture e.summary: Limits further debate on a Senate resolution that lets the Senate consider certain nominations on its executive calendar together as a group rather than one at a time.

us:S.J.Res. 196|motion to proceed to s j.title: Motion to Proceed to S.J.Res. 196; A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Education relating to "Reimagining and Improving Student Education-Federal Student Loan Program Final Regulations".
us:S.J.Res. 196|motion to proceed to s j.summary: Overturns the Education Department's May 2026 federal student loan regulations implementing 2025 law changes, including new borrowing limits for graduate students and parents, the phase-out of Grad PLUS loans and new repayment plans, so the rule has no force or effect.

us:S.Res. 520|motion to invoke cloture s.title: Motion to Invoke Cloture: S. Res. 520; An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
us:S.Res. 520|motion to invoke cloture s.summary: Makes it in order for the Senate to move to proceed to considering 88 specific nominations on its Executive Calendar en bloc, as a single group, rather than one at a time.

nv:SB2|revises provisions relating to co.title: Revises provisions relating to collective bargaining. (BDR 23-417)
nv:SB2|revises provisions relating to co.summary: Removes the open-meeting law exemption for certain public-sector collective bargaining proceedings: negotiations between unions or employees and local governments or the state executive branch, mediator meetings, and fact-finder or arbitrator proceedings.

pa:HB 853|an act amending the act of may.title: An Act amending the act of May 25, 1945 (P.L.1050, No.394), known as the Local Tax Collection Law, further providing for notices of taxes; providing for removal of deceased spouse; further providing for installment payment of taxes; and providing for imposition of fees for collection of delinquent per capita, poll and occupation taxes.
pa:HB 853|an act amending the act of may.summary: Lets tax collectors, taxing districts or designated private collectors charge a reasonable, publicly posted fee for collecting overdue per capita, poll and occupation taxes, for up to five years; Senate amendments removed House-passed provisions on tax notices, deceased spouses' names and installment payments.

pa:HB 852|an act amending the act of dec.title:
An Act amending the act of December 31, 1965 (P.L.1257, No.511), known as The Local Tax Enabling Act, in collection of delinquent taxes, further providing for collection of delinquent per capita, occupation, occupational 
 privilege, emergency and municipal services, local services and income taxes from employers, etc., for notice and for costs of collection of delinquent per capita, occupation, occupational privilege, emergency and municipal services, local services and income taxes.
pa:HB 852|an act amending the act of dec.summary: Lets local tax officials recover publicly posted costs of collecting overdue local taxes for up to five years, caps wage withholding for back taxes at 10% of pay, and requires 15 days' notice and pursuing the taxpayer first before taking a spouse's wages.

pa:HB 2380|an act amending title 66 publ.title: An Act amending Title 66 (Public Utilities) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in restructuring of electric utility industry, providing for energy storage procurement.
pa:HB 2380|an act amending title 66 publ.summary: Requires electric utilities with at least 500,000 customers to procure state-assigned shares of 3,500 megawatts of energy storage through competitive bidding by July 31, 2035, bars them from owning the storage, lets them recover costs from customers, and has state regulators review contracts for cost and benefit.

pa:HB 2154|an act amending title 61 pris.title: An Act amending Title 61 (Prisons and Parole) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, establishing the Prison Industry Enhancement Authority; providing for employment of incarcerated individuals by private industry and for subcontracts with correctional agencies; establishing guidelines for incarcerated individual compensation; and providing for location of private sector prison industry.
pa:HB 2154|an act amending title 61 pris.summary: Creates a Prison Industry Enhancement Authority and lets state and county prisons contract with private businesses to employ incarcerated people who volunteer, with deductions for taxes, victim compensation, room and board and family support capped at 70% of wages; workers cannot receive unemployment benefits.

pa:HB 2771|an act amending title 75 vehi.title: An Act amending Title 75 (Vehicles) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, providing for automated license plate reader systems; and imposing penalties.
pa:HB 2771|an act amending title 75 vehi.summary: As amended by the House Oct. 7, 2026 (PN 4026), bars government and private entities from using automated license plate readers except for listed purposes such as felony and missing-person investigations, stolen, uninsured or unregistered vehicles, parking and secured areas; requires most data be deleted within 72 hours; sets penalties.

pa:SB 806|an act providing for unfair me.title: An Act providing for unfair methods of competition and for enforcement and penalties.
pa:SB 806|an act providing for unfair me.summary: Bars advertisers from using AI-generated or AI-altered content that misleads consumers about a product or service's nature, origin or authenticity without a clear AI disclosure, exempting obvious fiction, parody and text-only content, with civil fines up to $3,000 enforced by the attorney general or district attorneys.

pa:SB 115|an act amending the act of jun.title: An Act amending the act of June 13, 1967 (P.L.31, No.21), known as the Human Services Code, in general powers and duties of the Department of Public Welfare, further providing for personal care home and assisted living residence administrators; providing for liability for false claims, for adoption of Congressional intent of the Federal False Claims Act, for damages, costs and civil penalties, for powers of Attorney General, for qui tam actions and for civil investigative demands; and establishing the Fraud Prevention and Recovery Account.
pa:SB 115|an act amending the act of jun.summary: Creates a state false claims law making people who knowingly defraud the state liable for triple damages plus civil penalties, enforced by the attorney general and whistleblower suits, and lets personal care home aides without a diploma qualify by passing reading and math tests.

pa:HB 2595|an act amending the act of no.title: An Act amending the act of November 30, 2004 (P.L.1672, No.213), known as the Alternative Energy Portfolio Standards Act, providing for interconnection reviews.
