pa:HB 2595|an act amending the act of no.summary: Requires electric utilities to give energy project developers the results of grid connection studies within 90 days of a study agreement and to sign agreements with timetables and cost estimates for needed grid upgrades, with missed deadlines taken to state utility regulators.

pa:HB 2702|an act amending title 35 heal.title: An Act amending Title 35 (Health and Safety) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in health care cost containment, repealing provisions relating to expiration.
pa:HB 2702|an act amending title 35 heal.summary: Repeals the scheduled expiration of the state's health care cost containment law, which was set to end 10 years after it took effect in April 2020, so the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council continues.

pa:HB 2006|an act providing for safety r.title: An Act providing for safety regarding artificial intelligence in companionship applications; and imposing a penalty.
pa:HB 2006|an act providing for safety r.summary: Sets safety rules for AI companion apps that simulate ongoing personal relationships, including disclosure requirements, safeguards for minors and annual reports on crisis referrals, enforced by the attorney general with civil penalties up to $100,000 per day for each violation.

pa:HB 2033|an act amending title 3 agric.title: An Act amending Title 3 (Agriculture) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in food protection, providing for correctional institutions; imposing duties on the Department of Agriculture; and promulgating regulations.
pa:HB 2033|an act amending title 3 agric.summary: Applies state food safety rules to state and county prisons and jails, lets the Department of Agriculture inspect their kitchens and food service areas and post the reports online, and subjects the facilities to state safe drinking water requirements.

pa:HB 71|an act amending title 75 vehicl.title: An Act amending Title 75 (Vehicles) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in size, weight and load, further providing for safety requirements for towed vehicles.
pa:HB 71|an act amending title 75 vehicl.summary: Lets drivers use safety cables, not only safety chains, when a towed vehicle is connected by a ball-and-socket hitch or pintle hook without a locking device.

pa:SB 730|an act amending title 20 deced.title: An Act amending Title 20 (Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in health care, further providing for applicability, for definitions, for criminal penalties, for emergency medical services, for definitions, for orders, bracelets and necklaces, for revocation, for absence of order, bracelet or necklace and for emergency medical services, repealing provisions relating to advisory committee and providing for discontinuance and for Pennsylvania orders for life-sustaining treatment.
pa:SB 730|an act amending title 20 deced.summary: Creates a standard state form for orders for life-sustaining treatment, for patients a physician finds have a life-limiting, irreversible condition, replacing out-of-hospital do-not-resuscitate orders; bars insurers and providers from requiring it or treating patients differently, and shields providers acting in good faith.

pa:HB 2391|an act amending the act of ja.title: An Act amending the act of January 30, 1974 (P.L.13, No.6), referred to as the Loan Interest and Protection Law, in protective provisions, further providing for prepayment penalty prohibited.
pa:HB 2391|an act amending the act of ja.summary: Lets borrowers pay off a residential mortgage taken for personal, family or household use early at any time without a prepayment penalty or other early-payment fee.

me:LD 210|an act making unified appropri.title: An Act Making Unified Appropriations and Allocations from the General Fund and Other Funds for the Expenditures of State Government and Changing Certain Provisions of the Law Necessary to the Proper Operations of State Government for the Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2025, June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2027
me:LD 210|an act making unified appropri.summary: Sets Maine's state budget for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 and adjusts fiscal 2025 spending, and changes related laws, including raising the cigarette tax from $2 to $3.50 per pack starting January 5, 2026, with a matching increase on other tobacco products.

me:LD 209|an act to make supplemental ap.title: An Act to Make Supplemental Appropriations and Allocations from the General Fund and Other Funds for the Expenditures of State Government and to Change Certain Provisions of the Law Necessary to the Proper Operations of State Government for the Fiscal Year Ending June 30, 2025
me:LD 209|an act to make supplemental ap.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations and allocations for state government for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2025, and changes related laws, including carrying unspent funds into the next fiscal year and updating state tax references to the federal tax code.

me:LD 609|an act making certain appropri.title: An Act Making Certain Appropriations and Allocations and Changing Certain Provisions of Law Necessary to the Proper Operations of State Government
me:LD 609|an act making certain appropri.summary: Sets baseline state government appropriations for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, adds fiscal 2025 funding, sets K-12 school funding amounts for 2025-26, and moves about $42.4 million in federal recovery-fund interest earnings into the General Fund.

me:LD 1849|an act to establish a minimum.title: An Act to Establish a Minimum Age at Which a Juvenile May Be Adjudicated
me:LD 1849|an act to establish a minimum.summary: Sets 11 as the minimum age at which a child can be charged with a juvenile crime, except for murder and manslaughter, and gives juvenile courts jurisdiction over any crime, including hunting, fishing and motor vehicle offenses, committed by a juvenile.

me:LD 1189|an act to prohibit arrest and.title: An Act to Prohibit Arrest and Detention for Civil Violations and Require an Attorney for the State to Determine Whether to Charge a Class E Offense as a Civil Violation
me:LD 1189|an act to prohibit arrest and.summary: Lets prosecutors charge certain Class E crimes as civil violations with a fine of up to $1,000, considering the conduct, its impact on the victim and prior record; excludes election-law crimes and those carrying probation or mandatory license suspension. Takes effect January 1, 2026.

me:LD 2098|an act to update certain high.title: An Act to Update Certain Higher Education Statutes
me:LD 2098|an act to update certain high.summary: Repeals state laws on correspondence schools, requires colleges to pay application fees covering the Department of Education's processing costs, lets the State Board of Education recommend recently approved institutions for degree-granting authority without further review, and broadens College of the Atlantic's degree-granting authority.

me:SP 101|joint order to amend joint rul.title: Joint Order, to Amend Joint Rule 215 to Clarify the Language of That Rule
me:SP 101|joint order to amend joint rul.summary: Amends the Legislature's joint rules to reword the existing requirement that a measure calling a U.S. constitutional convention pass by a two-thirds vote of members present in each chamber, so that it refers to conventions called under Article V.

me:SP 98|joint order to amend joint rule.title: Joint Order, to Amend Joint Rule 208 to Eliminate Most Concept Drafts
me:SP 98|joint order to amend joint rule.summary: Amends the Legislature's joint rules to end bills drafted in short "concept" form at a sponsor's request, while still requiring concept drafts for the governor's budget bills and adding them for proposals to adopt uniform or model acts.

me:LD 1673|resolve to establish a pilot.title: Resolve, to Establish a Pilot Project to Facilitate the Inclusion of Economic Impact Statements in the Legislative Process
me:LD 1673|resolve to establish a pilot.summary: Directs the Legislative Council to run a pilot project producing economic impact statements for three 2026 bills on labor, employment, taxes or the economy, seek proposals from outside entities by December 1, 2025, and report findings by December 15, 2026.

me:LD 1763|an act to regulate nonwater d.title: An Act to Regulate Nonwater-dependent Floating Structures on Maine's Waters
me:LD 1763|an act to regulate nonwater d.summary: Bans placing or using floating structures for uses that need not be on the water, such as floating homes, on Maine's internal waters, with exceptions including swim floats, ice fishing shacks and aquaculture; lets some pre-2025 structures continue under state leases; sets penalties; requires a 2026 report.

me:LD 2155|an act to exempt for licenses.title: An Act to Exempt, for Licenses Issued Prior to December 21, 2025, Persons Holding a Majority Ownership Interest from the Restriction on the Number of Manufacturing Facility Licenses and On-premises Retail Licenses
me:LD 2155|an act to exempt for licenses.summary: Permanently bars the state from suspending, revoking or refusing to renew alcohol manufacturing and on-premises retail licenses issued before December 21, 2025 solely because the majority owner holds more retail licenses than allowed per manufacturing facility; those licenses cannot be sold or transferred.

me:LD 2182|an act to implement a recomme.title: An Act to Implement a Recommendation of the Commission to Recommend Methods for Preventing Deed Fraud in the State
me:LD 2182|an act to implement a recomme.summary: As introduced, requires real estate brokers starting January 1, 2027, to verify a seller's identity before taking on the seller as a client, and requires settlement agents to verify the seller's identity before closing sales of vacant land or homes.

ma:S3143|an act to save people money rep.title: An Act to save people money, repair the climate and grow the economy
ma:S3143|an act to save people money rep.summary: As reported to the Senate, replaces utility efficiency programs with one statewide efficiency and building-decarbonization plan, at least 20% for low-income households; lets cities and towns bar competitive suppliers from residential electricity contracts; requires low- and moderate-income utility discounts; and allows bonds to refinance utility costs.

nc:HB 305|guilford county sales tax dist.title: Guilford County Sales Tax Distribution Modifications.
nc:HB 305|guilford county sales tax dist.summary: Requires Guilford County to share local sales tax revenue with towns that levy no property tax, and directs any voter-approved quarter-cent county sales tax to fire and rescue equipment, Guilford Technical Community College, teacher pay supplements and certain towns.

nc:HB 636|promoting wholesome content fo.title: Promoting Wholesome Content for Students.
nc:HB 636|promoting wholesome content fo.summary: Requires public schools to adopt library policies under which community advisory committees review books for quality and age-appropriateness, requires removal of material that fails the criteria, including depictions of sexual activity, and lets parents or county residents sue over violations.

nc:HB 926|regulatory reform act of 2025.title: Regulatory Reform Act of 2025.
nc:HB 926|regulatory reform act of 2025.summary: Changes dozens of state regulations, including barring local street paving standards stricter than the state's, limiting local rules on displaying American flags on private property, easing wastewater and stormwater permitting, and expanding where restaurants and food businesses may use liquor for cooking.

nc:HB 442|flounder red snapper seasons a.title: Flounder/Red Snapper Seasons and Shrimp Trawl.
nc:HB 442|flounder red snapper seasons a.summary: Directs state fisheries regulators to allow a recreational southern flounder season of at least six weeks, set a 750,000-pound commercial flounder quota and a year-round red snapper season, and bans shrimp trawling in inshore waters and within a half mile of the ocean shore.

nc:HB 920|virtual currency kiosk consume.title: Virtual Currency Kiosk Consumer Prot. Act.
nc:HB 920|virtual currency kiosk consume.summary: Requires cryptocurrency kiosk operators to be licensed and supervised by the state banking commissioner, caps daily transactions at $2,000 for new and $5,000 for existing customers, limits fees to 12%, and requires fraud warnings and refunds for some scam victims.

nc:SB 254|charter school changes.title: Charter School Changes.
nc:SB 254|charter school changes.summary: Shifts charter school oversight from the State Board of Education and state superintendent to the Charter Schools Review Board, lets charter schools move within 10 miles without approval, and lets large remote academies seek their own charters.

nc:HR 563|house permanent rules.title: House Permanent Rules.
nc:HR 563|house permanent rules.summary: Adopts the House's permanent rules for the 2025–2026 session, setting procedures for debate, motions, voting, committees and bill handling, and allows a veto override vote on the day a vetoed bill arrives or any day it is on the House calendar.

nc:HB 171|equality in state agencies pro.title: Equality in State Agencies/Prohibition on DEI.
nc:HB 171|equality in state agencies pro.summary: Bars state agencies from operating workplace diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and bars state agencies and local governments from spending public money on such programs or accepting federal funds that require them, with penalties under state budget laws.

nc:SB 153|north carolina border protecti.title: North Carolina Border Protection Act.
nc:SB 153|north carolina border protecti.summary: Requires state public safety, prison, Highway Patrol and SBI leaders to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement, ends state benefits and housing aid for noncitizens lacking legal status where federal law allows, and waives tort immunity for cities and counties with sanctuary ordinances when an unauthorized immigrant commits a crime there.

nc:SB 429|2025 public safety act.title: 2025 Public Safety Act.
nc:SB 429|2025 public safety act.summary: Makes many criminal law changes, including raising penalties for fentanyl and carfentanil offenses, creating crimes for exposing a child to controlled substances and habitual domestic violence, limiting post-conviction relief motions, and keeping 911 calls by minors out of public records.

nc:HB 402|nc regulations from the execut.title: NC Regulations from the Executive in Need of Scrutiny (REINS) Act.
nc:HB 402|nc regulations from the execut.summary: Requires state agency rules with an economic impact of at least $1 million over 12 months to go before the legislature, where any lawmaker can file a bill to block them, and requires judges to use independent judgment in agency cases.

nc:HB 415|modify math and social studies.title: Modify Math and Social Studies Graduation Requirements.
nc:HB 415|modify math and social studies.summary: Removes the Math III high school graduation requirement, counts computer science as a math course, adds a U.S. history test for graduation, and requires the UNC system to match its minimum math admission requirements to the graduation requirements.

nc:HB 606|civil procedure amendment.title: Civil Procedure Amendment.
nc:HB 606|civil procedure amendment.summary: Extends the deadline to sue over gender transition care to 10 years after the patient turns 18, removes the cap on noneconomic damages for such claims, and bars state funds for gender transition surgery or hormones for prisoners.

nc:HB 74|house budget technical correcti.title: House Budget Technical Corrections.
nc:HB 74|house budget technical correcti.summary: Makes technical and other changes to the 2023 state budget and other laws, including extending deadlines for certain local grants, moving project money among local governments, and broadening uses of funds for megasite and select-site economic development programs.

nc:SB 214|various local provisions vii.title: Various Local Provisions VII.
nc:SB 214|various local provisions vii.summary: Removes certain land from the town limits of Southport, Yadkinville and Kannapolis, ends Sunset Beach's land-use authority outside its limits, changes Yadkinville's, and lifts the cap on noncontiguous annexations for East Spencer.

nc:HB 125|continuing budget operations.title: Continuing Budget Operations.
nc:HB 125|continuing budget operations.summary: Funds state agencies for 2025–27 at base budget levels in the absence of a full new budget and makes targeted changes, including $600 million in added recurring Medicaid funding and $142 million for 2024 agricultural disaster crop losses.

nc:SB 416|personal privacy protection ac.title: Personal Privacy Protection Act.
nc:SB 416|personal privacy protection ac.summary: Bars public agencies from requiring or releasing information identifying members, donors or volunteers of nonprofit groups, with lawsuits for at least $2,500 per violation and criminal penalties for knowing violations.

nc:SB 442|parents protection act.title: Parents Protection Act.
nc:SB 442|parents protection act.summary: Provides that parents or caregivers who raise or refer to a child consistent with the child's biological sex cannot face abuse or neglect findings on that basis alone, and bars adoption agencies from rejecting parents who do not support a child's gender transition.

nc:HB 301|social media and ai safety.title: Social Media and AI Safety.
nc:HB 301|social media and ai safety.summary: Bars children under 14 from accounts on social media platforms with addictive features, requires parental consent for 14- and 15-year-olds and age verification, allows $50,000 civil penalties, and requires artificial intelligence instruction standards and policies in schools.

nc:SB 488|clarify disposition placement.title: Clarify Disposition Placement Analysis/Interest on Lawyers' Trust Accounts.
nc:SB 488|clarify disposition placement.summary: Requires judges to make written findings when deciding foster care placements, lets them compare all placement options when weighing a relative placement, and bars the lawyers' trust account interest program from making grants from July 2025 through June 2026.

nc:HB 1126|2026 dst admin technical clar.title: 2026 DST Admin/Technical/Clarifying Changes.-AB
nc:HB 1126|2026 dst admin technical clar.summary: Makes technical and administrative changes to state and local government retirement systems, lets the State Treasurer hire private counsel for them, extends State Health Plan maternity benefits to dependents, and updates unclaimed property and government finance laws.

nc:HB 48|increase unemployment insurance.title: Increase Unemployment Insurance Maximum Benefit/2025 Unemployment Insuranc
nc:HB 48|increase unemployment insurance.summary: Raises the maximum weekly unemployment benefit from $350 to $450 for claims filed on or after March 2, 2025, ratifies the governor's Hurricane Helene benefit order, and gives employers a credit equal to their late-2024 unemployment tax payment.

nc:HB 307|iryna s law.title: Iryna's Law.
nc:HB 307|iryna s law.summary: Tightens pretrial release rules for people charged with violent offenses or with significant criminal histories, requires mental health evaluations for some defendants before release, and makes other changes to criminal and court procedures.

nc:SB 391|dot omnibus.title: DOT Omnibus.
nc:SB 391|dot omnibus.summary: Makes many transportation changes, including letting local governments use speed cameras in school zones, barring heavy trucks from the far-left lane of highways with six or more lanes, ending window-tint inspections, and requiring background checks for contracted student drivers.

nc:HB 562|healthcare investment act.title: Healthcare Investment Act.
nc:HB 562|healthcare investment act.summary: Adds $690 million a year in recurring state funds for projected Medicaid costs plus money for Medicaid administration, funds UNC Children's Hospital and NC Care clinics, and cuts money set aside for future state buildings and capital projects.

nc:HB 443|constitutional amendment counc.title: Constitutional Amendment: Council of State Vacancies.
nc:HB 443|constitutional amendment counc.summary: Asks voters in November 2026 to amend the state constitution so the governor must fill vacancies in eight statewide elected offices from three nominees offered by the departing officeholder's political party, if the party submits names within 30 days.

mo:SB 888|relating to the juvenile justi.title: Relating to the juvenile justice system
mo:SB 888|relating to the juvenile justi.summary: Changes which juvenile felony arrests require fingerprinting and which charges allow adult certification, letting prosecutors seek it; closes juvenile criminal hearings to the public; sets fixed shares of prison sentences offenders must serve before parole starting in 2028; and adds offenses to the dangerous-felony list.

ia:HF 2133|designating kratom as a sched.title: Designating kratom as a schedule I controlled substance, and making penalties applicable
ia:HF 2133|designating kratom as a sched.summary: Adds kratom, including its plant parts, synthetic equivalents and compounds such as mitragynine, to the state's list of schedule I controlled substances, making possession a serious misdemeanor for a first offense, with harsher penalties for repeat offenses.

ia:HF 2748|relating to agriculture inclu.title: Relating to agriculture, including by providing for the powers and duties of the department of agriculture and land stewardship, including the promotion and regulation of commodities and products; the regulation of the transportation of agricultural commodities; the use of agricultural land; and taxation, including property taxes, excise and sales taxes, and income taxes; making penalties applicable; and including effective date and applicability provisions, previously deferred
ia:HF 2748|relating to agriculture inclu.summary: Makes broad changes to agriculture law: creates dollar-for-dollar matching funds for schools buying Iowa farm products and grants for small meat processors, allows permitted milk trucks up to 136,000 pounds, repeals the grain handling tax, and exempts honeybee sales and storage tanks of 91,000 gallons or less from tax.

ia:HF 2739|relating to state finances by.title: Relating to state finances by modifying the taxes imposed on health maintenance organizations, making transfers from the taxpayer relief fund, making and supplementing appropriations to the department of health and human services, and i ncluding effective date, contingent effective date, and retroactive applicability provisions
ia:HF 2739|relating to state finances by.summary: Replaces the premium tax on health maintenance organizations with a new health care-related tax, transfers about $347 million from the taxpayer relief fund to the general fund, and adds $89 million to Medicaid for the fiscal year ending June 2026.

ia:HF 970|relating to the double up food.title: Relating to the double up food bucks program, the supplemental nutrition assistance program and making appropriations and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 970|relating to the double up food.summary: Directs the state to seek federal approval to limit food stamp (SNAP) purchases to healthy foods, and, once approved, provides $1 million in grants for the Double Up Food Bucks program, which helps SNAP recipients buy fruits and vegetables.

ia:HF 2801|modifying the major economic.title: Modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions
ia:HF 2801|modifying the major economic.summary: Lets the state award one business a tax credit of up to 10% of its investment, paid over ten years, for a major project in a county of 50,000 people or fewer, instead of up to 5% credits for two businesses; credits are refundable and transferable.

dc:B 26-0661|fiscal year 2027 budget sup.title: Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Support Act of 2026
dc:B 26-0661|fiscal year 2027 budget sup.summary: Enacts and amends District laws needed to carry out the fiscal 2027 budget, making dozens of changes across government operations, economic development and housing, public safety, public schools and child care, human services such as TANF and rapid re-housing, environment and transportation, and taxes and revenue.

sd:SB 107|add licensed and registered ch.title: add licensed and registered child care programs to the definition of community safety zone.
sd:SB 107|add licensed and registered ch.summary: Adds licensed day care centers, licensed group family day care homes and registered family day cares to the sites within 500 feet of which registered sex offenders may not live, alongside schools, parks, playgrounds, pools, and domestic abuse and sexual assault shelters.

sd:SJR 508|proposing and submitting to t.title: proposing and submitting to the voters at the next general election, amendments to the Constitution of the State of South Dakota, removing the lieutenant governor as presiding officer of the Senate.
sd:SJR 508|proposing and submitting to t.summary: Asks voters at the next general election to amend the state constitution so the lieutenant governor is no longer president of the Senate with a tie-breaking vote, and to repeal the clause barring the lieutenant governor from sitting on the governor's impeachment trial.

nj:S 3521|strengthening trust between la.title: Strengthening Trust Between Law Enforcement & Immigrant Communities-concerns
nj:S 3521|strengthening trust between la.summary: Writes the Attorney General's immigrant-trust directive into law: bars state and local police, with exceptions, from stopping or detaining people based solely on suspected immigration status or civil immigration violations, or asking about immigration status, limits their help to federal immigration agents, and bans 287(g) agreements.

al:SB354|solar power facilities new faci.title: Solar power facilities; new facilities prohibited for one year
al:SB354|solar power facilities new faci.summary: For one year, bars new large solar farms in counties bordering the Gulf unless the operator first holds a local public hearing after 30 days' notice, bars stricter local solar rules, and bars new carbon dioxide storage sites on public land or covering 50,000 acres or more.

nm:HB 2|general appropriation act of 202.title: General Appropriation Act of 2026
nm:HB 2|general appropriation act of 202.summary: Sets New Mexico's operating budget for fiscal 2027, with about $11.05 billion in recurring general fund spending, a 2.6 percent increase, plus over $3 billion in one-time spending and fund transfers for areas including child care, health care, economic development and education.

nm:HB 7|children s future act fund.title: Children's Future Act & Fund
nm:HB 7|children s future act fund.summary: Creates a trust fund, with no initial appropriation, for children born in New Mexico since Jan. 1, 2025, for education, housing, business or retirement if they remain lifelong residents, obtain a high school equivalency credential and take a financial literacy course; exempts payouts from state income tax; creates a planning task force.

nc:SB 595|various revenue laws changes.title: Various Revenue Laws Changes.
nc:SB 595|various revenue laws changes.summary: Makes a range of tax law changes, including updating the state's link to the federal tax code, creating a Hurricane Helene timber-loss deduction, applying the 8% rental car tax to peer-to-peer rentals, and creating a 40% credit for rehabilitating corporate campuses.

nc:SB 24|govt mandates increase healthca.title: Govt Mandates Increase Healthcare Costs.
nc:SB 24|govt mandates increase healthca.summary: Requires any bill adding a health insurance mandate, including coverage, cost-sharing or prior-approval rules, to repeal at least as many existing mandates and fund its cost unless an actuarial note shows savings, and applies mandates effective July 1, 2025, or later to the State Health Plan.

nc:SB 58|ag restrict challenge to presid.title: AG/Restrict Challenge to Presidential EOs.
nc:SB 58|ag restrict challenge to presid.summary: Bars the state Attorney General from filing or joining any lawsuit that would invalidate a presidential executive order, and requires a report by June 1, 2025, on convictions for impersonating law officers, including federal immigration agents.

nc:HB 52|protect those who serve and pro.title: Protect Those Who Serve and Protect Act of 2025.
nc:HB 52|protect those who serve and pro.summary: Creates a felony for throwing or spraying water or other substances on public safety officers or police and rescue animals, expands officer-assault laws to cover attacks made because of the victim's role, and raises the penalty for assaulting officers with a firearm.

nc:SB 474|adjust counties reappraisal mo.title: Adjust Counties/Reappraisal Moratorium.
nc:SB 474|adjust counties reappraisal mo.summary: Changes which counties must delay their 2026 property revaluations to 2027, applying the delay to any county that reappraised for 2026 unless it has under 12,000 people, meets certain other tests, or is a Helene-affected county adopting a revenue-neutral tax rate.

nc:SJR 772|adjournment resolution.title: Adjournment Resolution.
nc:SJR 772|adjournment resolution.summary: Adjourns the 2025 legislative session on July 31, 2025, and sets a schedule of reconvened sessions through April 2026, limiting their business mainly to veto overrides, appointments, election and redistricting matters, and pending conference reports.

nc:SB 558|eliminating dei in public high.title: Eliminating "DEI" in Public Higher Ed.
nc:SB 558|eliminating dei in public high.summary: Bars public colleges and universities from endorsing or compelling belief in listed "divisive concepts" about race and sex, keeping diversity, equity and inclusion offices, or treating people differently based on federally protected traits, with exceptions for protected speech, research and legally required policies.

nc:SB 227|eliminating dei in public educ.title: Eliminating "DEI" in Public Education.
nc:SB 227|eliminating dei in public educ.summary: Bars public schools from promoting or compelling belief in listed "divisive concepts" about race and sex, teaching them except neutrally under state standards, keeping diversity, equity and inclusion offices, or treating people differently by federally protected traits, and bars state-backed teacher training on those concepts.

nc:HB 1089|constitutional amendment prop.title: Constitutional Amendment Property Tax Levy Limit.
nc:HB 1089|constitutional amendment prop.summary: Puts a state constitutional amendment on the November 3, 2026, ballot requiring the legislature to set limits on how much local property tax levies can be increased, with exceptions it may allow.

nc:SB 889|property tax reappraisal morat.title: Property Tax Reappraisal Moratorium.
nc:SB 889|property tax reappraisal morat.summary: Delays to 2027 the 2026 property revaluations in counties of 15,000 or more people, so those counties keep using prior property values for the 2026-27 tax year, and sets a $20 fee for the county assessor exam.

nc:HB 56|unc enrollment.title: UNC Enrollment.
nc:HB 56|unc enrollment.summary: Provides state money to University of North Carolina campuses to cover increased student enrollment, effective retroactively to July 1, 2025.

nc:HB 441|shrimp trawling transition pro.title: Shrimp Trawling Transition Program/Fees.
nc:HB 441|shrimp trawling transition pro.summary: Creates annual payments through October 1, 2028, for commercial fishers who sold shrimp trawled in inshore waters from 2023 to mid-2025, and temporarily raises commercial and recreational coastal fishing license fees, taking effect only if House Bill 442 becomes law.

nc:SB 280|private school security act.title: Private School Security Act.
nc:SB 280|private school security act.summary: Lets nonpublic school employees and volunteers with concealed carry permits, approved training and written school authorization carry guns or stun guns on school property, and lets permit holders carry handguns during worship services in places of worship on school property.

nc:SB 730|expand ceps nuclear and hydro.title: Expand CEPS/Nuclear and Hydro.
nc:SB 730|expand ceps nuclear and hydro.summary: Counts all nuclear and fusion power plants, including those placed in service before 2007, as "new clean energy facilities" under the state's clean energy portfolio standard, and drops the 10-megawatt size limit for hydroelectric plants to count as renewable energy facilities.

nc:HB 437|drug free zones unauthorized p.title: Drug-Free Zones/Unauthorized Public Camping.
nc:HB 437|drug free zones unauthorized p.summary: Creates felonies for selling drugs in posted drug-free zones around homeless service facilities, and bars local governments from allowing regular camping or sleeping on public property except at sites they designate for up to a year with Labor Department certification.

nc:HB 959|protecting students in a digit.title: Protecting Students in a Digital Age.
nc:HB 959|protecting students in a digit.summary: Requires school boards to adopt internet policies blocking student social media and TikTok on school devices, adds required lessons on social media's health effects, and requires schools to bar student phone use during instructional time, with exceptions.

nc:HB 737|doi omnibus bill.title: DOI Omnibus Bill.
nc:HB 737|doi omnibus bill.summary: Makes a range of insurance law changes, including ending required pre-licensing courses for insurance agents and adjusters, barring landlords from requiring renters insurance from a designated company, and treating credit card chargebacks of premiums as nonpayment.

nc:SB 1076|limit electric natural gas re.title: Limit Electric/Natural Gas Revenue Uses.
nc:SB 1076|limit electric natural gas re.summary: Bars Rocky Mount from moving revenue from its city electric and natural gas systems into other city funds, bars Louisburg from moving electric revenue to other funds, and repeals Louisburg's authority to spend electric revenue on economic development projects.

nc:HB 568|2025 omnibus labor amendments.title: 2025 Omnibus Labor Amendments.
nc:HB 568|2025 omnibus labor amendments.summary: Changes several labor laws, including limiting subpoenas of state workplace safety inspectors, dropping public hearings for state safety rules identical to federal ones, allowing pretrial discovery in safety-citation appeals, and requiring work-death autopsy reports within five months of a request.

nc:HB 388|amend business corporations ac.title: Amend Business Corporations Act.
nc:HB 388|amend business corporations ac.summary: Updates corporate and estate laws, letting corporations limit officers' personal liability, changing rules for shareholder lawsuits, emergency bylaws and mergers, allowing probate of wills stored electronically by attorneys, and extending emergency video notarization to as late as July 2026.

nc:SB 55|student use of wireless communi.title: Student Use of Wireless Communication Devices.
nc:SB 55|student use of wireless communi.summary: Requires public schools to adopt policies barring students from using or having phones and other wireless devices turned on during instructional time, with exceptions for teacher-approved, emergency, disability-plan and medical uses.

nc:HB 376|water wastewater affordability.title: Water/Wastewater Affordability and Capacity Act.
nc:HB 376|water wastewater affordability.summary: Changes water, sewer and septic laws, letting regulators suspend base rates proposed under multiyear water and sewer rate plans up to 300 days, requiring hearings before local governments sell water or sewer systems to private companies, ending local well programs and requiring state approval of local septic rules.

nc:SB 639|north carolina farm act of 202.title: North Carolina Farm Act of 2025.
nc:SB 639|north carolina farm act of 202.summary: Makes many farm law changes, including creating a feral swine working group, repealing a violation-points system for swine farms, presuming pesticide makers met their duty to warn when products carry federally approved labels, and letting local governments deny some special use permits that would harm farming.

nc:SB 472|amend 401 certification proces.title: Amend 401 Certification Process.
nc:SB 472|amend 401 certification proces.summary: Requires state environmental regulators to begin reviewing water quality certification applications immediately, notify applicants of fees within five business days, and create a five-business-day review for projects that already hold a federal nationwide permit.

nc:SJR 763|confirm don van der vaart uti.title: Confirm Don van der Vaart/Util. Comm.
nc:SJR 763|confirm don van der vaart uti.summary: Confirms the State Treasurer's appointment of Don van der Vaart to the North Carolina Utilities Commission for a term running from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2031.

nc:HB 173|wake county extraterritorial j.title: Wake County Extraterritorial Jurisdiction.
nc:HB 173|wake county extraterritorial j.summary: Bars Wake County cities and towns from expanding their land-use authority outside town limits beyond the area they covered on January 1, 2025, with the limit expiring December 31, 2028.

nc:HB 309|various local provisions vi.title: Various Local Provisions VI.
nc:HB 309|various local provisions vi.summary: Makes a series of local law changes, including switching school board elections in Columbus, Gaston, Scotland and Johnston counties to partisan elections, letting Buncombe County use some school sales tax money for operating costs for two years, and creating a Transylvania rural development authority.

nc:HB 268|2026 budget technical correcti.title: 2026 Budget Technical Corrections - II.
nc:HB 268|2026 budget technical correcti.summary: Makes technical, clarifying and other changes to the 2026 state budget law, including adjustments to Hurricane Helene recovery grants and programs, budget procedure rules, and several local and board appointment provisions.

nc:SB 858|general statutes commission ad.title: General Statutes Commission Add Member from High Point Law School.
nc:SB 858|general statutes commission ad.summary: Adds a member to the General Statutes Commission, appointed by the dean of the High Point University School of Law, to serve two-year terms beginning September 1 of odd-numbered years.

nc:SB 770|general assembly appointments.title: General Assembly Appointments.
nc:SB 770|general assembly appointments.summary: Appoints people recommended by the Senate President Pro Tempore and House Speaker to dozens of state boards, including University of North Carolina campus trustee boards, community college boards and the Charter Schools Review Board.

nc:HB 261|sentence enhancement immigrati.title: Sentence Enhancement/Immigration-Related Crimes.
nc:HB 261|sentence enhancement immigrati.summary: Raises by one felony class the sentence for felonies committed by people previously convicted of illegally reentering the U.S. after removal, and raises sentences for crimes committed while conspiring with others to further criminal activity.

nc:HB 47|disaster recovery act of 2025 p.title: Disaster Recovery Act of 2025 - Part I.
nc:HB 47|disaster recovery act of 2025 p.summary: Directs Hurricane Helene recovery money, including $524 million from the state's Helene Fund, to programs such as farm crop-loss aid, private road and bridge repair and small business infrastructure grants, extends the state of emergency to June 30, 2025, and eases various disaster-related rules.

nc:HB 517|modify nonprofit corp act char.title: Modify Nonprofit Corp. Act/Charitable Org.
nc:HB 517|modify nonprofit corp act char.summary: Changes nonprofit corporation law, allowing new kinds of mergers and conversions, requiring annual reports to the Secretary of State for a $25 paper or $18 electronic fee, requiring nonprofits other than private foundations formed on or after October 1, 2026, to have at least three directors, and extending emergency video notarization to as late as July 1, 2027.

nc:SB 554|farmers protection act.title: Farmers Protection Act.
nc:SB 554|farmers protection act.summary: Bars state-chartered banks, credit unions, savings banks and savings and loan associations from denying or canceling service to a farmer based on the farmer's greenhouse gas emissions or use of fossil-fuel fertilizer or machinery, with state regulators enforcing it.

nc:HB 279|filling vacancies haywood coun.title: Filling Vacancies/Haywood County Board of Commissioners.
nc:HB 279|filling vacancies haywood coun.summary: Lets the Haywood County Board of Commissioners fill a vacant seat without being bound by the recommendation of the departing member's political party, which the board currently must follow if made within 30 days.

nc:HB 918|standardized testing choice ac.title: Standardized Testing Choice Act.
nc:HB 918|standardized testing choice ac.summary: Directs the North Carolina Collaboratory to study whether UNC campuses should accept Classic Learning Test scores for admissions and state-funded scholarships, including whether the test predicts college success and what it would cost, reporting by December 15, 2025.

nc:SB 479|script act.title: SCRIPT Act.
nc:SB 479|script act.summary: Licenses pharmacy services administrative organizations and requires pharmacy benefit managers to report rebates and pricing, pay affiliated and independent pharmacies the same rates, and follow new audit rules; also requires drug makers to give notice of price increases.

nc:SB 401|nc farm act of 2025.title: NC Farm Act of 2025.
nc:SB 401|nc farm act of 2025.summary: Makes many changes to farm laws, including creating a feral swine working group, letting local boards deny special use permits that would harm farm production on land recently bought by businesses, repealing an unused swine-farm violation points system, and requiring excused school absences for agricultural events.

nc:HB 123|criminal falsification of medi.title: Criminal Falsification of Medical Records.
nc:HB 123|criminal falsification of medi.summary: Makes it a crime for health care providers to destroy, alter, falsify or omit medical records to hide errors, abuse or neglect, a felony when the patient was seriously injured or died, and makes paying or taking money for such falsification a felony.

nc:HB 483|juvenile justice legislative p.title: Juvenile Justice Legislative Proposals.
nc:HB 483|juvenile justice legislative p.summary: Changes juvenile justice laws, including allowing probation of up to three years and requiring three years of post-release supervision for juveniles who commit the most serious felonies, requiring victim notice before supervision ends, and creating a crime of escaping juvenile detention.

nc:HB 354|civil procedure gatekeeper ord.title: Civil Procedure/Gatekeeper Orders/Database.
nc:HB 354|civil procedure gatekeeper ord.summary: Requires people found legally incompetent and barred from filing court papers to file only through their guardian or lawyer, with exceptions, has courts strike other filings and issue gatekeeper orders, and requires the court system to keep a database of such people.

nc:HB 575|the hunter robinson act.title: The Hunter Robinson Act.
nc:HB 575|the hunter robinson act.summary: Lengthens post-release supervision after prison from 12 to 24 months for Class B1 through C felonies and from 12 to 18 months for Class D and E felonies, raising maximum sentences to match, for offenses on or after December 1, 2025.

nc:HB 15|support private property rights.title: Support Private Property Rights.
nc:HB 15|support private property rights.summary: Provides that a property's inclusion in a long-range, unfunded local transportation plan is not a fact sellers or real estate brokers must disclose, while barring sellers and agents from knowingly making false statements about it.

nc:SB 115|general assembly appointments.title: General Assembly Appointments.
nc:SB 115|general assembly appointments.summary: Appoints people recommended by the Senate leader and the House speaker to state boards and offices, including a special superior court judge, the Turnpike Authority, the Building Code Council and community college boards, and corrects earlier appointments.

nc:SB 311|the law and order act.title: The Law and Order Act.
nc:SB 311|the law and order act.summary: Creates or increases criminal penalties for offenses including assaulting utility workers, selling or possessing embalming fluid unlawfully, stealing gift cards, possessing explosive devices, reckless driving and street racing that cause injury, mail theft and armed burglary, and adds mass picketing to workplace violence laws.

nc:HR 19|amend temporary rules of the ho.title: Amend Temporary Rules of the House.
nc:HR 19|amend temporary rules of the ho.summary: Amends the House's temporary rules to revise its list of standing committees.

nc:HB 661|building industry efficiency a.title: Building Industry Efficiency Act of 2025.
nc:HB 661|building industry efficiency a.summary: Changes construction and development laws, including barring fees for inspections canceled more than a business day ahead, limiting local street standards stricter than the state's, exempting contractor-certified residential equipment replacements from inspection, and raising the cost threshold for formal public contract bidding.

nc:SB 754|school calendar flexibility a.title: School Calendar Flexibility:A New Alternative.
nc:SB 754|school calendar flexibility a.summary: Lets school boards choose a calendar starting as early as the Monday closest to August 19 and ending by late May if semesters are equal in length, and lets the State Board of Education withhold central office funding from districts that break the calendar law.

nc:HB 192|salary adjustments and budget.title: Salary Adjustments and Budget Offsets.
nc:HB 192|salary adjustments and budget.summary: Funds raises for 2025-2026, including an average 6.4% for teachers and 2.5% for most state, university and community college employees, a 1% one-time payment to retirees, and offsets them with budget transfers and cuts, including eliminating 20% of vacant state positions.

nc:SB 484|workplace violence prevention.title: Workplace Violence Prevention/Mass Picketing.
nc:SB 484|workplace violence prevention.summary: Adds blocking workplace entrances or public roads through mass picketing, and hindering lawful work by picketing, threats or force, to workplace violence laws, and lets employers seek court orders against such conduct; exempts peaceful protest and federally protected labor activity.

nc:HB 16|general assembly in god we trus.title: General Assembly: In God We Trust - Display.
nc:HB 16|general assembly in god we trus.summary: Requires the national motto "In God We Trust" to be displayed behind the presiding officers' desks in the state House and Senate chambers, paid for first with private donations and then with available funds if none arrive within 90 days.

nc:HB 557|the andy griffith show as stat.title: The Andy Griffith Show as State TV Show.
nc:HB 557|the andy griffith show as stat.summary: Adopts The Andy Griffith Show as North Carolina's official state television show.

nc:HB 236|remember 9 11 with freedom fla.title: Remember 9/11 with Freedom Flag.
nc:HB 236|remember 9 11 with freedom fla.summary: Designates the Freedom Flag as a state symbol of remembrance for lives lost in the September 11, 2001 attacks and allows it to be flown with the U.S. and state flags on public buildings and courthouses each September 11.

nc:HB 1015|general assembly appointments.title: General Assembly Appointments.
nc:HB 1015|general assembly appointments.summary: Appoints people recommended by the House speaker and Senate leader to state boards and commissions, including community college boards, the Wildlife Resources Commission, the State Property Tax Commission and NCInnovation, and corrects earlier appointments.

nc:HB 364|state transportation improveme.title: State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP) Grant Anticipation Notes.
nc:HB 364|state transportation improveme.summary: Lets local governments borrow money to speed up regional and division transportation projects scheduled for state funding, repaying it from expected state or federal money, after signing an agreement with the Department of Transportation.

nc:HB 928|allow physical therapists in s.title: Allow Physical Therapists in School Concussion Protocol.
nc:HB 928|allow physical therapists in s.summary: Adds licensed physical therapists to the health professionals who can evaluate middle and high school athletes showing concussion signs and give written clearance for them to return to play or practice.

nc:HB 187|credit union update.title: Credit Union Update.
nc:HB 187|credit union update.summary: Gives the state credit union regulator more power to impose penalties, remove officers and issue cease-and-desist orders, expands credit unions' services and investment authority, and lets them serve people at or below the poverty line and residents of areas more than eight miles from a bank branch.

nc:HB 975|ems personnel provisions.title: EMS Personnel Provisions.
nc:HB 975|ems personnel provisions.summary: Directs state emergency medical services officials to adopt rules letting EMS workers carry pepper spray, and lets EMS workers transport or treat injured police dogs and search and rescue dogs without a veterinary license or risk of prosecution.

nc:HR 1|house temporary rules.title: House Temporary Rules.
nc:HR 1|house temporary rules.summary: Adopts temporary rules of procedure for the House's 2025 regular session, covering the order of business, debate, committees, bill handling and voting, with Mason's Manual governing matters the rules do not address.

nc:HB 134|prohibit misbranding of certai.title: Prohibit Misbranding of Certain Food Products.
nc:HB 134|prohibit misbranding of certai.summary: Requires lab-grown, cell-cultured meat and poultry products whose labels use meat terms such as "beef" or "pork" to also carry a term like "lab-grown" near the product name in large type, starting October 1, 2025.

nc:HB 199|authorize municipal deannexati.title: Authorize Municipal Deannexation.
nc:HB 199|authorize municipal deannexati.summary: Creates a process for cities and towns to remove land from their limits, either on their own initiative after a report and public hearing or on a petition signed by all owners, with consent required from any local government taking over services.

nc:SB 375|harrison s law.title: Harrison's Law.
nc:SB 375|harrison s law.summary: Raises hazing by students from a Class 2 to a Class A1 misdemeanor, makes hazing by teachers, coaches or other school staff a Class I felony, and requires school boards to post central office employees' total pay and positions online each year.

nc:HR 904|house board of governors elect.title: House Board of Governors Elections.
nc:HR 904|house board of governors elect.summary: Elects six people — Wendy Floyd Murphy, Kellie Hunt Blue, Carolyn Coward, John A. Fraley, Reginald Ronald Holley and M. Lee Barnes — to the University of North Carolina Board of Governors for terms from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2029.

nc:HB 163|pharmacy benefits manager prov.title: Pharmacy Benefits Manager Provisions.
nc:HB 163|pharmacy benefits manager prov.summary: Requires pharmacy benefit managers to pay pharmacies at least federal benchmark drug costs, bars them from charging pharmacies various fees or stopping pharmacists from mentioning cheaper drugs, limits pharmacy audits, and requires quarterly reports on drug costs and manufacturer price concessions.

nc:HB 83|revise laws governing minors.title: Revise Laws Governing Minors.
nc:HB 83|revise laws governing minors.summary: Makes giving obscene material to a minor of any age a felony when the offender is at least four years older, lets judges order sex offender registration for such crimes, and creates habitual indecent exposure felonies that require registration.

nc:HB 1025|conetoe mayor voting authorit.title: Conetoe Mayor Voting Authority.
nc:HB 1025|conetoe mayor voting authorit.summary: Lets the mayor of Conetoe vote on any matter before the town's board of commissioners, instead of only to break ties.

nc:HB 547|children s services protection.title: Children's Services Protection Act.
nc:HB 547|children s services protection.summary: Caps the liability of private contractors serving children for state or county social services agencies at the same limits that apply to state agencies, shields them from the agencies' own negligence, and denies the cap to contractors who commit child abuse.

nc:HB 211|the kelsey smith act.title: The Kelsey Smith Act.
nc:HB 211|the kelsey smith act.summary: Requires wireless carriers to give police a phone's location when it was used to call 911 or is believed to be with someone at risk of death or serious harm, shields carriers from lawsuits for doing so, and requires them to file emergency contacts with the SBI.

nc:HB 434|lower healthcare costs.title: Lower Healthcare Costs.
nc:HB 434|lower healthcare costs.summary: Requires hospitals to report prices for common procedures, give cost estimates and out-of-network warnings, and itemize bills before collections; limits facility fees; ends certificate-of-need review for rehabilitation services; and sets deadlines for insurer prior-approval reviews.

nc:HB 789|mitigating factor pretrial use.title: Mitigating Factor/Pretrial Use of Ignition Interlock Device.
nc:HB 789|mitigating factor pretrial use.summary: Makes using an ignition interlock device for at least six months before trial a factor that can lower an impaired-driving sentence, for defendants with no recent impaired-driving convictions, a blood alcohol level under 0.15 and no crash causing serious injury or death.

nc:SB 775|general assembly appointments.title: General Assembly Appointments.
nc:SB 775|general assembly appointments.summary: Appoints people recommended by the Senate leader and House Speaker to 11 bodies, including six state boards, commissions and authorities and five community college boards of trustees, and corrects term dates and appointees in earlier appointment laws.

nc:SB 1074|eden mills river guilford art.title: Eden/Mills River/Guilford Article 46 Local Act.
nc:SB 1074|eden mills river guilford art.summary: Lets Eden agree not to annex Duke Energy's Dan River plant property through June 2030 in exchange for $1 million in payments, repeals Mills River's special zoning authority, and changes Guilford County's quarter-cent sales tax ballot question and revenue split.

nc:SB 777|general assembly appointments.title: General Assembly Appointments.
nc:SB 777|general assembly appointments.summary: Appoints four people recommended by the Senate leader and House Speaker to the College of The Albemarle and Eastern North Carolina School for the Deaf trustee boards and the Acupuncture Licensing Board, and repeals an earlier law's appointment of three people to the Continuing Care Advisory Committee.

nc:HB 696|medicaid hhs adjust other crit.title: Medicaid & HHS Adjust./Other Critical Needs.
nc:HB 696|medicaid hhs adjust other crit.summary: Adjusts the state budget and changes Medicaid and food assistance to follow 2025 federal law, including Medicaid work requirements with proof of compliance before enrolling, monthly eligibility checks, $319 million for Medicaid cost growth, and more veterans' children scholarship funds.

nc:HB 1104|improve ivc process and enhan.title: Improve IVC Process and Enhance Public Safety.
nc:HB 1104|improve ivc process and enhan.summary: Orders studies and plans on involuntary commitment, including a jail telehealth exam pilot proposal and examiner training; lengthens outpatient commitment to up to 180 days with new criteria; creates an inpatient program to restore defendants' capacity for trial; and delays parts of Iryna's Law to July 2028.

nc:HB 28|gun violence prevention act.title: Gun Violence Prevention Act.
nc:HB 28|gun violence prevention act.summary: Creates new crimes for convicted felons who have a gun while committing another felony: a Class F felony for possession, Class D if the gun is brandished, and Class C if it is fired, starting December 1, 2025.

nc:HB 147|various local provisions xi.title: Various Local Provisions XI.
nc:HB 147|various local provisions xi.summary: Removes the satellite annexation cap for Bear Grass, writes the Currituck County Game Commission's waterfowl blind rules into law with online applications and flexible fees, and requires ward-based primaries in Hickory when more than two candidates file for a ward.

nc:SB 13|political terrorism prevention.title: Political Terrorism Prevention Act.
nc:SB 13|political terrorism prevention.summary: Adds a sentencing aggravating factor and a one-class sentence increase without parole for crimes targeting victims over their political beliefs or activity, makes political motivation a death-penalty aggravating circumstance, and lets the Attorney General assign a special prosecutor in such cases.

nc:HB 149|school financial flexibility p.title: School Financial Flexibility Pilot Program.
nc:HB 149|school financial flexibility p.summary: Creates a pilot letting school districts with at least 5,000 students and special-tax authority move state funds more freely and hire unlicensed teachers for up to half of each school's teachers, starting in 2026-27, subject to State Board review.

nc:HJR 1244|adjournment resolution.title: Adjournment Resolution.
nc:HJR 1244|adjournment resolution.summary: Adjourns the legislature's 2025 regular session on July 2, 2026, until July 27, 2026, and limits business then to listed matters such as budget bills, constitutional amendments, local bills, appointments, veto overrides, election bills and conference reports.

nc:SB 220|protect private property right.title: Protect Private Property Rights.-AB
nc:SB 220|protect private property right.summary: Makes entering someone's land without written permission to hunt, fish, trap or reach public waters a misdemeanor even if unposted, and for posted land adds a $1,000 minimum fine and a two-year suspension of the related license.

nc:HB 183|various local provisions ii.title: Various Local Provisions II.
nc:HB 183|various local provisions ii.summary: Bars wake surfing on Lake Glenville within 200 feet of shore, structures, boats or swimmers, adds a runoff for Louisburg mayor when more than two candidates run, and lets Henderson, Johnston and Rutherford counties build community college buildings.

nc:HB 997|certify reading of nc constitu.title: Certify Reading of NC Constitution.
nc:HB 997|certify reading of nc constitu.summary: Requires each legislator, before taking the oath of office, to certify to their chamber's principal clerk whether they have read or reviewed the U.S. and North Carolina constitutions in the prior two years, starting January 1, 2027.

nc:HB 574|workforce development pilot pr.title: Workforce Development Pilot Project.
nc:HB 574|workforce development pilot pr.summary: Creates a grant program, run by the nonprofit North Carolina Workforce Development Coalition if money is provided, repaying state businesses with 20 to 1,500 employees half of eligible training costs, up to $2,000 per grant and $40,000 per employer yearly.

nc:HB 116|jacksonville annexation confor.title: Jacksonville Annexation & Conforming Changes.
nc:HB 116|jacksonville annexation confor.summary: Adds parts of Camp Lejeune, Marine Corps Air Station New River and Stones Bay to Jacksonville's city limits, limits city police powers and annexation north of N.C. Highway 24, and ends the city's zoning authority outside its limits.

nc:HB 26|various local provisions i.title: Various Local Provisions I.
nc:HB 26|various local provisions i.summary: Removes Madison's satellite annexation cap, takes specified properties out of the limits of Andrews, Four Oaks, Elizabeth City, King, Creedmoor and Wilson, and revises and consolidates the Town of Davidson's charter.

nc:HB 616|megasites selectsites program.title: Megasites/Selectsites Program Revisions.
nc:HB 616|megasites selectsites program.summary: Raises from 15 to 20 the number of smaller industrial "selectsites" the state may identify, requires three to five more in Hurricane Helene disaster counties, lets megasite grants cover infrastructure and site work beyond land purchases, and sends program funds in full to the Economic Development Partnership.

nc:HB 698|center for missing persons to.title: Center for Missing Persons to Highway Patrol.
nc:HB 698|center for missing persons to.summary: Moves the North Carolina Center for Missing Persons to the State Highway Patrol on July 1, 2025, narrows Amber Alerts to children believed abducted and in danger, renames the existing missing-endangered alert as the Silver Alert, and creates Missing Endangered, Ashanti and Missing-Weather alerts.

nc:HB 1237|appointments corrections.title: Appointments & Corrections.
nc:HB 1237|appointments corrections.summary: Appoints or reappoints more than 100 people to state boards, commissions and community college trustee boards on recommendations of the Senate president pro tempore and House speaker, and corrects terms in earlier appointment laws.

nc:HB 143|maysville occupancy tax.title: Maysville Occupancy Tax.
nc:HB 143|maysville occupancy tax.summary: Lets the Town of Maysville levy a 6% room occupancy tax, with proceeds sent to a new town tourism development authority that must spend at least two-thirds on promoting tourism and the rest on tourism-related expenses.

nc:HB 63|town of andrews deannexation.title: Town of Andrews/Deannexation.
nc:HB 63|town of andrews deannexation.summary: Removes four tracts of land from the town limits of Andrews, effective June 30, 2025, for tax years beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

nc:SB 316|lower healthcare costs.title: Lower Healthcare Costs.
nc:SB 316|lower healthcare costs.summary: Requires hospitals and surgical centers to report prices for common procedures, bars many facility fees, requires good-faith cost estimates and itemized bills before medical debt goes to collections, sets deadlines for insurer prior-approval reviews, and ends certificate-of-need review for rehabilitation services.

nc:HB 358|continuing budget operations p.title: Continuing Budget Operations Part II.
nc:HB 358|continuing budget operations p.summary: Makes mid-year budget changes, including $65.5 million for Tropical Storm Chantal disaster relief and recovery, plus spending and policy adjustments for education, the Department of Labor, economic development, state buildings, capital projects and transportation.

nc:HJR 1016|amend adjournment resolution.title: Amend Adjournment Resolution.
nc:HJR 1016|amend adjournment resolution.summary: Adds Medicaid rebase funding and state budget matters to the limited list of subjects the General Assembly may take up during its session reconvened on October 20, 2025.

nc:HB 71|respiratory care modernization.title: Respiratory Care Modernization Act.
nc:HB 71|respiratory care modernization.summary: Creates licensing for advanced respiratory care practitioners working under a supervising physician, barring them from diagnosing, prescribing or surgery, updates Respiratory Care Board rules, and makes the board's investigative records confidential.

nc:HB 801|legislative research commissio.title: Legislative Research Commission Study Paper Towns.
nc:HB 801|legislative research commissio.summary: Directs the Legislative Research Commission to study towns incorporated since 1995 that may not provide promised services, consider whether the state should suspend or revoke their charters, and report to the 2026 legislative session.

nc:HB 1067|rural hall unaffiliated candi.title: Rural Hall - Unaffiliated Candidates.
nc:HB 1067|rural hall unaffiliated candi.summary: Lets Rural Hall town candidates get on the ballot as unaffiliated by petition under state rules, with petitions due to the county elections board by noon on primary day starting with 2028 elections, and sets a noon July 6, 2026, deadline for 2026 only.

nc:HB 775|criminal history checks for sc.title: Criminal History Checks for School Positions.
nc:HB 775|criminal history checks for sc.summary: Requires criminal history checks, paid by applicants, for people seeking public school jobs and for initial charter school board members, adds intentional infliction of emotional distress on a child to school employee misconduct, and requires police to report certain misconduct allegations to superintendents.

nc:HB 421|motor vehicle dealers.title: Motor Vehicle Dealers.
nc:HB 421|motor vehicle dealers.summary: Extends the grace period for motor vehicle dealer licenses awaiting renewal from 30 to 60 days, makes dealer plates valid for two years instead of one, and requires replacing them every four years instead of three.

nc:HB 612|fostering care in nc act.title: Fostering Care in NC Act.
nc:HB 612|fostering care in nc act.summary: Changes child welfare and adoption laws, including letting people who report suspected abuse seek state review when a report is not investigated, expands guardianship assistance to youth age 10, and requires background checks for city and county jobs working with children.

nc:SB 690|various real estate and busine.title: Various Real Estate and Business Law Changes.
nc:SB 690|various real estate and busine.summary: Adds an alternative training pathway to become a certified residential real estate appraiser, lets securities salespeople register with more than one dealer, clarifies landlords' recovery of attorney fees in eviction appeals, and directs rules on preprinted real estate contracts.

nc:HB 1200|tax free family essentials ac.title: Tax-Free Family Essentials Act.
nc:HB 1200|tax free family essentials ac.summary: Exempts diapers, incontinence underpads, baby wipes and feminine hygiene products from sales and use tax starting April 1, 2027.

nc:HB 648|disposition placement findings.title: Disposition Placement/Findings of Fact.
nc:HB 648|disposition placement findings.summary: Requires judges to make written findings of fact supporting their placement decisions for abused, neglected or dependent children, and lets judges compare all placement options when deciding whether placing a child with a relative is against the child's best interest.

nc:HB 476|department of state treasurer.title: Department of State Treasurer Technical Corrections/Administrative Changes
nc:HB 476|department of state treasurer.summary: Makes administrative and technical changes to State Treasurer laws, including letting charter schools extend provisional entry into the state retirement system, moving pension forfeiture appeals to retirement boards, redirecting certain court fees, and limiting state claims on disability savings accounts after death.

nc:SB 124|state hiring accessibility and.title: State Hiring Accessibility and Modernization.
nc:SB 124|state hiring accessibility and.summary: Changes state government hiring by having job requirements reviewed for when experience can replace degrees, letting applicants upload resumes, requiring closing dates on postings, allowing direct hiring into some vacancies without posting, and letting local agencies offer signing and retention bonuses.

nc:HB 506|2025 state investment moderniz.title: 2025 State Investment Modernization Act.
nc:HB 506|2025 state investment moderniz.summary: Creates the North Carolina Investment Authority, governed by a five-member board including the State Treasurer, and transfers management of state and pension fund investments from the Treasurer to the Authority beginning January 1, 2026.

nc:HB 771|criminal law procedures.title: Criminal Law Procedures.
nc:HB 771|criminal law procedures.summary: Lets prosecutors take depositions to preserve testimony of witnesses who are threatened, gravely ill, leaving the state, age 65 or older or otherwise likely unavailable for trial, adds rights for sexual assault victims, and changes the Conference of District Attorneys.

nc:HB 87|cell phone free education.title: Cell Phone-Free Education.
nc:HB 87|cell phone free education.summary: Requires public school governing boards to adopt policies eliminating or severely restricting student cell phone use during instructional time, with exceptions for teacher-approved, disability-plan and medical uses, and to notify parents yearly, starting in 2025-2026; remote and virtual schools are exempt.

nc:SB 423|title fraud prevention.title: Title Fraud Prevention.
nc:SB 423|title fraud prevention.summary: Makes filing a knowingly false deed a felony, requires photo ID from most people recording property documents, lets registers of deeds refuse suspicious documents, lets property owners sue over fraudulent filings, and requires tax collector certification before deeds are recorded.

nc:HB 251|various disaster recovery refo.title: Various Disaster Recovery Reforms.
nc:HB 251|various disaster recovery refo.summary: Bars the state from denying disaster aid over political affiliation or speech, raises looting temporary housing during emergencies to a Class F felony, eases fire-resistant window rules for Helene-damaged downtown businesses, waives Helene debris-mulching rules, and lets Helene flood-damaged buildings be rebuilt under prior rules if FEMA agrees.

nc:HB 992|timeshare foreclosure paternit.title: Timeshare Foreclosure/Paternity Matters.
nc:HB 992|timeshare foreclosure paternit.summary: Creates a trustee foreclosure process, as an alternative to court foreclosure, for timeshare owners six months or more behind on assessments, and changes how paternity is established for children born outside marriage to inherit when a parent dies without a will.

nc:HB 315|prohibit litigation invest ame.title: Prohibit Litigation Invest/Amend WC Benefits.
nc:HB 315|prohibit litigation invest ame.summary: Bars third-party funding of civil lawsuits in exchange for a share of the outcome, with fines up to $50,000 per violation, and raises workers' compensation minimum weekly payments from $30 to $50 and caps for disfigurement and organ injuries.

nc:SB 117|gsc uniform comm code emerging.title: GSC Uniform Comm. Code/Emerging Technologies.
nc:SB 117|gsc uniform comm code emerging.summary: Updates the state's commercial code, as recommended by the General Statutes Commission, adding rules for transferring and controlling electronic records and electronic money and for using them as loan collateral, effective October 1, 2025.

nc:HB 332|various occupancy tax changes.title: Various Occupancy Tax Changes.
nc:HB 332|various occupancy tax changes.summary: Cuts Nash County's room occupancy tax authority from 5% to 3%, creates Rocky Mount District R covering the Nash County part of Rocky Mount, and lets the district levy a room occupancy tax of up to 2%.

nc:SB 605|ibt subbasin tmdl transport fa.title: IBT Subbasin/TMDL Transport Factor.
nc:SB 605|ibt subbasin tmdl transport fa.summary: Ends separate subbasin designations for the Haw, Deep and Contentnea Creek river basins so water can move between them without an interbasin transfer certificate, and applies a nutrient credit calculation to all Neuse River Basin local government wastewater permits.

nc:HB 875|dpi to redesign math instructi.title: DPI to Redesign Math Instruction.
nc:HB 875|dpi to redesign math instructi.summary: Requires the Department of Public Instruction to provide approved math assessments, curricula, intervention materials and teacher training for kindergarten through eighth grade, and to report to legislators before new state math standards take effect.

nc:HB 23|various state and local governm.title: Various State and Local Government Provisions.
nc:HB 23|various state and local governm.summary: Authorizes Gullah Geechee and South Fork Passage state trails, transfers about 11 state acres to Burgaw for $1, codifies the Lake Norman Marine Commission, names roads and bridges, and lets railroad rights-of-way count toward certain building code clearances.

nc:SJR 774|confirm stephanie lynch inves.title: Confirm Stephanie Lynch, Investment Authority.
nc:SJR 774|confirm stephanie lynch inves.summary: Confirms the State Treasurer's appointment of Stephanie Lynch to the North Carolina Investment Authority Board of Directors, as state law requires the legislature to approve such appointments by joint resolution.

nc:HB 429|turtle rescue team special reg.title: Turtle Rescue Team Special Registration Plate.
nc:HB 429|turtle rescue team special reg.summary: Authorizes a Turtle Rescue Team special license plate showing an eastern box turtle, costing $30 on top of regular registration, with $20 of each fee going to N.C. State University's veterinary college turtle rescue program.

nc:HB 773|school performance grade chang.title: School Performance Grade Changes.
nc:HB 773|school performance grade chang.summary: Replaces the formula behind public schools' A-F performance grades with point-based scores counting test proficiency, student growth, English learner progress and, for high schools, graduation and career or college readiness; sets new grade cutoffs and subgroup grading, starting with 2025-26 data.

nc:SB 328|age 21 hemp derived consumable.title: Age 21 Hemp-Derived Consumables.
nc:SB 328|age 21 hemp derived consumable.summary: Makes it a misdemeanor for anyone under 21 to possess hemp-derived products meant to be eaten, swallowed or inhaled, such as delta-8 or CBD products, or for anyone to knowingly sell or give them to someone under 21, starting October 1, 2025.

nc:SB 600|improve health and human servi.title: Improve Health and Human Services.
nc:SB 600|improve health and human servi.summary: Lets taxpayers sign up as organ donors on their income tax return, bans selling IV bags made with the chemical DEHP from 2030 and IV tubing from 2035, allows epinephrine nasal spray, and puts experienced registered nurses on the certified school nurse pay scale.

nc:SB 295|clarify motor vehicle dealer l.title: Clarify Motor Vehicle Dealer Laws.
nc:SB 295|clarify motor vehicle dealer l.summary: Changes rules between car manufacturers and their franchised dealers, covering dealership transfers, terminations, succession when a dealer retires, payments to dealers for over-the-air software sales, warranty repair reimbursement and loaner cars, and bars forcing dealers to accept unfinished vehicles.

nc:HB 747|2025 wildlife resources change.title: 2025 Wildlife Resources Changes.
nc:HB 747|2025 wildlife resources change.summary: Lets the Wildlife Resources Commission withhold records revealing locations of rare species or sensitive habitats, authorizes a new Lifetime Conservationist license plate, updates boating safety laws to match federal law, and creates a raffle and auction for two elk hunting permits in 2026.

nc:HB 567|ensure access to biomarker tes.title: Ensure Access to Biomarker Testing.
nc:HB 567|ensure access to biomarker tes.summary: Requires private health insurance plans, the State Health Plan and Medicaid to cover biomarker testing, lab analysis of tissue or blood for markers such as gene mutations, when medical evidence supports its use for diagnosing, treating or monitoring a disease.

nc:HB 308|criminal law changes.title: Criminal Law Changes.
nc:HB 308|criminal law changes.summary: Makes any assault by strangulation a felony, creates a felony of habitual domestic violence for people with two or more prior domestic violence convictions, bars expunctions while a petitioner has pending charges or warrants, and ends the default that multiple sentences run at the same time.

nc:HB 121|school calendar flexibility st.title: School Calendar Flexibility/Statewide/Open Calendar.
nc:HB 121|school calendar flexibility st.summary: Lets local school boards set their own school-year opening and closing dates, removing the statewide rule that classes start no earlier than the Monday closest to August 26 and end by the Friday closest to June 11, starting in 2025-26.

nc:HB 763|neighbor state license recogni.title: Neighbor State License Recognition Act.
nc:HB 763|neighbor state license recogni.summary: Requires most state licensing boards to license new residents who hold a license in good standing for at least a year in Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia or West Virginia; health care, legal, engineering, accounting and several other professions are excluded.

nc:HB 1219|mem of understanding tennesse.title: Mem. of Understanding Tennessee Cntys/Madison.
nc:HB 1219|mem of understanding tennesse.summary: Lets the Madison County Sheriff's Office sign agreements with sheriffs in Unicoi, Greene and Cocke counties in Tennessee to carry out joint law enforcement operations across the state line, with each agreement spelling out how liability is shared.

nc:HB 1029|nc digital asset and stableco.title: NC Digital Asset and Stablecoin Act.
nc:HB 1029|nc digital asset and stableco.summary: Sets state rules for financial institutions offering cryptocurrency custody, staking and transaction services, adds digital assets to unclaimed property law, and bars issuing payment stablecoins in North Carolina except by state-licensed or authorized issuers or federally qualified issuers, with reserve requirements.

nc:HB 152|access to transcranial magneti.title: Access to Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation.
nc:HB 152|access to transcranial magneti.summary: Requires health insurers that cover transcranial magnetic stimulation, a magnetic brain treatment, to cover it from any facility or licensed provider whose scope of practice includes treating depression and other mental disorders, without penalizing claims based on medical specialty; insurers still set coverage terms and rates.

nc:HB 217|driver education 18 years and.title: Driver Education/18 Years and Older and Unlicensed.
nc:HB 217|driver education 18 years and.summary: Requires first-time driver's license applicants 18 and older to complete a three-hour driver education course, offered online and in person, covering state driving laws and alcohol and drug use, for applications starting October 1, 2025.

nc:HB 95|threaten elected official incre.title: Threaten Elected Official/Increase Punishment.
nc:HB 95|threaten elected official incre.summary: Adds local elected officials to laws against assaulting or threatening public officers, raises penalties for those crimes, and requires a judge rather than a magistrate to set pretrial release conditions for people charged with assaulting or threatening such officials or election officials.

nc:HB 186|the stars and stripes commitme.title: The Stars and Stripes Commitment Act.
nc:HB 186|the stars and stripes commitme.summary: Requires public schools to schedule recitation of the Pledge of Allegiance within an hour of the start of each school day, and requires the State Board of Education and school governing boards to open meetings with the Pledge; no one can be compelled to recite it.

nc:HB 637|community of practice advanced.title: Community of Practice Advanced Teaching Roles Supplement.
nc:HB 637|community of practice advanced.summary: Lets Pitt County Schools split the $10,000 advanced teaching roles salary supplement for lead teachers between the lead teacher and collaborating teachers in schools using a community of practice teaching model, starting in 2025-26.

nc:HB 811|cc firearm safety instruction.title: CC Firearm Safety Instruction 18 and Older.
