nc:HB 198|amend law on notice of abc vio.summary: Replaces the rule that alcohol law enforcement agents and local ABC officers notify a permit holder of violations on the premises within five business days with a rule that the state ABC Commission does so after receiving any law enforcement report.

nc:HB 223|town of mooresville property c.title: Town of Mooresville/Property Conveyance.
nc:HB 223|town of mooresville property c.summary: Lets the Town of Mooresville convey town property, with or without payment, for housing for low- and moderate-income people, veterans and emergency responders, by board resolution posted online 10 days in advance, excluding land taken by eminent domain.

nc:HB 21|drivers license designation aut.title: Drivers License Designation/Autism.
nc:HB 21|drivers license designation aut.summary: Requires the Division of Motor Vehicles to create a voluntary driver's license record designation for people with documented autism, viewable only by law enforcement, and requires officer training on interacting with people with autism, with requests starting January 1, 2026.

nc:HB 37|enhance firefighter benefits an.title: Enhance Firefighter Benefits and Representation.
nc:HB 37|enhance firefighter benefits an.summary: Raises the monthly pension for eligible members of the state Firefighters' and Rescue Squad Workers' Pension Fund from $175 to $180 starting January 1, 2026, and gives the State Firefighters' Association a seat on the state EMS Advisory Council.

nc:HB 124|adopt official state cookie.title: Adopt Official State Cookie.
nc:HB 124|adopt official state cookie.summary: Makes the Moravian cookie the official state cookie of North Carolina.

nc:HB 182|revise law permanent protectiv.title: Revise Law Permanent Protective Order/Child Abuse.
nc:HB 182|revise law permanent protectiv.summary: Lets judges issue lifetime no-contact orders against people convicted of violent felonies, not just sex offenses, and extend them to victims' immediate family; makes it a felony for any caregiver of a child under 16 to commit or allow a sexual act on the child.

nc:HB 136|town of faith even yr elect fo.title: Town of Faith/Even-Yr. Elect./Four-Yr.Terms.
nc:HB 136|town of faith even yr elect fo.summary: Moves Town of Faith municipal elections to even-numbered years, cancels the 2025 election and extends current aldermen's terms by one year, and gives aldermen four-year terms starting with a 2026 election.

nc:HB 43|designate state balloon rally.title: Designate State Balloon Rally.
nc:HB 43|designate state balloon rally.summary: Designates the Carolina BalloonFest, held each October in Statesville, as North Carolina's official balloon rally.

nc:HB 34|establish larceny of mail offen.title: Establish Larceny of Mail Offense.
nc:HB 34|establish larceny of mail offen.summary: Raises the punishment for stealing, receiving or possessing stolen mail, including packages sent by any carrier or delivery service, by sentencing offenders one offense class higher, starting December 1, 2025.

nc:HB 42|burglary and breaking or enteri.title: Burglary and Breaking or Entering/Sentence Enhancement.
nc:HB 42|burglary and breaking or enteri.summary: Rewrites the definitions of first- and second-degree burglary without the old nighttime requirement and sentences people one class higher if they carried a firearm or other deadly weapon during a burglary or breaking or entering, starting December 1, 2025.

nc:HB 536|physical therapy practice act.title: Physical Therapy Practice Act Mods.
nc:HB 536|physical therapy practice act.summary: Updates physical therapy licensing law: ends temporary practice by graduates awaiting licenses, lets applicants complete clinical requirements under supervised board-approved plans, sets a November–January renewal window, adds ethics violations and misdemeanor convictions as grounds for discipline, and revises fees.

nc:SB 378|hoa revisions.title: HOA Revisions.
nc:SB 378|hoa revisions.summary: Changes rules for condominium and homeowners' associations, including capping fines for continuing violations at $2,500, limiting liens for fines, capping management contracts at two years, and regulating license plate readers; requires mediation before most association lawsuits and has the Justice Department track owner complaints.

nc:SB 207|litter law rebuttable presumpt.title: Litter Law/Rebuttable Presumption.
nc:SB 207|litter law rebuttable presumpt.summary: Lets courts presume that a person named on littered items such as bank statements, bills or prescription bottles committed the littering infraction, unless shown otherwise; advertising and campaign materials do not count. Applies to offenses from December 1, 2025.

nc:SB 229|authorize nil agency contracts.title: Authorize NIL Agency Contracts.
nc:SB 229|authorize nil agency contracts.summary: Brings agents who negotiate name, image and likeness deals for college athletes under the state's athlete-agent registration law, and exempts athletes' name, image and likeness contracts held by colleges from public records disclosure, retroactively.

nc:SB 310|religious property tax exempti.title: Religious Property - Tax Exemption.
nc:SB 310|religious property tax exempti.summary: Lets owners of religious property file late applications for property tax exemption covering up to the five prior years and, if approved, cancels unpaid taxes for those years, without refunding taxes already paid.

nc:SB 345|pa team based practice.title: PA Team-Based Practice.
nc:SB 345|pa team based practice.summary: Lets experienced physician assistants practice in physician-led team settings without a designated supervising physician, except in surgery and anesthesia, and makes the Board of Nursing the sole regulator of nurse practitioners and certified nurse midwives.

nc:SB 693|veteran access liberty options.title: Veteran Access, Liberty, Options for Recovery.
nc:SB 693|veteran access liberty options.summary: Regulates paid help with veterans' benefits claims: bars fees for initial disability claims and referrals, guarantees of outcomes and upfront charges, caps contingency fees at five times the monthly benefit increase, and requires written agreements and disclosures. Licensed attorneys are exempt.

nc:SB 79|boiling springs charter ot chan.title: Boiling Springs Charter/OT Changes.
nc:SB 79|boiling springs charter ot chan.summary: Rewrites and consolidates the Town of Boiling Springs charter and dissolves its Tourism Development Authority on July 1, 2025, having the town spend room occupancy tax revenue and the authority's unspent funds on tourism directly; ends the tax's exemption for nonprofit-provided lodging.

nc:SB 329|recognizing south fork passage.title: Recognizing South Fork Passage State Trail.
nc:SB 329|recognizing south fork passage.summary: Authorizes adding the South Fork Passage Trail along the South Fork River in Catawba, Lincoln and Gaston counties to the state parks system as a state trail, using donated land and existing trail and conservation funds.

nc:SB 357|pharmacists collaborative prac.title: Pharmacists/Collaborative Practice.
nc:SB 357|pharmacists collaborative prac.summary: Expands what clinical pharmacists under agreements with supervising physicians may do, including starting or stopping drugs, ordering tests and devices, and same-class substitutions, and requires health insurers to cover pharmacists' in-scope services that plans would cover from other providers.

nc:SB 445|reg relief for hospitals in di.title: Reg. Relief for Hospitals in Disaster Zones.
nc:SB 445|reg relief for hospitals in di.summary: Automatically waives or modifies state hospital rules to match temporary federal Medicare and Medicaid waivers issued during emergencies, for as long as the federal waiver lasts.

nc:SB 131|temp local sales tax changes b.title: Temp. Local Sales Tax Changes/Buncombe Co.
nc:SB 131|temp local sales tax changes b.summary: Lets Buncombe County use half of its Article 39 local sales tax revenue for school operating costs as well as school construction from July 2025 through June 2027, with the other half available for any public purpose.

nc:SB 190|physician assistant licensure.title: Physician Assistant Licensure Compact.
nc:SB 190|physician assistant licensure.summary: Enters North Carolina into the interstate PA Licensure Compact, letting physician assistants licensed in member states obtain the privilege to practice here, and sets Medical Board fees of $230 for an initial license or privilege and $140 for annual registration.

nc:SB 369|medicaid telehealth services.title: Medicaid Telehealth Services.
nc:SB 369|medicaid telehealth services.summary: Requires the state Medicaid program to let licensed providers and provider groups that offer care only through telehealth enroll as Medicaid providers without a physical presence or service address in North Carolina.

nc:SB 507|auto enrollment in advanced el.title: Auto Enrollment in Advanced ELA Courses.
nc:SB 507|auto enrollment in advanced el.summary: Requires schools offering advanced English language arts courses or programs to automatically place students who score at the highest level on state tests in them, as already done for math, unless a parent consents in writing to removal.

nc:SB 121|gsc conveyances between spouse.title: GSC Conveyances Between Spouses.
nc:SB 121|gsc conveyances between spouse.summary: Provides that a deed of real property from one spouse to the other does not waive the grantor's elective life estate unless expressly stated, nor equitable distribution rights, and that such property is separate only if a separate written agreement says so.

nc:SB 122|gsc unif community prop disp a.title: GSC Unif. Community Prop. Disp. at Death Act.
nc:SB 122|gsc unif community prop disp a.summary: Replaces the state's law on community property at death with a new uniform act under which half of property a married couple acquired while living in a community-property state belongs to the surviving spouse, effective January 1, 2026.

nc:SB 59|revise voluntary ag district la.title: Revise Voluntary Ag. District Laws.
nc:SB 59|revise voluntary ag district la.summary: Requires local farmland district ordinances to bar government agencies from starting condemnation of farmland in agricultural districts until 120 days after an advisory board hearing and recommendation, and gives the board 45 days instead of 30.

nc:SB 223|expand academic trans pathways.title: Expand Academic Trans. Pathways/Sophomore HS.
nc:SB 223|expand academic trans pathways.summary: Lets community colleges offer career and technical education pathways leading to industry credentials to qualified high school sophomores, in addition to juniors and seniors, starting in the 2025-26 school year.

nc:SR 104|senate bog elections.title: Senate BOG Elections.
nc:SR 104|senate bog elections.summary: Sets the Senate's procedure for nominating and electing six members of the University of North Carolina Board of Governors to four-year terms in 2025, including a February 24–28 nomination window and required ethics filings.

nc:SR 1|senate permanent rules.title: Senate Permanent Rules.
nc:SR 1|senate permanent rules.summary: Adopts the Senate's permanent rules for the 2025 regular session, covering order of business, debate, motions, voting, committees, handling of bills, and legislative officers and staff.

al:HB410|bail bonds bail reform act of 1.title: Bail Bonds; Bail  Reform Act of 1993 and Bail Bond Regulatory Act amended; certain undeposited fees forgiven; penalties for crime of bail jumping increased; to provide further for conditional forfeitures, out-of-state bondsmen and sureties, limitations on property owners as sureties; to provide further for the definition of an employee of a professional bail bond company or professional surety company, for the licensing and duties of apprentices; to increase the membership of the Alabama Professional Bail Bonding Board; provide for a late fee for renewals; and to require applicants for licensing to be residents of this state for at least one year
al:HB410|bail bonds bail reform act of 1.summary: As introduced, forgives certain uncollected bail bond fees, raises penalties for bail jumping, changes rules for forfeitures and out-of-state and property-owner sureties, enlarges the state bail bonding board, adds a late renewal fee and requires one year of state residency for licensing.

al:HB42|alabama bail reform act of 1993.title: Alabama Bail Reform Act of 1993, court authorized to accept cash deposit in certain circumstances
al:HB42|alabama bail reform act of 1993.summary: As introduced, lets a court accept a cash bail deposit smaller than the full amount of bail set, if the judicial officer who set the cash bail approves.

al:HB431|injection wells fees assessed o.title: Injection wells; fees assessed on certain wells, notice and participation for local governments provided, study commission established
al:HB431|injection wells fees assessed o.summary: Charges carbon dioxide storage operators 14 cents per ton stored from October 2027, split between the state General Fund and the county (shared with the city if inside one). Gives local governments notice of and a role in permit hearings and creates a fee study commission.

al:HB4|taxation establishes alabama broa.title: Taxation; establishes Alabama Broadband Investment Maximization Act; exempts ADECA project funded or administered purchases from sales and use tax
al:HB4|taxation establishes alabama broa.summary: Exempts broadband and internet equipment with at least a 10-year life from state sales and use tax when bought for projects funded or run by the state economic and community affairs department, from September 2026 through August 2029. Lets counties and cities offer the same exemption.

al:SB5|department of archives and histor.title: Department of Archives and History, composition of board and method of filling board vacancies further provided for, retroactive effect
al:SB5|department of archives and histor.summary: As passed by the Senate, changes the Archives and History board to 16 appointed seats plus the Governor, with seats appointed by the Governor, the House Speaker and the Senate President Pro Tempore instead of chosen by the board itself, retroactive to January 1, 2025.

al:SB262|lowndes county pari mutuel wage.title: Lowndes County, pari-mutuel wagering on simulcast past events and live horse and dog races under certain conditions; tax levied; distribution of revenue, provided
al:SB262|lowndes county pari mutuel wage.summary: Lets the White Hall town council in Lowndes County authorize a licensed bingo facility to take pari-mutuel bets on simulcast past and live out-of-state horse and dog races. Sets a local tax of up to 4%, shared with county government, schools and a wastewater program, and a 1% state tax.

al:HB56|motor vehicles autocycles headge.title: Motor vehicles; autocycles, headgear equipment required for operation
al:HB56|motor vehicles autocycles headge.summary: As introduced, requires drivers and riders of autocycles, three-wheeled motor vehicles, to wear the protective headgear and shoes already required for motorcycle riders.

al:SB85|vaccines religious exemption for.title: Vaccines; religious exemption for K-12 students, further provided for; religious exemption for students at public institutions of higher education, provided
al:SB85|vaccines religious exemption for.summary: Lets parents exempt K-12 students from school vaccine or testing requirements with a written statement and a physical form completed in the past 12 months, without giving reasons or getting approval. Bars public colleges from requiring vaccines or testing unless they offer religious and medical exemptions.

al:SR31|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR31|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Thursday, February 27, 2025, making a listed set of bills the first business taken up that legislative day, ahead of the regular order of business.

al:HB631|etowah county obsolete laws rep.title: Etowah County, obsolete laws repealed
al:HB631|etowah county obsolete laws rep.summary: Repeals four Etowah County laws as obsolete, including ones requiring the county to pay health premiums for laid-off workers, letting charities buy county fuel at cost, allowing facsimile signatures on county checks and requiring county approval for public concert licenses.

al:SB91|county and municipal authorities.title: County and municipal authorities; withdrawal from multi-jurisdiction authority authorized, taxes and distribution of monies from taxes further provided for
al:SB91|county and municipal authorities.summary: Lets a county or city withdraw by resolution from certain multi-county economic development authorities that have no outstanding debt, set up its own replacement entity and redirect related tax money. Requires the authority to return a proportional share of its unspent funds.

al:HB511|fayette county duties and compe.title: Fayette County, duties and compensation of revenue commissioner further provided for
al:HB511|fayette county duties and compe.summary: Keeps the Fayette County revenue commissioner's current salary until October 2027 and adds a $15,000 yearly expense allowance starting October 2025. Sets the base salary at $67,000 a year from October 2027, replacing the allowance.

al:SB227|office of occupational and prof.title: Office of Occupational and Professional Licensing established within Alabama Department of Workforce, powers and duties of Secretary of Workforce and executive director specified, Sunset Committee to consider transfer to office in recommendation for modification
al:SB227|office of occupational and prof.summary: Creates an Office of Occupational and Professional Licensing in the state workforce department, run by a director appointed by the Secretary of Workforce, to take over licensing, fees, records and investigations for licensing boards placed under it. Lets the Sunset Committee recommend moving boards there.

al:SR54|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR54|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Thursday, April 3, 2025, making routine business such as bill introductions and committee reports, followed by a listed set of bills, the paramount order of business that legislative day, ahead of the regular order.

al:SR76|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR76|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Tuesday, March 10, 2026, making a listed set of bills the first business taken up that legislative day, ahead of the regular order of business.

al:SR77|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR77|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Tuesday, April 22, 2025, making routine business such as bill introductions and committee reports, followed by two listed bills, the paramount order of business that legislative day, ahead of the regular order.

al:SB82|criminal procedure recall of war.title: Criminal procedure; recall of warrants required in certain circumstances
al:SB82|criminal procedure recall of war.summary: As amended in the House, requires municipal court magistrates every five years to audit Class B and C misdemeanor and violation warrants unserved for 10 years, except sex, domestic violence, weapon and felony-linked offenses, with the presiding judge and prosecutor deciding which to recall.

al:SR12|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR12|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Thursday, February 6, 2025, making a listed set of bills the first business taken up that legislative day, ahead of the regular order of business.

al:HB581|morgan county distribution of c.title: Morgan County, distribution of county's TVA in-lieu-of-taxes payments further provided for
al:HB581|morgan county distribution of c.summary: Rewrites how Morgan County divides its Tennessee Valley Authority payments in place of taxes among the legislative delegation office fund, the county rescue squad, school boards, bond payments, an economic development fund and local governments, and repeals older distribution laws.

al:SR96|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR96|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Thursday, March 19, 2026, making a listed set of bills the first business taken up that legislative day, ahead of the regular order of business.

al:SR64|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR64|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Wednesday, April 9, 2025, making routine business such as bill introductions and committee reports, followed by a listed set of bills, the paramount order of business that legislative day, ahead of the regular order.

al:SR99|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR99|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order calendar for Tuesday, March 31, 2026, making a listed set of bills the first business taken up that legislative day, ahead of the regular order of business.

al:HB273|municipal employees eligible to.title: Municipal employees; eligible to receive grant funds paid through municipal treasury in certain circumstances
al:HB273|municipal employees eligible to.summary: Lets a city-employed first responder receive community development block grant funds paid through the city treasury if treated like other recipients and not involved in eligibility decisions. Public officials and their family members are excluded.

al:HB265|crimes and offenses resisting a.title: Crimes and offenses, resisting arrest further provided for, enhanced penalties provided for in certain circumstances
al:HB265|crimes and offenses resisting a.summary: Raises resisting arrest from a Class B to a Class A misdemeanor. Makes it a felony when the person brandishes or uses a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument, or when resistance injures someone, with higher penalties for serious injury or weapon use.

al:HB435|manufactured homes certificate.title: Manufactured Homes; certificate of title for 1999 models and earlier, Alabama Department of Revenue authorized to issue titles upon request
al:HB435|manufactured homes certificate.summary: Lets current owners of manufactured homes from model year 1999 or earlier ask the state Department of Revenue for a certificate of title, which those older homes are otherwise not issued. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

al:HB395|liquor mark up fee charged by a.title: Liquor; mark up fee charged by Alcoholic Beverage Control Board further provided for
al:HB395|liquor mark up fee charged by a.summary: As introduced, limits the "cost of merchandise" used to calculate the state alcohol board's markup on wholesale liquor sales, capped at 16.99%, to only what the board pays for the cases of liquor.

al:HB586|alabama real estate commission.title: Alabama Real Estate Commission; license required for real estate wholesalers, real estate wholesalers and unsolicited real property solicitors must provide disclosures, Alabama Securities Commission, authorized to enforce, penalties imposed for violations
al:HB586|alabama real estate commission.summary: As passed by the House, requires residential real estate wholesalers to be licensed and disclose that they do not own the property, requires disclosures on unsolicited investor offers, lets sellers without an agent or attorney cancel such contracts within seven days, and adds fines and Securities Commission enforcement.

al:SB265|tax abatements for data process.title: Tax abatements for data processing centers, exemption period limited, collection of certain taxes on purchases required, sunset date extended
al:SB265|tax abatements for data process.summary: Caps data center abatements granted from 2027 at 20 years; for centers drawing 100 megawatts or more, ends state sales tax breaks on buildings and power equipment (except in targeted counties) and state property tax breaks once in service; extends the sunset to 2032.

al:HB67|parental rights prohibits public.title: Parental rights, prohibits public K-12 schools and public libraries from presenting or sponsoring drag performances in certain circumstances and state entities from allowing minors to share facilities with members of the opposite sex in certain circumstances during overnight programs
al:HB67|parental rights prohibits public.summary: Bars public schools and libraries from knowingly presenting or sponsoring drag performances before minors without parental consent, and bars certain state entities from having minors share facilities with the opposite sex on overnight programs, except family members with parental consent.

al:HB53|child custody rebuttable presump.title: Child custody; rebuttable presumption of joint legal custody and substantial parenting time for both parents created
al:HB53|child custody rebuttable presump.summary: Creates a presumption, which can be overcome by evidence, that child custody orders should give both parents joint legal custody and substantial parenting time, except in cases of domestic or family violence, and requires courts to explain in writing when they do not.

al:HB232|juvenile court required to prov.title: Juvenile court, required to provide written notification to local superintendent or principal of private K-12 school if student charged with or adjudicated delinquent for certain serious crimes; authorized to provide written notice of charges for or adjudication of delinquency for lesser crimes
al:HB232|juvenile court required to prov.summary: Requires juvenile courts to notify a student's superintendent or private school principal within seven days when the student is charged with or found delinquent for a capital offense, murder, first-degree rape or sodomy, replacing a Class A or B felony rule, and allows notice for other crimes.

al:HB556|montgomery county legislative d.title: Montgomery County; legislative delegation, office and fund established
al:HB556|montgomery county legislative d.summary: Directs the Montgomery County Commission to create a fund for the county's legislative delegation office, deposits certain state money distributed to the county into it, and requires the county's largest city to provide the office space and utilities, starting October 1, 2026.

al:HB633|etowah county membership of per.title: Etowah County, membership of personnel board
al:HB633|etowah county membership of per.summary: Changes who appoints Etowah County's five-member personnel board, giving seats to the probate judge, the county commission on recommendations of the county engineer and chief administrative officer, the revenue commissioner and a regional labor council, and sets four-year terms.

al:SB32|crimes and offenses further prov.title: Crimes and offenses; further provide for the crime of murder, manslaughter, and assault in the first and second degree; provide enhanced sentencing; define machinegun
al:SB32|crimes and offenses further prov.summary: Defines machinegun and requires life without parole for adults convicted of murder, and for anyone convicted of manslaughter, when a machinegun caused the death, and makes first- and second-degree assault with a machinegun Class A felonies carrying a life sentence.

al:SB34|public k 12 education violence p.title: Public K-12 education; violence prevention, conflict resolution, and mediation instruction required before graduation from high school, State Board of Education required to adopt standards
al:SB34|public k 12 education violence p.summary: Requires public school students entering middle school in 2026-2027 and later to complete a course in violence prevention, conflict resolution and mediation before starting high school, and directs the state education department to provide materials and teacher training.

al:HB39|seafood dealer license license f.title: Seafood dealer license; license fee for applicants holding other seafood licenses revised; retroactive effect provided
al:HB39|seafood dealer license license f.summary: Sets a $265 seafood dealer license fee, instead of $465, for Alabama residents who already hold certain other seafood licenses or permits, and applies the change retroactively to licenses issued on or after October 1, 2025.

al:SB105|counties and municipalities onl.title: Counties and municipalities; online publication of financial statements, audits, expenditures, and budgets required
al:SB105|counties and municipalities onl.summary: Requires county commissions and city governments to post their annual financial statements, audits, monthly expenditures and budgets on their websites, or on a statewide association's site if they have none, starting October 1, 2028, with security-related details allowed to be withheld.

al:SB329|lee county lee county revenue c.title: Lee County; Lee County Revenue Commissioner authorized to perform duties of selling and redeeming land for taxes
al:SB329|lee county lee county revenue c.summary: Moves duties for redeeming land sold for unpaid taxes in Lee County from the probate judge to the revenue commissioner, and lets the revenue commissioner charge an administrative fee of up to $50 per redemption.

al:HB215|calhoun county sheriff s compen.title: Calhoun County, sheriff's compensation further provided for
al:HB215|calhoun county sheriff s compen.summary: Gives the Calhoun County sheriff an added expense allowance of $13,966 a year starting June 1, 2025, and sets the sheriff's base salary at $114,290 a year, replacing all other allowances, starting January 18, 2027.

al:HB480|driver licenses use of foreign.title: Driver licenses;  use of foreign national driver licenses as photo identification for voting prohibited
al:HB480|driver licenses use of foreign.summary: Bars Alabama driver licenses, nondriver ID cards and vessel licenses issued to foreign nationals from being presented or accepted as photo identification for voting, effective June 1, 2025.

al:HB16|fair campaign practices act auth.title: Fair Campaign Practices Act; authorize notifications of civil penalties by electronic mail in lieu of certified mail in certain circumstances
al:HB16|fair campaign practices act auth.summary: Lets the Secretary of State notify people of civil penalties under the state campaign finance law by email, requiring certified mail only when the penalty exceeds the cost of sending it that way.

al:SB310|jefferson county filling of vac.title: Jefferson County, filling of vacancies on county commission and election dates further provided for
al:SB310|jefferson county filling of vac.summary: Changes how Jefferson County Commission vacancies are filled: the election commission sets special primary and general elections within fixed timeframes, but a seat vacated with fewer than six months left stays open until the next countywide general election; repeals separate election-date rules.

al:HB417|city of eclectic in elmore coun.title: City of Eclectic in Elmore County, corporate limits altered
al:HB417|city of eclectic in elmore coun.summary: Expands the city limits of Eclectic in Elmore County to take in specified parcels of land.

al:HB49|crimes and offenses rape 1st and.title: Crimes and offenses; rape 1st and sodomy 1st; penalties further provided for
al:HB49|crimes and offenses rape 1st and.summary: Makes first-degree rape or sodomy of a child under 12 a capital offense, punishable by death or life without parole for adult offenders, and requires anyone given a life sentence for it to serve at least 30 years before parole eligibility.

al:HB380|crimes and offenses human cloni.title: Crimes and offenses; human cloning prohibited, criminal penalties provided
al:HB380|crimes and offenses human cloni.summary: Makes human cloning, attempting it, or transferring embryos, eggs or cells for cloning a Class C felony, while exempting in vitro fertilization, fertility treatment and other research not specifically barred.

al:HB179|campus chaplains public k 12 sc.title: Campus chaplains; public K-12 schools authorized to hire or accept as volunteers, local boards of education and governing bodies authorized to vote on whether to allow, limitations provided
al:HB179|campus chaplains public k 12 sc.summary: Lets local school boards and charter school governing bodies vote to allow volunteer campus chaplains, who must complete chaplain training and pass a background check, and bars people required to register as sex offenders from serving.

al:HB2|vaccines parental consent for min.title: Vaccines, parental consent for minor to receive vaccine, required
al:HB2|vaccines parental consent for min.summary: Bars minors who are not emancipated from consenting to their own vaccinations without the written consent of a parent or legal guardian, creating an exception to the rule letting minors 14 and older consent to their own medical care.

al:HB471|local water sewer and fire prot.title: Local water, sewer, and fire protection authorities; prohibition on officers serving on board of directors of authority removed
al:HB471|local water sewer and fire prot.summary: Removes the ban on state or local officers serving on the boards of directors of local water, sewer and fire protection authorities.

al:HB323|motor vehicles oversize vehicle.title: Motor vehicles, oversize vehicle load permits, exemption for electric utility commodities and equipment provided
al:HB323|motor vehicles oversize vehicle.summary: Exempts commodities and equipment of electric providers, including the Tennessee Valley Authority and certain public power authorities, from the requirement to obtain oversize-load permits to move on state highways, as farm equipment already is.

al:SB355|chambers county city of valley.title: Chambers County, City of Valley; annexation
al:SB355|chambers county city of valley.summary: Expands the city limits of Valley in Chambers County to take in specified parcels of land.

al:HB630|etowah county number of continu.title: Etowah County; number of continuous days that lodging must be supplied before lodging tax no longer applies extended
al:HB630|etowah county number of continu.summary: Exempts Etowah County lodging stays from the county lodging tax only after 180 continuous days, up from 30, effective October 1, 2026.

al:HB332|education public k 12 schools c.title: Education, public K-12 schools, completion of approved computer science course required
al:HB332|education public k 12 schools c.summary: Requires public high school students, starting with the class of 2031, to earn a credit in an approved computer science course to graduate, without raising total credits, and lets it count as a math, science, career-tech or elective credit.

al:SB55|military spouses preference in h.title: Military spouses; preference in hiring and promoting in state service further provided for; preference authorized for political subdivisions, private employers
al:SB55|military spouses preference in h.summary: As introduced, adds points to state job test ratings for spouses of active-duty service members and lets local governments and private employers give hiring and promotion preference to veterans, their spouses and spouses of active-duty members.

al:HJR326|recognizing the need for a nor.title: Recognizing the need for a north-south transportation route in East Alabama
al:HJR326|recognizing the need for a nor.summary: Declares the Legislature's recognition that East Alabama needs a four-lane north-south transportation route connecting it to the Port of Mobile to serve manufacturing, commuting and tourism.

al:SR98|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR98|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for its 30th legislative day, putting a list of House bills, many of them local measures on county officials' pay, annexations and local taxes, ahead of other pending business.

al:SB75|public works contracts exemption.title: Public works contracts; exemption established for purchases made through cooperative purchasing agreements, requirements for certain public contracts to comply with applicable state or local competitive bid laws provided
al:SB75|public works contracts exemption.summary: Lets public bodies buy materials or equipment for a public works project through cooperative purchasing agreements, if those items were competitively bid under Alabama law; the rest of the project stays under public works bidding rules. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:SB359|chambers county ad valorem fire.title: Chambers County; ad valorem fire protection tax levied, opt-out for certain areas of county provided; constitutional amendment
al:SB359|chambers county ad valorem fire.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment levying a two-mill property tax in Chambers County to fund volunteer fire departments, letting cities, towns and fire districts that use paid firefighters opt their residents out of the tax.

al:HB253|distinctive license plates volu.title: Distinctive license plates; volunteer and professional firefighters plate fee increased, distribution of funds provided for
al:HB253|distinctive license plates volu.summary: Raises the extra annual fee on volunteer firefighter license plates from $1 to $10 and adds a $10 fee on professional firefighter plates, splitting the money among the firefighter memorial, a peer support program, the firefighters' annuity fund and an emergency relief fund.

al:SR15|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR15|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for February 11, 2025, scheduling floor consideration of bills on the Veterans Affairs board, a school psychologist licensure compact, military medical records as proof of school immunizations, and portable benefits accounts for independent contractors.

al:HB17|motor vehicles prohibitions on t.title: Motor vehicles; prohibitions on the alteration of the height of the fender of a vehicle, provided
al:HB17|motor vehicles prohibitions on t.summary: Bans driving a car or truck on state highways if its suspension, frame or chassis was altered to raise the front fender four or more inches above the rear, with fines up to $50, then $100, and $250 for third offenses; commercial or farm alterations are exempt.

al:HB285|traffic infractions requires la.title: Traffic infractions, requires law enforcement to contact parent or guardian when citing minor for traffic violation
al:HB285|traffic infractions requires la.summary: Requires police who give a traffic ticket to a driver under 19 to make a reasonable effort, such as one call, text or letter, to notify the driver's emergency contact. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:SB360|public service commission numbe.title: Public Service Commission; number of commissioners expanded to represent congressional districts, phase-in by election provided, term of office revised, position of Secretary of Energy established as cabinet member, calculation of electric utility rates revised
al:SB360|public service commission numbe.summary: Expands the Public Service Commission to seven district-based members, four initially appointed by the governor; creates a governor-appointed Secretary of Energy to direct it; freezes electric base rates until 2029, then bars utilities from charging customers for lobbying, most advertising and grants.

al:HB376|motor vehicles license plates v.title: Motor vehicles; license plates, validity period extended
al:HB376|motor vehicles license plates v.summary: Extends the minimum period that a license plate design stays valid before replacement from five years to 10 years.

al:HB256|motor vehicles license plates v.title: Motor vehicles; license plates, validity period extended
al:HB256|motor vehicles license plates v.summary: Extends the minimum period that a license plate design stays valid before replacement from five years to 10 years, starting January 1, 2027.

al:HB72|crimes offenses smoking or vapin.title: Crimes & offenses; smoking or vaping marijuana in motor vehicle when child is present prohibited, criminal penalties provided, notification of Department of Human Resources required, mandatory reporting if child smells of marijuana required
al:HB72|crimes offenses smoking or vapin.summary: Makes smoking or vaping marijuana in a vehicle with anyone under 19 present a misdemeanor, requires offenders to take a state education course, requires police to notify child welfare officials, and requires mandatory reporters to report children who smell of marijuana.

al:HB602|montgomery county probate judge.title: Montgomery County, probate judge compensation further provided for
al:HB602|montgomery county probate judge.summary: Sets the Montgomery County probate judge's salary at $153,725 a year starting October 1, 2025, for the person holding the office on June 1, 2025.

al:HB183|public k 12 schools home school.title: Public K-12 schools; home school students authorized to attend career and technical education programs in certain circumstances
al:HB183|public k 12 schools home school.summary: Lets home-schooled students take career and technical education programs at public schools starting in 2027-2028, if they enroll as nontraditional students and pay the same course fees; public students get first priority, and stand-alone technical schools may opt out.

al:HB632|etowah county privilege and lic.title: Etowah County, privilege and license tax on lodging, time of continuous supply for tax exemption increased
al:HB632|etowah county privilege and lic.summary: Raises from 30 to 180 continuous days the length of stay after which hotel and other lodging rentals in Etowah County are exempt from the county's 2% lodging tax. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB22|class iv municipalities audits r.title: Class IV municipalities; audits, restrictions on hiring accountant removed
al:HB22|class iv municipalities audits r.summary: Removes the rule barring the same accountant from auditing a Class IV city's books for more than three consecutive years.

al:HB604|public k 12 education accountab.title: Public K-12 education;  Accountability Council created; Alabama Workforce Development Board, State Department of Education, and Alabama Commission on Higher Education to develop system to analyze student performance data
al:HB604|public k 12 education accountab.summary: Creates a standing Accountability Council of state officials, lawmakers and education and business representatives to review the school report card and recommend changes, and requires the state workforce board to track and report graduates' college, military, credential, job and income outcomes.

al:HB61|public k 12 schools home school.title: Public K-12 schools, home school students authorized to attend career and technical education programs in certain circumstances
al:HB61|public k 12 schools home school.summary: Lets home-schooled students take career and technical education programs at public schools starting in 2026-2027, if they enroll as nontraditional students and pay the same course fees; public students get first priority, and stand-alone technical schools may opt out.

al:HB161|building codes standardization.title: Building codes; standardization of certain non-residential building codes, provided; practice architecture and duties of local building code officials, further provided
al:HB161|building codes standardization.summary: Applies the state's minimum building code to all non-residential buildings, lets counties and cities run permit and inspection programs for them, bars local officials from imposing stricter requirements, and lets coastal localities adopt supplemental coastal building codes.

al:HB216|firearms firearm hold agreement.title: Firearms; firearm hold agreements defined; civil immunity therefrom provided
al:HB216|firearms firearm hold agreement.summary: Shields licensed firearms dealers from lawsuits over returning a gun to its owner at the end of an agreement to hold the gun temporarily, unless the dealer acted unlawfully.

al:HB270|alabama department of environme.title: Alabama Department of Environmental Management; water well drillers, licenses and licensees, fees therefore, revised and further provides for; continuing education required
al:HB270|alabama department of environme.summary: Moves water well drillers to two-year licenses starting October 1, 2025, with fees of $1,000 for unrestricted and $500 for restricted or business licenses, requires continuing education for renewals starting in 2027, and lets regulators set fees for filing well completion reports.

al:HB91|court fees use of funds allocate.title: Court fees; use of funds allocated to sheriff's office for expenditure further provided
al:HB91|court fees use of funds allocate.summary: Lets sheriffs spend their share of an existing court docket fee on any law enforcement function of their office, rather than only on running the jail.

al:HB487|alabama g i dependent scholarsh.title: Alabama G.I. Dependent Scholarship Program, veterans, dependents, tuition assistance, disability requirements revised
al:HB487|alabama g i dependent scholarsh.summary: Lowers from 40% to 30% the disability rating that makes veterans' dependents eligible for the state G.I. dependent tuition scholarship, and for 2026-2027 lets up to 100 dependents a year qualify despite residency rules if the veteran is at least 50% disabled and lived in Alabama five years.

al:HB327|state employees paid parental l.title: State employees; paid parental leave authorized, parameters for eligibility established
al:HB327|state employees paid parental l.summary: As introduced, gives eligible state and public school employees paid parental leave: eight weeks for mothers and two weeks for fathers after a birth, stillbirth or miscarriage, and eight weeks after adopting a child age three or younger.

al:HB508|baldwin county constitutional a.title: Baldwin County, constitutional amendment, Belforest Landmark District established
al:HB508|baldwin county constitutional a.summary: Proposes a local constitutional amendment creating the Belforest Landmark District in Baldwin County and barring annexation of its land into any city by local law, except by a city incorporated later; the district has no taxing, zoning or other government powers.

al:HB298|public schools athletic associa.title: Public schools; athletic associations required to adjust athletic classification under certain circumstances
al:HB298|public schools athletic associa.summary: Requires high school athletic associations to adjust a public school's competitive classification to account for English language learner students who do not play sports, starting in 2026-2027, and adds two non-voting legislators to the association's governing body.

al:HB13|illegal immigration procedures f.title: Illegal immigration, procedures for arrest, detention, transportation of illegal immigrants provided for; reporting requirements established
al:HB13|illegal immigration procedures f.summary: Lets state and local police enter immigration enforcement agreements with federal agencies and, when federal law allows, arrest people for being in the country illegally and take them to federal custody; requires jails to check inmates' status, honor federal detainers and report foreign-national data yearly.

al:HB302|workforce regulating staffing a.title: Workforce; regulating staffing and hiring of  aliens with temporary or asylum status in the state
al:HB302|workforce regulating staffing a.summary: Requires labor brokers recruiting foreign workers for Alabama jobs to register and report to the state, with civil and criminal penalties; makes sponsors of parolees, asylum seekers and other humanitarian entrants repay benefits replacing promised support; and strips tax incentives from repeat employers of unauthorized workers.

al:HB636|washington county compensation.title: Washington County, compensation of circuit clerk further provided for
al:HB636|washington county compensation.summary: Provides that Section 1 of a 1984 Washington County local law on the circuit clerk's compensation is repealed once the clerk in office on January 1, 2026, leaves office, so it will not apply to future clerks. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB287|municipal police departments re.title: Municipal police departments; report number of law enforcement officers employed by department to Alabama Justice Information Commission, ALEA, and Attorney General
al:HB287|municipal police departments re.summary: Requires state, county and city police agencies to report their sworn officer counts yearly to the Alabama Justice Information Commission for sharing with state police and the Attorney General; agencies missing required reports face $1,000 fines every 30 days and lose state grants until compliant.

al:HB454|crimes and offenses crime of ta.title: Crimes and offenses; crime of tampering with a legislative record, established
al:HB454|crimes and offenses crime of ta.summary: Creates the misdemeanor crime of altering, without the sponsoring legislator's permission, a required legal notice describing a proposed local law in order to change its described scope or effect, and publishing it that way.

al:HB513|department of commerce alabama.title: Department of Commerce; Alabama Industrial Development Training Institute; exemptions from state procurement law and contract review, provided
al:HB513|department of commerce alabama.summary: Exempts the Alabama Industrial Development Training Institute, a Commerce Department division, from legislative contract review, and exempts purchases of goods, services and training for companies with Commerce or institute economic development agreements from state competitive bidding, with yearly reports to the chief procurement officer.

al:HB296|consumer protection rental home.title: Consumer Protection, Rental Home Marketplace Guarantees Act created
al:HB296|consumer protection rental home.summary: Creates the Rental Home Marketplace Guarantees Act, requiring online short-term rental platforms that offer damage-reimbursement guarantees to hosts to register with the Insurance Commissioner by March 2027, back them with a reimbursement insurance policy, disclose terms, and face fines up to $500 per violation.

al:HB105|law enforcement officers retire.title: Law enforcement officers, retirement benefits further provided for
al:HB105|law enforcement officers retire.summary: Requires county and municipal law enforcement agencies to give a retiring officer in good standing his or her badge, and lets them give the officer his or her service pistol or offer to sell it at a fair market price.

al:HB444|seafood country of origin agric.title: Seafood country of origin; Agriculture and Industries Commissioner authorized to test for compliance, notification methods revised, violations further provided
al:HB444|seafood country of origin agric.summary: Lets the Agriculture and Industries Commissioner test seafood sold by restaurants and food sellers to check country-of-origin labels, revises how origin must be posted, and requires the Health Department to publish violators quarterly and cut their sanitation scores by five points.

al:HB474|property provide additional pro.title: Property; provide additional procedures; clarify jurisdiction under which local law enforcement may remove unauthorized individuals from an owner's premises
al:HB474|property provide additional pro.summary: Expands the fast-track process for removing squatters from dwellings to any premises, requires police to serve notice and remove occupants no sooner than 24 hours after receiving the owner's sworn affidavit and within three business days of verifying it, and gives city police jurisdiction inside city limits.

al:HB166|motor vehicles impoundment cond.title: Motor vehicles; impoundment conditions and procedures, further provided; redemption procedures, further provided; issuance of local identification cards, restrictions provided
al:HB166|motor vehicles impoundment cond.summary: As introduced, lets officers impound a vehicle when the driver cannot show a valid license (with exceptions), sets proof and fee requirements to reclaim it within 60 days, and bars counties and cities from issuing local ID cards without driver-license-level proof of identity.

al:HB264|vessel registration amends boat.title: Vessel Registration; amends boater registration fees and their distribution
al:HB264|vessel registration amends boat.summary: As introduced, folds the separate $5 boat registration fee into the base fees, raising them to $23 to $103 depending on boat length, and sends $5 of each fee to the State Reservoir Management Grant Fund and the rest to the State Water Safety Fund.

al:HB403|electric utilities review by pu.title: Electric Utilities; review by Public Service Commission of certain contracts with large load customers further provided
al:HB403|electric utilities review by pu.summary: Lets the Public Service Commission deem an electricity contract with a customer expecting 100 megawatts or more, such as a data center, in the public interest if it should recover the added cost of serving that customer from it and benefit other utility customers.

al:HB318|traffic infractions parental el.title: Traffic infractions; parental electronic notification system authorized
al:HB318|traffic infractions parental el.summary: As introduced, requires the state law enforcement agency, if funds are available, to create an electronic system that notifies enrolled parents or guardians when their child under 19 is cited for a traffic infraction, starting October 1, 2026.

al:HB10|juvenile offenders delinquent ac.title: Juvenile offenders, delinquent acts for purposes of juvenile proceedings further provided for
al:HB10|juvenile offenders delinquent ac.summary: As introduced, provides that nonfelony traffic and water safety offenses by 14- and 15-year-olds, other than impaired driving or boating, are no longer handled as delinquent acts in juvenile court, matching existing treatment of 16- and 17-year-olds.

al:HB456|clarke county sheriff authorize.title: Clarke County, sheriff authorized to collect fees for certain services
al:HB456|clarke county sheriff authorize.summary: Lets the Clarke County sheriff charge reasonable fees for services such as fingerprinting, reports, record copies, ID cards, funeral escorts and court-ordered ankle monitors, and adds a court fee for serving legal papers, split between the circuit clerk and sheriff.

al:SB41|calhoun county authorizes the co.title: Calhoun County, authorizes the county commission and governing bodies of municipalities to regulate halfway houses
al:SB41|calhoun county authorizes the co.summary: Lets the Calhoun County Commission and city governments regulate halfway houses, sober living homes and similar facilities, including permits, size, location and occupancy limits, with fines up to $1,000 per day per resident, and requires barring registered sex offenders from certain facilities.

al:HB493|shelby county city of helena ci.title: Shelby County; City of Helena, civil service system established, board, director, policies, and appeals created
al:HB493|shelby county city of helena ci.summary: Creates a new civil service system for City of Helena employees, with a three-member personnel board that hears disciplinary appeals, a personnel director appointed by the mayor, job classification and pay plans, and hiring and promotion rules, replacing the city's 1992 system.

al:SB240|parole remote inmate participat.title: Parole, remote inmate participation at parole hearings, authorized, conditions established
al:SB240|parole remote inmate participat.summary: Requires the parole board, starting March 1, 2027, to let inmates take part in their parole hearings by video or phone, keeps victims hidden from the inmate unless they choose otherwise, and requires the prison system to provide the equipment.

al:HB502|city of prichard mobile county.title: City of Prichard; Mobile County, expedited quiet title process established
al:HB502|city of prichard mobile county.summary: Lets the City of Prichard use a fast-track court process to gain clear title to abandoned tax-sale properties it bought from the state, after notice to owners and lienholders, with a hearing within 90 days and a chance for owners to redeem.

al:HB613|marengo co city of demopolis an.title: Marengo Co., City of Demopolis; annexation
al:HB613|marengo co city of demopolis an.summary: Expands the city limits of Demopolis in Marengo County to take in about 116 acres along U.S. Highway 80, effective October 1, 2026.

al:HB188|scholarship program to create f.title: Scholarship program, to create for dependents of long-term law enforcement officers
al:HB188|scholarship program to create f.summary: Creates a scholarship covering up to $3,000 per term in tuition, fees and books, after other aid, for up to eight semesters at Alabama colleges for children under 27 and spouses of officers with seven years at one agency or 12 overall, funded partly by a $50 license plate.

al:SB65|paint rock in jackson county cor.title: Paint Rock in Jackson County, corporate limits altered
al:SB65|paint rock in jackson county cor.summary: Expands the town limits of Paint Rock in Jackson County to take in stretches of U.S. Highway 72 and its right-of-way east and west of town, out to the Paint Rock River and State Route 65, effective October 1, 2025.

al:HB211|calhoun county authorizes the c.title: Calhoun County, authorizes the county commission and governing bodies of municipalities to regulate halfway houses
al:HB211|calhoun county authorizes the c.summary: Lets the Calhoun County Commission and city governments regulate halfway houses, sober living homes and similar facilities, including permits, size, location and occupancy limits, with fines up to $1,000 per day per resident, until the law expires June 1, 2028.

al:HB209|jury duty exemption for nursing.title: Jury duty; exemption for nursing mothers
al:HB209|jury duty exemption for nursing.summary: Lets a nursing mother be excused from jury duty if she gives the court a written statement that she is nursing and a birth certificate or similar record for the child; she may be recalled for service after 24 months.

al:HB372|elmore county to levy a county.title: Elmore County; to levy a county rental tax; provide distribution of proceeds from tax
al:HB372|elmore county to levy a county.summary: Levies an Elmore County tax on renting or leasing goods, excluding registered vehicles, starting September 1, 2025, with the county rate set by a formula tied to a 9.5% combined rate, and sends proceeds 90% to infrastructure and 10% to economic development.

al:HB488|town of cusseta in chambers cou.title: Town of Cusseta in Chambers County, corporate limits altered
al:HB488|town of cusseta in chambers cou.summary: Expands the town limits of Cusseta in Chambers County to include several additional parcels of land, including tracts of about 452 and 170 acres.

al:HB360|drug courts name changed to acc.title: Drug courts; name changed to "accountability courts," eligibility expanded to include veterans and individuals with mental illness, duties of Administrative Office of Courts further provided for
al:HB360|drug courts name changed to acc.summary: Renames drug courts as accountability courts and expands them to serve offenders whose crimes involved mental illness and veterans with substance abuse or mental health conditions, and directs the Administrative Office of Courts to set policies for running them.

al:HB325|volunteer fire departments prov.title: Volunteer Fire Departments; provide means to establish and administer fire districts
al:HB325|volunteer fire departments prov.summary: Lets the Lawrence County Commission form volunteer fire districts and lets those districts charge annual fire protection fees on homes and businesses if approved by district voters, collected with property taxes and spent only on fire and emergency services.

al:HB371|elmore county to create motor v.title: Elmore County, to create motor vehicle and watercraft registration fees and provide for distribution of funds.
al:HB371|elmore county to create motor v.summary: Adds a $25 Elmore County fee on each motor vehicle registration, transfer or renewal starting January 1, 2026, rising $1 each year, with 95% going to infrastructure and 5% to economic development.

al:HB238|convicted felons restrictions o.title: Convicted felons; restrictions on obtaining occupational licenses by convicted felons revised; certificate of employability for convicted felons created; immunity to employers provided
al:HB238|convicted felons restrictions o.summary: Creates a presumption that people granted a court order of limited relief are fit for occupational licenses, sets a process to ask licensing boards whether a conviction disqualifies them, creates parole certificates of employability, and shields employers who hire such people from some negligent-hiring suits.

al:SB376|mobile county city of semmes an.title: Mobile County, City of Semmes annexation
al:SB376|mobile county city of semmes an.summary: Expands the city limits of Semmes in Mobile County to include several additional parcels of land, effective October 1, 2026.

al:SB379|madison county city of owens cr.title: Madison County, City of Owens Cross Roads annexation
al:SB379|madison county city of owens cr.summary: Expands the city limits of Owens Cross Roads in Madison County to include additional land, effective October 1, 2026.

al:HB646|mobile county city of semmes an.title: Mobile County, City of Semmes annexation
al:HB646|mobile county city of semmes an.summary: Expands the city limits of Semmes in Mobile County to include several additional parcels of land, effective October 1, 2026.

al:HB635|choctaw county ad valorem taxes.title: Choctaw County; ad valorem taxes, county commission authorized to increase, proceeds provided for
al:HB635|choctaw county ad valorem taxes.summary: Lets the Choctaw County Commission, with approval of county voters, raise property taxes by up to five mills for up to five years to pay for specific road and bridge projects, and borrow against that revenue.

al:HB639|escambia county municipalities.title: Escambia County, municipalities authorized to operate an automated photographic speeding enforcement system, jurisdiction of civil fines for violations provided for
al:HB639|escambia county municipalities.summary: Lets cities in Escambia County use officer-operated speed cameras in school and construction zones, with mailed civil fines up to $195, at least $10 of each going to school or zone safety, and hearings in municipal court.

al:HB498|city of prichard public nuisanc.title: City of Prichard; public nuisance defined, city enforcement authorized, procedures provided for
al:HB498|city of prichard public nuisanc.summary: Lets Prichard declare overgrown weeds, dumped debris and inoperable vehicles kept in public view on private property for 30 days to be public nuisances, order owners to remove them, with a hearing on request, and clear unabated sites, billing costs as a property-tax lien.

al:HB500|mobile county constable number.title: Mobile County; constable, number, territory, and qualifications amended
al:HB500|mobile county constable number.summary: Sets three constables for each state House district in Mobile County starting with terms that begin in 2029, and requires each constable to live in and be a voter of the district served, contingent on a general law allowing such local changes.

al:HB501|mobile county city of prichard.title: Mobile County; City of Prichard, business improvement districts authorized
al:HB501|mobile county city of prichard.summary: Lets the Prichard City Council create self-help business improvement districts when 60 percent of affected business owners petition, funded by assessments on those businesses capped at 4 percent of gross revenue, with public hearings, renewal and dissolution procedures.

al:HB622|city of jemison draft beer auth.title: City of Jemison; draft beer, authorization to sell amended
al:HB622|city of jemison draft beer auth.summary: Lets the Jemison City Council allow licensed retailers to sell draft beer, including for off-premises consumption in growlers, kegs or similar containers.

al:HB624|wilcox county probate recording.title: Wilcox County; probate recording fee, increased
al:HB624|wilcox county probate recording.summary: Raises the special recording fee charged by the Wilcox County probate judge on property and other recorded documents from $5 to $10, starting June 1, 2026, and repeals two older local probate fee laws.

al:HB625|cleburne county business person.title: Cleburne County; business personal property tax returns, electronic filing authorized
al:HB625|cleburne county business person.summary: Lets the Cleburne County revenue commissioner set up electronic filing of business personal property tax returns and, starting October 1, 2026, require it for leasing businesses, businesses with $10,000 or more in such property, and returns prepared by third-party preparers.

al:HB629|mobile county town of mt vernon.title: Mobile County; Town of Mt. Vernon annexation
al:HB629|mobile county town of mt vernon.summary: Extends the town limits of Mt. Vernon in Mobile County to take in four listed parcels, including a lot in the East Park Subdivision and lots in the Calvert Business Park.

al:SB343|mobile county temporary judges.title: Mobile County; temporary judges of probate, appointment amended
al:SB343|mobile county temporary judges.summary: Keeps the Mobile County probate judge's power to appoint temporary probate judges for up to 90 days at a time and 100 days a year by removing an end date tied to the judge serving in 2007.

al:SB346|mobile county local privilege t.title: Mobile County; local privilege tax on historical horse racing, levied
al:SB346|mobile county local privilege t.summary: As introduced, levies an 8 percent Mobile County privilege tax on net gambling revenue from historical horse racing machines, collected by the county racing commission, replacing other local taxes on that wagering but not on greyhound or simulcast racing.

al:HB169|department of archives and hist.title: Department of Archives and History; composition of board and method of filling board vacancies further provided for, retroactive effect
al:HB169|department of archives and hist.summary: Reshapes the state Archives and History board into 16 appointed seats plus the governor: seven by congressional district and one at-large named by the governor, four by the House speaker and four by the Senate president pro tem, replacing the board's self-appointment of members.

al:HB584|public education screen based i.title: Public education; screen-based instruction limited in kindergarten through fifth grade, State Board of Education required to adopt standards, Instructional Technology Task Force established
al:HB584|public education screen based i.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to set standards limiting screen-based instruction from kindergarten through 12th grade to a supplement to teacher-led teaching, with vision breaks and exceptions, and creates a task force to recommend those standards.

al:HB611|winston county lodging tax auth.title: Winston County, lodging tax authorized, fire protection fee imposed, collection and distribution provided, referendum provided
al:HB611|winston county lodging tax auth.summary: Lets Winston County levy an 8 percent lodging tax, split among roads and bridges, the sheriff, tourism and county debt, and imposes a $5 per night fee for volunteer fire departments, if county voters approve both in a referendum.

al:HB432|montgomery county probate judge.title: Montgomery County; probate judge, additional fee authorized for celebrating rites of matrimony
al:HB432|montgomery county probate judge.summary: Lets the Montgomery County probate judge charge an additional reasonable fee, beyond the existing state fee, for performing marriage ceremonies, with the fee kept by the judge or designee who performs the ceremony.

al:HB569|autauga county taxes additional.title: Autauga County; taxes, additional sales and use tax authorized, rental tax established
al:HB569|autauga county taxes additional.summary: Levies an extra half-cent sales and use tax and a 3 percent tax on renting or leasing personal property in Autauga County starting September 1, 2026, with the money going to the county general fund.

al:HB576|mobile county temporary judges.title: Mobile County; temporary judges of probate, appointment amended
al:HB576|mobile county temporary judges.summary: Keeps the Mobile County probate judge's power to appoint temporary probate judges for up to 90 days at a time and 100 days a year by removing an end date tied to the judge serving in 2007.

al:HB587|talladega county service of pro.title: Talladega County, service of process fee for service by sheriff established, collection and disposition provided for
al:HB587|talladega county service of pro.summary: Sets a $50 fee for the Talladega County sheriff to serve court papers in out-of-state cases, and $100 for serving inmates at the federal prison in Talladega, with the money going to a sheriff's account for law enforcement.

al:SB241|walker county temporary probate.title: Walker County; temporary probate judges, authorized
al:SB241|walker county temporary probate.summary: Lets the Walker County probate judge appoint lawyers who live in the county as temporary probate judges for up to 90 days at a time and 200 days a year, paid $50 per hearing from the judge's discretionary funds.

al:SB295|montgomery county probate judge.title: Montgomery County; probate judge, compensation revised
al:SB295|montgomery county probate judge.summary: Sets the annual salary of the Montgomery County probate judge in office on June 1, 2025, at $153,725 beginning October 1, 2026, in place of any other salary.

al:SB324|tallapoosa county remote access.title: Tallapoosa County;  remote access of records fee authorized
al:SB324|tallapoosa county remote access.summary: Lets the Tallapoosa County probate judge charge a fee for remote electronic access to probate office records, to be spent on the office and its technology, and ratifies such fees collected before the law took effect.

al:SB339|crenshaw county authorize law e.title: Crenshaw County; authorize law enforcement to take individual with mental illness into protective custody under certain conditions; legal immunity provided
al:SB339|crenshaw county authorize law e.summary: Lets officers from law enforcement agencies designated by the Crenshaw County sheriff take a person believed mentally ill and an immediate danger into protective custody for transport to a hospital, without counting it as an arrest, and gives those acting under it state-agent immunity.

al:HB521|board of registrars background.title: Board of Registrars; background checks required, authorize pay during emergencies, qualification for compensation during holidays and emergencies specified
al:HB521|board of registrars background.summary: Requires applicants for county voter registrar posts to undergo state and national fingerprint background checks at their own cost, pays registrars when offices close for declared emergencies, and lets registrars keep their details other than name off the public voter list.

al:HB100|lauderdale county sheriff autho.title: Lauderdale County, sheriff, authorized to use credit or debit cards, procedures
al:HB100|lauderdale county sheriff autho.summary: Lets the Lauderdale County sheriff use office credit or debit cards for approved purchases under written policies setting spending limits, card security, record-keeping and full monthly payment, with any card rewards going to the sheriff's discretionary account.

al:HB433|talladega county distribution o.title: Talladega County, distribution of special county sales and use tax further provided for
al:HB433|talladega county distribution o.summary: Changes Talladega County's special sales tax distribution so the economic development authority advises the local House delegation, which gets sole discretion over the water line and North Talladega County water shares, and lets the law enforcement share pay salaries.

al:HB522|cullman county county commissio.title: Cullman County; county commission, meeting time amended
al:HB522|cullman county county commissio.summary: Removes the requirement that the Cullman County Commission hold at least one monthly meeting after 6 p.m., instead requiring meetings as set by general law with posted dates, times and places, and lets it change regular meeting days by resolution and call special meetings.

al:HB532|shelby county sale of solid was.title: Shelby County; sale of solid waste commodities authorized, distribution of proceeds provided for
al:HB532|shelby county sale of solid was.summary: Lets the Shelby County Commission sell gas, minerals or other commodities produced by its landfill under competitively bid contracts of up to 20 years, with proceeds going to the county general fund for solid waste and other lawful uses.

al:HB536|henry county sheriff compensati.title: Henry County; sheriff, compensation revised
al:HB536|henry county sheriff compensati.summary: Brings the Henry County sheriff's total pay to $94,000 a year starting June 1, 2026, makes that the base salary from January 18, 2027, adds an 8 percent raise for each successive term won, and bars the sheriff from general county-official pay raises.

al:HB543|lawrence county sheriff use of.title: Lawrence County; sheriff, use of credit card or debit card authorized
al:HB543|lawrence county sheriff use of.summary: Lets the Lawrence County sheriff use office credit or debit cards for approved purchases under written spending, security and record-keeping policies, paid from the sheriff's discretionary fund except travel, which may come from the general fund budget.

al:HB546|incarceration to provide requir.title: Incarceration; to provide required time periods in the administration of the Lawrence County Community Corrections and Court Services Fund
al:HB546|incarceration to provide requir.summary: Changes Lawrence County community corrections fund rules so surpluses and city participation run on the fiscal year, gives court clerks 30 days instead of 10 to send the fund its 10 percent of bond deposits, and repeals a 1979 work-release law.

al:HB557|wilcox county ad valorem taxes.title: Wilcox County; ad valorem taxes, additional tax established
al:HB557|wilcox county ad valorem taxes.summary: Lets Wilcox County, if voters approve, raise a county property tax by 9 mills starting with the 2027 tax year to replace an expiring tax, with no net rate increase; 2 mills go to the county and 7 to schools.

al:HB374|montgomery county probate judge.title: Montgomery County; probate judge, compensation revised
al:HB374|montgomery county probate judge.summary: Sets the annual salary of the Montgomery County probate judge in office on June 1, 2025, at $153,725 beginning October 1, 2026, in place of any other salary.

al:HB430|montgomery county judge of prob.title: Montgomery County; judge of probate, fundraising activities authorized
al:HB430|montgomery county judge of prob.summary: Lets the Montgomery County probate judge hold fundraising events, such as rodeos, and use the proceeds for any lawful purpose related to running the probate office, and ratifies any such fundraising already done.

al:HB447|montgomery county judge of prob.title: Montgomery County; judge of probate, authorized to register wills
al:HB447|montgomery county judge of prob.summary: Lets Montgomery County residents file their wills with the county probate judge, who keeps a public docket of filings while keeping the wills themselves confidential until death, and may charge a reasonable filing fee.

al:HB451|montgomery county judge of prob.title: Montgomery County; judge of probate, credit card use authorized
al:HB451|montgomery county judge of prob.summary: Lets the Montgomery County probate judge use an office credit card for approved purchases under written policies setting per-purchase and monthly limits, access controls, record-keeping and full monthly payment, with any card rewards deposited in the probate judge's fund.

al:HB514|tuscaloosa county sheriff compe.title: Tuscaloosa County; sheriff, compensation revised
al:HB514|tuscaloosa county sheriff compe.summary: Gives the Tuscaloosa County sheriff an additional $36,000-a-year expense allowance from the county general fund starting June 1, 2026, counted as pay for retirement purposes and ending at the next vacancy in the office.

al:SB314|morgan county municipal utiliti.title: Morgan County; Municipal Utilities Board of Decatur, scope of operating parameters
al:SB314|morgan county municipal utiliti.summary: Requires the Municipal Utilities Board of Decatur to run the city's electric, gas, water and wastewater utilities in a way that encourages expansion and economic growth in their service areas, and rewords the board's existing management powers, effective October 1, 2026.

al:HB452|income taxes state income tax c.title: Income taxes, state income tax credit for qualified rehabilitation expenses of certified historic properties extended, annual credit amount increased
al:HB452|income taxes state income tax c.summary: Extends Alabama's income tax credit for rehabilitating certified historic buildings through 2032, raises the credit to 30% of qualified costs for projects in counties under 175,000 people for 2028–2032, and raises the program's total cap from $200 million to $300 million.

al:SB202|montgomery county sheriff expen.title: Montgomery County; sheriff; expense allowance and salary
al:SB202|montgomery county sheriff expen.summary: Raises pay for a Montgomery County sheriff who has served two consecutive full terms, increasing the extra expense allowance from $20,000 to $70,000 a year and, starting next term, the salary from $175,000 to $225,000.

al:SB299|barbour county coroner mileage.title: Barbour County; coroner, mileage rate revised
al:SB299|barbour county coroner mileage.summary: Changes the Barbour County coroner's mileage reimbursement from 50 cents per mile to the IRS business-use rate, starting October 1, 2026, while keeping a monthly expense allowance of up to $400 set by the county commission.

al:SB312|marshall county volunteer fire.title: Marshall County; volunteer fire districts, annexation of new areas, application of fire service fee, enforcement
al:SB312|marshall county volunteer fire.summary: Lets the Marshall County Commission annex areas into existing volunteer fire districts by petition, applies fire service fees to mobile homes, tiny homes, connected RVs and each separate unit, and adds a $25 late fee, citations and monthly public fee reports.

al:HB422|russell county distribution of.title: Russell County; distribution of county share of state gasoline excise tax to municipalities in county, repealed
al:HB422|russell county distribution of.summary: Repeals a 1969 law that required Russell County to share part of its state gasoline tax revenue with the cities and towns in the county, effective October 1, 2025.

al:HB301|choctaw county constable office.title: Choctaw County, constable office abolished next term
al:HB301|choctaw county constable office.summary: Abolishes the office of constable in each Choctaw County precinct, effective when the terms of constables serving on June 1, 2025, end.
