al:HB378|pickens county motor vehicle ta.title: Pickens County, motor vehicle tags, additional issuance fees, earmarked for ambulance service, referendum
al:HB378|pickens county motor vehicle ta.summary: Lets the Pickens County Commission add a $10 fee on each vehicle tag registration, renewal, transfer or replacement, with proceeds used only for county ambulance service, if county voters approve it in a referendum at the 2026 primary election.

al:HB347|russell county office of consta.title: Russell County, office of constable, abolished
al:HB347|russell county office of consta.summary: Abolishes the office of constable in each Russell County precinct, effective when the term of the constable serving on June 1, 2025, ends.

al:HB490|tallapoosa county compensation.title: Tallapoosa County; compensation of judge of probate and revenue commissioner revised
al:HB490|tallapoosa county compensation.summary: Sets total yearly pay for Tallapoosa County's revenue commissioner at $100,000 and probate judge at $106,000, paid through an expense allowance starting June 1, 2026, and as base salary starting with the next term.

al:HB491|tallapoosa county remote access.title: Tallapoosa County;  remote access of records fee authorized
al:HB491|tallapoosa county remote access.summary: Lets the Tallapoosa County probate judge charge a fee for remote electronic access to office records, deposits the money in a special fund for office operations and technology, and ratifies such fees collected in the past.

al:HB504|wilcox county probate mail fees.title: Wilcox County; probate mail fees, further provided
al:HB504|wilcox county probate mail fees.summary: Lets the Wilcox County Commission set an optional fee of up to $10 for mailing license plates or decals by priority mail, alongside the existing $3 mail order fee, and lets the probate judge charge up to $5 to mail other probate documents.

al:SB301|perry county new voting center.title: Perry County; new voting center established
al:SB301|perry county new voting center.summary: Establishes a new voting center for Perry County voters in Districts 1 through 4 at the new National Guard Armory building in Marion.

al:HB135|dale county lodging tax county.title: Dale County, lodging tax, county commission authority to increase levy, distribution for economic and tourism development, Sec. 45-23-243 amended
al:HB135|dale county lodging tax county.summary: Lets the Dale County Commission raise its lodging tax on hotel and other short-term room rentals from 2% to 4% of the room charge, with proceeds used only for economic and tourism development, and excludes RVs and campgrounds.

al:HB263|biological and neural data of i.title: Biological and neural data of individuals; certain disclosures, transfers, and use by a health and fitness app prohibited without express consent, Attorney General authorized to enforce, civil penalties provided
al:HB263|biological and neural data of i.summary: Bars health and fitness apps, without express consent and with exceptions, from transferring Alabama users' biological or neural data to third parties, using it beyond expected services or marketing with it; violations uncorrected 45 days after attorney general notice face fines up to $3,000 each.

al:HB479|coosa county probate judge sher.title: Coosa County; probate judge, sheriff, and revenue commissioner, salary and expense account provided for
al:HB479|coosa county probate judge sher.summary: Ties pay for Coosa County's probate judge to 70% of a district judge's salary starting October 1, 2026, and for the sheriff and revenue commissioner to 60%, paid through expense allowances until their new terms, and repeals the existing compensation law.

al:HB459|henry county disposition of spe.title: Henry County; disposition of special transaction fees further provided for
al:HB459|henry county disposition of spe.summary: Changes how Henry County's probate office transaction fee of up to $5 is split: the first $2 goes to a probate judge fund for records and equipment, the rest to the county general fund, and lets the judge transfer money to the general fund.

al:HB467|city of tallassee in elmore and.title: City of Tallassee in Elmore and Tallapoosa Counties; board of education compensation
al:HB467|city of tallassee in elmore and.summary: Lets Tallassee Board of Education members, by board vote, receive an expense allowance of up to $900 a month plus actual travel expenses, converting to a salary starting with the next term after June 1, 2026.

al:SB275|city of alabaster entertainment.title: City of Alabaster; entertainment districts authorized
al:SB275|city of alabaster entertainment.summary: Lets the Alabaster City Council create up to two entertainment districts, each no larger than half a mile square, where patrons may carry open alcoholic drinks from licensed bars and restaurants outside, with hours and penalties set by city ordinance.

al:SB276|city of alabaster weed nuisance.title: City of Alabaster; weed nuisance, abatement authorized, procedures established
al:SB276|city of alabaster weed nuisance.summary: Creates a process for Alabaster to order owners to clear nuisance weeds and plants within 14 to 28 days, with a hearing and court appeal; if not done, the city may clear them and charge the cost as a lien collected with property taxes.

al:HB413|tuscaloosa county longevity pay.title: Tuscaloosa County; longevity pay for sheriff, tax assessor, and tax collector provided for
al:HB413|tuscaloosa county longevity pay.summary: Makes the Tuscaloosa County sheriff, tax assessor and tax collector eligible for the same longevity pay given to full-time county employees, starting June 1, 2026, with the county commission setting the amount and payment date.

al:HB439|escambia county qualifications.title: Escambia County; qualifications of the sheriff further provided for
al:HB439|escambia county qualifications.summary: Changes Escambia County sheriff qualifications starting June 1, 2026: candidates out of certified law enforcement for over one year, instead of two, must be recertified, and anyone who has retired needs three years of post-retirement law enforcement service.

al:HB440|escambia county probate court f.title: Escambia County; probate court fees further provided for
al:HB440|escambia county probate court f.summary: Sets specific Escambia County probate court fees, including $105 to probate a will or administer an estate, $145 for guardianship or conservatorship, $125 for adoption and $65 for a name change, starting October 1, 2026.

al:HB441|escambia county sheriff authori.title: Escambia County; sheriff authorized to contract with municipalities to provide police services
al:HB441|escambia county sheriff authori.summary: Lets Escambia County towns contract with the county sheriff for police services, paid for by the town and approved by the sheriff and county commission, and lets the commission pay the sheriff a supplemental salary for the extra duties.

al:HB442|escambia county cigarette and b.title: Escambia County, cigarette and beer taxes further provided for
al:HB442|escambia county cigarette and b.summary: Raises the monthly cap on Escambia County inspector salaries and expenses under its cigarette and beer tax law from $450 to $1,200, paid from the county general fund and reimbursed, sets a separate $500 cap for beer tax inspectors, and repeals a 1953 beer tax law.

al:HB408|city of alabaster entertainment.title: City of Alabaster; entertainment districts authorized
al:HB408|city of alabaster entertainment.summary: Lets the Alabaster City Council create up to two entertainment districts, each no larger than half a mile square, where patrons may carry open alcoholic drinks from licensed bars and restaurants outside, with hours and penalties set by city ordinance.

al:HB409|city of alabaster weed nuisance.title: City of Alabaster; weed nuisance, abatement authorized, procedures established
al:HB409|city of alabaster weed nuisance.summary: Lets the City of Alabaster order property owners to clear nuisance weeds and plants within 14 days (up to 28), with a right to a hearing and court appeal, and lets the city do the work and collect its costs as a property-tax lien.

al:HB412|board of registrars expense all.title: Board of Registrars; expense allowance limit removed, amount set by county commission
al:HB412|board of registrars expense all.summary: Ends the $15-per-day expense allowance for Limestone County Board of Registrars members and instead lets the county commission set the allowance amount by resolution, starting October 1, 2026.

al:HB416|cleburne county cleburne county.title: Cleburne County; Cleburne County Economic Development Authority, established
al:HB416|cleburne county cleburne county.summary: Creates the Cleburne County Economic Development Authority, run by a five-member unpaid board appointed by county commissioners, with industrial development powers such as issuing bonds and buying or leasing property; local tax breaks require approval by the taxing government.

al:HB365|talladega county sheriff compen.title: Talladega County; sheriff, compensation revised
al:HB365|talladega county sheriff compen.summary: Sets the Talladega County sheriff's salary at $112,000 a year starting January 18, 2027, keeps the current salary until then plus a $15,200.32 yearly expense allowance, and repeals earlier local laws on the sheriff's pay.

al:HB383|tuscaloosa county county employ.title: Tuscaloosa County; county employees, probationary period required for new employees, part-time employees authorized
al:HB383|tuscaloosa county county employ.summary: Requires newly hired Tuscaloosa County civil service employees to serve a 12-month probationary period, lets the county civil service board adopt rules for hiring part-time employees, and repeals an older provision on temporary employees.

al:HB384|tuscaloosa county service of pr.title: Tuscaloosa County; service of process fee for personal service amended
al:HB384|tuscaloosa county service of pr.summary: Applies Tuscaloosa County's $60 per-document fee for sheriff's personal service of civil papers to mental health documents and orders from the probate office, which were previously exempt, and keeps $3 of each such fee for the probate office.

al:HB385|tuscaloosa county electronic fi.title: Tuscaloosa County; electronic filing of business personal property tax returns in the offices of the tax assessor and tax collector provided for
al:HB385|tuscaloosa county electronic fi.summary: Lets the Tuscaloosa County tax assessor and tax collector set up electronic filing of business personal property tax returns and, starting October 1, 2026, require it for leasing businesses, businesses with $10,000 or more in such property, and paid preparers.

al:HB386|elmore county pistol permit fee.title: Elmore County; pistol permit fee, revised
al:HB386|elmore county pistol permit fee.summary: Sets the Elmore County pistol permit issuance fee at $20 in place of an additional $20 charged on top of other fees, with $1 going to the county general fund and $19 to the sheriff's law enforcement fund.

al:HB366|randolph county compensation of.title: Randolph County; compensation of judge of probate and revenue commissioner revised
al:HB366|randolph county compensation of.summary: Sets annual salaries of $70,000 for the Randolph County revenue commissioner, starting with the next term, and for the Randolph County probate judge, starting October 1, 2027, with both eligible for cost-of-living raises given to other county officers.

al:HB367|randolph county booking fee est.title: Randolph County; booking fee, established
al:HB367|randolph county booking fee est.summary: Creates a $30 booking fee in Randolph County charged to defendants booked into the county jail who are convicted or plead guilty, collected with court costs and sent to the sheriff's law enforcement fund.

al:HB368|randolph county county commissi.title: Randolph County; county commission, terms staggered
al:HB368|randolph county county commissi.summary: Staggers Randolph County Commission terms: in the 2028 general election, members for Districts 1, 3, and 5 are elected to two-year terms and the others to four-year terms, with all later terms lasting four years.

al:HB369|randolph county distribution of.title: Randolph County; distribution of county tobacco tax further provided for
al:HB369|randolph county distribution of.summary: Directs the 24 percent share of Randolph County's tobacco tax set aside for economic development and tourism to be paid to the Randolph County Economic Development Authority, leaving the other shares unchanged.

al:HB175|income tax credit for donation.title: Income tax; credit for donation to food banks.
al:HB175|income tax credit for donation.summary: Creates a state income tax credit, for tax years 2027 through 2031, for farmers and food businesses that donate edible farm products to qualifying food banks, worth 15 percent of the donation's value up to $5,000, capped at $2 million a year statewide.

al:HB355|houston county temporary judge.title: Houston County; temporary judge of probate service period extended, compensation of temporary probate judge revised
al:HB355|houston county temporary judge.summary: Lets Houston County temporary probate judges be appointed for 180-day periods instead of 90 days, changes the existing 200-day yearly cap to count days presiding over hearings rather than days served, and raises their pay from $50 to $100 per hearing.

al:HB356|houston county related to sale.title: Houston County; related to sale or redemption of lands
al:HB356|houston county related to sale.summary: Transfers the Houston County probate judge's duties for selling and redeeming land for unpaid taxes to the county revenue commissioner.

al:HB330|etowah county repeal of alterna.title: Etowah County; repeal of alternative method for filling vacancies of office
al:HB330|etowah county repeal of alterna.summary: Repeals an Etowah County law that set an alternative process for filling vacancies in county offices occurring more than one year before the term ends.

al:HB1|motor vehicles suspension of driv.title: Motor vehicles; suspension of driver license and ignition interlock device following first driving while under the influence conviction required
al:HB1|motor vehicles suspension of driv.summary: Requires drivers convicted of a first DUI to install an ignition interlock device and hold an interlock-restricted license, either after a 90-day suspension or while it is stayed, and lets them restore a regular license only after 180 days with the restricted license.

al:HB331|blount county lodging tax incre.title: Blount County, lodging tax increased, additional lodging tax levied, collection and distribution provided for
al:HB331|blount county lodging tax incre.summary: Lets Blount County add a 1 percent lodging tax on top of its existing 4 percent tax and levy a separate tax of up to $3 per room per night on stays under 30 days, with proceeds going to the county tourism fund.

al:SB175|marshall county abandoned and s.title: Marshall County; abandoned and stolen property, auction procedures revised
al:SB175|marshall county abandoned and s.summary: Lets the Marshall County sheriff sell unclaimed recovered property by internet auction as well as public auction, and adds rules for unclaimed firearms: after 12 months they may be destroyed or sold by sealed bid only to federally licensed gun dealers.

al:HB297|city of monroeville annexation.title: City of Monroeville; annexation of corporate limits
al:HB297|city of monroeville annexation.summary: Extends the City of Monroeville's limits to include the rights-of-way of stretches of State Highway 21, U.S. Highway 84, and State Highway 136.

al:HB89|medicaid providing presumptive e.title: Medicaid; providing presumptive eligibility to pregnant women
al:HB89|medicaid providing presumptive e.summary: Lets pregnant women whose household income appears to qualify receive Medicaid prenatal outpatient care for up to 60 days while their Medicaid application is pending, based on a qualified provider's determination; the program ends October 1, 2028.

al:HB119|fire protection fee extend requ.title: Fire protection fee; extend requirement to manufactured homes
al:HB119|fire protection fee extend requ.summary: Requires Mobile County fire districts that charge a residential service fee to collect it from owners of owner-occupied single-family homes, duplex and condo units, apartment buildings, house trailers and manufactured homes, and lots in RV or motor-home parks.

al:HB144|vestavia hills entertainment di.title: Vestavia Hills; entertainment districts, city council authorized to establish
al:HB144|vestavia hills entertainment di.summary: Lets the Vestavia Hills City Council create up to five entertainment districts where people may drink alcoholic beverages bought from licensed on-premises sellers anywhere within the district.

al:HB160|tuscaloosa county overtime comp.title: Tuscaloosa County; overtime compensation, public safety employees, further provided
al:HB160|tuscaloosa county overtime comp.summary: Lets full-time firefighters in Tuscaloosa County cities choose time-and-a-half comp time instead of overtime pay, and makes the City of Tuscaloosa's executive director of public safety ineligible for overtime pay or comp time for police or fire work.

al:HB199|town of morris in jefferson cou.title: Town of Morris in Jefferson County, corporate limits annexation
al:HB199|town of morris in jefferson cou.summary: Extends the Town of Morris's limits in Jefferson County to include a described tract along Sardis Road.

al:HB234|jefferson county special reserv.title: Jefferson County; special reserve deputies, appointment and powers authorized
al:HB234|jefferson county special reserv.summary: Lets the Jefferson County sheriff, when writs pile up, appoint certified officers not on the sheriff's staff as special reserve deputies to serve property seizure writs, paid directly by the requesting party a fee of up to $250 per writ.

al:SB64|marshall county custodian of vot.title: Marshall County; custodian of voting tabulators, selection committee, salary increased, duties clarified
al:SB64|marshall county custodian of vot.summary: Raises the salary of Marshall County's custodian of voting tabulators from $8,900 to $27,000 a year starting July 1, 2026, changes who sits on the committee that appoints the custodian, lists the custodian's duties, and doubles the required bond to $20,000.

al:HB82|baldwin county annexation of the.title: Baldwin County, annexation of the City of Daphne
al:HB82|baldwin county annexation of the.summary: Extends the City of Daphne's limits in Baldwin County to include several described tracts of land, including an area bounded by County Road 54, County Road 64 and Rigsby Road.

al:HB202|baldwin county town of magnolia.title: Baldwin County; Town of Magnolia Springs, corporate limits altered
al:HB202|baldwin county town of magnolia.summary: Extends the Town of Magnolia Springs's limits in Baldwin County to include a described tract north of U.S. Highway 98.

al:HB57|pickens county city of carrollto.title: Pickens County; City of Carrollton, annexation
al:HB57|pickens county city of carrollto.summary: Extends the City of Carrollton's limits in Pickens County to include described parcels along the Carrollton-Pine Grove Mississippi State Line Road.

al:HB112|st clair county compensation re.title: St. Clair County; compensation revised for sheriff, judge of probate, revenue commissioner, chair and members of the county commission
al:HB112|st clair county compensation re.summary: Sets new pay for St. Clair County officials starting June 1, 2026: $160,000 a year for the sheriff, $130,000 each for the probate judge, revenue commissioner and county commission chair, and $45,000 for other commissioners, later converted to base salaries.

al:HB133|lamar county privilege license.title: Lamar County; privilege license tax, distribution of proceeds revised
al:HB133|lamar county privilege license.summary: Removes the requirement that Lamar County's half of its one-cent privilege license tax for roads be split equally among the four commission districts, letting the county use it for road construction and maintenance generally. Half still goes to county schools. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB134|lamar county disposition of per.title: Lamar County; disposition of personal property; process revised, online auctions authorized, public notice requirement revised
al:HB134|lamar county disposition of per.summary: Lets Lamar County auction surplus personal property online without advertising it, drops the once-a-year limit on auctions, and cuts required advertising for other sales from four weeks to two. Also removes the felony penalty for violating the county's property-sale rules.

al:HB184|henry county coroner and deputy.title: Henry County; coroner and deputy coroner, expenses further provided for
al:HB184|henry county coroner and deputy.summary: Lets the Henry County Commission give the coroner and deputy coroner a county vehicle with equipment, cover fuel and repairs including through a county gas card, and reimburse their costs for state-required training.

al:HB193|marshall county custodian of vo.title: Marshall County; custodian of voting tabulators, selection committee, salary increased, duties clarified
al:HB193|marshall county custodian of vo.summary: Raises the pay of Marshall County's custodian of voting tabulators from $8,900 to $27,000 a year starting July 1, 2026, changes who sits on the committee that appoints the custodian, lists the custodian's election duties, and doubles the required bond to $20,000.

al:HB194|marshall county compensation of.title: Marshall County; compensation of the county revenue commissioner
al:HB194|marshall county compensation of.summary: Raises the annual salary of the Marshall County revenue commissioner from $67,500 to $106,781 beginning with the next term of office, paid from the county general fund.

al:HB200|escambia county authorizing add.title: Escambia County; authorizing additional motor vehicle license and registration tax
al:HB200|escambia county authorizing add.summary: Lets the Escambia County Commission add a yearly fee of up to $5 on each vehicle registration, transfer or renewal starting with the 2027 registration year, with the money going to the sheriff's law enforcement fund.

al:HB201|escambia county sheriff authori.title: Escambia County; sheriff authorized to establish procedures for use of credit or debit card
al:HB201|escambia county sheriff authori.summary: Lets the Escambia County sheriff make purchases with an office credit or debit card after adopting written rules on spending limits, card access, record keeping and full monthly payment. Card rewards go to the sheriff's discretionary account.

al:HB203|henry county henry county sheri.title: Henry County; Henry County Sheriff's Office and Henry County Task Force, authorized to sell, use, and destroy certain abandoned, stolen, and unclaimed property
al:HB203|henry county henry county sheri.summary: Lets the Henry County sheriff auction, including online, abandoned or stolen property unclaimed for six months, after public notice, holding proceeds six months for owners before they go to the sheriff's fund for law enforcement use. Unclaimed firearms may be kept for sheriff's office use or destroyed if unsafe or unlawful.

al:HB204|henry county county lodging tax.title: Henry County; county lodging tax further provided for
al:HB204|henry county county lodging tax.summary: Extends Henry County's lodging tax of up to 4 percent so it can also apply to stays at recreational vehicle parks, along with hotels, motels and other short-term rentals.

al:HB205|henry county southeast alabama.title: Henry County; Southeast Alabama Human Development Council abolished, transfer of duties provided for
al:HB205|henry county southeast alabama.summary: Abolishes the Southeast Alabama Human Development Council in Henry County and transfers its duties to the Alabama Department of Youth Services.

al:HB87|marengo county coroner and deput.title: Marengo County; coroner and deputy coroner, compensation and travel expense
al:HB87|marengo county coroner and deput.summary: Raises the Marengo County coroner's expense allowance from $400 to $1,000 a month starting June 1, 2025, lets the county commission authorize a deputy coroner with an allowance, and lets the commission set and later raise both officials' mileage and expense allowances.

al:SB256|mobile county amend definition.title: Mobile County; amend definition of municipal tax lien to authorize the inclusion of certain weed liens on a tax bill under certain circumstances; deem municipality as prevailing party in certain bid auctions resulting in a tie; authorize municipality to enter property to make repairs under certain circumstances; and authorize tax collecting official to sell a tax lien under certain circumstances.
al:SB256|mobile county amend definition.summary: Lets Class 2 cities enter properties on which they hold tax lien certificates to make repairs serving a public purpose, without adding the cost to the owner's redemption price, and buy tax liens unsold after three auctions for the best price offered, with two required notices before foreclosing.

al:SB319|barbour county new court costs.title: Barbour County, new court costs and disbursement of fees provided for following referendum
al:SB319|barbour county new court costs.summary: Adds, if Barbour County voters approve in a referendum, a $25 court fee on civil cases and on criminal and traffic convictions and a $10 fee on small claims cases, funding hazardous duty pay for nonclerical sheriff's office employees who perform hazardous duties, excluding the sheriff.

al:SB326|sheriff use of credit card or d.title: Sheriff, use of credit card or debit card authorized
al:SB326|sheriff use of credit card or d.summary: Lets the Jackson County sheriff make purchases with an office credit or debit card after adopting written rules on spending limits, card access, record keeping and full monthly payment. Card rewards go to the sheriff's discretionary account.

al:SB328|jackson county probate judge sa.title: Jackson County Probate Judge, salary revised
al:SB328|jackson county probate judge sa.summary: Sets the Jackson County probate judge's salary at $132,000 a year starting October 1, 2025, in place of other pay and allowances, and gives the judge the same across-the-board raises granted to county employees.

al:HB46|physicians rural physicians inco.title: Physicians, rural physicians income tax credit, replace existing credit
al:HB46|physicians rural physicians inco.summary: Ends Alabama's $5,000 rural physician income tax credit after 2025 and replaces it with a $10,000-a-year credit for up to four years, for 2026 through 2030, for doctors who live and practice in rural communities and are newly practicing there or returning.

al:SB293|lee county to further provide f.title: Lee County; to further provide for solid waste collection fees
al:SB293|lee county to further provide f.summary: Lets the Lee County Commission exempt households with incomes at or below 75 percent of the federal poverty level from mandatory garbage collection fees, and adopt rules to carry this out.

al:SB128|calhoun county sheriff increase.title: Calhoun County, sheriff increase
al:SB128|calhoun county sheriff increase.summary: Gives the Calhoun County sheriff an added expense allowance of $13,966 a year starting June 1, 2025, and sets the sheriff's base salary at $114,290 a year starting January 18, 2027, in place of all other allowances.

al:HB283|data privacy processing of data.title: Data privacy, processing of data regulated, consumer actions related to data authorized
al:HB283|data privacy processing of data.summary: Gives consumers rights to access, correct, delete and copy their personal data and opt out of its sale, targeted ads and automated profiling, at businesses handling data on over 50,000 consumers (25,000 if over a quarter of revenue is from data sales), exempting non-selling firms under 500 employees. The attorney general enforces it, fining up to $10,000 per uncorrected violation.

al:SB288|barbour county compensation of.title: Barbour County, compensation of supernumerary revenue commissioner provided for, retroactive effect
al:SB288|barbour county compensation of.summary: Sets the salary of Barbour County's supernumerary (retired) revenue commissioner at $37,125 a year starting October 1, 2025, and approves any compensation paid before that date.

al:SB298|city of florence in lauderdale.title: City of Florence in Lauderdale County, corporate limits altered
al:SB298|city of florence in lauderdale.summary: Expands the city limits of Florence in Lauderdale County to take in a 60-foot strip along Gresham Road between Alabama Highway 133 and County Road 61.

al:HB540|randolph county distribution of.title: Randolph County, distribution of county tobacco tax further provided for
al:HB540|randolph county distribution of.summary: Changes how Randolph County's tobacco tax is shared: the 24 percent share that went to the county industrial development council is to be used for tourism or economic development in the county, and the 10 percent agriculture share goes to the Randolph County Agricultural Center.

al:SB221|mobile county compensation of j.title: Mobile County, compensation of judge of probate further provided for
al:SB221|mobile county compensation of j.summary: Keeps the Mobile County probate judge's current base salary and adds a $49,000-a-year expense allowance starting June 1, 2025, folding it into salary in 2031, and gives the judge the same across-the-board raises granted to county employees.

al:SB224|mobile county electronic monito.title: Mobile County, electronic monitoring further provided for
al:SB224|mobile county electronic monito.summary: Makes the Mobile County sheriff responsible for all electronic monitoring of pretrial defendants in the county's circuit, bars contracting it out, and lets the sheriff set and collect fees from people in monitoring programs, deposited in the county general fund.

al:SB46|class 2 municipalities scrap tir.title: Class 2 municipalities, scrap tires, enforcement of Scrap Tire Environmental Quality Act, jurisdiction of municipality court, criminal penalties
al:SB46|class 2 municipalities scrap tir.summary: Lets Class 2 cities sign agreements with the state environmental agency to enforce scrap tire laws locally, gives their municipal courts jurisdiction over violations, and makes illegally storing, processing or transporting scrap tires misdemeanors there.

al:SB219|clay county authorize sheriff t.title: Clay County; authorize sheriff to dispose of certain abandoned, stolen or unclaimed property and firearms
al:SB219|clay county authorize sheriff t.summary: Lets the Clay County sheriff auction, including online, abandoned or stolen property unclaimed for six months after public notice, and sell unclaimed firearms to licensed gun dealers by sealed bid or destroy them. Owners can reclaim property before sale; net proceeds go to the sheriff's office.

al:SB220|clay county sheriff authorized.title: Clay County; sheriff, authorized to conduct fundraising events, use of proceeds for sheriff's office
al:SB220|clay county sheriff authorized.summary: Lets the Clay County sheriff hold fundraising events and use the proceeds for any lawful purpose of the sheriff's office, and approves past actions taken that way.

al:SB235|etowah county fiduciary respons.title: Etowah County, fiduciary responsibility for Mega Sports Complex Authority immediately transferred to the City of Rainbow City and upon full payment of outstanding debts, assets of authority transferred to Rainbow City
al:SB235|etowah county fiduciary respons.summary: Transfers financial control of the Etowah County Mega Sports Complex Authority, including its tax revenue and obligations, to the City of Rainbow City starting October 1, 2025, and dissolves the authority once its 2022 debts are paid, moving its assets to the city.

al:SB238|coffee county town of kinston s.title: Coffee County, Town of Kinston, speeding enforcement, automated photo enforcement as civil violations, civil penalties, appeal procedures
al:SB238|coffee county town of kinston s.summary: Lets the Town of Kinston in Coffee County use speed cameras to issue civil tickets, fines up to $100 plus court costs, to vehicle owners for driving more than 10 mph over the limit, with hearings in municipal court and appeals to circuit court.

al:SB239|coffee county sheriff authorize.title: Coffee County, sheriff authorized to contract with municipalities to provide police services
al:SB239|coffee county sheriff authorize.summary: Lets towns in Coffee County contract with the county sheriff for police services, with the town paying the county for the officers and equipment agreed on; each contract needs approval from the sheriff and the county commission.

al:SB261|probate judge salary revised.title: Probate judge, salary revised
al:SB261|probate judge salary revised.summary: Sets the Bibb County probate judge's salary, if the judge is a lawyer, at 80% of a starting state district judge's pay plus the same raises district judges get, retroactive to January 1, 2021.

al:HB429|monroe county special county pr.title: Monroe County, special county privilege license tax further provided for
al:HB429|monroe county special county pr.summary: Extends a Monroe County business privilege license tax that was set to end once the new jail's debt is paid; afterward, the money goes to the county general fund for the jail, ambulance service or 911.

al:HB453|colbert county pistol permit fe.title: Colbert County, pistol permit fees further provided for
al:HB453|colbert county pistol permit fe.summary: Adds five-year Colbert County pistol permits costing $75, or $25 for people 60 and older, alongside one-year permits that stay at $15 and $5, with the fees going to the sheriff's law enforcement pistol permit fund.

al:HB455|clarke county coroner expenses.title: Clarke County, coroner, expenses further provided for
al:HB455|clarke county coroner expenses.summary: Lets the Clarke County Commission pay the coroner's office operating expenses, including mileage for personal vehicles or a county vehicle, and approves such payments the commission already made.

al:HB457|clarke county sheriffs expense.title: Clarke county, sheriffs, expense allowance and salary provided for
al:HB457|clarke county sheriffs expense.summary: Gives the Clarke County sheriff a $32,500 yearly expense allowance, which becomes a $32,500 salary increase starting with the sheriff's next term.

al:HB458|clarke county county commission.title: Clarke County, county commissioners, expense allowance and salary provided for
al:HB458|clarke county county commission.summary: Gives each Clarke County commissioner an $8,000 yearly expense allowance, which becomes an $8,000 salary increase starting with each commissioner's next term.

al:HB348|russell county probate recordin.title: Russell County, probate recording fee, further provided
al:HB348|russell county probate recordin.summary: Lets the Russell County Commission set the probate office recording fee on filed documents and marriage licenses at up to $10, replacing the fixed $5 fee and its two-year renewal votes; the money stays dedicated to modernizing probate records.

al:HB349|russell county sheriff salary f.title: Russell County; sheriff, salary further provided
al:HB349|russell county sheriff salary f.summary: Raises the Russell County sheriff's annual salary from $120,000 to $135,000, paid in the same manner as other county employees and in place of any other salary, effective June 1, 2025.

al:SB127|calhoun county authorizes the c.title: Calhoun County, authorizes the county commission to increase the compensation of the board of registrars
al:SB127|calhoun county authorizes the c.summary: Lets the Calhoun County Commission, by resolution, raise the $15-a-day extra pay that members of the county board of registrars receive for days they work.

al:HB299|choctaw county court cost in ci.title: Choctaw County, court cost in circuit court, district court, municipal court, district for county jail
al:HB299|choctaw county court cost in ci.summary: Adds a $50 court cost to civil and criminal cases in Choctaw County courts ($25 in small claims), with the money going to a fund to run, repair and pay off the county jail; takes effect only if voters approve a local constitutional amendment.

al:HB300|choctaw county probate court ad.title: Choctaw County, probate court, additional filing fees on deeds and mortgages, distribution for office of the judge of probate
al:HB300|choctaw county probate court ad.summary: Adds a $10 fee for each deed or mortgage document recorded in the Choctaw County probate office, with the money going to a new fund the probate judge uses to run the office, including digitizing records and technology.

al:SB162|marshall county tennessee valle.title: Marshall County; Tennessee Valley Authority in-lieu-of-tax payments distribution
al:SB162|marshall county tennessee valle.summary: Changes how Marshall County splits its Tennessee Valley Authority payments in place of taxes, including raising the economic development office's minimum to $247,000, shifting ambulance money from Arab to Boaz, and adding $25,000 for Snead State Community College.

al:HB313|houston county compensation of.title: Houston County, compensation of sheriff and coroner further provided for
al:HB313|houston county compensation of.summary: Sets the Houston County sheriff's salary at $150,000 and the coroner's at $22,000 a year starting June 1, 2025, with the same raises other county employees receive, and repeals the earlier pay laws for both offices.

al:HB314|sheriff to authorize use of cre.title: Sheriff, to authorize use of credit card or debit card
al:HB314|sheriff to authorize use of cre.summary: Lets the Houston County sheriff use office credit or debit cards for approved purchases under written rules, including spending limits, record keeping, monthly review and full monthly payment, without spending beyond appropriated funds.

al:HB226|homestead exemptions extending.title: Homestead exemptions, extending to unremarried widow or widower
al:HB226|homestead exemptions extending.summary: Extends existing property tax exemptions for homes of people who are over 65, disabled or blind to their unremarried widow or widower, for the same home, if the survivor's name is on the deed.

al:HB24|volunteer rescue squad tuition r.title: Volunteer Rescue Squad Tuition Reimbursement Program; to permit regional EMS agencies to participate in education instruction
al:HB24|volunteer rescue squad tuition r.summary: Lets the state health department's regional emergency medical services agencies teach courses under the tuition repayment program for volunteer rescue, fire and ambulance workers, with a cap on repayments for those courses and training standards for their instructors.

al:HB251|sex offenders restrictions for.title: Sex offenders, restrictions for certain sex offenders further provided
al:HB251|sex offenders restrictions for.summary: Lets parole or probation officers bar adult sex offenders convicted of offenses involving a child from using post office boxes or internet-connected devices, lets courts or the parole board require sex offender treatment with polygraph tests, and makes violations a felony.

al:HB220|sheriff to authorize use of cre.title: Sheriff, to authorize use of credit card or debit card
al:HB220|sheriff to authorize use of cre.summary: Lets the St. Clair County sheriff use office credit or debit cards for approved purchases under written rules, including spending limits, record keeping, monthly review and full monthly payment, without spending beyond appropriated funds.

al:HB221|st clair county further provide.title: St. Clair County, further provides for the compensation of the revenue commissioner
al:HB221|st clair county further provide.summary: Gives the St. Clair County revenue commissioner an extra $375 monthly expense allowance starting June 1, 2025, and, beginning with the next term of office after October 1, 2027, sets the commissioner's salary equal to the probate judge's, replacing the allowances.

al:HB223|st clair county cost of living.title: St. Clair County, cost-of-living payment
al:HB223|st clair county cost of living.summary: Lets the St. Clair County Commission give former sheriffs and revenue commissioners in supernumerary (retired) office the same cost-of-living raises or lump-sum payments it approves for county retirees in the state retirement system.

al:HB254|st clair county mental health o.title: St. Clair County; mental health officer, powers and duties further provided
al:HB254|st clair county mental health o.summary: Revises St. Clair County's mental health officer program, setting how officers are hired and supervised, and has officers assess people police believe are mentally ill and dangerous, who may be taken to a mental health facility and referred for commitment.

al:HB294|etowah county etowah county dru.title: Etowah County; Etowah County Drug Enforcement Unit, authorized to sell, use, and destroy certain abandoned, stolen, and unclaimed property
al:HB294|etowah county etowah county dru.summary: Lets the Etowah County Drug Enforcement Unit auction abandoned or stolen property unclaimed for six months, keeping proceeds for owners another six months before using them for law enforcement, and keep or destroy unclaimed firearms.

al:SB36|competitive bidding contract pro.title: Competitive bidding; contract protest procedures revised; requirements for submitting disclosure statements revised
al:SB36|competitive bidding contract pro.summary: Cuts the deadline to protest state contract bids from 14 to 5 days, puts volunteer fire departments and rescue squads under local bid laws, raises when disclosure statements are required, and exempts publicly traded companies and economic development incentives.

al:HB101|sheriff to authorize use of cre.title: Sheriff, to authorize use of credit card or debit card
al:HB101|sheriff to authorize use of cre.summary: Lets the Mobile County sheriff use office credit or debit cards for approved purchases under written rules, including spending limits, record keeping, monthly review and full monthly payment, without spending beyond appropriated funds.

al:HB210|calhoun county coroner s compen.title: Calhoun County, coroner's compensation further provided for
al:HB210|calhoun county coroner s compen.summary: Raises the Calhoun County coroner's expense allowance from $5,000 to $20,000 a year starting June 1, 2025, sets the coroner's base salary at $54,750 starting January 18, 2027, and raises assistant coroners' pay to $6,100.

al:HB213|calhoun county authorizes the c.title: Calhoun County, authorizes the county commission to increase the compensation of the board of registrars
al:HB213|calhoun county authorizes the c.summary: Lets the Calhoun County Commission, by resolution, raise the $15-a-day extra pay that members of the county board of registrars receive for days they work.

al:HB76|fayette county authorized the sh.title: Fayette County, authorized the sheriff and commissioner of licenses to obtain and use a credit card
al:HB76|fayette county authorized the sh.summary: Lets the Fayette County sheriff use an office credit card for approved purchases under written rules, including spending limits, record keeping, monthly review and full monthly payment.

al:HB98|lauderdale county sheriff author.title: Lauderdale County, sheriff, authorized to conduct fundraising events, including rodeos
al:HB98|lauderdale county sheriff author.summary: Lets the Lauderdale County sheriff hold fundraising events, such as rodeos, and use the proceeds for the sheriff's office, and approves such past actions.

al:HB99|lauderdale county revenue commis.title: Lauderdale County, revenue commissioner, business personal property returns, authorized to provide for electronic filing
al:HB99|lauderdale county revenue commis.summary: Lets the Lauderdale County revenue commissioner set up electronic filing of business personal property tax returns and, starting October 1, 2025, require it for leasing businesses, businesses with $10,000 or more in property, and paid preparers.

al:SB87|board of midwifery revise powers.title: Board of Midwifery; revise powers
al:SB87|board of midwifery revise powers.summary: Lets the State Board of Midwifery accept gifts and grants, and lets licensed midwives perform a heel-prick newborn screening test within 72 hours of birth but bars them from interpreting results, which go to a physician, or otherwise caring for newborns except in emergencies.

al:SB16|taxation sleep in heavenly peace.title: Taxation, Sleep in Heavenly Peace Inc., exempt from sales and use tax
al:SB16|taxation sleep in heavenly peace.summary: Exempts Sleep in Heavenly Peace, Inc. from state sales and use taxes from October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2029, and lets counties and cities exempt it from their local sales and use taxes.

al:SB28|retired state employees work as.title: Retired state employees; work as law enforcement officer or assistant district attorney authorized
al:SB28|retired state employees work as.summary: Lets certain retirees with at least 25 years of service, rising to 30 by 2031, keep retirement pay while earning up to $52,000 a year as sheriff's deputies, city police officers or assistant district attorneys; lets retirees work as full-time bus drivers; and extends the program through 2032.

al:SB177|health to require that coverage.title: Health; to require that coverage for breast cancer screening be provided without charging an insured a deductible or copayment
al:SB177|health to require that coverage.summary: Bars health plans in Alabama that cover supplemental or diagnostic breast exams, such as breast MRI, ultrasound or diagnostic mammography, from charging patients a deductible, copayment or coinsurance for them, starting January 1, 2027.

al:SB92|public k 12 schools cell phone p.title: Public K-12 schools, cell phone policy and Internet/social media safety
al:SB92|public k 12 schools cell phone p.summary: Creates the FOCUS Act, barring students from using phones and other wireless devices at public schools during the instructional day and requiring devices to be off and stored, with exceptions; requiring internet safety policies; and requiring a social media safety course before eighth grade.

al:SB190|health care policies eliminate.title: Health care policies; eliminate cost-sharing for prostate screening coverage of high risk men
al:SB190|health care policies eliminate.summary: Bars deductibles and other cost-sharing for prostate cancer screening of men over 50 and of high-risk men over 40, including African American men and men whose close relative had prostate cancer, and changes required screening coverage from all men over 40 to those groups.

al:SB18|child support retroactivity prov.title: Child support, retroactivity provided for in certain circumstances
al:SB18|child support retroactivity prov.summary: Allows a child support order entered within a child's first year to be made retroactive to nine months before birth, but not if the child is not born alive, and removes the provision letting courts order fathers to pay pregnancy and childbirth expenses.

al:HB579|taxation tigers for tomorrow ex.title: Taxation; Tigers for Tomorrow Exotic Animal Preserve, Incorporated, exempt from sales and use taxes
al:HB579|taxation tigers for tomorrow ex.summary: Exempts Tigers for Tomorrow Exotic Animal Preserve, Incorporated, from state sales and use taxes starting September 1, 2026, and lets counties and cities exempt it from their local sales and use taxes.

al:HB353|public k 12 education advanced.title: Public K-12 education; Advanced Math Pathway created and provided for
al:HB353|public k 12 education advanced.summary: Requires the state Education Department to create an Advanced Math Pathway, requires local school boards to automatically enroll qualifying students, lets parents opt children in or out, requires student support, and requires annual reports to the Legislature.

al:HB278|firefighters and rescue squad m.title: Firefighters and rescue squad members, income tax credit for training under certain conditions expanded
al:HB278|firefighters and rescue squad m.summary: Makes permanent the $600 income tax credit for advanced volunteer firefighters and rescue squad members, replaces the $300 basic credit with a $400 credit starting in 2027, adds a $200 credit for first responders and fire support persons, and adds documentation requirements.

al:HB354|department of workforce workfor.title: Department of Workforce; workforce talent recruitment grant program established, eligibility provided for, and fund established
al:HB354|department of workforce workfor.summary: Creates a state workforce grant program and fund for cities, counties and certain nonprofits that pay out-of-state households earning at least the state median income to move to Alabama, requiring a 20% local match and withholding half of each grant until half the household goal is met.

al:HB426|real property creation of the a.title: Real property; creation of the Alabama Property Protection Act of 2026, title fraud prevention
al:HB426|real property creation of the a.summary: Creates the Alabama Property Protection Act of 2026, letting the Securities Commission investigate title fraud complaints, void fraudulent property transfers and pay victims from a recovery fund; requires seller identity and online listing ownership checks; speeds quiet title cases; and makes fraudulent home sales a felony.

al:HB102|disabled veteran license plates.title: Disabled veteran license plates; surviving spouses authorized to receive distinctive spouse's plate
al:HB102|disabled veteran license plates.summary: Lets the surviving spouse of a veteran who held a "Disabled Veteran" license plate be issued a distinctive "Disabled Veteran Spouse" license plate.

al:HB398|taxation to exempt high socks f.title: Taxation; to exempt High Socks for Hope from payment of state, county, and municipal sales and use taxes
al:HB398|taxation to exempt high socks f.summary: Exempts High Socks for Hope from state sales and use taxes starting September 1, 2026, and lets counties and cities exempt it from their local sales and use taxes.

al:HB106|crimes and offenses to further.title: Crimes and offenses; to further provide for the crime of doxing; to further provide for penalties
al:HB106|crimes and offenses to further.summary: As introduced, makes it a crime, a misdemeanor on first offense, to post someone's personal identifying information online intending others to harass or harm them even if no harm occurs, and makes doxing that causes harm, including to officers, firefighters or public servants, a felony.

al:HB468|local commissions and authoriti.title: Local commissions and authorities; prohibition on officers serving on commission or board of directors of authority removed for certain municipalities
al:HB468|local commissions and authoriti.summary: Lets towns of 7,500 or fewer residents allow city officials to serve on planning commissions, lets county commissions allow city officials on water, sewer and fire authority boards, and lets certain local officials serve on solid waste authorities.

al:HB123|taxation cook museum of natural.title: Taxation; Cook Museum of Natural Science and the McWane Science Center, exempt from sales and use taxes
al:HB123|taxation cook museum of natural.summary: Exempts the Cook Museum of Natural Science and the McWane Science Center from state sales and use taxes starting September 1, 2026, and lets counties and cities exempt them from their local sales and use taxes.

al:HB326|taxation most worshipful prince.title: Taxation, Most Worshipful Prince Hall Grand Lodge Free and Accepted Masons of Alabama and the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. and A.M. of Alabama, exempt from sales, county and municipal fees and taxes
al:HB326|taxation most worshipful prince.summary: Exempts the state's two Masonic grand lodges and all their subordinate lodges from state fees and taxes beginning October 1, 2027, lets counties and cities exempt them from local sales and use taxes, and requires an annual list of subordinate lodges.

al:HB425|regional mental health authorit.title: Regional Mental Health Authority Boards; to revise membership and qualifications
al:HB425|regional mental health authorit.summary: Requires most regional mental health authority boards' executive committees to include a sheriff or representative and a probate judge serving on the board unless they opt out, bars boards from adding director qualifications, and raises the quorum from three members to one-third of the board.

al:HB411|taxation auxiliary of big oak r.title: Taxation; Auxiliary of Big Oak Ranch, Inc., exempt from payment or collection of sales and use taxes
al:HB411|taxation auxiliary of big oak r.summary: Exempts the Auxiliary of Big Oak Ranch, Incorporated, from paying or collecting state sales and use taxes starting September 1, 2026, and lets counties and cities exempt it from their local sales and use taxes.

al:HB97|geographic information technolog.title: Geographic Information Technology; to recognize the Geographic Information Executive Council, the Geographic Information Program Office, the Advisory Committee, and to provide for coordination with the 911 Board
al:HB97|geographic information technolog.summary: Puts into state law the Alabama Geographic Information Executive Council, Program Office, state Geographic Information Officer and an advisory committee to coordinate statewide mapping data, and sets how they coordinate with the 911 Board on emergency mapping data.

al:HB295|military punishment ranks of me.title: Military punishment; ranks of members that may discipline and be disciplined, disciplinary measures; revised and further provided for
al:HB295|military punishment ranks of me.summary: Lets Alabama National Guard battalion-level commanders also impose minor punishments without a court-martial, adds reductions in grade, including up to two grades for enlisted members in grades E-5 through E-9, and lets special courts-martial reduce enlisted members up to E-9 to the lowest rank.

al:HB342|taxation participation in the f.title: Taxation; participation in the federal tax credit for individuals making qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations provided for
al:HB342|taxation participation in the f.summary: Opts Alabama into the federal tax credit for individuals who donate to scholarship granting organizations, requiring the Department of Revenue to submit and publish a yearly list of qualifying in-state organizations for tax years after 2026.

al:HB244|taxation energy use in commerci.title: Taxation; Energy use in commercial greenhouses, pivot irrigation systems, and poultry houses, exempt from utility gross receipts and utility service use tax
al:HB244|taxation energy use in commerci.summary: Expands the state utility gross receipts tax exclusion for energy used to heat poultry houses to cover all natural gas and electricity used in commercial greenhouses, pivot irrigation systems and poultry houses, adds a matching utility service use tax exclusion, and excludes hemp or cannabis production.

al:HB190|railroad modernization act of 2.title: Railroad Modernization Act of 2019, to increase the cap on income tax credits and extend the sunset date for five years through tax year 2032
al:HB190|railroad modernization act of 2.summary: Extends the railroad track rehabilitation income tax credit, equal to half of qualifying spending and capped at $4,100 per mile of track, through tax year 2032, allowing up to $4.5 million a year and $22.5 million total for 2028 through 2032.

al:HB107|motor vehicle registration mili.title: Motor vehicle registration; military combat action license plate, criminal penalty for falsely obtaining, established
al:HB107|motor vehicle registration mili.summary: Creates a distinctive license plate for veterans who received a combat action ribbon, badge or medal, starting January 1, 2027, and makes falsely obtaining or certifying someone for the plate a Class C misdemeanor.

al:HB228|pretrial detention hearings pro.title: Pretrial detention hearings; procedure revised
al:HB228|pretrial detention hearings pro.summary: Requires pretrial detention hearings for certain serious felonies to be set within 10 days of arrest, allows delays up to 21 days or longer on joint motion, holds defendants until then unless both sides agree on bail, requires recordings, and sends appeals to the Court of Criminal Appeals.

al:HB276|k 12 school athletics physicals.title: K-12 school athletics physicals; endorsements by certified registered nurse practitioners, nurse midwives, and assistants to physicians deemed endorsement by physician, athletic associations, clubs, or leagues prohibited from refusing to accept
al:HB276|k 12 school athletics physicals.summary: Treats a nurse practitioner's, nurse midwife's or physician assistant's signature on a school sports physical form as a physician's, and bars athletic associations, clubs and leagues from refusing forms signed that way.

al:HB33|driver licenses and learner perm.title: Driver licenses and learner permits; age in which the Alabama State Law Enforcement Agency may deny an application for failure to meet certain school enrollment and graduation criteria changed, accepted criteria further provided for
al:HB33|driver licenses and learner perm.summary: Lowers from 19 to 17 the age under which the state must deny a driver license or learner permit to applicants not meeting school enrollment, job training, employment or other criteria, and replaces the any-state diploma option with graduation from an Alabama high school.

al:HB35|state board of adjustment provid.title: State Board of Adjustment, provide death benefit to survivors of volunteer firefighters who die of cancer.
al:HB35|state board of adjustment provid.summary: As introduced, makes survivors of certified volunteer firefighters who die of certain cancers eligible for the state's line-of-duty death benefit paid by the State Board of Adjustment, and sets conditions and a standard of proof for claims.

al:HB165|higher education to require pub.title: Higher education, to require public colleges and universities to submit annual report on the amount of state and federal funds received and expended, and plans for operating if federal or state funding reduced
al:HB165|higher education to require pub.summary: Requires each public college and university to report yearly to the state budget office the state and federal money it received and spent, and its plans for operating if that funding falls 5% or 20%; budget committees must review the reports every other year.

al:HB37|crimes and offenses penalties fo.title: Crimes and offenses; penalties for eluding or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer, penalties further provided
al:HB37|crimes and offenses penalties fo.summary: Makes fleeing police a Class D felony instead of a misdemeanor, adds factors such as a child in the car, being on probation or striking at an officer that make it a higher felony, and sets 90- or 180-day minimum terms for repeat convictions within 10 years.

al:HB284|marshall county abandoned and s.title: Marshall County; abandoned and stolen property, auction procedures revised
al:HB284|marshall county abandoned and s.summary: Lets the Marshall County sheriff sell unclaimed abandoned or stolen property by online auction, and sets rules for unclaimed firearms: the sheriff must try to find owners and may sell them only to licensed gun dealers by sealed bid or destroy them after 12 months.

al:HB80|evictions law enforcement role n.title: Evictions, law enforcement role, notices to tenants
al:HB80|evictions law enforcement role n.summary: Requires eviction notices to warn tenants that belongings left behind may be removed and discarded, requires officers to post a 24-hour warning before executing a writ of possession and remove occupants, and shields officers and landlords from liability for property damage.

al:HB69|alabama department of environmen.title: Alabama Department of Environmental Management; water well drillers, license types and fees revised
al:HB69|alabama department of environmen.summary: Revises well-driller licensing, creating unrestricted and restricted licenses covering water, monitoring, geothermal and cathodic protection wells and pump work, replacing the $200 annual fee with $1,000 or $500 two-year licenses, requiring continuing education, and allowing rule-set well completion filing fees up to $1,000.

al:HB3|taxation to exempt certain retail.title: Taxation; to exempt certain retail sales of fish or other seafood from sales and use taxes
al:HB3|taxation to exempt certain retail.summary: Exempts from state sales and use tax the retail sale of unprocessed fish and seafood by licensed commercial fishermen or licensed vessel owners, and lets counties and cities exempt those sales from local sales taxes, starting September 1, 2026.

al:HB109|baldwin county ad valorem tax c.title: Baldwin County, ad valorem tax continued, constitutional amendment
al:HB109|baldwin county ad valorem tax c.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, subject to approval by voters in certain Baldwin County precincts, continuing an existing 2-mill property tax for public hospital purposes in those precincts for 20 years starting October 1, 2027.

al:HB28|taxation to establish an income.title: Taxation; to establish an income tax credit for oyster shell recycling
al:HB28|taxation to establish an income.summary: Creates a refundable income tax credit for restaurants and residents holding certain commercial seafood licenses that donate oyster shells to approved recycling programs: $1 per 50 pounds, up to $2,000 each and $100,000 a year statewide, for tax years 2027 through 2031.

al:HB145|taxation tobacco interstate war.title: Taxation; tobacco interstate warehouser permits required, penalties imposed for violations
al:HB145|taxation tobacco interstate war.summary: Creates a state permit, costing $2,000 initially and $500 a year, for interstate tobacco warehousers that buy from manufacturers and resell to Alabama-licensed wholesalers untaxed, lets those wholesalers buy and affix tax stamps, adds record-keeping rules and sets $1,000-per-violation penalties.

al:SB287|barbour county qualifications a.title: Barbour County, qualifications and training of sheriff further provided for
al:SB287|barbour county qualifications a.summary: Sets minimum qualifications for Barbour County sheriff, including one year of county residency, age 25 or older, at least five years as a certified law enforcement officer and no felony convictions, and requires the sheriff to complete 12 hours of executive training.

al:SB308|lee county county engineer func.title: Lee County; county engineer, functions, duties, and responsibilities, further provided
al:SB308|lee county county engineer func.summary: Revises the duties of the Lee County engineer, placing management of the county highway department, roads and bridges, staffing, budgeting and purchasing under the direction of the county commission or its designee.

al:SB338|madison county boundary lines a.title: Madison County, boundary lines and corporate limits of the City of New Hope further provided for
al:SB338|madison county boundary lines a.summary: Removes a strip of land along a mountain roadbed near Oak Grove Road from the city limits of New Hope in Madison County.

al:SB327|town of saint florian in lauder.title: Town of Saint Florian in Lauderdale County, corporate limits altered
al:SB327|town of saint florian in lauder.summary: Removes several described tracts of land from the town limits of Saint Florian in Lauderdale County.

al:SB331|barbour county compensation of.title: Barbour County, compensation of the judge of probate further provided for
al:SB331|barbour county compensation of.summary: Sets the Barbour County probate judge's salary, starting October 1, 2025, at 70% of a state district court judge's salary with equal years of service, replacing a commission-set salary, rising with district judges' pay, and requires the judge to waive voter-list report fees.

al:HB527|civil liability liability limit.title: Civil liability, liability limited for certain entities operating off-roading parks
al:HB527|civil liability liability limit.summary: Shields off-road park operators from liability for participants' injuries or deaths from the inherent risks of off-roading, except for cases such as faulty vehicles they provided, known hidden hazards or willful misconduct, if they post warnings and carry $1 million per-occurrence insurance.

al:HB449|crimes and offenses crimes of u.title: Crimes and offenses; crimes of unlawful use of DNA in the first, second, and third degree created, criminal penalties provided
al:HB449|crimes and offenses crimes of u.summary: Creates crimes for intentionally collecting, testing, disclosing or selling another person's DNA or genetic data without consent, ranging from a misdemeanor to a Class C felony, with exceptions for law enforcement, court orders, regulated genetic testing companies, health providers and universities.

al:HB526|alabama 21st century fund furth.title: Alabama 21st Century Fund, further distribution of funds, one-time appropriation to the Department of Commerce
al:HB526|alabama 21st century fund furth.summary: Lets 21st Century Fund money above 1.3 times the authority's maximum annual debt service pay economic development project costs and Alabama Incentives Financing Authority bond debt, and transfers $5 million to the Commerce Department for international offices, rural development and operating costs.

al:HB255|employees retirement system of.title: Employees' Retirement System of Alabama, State Police Tier II Plan  members paid for up to 80 hours unused annual leave over 480 hours per year
al:HB255|employees retirement system of.summary: Lets law enforcement officers of the Alabama State Law Enforcement Agency be paid for up to 10 days a year of unused annual leave above 60 days, a benefit the law previously tied to the former Department of Public Safety.

al:HB492|juvenile offenders delinquent a.title: Juvenile offenders, delinquent acts for purposes of juvenile proceedings further provided for
al:HB492|juvenile offenders delinquent a.summary: Provides that nonfelony traffic and boating offenses committed by 14- and 15-year-olds, other than driving or boating under the influence, are no longer treated as delinquent acts in juvenile court.

al:HB539|randolph county judge of probat.title: Randolph County, judge of probate, county commission, additional special transaction fee imposed
al:HB539|randolph county judge of probat.summary: Requires Randolph County to charge an extra $50 fee for each plat map recorded and copied in the probate office, with the money going to the county general fund for costs of processing, recording, digitizing and laminating maps.

al:HB486|baldwin county ad valorem tax f.title: Baldwin County, ad valorem tax further provided for, constitutional amendment
al:HB486|baldwin county ad valorem tax f.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, subject to approval by voters in certain Baldwin County precincts, continuing an existing 2-mill property tax for public hospital purposes in those precincts for 20 years starting October 1, 2027.

al:HB464|st clair county compensation an.title: St. Clair County, compensation and benefits of coroner further provided for, retroactive
al:HB464|st clair county compensation an.summary: Sets the St. Clair County coroner's total base pay at $3,450 a month through an added expense allowance, retroactive to March 1, 2025; makes that the base salary plus a $600 monthly expense allowance starting January 18, 2027; and repeals earlier coroner pay laws.

al:HB497|shelby county city of alabaster.title: Shelby County, City of Alabaster, plant nuisance abatement further provided for
al:HB497|shelby county city of alabaster.summary: Lets the City of Alabaster order property owners to clear nuisance plants within 14 to 28 days after notice, with a hearing and court appeal available, and lets the city do the work itself and charge the cost as a lien collected with property taxes.

al:HB462|alabama department of public he.title: Alabama Department of Public Health; to qualify military training and education for emergency medical services personnel licensure
al:HB462|alabama department of public he.summary: Requires the state health department to credit military education, training and experience, along with passing the national EMT registry exam, toward licensing as emergency medical services personnel.

al:HB399|lamar county disposition of per.title: Lamar County; disposition of personal property; process revised, online auctions authorized, public notice requirement revised
al:HB399|lamar county disposition of per.summary: Lets Lamar County sell surplus personal property at in-person or online auctions without a once-a-year limit, cuts advance notice for in-person auctions to two weeks, drops notice for online auctions and statewide ads for sealed bids, and repeals the felony penalty for violations.

al:HB271|alabama commission on higher ed.title: Alabama Commission on Higher Education and ReEngage Alabama Grant Program, minimum age of an adult learner decreased from 25 to 22; definition of eligible student expanded
al:HB271|alabama commission on higher ed.summary: Lowers the minimum age for the state ReEngage grant for returning adult college students from 25 to 22, and extends eligibility to students seeking a first bachelor's degree after a two-year break following their first associate degree.

al:HB324|sheriffs start of term of offic.title: Sheriffs, start of term of office further provided for
al:HB324|sheriffs start of term of offic.summary: Sets a sheriff's four-year term to begin at noon on the first Monday after the second Tuesday of January after the election, and ties county commissioners' term dates to the general law on county commissions.

al:HB387|sales tax on food limit on loca.title: Sales tax on food, limit on local rate reduction and growth requirement removed
al:HB387|sales tax on food limit on loca.summary: Removes the 25% cap on how much counties and cities may cut their local sales tax rate on food, and drops the requirement that their general fund grow more than 2% before making such a cut.

al:HB388|income tax exemption for taxabl.title: Income tax, exemption for taxable retirement income increased
al:HB388|income tax exemption for taxabl.summary: Raises the state income tax exemption for retirement income of people 65 and older from the first $6,000 to the first $12,000, starting January 1, 2026.

al:HB389|income tax optional standard de.title: Income tax, optional standard deduction increased, adjusted gross income range allowed for maximum dependent exemption increased
al:HB389|income tax optional standard de.summary: Raises the income tax standard deduction starting in 2026 (for example, from $8,500 to $9,500 for married couples filing jointly), raises the income level where it begins phasing down (to $28,000 for most filers), and raises dependent exemption income limits from $50,000 and $100,000 to $60,000 and $120,000.

al:HB322|post partum depression to provi.title: Post-partum depression; to provide for education and assessment
al:HB322|post partum depression to provi.summary: Requires the state health department to publish materials on postpartum depression for parents and health care providers, and requires doctors and other licensed providers giving postnatal or infant care to assess birth mothers for postpartum depression. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB274|county board of education term.title: County board of education; term of office changed from six to four years, local constitutional amendment proposed
al:HB274|county board of education term.summary: Proposes a local constitutional amendment shortening the terms of Crenshaw County Board of Education members from six years to four years, starting with the November 2026 election, if county voters approve it.

al:SB139|scottsboro municipal elections.title: Scottsboro, municipal elections for Mayor and City Council and City Board of Education extended for one additional year based on staggered terms
al:SB139|scottsboro municipal elections.summary: Extends the terms of Scottsboro's mayor, city council and city school board members by one year, moving their elections to 2027, 2029 and 2031, and sets runoff elections on the fourth Tuesday after a regular election when no candidate wins a majority.

al:HB96|accommodations for expanded nati.title: Accommodations for expanded National Signing Day activities
al:HB96|accommodations for expanded nati.summary: Requires public high schools to excuse students from class to take part in organized National Signing Day events for athletic scholarships, college commitments, apprenticeships and military enlistment, and to provide accommodations such as meeting space, seating and internet access.

al:HB167|motor vehicles unclaimed towing.title: Motor vehicles, unclaimed, towing, towing company may notify the Revenue Department on the Unclaimed/Abandoned Vehicle Portal immediately after towing
al:HB167|motor vehicles unclaimed towing.summary: Lets a towing company report a towed vehicle as unclaimed to the state Revenue Department's online portal immediately after towing it, rather than only after the vehicle is considered unclaimed. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB66|abuse and exploitation of an eld.title: Abuse and exploitation of an elder, effect of conviction on intestate succession, wills, joint assets, and other contractual obligations provided
al:HB66|abuse and exploitation of an eld.summary: Bars people convicted of first- or second-degree elder abuse or financial exploitation of an elderly person from inheriting from the victim, from keeping survivorship rights in jointly owned property or accounts, and from collecting life insurance or similar benefits tied to the victim.

al:HB214|school psychologist interstate.title: School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact
al:HB214|school psychologist interstate.summary: Enters Alabama into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact, letting school psychologists licensed in one member state obtain an equivalent license to work in schools in other member states without meeting duplicate licensing requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB222|pardons and paroles sharing of.title: Pardons and paroles, sharing of electronic monitoring data in certain circumstances authorized
al:HB222|pardons and paroles sharing of.summary: Lets the Board of Pardons and Paroles share electronic monitoring GPS data and related biometric data on people it supervises with police agencies that request it during an active investigation. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB92|state waters alabama seagrass re.title: State waters; Alabama Seagrass Restoration Task Force established to address seagrass loss
al:HB92|state waters alabama seagrass re.summary: Creates an Alabama Seagrass Restoration Task Force, co-chaired by the Dauphin Island Sea Lab director and the University of South Alabama president, to develop a 10-year plan and technologies for restoring coastal seagrass and report yearly to state leaders.

al:HB9|three cueing system prohibited in.title: Three cueing system prohibited in public K-12 education
al:HB9|three cueing system prohibited in.summary: Bars public K-12 schools from using reading materials based on the three-cueing system or visual memory to teach word reading, requires phonics-based structured literacy instead, and requires teacher preparation programs to meet the same standards, with violations publicly reported.

al:HB156|criminal procedure out of state.title: Criminal procedure, out-of-state warrants further provided for
al:HB156|criminal procedure out of state.summary: Lets police or private citizens arrest someone without a warrant on reasonable information that the person is charged in another state with a crime punishable by more than one year in prison, rather than only crimes punishable by death or life imprisonment.

al:SB10|tuscaloosa county levy of additi.title: Tuscaloosa County; levy of additional or increased county or municipal sales and use tax prohibited without approval by referendum, constitutional amendment
al:SB10|tuscaloosa county levy of additi.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment barring any new or increased county or city sales and use tax in Tuscaloosa County unless voters in the affected area approve it at a general election referendum, with published notice and at least two public hearings beforehand.

al:SB380|teachers retirement system long.title: Teachers' Retirement System, longevity bonus for certain retirees and beneficiaries
al:SB380|teachers retirement system long.summary: Gives retired teachers and other Teachers' Retirement System retirees and beneficiaries a one-time bonus in October 2026 of $1 per month for each year of service, for those who retired before May 1, 2026.

al:SB375|class 1 municipalities mayor co.title: Class 1 municipalities; mayor, compensation amended
al:SB375|class 1 municipalities mayor co.summary: Requires the city council of Class 1 cities, currently Birmingham, to set the mayor's salary at no less than $220,000 a year, unchanged during a term; raises the mayor's expense allowance from $1,833.33 to $8,000 a month; and repeals older mayoral salary and allowance laws.

al:SB371|madison county senior property.title: Madison County; senior property tax exemption authorized; constitutional amendment
al:SB371|madison county senior property.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment letting Madison County homeowners age 65 or older who have lived in their home at least five years freeze its assessed value for property taxes while they live there, starting October 1, 2027.

al:SB330|courts criminal procedure elect.title: Courts; criminal procedure, electronic means authorized to swear warrants and citations in certain circumstances, law enforcement officers authorized to administer oaths in certain circumstances
al:SB330|courts criminal procedure elect.summary: Lets judges and magistrates issue warrants for misdemeanors, traffic and city ordinance violations by video, phone or other remote means, lets officers swear to tickets remotely, and lets police officers administer oaths to other officers on misdemeanor complaints and tickets. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:SB237|ethics certain research and dev.title: Ethics, Certain research and development activities of public institutions of higher education not covered by ethics laws
al:SB237|ethics certain research and dev.summary: States that the state ethics law does not limit public colleges and universities, or their officials and employees, from accepting grants and contracts, doing research, licensing and commercializing intellectual property, or forming business entities to promote innovation.
