al:SB201|k 12 education schools with jun.title: K-12 education, schools with Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps (JROTC) required to offer to home schooled and private school students who are dependents of active duty military parents performing certain covered military service
al:SB201|k 12 education schools with jun.summary: Requires local school boards, starting in 2026-2027, to let home-schooled and private school students who live in the district and are dependents of parents on active military duty join public school JROTC programs; home-schooled students must enroll as nontraditional students.

al:SB266|covington county underground ca.title: Covington County; underground carbon dioxide prohibited; constitutional amendment
al:SB266|covington county underground ca.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment banning anyone from injecting, storing or sequestering carbon dioxide in underground wells in Covington County, including federally defined Class VI wells, if voters approve it.

al:SB251|tax abatement and tax incentive.title: Tax abatement and tax incentive programs, North American Industry Classification System Code references and definitions updated to latest terms
al:SB251|tax abatement and tax incentive.summary: Updates state tax abatement, tax incentive and research corridor laws to use the 2022 federal industry classification codes and to refer to the Commerce Department's current economic development plan instead of the outdated Accelerate Alabama plan, with technical wording changes.

al:SB83|guardianships and conservatorshi.title: Guardianships and conservatorships; notice requirements further provided for, procedures to remove proceeding to circuit court revised, duties of guardian ad litem of a minor further provided for and training required, court representative required to be appointed for allegedly incapacitated adults in certain circumstances, appointment of temporary or emergency guardian or conservator authorized in certain circumstances
al:SB83|guardianships and conservatorshi.summary: Revises guardianship and conservatorship cases: sets notice deadlines and rules for moving cases to circuit court, requires training for guardians ad litem, generally requires a court representative to investigate petitions, and lets courts appoint temporary or emergency guardians or conservators to prevent substantial harm.

al:SB212|fayette county senior property.title: Fayette County; senior property tax exemption authorized, constitutional amendment
al:SB212|fayette county senior property.summary: As introduced, proposes a constitutional amendment letting Fayette County homeowners age 65 or older who have lived in their home at least five years freeze its assessed value for property taxes while they live there, starting October 1, 2027.

al:SB180|board of pardons and paroles co.title: Board of Pardons and Paroles; commencement date changed to March 1
al:SB180|board of pardons and paroles co.summary: Moves the start of new six-year terms for Board of Pardons and Paroles members from July 1 to March 1, ending current members' terms on the last day of February after their sixth year. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:SB39|boards and commissions certain m.title: Boards and Commissions, certain members required to complete training
al:SB39|boards and commissions certain m.summary: Requires members of state boards and commissions subject to the Sunset Law to complete a board governance course of at least five hours from the state auditing agency, covering open meetings, travel and pay rules and audit issues, and to sign an ethics pledge.

al:SB131|county subdivisions developer t.title: County subdivisions; developer transfers to immediate family members, subdivision regulation exceptions limited to 24 months
al:SB131|county subdivisions developer t.summary: Limits the exemption from county subdivision rules for land transferred to an immediate family member, so that land resold to anyone outside the family within 24 months of the family transfer becomes subject to those rules. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:SB67|walker county constitutional ame.title: Walker County; constitutional amendment, age to qualify for election or appointment as judge of probate increased to age 75
al:SB67|walker county constitutional ame.summary: As introduced, proposes a constitutional amendment letting a person be elected or appointed Walker County probate judge if not over age 75 when qualifying for election or appointment.

al:SB318|service contracts terms defined.title: Service contracts; terms defined; certain disclosures in advertising required; disclosures of limitations of contracts further provided for
al:SB318|service contracts terms defined.summary: Requires ads for service contracts to disclose in bold, larger print any right of the provider to refund less than the cost of repair or replacement, and requires contracts to state such limits prominently. Takes effect January 1, 2026.

al:SB51|health insurers to set a minimum.title: Health insurers; to set a minimum reimbursement rate for ambulance services that are out-of-network.
al:SB51|health insurers to set a minimum.summary: Sets minimum insurer payments for ambulance services, at least 200% of 2025 Medicare rates in-network and the lesser of billed charges or 180% out-of-network; bars billing patients beyond in-network cost-sharing and requires insurers to pay providers directly, through June 1, 2029.

al:SB117|counties and municipalities pro.title: Counties and municipalities, provides for memorandums of understanding related to traffic enforcement
al:SB117|counties and municipalities pro.summary: Lets Class 1, 2 or 3 cities enter agreements with the sheriff and county commission on traffic enforcement, which may add extra fees on traffic violations in the city, paid to the sheriff's office for law enforcement use only. Takes effect June 1, 2025.

al:SB44|tuscaloosa county constitutional.title: Tuscaloosa County, Constitutional Amendment, sales and use tax, additional required to be approved by referendum in a general election
al:SB44|tuscaloosa county constitutional.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment barring any new or increased sales and use tax in Tuscaloosa County unless voters in the affected area approve it at a general election referendum, with published notice and at least two public hearings beforehand.

al:SB106|small estates summary distribut.title: Small Estates; summary distribution for small estates; amount increased; Probate Court authorized to manage process
al:SB106|small estates summary distribut.summary: Replaces the inflation-adjusted $25,000 cap on personal-property-only estates that can be distributed without a personal representative with the combined homestead, exempt-property and family allowances, has the probate judge order each person's share, and requires notice to Medicaid. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:SB165|candidates revise statement of.title: Candidates; revise statement of economic interests filing requirements
al:SB165|candidates revise statement of.summary: Requires candidates to file a statement of economic interests with the State Ethics Commission within five days after the candidacy deadline (independents, the first primary; municipal candidates, their qualifying deadline), and requires those with a current statement on file to show proof or refile.

al:SB22|alabama jobs act further provide.title: Alabama Jobs Act, further provides for recapture of incentives
al:SB22|alabama jobs act further provide.summary: Requires state jobs-incentive agreements to let the state take back incentives from a company found guilty of violating state human trafficking laws or federal child labor law. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB662|madison county city of owens cr.title: Madison County, City of Owens Cross Roads annexation
al:HB662|madison county city of owens cr.summary: Extends the city limits of Owens Cross Roads in Madison County to take in one described parcel of land. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB634|washington county lodging tax l.title: Washington County; lodging tax, levied and proceeds distributed
al:HB634|washington county lodging tax l.summary: Levies a 4% tax on hotel, motel and other short-term lodging charges in Washington County, collected by the county commission, with proceeds going to the county general fund. Takes effect September 1, 2026.

al:HB542|highways department of transpor.title: Highways; Department of Transportation required to reimburse certain utilities for required facility relocation, subject to conditions
al:HB542|highways department of transpor.summary: Requires the state, starting October 1, 2027, to reimburse utilities with over $250 million in annual gross income for road-project relocation costs, up to $500,000 per relocation and $10 million a year, sets a $20 million yearly minimum for smaller utilities' relocations, and requires an annual report.

al:HB335|jefferson county pistol permits.title: Jefferson County, pistol permits further provided for
al:HB335|jefferson county pistol permits.summary: Adds a five-year pistol carry permit in Jefferson County costing $37.50, alongside the existing $7.50-per-year permit, with fees split the same way among the county retirement system, sheriff's fund and legislative office fund. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB564|jefferson county noise ordinanc.title: Jefferson County; noise ordinance for unincorporated areas authorized
al:HB564|jefferson county noise ordinanc.summary: Lets the Jefferson County Commission ban noise disturbances, such as loud music, vehicles or constantly barking dogs, in unincorporated residential areas, with civil fines of up to $200, $600 and $1,800 for first, second and third violations.

al:HB606|baldwin county employees revise.title: Baldwin County Employees; revise appointments by county commission of contract employees
al:HB606|baldwin county employees revise.summary: Makes the Baldwin County Commission's appointment of contract employees such as the county administrator and county engineer optional rather than required, and drops the development and environmental director from that list. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB583|madison county compensation of.title: Madison County, compensation of the sheriff further provided for
al:HB583|madison county compensation of.summary: Sets a newly elected Madison County sheriff's base salary at $170,000 with 7.5% raises for successive re-elections, and raises the sitting sheriff's pay from $154,086.40 to $170,000 on June 1, 2025, and to $182,750 for a second successive term.

al:HB438|income tax to reinstate the inc.title: Income tax; to reinstate the income tax refund check-off for Victims of Crime and Leniency, Incorporated (VOCAL), and to repeal entities whose check-offs have been rescinded
al:HB438|income tax to reinstate the inc.summary: Restores the state income tax refund check-off that lets taxpayers donate to Victims of Crime and Leniency (VOCAL), removes check-offs for groups whose check-offs had been rescinded, and combines the remaining check-offs into one law.

al:HB394|taxation freedom quilting bee l.title: Taxation; Freedom Quilting Bee Legacy exempt from sales and use taxes
al:HB394|taxation freedom quilting bee l.summary: Exempts Freedom Quilting Bee Legacy from state sales and use taxes and lets counties and cities exempt it from their local sales and use taxes.

al:HB423|taxation goodwill industries of.title: Taxation; Goodwill Industries of the Southern Rivers, exempt from sales and use tax
al:HB423|taxation goodwill industries of.summary: Exempts Goodwill Industries of the Southern Rivers from state sales and use taxes and lets counties and cities exempt it from their local sales and use taxes.

al:HB281|uniform child custody jurisdict.title: Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction Enforcement Act; certain temporary emergency child custody determinations authorized to become final
al:HB281|uniform child custody jurisdict.summary: Makes a child custody order issued under a court's temporary emergency jurisdiction automatically final if no custody case is started within six months in a state that has jurisdiction, replacing the rule that the order must say so explicitly.

al:HB370|counties and municipalities com.title: Counties and municipalities; compensation of local officials, revised
al:HB370|counties and municipalities com.summary: Sets the base pay of county commissioners, probate judges, sheriffs and county tax officials at May 31, 2026 levels, excludes longevity and merit pay from a new official's starting pay, and bars county-wide raises for officials whose pay is tied to a state official's.

al:HB306|teacher certification military.title: Teacher certification; Military Veteran Temporary Teaching Certificate established
al:HB306|teacher certification military.summary: Creates a five-year, one-time Military Veteran Temporary Teaching Certificate for veterans with 48 months of honorable active duty, 60 college credits with at least a 2.5 GPA, a passing Praxis score and a superintendent's recommendation, and requires mentoring for them.

al:HB377|military graduate medical field.title: Military; graduate medical field courses added to educational benefits provided to eligible dependents of certain veterans, tuition cost limited
al:HB377|military graduate medical field.summary: Expands state education benefits for children and spouses of veterans who died, were disabled, went missing or were held as prisoners of war to cover graduate courses in a medical field, with tuition limited to the school's in-state rate.

al:HB243|crimes and offenses manslaughte.title: Crimes and offenses; manslaughter, criminally negligent homicide, and other motor vehicle crimes amended, restitution amended
al:HB243|crimes and offenses manslaughte.summary: Makes causing a death while driving a vehicle or boat under the influence manslaughter, a Class B felony, raises the penalty for leaving the scene of a crash causing serious injury or death to a Class B felony, and treats those harmed as victims entitled to restitution.

al:HB26|sex offenders restrictions for c.title: Sex offenders; restrictions for certain sex offenders further provided, Board of Pardons and Paroles authorized to adopt rules
al:HB26|sex offenders restrictions for c.summary: Lets parole or probation officers bar adult sex offenders convicted of offenses involving children from using post office boxes or internet-capable devices, lets courts or the parole board require treatment including polygraphs as a release condition, and makes violations a Class C felony.

al:HB136|emergency rules require governo.title: Emergency rules; require Governor to certify that circumstances exist to justify emergency rules
al:HB136|emergency rules require governo.summary: Requires the governor to certify that an immediate danger to public health, safety or welfare justifies an agency's emergency rule before the rule can take effect. Takes effect June 1, 2026.

al:HB343|state rural electrification aut.title: State rural electrification authorities and electric membership corporations; removes requirement for Department of Finance approval for issuance of bonds
al:HB343|state rural electrification aut.summary: Removes the requirement that state rural electrification authorities and electric membership corporations get Department of Finance approval before issuing bonds or other debt. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB130|teachers retirement system reop.title: Teachers' Retirement System, reopened to allow the purchase of credit for prior service rendered to the St. Clair County DAY Program, Incorporated
al:HB130|teachers retirement system reop.summary: Lets the St. Clair County DAY Program's governing body elect to have its employees join the Teachers' Retirement System and credit their prior service there, with the program paying employer contributions and prior-service costs. Takes effect June 1, 2026.

al:HB292|motor vehicles disability perce.title: Motor vehicles; disability percentage for disabled veteran's license plate revised
al:HB292|motor vehicles disability perce.summary: Lets veterans with a disability rating of at least 50%, rather than more than 50%, get a disabled veteran license plate. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

al:HB79|state board of pharmacy and empl.title: State Board of Pharmacy and Employers, prohibited from disciplining pharmacists who recommend off-label medical treatments
al:HB79|state board of pharmacy and empl.summary: Bars the Board of Pharmacy from disciplining pharmacists for recommending or filling prescriptions for off-label drug uses, bars employers and pharmacy benefit managers from retaliating against them for it, and lets pharmacists sue employers who do.

al:HB111|crimes and offenses human cloni.title: Crimes and offenses; human cloning prohibited, criminal penalties provided
al:HB111|crimes and offenses human cloni.summary: Makes performing, attempting or participating in human cloning, or shipping or receiving cloned embryos or cells for cloning, a Class C felony, while not restricting in vitro fertilization, fertility treatment or other research that does not involve human cloning.

al:HB114|surety bonds and motor fuel ass.title: Surety bonds and motor fuel assessments; filing period for new or replacement surety bonds extended, payment period for assessments on illegally imported or transported motor fuels extended
al:HB114|surety bonds and motor fuel ass.summary: Gives natural gas and motor fuel sellers, suppliers and distributors 60 days instead of 30 to file new or replacement surety bonds, and 60 days instead of 30 to pay state assessments on illegally imported or transported motor fuel.

al:HB11|youthful offender status to proh.title: Youthful offender status, to prohibit a judge from granting youthful offender status to any person who is 16 years of age and older and charged with capital murder or murder
al:HB11|youthful offender status to proh.summary: Bars youthful offender status for anyone 16 or older charged with capital murder or intentional murder, requiring adult trial unless the charge is reduced, and extends youthful offender eligibility to crimes committed before age 21 instead of before 19. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB93|civil procedure provisions of ag.title: Civil procedure, provisions of agreements that prohibit disclosure of certain acts of sexual abuse rendered unenforceable
al:HB93|civil procedure provisions of ag.summary: Makes any provision in a nondisclosure, settlement, employment or other agreement that bars someone from disclosing sexual abuse or related facts void, for agreements made or amended on or after October 1, 2026; other terms, such as compensation, are unaffected.

al:HB74|law enforcement officers retirem.title: Law enforcement officers; retirement, benefits provided
al:HB74|law enforcement officers retirem.summary: Requires county and city law enforcement agencies to give retiring officers in good standing their agency-issued badge, and lets agencies give them their service pistol or sell it to them at fair market price. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:HB50|imagination library of alabama p.title: Imagination Library of Alabama Program, Department of Early Childhood Education to administer through Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
al:HB50|imagination library of alabama p.summary: Creates a state program, run by the Department of Early Childhood Education with a nonprofit partner, that mails one free book a month to registered children from birth to age five through Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, with the state paying half the cost and local partners the rest.

al:SB345|geneva county section providing.title: Geneva County, section providing for compensation of superintendent of education, repealed
al:SB345|geneva county section providing.summary: Repeals the local law setting the pay of the Geneva County superintendent of education, effective June 1, 2025.

al:HJR273|the joint interim study commis.title: The Joint Interim Study Commission on PTSD in Law Enforcement Officers, created
al:HJR273|the joint interim study commis.summary: Creates a temporary joint study commission of state officials, legislative leaders and county and city associations to study how governments can better fund services for first responders with PTSD from a traumatic on-duty event, with a report due early in the 2026 session.

al:HB567|class 2 municipalities tax incr.title: Class 2 municipalities, tax increment districts further provided for
al:HB567|class 2 municipalities tax incr.summary: Lets Class 2 cities, like Class 3 cities, place up to 50% of their total taxable property value in tax increment financing districts, instead of the usual 10% limit.

al:HB589|jefferson county authority of t.title: Jefferson County, authority of the county building commissioner further provided for
al:HB589|jefferson county authority of t.summary: Lets Jefferson County use its zoning enforcement and building permit powers to protect public health and welfare, including against businesses or activities run in a way that threatens public health, and lets the building commissioner sue or join lawsuits over such violations.

al:HB590|winston county lodging tax levi.title: Winston County, lodging tax levied, collection and distribution provided for
al:HB590|winston county lodging tax levi.summary: Levies an 8% tax on hotel and other short-term lodging in Winston County, if approved by county voters, splitting the money among roads and bridges (55%), the sheriff (20%), volunteer fire departments (20%) and the county general fund (5%).

al:HB414|municipalities municipal audits.title: Municipalities, municipal audits further provided for
al:HB414|municipalities municipal audits.summary: Raises the spending thresholds for city audits: cities spending $500,000 or more a year need annual audits, those below need audits every two years, and those under $300,000 may file an annual report to state examiners instead.

al:HB537|criminal procedure provides tha.title: Criminal procedure, provides that an Aniah's Law hearing satisfies the right to a preliminary hearing
al:HB537|criminal procedure provides tha.summary: Provides that a pretrial detention hearing held under Aniah's Law, which lets courts deny bail for certain violent charges, satisfies a felony defendant's right to a preliminary hearing.

al:HB585|washington county compensation.title: Washington County, compensation of circuit clerk further provided for
al:HB585|washington county compensation.summary: Ends the Washington County circuit clerk's monthly county pay supplement, equal to 2% of the clerk's state pay, once the person holding the office on January 1, 2025, leaves it.

al:HB591|henry county county lodging tax.title: Henry County, county lodging tax further provided for
al:HB591|henry county county lodging tax.summary: Adds recreational vehicle parks to the places covered by Henry County's lodging tax of up to 4% of the charge for rooms or accommodations rented to short-term guests.

al:HB592|henry county southeast alabama.title: Henry County, Southeast Alabama Human Development Council abolished, transfer of duties provided for
al:HB592|henry county southeast alabama.summary: Abolishes the Southeast Alabama Human Development Council in Henry County and transfers its duties to the state Department of Youth Services, effective June 1, 2025.

al:HB595|madison county boundary lines a.title: Madison County, boundary lines and corporate limits of the City of New Hope further provided for
al:HB595|madison county boundary lines a.summary: Removes from the New Hope city limits in Madison County a strip of land extending 30 feet on each side of an existing mountain roadbed that runs down to Oak Grove Road.

al:HB601|escambia county deposit and use.title: Escambia County, deposit and use of monies by sheriff further provided for
al:HB601|escambia county deposit and use.summary: Combines the Escambia County sheriff's separate fee and process-service funds into one Sheriff's Law Enforcement Fund, to be audited annually by state examiners and used for law enforcement, public safety or community relations, and moves existing balances into it on October 1, 2025.

al:HB375|jefferson county pistol permits.title: Jefferson County, pistol permits further provided for
al:HB375|jefferson county pistol permits.summary: Adds a five-year pistol permit in Jefferson County for $37.50, alongside the existing $7.50 one-year permit, with the fee split among the same county funds as the one-year permit.

al:HB494|jefferson county compensation o.title: Jefferson County, compensation of tax collector and tax assessor further provided for
al:HB494|jefferson county compensation o.summary: Sets the base salaries of the Jefferson County tax assessor and tax collector, starting October 1, 2027, at 110% of the highest salary of any merit-system employee in their offices, adjusted yearly and never lowered, and removes outdated expense-allowance provisions.

al:HB510|temporary release program to re.title: Temporary release program; to revise periods for distributing monies and the effective date for opt-in by municipalities
al:HB510|temporary release program to re.summary: Changes Lawrence County's community corrections law: fiscal-year (not calendar-year) surpluses go to the county general fund only by a three-fourths commission vote, people charged with bailable non-capital offenses shall rather than may be released pending trial, clerks get 30 days instead of 10 to remit bond deposits, and a 1979 work release law is repealed.

al:HB570|pike county pistol permit fee f.title: Pike County, pistol permit fee further provided for
al:HB570|pike county pistol permit fee f.summary: Sets Pike County pistol permit fees at $20 for one year and $100 for five years, and sends the entire fee to the sheriff's law enforcement fund instead of splitting it with the county treasury.

al:HB571|escambia county cigarette and b.title: Escambia County, cigarette and beer taxes further provided for
al:HB571|escambia county cigarette and b.summary: Raises the monthly cap on what Escambia County may spend on inspectors enforcing its cigarette tax from $450 to $1,200, lets it spend up to $500 a month on beer tax inspectors, and repeals a 1953 local beer tax law.

al:HB572|escambia county county commissi.title: Escambia County, county commission authorized to levy an additional motor vehicle license and registration issuance fee, distributions of proceeds provided for
al:HB572|escambia county county commissi.summary: Lets the Escambia County Commission add an annual fee of up to $5 on vehicle registrations and renewals starting in 2026, with the money going to the Sheriff's Law Enforcement Fund.

al:HB573|escambia county qualifications.title: Escambia County, qualifications of the sheriff further provided for
al:HB573|escambia county qualifications.summary: Changes qualifications for Escambia County sheriff: candidates may be out of active law enforcement for no more than one year (rather than two) without recertification, and those who ever retired from law enforcement need three years of post-retirement service.

al:HB574|jackson county probate judge sa.title: Jackson County Probate Judge, salary revised
al:HB574|jackson county probate judge sa.summary: Sets the Jackson County probate judge's salary at $132,000 a year starting October 1, 2025, in place of all other pay and fees, plus any across-the-board raises given to county employees.

al:HB176|taxation sales tax exemptions s.title: Taxation, sales tax exemptions, sales and use tax exemption with local option provided for purchases of optical aids, including eyeglasses and contact lenses
al:HB176|taxation sales tax exemptions s.summary: Exempts prescribed eyeglasses, contact lenses and other vision aids from state sales and use tax starting September 1, 2025; counties and cities may extend the exemption to their own sales taxes.

al:HB472|state employees travel meal all.title: State employees, travel meal allowance further provided for
al:HB472|state employees travel meal all.summary: Raises the meal allowance for state employees on trips of six to 12 hours without an overnight stay from 15% to 17.5% of the regular daily travel allowance.

al:HB424|montgomery county sheriff expen.title: Montgomery County, sheriff, expense allowance and salary
al:HB424|montgomery county sheriff expen.summary: Raises the extra yearly expense allowance for a Montgomery County sheriff who has served two consecutive full terms from $20,000 to $70,000, and raises the future salary for such sheriffs from $175,000 to $225,000.

al:HB549|butler county sheriff fundraisi.title: Butler County, sheriff, fundraising events authorized
al:HB549|butler county sheriff fundraisi.summary: Lets the Butler County sheriff hold fundraising events, such as rodeos, and use the proceeds for any lawful purpose of the sheriff's office, and ratifies such past actions.

al:HB550|butler county levy of additiona.title: Butler County, levy of additional motor vehicle license and registration fee authorized
al:HB550|butler county levy of additiona.summary: Lets the Butler County Commission add an annual fee of up to $5.25 on vehicle registrations and renewals starting in 2026, split equally among the sheriff, the revenue commissioner and the probate judge.

al:HB551|butler county sheriff authorize.title: Butler County, sheriff authorized to sell surplus property
al:HB551|butler county sheriff authorize.summary: Lets the Butler County sheriff sell the office's surplus property, including vehicles, with the money going into a new audited fund for buying sheriff's vehicles and equipment.

al:HB552|covington county county excise.title: Covington County, county excise tax levied on vapor products, vaping devices, alternative nicotine products, and psychoactive cannabinoids
al:HB552|covington county county excise.summary: Levies a 5% Covington County tax on retail sales of vaping devices, vapor products, alternative nicotine products and hemp-derived psychoactive products such as delta-8 THC, with proceeds going to the county general fund and civil penalties of at least $250 for violations.

al:HB465|alabama emergency management ag.title: Alabama Emergency Management Agency; authorize to spend public funds on promotional materials
al:HB465|alabama emergency management ag.summary: Specifies that the state Emergency Management Agency director may use appropriated funds to buy items promoting the agency's work, including materials educating the public on emergency preparedness, and updates outdated wording in the law.

al:HB531|conecuh county commission autho.title: Conecuh County, commission authorized to levy motor vehicle license & registration tax, distribution provided for
al:HB531|conecuh county commission autho.summary: Lets the Conecuh County Commission add an annual fee of up to $12 on vehicle registrations and renewals starting June 1, 2025, with the money going to the Evergreen-Conecuh Health Care Authority, until the fee ends in 2040.

al:HB534|blount county lodging tax incre.title: Blount County, lodging tax increased, additional lodging tax levied, collection and distribution provided for
al:HB534|blount county lodging tax incre.summary: Lets Blount County levy an extra 1% lodging tax on top of its existing 4% tax, plus a new tax of up to $3 per room per night on stays under 30 days, with proceeds going to tourism, beautification, parks and covered bridges.

al:HB545|escambia county probate court f.title: Escambia County, probate court fees further provided for
al:HB545|escambia county probate court f.summary: Sets new Escambia County probate court fees starting October 1, 2025, including $105 to probate a will or open an estate administration, $145 for guardianships and conservatorships, $125 for adoptions, $65 for name changes and $35 to record a plat.

al:HB481|contracts for public works exem.title: Contracts for public works; exemptions further provided
al:HB481|contracts for public works exem.summary: Lets public works awarding authorities, including local school boards, buy and install materials or equipment through existing purchasing exemptions instead of public works bidding; school board installations must meet design, building code, bonding, competitive-bid and licensed-contractor requirements.

al:HB443|public utilities underground da.title: Public utilities; Underground Damage Prevention Program; certain statutory sunset clauses deleted
al:HB443|public utilities underground da.summary: Extends the scheduled end date of the state program that runs the call-before-you-dig notification system for underground utility lines from January 1, 2027, to January 1, 2035.

al:HB393|city of alabaster entertainment.title: City of Alabaster; entertainment districts authorized
al:HB393|city of alabaster entertainment.summary: Lets the Alabaster City Council create up to two entertainment districts, each no larger than a half mile square, where patrons of licensed bars and restaurants may carry open alcoholic drinks outside, with the city setting hours and penalties. Takes effect June 1, 2025.

al:HB446|baldwin county annexation the c.title: Baldwin County, annexation the City of Daphne
al:HB446|baldwin county annexation the c.summary: Extends the city limits of Daphne in Baldwin County to take in specified parcels of land described in the bill.

al:HB485|city of loxley in baldwin count.title: City of Loxley in Baldwin County, corporate limits altered
al:HB485|city of loxley in baldwin count.summary: Extends the city limits of Loxley in Baldwin County to take in specified parcels of land described in the bill.

al:HB396|taxation and revenue homestead.title: Taxation and Revenue; Homestead ad valorum taxes of certain veterans prohibited from inclusion in debt-to-income ratio
al:HB396|taxation and revenue homestead.summary: Requires county property tax officials to issue temporary homestead tax exemption certificates to 100% permanently disabled veterans on request, and bars loan closing officers from counting homestead property taxes in those veterans' debt-to-income ratio for a home mortgage once they hold one.

al:HB461|alabama educational television.title: Alabama Educational Television Foundation Authority, authorized to secure additional funds
al:HB461|alabama educational television.summary: Lets the Alabama Educational Television Foundation Authority spend money on fundraising, soliciting donations and otherwise seeking more funding, despite its ban on attempting to influence legislation, if consistent with federal tax law. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB428|houston county sale or redempti.title: Houston County, sale or redemption of lands for taxes further provided for
al:HB428|houston county sale or redempti.summary: Transfers duties for selling and redeeming land for unpaid property taxes in Houston County from the probate judge to the revenue commissioner, starting October 1, 2025.

al:HB434|talladega county compensation o.title: Talladega County, compensation of the sheriff further provided for
al:HB434|talladega county compensation o.summary: Gives the Talladega County sheriff a $15,200.32 yearly expense allowance on top of current salary starting June 1, 2025, then sets the sheriff's salary at $112,000 a year starting January 18, 2027, replacing the allowance and earlier local pay laws.

al:HB499|sheriff to authorize use of cre.title: Sheriff, to authorize use of credit card or debit card
al:HB499|sheriff to authorize use of cre.summary: Lets the Lawrence County sheriff use office credit or debit cards for approved purchases, requiring written policies with purchase limits, monthly review and full payment of bills, with purchases generally paid from the sheriff's discretionary fund and any card rewards deposited there.

al:HB272|alabama math and science teache.title: Alabama Math and Science Teacher Education Program (AMSTEP), renamed the  Loan Assistance in Support of Educators in Alabama (LASEA) Program; providing loan assistance in acute educator shortage programs  as determined by the Alabama Commission on Higher Education in consultation with the State Department of Education
al:HB272|alabama math and science teache.summary: Renames the state's math and science teacher loan repayment program and expands it to teachers certified in any subject with an acute teacher shortage, with extra aid for those working in shortage schools or districts, as identified by state higher education and education officials.

al:HB310|fair campaign practices act aut.title: Fair Campaign Practices Act; authorize notifications of civil penalties by electronic mail in lieu of certified mail in certain circumstances
al:HB310|fair campaign practices act aut.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to notify campaign and political action committees of civil penalties for late campaign finance reports by email to the address on file, instead of certified mail, with certified mail also required only when the penalty exceeds its mailing cost.

al:HB363|fair campaign practices act pro.title: Fair Campaign Practices Act; prohibit campaign contributions and expenditures from foreign nationals
al:HB363|fair campaign practices act pro.summary: Bars foreign nationals, including noncitizens without permanent residency, foreign governments, foreign companies and some majority foreign-owned U.S. companies, from contributing to or spending on Alabama candidate or ballot measure elections or state and local parties; giving or accepting such money is a Class C felony.

al:HB361|ma chis lower creek indian trib.title: Ma-Chis Lower Creek Indian Tribe; authorization to hire a police officer
al:HB361|ma chis lower creek indian trib.summary: Lets the state-recognized Ma-Chis Lower Creek Indian Tribe hire certified police officers, paid without state or local law enforcement funds, with state police powers on tribal land and limited authority to act off it during pursuits or certain felony arrests.

al:HB336|interstate compact respiratory.title: Interstate Compact, respiratory therapists
al:HB336|interstate compact respiratory.summary: Enters Alabama into the Respiratory Care Interstate Compact, letting respiratory therapists licensed in one member state practice in others, and creates a multistate commission to run the compact and coordinate discipline and investigations.

al:HB359|firefighters to include parkins.title: Firefighters; to include Parkinson's Disease in occupational diseases to be compensated for death or disability
al:HB359|firefighters to include parkins.summary: Adds Parkinson's disease to the occupational diseases that qualify city and state firefighters for disability and death benefits, presuming it job-related if the firefighter shows exposure on the job to a known toxin linked to higher Parkinson's risk.

al:HB345|jefferson county appointment an.title: Jefferson County, appointment and service of special reserve deputies provided for
al:HB345|jefferson county appointment an.summary: Lets the Jefferson County sheriff appoint certified officers not on staff as special reserve deputies to serve property seizure writs when more than 250 are pending, paid up to $250 per writ directly by property owners rather than from county funds.

al:HB351|choctaw county ad valorem tax o.title: Choctaw County; ad valorem tax on certain property increased
al:HB351|choctaw county ad valorem tax o.summary: Lets Choctaw County raise its property tax for roads and bridges by up to five mills for five-year periods, if voters approve the increase and each list of specific road and bridge projects to be funded, and lets the county borrow to finance them.

al:HB319|imagination library of alabama.title: Imagination Library of Alabama Program, Department of Early Childhood Education to administer through Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
al:HB319|imagination library of alabama.summary: Creates a state program, run by the Department of Early Childhood Education, that pays half the cost of mailing one free book a month to registered children from birth to age five through Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, with local partners paying the rest.

al:HB233|crimes and offenses making a te.title: Crimes and offenses; making a terrorist threat in the second degree, elements revised, criminal penalties further provided for
al:HB233|crimes and offenses making a te.summary: Makes threatening to commit a violent crime or damage property with a weapon or explosive, with intent to cause fear or harm, a second-degree terrorist threat even if not credible or imminent, and makes a second or later conviction a Class D felony.

al:HB212|state waters persons commercial.title: State waters; persons commercially cutting aquatic plants required to remove cut plants, criminal penalties established
al:HB212|state waters persons commercial.summary: Requires businesses that cut or uproot aquatic plants in public waters to use commercially reasonable methods to remove the cut plant matter, with violations a misdemeanor carrying a fine of at least $500, and directs state conservation officials to write rules.

al:HB151|distinctive license plate fire.title: Distinctive License Plate; Fire Chaplains
al:HB151|distinctive license plate fire.summary: Makes fire chaplains who belong to the Alabama Fellowship of Fire Chaplains eligible for one firefighter license plate, and makes falsely obtaining or certifying someone for a firefighter plate a misdemeanor. Takes effect January 1, 2026.

al:HB236|county board of equalization to.title: County Board of Equalization; to increase the per diem for board members.
al:HB236|county board of equalization to.summary: Raises the local supplement for Baldwin County Board of Equalization members so their daily pay reaches $200 starting in 2025, up from $100, with annual cost-of-living increases starting in 2026.

al:HB289|marshall county tennessee valle.title: Marshall County; Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in-lieu-of-tax payments distribution
al:HB289|marshall county tennessee valle.summary: Changes Marshall County's split of Tennessee Valley Authority payments: sets a $240,000 minimum for the legislative delegation office, raises the economic development minimum to $247,000, drops a $15,000 development grant, replaces Arab's $27,000 ambulance share with $13,000 for Boaz, and adds $25,000 for Snead State.

al:HB187|court fees use of funds allocat.title: Court fees; use of funds allocated to sheriff's office expended
al:HB187|court fees use of funds allocat.summary: Lets sheriffs spend their share of an existing court docket fee to support their office's law enforcement functions, rather than only on running the jail.

al:HB44|teachers retirement system reope.title: Teachers' Retirement System, reopened for service rendered to St. Clair County, DAY Program, Inc.
al:HB44|teachers retirement system reope.summary: Lets the St. Clair County DAY Program join the Teachers' Retirement System and count its current employees' past service toward retirement, with the program paying the full cost and no cost to the state.

al:HB73|jefferson county fine for posses.title: Jefferson County; fine for possession of trigger activator, established
al:HB73|jefferson county fine for posses.summary: Bans possessing devices that make a gun fire automatically with one trigger pull in Jefferson County, with a civil penalty of at least $1,000 per violation; police on duty, federally permitted owners and devices allowing no more than two shots are exempt.

al:HB269|town of morris corporate limits.title: Town of Morris, corporate limits altered to annex property
al:HB269|town of morris corporate limits.summary: Extends the town limits of Morris in Jefferson County to take in a specified tract of land described in the bill.

al:HB195|motor vehicles disabled veteran.title: Motor vehicles, disabled veteran's license plate, further provided
al:HB195|motor vehicles disabled veteran.summary: Lets disabled veterans whose physical disability is rated at 50 percent obtain a special disabled veteran license plate; currently the disability must exceed 50 percent. Takes effect January 1, 2026.

al:HB261|department of insurance surplus.title: Department of Insurance, surplus line brokers providing insurance not readily available by licensed agents in this state
al:HB261|department of insurance surplus.summary: Drops the extra surety bond requirement for out-of-state surplus line insurance brokers seeking an Alabama license, so they need only file an application and pay the license fee.

al:HB262|department of insurance interna.title: Department of Insurance, internal Code of Alabama 1975 citations  corrected
al:HB262|department of insurance interna.summary: Corrects outdated cross-references to other sections of state law within the insurable interest and life insurance policy loan statutes, without changing their substance.

al:HB140|public utilities private sewer.title: Public utilities; private sewer or wastewater systems, authorized to come under the jurisdiction of the Public Service Commission
al:HB140|public utilities private sewer.summary: Lets private sewer and wastewater systems affiliated with systems already regulated by the Public Service Commission elect to come under its regulation, and lets the commission set a single combined rate structure for the affiliated systems' customers.

al:HB132|scottsboro municipal elections.title: Scottsboro, municipal elections for Mayor and City Council and City Board of Education extended for one additional year based on staggered terms
al:HB132|scottsboro municipal elections.summary: Extends by one year the terms of Scottsboro's mayor, city council members and city school board members, moving future city elections to the fourth Tuesday in August of 2027, 2029 and 2031, and sets runoffs four weeks after a general election.

al:HB54|juvenile court additional courts.title: Juvenile court; additional courts authorized to issue emergency ex parte orders for protection of juveniles; process provided for
al:HB54|juvenile court additional courts.summary: Lets a circuit or district court handling a divorce, separation or custody-related case issue an emergency order protecting a child after finding evidence of abuse or neglect, including placing the child with a relative or the state human resources department until a juvenile court hearing.

al:SB357|macon county local privilege ta.title: Macon County; local privilege tax on pari-mutuel activities, established
al:SB357|macon county local privilege ta.summary: Levies an 8 percent Macon County privilege tax on net revenue from wagering on historical horse racing machines, collected by the county racing commission and replacing other local taxes on that activity; live and simulcast racing taxes are unchanged.

al:SB369|lauderdale county economic deve.title: Lauderdale County; Economic Development Authority and Economic Development Authority Fund established, county commission authorized to levy additional sales and use tax
al:SB369|lauderdale county economic deve.summary: Creates a five-member Lauderdale County Economic Development Authority appointed by the county commission to support business and job growth, and lets the commission levy up to an extra three-quarters of one percent sales and use tax to fund it.

al:SR95|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR95|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for March 17, 2026, scheduling floor consideration of 27 bills, including utility tax exemptions for greenhouses, poultry houses and irrigation, a work-zone speed camera pilot, cryptocurrency kiosk fraud rules and a one-year pause on new solar facilities.

al:SB294|public officers and employees d.title: Public Officers and Employees; Division of Risk Management authorized to provide bond program, authorize delinquencies, notification required
al:SB294|public officers and employees d.summary: Requires the office receiving public officials' bonds to notify officials when their bond is deficient, gives them 15 days to fix it before their office is vacated, separates county bond rules from state rules, and lets the state risk management division file bonds for officials.

al:SB243|jefferson county pistol permits.title: Jefferson County, pistol permits further provided for
al:SB243|jefferson county pistol permits.summary: Sets a $37.50 fee for a five-year pistol carry permit in Jefferson County, divided in the same shares as the county's $7.50 one-year permit fee among the county retirement system, sheriff's fund and a legislative office fund.

al:SB47|child support retroactivity prov.title: Child support; retroactivity provided for in certain circumstances
al:SB47|child support retroactivity prov.summary: Allows a child-support order entered within the first year after a child's birth to be made retroactive to nine months before the birth.

al:SB334|shelby county sale of solid was.title: Shelby County; sale of solid waste commodities authorized, distribution of proceeds provided for
al:SB334|shelby county sale of solid was.summary: Lets the Shelby County Commission sell gas, minerals or other products generated by its public landfill through competitively bid contracts of up to 20 years, with proceeds going to the county general fund for solid waste and landfill costs and other lawful purposes.

al:SB255|quiet title claims requirement.title: Quiet Title Claims; requirement to show tax payments in quiet title action exempted for nonprofit entities
al:SB255|quiet title claims requirement.summary: Exempts owners of land that is tax-exempt because it is used for religious, educational, charitable or other exempt purposes from having to show property tax payments to bring or prove a lawsuit to establish clear title, and rewrites the standards of proof in such suits.

al:SB332|firefighters to include parkins.title: Firefighters; to include Parkinson's Disease in occupational diseases to be compensated for death and disability
al:SB332|firefighters to include parkins.summary: Adds Parkinson's disease to the occupational diseases for which city and state firefighters can receive disability and death benefits, presuming it job-related if the firefighter shows on-the-job exposure to a known toxin linked to higher Parkinson's risk.

al:SR75|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR75|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for March 5, 2026, scheduling floor consideration of seven bills, including a physician assistant licensure compact, a ban on foreign nationals' campaign contributions, child custody modification standards and letting state retirees work as school bus drivers.

al:SB229|national guard duties of legal.title: National Guard; duties of Legal Service Office positions revised and further provide for
al:SB229|national guard duties of legal.summary: Revises the duties of positions in the Alabama National Guard's Legal Services Office, including the state staff judge advocates, general counsel, deputy general counsel and associate general counsels for military justice, contracts, civil law, operational law and legal assistance.

al:SB305|campus chaplains public k 12 sc.title: Campus chaplains; public K-12 schools authorized to accept as volunteers, local boards of education and governing bodies authorized to vote on whether to allow, limitations provided
al:SB305|campus chaplains public k 12 sc.summary: Lets local school boards and charter school governing bodies vote on whether to accept volunteer campus chaplains, who would serve at a teacher's request and must complete chaplain training and a criminal background check; registered sex offenders are barred.

al:SB274|alabama board of cosmetology an.title: Alabama Board of Cosmetology and Barbering; make up application and blow-dry styling exempt from regulation
al:SB274|alabama board of cosmetology an.summary: Exempts people who offer only makeup application or only blow-dry styling, and no other barbering, cosmetology or esthetics services, from regulation by the state Board of Cosmetology and Barbering, and removes makeup services from the regulated practice of esthetics.

al:SB222|motor vehicles operation of ove.title: Motor vehicles; operation of oversized vehicles operated by automated driving systems, prohibited
al:SB222|motor vehicles operation of ove.summary: Bars vehicles that need an oversize or overweight permit from being operated by an automated driving system, and states that allowing self-driving vehicles creates no duty to upgrade state or local roads for them.

al:SB216|state military awards criteria.title: State military; awards criteria revised, new awards established, authority to present prescribed
al:SB216|state military awards criteria.summary: Revises eligibility rules for Alabama National Guard military awards, creates new awards, and specifies which awards the Governor may present and which the Adjutant General may present. Takes effect October 1, 2026.

al:SB84|incarceration to require the ala.title: Incarceration; to require the Alabama Department of Public Health to adopt and enforce sanitation standards for food services in corrections facilities, county, and municipal jails
al:SB84|incarceration to require the ala.summary: Requires the state Department of Public Health to adopt and enforce food sanitation rules, including regular inspections and correction of violations, for kitchens serving state prisons and county and municipal jails.

al:SB70|crimes and offenses sex offenses.title: Crimes and offenses; sex offenses involving a child; crime of transmitting obscene material to a child by computer, further provided for
al:SB70|crimes and offenses sex offenses.summary: Expands the crime of sending obscene material by computer to a child for sexual purposes to cover sending it to someone the sender believes is a child.

al:SB88|division of construction managem.title: Division of Construction Management; capital improvement projects valued less than $750,000 at covered K-12 and higher education institutions exempted from division inspections and recommendations
al:SB88|division of construction managem.summary: Exempts K-12 schools and four-year public universities from state construction division inspections and recommendations, including on disability access and fire safety, for capital projects costing $750,000 or less.

al:SB72|alabama commission on higher edu.title: Alabama Commission on Higher Education, ReEngage Alabama Grant Program, minimum age of adult learner decreased, eligibility requirements revised
al:SB72|alabama commission on higher edu.summary: Lowers the minimum age for the ReEngage Alabama adult learner grant from 25 to 22 and makes eligible certain people pursuing a first bachelor's degree after a two-year break following their first associate degree.

al:SB74|alabama math and science teacher.title: Alabama Math and Science Teacher Education Program (AMSTEP), renamed the  Loan Assistance in Support of Educators in Alabama (LASEA) Program; providing loan assistance in acute educator shortage programs  as determined by the Alabama Commission on Higher Education in consultation with the State Department of Education and the Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services
al:SB74|alabama math and science teacher.summary: Renames the state's math and science teacher loan repayment program and extends its loan assistance to teachers certified in subjects with acute shortages, with extra aid for those working in shortage schools or systems, and requires an accountability and evaluation plan.

al:SB79|individual income taxes to allow.title: Individual income taxes, to allow an exclusion from gross income for contributions to Trump Accounts and to make permanent the exclusion for amounts paid by an employer on any qualified education loan
al:SB79|individual income taxes to allow.summary: Excludes employer contributions to an employee's federal Trump Account from state taxable income, and makes permanent the state income tax exclusion for employer payments on employees' student loans.

al:SB253|entertainment industry incentiv.title: Entertainment Industry Incentive Act of 2009 amended, create additional incentive program, extend review and evaluation deadline
al:SB253|entertainment industry incentiv.summary: Creates a film incentive rebate of 45 percent of payroll paid to Alabama residents for small productions spending $100,000 to $499,999, clarifies how payments to loan-out companies count, and extends the deadline for an outside review of the incentives to 2028.

al:SR34|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR34|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for February 5, 2026, scheduling floor consideration of 18 bills, including app store age verification, penalties for first-degree rape and sodomy, charter school bonding and campaign funds for security expenses.

al:SR30|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR30|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for January 29, 2026, scheduling floor consideration of four bills on underground utility damage prevention, municipal runoff elections, adding vaping to the public smoking ban, and elder abuse convictions' effect on inheritance.

al:SB95|public utilities underground dam.title: Public utilities; Underground Damage Prevention Program; certain statutory sunset clauses deleted
al:SB95|public utilities underground dam.summary: Extends the program that runs Alabama's statewide call-before-you-dig notification system, and the requirement that underground utility operators join it, from January 1, 2027, to January 1, 2036.

al:SR25|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR25|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for January 27, 2026, scheduling floor votes on bills including renewals of the massage therapy board and 911 Board, military aptitude testing in high schools, warrant checks on prison inmates, and peer-to-peer car sharing rules.

al:SB60|criminal procedure department of.title: Criminal procedure; Department of Corrections, outstanding warrant check procedures on inmates, provided; virtual hearings on inmates, required under certain conditions
al:SB60|criminal procedure department of.summary: Requires the prison system to check a national database for outstanding warrants on inmates at intake, before work release, parole or release, and to help serve them, holding resulting hearings by video when possible; the parole board must also check before parole. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

al:SR21|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR21|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for January 21, 2026, scheduling floor votes on bills including renewals of the electrical contractors board and surface mining commission, mayoral tie-breaking votes, vehicle repair bidding, and nondisclosure agreements covering sexual abuse.

al:SB33|veteran license tags certain vet.title: Veteran license tags; certain veterans exposed to radiation added to those eligible for distinctive tag
al:SB33|veteran license tags certain vet.summary: Replaces the 1944–1962 atomic testing criterion for the radiation-exposed veterans license plate with veterans who took part in an atomic weapon detonation, cleaned up radioactive material from an atomic detonation or accident, or were exposed to radiation from atomic weapons used in World War II.

al:SB337|montgomery county probate judge.title: Montgomery County, probate judge compensation further provided for
al:SB337|montgomery county probate judge.summary: Pays the Montgomery County probate judge, once he or she has served at least six full years, a salary equal to that of a circuit judge with the same years of service, replacing other compensation. Takes effect June 1, 2025.

al:SB89|criminal procedure warrants serv.title: Criminal procedure; warrants served on inmates in Department of Corrections
al:SB89|criminal procedure warrants serv.summary: Requires the prison system to serve arrest warrants on inmates when they are processed and within seven days of receiving a warrant, to periodically search a national database for warrants, and to hold resulting hearings by video from prison. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:SB277|public k 12 schools sex educati.title: Public K-12 schools, sex education curriculum further provided for, sexual risk avoidance established as sex ed curriculum, policies of local boards of education related to sex ed further provided for, parent or guardian notice of sex ed curriculum required, Attorney General authorized to enforce
al:SB277|public k 12 schools sex educati.summary: As introduced, requires public school sex education to teach abstinence-centered "sexual risk avoidance," bars demonstrating contraceptives or giving abortion referrals, gives parents 14 days' notice and an opt-out, and lets the Attorney General sue to enforce.

al:SB248|administrative procedure act st.title: Administrative Procedure Act, standard of judicial review of agency rulings revised
al:SB248|administrative procedure act st.summary: Directs courts reviewing agency decisions to interpret laws and rules without deferring to the agency, resolving remaining doubt toward a reasonable reading that limits agency power and maximizes individual liberty, and repeals the presumption that agency orders are just and reasonable. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:SB315|alabama 21st century fund furth.title: Alabama 21st Century Fund, further distribution of funds, one-time appropriation to the Department of Commerce
al:SB315|alabama 21st century fund furth.summary: Lets money in the state's tobacco-settlement-funded 21st Century Fund that is not needed for its bonds pay for economic development projects and other bond debt, and transfers $5 million to the Department of Commerce for international offices, rural development and operating costs.

al:SB153|restoration of voting rights no.title: Restoration of Voting Rights; notification to convicted individuals seeking restoration; Pardons and Paroles Board required to notify individuals and Secretary of State when voting rights restored
al:SB153|restoration of voting rights no.summary: Requires the parole board and Secretary of State to post a form by September 1, 2026, for people with past convictions to seek restoration of voting rights, and requires the board to publish names of those restored and notify election officials, who must return previously registered voters to the rolls.

al:SB234|cherokee county off road vehicl.title: Cherokee County, off-road vehicle parks, provide for the permitting, inspection, operation, and to provide fines for violations
al:SB234|cherokee county off road vehicl.summary: Requires fee-charging off-road vehicle parks in Cherokee County that host races or meet size or revenue thresholds to obtain a county permit after inspection, starting October 1, 2025; lets the county commission impose civil fines up to $5,000 for unpermitted operation; and requires forestry watershed practices.

al:SB178|courts appointment support and.title: Courts, appointment, support, and powers of visiting judges provided for
al:SB178|courts appointment support and.summary: Lets the Chief Justice, at a prosecutor's request, appoint a sitting or retired circuit judge as a visiting judge to handle specific violent crime cases until they are resolved, and creates a state Speedy Trial Fund to pay those costs. Takes effect June 1, 2025.

al:SB68|local emergency management organ.title: Local emergency management organizations; mutual aid agreements with other public and private agencies
al:SB68|local emergency management organ.summary: Gives the city or county that set up a local emergency management agency, instead of its director, the power to make mutual aid agreements, allows such agreements for public safety as well as disasters, and gives employees aiding other areas the same powers and immunities.

al:SB66|crimes and offenses crime of pre.title: Crimes and offenses, crime of presentment of a forged instrument established, penalties established
al:SB66|crimes and offenses crime of pre.summary: Creates the crime of presenting a forged document, or a document tied to another person, to a state or local government employee or official with intent to defraud, punishable as a Class D felony. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HJR198|alabama mental health task for.title: Alabama Mental Health Task Force, established
al:HJR198|alabama mental health task for.summary: Creates an Alabama Mental Health Task Force of state officials, lawmakers, health professionals and appointees to study mental health care, gaps in services and workforce, and recommend long-term policies in a report due November 1, 2026.

al:HJR51|artificial intelligence and chi.title: Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety Study Commission, created
al:HJR51|artificial intelligence and chi.summary: Creates a study commission of lawmakers, the Attorney General and appointees from mental health, child advocacy, broadband, technology and broadcasting groups and the Lieutenant Governor to study how artificial intelligence, social media and the internet affect children and recommend legislation by November 1, 2026.

al:HB154|criminal procedure out of state.title: Criminal procedure; out-of-state warrants, arrest authorized for crime punishable by more than one year, arrest by out-of-state officers authorized
al:HB154|criminal procedure out of state.summary: Lets police or private citizens arrest without a warrant someone charged with any felony in another state, not just crimes punishable by death or life, and lets out-of-state officers in fresh pursuit arrest felony suspects in Alabama, followed by a court hearing.

al:HB608|henry county coroner and deputy.title: Henry County, coroner and deputy coroner, expenses further provided for
al:HB608|henry county coroner and deputy.summary: Lets the Henry County Commission provide the coroner and deputy coroner a county vehicle with equipment, fuel and repairs, and reimburse their costs for state-required training. Takes effect October 1, 2025.

al:HB609|henry county henry county sheri.title: Henry County; Henry County Sheriff's Office and Henry County Task Force, authorized to sell, use, and destroy certain abandoned, stolen, and unclaimed property
al:HB609|henry county henry county sheri.summary: Lets the Henry County sheriff auction abandoned or stolen property unclaimed for six months, holding proceeds six months for owners before they go to a sheriff's fund for law enforcement, and lets unclaimed firearms be kept for police use or destroyed.

al:HJR226|alabama unmanned aircraft syst.title: Alabama Unmanned Aircraft System Study Commission created
al:HJR226|alabama unmanned aircraft syst.summary: Creates a 12-member study commission to examine the use of drones in Alabama, their vulnerability to data transfers to hostile foreign actors, data security practices, and alternatives to foreign-made drones, reporting by the 15th legislative day of the 2026 session.

al:HB328|national guard legal services o.title: National Guard; legal services office and legal assistance program created
al:HB328|national guard legal services o.summary: As introduced, creates an Alabama National Guard Legal Services Office and a Legal Assistance Program, setting duties for Guard lawyers in advising leaders and helping eligible members with personal legal matters, and lets Guard lawyers and paralegals act as notaries.

al:SR122|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR122|special order calendar.summary: Sets the Senate's special order of business for April 8, 2026, scheduling floor votes on House bills including an income tax deduction for overtime pay, school consolidation, rural health appropriations, protections for living organ donors, and daily school prayer and pledge.

al:SCF92|alexander atwater.title: Alexander Atwater
al:SCF92|alexander atwater.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Alexander Atwater of Birmingham to the Alabama Drycleaning Environmental Response Trust Fund Advisory Board, for a term ending April 30, 2026.

al:SCF93|charles dean.title: Charles Dean
al:SCF93|charles dean.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Charles Dean of Opelika to the Alabama Drycleaning Environmental Response Trust Fund Advisory Board, for a term ending April 18, 2028.

al:SCF95|steve mckinnon.title: Steve McKinnon
al:SCF95|steve mckinnon.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Steve McKinnon of Daleville to the Alabama Drycleaning Environmental Response Trust Fund Advisory Board, for a term ending April 30, 2026.

al:SCF91|bonnie temple.title: Bonnie Temple
al:SCF91|bonnie temple.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Bonnie Temple of Montgomery to the Alabama Drycleaning Environmental Response Trust Fund Advisory Board, for a term ending May 3, 2027.

al:SCF103|dewayne jenkins.title: DeWayne Jenkins
al:SCF103|dewayne jenkins.summary: Confirms the lieutenant governor's appointment of DeWayne Jenkins of Parrish to the Board of Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, for a term ending June 30, 2029.

al:SCF101|troy skipworth.title: Troy Skipworth
al:SCF101|troy skipworth.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Troy Skipworth of Florence to the Alabama Family Trust Board of Trustees, for a term ending January 16, 2029.

al:SCF97|gloria watts.title: Gloria Watts
al:SCF97|gloria watts.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Gloria Watts of Gadsden to the Alabama A&M University Board of Trustees, for a term ending January 31, 2028.

al:SCF98|tracy doughty.title: Tracy Doughty
al:SCF98|tracy doughty.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Tracy Doughty of Madison to the Alabama A&M University Board of Trustees, for a term ending January 31, 2032.

al:SCF99|kevin ball.title: Kevin Ball
al:SCF99|kevin ball.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Kevin Ball of Mobile to the Alabama A&M University Board of Trustees, for a term ending January 31, 2032.

al:SCF100|joe d briggs.title: Joe D. Briggs
al:SCF100|joe d briggs.summary: Confirms the governor's appointment of Joe D. Briggs of Washington, D.C. to the Alabama A&M University Board of Trustees, for a term ending January 31, 2032.

al:SCF104|josh bryant.title: Josh Bryant
al:SCF104|josh bryant.summary: Confirms the Alabama Association of Volunteer Fire Departments' reappointment of Josh Bryant of Fultondale, a volunteer fire captain, to the association's seat on the Alabama Personnel Standards Commission; his current term expires in July 2026.

al:SCF105|judge carol smitherman.title: Judge Carol Smitherman
al:SCF105|judge carol smitherman.summary: Confirms the lieutenant governor's appointment of retired Jefferson County circuit judge Carol Smitherman to the Alabama Ethics Commission, for a term ending March 31, 2031.

al:SR116|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR116|special order calendar.summary: As introduced, sets the Senate's special order of business for April 7, 2026, scheduling 24 bills for debate ahead of other business, including a one-year ban on new solar power facilities and a required computer science course in public K-12 schools.

al:SR108|senate rules amended.title: Senate Rules amended
al:SR108|senate rules amended.summary: As introduced, amends seven Senate rules, mostly shifting powers from the presiding officer to the President Pro Tempore over recommitting bills, calling up carried-over bills, and committee assignment and conference committee appointments. Also adds a 17th standing committee and changes reading-at-length rules.

al:SR111|special order calendar.title: SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR
al:SR111|special order calendar.summary: As introduced, sets the Senate's special order of business for April 2, 2026, scheduling 12 bills for debate, including the 2027 education budget, supplemental education spending for 2026, a pay raise for public education employees and a retiree bonus.

nm:HB 253|sealing of certain court recor.title: Sealing of Certain Court Records
nm:HB 253|sealing of certain court recor.summary: Requires courts to seal eviction case records once an eviction case is filed, lets landlords seek unsealing at least 15 days after winning possession, requires resealing within three years, limits access to parties, court staff and authorized attorneys, and says tenants need not disclose sealed records.

nm:SB 73|driver s ed requirements.title: Driver's Ed Requirements
nm:SB 73|driver s ed requirements.summary: Requires approved driver's education courses, starting Jan. 1, 2027, to include at least three hours on driving around vulnerable road users, such as pedestrians, roadside workers, people riding or leading animals and riders of less-protected vehicles, with the Transportation Department setting standards.

nm:SB 21|medicare supplement open enroll.title: Medicare Supplement Open Enrollment
nm:SB 21|medicare supplement open enroll.summary: Requires Medicare supplement insurers, starting Jan. 1, 2027, to give policyholders 65 and older a yearly 60-day window beginning in their birthday month to switch to a policy of equal or lesser value without medical underwriting or health-based pricing, with advance written notice.

nm:SB 48|state fairgrounds district bond.title: State Fairgrounds District Bonds
nm:SB 48|state fairgrounds district bond.summary: Authorizes the State Fairgrounds District to issue revenue bonds with up to $92 million in net proceeds, repaid from state gross receipts and gaming tax revenue attributable to economic activity within the district.

nm:HB 8|criminal competency treatment.title: Criminal Competency & Treatment
nm:HB 8|criminal competency treatment.summary: Allows community-based competency restoration for non-dangerous defendants and widens crimes allowing criminal commitment; makes possessing an unlawfully obtained device converting guns to automatic fire a third-degree felony; raises penalties for repeat car theft and shooting threats; lengthens sentences for trafficking large fentanyl amounts; changes DUI blood-draw rules.

nm:HB 156|repeal special session vaccina.title: Repeal Special Session Vaccination Laws
nm:HB 156|repeal special session vaccina.summary: Makes permanent the Department of Health's authority to base required childhood and recommended adult vaccinations on its own recommendations, rather than federal advisory schedules, by repealing 2025 special-session provisions that would have restored prior law on July 1, 2026.

nm:SB 38|special education act.title: Special Education Act
nm:SB 38|special education act.summary: Creates an Office of Special Education in the Public Education Department to enforce special education law and write a state plan, moves early-childhood special education grants to the early childhood department, and requires schools to provide gifted education under department standards.

nm:SB 23|exceptions to student use of ph.title: Exceptions to Student Use of Phones
nm:SB 23|exceptions to student use of ph.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt policies barring student use of phones and other wireless devices during the school day, with limited exceptions, consequences and device storage, and caps grants for carrying out the policies at $1 million in each of fiscal 2027 and 2028.

nm:HB 129|public employee probation peri.title: Public Employee Probation Period
nm:HB 129|public employee probation peri.summary: Shortens the probationary period for classified state employees from one year to 180 days and bars requiring another probation period after a move to a new position, unless the employee has a break in service not caused by a layoff or job-related injury or illness.

nm:SB 3|commitment procedure changes def.title: Commitment Procedure Changes & Definitions
nm:SB 3|commitment procedure changes def.summary: Rewrites the definitions of "harm to self" and "harm to others" used for involuntary mental health commitment and court-ordered outpatient treatment, covering inability to meet basic needs that risks death or serious injury, dropping extreme property destruction as grounds, and letting crisis triage centers do evaluations.

nm:HB 49|increase felon firearm penalty.title: Increase Felon Firearm Penalty
nm:HB 49|increase felon firearm penalty.summary: Raises the penalty for a serious violent felon who receives, transports or possesses a firearm or destructive device from a third-degree felony with a six-year sentence to a second-degree felony; possession by other felons remains a third-degree felony.

nm:SB 20|prior authorization prescriptio.title: Prior Authorization & Prescription Drugs
nm:SB 20|prior authorization prescriptio.summary: Bars prior authorization and step therapy for drugs treating serious mental illness, bars repeat prior authorization for chronic maintenance drugs for three years, deems drug requests approved if not decided within three business days, and covers certain pharmacy benefit managers, starting Jan. 1, 2027.

nm:HB 291|tax changes.title: Tax Changes
nm:HB 291|tax changes.summary: Makes numerous tax changes, including letting the tax department waive interest on approved filing extensions, round amounts to the nearest five cents and renew licenses under payment plans, capping research-credit wages at $500,000 per employee, and taxing vape cartridges over five milliliters at 12.5 percent of wholesale value.

nm:HB 111|search for missing qualified s.title: Search for Missing Qualified Service Animal
nm:HB 111|search for missing qualified s.summary: Requires police, firefighters and emergency medical responders at an emergency who learn a qualified service animal is missing to make a reasonable effort to search for it, as far as practicable and while putting human safety first.

nm:HB 20|technology innovation division.title: Technology & Innovation Division
nm:HB 20|technology innovation division.summary: Creates a Technology and Innovation Division in the Economic Development Department, an advisory board, a research and deployment fund for early-stage technology projects, and a prize program of up to $5 million for companies in sectors such as aerospace, biosciences, clean energy and advanced computing.

nm:SB 235|school math changes.title: School Math Changes
nm:SB 235|school math changes.summary: Requires early math screening before students finish second grade, interventions and parent notice for K-5 students with math difficulties, district math teacher training plans, a statewide math leadership framework, and a specialist endorsement for math coaches.

nm:SB 2|public health safety initiatives.title: Public Health & Safety Initiatives
nm:SB 2|public health safety initiatives.summary: Appropriates $200 million from the general fund for behavioral health, including grants for community clinics, crisis response, addiction treatment medication, treatment courts, housing services, suicide prevention and peer support, with many items contingent on passage of a companion behavioral health bill.

nm:HB 295|accessibility act.title: Accessibility Act
nm:HB 295|accessibility act.summary: Creates an Office of Accessibility in the Department of Health to train and assist state agencies on making websites, apps and buildings accessible to people with disabilities, requires yearly reports starting May 2028, and appropriates $350,000.

nm:HB 183|magistrate retirement changes.title: Magistrate Retirement Changes
