nm:HB 183|magistrate retirement changes.summary: Raises magistrate judges' pensions for future service by increasing the benefit multiplier to 3.5 percent and the cap to 100 percent of salary, lets judges over 65 retire after five years instead of eight, and raises employer and employee contributions to 19.24 and 14.74 percent of salary.

nm:HB 120|accessibility of state agencie.title: Accessibility of State Agencies
nm:HB 120|accessibility of state agencie.summary: Requires state agency websites and mobile apps to meet digital accessibility standards by April 1, 2026, and agency facilities to meet federal disability access standards, and creates an Office of Accessibility under the governor's disability commission to assist agencies and report on compliance every two years.

nm:SB 42|comprehensive addiction and rec.title: Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Pgm
nm:SB 42|comprehensive addiction and rec.summary: Revises care plans for substance-exposed newborns, making the Health Care Authority the lead agency and requiring treatment referrals; requires the children's agency to offer federally reimbursable family prevention services, release more information on child deaths and near-deaths, and retain staff device records.

nm:SB 201|public ed reform fund uses.title: Public Ed. Reform Fund Uses
nm:SB 201|public ed reform fund uses.summary: Requires the Public Education Department to create accountability and evaluation plans, approved by the state finance department and two legislative committees, for programs paid from the public education reform fund, and moves its budget request deadline from Nov. 30 to Sept. 1.

nm:HB 124|death of protected person or g.title: Death of Protected Person or Guardian
nm:HB 124|death of protected person or g.summary: Ends a guardianship or conservatorship when the guardian or conservator dies, requires notice to the court within three days of a protected person's death, lets the guardian or conservator serve as personal representative if no one else is named, and requires an asset report within 45 days.

nm:SB 19|school finance unit value reset.title: School Finance Unit Value Reset
nm:SB 19|school finance unit value reset.summary: Lets the public education secretary adjust the fiscal 2026 per-unit value used in the public school funding formula, after verifying statewide unit counts and no later than Feb. 27, 2026, in consultation with state finance and legislative agencies; takes effect immediately.

nm:HB 128|firefighter occupational disea.title: Firefighter Occupational Disease Disablement
nm:HB 128|firefighter occupational disea.summary: Presumes 21 listed cancers in full-time firefighters are job-caused after five years of service, replacing service requirements that ranged up to 12 years for most covered cancers, and adds conditions to the presumption list for workers' compensation purposes.

nm:HB 154|bingo raffle act exemptions.title: Bingo & Raffle Act Exemptions
nm:HB 154|bingo raffle act exemptions.summary: Exempts fundraising raffles held by tax-exempt service, educational, athletic or extracurricular groups that mainly serve youth 18 and younger from the state Bingo and Raffle Act.

nm:SB 252|social work telehealth service.title: Social Work Telehealth Services
nm:SB 252|social work telehealth service.summary: Adds certified peer support workers and other professionals with a Medicaid provider number to the providers covered by the state telehealth law, includes all licensed social workers, and requires telehealth providers to follow the same supervision rules as in-person practice.

nm:HB 112|cannabis licensure changes.title: Cannabis Licensure Changes
nm:HB 112|cannabis licensure changes.summary: Requires everyone who controls a business applying for a commercial cannabis license to submit fingerprints for state and FBI criminal history checks, keeps those records confidential, requires license applications to be signed by the applicant or an authorized officer, and adds definitions to the state's cannabis law.

nm:HB 103|battery on peace officer penal.title: Battery on Peace Officer Penalty
nm:HB 103|battery on peace officer penal.summary: Raises aggravated battery on a peace officer that causes great bodily harm, or is committed with a deadly weapon or in a way that could cause death or great bodily harm, from a third-degree to a second-degree felony, starting July 1, 2025.

nm:SB 37|high quality literacy instructi.title: High Quality Literacy Instruction Act
nm:SB 37|high quality literacy instructi.summary: Requires reading instruction and materials to follow the science of reading, bans the three-cueing method, requires state-approved literacy screening for kindergarten through third grade starting in fiscal 2028 with parent notice and support plans, and assigns literacy coaches to the lowest-performing elementary schools for three years.

nm:SB 101|health care delivery access ac.title: Health Care Delivery & Access Act Repeal
nm:SB 101|health care delivery access ac.summary: Repeals the scheduled July 1, 2030, expiration of the Health Care Delivery and Access Act, which charges assessments on hospital services that are used to draw federal Medicaid matching money for hospitals, so the act continues indefinitely.

nm:HB 255|public safety workforce buildi.title: Public Safety Workforce Building Program
nm:HB 255|public safety workforce buildi.summary: Creates a public safety workforce grant program and fund, run by the Department of Finance and Administration, for recruiting, retaining and training police, firefighters, corrections officers and prosecutor and public defender attorneys, distributed by county population; repeals three existing sector-specific funds and moves their balances into it.

nm:HB 66|health care professional loan f.title: Health Care Professional Loan Fund Changes
nm:HB 66|health care professional loan f.summary: Lists eligible health professions by state licensing law, gives physicians top priority with awards of at least $75,000 a year for four years, capped at education debt, reserves at least half of funds for physicians and allows up to 18% interest for broken service contracts.

nm:HB 64|public project revolving fund a.title: Public Project Revolving Fund Appropriations
nm:HB 64|public project revolving fund a.summary: Appropriates $13.25 million from the public project revolving fund for fiscal 2027 and later: $6.25 million to the drinking water state revolving loan fund, $2 million to the local government planning fund and $5 million to the cultural affairs facilities infrastructure fund.

nm:SB 1|interstate medical licensure com.title: Interstate Medical Licensure Compact Act
nm:SB 1|interstate medical licensure com.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact, creating an expedited path for physicians licensed in another member state to get a New Mexico license, with shared licensing data and joint investigations among member states, alongside the existing licensing process.

nm:SB 100|indebtedness limit of arroyo f.title: Indebtedness Limit of Arroyo Flood Control
nm:SB 100|indebtedness limit of arroyo f.summary: Raises the limit on outstanding debt that the Albuquerque Metropolitan Arroyo Flood Control Authority may carry without legislative approval from $80 million to $120 million, effective July 1, 2025; voter approval of bond issues is still required.

nm:SB 17|parole parole board changes.title: Parole & Parole Board Changes
nm:SB 17|parole parole board changes.summary: Directs the parole board to base parole decisions for inmates serving life sentences on risk and readiness for release, such as prison conduct, program participation and rehabilitation, requires it to hear from victims' families, and limits removal of board members to cause after notice and a public hearing.

nm:HB 195|school nurse salary tiers mini.title: School Nurse Salary Tiers & Minimums
nm:HB 195|school nurse salary tiers mini.summary: Creates a three-level licensing system for school nurses with minimum salaries matching those of teachers at corresponding levels, and adds school funding formula units for nurses certified by the national board for school nurses who receive a salary differential.

nm:HB 65|instructional days in school ye.title: Instructional Days in School Year
nm:HB 65|instructional days in school ye.summary: Lets local school boards and charter school governing bodies decide how many instructional days per year and per week students attend, while keeping the state minimum of 1,140 instructional hours a year, starting with the 2025-2026 school year; takes effect immediately.

nm:HB 158|military base planning impact.title: Military Base Planning & Impact Act
nm:HB 158|military base planning impact.summary: Creates a military base impact fund and grant program for infrastructure projects in communities near military bases and defense facilities, run by the state Office of Military Base Planning and Support, requires annual reports, and removes the scheduled end date for that office and the military base planning commission.

nm:HB 206|nmfa water project fund projec.title: Nmfa Water Project Fund Projects
nm:HB 206|nmfa water project fund projec.summary: Authorizes the New Mexico Finance Authority to make loans or grants from the water project fund to a list of local water projects, with the Water Trust Board deciding which projects get funding and how much; takes effect immediately.

nm:HB 99|nonrepairable vehicle certifica.title: Nonrepairable Vehicle Certificates
nm:HB 99|nonrepairable vehicle certifica.summary: Lets an insurer that has paid a total-loss claim apply directly to the Motor Vehicle Division for a salvage or nonrepairable vehicle certificate if it cannot get the owner's signed title, after waiting 30 days, sending two certified letters, proving payment and paying towing and storage charges.

nm:HB 47|veteran property tax exemptions.title: Veteran Property Tax Exemptions
nm:HB 47|veteran property tax exemptions.summary: Raises the veteran property tax exemption from $4,000 to $10,000 for 2025, adjusted for inflation afterward, and starting in 2026 exempts a share of a disabled veteran's home value equal to the veteran's disability percentage, carrying out 2024 voter-approved constitutional amendments; takes effect immediately.

nm:HR 1|house investigatory subcommittee.title: House Investigatory Subcommittee
nm:HR 1|house investigatory subcommittee.summary: Creates a four-member special House committee, two from each party, to investigate allegations of criminal activity and public corruption at the former Zorro Ranch in Santa Fe County, gives it subpoena power, and requires a final report by Dec. 31, 2026.

nm:HB 36|accessibility act office.title: Accessibility Act & Office
nm:HB 36|accessibility act office.summary: As introduced, appropriates $350,000 to the Department of Health to create an Office of Accessibility that reviews state agency websites, mobile apps and buildings for accessibility, trains agencies, and issues annual public reports starting May 1, 2028.

nm:HB 10|physician assistant interstate.title: Physician Assistant Interstate Compact
nm:HB 10|physician assistant interstate.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Physician Assistant Licensure Compact, letting physician assistants licensed in a member state practice in other member states through a compact privilege, subject to each state's practice laws and criminal background check requirements.

nm:HB 11|audiology speech language patho.title: Audiology & Speech-Language Pathology Compact
nm:HB 11|audiology speech language patho.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact, letting audiologists and speech-language pathologists licensed in one member state practice in others, in person or by telehealth, with federal background checks required.

nm:HB 12|physical therapy licensure comp.title: Physical Therapy Licensure Compact
nm:HB 12|physical therapy licensure comp.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Physical Therapy Licensure Compact, letting physical therapists licensed in one member state practice in other member states under a compact privilege while following each state's practice laws.

nm:HB 13|occupational therapy licensure.title: Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact
nm:HB 13|occupational therapy licensure.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact, letting occupational therapists and assistants licensed in one member state practice in others, including by telehealth, with biometric criminal background checks required.

nm:HB 14|dentist dental hygienist compac.title: Dentist & Dental Hygienist Compact
nm:HB 14|dentist dental hygienist compac.summary: Enters New Mexico into the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Interstate Compact, letting dentists and dental hygienists licensed in one member state practice in New Mexico and other member states under a compact privilege.

nm:HJM 2|combine standing interim commit.title: Combine Standing & Interim Committees
nm:HJM 2|combine standing interim commit.summary: Asks the Legislative Council to form an 11-member task force of legislators and public members to study combining the legislature's session and interim committees into year-round committees, reporting findings by Nov. 30, 2025.

nm:HB 348|water law violation penalty.title: Water Law Violation Penalty
nm:HB 348|water law violation penalty.summary: Raises the maximum daily civil penalty for water law violations from $100 to $2,000, adjusted yearly for inflation, sets higher penalties when illegally diverted water is sold, and bars fines for overdiversion of a water right, making water repayment the preferred remedy.

nm:HB 371|off highway motor vehicles on.title: Off-Highway Motor Vehicles on Roads
nm:HB 371|off highway motor vehicles on.summary: Lets city and county elected governments allow recreational off-highway vehicles and ATVs on paved streets and highways other than freeways within their boundaries, not just roads they own, removes the state transportation commission's role, and lets local governments set separate speed limits and rules for them.

nm:SB 274|public peace health safety wel.title: Public Peace, Health, Safety & Welfare
nm:SB 274|public peace health safety wel.summary: Appropriates $33.7 million from the general fund: $9.7 million in fiscal 2026 for the Children, Youth and Families Department's juvenile justice and protective services divisions, and $24 million in fiscal 2027 for a child welfare data system, school improvement, a Zia Pueblo payment for the Zia symbol, New MexiCare and rural air service.

nm:HB 63|nmfa water project fund project.title: Nmfa Water Project Fund Projects
nm:HB 63|nmfa water project fund project.summary: Authorizes the New Mexico Finance Authority to make loans or grants from the water project fund to 75 listed local governments, tribes, water associations and conservation districts for water supply, wastewater, flood prevention and watershed projects, effective immediately.

nm:SM 14|address forced sterilization po.title: Address Forced Sterilization Policy
nm:SM 14|address forced sterilization po.summary: Asks the state Indian affairs department and commission on the status of women to study forced and coerced sterilization of Indigenous women and other women of color in New Mexico, gather survivor testimony, and report findings and recommendations to the governor and Legislature by December 31, 2027.

nm:SB 32|prosecution of human traffickin.title: Prosecution of Human Trafficking
nm:SB 32|prosecution of human traffickin.summary: As introduced, makes human trafficking a second-degree felony (first-degree if the victim is under 18), broadens the offense, allows second-degree trafficking prosecutions within six years of a police report, raises the child prostitution-exploitation age from 16 to 18, adds trafficking victims to crime-victim rights law and limits good-time credit.

nm:SB 58|childcare facility licensing ac.title: Childcare Facility Licensing Act
nm:SB 58|childcare facility licensing ac.summary: Exempts the early childhood department's purchases of child care for families eligible for child care assistance from the state procurement code, funds prekindergarten providers through applications instead of proposals, and adds required application details such as curriculum, class sizes and special-needs plans, starting July 1, 2025.

nm:SM 22|k 12 water conservation curricu.title: K-12 Water Conservation Curriculum
nm:SM 22|k 12 water conservation curricu.summary: Asks the public education department to study creating a kindergarten-through-12th-grade water conservation and management curriculum, including ways to work it into math, science and history, and to report its findings to the legislative education study committee by December 1, 2025.

nm:SM 2|wildfire study group.title: Wildfire Study Group
nm:SM 2|wildfire study group.summary: Asks the legislative council to create a wildfire study group of at least 14 members from state agencies, local governments, utilities, insurers and other stakeholders to recommend a statewide approach to preventing and mitigating wildfires, including funding and legislation, and report to an interim legislative committee by November 1, 2025.

nm:SB 18|crime of swatting.title: Crime of Swatting
nm:SB 18|crime of swatting.summary: Creates the crime of swatting, making it a fourth-degree felony to knowingly make a false or misleading report of an ongoing emergency or threat of violence to police, firefighters, emergency medical services or 911 centers in order to trigger an immediate response.

nm:SB 143|create utility oversight fund.title: Create Utility Oversight Fund
nm:SB 143|create utility oversight fund.summary: Creates a utility oversight fund for the public regulation commission from utility, telephone and pipeline fees, raises utility and telephone fees from about 0.51% to 0.59% of gross receipts, and lets the commission adjust fees yearly until July 2031, effective January 2026.

ok:SB 1732|professional licensing fees e.title: Professional licensing fees; establishing license fees. Effective date.
ok:SB 1732|professional licensing fees e.summary: Raises caps on home inspector fees, including the license fee from $250 to $400 and renewal from $150 to $240, and sets fixed state fees for plumbing, electrical and mechanical licenses, such as $480 for an initial contractor license and $80 for a journeyman license.

ok:HB 3834|ibogaine clinical trials okla.title: Ibogaine clinical trials; Oklahoma Breakthrough Therapy Act; terms; requirements for drug developers; contractual terms; intellectual property rights; reports; intellectual property account; effective date.
ok:HB 3834|ibogaine clinical trials okla.summary: Directs the State Department of Health, if funds are available, to contract with a drug developer for multistate clinical trials seeking federal approval of ibogaine, requiring the developer to match state funding, file reports, plan in-state treatment access and share intellectual-property proceeds with the state.

ok:SB 2095|game and fish prohibiting tak.title: Game and fish; prohibiting taking of game for compensation without certain licenses. Effective date.
ok:SB 2095|game and fish prohibiting tak.summary: Requires hunting guides and outfitters paid to help hunt waterfowl or cranes to hold state licenses costing up to $1,000 for resident outfitters and $2,000 for nonresidents, with violations punishable by fines of $1,500 to $2,000, jail, and license revocation.

ok:HB 4432|revenue and taxation adjustme.title: Revenue and taxation; adjustments; eliminating limitation on itemization of wagering losses for certain tax years; effective date.
ok:HB 4432|revenue and taxation adjustme.summary: Lets taxpayers who itemize deduct gambling losses outside the state's $17,000 cap on itemized deductions, starting with tax year 2027.

ok:SB 1307|oklahoma historical society r.title: Oklahoma Historical Society; removing certain prohibition on use of funds. Effective date.
ok:SB 1307|oklahoma historical society r.summary: Removes the ban on the Oklahoma Historical Society, the Oklahoma Arts Council and the J.M. Davis Memorial Commission using their funds for the benefit of any church, religion, religious leader or religious institution.

ok:SB 1423|oklahoma hospital advisory co.title: Oklahoma Hospital Advisory Council; eliminating the Advisory Council. Effective date.
ok:SB 1423|oklahoma hospital advisory co.summary: Abolishes the Oklahoma Hospital Advisory Council, removing its advisory role in hospital rules and stroke-care planning, and gives the State Commissioner of Health, rather than the State Board of Health, authority to adopt hospital and stroke-care rules.

ok:SB 1944|administrative workers compen.title: Administrative Workers' Compensation Act; modifying definition. Effective date.
ok:SB 1944|administrative workers compen.summary: Raises from $100,000 to $250,000 the annual farm, ranch or horticulture payroll below which workers are exempt from workers' compensation coverage, and extends the exemption to independent contractors in those fields who meet at least four of five listed conditions.

ok:HB 3986|taxes gross production tax re.title: Taxes; gross production tax; requiring certain completion methods for specific exemptions; effective date.
ok:HB 3986|taxes gross production tax re.summary: Expands the two-year gross production tax exemption for oil and gas wells completed with recycled water to all such wells, dropping the requirement that the well was drilled but not completed by July 1, 2021.

ok:SB 1238|assault and battery modifying.title: Assault and battery; modifying provisions of offense related to domestic abuse in presence of a child. Effective date.
ok:SB 1238|assault and battery modifying.summary: Makes a first conviction for domestic abuse committed in the presence of a child a Class B5 felony punishable by one to five years in prison, a fine up to $7,000, or both, instead of six months to one year in county jail, a fine up to $5,000, or both.

ok:SJR 49|joint resolution repealing cer.title: Joint resolution; repealing certain permanent rules of the Oklahoma Wildlife Conservation Commission.
ok:SJR 49|joint resolution repealing cer.summary: Repeals paragraph (1) of Oklahoma Administrative Code 800:30-3-2, part of an adopted permanent rule of the Oklahoma Wildlife Conservation Commission dealing with mineral exploration and production, and directs distribution of the resolution.

ok:HJR 1101|joint resolution oklahoma me.title: Joint Resolution; Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority; approving certain proposed permanent rules; directing distribution.
ok:HJR 1101|joint resolution oklahoma me.summary: Approves fourteen listed proposed permanent rules in Title 442 of the Oklahoma Administrative Code submitted by the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority on or before February 1, 2026, and directs copies to the Governor and the Oklahoma Register.

ks:SB 125|making and concerning suppleme.title: Making and concerning supplemental appropriations for fiscal year 2025 and appropriations for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 for various state agencies, authorizing certain capital improvement projects and fees, authorizing certain transfers authorizing the payment of certain claims against the state.
ks:SB 125|making and concerning suppleme.summary: Overrides a governor's line-item veto in the state budget bill, which provides $25.60 billion in fiscal 2026 spending, including $10.64 billion from the State General Fund, plus supplemental fiscal 2025 spending, capital projects, fees, fund transfers and claims payments.

ks:HB 2569|requiring actions challenging.title: Requiring actions challenging the constitutionality of an election statute to be brought in the district court of Shawnee county and providing a conditional amendment to limit advance voting if a court order invalidates or enjoins the signature verification requirement.
ks:HB 2569|requiring actions challenging.summary: Requires lawsuits claiming a statewide election law violates the U.S. or Kansas Constitution to be heard in Shawnee County district court, and, if a court blocks mail-ballot signature checks, limits mail voting to voters who are away, ill, disabled, religiously unable or working the polls.

ks:HB 2007|senate substitute for substit.title: Senate Substitute for Substitute for HB 2007 by Committee on Ways and Means - Reconciling multiple amendments to certain statutes.
ks:HB 2007|senate substitute for substit.summary: Reconciles state laws that were amended more than once in the current and prior sessions, repealing duplicate versions and combining the non-conflicting changes into a single version of each law.

ks:SB 137|authorizing the sale or transf.title: Authorizing the sale or transfer of forfeited firearms under the Kansas standard asset seizure and forfeiture act to a licensed firearm dealer.
ks:SB 137|authorizing the sale or transf.summary: Lets firearms forfeited under the state asset seizure law be sold or transferred to a federally licensed firearm dealer, adding to existing options of destroying them, keeping them for official use, trading them to another agency or giving them to the state crime lab.

ks:HB 2372|senate substitute for hb 2372.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2372 by Committee on Federal and State Affairs - Creating the crime of unlawful approach of a first responder and providing penalties therefore, requiring traffic laws that apply to local and state law enforcement to apply to federal law enforcement; including federal law enforcement in the definitions used in the crime of interference with law enforcement; including buildings owned by the United States in the crime of interference with the conduct of public business of public buildings; including enforcement of federal laws and executive orders in the exceptions from liability in the tort claims act, relating to the enforcement of detainers issued by the United States immigration and customs enforcement by a county sheriff operating a county jail; requiring municipal insurance pools to provide coverage of law enforcement agencies enforcing federal law; requiring the state to pay certain judgements in federal civil actions and provide legal representation by the attorney general, exempting section 287(g) federal immigration agreements from certain provisions of the interlocal cooperation act.
ks:HB 2372|senate substitute for hb 2372.summary: Makes it a misdemeanor to come within 25 feet of an on-duty first responder after a warning if it distracts them or raises safety concerns, lets sheriffs hold people on immigration detainers, and gives officers acting in good faith under 287(g) agreements state legal defense, immunity and judgment coverage.

ks:HB 2027|reorganizing subsections of t.title: Reorganizing subsections of the public assistance statute.
ks:HB 2027|reorganizing subsections of t.summary: Reorganizes the subsections of the state public assistance statute covering eligibility for cash assistance, food assistance and child care subsidies, drug screening and conviction rules, child support assignment and fraud investigations, keeping the existing drug screening requirements.

ks:SB 394|house substitute for sb 394 by.title: House Substitute for SB 394 by Committee on Elections - Relating to signature verification for advance voting ballots, concerning court orders that invalidate or enjoin signature verification triggering a return to allowing advance voting only if certain conditions exist, establishing venue in the district court in Shawnee county for all constitutional challenges to election laws.
ks:SB 394|house substitute for sb 394 by.summary: Requires the Secretary of State to track lawsuits over mail-ballot signature checks and, if a final court ruling strikes them down or blocks them, ends voting by mail except where federal law requires it; lets another person sign a ballot envelope for a voter whose signature does not match.

ks:HB 2676|permitting a pharmacist to in.title: Permitting a pharmacist to initiate therapy for certain conditions consistent with the pharmacist's education, training and experience, adding pharmacists who initiate such therapy to the healthcare stabilization fund and allowing a pharmacist to dispense a one-time emergency refill of a noncontrolled prescription drug for up to a 90-day supply when no refills remain.
ks:HB 2676|permitting a pharmacist to in.summary: Lets pharmacists start treatment, including medicines and medical equipment, for minor conditions, conditions needing no new diagnosis or emergencies; allows a one-time emergency refill of up to 90 days; and requires pharmacists who start treatment to carry liability insurance from 2028.

ks:HB 2016|including funeral home online.title: Including funeral home online obituary notices as sufficient grounds for removal of a deceased voter from the voter registration books; requiring that poll workers be citizens of the United States and live within the state of Kansas; prohibiting the disqualification of active military members, spouses or other dependents who are citizens of the United States as poll workers on the basis of residency or being a registered voter; relating to advance voting ballot applications; modifying the requirements for soliciting registered voters to submit advance voting applications.
ks:HB 2016|including funeral home online.summary: Requires removing deceased voters from the rolls when a local funeral home posts an online obituary, requires election judges and clerks to be U.S. citizens and Kansas residents, bars disqualifying active military members and families as poll workers over residency or voter registration, and changes rules for advance-ballot application mailers.

ks:HB 2535|providing that certain portio.title: Providing that certain portions of the crime of cruelty to animals do not apply to any person who catches a feral cat to provide vaccination, spaying or neutering and returns such cat back to the location where such cat is caught.
ks:HB 2535|providing that certain portio.summary: As rewritten by the conference report voted on, lets Butler, Labette and Leavenworth counties ask voters to approve extra countywide sales taxes for property tax relief, fire departments and emergency management, and keeps the current city-county sales tax sharing formula through 2027.

ks:HCR 5003|providing for the joint rule.title: Providing for the Joint Rules of the House of Representatives and the Senate for the 2025-2026 biennium.
ks:HCR 5003|providing for the joint rule.summary: Adopts the joint rules of the Kansas House and Senate for 2025 and 2026, covering joint sessions, conference committee procedures, deadlines for introducing and acting on bills, and closed meetings on the security of state officials and buildings.

ks:HB 2594|modifying the elements of the.title: Modifying the elements of the crime of blackmail related to threatened dissemination of any image, video or other recording of another identifiable person who is nude or engaged in sexual activity by changing the connection to breach of privacy and describing the content of the image, video or other recording.
ks:HB 2594|modifying the elements of the.summary: As rewritten by the conference report voted on, puts Kansas on permanent standard time once Missouri passes a similar law, and moves the state to year-round daylight saving time if federal law ever requires it.

ks:HB 2334|enacting the kansas protected.title: Enacting the Kansas protected cell captive insurance company act, providing for the redomestication of a foreign or alien captive insurance company and updating certain terms, requirements and conditions of the captive insurance act, reducing insurance company premium tax rates, creating parity between the insurance agent and public adjuster licensing requirements, authorizing insurers to file certain travel insurance policies under the accident and health line of insurance and authorizing the commissioner of insurance to select and announce the version of certain instructions, calculations and documents in effect for the upcoming calendar year and cause such announcement to be published in the Kansas register not later than December 1 of the current year.
ks:HB 2334|enacting the kansas protected.summary: Creates rules for protected cell captive insurance companies and for moving captive insurers to Kansas, cuts the insurance company premium tax rate from 2% to 1.98% starting in 2026, adds disciplinary rules for public adjusters and changes how travel insurance is classified.

ks:HB 2413|enhancing the criminal penalt.title: Enhancing the criminal penalty for an offense committed with the intent to commit transnational repression, requiring the development of transnational repression recognition and response training, providing that theft of livestock or implements of husbandry is a severity level 5, nonperson felony, providing that the theft of grain or hay is a severity level 6, nonperson felony and providing that certain portions of the crime of cruelty to animals do not apply to any person who catches a feral cat to provide vaccination, spaying or neutering and returns such cat back to the location where such cat is caught.
ks:HB 2413|enhancing the criminal penalt.summary: Makes theft of cattle, horses or farm equipment a felony and theft of at least 400 bushels of grain or 20,000 pounds of hay a lesser felony, raises penalties for transnational repression crimes, and exempts trap-neuter-return of feral cats from animal abandonment and care rules.

ks:HB 2039|adding maternity center to th.title: Adding maternity center to the definition of healthcare provider for purposes of the healthcare provider insurance availability act, amending definitions in the Kansas credentialing act to provide that certain entities providing physical therapy, occupational therapy and speech-language pathology are not home health agencies, clarifying that the authorized activities of paramedics, advanced emergency medical technicians, emergency medical technicians and emergency medical responders may be authorized upon the order of a healthcare professional, permitting certain ambulance services to offer service for less than 24 hours per day, every day of the year, and requiring entities that control automated external defibrillators to register the device with the emergency medical services board.
ks:HB 2039|adding maternity center to th.summary: Expands tasks paramedics, EMTs and emergency responders may perform, exempts non-emergency ambulance services from 24-hour operation, requires registering defibrillators placed in public places, lets accredited maternity centers join the state malpractice coverage fund, and exempts certain therapy-only providers from home health agency rules.

ks:SB 204|providing that the attorney me.title: Providing that the attorney members of the board of trustees of the county law library in certain counties shall be appointed by the chief judge of the judicial district, allowing such boards to authorize the chief judge to use certain fees for the purpose of facilitating and enhancing functions of the district court of the county and requiring the case, warrant and subpoena information be sealed in criminal and juvenile offender cases.
ks:SB 204|providing that the attorney me.summary: Seals criminal and juvenile cases while an arrest warrant is sought until it is served or denied, keeps related subpoenas sealed unless a court orders otherwise, has chief judges appoint attorney members of most county law library boards and lets those boards share library fees with district courts.

ks:HB 2134|amending the kansas open reco.title: Amending the Kansas open records act by limiting certain charges for furnishing records and employee time required to make records available and exempting certain records from disclosure and amending the Kansas open meetings act by providing for the membership calculation of subordinate groups and requiring public bodies or agencies that live stream meetings to ensure that the public is able to observe.
ks:HB 2134|amending the kansas open reco.summary: Limits open-records fees to actual costs, billing staff time at the lowest-cost staff level reasonably needed, without benefits; requires agencies to contact requesters when costs exceed $200 or five staff hours; exempts closed investigations finding no violation; and requires livestreamed meetings be fully viewable.

ks:HB 2280|adding a citation to the code.title: Adding a citation to the code of federal regulations to the definition of veteran and disabled veteran and removing the active requirement from military service members for occupational licensure.
ks:HB 2280|adding a citation to the code.summary: Expands the state definitions of veteran and disabled veteran to include all groups recognized in federal veterans regulations, and lets military spouses qualify for occupational licensing and fee waivers even when the service member is not on active duty.

ks:HB 2075|determining when a law enforc.title: Determining when a law enforcement officer may or shall take a child into custody and requiring that the secretary provide support to such law enforcement officers, the court review involvement in permanency planning and a permanency hearing for a child in custody of the secretary be held within nine months from such child's removal from the and every subsequent hearing 6 months thereafter.
ks:HB 2075|determining when a law enforc.summary: Requires officers to try other options before taking a child into protective custody, requires the state children's agency to begin investigating police referrals within 24 hours, and requires permanency hearings for children in state custody within nine months of removal and every six months after.

ks:SB 139|updating certain definitions t.title: Updating certain definitions, terms and conditions relating to the state banking code.
ks:SB 139|updating certain definitions t.summary: Updates state banking law: requires banks to notify the bank commissioner of top leadership changes, exempts federally insured banks from separate state approval to do business, sets when a merged bank's charter ends, drops some trust-transfer paperwork and changes rules for out-of-state trust companies.

ks:HB 2263|designating a future intercha.title: Designating a future interchange on K-10 highway as the Kris Norton memorial interchange, a portion of K-5 highway as the Rep Marvin S Robinson memorial highway, a portion of United States highway 160 as the CPL Monte Wayne Forrest memorial highway, a portion of United States highway 77 as the POW MIA memorial highway and bridge No. 82-14-6.88 (026) in Clay county as the POW MIA memorial bridge, and redesignating a current portion of the Harry Darby memorial highway for interstate highway 635.
ks:HB 2263|designating a future intercha.summary: Names a future K-10 interchange near Lawrence for Kris Norton, parts of K-5, US-160 and US-77 for Rep. Marvin S. Robinson, CPL Monte Wayne Forrest and POW/MIAs, and a Clay County bridge for POW/MIAs, and redesignates part of the Harry Darby Memorial Highway on I-635.

ks:HB 2653|requiring the secretary of co.title: Requiring the secretary of corrections to assist inmates with obtaining identification and employment-related documentation prior to release from custody.
ks:HB 2653|requiring the secretary of co.summary: Requires the corrections department, within nine months before an inmate's release, to help obtain a birth certificate, Social Security card and state ID, and to give inmates records of their job training, work and education plus a resume, with exceptions for some inmates.

ks:SB 408|excluding a child engaging in.title: Excluding a child engaging in age-appropriate independent activities from the definition of a child in need of care in the revised Kansas code for care of children, requiring the secretary for children and families to enter into a memorandum of understanding with military organizations and create a referral process for children in need of care cases involving children of military personnel to provide families with services that a military family advocacy program offers, authorizing a challenge to a voluntary acknowledgment of paternity as soon as practicable after discovery of fraud, duress or mistake of fact and specifying that certain genetic testing results shall constitute a change of circumstances that warrants a court finding of material mistake of fact.
ks:SB 408|excluding a child engaging in.summary: Lets children do age-appropriate activities like walking to school unsupervised without being deemed in need of care, requires agreements to refer child-welfare cases involving military families to military advocacy programs, and changes rules for signing and challenging voluntary paternity acknowledgments, including with genetic tests.

ks:HB 2149|substitute for hb 2149 by com.title: Substitute for HB 2149 by Committee on Energy, Utilities and Telecommunications - Requiring distributed energy retailers to disclose certain information to residential customers who are offered or seeking to install a distributed energy system, requiring the attorney general to convene an advisory group to develop, approve and periodically revise a standard form for such disclosures and requiring publication thereof, establishing requirements for interconnection and operation of distributed energy systems, increasing the total capacity limitation for an electric public utility's provision of parallel generation service and a formula to determine appropriate system size.
ks:HB 2149|substitute for hb 2149 by com.summary: Requires sellers of home solar and similar systems to give customers disclosures on a standard attorney general form, sets rules for connecting such systems to utilities, sizes them by a usage formula and raises utilities' total limit for them to 8% of peak demand by 2027.

ks:SB 445|providing that the law enforce.title: Providing that the law enforcement officers memorial advisory committee may receive requests for the Kansas highway patrol and the Kansas bureau of investigation to provide temporary personal and other assistance in support of funeral services honoring law enforcement officers who have lost their lives in the line of duty in the service of the state.
ks:SB 445|providing that the law enforce.summary: Requires the Highway Patrol and Kansas Bureau of Investigation, when a law enforcement agency asks through the officers memorial advisory committee, to provide temporary staff and other help for funerals of officers killed in the line of duty.

ks:HB 2605|designating a portion of u s.title: Designating a portion of U.S. highway 36 as the undersheriff Brandon Gaede memorial highway.
ks:HB 2605|designating a portion of u s.summary: Names the part of US-36 within Phillipsburg as the Undersheriff Brandon Gaede Memorial Highway, with signs placed once donations cover their cost plus 50% for upkeep.

ks:HB 2579|designating a portion of k 49.title: Designating a portion of K-49 highway as the Pvt Michael E Gerber memorial highway
ks:HB 2579|designating a portion of k 49.summary: Names part of K-49 in Sumner County, from West 119th Street to US-160, as the Pvt Michael E Gerber Memorial Highway, with signs placed once donations cover their cost plus 50% for upkeep.

ks:HB 2542|designating a portion of unit.title: Designating a portion of United States highway 56 as the Bill Tucker memorial highway.
ks:HB 2542|designating a portion of unit.summary: Names part of US-56 in Morton County, between County Roads 14 and 16, as the Bill Tucker Memorial Highway, with signs placed once donations cover their cost plus 50% for upkeep.

ks:HB 2471|designating a portion of i 35.title: Designating a portion of I-35 as the deputy Sam Smith memorial highway and redesignating a current portion of the 35th infantry division memorial highway for I-35.
ks:HB 2471|designating a portion of i 35.summary: Names part of I-35 in Franklin County as the Deputy Sam Smith Memorial Highway, removing that stretch from the 35th Infantry Division Memorial Highway, with signs placed once donations cover their cost plus 50% for upkeep.

ks:SB 367|providing cities the authority.title: Providing cities the authority to allow the driving of golf carts upon sidewalks.
ks:SB 367|providing cities the authority.summary: Lets cities allow golf carts to be driven on sidewalks, as an exception to the general ban on driving on sidewalks, if the driver is at least 16 and holds a valid class C driver's license.

ks:SB 231|house substitute for sb231 by.title: House Substitute for SB231 by Committee on Elections - Changing the timing of city, school, community college and certain other municipality elections to fall in even-numbered years and requiring the term of office of municipal elected officials to be either two years or four years.
ks:SB 231|house substitute for sb231 by.summary: As passed by the Senate, revises rules for mailings that solicit advance-ballot applications: the sender's name, address and "not a government mailing" disclosure go on one page in 10-point type, the election date may be pre-printed, and mailing instructions replace a pre-addressed return envelope.

tx:SB 33|relating to certain prohibited.title: Relating to certain prohibited transactions and logistical support between a governmental entity and an abortion assistance entity or abortion provider for the procurement of an abortion or related services
tx:SB 33|relating to certain prohibited.summary: Bars cities, counties and other governmental entities from contracting with or spending public money on groups that provide abortion assistance, including travel, lodging or child care for obtaining an abortion, and lets the attorney general sue to stop and recover such spending.

tx:HB 17|relating to the requirements re.title: Relating to the requirements regarding notice of certain property tax-related information to be provided by taxing units and appraisal districts
tx:HB 17|relating to the requirements re.summary: Requires school districts and other local taxing units to mail notice of proposed property tax rates to each property owner, and requires those notices and appraisal district databases to compare proposed tax collections with inflation and population or enrollment growth.

tx:SB 24|relating to the inclusion of an.title: Relating to the inclusion of an understanding of communist regimes and ideologies in the essential knowledge and skills for the social studies curriculum for certain public school students
tx:SB 24|relating to the inclusion of an.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to add instruction on communist regimes and ideologies to social studies standards for grades 4 through 12, covering their history, atrocities, a comparison with U.S. founding principles, and first-person accounts from victims.

tx:SB 509|relating to requiring notice t.title: Relating to requiring notice to the attorney general in an action under the Election Code seeking a temporary restraining order
tx:SB 509|relating to requiring notice t.summary: Requires courts to notify the attorney general by email before a hearing on a temporary restraining order sought under the Election Code, wait at least one hour unless the attorney general waives it, and allow remote participation; orders issued otherwise are void.

tx:HB 4099|relating to the treatment of.title: Relating to the treatment of a patient by a physical therapist without a referral
tx:HB 4099|relating to the treatment of.summary: Lets physical therapists treat a patient without a referral for up to 30 consecutive calendar days, instead of 10 or 15 business days, before needing a referral from a physician or other practitioner to continue.

tx:SB 241|relating to prohibitions on ca.title: Relating to prohibitions on camping in a public place
tx:SB 241|relating to prohibitions on ca.summary: As reported by the House committee, requires cities and counties to set up complaint processes for public camping ban violations and act on complaints within 90 days, and lets the attorney general and state police enforce the ban and recover costs from local governments that fail to act.

tx:HB 3664|relating to the training of p.title: Relating to the training of prospective grand jurors and to grand jury proceedings
tx:HB 3664|relating to the training of p.summary: Requires prospective grand jurors to complete a training course, which may be online, on grand jury rules, selection and procedures run by the state Office of Court Administration before being impaneled; missing training cannot be used to overturn an indictment or conviction.

tx:SB 12|relating to parental rights in.title: Relating to parental rights in public education, including the imposition of certain requirements and prohibitions regarding instruction and diversity, equity, and inclusion duties
tx:SB 12|relating to parental rights in.summary: Bars public schools from assigning diversity, equity and inclusion duties, from offering instruction or programs on sexual orientation or gender identity in pre-K through 12th grade, and from sponsoring clubs based on those topics; requires parental consent for clubs and expands parents' rights to records and grievances.

tx:SB 1150|relating to the plugging of a.title: Relating to the plugging of and reporting on inactive wells subject to the jurisdiction of the Railroad Commission of Texas; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:SB 1150|relating to the plugging of a.summary: Limits extensions of plugging deadlines for oil and gas wells inactive more than 15 years and completed over 25 years earlier, requires annual testing reports on long-inactive wells, and directs the Railroad Commission to set penalties and report yearly to state leaders.

tx:SB 2253|relating to the certification.title: Relating to the certification of public school educators, including financial and other assistance provided to public schools by the Texas Education Agency
tx:SB 2253|relating to the certification.summary: Bars school districts from hiring uncertified teachers for core-subject courses, allowing approved delays until the 2029-30 school year; sets traditional, residency and alternative teacher preparation routes; and pays districts $1,000 for each recently hired uncertified teacher who earns certification.

tx:SJR 27|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment regarding the membership of the State Commission on Judicial Conduct, the membership of the tribunal to review the commission's recommendations, and the authority of the commission, the tribunal, and the Texas Supreme Court to more effectively sanction judges and justices for judicial misconduct
tx:SJR 27|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment reshaping the State Commission on Judicial Conduct into six judges appointed by the Supreme Court and seven citizens appointed by the governor, changing the tribunal that reviews its findings, and requiring removed judges be barred from future judicial office.

tx:HB 2983|relating to impoundment stora.title: Relating to impoundment, storage, and notification fees for vehicles stored at vehicle storage facilities; authorizing fee increases and decreases; requiring the adjustment of authorized fees
tx:HB 2983|relating to impoundment stora.summary: As reported by the House committee, lets vehicle storage facilities charge $70 a day to store electric or hybrid passenger vehicles, requires state regulators to adjust impoundment, storage and notice fees for inflation from 2005 through 2019, and revises later two-year fee adjustments.

tx:HB 104|relating to the creation of th.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas future fund, the Texas future fund investment review board, and permissible investments by the economic stabilization fund
tx:HB 104|relating to the creation of th.summary: Creates the Texas future fund, starting with $5 billion from the state's rainy day fund, to invest in frontier technology, defense-critical industries and other innovative technologies, overseen by a nine-member board appointed by the comptroller, governor and lieutenant governor.

tx:SB 800|relating to a public instituti.title: Relating to a public institution of higher education's orientation on the institution's sexual harassment, sexual assault, dating violence, and stalking policy
tx:SB 800|relating to a public instituti.summary: Requires colleges' sexual harassment and assault policy orientations to include a video naming Title IX coordinators, explaining how to report sexual assault and listing support services, and requires public college student ID cards to show the National Sexual Assault Hotline.

tx:HB 5246|relating to the administratio.title: Relating to the administration, powers, and duties of the Texas Space Commission, the Texas Aerospace Research and Space Economy Consortium, and other governmental entities and institutions regarding aerospace, aviation, and space exploration initiatives and to the abolishment of the spaceport trust fund
tx:HB 5246|relating to the administratio.summary: Lets the Texas Space Commission buy or lease capacity on rockets, satellites and other space vehicles after a public board vote, allows closed meetings on certain grants and defense facilities, and abolishes the spaceport trust fund, moving most of its balance to general revenue.

tx:HB 1353|relating to international coo.title: Relating to international cooperation agreements between certain state agencies and the United Mexican States and funding for infrastructure investment in this state; providing authority for certain agencies to issue bonds
tx:HB 1353|relating to international coo.summary: Adds the environmental quality and utility commissions to the state agencies that may issue bonds for agreements with Mexico, and lets those agencies jointly invest in Texas infrastructure with the North American Development Bank, with governor and budget board approval for spending.

tx:HB 2149|relating to nonconforming lan.title: Relating to nonconforming land uses after the adoption of or change to a zoning regulation or boundary
tx:HB 2149|relating to nonconforming lan.summary: Bars cities from forcing owners to stop a land use made nonconforming by new zoning unless the owner agrees, with payment or time to recoup losses, and bars state and local governments from blocking repair, rebuilding or necessary expansion of such properties.

tx:SB 785|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of new HUD-code manufactured housing
tx:SB 785|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires cities with zoning to allow new HUD-code manufactured homes by right in at least one residential zone, bars special use permits for them when not required for other homes in that zone, and exempts historic districts and certain deed-restricted cities.

tx:HB 168|relating to the age at which a.title: Relating to the age at which a person in this state may marry
tx:HB 168|relating to the age at which a.summary: Bars anyone under 18 from marrying in Texas, even if a court has granted them adult legal status, makes such marriages void, and lets a person who married as a minor seek property division and spousal support.

tx:HB 150|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Texas Cyber Command as a component institution of The University of Texas System and the transfer to it of certain powers and duties of the Department of Information Resources
tx:HB 150|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates the Texas Cyber Command, a state agency led by a governor-appointed chief with a San Antonio facility, to prevent and respond to cyberattacks on governments and critical infrastructure, and transfers cybersecurity duties to it from the Department of Information Resources.

tx:SB 2807|relating to the consideration.title: Relating to the considerations when determining whether an operator of a motor vehicle is an employee of a motor carrier or an independent contractor
tx:SB 2807|relating to the consideration.summary: Requires state authorization to operate driverless vehicles commercially and lets the motor vehicle department suspend unsafe ones; bars counting a trucking company's safety technology or practices when deciding whether a driver is an employee or independent contractor.

tx:SB 1191|relating to the development o.title: Relating to the development of a standard method of computing a student's high school grade point average
tx:SB 1191|relating to the development o.summary: Requires the education commissioner to create, and school districts to use, a standard high school grade point average method that gives equal extra weight to AP, IB, OnRamps and academic dual credit courses and different weight to workforce dual credit courses.

tx:HB 2876|relating to the amendment of.title: Relating to the amendment of an existing comprehensive development agreement for a portion of State Highway 130 to facilitate nontolled transportation projects
tx:HB 2876|relating to the amendment of.summary: Requires the transportation department to extend its private toll agreement for State Highway 130 Segments 5 and 6 by up to 20 years in exchange for payments, which must fund county-approved non-toll road projects between I-35 and SH 130.

tx:HB 4234|relating to a requirement tha.title: Relating to a requirement that a student's postsecondary transcript include the average or median grade awarded in each class
tx:HB 4234|relating to a requirement tha.summary: Requires public universities to show, next to each student's grade on transcripts, the class's average grade or median letter grade, beginning fall 2025, except for pass-fail, independent study and classes of 10 or fewer students.

tx:SB 8|relating to agreements between s.title: Relating to agreements between sheriffs and the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement to enforce federal immigration law
tx:SB 8|relating to agreements between s.summary: Requires sheriffs of counties that operate or contract for a jail to seek agreements with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement letting their officers enforce federal immigration law, and creates a state grant program based on county population to cover unreimbursed costs.

tx:SB 1388|relating to family support se.title: Relating to family support services provided under a Health and Human Services Commission program
tx:SB 1388|relating to family support se.summary: Renames the state's alternatives to abortion program the Thriving Texas Families Program, requires the state to verify providers are not associated with abortion services providers, bars family planning services through it, and simplifies grant processes for providers with under $2 million in revenue.

tx:HB 13|relating to creating the texas.title: Relating to creating the Texas Interoperability Council and a grant program administered by the council
tx:HB 13|relating to creating the texas.summary: Creates the Texas Interoperability Council, chaired by the state emergency management chief, to plan a statewide emergency communications network for first responders and run a grant program helping local governments buy compatible communication equipment, build infrastructure and train staff.

tx:HB 3700|relating to detection and pre.title: Relating to detection and prevention of fraud, waste, and abuse in all Texas Workforce Commission programs
tx:HB 3700|relating to detection and pre.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to set up procedures and systems to prevent, detect and investigate fraud, waste and abuse in its programs and grants, including public and anonymous reporting options, annual reports to the Legislature and protection for employees who report.

tx:SB 2312|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment and powers and duties of the Texas Advisory Committee on Geopolitical Conflict
tx:SB 2312|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a nine-member state advisory committee that must run a foreign-invasion tabletop exercise and report to the governor by October 1, 2026, on conflict risks to supply chains, prescription drugs and critical infrastructure; it can issue subpoenas and expires in 2029.

tx:SB 458|relating to an appraisal proce.title: Relating to an appraisal process for disputed losses under personal automobile or residential property insurance policies
tx:SB 458|relating to an appraisal proce.summary: Requires personal auto and home insurance policies issued or renewed starting January 1, 2026, to include an appraisal process for settling disputes over the amount of a loss, with the appraisal result binding on both the policyholder and insurer except for fraud or material mistake.

tx:SB 205|relating to fetal development.title: Relating to fetal development instruction included as part of the public school health curriculum in certain grade levels
tx:SB 205|relating to fetal development.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to add medically accurate instruction on fetal development, including growth during each trimester of pregnancy, to the health curriculum for seventh and eighth graders, and lets local school health councils recommend curriculum for it.

tx:SB 609|relating to requiring independ.title: Relating to requiring independent school districts, home-rule school districts, and open-enrollment charter schools to comply with legally required policies
tx:SB 609|relating to requiring independ.summary: Requires school districts, home-rule districts and charter schools, along with their boards and staff, to carry out and follow any policy that state law requires them to adopt, not just adopt it.

tx:SB 1871|relating to discipline manage.title: Relating to discipline management and access to telehealth mental health services in public schools
tx:SB 1871|relating to discipline manage.summary: Lets teachers remove a student from class after a single disruptive incident, lifts the time limit on in-school suspensions, allows virtual alternative programs for expelled students, shields teachers from discipline for good-faith removals, and requires parental consent for school telehealth mental health services.

tx:SB 925|relating to certain agreements.title: Relating to certain agreements with collective bargaining organizations related to certain publicly funded public work contracts
tx:SB 925|relating to certain agreements.summary: Bars governments awarding public works contracts paid for with state, local or federal money, ratepayer money or user fees from favoring or penalizing bidders based on whether they have agreements with labor unions, expanding a ban that previously covered state-funded projects.

tx:HB 2086|relating to a motion for dete.title: Relating to a motion for determining a plaintiff is a vexatious litigant
tx:HB 2086|relating to a motion for dete.summary: Lets a court, on its own motion within 90 days after a defendant answers a lawsuit, hold a hearing to decide whether the plaintiff is a vexatious litigant, except in cases involving parent-child relationships; currently only a defendant can seek that finding.

tx:SB 9|relating to the confinement or r.title: Relating to the confinement or release of defendants before trial or sentencing, including regulating charitable bail organizations, and the conditions of and procedures for setting bail and reviewing bail decisions
tx:SB 9|relating to the confinement or r.summary: Bars court-appointed magistrates from granting bail to certain felony defendants, including those on bail, parole or probation, with immigration detainers, or charged with murder or aggravated sexual assault; lets prosecutors seek next-day district judge review of felony bail decisions; expands charitable bail group reporting.

tx:HB 138|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Health Impact, Cost, and Coverage Analysis Program; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 138|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a program at the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston to analyze, at legislative leaders' request, the cost and health effects of proposed health insurance coverage mandates, funded by an annual fee on health insurers and HMOs.

tx:HB 4735|relating to rural development.title: Relating to rural development funds and insurance tax credits for certain investments in those funds; authorizing fees
tx:HB 4735|relating to rural development.summary: Lets the state comptroller approve private rural development funds that invest in small businesses in rural areas, with up to $300 million in investment authority, and gives insurance companies that invest in them up to $150 million in credits against state insurance taxes.

tx:HR 1499|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, S.B. No. 650
tx:HR 1499|suspending limitations on con.summary: Suspends House rules to let negotiators on a bill requiring electronic ID scanning in alcohol sales drop an exemption for package stores, so package store permit holders would also have to scan IDs to verify a buyer's age.

tx:HB 18|relating to the making to or ac.title: Relating to the making to or acceptance of political contributions by, and the making of political expenditures by, a member of the legislature during certain absences from the state; authorizing a civil penalty
tx:HB 18|relating to the making to or ac.summary: Bars legislators who leave the state to block legislative action, and committees supporting them, from accepting contributions above a daily per diem from any one donor or spending campaign money on travel, food or lodging for the absence; violations carry civil penalties up to $5,000.

tx:HB 121|relating to measures for ensur.title: Relating to measures for ensuring public school safety, including the commissioning of peace officers by the Texas Education Agency, public school safety and security requirements, and the provision of safety-related resources
tx:HB 121|relating to measures for ensur.summary: Lets the Texas Education Agency hire inspectors with peace-officer status to monitor school safety, makes exemptions from the armed-security-officer requirement expire yearly, requires an annual state school-security report, and adds disability experts to threat assessments of special education students.

tx:SB 2753|relating to a study on the fe.title: Relating to a study on the feasibility of integrating early voting by personal appearance and election day voting, including the manner in which election returns are processed and other related changes
tx:SB 2753|relating to a study on the fe.summary: Shortens early voting to start 12 days before an election and run through the day before Election Day, makes early voting sites Election Day polling places, and counts in-person early ballots with Election Day ballots, starting once the secretary of state certifies counties are ready.

tx:SB 510|relating to the failure of a v.title: Relating to the failure of a voter registrar to comply with voter registration laws
tx:SB 510|relating to the failure of a v.summary: Lets the secretary of state withhold certain state election funds from a county voter registrar who, after written notice, fails to timely approve, change or cancel registrations, schedule or decide voter challenges, or send required challenge notices under any part of the election code.

tx:SB 314|relating to prohibiting certai.title: Relating to prohibiting certain food additives from being included in free or reduced-price meals provided by school districts
tx:SB 314|relating to prohibiting certai.summary: Bars public schools and charter schools from serving free or reduced-price meals containing 17 listed additives, including several artificial dyes, titanium dioxide and potassium bromate, starting with the 2025-26 school year, with food contracts covered when signed or renewed on or after September 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1349|relating to creating the crim.title: Relating to creating the criminal offenses of transnational repression and unauthorized enforcement of foreign law and to a study and law enforcement training regarding transnational repression
tx:SB 1349|relating to creating the crim.summary: Creates crimes for committing assault, stalking, harassment or similar offenses as an agent of a foreign government or terrorist group, with enhanced penalties, and for enforcing foreign law in Texas without approval; requires police training and a state study on transnational repression.

tx:SB 2722|relating to the use of certai.title: Relating to the use of certain tolls and charges imposed by certain counties; authorizing a civil penalty
tx:SB 2722|relating to the use of certai.summary: Limits how counties of four million or more people may spend toll road revenue, requiring surplus to go mainly to county roads divided among commissioners precincts and, through 2030, a share to the main city for emergency services, with civil penalties for violations.

tx:SB 1395|relating to the membership of.title: Relating to the membership of a school district's local school health advisory council
tx:SB 1395|relating to the membership of.summary: Requires school health advisory council members to be appointed by individual trustees for one-year terms, makes district employees and students nonvoting members, and allows only parents who are not district employees or relatives of employees to hold council leadership positions.

tx:SB 16|relating to requiring a person.title: Relating to requiring a person to submit proof of citizenship to register to vote; creating criminal offenses
tx:SB 16|relating to requiring a person.summary: Requires people registering to vote to provide proof of U.S. citizenship, such as a passport or birth certificate, unless officials can verify citizenship through government databases; unverified voters may vote only for Congress; makes it a state jail felony for noncitizens to apply to register.

tx:SB 1978|relating to the interconnecti.title: Relating to the interconnection of a facility in the ERCOT power region to certain other facilities
tx:SB 1978|relating to the interconnecti.summary: Bars utilities and others from connecting the state's main power grid to out-of-state facilities unless the connection would not add federal control over the grid and state regulators first find it in the public interest and later approve a certificate.

tx:SB 1950|relating to the eligibility o.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain individuals for unemployment benefits and the validity of certain claims for unemployment benefits submitted to the Texas Workforce Commission
tx:SB 1950|relating to the eligibility o.summary: Raises eligibility requirements for unemployment benefits, requiring at least five weekly job search activities, wages in three quarters of the base period and identity verification; disqualifies people who skip job interviews; requires claim cross-checks against other records; and bars benefits for five years after fraud.

tx:SB 2422|relating to investigations an.title: Relating to investigations and disciplinary or punitive action by the Texas Medical Board regarding certain treatments or practices regarding COVID-19 and to the required expungement of certain records
tx:SB 2422|relating to investigations an.summary: Bars the Texas Medical Board from investigating or disciplining doctors for prescribing ivermectin, hydroxychloroquine or budesonide for COVID-19 or for statements or practices about masks, and requires it to expunge related records since 2020 and vacate related discipline by December 1, 2025.

tx:SB 2322|relating to the findings requ.title: Relating to the findings required to be made by the comptroller of public accounts in order to recommend for approval an application for a limitation on the taxable value of eligible property for school district maintenance and operations ad valorem tax purposes under the Texas Jobs, Energy, Technology, and Innovation Act
tx:SB 2322|relating to the findings requ.summary: Exempts electric generation facilities from the requirement that a school property tax limitation agreement under the state's business incentive program be a compelling factor in a competitive site selection decision before the comptroller can recommend approval.

tx:SB 1962|relating to the assessment of.title: Relating to the assessment of public school students, public school accountability and actions, and proceedings challenging the operations of the public school system
tx:SB 1962|relating to the assessment of.summary: Requires the state to replace its standardized tests by 2027-28 with shorter end-of-year exams and optional beginning- and middle-of-year progress tests, limits district benchmark tests, bars schools from using public money to sue the state, and allows state conservators for districts that do.

tx:SB 28|relating to a lottery game play.title: Relating to a lottery game played or facilitated for play by telephone or through an Internet or mobile Internet application; creating criminal offenses
tx:SB 28|relating to a lottery game play.summary: Bars buying lottery tickets by phone or through internet or mobile apps, and bars businesses from taking orders, selling tickets or arranging ticket purchases for players that way for pay, making buying a Class C misdemeanor and courier services a Class A misdemeanor.

tx:SB 1719|relating to the rulemaking po.title: Relating to the rulemaking power of the Texas Supreme Court
tx:SB 1719|relating to the rulemaking po.summary: Revises the Texas Supreme Court's rulemaking power so its civil procedure rules supersede only procedural laws passed before May 15, 1939, invalidates court rules that conflict with laws for cases filed on or after the bill takes effect, and repeals related provisions in several codes.

tx:SB 379|relating to prohibiting the pu.title: Relating to prohibiting the purchase of sweetened soft drinks under the supplemental nutrition assistance program
tx:SB 379|relating to prohibiting the pu.summary: Bars recipients of food assistance benefits under the federal SNAP program from using them to buy sweetened drinks or candy, and requires state agencies to seek any needed federal waiver before putting the ban into effect.

tx:SB 1025|relating to the text of ballo.title: Relating to the text of ballot propositions that increase taxes
tx:SB 1025|relating to the text of ballo.summary: Requires ballot propositions asking voters to approve a new or higher tax to state the tax rate or amount sought and to begin with the statement "THIS IS A TAX INCREASE" in capital letters.

tx:HB 184|relating to student loan repay.title: Relating to student loan repayment assistance for certain prosecuting attorneys who are employed as part of the border prosecution unit
tx:HB 184|relating to student loan repay.summary: Creates a student loan repayment program for licensed attorneys working as prosecutors in the border prosecution unit, paying 25 percent of their loan balance for each of up to four years of service, capped at $110,000 per attorney and $2 million per budget period.

tx:HB 3154|relating to the creation powe.title: Relating to the creation, powers, duties, and financing of the Wise Regional Water District; granting a limited power of eminent domain; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose fees; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 3154|relating to the creation powe.summary: Creates the Wise Regional Water District, covering Wise County and member cities' areas and run by a board of local appointees, to build and operate wholesale water and wastewater systems and reservoirs; lets it issue bonds, charge fees and use limited eminent domain, but bars property taxes.

tx:HB 1533|relating to the system for ap.title: Relating to the system for appraising property for ad valorem tax purposes
tx:HB 1533|relating to the system for ap.summary: Requires appraisal districts in counties of 120,000 or more to post appraisal records online and update them weekly, eases notice for phone or video protest hearings, lets certain tenants who pay a property's taxes appeal values up to $5 million through arbitration, and adds taxpayer representatives as review-board trainers.

tx:HB 5680|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Bayou Belle Municipal Management District No. 1; granting a limited power of eminent domain; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes
tx:HB 5680|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates the Bayou Belle Municipal Management District No. 1 on about 605 acres in Liberty County with a five-member elected board, letting it build water, sewer, drainage, road and other improvements, levy assessments and fees, issue bonds and use limited eminent domain; property taxes require voter approval.

tx:SB 739|relating to the definition of.title: Relating to the definition of authorized peace officer for purposes of certain laws governing the installation and use of tracking equipment and access to certain communications
tx:SB 739|relating to the definition of.summary: Adds investigators commissioned by the state insurance commissioner to the peace officers who may seek court approval to install tracking equipment and obtain access to electronic communications during investigations.

tx:SB 769|relating to a report by the te.title: Relating to a report by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board regarding enrollment and success in higher education for students with disabilities
tx:SB 769|relating to a report by the te.summary: Requires the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to report to the Legislature by December 1, 2027, on college enrollment and success of students with disabilities, including factors affecting them, with public colleges required to supply information on request.

tx:SB 1568|relating to the issuance of a.title: Relating to the issuance of animal friendly specialty license plates
tx:SB 1568|relating to the issuance of a.summary: Requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to issue an additional specialty license plate reading "Spay. Neuter. Adopt." alongside the existing "Animal Friendly" plate, with fees beyond administrative costs going to the state's animal friendly account.

tx:SB 2943|relating to the prohibition o.title: Relating to the prohibition of certain actions by a state agency against an applicant for or holder of an occupational license
tx:SB 2943|relating to the prohibition o.summary: Bars state licensing agencies from limiting licenses or imposing penalties based on an applicant's or license holder's sincerely held religious beliefs, religious speech or religious group membership, with exceptions for peace officers, standards of care and emergency medical care; lets people sue for relief.

tx:HB 643|relating to the requirement fo.title: Relating to the requirement for payment bonds from certain public work contractors
tx:HB 643|relating to the requirement fo.summary: Raises from $25,000 to $100,000 the contract value at which prime contractors on public works for governmental entities other than cities and joint airport boards must post a payment bond, for contracts solicited after the law takes effect.

tx:SB 1592|relating to the collection of.title: Relating to the collection of state and local hotel occupancy taxes and assessments related to hotels by an accommodations intermediary
