tx:SB 1592|relating to the collection of.summary: Requires online booking companies and other accommodations intermediaries to collect state and local hotel occupancy taxes on rooms booked through them and send them to the comptroller, and relieves hotels of collecting the tax on those bookings.

tx:HB 5247|relating to alternative capit.title: Relating to alternative capital recovery process for certain utilities
tx:HB 5247|relating to alternative capit.summary: Lets certain electric utilities operating only in the ERCOT grid and building Permian Basin transmission lines, whose yearly capital spending exceeds three times depreciation, adjust rates through one annual proceeding to recover transmission and distribution investments, deferring some costs; expires at the end of 2035.

tx:SB 1261|relating to the financing of.title: Relating to the financing of water supply projects included in the state water plan; authorizing the issuance of obligations
tx:SB 1261|relating to the financing of.summary: Lets state and local governmental entities issue bonds and other debt, not backed by property taxes, to finance state water plan supply projects costing at least $750 million, with terms up to 50 years or, if shorter, the project's expected useful life.

tx:HB 1621|relating to a matching grant.title: Relating to a matching grant program for technological enhancements at hospitals providing mental health care services
tx:HB 1621|relating to a matching grant.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to create a grant program helping hospitals that provide mental health care upgrade technology such as health records and data security, with hospitals matching each grant dollar-for-dollar from non-state funds.

tx:HB 5093|relating to disclosure under.title: Relating to disclosure under the public information law of certain contact information of a notary public that is maintained by the secretary of state
tx:HB 5093|relating to disclosure under.summary: Lets the secretary of state release the home address, home phone number and email address of notaries public under the public information law, creating an exception to an existing confidentiality protection for personal identifying information.

tx:HB 2284|relating to the licensing and.title: Relating to the licensing and regulation of music therapists; requiring an occupational license; authorizing fees
tx:HB 2284|relating to the licensing and.summary: Creates state licensing of music therapists by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, requiring a license to practice or use the title starting September 1, 2026, with age, degree, board certification and criminal background check requirements and fees.

tx:HB 4222|relating to authorizing certa.title: Relating to authorizing certain counties to impose a hotel occupancy tax, the applicability and rates of that tax in certain counties, and the use of revenue from that tax
tx:HB 4222|relating to authorizing certa.summary: Lets a county of over 90,000 people that borders a Gulf bay and contains part of the Guadalupe River impose a hotel tax of up to 7% (2% in or near cities with their own hotel tax) and use revenue for county airport improvements for up to 20 years.

tx:HB 2652|relating to establishing a ce.title: Relating to establishing a certified caregiver pilot program in the Borderplex workforce development area
tx:HB 2652|relating to establishing a ce.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to run a pilot program in the Borderplex area that licenses child-care workers to provide after-hours care in their homes and subsidizes up to six months of such care for 30 single-parent families in job training.

tx:HB 3711|relating to the investigation.title: Relating to the investigation and prosecution of certain open meetings offenses as offenses against public administration
tx:HB 3711|relating to the investigation.summary: Requires police to send the attorney general's open records division copies of probable-cause reports on open meetings crimes, lets prosecutors request that division's help investigating, and requires prosecutors who drop such cases to post notice and their reasons online for a year.

tx:SB 1567|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of home-rule municipalities to regulate the occupancy of dwelling units
tx:SB 1567|relating to the authority of.summary: Bars home-rule cities under 250,000 people that contain or adjoin a university campus of over 20,000 students from limiting how many people may live in a home based on age, family status, occupation or relationship, while allowing limits tied to bedroom size; lets residents sue.

tx:SB 2137|relating to the allocation of.title: Relating to the allocation of low income housing tax credits
tx:SB 2137|relating to the allocation of.summary: Bars the state housing agency, for the 2026 and 2027 award cycles, from using local public school ratings as a requirement or scoring factor when awarding low-income housing tax credits, and requires a report on the effects by November 1, 2027.

tx:SB 1844|relating to disannexation of.title: Relating to disannexation of certain areas of a municipality for failure to provide services
tx:SB 1844|relating to disannexation of.summary: Lets a majority of property owners, rather than voters, petition to remove an area from a city that fails to provide services, adds areas along navigable waterways not connected to city water and sewer service, speeds court hearings, and denies tax refunds for those waterway areas.

tx:HB 4744|relating to the role of the m.title: Relating to the role of the members of the board of an appraisal district
tx:HB 4744|relating to the role of the m.summary: Requires appraisal district boards to develop their two-year property reappraisal plans according to state appraisal law as well as generally accepted appraisal practices.

tx:SB 2075|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment, powers and duties, terms, and governance of certain advisory bodies for programs administered by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx:SB 2075|relating to the establishment.summary: Standardizes advisory boards for programs run by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, renaming committees and councils as boards, setting staggered six-year member terms and two-year terms for presiding officers, and letting the licensing commission create new program advisory boards.

tx:HB 5627|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas Commission on Public School Teacher Retirement Funding Transparency
tx:HB 5627|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates a seven-member commission of legislators and a governor's appointee to recommend how to fold state teacher retirement contributions into school funding formulas and set employer contributions that keep the Teacher Retirement System sound, reporting by December 31, 2026.

tx:HB 5085|relating to a study on the im.title: Relating to a study on the impact of certain seed banks and seed preservation on access to food and the environment
tx:HB 5085|relating to a study on the im.summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to study how seed banks and seed preservation in counties of over 2 million people with a conservation facility affect food access and the environment, including ecosystem recovery after natural disasters, and to report recommendations by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 4226|relating to an exemption from.title: Relating to an exemption from the taxes imposed on the sale, use, or rental of a motor vehicle for a vehicle purchased, used, or rented by a nonprofit food bank
tx:HB 4226|relating to an exemption from.summary: Exempts from motor vehicle sales, use and rental taxes vehicles bought or rented by nonprofit food banks for their work, and vehicles used to house people by certain nonprofits serving chronically homeless people with disabling conditions.

tx:HB 3595|relating to an emergency prep.title: Relating to an emergency preparedness and contingency operations plan, including temperature regulation, for assisted living facility residents during an emergency; providing penalties
tx:HB 3595|relating to an emergency prep.summary: Requires assisted living facilities to adopt emergency plans by January 1, 2026, providing climate-controlled areas kept between 68 and 82 degrees during power outages and notifying the state of outages over 12 hours; requires state backup-power standards for newly built facilities and allows penalties.

tx:HB 1523|relating to a prohibition on.title: Relating to a prohibition on the authorization by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality of the use of a Class V injection well for certain aquifer storage and recovery projects
tx:HB 1523|relating to a prohibition on.summary: Bars state environmental regulators, through 2027, from authorizing Class V injection wells for aquifer storage projects of a utility serving a city of 750,000 or more where a groundwater district in a neighboring county has declared such wells an environmental risk.

tx:SB 552|relating to changing the eligi.title: Relating to changing the eligibility of certain persons to receive community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision
tx:SB 552|relating to changing the eligi.summary: Makes defendants who entered the country without inspection or violated their visa status, and lacked legal status when the offense occurred, ineligible for probation or deferred adjudication, for offenses committed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 26|relating to public education in.title: Relating to public education, including the rights and compensation of public school educators and funding for teacher compensation under the Foundation School Program
tx:SB 26|relating to public education in.summary: Gives school districts $2,500 to $10,000 per teacher with three or more years' experience, depending on experience and district size, to fund raises; raises incentive pay amounts; funds liability insurance and job-rights assistance for teachers; and makes teachers' children eligible for prekindergarten in their district.

tx:HB 5666|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Fenske Road Municipal Utility District of Harris County; granting a limited power of eminent domain; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes
tx:HB 5666|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates the Fenske Road Municipal Utility District on about 34 acres in Harris County, subject to city consent and a confirmation election, letting it build water, sewer, drainage and road facilities, issue bonds and impose fees; property taxes require voter approval.

tx:HB 5228|relating to the collection of.title: Relating to the collection of certain incident-based data reported to the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement
tx:HB 5228|relating to the collection of.summary: Requires the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement to set quality and accuracy policies for police traffic-stop data, post the data and a glossary online, review its reporting guidelines every two years, and report on a study of the data by January 1, 2027.

tx:HB 561|relating to the eligibility of.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain local governmental entities affected by the realignment of defense worker jobs or facilities to receive grants
tx:HB 561|relating to the eligibility of.summary: Makes city-owned water and sewer utilities in defense communities eligible for state Texas Military Preparedness Commission grants given to local entities affected by federal realignment of defense jobs or facilities.

tx:HB 1773|relating to allowing the boar.title: Relating to allowing the board of trustees of certain school districts to create a nonvoting student trustee position on the board
tx:HB 1773|relating to allowing the boar.summary: Lets school boards appoint a student trustee from the 11th or 12th grade who can attend and take part in open meetings but cannot vote, make motions, attend closed sessions, count toward a quorum, or be paid.

tx:HB 499|relating to a warning label on.title: Relating to a warning label on social media platforms concerning the association between a minor's social media usage and significant mental health issues
tx:HB 499|relating to a warning label on.summary: Requires certain social media platforms to show users a warning about links between minors' social media use and mental health problems each time the platform opens, including the 988 crisis line, starting April 1, 2026; excludes gaming sites.

tx:HB 1277|relating to the study of plan.title: Relating to the study of plant disease and pest outbreaks by the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service
tx:HB 1277|relating to the study of plan.summary: Requires the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service to study each plant disease or pest outbreak in Texas every year, publish annual reports, and issue a summary report with policy recommendations by January 1, 2028.

tx:HB 2015|relating to the consideration.title: Relating to the consideration of water conservation by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality when determining whether to grant or deny a petition for the creation of a municipal utility district
tx:HB 2015|relating to the consideration.summary: Requires petitions to create a municipal utility district in Hill Country counties to include a water conservation plan, and requires state environmental regulators to weigh whether the district would unreasonably harm water conservation before approving it.

tx:HB 4530|relating to the dedication an.title: Relating to the dedication and management of water rights placed in the Texas Water Trust
tx:HB 4530|relating to the dedication an.summary: Directs the state parks and wildlife department to encourage donations, leases or sales of surface water rights to the Texas Water Trust for environmental needs, and lets the trust hold groundwater rights approved by the state water board, with notice to local groundwater districts.

tx:HB 1804|relating to compliance with t.title: Relating to compliance with the filing requirements of certain reports of political contributions and expenditures, including as a qualification for public elective office; providing an administrative penalty
tx:HB 1804|relating to compliance with t.summary: Requires the Texas Ethics Commission to monitor whether local governments post required campaign finance reports online and lets it fine those that do not comply within 30 days of notice up to $2,500 per day, starting in 2026.

tx:HB 5678|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Rivers Market Place Municipal Management District; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes; granting a limited power of eminent domain
tx:HB 5678|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates the Rivers Market Place Municipal Management District in the Elgin area to provide public improvements and services, allowing it, subject to voter approval, to issue bonds, impose assessments, fees and taxes, and use limited eminent domain.

tx:HB 876|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of certain information sharing and analysis organizations by the Department of Information Resources
tx:HB 876|relating to the establishment.summary: Lets the Department of Information Resources set up an interstate organization for states to share information on cybersecurity threats and fixes, alongside the existing in-state cybersecurity information-sharing organization.

tx:HB 1269|relating to the plant disease.title: Relating to the plant disease and pest prevention grant program
tx:HB 1269|relating to the plant disease.summary: Creates a Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service grant program, with up to 20 grants a year, for Texas university-affiliated researchers studying prevention of plant diseases and pests, funded by a new state fund of donations and appropriations.

tx:HB 2578|relating to landlord and tena.title: Relating to landlord and tenant dispute information reported by courts and published on a publicly accessible Internet website
tx:HB 2578|relating to landlord and tena.summary: Requires courts to report landlord-tenant cases such as evictions, lockouts and security deposit disputes by category, and requires the state court administration office to publish searchable online data on each case's court, legal representation and outcome.

tx:HB 3540|relating to the administratio.title: Relating to the administration of a medication and the ordering and administration of an immunization or vaccination by a pharmacist
tx:HB 3540|relating to the administratio.summary: Lets pharmacists order and give flu and COVID-19 vaccines to patients 3 and older and other FDA-approved or federally recommended vaccines to patients 5 and older without a physician protocol, allows delegation to certified pharmacy technicians, and requires notifying the patient's provider within three business days.

tx:SB 2268|relating to loans and grants.title: Relating to loans and grants awarded from the Texas energy fund
tx:SB 2268|relating to loans and grants.summary: Lets the state utility commission disburse Texas energy fund power plant loans after December 31, 2025, when market factors justify it, allows different loan security for city-owned utilities and electric co-ops, and keeps loan and grant applicant information confidential.

tx:HB 4683|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to use certain tax revenue for hotel and convention center projects
tx:HB 4683|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets a city of 15,000 to 30,000 people bisected by U.S. Highway 75, in a large county next to a county of at least 2 million, receive and pledge certain tax revenue from a hotel and convention center project to pay for it.

tx:HB 2614|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of motor vehicle booting
tx:HB 2614|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires a 30-minute observed violation and 30-minute warning before booting, limits booting to business hours at many lots, bars booting companies from big cities and college towns lacking local rules, and makes violators liable for owners' lost work and travel costs from reckless or intentional violations.

tx:HB 213|relating to the inclusion of c.title: Relating to the inclusion of chronically absent students as students at risk of dropping out of school and the collection and reporting of data regarding those students
tx:HB 213|relating to the inclusion of c.summary: Adds students absent more than 10 percent of instructional time to the at-risk-of-dropping-out category that gets accelerated instruction, and requires schools to report chronic absence numbers by student group, which the state must publish annually.

tx:HB 365|relating to the authority of t.title: Relating to the authority of the Texas Water Development Board to provide financial assistance from the economically distressed areas account that is not required to be repaid
tx:HB 365|relating to the authority of t.summary: Raises the share of state economically distressed areas bonds that the Texas Water Development Board may give as water and sewer aid that does not have to be repaid, from 70 percent to 90 percent.

tx:HB 220|relating to the minimum standa.title: Relating to the minimum standards of care provided to sexual assault survivors by health care facilities
tx:HB 220|relating to the minimum standa.summary: Requires health care facilities treating sexual assault survivors to provide FDA-approved emergency contraception that works by delaying ovulation, if the survivor consents and it is clinically indicated, and bars them from providing drugs or devices that end a pregnancy.

tx:SB 57|relating to provisions and plan.title: Relating to provisions and plans by public schools to ensure the safety of individuals with disabilities or impairments during a mandatory school drill or a disaster or emergency situation
tx:SB 57|relating to provisions and plan.summary: Requires the education commissioner to set rules on accommodations for students with disabilities during school drills and emergencies, requires district emergency plans to address equal access to safety, and adds a special education administrator to school safety committees.

tx:HB 4098|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to receive certain tax revenue derived from a hotel and convention center project and to pledge certain tax revenue for the payment of obligations related to the project
tx:HB 4098|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets a city of 16,000 to 27,000 people, in a county of at least 600,000 next to the county containing the State Capitol, receive and pledge certain tax revenue from a hotel and convention center project to pay for it.

tx:HB 3637|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a county commissioners court to adopt an exemption from ad valorem taxation by each taxing unit that taxes the property of the portion of the appraised value of a person's property that is attributable to the installation in or on the property of certain water conservation systems
tx:HB 3637|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets county commissioners courts, if voters approve a related constitutional amendment, exempt from all local property taxes the portion of a property's value added by installing a rainwater harvesting or graywater system, starting with the 2026 tax year.

tx:SCR 6|designating rockwall county as.title: Designating Rockwall County as the official Marriage Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:SCR 6|designating rockwall county as.summary: Designates Rockwall County as the official Marriage Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 2417|relating to the eligibility o.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain wrongfully imprisoned persons for compensation and for the expunction of arrest records and files in the case
tx:HB 2417|relating to the eligibility o.summary: Lets courts erase arrest records when a conviction is reversed on appeal and prosecutors recommend it, and makes such people who served prison time eligible for wrongful-imprisonment compensation, with three years to apply for past cases.

tx:HB 1035|relating to the criteria for.title: Relating to the criteria for a local option exemption from ad valorem taxation by a county or municipality of all or part of the appraised value of real property used to operate a child-care facility
tx:HB 1035|relating to the criteria for.summary: Lets owners of property leased to child-care centers qualify for a local property tax exemption by certifying that the center pays the property taxes under a net lease, instead of documenting rent reductions passed on to the center.

tx:HB 4926|relating to authorizing certa.title: Relating to authorizing certain counties to impose a hotel occupancy tax and the use of revenue from that tax
tx:HB 4926|relating to authorizing certa.summary: Lets a county of under 100,000 people bordering the Navasota River that hosts an annual renaissance festival impose a hotel tax of up to 7 percent, or 2 percent where a city hotel tax applies, for tourism, a rodeo arena, and historic preservation.

tx:HB 1664|relating to the eligibility o.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain retired or former district court judges for assignment as a visiting judge
tx:HB 1664|relating to the eligibility o.summary: Lets retired or former district judges serve as visiting judges if they certify they were not publicly reprimanded or censured and did not resign during a misconduct investigation in the prior 15 years; expires in 2033.

tx:SB 2284|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to regulate certain matters related to firearms, air guns, archery equipment, and other weapons and related supplies
tx:SB 2284|relating to the authority of.summary: Bars cities and counties from regulating the sale, possession, carrying, storage or licensing of bows, crossbows and arrows, ends Type A general-law cities' power to regulate firearm use, and limits county bow-hunting rules to subdivision lots under seven acres instead of 10 acres or less.

tx:HB 5141|relating to the lease of cert.title: Relating to the lease of certain state property from the Department of State Health Services to Travis County
tx:HB 5141|relating to the lease of cert.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to lease certain state land to Travis County, which must use it mainly for a public purpose or the lease ends and the property reverts to the state.

tx:HB 4870|relating to a relative and ki.title: Relating to a relative and kinship care grant program administered by the Office of Court Administration of the Texas Judicial System
tx:HB 4870|relating to a relative and ki.summary: Creates a state court administration office grant program for nonprofits giving legal help to relatives and kin caring for a child, for caregivers earning up to 400 percent of the federal poverty level, using available or appropriated funds.

tx:HB 3196|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to receive certain tax revenue derived from a hotel and convention center project and to pledge certain tax revenue for the payment of obligations related to the project
tx:HB 3196|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets a Gulf Coast barrier-island city near Mexico receive and pledge certain tax revenue from a hotel and convention center project, lets its hotel, convention center and parking sit up to 2,000 feet apart where water or wetlands intervene, and lets one other city pledge such revenue.

tx:SB 1169|relating to the provision of.title: Relating to the provision of water or sewer service by public entities operating jointly or concurrently
tx:SB 1169|relating to the provision of.summary: Expands the powers of public utility agencies that local governments form jointly for water or sewer service, letting them issue notes, buy utilities and partner with the North American Development Bank; sets withdrawal rules and lets the Public Utility Commission hear appeals of their rates.

tx:HB 200|relating to jury instructions.title: Relating to jury instructions regarding parole eligibility and the release on parole of certain inmates convicted of an offense committed when younger than 18 years of age; changing parole eligibility
tx:HB 200|relating to jury instructions.summary: Makes people imprisoned for felonies committed before age 18 eligible for parole after 20 years, unless already eligible sooner, excluding certain capital murders and mass-shooting assaults; requires parole panels to weigh youth, maturity and growth, and updates jury instructions to match.

tx:SB 991|relating to the inclusion of c.title: Relating to the inclusion of chronically absent and truant students as students at risk of dropping out of school and the collection and reporting of data regarding those students
tx:SB 991|relating to the inclusion of c.summary: Adds chronically absent students (absent more than 10 percent of the time) and truant students to those counted as at risk of dropping out, and requires schools to report their numbers by campus, which the state education agency must publish yearly.

tx:HB 38|relating to improvements to the.title: Relating to improvements to the Texas Information and Referral Network
tx:HB 38|relating to improvements to the.summary: Expands requirements for the Texas Information and Referral Network, including 24-hour call centers, two-way text messaging, disaster backup service, voluntary screening for nonmedical health needs, tracked referrals, data sharing with partners and publication of de-identified client demographics.

tx:HB 4041|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the Railroad Commission of Texas to impose an administrative penalty on a propane distribution system retailer
tx:HB 4041|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets the Railroad Commission fine propane distribution system retailers up to $1,000 per violation, capped at $10,000 for a related series, after offering a hearing, including for failing to meet required performance guarantees.

tx:HB 2421|relating to the date of disso.title: Relating to the date of dissolution of the Save Historic Muny District
tx:HB 2421|relating to the date of disso.summary: Extends from May 31, 2025, to May 31, 2027, the deadline for the Save Historic Muny District in Austin to reach an agreement to buy or preserve the Lions Municipal Golf Course land before the district must dissolve.

tx:HB 3240|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Texas geothermal energy production policy council
tx:HB 3240|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates an unpaid Texas geothermal energy production policy council within the Railroad Commission to study geothermal industry development and tax incentives, draft a state oversight plan and recommend law changes; the council expires January 1, 2032.

tx:HB 35|relating to a peer support netw.title: Relating to a peer support network for first responders
tx:HB 35|relating to a peer support netw.summary: Requires the state emergency management division to create, by March 31, 2026, a peer support network for firefighters and emergency medical personnel, keeps participation confidential, and bars their licensing agencies from disciplining them for taking part; implementation depends on funding.

tx:HB 4916|relating to the assignment of.title: Relating to the assignment of a motor vehicle title by a dealer
tx:HB 4916|relating to the assignment of.summary: Lets a licensed vehicle dealer that holds a title issued in its own name resell the vehicle without first assigning the title to itself, as long as the name on the title matches the name on the dealer's license.

tx:HB 1126|relating to sunscreening devi.title: Relating to sunscreening devices installed on a motor vehicle displaying a judicial specialty license plate
tx:HB 1126|relating to sunscreening devi.summary: Exempts vehicles that display or qualify for certain judges' specialty license plates from the state ban on window tint and other materials that block or reduce the driver's view through the windshield or windows.

tx:HB 4327|relating to wrongful death ac.title: Relating to wrongful death actions by siblings of a decedent
tx:HB 4327|relating to wrongful death ac.summary: Lets surviving siblings of a person killed by wrongful conduct, including half-siblings, adopted siblings and stepsiblings, bring or benefit from a wrongful death lawsuit; applies to lawsuits filed after the law takes effect.

tx:SB 1210|relating to the jurisdiction.title: Relating to the jurisdiction of the Texas Supreme Court and the Court of Criminal Appeals
tx:SB 1210|relating to the jurisdiction.summary: Gives the Texas Supreme Court final authority to resolve conflicts between it and the Court of Criminal Appeals over interpreting the state constitution, and ends the Court of Criminal Appeals' power to review lower-court rulings on its own motion.

tx:SB 660|relating to the installation o.title: Relating to the installation of bollards or another safety barrier adjacent to certain hospital emergency rooms
tx:SB 660|relating to the installation o.summary: Requires hospitals with emergency rooms near vehicle traffic to install crash-rated bollards or similar barriers by January 1, 2026, exempting hospitals in counties of 68,750 or fewer people, certain federally designated rural hospitals, and those already protected.

tx:SB 2448|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Rural Workforce Development Grant Program
tx:SB 2448|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a Rural Workforce Development Grant Program letting the Texas Workforce Commission give grants to nonprofits that help rural colleges and school districts align job training with local workforce needs, with annual reports on grants and results.

tx:SB 441|relating to civil liability fo.title: Relating to civil liability for the production, solicitation, disclosure, or promotion of artificial intimate visual material
tx:SB 441|relating to civil liability fo.summary: Lets people sue those who make or share AI-generated sexual images of them without consent, and websites, nudification apps and payment processors that facilitate it; requires sites to remove such images within 72 hours of a request, and expands the deepfake crime to include threats.

tx:HB 3234|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a political subdivision to regulate construction and renovation of structures owned by certain counties
tx:HB 3234|relating to the authority of.summary: Bars cities and other local governments from requiring notice or a building permit for construction or renovation of buildings owned by counties of one million or more people, down from 3.3 million, when a licensed engineer or architect supervises the work.

tx:HB 1441|relating to the model trainin.title: Relating to the model training curriculum for school district peace officers and school resource officers
tx:HB 1441|relating to the model trainin.summary: Requires the state's model training for school district police and school resource officers to cover how mental health conditions, gang influence, drug use, mistreatment, neglect, grief and trauma affect student behavior, and trauma-informed ways to keep schools safe.

tx:SB 918|relating to the licensing and.title: Relating to the licensing and regulation of orthotists and prosthetists
tx:SB 918|relating to the licensing and.summary: Lets the state licensing commission, by rule, waive specific academic, clinical training or exam requirements for orthotist and prosthetist applicants with unique qualifications, replacing an automatic exemption, and holds those license holders to renewal requirements other than the waived ones.

tx:SB 783|relating to certain regulation.title: Relating to certain regulations adopted by governmental entities for the construction or alteration of residential or commercial buildings
tx:SB 783|relating to certain regulation.summary: Extends the existing once-every-six-years limit on updating the state's residential energy code to amendments, requires a prior analysis of effects on housing attainability, construction costs, energy savings and payback periods, and exempts state energy codes and building standards from a law limiting government building-product rules.

tx:HB 5681|relating to the powers of the.title: Relating to the powers of the Westwood Magnolia Parkway Improvement District
tx:HB 5681|relating to the powers of the.summary: Lets the Westwood Magnolia Parkway Improvement District make an agreement with a local government to run a county assistance district located in a county the district overlaps, treating the district as a city for that purpose.

tx:HB 1904|relating to the release of a.title: Relating to the release of a balloon and associated littering; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 1904|relating to the release of a.summary: Makes intentionally releasing gas-filled Mylar balloons outdoors a crime, ranging from a Class C misdemeanor for five pounds or less to a state jail felony for releases of 1,000 pounds or more, or 200 pounds for commercial purposes, and requires community service picking up litter or recycling.

tx:HB 484|relating to the use of cigaret.title: Relating to the use of cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and tobacco products on the campus of a public institution of higher education
tx:HB 484|relating to the use of cigaret.summary: Lets public colleges and universities adopt policies banning the use of cigarettes, e-cigarettes and tobacco products anywhere on campus grounds or in campus buildings.

tx:SB 21|relating to the establishment a.title: Relating to the establishment and administration of the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve for the purpose of investing in cryptocurrency and the investment authority of the comptroller of public accounts over the reserve and certain other state funds
tx:SB 21|relating to the establishment a.summary: Creates a Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, a fund outside the state treasury run by the comptroller, that may buy bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies with an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over 24 months, with an advisory committee, optional audits and reports every two years.

tx:HB 4473|relating to a study by the te.title: Relating to a study by the Texas Department of Transportation of the construction and maintenance of certain county road systems in this state
tx:HB 4473|relating to a study by the te.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Transportation to study and rank the cost of building and maintaining county roads under each county road management system, assess unpaved border-county roads' effect on border security, and report by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 1039|relating to the use of hotel.title: Relating to the use of hotel occupancy tax revenue by certain municipalities
tx:HB 1039|relating to the use of hotel.summary: Repeals rules dictating how the largest city in a border county containing a national park over 400,000 acres must spend hotel tax revenue, and lets a border county containing part of the West Nueces River levy a hotel tax outside cities that have one.

tx:HB 4014|relating to a study on the us.title: Relating to a study on the use of psychedelic therapies in the treatment of certain conditions
tx:HB 4014|relating to a study on the us.summary: Requires the state health agency, consulting with Baylor College of Medicine and UT Austin's Dell Medical School, to study psychedelic therapies for PTSD, depression and related conditions and report by December 1, 2026 on access after federal approval.

tx:SJR 87|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment requiring the denial of bail to persons accused of certain offenses punishable as a felony who have previously been convicted of or who were released on bail for certain offenses punishable as a felony at the time of the new offense
tx:SJR 87|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment requiring denial of bail, after a hearing where prosecutors show probable cause, to people accused of murder, aggravated assault, aggravated sexual assault, human trafficking or certain other serious felonies who were previously convicted of, or out on bail for, one of those offenses.

tx:HJR 1|proposing a constitutional amen.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to authorize the legislature to exempt from ad valorem taxation a portion of the market value of tangible personal property a person owns that is held or used for the production of income
tx:HJR 1|proposing a constitutional amen.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, letting the Legislature exempt from property tax $125,000 of the market value of personal property used to produce income, replacing an exemption limited to property worth less than the cost of taxing it.

tx:HB 4582|relating to reimbursement of.title: Relating to reimbursement of infrastructure costs incurred by a developer of certain housing developments by certain municipalities and counties
tx:HB 4582|relating to reimbursement of.summary: Lets cities and counties in counties of 2.5 million to 4 million people, and certain adjacent counties, reimburse developers for utility, broadband and road infrastructure serving developments of at least 50 manufactured homes, capped yearly at the developer's property taxes, for up to 10 years.

tx:HB 2363|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain peace officers to arrest a person without a warrant while outside the officer's jurisdiction
tx:HB 2363|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets peace officers commissioned by water control and improvement districts arrest people without a warrant for offenses committed in their presence outside their district, with traffic arrests limited to counties of 500,000 or more where the district is located.

tx:SB 790|relating to the procedure for.title: Relating to the procedure for resolving certain customer complaints before the Public Utility Commission of Texas
tx:SB 790|relating to the procedure for.summary: Lets the Public Utility Commission adopt a simplified process, outside the standard administrative hearing procedures, for resolving tenant complaints against property owners over water or wastewater bills.

tx:HB 2807|relating to the statewide int.title: Relating to the statewide intellectual and developmental disability coordinating council
tx:HB 2807|relating to the statewide int.summary: Creates a statewide council of state agencies, universities, providers and families to coordinate services for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, write a five-year strategic plan, inventory state programs and propose coordinated spending every two years.

tx:HB 5219|relating to an interim study.title: Relating to an interim study on water resources development in certain counties
tx:HB 5219|relating to an interim study.summary: Requires the Texas Water Development Board to study groundwater and other water resources in the counties of one regional water planning area, including state funding programs and aid for economically distressed areas, and report to lawmakers by September 1, 2026.

tx:SB 326|relating to the procedure for.title: Relating to the procedure for determining whether a student's violation of a public school's or public institution of higher education's student code of conduct was motivated by antisemitism
tx:SB 326|relating to the procedure for.summary: Requires public schools, charter schools and public colleges, when disciplining a student for a conduct-code violation that may have been motivated by antisemitism, to use the definition of antisemitism already in state law, starting in the 2025-2026 school year.

tx:HB 1403|relating to the collection an.title: Relating to the collection and confidentiality of information regarding weapons in agency foster homes; creating a civil penalty
tx:HB 1403|relating to the collection an.summary: Bars state agencies and contracted child-placing agencies from requiring foster homes to disclose the specific types of firearms they keep, limits use of such information, makes it confidential, and sets civil penalties up to $5,000 per misuse.

tx:HB 1765|relating to the issuance of a.title: Relating to the issuance of an arrest warrant or search warrant authorizing the use of a no-knock entry by a peace officer
tx:HB 1765|relating to the issuance of a.summary: Bars no-knock arrest or search warrants unless the request is approved in writing by the head of the officer's agency and officers are in uniform or clearly identifiable, and limits which judges may issue them.

tx:SB 1073|relating to discrimination ag.title: Relating to discrimination against or burdening certain constitutional rights of an applicant for or holder of a license to practice law in this state
tx:SB 1073|relating to discrimination ag.summary: Bars state bar rules, policies or penalties that limit lawyers' or applicants' licenses based on sincerely held religious beliefs or that burden their religion, speech or association, with exceptions, and lets them sue or raise this as a defense.

tx:SB 1524|relating to the collection an.title: Relating to the collection and confidentiality of information regarding weapons in agency foster homes; creating a civil penalty
tx:SB 1524|relating to the collection an.summary: Bars state agencies and contracted child-placing agencies from requiring foster homes to disclose the specific types of weapons, including firearms, they keep, limits use of such information, makes it confidential, and sets civil penalties up to $5,000 per misuse.

tx:SB 2225|relating to the creation of a.title: Relating to the creation of a spirit cooler certificate; authorizing a fee
tx:SB 2225|relating to the creation of a.summary: Creates a category of ready-to-drink spirit beverages, premixed drinks of up to 10 percent alcohol, and lets distillers sell them through beer distributors to grocery, convenience and other beer-and-wine retailers during beer sale hours.

tx:SB 290|relating to notice to property.title: Relating to notice to property owners regarding certain stationary LP-gas installations
tx:SB 290|relating to notice to property.summary: Requires applicants seeking to install or modify a propane storage installation holding 10,000 gallons or more to notify, by mail with proof of delivery, all property owners within 500 feet of the proposed tank location.

tx:HB 3066|relating to the entitlement o.title: Relating to the entitlement of certain municipalities to certain tax revenue associated with hotel and convention center projects
tx:HB 3066|relating to the entitlement o.summary: Extends from 10 to 20 years after a hotel opens the period during which certain cities meeting population criteria may keep state hotel and sales tax revenue from qualified hotel and convention center projects.

tx:SB 1079|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a county to dispose of sensitive media devices
tx:SB 1079|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets county commissioners courts order the destruction, rather than sale or other disposal, of surplus or salvage devices holding sensitive data when needed to prevent accidental disclosure of information.

tx:HB 4236|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the property value study task force
tx:HB 4236|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a six-member legislative study group to review how the comptroller's school district property value study affects state school funding, recommend ways to verify valuations of complex properties, and report by December 1, 2026.

tx:SB 995|relating to the approval of a.title: Relating to the approval of a surety bond for a contract authorizing an oversize or overweight vehicle to cross a road or highway
tx:SB 995|relating to the approval of a.summary: Requires that the surety bond for a contract letting an oversize or overweight vehicle cross a state highway be approved by the Texas Department of Transportation instead of the comptroller and attorney general.

tx:HB 422|relating to limitations on the.title: Relating to limitations on the issuance of bonds by the Texas Water Development Board for the development of certain projects in economically distressed areas
tx:HB 422|relating to limitations on the.summary: Replaces the yearly caps of $25 million in dedicated bonds and $50 million in general obligation bonds for Water Development Board aid to economically distressed areas with a single $100 million yearly cap on general obligation bonds.

tx:HB 1876|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of a career and technical education reporting grant program by the Texas Education Agency
tx:HB 1876|relating to the establishment.summary: Directs the Texas Education Agency to create a grant program, if funded, giving school districts and charter schools up to $5,000 each to collect and report career and technical education data, capped at $1.75 million a year.

tx:HB 4732|relating to state recognition.title: Relating to state recognition of the Lipan Apache Tribe of Texas
tx:HB 4732|relating to state recognition.summary: Recognizes the Lipan Apache Tribe of Texas as a state-recognized tribe eligible for benefits available to such tribes, and prohibits on its lands all gaming that state law prohibits, with the same penalties.

tx:SB 243|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of migrant labor housing facilities; changing the amount of a civil penalty
tx:SB 243|relating to the regulation of.summary: Sets a migrant labor housing complaint process with deadlines for operators to fix problems, changes the civil penalty from $200 to at least $50 per occupant per day, lets certain resident workers sue to collect it, and bars retaliation against complainants.

tx:HB 2370|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to use hotel occupancy tax revenue for certain venue projects
tx:HB 2370|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets voters in certain cities of 70,000 to 180,000 in a county bordering Mexico and the Gulf approve a hotel occupancy tax of up to 2 percent to pay for a convention center built before 2023, ending by 2054.

tx:HB 1136|relating to a study conducted.title: Relating to a study conducted by the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles regarding parking for certain individuals with disabilities
tx:HB 1136|relating to a study conducted.summary: Requires the Governor's Committee on People with Disabilities, with other state agencies, to study current and future disability parking needs and enforcement and report findings and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 4264|relating to creation of a gra.title: Relating to creation of a grant program for certain peace officers who hold a master proficiency certificate
tx:HB 4264|relating to creation of a gra.summary: Lets the governor's criminal justice division create a grant program, if funded, giving law enforcement agencies a one-time $6,500 per officer to raise pay for full-time peace officers who earn a master proficiency certificate.

tx:HB 4520|relating to requirements for.title: Relating to requirements for loans or grants provided by the Texas Transportation Commission to aviation facilities located in economically disadvantaged counties
tx:HB 4520|relating to requirements for.summary: Lowers the local share required for state airport loans or grants from 10 percent to 5 percent of project costs for airports in economically disadvantaged counties.

tx:HB 3223|relating to statutes of limit.title: Relating to statutes of limitation and repose for certain claims involving the construction or repair of an improvement to real property
tx:HB 3223|relating to statutes of limit.summary: Shortens from 10 to 8 years the deadline for most suits over defects in the design or construction of improvements to real property, and shortens related extension and filing periods, for work starting after the law takes effect.

tx:HB 2017|relating to increasing the mi.title: Relating to increasing the minimum term of imprisonment and changing the eligibility for community supervision, mandatory supervision, and parole for certain persons convicted of intoxication manslaughter
tx:HB 2017|relating to increasing the mi.summary: Makes intoxication manslaughter a first-degree felony when the person has a prior intoxicated-driving conviction and was violating the state's illegal-entry law, bars probation for it, and requires 10 years served before parole or release.

tx:HB 4412|relating to the use of hotel.title: Relating to the use of hotel occupancy tax revenue by certain municipalities
tx:HB 4412|relating to the use of hotel.summary: Lets the county-seat city of a certain county bordering New Mexico use hotel occupancy tax revenue for up to 25 percent of tourism-related public improvement projects through 2034, capping its hotel tax rate at 2 percent eight years after it first does so.

tx:SB 1400|relating to a study on measur.title: Relating to a study on measurable outcomes for certain transfer students for performance tier funding under the public junior college state finance program
tx:SB 1400|relating to a study on measur.summary: Requires the Higher Education Coordinating Board to study the cost and effects of counting students previously enrolled at a university who later transfer from a community college in community college performance funding, reporting by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 4105|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain counties to consider a prospective contractor's principal place of business when awarding certain contracts
tx:HB 4105|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets counties of more than 3.3 million award construction and service contracts to a bidder based in the county or a neighboring county if its price is within 3 percent of the lowest outside bid and offers the best overall value.

tx:SB 1036|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of residential solar retail transactions; requiring an occupational registration; authorizing fees; providing civil and administrative penalties
tx:SB 1036|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires residential solar sellers and salespeople to register with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, sets rules on sales practices and contracts, gives buyers five business days to cancel, and authorizes fees and penalties.

tx:HB 2462|relating to the use of a high.title: Relating to the use of a high occupancy vehicle lane by an operator of a motor vehicle who is pregnant
tx:HB 2462|relating to the use of a high.summary: Lets women who are pregnant or who are a parent or legal guardian drive in any high-occupancy vehicle lane regardless of how many people are in the vehicle, unless federal highway officials notify the state it would lose federal highway funding or face other penalties.

tx:HB 573|relating to a request by a mem.title: Relating to a request by a member of the legislature for an unannounced inspection of a concrete batch plant by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
tx:HB 573|relating to a request by a mem.summary: Lets a state legislator ask the state environmental agency, on behalf of an affected constituent who files a written complaint, to make an unannounced inspection of a permanent concrete batch plant; the agency must prioritize such requests and explain any denial within 90 days.

tx:HB 366|relating to required disclosur.title: Relating to required disclosures on certain political advertising that contains altered media; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 366|relating to required disclosur.summary: Requires political ads that show a candidate or officeholder saying or doing something that did not happen, including AI-altered images, audio or video, to carry a disclosure; violations by candidates, political committees, paid distributors or anyone spending over $100 on ads are Class A misdemeanors.

tx:HB 2448|relating to the waiver of a d.title: Relating to the waiver of a defendant's arraignment
tx:HB 2448|relating to the waiver of a d.summary: Lets a defendant's attorney sign and present a waiver of arraignment on the defendant's behalf, and bars court clerks from requiring the defendant to be present before accepting the waiver.

tx:SB 1018|relating to distribution of s.title: Relating to distribution of state traffic fine revenue received by the comptroller
tx:SB 1018|relating to distribution of s.summary: Changes how the state splits traffic fine revenue it receives, sending 50 percent (up from 30) to the trauma facility and emergency medical services account and 50 percent (down from 70) to the general revenue fund.

tx:HB 2856|relating to a study by the te.title: Relating to a study by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board on the feasibility of implementing a statewide system for coordinating clinical training placements
tx:HB 2856|relating to a study by the te.summary: Requires the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to study the cost and feasibility of regional portals for reserving clinical training rotations at health care facilities for college students, and report findings to state leaders by December 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1353|relating to the licensing and.title: Relating to the licensing and regulation of pilots in the jurisdiction of the pilot board of a navigation district located in Cameron County
tx:SB 1353|relating to the licensing and.summary: Creates a separate set of rules for ship pilots in Cameron County, giving the local navigation district's pilot board authority to license and discipline pilots, set pilotage rates and adopt rules for guiding vessels between the Gulf and its ports.

tx:HB 1347|relating to the prosecution o.title: Relating to the prosecution of the offense of exploitation of a child, elderly individual, or disabled individual
tx:HB 1347|relating to the prosecution o.summary: Redefines the crime of exploiting a child, elderly or disabled person as knowingly taking their resources for the offender's or another person's benefit through exploitation, deception, coercion or isolation, and defines those terms, including withholding documents, drugging, confinement and financial control.

tx:HB 117|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the governor's task force on the governance of early childhood education and care
tx:HB 117|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a temporary governor's task force, with a steering committee of state agency heads, to review how early childhood education and child care are run across state agencies and recommend standards and changes to the Legislature by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 5370|relating to the requirements.title: Relating to the requirements for interlocal contracts
tx:HB 5370|relating to the requirements.summary: Lets a water utility owned by a city holding more than 60 percent of the population of a county of 2 million or more set procedures for entering interlocal contracts of up to $100,000 without governing-body approval, as municipal electric utilities already may.

tx:HB 2253|relating to the authority to.title: Relating to the authority to cancel certain elections on a measure
tx:HB 2253|relating to the authority to.summary: Lets a local government cancel a scheduled bond election, at least 74 days before election day, after a governor's disaster declaration within 90 days of the election, if its governing body votes that canceling is needed to protect voters, election workers or election systems.

tx:HB 5686|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Montgomery County Management District No. 3; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes
tx:HB 5686|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates the Montgomery County Management District No. 3 to provide public improvements and services, with power to issue bonds and impose assessments and sales, property and maintenance taxes, subject to voter approval for certain taxes; bars the district from using eminent domain.

tx:HB 2618|relating to the development o.title: Relating to the development of a severe weather adaptation plan by certain entities
tx:HB 2618|relating to the development o.summary: Requires 13 state agencies, including the Department of Public Safety, the transportation and environmental agencies and the utility commission, to publish severe weather adaptation plans every two years, including vulnerability assessments, budget effects and funding sources, subject to state audit.

tx:SB 777|relating to compensation and e.title: Relating to compensation and employment condition standards by municipal charter or collective bargaining agreement and to impasse resolution in collective bargaining with certain political subdivisions
tx:SB 777|relating to compensation and e.summary: Requires fire departments and firefighter unions to follow impasse-resolution procedures set in a city charter or bargaining agreement over default state rules, and requires binding arbitration for firefighter bargaining impasses in cities of about 950,000 to 1,050,000 people.

tx:HB 1142|relating to coverage for ment.title: Relating to coverage for mental health conditions and substance use disorders under certain governmental health benefit plans
tx:HB 1142|relating to coverage for ment.summary: Applies state mental health and substance use disorder coverage rules to health plans for state, school and university employees and retired teachers, extends required chemical dependency coverage to individual and small self-funded plans, and bars lifetime limits on it, for plans issued from 2026.

tx:SB 2124|relating to publication of th.title: Relating to publication of the Texas Groundwater Protection Committee's annual report
tx:SB 2124|relating to publication of th.summary: Moves the annual deadline for the Texas Groundwater Protection Committee's joint groundwater monitoring and contamination report from April 1 to June 1.

tx:HB 2993|relating to the carrying of a.title: Relating to the carrying of a handgun by a county commissioner in certain locations
tx:HB 2993|relating to the carrying of a.summary: Exempts county commissioners who are licensed to carry a handgun from the offenses of unlawfully carrying a weapon and carrying a weapon in places where weapons are otherwise prohibited.

tx:HB 1275|relating to the issuance of p.title: Relating to the issuance of permits for producer dairies in certain areas of this state
tx:HB 1275|relating to the issuance of p.summary: Narrows an existing ban on state dairy permits in areas infected with or at high risk for bovine tuberculosis, as defined by the Texas Animal Health Commission, so that it applies only to cattle dairy farms rather than all producer dairies.

tx:HB 148|relating to the qualification.title: Relating to the qualification of candidates for, and the training and education of members of, the board of directors of an appraisal district
tx:HB 148|relating to the qualification.summary: Requires appraisal district board members in counties of 75,000 or more to complete annual training from an accredited college, with failure counting as grounds for removal, and requires board candidates to sign an acknowledgment of the board's duties, starting with terms beginning in 2026.

tx:HB 2399|relating to procedures and re.title: Relating to procedures and required findings in certain suits affecting the parent-child relationship
tx:HB 2399|relating to procedures and re.summary: Requires judges in child protection cases who decide not to return a child to the parents at a permanency hearing to write specific factual findings explaining why; citing the record is not enough, and the findings cannot be used as evidence at final trial.

tx:HB 4486|relating to directing payment.title: Relating to directing payment, after approval, of certain miscellaneous claims and judgments against the state out of funds designated by this Act; making appropriations
tx:HB 4486|relating to directing payment.summary: Appropriates state funds to pay listed claims and judgments against the state, including $142.7 million in outside-counsel fees from the state's Meta lawsuit, contingent Google case fees, $63,750 in salary Ken Paxton did not receive during his impeachment, settlements and voided-warrant replacements.

tx:HB 2712|relating to test years used f.title: Relating to test years used for ratemaking purposes by certain water and sewer utilities
tx:HB 2712|relating to test years used f.summary: Lets water and sewer utilities choose a rate-case test year based on historic, projected future or combined data, requires refunds if projected data led to excessive returns, and directs the utility commission to adopt rules by September 1, 2026.

tx:HB 2040|relating to the required numb.title: Relating to the required number of minutes of instructional time to be provided by a juvenile justice alternative education program
tx:HB 2040|relating to the required numb.summary: Changes the minimum instructional time for juvenile justice alternative education programs from seven hours a day for 180 days to 43,200 minutes a year, with waivers limited to what school districts they serve received, starting in 2025-26.

tx:SB 1409|relating to health benefits o.title: Relating to health benefits offered by postsecondary educational institutions to students and their families
tx:SB 1409|relating to health benefits o.summary: Lets colleges and universities offer optional health benefit plans to students and their families that are not regulated as insurance, requiring signed disclosures, state registration, actuarial soundness and a waiting period of no more than six months for preexisting conditions.

tx:HB 3125|relating to establishment by.title: Relating to establishment by the Texas Workforce Commission of a geothermal energy workforce education and training initiative
tx:HB 3125|relating to establishment by.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission, with the higher education board, to create a geothermal energy workforce training initiative, including curriculum for college and career school programs, funding opportunities and employer partnerships, with annual reports to the Legislature.

tx:HR 1519|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, H.B. No. 705
tx:HR 1519|suspending limitations on con.summary: Lets negotiators on the cosmetology licensure compact bill add language voiding Texas's participation if the compact commission finds its law differs materially from the model compact, and letting the governor withdraw the state from the compact at any time.

tx:SB 1789|relating to electric service.title: Relating to electric service quality and reliability
tx:SB 1789|relating to electric service.summary: Requires the state utility commission to set inspection and maintenance standards for electric transmission and distribution poles, requires annual reports from utilities and co-ops, tightens outage thresholds for enforcement, and allows lower profit rates for noncompliant utilities after storm damage.

tx:HB 1868|relating to performance tier.title: Relating to performance tier funding under the public junior college state finance program
tx:HB 1868|relating to performance tier.summary: Requires the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to study lowering from 15 to nine the dual credit hours that count toward community college performance funding, and the supply of dual credit instructors, reporting to the Legislature by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 3333|relating to a restriction on.title: Relating to a restriction on permits authorizing direct discharges of waste or pollutants into water in certain stream segments, stream assessment units, and drainage areas
tx:HB 3333|relating to a restriction on.summary: Bars the state environmental agency from issuing new permits for wastewater treatment facilities to discharge waste directly into the Devils River in Val Verde County or county waters that drain into it; stormwater permits are not affected.

tx:SB 2206|relating to a franchise tax c.title: Relating to a franchise tax credit for, and the application of sales and use taxes to, certain research and development expenses
tx:SB 2206|relating to a franchise tax c.summary: Replaces the expiring research and development tax incentives with a new franchise tax credit tied to federal rules, raising the basic rate from 5 to 8.722 percent of qualifying new research spending, and repeals the related sales tax exemption, starting January 1, 2026.

tx:HB 2545|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Rural Workforce Training Grant Program
tx:HB 2545|relating to the establishment.summary: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to create a Rural Workforce Training Grant Program funding on-the-job training, apprenticeships and job courses in counties under 200,000 people, with grants to groups such as business associations, local governments, workforce boards and schools, and annual reports.

tx:SB 1214|relating to the operations an.title: Relating to the operations and administration of the Concho County Hospital District
tx:SB 1214|relating to the operations an.summary: Changes rules for the Concho County Hospital District: board candidates file an application instead of a petition, directors need not own land but cannot be district employees, the board adds a vice president, and construction contracts may use state public-works law instead of local bidding rules.

tx:HB 2798|relating to disclosures and o.title: Relating to disclosures and other requirements concerning virtual currency kiosk transactions; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 2798|relating to disclosures and o.summary: Requires cryptocurrency kiosk operators to show customers risk and fraud warnings, disclose fees and exchange rates, and give receipts; caps new customers at $2,000 a day; refunds fees for transactions investigators find were fraudulently induced; and puts the state banking department in charge, with fees.

tx:SB 2143|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a county to commission certain individuals as peace officers and establish certain law enforcement agencies and to certification requirements for fire marshals
tx:SB 2143|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets counties commission fire marshals, fire officers, fire inspectors and fire investigators as peace officers to support fire investigations and enforce building and hazardous-materials codes, and allows a county to create a law enforcement agency only if the constitution or other law authorizes it.

tx:SB 1537|relating to the appointment o.title: Relating to the appointment of an interpreter in a criminal proceeding
tx:SB 1537|relating to the appointment o.summary: Requires that, when a criminal court determines on a party's or its own motion that a defendant or witness does not understand and speak English, the interpreter be appointed under the state's general court-interpreter law, which also governs subpoenaing interpreters.

tx:HB 426|relating to medicaid and child.title: Relating to Medicaid and child health plan program coverage and reimbursement for childhood cranial remolding orthosis
tx:HB 426|relating to medicaid and child.summary: Requires Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program to fully cover custom cranial remolding helmets for children diagnosed with craniosynostosis, or with flat or misshapen heads that meet set age, measurement and failed-treatment criteria.

tx:HB 4396|relating to the major events.title: Relating to the major events reimbursement program, including event funding eligibility, site selection organizations, and single event and single year classifications
tx:HB 4396|relating to the major events.summary: Adds the American Performance Horseman and the American Rodeo, and their organizers Teton Ridge Live Productions and Teton Ridge The American, to the events and organizations eligible for the state's major events reimbursement program.

tx:SB 1620|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Texas forensic analyst apprenticeship pilot program
tx:SB 1620|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a forensic analyst apprenticeship pilot program, running until 2030, in which the state contracts with public universities and publicly funded accredited crime labs, and the Texas Forensic Science Commission sets eligibility rules and awards apprentice positions.

tx:SB 1173|relating to the amount of an.title: Relating to the amount of an expenditure made by certain political subdivisions for which a competitive procurement method may be required
tx:SB 1173|relating to the amount of an.summary: Raises from $50,000 to $100,000 the purchase and contract amount at which school districts, cities, counties, emergency services districts and certain transit authorities must use competitive bidding or another competitive procurement method.

tx:HB 3483|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a Special Utility District to issue revenue bonds
tx:HB 3483|relating to the authority of.summary: Adds special utility districts to the local governments allowed to issue public securities under the state's alternative financing law, and exempts these districts from state environmental commission approval and oversight of their bonds and projects.

tx:HB 3305|relating to the continuation.title: Relating to the continuation of health care provider participation programs in certain counties
tx:HB 3305|relating to the continuation.summary: Lets certain large counties without a hospital district charge private hospitals a mandatory fee of up to 6 percent of patient revenue, through 2030, to fund the local share of federally matched Medicaid payments to those hospitals; hospitals may not pass the fee to patients.

tx:HB 3680|relating to subdivision plat.title: Relating to subdivision plat requirements in certain counties
tx:HB 3680|relating to subdivision plat.summary: Gives Cameron County, which borders Mexico and the Gulf, its own subdivision rules in place of border-county rules: plats are required when any lot is under five acres, the county may exempt lots near existing water, sewer and roads, and some bond and utility-hookup requirements are loosened.

tx:HB 2088|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of a public law school in the Rio Grande Valley
tx:HB 2088|relating to the establishment.summary: Lets a university system establish a law school in Cameron or Hidalgo County, subject to available funding, with the Higher Education Coordinating Board choosing among competing systems and first preparing a feasibility study on accreditation.

tx:SB 546|relating to seat belts on buse.title: Relating to seat belts on buses that transport children
tx:SB 546|relating to seat belts on buse.summary: Requires all buses used by school districts, including older models, to have three-point seat belts by September 2029, unless a district finds it cannot afford them or belts would void a bus's warranty; districts using the cost exemption must report bus counts and costs.

tx:SB 4|relating to an increase in the a.title: Relating to an increase in the amount of the exemption of residence homesteads from ad valorem taxation by a school district and the protection of school districts against certain losses in local revenue
tx:SB 4|relating to an increase in the a.summary: Raises the school property tax homestead exemption from $100,000 to $140,000 starting with 2025 taxes, if voters approve a constitutional amendment, and provides state aid to make up school districts' resulting losses in local tax revenue.

tx:SB 378|relating to certain prohibited.title: Relating to certain prohibited practices by a barber or cosmetologist
tx:SB 378|relating to certain prohibited.summary: Bars barbers and cosmetologists, while providing their licensed services, from cutting into the deeper layer of the skin, including to inject substances, or using medical devices, unless they hold another license or legal authority to do so.

tx:HB 645|relating to the provision of c.title: Relating to the provision of certain co-navigation services to individuals who are deaf-blind
tx:HB 645|relating to the provision of c.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to run a statewide program, starting by September 2026, that pays trained co-navigators to help people who are deaf-blind move around and communicate, with reimbursement rates tiered by training and skill.

tx:HB 3963|relating to an early childhoo.title: Relating to an early childhood integrated data system
tx:HB 3963|relating to an early childhoo.summary: Requires the Texas Education Agency to build, by January 2027, an early childhood data system linking existing data from state health, education and workforce agencies to report on program outcomes and service gaps, if the legislature funds it.

tx:HB 5696|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of The Reserve Municipal Management District; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose assessments, fees, and taxes
tx:HB 5696|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates The Reserve Municipal Management District in the Mansfield area to fund improvements such as roads, utilities and parking, letting it levy petition-approved assessments, voter-approved taxes and bonds with city consent; it may not use eminent domain.

tx:HB 1675|relating to the interment of.title: Relating to the interment of certain cremated animal remains with human remains in perpetual care cemeteries
tx:HB 1675|relating to the interment of.summary: Lets perpetual care cemeteries allow a person's cremated pet to be buried in the owner's casket or placed beside the owner's ashes, bars euthanizing a pet for that purpose, and keeps such cemeteries' property tax exemption.

tx:SB 2023|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of a grant program to support the disposition of deceased paupers' bodies
tx:SB 2023|relating to the establishment.summary: Lets the Health and Human Services Commission create a grant program paying counties' costs of disposing of the bodies of deceased paupers, funded through a new state account of legislative appropriations, gifts and interest.

tx:SB 506|relating to requirements for c.title: Relating to requirements for certain ballot propositions and to related procedures and provisions
tx:SB 506|relating to requirements for c.summary: Requires ballot propositions to be definite and neutral so voters are not misled, lets voters or home-rule cities seek secretary of state review of charter and petition propositions, allows court-ordered rewrites and attorney fees, and bars competing local measures alongside petition-initiated ones.

tx:HB 322|relating to the use of funds a.title: Relating to the use of funds awarded under the Jobs and Education for Texans (JET) Grant Program
tx:HB 322|relating to the use of funds a.summary: Lets Jobs and Education for Texans grants for career and technical education programs at colleges and schools also pay to buy, set up and maintain technology needed to support those programs.

tx:HB 4042|relating to the applicability.title: Relating to the applicability of certain safety provisions and regulatory fees administered by the Railroad Commission of Texas to gas distribution pipelines
tx:HB 4042|relating to the applicability.summary: Extends Railroad Commission pipeline safety fees and rules that apply to natural gas distribution systems to all gas distribution and master-metered pipelines by removing the word "natural"; operators still recover the fees through rate surcharges.

tx:HB 2189|relating to methods to improv.title: Relating to methods to improve health profession-related career and technology education and dual credit programs offered by school districts
tx:HB 2189|relating to methods to improv.summary: Requires the Texas Education Agency to provide free instructional materials for high school health-career programs starting in 2026-27, and directs state agencies to study sharing college lab space with schools and review health dual-credit courses, reporting by December 2026.

tx:HB 2844|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of mobile food vendors; requiring an occupational license; imposing fees; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:HB 2844|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires food trucks to hold a yearly state license for each vehicle starting July 2026, with state health inspections and fees, bars local governments from banning licensed vendors or adopting conflicting rules, and exempts state-permitted small food businesses from local permits.

tx:HB 5154|relating to the reporting of.title: Relating to the reporting of the Joint Admission Medical Program
