tx:HB 5154|relating to the reporting of.summary: Adds duties for the council running the Joint Admission Medical Program for low-income students, including public meeting notices, an online student complaint portal, efforts to raise scholarships to 30 percent of program funding, and detailed annual reports on spending and enrollment.

tx:HB 2529|relating to the annual state.title: Relating to the annual state salary supplement for certain county judges
tx:HB 2529|relating to the annual state.summary: Bases the state salary supplement for county judges who spend at least 18 percent of their work on judicial functions on 18 percent of the salary of a district judge with comparable years of service, instead of the district judge base salary.

tx:HB 1237|relating to the renewal by th.title: Relating to the renewal by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality of certain expired occupational licenses and registrations
tx:HB 1237|relating to the renewal by th.summary: Lets holders of lapsed state environmental agency licenses or registrations renew within 90 days, instead of 30, at up to 1.5 times the normal fee while still working, or within 90 to 180 days at up to twice the fee; after 180 days they must reapply.

tx:HB 119|relating to the registration a.title: Relating to the registration as a lobbyist of persons who engage in certain lobbying activities on behalf of a foreign adversary and to prohibitions on the receipt of compensation related to those lobbying activities; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 119|relating to the registration a.summary: Requires anyone who lobbies Texas officials for a government, party, company or official of a federally designated foreign adversary to register as a lobbyist, bars them from being paid by those clients, and lets the attorney general seek civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation.

tx:SB 1574|relating to a centers of exce.title: Relating to a centers of excellence program developed by the Texas Judicial Council for certain justices and judges
tx:SB 1574|relating to a centers of exce.summary: Requires the Texas Judicial Council to create a program recognizing judges and justices as centers of excellence, judged on governance, access, fairness, case management, court operations and their courts' compliance with reporting, security, fee, indigent defense and guardianship requirements.

tx:SB 1032|relating to the eligibility o.title: Relating to the eligibility of postsecondary educational institutions to participate in the governor's university research initiative
tx:SB 1032|relating to the eligibility o.summary: Lets private and independent colleges and universities qualify for state matching grants under the governor's university research initiative, which helps institutions recruit distinguished researchers, starting with the 2025–2026 academic year.

tx:HB 2229|relating to the expunction of.title: Relating to the expunction of arrest records and files by a statutory county court
tx:HB 2229|relating to the expunction of.summary: Gives statutory county courts, alongside district courts, the power to expunge arrest records for offenses within their jurisdiction when the person was acquitted or prosecutors recommend expunction, and lets people file expunction petitions in those courts.

tx:HB 5663|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the Wood County Central Hospital District of Wood County, Texas, to provide brain and memory care services to residents of the hospital district through the creation and operation of brain and memory health care services districts
tx:HB 5663|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets the Wood County Central Hospital District provide brain and memory care services, including by creating a special district run by a seven-member appointed board that contracts with the hospital district and may not levy taxes or issue bonds.

tx:SB 1405|relating to increasing access.title: Relating to increasing access to and reducing taxation of Internet services
tx:SB 1405|relating to increasing access.summary: Removes internet access from the state's list of taxable services, excludes state broadband grants and pole-replacement reimbursements from franchise-tax revenue, updates the speeds that define broadband, lets the state broadband office use federal coverage maps, and abolishes the governor's broadband council.

tx:HB 27|relating to the consideration b.title: Relating to the consideration by a groundwater conservation district of modeled available groundwater when issuing permits
tx:HB 27|relating to the consideration b.summary: As amended by the Senate, requires the Texas Water Development Board to study how much groundwater can be pumped indefinitely from aquifers under the Neches and Trinity Valleys district and effects of proposed pumping and exports, reporting by January 12, 2027, without pausing new permits.

tx:SB 890|relating to the issuance of a.title: Relating to the issuance of a license to carry a handgun to certain active and retired judicial officers
tx:SB 890|relating to the issuance of a.summary: Adds statutory probate court judges, and visiting judges appointed to county and probate courts, to the active and retired judicial officers eligible for the special process to obtain a license to carry a handgun.

tx:HB 21|relating to housing finance cor.title: Relating to housing finance corporations; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 21|relating to housing finance cor.summary: Limits housing finance corporations to owning or developing housing within their sponsoring city or county unless other local governments approve, subjects them to open-meetings and public-records laws, sets rent and income conditions for their apartments' property tax exemptions, and requires annual compliance audits.

tx:SB 19|relating to a prohibition on th.title: Relating to a prohibition on the making and acceptance of political contributions during a special legislative session
tx:SB 19|relating to a prohibition on th.summary: Bars anyone from giving political contributions to statewide officeholders, legislators or committees supporting them during a special legislative session that begins before September 1 of an odd-numbered year, and requires recipients to refuse and return such contributions within 30 days.

tx:HB 4755|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to authorize and finance certain venue projects and to use municipal hotel occupancy tax revenue for certain of those projects; authorizing the imposition of a tax
tx:HB 4755|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets certain cities of up to 25,000 people in a county bordering Mexico and the Gulf, with a cultural heritage museum, ask voters to approve a hotel occupancy tax of up to 2% to finance a convention center built before 2025, expiring by 2056.

tx:HB 3490|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the governing board of certain state agencies to conduct a closed meeting with the agency's internal auditor to deliberate or receive information about certain internal audit matters
tx:HB 3490|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets a state agency's governing board meet in closed session with its internal auditor to discuss matters the auditor determines would compromise the independence, effectiveness or confidentiality of internal audits if disclosed publicly.

tx:SB 2204|relating to the applicability.title: Relating to the applicability of uniform grant and contract management standards to certain Texas Water Development Board programs
tx:SB 2204|relating to the applicability.summary: Exempts contracts under the Texas Water Development Board's water assistance, water loan assistance and rural water assistance programs from the state's uniform grant and contract management standards.

tx:HB 791|relating to the issuance of ce.title: Relating to the issuance of Central Catholic High School specialty license plates
tx:HB 791|relating to the issuance of ce.summary: Requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to issue Central Catholic High School specialty license plates bearing the school's logo and "With Loyal Hearts," with fees beyond administrative costs going to the state general revenue fund.

tx:SB 22|relating to the texas moving im.title: Relating to the Texas moving image industry incentive program and the establishment and funding of the Texas moving image industry incentive fund
tx:SB 22|relating to the texas moving im.summary: Creates a fund outside the state treasury for film, TV and video game incentive grants, deposits $300 million in sales tax revenue every two years until 2035, sets grant rates and bonuses capped at 31% of in-state spending, and lowers Texas-resident hiring requirements.

tx:SB 401|relating to participation by n.title: Relating to participation by non-enrolled students in University Interscholastic League-sponsored activities
tx:SB 401|relating to participation by n.summary: Requires public schools in University Interscholastic League activities to let homeschooled students participate unless the district or charter adopts a policy opting out; homeschooled students in opted-out districts may join the closest participating school's activities.

tx:SB 2122|relating to imposition of app.title: Relating to imposition of application fees for certain permits and permit amendments for the disposal of oil and gas waste
tx:SB 2122|relating to imposition of app.summary: Sets nonrefundable Railroad Commission application fees for oil and gas waste permits: $500 for landfarm, landtreatment or land application permits; $2,000 or $3,000 for commercial waste separation or disposal facilities; $1,000 for their amendments; and repeals a $300 surface-water discharge permit fee.

tx:SB 2138|relating to prohibiting the i.title: Relating to prohibiting the investment of the permanent university fund, the Texas University Fund, or money held by a public institution of higher education in financial companies that boycott certain energy companies
tx:SB 2138|relating to prohibiting the i.summary: Applies the state's ban on investing in financial companies that boycott energy companies to public university governing boards, the Texas University Fund and the Permanent University Fund.

tx:SB 578|relating to surveillance camer.title: Relating to surveillance cameras for certain housing developments that receive an allocation of low income housing tax credits
tx:SB 578|relating to surveillance camer.summary: Requires housing developments receiving low income housing tax credits to install and maintain working exterior surveillance cameras throughout the property, except developments in rural areas or those awarded credits before September 1, 2025.

tx:SR 687|suspending limitations on conf.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, H.B. No. 3556
tx:SR 687|suspending limitations on conf.summary: Lets the conference committee on a bill requiring Parks and Wildlife Department review of tall structures in counties with national wildlife refuges raise the height threshold in the bill from 500 to 575 and add rulemaking authority for the Parks and Wildlife Commission.

tx:HB 5671|relating to the election of d.title: Relating to the election of directors for and the authority to issue bonds of the Johnson County Special Utility District
tx:HB 5671|relating to the election of d.summary: Requires Johnson County Special Utility District board candidates to be qualified voters, district water or sewer customers and owners of land the district serves; removes limits on the district's powers; and lets it issue bonds without state environmental commission approval.

tx:HB 5323|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Texas Energy Waste Advisory Committee
tx:HB 5323|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates the Texas Energy Waste Advisory Committee of eight ex officio members, including state agency leaders and ERCOT's chief executive, chaired by the Public Utility Commission, to recommend ways state programs can cut electricity demand during high-risk hours on the ERCOT grid, reporting every two years.

tx:HB 1052|relating to health benefit pl.title: Relating to health benefit plan coverage of telemedicine, teledentistry, and telehealth appointments with an originating site or distant site located outside this state
tx:HB 1052|relating to health benefit pl.summary: Requires health plans to cover telemedicine, teledentistry and telehealth visits where the patient or provider is outside Texas, if the patient mainly lives in Texas and the provider is licensed here and has a Texas office, starting in 2026.

tx:HB 206|relating to limitations on a c.title: Relating to limitations on a county's authority to require a cash bond before approving the construction of a pipeline
tx:HB 206|relating to limitations on a c.summary: Bars counties from requiring a cash bond as a condition of approving construction of a pipeline within the county.

tx:HB 43|relating to the texas agricultu.title: Relating to the Texas Agricultural Finance Authority and to a study and report on plant diseases and pest outbreaks
tx:HB 43|relating to the texas agricultu.summary: Restructures the Texas Agricultural Finance Authority's board, removes age limits from its grant and interest rate reduction programs, raises maximum grants to $500,000 and loans to $1 million, cuts grant matching to 10%, and funds pest and disease control programs.

tx:SB 1453|relating to the current debt.title: Relating to the current debt rate and tax rate of a taxing unit for ad valorem tax purposes
tx:SB 1453|relating to the current debt.summary: Limits a local taxing unit's debt tax rate to what is needed for minimum required debt payments, unless 60% of its governing body approves a higher rate in a motion stating the difference and how extra revenue will be used, starting in 2026.

tx:HB 3976|relating to the waiver of lic.title: Relating to the waiver of license renewal fees for certain instructors in high-demand fields at public institutions of higher education
tx:HB 3976|relating to the waiver of lic.summary: Requires state licensing agencies to waive license renewal fees for public college faculty and adjunct professors who teach in fields such as nursing, pharmacy, engineering, plumbing, electrical work, air conditioning and teaching.

tx:HB 1579|relating to establishing the.title: Relating to establishing the Texas State Seal of Bilingualism and Biliteracy for public high school students
tx:HB 1579|relating to establishing the.summary: Requires the Texas Education Agency to create a Texas Seal of Biliteracy for high school graduates highly proficient in English and another language, with requirements not tied to a dedicated exam, and requires districts to note it on diplomas and transcripts.

tx:HB 103|relating to the creation and m.title: Relating to the creation and maintenance of a database of taxing unit bonds, taxes, and bond-related projects; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 103|relating to the creation and m.summary: Requires the comptroller to build a free public online database of local governments' bonds, bond elections, tax rate elections and debt-funded projects, requires taxing units to submit data including 2015–2025 history, and sets a $1,000 civil penalty for noncompliance.

tx:HB 1211|relating to tuition and fee e.title: Relating to tuition and fee exemptions at public institutions of higher education for certain students who were under the conservatorship of the Department of Family and Protective Services
tx:HB 1211|relating to tuition and fee e.summary: Extends the deadline for former foster youth to enroll in a public college or dual credit course and use the state tuition and fee exemption, from their 25th birthday to their 27th, starting with fall 2025.

tx:SB 1371|relating to the operation of.title: Relating to the operation of certain metropolitan transit authorities
tx:SB 1371|relating to the operation of.summary: Lets the Corpus Christi regional transit authority share its tax-exempt natural gas fueling stations with other governments in emergencies, adopt fare changes without joint city-county committee approval, and excludes certain partial terms from its board members' eight-year limit.

tx:HB 2301|relating to registration with.title: Relating to registration with and searches of the state registry of paternity
tx:HB 2301|relating to registration with.summary: Requires the state vital statistics unit to provide a certificate of the results of a state paternity registry search within 10 days after receiving a request from an authorized person, court or agency.

tx:HB 4454|relating to solicitation of p.title: Relating to solicitation of patients and other prohibited marketing practices and the establishment of the task force on patient solicitation; increasing criminal penalties
tx:HB 4454|relating to solicitation of p.summary: Creates an eight-member task force to report on illegal patient solicitation, bars mental health and addiction treatment facilities from false or misleading advertising and undisclosed lead-referral contracts, raises the minimum civil penalty to $2,000, and extends patient-referral payment crimes to any benefit.

tx:SB 1948|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of fire prevention standards for certain agricultural facilities
tx:SB 1948|relating to the regulation of.summary: Bars state and local governments from requiring fire sprinkler systems in barns and other nonresidential farm buildings, cotton gins, cottonseed and grain storage facilities, livestock markets and commercial feed mills.

tx:SB 1372|relating to access to the cri.title: Relating to access to the crime laboratory portal
tx:SB 1372|relating to access to the cri.summary: Limits access to the state crime laboratory portal for requesting lab records in criminal cases to the defendant's attorney, removing the option for prosecutors to designate the defendant personally, for cases starting on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:HB 2012|relating to regulation by cer.title: Relating to regulation by certain counties of roadside or parking lot vendors and solicitors
tx:HB 2012|relating to regulation by cer.summary: Lets commissioners courts in counties of more than 600,000 people that border a county of more than 4 million regulate roadside and parking-lot vendors, vendor structures and solicitation of money in unincorporated areas, as the largest counties already may.

tx:HB 4212|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment, administration, and use of the Texas land, water, and wildlife conservation account
tx:HB 4212|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a state conservation board led by the land commissioner and a dedicated account to award grants, split evenly when possible between public parks projects and land, water and wildlife conservation projects; bars use of the money for eminent domain or federal land transfers.

tx:SB 1577|relating to the temporary sal.title: Relating to the temporary sale of alcoholic beverages at certain racing facilities
tx:SB 1577|relating to the temporary sal.summary: Lets mixed beverage permit holders sell liquor as well as beer and wine in public areas at racing facilities seating over 40,000 during races and other events, and removes limits of four events a year and half of concession stands.

tx:HB 3463|relating to the prosecution o.title: Relating to the prosecution of the offense of theft of service
tx:HB 3463|relating to the prosecution o.summary: Lets the written notice demanding payment that is required before a theft of service charge for unpaid services be sent by e-mail, text message or commercial delivery as well as certified mail, and presumes it received within two days.

tx:HB 4924|relating to certain electroni.title: Relating to certain electronic documentation for the transfer of a motor vehicle title
tx:HB 4924|relating to certain electroni.summary: Bars the state motor vehicle department from requiring that electronic signatures be physically printed on electronically filed vehicle title transfer documents, or requiring proof that a replaced title was stamped invalid, as a condition of accepting them.

tx:HB 5165|relating to the use of munici.title: Relating to the use of municipal hotel occupancy tax revenue in certain municipalities
tx:HB 5165|relating to the use of munici.summary: Lets a county-seat city in a county of more than 10,000 people with a sandhills state park use hotel occupancy tax revenue to build and operate a recreational facility or rodeo and livestock show arena.

tx:HB 4406|relating to the reporting of.title: Relating to the reporting of direct campaign expenditures by certain persons and political committees
tx:HB 4406|relating to the reporting of.summary: Requires campaign finance reports to list each candidate or officeholder a direct campaign expenditure was made to support or oppose, replacing the current requirement to list candidates who benefit from such spending.

tx:SB 1049|relating to excused absences.title: Relating to excused absences from public school for the purpose of attending a released time course
tx:SB 1049|relating to excused absences.summary: Requires public and charter schools, at a parent's written request, to excuse students one to five hours a week for religious instruction offered by private entities, which must keep attendance records and assume liability; bars school spending beyond minimal costs, and leaves transportation to the entity or family.

tx:SB 2129|relating to the operation of.title: Relating to the operation of vehicles at railroad grade crossings; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:SB 2129|relating to the operation of.summary: Raises the fine for driving through a railroad crossing after a flagger warns of an approaching train to $100 to $400, double the regular $50 to $200 fine for disobeying crossing signals.

tx:SB 627|relating to the licensing and.title: Relating to the licensing and regulation of dietitians
tx:SB 627|relating to the licensing and.summary: Removes outdated provisions from dietitian licensing law, including references to provisional licensed dietitians, a requirement that regulators judge applicants' fitness, and separate registry and sanctions sections, and updates the penalty provision cited for refusing license renewal.

tx:SB 922|relating to the disclosure of.title: Relating to the disclosure of certain medical information by electronic means
tx:SB 922|relating to the disclosure of.summary: Bars releasing sensitive test results, such as pathology or imaging reports likely to show cancer or genetic test results, to patients through online portals or apps until the third day after the results are finalized, with no liability for noncompliance.

tx:HB 4449|relating to the sale of alcoh.title: Relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages in areas annexed by certain municipalities
tx:HB 4449|relating to the sale of alcoh.summary: Provides that land annexed by a city of more than 12,000 people in a county crossed by U.S. Highways 60 and 87 takes on that city's wet or dry status for alcohol sales, including areas annexed before the law takes effect.

tx:HB 4027|relating to the taking of cer.title: Relating to the taking of certain depositions and the dismissal of certain civil actions in connection with allegations of family violence and abusive conduct
tx:HB 4027|relating to the taking of cer.summary: Requires courts to deny petitions to depose, and to dismiss lawsuits against, people alleging family violence or abuse if clear and convincing evidence shows the other party has a history of such abuse and seeks to harass or control them; that party must disclose related protective orders and criminal complaints.

tx:HB 2725|relating to discount programs.title: Relating to discount programs provided by toll project entities for certain customers
tx:HB 2725|relating to discount programs.summary: Requires toll road discount programs for electronic toll customers, which now must cover certain veterans, to also give free or discounted use to vehicles registered to paramedics, peace officers and firefighters.

tx:HB 1285|relating to inspections and e.title: Relating to inspections and examinations by the Railroad Commission of Texas of certain sites and facilities conducted using unmanned aircraft
tx:HB 1285|relating to inspections and e.summary: Makes it lawful for the Railroad Commission and its agents to capture images with drones while inspecting oil and gas sites, wells, pipeline facilities and surface mining sites, and states that its property inspection access includes drone inspections.

tx:HB 3801|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Health Professions Workforce Coordinating Council and the abolition of the statewide health coordinating council and the nursing advisory committee of that council
tx:HB 3801|relating to the establishment.summary: Replaces the statewide health coordinating council and its nursing advisory committee with a new Health Professions Workforce Coordinating Council of state agency, licensing board and governor-appointed members that must publish a strategic plan with 10-year workforce projections every two years, and creates a nursing career pathways workgroup.

tx:SB 2112|relating to the punishment fo.title: Relating to the punishment for certain criminal offenses related to cultivated oyster mariculture; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:SB 2112|relating to the punishment fo.summary: Raises penalties for repeat oyster farming violations: operating without a permit or other prohibited acts becomes a Class A misdemeanor for a repeat offense within five years, and rule violations become Class B after two prior convictions.

tx:HR 4|adopting the house rules of proc.title: Adopting the House Rules of Procedure for the 89th Legislature
tx:HR 4|adopting the house rules of proc.summary: Adopts the Texas House's permanent rules of procedure for the 89th Legislature, covering the speaker's powers, committees, floor debate and bill handling; requires all standing committee chairs to come from the majority party and bars that party's members from serving as vice-chairs.

tx:SB 457|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of certain nursing facilities, including licensing requirements and Medicaid participation and reimbursement requirements
tx:SB 457|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires nursing homes to disclose owners of 5 percent or more, keeps Medicaid payments flowing during ownership changes, and requires Medicaid nursing homes to spend at least 80 percent of patient care payments on patient care, with recoupment exceptions for highly rated facilities, disaster costs and some low-occupancy facilities.

tx:HB 4848|relating to requiring that co.title: Relating to requiring that competency-based baccalaureate degree programs be offered at certain public institutions of higher education
tx:HB 4848|relating to requiring that co.summary: Requires each public university system to offer competency-based bachelor's degree programs in high-demand fields, costing students no more than half the average cost of attendance, adjusted yearly for inflation starting in 2027-28, beginning with the 2026-27 school year.

tx:SB 2141|relating to the issuance of s.title: Relating to the issuance of specialty license plates to state and federal judges
tx:SB 2141|relating to the issuance of s.summary: Lets state and federal judges who qualify for judge specialty license plates choose plates without the words "State Judge" or "U.S. Judge."

tx:HB 503|relating to the eligibility of.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain counties to participate in the rural sheriff's office salary assistance grant program and the rural prosecutor's office salary assistance grant program
tx:HB 503|relating to the eligibility of.summary: Expands rural sheriff's and prosecutor's office salary grant programs to counties of up to 400,000 people, up from 300,000, with new grants of $650,000 for sheriff's offices and $375,000 for prosecutor's offices in counties of 300,000 to 400,000.

tx:HB 1871|relating to the punishment fo.title: Relating to the punishment for the criminal offense of attempted capital murder of a peace officer; increasing a criminal penalty; changing eligibility for parole and mandatory supervision
tx:HB 1871|relating to the punishment fo.summary: Makes attempted capital murder of a peace officer a first-degree felony punishable by 25 to 99 years or life in prison, and makes people convicted of it ineligible for parole or mandatory supervision release.

tx:HB 3349|relating to the events trust.title: Relating to the events trust fund and to abolishing the Pan American Games trust fund, Olympic Games trust fund, and motor sports racing trust fund
tx:HB 3349|relating to the events trust.summary: Raises the state's matching share of events trust fund money for events in counties or cities under 500,000 people, sets new application and payment deadlines, requires local governments to put up their share, and abolishes the Pan American Games, Olympic Games and motor sports racing trust funds.

tx:HB 713|relating to an exception to ce.title: Relating to an exception to certain reporting requirements for health care providers reviewing selected cases for the Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee
tx:HB 713|relating to an exception to ce.summary: Exempts health care providers, including nurses, who review cases for the state Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee from professional reporting requirements for conduct they learn about in the case information they review.

tx:HB 4580|relating to the exemption fro.title: Relating to the exemption from ad valorem taxation of property of a charitable organization that provides financial support for promoting agriculture, supporting Texas youth and providing educational support
tx:HB 4580|relating to the exemption fro.summary: Exempts from property taxes property in counties of 3.3 million or more people owned by a charitable nonprofit and used to promote agriculture, support youth and provide education, including incidental other uses whose revenue benefits the charity's beneficiaries; for-profit tenants' interests stay taxable.

tx:HB 107|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the sickle cell disease registry
tx:HB 107|relating to the establishment.summary: Requires the state health department to create a confidential sickle cell disease registry using data from hospitals and treatment facilities, including patients only with their consent, and to report annually to the Legislature; implementation depends on funding.

tx:HB 1716|relating to the provision of.title: Relating to the provision of counseling services by certain providers under Medicaid and reimbursement for those services
tx:HB 1716|relating to the provision of.summary: Requires Medicaid to cover services by counselors, social workers and marriage and family therapists who are still completing supervised hours toward clinical licenses, paying them 50% of the psychiatrist or psychologist rate for up to 3,000 hours.

tx:HB 3426|relating to the issuance of d.title: Relating to the issuance of digital driver's licenses, commercial driver's licenses, and personal identification certificates; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 3426|relating to the issuance of d.summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety to offer digital driver's licenses and ID cards through a phone app, allows a fee to cover costs, bars using them for voting, and states that showing one does not consent to a search of the phone.

tx:HB 2658|relating to the kimble county.title: Relating to the Kimble County Hospital District of Kimble County, Texas
tx:HB 2658|relating to the kimble county.summary: Updates the laws governing the Kimble County Hospital District, easing eligibility rules for its board, expanding the facilities its hospital system may include, letting the board set the fiscal year and amend budgets, and requiring bids to choose its bank.

tx:HB 557|relating to the enforcement of.title: Relating to the enforcement of an order to pay child support by contempt
tx:HB 557|relating to the enforcement of.summary: Bars courts from holding a parent in contempt for unpaid child support if the parent shows they are current or have a plan to catch up and that missed payments stemmed from a third party's error or circumstances beyond their control; stops interest on arrears judgments in such cases.

tx:HB 3592|relating to restrictions on p.title: Relating to restrictions on political contributions by out-of-state contributors; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 3592|relating to restrictions on p.summary: Limits how much candidates and officeholders may accept per election from any single out-of-state contributor to $5,000 for statewide, $2,500 for district and $1,000 for county offices, requires excess gifts be returned, and sets civil penalties up to three times the amount.

tx:SB 1921|relating to a common characte.title: Relating to a common characteristic or use project in a public improvement district in certain municipalities
tx:SB 1921|relating to a common characte.summary: Limits tourism public improvement districts to hotel-related advertising, promotion and business recruitment, lets authorized hotel managers sign petitions to create them, and requires petitions backed by over 60% of hotel property value and 60% of hotels or land area.

tx:HJR 35|proposing a constitutional ame.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the creation of and use of money in the Grow Texas fund and allocating certain general revenues to that fund, the economic stabilization fund, and the state highway fund
tx:HJR 35|proposing a constitutional ame.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment creating a Grow Texas fund for infrastructure in areas affected by oil and gas production, diverting 12% of oil and gas tax money bound for the rainy day fund, up to $250 million every two years, overseen by a seven-member commission.

tx:SB 2177|relating to the creation of a.title: Relating to the creation of a grant program to assist local law enforcement agencies in solving violent and sexual offenses
tx:SB 2177|relating to the creation of a.summary: Creates a grant program in the governor's office to help city police and sheriff's departments solve more violent and sexual crimes, paying for staff, forensic technology and records systems, and requires recipients to report solve rates and case times yearly.

tx:SB 1697|relating to a customer guide.title: Relating to a customer guide to home solar energy devices
tx:SB 1697|relating to a customer guide.summary: Requires the Public Utility Commission to publish a consumer guide on installing home rooftop solar, covering questions for utilities, design and financial factors, and requires electric utilities, cooperatives and retail providers to link to it and mention it on bills for at least 12 months.

tx:SB 2145|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the advisory body of a public improvement district and the board of directors of a reinvestment zone to hold a meeting by a telecommunication device
tx:SB 2145|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets members of public improvement district advisory bodies and tax increment reinvestment zone boards attend and vote at meetings by phone or video, as long as one member, or for zone boards the chair or vice chair, is physically present.

tx:HB 4751|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment and administration of the Texas Quantum Initiative
tx:HB 4751|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates the Texas Quantum Initiative in the governor's office, with a six-member appointed advisory committee, a yearly strategic plan for growing the quantum technology industry, and a dedicated fund for grants to universities and businesses for quantum design and manufacturing.

tx:HB 1119|relating to a biennial report.title: Relating to a biennial report on the regional allocation of mental health beds
tx:HB 1119|relating to a biennial report.summary: Removes the Department of State Health Services from preparing the state's two-year report on regional allocation of mental health beds and expands the report to cover mental health spending, facility capacity and waitlists, patient outcomes, and grant applicants denied for lack of funds.

tx:HB 700|relating to disclosures for ce.title: Relating to disclosures for certain commercial sales-based financing transactions and the registration of commercial sales-based financing brokers; authorizing a fee and providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 700|relating to disclosures for ce.summary: Requires companies and brokers offering business financing repaid from a share of sales to register with the state and disclose costs and terms on offers under $1 million, voids confession-of-judgment clauses, limits automatic account debits, and sets $10,000 penalties per violation.

tx:HB 2692|relating to the codification.title: Relating to the codification and clarification of local laws concerning the San Antonio River Authority
tx:HB 2692|relating to the codification.summary: Gathers the San Antonio River Authority's governing laws, scattered across acts dating to 1937, into one chapter of state code covering its board, powers, voter-approved taxes, bonds and pollution control district, and repeals the older acts.

tx:SB 840|relating to certain municipal.title: Relating to certain municipal regulation of certain mixed-use and multifamily residential development projects and conversion of certain commercial buildings to mixed-use and multifamily residential occupancy
tx:SB 840|relating to certain municipal.summary: Requires cities over 150,000 people in counties over 300,000 to allow apartments and mixed-use housing without rezoning on land zoned for commercial, office, retail or warehouse use, limits rules and fees on converting older commercial buildings to housing, and lets affected parties sue.

tx:HB 126|relating to the compensation a.title: Relating to the compensation and professional representation of prospective student athletes and student athletes participating in intercollegiate athletic programs at certain institutions of higher education
tx:HB 126|relating to the compensation a.summary: Removes state bans on colleges paying athletes for use of their name, image and likeness, lets schools and athletes follow athletic association rules and court orders on such pay, and bars these deals with recruits under 17 not yet enrolled in college.

tx:HB 2525|relating to the exemption fro.title: Relating to the exemption from ad valorem taxation of certain property owned by a charitable organization that is engaged in providing housing and related facilities and services to persons who are at least 62 years of age
tx:HB 2525|relating to the exemption fro.summary: Extends the property tax exemption for charities housing people 62 and older to groups spending at least 4% of net resident revenue on charitable housing and services for needy seniors, if they have existed 20 years or share common control with such a group.

tx:HB 2278|relating to the home producti.title: Relating to the home production of certain alcoholic beverages
tx:HB 2278|relating to the home producti.summary: Lets adults and heads of household make liquor at home for personal or family use without a license, within the existing 200-gallon yearly limit for homemade alcohol, and adds honey to the ingredients allowed for homemade wine.

tx:HJR 144|proposing a constitutional am.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to authorize the creation of a regional mobility authority by local law
tx:HJR 144|proposing a constitutional am.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment letting the Legislature create a regional mobility authority by local law, without the usual advance local notice, to build, maintain and operate transportation projects in a region of the state.

tx:SB 529|relating to the entitlement of.title: Relating to the entitlement of certain municipalities to receive tax revenue from certain establishments located near a hotel and convention center project
tx:SB 529|relating to the entitlement of.summary: Lets certain cities of 130,000 or more people pledge certain state tax revenue to two qualified hotel and convention center projects instead of one and extends to them an existing entitlement to added tax revenue from businesses near such projects.

tx:HB 4088|relating to the qualification.title: Relating to the qualifications for jury service and the establishment of a juror mental health services reimbursement program
tx:HB 4088|relating to the qualification.summary: Disqualifies people from serving on a trial jury if they served as trial jurors for three consecutive months within the preceding 60 months in county or district court; the House-passed version dropped a proposed juror mental health reimbursement program.

tx:HB 3385|relating to the promotion and.title: Relating to the promotion and sale of wine produced in this state; creating a farm winery permit; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 3385|relating to the promotion and.summary: Creates a farm winery permit, costing up to $500 a year, for wineries using at least 75% Texas-grown fruit, allowing up to five off-site locations serving Texas wine and up to 250,000 gallons a year of to-go sales, with half of fees funding farm winery marketing.

tx:HB 1592|relating to an alert system f.title: Relating to an alert system for dangerous plant and wildlife pests and diseases administered by the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service
tx:HB 1592|relating to an alert system f.summary: Requires the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, working with state agriculture, animal health and wildlife agencies, to run a statewide email alert system on dangerous plant and wildlife pests, diseases and quarantines, sending alerts within 72 hours of agency action.

tx:HB 406|relating to notification of th.title: Relating to notification of the execution of certain local economic development agreements by a municipality or county to local workforce development boards
tx:HB 406|relating to notification of th.summary: Requires cities and counties to notify their local workforce development board in writing within 14 days of entering into, amending or renewing a local economic development agreement, including the details reported to the state's agreement database.

tx:HB 2818|relating to the artificial in.title: Relating to the artificial intelligence division within the Department of Information Resources
tx:HB 2818|relating to the artificial in.summary: Creates an artificial intelligence division in the Department of Information Resources to help state agencies use generative AI to replace outdated computer systems and on other projects, and requires a report on time and money saved for each project.

tx:HB 3062|relating to fentanyl preventi.title: Relating to fentanyl prevention and drug poisoning awareness education for students enrolled in public institutions of higher education
tx:HB 3062|relating to fentanyl preventi.summary: Requires public colleges and universities, starting with students entering in fall 2026, to give new undergraduates first-semester instruction on fentanyl and drug poisoning prevention, suicide prevention, substance abuse and available support resources.

tx:SB 924|relating to entities that prov.title: Relating to entities that provide video services
tx:SB 924|relating to entities that prov.summary: Excludes satellite TV and internet video streaming services from the state's definition of "video service" under cable and video franchise law, which carries local right-of-way fees, while preserving existing franchise holders' payment duties and certain claims for service before September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 1758|relating to the operation of.title: Relating to the operation of a cement kiln and the production of aggregates near a semiconductor wafer manufacturing facility
tx:SB 1758|relating to the operation of.summary: Shields cement kilns and aggregate operations from liability for vibration damage to semiconductor plants that began operating after them, orders a University of Texas study of vibration effects in Grayson County, and bars permits for such operations within 10 miles of a new chip plant there until 2031.

tx:SB 883|relating to patient access to.title: Relating to patient access to prescription drugs for off-label use for COVID-19 treatment
tx:SB 883|relating to patient access to.summary: Bars state officials from restricting physicians from prescribing FDA-approved drugs off-label to patients exposed to or diagnosed with COVID-19, and bars the Texas Medical Board from disciplining a physician solely for such prescribing if the care meets the medical standard of care.

tx:SJR 4|proposing a constitutional amen.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the maximum amount of money allowable in the economic stabilization fund
tx:SJR 4|proposing a constitutional amen.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, raising the cap on the state's economic stabilization (rainy day) fund from 10% to 15% of general revenue deposited in the prior two-year budget period, effective September 1, 2028.

tx:SB 311|relating to the writ power of.title: Relating to the writ power of the Texas Supreme Court
tx:SB 311|relating to the writ power of.summary: Broadens the Texas Supreme Court's power to issue writs such as mandamus and quo warranto by dropping the list of judges and state officers they may be directed to and the exemption for the Court of Criminal Appeals, leaving only the governor exempt.

tx:HB 2974|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain municipalities to use certain tax revenue for a hotel and convention center project and to receive certain tax revenue related to the project
tx:HB 2974|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets more cities use hotel occupancy tax revenue and state tax rebates to finance hotel and convention center projects, authorizes additional counties to levy hotel occupancy taxes, and revises how cities may spend hotel tax money, including state beach-cleaning funds for coastal cities.

tx:SB 2480|relating to the texas physici.title: Relating to the Texas Physician Health Program and the regulation of certain occupations by the Texas Medical Board; expanding the applicability of surcharges
tx:SB 2480|relating to the texas physici.summary: Extends the Texas Medical Board's license surcharges, including up to $15 for the confidential Texas Physician Health Program and a fee for continuous national practitioner database checks, to all board licensees rather than mainly physicians, and specifies that the program serves and accepts self-referrals from all of them.

tx:SB 2900|relating to a review of certa.title: Relating to a review of certain advisory entities under the jurisdiction of the comptroller of public accounts and to the repeal or redesignation of certain of those entities
tx:SB 2900|relating to a review of certa.summary: Requires the comptroller to review its advisory boards and report by December 1, 2026, on any that are unneeded; abolishes several, including a jobs-incentive oversight committee, a community reinvestment work group and greenhouse-gas advisory committees, and shifts tobacco-settlement investment advice to an existing committee.

tx:SB 663|relating to the approval of a.title: Relating to the approval of a community supervision and corrections department's budget and strategic plan
tx:SB 663|relating to the approval of a.summary: Requires local probation (community supervision) departments to have their budgets and strategic plans approved by a state criminal justice division as a condition of state aid, with local criminal judges reviewing rather than approving them, and removes these departments from a county juvenile-board budget law.

tx:HB 3308|relating to charitable raffle.title: Relating to charitable raffles conducted by the professional sports team charitable foundations of rodeo organizations sanctioned by certain professional associations or hosting a Professional Rodeo Event at rodeo venues
tx:HB 3308|relating to charitable raffle.summary: Expands the state's charitable raffle law for professional sports team foundations to cover organizations hosting a Professional Rodeo Event, letting their foundations hold raffles at those organizations' rodeo venues in Texas.

tx:HB 1232|relating to the reporting of.title: Relating to the reporting of violations of law under the whistleblower protection laws
tx:HB 1232|relating to the reporting of.summary: Extends whistleblower protection to public employees who in good faith report a violation of law by an elected officer of their employing government to law enforcement, barring firing, suspension or other retaliation for such reports.

tx:HB 1866|relating to the state law enf.title: Relating to the state law enforcement authority of federal National Park Service law enforcement officers
tx:HB 1866|relating to the state law enf.summary: Lets commissioned National Park Service officers, within national parks and recreation areas in Texas, execute state arrest and search warrants and use state peace-officer powers to take people into emergency mental health custody, in addition to their existing state arrest powers there.

tx:SB 992|relating to the procedure by w.title: Relating to the procedure by which the attorney general approves or denies approval of a state agency contract for outside legal services
tx:SB 992|relating to the procedure by w.summary: Requires the attorney general to approve or deny a state agency's contract for outside lawyers within 25 days of receiving it and to give the agency a written reason for any denial, replacing a separate 'timely action' rule for Teacher Retirement System contracts.

tx:HB 2967|relating to vision screenings.title: Relating to vision screenings for students in public or private school, including vision screening information reporting for public school students and the creation of a vision care allotment under the Foundation School Program
tx:HB 2967|relating to vision screenings.summary: Requires the Texas Education Agency to publish yearly data on students found to have vision problems in school screenings, creates a grant program, if funded, for screenings, eye exams and glasses for educationally disadvantaged students, and adds depth-perception and color-blindness screening options.

tx:HB 3071|relating to cancellation of c.title: Relating to cancellation of certain solid waste disposal permits issued by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
tx:HB 3071|relating to cancellation of c.summary: Requires the state environmental agency to cancel the permit of a municipal landfill that has not accepted waste for 25 consecutive years, if it lies in a county of more than 2.1 million people and just outside that county's main city of more than 900,000.

tx:HB 3848|relating to the electronic su.title: Relating to the electronic submission of inspection reports and filing fees for the inspection of elevators, escalators, and related equipment
tx:HB 3848|relating to the electronic su.summary: Lets the state allow elevator, escalator and related equipment inspection reports and filing fees to be submitted electronically, and counts electronic submissions as filed on the date they are submitted for deadline purposes.

tx:HB 5659|relating to the procedural re.title: Relating to the procedural requirements applicable to certain water-related transactions involving the Northeast Texas Municipal Water District
tx:HB 5659|relating to the procedural re.summary: Requires the Northeast Texas Municipal Water District to hold a public hearing before contracting for or seeking a state permit for an interbasin water transfer, and to get approval from the governing bodies of at least five of its member cities.

tx:SB 705|relating to the air conditioni.title: Relating to the air conditioning and refrigeration contractors advisory board
tx:SB 705|relating to the air conditioni.summary: Removes the two nonvoting ex officio members from the state Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors Advisory Board and adjusts the appointed members' staggered terms so that three expire every odd-numbered year.

tx:HB 4588|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of aquatic vegetation management by the Parks and Wildlife Department; providing a civil penalty; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 4588|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires anyone controlling aquatic vegetation in public waters to follow state and local management plans, integrated pest management principles and state wildlife agency rules, with civil penalties of $100 to $10,000 per violation per day and a Class C misdemeanor for violations.

tx:SB 569|relating to the provision of v.title: Relating to the provision of virtual education in public schools and to certain waivers and modifications by the commissioner of education to the method of calculating average daily attendance in an emergency or crisis for purposes of preserving school district funding entitlements under the Foundation School Program during that emergency or crisis; authorizing a fee
tx:SB 569|relating to the provision of v.summary: Replaces the state virtual school network with a framework letting school districts and charter schools offer virtual and hybrid courses and, with state approval, full-time virtual or hybrid campuses funded through state school finance, and requires attendance-funding adjustments after emergencies that reduce attendance.

tx:HB 2542|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of a work group to study and make recommendations on certain services needed by individuals with an intellectual or developmental disability
tx:HB 2542|relating to the establishment.summary: Requires the state health and human services agency to form a work group by October 1, 2025, to study services for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities, including those with mental health or high behavioral needs, and to report recommendations by December 1, 2026.

tx:HJR 5|proposing a constitutional amen.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the creation of funds to support the capital needs of educational programs offered by the Texas State Technical College System and repealing the limitation on the allocation to that system and its campuses of the annual appropriation of certain constitutionally dedicated funding for public institutions of higher education
tx:HJR 5|proposing a constitutional amen.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment creating permanent and available funds for Texas State Technical College System buildings, land and equipment, seeded with an $850 million general revenue deposit in January 2026, and removing the system from an existing constitutional higher-education construction fund.

tx:SB 2351|relating to the construction.title: Relating to the construction of certain concrete plants under a standard permit
tx:SB 2351|relating to the construction.summary: Lets the state environmental agency, when it amends a standard air permit for concrete plants, require operators that have not yet begun construction and sought an extension of their construction deadline to update their plans to meet the amended permit.

tx:HB 3627|relating to the employment of.title: Relating to the employment of persons by the State Board of Education
tx:HB 3627|relating to the employment of.summary: Lets the chair of the State Board of Education hire, direct, pay and fire staff to assist all board members using funds the legislature provides, with those employees eligible for state retirement and benefits and supported administratively by the Texas Education Agency.

tx:HB 668|relating to the renewal of a l.title: Relating to the renewal of a license to carry a handgun
tx:HB 668|relating to the renewal of a l.summary: Gives handgun license holders until one year after their license expires to renew it, instead of requiring renewal by the expiration date, including for licenses that expired before the change; the $40 renewal fee is unchanged.

tx:SB 1310|relating to senior retirement.title: Relating to senior retirement communities
tx:SB 1310|relating to senior retirement.summary: Requires senior retirement communities with at least 20 units and shared amenities to adopt and share an annual emergency plan, bars their contracts from controlling residents' advance directives or wills, and bars them from blocking residents' contact with police, social workers or family about safety.

tx:SB 2681|relating to the basis for a t.title: Relating to the basis for a third-party challenge to a voter's registration
tx:SB 2681|relating to the basis for a t.summary: Lets a voter challenge another person's voter registration based on a fact that is generally known or can be confirmed from a reliable source, not only on the challenger's personal knowledge, in the required sworn statement.

tx:SB 310|relating to the determination.title: Relating to the determination of a majority vote in certain elections
tx:SB 310|relating to the determination.summary: Requires candidates in elections that need a majority to win more than half of the votes as originally cast, and bars using ranked-choice (preferential) voting to reassign votes to produce a majority.

tx:SB 2230|relating to the evacuation of.title: Relating to the evacuation of unauthorized persons from a hazard area in connection with space flight activities; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 2230|relating to the evacuation of.summary: Requires cities, and lets counties, to order unauthorized people out of the federally calculated hazard area on space launch days, making violations a Class B misdemeanor (Class A for repeat offenses); takes effect only if related beach-closure legislation becomes law.

tx:SB 371|relating to parental approval.title: Relating to parental approval for a student's participation in human sexuality instruction in public schools
tx:SB 371|relating to parental approval.summary: Requires school districts to get a parent's written consent, requested separately and at least 14 days in advance, before a student receives human sexuality instruction, starting in the 2025-26 school year.

tx:SR 713|suspending limitations on conf.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, H.B. No. 40
tx:SR 713|suspending limitations on conf.summary: Lets House and Senate negotiators on the business court bill add language, found in neither chamber's version, allowing civil cases filed before September 1, 2024, to move to the business court if the parties agree and the court permits.

tx:SB 2269|relating to dispute resolutio.title: Relating to dispute resolution for and enforcement actions against certain long-term care facilities
tx:SB 2269|relating to dispute resolutio.summary: Makes informal dispute decisions on nursing facility violations binding on the state health commission, bars state administrative penalties for acts already penalized federally, or under federal appeal when requirements are substantially similar, and forbids retaliation against facilities that challenge commission decisions in good faith.

tx:HB 4936|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Department of Marketing Services
tx:HB 4936|relating to the creation of t.summary: Requires the state economic development and tourism office to study state agencies' total marketing costs and whether a central Department of Marketing Services could save money, reporting findings to state leaders by September 30, 2026.

tx:HB 2091|relating to the provision of.title: Relating to the provision of financial assistance by the Texas Water Development Board for certain projects
tx:HB 2091|relating to the provision of.summary: Lets the Texas Water Development Board give grants to drainage districts for water supply projects, including ones with flood control components, without disqualifying them for lacking water-use data or retail water service, and adds such projects as a factor in prioritizing state water fund projects.

tx:HB 180|relating to border protection.title: Relating to border protection agreements between this state and the United Mexican States
tx:HB 180|relating to border protection.summary: Lets the governor negotiate and sign border protection agreements with Mexico and Mexican states, and appoint representatives who may work in Mexico to meet with officials there, subject to state ethics rules; also states that people entering from abroad must use legal ports of entry.

tx:HB 1327|relating to the continuation.title: Relating to the continuation of a health care provider participation program by the Harris County Hospital District
tx:HB 1327|relating to the continuation.summary: Extends the Harris County Hospital District's authority to run its health care provider participation program, and the law creating it, by two years, from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2027.

tx:HB 2038|relating to the issuance by t.title: Relating to the issuance by the Texas Medical Board of certain licenses to practice medicine and the authority of an insured to select certain license holders under the insured's health policy; requiring an occupational license; authorizing fees
tx:HB 2038|relating to the issuance by t.summary: Creates provisional medical licenses for foreign-licensed doctors with Texas job offers, convertible to full licenses after passing exams, and limited licenses letting recent medical graduates not in residency practice under a sponsoring physician in counties under 100,000 people; lets insured patients choose these graduates.

tx:SB 1266|relating to medicaid provider.title: Relating to Medicaid provider enrollment and credentialing processes
tx:SB 1266|relating to medicaid provider.summary: Requires the state health commission to provide a support team helping providers enroll in Medicaid, evaluate and report on it yearly, accept online complaints, and give providers 30 days' notice and a chance to fix problems before removing them for incomplete revalidation.

tx:HB 1238|relating to the inspection of.title: Relating to the inspection of the location of a proposed Class I injection well
tx:HB 1238|relating to the inspection of.summary: Lets state environmental regulators meet the required site inspection for a proposed Class I injection well by accepting a report from a licensed Texas engineer or geoscientist, who may inspect in person or virtually using aerial imagery or mapping software.

tx:HB 4830|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of service contracts and service contract providers and administrators
tx:HB 4830|relating to the regulation of.summary: Revises service contract rules: adds coverage for lease-end vehicle wear and mileage charges, requires home service contract companies to take reasonable care that repairs use licensed workers and that service starts or delays are explained within 48 hours, and makes sellers liable for penalties.

tx:HB 204|relating to the total annual s.title: Relating to the total annual salary from state and county sources for certain state prosecutors
tx:HB 204|relating to the total annual s.summary: Exempts state prosecutors serving districts or counties with fewer than 400,000 people from the cap that limits their combined state and county salary to that of a comparable district judge.

tx:HB 4903|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Quad-Agency Child Care Initiative and the Quad-Agency Child Care Initiative Commission
tx:HB 4903|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a commission of the heads of four state agencies to coordinate child care policy, review rules affecting child care cost, quality or access with public comment, and send rules it finds inconsistent to a state regulatory efficiency office, which can require their withdrawal.

tx:HB 1650|relating to a special bill of.title: Relating to a special bill of review to reform a final judgment of forfeiture of a bail bond
tx:HB 1650|relating to a special bill of.summary: Gives bail bond sureties four years, instead of two, after a final bond forfeiture judgment to ask the court to reform the judgment and return all or part of the forfeited bond amount, for judgments entered after the law takes effect.

tx:HB 4609|relating to participation in.title: Relating to participation in, administration of, contributions to, and benefits under the Texas Municipal Retirement System
tx:HB 4609|relating to participation in.summary: Changes Texas Municipal Retirement System rules: removes caps so cities pay actuarially required contribution rates, adds 40% and 60% retiree cost-of-living options, sets venue for lawsuits against the system in Travis County, and makes many city benefit changes start the next January 1.

tx:HB 3697|relating to the text on an ap.title: Relating to the text on an application for a ballot to be voted by mail and other balloting materials
tx:HB 3697|relating to the text on an ap.summary: Requires the official application form for a mail-in ballot to be printed in black text in at least 10-point type, up from six-point, for elections ordered on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 1300|relating to the prosecution a.title: Relating to the prosecution and punishment of the criminal offense of organized retail theft; increasing criminal penalties
tx:SB 1300|relating to the prosecution a.summary: Redefines organized retail theft to include stealing with others, stealing twice from merchants within 180 days, profiting from such thefts, or overwhelming store security; raises penalties one level at each value threshold; and lets price tags serve as evidence of value and ownership.

tx:SB 1333|relating to the unauthorized.title: Relating to the unauthorized entry, occupancy, sale, rental, lease, advertisement for sale, rental, or lease, or conveyance of real property, including the removal of certain unauthorized occupants of a dwelling; creating criminal offenses; increasing a criminal penalty; authorizing a fee
tx:SB 1333|relating to the unauthorized.summary: Lets residential property owners have a sheriff or constable remove unauthorized occupants who are not tenants or family, for a fee, subject to wrongful-removal suits; makes knowingly selling or renting residential property without authority a felony and presenting fake leases or deeds a misdemeanor.

tx:SB 387|relating to bond requirements.title: Relating to bond requirements for certain judges
tx:SB 387|relating to bond requirements.summary: Raises the minimum bond that county judges and statutory county court judges presiding over guardianship or probate cases must post to $500,000, replacing minimums of $100,000 or $250,000 based on county population.

tx:HB 5153|relating to amending chapter.title: Relating to amending Chapter 62, Health and Safety Code, by adding certain local health entities as provider types for reimbursement under the Children's Health Insurance Program
tx:HB 5153|relating to amending chapter.summary: Requires the state health commission to create a separate provider type so local health departments and public health districts can enroll and be paid as providers in the Children's Health Insurance Program, contingent on funding.

tx:SB 1302|relating to eligibility to us.title: Relating to eligibility to use a general permit to discharge waste into or adjacent to waters in this state
tx:SB 1302|relating to eligibility to us.summary: Bars a discharger whose authority to discharge waste under a general water permit was denied or suspended from resuming until the state environmental agency's executive director actively reauthorizes it, without using an automatic approval process.

tx:HB 3171|relating to compensation and.title: Relating to compensation and employment condition standards by municipal charter or collective bargaining agreement and to impasse resolution in collective bargaining with certain political subdivisions
tx:HB 3171|relating to compensation and.summary: Requires some public employers and firefighter unions to follow impasse procedures in a city charter or labor contract, and requires binding arbitration between a city of 950,000 to 1,050,000 people and its firefighters' union at impasse, limiting what arbitrators may consider.

tx:HB 1845|relating to the use of funds.title: Relating to the use of funds from the rural prosecutor's office salary assistance grant program
tx:HB 1845|relating to the use of funds.summary: Lets rural prosecutor's offices use state salary assistance grant money to raise paralegals' salaries, in addition to assistant attorneys, investigators and victim assistance coordinators.

tx:HB 2785|relating to the display of ce.title: Relating to the display of certain information on the secretary of state's Internet website prior to the completion of an online voter registration application
tx:HB 2785|relating to the display of ce.summary: Requires the secretary of state's online voter registration application to make applicants acknowledge, before continuing, that completing the online form does not register them and that the form must be submitted to the county voter registrar.

tx:SB 66|relating to a study on authoriz.title: Relating to a study on authorizing a supporter under a supported decision-making agreement to assist an adult with a disability with legal proceedings
tx:SB 66|relating to a study on authoriz.summary: Requires the state Office of Court Administration to study letting a supporter under a supported decision-making agreement help an adult with a disability in legal proceedings, including effects on attorney-client privilege, and report recommendations by December 1, 2026.

tx:HB 3940|relating to the provision of.title: Relating to the provision of certain information about Medicaid benefits in relation to newborn children
tx:HB 3940|relating to the provision of.summary: Requires prenatal care providers to tell Medicaid-covered mothers that newborns are automatically eligible and can be billed under the mother's Medicaid number until enrolled, adds Medicaid information to pamphlets for new parents, and requires annual reminders to providers.

tx:SB 763|relating to standard permits f.title: Relating to standard permits for certain concrete plants
tx:SB 763|relating to standard permits f.summary: Requires state environmental regulators to conduct a protectiveness review of the standard air permit for permanent concrete plants at least every eight years, giving existing plants reasonable time to comply with any amendments, and to adopt implementing rules by March 1, 2026.

tx:HJR 88|proposing a constitutional ame.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to authorize the commissioners court of a county to exempt from ad valorem taxation by each political subdivision that taxes the property the portion of the assessed value of a person's property that is attributable to the installation in or on the property of a rainwater harvesting or graywater system
tx:HJR 88|proposing a constitutional ame.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025, ballot, letting the Legislature allow county commissioners courts to exempt from property taxes the added value of installing a rainwater harvesting or graywater system.

tx:SB 1532|relating to the information r.title: Relating to the information required to be posted by the Texas Water Development Board on the board's Internet website regarding the use of the state water implementation fund for Texas
tx:SB 1532|relating to the information r.summary: Removes the requirement that the Texas Water Development Board post on its website nonconfidential information from approved applications for state water implementation fund assistance, keeping other required postings on the fund's use.

tx:HB 3134|relating to advanced air mobi.title: Relating to advanced air mobility
tx:HB 3134|relating to advanced air mobi.summary: Requires the state transportation department to create an advanced air mobility office and statewide plan for electric and autonomous aircraft, provide planning guidance and university research matching funds, and bars local governments other than airport operators from regulating such aircraft.

tx:HB 163|relating to the possession and.title: Relating to the possession and administration of an epinephrine auto-injector by certain entities
tx:HB 163|relating to the possession and.summary: Lets any entity in Texas, including a government body, adopt a policy for keeping, administering and disposing of epinephrine delivery systems, rather than only entities listed in current law; entities required by other laws to have such a policy are excluded.

tx:HB 4766|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of sanitarians and sanitarians in training
tx:HB 4766|relating to the regulation of.summary: Revises state certification of sanitarians, defining a sanitarian in training as someone training in sanitary science while working in sanitation, making under one year of full-time experience a qualifying criterion, and repealing the exam-fee and exam-evaluation provisions.

tx:HB 3420|relating to certain mental he.title: Relating to certain mental health policies and services for peace officers, fire fighters, and telecommunicators
tx:HB 3420|relating to certain mental he.summary: Extends the mental health leave policies that government employers must offer peace officers and telecommunicators who experience a traumatic event on the job to firefighters as well.

tx:HB 3675|relating to consideration of.title: Relating to consideration of criminal history of applicants for public employment
tx:HB 3675|relating to consideration of.summary: Bars state agencies, public colleges and local governments from checking or asking about a job applicant's criminal history until after a conditional job offer, except for questions about legally disqualifying offenses; school districts and law enforcement jobs are exempt.

tx:HB 3348|relating to the creation and.title: Relating to the creation and operations of a health care provider participation program in certain counties
tx:HB 3348|relating to the creation and.summary: Lets three described counties without hospital districts collect mandatory payments from private hospitals, capped at 6 percent of their net patient revenue, into a local fund used mainly to draw federal Medicaid matching money for hospital care; hospitals may not pass the charges to patients.

tx:HB 127|relating to measures to protec.title: Relating to measures to protect public institutions of higher education from foreign adversaries and to the prosecution of the criminal offense of theft of trade secrets; providing civil and administrative penalties; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:HB 127|relating to measures to protec.summary: Creates a university research security council, bars universities from accepting most gifts from foreign adversary sources, requires screening of certain foreign researchers and approval of some foreign travel, and makes trade-secret theft benefiting a foreign government a second-degree felony.

tx:HB 1831|relating to the eligibility t.title: Relating to the eligibility to participate in certain drug court programs
tx:HB 1831|relating to the eligibility t.summary: Lets juveniles whose conduct involved a weapon, death or serious injury join drug court programs if the prosecutor consents, and removes the rule barring juveniles whose conduct involved use of force against another person.

tx:HB 1234|relating to certain procedure.title: Relating to certain procedures required for the denial of certain applications for a license to carry a handgun
tx:HB 1234|relating to certain procedure.summary: Bars the Department of Public Safety from denying a handgun license application over a medical advisory panel's concern about the applicant's judgment until it gives written reasons and at least 30 days to submit more information for the panel to review.

tx:SB 2037|relating to permit applicatio.title: Relating to permit application review and contested case procedures for environmental permits involving a project to construct or modify a liquefied natural gas export terminal; authorizing a fee
tx:SB 2037|relating to permit applicatio.summary: Requires state environmental regulators to offer liquefied natural gas export terminal permit applicants an optional expedited review for an extra fee, answer public comments within 120 days after comment closes, and hold contested-case preliminary hearings within 60 days of referral; challengers must state why they are affected.

tx:HB 923|relating to the texas medical.title: Relating to the Texas Medical Disclosure Panel
tx:HB 923|relating to the texas medical.summary: Expands the state panel that sets required medical risk disclosures for patients from nine to 13 members by adding three public members and another physician, requires a majority of its physician members to be present for any vote, and bars the panel from changing practice scope.

tx:SB 40|relating to the use by a politi.title: Relating to the use by a political subdivision of public funds to pay bail bonds; authorizing injunctive relief
tx:SB 40|relating to the use by a politi.summary: Bars cities, counties and other local governments from paying public money to nonprofit groups that use public donations to post bail for defendants, and lets local taxpayers or residents sue to stop such payments and recover legal fees.

tx:SB 1502|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the governing body of a school district to adopt an ad valorem tax rate that exceeds the district's voter-approval tax rate
tx:SB 1502|relating to the authority of.summary: Bars a school district from using the disaster exception to adopt a tax rate above its voter-approval rate without an election in a year when voters have already rejected a higher tax rate the district adopted.

tx:HB 2842|relating to the control by le.title: Relating to the control by lethal means of white-tailed deer in certain areas
tx:HB 2842|relating to the control by le.summary: Lets government agencies, universities and property owners' associations get state permits to kill white-tailed deer by showing it is needed to protect endangered species habitat or to control overpopulation where recreational hunting is not feasible.

tx:HB 1896|relating to a mental health l.title: Relating to a mental health leave policy for certain telecommunicators
tx:HB 1896|relating to a mental health l.summary: Expands required state and local government mental health leave policies, with no loss of pay, from peace officers and telecommunicators to also cover firefighters, detention officers, county jailers and emergency medical services employees who experience a traumatic event on the job.

tx:SB 1055|relating to permit fees for g.title: Relating to permit fees for groundwater wells imposed by the Southeast Texas Groundwater Conservation District
tx:SB 1055|relating to permit fees for g.summary: Raises the maximum fee the Southeast Texas Groundwater Conservation District may charge on wells from one cent to seven cents per thousand gallons of groundwater pumped.

tx:HB 4205|relating to compensation and.title: Relating to compensation and employment benefits for law enforcement personnel in certain counties
