tx:HB 4205|relating to compensation and.summary: Requires commissioners courts in counties of 3.3 million or more that raise pay or benefits for a class of county-funded police officers, including district attorney investigators and fire marshal officers, to raise them equally across that class and fund the increase.

tx:SB 1023|relating to the calculation o.title: Relating to the calculation of certain ad valorem tax rates
tx:SB 1023|relating to the calculation o.summary: Requires the state's property tax rate calculation forms to be electronic with links to documents supporting each entry, and requires local tax rate calculations to handle each tax increment reinvestment zone separately, starting in 2026.

tx:HB 2215|relating to the carrying or p.title: Relating to the carrying or possession of a handgun by certain retired attorneys representing the state
tx:HB 2215|relating to the carrying or p.summary: Exempts licensed handgun carriers who retired as attorney general, U.S. attorney, district, criminal district or county attorney, an assistant in those offices, or a city attorney from the offenses of unlawfully carrying a weapon and carrying weapons in prohibited places.

tx:SB 1663|relating to notification proc.title: Relating to notification procedures concerning groundwater contamination
tx:SB 1663|relating to notification proc.summary: Requires the state environmental agency, within 30 days of learning of groundwater contamination, to try to notify affected well owners, groundwater districts and residents within one mile by mail, email, door notice or other effective means.

tx:HB 3309|relating to the use of automa.title: Relating to the use of automated traffic control systems by local authorities and law enforcement agencies
tx:HB 3309|relating to the use of automa.summary: Bars local governments and police from using automated traffic cameras to enforce traffic laws, except in construction or maintenance work zones with posted warning signs, where a peace officer must issue the ticket at the time of the violation.

tx:HJR 47|proposing a constitutional ame.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the creation of the Texas severance tax revenue and oil and natural gas (Texas STRONG) defense fund, dedicating the money in that fund to benefit areas of the state significantly affected by oil and gas production, and providing for the transfer of certain general revenues to that fund, the economic stabilization fund, and certain other funds and accounts
tx:HJR 47|proposing a constitutional ame.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment creating a grant fund for areas heavily affected by oil and gas production, and shifting 12 percent of oil and gas tax revenue now bound for the rainy day fund: 10 percent to it, up to $500 million yearly, and 2 percent to cleanup and emissions funds.

tx:SB 2155|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of veterinary professionals and facilities by the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners and the temporary administration of the board by the Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx:SB 2155|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires veterinary clinics, including remote practices, to register with the state veterinary board by September 2027, puts the board's executive director under the licensing department's direction, and revises how the board handles complaints, discipline, hearings and emergency orders.

tx:HB 4464|relating to removing the requ.title: Relating to removing the requirement of provision of workers' compensation insurance coverage for Texas Task Force 1 members and members of intrastate fire mutual aid system teams and regional incident management teams
tx:HB 4464|relating to removing the requ.summary: Treats deployments and training with Texas Task Force 1 and state fire mutual aid and incident management teams as part of members' regular government jobs for workers' compensation, and ends state coverage for members who are not government employees.

tx:HJR 2|proposing a constitutional amen.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment prohibiting the legislature from imposing death taxes applicable to a decedent's property or the transfer of an estate, inheritance, legacy, succession, or gift
tx:HJR 2|proposing a constitutional amen.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment barring the state from taxing a person's estate because of death, and from creating or raising taxes on inheritances, gifts or other transfers of wealth beyond those in effect on January 1, 2025.

tx:HB 1557|relating to waiver programs f.title: Relating to waiver programs for certain veterans provided by toll project entities
tx:HB 1557|relating to waiver programs f.summary: Requires toll road authorities to run discount programs for electronic toll customers that give free use to vehicles registered to certain veterans, and lets the programs also offer free or discounted use to other customers.

tx:HB 3177|relating to the peace officer.title: Relating to the peace officer status of designated investigators of a municipal office of inspector general
tx:HB 3177|relating to the peace officer.summary: Lets cities of more than 1.2 million with an inspector general's office make its investigators peace officers, but bars them from investigating police misconduct where the police agency has an internal affairs unit, and requires findings to go to prosecutors.

tx:HB 2756|relating to training on de es.title: Relating to training on de-escalation, crisis intervention, and behavioral health for correctional officers and certain other employees of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice
tx:HB 2756|relating to training on de es.summary: Requires the state prison system to train correctional officers and their direct supervisors in de-escalation, crisis intervention and behavioral health, including alternatives to restraints and suicide prevention, as part of preservice training and every year, starting by December 1, 2025.

tx:HB 3516|relating to the availability.title: Relating to the availability of certain working papers and electronic communications of certain administrative law judges and technical examiners under the public information law
tx:HB 3516|relating to the availability.summary: Extends the public-records exemption for working papers and electronic communications of administrative law judges at the State Office of Administrative Hearings to administrative law judges and technical examiners at the Railroad Commission.

tx:HB 2081|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the Building Better Futures Program to support educational and occupational skills training opportunities and support services for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities at public and private institutions of higher education
tx:HB 2081|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates the Building Better Futures Program, run by the Higher Education Coordinating Board, to award money to public and private colleges offering educational and job-skills training and support services to students with intellectual and developmental disabilities, with credits not transferable to associate or bachelor's degree programs.

tx:HB 1803|relating to the dentist and d.title: Relating to the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact; authorizing fees
tx:HB 1803|relating to the dentist and d.summary: Enters Texas into the multistate Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact, letting dentists and hygienists licensed in one member state practice in others, creating a compact commission and shared licensing database, and making the state dental board the administrator.

tx:HB 500|relating to making supplementa.title: Relating to making supplemental appropriations and reductions in appropriations and giving direction and adjustment authority regarding appropriations
tx:HB 500|relating to making supplementa.summary: Makes supplemental appropriations to, and reduces some existing appropriations for, state agencies, including health and human services, schools and universities, courts, prisons and state facilities, and gives directions on how the money is used.

tx:HB 1828|relating to legislative leave.title: Relating to legislative leave for correctional officers employed by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice
tx:HB 1828|relating to legislative leave.summary: Lets state prison correctional officers donate up to eight hours a year of compensatory time or annual leave to a pool that officers may draw from for legislative work on behalf of a qualifying employee association, within set hourly limits.

tx:HB 2621|relating to the recording and.title: Relating to the recording and archiving of live video feed by the Texas Department of Transportation
tx:HB 2621|relating to the recording and.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Transportation to record and keep for at least 30 days the live video from its cameras, making the recordings confidential except for sharing with police for criminal investigations or to respond to emergencies.

tx:SB 527|relating to health benefit cov.title: Relating to health benefit coverage for general anesthesia in connection with certain pediatric dental services
tx:SB 527|relating to health benefit cov.summary: Bars health plans that cover general anesthesia from excluding medically necessary general anesthesia for dental care for covered individuals who meet set criteria, for plans starting January 1, 2026, without requiring dental coverage itself.

tx:SB 2349|relating to notice requiremen.title: Relating to notice requirements for a leased dwelling located in a floodplain
tx:SB 2349|relating to notice requiremen.summary: Exempts leases shorter than 30 days and short-term occupancy tied to a home sale from landlord floodplain and flood-damage notice requirements, and requires landlord and tenant to sign the document containing the notices.

tx:HB 3641|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of counties to regulate noise levels in residential areas; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 3641|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets county commissioners courts regulate noise from homes and residential land in unincorporated areas, excluding fireworks and business activity, and makes violating such an order two or more times a Class C misdemeanor.

tx:HB 290|relating to assistance for tui.title: Relating to assistance for tuition and fees at postsecondary educational institutions for certain members of the Texas military forces
tx:HB 290|relating to assistance for tui.summary: Expands state tuition aid for Texas military forces members, raising the per-term credit-hour cap from 12 to 15, the time limit from five to seven years or 10 to 15 terms, and State Guard awards from 30 to 45 per term.

tx:SJR 18|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment prohibiting the imposition of a tax on the realized or unrealized capital gains of an individual, family, estate, or trust
tx:SJR 18|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, barring the Legislature from taxing realized or unrealized capital gains of individuals, families, estates or trusts, without affecting property, sales or use taxes.

tx:HB 4488|relating to the creation and.title: Relating to the creation and re-creation of funds and accounts, the dedication and rededication of revenue and allocation of accrued interest on dedicated revenue, and the exemption of unappropriated money from use for general governmental purposes
tx:HB 4488|relating to the creation and.summary: Abolishes new state funds, accounts and revenue dedications created by other 2025 laws unless specifically exempted, sends that revenue to the general fund, lists exempted funds, and makes interest on certain dedicated accounts available for general spending.

tx:HB 108|relating to the use of metal o.title: Relating to the use of metal or body armor while committing an offense; increasing a criminal penalty
tx:HB 108|relating to the use of metal o.summary: Raises the penalty for second- and third-degree felonies against a person to the next higher level when the judge or jury finds the defendant used metal or body armor, with exceptions for peace officers, military members and security officers.

tx:SB 1038|relating to administrative re.title: Relating to administrative remedies for certain fraud and abuse violations under Medicaid; providing administrative penalties
tx:SB 1038|relating to administrative re.summary: Broadens administrative remedies for Medicaid fraud and abuse, making violators repay amounts received with interest and face penalties up to twice that amount plus per-violation fines, and allows either repayment or a penalty of up to $500 per violation for missing claim documentation.

tx:HB 3619|relating to the rights and li.title: Relating to the rights and liabilities of the owner of the surface estate of the tract of land on which a well to be plugged or replugged by the Railroad Commission of Texas is located
tx:HB 3619|relating to the rights and li.summary: Requires the Railroad Commission, when it plugs or replugs a well, to restore the land's surface unless the owner declines, bars people entering the land from blocking the owner's access except to protect public health, and shields surface owners from liability for that work.

tx:SB 2781|relating to the imposition of.title: Relating to the imposition of civil penalties for certain violations with respect to political contributions and expenditures made by certain persons who engage in lobbying activities
tx:SB 2781|relating to the imposition of.summary: Sets civil penalties of up to twice the amounts involved for lobbyists who make prohibited political contributions or expenditures and for people who lobby within two years of making certain restricted contributions.

tx:SB 2063|relating to ad valorem tax pr.title: Relating to ad valorem tax protests and appeals on the ground of the unequal appraisal of property
tx:SB 2063|relating to ad valorem tax pr.summary: Bars appraisal review boards and courts from considering a property's market value as evidence when an owner protests or appeals a tax appraisal solely on the ground that it is unequal to comparable properties, starting January 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1822|relating to the use of artifi.title: Relating to the use of artificial intelligence-based algorithms in utilization review conducted for certain health benefit plans
tx:SB 1822|relating to the use of artifi.summary: Requires health insurers and HMOs to disclose whether they use artificial intelligence in reviewing whether care is covered, ensure those systems minimize bias and follow clinical guidelines, and file yearly compliance statements with the state insurance department.

tx:HB 171|relating to the certificate of.title: Relating to the certificate of medical examination for chemical dependency and the duration of court-ordered treatment for a person with a chemical dependency
tx:HB 171|relating to the certificate of.summary: Changes court-ordered chemical dependency treatment by requiring the examining physician's certificate to state the person meets commitment criteria and letting facilities discharge patients early once they no longer meet those criteria.

tx:SB 2610|relating to a limitation on c.title: Relating to a limitation on civil liability of business entities in connection with a breach of system security
tx:SB 2610|relating to a limitation on c.summary: Bars punitive damages in data breach lawsuits against businesses with fewer than 250 employees that hold sensitive personal data if they had a cybersecurity program meeting recognized industry standards at the time of the breach.

tx:HR 1515|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, S.B. No. 2972
tx:HR 1515|suspending limitations on con.summary: Suspends House rules so the conference committee on a bill about expressive activities at public colleges can restore wording requiring that restrictions on such activities be content-neutral and remove an unneeded word.

tx:HB 4700|relating to the responsibilit.title: Relating to the responsibilities and composition of the Health and Human Services Commission Executive Council
tx:HB 4700|relating to the responsibilit.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Executive Council to seek and receive public comment on the commission's rulemaking and rule review activities rather than only proposed rules, and updates which division directors serve on the council.

tx:HB 249|relating to installment paymen.title: Relating to installment payments of ad valorem taxes imposed on residence homesteads in certain counties
tx:HB 249|relating to installment paymen.summary: Lets any homeowner with a homestead exemption in a county of more than 1.5 million where over 70 percent of residents live in one city pay property taxes on the home in quarterly installments, starting with 2027 taxes.

tx:HB 1731|relating to the physician ass.title: Relating to the physician assistant licensure compact; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 1731|relating to the physician ass.summary: Enters Texas into the multistate Physician Assistant Licensure Compact, letting physician assistants licensed in one member state practice in others, creating a compact commission and shared data system, and making the state physician assistant board the administrator.

tx:HB 1318|relating to a certificate of.title: Relating to a certificate of public convenience and necessity to provide water or sewer service in an area incorporated or annexed by a municipality
tx:HB 1318|relating to a certificate of.summary: Changes how water or sewer utilities are paid when a city takes over their service area, requiring compensation for transferred property and for damage to property they keep rather than for property made useless, and limiting what courts may weigh in valuing that damage.

tx:HB 3260|relating to the texas industr.title: Relating to the Texas Industry-Recognized Apprenticeship Programs Grant Program
tx:HB 3260|relating to the texas industr.summary: Lets the Texas Workforce Commission pay industry-recognized apprenticeship grants in stages as training and job milestones are met, and requires rules on qualifying occupations, program certification and performance measures, with yearly public reporting.

tx:HB 2294|relating to reimbursement rat.title: Relating to reimbursement rates for child-care providers participating in the Texas Rising Star Program
tx:HB 2294|relating to reimbursement rat.summary: Lets local workforce boards pay Texas Rising Star child-care providers the board's maximum reimbursement rate for their quality rating regardless of the provider's published rate, if it does not cut the number of subsidized children served.

tx:SB 1963|relating to a financing mecha.title: Relating to a financing mechanism allowing electric utilities to obtain recovery of costs associated with a weather-related event or other natural disaster; granting authority to issue bonds
tx:SB 1963|relating to a financing mecha.summary: Lets any electric utility seek bond financing for at least $50 million in a year of estimated and actual storm or disaster restoration costs, requiring a utility commission decision within 150 days and later adjustment of charges to actual costs.

tx:HB 318|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of grant programs to provide financial assistance to qualified sheriff's departments in certain rural counties
tx:HB 318|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a comptroller grant program, paid from appropriations and capped at $150 million a year, for sheriff's departments in counties of 300,000 or fewer with low deputy or investigator staffing, paying $50,000 to $100,000 per added deputy or investigator and $35,000 per dispatcher or investigative support worker.

tx:SB 1951|relating to the imposition of.title: Relating to the imposition of a penalty for failure to timely file a rendition statement or property report with the chief appraiser of an appraisal district
tx:SB 1951|relating to the imposition of.summary: Requires appraisal districts to mail notice of a late-rendition penalty by June 1, by certified mail if the property was not on the prior year's roll, requires tax bills to list the penalty separately, and ends districts keeping 5% of penalties collected.

tx:HB 4044|relating to certain expenditu.title: Relating to certain expenditures by public institutions of higher education and university systems that are eligible for certain tax credits
tx:HB 4044|relating to certain expenditu.summary: Makes costs that public colleges, universities and university systems incur to rehabilitate certified historic buildings eligible again for the state historic preservation tax credit, with that eligibility ending January 1, 2035.

tx:SB 1285|relating to the protection of.title: Relating to the protection of bats
tx:SB 1285|relating to the protection of.summary: Narrows exemptions from the state ban on entombing, hunting or selling bats by removing the blanket exemption for licensed pest control services, leaving exemptions only for capturing injured or diseased bats and for transporting bats for rabies testing or rehabilitation.

tx:SB 2541|relating to the calculation o.title: Relating to the calculation of the unused increment rate of a taxing unit
tx:SB 2541|relating to the calculation o.summary: Limits local taxing units to banking unused property tax rate room from the previous two years, rather than three, when calculating the highest rate they may adopt without an election, beginning with tax year 2027.

tx:SB 2595|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the criminal offense of harassing, intimidating, or threatening another person while concealing identity with a mask or other headgear
tx:SB 2595|relating to the creation of t.summary: Makes it a Class B misdemeanor to intentionally harass, intimidate or threaten someone in a public place while wearing a mask or headgear to hide one's identity, with defenses for holidays, job safety, weather, theater, emergencies, health and religious reasons.

tx:SB 2366|relating to a grant program t.title: Relating to a grant program to fund certain short line railroad projects
tx:SB 2366|relating to a grant program t.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Transportation to create a grant program for rail districts that own or operate short line railroads to replace tracks or bridges, add capacity or restore rail lines, with at least 10% non-state matching money and no state highway fund money.

tx:SB 732|relating to required generator.title: Relating to required generators or other power sources for certain housing developments that receive an allocation of low income housing tax credits
tx:SB 732|relating to required generator.summary: Requires low-income housing tax credit developments for residents 55 and older to have a generator or other power source that runs essential elevators and keeps at least one enclosed area at 68 to 82 degrees during outages, with hardship waivers and a 2030 deadline for existing buildings.

tx:SB 2183|relating to the periods durin.title: Relating to the periods during which a retail fireworks permit holder may sell fireworks to the public
tx:SB 2183|relating to the periods durin.summary: Lets retail fireworks sellers statewide sell during set periods around Texas Independence Day, San Jacinto Day, Cinco de Mayo, Memorial Day and Diwali, in addition to the July 4 and New Year's periods, replacing rules that tied those extra periods to county approval or border locations.

tx:SB 1124|relating to discovery in a cr.title: Relating to discovery in a criminal case
tx:SB 1124|relating to discovery in a cr.summary: Defines the state's discovery duties in criminal cases to cover both prosecutors and investigating police agencies, lets courts limit overly broad or burdensome defense requests, creates pretrial discovery conferences, and limits suppressing undisclosed evidence to knowing violations or harm other remedies cannot cure.

tx:SB 2231|relating to requiring the tex.title: Relating to requiring the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to waive fees for admission applications submitted to public institutions of higher education during certain periods
tx:SB 2231|relating to requiring the tex.summary: Requires the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to designate the second full week of October as Free College Application Week, when people may apply for undergraduate admission to any public college or university without paying an application fee, starting in 2025-26.

tx:HB 2820|relating to the limits on the.title: Relating to the limits on the amount of operating capital by a charitable bingo organization
tx:HB 2820|relating to the limits on the.summary: Raises from $50,000 to $100,000 the maximum operating capital a licensed charitable bingo organization, or each member of a bingo unit, may keep in its bingo account.

tx:HB 4518|relating to the formation of.title: Relating to the formation of decentralized unincorporated nonprofit associations and the use of distributed ledger or blockchain technology for certain business purposes; authorizing fees
tx:HB 4518|relating to the formation of.summary: Lets groups of at least 100 members form decentralized unincorporated nonprofit associations whose governing rules may run on blockchain or smart contracts, makes them legal entities separate from their members, bars paying profits to members, and shields members from the association's debts.

tx:HB 4116|relating to information made.title: Relating to information made available to a relative or other designated caregiver
tx:HB 4116|relating to information made.summary: Requires the Department of Family and Protective Services to tell relatives and other caregivers in writing, when a child is placed with them, about becoming a foster home and the added payments it brings, TANF benefits, and other financial help available to them.

tx:HB 4687|relating to the applicability.title: Relating to the applicability of certain immunity and liability laws to certain charter school campuses or programs
tx:HB 4687|relating to the applicability.summary: Gives governing board members of district-authorized charter campuses or programs, and entities running adult high school charter programs along with their employees and volunteers, the same immunity from lawsuits and liability as school districts, trustees and district employees.

tx:SB 670|relating to patient authorizat.title: Relating to patient authorization to access certain investigational sun protection products
tx:SB 670|relating to patient authorizat.summary: Lets patients use sun protection products not yet approved by the FDA if their doctor finds approved products less effective and recommends one in writing and the patient signs informed consent; makers may supply them voluntarily, and state officials may not block access.

tx:HB 413|relating to the release of cer.title: Relating to the release of certain defendants detained in jail pending trial
tx:HB 413|relating to the release of cer.summary: Bars keeping a defendant charged with a Class B misdemeanor or more serious offense in jail before trial longer than the maximum sentence for the charge, counting good-conduct credit, except defendants under competency evaluation or commitment.

tx:HB 658|relating to the carrying of we.title: Relating to the carrying of weapons by community supervision and corrections department officers, juvenile probation officers, and certain retired law enforcement officers and to criminal liability for taking a weapon from certain of those officers
tx:HB 658|relating to the carrying of we.summary: Lets community supervision officers and juvenile probation officers carry weapons whether or not on duty, bars businesses open to the public from barring them and certified retired officers from carrying, and makes taking a weapon from a juvenile probation officer a crime.

tx:HB 1043|relating to a study by the ge.title: Relating to a study by the General Land Office on the establishment and implementation by the General Land Office of a distributed ledger-based title registry pilot program
tx:HB 1043|relating to a study by the ge.summary: Requires the General Land Office, with a working group of county, title, banking, state agency and blockchain representatives, to study a pilot program for recording property titles on a distributed ledger in at least one rural and one urban county, reporting by January 1, 2027.

tx:SB 434|relating to the authority of t.title: Relating to the authority of the Harris County Hospital District to employ and commission peace officers
tx:SB 434|relating to the authority of t.summary: Lets the Harris County Hospital District's board employ and commission its own peace officers for the district, an authority certain other hospital districts in the state already have.

tx:SB 2477|relating to certain municipal.title: Relating to certain municipal regulation of conversion of certain office buildings to mixed-use and multifamily residential occupancy
tx:SB 2477|relating to certain municipal.summary: Bars cities over 150,000 people in counties over 300,000 from requiring traffic studies, extra parking, rezoning, or stricter density or design rules to convert office buildings at least five years old to housing, limits impact fees, and requires administrative approval of compliant conversions.

tx:HB 4621|relating to the electronic re.title: Relating to the electronic return of a completed marriage license to a county clerk by a federal or state judge who conducted the marriage ceremony
tx:HB 4621|relating to the electronic re.summary: Lets the person who conducts a marriage ceremony authorize the couple to return the completed marriage license to the issuing county clerk themselves, and exempts both from the $200 to $500 fine for failing to return it.

tx:HB 2849|relating to policies on the r.title: Relating to policies on the recess period in public schools
tx:HB 2849|relating to policies on the r.summary: Requires each school district to adopt a recess policy by May 2026, based on state model policies, that sets weekly minutes of unstructured playtime and says whether recess may be withheld as discipline, and to review it every five years.

tx:SB 1660|relating to the retention and.title: Relating to the retention and preservation of toxicological evidence of certain intoxication offenses
tx:SB 1660|relating to the retention and.summary: Requires crime labs holding toxicology evidence from intoxication cases to notify county prosecutors each year, and lets the evidence be destroyed after its retention period ends if prosecutors do not object in writing within 90 days of a request.

tx:SB 304|relating to the jurisdiction o.title: Relating to the jurisdiction of municipal courts over health and safety and nuisance abatement ordinances
tx:SB 304|relating to the jurisdiction o.summary: Lets a city, by ordinance, give its regular municipal court power to enforce dangerous-building, junked-vehicle and other health, safety and nuisance ordinances, including civil jurisdiction and authority to issue search and seizure warrants for violations.

tx:HB 4991|relating to open meetings and.title: Relating to open meetings and public information training for certain public officials and attorneys regarding the open meetings and public information laws
tx:HB 4991|relating to open meetings and.summary: Requires attorneys who help governments handle open meetings and public records duties to complete state training within 10 days of being hired, and ends officials' option of having a records coordinator take the required training in their place.

tx:HB 135|relating to an exemption from.title: Relating to an exemption from sales and use taxes for game animals and exotic animals
tx:HB 135|relating to an exemption from.summary: Adds exotic animals and game animals to the list of agricultural items exempt from state sales and use taxes, alongside horses, work animals and animals raised for food.

tx:HB 1057|relating to placement on the.title: Relating to placement on the minimum salary schedule and service credit in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas for certain public school career or technology education teachers
tx:HB 1057|relating to placement on the.summary: Lets certified career and technology education teachers count up to five years, instead of two, of required industry work experience toward their salary step, and establish up to five years of matching Teacher Retirement System service credit.

tx:HB 5084|relating to the sale of firew.title: Relating to the sale of fireworks on and before the Lunar New Year holiday
tx:HB 5084|relating to the sale of firew.summary: Lets retail fireworks permit holders sell fireworks to the public during the five days before and on Lunar New Year, in counties whose commissioners court approves sales during that period.

tx:SB 1378|relating to the powers of cer.title: Relating to the powers of certain nonresident seller's permit holders who also hold a winery permit
tx:SB 1378|relating to the powers of cer.summary: Bars a holder of a nonresident seller's alcohol permit who also holds a winery permit, or whose affiliate does, from selling wine to the holder of that winery permit.

tx:SB 963|relating to allowing medicaid.title: Relating to allowing Medicaid managed care organizations to engage in marketing about the availability of certain private health benefit plan coverage
tx:SB 963|relating to allowing medicaid.summary: Bars state rules from stopping Medicaid managed care plans from telling people about federal marketplace health plans or advertising Medicare Advantage at community events, and requires plans to explain marketplace costs and offer no enrollment incentives.

tx:SB 1923|relating to the modification.title: Relating to the modification of certain orders providing for the support of a child
tx:SB 1923|relating to the modification.summary: Adds a signed caregiver authorization agreement as grounds for redirecting child support to the person who has physical possession of a child, and lets notice of support modification motions be served by e-mail through the state's electronic filing system.

tx:HB 2193|relating to a study by the te.title: Relating to a study by the Texas Veterans Commission regarding the provision of veterans benefits in this state
tx:HB 2193|relating to a study by the te.summary: Requires the Texas Veterans Commission to study how many veterans in each county are eligible for benefits, how many claims advisors it needs and where, and the costs, and to report results by June 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1448|relating to decedents estates.title: Relating to decedents' estates and other matters involving probate courts
tx:SB 1448|relating to decedents estates.summary: Changes probate procedures, including electronic transfer of case files between counties, how notice is served on heirs who have since died, use of copies of self-proved wills, property listings in estate inventories, and electronic delivery of probate court orders.

tx:HB 3812|relating to health benefit pl.title: Relating to health benefit plan preauthorization requirements for certain health care services and the direction of utilization review by physicians
tx:HB 3812|relating to health benefit pl.summary: Changes insurers' preauthorization exemptions for providers to a yearly review counting requests across all of an insurer's and affiliates' plans, requiring 90% approval and at least five uses of the service, limits rescissions, requires annual reports, and bars administrative-medicine physicians from directing utilization review.

tx:SB 1012|relating to authorizing the s.title: Relating to authorizing the sale or lease by the State of Texas of certain real property located in Austin, Texas
tx:SB 1012|relating to authorizing the s.summary: Directs the General Land Office to sell or lease a state records facility site in Austin once a replacement is built, with proceeds going to state library and archives improvements, and lets the Health and Human Services Commission lease another Austin tract.

tx:SB 906|relating to the authority of t.title: Relating to the authority of the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo to commission peace officers
tx:SB 906|relating to the authority of t.summary: Adds the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo to the federally recognized tribes whose tribal councils may employ and commission peace officers to enforce state law within their reservations.

tx:SB 2986|relating to use by a religiou.title: Relating to use by a religious organization of public school or institution of higher education facilities
tx:SB 2986|relating to use by a religiou.summary: Lets school districts, charter schools and public colleges allow religious groups to use their facilities for worship services if it does not interfere with education, groups pay costs and accept liability for damage, and the same terms apply as for nonreligious renters.

tx:HB 3687|relating to certification req.title: Relating to certification requirements for a fire marshal and any related employee, officer, inspector, and investigator appointed by certain counties and emergency services districts
tx:HB 3687|relating to certification req.summary: Requires fire marshals in counties of 100,000 or more people, and in emergency services districts there, to earn specified state fire certifications within 12 to 24 months of appointment, and a peace officer license when acting as officers.

tx:HB 3960|relating to the effect of cer.title: Relating to the effect of certain misrepresentations on certain insurance policies
tx:HB 3960|relating to the effect of cer.summary: Changes when insurers may deny claims or cancel policies over misstatements in applications, letting life insurers rescind a policy within two years for a material misrepresentation with a premium refund, for policies issued or renewed starting in 2026.

tx:HR 1514|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, H.B. No. 40
tx:HR 1514|suspending limitations on con.summary: Suspends House rules so the conference committee on the business court bill can add text letting civil cases filed before September 1, 2024, move to the business court with the parties' agreement and the court's permission.

tx:SB 2221|relating to the filing of a f.title: Relating to the filing of a fraudulent financing statement in relation to certain secured transactions; authorizing the imposition of a fee
tx:SB 2221|relating to the filing of a f.summary: Raises damages for knowingly filing a fraudulent financing statement to at least $10,000, and lets a person named as debtor file a sworn affidavit, after notice, to have the filing office terminate the statement, subject to court challenge.

tx:SB 1255|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of mold assessors and remediators
tx:SB 1255|relating to the regulation of.summary: Removes mycotoxins from the state's definition of mold, exempts demolition after a fire or disaster from mold assessment and cleanup rules, and ends the exception allowing unlicensed employees to do mold work under a license holder's supervision.

tx:HB 5339|relating to the advancing res.title: Relating to the advancing research for agricultural sustainability and pesticide harm reduction in institutions of higher education
tx:HB 5339|relating to the advancing res.summary: Creates a state grant program for public colleges and universities to research and teach regenerative agriculture, capping any one school at 30% of funds and favoring research done with nonprofits, starting in the 2026-27 academic year.

tx:HB 3334|relating to wildfire preventi.title: Relating to wildfire prevention, mitigation, and response at certain wells under the jurisdiction of the Railroad Commission of Texas; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:HB 3334|relating to wildfire preventi.summary: Requires electrical code inspections and repairs before oil and gas wells with fire- or power-line-related violations in the past five years can change operators, orders power cut to orphaned, inactive or wildfire-noncompliant wells, and allows penalties up to $10,000 per violation.

tx:HB 2559|relating to the imposition by.title: Relating to the imposition by a municipality of a moratorium on property development in certain circumstances
tx:HB 2559|relating to the imposition by.summary: Requires cities to hold two public hearings and pass an ordinance on two readings 28 days apart by a three-fourths vote to impose a development moratorium, ends temporary moratoriums, and limits moratoriums to 90 days, extendable to 180.

tx:HB 2310|relating to developing a stra.title: Relating to developing a strategic plan for the improvement and expansion of early learning and educational opportunities for young children with disabilities
tx:HB 2310|relating to developing a stra.summary: Requires the Texas Education Agency, with the state health and workforce agencies, to publish by September 2026 a strategic plan to include young children with disabilities in prekindergarten, child care and early education programs, updated every four years.

tx:HB 2136|relating to design and use of.title: Relating to design and use of a model criminal citation
tx:HB 2136|relating to design and use of.summary: Requires the state Office of Court Administration to design a plain-language model citation and addendum for fine-only offenses listing court dates, consequences and payment options, and requires law enforcement agencies to adopt matching citations by September 2027.

tx:HB 2147|relating to remotely conducti.title: Relating to remotely conducting depositions, hearings, and other proceedings in juvenile cases
tx:HB 2147|relating to remotely conducti.summary: Lets juvenile courts hold hearings, depositions and other juvenile proceedings remotely by video or teleconference without the parties' consent unless the constitution requires it, and requires each juvenile court judge to submit a remote-proceedings plan to the state court administration office.

tx:HB 809|relating to the execution of a.title: Relating to the execution of a waiver of citation by digitized signature in a suit for the dissolution of a marriage
tx:HB 809|relating to the execution of a.summary: Lets a spouse sign a waiver of formal notice in a divorce case with a digitized signature, and allows electronic notarization of signatures in marriage-related family court cases as well as parent-child cases.

tx:SB 1939|relating to the ship channel.title: Relating to the ship channel improvement revolving fund
tx:SB 1939|relating to the ship channel.summary: Exempts the ship channel improvement revolving fund from the rule that moves interest earned on certain dedicated state accounts into the general revenue fund, so the fund's interest is no longer redirected.

tx:HB 2159|relating to the capacity of a.title: Relating to the capacity of a minor to consent to certain treatment for the minor or the minor's child
tx:HB 2159|relating to the capacity of a.summary: Lets an unmarried minor who has custody of their own child consent to medical, dental, psychological and surgical treatment both for themselves and, separately, for their child.

tx:SB 2964|relating to an opportunity to.title: Relating to an opportunity to correct certain defects in an early voting ballot voted by mail
tx:SB 2964|relating to an opportunity to.summary: Requires early voting clerks, within two days of finding a defect in a returned mail-ballot envelope, to send the voter a notice and state correction form and flag it in the online tracker, letting the voter fix the defect or cancel the mail-ballot request.

tx:HB 4614|relating to the licensing and.title: Relating to the licensing and regulation of state correctional officers; requiring an occupational license
tx:HB 4614|relating to the licensing and.summary: Requires Texas prison correctional officers, starting September 1, 2027, to hold a Texas Commission on Law Enforcement license requiring at least 240 training hours, an exam, age 18 and a high school diploma or equivalent; officers already permanently employed then are exempt and can obtain licenses by applying beforehand.

tx:HB 186|relating to prohibiting use of.title: Relating to prohibiting use of social media platforms by children
tx:HB 186|relating to prohibiting use of.summary: Bars children under 18 from holding social media accounts starting in 2026, requires platforms to verify users' ages and delete the verification data, requires deleting a child's account within 10 days of a parent's request, and treats violations as deceptive trade practices.

tx:HCR 54|granting the legislature permi.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning on Wednesday, January 29, 2025, and ending on Tuesday, February 4, 2025
tx:HCR 54|granting the legislature permi.summary: Grants each chamber of the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days between January 29 and February 4, 2025.

tx:HB 3000|relating to a grant program t.title: Relating to a grant program to provide financial assistance to qualified ambulance service providers in certain rural counties
tx:HB 3000|relating to a grant program t.summary: Creates a state comptroller grant program to help counties of 68,750 people or fewer buy ambulances for rural ambulance providers, with grants of up to $500,000 for counties under 10,000 people and up to $350,000 for other qualifying counties.

tx:HB 4783|relating to a report on gover.title: Relating to a report on governmental opioid antagonist programs to reverse and prevent opioid overdoses
tx:HB 4783|relating to a report on gover.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to report to state leaders every two years on distribution of opioid overdose-reversal drugs, including a needs assessment, a statewide supply goal, funding sources, distribution strategies and recommendations for high-risk groups.

tx:HB 2458|relating to a defense to pros.title: Relating to a defense to prosecution for the offense of aggravated assault
tx:HB 2458|relating to a defense to pros.summary: Creates a defense to an aggravated assault charge for a person who threatened someone by displaying a deadly weapon, if the threat was legally justified and the person reasonably believed it was immediately necessary to defend against unlawful or deadly force.

tx:SB 482|relating to increasing the cri.title: Relating to increasing the criminal penalties for the offenses of assault and harassment committed against certain employees or agents of a utility
tx:SB 482|relating to increasing the cri.summary: Raises the penalty for assaulting an on-duty utility employee or agent to a third-degree felony and for harassing one to a Class A misdemeanor, and makes it a crime to interfere with such workers while they perform their duties.

tx:HB 745|relating to an exemption from.title: Relating to an exemption from jury service for certain crime victims or close relatives of deceased crime victims
tx:HB 745|relating to an exemption from.summary: Lets crime victims, and close relatives of deceased victims, who testified in a court proceeding about the crime claim an exemption from jury service if attending court would cause them severe anxiety or post-traumatic stress.

tx:SB 2514|relating to establishing the.title: Relating to establishing the hostile foreign adversaries unit at the Department of Public Safety and training, prohibitions, and reporting requirements designed to combat foreign influence and foreign adversary operations; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 2514|relating to establishing the.summary: Creates a hostile foreign adversaries unit in the Department of Public Safety; bars state and local government employees and volunteers from accepting travel or gifts paid by foreign adversaries and requires them to report contacts within 30 days, making violations a state jail felony.

tx:SB 1194|relating to creating the cent.title: Relating to creating the Central Texas Water Alliance; providing authority to issue bonds; granting the power of eminent domain; providing authority to impose fees
tx:SB 1194|relating to creating the cent.summary: Creates the Central Texas Water Alliance of Bell and McLennan counties and two water districts to supply wholesale water and wastewater services, letting it issue bonds, charge fees and use eminent domain except to acquire water rights; bars it from levying property taxes.

tx:HB 3477|relating to the expunction of.title: Relating to the expunction of all records and files related to a finding of criminal contempt by a court
tx:HB 3477|relating to the expunction of.summary: Lets a person found in criminal contempt of court have all related records expunged once at least two years have passed, by filing a petition with the court that held them in contempt.

tx:HB 2546|relating to vehicles eligible.title: Relating to vehicles eligible for replacement under the clean school bus program
tx:HB 2546|relating to vehicles eligible.summary: Expands the state clean school bus program so that school buses from model year 2010 or earlier, rather than 2006 or earlier, are eligible for replacement.

tx:HB 3611|relating to the civil penalty.title: Relating to the civil penalty for certain signs placed on the right-of-way of a public road
tx:HB 3611|relating to the civil penalty.summary: Sets maximum civil penalties for unauthorized signs on public road rights-of-way at $1,000, $2,500 and $5,000 for first, second and later violations, replacing a $500 to $1,000 penalty chargeable per day, requires a removal warning before a first penalty, and extends liability to advertisers on such signs.

tx:HB 1943|relating to compensation for.title: Relating to compensation for the members of the Winkler County Juvenile Board
tx:HB 1943|relating to compensation for.summary: Requires the Winkler County commissioners court to pay all juvenile board members additional yearly compensation, in an amount it sets, from the county general fund, replacing optional payments of $1,200 to the board chair and up to $1,200 to other members.

tx:HB 145|relating to risk mitigation pl.title: Relating to risk mitigation planning and associated liability for providers of electric service
tx:HB 145|relating to risk mitigation pl.summary: Requires electric utilities and cooperatives with lines in high wildfire-risk areas to file wildfire mitigation plans with state regulators, shields those following approved plans from wildfire damage liability unless negligent, and lets utilities self-insure against wildfire liability.

tx:HB 3057|relating to network standards.title: Relating to network standards for Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell (CAR T) therapy
tx:HB 3057|relating to network standards.summary: Requires health plans that cover CAR T-cell therapy to cover it, when medically necessary, at any FDA-certified treatment facility already in the plan's network for other services, for plans issued or renewed starting in 2026; excludes Medicaid and CHIP.

tx:HB 2598|relating to a school psycholo.title: Relating to a school psychologist licensed under the Occupations Code
tx:HB 2598|relating to a school psycholo.summary: Renames the licensed profession of "licensed specialist in school psychology" to "school psychologist" throughout state education, government and occupational licensing laws.

tx:SB 1555|relating to a grant program t.title: Relating to a grant program to fund certain railroad grade separation projects
tx:SB 1555|relating to a grant program t.summary: Creates a Texas Department of Transportation grant program for local governments to separate railroad crossings from roads and pedestrian paths off the state highway system, requiring at least 10% non-state funding and barring use of state highway fund money.

tx:HB 1576|relating to a grant program f.title: Relating to a grant program for hurricane and windstorm loss mitigation for single-family residential property
tx:HB 1576|relating to a grant program f.summary: Creates a state grant program to help homeowners retrofit their single-family or manufactured homes against hurricanes and windstorms, and requires home insurers to give actuarially justified premium discounts for homes certified as meeting program standards, both only if the legislature funds the grants.

tx:HB 5333|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of the STEM Excellence Graduate Fellowship Program
tx:HB 5333|relating to the establishment.summary: Creates a state merit-based fellowship for U.S. citizen doctoral students in science, technology, engineering and math research programs at Texas public universities, funded by appropriations and donations, for up to five years per student.

tx:HB 647|relating to the removal of cer.title: Relating to the removal of certain restrictions imposed on driver's licenses; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 647|relating to the removal of cer.summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety, if funded, to remove the corrective-lens restriction from a driver's license for a fee and mail a new license when a physician or optometrist certifies the holder's vision was surgically corrected; registered sex offenders cannot get the new license by mail.

tx:HB 3159|relating to a severance tax e.title: Relating to a severance tax exemption for oil and gas produced from certain restimulation wells; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 3159|relating to a severance tax e.summary: Exempts oil and gas from re-fractured, previously inactive wells from state severance taxes for up to 36 months or until savings reach the lesser of treatment costs or $750,000, starting in 2026, with civil penalties for knowingly false claims.

tx:SB 111|relating to reporting by schoo.title: Relating to reporting by school districts regarding special education legal proceedings in which a certain amount of legal fees has been incurred by the district
tx:SB 111|relating to reporting by schoo.summary: Requires school districts to post online and report to the Texas Education Agency each month every ongoing special education due process case in which their legal fees exceed $10,000, with the subject and fees to date; the agency publishes the totals.

tx:SB 1643|relating to prior approval of.title: Relating to prior approval of certain property and casualty insurance rate increases or decreases
tx:SB 1643|relating to prior approval of.summary: Requires property and auto insurers to get state approval before using rates that rise or fall more than 10% from their current filed rates, and lowers from 12.5% to 10% the increase that blocks automatic approval of a rate filing.

tx:SB 1316|relating to a prohibition on.title: Relating to a prohibition on e-cigarette advertising in certain locations
tx:SB 1316|relating to a prohibition on.summary: Extends the ban on cigarette and tobacco advertising signs within 1,000 feet of a church or school to cover e-cigarette advertising.

tx:SB 1313|relating to prohibited signs.title: Relating to prohibited signs, logos, and designs in advertising or marketing cigarettes, e-cigarettes, or other tobacco products; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 1313|relating to prohibited signs.summary: Makes it a Class B misdemeanor for a retailer to use signs, logos or designs in marketing or selling cigarettes, e-cigarettes or tobacco products that show cartoon characters aimed at children, mimic products marketed to minors, show celebrities, or resemble foods such as candy or juice.

tx:SB 1527|relating to the administratio.title: Relating to the administration of, contributions to, and benefits under the public retirement systems for police and firefighters in certain municipalities
tx:SB 1527|relating to the administratio.summary: Moves Dallas's city contributions to its police and fire pension system to an actuarially determined rate phased in over five years, requires city council and pension board approval of benefit increases, settlements or assumption changes that raise liabilities, and voids the board's own funding plan.

tx:HB 3358|relating to the definition of.title: Relating to the definition of an emergency service provider for purposes of critical incident stress management and crisis response services
tx:HB 3358|relating to the definition of.summary: Expands who counts as an emergency service provider eligible for critical incident stress management and crisis response services to include people providing post-emergency services, prosecutors' attorneys, investigators and staff, and justices of the peace and justice court staff.

tx:SJR 34|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment affirming the rights and responsibilities of parents
tx:SJR 34|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, affirming that parents have the responsibility to nurture and protect their children and a fundamental right to exercise care, custody and control of them, including decisions about their upbringing.

tx:HCR 169|instructing the enrolling cle.title: Instructing the enrolling clerk of the senate to make corrections in S.B. No. 1
tx:HCR 169|instructing the enrolling cle.summary: Directs the enrolling clerk to fix a technical error in the state budget bill by rewording a budget provision whose changes depend on enactment of a separate bill on judicial discipline, judicial pay and judicial retirement benefits.

tx:HB 361|relating to the appraisal of a.title: Relating to the appraisal of a residence homestead for ad valorem tax purposes
tx:HB 361|relating to the appraisal of a.summary: Bars chief appraisers in counties of more than 50,000 people from using a home sale as a comparable sale when valuing a homestead unless the sold home also had a homestead exemption and is in the same neighborhood, starting with the 2026 tax year.

tx:SB 1267|relating to certificates of n.title: Relating to certificates of number and certificates of title issued by and records kept by the Parks and Wildlife Department; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 1267|relating to certificates of n.summary: Overhauls boat title and registration rules: cuts new owners' deadline to apply for a title from 45 to 20 days, allows electronic registration certificates, and requires a "Hull Damaged" title brand before damaged boats are sold, making knowing failure a crime.

tx:HB 3788|relating to the operations of.title: Relating to the operations of municipal hospital authorities
tx:HB 3788|relating to the operations of.summary: Changes rules for municipal hospital authorities: lets boards set how directors are chosen, bars authority employees from serving as directors, lets authorities without a hospital fund clinics, fitness centers, offices and other health initiatives, and lets them issue revenue bonds for those purposes.

tx:SB 1964|relating to the regulation an.title: Relating to the regulation and use of artificial intelligence systems and the management of data by governmental entities
tx:SB 1964|relating to the regulation an.summary: Requires the state technology agency to set an artificial intelligence code of ethics and risk standards that state agencies and local governments must adopt, requires agencies to inventory their AI systems, and creates an AI advisory board, training materials and a testing sandbox program.

tx:HB 5081|relating to the protection of.title: Relating to the protection of personal identifying information of certain persons in the judicial system; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 5081|relating to the protection of.summary: Lets judges, court clerks and judicial-branch employees demand that people and data brokers stop selling or posting their home addresses, phone numbers, family details and other personal information online, and makes posting it to threaten harm, or failing to remove it within 10 business days, a misdemeanor.

tx:HB 851|relating to the determination.title: Relating to the determination and reporting of the number of residence homesteads of certain property owners for which the owner is receiving certain ad valorem tax benefits
tx:HB 851|relating to the determination.summary: Requires appraisal districts to count, for each school district, homesteads with a frozen school-tax ceiling and homesteads whose owners deferred or delayed collection of property taxes, and requires the comptroller to report the totals to legislators by November 1 each year without personal information.

tx:HB 14|relating to funding mechanisms.title: Relating to funding mechanisms within the Office of the Governor and Texas Public Utility Commission to support the deployment of advanced nuclear reactors in this state
tx:HB 14|relating to funding mechanisms.summary: Creates a Texas Advanced Nuclear Energy Office in the governor's office, set to end in 2035 unless renewed, and a fund for grants reimbursing costs of developing, building and connecting advanced nuclear reactors and their supply chains, plus a nuclear permitting coordinator.

tx:SB 2217|relating to certain election.title: Relating to certain election practices and procedures
tx:SB 2217|relating to certain election.summary: Requires counties to reconcile votes cast with voters checked in at each polling place within 30 days and post the results online, requires ballot-count reports from scanners and electronic poll books, and lets voters who moved within their county vote in their new precinct.

tx:HB 3486|relating to a reduction in th.title: Relating to a reduction in the amount of sales and use tax collections that the owners of restaurants that purchase Texas farm-raised oysters are required to remit to the comptroller of public accounts
tx:HB 3486|relating to a reduction in th.summary: Lets restaurant owners deduct $5 from their taxable sales for every 100 Texas farm-raised oysters they buy to serve, lowering the sales tax they owe, starting October 1, 2025.

tx:HB 1393|relating to daylight saving t.title: Relating to daylight saving time
tx:HB 1393|relating to daylight saving t.summary: Puts Texas on year-round daylight saving time, called Texas Time, in both its central and mountain time zones, but only if Congress passes a law allowing it.

tx:HB 1893|relating to the disclosure un.title: Relating to the disclosure under the public information law of a motor vehicle license plate number captured in a video recording obtained or maintained by a law enforcement agency
tx:HB 1893|relating to the disclosure un.summary: Makes license plate numbers seen or heard in police video recordings releasable under the public information law, so agencies need not redact them before release, while letting agencies still claim other exceptions to disclosure.

tx:SB 719|relating to the collection of.title: Relating to the collection of information on available beds at inpatient mental health facilities providing acute psychiatric treatment
tx:SB 719|relating to the collection of.summary: Requires hospitals to report inpatient psychiatric bed counts by age and by whether beds are in service, and directs the Health and Human Services Commission to study current psychiatric bed capacity and 10-year bed and workforce needs, reporting by December 1, 2026.

tx:SB 2497|relating to the installation.title: Relating to the installation of a filtration system by certain public drinking water supply systems
tx:SB 2497|relating to the installation.summary: Lets the state environmental agency order small groundwater-supplied public water systems with fewer than 100 connections to install treatment such as filtration if they repeatedly exceed contaminant limits, draw multiple substantiated complaints in a year, and, where applicable, can do so at reasonable cost.

tx:SB 1802|relating to a landlord s duty.title: Relating to a landlord's duty to repair or remedy certain conditions
tx:SB 1802|relating to a landlord s duty.summary: Requires landlords, after tenant notice, to repair ramps, elevators and handrails on the route to or inside a tenant's home, gives tenants existing repair remedies if they do not, and lets landlords offer free alternative housing until repairs are made.

tx:SB 2605|relating to the formation of.title: Relating to the formation of a municipal housing authority asset commission by certain municipal housing authorities
tx:SB 2605|relating to the formation of.summary: Lets municipal housing authorities in large border cities create a five-member asset commission of real estate, finance and housing experts that must approve the authority's property deals over $100,000 and any bond financing tied to its assets.

tx:SB 2846|relating to the control of di.title: Relating to the control of disease in wildlife; creating criminal offenses; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:SB 2846|relating to the control of di.summary: Gives the Parks and Wildlife Department power to control wildlife diseases, including quarantining areas, ranches or deer breeding facilities and restricting animal movement, makes mishandling infected wildlife or breaking a quarantine a misdemeanor, and allows administrative fines up to $5,000 a day.

tx:SB 1757|relating to the operation of.title: Relating to the operation of rock crushing facilities
tx:SB 1757|relating to the operation of.summary: Requires the state environmental agency to issue a standard air permit for rock crushing facilities that requires a year of monitoring, emergency notice plans for neighbors, best practices and a post-mining land use plan, with published notice, a local public meeting and public comment before approval.

tx:SB 1152|relating to creating the crim.title: Relating to creating the criminal offense of continuous manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance
tx:SB 1152|relating to creating the crim.summary: Creates the crime of continuous manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance, a third-degree felony, for committing two or more drug manufacturing or delivery offenses within 12 months; jurors need not agree on which specific acts or dates occurred.

tx:SB 1750|relating to instructional fac.title: Relating to instructional facilities funding for certain open-enrollment charter schools
tx:SB 1750|relating to instructional fac.summary: Replaces a $60 million cap on charter school facilities funding with a per-student formula tied to the basic allotment, requires schools to certify that no insiders or their relatives profit from school real estate deals, and lets the funds pay for buses, technology, security, arts and athletic facilities.

tx:SB 1208|relating to increasing the cr.title: Relating to increasing the criminal penalty for the offense of interference with public duties
tx:SB 1208|relating to increasing the cr.summary: Raises the offense of interfering with public servants, such as police officers, performing their duties from a Class B misdemeanor to a state jail felony, for offenses committed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 472|relating to the right of the c.title: Relating to the right of the chief appraiser of an appraisal district, the appraisal district, or the appraisal review board of the appraisal district to bring certain claims in an appeal of an order of the appraisal review board
tx:SB 472|relating to the right of the c.summary: Repeals a chief appraiser's right to appeal appraisal review board decisions to court and bars appraisal districts, chief appraisers and review boards from filing counterclaims in property tax appeals, for appeals filed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 990|relating to increasing the pun.title: Relating to increasing the punishment for certain conduct constituting the offense of murder
tx:SB 990|relating to increasing the pun.summary: Repeals Code of Criminal Procedure Article 37.071, Section 1(b), which barred a death sentence for certain capital murder convictions, so those defendants can face the death penalty for offenses committed on or after September 1, 2025.

tx:HB 2512|relating to release of an are.title: Relating to release of an area from a municipality's extraterritorial jurisdiction by petition or election
tx:HB 2512|relating to release of an are.summary: Bars release from the extraterritorial jurisdiction of certain large multi-county cities for land under active development agreements, lots under 12 acres petitioned alone, and single lots in larger subdivisions; requires cities to give notice of release-election petitions and lets landowners opt to stay.

tx:HB 3748|relating to reimbursing emplo.title: Relating to reimbursing employees of the Department of Family and Protective Services for loss of or damage to personal property
tx:HB 3748|relating to reimbursing emplo.summary: Lets the Department of Family and Protective Services use existing resources to reimburse current and former employees for personal property lost or damaged while performing their job duties.

tx:SB 1171|relating to compensation leav.title: Relating to compensation, leave, and physical fitness programs and standards for certain employees of the office of inspector general of the Texas Juvenile Justice Department
tx:SB 1171|relating to compensation leav.summary: Requires hazardous duty pay for investigators, security officers and apprehension specialists in the juvenile justice department's inspector general office, pays its commissioned peace officers on the state's law enforcement salary schedule, and extends injury leave for peace officers to them.

tx:HB 1089|relating to creation of the g.title: Relating to creation of the gulf coast protection account to be administered by the General Land Office
tx:HB 1089|relating to creation of the g.summary: Creates a gulf coast protection account, run by the General Land Office and funded by gifts, grants and legislative appropriations, to pay the state's share of coastal storm protection projects planned with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

tx:SB 5|relating to the creation of the.title: Relating to the creation of the Dementia Prevention and Research Institute of Texas
tx:SB 5|relating to the creation of the.summary: Creates the Dementia Prevention and Research Institute of Texas, overseen by a nine-member appointed committee, to award grants for research, facilities and prevention programs on dementia, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, if voters approve a constitutional amendment moving $3 billion into a research fund.

tx:HB 3488|relating to representation fo.title: Relating to representation for an indigent person subject to a civil commitment proceeding
tx:HB 3488|relating to representation fo.summary: Shifts the duty to represent people who cannot afford a lawyer in civil commitment proceedings for sexually violent predators from the Office of State Counsel for Offenders to the Texas Board of Criminal Justice, with courts appointing other counsel if the board cannot.

tx:SB 1202|relating to third party revie.title: Relating to third-party review of property development documents and inspections of improvements related to those documents, including home backup power installations
tx:SB 1202|relating to third party revie.summary: Lets qualified third parties, instead of local officials, review plans for and inspect home backup power installations; lets work begin once approval notice is filed; requires local permits within three business days; and bars local fees when required fee schedules are not posted.

tx:HB 2713|relating to the repeal of a m.title: Relating to the repeal of a municipal civil service system for firefighters and police officers in certain municipalities
tx:HB 2713|relating to the repeal of a m.summary: Limits voter petitions to repeal a city's civil service system for police officers and firefighters to cities under 50,000 people, down from 950,000, for petitions where an election has not yet been ordered.

tx:SB 1706|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the governing board of a state governmental body to conduct a closed meeting to deliberate an issue involving certain defense, military, or aerospace issues
tx:SB 1706|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets the governing boards of state government bodies hold closed meetings to deliberate certain defense, military or aerospace issues.

tx:HB 4995|relating to the carrying of h.title: Relating to the carrying of handguns by tactical medical professionals while on duty providing support to tactical units of law enforcement agencies
tx:HB 4995|relating to the carrying of h.summary: Lets licensed tactical medical professionals who support police tactical units carry handguns on duty where carrying is otherwise barred, if they complete a state-approved training course renewed yearly, and shields governments from liability when such personnel fire a handgun.

tx:SCR 3|designating bandera as the offi.title: Designating Bandera as the official Cowboy Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:SCR 3|designating bandera as the offi.summary: Designates Bandera as the official Cowboy Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 1500|relating to the continuation.title: Relating to the continuation and functions of the Department of Information Resources, including the composition of the governing body of the department
tx:HB 1500|relating to the continuation.summary: Continues the Department of Information Resources until 2037, replaces rotating agency-head board members with four governor-appointed nonvoting agency employees, creates a technology procurement certification course and advisory committees, and requires a single online listing of state grant opportunities.

tx:HB 2078|relating to the joint plannin.title: Relating to the joint planning of desired future conditions in groundwater management areas
tx:HB 2078|relating to the joint plannin.summary: Requires groundwater districts planning jointly to set desired aquifer conditions for roughly 50-year planning periods with interim checkpoints of up to 10 years, and to explain in plain language how each district is tracking and meeting those goals.

tx:SB 1248|relating to the disclosure of.title: Relating to the disclosure of certain harvest report information submitted to the Parks and Wildlife Department
tx:SB 1248|relating to the disclosure of.summary: Makes hunting and fishing harvest reports submitted to the Parks and Wildlife Department, including harvest locations, confidential and exempt from public records law, while allowing anonymous statistics and sharing with the reporter, law enforcement and other agencies.

tx:HB 3849|relating to the program categ.title: Relating to the program categories in the unified transportation program
tx:HB 3849|relating to the program categ.summary: Requires the state's transportation funding program to include a category for border security and international trade corridor projects, such as easing congestion within 60 miles of border crossings, once the legislature specifically funds it.

tx:HCR 75|designating hemphill as the of.title: Designating Hemphill as the official Bass Fishing Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 75|designating hemphill as the of.summary: Designates Hemphill as the official Bass Fishing Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:SJR 37|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment clarifying that a voter must be a United States citizen
tx:SJR 37|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, stating that people who are not U.S. citizens may not vote in Texas.

tx:SB 914|relating to authorizing certai.title: Relating to authorizing certain cities to change the date on which their general election for officers is held
tx:SB 914|relating to authorizing certai.summary: Lets certain small cities with council-manager governments and a certain county along the San Jacinto River move their general elections for officers to the November uniform election date, if they act by the end of 2026.

tx:HCR 86|designating denton as the offi.title: Designating Denton as the official Halloween Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 86|designating denton as the offi.summary: Designates Denton as the official Halloween Capital of Texas for 10 years, replacing its designation as the Redbud Capital of Texas.

tx:HB 272|relating to the prosecution of.title: Relating to the prosecution of the offense of fraudulent use or possession of credit card or debit card information
tx:HB 272|relating to the prosecution of.summary: Lets prosecutors bring charges for fraudulent use or possession of credit or debit card information in the county where any victim lives, and removes the need to prove intent to defraud a particular person.

tx:HB 50|relating to informed consent fo.title: Relating to informed consent for certain screening tests
tx:HB 50|relating to informed consent fo.summary: Requires health care providers who draw blood to screen for sexually transmitted diseases to also test it for HIV unless the patient opts out, starting January 2026, and to give patients who test positive information on available services.

tx:HB 3993|relating to taxes imposed on.title: Relating to taxes imposed on vinous liquor
tx:HB 3993|relating to taxes imposed on.summary: Raises the alcohol content limit for the lower 20.4-cents-per-gallon wine tax from 14% to 16%, so the 40.8-cent rate applies only to wine above 16% alcohol.

tx:SCR 16|granting the legislature permi.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning Thursday, February 20, 2025, and ending Tuesday, February 25, 2025
tx:SCR 16|granting the legislature permi.summary: Gives each chamber of the Legislature the other's consent to adjourn for more than three days between Thursday, February 20, and Tuesday, February 25, 2025, as the state constitution requires.

tx:SB 2569|relating to the reporting req.title: Relating to the reporting requirement for certain law enforcement agencies regarding the agencies' use or operation of an unmanned aircraft
tx:SB 2569|relating to the reporting req.summary: Requires state law enforcement agencies, and local agencies in places over 150,000 people, to post their biennial drone-use reports on their public websites instead of sending written reports to the governor, lieutenant governor and every legislator.

tx:HB 3689|relating to funding of excess.title: Relating to funding of excess losses and operating expenses of the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association; authorizing an assessment; authorizing a surcharge
tx:HB 3689|relating to funding of excess.summary: Replaces bond financing for Texas Windstorm Insurance Association losses after 2025 with loans from the state's rainy day fund, up to $500 million before and $1 billion after a disaster, repaid by surcharges on property insurance policies statewide, then up to $1 billion in insurer assessments.

tx:HB 3918|relating to information on lo.title: Relating to information on local regulations governing the placement of political signs in a municipality
tx:HB 3918|relating to information on lo.summary: Requires cities to post their rules on where political signs may be placed, plus a map of restricted areas, on their websites, and to send copies to city candidates, local election officials and county political party chairs.

tx:SB 519|relating to the creation of a.title: Relating to the creation of a grant program to promote educational engagement with Texas history
