tx:SB 519|relating to the creation of a.summary: Creates a Texas Historical Commission program awarding annual grants to nonprofits that host a statewide Texas history competition for students and publish Texas history works by students or faculty, with grant recipients bound by performance contracts.

tx:HB 46|relating to the medical use of.title: Relating to the medical use of low-THC cannabis under and the administration of the Texas Compassionate-Use Program
tx:HB 46|relating to the medical use of.summary: Expands the state's medical cannabis program to patients with chronic pain, traumatic brain injury, Crohn's disease or terminal illness, sets a 10-milligram THC limit per dose, allows prescribed vaping, and requires licensing at least 12 new dispensing organizations by April 2026.

tx:HB 3157|relating to interim rates cha.title: Relating to interim rates charged by electric utilities during a rate suspension period
tx:HB 3157|relating to interim rates cha.summary: Requires electric utilities operating only inside the main state grid to start charging interim rates 90 days after filing for a rate change that regulators suspend, with refunds plus interest if final rates are lower; regulators may modify or deny interim rates in exigent circumstances.

tx:SB 3034|relating to the designation o.title: Relating to the designation of a portion of State Highway 249 in Grimes and Montgomery Counties as the Doug Pitcock Aggie Expressway
tx:SB 3034|relating to the designation o.summary: Names the stretch of State Highway 249 in Grimes and Montgomery counties between State Highway 105 and Farm-to-Market Road 1774 the Doug Pitcock Aggie Expressway, with markers to be erected if donated funds cover the cost.

tx:SB 2237|relating to severance pay for.title: Relating to severance pay for certain political subdivision employees
tx:SB 2237|relating to severance pay for.summary: Limits severance pay from tax revenue for top local government executives, including school superintendents and charter school chiefs, to 20 weeks of pay, bars severance for those fired for misconduct, and requires severance agreements to be posted online.

tx:HB 170|relating to civil liability ar.title: Relating to civil liability arising out of justified uses of or threats to use force or deadly force
tx:HB 170|relating to civil liability ar.summary: Shields people from civil lawsuits over legally justified threats of force, presumes their force was justified when a grand jury declines to indict or criminal charges end in acquittal or dismissal, and lets those found immune recover legal fees and lost income.

tx:HB 125|relating to the creation of th.title: Relating to the creation of the Tarleton State University College of Osteopathic Medicine
tx:HB 125|relating to the creation of th.summary: Creates a College of Osteopathic Medicine at Tarleton State University under the Texas A&M University System and makes it eligible for money from the state's permanent health fund for higher education.

tx:SJR 3|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the establishment of the Dementia Prevention and Research Institute of Texas, establishing the Dementia Prevention and Research Fund to provide money for research on and prevention and treatment of dementia, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related disorders in this state, and transferring to that fund $3 billion from state general revenue
tx:SJR 3|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, creating a Dementia Prevention and Research Institute and moving $3 billion from general revenue into a fund for dementia, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's research grants, with spending capped at $300 million a year.

tx:HCR 157|designating rockport as the o.title: Designating Rockport as the official Redfish Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 157|designating rockport as the o.summary: Designates Rockport as the official Redfish Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 1532|relating to the creation of t.title: Relating to the creation of the Lake Houston Dredging and Maintenance District; providing the authority to issue bonds
tx:HB 1532|relating to the creation of t.summary: Creates the Lake Houston Dredging and Maintenance District, with a board appointed by Houston city officials and the Harris County Flood Control District, allowed to issue bonds but barred from levying taxes or fees or using eminent domain.

tx:HB 4213|relating to the accrual of in.title: Relating to the accrual of interest on overdue child support
tx:HB 4213|relating to the accrual of in.summary: Replaces the 6% simple interest rate on overdue child support and child support judgments with the state's standard court-judgment interest rate, for support coming due or judgments issued on or after January 1, 2026.

tx:SCR 14|granting the legislature permi.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning Thursday, February 13, 2025, and ending Tuesday, February 18, 2025
tx:SCR 14|granting the legislature permi.summary: Gives each chamber of the Legislature the other's consent to adjourn for more than three days between Thursday, February 13, and Tuesday, February 18, 2025, as the state constitution requires.

tx:HB 4765|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of code enforcement officers and code enforcement officers in training
tx:HB 4765|relating to the regulation of.summary: Revises state registration of code enforcement officers, limiting the requirement to individuals, dropping exam and registration fees in favor of an application fee, setting two-year renewal with continuing education, and allowing registration of officers licensed in states with similar standards.

tx:HB 5431|relating to the exclusion of.title: Relating to the exclusion of at-large and mayoral seats from the requirement of re-election following apportionment
tx:HB 5431|relating to the exclusion of.summary: Exempts at-large city council seats and mayors from having to stand for election after redistricting unless their terms would otherwise expire.

tx:HB 5331|relating to the enforceabilit.title: Relating to the enforceability of certain state agency and local government contract language regarding required security incident notifications
tx:HB 5331|relating to the enforceabilit.summary: Voids contract terms, including in cybersecurity insurance contracts, that bar or restrict state agencies and local governments from making legally required security incident notifications, and states that this clarifies existing law.

tx:HB 932|relating to the occupational t.title: Relating to the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact; authorizing fees
tx:HB 932|relating to the occupational t.summary: Enters Texas into the Occupational Therapy Licensure Compact, letting occupational therapists and assistants licensed in member states practice across them, with provisions for military families, a multistate commission funded by assessments and fees, and a shared licensing database.

tx:HB 4230|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of a hike and bike trail to be known as the Bicentennial Trail
tx:HB 4230|relating to the establishment.summary: Directs the General Land Office to coordinate a hike and bike trail network linking the Alamo to the State Capitol, with connections to four major springs, by 2036, without using eminent domain to acquire land.

tx:HCR 155|designating san antonio as mi.title: Designating San Antonio as Military City Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 155|designating san antonio as mi.summary: Designates San Antonio as Military City Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 5606|relating to a sick day pool o.title: Relating to a sick day pool of school employees in the state
tx:HB 5606|relating to a sick day pool o.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to create a pool for sick leave left by retiring employees, which other employees who have used up their own sick leave may draw on, unless it conflicts with a policy adopted before September 1, 2025.

tx:SB 1006|relating to declination cance.title: Relating to declination, cancellation, or nonrenewal of insurance policies
tx:SB 1006|relating to declination cance.summary: Requires insurers to give written reasons whenever they decline, cancel or refuse to renew a policy, and to file quarterly reports by zip code, posted online, disclosing decisions based on environmental, social or governance scores or diversity, equity and inclusion factors.

tx:SB 2196|relating to the period during.title: Relating to the period during which an order for emergency protection remains in effect
tx:SB 2196|relating to the period during.summary: Lengthens emergency protective orders that magistrates issue after certain arrests to last 61 to 91 days, from 31 to 61, and to 91 to 121 days, from 61 to 91, when a deadly weapon was used.

tx:HB 4668|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of the Public Utility Commission of Texas to retain assistance for regional proceedings affecting certain electric utilities and consumers
tx:HB 4668|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets the Public Utility Commission hire consultants, auditors, engineers or attorneys to represent it before regional grid organizations in matters affecting electric utilities' rates. The utility involved pays up to $1.5 million a year and may recover the cost from customers through an annual rider.

tx:HB 1607|relating to license plates an.title: Relating to license plates and license plate windshield insignia issued for and displayed on a vehicle; authorizing a fee; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 1607|relating to license plates an.summary: Lets passenger cars and light trucks built without a front license plate mount display only a rear plate plus a windshield sticker, for a fee, if the driver carries the unmounted front plate and shows it to police on request; failing to do so is an offense.

tx:SB 1730|relating to the recovery of d.title: Relating to the recovery of damages for injuries arising out of certain uses of force or deadly force
tx:SB 1730|relating to the recovery of d.summary: Bars lawsuits for injury or death caused by a person's use of force or deadly force when a grand jury declines to indict, criminal charges are dismissed, or the person is acquitted, and makes the barred claimant pay the defendant's court costs and attorney's fees.

tx:HB 3133|relating to user reports of e.title: Relating to user reports of explicit deep fake material on social media platforms
tx:HB 3133|relating to user reports of e.summary: Requires social media platforms to let users report sexually explicit deep fake images, immediately acknowledge reports, remove the reported material and known copies, update the user within seven days, and block reposting of confirmed material; violations become deceptive trade practices.

tx:HB 2775|relating to the i 27 advisory.title: Relating to the I-27 Advisory Committee
tx:HB 2775|relating to the i 27 advisory.summary: Expands the I-27 Advisory Committee by adding representatives of Ector and Schleicher counties and the city of Odessa, raising county members from 10 to 12 and city members from seven to eight.

tx:HB 594|relating to the positions desi.title: Relating to the positions designated as exempt from sheriff's department civil service systems in certain counties
tx:HB 594|relating to the positions desi.summary: Lets sheriffs in counties of more than 2 million and up to 3.3 million people exempt up to 18 positions from the department's civil service system, instead of 10; sheriffs in counties of 2 million or fewer keep the 10-position limit.

tx:HB 1629|relating to fireworks sales t.title: Relating to fireworks sales to the public by retail fireworks permit holders in certain counties
tx:HB 1629|relating to fireworks sales t.summary: Lets retail fireworks sellers in counties that approve it sell fireworks from May 1 through May 5 at locations up to 150 miles from the Texas-Mexico border, up from 100 miles.

tx:SB 305|relating to the criminal offen.title: Relating to the criminal offense of passing certain vehicles on a highway
tx:SB 305|relating to the criminal offen.summary: Adds animal control vehicles removing animals or carcasses from roads, and local parking enforcement vehicles, to the vehicles drivers must move over for or slow down when passing while those vehicles display warning lights.

tx:HB 4763|relating to reports by certai.title: Relating to reports by certain public institutions of higher education on fraud, waste, and abuse involving state resources
tx:HB 4763|relating to reports by certai.summary: Requires public colleges and universities that run a system for reporting suspected fraud, waste or abuse of state resources to send each report to the state auditor within two business days of receiving it.

tx:HCR 108|urging the u s department of.title: Urging the U.S. Department of Commerce to maintain the Tomato Suspension Agreement
tx:HCR 108|urging the u s department of.summary: Urges the U.S. Department of Commerce to keep the Tomato Suspension Agreement with Mexican tomato producers and exporters, which sets minimum prices for imported Mexican tomatoes in place of a 17.09 percent duty.

tx:HCR 135|designating slaton as the off.title: Designating Slaton as the official Banana Pudding Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 135|designating slaton as the off.summary: Designates the city of Slaton as the official Banana Pudding Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 3185|relating to investigations of.title: Relating to investigations of certain cybercrimes
tx:HB 3185|relating to investigations of.summary: Lets prosecutors issue administrative subpoenas to internet and electronic service providers for subscriber records, such as names, addresses, connection logs and payment sources, in cybercrime investigations; account contents and passwords still require a warrant or court order.

tx:HB 4207|relating to obstructing a rai.title: Relating to obstructing a railroad crossing and the liability of a railway company for such an obstruction; providing a civil penalty
tx:HB 4207|relating to obstructing a rai.summary: Bars trains from blocking a street, highway or railroad crossing for 30 minutes or more, except for breakdowns or acts of God, with civil penalties up to $10,000 per hour, and makes railroads liable to people harmed by resulting emergency-service delays.

tx:SB 1198|relating to the designation o.title: Relating to the designation of spaceports as critical infrastructure facilities for purposes of criminal and civil liability
tx:SB 1198|relating to the designation o.summary: Adds spaceports, including launch, landing, recovery and testing facilities and temporary launch hazard areas, to the critical infrastructure facilities covered by state laws on criminal and civil liability for damaging or interfering with them.

tx:HB 2510|relating to assisted living f.title: Relating to assisted living facility operations and provision of certain services to assisted living facility residents without a license; creating a criminal offense
tx:HB 2510|relating to assisted living f.summary: Makes it a crime to operate an assisted living facility without a license, or to provide personal assistance services to assisted living residents without a required home and community support services license; a first offense is a Class A misdemeanor and a repeat offense a third-degree felony.

tx:HB 285|relating to the prosecution of.title: Relating to the prosecution of the offense of cruelty to nonlivestock animals
tx:HB 285|relating to the prosecution of.summary: Expands animal cruelty offenses involving non-livestock animals to cover acts committed with criminal negligence, not only intentionally, knowingly or recklessly, with a defense for licensed veterinarians and their assistants acting on the job.

tx:HB 4163|relating to the applicability.title: Relating to the applicability of certain city requirements to agricultural operations
tx:HB 4163|relating to the applicability.summary: Bars cities from requiring owners or lessees of agricultural operations to mow, bale, shred or hoe public road right-of-way next to their land, applying to existing and future city rules.

tx:HB 2517|relating to the applicability.title: Relating to the applicability of premium and maintenance taxes to Texas Windstorm Insurance Association and Texas FAIR Plan Association
tx:HB 2517|relating to the applicability.summary: Exempts the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association and the Texas FAIR Plan Association from the state's property and casualty insurance premium tax and the fire insurance maintenance tax, starting with taxes for 2023.

tx:SB 648|relating to recording requirem.title: Relating to recording requirements for certain instruments concerning real property
tx:SB 648|relating to recording requirem.summary: Requires real estate deeds and heirship affidavits filed by individuals, rather than by title companies, attorneys, utilities or governments, to be signed before two witnesses and notarized for the signer and witnesses; heirship affidavits must also be notarized by each living heir.

tx:SB 2637|relating to disclosures about.title: Relating to disclosures about certain automated posts on social media platforms; providing a civil penalty
tx:SB 2637|relating to disclosures about.summary: Requires social media platforms to label content known to be posted by automated bot accounts with a notice saying so and a warning that it may contain misinformation, with attorney general enforcement and civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation.

tx:SB 414|relating to the text of ballot.title: Relating to the text of ballot propositions for bond elections
tx:SB 414|relating to the text of ballot.summary: Requires ballots for local bond elections backed by property taxes to list the bonds' estimated interest and estimated total principal-plus-interest cost, in addition to their purpose, principal amount and the statement that taxes will be imposed to repay them.

tx:SB 1952|relating to the administratio.title: Relating to the administration and operation of the school health and related services program
tx:SB 1952|relating to the administratio.summary: Names the Health and Human Services Commission as the sole agency running the school health and related services program, requires it to train and guide participating school districts and charter schools, and requires an agreement with the Texas Education Agency dividing duties.

tx:HB 2868|relating to the consideration.title: Relating to the consideration of the proportion of long-term debt and equity capitalization in establishing the rates of certain electric utilities
tx:HB 2868|relating to the consideration.summary: Requires regulators setting rates for electric utilities operating only within ERCOT to presume reasonable a utility's proposed debt-to-equity mix based on its recent books, unless found unreasonable, in which case the national average equity ratio is used.

tx:HB 3658|relating to continuing educat.title: Relating to continuing education program contents and format relating to building codes for insurance adjusters
tx:HB 3658|relating to continuing educat.summary: Requires licensed insurance claims adjusters to take at least one hour of continuing education on state and local building codes each licensing period, covering damage assessment, coverage and rebuilding standards, offered in classroom, online and self-paced formats.

tx:HB 252|relating to the payment of emp.title: Relating to the payment of employment compensation by certain state agencies
tx:HB 252|relating to the payment of emp.summary: Lets certain state agencies choose to pay employees in salary Schedule A positions twice a month instead of monthly, if the agency meets the state comptroller's requirements for twice-monthly payroll.

tx:HCR 118|expressing support for the ex.title: Expressing support for the expansion of the warship manufacturing industry in Texas
tx:HCR 118|expressing support for the ex.summary: Expresses the Legislature's support for expanding the warship manufacturing industry in Texas, noting steps such as workforce development, port expansion and new facilities.

tx:HB 2791|relating to the continuation.title: Relating to the continuation of functions of the Vocational Rehabilitation Division administered by the Texas Workforce Commission
tx:HB 2791|relating to the continuation.summary: Lets the Texas Workforce Commission buy goods and services for vocational rehabilitation using any procurement method that gives the best value, use open-enrollment contracts with multiple vendors, and negotiate contracts of up to five years when no bids are received.

tx:HB 1677|relating to the investigation.title: Relating to the investigation of municipal fire fighters in certain municipalities
tx:HB 1677|relating to the investigation.summary: Bars cities of 10,000 or more from disciplining paid firefighters unless an investigation follows set state procedures, applying even where a collective bargaining or meet-and-confer agreement exists and overriding conflicting terms in new agreements.

tx:HB 3512|relating to artificial intell.title: Relating to artificial intelligence training programs for certain employees and officials of state agencies and local governments
tx:HB 3512|relating to artificial intell.summary: Requires officers of state agencies, and state and local government employees and officials who use computers for at least a quarter of their duties, to complete a state-certified artificial intelligence training program each year, in addition to existing cybersecurity training.

tx:HB 2348|relating to the video recordi.title: Relating to the video recording of a deposition taken of the testimony of certain elderly or disabled persons in a criminal case
tx:HB 2348|relating to the video recordi.summary: Lets a court, at either side's request, order prosecutors to take a video-recorded deposition of an elderly or disabled person in a criminal case, admissible if the camera operator can testify to its authenticity.

tx:HB 3376|relating to training on demen.title: Relating to training on dementia and Alzheimer's disease for certain guardians
tx:HB 3376|relating to training on demen.summary: Requires guardians of wards age 60 or older, or younger wards diagnosed with dementia, to complete a free one-hour training on Alzheimer's disease and dementia within six months of appointment and yearly afterward, unless a court waives it.

tx:HB 4749|relating to reconstitution of.title: Relating to reconstitution of the jury wheel and juror qualifications in certain counties
tx:HB 4749|relating to reconstitution of.summary: Lets counties with fewer than 1,000 residents draw grand and trial jurors from neighboring counties in the same judicial district, and allows residents of those neighboring counties to serve.

tx:SB 1734|relating to status of certain.title: Relating to status of certain documents or instruments purporting to convey title to or an interest in real property
tx:SB 1734|relating to status of certain.summary: Creates a process for property owners to challenge a recorded deed or lien they believe is fraudulent: the owner files an affidavit and notifies the parties, and if no response comes within 120 days, a judge can rule the document invalid without filing fees.

tx:HB 3631|relating to a credit against.title: Relating to a credit against required recapture payments for certain school districts for the cost of windstorm and hail insurance under the public school finance system
tx:HB 3631|relating to a credit against.summary: Reduces the amount that property-wealthy school districts in coastal counties must pay the state under school finance "recapture" by what the district spent on windstorm and hail insurance the previous school year.

tx:SB 2662|relating to the enforcement o.title: Relating to the enforcement of drought contingency plans by water and sewer utilities and the Public Utility Commission of Texas
tx:SB 2662|relating to the enforcement o.summary: Requires private water and sewer utilities to include drought contingency plans in their filed tariffs, lets them reduce or cut off service to enforce those plans, and requires plans to include enforcement steps such as fines, surcharges or service restrictions.

tx:HB 4945|relating to a study conducted.title: Relating to a study conducted by the Teacher Retirement System of Texas on the feasibility of offering alternative service retirement benefits to Texas A&M Forest Service wildland firefighters that are members of the retirement system
tx:HB 4945|relating to a study conducted.summary: Requires the Teacher Retirement System to study the cost and feasibility of earlier or enhanced retirement benefits for Texas A&M Forest Service wildland firefighters and support staff, and report to the Legislature by December 31, 2026.

tx:HB 4187|relating to the authority and.title: Relating to the authority and responsibilities of the Texas Historical Commission; authorizing fees
tx:HB 4187|relating to the authority and.summary: Makes the Texas Historical Commission responsible for maintaining official historical markers, lets it negotiate contracts when bidding fails, sets rules for affiliated nonprofits that may charge fees at historic sites, and requires commission-approved historical themes for site exhibits.

tx:HB 1851|relating to the disposition o.title: Relating to the disposition of certain surplus motor vehicles and other law enforcement equipment by the Texas Facilities Commission to certain school districts
tx:HB 1851|relating to the disposition o.summary: Lets the Texas Facilities Commission transfer surplus Department of Public Safety vehicles and law enforcement equipment to school districts in economically disadvantaged areas, for use only by school police or security staff and not resold for two years.

tx:HB 3909|relating to the use of a wire.title: Relating to the use of a wireless communication device at a polling place
tx:HB 3909|relating to the use of a wire.summary: Bars using phones and other wireless devices anywhere in a room where voting is taking place, replacing the current 100-foot limit around voting stations, and requires polling places to post a notice of the ban outside the room.

tx:HB 3698|relating to participation in.title: Relating to participation in reemployment services as a condition of eligibility for unemployment benefits
tx:HB 3698|relating to participation in.summary: Lets the Texas Workforce Commission require people receiving unemployment benefits to take part in reemployment services, such as job search help, as a condition of eligibility, even if they were not flagged as likely to exhaust benefits, unless they have reasonable cause.

tx:HCR 35|urging congress to amend the i.title: Urging Congress to amend the Internal Revenue Code to make spaceports eligible for tax-exempt private activity bonds
tx:HCR 35|urging congress to amend the i.summary: Urges Congress to amend the federal tax code so spaceports can be financed with tax-exempt private activity bonds, as airports and docks already can.

tx:HB 5437|relating to the validation of.title: Relating to the validation of the creation of and certain acts of the Austin County Municipal Utility District No. 1
tx:HB 5437|relating to the validation of.summary: Validates the creation of the Austin County Municipal Utility District No. 1 and its past actions, including its November 2021 election approving bonds and property taxes, except for matters in pending litigation or already ruled invalid.

tx:SB 3074|relating to communications be.title: Relating to communications between the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and the governor, the lieutenant governor, or a member of the legislature
tx:SB 3074|relating to communications be.summary: Lets the governor, lieutenant governor and legislators send written comments to state environmental commissioners about pending permit applications, with legislators limited to facilities in their district, and requires the comments to be placed in the public record for parties to answer.

tx:HB 5668|relating to the powers and du.title: Relating to the powers and duties of the Far North Fort Worth Municipal Utility District No. 1 of Tarrant and Wise Counties; providing authority to impose a tax and issue bonds
tx:HB 5668|relating to the powers and du.summary: Lets the Far North Fort Worth Municipal Utility District No. 1 set up defined areas, including noncontiguous tracts and regardless of acreage minimums, where it can levy taxes and issue bonds for improvements that mainly benefit those areas.

tx:SB 1705|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of virtual currency kiosks; providing an administrative penalty
tx:SB 1705|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires cryptocurrency kiosks to be registered with the state banking department, caps transactions at $3,000 per customer daily and fees at the greater of $5 or 12%, and requires ID scans, fraud warnings and 72-hour holds for new customers, with penalties up to $5,000 per violation.

tx:SB 2857|relating to a prescription dr.title: Relating to a prescription drug purchasing pool for certain health benefit plan issuers and employers
tx:SB 2857|relating to a prescription dr.summary: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission to create a prescription drug purchasing pool that health insurers, local governments, public universities and self-insured private employers can join to buy drugs at negotiated discounts, if funding is provided.

tx:SB 2035|relating to prohibiting contr.title: Relating to prohibiting contributions, expenditures, and related activities involving political committees that support or oppose a ballot measure; creating a criminal offense; providing a civil penalty
tx:SB 2035|relating to prohibiting contr.summary: Bars political committees backing or opposing ballot measures from accepting money from foreign nationals or from donors who took over $100,000 from foreign nationals in four years, requires donor and committee certifications, makes certification violations a misdemeanor, and lets the attorney general sue for civil penalties.

tx:SB 2523|relating to the release of an.title: Relating to the release of an area from the extraterritorial jurisdiction of a municipality by petition
tx:SB 2523|relating to the release of an.summary: Changes how residents or landowners petition to remove land from a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction, limiting petitioners to land where they live or own property, requiring city notice within seven business days, and letting landowners opt out of a release.

tx:SB 1442|relating to a study by the st.title: Relating to a study by the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners on establishing a veterinarian-client-patient relationship by telephone or electronic means
tx:SB 1442|relating to a study by the st.summary: Requires the state veterinary board to study letting veterinarians establish a relationship with clients and animals by phone or video without an in-person exam, and report recommendations by December 1, 2026.

tx:SB 659|relating to the prosecution an.title: Relating to the prosecution and punishment of the offense of smuggling of persons
tx:SB 659|relating to the prosecution an.summary: Expands the crime of smuggling persons to include guiding even one person onto any public or private property without the owner's consent, or holding someone on property against their will, and makes it a first-degree felony when government resources are used.

tx:SB 1681|relating to an annual boardin.title: Relating to an annual boarding home facility report for certain counties and municipalities
tx:SB 1681|relating to an annual boardin.summary: Requires counties and cities that regulate boarding homes to report yearly to the state on their rules, accommodation requests, fair housing complaints and facility closures, starting September 30, 2026.

tx:SB 816|relating to authorizing the di.title: Relating to authorizing the disclosure of certain electronic customer data by a provider of an electronic communications service or a remote computing service in certain immediate life-threatening situations
tx:SB 816|relating to authorizing the di.summary: Lets phone, internet and data storage companies give customer data to police without a warrant when they believe in good faith it is needed immediately to prevent death or serious injury, and shields them from lawsuits for doing so.

tx:SB 878|relating to limitations on the.title: Relating to limitations on the use of public money under certain economic development agreements or programs adopted by certain political subdivisions
tx:SB 878|relating to limitations on the.summary: Bars cities and counties from granting property tax relief through their economic development loan and grant programs, requires public hearings and advance notice before such loans or grants, requires performance goals, and limits agreements to 10 years, or 25 with renewals.

tx:SB 35|relating to design build contra.title: Relating to design-build contracts
tx:SB 35|relating to design build contra.summary: Lowers from six to two the number of design-build contracts the Texas Department of Transportation may enter into for highway projects in each two-year state budget period.

tx:SCR 7|granting the legislature permis.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning on Wednesday, January 15, 2025, and ending on Wednesday, January 22, 2025
tx:SCR 7|granting the legislature permis.summary: Gives each chamber of the legislature the other's consent to adjourn for more than three days between January 15 and January 22, 2025, as the state constitution requires.

tx:SB 1383|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of referral agencies for senior living communities
tx:SB 1383|relating to the regulation of.summary: Regulates businesses that refer seniors to senior living communities, requiring written disclosures about services and who pays fees, background checks, liability insurance and license audits, and barring referrals to communities the agency has a financial stake in or that are unlicensed.

tx:SB 1490|relating to adult high school.title: Relating to adult high school charter program funding
tx:SB 1490|relating to adult high school.summary: Increases funding for adult high school charter programs by counting part-year students as attending a larger share of the school year, such as three-quarters instead of half for students enrolled 50 to 75 percent of the year.

tx:HB 824|relating to the inclusion of c.title: Relating to the inclusion of civics instruction in public school government curriculum requirements for high school students
tx:HB 824|relating to the inclusion of c.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to add civics topics to the high school government curriculum, including the roles of state and local officials, voting and election laws, eligibility to run for office, Robert's Rules of Order, and students' own elected representatives.

tx:SCR 11|granting the legislature permi.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning on Wednesday, February 5, 2025, and ending on Tuesday, February 11, 2025
tx:SCR 11|granting the legislature permi.summary: Gives each chamber of the legislature the other's consent to adjourn for more than three days between February 5 and February 11, 2025, as the state constitution requires.

tx:HB 2516|relating to the eligibility o.title: Relating to the eligibility of certain individuals younger than 65 years of age to purchase Medicare supplement benefit plans
tx:HB 2516|relating to the eligibility o.summary: Requires insurers selling Medicare supplement plans to offer them to people under 65 on Medicare because of end-stage kidney disease or ALS, with guaranteed enrollment periods, Plans A, B and D at age-65 rates, and other plans capped at twice that rate.

tx:SJR 59|a joint resolution proposing a.title: A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the creation of funds to support the capital needs of educational programs offered by the Texas State Technical College System and repealing the limitation on the allocation to that system and its campuses of the annual appropriation of certain constitutionally dedicated funding for public institutions of higher education
tx:SJR 59|a joint resolution proposing a.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2025 ballot, creating a permanent investment fund and a spending fund for Texas State Technical College System buildings and equipment, with the system's combined capital funding capped at $52 million in fiscal 2026 and adjusted for construction costs afterward.

tx:SB 462|relating to establishing a chi.title: Relating to establishing a child-care services waiting list priority for the children of certain child-care workers
tx:SB 462|relating to establishing a chi.summary: Requires waiting lists for state-subsidized child care to give priority to eligible children of child-care workers, whose eligibility is rechecked each year under Texas Workforce Commission rules.

tx:HB 2180|relating to a waiver of the p.title: Relating to a waiver of the preservation of evidence and the return of a seized weapon in a criminal case
tx:HB 2180|relating to a waiver of the p.summary: Lets a defendant who has pleaded guilty or no contest waive, with a lawyer and at least 120 days after the plea, the right to preservation of case evidence and return of seized weapons; the waiver cannot be part of a plea deal.

tx:SB 2885|relating to the use of reclai.title: Relating to the use of reclaimed water that has been treated to meet certain standards as part of an aquifer storage and recovery project
tx:SB 2885|relating to the use of reclai.summary: Lets the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, by rule or permit, allow reclaimed wastewater treated to its standards to be injected underground for storage and later recovery in aquifer storage projects.

tx:HB 4802|relating to certain benefits.title: Relating to certain benefits payable by the Judicial Retirement System of Texas Plan One and the Judicial Retirement System of Texas Plan Two
tx:HB 4802|relating to certain benefits.summary: Grants 5 percent cost-of-living increases on September 1, 2025, and again on September 1, 2026, to judicial retirement and survivor annuities that began on or before September 1, 2024, but only if the legislature appropriates enough money to cover them.

tx:HB 1968|relating to a duty to contrac.title: Relating to a duty to contract for election services furnished for an election held on the first Saturday in May in an even-numbered year
tx:HB 1968|relating to a duty to contrac.summary: Requires county elections administrators to contract with cities, school districts and other local governments that request election services for elections on the May uniform election date in even-numbered years, removing their option to decline.

tx:HB 3800|relating to an advisory board.title: Relating to an advisory board established to develop a resource guide that facilitates collaboration in identifying and addressing local health care workforce needs
tx:HB 3800|relating to an advisory board.summary: Directs the Texas Workforce Commission to create a temporary advisory board of colleges, workforce boards, hospitals, health professionals and community health centers to write a guide on meeting local health care workforce needs, due to the legislature by November 1, 2026.

tx:HB 149|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of the use of artificial intelligence systems in this state; providing civil penalties
tx:HB 149|relating to the regulation of.summary: Regulates artificial intelligence: bars systems intended to encourage self-harm or crime, unlawfully discriminate, or produce child sexual content; bars government social scoring; requires agencies to tell consumers they are dealing with AI; creates a testing sandbox and council; and lets the attorney general seek civil penalties.

tx:SB 865|relating to instruction in car.title: Relating to instruction in cardiopulmonary resuscitation and the use of automated external defibrillators and to a cardiac emergency response plan for certain school employees and volunteers
tx:SB 865|relating to instruction in car.summary: Requires school districts and certain private schools to adopt cardiac emergency response plans, with response teams, CPR and defibrillator training and annual drills, by the 2027-28 school year, and requires coaches, band directors, nurses and certain other staff to take CPR and defibrillator training.

tx:HB 1399|relating to an exemption from.title: Relating to an exemption from ad valorem taxation of tangible personal property consisting of animal feed held by the owner of the property for sale at retail
tx:HB 1399|relating to an exemption from.summary: Exempts from property taxes animal feed held by its owner for retail sale, starting in 2026 if voters approve a related constitutional amendment.

tx:SB 1455|relating to the funding mecha.title: Relating to the funding mechanism for the regulation of workers' compensation and workers' compensation insurance; authorizing surcharges
tx:SB 1455|relating to the funding mecha.summary: Converts the maintenance taxes workers' compensation insurers pay to fund state regulation into surcharges, caps the combined rate at 2.7 percent of premiums, and lets insurers recover the surcharges in rates or from policyholders, effective January 1, 2026.

tx:HB 1813|relating to a parental right.title: Relating to a parental right to information concerning a public school special education program and certain requirements for persons serving as special education representatives and hearing officers at impartial due process hearings
tx:HB 1813|relating to a parental right.summary: Requires paid non-attorney representatives of students in special education due process hearings to complete a state training course, creates that course with a fee and financial-need discounts, and requires the state to tell parents about representation rights and how to file complaints.

tx:HB 2854|relating to the required appr.title: Relating to the required approval of certain hospital visits as a condition of release on parole or to mandatory supervision for certain releasees and to the hospital's liability for damages resulting from those visits
tx:HB 2854|relating to the required appr.summary: Requires parolees on electronic monitoring for certain serious offenses to get parole officer approval before visiting a hospital other than for treatment, requires notice to hospital or local police, and shields hospitals from liability for such visits except for gross negligence, recklessness or intentional misconduct.

tx:HB 9|relating to an exemption from ad.title: Relating to an exemption from ad valorem taxation of a portion of the appraised value of tangible personal property a person owns that is held or used for the production of income
tx:HB 9|relating to an exemption from ad.summary: Exempts the first $125,000 of value of business personal property at each location, replacing an exemption for property worth under $2,500, and lets owners under that amount skip annual filings, starting in 2026 if voters approve a constitutional amendment.

tx:HB 42|relating to the amount and allo.title: Relating to the amount and allocation of the annual constitutional appropriation to certain agencies and institutions of higher education and to the permissible uses of that money
tx:HB 42|relating to the amount and allo.summary: Raises the annual constitutional appropriation for building and capital needs at universities outside the Permanent University Fund from $393.75 million to about $590.6 million starting in fiscal 2026, sets new amounts for each institution, and lets the money pay certain bond debts.

tx:SB 2550|relating to an exemption of t.title: Relating to an exemption of the transfer of certain rights in water from certain disclosure requirements applicable to the transfer of certain interests in real property
tx:SB 2550|relating to an exemption of t.summary: Exempts sales or transfers of only groundwater or surface water rights from several notices and disclosures required in real estate sales, such as notices about coastal property and possible annexation.

tx:HB 5509|relating to the suspension or.title: Relating to the suspension or revocation of a hotel's or motel's certificate of occupancy by a municipality for suspected human trafficking
tx:HB 5509|relating to the suspension or.summary: Lets a city suspend or revoke a hotel's certificate of occupancy if police swear to probable cause and a criminal court finds probable cause that human trafficking is occurring there, using the city's usual procedures and preserving the owner's right to a hearing.

tx:HB 2637|relating to the practice and.title: Relating to the practice and procedures for summoning prospective grand jurors and petit jurors and the exemption of certain persons from grand jury and petit jury service; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 2637|relating to the practice and.summary: Raises the grand jury age exemption from over 70 to 75 and older and lets those 75 and up claim a permanent exemption, moves age-exemption filings from voter registrars to district clerks, and requires clerks to remove people with felony or theft convictions from jury lists.

tx:HB 2029|relating to vehicle safety in.title: Relating to vehicle safety inspections of certain travel trailers
tx:HB 2029|relating to vehicle safety in.summary: Repeals the option for owners of travel trailers still subject to safety inspection to meet it by filing a self-inspection affidavit at registration, and restates the existing $7.50 annual inspection replacement fee charged at vehicle registration.

tx:HB 1481|relating to the use of person.title: Relating to the use of personal wireless communication devices by students during instructional time
tx:HB 1481|relating to the use of person.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to adopt policies barring students from using phones, smartwatches and similar devices on school property during the school day, with discipline for violations and exceptions for disability plans, medical needs and safety requirements.

tx:HB 3255|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a development corporation created by the Gulf Coast Authority to finance certain projects
tx:HB 3255|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets a development corporation created by the Gulf Coast Authority finance projects inside or outside Texas, including education, housing, health, nonprofit, energy and telecommunications facilities and natural gas or electricity purchases, with attorney general notice for out-of-state bond issues.

tx:HB 4240|relating to the exemption fro.title: Relating to the exemption from ad valorem taxation of property of a charitable organization that provides financial support for medical care at certain institutions of higher education
tx:HB 4240|relating to the exemption fro.summary: Adds providing financial support for medical care at listed public health-science universities and Baylor College of Medicine to the charitable activities that qualify an organization for a property tax exemption, starting with 2026 tax years.

tx:HB 721|relating to the applicability.title: Relating to the applicability of certain laws requiring health care cost disclosures by health benefit plan issuers and administrators
tx:HB 721|relating to the applicability.summary: Exempts regional or local health care programs that contract with providers in participating counties to serve employees of participating small employers and their dependents from state laws requiring health plan issuers and administrators to disclose health care costs.

tx:SCR 37|recognizing the strategic impo.title: Recognizing the strategic importance of the Panama Canal to the economic strength of the United States and the State of Texas
tx:SCR 37|recognizing the strategic impo.summary: Recognizes the Panama Canal's importance to the U.S. and Texas economies, supports continued investment in Texas ports, and urges the federal administration to prioritize diplomacy with Panama to keep the canal secure and accessible for U.S. commerce.

tx:HB 1266|relating to expedited credent.title: Relating to expedited credentialing of certain physician assistants and advanced practice nurses by managed care plan issuers
tx:HB 1266|relating to expedited credent.summary: Requires managed care plans to pay for services by physician assistants and advanced practice nurses who join an already-contracted medical group as in-network while their credentialing is pending, and protects patients from extra charges if credentialing is later denied.

tx:HB 195|relating to the dissemination.title: Relating to the dissemination of certain school district ad valorem tax-related information
tx:HB 195|relating to the dissemination.summary: Requires appraisal district property tax databases to show, for school districts subject to recapture, the estimated share of each property's school operating taxes sent to the state and the share kept locally.

tx:HB 2464|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of a municipality to regulate a home-based business
tx:HB 2464|relating to the authority of.summary: Bars cities from banning or requiring permits for home businesses within occupancy limits that cause no on-street parking, substantial traffic or noise, or street-visible activity, and from requiring home businesses to rezone or, in single-family homes or duplexes, install fire sprinklers; local codes and HOA rules still apply.

tx:HCR 107|designating the texas almanac.title: Designating the Texas Almanac as the official State Book of Texas
tx:HCR 107|designating the texas almanac.summary: Designates the Texas Almanac as the official State Book of Texas.

tx:HCR 111|designating combes as the off.title: Designating Combes as the official Bee Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 111|designating combes as the off.summary: Designates the city of Combes as the official Bee Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 2014|relating to the board of dire.title: Relating to the board of directors of Somervell County Hospital District
tx:HB 2014|relating to the board of dire.summary: Sets the Somervell County Hospital District board at seven elected directors serving staggered four-year terms, with elections on the May uniform election date, and has directors elected in 2026 draw lots for two- or three-year first terms to begin the staggering.

tx:SB 748|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of laser hair removal
tx:SB 748|relating to the regulation of.summary: Limits the state licensing department's enforcement role under the radiation law to its laser hair removal provisions, and removes requirements that it set warning-sign rules and include sign standards with license applications.

tx:HCR 74|designating carthage as the of.title: Designating Carthage as the official Country Music Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 74|designating carthage as the of.summary: Designates Carthage as the official Country Music Capital of Texas for 10 years.

tx:HB 1939|relating to a credit for prep.title: Relating to a credit for prepayment of the amount required to be paid by a school district for the purchase of attendance credit under the public school finance system
tx:HB 1939|relating to a credit for prep.summary: Gives school districts that must buy attendance credits under the school finance recapture system a 4 percent discount if they pay the full amount in a single payment by February 15 of the school year.

tx:SB 2581|relating to the repeal of a p.title: Relating to the repeal of a provision governing the operation of jail commissaries in certain counties
tx:SB 2581|relating to the repeal of a p.summary: Repeals a law that applied only to certain large counties governing how sheriffs run jail commissaries, so those counties follow the same commissary rules as the rest of the state.

tx:SB 1723|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of a rapid DNA analysis pilot program in certain counties
tx:SB 1723|relating to the establishment.summary: Lets approved local law enforcement agencies perform rapid DNA analysis of samples taken at booking under state police standards, and requires the Department of Public Safety to start a rapid DNA pilot program in two counties by September 2026 and report results by 2028.

tx:HB 2213|relating to the composition o.title: Relating to the composition of the board of directors of the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association
tx:HB 2213|relating to the composition o.summary: Changes Texas Windstorm Insurance Association board rules: three members must live outside a catastrophe area rather than over 100 miles from the coast; industry members must write or sell coverage in first-tier coastal counties and live in Texas; at least one agent member must actively offer or sell association policies.

tx:HB 2518|relating to the use of instal.title: Relating to the use of installment premium payment plans on Texas Windstorm Insurance Association policies
tx:HB 2518|relating to the use of instal.summary: Bars the use of outside premium financing arrangements for Texas Windstorm Insurance Association policies, which already offer installment payment plans at no extra cost, for policies issued or renewed starting January 1, 2026.

tx:HB 3114|relating to the view of the s.title: Relating to the view of the State Capitol
tx:HB 3114|relating to the view of the s.summary: Removes four protected Capitol view corridors, including ones along Interstate 35 and from the old Mueller airport and Oakwood Cemetery, and raises the height cap for the University of Texas football stadium to 670 feet above sea level, exempting its north end.

tx:SB 1184|relating to the age of wine a.title: Relating to the age of wine authorized to be sold by a wine collection seller
tx:SB 1184|relating to the age of wine a.summary: Lets licensed wine collection sellers sell wine to permitted restaurants if it was made at least 10 years earlier, down from 20 years.

tx:SB 1355|relating to liquor sales on c.title: Relating to liquor sales on credit by the holder of a distiller's and rectifier's permit to a wholesaler
tx:SB 1355|relating to liquor sales on c.summary: Requires distillers to give wholesalers written invoices and wholesalers to pay on agreed contract terms, and lets the state alcohol commission discipline wholesalers who stay delinquent after a demand for payment.

tx:HB 1990|relating to limitation of cer.title: Relating to limitation of certain liability of owners, lessees, and occupants of nonagricultural land
tx:HB 1990|relating to limitation of cer.summary: Shields owners, renters and occupants of nonagricultural land from liability for injuries or damage caused by wildlife, acts of God, trespassers, officers or firefighters entering the land, or others who damage fences or gates, except for their own gross negligence or willful acts.

tx:HB 1585|relating to the areas of oper.title: Relating to the areas of operation of housing finance corporations
tx:HB 1585|relating to the areas of oper.summary: Limits the tax and fee exemption for housing developments owned by housing finance corporations to developments located within the boundaries of the local government that created the corporation, for properties newly built or acquired after the law takes effect.

tx:HB 1169|relating to the adoption of a.title: Relating to the adoption of a comprehensive plan to protect oil and gas infrastructure in this state
tx:HB 1169|relating to the adoption of a.summary: Requires the Railroad Commission to adopt by September 1, 2026, and periodically update, a plan to protect oil and gas wellheads and pipelines from natural disasters, severe weather, cyberattacks, terrorism and widespread power outages.

tx:HB 4879|relating to the creation of a.title: Relating to the creation of a grant program to assist local law enforcement agencies in testing certain substances suspected of containing delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol
tx:HB 4879|relating to the creation of a.summary: Creates a grant program in the governor's office paying for third-party lab tests to determine whether substances seized by police exceed the legal THC limit, for agencies whose prosecutors agree to review the results, with annual reporting on testing and cases.

tx:HR 1495|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, S.B. No. 2308
tx:HR 1495|suspending limitations on con.summary: Lets the House-Senate conference committee on a bill to fund a consortium for federal ibogaine drug trials for opioid use disorder go beyond the two versions, including dropping a grant program and adding rules for selecting and contracting with the consortium and matching funds.

tx:HB 143|relating to the authority of t.title: Relating to the authority of the Railroad Commission of Texas and the Public Utility Commission of Texas to address a failure by an operator to maintain an electrical power line serving a well site or certain surface facilities in accordance with the National Electrical Code
tx:HB 143|relating to the authority of t.summary: Requires oil and gas operators to keep well-site power line poles free of visible defects, and requires the Railroad Commission and Public Utility Commission to resolve hazardous power line conditions within 10 days, such as by requesting electric service disconnection, with landowner notice.

tx:HB 136|relating to medicaid coverage.title: Relating to Medicaid coverage and reimbursement for lactation consultation
tx:HB 136|relating to medicaid coverage.summary: Requires Texas Medicaid to pay lactation consultants for breastfeeding consultation services provided to enrollees, and directs the state health agency to create a separate Medicaid provider type for lactation consultants.

tx:HB 201|relating to the financial crim.title: Relating to the financial crimes intelligence center
tx:HB 201|relating to the financial crim.summary: Expands the state's Financial Crimes Intelligence Center beyond card-skimmer fraud to cover motor fuel theft, including devices that tamper with gas pump meters, and lets the center assist law enforcement and other agencies on request.

tx:HB 1718|relating to the definition of.title: Relating to the definition of "closing" for purposes of certain private activity bonds
tx:HB 1718|relating to the definition of.summary: Redefines when certain state and local private activity bonds are considered "closed" so that bonds for qualified rental housing projects can be delivered for partial, incremental payments of at least 10 percent of the full amount.

tx:SB 1119|relating to liability of a wa.title: Relating to liability of a water park entity for injuries arising from certain activities
tx:SB 1119|relating to liability of a wa.summary: Shields water parks from liability for visitor injuries if a prescribed warning sign is posted at the entrance, except for injuries caused by the park's negligence, known dangerous conditions, inadequate staff training, or intentional acts.

tx:SCR 1|granting the legislature permis.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning on Wednesday, July 30, 2025, and ending on Monday, August 4, 2025
tx:SCR 1|granting the legislature permis.summary: Gives each chamber of the Legislature the other's consent to adjourn for more than three days between Wednesday, July 30, and Monday, August 4, 2025, during the first special session.

tx:HB 3487|relating to a reduction in th.title: Relating to a reduction in the amount of sales and use tax collections that the owners of restaurants that participate in an oyster shell recycling program are required to remit to the comptroller of public accounts
tx:HB 3487|relating to a reduction in th.summary: Lets restaurant owners who take part in a state-recognized oyster shell recycling program deduct $2 from their taxable sales for every 50 pounds of oyster shells they send for recycling, starting October 1, 2025.

tx:HB 4960|relating to political adverti.title: Relating to political advertising distributed or broadcast as part of a mass text message campaign and civil penalties for required disclosures on certain political advertising
tx:HB 4960|relating to political adverti.summary: Treats paid mass political text-message campaigns as political advertising subject to disclosure rules, and counts all texts in one campaign that lack required disclosures as a single violation when civil penalties are set.

tx:SCR 18|designating the town of trophy.title: Designating the Town of Trophy Club as the official Texas Town of Patriotism for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:SCR 18|designating the town of trophy.summary: Designates the Town of Trophy Club as the official Texas Town of Patriotism, with the designation lasting until the 10th anniversary of the resolution's final passage.

tx:HB 705|relating to the cosmetology li.title: Relating to the Cosmetology Licensure Compact; authorizing fees
tx:HB 705|relating to the cosmetology li.summary: Enters Texas into the multistate Cosmetology Licensure Compact, letting cosmetologists holding a multistate license from a member state practice in other member states; names the state licensing department administrator and lets the governor withdraw Texas by proclamation.

tx:HB 3371|relating to the recovery of c.title: Relating to the recovery of certain state border security expenditures from the federal government
tx:HB 3371|relating to the recovery of c.summary: Lets the governor ask Congress to reimburse Texas for southern border security spending, initially seeking at least $4.72 billion for 2022-23 and $6.54 billion for 2024-25, and lets the attorney general sue the federal government if unpaid.

tx:HCR 148|designating bridge city as th.title: Designating Bridge City as the official Corn Dog Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 148|designating bridge city as th.summary: Designates Bridge City as the official Corn Dog Capital of Texas, with the designation lasting until the 10th anniversary of the resolution's final passage.

tx:SB 1499|relating to the operations of.title: Relating to the operations of the Financial Crimes Intelligence Center
tx:SB 1499|relating to the operations of.summary: Broadens the Financial Crimes Intelligence Center's focus from card fraud to payment fraud, including check fraud and unauthorized electronic payments, renames its leader a director, and moves its governing law into the Government Code.

tx:HB 4310|relating to a special right o.title: Relating to a special right of access under the public information law for a member of a governing board
tx:HB 4310|relating to a special right o.summary: Gives members of government boards, such as city council members and county commissioners, a right to promptly obtain their body's public records free of charge, with confidential details redacted or covered by a confidentiality agreement, enforceable in court.

tx:SB 1733|relating to the composition o.title: Relating to the composition of the board of the Calhoun Port Authority
tx:SB 1733|relating to the composition o.summary: Expands the Calhoun Port Authority board from six to seven commissioners by adding one elected at large, first elected in May 2027, with the governor appointing someone to fill the seat until then.

tx:HB 1105|relating to the exemption of.title: Relating to the exemption of tuition and laboratory fees at public institutions of higher education for certain paramedics
tx:HB 1105|relating to the exemption of.summary: Requires public colleges to waive tuition and lab fees for paramedics employed by a Texas local government who take emergency medical services courses, starting fall 2025, with continued eligibility tied to satisfactory academic progress.

tx:HB 766|relating to the ballot applica.title: Relating to the ballot application requirements for the election of a precinct chair
tx:HB 766|relating to the ballot applica.summary: Requires candidates for party precinct chair to include an email address, a phone number, or both on their ballot application, and makes that contact information confidential rather than public.

tx:HB 23|relating to the exemption from.title: Relating to the exemption from ad valorem taxation of property owned by certain nonprofit corporations, located in a populous county, and used to promote agriculture, support youth, and provide educational support in the community
tx:HB 23|relating to the exemption from.summary: Exempts from property taxes, in counties of 3.3 million or more people, property owned by charitable nonprofits and used to promote agriculture, support youth and provide educational support, starting January 1, 2026; for-profit tenants' interests remain taxable.

tx:HR 1446|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, SB 1
tx:HR 1446|suspending limitations on con.summary: Suspends House rules so the chamber can take up a conference committee report on the 2026-27 state budget bill that adds new provisions and sets funding outside both chambers' versions for specific listed agency items, and reformats parts of the bill.

tx:SB 1254|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of professional employer organizations
tx:SB 1254|relating to the regulation of.summary: Keeps a professional employer organization's status as employer of its covered workers for 18 months after its license lapses, ends that status afterward, and lets state regulators penalize anyone offering such services without a valid license.

tx:HB 4139|relating to the use of videog.title: Relating to the use of videography in relation to certain court proceedings
tx:HB 4139|relating to the use of videog.summary: Bars recording or livestreaming jury selection, bench conferences and court proceedings involving alleged victims of sexual, trafficking, family violence and similar offenses (adult victims may consent), and requires 72 hours' public notice before any proceeding is recorded.

tx:HB 1820|relating to the expunction of.title: Relating to the expunction of arrest records and files when a grand jury fails to find that probable cause exists to believe the alleged offense was committed
tx:HB 1820|relating to the expunction of.summary: Entitles a person to have arrest records erased when a grand jury declines to indict because it finds no probable cause, the charge is no longer pending, and there was no conviction or court-ordered supervision beyond a Class C misdemeanor.

tx:SB 1243|relating to the dissolution o.title: Relating to the dissolution of a public utility agency
tx:SB 1243|relating to the dissolution o.summary: Lets the local governments that participate in a public utility agency dissolve it by concurrent ordinances and transfer its obligations, assets, permits and licenses to themselves, or lets a sole remaining participant dissolve it by ordinance.

tx:HB 3466|relating to the cancellation.title: Relating to the cancellation of certain consumer transactions
tx:HB 3466|relating to the cancellation.summary: Exempts state-regulated service contracts, and services the consumer can cancel at any time with that right stated in writing, from the state law giving consumers a right to cancel certain transactions.

tx:SB 2965|relating to territory in an e.title: Relating to territory in an emergency services district that is annexed by a municipality
tx:SB 2965|relating to territory in an e.summary: Lets an emergency services district keep territory a city annexes unless the city's planned fire and ambulance service will match or exceed the district's, deems approval if the district does not act within 30 days, and sends disputes to binding arbitration.

tx:HB 5402|relating to fiscal impact sta.title: Relating to fiscal impact statements for legislation imposing mandates on health benefit plan issuers
tx:HB 5402|relating to fiscal impact sta.summary: Requires the Legislative Budget Board to attach a statement to bills that mandate new health insurance benefits, higher provider payments, or new administrative requirements, estimating their effect on insurer spending and on enrollees' premiums and other costs.

tx:HB 4665|relating to training requirem.title: Relating to training requirements for childcare employees and directors
tx:HB 4665|relating to training requirem.summary: Adds public school districts and the Texas Education Agency to the entities allowed to provide the minimum training required for employees, directors and operators of day-care centers, group day-care homes and registered family homes.

tx:SB 815|relating to the use of certain.title: Relating to the use of certain automated systems in, and certain adverse determinations made in connection with, the health benefit claims process
tx:SB 815|relating to the use of certain.summary: Bars health insurance utilization review agents from using automated decision systems, including artificial intelligence, to make denials of care in whole or part, lets the insurance commissioner audit their use, and still allows such tools for administrative and fraud-detection work.

tx:SB 1057|relating to the submission an.title: Relating to the submission and approval of certain proposals by shareholders of nationally listed corporations
tx:SB 1057|relating to the submission an.summary: Lets nationally listed corporations opt in to rules requiring shareholders who submit proposals to hold at least $1 million or 3 percent of voting shares for six months and to solicit holders of 67 percent of the voting power.

tx:SB 503|relating to the establishment.title: Relating to the establishment of an electronic registry of livestock marks and brands
tx:SB 503|relating to the establishment.summary: Requires the Texas Animal Health Commission to create a public, searchable online registry of livestock marks and brands recorded with county clerks, with owners' personal information shielded from the public. Requires clerks to keep electronic records and accept electronic filings.

tx:SB 2501|relating to selection of an a.title: Relating to selection of an attorney by an indigent parent as attorney ad litem for the parent in certain suits affecting the parent-child relationship
tx:SB 2501|relating to selection of an a.summary: Lets an indigent parent in a state-filed child protection or parental-rights termination case choose their own qualified lawyer, paid by the county at the same rate as a court-appointed lawyer, and bars courts from interfering with that choice.

tx:SB 2417|relating to investigations co.title: Relating to investigations conducted and actions brought by the attorney general under the Texas Free Enterprise and Antitrust Act of 1983
tx:SB 2417|relating to investigations co.summary: Makes the attorney general's notes from antitrust investigation interviews confidential attorney work product shielded from discovery, and treats the attorney general as the only state party for discovery in state antitrust suits, not responsible for other agencies' or lawmakers' documents.

tx:SB 1067|relating to prohibiting publi.title: Relating to prohibiting public institutions of higher education and employees of public institutions of higher education and their spouses from soliciting or accepting gifts, grants, donations, or investments from certain foreign entities
tx:SB 1067|relating to prohibiting publi.summary: Bars public colleges and universities, their employees and employees' spouses from soliciting or accepting gifts, grants, donations or investments from governments or political parties of designated countries, or from companies headquartered there with government ownership, and requires returning money received in violation during the preceding fiscal biennium.

tx:SB 2260|relating to the disclosure an.title: Relating to the disclosure and posting of certain information regarding multifamily residential developments that receive certain tax exemptions and the eligibility of those developments to receive those exemptions
tx:SB 2260|relating to the disclosure an.summary: Requires owners of tax-exempt multifamily housing developments to file yearly disclosures on ownership, units, appraised value, tax savings, rents and income-restricted units, which the state housing agency posts online; developments that fail to file lose the exemption.

tx:SCR 46|expressing support for renamin.title: Expressing support for renaming the New York strip steak as the Texas strip steak and directing the Texas Department of Agriculture to promote the Texas strip steak as part of efforts to support Texas beef and agricultural products
tx:SCR 46|expressing support for renamin.summary: Expresses the Legislature's support for renaming the New York strip steak the Texas strip steak, encourages restaurants and Texans to use the new name, and directs the Texas Department of Agriculture to promote it.

tx:SB 927|relating to the issuance of na.title: Relating to the issuance of Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal specialty license plates
tx:SB 927|relating to the issuance of na.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles to issue specialty license plates for recipients of the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal, showing the medal's emblem and name.

tx:HB 1506|relating to the issuance of a.title: Relating to the issuance of a license to carry a handgun to certain retired county court judges
tx:HB 1506|relating to the issuance of a.summary: Lets retired judges of constitutional or statutory county courts who served at least 48 months on such a court qualify as retired judicial officers for purposes of getting a license to carry a handgun.

tx:SCR 29|designating el paso as the off.title: Designating El Paso as the official Boot Capital of Texas for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:SCR 29|designating el paso as the off.summary: Designates El Paso as the official Boot Capital of Texas for 10 years from the resolution's final passage.

tx:HB 3866|relating to the installation.title: Relating to the installation and ownership of certain outdoor storage containers; authorizing a fee
tx:HB 3866|relating to the installation.summary: Bars new recycling facilities for federally regulated intermediate bulk containers within 2,000 feet of a private residence and requires them to register with the state environmental agency, pay an annual fee and undergo inspections. Exempts facilities handling 50 or fewer containers.

tx:HB 431|relating to the regulation by.title: Relating to the regulation by a property owners' association of the installation of solar roof tiles
tx:HB 431|relating to the regulation by.summary: Adds solar roof tiles to the solar energy devices covered by state limits on how property owners' associations may restrict their installation, clarifying existing law.

tx:HB 1760|relating to increasing the mi.title: Relating to increasing the minimum term of imprisonment and changing the eligibility for community supervision, mandatory supervision, and parole for persons convicted of intoxication manslaughter
tx:HB 1760|relating to increasing the mi.summary: Raises the minimum prison term for intoxication manslaughter from two to five years, requires at least five years' prison time as a condition of probation unless a judge reduces it to two, and bars parole or mandatory supervision until five years are served.

tx:HCR 9|designating the first saturday.title: Designating the first Saturday of every month as Small Business Saturday for a 10-year period ending in 2035
tx:HCR 9|designating the first saturday.summary: Designates the first Saturday of every month as Small Business Saturday in Texas for 10 years from the resolution's final passage.

tx:SB 896|relating to the enrollment per.title: Relating to the enrollment period for newborns under certain health benefit plans
tx:SB 896|relating to the enrollment per.summary: Extends the period for enrolling a newborn under certain health benefit plans, so coverage continues through the child's first 60 days and parents have 60 days, instead of 31, to give notice of the birth and pay any added premium.

tx:SB 1215|relating to the placement of.title: Relating to the placement of a cultivated oyster in a natural oyster bed, a private oyster bed, or coastal waters
tx:SB 1215|relating to the placement of.summary: Lets a person place cultivated oysters in natural or private oyster beds or coastal waters only with written approval from the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, which must adopt best practices for approving such placements.

tx:HB 762|relating to severance pay for.title: Relating to severance pay for political subdivision employees and independent contractors
tx:HB 762|relating to severance pay for.summary: Requires local government contracts that include severance pay to cap severance paid from public money at 20 weeks of compensation and bar it for workers fired for misconduct, and requires posting severance agreements online. Exempts public and teaching hospitals.

tx:HB 2080|relating to the review of the.title: Relating to the review of the duties of a groundwater conservation district by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
tx:HB 2080|relating to the review of the.summary: Changes reviews of groundwater conservation districts by the state environmental agency: requires public notice of review panel meetings, reimburses panel members' expenses, makes panel records public, and lets panels get technical help from the water board and legal advice from agency counsel.

tx:HB 5560|relating to penalties in cert.title: Relating to penalties in certain suits involving a groundwater conservation district; increasing a penalty
tx:HB 5560|relating to penalties in cert.summary: Raises groundwater districts' maximum civil penalty from $10,000 to $25,000 per day per violation, lets courts exceed it when a violator's economic gain is larger, allows deferring up to half for corrective spending, and lets courts allow water utilities to recover penalties from customers who caused violations.

tx:HB 4157|relating to liability protect.title: Relating to liability protections for commercial space flight and exploration
tx:HB 4157|relating to liability protect.summary: Makes reciprocal waivers of claims between parties in commercial space flight activities, as provided under federal aviation rules, enforceable in Texas, and drops the requirement that a space flight participant's liability agreement be signed by a witness.

tx:SB 2774|relating to the classificatio.title: Relating to the classification of certain entities as primarily engaged in retail trade for purposes of the franchise tax
tx:SB 2774|relating to the classificatio.summary: Classifies businesses that rent industrial uniforms, garments and linens as engaged in retail trade for the state franchise tax, starting January 1, 2027.

tx:SB 904|relating to the licensing and.title: Relating to the licensing and regulation of hearing instrument fitters and dispensers
