tx:SB 904|relating to the licensing and.summary: Changes hearing aid seller licensing: separates rules for sales by audiologists and by hearing instrument fitters, ends a continuing education exemption for new licensees, and drops the requirement that minors get a physician's written statement before buying a hearing aid.

tx:SB 823|relating to labeling and repre.title: Relating to labeling and representation of imported shrimp; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:SB 823|relating to labeling and repre.summary: Requires suppliers and distributors to label whether shrimp sold in Texas is imported, and bars restaurants from calling imported shrimp Texas, American, domestic or Gulf shrimp, with administrative penalties for violations. Exempts grocery stores and packaged products.

tx:SB 1359|relating to the creation powe.title: Relating to the creation, powers, duties, and financing of the Wise Regional Water District; granting a limited power of eminent domain; providing authority to issue bonds; providing authority to impose fees; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 1359|relating to the creation powe.summary: Creates the Wise Regional Water District covering Wise County, without a confirmation election, with a board appointed by the county and participating cities and water districts, and powers to supply water, issue bonds, charge fees and use eminent domain, but not to levy property taxes.

tx:SB 582|relating to certain agreements.title: Relating to certain agreements arising out of special investigations conducted by the Texas Education Agency
tx:SB 582|relating to certain agreements.summary: Makes agreements between the Texas Education Agency and a school district that settle a special investigation and impose sanctions public records, and requires them to describe the allegations in plain language and include agreed factual findings.

tx:SB 2633|relating to a local option el.title: Relating to a local option election on the sale of alcoholic beverages in certain areas of a municipality and the local regulation of premises in those areas
tx:SB 2633|relating to a local option el.summary: Extends the law on city alcoholic beverage zones to a city of 240,000 or more people spanning two or more counties and bordering a man-made lake of at least 20,000 acres, and lets such cities adopt zoning rules for alcohol-selling premises in those zones.

tx:SB 1263|relating to a pilot program f.title: Relating to a pilot program for the safe disposal of prescription drugs, including controlled substance prescription drugs
tx:SB 1263|relating to a pilot program f.summary: Moves the prescription drug safe disposal pilot program from the pharmacy board to the Department of State Health Services, which pays for drug collection bins at participating pharmacies, and lets controlled, noncontrolled and over-the-counter drugs be collected together.

tx:SB 2844|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of deer breeding; creating criminal offenses
tx:SB 2844|relating to the regulation of.summary: Cuts the maximum size of a breeder deer enclosure from 100 to 20 acres, except for existing permitted enclosures, creates new offenses for deer breeders such as failing to report deaths or submit disease samples, and raises penalties for repeat violations.

tx:SB 1030|relating to the exemption fro.title: Relating to the exemption from sales and use taxes for certain aircraft components and other property required for normal aircraft operations
tx:SB 1030|relating to the exemption fro.summary: Extends the sales and use tax exemption for parts permanently attached to an aircraft, and for items needed for normal aircraft operations, to all aircraft rather than only those used by licensed carriers or for flight instruction.

tx:HB 5699|relating to the exclusion of.title: Relating to the exclusion of certain territory from Harris County Municipal Utility District No. 405
tx:HB 5699|relating to the exclusion of.summary: Lets Harris County Municipal Utility District No. 405 contract with owners of undeveloped land to remove that land from the district; removed land keeps paying district debt taxes until its share of existing debt is paid, and past district actions are validated.

tx:HB 1639|relating to a study on the in.title: Relating to a study on the increased incidence of cancer in female firefighters in this state
tx:HB 1639|relating to a study on the in.summary: Requires the state health department, with the Texas Commission on Fire Protection, to study cancer rates among female firefighters compared with other women, focusing on cancers such as ovarian and breast cancer, and report to the Legislature by September 1, 2026.

tx:SB 2850|relating to the task force on.title: Relating to the task force on pollinator health
tx:SB 2850|relating to the task force on.summary: Creates a temporary Parks and Wildlife Department task force on pollinator health, with members from science, agriculture, nursery, pesticide, beekeeping and conservation groups, to study habitat, public education and bee population data and report recommendations to the Legislature by October 1, 2026.

tx:SB 1536|relating to training on alzhe.title: Relating to training on Alzheimer's disease, dementia, and related disorders for certain guardians
tx:SB 1536|relating to training on alzhe.summary: Requires guardians covered by the state's guardian training rules whose wards are 60 or older, or younger and diagnosed with dementia, to complete a free one-hour course on Alzheimer's and dementia within six months of appointment and yearly afterward, unless a court waives it.

tx:HB 3146|relating to certain hearings.title: Relating to certain hearings conducted by the State Office of Administrative Hearings
tx:HB 3146|relating to certain hearings.summary: Repeals requirements that the State Office of Administrative Hearings keep separate written agreements with the agriculture, health and human services, family and protective services, insurance, workers' compensation and public safety agencies on how it conducts their hearings, with related conforming changes.

tx:HB 1936|relating to the issuance of a.title: Relating to the issuance of a citation for the offense of the unauthorized use of parking designated for persons with disabilities
tx:HB 1936|relating to the issuance of a.summary: Repeals a rule that let police only warn, not ticket, drivers parked in a disability-designated space whose sign does not meet state standards, allowing citations in those cases for offenses committed after the law takes effect.

tx:HB 1109|relating to an exemption from.title: Relating to an exemption from certain motor fuel taxes for counties in this state
tx:HB 1109|relating to an exemption from.summary: Exempts gasoline and diesel bought by Texas counties for their own use from state motor fuel taxes, lets fuel sellers claim a credit for such untaxed sales, and lets counties seek refunds of fuel taxes they paid.

tx:HB 3824|relating to fire safety stand.title: Relating to fire safety standards and emergency operations plans for the operation of battery energy storage
tx:HB 3824|relating to fire safety stand.summary: Requires the state insurance commissioner to set fire safety standards, based on national UL and fire-protection codes, for battery energy storage sites of at least one megawatt-hour starting operation in 2027 or later, with outside inspections, site emergency plans, free first-responder training and fire marshal enforcement.

tx:HB 1400|relating to creation of the g.title: Relating to creation of the groundwater science, research, and innovation fund to be administered by the Texas Water Development Board
tx:HB 1400|relating to creation of the g.summary: Creates a groundwater science, research and innovation fund, run by the Texas Water Development Board, to give grants to local groundwater conservation districts for research, modeling, conservation, recharge and water-quality projects, reserving at least 35% for small, low-revenue districts.

tx:HB 1160|relating to increasing the cr.title: Relating to increasing the criminal penalty for the offense of assault committed against certain employees or agents of a utility and to the prosecution of the criminal offense of interference with public duties of those employees or agents
tx:HB 1160|relating to increasing the cr.summary: Makes assaulting an on-duty utility worker a third-degree felony, raises harassment of such workers to a Class A misdemeanor, and makes interfering with utility workers on the job a crime, with a higher penalty in declared disaster or evacuation areas.

tx:HB 4769|relating to electronic delive.title: Relating to electronic delivery of documents sent or received by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx:HB 4769|relating to electronic delive.summary: Lets the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation's governing commission require that agency notices, orders and other correspondence be sent and received electronically, and ends the requirement that penalty and contested-case notices go by certified mail.

tx:HJR 175|proposing a constitutional am.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment relating to the right to own, hold, and use a mutually agreed upon medium of exchange
tx:HJR 175|proposing a constitutional am.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 4, 2025 ballot, guaranteeing people's right to own and use any mutually agreed medium of exchange, including cash, coin, bullion, digital currency or private scrip, and barring governments from restricting the money people hold.

tx:HB 1193|relating to the confidentiali.title: Relating to the confidentiality of certain information on a marriage license, an application for a marriage license, and a declaration of informal marriage
tx:HB 1193|relating to the confidentiali.summary: Lets either party filing a declaration of informal (common-law) marriage check a box to keep identifying information other than names confidential, barring county clerks and the state vital statistics office from publishing it or releasing it to anyone but the parties or their legal representatives.

tx:HB 4284|relating to an excessive disc.title: Relating to an excessive discount on certain alcoholic beverages
tx:HB 4284|relating to an excessive disc.summary: Repeals bans on alcohol producers, wholesalers and distributors giving retailers and bars an "excessive discount," and on liquor stores offering excessive discounts on liquor.

tx:SB 1058|relating to the exclusion of.title: Relating to the exclusion of certain securities transaction payments from the total revenue of a taxable entity that is a registered securities market operator
tx:SB 1058|relating to the exclusion of.summary: Lets registered securities exchange operators exclude from the revenue counted for the state franchise tax the rebate payments they make to brokers and dealers to encourage trading liquidity, starting with reports due after the law takes effect.

tx:SB 1044|relating to newborn screening.title: Relating to newborn screening tests for Duchenne muscular dystrophy
tx:SB 1044|relating to newborn screening.summary: Adds Duchenne muscular dystrophy to the state's newborn screening tests and related follow-up and treatment referral services once the state health department's lab is ready, with implementation required only if the Legislature specifically funds it.

tx:HB 26|relating to requiring contracts.title: Relating to requiring contracts with Medicaid managed care organizations to permit the organizations to offer nutrition counseling and instruction services in lieu of other state Medicaid plan services
tx:HB 26|relating to requiring contracts.summary: Lets Medicaid managed care plans offer approved nutrition counseling in place of other Medicaid services, excluding meals or grocery support, and lets the state run a pilot through August 2030 offering medically tailored meals and nutrition support to pregnant enrollees with conditions such as gestational diabetes.

tx:HB 1024|relating to the execution of.title: Relating to the execution of a warrant issued for certain releasees who violate a condition of parole or mandatory supervision related to the electronic monitoring of the releasee
tx:HB 1024|relating to the execution of.summary: Requires law enforcement agencies to carry out, as soon as practicable, warrants to return parolees in the state's super-intensive supervision program who violate parole conditions tied to their electronic monitoring.

tx:HJR 7|proposing a constitutional amen.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment to dedicate a portion of the revenue derived from state sales and use taxes to the Texas water fund
tx:HJR 7|proposing a constitutional amen.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2025 ballot, sending up to $1 billion a year in state sales tax revenue above $46.5 billion to the Texas water fund from 2027 through 2047, and bars using it for pipelines carrying fresh groundwater.

tx:HB 3336|relating to an alcoholic beve.title: Relating to an alcoholic beverage tax credit for certain liquor or malt beverage byproducts donated for agricultural use in this state
tx:HB 3336|relating to an alcoholic beve.summary: Gives alcohol producers and importers that pay state alcohol taxes a credit of 8 cents per dry pound of spent brewing or distilling grain donated within 100 miles for farm use, such as compost or animal feed, capped at $30,000 a year.

tx:SB 1737|relating to service retiremen.title: Relating to service retirement benefits payable by the Employees Retirement System of Texas to certain law enforcement officers and custodial officers
tx:SB 1737|relating to service retiremen.summary: Extends the state employee retirement system's law enforcement and custodial officer benefits, including retirement at 55 with 10 years of service, to peace officers of the comptroller and attorney general and certain juvenile justice staff, if lawmakers provide enough funding.

tx:HB 3666|relating to global profession.title: Relating to global professional standards for internal auditing
tx:HB 3666|relating to global profession.summary: Requires state agency internal audit programs to follow the Institute of Internal Auditors' Global Internal Audit Standards, dropping references to its older standards and to government auditing standards, rewrites internal auditing's stated purpose, and relabels required audits as covering financial, operational and technology systems.

tx:HB 2221|relating to certain trade pra.title: Relating to certain trade practices related to life insurance, annuity contracts, and accident and health coverage
tx:HB 2221|relating to certain trade pra.summary: Rewrites state rules on rebates and inducements by life, annuity and health insurers and agents, keeping bans on premium rebates and unfair discrimination while allowing reasonably priced value-added services, noncash gifts and free raffles within limits the insurance commissioner sets.

tx:SB 1318|relating to restrictions on c.title: Relating to restrictions on covenants not to compete for physicians and certain health care practitioners
tx:SB 1318|relating to restrictions on c.summary: Limits noncompete agreements for physicians to one year and a five-mile radius, caps buyouts at the doctor's annual pay, voids them for doctors fired without good cause, and applies similar limits to dentists, nurses and physician assistants.

tx:SCR 55|instructing the enrolling cler.title: Instructing the enrolling clerk of the senate to make corrections in SB 1964
tx:SCR 55|instructing the enrolling cler.summary: Directs the Senate enrolling clerk to correct a technical error in a passed bill on government use of artificial intelligence by replacing the abbreviation "AI" with "an artificial intelligence system."

tx:SB 614|relating to the authority of t.title: Relating to the authority of the Texas Forensic Science Commission to review and refer certain cases to the office of capital and forensic writs
tx:SB 614|relating to the authority of t.summary: Lets the Texas Forensic Science Commission refer to the state's office of capital and forensic writs cases it dismisses by expressly pointing to an earlier published commission report on the same subject, in addition to cases it investigates.

tx:HB 214|relating to the prosecution of.title: Relating to the prosecution of the criminal offenses of firearm and ammunition smuggling and terrorism
tx:HB 214|relating to the prosecution of.summary: Makes it a state jail felony to acquire a gun intending to give it to someone barred by state law from having one, extends firearm smuggling to ammunition, and adds crimes such as aggravated kidnapping and computer breaches to those prosecutable as terrorism.

tx:HR 1523|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, H.B. No. 46
tx:HR 1523|suspending limitations on con.summary: Suspends House rules so negotiators on the medical low-THC cannabis bill can add language letting a physician prescribe more than one package of low-THC cannabis to a patient within a 90-day period.

tx:SB 2371|relating to skimmers on elect.title: Relating to skimmers on electronic terminals; authorizing a civil penalty; creating criminal offenses
tx:SB 2371|relating to skimmers on elect.summary: Requires merchants that find a card skimmer on a checkout terminal, ATM or crypto kiosk to disable the terminal and report it to police and the state financial crimes center, sets civil penalties up to $5,000 a day, and criminalizes refusing inspections or improperly discarding skimmers.

tx:SB 1494|relating to the authority of.title: Relating to the authority of certain political subdivisions to change the date of their general elections
tx:SB 1494|relating to the authority of.summary: Lets local governments other than counties and municipal utility districts decide by December 31, 2025, to move their general elections to the November election date in odd-numbered years; the previous deadline for such a switch was 2016.

tx:SB 263|relating to the computation of.title: Relating to the computation of the cost of goods sold by television and radio broadcasters for purposes of the franchise tax
tx:SB 263|relating to the computation of.summary: Lets federally licensed television and radio broadcasters count broadcast-related costs, such as depreciation and the right to air programming, as cost of goods sold when figuring the state franchise tax, as film and TV producers already can.

tx:SB 610|relating to combating human tr.title: Relating to combating human trafficking by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
tx:SB 610|relating to combating human tr.summary: Lets the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation create an anti-human-trafficking unit, identify affected regulated businesses, coordinate with law enforcement and others, and adopt related inspection rules, and makes information identifying trafficking victims confidential.

tx:HB 3113|relating to requiring the bal.title: Relating to requiring the ballots of certain counties to be scannable
tx:HB 3113|relating to requiring the bal.summary: Requires counties that hand-count voted paper ballots to use ballots that can also be scanned and processed by an optical scanner.

tx:HB 4384|relating to the recovery of a.title: Relating to the recovery of a gas utility's gross plant placed in service not yet being recovered in rates
tx:HB 4384|relating to the recovery of a.summary: Lets gas utilities set aside, for later recovery in customer rates, the financing costs, depreciation and property taxes on equipment placed in service but not yet in rates, subject to Railroad Commission review and refund with interest if disallowed.

tx:HB 106|relating to the maintenance of.title: Relating to the maintenance of certain improvements associated with oil and gas development and production; authorizing an administrative penalty
tx:HB 106|relating to the maintenance of.summary: Requires oil and gas well operators to maintain the overhead power distribution lines they own or control for drilling and production under Railroad Commission rules, with administrative penalties for violations deposited in the state oil and gas cleanup fund.

tx:HJR 8|proposing a constitutional amen.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment providing for the creation of the Texas nuclear development fund to support the development, construction, and operation of advanced nuclear reactor projects
tx:HJR 8|proposing a constitutional amen.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2025 ballot, creating a Texas nuclear development fund the Public Utility Commission would use, on the governor's office's recommendations, for grants to build and operate advanced nuclear reactors and related infrastructure.

tx:HB 3204|relating to the polytechnic c.title: Relating to the Polytechnic College at Sam Houston State University, including the college's eligibility to participate in certain programs
tx:HB 3204|relating to the polytechnic c.summary: Renames the Josey School of Vocational Education at Sam Houston State University the Polytechnic College, has it offer career and technical certificate programs, funds it like a public state college, and makes its students eligible for certain state grant programs.

tx:SB 1141|relating to confirming the pr.title: Relating to confirming the provision of certain notices before the full adversary hearing in a suit affecting the parent-child relationship filed by the Department of Family and Protective Services
tx:SB 1141|relating to confirming the pr.summary: Requires judges, before the full hearing in a child-protection case brought by the state, to confirm in writing and in court that the agency told the alleged perpetrator of the right to record interviews and seek review of findings, and gave required information.

tx:SB 765|relating to the confidentialit.title: Relating to the confidentiality of fraud detection and deterrence information under the public information law
tx:SB 765|relating to the confidentialit.summary: Makes information governments hold about how they detect, prevent and investigate fraud, such as risk assessments, data, protocols and investigative materials, confidential and exempt from public records requests, while still allowing sharing for law enforcement and fraud prevention.

tx:HR 1501|suspending limitations on con.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, S.B. No. 568
tx:HR 1501|suspending limitations on con.summary: Suspends House rules so negotiators on the special education funding bill can make listed changes, including capping parent-directed special education grants at $1,500 subject to available funding, dropping a dyslexia teacher-training grant program and clarifying behavioral-support training for staff.

tx:HB 1130|relating to liability of a ca.title: Relating to liability of a cavern entity for injuries arising from certain activities
tx:HB 1130|relating to liability of a ca.summary: Shields commercial cave operators from liability for visitor injuries during recreational or educational cave activities if a required warning sign is posted, except for injuries caused by the operator's negligence, known dangers, poor staff training or intentional acts.

tx:HB 123|relating to measures to suppor.title: Relating to measures to support kindergarten readiness and early literacy and numeracy skills for public school students, including an early childhood parental support program, and to funding under the Foundation School Program for certain school districts and to support those measures
tx:HB 123|relating to measures to suppor.summary: Requires schools to test kindergarten through third graders' reading and math skills and give reading help to at-risk students, adds $250 per student served, offers parents $400 tutoring grants for struggling readers, and funds extra half-day intervention days.

tx:HB 4638|relating to the texas pharmac.title: Relating to the Texas Pharmaceutical Initiative
tx:HB 4638|relating to the texas pharmac.summary: Expands the board of the Texas Pharmaceutical Initiative, which plans state prescription drug services, from three to five governor-appointed members with staggered six-year terms, requires a business plan every two years, and extends the program from 2025 to 2027.

tx:HB 346|relating to support for new bu.title: Relating to support for new businesses
tx:HB 346|relating to support for new bu.summary: Lets the secretary of state set fees for expedited business and lien filings and searches, removing $15 and $25 caps and allowing different rates by business type, and keeps franchise tax and filing fee exemptions for new veteran-owned businesses from expiring in 2026.

tx:HB 3126|relating to the election of c.title: Relating to the election of certain school districts to participate in the uniform group coverage program for active school employees
tx:HB 3126|relating to the election of c.summary: Lets school entities that left the state's school-employee group health plan in 2022 rejoin in September 2026 by giving notice by December 31, 2025; they pay a risk stabilization fee the first year and must stay until 2031.

tx:HJR 182|proposing a constitutional am.title: Proposing a constitutional amendment authorizing the Veterans' Land Board to issue general obligation bonds in an aggregate principal amount that is greater than amounts previously authorized
tx:HJR 182|proposing a constitutional am.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2025 ballot, letting the Veterans' Land Board have up to $6 billion in outstanding general obligation bonds to fund land sales and home and land loans to Texas veterans.

tx:SB 2055|relating to participation in.title: Relating to participation in the Texas Leadership Scholars Program
tx:SB 2055|relating to participation in.summary: Bars the Higher Education Coordinating Board from adopting rules that limit which public universities may take part in the Texas Leadership Scholars Program or that favor students at certain universities, and requires each eligible university to receive at least one research scholarship award.

tx:SB 996|relating to fireworks sales to.title: Relating to fireworks sales to the public by retail fireworks permit holders on certain dates
tx:SB 996|relating to fireworks sales to.summary: Lets retail fireworks permit holders sell fireworks to the public through 11:59 p.m. on July 5, 2026, one extra day beyond the usual July 4 cutoff; the provision expires September 1, 2026.

tx:HB 5196|relating to telework for stat.title: Relating to telework for state employees
tx:HB 5196|relating to telework for stat.summary: Lets state agency heads approve telework through written agreements that must be renewed yearly and can be revoked at any time, bars offering telework as a condition of employment, and requires agencies allowing telework to adopt and publish a telework plan.

tx:SCR 47|granting the legislature permi.title: Granting the legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period beginning on Wednesday, April 16, 2025, and ending on Tuesday, April 22, 2025
tx:SCR 47|granting the legislature permi.summary: Gives each chamber of the Legislature permission to adjourn for more than three days during the period from April 16 through April 22, 2025.

tx:SB 1220|relating to the subject matte.title: Relating to the subject matter jurisdiction of the criminal trial courts of this state
tx:SB 1220|relating to the subject matte.summary: Provides that criminal trial courts can hear a criminal case without first requiring that civil or administrative remedies be exhausted, unless a law expressly says otherwise, and applies this to pending as well as future cases.

tx:SB 599|relating to the authority of a.title: Relating to the authority of a political subdivision to regulate a licensed, registered, or listed group day-care home or family home
tx:SB 599|relating to the authority of a.summary: Bars cities, counties and other local governments from requiring state-licensed, registered or listed group day-care homes or family homes to meet health and safety standards stricter than those set by state law or Health and Human Services Commission rules.

tx:HB 1094|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of transportation protection agreements
tx:HB 1094|relating to the regulation of.summary: Defines transportation protection agreements, contracts guaranteeing transport of a body after death to a holding facility or crematory, and provides that they are not prepaid funeral benefits and are exempt from state insurance law.

tx:HB 3135|relating to the issuance of s.title: Relating to the issuance of specialty license plates for retired firefighters
tx:HB 3135|relating to the issuance of s.summary: Requires the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles to design and issue specialty license plates for retired firefighters, including former volunteer and certified fire protection personnel, with no fee for issuing the plates.

tx:HB 1965|relating to a study on mental.title: Relating to a study on mental health services provided to veterans through the Texas Veterans Commission
tx:HB 1965|relating to a study on mental.summary: Requires the Texas Veterans Commission to study ways to expand mental health services through its Military Veteran Peer Network, focusing on peer service coordinators in rural areas, and to report findings to the Legislature by December 1, 2026.

tx:SB 571|relating to the reporting and.title: Relating to the reporting and investigation of certain misconduct and child abuse and neglect; creating a criminal offense
tx:SB 571|relating to the reporting and.summary: Expands the do-not-hire registry for school employees and contractors to cover more misconduct toward students, requires school leaders to report suspected harm to students to state education officials within 48 hours, and makes failing to disclose required history on a school job affidavit a Class B misdemeanor.

tx:HB 4748|relating to multiple award of.title: Relating to multiple award of contracts with indefinite delivery and indefinite quantity terms
tx:HB 4748|relating to multiple award of.summary: Lets the comptroller and state agencies award one contract to several vendors for similar goods or services when needed for adequate delivery, service or compatibility, with a written justification and best-value ordering, and exempts professional services contracts from state purchasing-method rules.

tx:SB 888|relating to the attorney gener.title: Relating to the attorney general's defense of a district or county attorney against certain lawsuits in federal court
tx:SB 888|relating to the attorney gener.summary: Allows the attorney general to defend a district or county attorney sued in federal court because of their office, when the case concerns enforcing a state law and the local prosecutor asks for help.

tx:SB 2420|relating to the regulation of.title: Relating to the regulation of platforms for the sale and distribution of software applications for mobile devices
tx:SB 2420|relating to the regulation of.summary: Requires app stores to verify users' ages, link minors' accounts to a parent's account and get parental consent for each app download or purchase by a minor, display app age ratings, and limit collection of personal data, starting January 1, 2026.

tx:SB 651|relating to the requirement th.title: Relating to the requirement that a veterans county service office report to the commissioners court or a designated county executive official
tx:SB 651|relating to the requirement th.summary: Lets a county's veterans county service office report to a county executive official designated by the county instead of directly to the commissioners court.

tx:HCR 101|designating the tomahawk rib.title: Designating the tomahawk rib-eye steak as the official State Steak of Texas and directing the Texas Department of Agriculture to promote the tomahawk rib-eye steak as part of efforts to support Texas beef and agricultural products
tx:HCR 101|designating the tomahawk rib.summary: Designates the tomahawk rib-eye steak as the official State Steak of Texas and directs the Texas Department of Agriculture to promote it as part of the state's efforts to support Texas beef and agricultural products.

tx:HB 2286|relating to the renewal of a.title: Relating to the renewal of a certificate of registration by certain interior designers
tx:HB 2286|relating to the renewal of a.summary: Lets interior designers who were registered without passing the registration exam keep renewing their registration until September 1, 2037, instead of September 1, 2027, after which they must pass the exam to renew.

tx:HB 865|relating to civil liability ar.title: Relating to civil liability arising from a firearm hold agreement
tx:HB 865|relating to civil liability ar.summary: Shields licensed firearm dealers and congressionally chartered veterans groups from lawsuits over injuries or deaths arising from agreements to temporarily hold a person's guns at the owner's request, except for unlawful conduct or gross negligence; veterans groups must follow dealer storage rules.

tx:HB 1449|relating to permits for mobil.title: Relating to permits for mobile food service establishments operating in certain counties
tx:HB 1449|relating to permits for mobil.summary: Extends county permitting of mobile food vendors to all counties over 1 million people, bars cities in those counties from requiring their own permits, lets counties partner with cities on inspections, and limits county permit fees to program costs.

tx:SCR 8|expressing opposition to the cr.title: Expressing opposition to the creation of a central bank digital currency
tx:SCR 8|expressing opposition to the cr.summary: Expresses the Legislature's opposition to the creation of a central bank digital currency, a digital form of money that would be a liability of the Federal Reserve rather than of commercial banks.

tx:HB 2970|relating to the implementatio.title: Relating to the implementation of projects by the Gulf Coast Protection District
tx:HB 2970|relating to the implementatio.summary: Bars Gulf Coast Protection District projects from disrupting navigation safety or two-way ship traffic in violation of Harris County port pilot commission rules, and has the governor, rather than the district board, appoint the board's presiding officer.

tx:SB 250|relating to municipal annexati.title: Relating to municipal annexation of an area adjacent to contiguous or connecting railroad rights-of-way
tx:SB 250|relating to municipal annexati.summary: Lets a city that is annexing land also annex an area beyond an adjacent railroad right-of-way running along its boundary if every owner of that area agrees, treating the area as contiguous to the city and waiving width requirements.
